text:
Once upon a time there was a little girl. She wanted to explore the world. One day, she saw a building. It looked fragile. She wanted to get closer to see it.

So she started to bow. She was hoping it was safe. She went further and further until the building started to move! She was scared, but it was too late. The building started to collapse.

The girl was so sad. She could not believe what had happened. The building was too fragile and it cracked down right in front of her eyes. There was nothing she could do.

The little girl went home and never explored the world again.

One day, Jack and Jill went to the park. They saw a big swing. Jack said, "Can I swing?" Jill said, "Yes, go ahead and swing!" Jack jumped onto the swing and started swinging. It was so much fun!

Suddenly, a rat scurried by. It was a high rat – much bigger than the other rats that Jack had seen. Jack yelled, "Look! A high rat!" Jill said, "Don't worry. The rat will go away soon."

Jack kept swinging. Every time he swung, he got higher and higher. He could almost touch the sky. When he was at the very top of the swing, he stopped and shouted, "Woo-hoo!"

Jack and Jill had a great day at the park. When it was time to go, Jack said, "Let's come back tomorrow to swing!" Jill said, "Yes, let's!"

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Jenny. She liked to play outside with her friends, but today she felt a bit upset. She didn't think she would be able to play because she had not had her cocoa yet.

So, Jenny's mummy said that she would get some cocoa for her. Jenny was very excited and went running around the house. She was so happy that she even quit doing her puzzles!

When the cocoa arrived, Jenny couldn't wait to try it. She took a big sip and it was so tasty! Jenny kept drinking until the cocoa was gone and she was feeling much better.

But when Jenny wanted to go outside and play again, her friends had already quit. They had gone home because it had been too long.

Jenny was disappointed and felt very upset. She started to cry, but then her mummy gave her a big hug and said, "Don't worry Jenny. We can play together inside instead".

Jenny smiled and they had lots of fun together until it was time for bed.

The sun was bright in the sky and little Timmy was excited. He was going to camp with his family. As they walked towards the camp, he noticed it was small.

Timmy said to his mom, “Why is camp so small?”

His mom smiled and said, “Don’t worry Timmy, there will be plenty to do.”

When they arrived at camp, Timmy was disappointed. He hadn’t expected it to be so small. But he tried to make the most of it. He joined some of the other campers playing a game.

The game was lots of fun, but Timmy started to struggle. He couldn’t keep up with the bigger kids. He was getting the ball wrong and was always the last one to finish.

At first, he started to cry. Then he looked up at his mom. His mom smiled and told him it was okay. She said he was doing his best.

That made Timmy feel better and he stopped struggling. He knew he might not be the fastest or strongest but he was determined to do his best.

And that was how Timmy conquered his small camp adventure.

Jessie had a thin guitar. It made him happy to play it. Every day, he would strum the strings and pluck little tunes. One day, however, something strange happened. He felt a tickle in his nose. He paused his playing and then he sneezed! His guitar made a funny noise when he sneezed. He smiled and continued playing, with the guitar sounding slightly different after the sneeze. Jessie kept playing and eventually the strange sound went away. Jessie kept his guitar thin and kept playing delicious melodies every day.

Once upon a time, there was a little blueberry. This blueberry was very interesting because it could balance on things. One day, the blueberry went to the park to play.

At the park, the blueberry saw a big slide. It wanted to balance on the slide. So, it climbed up the slide and balanced on the top. The blueberry was very happy and proud.

Then, the blueberry saw a swing. It wanted to balance on the swing, too. The blueberry jumped onto the swing and balanced there. It was fun! The blueberry had a great day at the park.

Lily and Max were at the big house with many seats. They came to see a show with their mom and dad. They had to wait for a long time before the show started. Lily and Max felt restless. They wanted to see the show now.

"Mom, when will the show start?" Lily asked.

"Soon, honey. Just be patient. Look, the lights are getting dim. That means the show is about to start." Mom said.

Lily and Max looked at the big curtain in front of them. They wondered what was behind it. They heard some music and some noises. They got excited.

Suddenly, the curtain opened and a man appeared on the stage. He wore a funny hat and a colorful suit. He had a big smile and a loud voice.

"Hello, everyone! Welcome to the magic show! Are you ready to see some amazing tricks?" He said.

Lily and Max clapped their hands and cheered. They loved magic. They wanted to see what the man could do.

The man took out a wand and a hat. He waved the wand and said some words. Then he reached into the hat and pulled out a rabbit. The rabbit was white and fluffy. It had long ears and a pink nose.

"Wow!" Lily and Max said.

The man put the rabbit back into the hat. He said some more words and waved the wand again. Then he reached into the hat and pulled out a bunch of flowers. The flowers were bright and pretty. They had different colors and smells.

"Ooh!" Lily and Max said.

The man gave the flowers to a lady in the front row. She smiled and thanked him. The man bowed and said, "Thank you, thank you. That was just the beginning. I have many more tricks to show you. Are you ready for more magic?"

Lily and Max nodded and shouted, "Yes, yes!"

They watched the man do more tricks on the stage. He made things appear and disappear. He cut a rope and put it back together. He guessed what people were thinking. He made a bird fly out of a paper. He made a coin multiply. He made a balloon turn into a dog.

Lily and Max were amazed and happy. They forgot about being restless. They enjoyed the show very much. They clapped and laughed and cheered. They had a lot of fun. They liked the man and his magic. They wanted to see more. They hoped the show would never end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved to go to the beach. One day, she went to the beach with her mommy and saw a big octopus in the water. She said, "Mommy, look! An octopus!" Her mommy said, "Yes, it's a big octopus. It has many arms."

Lily wanted to touch the octopus, but her mommy said it's not polite to touch sea creatures. Instead, her mommy gave her a popsicle to taste. It was very yummy! Lily said, "Mommy, this tastes so good!" Her mommy smiled and said, "I'm glad you like it."

As they were walking on the beach, they saw a little boy crying. Lily asked him, "What's wrong?" The little boy said, "I lost my toy." Lily said, "Don't worry, we'll help you find it." They searched and searched until they found the toy. The little boy said, "Thank you for being polite and helping me." Lily smiled and said, "You're welcome."

One day, a little girl named Amy went to the bathroom. She saw a big faucet on the wall. She thought it was funny and beautiful. She wanted to touch it but her mom said it was fragile. So Amy was careful and she only touched it lightly. Then she got brave and tried to push it. But the faucet didn't move. It stayed in the same spot. Amy got very frustrated and she pushed harder and harder. Suddenly, the faucet started to move! Water started coming out! Amy was so happy and she started to laugh and laugh. Her mom came into the bathroom and saw what had happened. She said, "Amy, you have to be careful with the fragile faucet!" Amy learned her lesson and made sure not to push too hard next time.

Once upon a time, there was a gifted fish. She liked to swim in the deep blue sea. Each day, the fish washed up onto the shore with the tide. She was looking for something special. One day, she spotted something shiny in the sand. It was a spoon!

The fish was so excited that she asked the other sea creatures for help. They all agreed to wash the spoon and make it sparkle. They used the sea water to rub the spoon until it glowed.

The gifted fish was so happy that she thanked the other animals with a special dance in the sea. She was so proud of her sparkling spoon and she knew she would never forget the day she found it.

Lily was in her classroom. She saw a large desk in the corner which was the teacher's. Although it was distant, she could see the colorful papers and objects on it. Lily was only three but she was learning a lot in school. She wanted to learn new things!

So one day, while her teacher was not around, Lily decided to walk to the desk. When she got there she looked carefully at all the things on the desk. She touched a pencil and pretended to write like her teacher did. She also looked at a book and pretended to be a scientist. Even though she couldn't read yet, she had fun pretending!

After a few minutes, Lily heard someone coming. It was her teacher. She quickly ran back to her seat. On her way she was very careful to make sure she didn't get caught.

The next day, Lily was very happy when the teacher asked her to come to the desk. She had learned that it was OK for her to explore and use her imagination. So, she went to the desk with a smile on her face, ready to learn something new.

Once upon a time, there was a small flower. Each morning, the sun would rise and the flower would bloom big and bright. All the bugs and the animals around would admire the flower's beauty.

One day, the sky suddenly got dark. The small flower trembled in fear as the thunder and lightning began to roar. It was so dark and loud that the small flower began to cry.

Then, a little bug flew over to the flower and said, "Do not cry, lovely flower! The darkness will not last. The sun will rise soon and you will bloom again."

At first the flower didn't believe the bug, but then—just as the bug said—the dark sky eventually turned to light. And then what do you know, the small flower began to bloom again, just like it did every other day.

The little bug smiled, glad to have been able to help the flower. From that day on, the small flower thanked the bug for its kindness every morning when it bloomed.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Mia. She loved to play in the park with her friends, but one day she came home feeling really ashamed. She had been playing with her friends and one of them gave her a tube. Mia was so excited and decided to count how many things she could put inside.

She filled up the tube with leaves, stones, feathers and even some of her toys. So she went over to her mom and proudly showed her what she had collected. Her mom was very surprised and said: "That’s a lot of things you’ve got there, Mia! Why do you have them all in the tube?"

Mia felt ashamed again, she hadn’t thought of that and she had never been so embarrassed. She quickly replied: “I wanted to count them all before I put them away.” Her mom gave her a big hug and said: “That’s very clever of you, Mia. Collecting things like that is lots of fun.”

Mia was so happy that her mom was proud of her. From that day, Mia always made sure to count all the things she collected in the tube before she put them away.

One day, Joey was playing in the park. He noticed there was a mug on the ground. He was curious and he picked it up and looked at it closely.

He called out to his Mom and said, "Mama, see this mug?"

Mom came over and said, "Yes, Joey, I'm sorry the mug looks so dirty. Put the mug back where you found it."

Joey understood what Mom said and put the mug back carefully on the ground. Then he looked around and noticed a bird hopping around on the park bench. He giggled with excitement.

Mom smiled and said, "Let's go see the bird, Joey."

Joey smiled and they went over to the park bench. Joey was so happy and he said, "Mama, I love the little bird."

Mom smiled and said, "Yes, Joey! Nature is so beautiful."

The two of them watched the bird for a few minutes before it flew away. Joey was sad but happy at the same time. He said to Mom, "Bye birdie, I'm sorry you had to go."

Mom hugged Joey and said, "We can look for more birds next time, Joey. Let's go home now."

And so, Joey and Mom went home, happy and thankful for such a wonderful day in the park.

Once upon a time, there was a little birdie named Tweety. Tweety lived in a cozy nest on top of a big tree. One day, Tweety saw a beautiful flower bloom in the meadow. It was so pretty that Tweety wanted to bring it to the nest.

Tweety tried to fly with the flower, but it was too heavy. Suddenly, Tweety saw smoke coming out of the chimney nearby. Tweety got worried and flew towards the chimney to see what was happening. Tweety saw a deaf kitty stuck in the chimney, meowing for help.

Tweety quickly flew back to the nest and called all the birdies to help. Together, they flew to the chimney and rescued the kitty. The kitty was very grateful and gave Tweety a big hug. From that day on, Tweety and the kitty were the best of friends and always went on adventures together.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a favorite pillow that she loved to snuggle with every night. One day, Lily's mommy noticed that the pillow was very dirty and needed to be cleaned.

Mommy said to Lily, "Your pillow is dirty. We need to wash it so it can be clean and cozy again."

Lily replied, "Okay mommy, I want my pillow clean so I can sleep with it tonight."

Mommy washed the pillow and when it was clean, she gave it back to Lily. Lily hugged her pillow and said, "Thank you mommy, my pillow is clean and smells good now. I can sleep well tonight."

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim lived in a small house with his mom, dad, and his dog, Spot. Tim loved to play with Spot every day after school. They would run around the yard and have lots of fun together.

One night, Tim's mom and dad decided to buy a new mattress for Tim's bed. They went to the store and picked out a big, soft mattress for him. When they got home, they put the new mattress in Tim's room. It was getting dark outside, so Tim's mom turned on the light so they could see better.

Tim was excited to sleep on his new mattress. It was so soft and cozy. He put on his pajamas and climbed into bed. Spot jumped up on the bed too, and they both snuggled under the covers. Tim's mom turned off the light, and the room was dark. Tim and Spot fell asleep on the new mattress, and they had sweet dreams all night long.

Once upon a time there was a bird called Jay. One day Jay wanted to fly and play with his friends, but he was tangled in a thread. The thread was too strong and Jay couldn’t fly away no matter how hard he tried. He was very upset, so he started to cry. Then a friendly butterfly came and saw Jay. The butterfly said, “Hey Jay, why don’t you relax, and I will help you get free.” So Jay settled down and the butterfly slowly unwound the thread. Jay thanked him and the butterfly said, “My friend, always remember that if you stay calm and don't panic, you can always find a way out of any problem.” Jay thanked the butterfly for his advice and flew away happily with his friends. The moral of the story is that if you remain calm and don't panic, you can always find a way out of any problem.

One day, Andy and Sarah were playing together in the park. Andy wanted to play a game, so he said "let's draw a circle". Sarah liked the idea, so they both drew a big circle on the ground. It was so big that they could both stand inside it.

The game they were playing was very competitive. They both wanted to be the winner. So they let go of each other's hands and began running around and around in the circle. Faster and faster they went until Sarah was almost out of breath.

Andy wanted to win, so he tried to make Sarah fall by pushing her with his shoulder. But Sarah was too fast. She kept running and running, getting around the circle more than Andy. Finally, she touched one of the sides of the circle and won the game.

The end.

Tom and Sue are twins. They like to play in the attic. The attic is full of old things. Some things are ancient. Ancient means very, very old.

One day, they find a big box. The box is dusty and heavy. They open the box. Inside, they see many shiny things. They see coins, rings, necklaces, and a lamp. The lamp is ancient. It has a bulb on top.

"Wow, look at this lamp!" Tom says. He picks up the lamp and rubs it. He wants to see if it works.

"Be careful, Tom. It might be broken," Sue says. She is afraid of the dark. She wants to go back downstairs.

Suddenly, the bulb flashes. A puff of smoke comes out of the lamp. Tom and Sue are scared. They drop the lamp and hide behind the box.

"Hello, hello. Who are you?" a voice says. The voice is loud and strange. Tom and Sue peek from behind the box. They see a man. The man is big and blue. He has a long beard and a turban. He is smiling.

"I am the genie of the lamp. You have freed me from my prison. I am very grateful. I will grant you three wishes. Anything you want, I can do," the man says.

Tom and Sue are amazed. They have never seen a genie before. They have read about them in books. They wonder what to wish for.

"Can you make us fly?" Tom asks. He wants to fly like a bird.

"Can you make us rich?" Sue asks. She wants to have all the shiny things.

"Of course, of course. Anything you want. But be careful what you wish for. Sometimes, wishes can have consequences," the genie says. He snaps his fingers. Tom and Sue feel a tingling in their feet. They look down. They see wings on their shoes. They look at each other. They smile. They are ready to fly.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Stella who was ready to go for a walk. She put on her shoes and said goodbye to her mom. As she walked, Stella approached a big hill. She was scared that she wouldn't be able to pass over it. But her mom had said that if she was ready, she could do anything. So she said to herself, "I'm ready!"

Stella started to walk up the hill. She climbed and climbed, and the hill just kept getting bigger. She was starting to get tired, but she kept going. Finally, she reached the top. She was so proud of herself!

But then, Stella noticed something: the other side of the hill was very steep. She hesitated, but suddenly remembered what her mom said. She was ready, she could do it! So Stella started to run down the hill.

At first, it was so much fun! But then, Stella started to fall faster and faster. She held on tight and closed her eyes. At last, she reached the bottom of the hill. She opened her eyes and was so happy to see that she had made it!

Stella realized that she could do anything if she was ready. And from that day on, she was ready for anything.

Once upon a time, there was a girl. She was walking along a shore. The shore was ugly and she wasn't happy. Suddenly, something flew up in the sky. It was an orange bird. The bird was so close she could kick it! She quickly raced forward and tried to kick it, but she missed. The bird flew away and landed on the shore. The girl ran to the shore and tried to kick the bird again, but it flew away. The girl was sad, but she kept walking along the shore. She saw something in the water. It looked like a fish! She walked closer and tried to kick the fish, but again, she missed. She kept trying, but it seemed too hard. After some time, she finally kicked it! The fish splashed back into the water, and the girl was so happy. She smiled and kept walking along the shore.

Once upon a time, there was a little bird who loved to sit on branches. One day, the little bird saw a beautiful branch that had a gentle wind blowing through it. He decided to sit on the branch and take a nap.

The branch was so comfy and gentle that the little bird fell fast asleep. Suddenly, the wind picked up and sway the branch back and forth. The little bird was scared, but he held on tight.

Then the branch stopped moving and the little bird looked around. He was so happy to see that he was in a big tree, with lots of branches and leaves!

The little bird decided to make the branch his home. He slept there every night and played on it during the day. He was very happy in his new home and he was never scared of the gentle breeze again!

Once upon a time there was a famous bear. His name was Barney and he had a very special pair of sunglasses. Everyone admired his sunglasses and wanted a pair just like his.

One day Barney was walking in a field and he saw something shiny in the grass. When he got closer he realised it was a shiny pair of sunglasses! He was so excited and quickly put them on. He decided to keep them as they were even better than the ones he already had.

Unfortunately, that same day there was a very windy storm and Barney had to surrender his new sunglasses to the wind. He watched sadly as the wind carried them away.

Although Barney was sad about losing his cool looking glasses, he was happy that he had been lucky enough to find them in the first place. He also knew that wearing his old famous sunglasses made him look special too!

Once upon a time, there was a famous snack. It was a yummy cookie. Everyone loved it. The cookie was sweet and tasty. It was the best snack in the town.

One day, a little boy named Tim wanted to taste the famous snack. He asked his mom for the cookie. His mom said, "Yes, you can have the cookie." Tim was very happy.

Tim took a big bite of the cookie. It tasted so good! He shared the cookie with his friends. They all loved the famous snack. They played and ate the cookie together. It was a fun day.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to pick flowers in her garden. One day, she saw a purple flower that she really wanted to pick. But she knew she had to resist the urge to pick it because it was the only one of its kind in the garden.

Lily decided to sit next to the purple flower and admire it instead. As she sat there, she noticed a butterfly flying around it. The butterfly was also attracted to the purple flower.

Lily was happy that she resisted picking the flower because now the butterfly could enjoy it too. She watched as the butterfly fluttered around the flower, and she felt happy knowing that she did the right thing.

Tim and Lily were playing in the park with their ball. They liked to kick the ball to each other and run after it. Sometimes they would pause and look at the birds and the flowers. They were having fun.

But then they saw a big brown dog. The dog was barking and running towards them. Tim and Lily were scared. They did not know the dog. They did not know if the dog was nice or mean. They wanted to run away, but they did not want to leave their ball.

The dog reached the ball and picked it up with his mouth. He wagged his tail and looked at Tim and Lily. He wanted to play with them. He dropped the ball and waited for them to kick it. But Tim and Lily did not move. They were still scared.

Then they heard a voice. It was the dog's owner. He was a man with a hat and a leash. He called the dog's name. It was Rex. He said, "Rex, come here. Stay. Good boy." He walked towards the dog and the children. He smiled and said, "I'm sorry. Rex is very friendly. He loves to play with balls. He won't hurt you. Do you want to play with him?"

Tim and Lily looked at each other. They looked at the man and the dog. They saw that the dog was not mean. He was just playful. They decided to give him a chance. They nodded and said, "Yes, we want to play with him."

The man gave them the leash and said, "OK, you can play with him for a while. I'll sit on that bench and watch. Just be careful and don't let him run away." He went to the bench and sat down.

Tim and Lily took the leash and the ball. They kicked the ball to Rex and he chased it. He brought it back and dropped it. They did it again and again. They laughed and had fun. They made a new friend. They were not scared anymore.

Once upon a time there was a yellow billboard in a meadow. This billboard was the only thing in the meadow and it stood quiet and still. No one paid it much attention until one day a little girl came to visit. She stepped into the meadow and saw the yellow billboard and was curious. She started to explore it and as she did she forgot all of her troubles and began to relax. She enjoyed the peaceful meadow and knew her day would be filled with fun. After a while she decided to take a break and sat near the yellow billboard. As she sat and relaxed, she smiled, knowing that this special place could be her new hidden spot.

Once upon a time there was a gifted girl. Her name was Anna and she was three years old. She could run fast and she loved to play.

One day, Anna's mom called out. "Anna, it's time for exercise!"

Anna smiled but said, "Can I play first?"

Her mom smiled too. "Well, okay, but first you have to do your exercise. It will help you stay strong and healthy."

So Anna exercised. She jumped, stretched and ran. She even did a little dance. When she finished she was very tired, but she felt good.

"Good job, Anna!" her mom said and gave her a hug. "Now you can go play!"

Anna smiled. She knew that exercise was important and she was glad her mom reminded her. She ran off to play, feeling happy and gifted.

The clown was very smart. He was standing at the center of the park, entertaining a group of kids. He wowed them with his tricks and jokes and the kids were mesmerized.

Suddenly, he noticed one little girl who was not amused. She was standing off to the side, staring at him with her big eyes.

The clown felt a bit uneasy. He cleared his throat and said, "What's wrong, little girl?"

The girl pointed at him and said, "You look silly."

The clown was surprised. "Why do you think I look silly?" he asked.

The girl shrugged her shoulders. "I don't know. I just don't like clowns."

The clown knew he had to do something, so he smiled and said, "I have some special magic just for you. Would you like to see it?"

The girl hesitated but then nodded her head. The clown did his trick, but the girl didn't seem impressed. She continued to stare at him in silence.

Finally, the clown said, "You're a very smart little girl, don't you think so?"

The girl smiled, and the clown knew he had won her over. She said, "Yes, I'm very smart."

The clown winked. "That's good. Now can you do me a favor and smile?"

The girl smiled and the clown's heart

Mike and his mommy went for a visit. They drove to a special point. Mike had never been there before.

When they got there, Mike saw so many new things. He saw lots of trees and animals. He was so excited! He ran around, exploring the area.

He got very tired. He lay down under a tree. His Mommy sat with him. They looked at the clouds in the sky together. They saw a butterfly and some birds.

After a while, when Mike was not tired anymore, they visited the pond near by. They saw so many fish and a frog. Mike had a great time.

Then it was time to go home. Mike said goodbye to the special point and vowed to visit again soon!

Once upon a time, there was a kid named Timmy. Timmy loved playing outside with his friends. One day, Timmy found a shiny light in the park. He picked it up and showed it to his friends. They all thought it was very pretty.

But then, a big bully came and took the light away from Timmy. Timmy was sad and didn't know what to do. His friend, Lily, said, "I think we should tell a grown-up." So, they went to tell the teacher.

The teacher talked to the bully and gave the light back to Timmy. Timmy was happy again and learned that it's important to tell a grown-up when someone takes something from you. The moral of the story is that it's always good to ask for help when you need it.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved the snow so much! When it snowed, she would put on her warm coat and go outside to play. But one day, her coat didn't fit anymore. It was too small for her.

Lily's mom said, "Don't worry, I will buy you a new coat that will fit you." And she did! The new coat was warm and cozy, and it fit Lily perfectly.

Now Lily could go outside and play in the snow without feeling cold. Her mom allowed her to stay outside for as long as she wanted, as long as she wore her new coat. Lily was so happy and grateful for her new coat. She could enjoy the snow and make snowmen again!

Isaac was preparing breakfast in the kitchen. He was getting ready to make porridge and pancakes. He had already set the table and was busy preparing the ingredients.

Suddenly, Isaac's pet puppy began to bark excitedly. They both ran to the door. Standing there was a strange man. He was wearing a big coat and was impatiently tapping his foot.

The man smiled at Isaac and asked, "Are you ready for the surprise?" Isaac wrung his hands nervously and shook his head.

The man persisted, "Come on then! You need to be patient - I'm sure you will love it!"

Isaac gulped and said, "OK!" He looked back at his pet puppy and they both walked towards the man.

The man opened his coat and out popped a tiny brown kitten. Isaac smiled and hugged the little kitten. He couldn't believe it. He had a pet of his own!

Lily and Ben love to play music. They have a band with their toys. Lily plays the drum and Ben plays the guitar. They sing loud and have fun.

One day, they see a big snowman in the park. He has a hat, a scarf and a carrot nose. They want to play with him.

"Hello, snowman!" Lily says. "Do you want to join our band?"

The snowman does not answer. He does not move.

"Maybe he is shy," Ben says. "Or maybe he is cold. Let's give him a hug."

They run to the snowman and hug him. He is very cold and hard.

"Ouch!" Lily says. "He is not soft. He is like ice."

"He is frozen," Ben says. "That's why he does not talk or play. He is not a real person. He is made of snow."

Lily and Ben feel sad. They want a friend to play with.

"Maybe we can make him happy," Lily says. "Maybe we can play music for him. Maybe he will like it."

They go back to their band and start to play. They play a long song for the snowman. They hope he will smile.

The snowman does not smile. He does not move. He does not hear them. He is frozen.

Lily and Ben stop playing. They look at the snowman.

"He does not like our music," Lily says. "He does not like anything. He is not a good friend."

"Let's go home," Ben says. "We have each other. We are a good band."

They take their toys and leave. They do not look at the snowman. He is frozen.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy. His name was Josh. He was three-years-old and he was excited because he was going to get a new mattress. Josh's parents took him to visit a store. He was amazed by all the different colours of mattresses! After he chose his favourite one, his parents said they were ready to purchase it. Josh asked his mom and dad to please carry the mattress home. He was so excited that he wanted to help carry it! His parents smiled and said, "Yes, of course you can help." So the three of them carefully carried the mattress home.

When they arrived, Josh's dad asked, "Do you want to help put the mattress on the bed?" Josh was delighted and answered, "Yes, please!" His dad smiled and said, "Let's do it!" So Josh and his dad put the mattress on the bed and Josh said, "It looks amazing!" His mom and dad smiled with pride and said, "Yes, it looks perfect. Now go to sleep and have sweet dreams!" Josh smiled and snuggled down on the new, colorful mattress. He said "Goodnight" and fell asleep with a smile on his face.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lily. She loved to sing and talk a lot. One day, she went to a party where she saw a big, shiny microphone. She was so excited to use it and speak into it.

But when she got close to the microphone, she saw that it wasn't clean. It was covered in dust and dirt. Lily didn't want to use the dirty microphone, so she asked her mom for a cloth to clean it.

After cleaning the microphone, Lily spoke into it and sang her favorite song. Everyone at the party clapped and cheered for her. From that day on, Lily made sure to always clean the microphone before using it to speak or sing.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, she was playing with her toys when her mom called her for lunch. Lily went to the kitchen and saw a big bowl of soup on the table. The soup looked rich and yummy.

Lily's mom asked, "Do you want some soup, Lily?" Lily said, "Yes, please!" She took a spoon and started eating. Suddenly, she saw her brother playing outside and she wanted to join him. She asked her mom, "Can I go outside and play with my brother?" Her mom said, "Sure, but be careful not to splash the soup."

Lily went outside and saw her brother playing with water. She wanted to join him but she didn't want to get her clothes wet. Her brother said, "Come on, Lily! Let's splash together!" Lily thought for a moment and said, "Okay, but let me finish my soup first." After she finished her soup, she joined her brother and they splashed together happily.

Once upon a time there was a deaf plastic man. He lived in a very quiet place where he could not hear anything. One day he wanted to make something special with all the plastic he had.

So he started to mix all of the plastic together. He took the red plastic and mixed it with the blue plastic. Then he added some green plastic and a bit of yellow plastic. He mixed it all together until it was a beautiful rainbow.

He was so excited to show everyone his work, but he could not hear if anyone was talking about it. Nevertheless everyone was very impressed! He showed them all how the rainbow he created changed colour when the light hit it from different angles.

It wasn't long before the deaf plastic man was famous and people from all over the world started coming to see his work. Everyone was so amazed by his beautiful colours and the way he mixed them together.

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to read books. One day, her mom took her to a library. When they arrived, the librarian introduced herself to Lily and her mom.

Lily saw a big bookshelf filled with books. She asked her mom if she could pick a book. Her mom said yes, so Lily walked over to the bookshelf. She looked at all the books and found a gray one that looked interesting.

Lily brought the gray book to her mom and showed it to her. "Look, Mommy! I found a gray book!" she said. Her mom smiled and said, "That's great, Lily. Let's check it out and take it home to read."

Lily was so happy to have a new book to read. She thanked the librarian for introducing herself and for letting her borrow the gray book. Then, she and her mom went home to read the book together. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a tiny mouse named Speedy. He was the fastest mouse in the entire world. Everywhere Speedy went, he was known for being fast. He loved to run and play.

One day, Speedy heard about a special contest. The contest was to find the fastest mouse in the world. Whoever won would get a very special microphone. So Speedy decided to enter the contest.

Speedy practiced and practiced to make sure he was ready. Finally, the day of the contest arrived. Speedy was ready and raring to go. He ran faster than all the other mice. In the end, Speedy beat all the other mice and won the microphone. Everyone was very impressed with Speedy's speed and he was very proud.

Speedy was so happy that he was the fastest mouse in the world. He was even happier because his fast speed won him the very special microphone. Speedy couldn't wait to show everyone his new prize.

Once upon a time there were two friends: a turtle and a rabbit. They often raced each other, and each time the rabbit would win. "You're too slow," the rabbit would tease the turtle.

One day, the turtle had an idea. He asked the rabbit if they could race on a sail. The rabbit thought the idea was stupid but agreed anyway.

The next day they meet at the beach. The turtle hopped onto his sail, but before the rabbit could get onto his own, a big gust of wind came and blew the turtle further and further away from shore. The rabbit shouted, "Hurry Turtle! Race back!" But it was too late. Eventually the turtle disappeared over the horizon and the rabbit never saw him again.

The rabbit learnt a valuable lesson that day about not being too stupid and trusting the turtle's ideas!

One day, Johnny was walking in the park and he saw a cool hanger. He got curious and he walked towards it. When he touched it, it made a funny noise.

Johnny paused for a moment and looked around, then he continued to touch the hanger. He thought it was really cool!

Suddenly, a little girl walked towards him and said, "What you doin'?" Johnny was surprised, but he replied, "I'm just touching this cool hanger".

The girl smiled, then said, "Can I touch it too?" Johnny smiled, and said, "Sure, go ahead".

The little girl touched the hanger and it made the same noise. She was so happy and she laughed.

Johnny and the girl kept touching the cool hanger until they had to go home. Johnny was so happy that he got to make a new friend in the park!

Once there was a little girl called Jane. She was three years old and loved to play in her house. One day she saw something very shiny in the corner of the room - a mop! It was white with a long handle and Jane was curious.

Jane asked her mom what it was. Her mom said it was a mop and that it was used to make the floor clean. Jane was very excited and asked if she could try using it. Her mom said that of course she could.

So Jane took the mop and started to make the floor very clean. She moved it in big circles and was very careful not to get any dirt on the white part. When she had finished cleaning, she was very proud of herself.

The floor looked very shiny and she was amazed at how tidy it was. Her mom was also very happy that she had made the floor so clean. From then on, Jane and her mom used the mop to make the floor always very clean.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who always loved helping her mom around the house. Every day, when she was done playing outside, she would go inside and help her mom with the laundry.

Today was no different. The little girl grabbed the basket of clothes, placed them in the washing machine, and added some special soap. She pushed the button and watched as the machine started spinning.

"Mom, can I help dry the clothes?" asked the little girl.

"Of course you can, sweetie," said Mom.

The little girl grabbed the freshly washed clothes and hung them on the line outside. She hummed as she worked, dancing around the clothesline and making sure the clothes were nice and dry.

When she was done, the little girl took the clothes down from the line and folded them neatly. She placed them in a basket and brought them to her mom.

"Mom, I'm done drying the clothes!" the little girl said with a smile.

"Great job, sweetie!" said Mom. "Your help is so useful!"

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to eat sour candy. One day, she went to the store with her mommy to buy some candy. She saw a big white bag of sour gummies and asked her mommy to buy it for her.

Mommy said, "Sure, we can put it in the cart."

Lily was so happy and said, "Thank you, mommy! Can I have some now?"

Mommy said, "Not yet, we have to pay first."

After they paid, they went to the park and Lily shared her sour gummies with her friend. They both loved the sour taste and had so much fun playing together.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside with her friends. One day, they found a weapon in the bushes. It was a big stick that looked sharp and dangerous.

Lily thought it was charming and wanted to keep it. But her mom told her it was not safe and took it away. Lily was sad, but she knew her mom was right.

Later that day, Lily and her friends were playing catch. They threw a ball back and forth, but it went too far. Lily ran after it, but she didn't see the big stick on the ground. She tripped and fell, and the stick hurt her badly.

Lily's mom rushed her to the hospital, but it was too late. Lily had been hurt too badly by the weapon. Her friends were sad and sorry, and they knew they should have listened to Lily's mom.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy who loved tomatoes. He went to pick some tomatoes in the garden everyday, because they were so yummy!

One morning he spotted a huge tomato. He smiled and started to slip towards it, but he was too excited and he slipped over. He began to cry - the huge tomato was ruined!

"It's ok, my little one," his mum said. "Let's go get another tomato".

So the little boy and his mum went to find another tomato, but none were as big or as yummy as the huge one. They had to go home empty handed.

The little boy was so sad. He had wanted that huge tomato so badly. He didn't like the ending at all.

Once upon a time there was a little girl. Her name was Lily. Lily lived in a big city. She wanted to measure it to see how big it is.

One day, Lily went around the city with a tape measure. She measured the roads, the buildings, and the parks.

She was about to measure one of the parks when she saw something disgusting. It was a big yucky puddle with some creepy wriggling things in it. She didn't want to measure it so she decided to go somewhere else.

Lily measured a few more places in the city. When she was done, she went back home, happy that she had measured the city.

Once upon a time there was a selfish old man who lived all by himself. Each day he went into the forest to look for special plants. He had one special plant that he was especially proud of.

One day, the old man was walking in the woods and he heard a strange noise. He followed the noise until he came to a small, shiny box that was rattling around.

The old man opened the box and found a small, furry creature inside. The old man was happy and he decided to take the creature home with him.

The old man named the creature Bob and he was very nice to him. Bob wanted to return the favor, so he decided to take the old man's special plant to the market and try to sell it.

The old man was very angry and he yelled at Bob to bring the plant back. But Bob would not listen.

The old man had to leave the next day for an important errand, so he asked Bob to stay and watch over his house. Bob happily agreed.

When the old man returned, he found that Bob had delivered the special plant and had used the money to buy the old man a new plant.

The old man was so touched that he could no longer be selfish. From then on, he welcomed Bob and loved him like his own.

Once upon a time, there was a happy girl. She had a special dream that was very bright. Every night, she saw a magical garden filled with beautiful flowers. The flowers were so happy and they glowed like the stars. One night, the girl decided to visit the garden.

When she arrived, it was more dazzling than she imagined. The flowers were huge and so colorful! She was so excited and started running and dancing between the flowers. As she danced, the flower started to bloom. Soon the whole garden was full of blooming flowers and the girl's dream came to life.

But then something scary happened. All of the blooming flowers turned into monsters and started chasing the girl. She was so scared that she started to cry. But then she saw a tiny flower in the corner and she remembered her dream. She blew on the flower and suddenly a beautiful rainbow filled the sky. The monsters were scared of the rainbow and they ran away. The girl smiled and felt so happy.

The garden was full of light and beauty again. The girl hugged the little flower and thanked it for helping her. From then on, she would come to the garden often and her dream would keep blooming.

Once upon a time, a wise old owl lived in a tall tree. He had big eyes that gave him a special look. Every day, he watched the animals play in the forest.

One day, a little rabbit came to the wise owl with a problem. He had a big load of carrots and didn't know how to carry them home. The wise owl thought for a moment and said, "I have an idea! Let's ask our friend, the strong ant, for help."

The rabbit and the wise owl went to the strong ant. The ant agreed to help the rabbit carry the load of carrots. They all worked together to move the carrots to the rabbit's home. The rabbit was very happy and thanked the wise owl and the strong ant.

From that day on, the animals in the forest knew that they could always ask the wise owl for help. They learned that when they worked together, they could solve any problem. The wise owl's special look and big eyes always watched over the forest, making sure all the animals were happy and safe.

Once upon a time, a little girl named Lily had a task to do. Her task was to cover her teddy bear with a blanket. She went to her room and saw her teddy bear was not clear, it was dirty! So, she took a cloth and cleaned her teddy bear. After that, she covered her teddy bear with a soft blanket. Her teddy bear looked so cozy and warm now! Lily was happy that she completed her task.

Once upon a time there was a grumpy man. He never smiled. One day he went to the park with a sword. He wanted to swing on the swing. He held his sword in his hand, sat on the swing and started to swing. It was so much fun. Suddenly, he started to laugh and smile. He kept on swinging and playing. All the other children saw the grumpy man become happy. They all joined in and started to have lots of fun on the swings. Everyone in the park was laughing, smiling and playing together. They all enjoyed the afternoon swinging together.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to go to the beach with his parents. One day, while they were at the beach, Timmy saw a dolphin swimming in the ocean. He was so excited and wanted to take a closer look.

Timmy asked his dad, "Can we take a boat and go see the dolphin?" His dad said, "Sure, let's go!" They got on a boat and went to see the dolphin. When they got there, they saw that the dolphin was very clean and shiny.

Timmy said, "Wow, that dolphin is so clean! Can we take a picture with it?" His dad said, "Sure thing, Timmy!" They took a picture with the dolphin and Timmy was very happy. He will always remember the day he saw the clean dolphin.

One morning, Jack woke up. He was feeling healthy and happy. He put on his clothes and went to the kitchen. His mommy was in the kitchen and she had a special surprise for him. She made Jack some spaghetti with a delicious red sauce. He tasted it and it was yummy! He ate it all and felt full and healthy. Then he smiled and thanked his mommy.

After breakfast, Jack was ready to explore the garden. He ran outside and saw the flowers, the bees and the butterflies. He was so excited! He ran around and around the garden, enjoying it until he was tired.

When Jack went back inside, he went to take a nap. He closed his eyes and soon fell asleep. So he could wake up later and explore the garden again!

Lila and Sam were friends who liked to play in the snow. They wanted to make an igloo, a big house of snow. They worked hard to roll snowballs and stack them together. They made a door and a window and crawled inside. They felt warm and cozy in their igloo.

But they were also hungry. They wished they had something to eat. They remembered that Lila's mom had baked some cookies for them. They were in a tin on the kitchen table. They decided to go back to Lila's house and get some cookies. They put on their hats and gloves and left their igloo.

On their way, they saw a little bird. The bird was shivering and looked sad. It had no food and no shelter. Lila and Sam felt sorry for the bird. They wanted to help it. They had an idea. They took one cookie from the tin and broke it into small pieces. They sprinkled the pieces around the igloo. They hoped the bird would find them and eat them.

Then they went to Lila's house and shared the rest of the cookies. They drank some hot chocolate and told Lila's mom about their igloo and the bird. Lila's mom was proud of them. She said they were kind and generous. She said they had learned a valuable lesson. She said that it is better to give than to receive. She said that by helping the bird, they had made themselves and the bird happy.

Lila and Sam agreed. They felt grateful for their cookies, their igloo, and their friendship. They also felt grateful for the bird, who had taught them how to be compassionate. They smiled and hugged each other. They knew they had done a good thing. They hoped the bird was warm and full in their igloo. They decided to visit their igloo and the bird again the next day.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a good day at the park with her friends. As she was walking home, she noticed her toe hurt. She asked her mom, "Mommy, why does my toe hurt?" Her mom replied, "Let's go home and weigh you to see if you need new shoes."

Lily was excited to weigh herself because she loved seeing how much she had grown. Her mom put her on the scale and Lily saw she had grown two pounds since her last check-up. Her mom said, "You're getting so big! We need to buy you new shoes."

Lily was happy to hear that, and her toe stopped hurting once she had new shoes. She ran around the house, showing off her new shoes to her family. From that day on, Lily made sure to weigh herself regularly to see how much she was growing.

Mia and Jack were two competitive friends. They were both very eager to fight. They each had a toy pistol for the fight.

Mia said, “I don’t want to fight. I just want to play.”

Jack said, “No, let’s fight. It’s fun.”

Mia thought for a moment. She said, “Okay, let’s fight. But let’s make sure we’re being fair and not too competitive.”

Jack agreed and they started the fight. They ran around and shot each other with their toy pistols.

Mia and Jack laughed and had lots of fun. It was a long and exciting fight.

In the end, they decided to call it a draw. They decided to be friends again and they hugged each other. They both enjoyed the fight and they became even closer friends.

Once upon a time, in a quiet little town, there lived a girl named Anna. She loved to play outside with her friends. One sunny day, Anna found a pair of sunglasses on the ground. She picked them up and put them on. She felt very cool and happy wearing her new sunglasses.

Anna showed her friends the sunglasses and they all wanted to try them on. But Anna didn't want to share her cool sunglasses. She felt special wearing them and thought her friends would feel special too if they wore them. So, she kept the sunglasses to herself and didn't let anyone else try them on.

As the days went by, Anna's friends stopped playing with her because she wouldn't share her sunglasses. Anna started to feel sad and lonely. She realized that it's better to share and be kind to others. So, she decided to share her sunglasses with her friends. They all took turns wearing the sunglasses and had lots of fun together. From that day on, Anna always shared her things with her friends and they all felt happy together.

The moral of the story is that sharing and being kind to others makes everyone happy.

Once there was a man who wanted to put something at the top of the stairs. But he was a really tall man, and he had a really tall ladder. The ladder was too tall to fit through the door and up the stairs.

The man thought and thought and eventually realised he had an old thin ladder. He put the thin ladder through the door, put it against the stairs, and carefully began to climb up it.

The man felt relieved to finally be at the top of the stairs. He took out a large box from his pocket and put it on the last step. He then took out a tiny toy and placed it on the box.

He smiled and said "I can now put the toy on top of the stairs!" The man was happy he was able to put the toy on top of the stairs with his thin old ladder.

Tom and Mia are friends. They like to play in the sand. They make a big pile of sand and say it is an island. They want to go to the island and have fun.

They find two sticks and use them as oars. They pretend they have a boat and row to the island. They say they are pirates and look for treasure. They dig in the sand and find a shiny stone. They are happy and say it is a gold coin.

But then they hear a loud roar. They see a big dog running towards them. The dog is angry and wants to take their coin. They are scared and want to go back to the shore.

"Help, help!" they shout. "The dog is coming!"

A man hears them and runs to them. He is strong and picks up the dog. He says it is his dog and he is sorry. He says the dog likes shiny things and did not want to hurt them.

He gives them a hug and a cookie. He says they are brave and clever. He says they can keep the coin and play with the dog if they want.

Tom and Mia smile and say thank you. They are not scared anymore. They share the cookie and the coin. They play with the dog and the man. They have fun on the island.

John thought a lot. He thought about the hurricane. He was very scared, but his parents told him it was ok. He watched the hurricane come closer and closer. His parents told him it was very strong and he needed to be careful. John was very intelligent. He thought about ways to be safe. He decided to hide in the closet and it was the best idea. John stayed in the closet until the hurricane was gone. He felt good knowing he had made an intelligent decision. He was glad the hurricane was over.

One day, Rob heard a ringing. It was coming from the river. He ran to the river and saw a fine boat. The boat had a bell that was ringing. Rob climbed aboard the boat and waved goodbye to the river.

Rob sailed down the river. He could see fish swimming and birds flying in the sky. The boat made a soft rocking motion as it sailed along. Rob was having a great time.

Suddenly, the boat hit a rock in the river and stopped. Rob began to feel worried. He got off the boat and saw an old man standing by the riverbank. The old man showed Rob how to use a paddle to move the boat.

Rob hopped back in the boat and took the paddle. He pushed and pulled the paddle and the boat started moving again. Pretty soon, Rob was fine and the boat was back on course. He waved goodbye to the old man and continued down the river.

Rob arrived at his destination safely. He was happy and relieved. He thanked the river and the old man for helping him, and he paddled back to shore. He couldn't wait to tell his friends about his river adventure.

Once upon a time, there was a noisy house. The wind would blow and make the windows rattle. It scared the little boy who lived there. He thought a ghost was making the noise.

One day, the boy's dad took him for a ride in his car. The car was very fast and went at great speed. The boy loved feeling the wind in his hair.

As they drove, they saw a spooky ghost on the side of the road. The boy was scared but his dad said it was just a decoration for Halloween. They drove past it and the boy felt better.

When they got home, the boy was excited to tell his mom about their adventure. He told her about the spooky ghost and how they went at great speed in the car. The noisy house didn't seem so scary anymore.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved to draw with chalk. She would make pretty pictures on the sidewalk with her colorful chalks. One day, Lily woke up to a very cold day. Everything outside was icy and slippery.

Lily's mom warned her not to go outside because it was too slippery. But Lily really wanted to make a pretty picture with her chalks. She begged and begged until her mom finally let her go outside, but only for a little bit.

Lily went outside and started to draw with her chalks. But then, she slipped on the icy sidewalk and fell. She hit her head and started to cry. Her mom came outside and saw what happened. She rushed Lily to the hospital, but it was too late. Lily had hurt herself too badly and could not be saved.

Lily's mom cried and cried, wishing she had never let Lily go outside. She knew in her heart that she should have listened to her own warning. From then on, she made sure to always keep Lily safe, no matter how much she begged to do something dangerous.

Davey was a happy 3 year old. Today he was visiting his great grandpa's farm. Great grandpa showed him all around. Davey saw a lot of exciting things.

Great grandpa asked Davey to kneel down beside the barn and listen carefully. Davey heard a noise. It sounded like a far away roar. It was a surprise for Davey.

Great grandpa explained that it was a clean river far away from the farm. Davey was so excited to hear the noise and he was so proud that he could hear it.

Davey thanked Great grandpa for the surprise and then he ran home to tell his mom about it. Davey had had a great day at the farm.

Once upon a time there was a girl. She was lovely and always looked for fun things to do. One day she got an idea. She decided to visit the junk yard.

She walked for a long time until she arrived at the junk yard. There was lots of exciting things to find. The girl found an old bike wheel and a broken toy car. She had lots of fun exploring the junk.

She was very sad when it was time to leave. But she was sure she would come back again. She said goodbye with a smile on her face and was sure the junk would still be there when she returned.

Before the girl left she took one more look around. In the corner of the yard she saw a teddy bear. It was very old but made the girl so happy. The bear was lovely and she knew it would be her friend forever.

The girl was glad she had decided to visit the junk yard. She was sure she would come back soon and enjoy the lovely things she had seen.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved going on adventures with her family. One day, they went on a trip to the beach. When they arrived, Lily's dad asked her to help unpack the bags from the car.

As they were unpacking, Lily noticed a small cell phone in one of the bags. She asked her dad what it was for, and he told her it was in case of emergencies.

Later that day, Lily and her family went for a walk on the beach. They came across a scary looking cave. Lily's mom said they should stay away from it. But Lily's dad said they should explore it. Lily was scared, but her dad promised to keep her safe.

As they went inside the cave, Lily's dad used the cell phone to light the way. They found a treasure chest filled with gold coins. Lily was so happy they found treasure, and she knew that her dad would always keep her safe on their adventures.

Mummy was really sad. Her vest was ripped, and it was her favourite. She looked for someone who could repair it.

One day she found Grandpa in the garden. Grandpa was a handyman! She asked him to help repair her vest.

Grandpa worked hard. He put lots of threads into the vest and stitched up the rip. He also made sure it was clean.

Mummy was so happy. Her vest was fixed and looking good as new. She thanked Grandpa and gave him a big hug.

Grandpa smiled. He was glad that he could help Mummy repair her vest.

Lily and Ben are friends. They like to play with toys. One day, they find a big box in the garage. It has many modern toys inside. They are shiny and make noises.

"Wow, look at these toys!" Lily says. "Can we play with them?"

"I don't know," Ben says. "Maybe they belong to someone else."

Lily picks up a robot. It has lights and buttons. She presses a button and the robot says, "Hello, I am Robo. Do you want to be my friend?"

"Yes, I do!" Lily says. She hugs the robot.

Ben sees a car. It has wheels and a remote. He picks up the remote and the car moves. He likes the car.

"Look, Lily, I have a car!" Ben says. "It can go fast and turn."

"That's cool, Ben," Lily says. "But I like my robot more. He can talk and sing."

They play with their toys for a while. Then they hear a voice.

"Hey, what are you doing with my toys?" The voice is angry. It is Tom, the big boy who lives next door. He comes into the garage. He sees Lily and Ben with his toys.

"Give me back my toys!" Tom says. "They are mine!"

Lily and Ben are scared. They don't want to give up their toys. They like them a lot.

"Please, Tom, can we play with them for a little bit?" Lily says. "They are so fun and modern."

"No, you can't!" Tom says. "They are not for you. They are for me. I got them for my birthday."

He grabs the robot from Lily and the car from Ben. He puts them back in the box. He glares at Lily and Ben.

"Go away!" Tom says. "And don't touch my toys again!"

Lily and Ben are sad. They run out of the garage. They go to Lily's house. They sit on the couch.

"I'm sorry, Lily," Ben says. "I should have listened to you. You said we should ask before we play with someone else's toys."

"It's okay, Ben," Lily says. "I should have listened to you too. You said we should be careful with the modern toys. They might break or get lost."

They hug each other. They are still friends.

"Maybe we can play with our own toys," Lily says. "They are not modern, but they are fun and ours."

"Good idea, Lily," Ben says. "Do you want to play with my blocks or your dolls?"

Lily thinks for a moment. She has an idea.

"Why don't we play with both?" she says. "We can make a house for the dolls with the blocks. And we can make them talk and sing."

Ben likes the idea. He smiles.

"That sounds fun, Lily," he says. "Let's do that."

They get their toys and start to play. They are happy. They have fun. They are good friends.

Once upon a time, there was a wide river. On the other side of the river, was a distant land, full of wonders. Little Jack and his friend Jessica wanted nothing more than to explore the far away place.

One day, Jack's Dad presented him with a passport. Without a moment's hesitation, Jack and Jessica set off to cross the river. The water was cold, but they were so excited to go, they didn't care.

Just as the children reached the center of the river, the current became much stronger. Jack was about to thank his Dad for the passport, but the current pulled him and Jessica too far away.

Suddenly, the strong current pushed the children into the deep depths of the river. Jack and Jessica were never seen again.

The moral of the story is to cherish gifts from family and never take your loved ones for granted. No matter how far you go, they will always be with you in your heart.

Once upon a time there was a young boy who decided he wanted to be the best. He worked very hard, night and day, but he was not having any luck. He became sad and thought he would never succeed.

Then, one day he had an idea and went outside to try it. With a strong arm, he struck the ground with a stick and a diamond popped out. He was so excited and was certain he was headed for success.

He ran to the store to sell the diamond and was met with a big smile from the man behind the desk. The man offered him lots of money and the young boy was happy and proud of his success.

The young boy was finally on his way to greatness. He kept striking new ground and before long his success was everywhere. Everyone wanted to be like him and he was loved by many.

The young boy was now rich and famous and everyone wanted to be like him. He had struck success and was living happily ever after.

Lila and Ben were playing in the garden. They liked to look at the flowers and the bees. Lila saw a big sunflower. It was yellow and bright. She wanted to pick it and give it to her mom.

"Look, Ben, a sunflower!" she said. "It is so pretty. I will take it to mom."

Ben shook his head. He knew the sunflower was not theirs. It was Mrs. Lee's. Mrs. Lee lived next door. She loved her flowers. She worked hard to grow them. She said they were expensive.

"No, Lila, you can't take the sunflower," he said. "It is Mrs. Lee's. She will be mad. She will yell at us. She will tell our mom. She will warn us to stay away from her garden."

Lila did not listen. She reached for the sunflower. She pulled it hard. She broke the stem. She smiled. She held the sunflower in her hands.

"Look, Ben, I have the sunflower!" she said. "It is so pretty. Mom will love it."

Ben was scared. He saw Mrs. Lee coming out of her house. She saw Lila and the sunflower. She was angry. She frowned. She shouted.

"Hey, you, little girl, what are you doing with my sunflower?" she said. "That is my sunflower. You stole it. You broke it. You are bad. Give it back to me. Go away from my garden. I will warn your mom. I will call her now."

Lila was shocked. She dropped the sunflower. She ran to Ben. She cried. She was sorry. She did not mean to make Mrs. Lee mad. She did not know the sunflower was expensive.

"Ben, I am sorry, I am sorry," she said. "I did not know. I just wanted to make mom happy. I did not want to make Mrs. Lee sad. What can we do?"

Ben hugged Lila. He was sorry too. He tried to calm her down. He had an idea.

"Maybe we can say sorry to Mrs. Lee," he said. "Maybe we can help her with her garden. Maybe we can give her some of our cookies. Maybe she will forgive us. Maybe she will not warn our mom. Maybe she will be nice to us."

Lila nodded. She liked Ben's idea. She wiped her tears. She took Ben's hand. They walked to Mrs. Lee. They said sorry. They asked if they could help. They offered some cookies. They hoped Mrs. Lee would be nice to them.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved playing outside with her puppy, Max. One day, Lily wanted to go to the park, but it was very cold outside. Max didn't want to go because he was a little puppy and he didn't like the cold.

Lily suggested they play inside instead, where it was warm and cozy. Max wagged his tail and barked happily. They played with toys and read books until they got tired. Then, they cuddled up together and took a nap. Lily was happy she could still have fun with Max even if it was too cold to go outside.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved music and wanted to learn how to play the guitar. His parents got him a long guitar, and he was very happy. Timmy practiced every day and learned how to play some songs.

One day, Timmy took his guitar to show his friends at the park. They all gathered around him, and he started to play. But then, a big gust of wind came and knocked the guitar out of his hands. The guitar fell to the ground and broke into many pieces. Timmy was very sad and cried a lot.

Timmy's parents tried to fix the guitar, but it was too broken. Timmy never got to play his guitar again. He learned that sometimes bad things happen, and it's important to be careful with things we love.

Tom and Anna are friends. They like to play together. One day, Anna has a birthday. She gets a gift from her mom. It is a red dress. She is very happy.

She shows the dress to Tom. She says, "Look, Tom, this is my gift. It is a red dress. I will wear it to my party. Do you like it?"

Tom does not like the dress. He thinks it is too bright and too frilly. He is rude. He says, "No, I don't like it. It is ugly. You look like a clown. You should not wear it to your party. You should wear something else."

Anna is sad. She likes the dress. She thinks it is pretty. She is angry. She says, "Tom, you are rude. You are not my friend. You hurt my feelings. You should say sorry."

Tom does not say sorry. He is stubborn. He says, "No, I will not say sorry. I am honest. I tell you the truth. You should thank me."

Anna does not thank him. She cries. She runs away. She does not want to play with Tom anymore. She wants a new friend. A friend who is nice and who likes her dress.

Todd was a little curious boy. One day, he saw a strange jacket on the ground. He wanted to try it on. But when he reached for it, his mother said, "No, Todd. Don't touch it." Todd did not want to listen and resist his mother's orders. So he put on the jacket. As soon as he put it on, he felt very dizzy. He started spinning and spinning until he fell on the ground. Then his mother quickly took off the jacket and said, "It's best to not resist me, Todd".

Once there was a charming girl. She loved to go to the mall and look at all the fun things. Every time she went to the mall, something changed. One day, she saw a new store selling toys. She was so excited to visit the store. She spent forever looking at the new toys and trying to find one that she liked. She finally picked out a beautiful doll.

The next week, she visited the mall again. She couldn't believe it, but something changed again! There was a store selling clothing now. She thought it was really cool, and had a great time trying on a bunch of different clothes.

Every time she visited the mall, something changed. She loved to explore all the new things she could find. It was always so much fun. She never got bored at the mall, because it was always so charming.

Hannah and her brother Joe were running around the garden. Joe pointed to a bee that was buzzing around the flowers and said to Hannah, “Look, a bee!”

“Let's perform a dance for the bee!” said Hannah.

Joe nodded excitedly and they ran to the middle of the garden. They put their hands up in the air and started to jump up and down.

The bee seemed to be watching them, and it began to fly in a loop around them, as if it was trying to join in the dance. It was orange and sparkly.

Joe said, “Maybe the bee is doing the dance with us!”

Hannah smiled and said, “Yes, it looks like the bee is having lots of fun!”

The two children continued to perform the dance for the bee, until the sun set, and the bee flew away.

Once upon a time, there was a hunter who was very smart. He wanted to gain lots of treasures. So, he had an idea. He gathered some of his friends and they went on a great hunt. They searched high and low, looking for all kinds of things.

Finally, they found the perfect spot. It was full of fruits, vegetables and other wonderful treats. So, the hunter used his smarts to gather all the things. He worked hard until he gained all the treasures.

When the hunter returned home, he shared all the things he had gained with his friends. Everyone was so pleased with his intelligent hunt. They all enjoyed the wonderful goodies from their successful adventure.

The hunter was proud of himself and thanked his friends for helping him gain the treasures. From that day on, the hunter went on many more hunts and became known as the smartest, most successful hunter around.

Once upon a time, there was a brave lion who went on many adventures. He liked to roar as loud as he could and it scared all of the animals on the other side of the forest.

One day, the lion heard a noise coming from a cave. He decided to investigate, but he was scared so he roared as loud as he could.

When he got to the cave, a tiny mouse appeared. The mouse said, "I can help you find something special. If you follow me quietly, I will take you to it."

The lion nodded and kept his roaring to a minimum. The mouse took him to a cave filled with treasures. One of the treasures was a shiny medal! "You were brave to come here, so you deserve this medal," said the mouse.

The lion was so happy. He thanked the mouse and ran back home. But, he was so careless that he dropped the medal along the way.

The next day, the lion went out looking for his medal but he could not find it. He asked the other animals if they had seen it, but no one had.

Suddenly, the lion heard a roar! It was coming from the cave where he found the medal! He followed the noise, and sure enough, there was the mouse, playing with the medal!

The lion was thankful to have his medal back. From that day on, he made sure

Sara and Ben were playing in the kitchen. They liked to pretend they were chefs and make yummy food. Sara was bossy. She told Ben what to do all the time. She said, "Ben, you cut the cauliflower. I will fix the soup. Hurry up, we have guests coming soon."

Ben did not like to cut the cauliflower. It was hard and white and boring. He wanted to fix the soup too. He said, "Sara, can I help you with the soup? I like soup. It is hot and tasty and fun."

Sara said, "No, Ben. You are too little to fix the soup. You will make a mess. You will burn yourself. You will spill the soup. You stay with the cauliflower. I am the big chef. I know what to do."

Ben was sad and angry. He did not want to play with Sara anymore. He thought she was mean and rude. He said, "Fine, Sara. You can have the soup. I don't care. I will make my own food. I will make a cauliflower cake. It will be better than your soup."

Sara laughed. She said, "A cauliflower cake? That sounds gross. No one will eat that. You are silly, Ben. You don't know how to cook. You should listen to me. I am the big chef. I know what to do."

Ben did not listen to Sara. He took the cauliflower and some eggs and some flour and some sugar and some milk. He mixed them all together in a big bowl. He put the bowl in the oven. He waited for his cake to bake. He smelled something funny. He opened the oven. He saw his cake. It was brown and lumpy and smelly. He tasted his cake. It was bitter and sour and yucky. He spit it out. He cried.

Sara heard Ben cry. She saw his cake. She felt sorry for him. She said, "Ben, I'm sorry. I was wrong. I was too bossy. I should have let you help me with the soup. I should have been nice to you. You are my brother. I love you. Do you want to share my soup?"

Ben looked at Sara. He saw her smile. He felt happy. He said, "Yes, Sara. I'm sorry too. I was silly. I should have listened to you. You are my sister. I love you. Do you want to try my cake?"

Sara and Ben hugged. They laughed. They threw away the cake. They ate the soup. They learned to share and to be kind. They had fun. They were happy.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lily. She got an invitation to a party from her friend, Tim. She was very happy and wanted to go to the party.

Lily asked her mom to help her open the invitation. Her mom used scissors to cut the envelope and then gave the invitation to Lily.

Lily was excited to use her new dress and shoes for the party. She put on her dress and shoes and went to the party with her mom. She had lots of fun playing with her friends and eating yummy cake.

Once upon a time there was a special plane. It was very unique and special because it was the only plane that had a telephone inside. The pilot could use the phone to call people wherever he went in the sky.

One day the plane flew to a far away city. It flew as high as it could until it was in the clouds. The pilot used his telephone to make a call. He called a friendly old man who lived in the city and asked him to come meet him at the airport.

The old man was very excited. He quickly grabbed his hat and ran to the airport. When he got there he saw the plane. He waved his arms and shouted hello to the pilot.

The pilot waved back. Soon the plane landed at the airport and the pilot and the old man hugged and talked. Together they went for a ride in the special plane and flew around the city.

It was a wonderful day. The old man and the pilot smiled and laughed as they listened to stories over a cup of tea. They even flew high enough to see some of the stars. What a unique and exciting experience!

Once upon a time, a boy named Timmy went to the beach with his mom and dad. They played in the sand and swam in the water. Timmy found a big rock on the beach and he picked it up. He threw the rock into the water and watched it splash.

Suddenly, a rude crab came out of the water and pinched Timmy's toe! Timmy cried and his mom and dad came to help. They scared the crab away and Timmy felt better. They all went back to playing on the beach, but Timmy made sure to stay away from any more rude crabs.

Once upon a time there was a farmer called Mary. Mary was incredible; she loved to work in her garden and enjoyed talking to the animals on her farm. One day Mary was busy working away in her garden when a rabbit hopped over. The rabbit asked Mary if she wanted to come on an adventure with him. Mary thought this was a great idea and agreed. The farmer and the rabbit then traveled far away and before long they had an incredible day. The farmer and the rabbit spent the day running around, enjoying their adventure. Eventually they both said goodbye, and the rabbit hopped off home. Mary returned to her garden with a huge smile on her face, safe in the knowledge that she had had an incredible day with her new friend.

Once upon a time, there was a little duck named Ducky. Ducky loved to swim in the pond with his friends. One day, Ducky's friend, Bunny, came to the pond. Bunny said, "Ducky, I worry that I can't swim like you. I don't want to splash and make a terrible mess."

Ducky said, "Don't worry, Bunny! You can swim with me. It's easy. You just paddle your feet and move your wings. See, like this!" Ducky showed Bunny how to swim and they had a lot of fun together.

Suddenly, a big wind blew and the water started to splash everywhere. Bunny said, "Oh no, this is terrible! I'm scared!" Ducky said, "Don't worry, Bunny. Just stay close to me and we'll be okay." They swam together until the wind stopped and the water became calm again.

Bunny was so happy that he could swim with Ducky. He said, "Thank you, Ducky. You're the best friend ever!" And Ducky said, "No problem, Bunny. Anytime you need me, I'll be here to help you."

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the park. One day, she saw a beautiful green tree with big leaves. She wanted to touch the leaves, but they were too high up.

Suddenly, her friend Ben came with a spray bottle. He filled it with water and sprayed the leaves so they came down a bit. Lily was so happy! She touched the leaves and they were soft.

After playing for a while, Lily noticed her ear was itchy. She asked her mom to look at it and found out there was a little bug inside. Her mom sprayed some medicine in her ear and the bug went away. Lily was happy again and continued to play in the park with her friend Ben. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a bear named Bob. Bob was very kind, and loved to help his forest friends. One day, Bob was walking through the forest when he heard a rustling in the bushes. He peeked in and saw a little rabbit caught in a snare! Bob quickly grabbed the bunny, and took him away to a safe place.

But the bunny was still scared, so Bob grabbed a brush he found nearby and slowly brushed the rabbit's fur until he started to relax. Finally, the little rabbit felt safe and smiled at Bob.

Bob smiled back at the bunny. Then, he waved goodbye and walked away. Bob knew the little rabbit was now safe and happy. The End.

Once upon a time, there was a brave bunny. He lived in a big, quiet forest. Every day, he hopped around and looked for food. One day, the bunny was looking for breakfast in the forest when he saw a big bear! The bunny was very scared! He knew he had to hide or the bear would catch him. So the bunny ran away as fast as he could. He hid behind a big rock, but the bear was still there. The brave bunny stayed very still and quiet. Finally, the bear sniffed the air and rolled away. The bunny was safe! He hopped away, happy that he had been so brave.
