Once upon a time, there was a fake earth that could not stay up in the sky. One day, the silly earth began to wobble and before long it was falling! It got faster and faster, until finally it was on the ground. Everyone was so scared, but then they realised that the earth was not real. They all laughed and gave a big cheer, glad that it was only a fake.

Afterwards, the sky stayed clear, with the real earth safe and sound. The people all thanked the sky for the happy ending, feeling thankful that the fake earth had fallen instead.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Sue. Sue was feeling miserable one day because she couldn't find her favorite toy. She looked everywhere in her room, but she just couldn't find it. Sue's mommy saw her looking sad and asked, "Sue, why are you so sad?"

Sue told her mommy, "I can't find my favorite toy, and it makes me very sad." Her mommy said, "Don't worry, Sue. We will find it together." So, Sue and her mommy started to look for the toy together.

While they were searching, Sue's mommy found an old magazine. She showed it to Sue and said, "Look, Sue! This magazine has a picture of your favorite toy on the cover. Maybe it will help us find your toy." Sue looked at the magazine and smiled.

As they continued to look for the toy, Sue noticed that the magazine had fallen on the floor. She picked it up and saw her toy hiding behind it! Sue was so happy to find her toy, and she hugged her mommy.

From that day on, Sue always remembered to look behind the magazines when she couldn't find her toys. And she was never miserable again.

One day, there was a little boy who was frightened. He had never been on a boat before, and his parents wanted him to have an adventure. He was scared but went anyway.

The boat rocked back and forth on the water. He felt scared and a little bit sick. His mom held him close and said, "Don't be frightened. It's ok."

He looked out over the water and saw a big sail. It was white and beautiful. He loved it! His dad said, "Let's go and explore!"

They all hopped in the boat, and they slowly sailed away. The boat rocked gently, and the sail caught the wind. The little boy felt really happy. He laughed and smiled, not feeling frightened anymore.

The boat took them all the way around the bay, and the little boy was so proud that he had gone on the adventure. He was so glad he wasn't scared anymore.

They sailed back to shore, and the little boy felt so brave. He could hardly wait to tell his friends. They had gone on an adventure and rocked on the big white sail. What an adventure!

Once upon a time there was a small sausage. The sausage was mild and needed someone to provide for it.

One day, the sausage met a little girl in the park. She was very kind and said she would provide for the sausage.

The small sausage was so happy and followed the girl home. When they reached her house, the girl gave the sausage some food. She was very kind and provided it with water and lots of yummy food.

The sausage was very grateful and thanked the girl. They became friends and the girl continued to provide the sausage with food, water and friendship.

The small sausage was so lucky to have found a friend who was willing to provide it with love and care.

Timmy was a young boy who loved going to school. He was friendly and smiled at all his friends in class. Today however, something was different. A few of the other boys in his class were teasing him. It made him feel angry.

Suddenly, he saw one of the boys with a jar of something disgusting. It smelled bad and Timmy knew right away it was mean. The other boys were laughing and pointing at him.

Timmy was so mad! He came up with a plan. He took a seat at his desk and started to make a funny noise. Everyone stopped what they were doing and looked at him. Then, he made all the funny noises at once.

The boys in his class started laughing and his teacher clapped her hands in amusement. The other boys had to leave Timmy alone. From that day onwards, no one ever teased him again!

Tom and Anna were friends who liked to play outside. One day, they went to the park with their moms. They saw a big pond with ducks and geese. The water was icy and shiny.

"Look, Anna, the ducks are swimming in the icy water. They are brave and strong," Tom said.

"I like the geese better. They have long necks and make funny noises. They are smart and funny," Anna said.

They admired the ducks and geese for a while. Then they heard their moms calling them.

"Tom, Anna, it's time for lunch. Come here, we have sandwiches and juice for you," their moms said.

Tom and Anna ran to their moms. They were hungry and happy. They ate their lunch on a bench near the pond. They shared their sandwiches and juice. They thanked their moms for the yummy lunch.

"Can we play some more after lunch, mom?" Tom asked.

"Sure, honey, but you have to wear your hats and gloves. It's very cold today," his mom said.

"OK, mom. We will be careful and warm," Anna said.

They finished their lunch and put their hats and gloves on. Then they went back to the pond. They played with the ducks and geese. They threw some bread crumbs for them. They had a lot of fun. They liked the icy pond and the animals. They were good friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to drink from her blue cup every day. One day, she accidentally dropped her cup and it broke into many little pieces. Lily was very sad because her cup was her favorite thing in the world.

Lily's mom saw how sad she was and decided to give her a new blue cup. Lily was happy again and she learned that sometimes when we lose something, we can gain something even better. She also learned that it's important to take care of our things so they don't break.

From that day on, Lily was very careful with her new blue cup and she never let it out of her sight. She was grateful for her new cup and she knew that she had gained something special.

Tom is a little boy who likes to play with his cars. He has many cars of different colors and sizes. He likes to make them zoom and crash on the floor. One day, he takes his cars to the park with his mom. He finds a big hill and rolls his cars down the hill. He has a lot of fun.

But then, he sees a big dog running towards him. The dog is barking and wagging its tail. Tom is scared of the dog. He drops his cars and runs to his mom. His mom hugs him and tells him the dog is friendly. She says the dog just wants to play. Tom looks at the dog and sees it is not angry. It is licking his cars and wagging its tail.

Tom wants to get his cars back, but he sees that one of his cars is missing. It is his favorite car, a red one with a blue stripe. He looks around the hill, but he cannot find it. He feels sad. He thinks he lost his car forever. He starts to cry.

His mom sees him crying and asks him what is wrong. Tom tells her he lost his favorite car. His mom says they will look for it together. They walk around the hill and ask other people if they have seen his car. No one has seen it. Tom feels more sad.

Then, he sees a lady in a white dress and a hat. She is a nurse. She works at the park and helps people who get hurt. She is holding something in her hand. It is his car! She says she found it near a bench. She says she was looking for the owner. She smiles and gives him his car. Tom is very happy. He says thank you to the nurse. He hugs his car and his mom. He says he will not lose his car again. He says he likes the nurse. The nurse says she likes him too. She says he is a brave and polite little boy. She says he can play with his cars at the park anytime. She says she will watch over him and the dog. Tom smiles and says okay. He goes back to the hill and plays with his cars and the dog. He has a lot of fun.

Once upon a time, there was a hairy bear who lived in the woods. He liked to sing and play all day long. One day, he heard the police coming and he got very scared.

The bear said to the police, “Let me go! I don’t want to get into any trouble!” The police said, “We just want to help. We will take care of you.”

The police took the bear to the doctor’s office. The doctor gave the bear a checkup and made sure he was safe.

Then, the police drove the bear back to his home in the woods. Before they said goodbye, the police said, “Stay out of trouble and be happy!”

The bear was so happy that he started singing and dancing. He thanked the police for their help and ran off into the woods. From that day on, he always stayed out of trouble and was never scared of the police again.

Once upon a time there was a helpless little swan. He longed to fly high above the sky but he wasn't able to with his small wings.

One day, the swan sat by the lake pondering about how to fly. He said to himself, "How can I gain the gift of flight?"

Just then, a tiny bird flew by and heard the swan's plea. She stopped to chat with him and said, "You should try flapping your wings faster and harder. Try it and see if it works."

The swan was very pleased with the advice and thanked the bird. He then began practice flapping his wings faster and harder and soon he could feel himself lifting off the ground!

The swan was very excited and each day he practiced more and more. Soon, he gained the gift of flight and soared above the sky he had been longing to see.

The helpless little swan had finally achieved his dream!

Lily likes to number her toys. She has one doll, two cars, three balls, and four books. She numbers them with stickers. She puts one sticker on her doll, two stickers on her cars, and so on. She is very good at counting.

One day, Lily goes to the park with her mom. She brings her doll and her jacket. She puts her jacket on a bench and plays with her doll on the grass. She makes her doll talk and sing. She is very happy.

But then, a big wind comes. It blows Lily's jacket off the bench. It flies away in the air. Lily does not see it. She is busy with her doll. Her mom does not see it either. She is talking to another mom.

A boy sees the jacket. He likes the jacket. It is blue and soft. He runs after it. He catches it. He puts it on. He thinks it is his jacket. He is very lucky.

Lily finishes playing with her doll. She goes back to the bench. She looks for her jacket. She does not find it. She is very sad. She asks her mom, "Where is my jacket?"

Her mom looks around. She sees the boy with the jacket. She says, "That is your jacket, Lily. That boy has it. Let's go and get it back."

Lily and her mom walk to the boy. They say, "Excuse me, that is not your jacket. That is Lily's jacket. She numbered it with stickers. See, there is one sticker on the sleeve. Can you please give it back?"

The boy looks at the jacket. He sees the sticker. He says, "Oh, I'm sorry. I did not know. I thought it was my jacket. Here, you can have it back."

He gives the jacket to Lily. Lily says, "Thank you. This is my jacket. I like it very much. It is blue and soft. And it has stickers."

She puts on her jacket. She feels warm and cozy. She is very happy. She says, "I'm lucky. I have my jacket back. And I have my doll. And I have my mom. And I can number my toys."

One day, Jen and her dad were in the kitchen. Jen was excited; her dad was going to make her some special pancakes. She watched as her dad mixed the ingredients. He added some sugar and eggs. Then he added something that Jen didn't recognize.

"What's that, Daddy?" she asked.

"It's pepper," her dad said. He sprinkled it into the bowl.

Jen watched as he stirred the pancake batter. He was so careful, but she could tell he was a little nervous.

Soon, the batter was ready. Her dad poured it onto the hot griddle. He made sure to separate the pancakes so they wouldn't all be stuck together.

At last, the pancakes were ready. Jen's dad sprinkles some more pepper onto the pancakes. Jen had never seen pepper on pancakes before, but it smelled delicious!

They sat together and ate their special pancakes. Jen ate three – and she loved them!

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to paint. One day, he asked his mom if he could paint a picture of a wheel. "Of course, Timmy!" said his mom.

Timmy got out his paint and started to paint a picture of a big, round wheel. He used the color yellow for the wheel and blue for the background. When he was done, he showed his mom. "Wow, Timmy! That's a great painting!" said his mom.

But Timmy wasn't happy. He thought the wheel looked too pale. So, he added some more yellow paint to make it brighter. "Now it looks perfect!" said Timmy. His mom smiled and said, "You're right, Timmy. It looks much better now."

Timmy was so proud of his painting that he showed it to everyone he saw that day. "Look at my painting of a wheel! I painted it all by myself!" he said. And everyone was impressed with Timmy's painting skills.

Once upon a time there were two friends who were looking for something special. They had heard about a magical root which could make their wildest dreams come true. So they set off on an adventure to find it.

The two walked through a forest and up a mountain, but they couldn't find the root. It seemed like they were never going to find it.

Just when they were about to give up, they heard a voice. It said "Please, you must be persistent".

The friends kept walking and sure enough, they found the magical root! They were so excited! They thanked the voice for helping them, and promised to be persistent in their search for their wildest dreams.

The magical root granted their wishes and the friends lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a pretty little bird. He wanted to soar high up into the sky. He flapped his wings and flew higher and higher until he could almost touch the clouds. It was the most amazing thing he had ever seen. He looked down and saw the beautiful lake. He wanted to go down and swim in it. He flew to the lake and went for a swim. The water felt so nice and cool. He swam around for a long time and felt so free and happy. Before he knew it, the sun was setting and it was time to go home. He flapped his wings and started to soar up into the sky again. He twirled and flew until he got back to his nest. The pretty little bird was so glad he got to see the lake and be free to fly and soar up high.

Jimmy was a powerful kid who never gave up. He balanced one book ontop of the other, determined to read all three pages. He opened each book one by one and carefully turned the pages.

"Wooow, this is so cool," thought Jimmy. He was having fun reading the books and learning new things.

Suddenly, Jimmy's mom poked her head in the door and said, "Jimmy, I'm so proud of how you're balancing the books and reading the pages. You're so powerful!"

Jimmy grinned from ear to ear and said, "Thanks, Mom. Can I please have some juice now?"

"Of course you can," said his mom with a smile.

Jimmy hopped out of his chair and ran to the kitchen to get his juice. He was proud of himself for being so powerful and knew that with practice and patience he would get even better.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim had a toy dog named Spot. One day, Tim and Spot went for a walk in the woods. They saw a big fire far away. Tim said, "Oh no, Spot! We must tell Mom and Dad about the fire!"

Tim and Spot ran back home to tell Mom and Dad. On their way, they met a big, sorry bear. The bear said, "I am so sorry, I made the fire by accident. Can you help me put it out?" Tim and Spot agreed to help the sorry bear.

Tim, Spot, and the bear got water from the river and used it to put out the fire. The fire was gone, and the woods were safe again. The sorry bear thanked Tim and Spot for their help. From that day on, they all became good friends and had many fun adventures together.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys and eat yummy food. One day, she was sitting at the table eating her cereal when she heard a soft sound. She looked around and saw her mom using a teaspoon to stir her tea.

Lily loved to help her mom in the kitchen, so she asked if she could help too. Her mom said yes, and gave her a soft pink apron to wear. Lily carefully took a teaspoon from the drawer and helped her mom stir the tea.

As they stirred, they heard a bird chirping outside. Lily and her mom went to the window and saw a little bird sitting on a branch. They listened carefully and heard the bird singing a soft song. Lily was so happy to hear the bird's beautiful song and she smiled from ear to ear.

Once upon a time there were two friends, Jack and Hank. They loved to play together and explore the world.

One day they were on a big adventure. They were running and jumping and having lots of fun.

Suddenly, they heard something. Jack said, "what do you think that noise is?"

Hank replied, "I don't know, let's go check it out!"

So, the two friends began walking towards the noise. It was getting louder and louder.

When they finally reached the source of the noise, they looked around in amazement. It was a tough world with its own rules. There were big rock walls, a river, and a waterfall. It was beautiful.

Jack and Hank couldn't help but smile. It was an amazing place. But then they heard a voice.

"Stop," the voice said. "This world is tough, so be careful."

The two friends listened to the voice, and remembered to be careful. They enjoyed their time in the tough world, but when the sun began to set, Jack and Hank knew it was time to go home.

Once upon a time, there was a rich crab who lived in a big, fancy house. He loved to play in the sand by the sea. Every day he searched for yummy food to eat.

One day, the crab saw a big clam in the water. He demanded the clam open so he could eat it. But the clam wouldn't open no matter how much the crab shouted and waved his claws. He got angry and stomped his feet.

Suddenly, the clam opened! Out from inside the clam stepped a beautiful mermaid. "I heard your demands, crab," the mermaid said. "I have a special gift to give you." She put a shiny, golden coin in the crab's claw.

The crab was so happy and thanked the mermaid many times. With his new coin he was now very rich. So he decided to give lots of coins to the other creatures in the sea. He even gave a coin to the stubborn clam. The crab was now the richest of them all!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to draw and color with her crayons. One day, she went to the store with her mom to buy more crayons.

At the store, Lily saw a big box of crayons with all different colors, but she really wanted the black crayon. She asked her mom if she could have the black crayon, but her mom said she couldn't just buy one crayon.

Lily was sad, but her mom told her that sometimes it's better to order things in a set because it can be more useful. So, they bought the big box of crayons and went home.

When Lily opened the box, she was so happy to see that there were so many colors to use. She realized that her mom was right, and that sometimes it's better to order things in a set. From then on, Lily always remembered to think about what would be most useful before making a decision.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily had a white cup that she loved to drink from. One day, Lily's mom asked her to help complete a puzzle.

Lily said, "Sure mom, I can help!"

As they were working on the puzzle, Lily accidentally knocked over her cup and it spilled all over the table.

"Oh no!" Lily exclaimed. "My white cup is all wet."

"It's okay," said her mom. "Let's clean it up and then we can complete the puzzle together."

Lily smiled and helped her mom clean up the spilled water. They were able to complete the puzzle and Lily felt proud of herself for helping. Her white cup was dry and ready for her to use again.

Once, there was a sad little girl called Sophie. She never had anyone to play with. Every day, all she did was sit in her garden and look at the swing.

One day, Sophie saw a rabbit in the garden. She smiled and went closer to say hello. The rabbit smiled back and nodded. Then it jumped onto the swing. Sophie was so excited, she sat down on the swing too.

Together, she and the rabbit went on the swing higher and higher. Sophie was so happy. She laughed and laughed.

But soon, the rabbit had to leave. It looked at Sophie sadly, and she nodded. The rabbit hopped away, leaving Sophie alone again. But the happy memories of the time they spent together on the swing made her feel not so sad anymore.

Once upon a time there was a seed. It was so small that nobody could see it. But the seed kept growing and growing until it was bigger and taller than anything else around.

The seed grew into a tree with branches that reached up to the sky. Eventually it started to make leaves and soon the leaves grew into different styles like stars or spirals. Everyone was so grateful for the tree and its beautiful leaves.

One day the tree's leaves started to make shadows everywhere. All the animals, people, and even the birds that came to sit in the branches were glad of this. They all enjoyed the coolness that the tree’s leaves made.

The seed kept growing until it was much bigger and taller than before. As the tree became bigger its leaves also grew in styles that were bigger and more beautiful than before. Everyone was so grateful to the tree and its amazing leaves that they named their city after it!

There was a jolly family that had been waiting for a very long time. They had all been so excited for something special to arrive.

Finally, one day, something arrived. It was an x-ray. The family was amazed and they looked at the x-ray together. It showed a very special thing inside their family.

The family smiled when they looked at it. It was a happy picture that made them very happy and jolly.

The next day the family made a plan. They were going to have a party to celebrate the special thing that had arrived. All the family's friends and family were invited, and they had a great time. Everyone was very jolly.

The family was so happy that the special thing had arrived. They all thanked the x-ray for bringing them such good news.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily was a smart girl who loved to play games. One day, she wanted to make a quiz for her friends.

Lily thought about what to put in her quiz. She didn't want it to be boring. She wanted her friends to have fun. So, she asked her mom for help. Her mom said, "Why not make a quiz about animals and their names?"

Lily liked the idea. She made a fun quiz with questions about animals and their names. When her friends came over, they played the quiz game. Everyone had a great time, and no one thought it was boring. Lily was happy that her friends loved her quiz.

Sara and Ben were twins who liked to walk in the park with their mom. One day, they saw a big pile of white powder on the grass. It looked like snow, but it was not cold.

"Can we play with the powder, mom?" Sara asked.

"No, my loves, that is not snow. That is soap powder. Someone spilled it by mistake. It is not good for you or the plants. We should leave it alone," mom said.

But Ben was curious. He wanted to touch the powder and see what it felt like. He sneaked away from mom and Sara and ran to the pile. He grabbed a handful of powder and threw it in the air. It made a lovely cloud of white.

"Wow, this is fun!" Ben said. He did not see the dog that was coming towards him.

The dog was big and brown and liked to chase things. He saw the white cloud and thought it was a bird. He ran after it and jumped on Ben. He knocked him down and licked his face. He also got some powder in his mouth and nose. He did not like it. He started to cough and sneeze.

"Help, mom, help!" Ben cried. He was scared and dirty.

Mom heard Ben and ran to him. She saw the dog and the powder and understood what happened. She shooed the dog away and picked up Ben. She hugged him and checked if he was hurt.

"Are you okay, Ben?" mom asked.

"I'm sorry, mom. I was naughty. I did not listen to you. I wanted to play with the powder. But it was not fun. It was bad. The dog was scary. And the powder was yucky. It made me and the dog sick," Ben said.

Mom was not angry. She was glad that Ben was safe. She also felt sorry for the dog. She took Ben to a fountain and washed his face and hands. She also gave him some water to drink.

"It's okay, Ben. I forgive you. But you have to learn to obey me. I know what is good for you and what is not. The powder was not for playing. It was for washing clothes. It can hurt you and the animals and the plants. You have to be careful and respectful of nature. Do you understand?" mom said.

"Yes, mom. I understand. I'm sorry. I love you," Ben said.

"I love you too, Ben. And I love you, Sara. Come on, let's go home. We have some lovely cookies waiting for us," mom said.

Sara had been watching the whole thing. She was glad that Ben was okay. She also learned a lesson. She did not want to play with the powder. She wanted to play with mom and Ben and the cookies. She hugged them and they walked home together. They were happy.

One day, a little girl named Sue went to her friend Tom's house to play. They liked to play hide and seek. Tom said, "Sue, let's play hide and seek today!" Sue was very happy and said, "Yes, let's play!"

Sue started to hide first. She saw a big curtain in the room. The curtain was pale and soft. Sue went behind the curtain and waited for Tom to find her. Tom started to look for Sue. He looked under the bed, behind the door, but he could not find Sue.

Tom thought for a moment and then he asked his mom, "Mom, have you seen Sue?" His mom smiled and said, "Look near the window." Tom went to the window and saw the pale curtain. He pulled the curtain and found Sue. They both laughed and continued to play hide and seek all day long.

Once upon a time there was a grumpy vegetable. He was in the garden and no one knew he was there. Every day he made the other vegetables look sad.

One day when the sun was shining, something special happened. A friendly butterfly appeared. He smiled at the grumpy vegetable and said hello. The grumpy vegetable was so surprised that he couldn't help but smile back.

The butterfly flew around the garden and brought smiles to all of the other vegetables. They were all so happy to see him. The grumpy vegetable was the happiest of all! He realized that it was nice to be friendly and he never wanted to be grumpy again.

The garden became a much more cheerful place with the butterfly around. From that day onwards he came back every day to make sure the vegetables were always happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim loved to play with his toy cart. He would push it around the house and fill it with his favorite toys.

One day, Tim saw his friend, Sam, playing with a big, shiny new cart. Tim felt envious of Sam's cart. He wanted one just like it. Tim's face showed a frown because he was sad.

Tim's mom saw his frown and asked him what was wrong. Tim told her about Sam's cart. His mom said, "It's okay to feel envious, but remember to be happy with what you have." Tim thought about it and smiled. He played with his cart, happy that he had a toy he loved.

Teddy was a three year old who loved to play and explore. One day, he was in the garden looking for something special. Suddenly, he noticed a pin in a corner. It had a bright, shiny color that made it look special. Teddy decided to pick it up and play with it.

He held it and ran around with it in his hand. Then he noticed something was different - the pin was dull! Teddy was very curious and wanted to know what had happened.

"Where is the sparkle?" Teddy asked.

His mom explained that the pin was made with special material that could no longer shine. She ordered Teddy to put the pin away so it would stay safe. Teddy did as he was told and put the pin in a safe place.

Although the pin was no longer shiny, Teddy had fun playing with it. He discovered that it still had its own dull, special sparkle.

Once upon a time, there was a vegetable. The vegetable was split into two pieces. One piece was big, and the other was small. The big piece of the vegetable was scary. The small piece was not scared.

One day, the small piece of the vegetable decided to go on an adventure. He wanted to explore the world. So he left his home, and walked for a long time. He passed by some trees, and he saw some birds. He even saw a big mountain!

But then, he came across a scary looking creature. It was so big and so scary! The vegetable became scared and he split in two again. One piece ran away and the other stayed behind.

The small piece of vegetable was safe, but he was very scared. He decided then and there that he would never go on an adventure again.

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a wealthy family who lived in a big house. One day, someone special wanted to come and visit. So the family opened the door and the special guest entered. The visitor had a big bag of wine!

The family was excited to see the wine, so they asked the visitor, “What kind of wine do you have?”

The visitor smiled and said, “This is some of the best wine in the world. It’s for you to enjoy!”

So the family opened the bag of wine and shared it with their special guest. They all enjoyed the wine and had a great time. The visitor stayed for dinner and they all shared stories and made lots of new memories.

At the end of the night, the visitor thanked the family for the wonderful evening, and then left to go home. The family was so grateful for the gift of wine, and they all felt very happy and wealthy.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside and watch the birds fly in the sky. One day, she saw a bird with perfect feathers and she wanted to catch it.

Her friend, Timmy, dared her to catch the bird. Lily didn't want to look like a scaredy-cat, so she tried to catch the bird. She chased the bird until she was very tired, but she couldn't catch it.

Lily learned that it's not good to do things just because someone dared her to. She also learned that it's not good to try to hurt animals. Sadly, the bird flew away and Lily felt very bad. She promised to never try to catch a bird again and to always be kind to animals.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lucy. She wanted to be a doctor when she grew up. Every day she would point to doctors she saw in the street, and say to herself, "That's what I want to be one day".

One day, she went with her dad to the park. She saw a group of doctors talking, and she pointed at them excitedly. Then her dad shook his head and told her she wouldn't become a doctor because she wasn't flexible enough. Lucy was very sad, but she tried hard not to cry.

Suddenly, Lucy had an idea. She ran up to the group of doctors and showed them how she could stretch her arm very far. Much to everyone's surprise, she was very flexible! The doctors cheered her on, and gave her a huge hug.

From that moment on, Lucy knew that she really could become a doctor one day. She kept training her flexibility and kept dreaming of her future. Years later, Lucy was a successful doctor. She always said to the children she worked with, "You can do anything - if you just try hard and stay flexible!".

Two furry friends were walking through the forest on a sunny day. The fox was eager to explore the area, but the rabbit was more cautious. "Let's go, Rabbit!" said the fox.

The rabbit replied, "Wait, I don't feel comfortable."

"Why don't you trust me? I promise you'll have fun," said the fox.

The rabbit paused for a moment, and then started walking. The fox jumped ahead with delight, and the rabbit followed slowly. The fox's tail waved back and forth in the air with happy motion.

They explored the trees, the flowers, and the creatures that lived in the forest. The fox was always eager to find something new. The rabbit, on the other hand, enjoyed taking it all in.

The two furry friends eventually made it back safe and sound, and the fox thanked the rabbit for coming along. The rabbit was glad that the fox was there, too.

Once there was a little girl who was feeling very sad. Her mommy noticed and came to her room to give her a hug. She stroked her hair and said, "It's ok, sweetheart. Everything will be alright."

The little girl's mommy asked her if she wanted to do something fun. The little girl said yes, so they went together to the store to buy some paint. When they got home, they got out the paint and the little girl's mommy helped her to make a happy picture.

The little girl was feeling much better by the time the picture was finished. Then her mommy hugged her again to make her feel even more comforted.

The little girl was now so happy. She smiled and said, "Thank you mommy for understanding me and helping me to feel better." Her mommy smiled back and said, "Anytime, sweetheart." They hugged one more time and then went off to bed with a happy feeling in their hearts.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside, no matter what the weather was like. One day, Lily went outside to play and the weather was very hot. She wore a pink dress and a hat to protect her from the sun.

As she played, Lily started to feel very sleepy. She couldn't stop yawning! She decided to take a nap under a big tree. When she woke up, she saw that the weather had changed. It was now cloudy and the sky was gray.

Lily went back inside and her mom asked her how her day was. Lily told her mom about the weather and how she had to take a nap because she was so tired. Her mom smiled and gave her a big hug. Lily felt happy and loved. The end.

Lily was a cute bunny who lived in the forest. She liked to hop and play with her friends, but she was also very curious. One day, she saw a big shiny thing in a clearing. It was a crown that belonged to the king of the animals.

"Wow, what is this?" Lily said. She wanted to touch it and see how it felt. But then she heard a loud roar. It was the king, a fierce lion, who was coming back to get his crown.

"Who are you?" the king said. He saw Lily near his crown and was angry. "Did you try to steal my crown?"

Lily was scared. She shook her head and said, "No, no, I was just looking. I'm sorry, Mr. King. Please don't hurt me."

The king looked at Lily and saw that she was telling the truth. He also saw that she was cute and harmless. He decided to be kind and said, "It's okay, little bunny. I forgive you. But you should be careful. The forest is full of dangers. You need to trust your friends and stay away from strangers."

Lily nodded and said, "Thank you, Mr. King. You are very wise and good. Can I be your friend?"

The king smiled and said, "Sure, you can be my friend. But you have to promise me one thing. Never touch my crown again. It is very important and precious to me."

Lily promised and said, "I promise, Mr. King. I will never touch your crown again. I will respect you and your things."

The king and Lily became friends and often talked and played in the forest. Lily learned a lot from the king and the king enjoyed her company. They trusted each other and were happy.

Once upon a time, Peter was a little boy. He had a trumpet. He always wanted to play it but he never could. One day, Peter decided to jog. He jogged and jogged and jogged until he found a beautiful park.

Peter stopped and looked around. He was so happy that he got his trumpet out and started playing it.

Suddenly, a big and grumpy man came up to him. He said, "Stop playing your trumpet! You are making too much noise."

Peter was very sorry. He put his trumpet away and started to jog away.

Before he left, he said, "I'm sorry. I just wanted to play my trumpet."

The man smiled and told Peter, "It's alright. I understand. Just make sure to only play the trumpet in the park when no one else is around, okay?"

Peter nodded and then continued to jog away with a smile on his face. He knew he had found a special place where he could always play his trumpet.

Once upon a time, there was a crab. He was happy and he played by the beach all day. One day, the crab met a bird. The bird mentioned some interesting news. "There is a big beach party tonight," said the bird.

The crab was so grateful for the bird's mention of the party. He excitedly waved his claws and said, "Yes! I'll be there!"

That night, the crab made his way to the beach and he popped out from the sand. There were so many animals at the beach that night. The crab met lots of new friends and they all enjoyed the party together.

The crab was very grateful for the nice evening. He thanked the bird for mentioning the party. The crab waved goodbye to all his new friends, and happily went home.

Tommy was a curious little boy. One day, he found a big jar of beans on the kitchen table. Tommy really wanted to try one, so he opened the jar. But as soon as he opened it, one of the beans slipped away and fell on the floor! Tommy picked it up and smelled it. It smelled sour! He had never had a sour bean before and he wanted to give it a try. So he put the bean in his mouth and took a bite. It was very sour! He made a sour face and spat it out. That was not a fun experience. Tommy learned that not all beans are tasty, and he should be more careful when trying something new!

Once upon a time, there was a big ship. The ship had a baker who loved to bake. One day, the baker made a big cake for everyone on the ship. He was very happy and excited to share his cake.

But, the cake did not look nice. The baker was ashamed of the cake. He thought no one would like it. So, he hid the cake and did not share it with anyone.

A friend saw the baker was sad and asked why. The baker told his friend about the cake. The friend said, "Do not be ashamed. Let's share the cake with everyone." They shared the cake and everyone loved it. The baker learned that it is important to share, even if something is not perfect.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play outside in the park with his friends. One day, Timmy and his friends were playing hide and seek. Timmy was hiding behind a big tree when he saw something black in the dark.

"Hey guys, come over here!" Timmy shouted. "I see something black in the dark!"

His friends came running over to see what Timmy had found. They all looked carefully and saw a black cat hiding in the bushes.

"Can we touch the cat?" Timmy asked.

"I don't know," replied his friend. "We should ask the owner first."

So, they went to find the owner of the cat and asked if they could touch it. The owner said yes, and they all took turns petting the soft, black fur of the cat. Timmy was very happy that he got to touch the black cat in the dark.

Ana liked to play the guitar. She would practice every day. One day, her mother gave her a present. It was a very pretty guitar. Ana was so excited. She hugged her Mom and said "Thank you for the pretty guitar, Mommy"

Her Mom said "You can use it to practice and make beautiful music".

Ana took the guitar and strummed the strings. She thought it sounded so beautiful. She smiled and said "I like my new guitar".

Her Mother smiled too. She said "Let's practice together, you can teach me how to use the guitar".

Ana and her mother spent the whole afternoon playing their guitars together. It was so much fun! They were both so happy. Ana thought: "This is the best day ever!

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play outside with his friends. One day, Timmy found a tie hidden in the bushes. He thought it was very pretty and decided to own it.

Later that day, Timmy's friend Billy came over to play. Billy saw the tie and said it belonged to his dad. Timmy didn't want to give it back because he liked owning it.

The two boys started to argue and fight over the tie. In the end, the tie got ripped and ruined. Billy was very upset and went home crying. Timmy felt bad but it was too late. He learned that sometimes it's better to share than to own something all by yourself.

Lily and Max were adventurous kids. They liked to explore the park near their home. One day, they found a big hill with a lot of rocks and flowers. They decided to climb it and see what was on the other side.

"Come on, Max, let's go!" Lily said, holding her brother's hand.

"OK, Lily, but be careful. The rocks are slippery and the flowers have thorns," Max said, following her.

They climbed and climbed, until they reached the top of the hill. They saw a beautiful view of the park, the trees, the pond, and the sky. They also saw a small table with two plates, two cups, and two spoons.

"Wow, look at that! Someone left a picnic for us!" Lily said, running to the table.

"Maybe it's a trap. Maybe it's a witch or a giant who wants to eat us," Max said, staying behind.

"Don't be silly, Max. It's just a nice surprise. Come on, let's see what they have," Lily said, lifting the lid of a pot.

She smelled something delicious. It was soup, with carrots, potatoes, and chicken. She poured some soup into the cups and gave one to Max.

"Here, Max, this will warm us up. It's getting cold and dark," Lily said, sipping her soup.

Max took the cup and smelled the soup. He was hungry and curious. He tasted the soup and smiled.

"Mmm, this is good. Thank you, Lily. And thank you, whoever left this for us," Max said, drinking his soup.

They ate the soup and felt happy and cozy. They looked at the sky and saw the sunset. It was orange, pink, and purple. It looked like a painting.

"Look, Lily, the sunset. It's so pretty," Max said, pointing at the sky.

"Yes, Max, it is. It's like a gift from the sun, to say goodbye and good night," Lily said, looking at the sky.

They finished their soup and put the cups and spoons back on the table. They thanked the sun and the picnic for their adventure. They held hands and walked down the hill, back to their home. They had a wonderful day.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to draw pictures of animals and flowers. One day, she saw a sign in the park that said "Beware of the ducks". She didn't believe it because she thought ducks were harmless.

Lily went to the pond to feed the ducks. She saw a big duck with a sign around its neck that said "I bite". Lily was scared and didn't know what to do. She remembered the sign in the park and realized she should have believed it.

From that day on, Lily always read signs and believed them. She learned that even if something seems harmless, it could still be dangerous.

One day, a bee hive was floating near the woods. It was filled with lots of buzzing bees.

The bees looked around but couldn't find their home. The hive was fake and they had nowhere to go. The bees were confused and sad.

Suddenly, a little girl noticed the lost bees. She felt sorry for them and decided to help.

The girl paused and thought of a plan. She smiled and started to gather some sticks and leaves. She then carefully put them together to make a new home for the bees.

The bees were so happy and grateful. They thanked the girl with a buzz and flew away to their new home.

The girl smiled and watched her work until the hive was out of sight.

Once upon a time, there was a big wide pot on the stove. Mommy put water in it and turned on the fire. She added some pasta and waited for it to cook. While waiting, she called her little girl to come and help her. The little girl ran to the kitchen and saw the pot of pasta. She was excited to help her mommy. They both stirred the pasta and waited for it to be ready. When it was cooked, they put some sauce on it and enjoyed a yummy dinner together.

Sammy and Maria were playing in the park. They had a balloon and they were passing it back and forth. Maria said to Sammy, "Let's play a game!".

Sammy said, "What kind?"

Maria said, "Let's pretend this balloon is a yummy treat. We can take turns passing it. Who ever has the balloon gets a turn to eat it. Ready? Go!"

Sammy and Maria took turns passing the balloon back and forth. They laughed and laughed at the silly game. Then, the balloon burst and Sammy and Maria had to stop playing.

Sammy said, "That was fun. Wasn't it yummy?"

Maria smiled and said, "Yes. It was yummy!"

One day, mommy took a box out of the closet and opened it. Inside the box, there was a big surprise: a pretty picture. Mommy smiled and gave the picture to the little girl. She was so excited and ran around the room, thanking mommy for the surprise.

Mommy had a plan. She gathered some paper and a few markers, then handed them to the little girl. Mommy said, “Now let's make something special!” The little girl knew what to do, and began drawing a beautiful picture. She thanked mommy for teaching her how to draw.

While she was drawing, a mean boy came into the room. He was very ignorant and started making fun of the little girl’s picture. The little girl felt sad, but mommy immediately stepped in. She explained to the boy that the picture was special and that he should be respectful.

The boy understood and immediately apologized. He thanked the little girl for her beautiful picture, and left the room. The little girl was so happy, and hugged mommy in excitement. Mommy smiled, happy that the boy had learned a lesson.

Once upon a time there was a truck that had been very busy all day. It had been loading lots of heavy boxes. When it was finished, the truck drove away to take the boxes to the new home.

As the truck drove down the road it spotted a big, round circle. All the other trucks were driving in the circle. The truck driver wanted to join them, so he drove the truck into the middle.

The circle was very busy. All the trucks were unloading and loading boxes. The truck driver worked quickly to help out with his own boxes. His truck was soon packed with all of the boxes from the circle.

Once all the boxes were loaded, the truck driver said goodbye to all the other truck drivers. They shouted back to him, waving from the circle as the truck drove away.

Once upon a time there was a poor little mouse. He was very small, no more than an inch from nose to tail. He was always so tired from all the harsh sun and hard work but he never had the chance to rest.

One day the mouse was particularly tired and he wanted to find a safe spot to rest. He searched and searched until he found a small crack beneath a nearby tree. It seemed like the perfect spot to hide and rest - but the tiny mouse should have been more careful!

Just as the mouse was about to settle into his resting place, he heard a harsh noise. Suddenly, a large owl swooped down and snatched him up in his claws. The poor little mouse cried out in fear, but it was too late.

The owl took the mouse away to a dark cave and made him his dinner. The poor mouse was never seen again.

Moral of the story: Always be careful when resting - you never know what danger might be lurking nearby!

Once upon a time there was a lion. He was an ordinary lion with a yellow mane. He liked to play games and loved exploring. One day he decided to go for a walk. He let his yellow mane flow in the wind as he walked.

He came across a meadow where he saw other animals. He was so excited and wanted to make new friends. He walked closer to them and let out a loud roar. The animals all ran away in fear.

The lion was so sad and was about to give up his journey when he heard a voice. It was an ordinary little bunny. The bunny said, “Hi! I’m not scared of you. Would you like to play?”The lion was so delighted. He jumped and let out a roar of joy.

The lion and the bunny became best friends and they played and explored the world together. They were an ordinary team but they were a lot of fun!

Once upon a time, there was a kind lady. She lived in a warm little house. The house was near a big park. The lady liked to go to the park every day.

One day, the lady went to the park. She had a bag of seeds. She wanted to scatter the seeds for the birds. The birds liked to eat the seeds. The lady smiled as she scattered the seeds.

The birds flew down to eat the seeds. They were happy and sang a pretty song. The lady felt happy too. She went back to her warm house. The lady and the birds were friends forever.

Once upon a time, there were two best friends, Jack and Lucy. They were very happy, until one day, Jack said that he was going to marry someone and he couldn't tell Lucy who it was. Lucy was sad and asked Jack to tell her. He said that the language was too weird for her to understand.

Lucy didn't understand why she couldn't know and started to cry. Jack noticed and sat next to her. He said, "Don't worry, Lucy. I think you'll be pleased when I marry. It'll be like a happy surprise."

Lucy sniffed and asked Jack, "Will it make you happy?"

"Yes, of course," said Jack with a smile. "I'm going to marry my love and that's what makes me happy."

Lucy was surprised but happy. She hugged Jack and said, "That's the best surprise ever!"

John and his mom were in the kitchen, looking for something.

"We need to find it," said his mom. "Where could it be?"

John looked around. He saw a little space behind the counter.

"Maybe it's in this hidden space!" said John.

His mom came over and squinted. She smiled and said "you're right, John! Now, let's see if we can manage to get it out."

John watched as his mom fit her hand into the space. After a little wiggling, she pulled her hand out and held something up. It was a big bag of candy!

John's eyes lit up. "Can I have one?" he asked.

His mom smiled and handed him a candy.

John was happy and sure felt thankful that he had managed to find the hidden space and all the candy that was inside.

Once upon a time, a big rhinoceros was walking in the jungle. He was very loud and made lots of noise. Suddenly, he slipped on a banana peel and fell down.

The rhinoceros was not hurt, but he felt embarrassed because all the other animals saw him fall. He got up and continued walking, but he was more careful now.

As the rhinoceros walked, he saw a bird flying above him. The bird said, "Hello, Mr. Rhinoceros! I saw you fall earlier. Are you okay?" The rhinoceros smiled and said, "Yes, I'm okay. Thank you for asking."

From that day on, the rhinoceros was more careful when he walked and didn't make as much noise. He also became friends with the bird who helped him when he fell. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily loved to play outside with her friends. One day, Lily went to the park with her friends. They saw a big slide and they all wanted to try it. Lily was scared because the slide was hard and she didn't want to get hurt.

Lily's friend, Timmy, said, "Don't be scared, Lily. Just slide down slowly and you'll be okay." Lily listened to Timmy and slowly slid down the slide. It was so much fun! Lily laughed and said, "That was great!"

Later that day, Lily's mom asked her to clean her closet. Lily didn't want to because it was hard work. But then she remembered what Timmy said, "Don't be scared, just do it slowly." So, Lily cleaned her closet slowly and it wasn't so hard after all.

The moral of the story is that sometimes things might seem hard or scary, but if you take it slow and don't give up, you can do it!

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy liked to walk on the path in the woods. He would walk on the path every day with his mommy and daddy. One day, Timmy saw a big rock on the path. He didn't like the rock, it made the path not as good.

Timmy told his mommy and daddy about the rock. His mommy said they would add some tools to their backpacks for next time. The next day, they brought the tools with them. Timmy's daddy used a hammer to break the rock into little pieces. Timmy helped by carrying the little pieces off the path. Now, the path was good again and Timmy was happy.

From that day on, Timmy always checked the path for rocks and other things that might make it not as good. And if he saw something, he knew just what to do – add some tools and fix it!

Ben and Sam were best friends. They liked to play with toys. They had many toys, but their favorite was a big tank. The tank was green and had a long gun. It could make loud noises and move fast.

One day, they took the tank to the park. They saw other kids playing with balls and dolls. Ben and Sam wanted to show them their tank. They drove the tank around and made it shoot. They said, "Look at our tank! It is fierce! It can beat any toy!"

Some kids were scared of the tank. They ran away or hid behind trees. Some kids were angry at the tank. They threw rocks or sticks at it. They said, "Stop that! You are mean! You are not nice!"

Ben and Sam did not care. They thought it was fun to make the other kids afraid or mad. They laughed and drove the tank faster. They said, "We are the best! We have the fiercest tank!"

But then, something bad happened. The tank hit a big rock and flipped over. The gun broke and the noises stopped. The tank was broken. Ben and Sam were sad. They tried to fix the tank, but they could not. They cried and hugged the tank.

A girl came over to them. She had a doll in her hand. She said, "I am sorry your tank is broken. Do you want to play with my doll? She is nice. She can be your friend."

Ben and Sam looked at the girl. They looked at the doll. They looked at each other. They felt sorry for being mean to the other kids. They said, "Thank you. We are sorry too. We want to play with you. We want to be your friend."

They gave the girl the tank. She gave them the doll. They played together and had fun. They learned that being nice is better than being fierce. They learned that having friends is better than having toys.

Once upon a time, there was a tall tree in a big forest. The tall tree had a shiny jewel at the very top. All the animals in the forest wanted the jewel because it was so pretty.

One day, a small bird tried to fly up and get the jewel. The bird tried and tried, but it could not manage to reach the top. The bird felt sad and asked for help from the other animals. A kind squirrel heard the bird and wanted to help.

The squirrel climbed the tall tree and got the jewel for the bird. The two animals shared the pretty jewel and became good friends. The other animals saw this and learned that helping each other is better than trying to get things all by themselves.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a big garden with many plants. In the garden, there was a pink radish. Lily liked the pink radish very much.

One day, Lily's friend Tom came to play. Lily showed Tom the pink radish. Tom said, "I want to eat the pink radish." Lily said, "No, it is mine. You cannot eat it." Tom was sad, but he did not cry.

Later, when Lily was not looking, Tom took the pink radish. He ate it all up. When Lily saw that the pink radish was gone, she began to cry. She was very sad that her friend had taken her favorite thing. And now, the pink radish was gone forever.

Once upon a time there was a little girl who loved to explore. One day she came across an amazing object in the park. It was a pretty pink recorder.

The little girl was so excited. She wanted to play with it. She picked it up and looked at it, turning it around in her hands.

"What's that?" She asked her mom who came over to see what was happening.

"That's a recorder. It will record the noises you make," replied her excited mom.

The little girl was so happy. She started to move her hand over it and began to make funny little sounds.

Her mom smiled and said, "That's great - it's recording your noises! You're making music."

The little girl smiled. She loved making music with her new pink recorder.

Tom is a curious cat. He likes to explore new places and find new things. One day, he sees a big box in the living room. He wonders what is inside. He jumps on the box and sniffs it. He hears a soft sound. He scratches the box and makes a hole. He peeks inside.

He sees a small ball of fur. It is a puppy. The puppy is scared and shakes. Tom feels sorry for the puppy. He says, "Hello, little fur. I am Tom. Do not be afraid. I am your friend." The puppy looks at Tom and wags his tail. He says, "Hello, Tom. I am Max. I am glad you are my friend. I was lonely in the box."

Tom and Max become friends. They play together and share their toys. They cuddle and nap together. They hope to stay together forever. They are happy.

Once there was a kind boy named Tom. Tom was very thoughtful and knew how to show people how much he cared. One day, he had a great idea.

He ran to his mom and said, “Mom, I want to send mail to grandma!” His mom smiled and nodded. She said, “That’s a great idea, Tom. Let’s go buy some postcards and stamps.”

Tom was so excited to send mail to his grandma. At the store, he picked out a card with a picture of a cute puppy on it. He wrote a nice message and signed it with lots of love.

When they got home, Tom’s mom showed him how to place the stamp on the postcard and drop it in the mailbox. “Goodbye postcard!” Tom called out.

A few days later, Tom got a phone call from his grandma. She said, “Thank you for the thoughtful postcard, Tom! I love it!” Tom was so happy to know that his grandma loved his kind gesture. Tom smiled and thanked his mom for helping him send mail. She was very proud of her thoughtful son.

Once upon a time there was a friendly little girl named Jenny. Jenny was three years old and she loved to help do chores with her mom. Today, Jenny's mom was cleaning the house and asked Jenny to help her.

Jenny said, "Yes Mommy, I'll help!" She grabbed her mop and started helping her mom clean the kitchen floor.

When they finished, Jenny went to the closet to store the mop away. She opened the closet door and placed the mop inside. As she was putting the mop away, she saw a big box with lots of toys in it.

Jenny looked at her mom with a big smile and said, "Mommy, can I play with the toys inside?" Her mom smiled back and said, "Sure, why not? You can play with those toys anytime you want."

Jenny was so excited! She thanked her mom for being so friendly and then she started playing with the toys.

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a curious little girl named Lily. She loved to explore the world around her and ask lots of questions. One day, she decided to go on an adventure in the forest near her house.

As she was walking, she noticed a little bird with a vest stuck in a tree. The bird looked sad and scared, so Lily decided to help. She tried to reach the bird, but it was too high up.

Lily knew she had to hurry and find a way to save the bird. She looked around and found a long stick. She used it to gently push the vest off the tree, and the bird flew away happily. Lily felt proud of herself for helping the little bird and continued on her adventure with a smile on her face.

Once upon a time, there lived a little girl. She loved going outside to play in the sun. One day, the sun was shining so brightly and everything was so warm.

The little girl excitedly started to run around. She ran so fast she got dizzy, then fell to the ground.

But then, to her surprise, she felt something cold. She looked down and saw the ground was covered in snow. The little girl gasped.

She quickly ran to her mom and said, "Mommy, there's snow outside! Can we go play?"

Her mom chuckled and said, "Yes, but we have to grab a sack first."

So they went outside and gathered up the snow in a sack. The little girl was so excited that she twirled around and around, making a mini snow storm.

They took the sack home and put it near the fireplace. The little girl wanted to play with the snow all day, and her mom said she could do just that.

So the little girl spent the day playing with the snow until the sack was empty. It was cold but still so much fun!

The little girl was walking around the garden with her big brother. She saw a big brown apple on a tree. She reached up as high as she could to get it but it was too high for her. She asked her brother to get it for her.

He smiled and said, "Sure, let's give it a try". He stretched up his arms and picked the apple from the tree. He showed it to the girl and she beamed with joy.

The girl said, "Thank you, Big Brother. Now I'm going to call it my special apple". She hugged the apple tightly as she walked back home with her brother.

Back home, the girl asked her mum if she could take a bite. Her mum smiled and said, "Yes, of course, sweetheart".

The little girl took a juicy, crunchy bite and it tasted delicious. She grinned and said, "Mum, this brown apple is the most yummiest one I've ever tasted!"

Once there was a boy named Bob. He was not very wealthy, but he was happy. One day Bob was walking in the park and he saw a big, fluffy cloud in the sky. He thought it looked so soft and snugly that he wanted to steal it! So Bob reached up high and tried to grab the cloud. But it was too far away.

Bob was sad and he thought he could never get the cloud. A kindly wealthy man saw Bob and said, "I can help you, Bob." The man pulled a long stick out of his coat and gave it to Bob. He said, "Now you can reach the cloud!"

Bob took the stick and swung it up to the sky. He had never seen anything so beautiful! He grabbed hold of the cloud and held tight. Before the man could say a word, Bob ran off with his stolen cloud.

Bob was so happy! He ran around, laughing and twirling all day with his new cloud close to him. He showed it to his friends, who all thought it was the best cloud ever. And Bob never felt so happy and wealthy.

Once upon a time, there was a chubby bee named Buzzy. Buzzy loved to fly around and explore the world. He flew above a river and saw something very interesting. It was an oxygen tank, split in two!

Buzzy flew around the tank, confused. He had never seen anything like it before. Buzzy wanted to get closer, so he carefully flew inside the oxygen tank. It was dark, but he could still see water everywhere around him.

He decided it was time to find out where the split had happened. He flew up to the top of the oxygen tank and saw that it was very broken. There was a big crack in the middle. That must have been what caused the tank to split.

Buzzy flew out of the tank and went back to his friends. He told them all about his amazing discovery. They were very impressed! From that day on, they all paid more attention to the world around them.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl. She was very lonely because she didn't have any friends. She wanted to make a friend so she could have someone to play with.

One day, she decided to shoot her arrow up in the sky. She closed her eyes and wished with all her heart that her arrow could take her to a new friend.

When she opened her eyes, she was surprised to see that the arrow had taken her to a new year! It was a lovely, sunny year and all of the trees were full of flowers. She could hear birds singing in the trees.

The little girl was so happy to have found her new friend. She and her new friend ran around in the sun and played lots of games. They were never lonely again.

The little girl and her new friend lived happily ever after. They would spend every day shooting their arrows up in the sky, wondering what their next adventure would bring!

The sun was shining brightly outside and Colin was playing happily in his garden. He saw a lovely prune tree and was impressed. Colin wanted to pick some prunes from the tree, but his mommy told him he could not. Colin was very disappointed and asked his mommy to discuss the matter. "Please, mommy," he begged. His mommy smiled and said, "No, Colin. Prunes are lovely, but we can't pick them today." No matter how hard he begged, his mommy would not change her mind. Colin was sad and tried to think of a way to get his prunes. Suddenly, he had a great idea! The next day, he went outside and started to carefully discuss the situation with the prune tree. "Please," he asked politely, "can I have some prunes?" Amazingly, the prune tree seemed to understand and shook gently, dropping a few lovely prunes down to the ground. Colin was delighted! He thanked the prune tree and ran off to show his mommy. His mommy was very happy and she hugged him tightly. From then on, Colin and the prune tree were the best of friends.

Mary and her mom were out running errands. Mary was three years old and eager to help her mom. As they walked along, Mary saw a big puddle blocking the path ahead. Without hesitating, she said, "Mommy, let me support you so you don't have to walk in the drain!"

Her mom was proud of her daughter's resourcefulness and smiled. She gratefully took Mary's hand and the two of them crossed the drain safely.

Later that day, Mary felt ashamed when her mom scolded her for not taking her shoes off before coming in the house. She swallowed hard, not wanting to cry in front of her mom.

Her mom looked kindly at Mary and said, "Mary, don't be ashamed. You are so helpful and you were so brave offering to support me crossing the drain. That was very kind of you. As a reward, you can stay up an extra 30 minutes tonight."

Mary smiled softly and promised never to forget that kindness pays off. She hugged her mom tightly, thankful for her support.

Auntie was feeling very happy. She had come to visit her lovely niece, who was three years old. The two were having a great time together.

Auntie showed her niece a toy that she had brought. It was a bright, yellow ball. The little girl smiled at it. Auntie said, “Let’s play with it!”

The little girl picked up the ball and started to roll it around the room. Auntie laughed and joined in. She poked the ball with her finger so that it rolled towards her niece. The little girl squealed with delight and chased after it.

Auntie and her niece kept playing with the ball until the little girl was too tired to continue. Auntie hugged her and said, “Thank you for such a lovely time!” The little girl smiled and hugged her aunt back.

It had been such a lovely afternoon, full of fun and laughter. Auntie was feeling very happy and thanked the little girl for being so brave and giving her aunt so much love.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved the color pink and always wore a pink dress. One day, Lily's mommy said they were going to a festival. Lily was so excited, she jumped up and down.

At the festival, there were lots of fun things to do. They played games and ate yummy food. Suddenly, Lily saw her friend Emily. She ran over to her and they hugged. Emily was wearing a pretty pink bow in her hair.

Later, when it was time to go home, Lily's mommy called her name. Lily ran over to her and they went home together. Lily was so happy and couldn't wait to go to another festival.

Once upon a time in a small village there were two best friends, Jack and Jill. Jack had a big garden where he grew a big, round and orange pumpkin.

One day Jill came to Jack's garden and admired his pumpkin. She told Jack that it was the most beautiful she had ever seen. Jack smiled and told Jill he had worked hard to grow it with lots of love and attention.

Surprisely, the next day Jack noticed that the color of the pumpkin had changed. It was no longer orange but gray.

Jill sadly told Jack that someone had probably taken the pumpkin away in the night. Jack was sad but he knew what had happened. He told Jill:

"We must be respectful and admirative of others and the things they have. We must not take away what belongs to someone else".

And from that day on, Jack and Jill never took away from anyone else. They showed admiration for what each other had and respected each other's possesions.

Once upon a time, there was a bird. The bird liked to fly in the sky. It was very graceful when it flew. One day, the bird flew to a party. At the party, there was a big dessert. The bird wanted to eat the dessert. But, the bird was too full from flying. So, the bird watched everyone else eat the dessert. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lily. She had a desk in her room where she liked to draw pictures. One day, Lily's little brother came into her room and wanted to play with her markers. But Lily said no because she didn't want him to ruin her pictures.

Her brother got mad and started to cry. Lily felt bad and wanted to make him happy again. She remembered she had a thin piece of paper and decided to make him a paper airplane. She folded the paper carefully and gave it to him. Her brother stopped crying and smiled.

He took the paper airplane and flew it around the room. Lily was happy to see her brother smile again. She nodded and said, "I'm glad you like it." From that day on, Lily and her brother played together more often and shared their toys. They never fought again. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play in the park with her friends. One day, she saw a big slide and she wanted to go on it so badly.

Lily's friend, Tommy, came over and asked her, "Do you want to play with my brush?"

Lily replied, "No, I want to slide down that big slide!"

Tommy said, "Okay, let's go!"

They ran over to the slide and Lily climbed up the ladder. She was so excited to slide down. When she got to the top, she yelled, "Whee!" and slid down as fast as she could.

Afterwards, Tommy said, "That was so much fun! Can we do it again?"

Lily smiled and said, "Yes, let's do it again!"

They climbed back up the ladder and slid down the big slide over and over again. It was the best day ever!

Once there was a little lamb named Lily. Lily was very happy and loved running and playing in the fields. Every day, she would spend hours running and leaping in the sunshine and she was always full of joy. But one day, Lily's mom said something to her that made her sad.

"Lily, you must remember to always eat your meat," her mom said. "It is very important for your health."

At first, Lily was confused. Meat was something she didn't like and she wanted to keep playing. But her mom was very serious and Lily knew she had to do it.

So, Lily started eating her meat every day, and she found it was not so bad after all. Soon, she loved it and she felt much better, more energetic and happier.

This story teaches us that it is important to remember to do the things that are important for our health. Even if we don't like it, making small changes can help us to feel much better and be more cheerful.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Katie. She was only three years old, but she was very adventurous.

One day, Katie was exploring in her backyard when she noticed something mysterious. "What is that?" she said as she looked at the little knob in the ground.

Katie's mom heard her and came running over.

"It looks like someone has buried something here, Katie," her mom said. "Let's bring it inside and see what it is."

So Katie's mom carefully dug the knob out of the ground and brought it inside. Katie jumped up and down with excitement!

Once inside, Katie and her mom brushed the dirt off the knob and unscrewed it. To their surprise, inside was a secret note!

Katie's mom read the note aloud. It said: "Today is a very mysterious day, find the treasures and let the fun come your way!"

Katie and her mom laughed and clapped their hands. It was going to be an exciting day!

Once upon a time, there was a bunny named Benny. Benny was very nosy and liked to hop around and sniff everything. One day, Benny saw a pretty ribbon and decided to tie it around his ear. He hopped around showing off his fancy ear to all his bunny friends.

But as he was hopping, the ribbon became too tight and started to hurt his ear. Benny tried to untie the ribbon but his little bunny paws couldn't do it. He was starting to feel sad and scared.

Just then, his friend Lucy the squirrel came by and saw Benny's problem. She quickly untied the ribbon and Benny felt much better. From that day on, Benny learned to be careful when tying things around his ears and was grateful for his helpful friend Lucy. The end.

Lily and Tom were playing with their blocks in the living room. They liked to build towers and houses and bridges with the colorful blocks. They were having fun and making noises.

But then, their big brother Sam came in. He was bored and wanted to play too. He saw the blocks and had a bad idea. He decided to destroy what Lily and Tom had built. He kicked and smashed and threw the blocks everywhere. He laughed and said, "This is more fun!"

Lily and Tom were very sad and angry. They saw their blocks broken and scattered. They cried and shouted, "Stop it, Sam! You are mean and naughty! You ruined our game!"

Mom heard the noise and came to see what was wrong. She saw the mess and the tears. She was not happy with Sam. She scolded him and said, "Sam, what did you do? You should not destroy your siblings' toys. You should be kind and share. Go to your room and think about what you did."

She hugged Lily and Tom and said, "I'm sorry, my loves. Don't worry, we can fix the blocks and play again. You did a good job building. I'm proud of you." She helped them pick up the blocks and put them in a box. She gave them some cookies and milk and said, "Let's go to the couch and read a story. That will make you feel better."

Lily and Tom nodded and smiled. They followed Mom to the couch and snuggled with her. They felt comfortable and safe. They listened to Mom's voice and looked at the pictures. They forgot about Sam and the blocks. They were happy again.

Once upon a time there was a little boy called Jack. He was three years old and very happy.

One day he saw something round and shiny on the ground. It was a battery! He picked it up and started to roll it between his hands. He rolled it all around his garden and then back into the house.

At first, Jack was having lots of fun, but after a while the battery made his hands feel uncomfortable. He decided to put it back on the ground and never touch it again!

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a wise old man. The man was very clever and he always thought of different ways to help others. One day, the man had an idea. He wanted to guess what his pupils were thinking. He started with the first pupil, who was a little bit shy.

The man asked the pupil to close their eyes and think of something, then he guessed what they were thinking. The pupil was amazed - he was right! He guessed the pupil was thinking of elephants.

The man went to the next pupil, who was a little bit bolder. He asked them to close their eyes and think of something, then he guessed. The pupil was astonished - the man had guessed correctly. This time, the man had guessed the pupil was thinking of balloons!

The man went to the last pupil, who was the wisest of them all. The pupil closed their eyes and the man guessed again. This time he guessed the pupil was thinking of stars. The wise pupil opened their eyes and smiled - the man had guessed right once again!

The old man was very pleased. He had used his wisdom to guess what his pupils were thinking. From that day forwards, his pupils were always eager to hear his wise guesses.

Tom and Sam are friends. They like to play games. Today they play a game with a rope. They tie the rope to a tree and to a stick. They pull the rope to see who is stronger.

"Pull, pull, pull!" Tom says. He tries to make Sam fall.

"Pull, pull, pull!" Sam says. He tries to make Tom fall.

They pull and pull and pull. The rope is tight. The stick is bent. They are both strong. They both want to win.

But then, the rope breaks. Snap! The rope is not strong. Tom and Sam fall to the ground. They are not hurt. They are surprised. They look at each other and laugh.

"Who wins?" Tom asks.

"Nobody wins," Sam says. "The rope wins."

They get up and hug. They are warm. They are happy. They are still friends. They go to find a new game.

Once upon a time there was a little girl who loved to play. She had a wide stretching garden with a tall tree in the middle. One day, the little girl was playing near the tree and she heard a strange noise! She stopped and listened carefully.

"Help! Help me!" she heard a voice coming from the branches of the tree. The little girl couldn't believe it. She looked up and saw a dog stuck in the branches!

"I'm stuck!" cried the dog. The little girl hastily scrambled onto the tree and tried to get to the dog. "Don't worry," she said, "I'll rescue you!" Fortunately, the little girl was brave and clever. She grabbed a cushion from the garden and propped it up against the tree. Then, she told the dog to jump onto the cushion. The dog jumped and the little girl caught him safely in her arms.

The little girl felt relieved that she was able to rescue the dog. She hugged the dog tightly and thanked him for being brave. The dog was so happy to be free again. From that day on, the little girl and the dog became best friends!

Once upon a time, there was a girl. She had long, brown hair and a big, caring heart. The girl loved choosing new shoes. She liked to run around in the bright sunlight, looking for the perfect pair of shoes.

One day, the girl spotted a shoe in the window that she liked. It was blue and sparkly. She couldn't resist it and decided to choose it.

The girl ran excitedly into the store and went straight up to the shopkeeper.

“Please may I have the blue shoe, please?” she asked sweetly.

The shopkeeper smiled and said “Yes, of course. Here you go!”. He handed the shoe to the girl and she put it on straight away.

The girl loved her new blue, sparkly shoe and couldn’t wait to show it off. She thanked the shopkeeper, before skipping out of the store with a big grin on her face.

The girl had made the perfect choice.

The end.

One sunny day, a small girl and her mother set out to go to the park. The small girl was so happy; she could barely contain her excitement.

As the two reached the park the small girl wanted to run ahead, but her mother said no.

“Okay, Mommy,” said the small girl, who listened to her mother and stayed put.

The mother made the little girl sit on a park bench and asked her to wait there.

“But why?” the small girl asked.

“I'll be back soon,” said the mother, “But you have to stay here.”

The small girl was frustrated, but she listened to her mother and waited. After a few minutes, she saw a group of children running in the park and playing.

“Mommy, why can't I play with the other kids?” she asked.

The mother looked around, and then raised her finger to her lips.

“Shh,” she said. “We'll talk about it later.”

The little girl was perplexed, and even more frustrated. She sighed and continued to wait.

A few moments later, her mother came back holding a big box. She said, “I got you a present!”

The small girl opened the box, and

John and Tara were playing in the park. John looked towards the horizon and saw an ancient house in the distance. He said to Tara, "Let's go explore the old house!"

Tara agreed, so they ventured off to the house. When they got there, John saw a desk in the corner. He said, "Let's search inside the desk!"

They opened it up and found the most amazing things. There were shiny coins, old jewelry, and ancient books. John wanted to keep all the treasure, but Tara said, "We have to surrender it. We can't keep these things."

John was sad but he knew Tara was right. They returned the treasure to the desk and quietly left the old house. Even though they couldn't keep the treasure, they had an amazing adventure that they would never forget.
