"Goodbye, Lily and Tom. You made me happy. Remember to be kind to everyone, even if they are different from you," Bob said.

Then Bob melted away and became a puddle. Lily and Tom cried a little, but they smiled too. They learned a lesson from Bob. They learned to be kind and to respect others. They also learned to enjoy the snow while it lasted.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She lived in a small house with her mommy and daddy. One day, Lily saw smoke coming out of the house next door. She was scared and told her mommy.

Mommy called the big, red fire truck to come and help. The fire truck used its long hose to spray wet water on the smoke. The water put out the fire and made everything wet. Lily watched as the fire truck made the smoke go away.

After the fire was gone, Lily saw her friend, Ben, crying. Ben had a small hurt on his arm. Lily wanted to help Ben heal. She got a band-aid from her mommy and put it on Ben's arm. Ben stopped crying and smiled at Lily. They played together in the wet grass, happy that the smoke was gone and that Ben's hurt was healing.

Once upon a time, there was a witch. She lived in a small house. She had a cat. The cat was her best friend. The witch wanted to find a new friend. She looked for someone who was available to play with her.

One day, the witch saw a little girl. The little girl was alone. The witch went to the little girl and said, "Hi, do you want to play with me? I don't have anyone to play with." The little girl looked at the witch and said, "Okay, I will play with you. But you have to be nice."

The witch and the little girl played together. They had fun. But the witch did not mind her manners. She was mean to the little girl. The little girl did not like it. She said, "You are not nice. I don't want to play with you anymore."

The witch was sad. She wanted to have a friend. But she did not know how to be nice. The witch went back to her house. She was alone again. The witch learned that being mean made her lose her new friend. The witch was sad and had a bad ending.

Max and Milly went for a walk in the park. They saw a bush with lots of berries on it. Max and Milly stopped to discuss the berries, Milly thought they were delicious. She picked a pale berry and ate it. Max was worried it might make her sick, but Milly just laughed. "Delicious!" she said. The two children talked and talked about the different types of berries they could see. eventually, they decided to pick some of the pale ones. But then a big gust of wind came and all the berries flew away. Max and Milly just laughed, and went home.

Lily was a little girl who liked to play with her toys. She had a lot of dolls, cars, blocks and books. She also had a big, soft bathrobe that she wore when she was cold or sleepy. She loved her bathrobe very much.

One day, Lily was playing in her room with her toys. She heard a loud noise from the kitchen. She was nervous. She ran to see what was happening. She saw her big brother Tom and his friend Sam. They were making a mess. They had flour, eggs, milk and sugar all over the floor, the table and the walls. They were trying to make a cake, but they did not know how.

Lily was angry. She did not like messes. She wanted to tell them to stop. But she was also scared. Tom and Sam were bigger and stronger than her. They sometimes teased her and took her toys. She did not want to make them mad. She decided to go back to her room and hide.

She ran to her room and closed the door. She looked for her bathrobe. She wanted to wrap herself in it and feel safe. But she could not find it. She searched under her bed, in her closet, in her drawers. She could not see it anywhere. She started to cry.

She heard another loud noise from the kitchen. She heard Tom and Sam laughing. She heard them say something about a fire. She was curious. She opened the door and peeked outside. She saw smoke and flames coming from the oven. She saw Tom and Sam running away. She saw her bathrobe on the floor. It was covered in flour, eggs, milk and sugar. It was also on fire. It was destroyed.

Lily screamed. She was sad and scared. She lost her bathrobe. She lost her toys. She lost her room. She lost her home. She wished she had told Tom and Sam to stop. She wished she had a new bathrobe. She wished she had a happy ending. But she did not. She had a bad ending.

Once upon a time, there was a pretty girl called Mia. Mia loved to explore the world around her and see the beauty of nature. One day, Mia found a stand in the middle of the forest. She was curious and wanted to find out what it was. She went closer and noticed that the stand was made of old wood.

Mia wanted to protect the stand, so she decided to give it a nice makeover. She went to the nearby lake and collected some flowers. Then, she carefully arranged the flowers around the stand. She also placed a few shiny stones on the top, to make it look even prettier.

The next day, Mia was very pleased to see that her stand still looked beautiful. She hugged it and said: "I will protect you forever". From that day on, Mia visited the stand every day to make sure it was always safe.

Mia's stand still stands in the forest, a reminder to everyone to protect their nature and the things they love.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to draw pictures for his grandma who lived far away. One day, Timmy's mom said, "Let's send your picture to grandma in the mail!" Timmy was so excited!

Timmy drew a beautiful picture of a flower and his mom helped him put it in an envelope. "Is it ready to send?" Timmy asked. "Yes, it is!" said his mom. They put a stamp on the envelope and sent it off in the mail.

A few days later, Timmy's grandma called and said, "Thank you for the beautiful picture! It made me so happy." Timmy was so glad that his picture made his grandma happy. From then on, Timmy loved to send pictures in the mail to his grandma.

Once there was a fierce tooth. It was sitting in a park, near the swings. Suddenly, it spotted a small girl walking by and waved to her. She smiled and waved back.

The tooth was very happy and waved to the girl again. She smiled and waved back. This happened over and over again, every time the tooth waved, the girl waved back.

Finally, after a few weeks, the tooth and the girl met in the park. The tooth waved and the girl happily waved back. She laughed and asked the tooth what it was doing there by itself.

The tooth smiled and said “I've been waiting all this time just to be friends with you!” The girl was so happy that she gave the fierce tooth a big hug. From that day forward, the tooth and the girl were best friends. They both waved at each other every day as a sign of their friendship.

Tom and Mia were playing in the garden. They liked to run and jump and hide. But they did not like to touch the vegetables. The vegetables were green and red and yellow. They looked yucky.

"Let's go to the swing," Tom said. "The swing is fun."

"OK," Mia said. "But we have to go past the vegetables."

They ran to the swing, but they saw a big dog. The dog was barking and growling. It had sharp teeth and a long tail. It was blocking the way to the swing.

"Go away, dog!" Tom shouted. "We want to play on the swing!"

But the dog did not go away. It came closer and closer. Tom and Mia were scared. They wanted to run away, but they had nowhere to go.

"Maybe we can touch the vegetables," Mia said. "Maybe the dog does not like vegetables."

Tom looked at the vegetables. He did not want to touch them, but he wanted to be brave. He picked up a carrot and threw it at the dog. The dog caught the carrot and ate it. It wagged its tail and stopped barking.

"Good dog!" Mia said. "You like carrots!"

She picked up a tomato and threw it at the dog. The dog caught the tomato and ate it. It licked its lips and came closer to Mia.

"Can we pet you, dog?" Mia asked. "You are nice!"

The dog nodded and let Mia and Tom touch its fur. It was soft and warm. Mia and Tom smiled and laughed. They were not scared anymore.

They played with the dog and the vegetables. They gave the dog more carrots and tomatoes. They made a necklace of peas and a hat of lettuce. They had fun.

They learned that touching vegetables was not so bad. And they learned that being brave was good. They made a new friend. The dog was happy too. It liked Mia and Tom. And it liked vegetables.

Once upon a time, there was a family who had a problem. They had a big, thick roof, but it had a hole in it! Every time it rained, water came through the hole and made lots of mess.

The family didn't know how to fix the roof. They decided to call in the roof specialist to help. He said that it would take a lot of work to complete the roof and it would take a long time. The family agreed and they started to work.

They worked really hard, but soon enough the roof was complete. It was so thick and strong...no rain would be able to get through anymore! The family was so happy that they hugged the roof specialist and thanked him for his help.

The moral of this story is: When it looks like you have a problem that's too big to fix, just keep working and you can complete it!

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Gemma. She was so intelligent! Every day of her life she would skip around her house.

One day she went to an exit. She had never been so excited before! But when she got there, there was a big sign that said "No skipping here, only walking!". Gemma tried her best to walk, but eventually she couldn't resist and started skipping again.

The guard at the exit noticed and smiled. He said that he could see Gemma was very intelligent and would let her skip, but only if she promised always to remember the rules.

Gemma agreed, thanked the guard and skipped off towards home. From that day on, whenever Gemma went to the exit she skipped like she had promised, but always followed the rules.

Once upon a time, in a small house, there lived a little girl named Mia. Mia had a big dog named Max. Max was a fierce dog, but he loved Mia very much. They played together every day.

One day, Mia and Max went to the park. They saw a big tree with a swing. Mia wanted to play on the swing, but she was too small to push herself. Max sighed, and he had an idea. He used his strong legs to push Mia on the swing. Mia felt the weight of Max's push and she swung high into the air. She was so happy and laughed.

Mia and Max played on the swing all day long. They had so much fun together. The sun began to set, and it was time to go home. Mia hugged Max and said, "Thank you, Max, for being my best friend." Max wagged his tail and they walked home together, ready for another adventure tomorrow.

Lila and Lulu were twins. They liked to play with their dolls. They had many dolls, but their favorite was Molly. Molly had smooth hair and a pretty dress.

One day, Lila and Lulu had a fight. Lila wanted to play with Molly, but Lulu said no. She said Molly was her doll. Lila said no, Molly was their doll. They both pulled Molly's arms. Molly's dress ripped.

Lila and Lulu stopped pulling. They looked at Molly. They felt sad. They had hurt their doll. They had hurt each other.

"I'm sorry, Lulu," Lila said. "I didn't mean to rip Molly's dress."

"I'm sorry, Lila," Lulu said. "I didn't mean to be mean to you."

They hugged each other. They hugged Molly. They said they loved each other. They loved Molly.

They went to their mom. They showed her Molly's dress. They told her what happened. Mom smiled. She said she was proud of them for saying sorry. She said she could fix Molly's dress.

She took Molly and a needle and some thread. She sewed Molly's dress. She made it look new. She gave Molly back to Lila and Lulu. They thanked her. They said they would share Molly. They said they would not fight.

They went back to their room. They played with Molly. They made her shake her smooth hair. They made her talk. They made her laugh. They laughed too. They were happy. They were twins.

Once there was a little girl named Jane, who was three years old. She was an alert and curious girl, who loved to explore.

One day Jane was out playing in the playground and found an old, rusty watch. She picked it up and started to celebrate. She ran around the playground, proudly showing her watch to all her friends.

Suddenly, she bumped into an old, grumpy man. He grabbed the watch from her and said, "This watch is mine! You can't have it!" Jane started to cry and was very upset.

She ran to her father and told him about the old man. Her father was alert and immediately took action. He put on his brave face and marched to the playground. When he saw the old man, he said, "Please give my daughter back her watch." The old man hesitated, and then reluctantly handed it over.

Now Jane and her father celebrate their victory together. They laugh and play with the watch, looking forward to many more happy days ahead.

Once upon a time, there lived a tiny girl named Sarah. She was only three years old. She loved to explore and try new things.

One day, Sarah was in her bedroom when she heard a funny noise coming from the bathroom. She walked over to the bathroom and opened the door. To her surprise, she saw something very unusual inside.

It was the family pet, a puppy. The puppy was teasing Sarah with its tail! Sarah laughed and thought it was so funny.

But then something else happened. The puppy started to jump around the bathroom! It was creating a lot of messes and Sarah started to get mad. She shouted at the puppy and chased it away.

But later that night Sarah couldn't help but giggle when she thought about the unusual way the puppy had teased her in the bathroom. She was glad that she had such an adventurous friend to explore the world with!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to explore the forest with her friends. One day, they found an unusual trap in the middle of the path.

Lily's friend, Timmy, said "Let's open it and see what's inside!" But Lily knew that it was not a good idea. "No, Timmy. It might be dangerous. We should leave it alone," she said.

But Timmy didn't listen and opened the trap. Suddenly, a loud noise came from inside and a big angry bear came out! The children were so scared and ran away as fast as they could.

Lily learned that it's important to listen to your instincts and not do something that might be dangerous, even if it seems like fun. She also learned to always be careful when exploring the forest.

Freddy was very excited. He had a present! His mommy and daddy had bought him a special surprise. He couldn't wait to open it.

When he finally got to open the present, he thought it was something very ordinary. He expected to see something exciting and new. But when he opened the package, he saw it was just a toy car.

Freddy was disappointed. But then, he started to think about what he could do with the car. He could race it with his friends, or take it to the park. Suddenly, Freddy was happy again.

He knew there were so many things he could do with an ordinary toy car. He hugged his mommy and daddy and thanked them for the present. From that day on, Freddy loved playing with his toy car.

Once upon a time, there was small girl named Daisy. Daisy was very kind and always thought of others before herself. One day, Daisy wanted to make a special cake for her family. She carefully mixed the ingredients, but when she poured them into the pan she noticed she forgot to buy butter.

Daisy was sad and asked her mum for help. Her mum had a plan. She said,” Instead of buying butter, why don't you share what you have at home with others?” Daisy smiled, she knew her mum was right. Daisy shared some of her food with the neighbours and as a thank you, they gave Daisy some butter.

Daisy was excited to bake her special cake. She added the butter and the cake tasted delicious. Daisy smiled and said,”That's what happens when we share and belong.”

Tom and Jen are friends. They like to play together. One day, they want to travel to the big building. The big building has many books and toys. They ask their moms if they can go.

"Yes, you can go, but you have to be patient and careful," their moms say. "The big building is far away. You have to take the bus and walk a lot. And you have to listen to the lady who works there. She will help you find what you want."

Tom and Jen are happy. They pack their backpacks with snacks and water. They hold their moms' hands and go to the bus stop. They wait for the bus. They see many cars and people and animals. They talk about what they want to see and do at the big building.

The bus comes. They get on the bus and find seats. They look out the window. They see more things. They see a park, a school, a store, a bridge. They see a river, a boat, a bird, a fish. They see the big building. It is very tall and shiny. They are excited.

They get off the bus and walk to the big building. They see a sign that says "Library". They go inside. They see a lady who smiles at them. She says, "Hello, welcome to the library. What are you looking for today?"

Tom and Jen say, "We want to see books and toys, please."

The lady says, "Sure, follow me. I will show you where they are. But first, you have to be quiet and respectful. The library is a place where people read and learn. You have to use your inside voice and share with others."

Tom and Jen nod. They say, "OK, we will be quiet and respectful. We will use our inside voice and share with others."

The lady leads them to a section of the library that has books and toys for children. She says, "Here you are. You can look at the books and play with the toys. But remember, you have to put them back where you found them when you are done. And you have to watch the time. You have to leave before the library closes."

Tom and Jen say, "Thank you, lady. We will put them back and watch the time. We will have fun."

The lady says, "You're welcome. Have fun. I will be around if you need me."

Tom and Jen explore the books and toys. They find many things that interest them. They read stories and learn facts. They play games and puzzles. They make friends with other children. They have fun.

They are patient and careful. They are quiet and respectful. They use their inside voice and share with others. They put the books and toys back where they found them. They watch the time. They leave before the library closes.

They say goodbye to the lady and thank her for her help. They say goodbye to their new friends and promise to come back. They go outside and walk to the bus stop. They wait for the bus. They see the big building. It is still tall and shiny. They are happy.

They get on the bus and find seats. They look out the window. They see the same things they saw before. They talk about what they saw and did at the big building. They tell their moms about their adventure.

Their moms are proud of them. They say, "You did a great job. You were patient and careful. You were quiet and respectful. You used your inside voice and shared with others. You had fun and learned something new. You are good friends."

Tom and Jen smile. They hug their moms. They say, "We love you, mom. We love the big building. We love the library. We want to go again."

Their moms say, "We love you, too. We love the big building. We love the library. We will go again."

Once upon a time, there was a dependable dog named Spot. Spot loved to play with his friends in the park. They would run, jump, and have lots of fun.

One day, Spot found a big bag of rice. He thought it would be fun to bury the rice and play a game with his friends. So, he dug a big hole and put the rice in it. Then, he covered it with dirt.

Spot called his friends to play a game of finding the rice. They all looked and looked, but they could not find it. Finally, Spot showed them where the rice was. They all laughed and had a great time. Spot was a very dependable friend.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved to eat ice cream. One day, she went to the ice cream shop and ordered a big scoop of purple ice cream. She got a spoon and started to eat it.

Suddenly, a big dog came out of nowhere and scared her. She dropped her spoon and ran away. She was so scared that she didn't even finish her ice cream.

When she got home, she told her mom what happened. "Mommy, a big dog scared me and I dropped my spoon," she said. Her mom hugged her and said, "Don't worry, Lily. We'll go back to the ice cream shop another day and get you a new spoon and some more purple ice cream."

Once upon a time, there was a pink balloon. It loved to fly around in the sky, but it was lonely. One day, it went to a park to meet some new friends.

The first thing it saw was a boy playing with a ball. He noticed the balloon and asked if it wanted to play. The balloon was excited and said yes!

They started to play and the balloon was having lots of fun. But then the balloon bumped the ball too hard and the boy started to complain. He said the balloon was too rough and not being careful.

The balloon felt sad and started to cry. But the boy said he was sorry and gave it a hug. He said it was okay and told the balloon to try again.

So the balloon flew around the park, slowly and carefully. And the balloon stayed friends with the boy for many years afterwards. The end.

Once upon a time there was a pirate named Pete. Pete was headed out to sea when he spotted a small boat. Inside the boat was a little boy.

Pete shouted, "Come here, little boy!" The boy was obedient and sailed his boat close to pirate Pete so he could climb onto his ship.

"What's your name, little boy?" asked the pirate. "My name is Tom," replied the boy.

Pete grinned. "Well Tom, I'm going to send you away on a secret adventure." Pete yelled to his crew, "Set sail now!"

Tom was very scared, but he was obedient. So he stayed quiet and helped the crew. Soon they were out at sea, with no land in sight.

The pirate laughed. "Ha ha ha! I've sent you far away and you'll never find me again!"

Tom cried and screamed, but the salty waves swallowed his words. Even though Tom was obedient, he had a bad ending.

Once upon a time, there lived a fat cat. His name was Jack, and he lived in a house with his family. Every morning, Jack would dress in his best vest and explore the neighbourhood.

One morning, as Jack walked down the street, he noticed a light coming from a nearby garden. As he walked closer, Jack saw an old man wearing a very big vest.

"What a beautiful vest you have," said Jack.

The old man smiled and said, "would you like to try it on?"

Jack was overjoyed, and quickly said yes. He put on the vest and looked in the mirror. Jack loved the way the vest hung off his shoulders.

The old man chuckled and said, "Always remember, my fat friend, that your own vest will always be the best."

Jack thanked the old man and went back home. From that day on, he made sure to always dress in his best vest.

Zoe was a very sleepy girl. She put on her blouse, but it was a bit too big. Her mum smiled at her, because she knew how much Zoe liked big things.

'Let's go outside and play,' her mum said.

Zoe nodded and followed her mum outside. Together they stood in the middle of the garden and bowed down. Zoe's mum started counting: 'One, two, three, bow!' and Zoe started to laugh. She felt happy and stretched her arms as far as she could.

A few minutes later, Zoe was feeling very sleepy. She could hardly keep her eyes open. 'Let's go inside, Zoe. It's time for bed,' her mum said, and Zoe nodded.

'Goodnight,' her mum said as she hugged Zoe tight. Zoe smiled and said 'Night night!' before drifting off to sleep.

Lily was a popular person. She had many friends who liked to play with her. She was good at sharing, singing and making jokes. She was happy most of the time.

But one day, a new person came to her school. His name was Max. He was not very nice. He did not share, he shouted and he pushed. He wanted to be the most popular person. He tried to take Lily's friends away from her.

Lily was sad and angry. She did not like Max. She wanted her friends back. She tried to talk to them, but they did not listen. They followed Max everywhere. They thought he was cool and fun.

Lily felt lonely. She did not know what to do. She missed her friends. She wished Max would go away.

Then, one day, something happened. Max was playing with a ball. He threw it too hard. It hit a window. The window broke. Glass fell everywhere. Everyone was scared. Max was in trouble.

Lily saw what happened. She ran to help. She picked up the glass and threw it in the bin. She checked if anyone was hurt. She told the teacher what happened. She was brave and kind.

The teacher was proud of Lily. She thanked her for being helpful. She scolded Max for being careless. She told him to say sorry and to pay for the window. Max was ashamed and sorry.

Lily's friends saw what happened. They realized that Lily was a better person than Max. They felt bad for leaving her. They went to her and said sorry. They asked her to be their friend again. Lily was happy. She forgave them. She hugged them.

Lily was a popular person again. She had many friends who liked to play with her. She was good at sharing, singing and making jokes. She was happy most of the time. And Max? He learned his lesson. He tried to be nicer. He said sorry to Lily. He asked her to be his friend too. Lily was kind. She said yes. She taught him how to share, sing and make jokes. He was happy too.

It was a cold day. The little girl was looking for a way to stay warm. She found her pillow and felt comfort as she hugged it close. Her eyes began to close when suddenly, there was a sharp sound outside her window.

The little girl was scared. She knew she had to find a safe place. She picked up her pillow and ran outside. She looked around and saw nothing but darkness. Then, she felt something cold. It was coming closer and closer.

The little girl was scared and there was nowhere to hide. The cold thing was getting closer and closer. Finally, it stopped and put its cold hand on her shoulder. The little girl screamed. She tried to run away but the cold thing followed her.

The little girl knew there was nowhere to hide. She felt so scared and cold, until the cold thing put its cold hands around her neck. She couldn't breathe and suddenly everything went black. The pillow dropped to the ground and she was dead.

Tom and Lily are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big tire on the grass. It is black and round.

"Look, a tire!" Tom says. "Let's hop on it!"

"OK!" Lily says. They run to the tire and hop on it. They bounce up and down. They laugh and have fun.

But then, a man comes. He is angry. He has a sour face. He says the tire is his.

"Hey, you kids! Get off my tire!" he shouts. "That's my tire! I need it for my car!"

Tom and Lily are scared. They hop off the tire. They say sorry to the man.

"Sorry, mister. We didn't know it was your tire. We just wanted to play," Tom says.

"Yeah, sorry. We won't do it again," Lily says.

The man takes the tire and puts it in his car. He drives away. Tom and Lily look at each other. They are sad.

"Let's go play something else," Tom says.

"OK. Maybe we can find a ball or a swing," Lily says.

They hold hands and walk to the other side of the park. They hope to find something else to hop on.

Once upon a time there was a girl named Lucy who had a foolish dream. She wanted to marry a prince and have a grand wedding.

One day, she decided to go for a walk to try and find her prince. She walked through the woods and came to a castle. She peeked inside, but there was no prince.

Suddenly, she heard a voice from behind her shoulder. "Who are you looking for?" asked the voice. Lucy turned around and was shocked to see that it was the prince!

The prince asked Lucy if she wanted to marry him. She smiled and said yes. The prince put a ring on her finger and they hugged each other.

The prince and Lucy got married and had a big party. Everyone was so happy they danced and laughed all night.

The prince and Lucy lived happily ever after and were never foolish again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to draw and color. One day, she drew a beautiful pattern with lots of colors. She was so proud of her drawing and showed it to her mom.

Mom said, "Wow, Lily! You did a great job. Let's show it to your dad when he comes home."

But then, the wind blew and scattered all of Lily's papers on the ground. She was sad and started to cry.

Mom said, "Don't worry, Lily. We can pick them up and put them back together. And we'll be even more proud of your drawing because you never gave up."

Once upon a time there was a little girl. She was three years old and really loved going to the zoo. Every day she would go to the zoo and poke the different animals with a stick - but very gently!

The animals at the zoo were very nice to her and always let her poke them. The giraffe was especially gentle and the little girl was very grateful.

One day the little girl realized that she had poked all the animals in the zoo at least once. She was very happy and felt proud of herself.

From then on, whenever the little girl visited the zoo she was always very gentle with the animals and always made sure to give them a friendly poke!

Once there was a brave little girl called Liza. She wanted to understand how onions grow. So Liza went to the vegetable garden to find out.

When Liza got there she couldn't believe what she saw. Onions were growing everywhere. She asked the gardener, "How do onions grow?"

The gardener smiled and said, "It's quite simple. You just plant an onion in the ground, water it each day and the roots will grow down and the onion will grow up."

Liza was so excited. She thanked the gardener and went home. She understood that onions need soil, water and sunshine to grow. She was so proud of herself for being brave and asking questions to learn more.

Once upon a time, there was a good man named Tom. He liked to supply food to the animals in the forest. Every day, Tom went to the forest with a big bag of food.

One day, while Tom was walking in the forest, he met a talking bird. The bird said, "Thank you, Tom, for the food you supply. Can you help me find my friend?"

Tom said, "Yes, I can help you." They walked and walked until they found the bird's friend. The friend was very happy to see them.

In the end, the two birds thanked Tom for his help. They learned that it is good to help others when they need it, just like Tom did. And Tom learned that being kind to animals made him feel happy too.

One day, two friends went outside to play. It was a quiet day and the sun was shining brightly. The two friends wanted to have fun.

One of the friends had a toy gun. He said he could shoot it. The other friend was excited to try it.

The first friend pointed the gun at the sky. He pulled the trigger and it made a loud noise. He looked up and saw the sun. He had shot at the sun!

The second friend was scared by the loud noise. He scrunched his eyes tightly and put his hands over his head.

The first friend laughed at his friend. He said it was okay and they could still have fun.

So they played together under the quiet sun. They had a lot of fun and laughed a lot. They were sure the sun was very proud of them.

Lila and Ben were playing by the river. They liked to throw stones and watch the water splash. Sometimes they saw fish or ducks or frogs. But today they saw something new. It was an otter.

The otter was brown and furry. It had a long tail and a round nose. It was swimming and diving in the water. It looked happy and fun. Lila and Ben wanted to say hello.

"Hi, otter!" Lila shouted. "Do you want to play with us?"

The otter heard Lila and came closer. It popped its head out of the water and looked at the children. It made a soft noise like a whistle.

"Hi, children!" the otter said. "I like to play. What are you doing?"

"We are throwing stones," Ben said. "Do you want to try?"

The otter nodded. It climbed out of the water and picked up a stone with its paws. It threw the stone as hard as it could. The stone flew in the air and landed in the water with a big splash.

"Wow, otter, you are good!" Lila said. "Can you do it again?"

The otter smiled. It picked up another stone and threw it even farther. It made a bigger splash.

"Wow, otter, you are better!" Ben said. "Can you do it one more time?"

The otter nodded. It picked up the biggest stone it could find and threw it with all its strength. The stone soared in the air and landed in the water with a huge splash.

"Wow, otter, you are the best!" Lila and Ben said together. They clapped their hands and cheered.

The otter was proud. It jumped in the air and did a flip. It landed back in the water and splashed the children.

"Ha, ha, otter, you are funny!" Lila and Ben said. They laughed and splashed back.

The otter, Lila and Ben played for a long time. They had a lot of fun. They became friends. The otter was sweet and kind. Lila and Ben were happy. They liked the otter. They liked the river. They liked to play.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily loved to play with her toys and have fun. One day, Lily's mom told her that she had to get dressed in her uniform for school. Lily didn't want to wear her uniform because she thought it was boring.

Lily's mom said, "You have to wear your uniform to school because it's the rule." Lily said, "That's crazy! I want to wear my pretty dress." But her mom said no.

At school, Lily's friend Tommy asked her if she wanted to drink some juice. Lily said yes and they went to get some juice. While they were drinking their juice, Lily said, "I don't like my uniform. It's so boring." Tommy said, "I like your uniform. It looks nice on you." Lily smiled and felt better about wearing her uniform.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a pink dress that she loved very much. She wore it everywhere she went and felt so proud when people complimented her on it.

One day, Lily went to the park to play with her friends. She was having so much fun on the swings that she didn't notice her dress had gotten caught on a branch. When she got off the swing, she realized her dress was torn and she had lost a button.

Lily felt sad and embarrassed that her favorite dress was ruined. But her mom told her that it's okay to lose things sometimes, and that what's important is how we handle it. Lily learned that she didn't need a fancy dress to feel proud of herself, and that true happiness comes from within. From that day on, Lily wore a big smile on her face and felt proud of who she was, even without her pink dress.

Tom and Lily like to play with their toy cars. They have many cars of different colors and sizes. They race them on the floor and make loud noises. Sometimes, their cars crash and break. Then, they need to repair them.

One day, Tom's blue car broke its wheel. He was sad and did not want to play anymore. Lily saw him and wanted to help. She said, "Don't worry, Tom. I can repair your car. I have a stamp that can fix it."

Lily took her stamp and showed it to Tom. It was a red stamp with a star on it. She said, "This is a magic stamp. It can make anything better. Watch this." She stamped the broken wheel of the car and said, "Abracadabra!"

Tom looked at his car and saw that the wheel was fixed. He was amazed and happy. He said, "Wow, Lily, you are right. Your stamp is magic. Thank you for repairing my car. You are a good friend."

Lily smiled and said, "You are welcome, Tom. I am glad you like my stamp. It is very reliable. It always works. Do you want to play with me?"

Tom nodded and said, "Yes, I do. Let's race our cars again. But be careful, don't crash them."

They played with their cars and had fun. They did not crash them again. They used Lily's stamp to decorate their cars with stars. They were happy and proud of their cars. They were good friends.

Tim and Lily liked to play with cars. They had many cars of different colors and sizes. They liked to zoom them on the floor and make loud noises. Sometimes they had races to see who was faster.

One day, they found a big box in the garage. It had a picture of a car track on it. They asked their mom if they could open it. She said yes, but they had to be careful. She helped them take out the pieces and put them together. It was a flexible track that they could bend and twist in different ways. They were very excited.

They each picked a car and put it on the track. They pushed a button and the cars started to zoom. They went up and down, around and around, and through a loop. Tim and Lily cheered and clapped. They had so much fun.

But then, something happened. Tim's car went too fast and hit Lily's car. They both flew off the track and crashed on the floor. Tim and Lily gasped. They ran to their cars and picked them up. They looked at them and saw that they were broken. They felt sad and angry.

"Hey, you broke my car!" Tim said.

"No, you broke my car!" Lily said.

They started to argue and blame each other. They forgot that they were playing and having fun. They forgot that they were friends.

Their mom heard them and came to see what was wrong. She saw the broken cars and the angry faces. She felt sorry for them. She hugged them and said, "I'm sorry your cars are broken. But you know what? They are not the most important thing. You are. You are both very special and I love you. And you should love each other, too. You are brother and sister, and you should be kind and share. Maybe you can fix your cars together, or find another way to play. What do you think?"

Tim and Lily looked at each other. They remembered that they liked to play with cars. They remembered that they liked to zoom them on the floor and make loud noises. They remembered that they liked to have races and see who was faster. But they also remembered that they liked each other. They liked to laugh and hug and help each other. They felt sorry for being mean and rude. They nodded and said, "Okay, mom. We're sorry. We love you. And we love each other, too."

They smiled and hugged. They put their cars aside and looked at the box. It had another picture on it. It was a picture of a match. A match that could light up and make fire. They wondered what it was for. They asked their mom if they could try it. She said yes, but they had to be careful. She helped them take out the match and show them how to use it. They were very curious.

They lit the match and saw the flame. It was bright and warm and flickered. They were amazed. They held it close to the track and saw something happen. The track started to glow and sparkle. It was a magic track that could change colors and patterns. They were very surprised.

They put the match in a safe place and put their cars back on the track. They pushed the button and the cars started to zoom again. They went up and down, around and around, and through the loop. But this time, they also changed colors and patterns. They matched the track and looked beautiful. Tim and Lily cheered and clapped. They had so much fun.

They played with the cars and the track for a long time. They zoomed and zoomed and zoomed. They forgot about the broken cars and the angry words. They remembered the magic match and the happy hugs. They remembered that they were friends. And they had the best day ever.

Once upon a time, there was a curious little bear. He wanted to explore and have lots of fun. So he followed a path to try and do just that. He was excited when he saw a deep hole. He wanted to make it bigger so he could jump in and explore what was inside.

He spent the whole day making the hole bigger and bigger. Finally, the hole was ready and deep enough for him to jump in. He was so happy and jumped in with a smile.

But when he landed, he quickly noticed that something was wrong. The hole was too deep! The little bear was stuck in the deep hole and he couldn't get out. He was so scared and started crying for help.

But no one could hear him and he was stuck in the deep hole forever. The curious little bear never got to explore and have fun like he wanted.

The end.

Henry was a happy little bear. He liked to explore and discover new things. One crisp morning he decided to visit the meadow. He put on his red boots and made sure his mommy had tied his laces tight around his heels.

Off he went into the meadow. It was so beautiful with all the different colours around him. He ran around, exploring and bouncing around. He even discovered a yummy looking berry bush. Henry was so excited that he couldn't help but eat one. It was incredibly sweet.

Henry was thoroughly enjoying himself in the meadow but eventually it was time to leave. He said goodbye to the berry bush and, with a sigh, headed back home.

Henry had had a wonderful time visiting the meadow. He couldn't wait to tell his friends all about his adventure. He thumped his way back home, happy that his heels were tightly held in his red boots, and dreamed of visiting the meadow again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved Christmas because her mommy and daddy would put up a big tree with lots of pretty ornaments. One day, Lily found a shiny red ornament that she really liked. She wanted to keep it all for herself and not share with her little brother.

But her mommy told her that it wasn't nice to be bossy and that she should share her toys. Lily felt sad, but then she had an idea. She decided to give her brother a different ornament to keep, so they could both have their own special one.

Lily learned that it feels good to share and be kind to others. And every year, when they put up the Christmas tree, she remembers the lesson she learned and looks for her shiny red ornament.

One day, a furry cat named Tom went to the park. He saw a man with a big leather ball. The man said, "Tom, do you want to play?"

Tom wanted to perform a trick for the man. He jumped high in the air and hit the leather ball. The ball went very far. The man clapped and said, "Good job, Tom!"

Tom felt happy. He liked to perform tricks for his friends. He played with the leather ball until it was time to go home. The man said, "Bye, Tom! See you soon!"

Once upon a time, there was a normal boy named Tim. Tim liked to spend his days playing outside. One day, he went to the park to play ball with his friends.

At the park, there was a lot of green grass. Tim and his friends played on the grass all day long. They laughed, ran, and had a lot of fun. The sun was shining, and the birds were singing.

But then, something bad happened. Tim tripped on a rock and fell down. He started to cry because it hurt a lot. His friends tried to help him, but they couldn't. Tim's mom came and took him home. Tim was sad because he couldn't play with his friends anymore that day.

Once upon a time, in a small house, there lived a loyal dog named Buddy. Buddy loved to play with his ball. He would throw it up in the air and catch it with his mouth. Buddy's best friend was a little girl named Anna. They played together every day.

One day, while Anna and Buddy were playing, the ball rolled into the street. Buddy ran after it, but Anna knew that was trouble. She shouted, "Buddy, stop!" Buddy stopped and looked at Anna. He knew he should listen to her.

Anna walked over to Buddy and picked up the ball. She said, "We have to be careful, Buddy. The street can be dangerous." Buddy wagged his tail, happy that Anna was looking out for him. From that day on, they made sure to only play in the yard, away from the street. And they lived happily ever after, always staying loyal to each other.

Once upon a time there was a kind and gentle foot. The foot had special powers and it could help people in need. One day, the foot decided to print a letter for somebody. It knew that the person it was printing for could be very happy with its help.

But when the foot started to print, it made a huge mess! The letter was all over the floor. The kind foot was feeling sad. It wanted to help but it was not sure what to do.

Suddenly, an idea came to it! The foot started to dance around the room. It spun and twirled until all of the pieces of the letter flew into the air. Each piece floated back down in the right place.

When the foot looked, the letter was complete! It had printed it perfectly! The foot was so happy and it smiled. The letter had been printed in record time and it was perfect!

The foot had used its special powers to help someone in need. It was a kind and gentle foot and it was proud of what it had done.

Once upon a time, there was a friendly cat named Mittens. Mittens loved to play with her toys and chase after butterflies. One day, she found a ball of yarn in the attic. Mittens started to play with the yarn and accidentally scatter it all over the place.

Mittens didn't know what to do, so she ran to her owner, a little girl named Lily. Lily saw the mess in the attic and started to help Mittens gather the yarn. They worked together and soon the attic was clean again.

Mittens was happy that Lily was such a friendly helper. They played with the ball of yarn together and had a lot of fun. From then on, Mittens knew that if she ever needed help, she could always count on Lily to be a good friend.

Once upon a time, there lived a 3 year old girl named Clare. She was often told off for walking too tall, so she had to surrender her tall walking.

One day, Clare was so sad that she wore her big bathrobe and kept it on all day. Her mom found her looking all weird, surrounded by her toys and wearing the bathrobe despite it being a hot day.

Her mom asked her, "What's wrong, Clare? Why are you wearing the bathrobe?"

Clare said, "I want to look like my toy; he has a bathrobe too."

Her mom hugged her and said, "It's okay, Clare. You can surrender your sadness and be happy again. Come on, let's take off the bathrobe and you can play with your toys!"

Clare was so relieved and took off the bathrobe. She hugged her mom and was happy again. She was never told off for walking too tall again.

There was a kid who was shy. She never talked to the other kids. She would just keep to herself and play alone. One day, she decided to try and make some friends. She was really nervous, but she pushed through it.

First, she said "hello" to one of the other kids. The other kid was surprised and stepped back. She was scared of the shy kid. But the shy kid smiled, and the other kid smiled back.

Pretty soon, the shy kid had made a few more friends in the playground. She talked, laughed and played with them. She had gained the trust of her new friends.

The shy kid was so happy that she had been brave to try and make new friends. From then on, she was much less shy and was able to play with all the other kids every day.

Sally was playing in the park one day when a funny man walked up to her. He started to joke around, and Sally laughed so hard that she could barely stand up. The man was playing on the side of the slide, making it wobble back and forth. All the sudden, the slide started to break because it was so fragile! Sally was so scared, but the man was still joking around. He laughed and said it was no big deal and then helped fix the slide. After everything was back in place, Sally and the man laughed and played on the slide together. Sally's mom saw them and smiled. They had a lot of fun together, and the slide was all fixed.

On Sunday, Anna and Tom went to the park with Mom and Dad. They liked to play on the swings, the slide and the seesaw. They also liked to feed the ducks in the pond.

But today, the park was empty. There were no other kids, no ducks, no squirrels. Anna and Tom felt sad and bored.

"Where is everyone?" Anna asked Mom.

"Maybe they are at home, or at church, or at the store," Mom said. "It is a very cold day, so maybe they don't want to come out."

Anna and Tom looked around. They saw only snow and ice and bare trees. They shivered in their coats and hats.

"Can we go home too?" Tom asked Dad.

"Sure, we can go home," Dad said. "But first, let's have some fun in the snow. Do you want to make a snowman, or a snow angel, or a snowball?"

Anna and Tom nodded. They liked to make things in the snow. They followed Dad to a big pile of snow.

"Look, there is something in the snow!" Anna said. She pointed to a small black shape sticking out of the white.

"What is it?" Tom asked. He pointed to it too.

Dad bent down and dug out the shape. It was a hat. A red hat with a pom-pom.

"Wow, it's a hat!" Anna said. "Who left it here?"

"Maybe someone forgot it, or lost it, or gave it away," Dad said. "Do you want to try it on?"

Anna and Tom took turns to try on the hat. It was warm and soft and funny. They laughed and smiled.

"Can we keep it?" Anna asked.

"Sure, we can keep it," Dad said. "But we have to share it, okay?"

Anna and Tom agreed. They shared the hat and played in the snow. They made a snowman, a snow angel and a snowball. They had fun in the empty park. They forgot they were sad and bored. They were happy.

Billy was walking in the park one day, when he suddenly saw a rhinoceros in front of him! “Wow!” he cried out in excitement, clapping his hands together. He was about to go closer to take a better look, when he noticed that the rhinoceros looked very unhappy.

“What’s wrong, rhinoceros?” said Billy with concern.

“My skin is all itchy and I can’t wipe it off!” replied the rhinoceros sadly. It had an ugly rash that kept bothering it.

Billy looked around the park, and then he saw a tree with soft leaves. “I have an idea!” he said with a smile. He ran to the tree and carefully picked some of the leaves. Then he walked back to the rhinoceros and showed it what he had taken.

“If you rub these leaves on your skin, you’ll feel so much better!” said Billy. The rhinoceros looked at Billy with gratitude, and did just as Billy said. Soon the itchy feeling was gone and the rhinoceros was happy again.

“Thank you, Billy,” said the grateful rhinoceros. “You’re a real friend!”

Once upon a time, there was a big jungle with lots of animals. One day, a little monkey named Jack was playing in the jungle. Jack liked to play with his friends, but he also liked to explore the jungle by himself.

One day, Jack saw something wild and impressive in the distance. He couldn't quite make out what it was, but he knew he wanted to find out. So, he set off on an adventure to discover what it was.

As Jack got closer, he saw that it was a big and beautiful tiger. The tiger had stripes and was very strong. Jack was scared at first, but he soon realized that the tiger was friendly. From that day on, Jack and the tiger became good friends and had many more adventures together in the wild jungle.

Once upon a time, a little girl named Lily found a tape in her room. She did not know what was on the tape. Lily asked her mom, "Can we play this tape, please?" Her mom said, "Sure, let's see what it is."

They put the tape in the player and pressed play. It was a fun song that made Lily want to dance. The song had a part where it said to repeat the words. Lily liked this part a lot. She sang and danced with the song. It was a mild day, so they opened the window and let the air in.

The next day, Lily went to school. She told her friends about the fun song on the tape. They all wanted to hear it too. Lily knew what to do. She asked her mom to play the tape at her next birthday party. At the party, all her friends danced and sang to the fun song. They all loved the part where they had to repeat the words. Lily was very happy that she found the tape and could share it with her friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little brown cow named Moo. She lived on a farm with her family.

One day, Moo decided she wanted to try playing the horn. She went to the barn and found a shiny brown horn. She tried to play it but it made a very strange noise!

Moo's brother, Jojo, heard her trying to play the horn and came over to see what she was doing.

"Why don't you go ask Farmer Brown to teach you how to play it?" Jojo suggested.

Moo thought it was a great idea, so she went to Farmer Brown's house. When she got there, Farmer Brown showed her how to blow on the horn to make different sounds.

Moo tried her best to play the horn like Farmer Brown, and soon she was making beautiful music!

She was so proud of herself and her brother was very happy for her too. From that day on, Moo never stopped trying to learn new things.

Once upon a time, there was a pig. The pig loved eating meat. Every day, he would search for the best meat he could find.

One day, the pig went to a cool place. It was full of meat! The pig was so excited. He ate as much as he could and gained some weight.

The pig was so happy. He loved the taste of the new meat. Every day he went to the cool place to get more yummy meat.

The pig ate and ate until he was happy and very full. He was now the biggest pig in the village. He was so proud of what he had gained!

The pig was now able to eat lots of meat every day. He would go to the cool place, get some meat and munch away. And that is how the pig gained so much weight!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved animals and had many stuffed animals in her room. One day, her mom came in and said, "Lily, let's organize your stuffed animals. We can put the dogs in one pile and the cats in another pile."

Lily agreed and they began to organize her stuffed animals. As they were working, Lily noticed her favorite stuffed animal, a mule, was missing. She looked around her room and couldn't find it anywhere. "Mommy, where is my mule?" she asked.

Her mom looked around and finally found the mule under the bed. "Here it is, Lily," she said, handing it to her. Lily hugged her mule tightly and said, "I was scared I lost it forever."

Her mom smiled and said, "Don't worry, we found it. Now let's finish organizing your stuffed animals." And they continued to sort the animals into different piles until everything was in its right place.

Once upon a time there was a white label in a dark room. It was very scary there. A brave little boy went into the dark room to find the white label. He was scared but he had to find the label. He looked around and saw a scary old chair. He kept looking and he saw the white label in a corner of the room. He was very happy. He picked up the white label and took it out of the dark room with him. He was no longer scared. The end.

One night, a three year old girl saw that her room was dark. She wanted to see better so she asked her mother, “Can I fill my room with light?”

“Yes, of course,” her mother said. She handed her a candle.

The girl was excited and she smiled. She grabbed the candle and filled it with wax. When it was ready, she touched the little red light on the candle and it was filled with a beautiful light.

But then something happened. The light flickered, and then it went out.

The girl was disappointed. She frowned and tried to light it again. But it wouldn’t light.

Her mother saw this and said, “It’s okay, it happens sometimes. Let’s try to fill the candle with new wax and light it again.”

The girl listened, and soon she was filling the candle with fresh wax. When it was just right, she touched the little red light again and this time it stayed lit, filling her room with a fine light.

The girl was happy and smiled with satisfaction. She knew that with a little help, she could fill the darkness away.

Once upon a time, there was a little brown bear. He loved to play in the forest and climb trees. One day, he found a shiny lock in the grass. He tried to open it, but it was locked tight. The bear wanted to know what was inside, so he decided to mail the lock to his friend, the wise old owl.

The owl received the lock and carefully examined it. He found a keyhole and used his special key to unlock it. Inside was a delicious honeycomb! The owl knew the bear loved honey, so he mailed the honeycomb back to him. The bear was so happy when he received the package in the mail. He opened it and ate all the honey. From that day on, the bear and the owl were the best of friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily loved to play with her toys, especially her teddy bear. One day, Lily's mom mentioned that they would be going to a birthday party for her friend's son. Lily was very eager to go to the party because she loved cake and balloons.

When they arrived at the party, Lily saw that there were lots of presents wrapped in colorful paper. She asked her mom if she could help wrap the presents, but her mom said they were already wrapped. Lily was a little disappointed, but she still had fun playing with the other kids and eating cake.

Later on, Lily overheard her mom talking to her friend about a surprise gift they had for the birthday boy. Lily was curious and asked her mom what the surprise was. Her mom whispered in her ear that it was a big toy truck. Lily was so excited and couldn't wait to see the birthday boy's reaction when he opened his gift.

At the end of the party, Lily and her mom said goodbye to their friends and went home. Lily couldn't stop talking about the party and how much fun she had. She even mentioned the surprise gift they had brought for the birthday boy. Her mom smiled and said that it was nice to make someone else happy. Lily agreed and went to bed with a big smile on her face.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a big sister named Emma. Emma was very pretty and had very nice lips. Lily was jealous of her sister's lips because she wanted lips like that too.

One day, Lily asked her sister, "Emma, how do you get such pretty lips?" Emma replied, "I study how to take care of them." Lily asked, "Can you teach me how to take care of my lips too?" Emma said, "Of course I can. First, you have to put on lip balm every day to keep them soft."

Lily listened carefully and followed her sister's advice. She started to take care of her lips every day. Soon, her lips became soft and pretty too. Emma was happy for her little sister and Lily was no longer jealous of Emma's lips. They both smiled and hugged each other, happy to be sisters.

Once upon a time, Mason and his mommy set out on an adventure. They were going to a nearby town to go to the festival. Mason was so excited to see what the festival would bring!

On the way to the festival, Mason saw plenty of charming things. Fields of wildflowers, a tall mountain, and even a pond with ducks!

Once Mason and his mommy got to the festival, Mason saw even more charming things! Brightly colored tents full of interesting toys, sparkling lights, and a stage with a band playing music.

Mason had so much fun walking around the festival with his mommy. But after a while, it was time to turn and head back home.

Mason asked his mommy, "Will we come back to the festival again soon?"

His mommy smiled and said, "Yes, Mason. We can always turn and come back for the festival again!"

And so, Mason's adventure to the festival came to an end. But he knew it wasn't the last time he would turn and come back to the charming festival!

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Sue. One day Sue’s mommy gave her a spade. The spade was so shiny and new! It was just the right size, fit for Sue.

Sue ran out into the yard with her spade and started playing. She used it to dig a big hole in the ground and then fill it back in. She dug so deep that she found a little bug in the dirt.

Sue liked to joke and she laughed and said, “Hey little bug, are you fit for my spade?” Sue giggled at her joke and the bug just laughed too.

Sue and the bug played together all day in the yard with Sue’s spade. They made little tunnels and moats and even built a little castle. It was so much fun!

At the end of the day, Sue said goodbye to the bug and put her spade away. She had had a really fun day full of laughter and jokes.

It was time to clean. Grandma went into the kitchen and grabbed a cloth. She opened the cabinet, took out a soft brush and started scrubbing. Grandma opened the drawers and wiped inside, then cleaned outside.

Once she was finished, Grandma was happy. Everything was nice and clean. She put the cloth and the brush back into the cabinet and closed it. She smiled, everything was nice and neat.

Grandma was very proud of her work. The kitchen was sparkling, everything was in its place, and it was all nice and soft. Grandma opened the cabinet one more time and took out a treat for being so good at cleaning. She smiled and took a bite.

Once upon a time there was a rabbit and a mouse who were good friends. The rabbit was always very careful and thought before she moved. The mouse, who was very foolish, was always in a hurry and didn't think before he moved.

One day, the rabbit and mouse were walking along and saw a cactus. The mouse saw the cactus and was very excited. He quickly moved and touched it. But, to his surprise, he felt a sharp prick! He screamed in pain.

The rabbit quickly ran to the mouse. The rabbit said, "You're so foolish! Why did you move so fast? You should have thought before you moved. Always use caution when touching something you're not familiar with."

The mouse learned his lesson and was more careful after that. He thought before he moved and never made the same mistake again. Since then, the mouse and the rabbit had a great time exploring their new world. They never forgot the moral of their story: it is important to think before you move.

Once there was a brother who wanted to fly. He was very excited but he was also scared. He had never flown before and it was something new and different.

He asked his big brother to help him. His big brother said he would help him, but he told him they would have to do it in the morning when it was safe.

The little brother was so scared but he was also excited. He got up early in the morning and he and his big brother went outside. He was so scared he was shaking. But then, his big brother held out his arms and said "just jump!"

The little brother jumped, and suddenly he was flying! It was a beautiful morning and he could see all around him. He looked over to his big brother and he was smiling. The little brother flew for a few minutes, feeling joyful and free.

Eventually, he landed back on the ground and he ran up to his big brother. He smiled at him, feeling happy and brave. His big brother had helped him do something amazing, and he would never forget it.

Lily and Ben were friends. They liked to play outside in the sun. They had a big box of toys. They had cars, dolls, balls, and books. They had fun every day.

One day, it was not sunny. It was gray and wet. It started to rain. Lily and Ben were sad. They could not play outside. They looked at the window and saw the rain.

"Rain, rain, go away. Come again another day," they sang.

But the rain did not go away. It rained more and more. Lily and Ben were bored. They did not know what to do.

They looked at the box of toys. They saw a button. It was red and shiny. It was on a string. Lily liked the button. She wanted to play with it.

"Can I have the button?" she asked Ben.

"No, it is mine. I found it first," Ben said.

"But I like it too. It is pretty. Please, can I have it?" Lily said.

"No, you can not. It is mine. Go find another toy," Ben said.

Lily and Ben were angry. They did not want to share. They pulled the button. They pulled hard. The string broke. The button flew away. It hit the window. It made a loud noise.

Lily and Ben were scared. They stopped pulling. They looked at the window. They saw a crack. They saw the rain.

"Oh no, we broke the window. We are in trouble," they said.

They heard a voice. It was Mom. She came into the room. She saw the window. She saw the button. She saw Lily and Ben.

"What happened here?" she asked.

Lily and Ben were sorry. They told Mom what they did. They said they were sorry. They said they would not fight again.

Mom was not happy. She said they had to fix the window. She said they had to pay for it. She said they had to use their allowance. She said they had to be nice to each other.

Lily and Ben nodded. They hugged Mom. They hugged each other. They said they were sorry. They said they were friends.

They looked at the window. They saw the rain. It was still raining. But they did not mind. They had each other. They had the box of toys. They had the button. They decided to share. They decided to be playful. They decided to have fun. They smiled.

Once upon a time there was a helpful musician. He was always trying to make music and help people smile. Every day he would practice his music so that the people in the neighborhood could enjoy it.

One day, he invited some children to his house to make music with him. He wanted to keep everyone happy and help them make their own melodies. He showed them how to make the different sounds, and soon the kids were having lots of fun!

The musician kept playing and the kids kept having a great time. Soon they were all smiling and singing along to the musician’s tunes. They even asked him to play again the next day! The musician was so happy that he kept playing until it was time for the kids to go home.

The musician was very helpful. Thanks to him, the kids could keep on having music and dance parties at his house. He was always playing great music and was a great friend to the kids in the neighborhood.

Lily and Ben were playing with paint in the garden. They had many colors and brushes. They wanted to make a big picture on the wall. They were having fun.

But then they heard a loud noise. It was Dad coming home from work. He was bald and he did not like paint. He always said paint was messy and bad. Lily and Ben panicked. They tried to hide the paint and the brushes. They ran to the other side of the garden.

Dad saw the wall. It was full of paint. There were red and blue and green and yellow spots everywhere. He was very angry. He shouted, "Who did this? Who made this mess?"

Lily and Ben were scared. They did not want to get in trouble. They did not know what to say. They looked at each other.

Then Ben had an idea. He pointed at the cat. The cat was sleeping under a tree. It had some paint on its fur. Ben said, "It was the cat, Dad. The cat did it. The cat likes paint."

Dad looked at the cat. He did not believe Ben. He knew Ben was lying. He said, "Nice try, Ben. But I know it was you and Lily. You have paint on your hands and clothes. And the cat does not have a brush. You are in big trouble, young man. And so are you, Lily. Come here right now."

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to draw and always had a pencil and eraser with her. One day, she was getting ready to draw a picture of her family, but she couldn't find her eraser. She looked everywhere, but it was nowhere to be found.

Later that day, Lily went for a walk with her mom. As they were walking, Lily stumbled over a rock and fell down. Her mom helped her up and they continued walking. Suddenly, Lily saw something shiny on the ground. It was her eraser! She was so happy to have found it.

When they got back home, Lily was ready to draw her family picture. She used her pencil and eraser to draw and fix any mistakes. Her picture turned out great and she was proud to show it to her family. From that day on, she made sure to always keep her eraser close by.

Once upon a time, there was a clever puppy named Max. Max loved to read books and he had a big collection of them. One day, Max's friend Lily came to visit him.

Lily asked, "Max, can we read a book together?"

Max replied, "Sure, let's sort through my books and find a good one."

Max and Lily sat on the floor and sorted through Max's books. They found a book with a picture of a cat on the front page.

Lily said, "This book looks interesting, let's read it!"

Max agreed and they started to read the book. They turned each page carefully and looked at all the pictures. Max was happy to have a friend to read with.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with bubbles. He would blow and blow until the bubbles were as big as his head. One day, Timmy was playing with his bubbles when he fell and scraped his knee.

"Ouch!" cried Timmy. "My knee hurts!"

His mommy came running over and saw his wide scrape. "Don't worry, Timmy," she said. "We'll put a band-aid on it to help it heal."

Timmy watched as his mommy put a band-aid on his knee. "Wow, it feels better!" he said. "Thanks, mommy!"

"You're welcome, Timmy," said his mommy. "Now let's go blow some more bubbles!"

Once upon a time there lived a little girl named Lucy. She loved animals, and one day she saw a little mother bird in her garden. The bird was holding an egg in her beak, and Lucy wanted to help. Carefully, she took the egg from the bird and held it in her hands.

The egg was peaceful and Lucy admired it. All day she watched over it, making sure it was safe. She kept it warm and cozy, under her blanket.

At the end of the day, the little bird came back and Lucy returned the egg to its mother. They said their goodbyes, and Lucy smiled as the bird flew away with her egg.

From that day on Lucy made sure the birds in her garden were safe and peaceful under her watchful eye.

Anna was a lonely girl. She had no friends to play with at school. She only had one toy, a brown bear named Ben. Ben was her best friend. She hugged him every night and told him stories.

One day, Anna saw a new girl in her class. Her name was Lily. Lily had a lot of toys in her backpack. She had dolls, cars, puzzles, and books. Anna wanted to talk to Lily, but she was shy.

At recess, Anna sat on a bench with Ben. She watched Lily play with her toys. Lily looked happy and fun. Anna wished she could join her.

"Hi, I'm Lily. What's your name?" Lily came over to Anna and smiled.

Anna was surprised. She looked at Lily and said, "I'm Anna. This is Ben. He's my bear."

Lily nodded. She looked at Ben and said, "He's cute. Can I play with him?"

Anna hesitated. She loved Ben, but she also wanted to make a friend. She decided to share. She said, "Okay, you can play with him. But be careful. He's very special to me."

Lily smiled. She took Ben and hugged him. She said, "Thank you, Anna. You're very nice. Do you want to play with my toys, too?"

Anna nodded. She felt happy. She said, "Yes, please. I like your toys. They look fun."

Lily and Anna became friends. They played with their toys and talked. They laughed and had fun. Anna was not lonely anymore. She had a new friend and a bear. She was glad she mentioned Ben to Lily.

Once upon a time, there was a small mouse named Sam. He had a deep nose and he liked to explore. One day, Sam decided to explore the nearby forest. He was so excited, but he was also a bit scared.

So, Sam slowly walked forward, trembling with fear. As he walked further into the forest, he heard a loud noise. He then saw a big, deep-voiced bear! Sam was so scared he nearly passed out.

The bear said, "What are you doing here?" Sam shivered and said, "I-I was just exploring." The bear smiled and said, "Well then, why don't we explore together?"

Sam bravely nodded his head and followed the bear deeper into the forest. Sam learned about the trees and animals and smiled the entire time! He was no longer trembling with fear.

When it was time to go home, Sam waved goodbye to his new bear friend and ran back to his home. He took a deep breath and remembered the fun day he just had.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her soft teddy bear and watch the boats with her dad. One day, Lily and her dad went on a boat ride. They saw a big anchor and Lily asked her dad what it was. Her dad said it was used to keep the boat from moving.

As they were sailing, Lily saw a beautiful seashell in the water. She asked her dad if she could jump in and get it. Her dad said no because it was too dangerous. But Lily didn't listen and jumped in anyway. She quickly realized she couldn't swim and started to panic.

Her dad tried to save her, but it was too late. Lily's mom came to the dock and saw what happened. She regretted not being there to stop Lily from jumping in. Everyone was very sad and it was a bad ending to their boat ride.

Once upon a time, there was a mighty lamp. It lit up the night and made everyone happy. Every day more and more people noticed the lamp. They were amazed at its power.

The lamp shone brighter and brighter each day. It increased in size and strength. Soon it was so bright that everyone could see it from far away.

The lamp made the dark go away. Everyone felt happy and safe. The lamp was so mighty that it could protect them.

The people began to celebrate the lamp. They had parties and dances under its light. They celebrated its power and held it in their hearts forever.

The mighty lamp was a symbol of hope and joy. It increased in size and brightness every day until it shone above them all.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with bubbles and soap in the bathtub. One day, she tried to make a big bubble with her hands, but it popped quickly.

Lily wanted to learn how to make a big bubble that wouldn't pop. She asked her mom for help. Her mom showed her how to blow air into the soap to make a big bubble. Lily was so happy that she learned something new!

After bath time, Lily's mom wrapped her up in a flexible towel and gave her a big hug. Lily felt warm and cozy. She smiled and said, "I love learning new things!"

Once upon a time, there was a three year old boy called Tim. He wanted to understand things better. One day, he saw a bright yellow cauliflower in his mum's shopping bag. He couldn't understand what it was and asked his mum.

"Mummy, what is this?" Tim asked.

His mum smiled and said, "That is a cauliflower, sweetheart."

"What does it do?" Tim asked.

His mum laughed and said, "You can eat it, it is very tasty. Here, try a piece."

Tim took a bite, it was crunchy. He didn't understand why it was so crunchy. His mum said, "It's because it is a bit broken."

Tim smiled and understood why it was so crunchy.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She wanted to go on a trip with her mommy and daddy. She asked them, "Can we go on a trip, please?"

Mommy and daddy said, "Yes, we can go on a trip! Where do you want to go, Lily?"

Lily thought for a moment and said, "I choose to go to the pretty park with the flowers and swings!"

Mommy and daddy were happy with her choice. They packed snacks and toys and went on their trip to the park. They played on the swings, smelled the flowers, and had a picnic. It was a very fun trip.

After the trip, Lily said, "That was the best trip ever! Can we go on another trip soon?"

Mommy and daddy smiled and said, "Of course, we can go on another trip soon. We love going on trips with you, Lily."

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She was going to a party. Lily was very excited. She put on her pretty dress and her shiny shoes.

At the party, Lily saw a lot of yummy food. There were fruits, veggies, and other healthy snacks. Her mommy explained to her that eating healthy food helps her grow big and strong.

Lily had so much fun at the party. She danced, she played, and she ate the healthy food. She was very happy. And when the party was over, Lily went home and told her daddy all about the fun she had.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Sam. Sam loved playing with balloons. He had a red balloon, a blue balloon, and a green balloon. One day, Sam's little sister came to play with him. She had a terrible cough and was feeling sick.

Sam wanted to help his sister feel better, so he decided to sort his balloons. He put all the red balloons together, all the blue balloons together, and all the green balloons together. Then, he gave his sister the green balloon because it was her favorite color. She smiled and started to feel a little better.

From that day on, Sam always sorted his balloons when he wanted to make someone feel happy. He knew that a little kindness could make a big difference.

Tom and Lily were playing in the park. It was a sunny day and they had fun on the swings and the slide. Tom had a pair of sunglasses that he liked very much. He wore them all the time and felt very cool.

Lily wanted to try the sunglasses too. She asked Tom, "Can I use your sunglasses, please? They look nice."

Tom said, "No, they are mine. You can't use them. Go away."

Lily felt sad and angry. She thought Tom was not a nice friend. She said, "You are mean. I don't want to play with you anymore."

She ran away to find another friend. Tom felt lonely and sorry. He realized he was not very kind to Lily. He wanted to say sorry and share his sunglasses with her.

He looked for Lily in the park. He saw her playing with a boy who had a ball. He ran to her and said, "Lily, I'm sorry. I was wrong. You can use my sunglasses if you want. Can we be friends again?"

Lily smiled and said, "Thank you, Tom. That's very nice of you. Yes, we can be friends again."

They hugged and tried the sunglasses. They looked funny and laughed. They played with the ball and had fun. They learned to share and be kind.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who had a friendly dog named Max. One day, Lily's mom told her to clean her closet. Lily didn't want to do it, but her mom said she would receive a surprise if she did. So, Lily started to clean her closet, and Max helped her by bringing her toys to put away.

After a while, Lily found a toy she had lost a long time ago. She was happy and showed it to Max. Max barked happily, and Lily said, "I received a surprise!" Her mom came in and said, "See, I told you that you would receive a surprise if you cleaned your closet. Now you know it's good to keep things organized."

Lily learned that it's important to keep her things neat and tidy, and Max learned that helping friends is fun. From that day on, Lily and Max always kept their things in order and helped each other.

Once upon a time there was a very kind girl. Her name was Lise. She liked to play outside. One day she went to the park. She saw a slide there. It was so much fun! She kept sliding down, over and over again.

When it was time to go home, she saw a big bag of laundry. She thought it may be from her mom. Lise thought the laundry was too heavy. She was kind and wanted to help bring it home.

Lise knew the best thing to do. She put the bag of laundry at the top of the slide. Then, she sat next to it and held it tight. When she was ready, she said, "Weeee!" and off she went, sliding and bringing the laundry home.

When she reached the bottom of the slide, she was so proud of herself! Lise carried the laundry into the house and saw her mom. "Mom, I helped bring the laundry home," she said. Her Mom smiled, thanked her and gave her a hug.

The end.

Anna and Ben like to play with blocks. They build towers and bridges and castles. Sometimes they measure how tall their towers are. They use a ruler or a book or a stick. They want to see who can make the tallest tower.

One day, they find a big box of blocks in the attic. They are very happy. They take the blocks to the living room and start to build. Anna makes a tower with red and blue blocks. Ben makes a bridge with green and yellow blocks. They measure their blocks with a ruler. Anna's tower is 20 centimeters tall. Ben's bridge is 15 centimeters long.
