They keep building and measuring. They use more and more blocks. They make their tower and bridge bigger and bigger. They measure their blocks with a book. Anna's tower is 40 centimeters tall. Ben's bridge is 35 centimeters long.

They want to make their tower and bridge even bigger. They look for more blocks. They see a pass in the wall. It is a small door that leads to another room. They open the pass and go inside. They find more blocks. They are very happy. They take the blocks to the living room and keep building and measuring.

They use all the blocks they can find. They make their tower and bridge very big. They measure their blocks with a stick. Anna's tower is 80 centimeters tall. Ben's bridge is 75 centimeters long. They are very proud of their work.

But then, they hear a loud noise. It is their mom. She is coming home from work. She sees the mess in the living room. She sees the blocks everywhere. She sees the pass open. She is very angry. She has a harsh voice. She says, "What have you done? You made a big mess. You took the blocks from the attic. You opened the pass. You are not allowed to do that. You have to clean up now. And no more blocks for a week."

Anna and Ben are very sad. They cry. They say, "We are sorry, mom. We just wanted to play. We just wanted to measure our blocks. We didn't know we were not allowed to do that. Please don't be mad at us. Please let us keep our blocks."

Mom sighs. She sees their sad faces. She sees their big tower and bridge. She knows they worked hard. She knows they had fun. She softens her voice. She says, "I understand, Anna and Ben. You are very creative and clever. You made amazing things with your blocks. But you have to follow the rules. You have to ask before you take things. You have to close the pass. You have to clean up after you play. Do you understand?"

Anna and Ben nod. They say, "We understand, mom. We are sorry. We will follow the rules. We will clean up. We will close the pass. We will ask before we take things. Can we keep our blocks?"

Mom smiles. She says, "Yes, you can keep your blocks. But only after you clean up. And only if you promise to be careful and respectful. And only if you give me a hug and a kiss."

Anna and Ben hug and kiss their mom. They say, "We promise, mom. We love you, mom. Thank you, mom."

They clean up their mess. They put the blocks back in the box. They close the pass. They keep their tower and bridge in a corner. They are happy. They learned a lesson. They still like to play with blocks. They still like to measure their blocks. But they also like to follow the rules. And they love their mom.

Once upon a time, in a small house, there lived a little girl named Lily and her mom. They loved to cook together. One day, they decided to make some yummy sauce for their dinner.

As they mixed the sauce, Lily's mom asked her to wave the spoon to help mix it better. Lily waved the spoon, but the sauce splashed everywhere! Lily's mom looked at the mess and said, "Oh no, the sauce is all over the floor!"

Lily felt very sorry for making the mess. She said, "I'm sorry, Mom. I didn't mean to make a mess." Her mom smiled and said, "It's okay, Lily. We can clean it up together."

So, Lily and her mom cleaned up the sauce and finished making their dinner. They had a great time cooking and learned to be more careful next time. And they all lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a lazy cat. The cat liked to sleep all day by the window. One day, a bird flew by and saw the cat sleeping. The bird said, "Hello, lazy cat! Why do you sleep all day?"

The cat opened one eye and said, "I like to rest by the window. It's nice and warm."

The bird replied, "But there's so much to do outside! You should come with me and sign up for singing lessons."

The cat thought for a moment and said, "Okay, I'll come with you. Maybe I'll learn something new."

So, the cat got up from the window and followed the bird outside. They signed up for singing lessons and had a lot of fun. The cat learned to sing and the bird made a new friend. From that day on, the cat wasn't lazy anymore and enjoyed doing new things.

One day, Therese was very bored. She was just three years old, but she already had a telephone. She decided to call her Grandma to see if she wanted to come and play.

When Grandma answered the telephone, she and Therese had a plan. They would both go to the park. There was a big tree there and they could play underneath it.

At the park, Therese found a big log. She wanted to climb it, but it was too hard. But then Grandma showed her how to be flexible. She showed Therese how to twist her body to fit over the log. Then, Therese could easily climb it.

When Therese made it to the top, she was so happy. She shouted, "Look at me! I did it!" Grandma clapped and cheered.

Before they left the park, they took a picture. Grandma snapped the picture with her phone and Theyse smiled big.

That day was so much fun. Now, whenever Therese gets bored, she looks at the picture of her and Grandma at the park and remembers how flexible she can be.

Once upon a time, there was a pink bunny. The bunny loved to go to the store. She would hop all the way there. At the store, she would buy carrots and lettuce to eat.

One day, the bunny saw a toy she really wanted. She asked her mommy to buy it for her. But mommy said no. The bunny was sad and wanted to quit.

But then she remembered how much she loved going to the store. So, she decided to save her money and buy the toy herself. Every day, the bunny would put some money in her piggy bank. Finally, she had enough money to buy the toy. She was so happy and proud of herself for not quitting. From then on, she knew she could do anything she set her mind to.

Once upon a time, a boy named Timmy woke up early in the morning. The sun was shining bright and the light came into his room. He stood up from his bed and went to the window. Timmy saw the birds flying in the sky and the trees standing tall. He felt happy and excited to start the day.

Timmy went to the kitchen and had his breakfast. He ate his pancakes and drank his juice. After that, he went to play outside. It was noon and the sun was still shining bright. Timmy played with his ball and ran around in the park. He saw his friends and they played together.

When Timmy got tired, he sat down on the grass. He looked up at the sky and saw the clouds moving slowly. He felt relaxed and happy. Timmy loved to be outside and enjoy the light and the nature around him.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Jacky. Jacky loved fairies and dreamed of becoming one.

One day, Jacky saw many fairies flying across the sky. She wanted one for her very own.

The fairies noticed Jacky and told her that one of them could come live with her. She just had to choose one.

The fairies were all so adorable! There was one with pink wings, one with purple wings, and another with sparkly silver wings.

Jacky chose the fairy with pink wings. The fairy smiled at Jacky and flew into her hand.

Jacky was so happy with her new friend! From then on, Jacky and her fairy did everything together.

The end.

Once there was a girl who had a very special purse. She never went anywhere without it. It was a bright pink color, and it always made her feel special and happy.

One day, she decided to take her purse to a special place. She took it to a garden, where the flowers were blooming. She spread out a blanket, and watched the beautiful flowers in full bloom.

The girl was so happy! She opened up her purse and put some of the flower petals inside. She zipped her purse tight to keep them safe.

The girl held her purse tightly and dreamed of the beautiful garden she had seen. She knew that she would always keep the memory of this special place in her purse.

Once upon a time, there was a gentle cat named Tom. Tom loved to poke things with his soft paw. One day, he found a book with a poem inside.

Tom poked the book and it opened. He saw the pretty words and wanted to read them. He called his friend, a bird named Sue, to help him. Sue could read the poem out loud.

Sue said, "I will read the poem for you, Tom." She read the poem with her sweet voice. Tom listened and smiled. They both loved the poem and were very happy. They spent the day sharing the poem with all their friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Mia. One day Mia went to the post office. She wanted to send a card to her grandmother. Mia chose a beautiful card with a picture of a butterfly. She was excited to mail it!

When Mia got to the post office, the postmaster said, “Oh no! We are all out of stamps!” Mia thought for a moment, and then she said, “That’s okay. I’ll just wait.” She paused and watched while the postmaster found some stamps.

Once the stamps were ready, Mia put them on her card. Then she handed the card to the postmaster with a big smile. But the postmaster had bad news. He said, “I’m sorry, Mia, but your card is too heavy. You need more stamps.” Mia felt sad.

Mia paused and thought really hard. She had saved up her pocket money and had enough money to buy the extra stamps. She quickly bought the stamps and put them on the card. The postmaster cheered! Mia was very happy. She said, “Thanks! I’m sorry I didn’t have enough money at first. ” The postmaster smiled and said, “That’s okay Mia, I’m just glad you were able to send your card!”

Lily and Ben were playing with blocks in the living room. They liked to build towers and houses and bridges with the blocks. They had many blocks of different colors and shapes.

"Look, I made a big tower!" Lily said, showing Ben her creation. "It is very tall and strong. How do you like it?"

"It is nice, but I can make a better one," Ben said. He started to take some blocks from Lily's tower and add them to his own. "See, my tower is taller and stronger now. You have a poor tower."

Lily was sad and angry. She did not like that Ben took her blocks without asking. She wanted to have her tower back. She tried to pull some blocks from Ben's tower, but he pushed her away.

"Stop it! These are my blocks now. You have enough blocks. Go away!" Ben shouted.

Lily and Ben started to fight over the blocks. They pulled and pushed and yelled at each other. They did not notice that their towers were falling down. The blocks crashed on the floor and rolled under the sofa and the table. Some blocks even went into the drain of the sink.

"Oh no! Our blocks!" Lily and Ben cried. They stopped fighting and looked at the mess. They had lost many blocks and their towers were gone. They felt sorry and ashamed.

"I'm sorry, Lily. I was mean to you. I should not have taken your blocks. Can we be friends again?" Ben said.

"I'm sorry, too, Ben. I should not have fought with you. You are my friend. Can we share the blocks?" Lily said.

They hugged and smiled. They decided to work together and build a new tower with the blocks they had left. They learned that sharing is better than fighting and that friends are more important than blocks.

Once upon a time, there was a little dove. The dove was sad because it was wet from the rain. It felt very uncomfortable.

The dove saw a big tree. It flew to the tree to get dry. Under the tree, the dove met a kind friend, a small cat. The cat was also wet and uncomfortable.

Together, they sat under the tree. The sun came out and dried them both. They were happy and warm. The dove and the cat became best friends. They played together all day long, and they were never uncomfortable again.

Tim and Sam are brothers. They like to play with their toys. One day, they find a big box in the garage. It has many screws and tools inside.

"Wow, look at this!" Tim says. "We can make something cool with these screws and tools!"

"Let's do it!" Sam says. They take out the screws and tools and start to build. They use a hammer, a saw, a drill and a wrench. They make a lot of noise.

"Boys, what are you doing?" Mom asks. She comes to the garage and sees the mess. She sees screws and wood and metal everywhere. She sees Tim and Sam with their tools. She is not happy.

"Stop that right now!" Mom says. "You are making too much noise and you are making a big mess! You could hurt yourself with those tools! Put them back in the box and come inside!"

"But Mom, we are making something cool!" Tim says.

"We are making a robot!" Sam says.

"I don't care what you are making!" Mom says. "You are not allowed to play with those tools! They are not toys! They are for Dad to fix things!"

Tim and Sam are sad. They put the tools and screws back in the box. They follow Mom to the house. They go to their room.

"Mom is mean!" Tim says.

"Yeah, she is!" Sam says. "She doesn't let us have fun!"

They sit on their bed and look at their toys. They see a blue car, a red truck, a yellow plane and a green train. They are bored.

"Hey, I have an idea!" Tim says. "Let's play with our toys!"

"OK!" Sam says. They take out their toys and start to play. They make vroom and beep and zoom sounds. They have fun.

"Boys, are you OK?" Mom asks. She comes to their room and sees them playing. She sees their toys and their smiles. She is happy.

"Yes, Mom, we are OK!" Tim says.

"We are playing with our toys!" Sam says.

"That's good!" Mom says. "I'm sorry I yelled at you before. I was just worried about you. Those tools are dangerous. You have to be careful."

"We know, Mom. We are sorry too." Tim and Sam say.

Mom hugs them and kisses them. She says, "I love you, boys. You are very smart and creative. But sometimes you have to relax and play with your toys. They are safer and more fun."

Tim and Sam nod and hug Mom. They say, "We love you too, Mom. You are very nice and caring. And you are right. We have to relax and play with our toys. They are safer and more fun."

Sam loved to tour his neighborhood with his mom. He always noticed something new each time. He especially liked to visit the big park with the tall slides and the huge playground.

One day, Sam and his mom went to the park and something embarrassing happened. As Sam was sliding down the really tall slide, his shorts got caught! He got stuck and started to cry. His mom quickly went over to help.

"Don't worry Sam," said his mom, "I can help you down the slide."

"But I'm embarrassed,"said Sam.

His mom hugged him and said, "I love you no matter what, and even when things get a little embarrassing!"

So, with his mom's help, Sam slid down and all was well. He and his mom laughed together and the rest of their tour was amazing.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved animals and playing outside. One day, she went to the park and saw a big, brown horse. The horse looked very kind and mild. Lily wanted to pet the horse, but she was a little scared.

Suddenly, a man came over and said, "Don't be afraid, he's a friendly horse. Would you like to ride him?" Lily was so excited and told the man, "Yes please!" The man helped her onto the horse's back and she held on tight.

As they rode around the park, Lily talked to the horse and told him all about her day. The horse listened and even seemed to nod his head in agreement. When the ride was over, Lily thanked the man and the horse for a fun adventure. From that day on, whenever Lily went to the park, she always looked for her horse friend.

One day, Mummy took her little three year old daughter, Sophia, to the office. Sophia couldn't believe how impressive the office was; it had lots of shiny tables and knew gadgets everywhere. She heard people talking in the background and wondered what they could be doing.

"Why are we here, Mummy?" Sophia asked, looking around.

Mummy looked at her seriously. "I have to do some work, sweetheart," she said. "I need to be here, and I need you to mind me and stay close. Can you do that?"

Sophia nodded. She wanted to help her Mummy and make her proud. She watched quietly as Mummy worked, and soon, Sophia started to get bored.

"Mummy, can I do something too?" she asked, hopefully.

Mummy smiled and said, "Of course you can. Why don't you get some paper and pencils and draw a picture? That will be very helpful."

Sophia happily agreed, and she found some paper and pencils. She drew a colorful picture of the office, with some of the impressive furniture and gadgets. When she was finished, she proudly showed it to Mummy.

Mummy clapped her hands in delight. "That's wonderful, Sophia!" she said. "You are so helpful, and I'm so proud of you!"

Sophia smiled and went back

Anna liked to look at tiny things with her microscope. She had a book with pictures of bugs and flowers and other things that were too small to see. She would put a slide under the microscope and turn the knob to make it bigger and clearer.

One day, her brother Tom came into her room and saw her microscope. He wanted to play with it too. He grabbed the book and the slides and said, "I want to look at these. You can't have them. They are mine now."

Anna was angry. She said, "No, they are not. They are mine. You are being bossy and mean. Give them back to me."

Tom said, "No, I won't. I am older and smarter than you. I can do what I want. You can't tell me what to do."

They started to fight and pull and push each other. They knocked over the microscope and it fell on the floor. It broke into pieces and made a loud noise.

Their mom heard the noise and came into the room. She saw the broken microscope and the mess. She was very upset. She said, "What did you do? How could you be so careless and rude? You have to share and be nice to each other. You are both in trouble now."

Anna liked to play with her dolls in her room. She had many dolls, but her favorite was Lily. Lily had long hair, a pink dress and a smile. Anna liked to brush Lily's hair and make her talk.

One day, Anna wanted to play with Lily on her bed. She put Lily on the pillow and climbed up. But she was not careful and she fell off the bed. She hit her head on the wall and it hurt. She started to cry.

Mama heard Anna cry and ran to her room. She saw Anna on the floor and Lily on the bed. She picked up Anna and hugged her. She said, "Don't cry, Anna. You are OK. You just have a bump on your head. It will go away soon."

Anna stopped crying and looked at Mama. She said, "Mama, I'm sorry. I was not careful. I wanted to play with Lily on the bed, but I fell off and hit the wall. I was scared."

Mama smiled and said, "It's OK, Anna. I'm not mad at you. You just have to be more careful next time. You don't want to gain more bumps on your head, do you?"

Anna shook her head and said, "No, Mama. I don't want to gain more bumps. I want to play with Lily."

Mama said, "OK, Anna. You can play with Lily, but on the floor, not on the bed. And be gentle with her. She is your friend."

Anna nodded and said, "OK, Mama. Thank you. I love you."

Mama said, "I love you too, Anna. Have fun with Lily."

Mama put Anna on the floor and gave her Lily. Anna hugged Lily and said, "I'm sorry, Lily. I didn't mean to leave you on the bed. You are my best friend."

Lily smiled and said, "I'm not scared, Anna. I know you love me. You are my best friend too."

Anna and Lily played happily on the floor. They forgot about the wall and the bump. They were not scared anymore. They were happy.

Tom and Sue like to jog in the park. They jog fast and slow, up and down, and round and round. They have fun and feel good.

One day, they see a big house in the park. It is dark and old and scary. They hear a noise from inside. It sounds like a laugh. A mean laugh.

"Who lives there?" Tom asks.

"I don't know. Maybe a witch," Sue says.

"A witch? What is a witch?" Tom says.

"A witch is a bad lady who does magic. She can turn you into a frog or a mouse or a bug. She likes to eat children. She is very hungry and very angry," Sue says.

Tom and Sue are afraid. They want to run away. But they are curious too. They want to see the witch.

They go closer to the house. They peek through a window. They see a big pot on a fire. They smell something tasty. They see a cake on a table. It has icing and sprinkles and candles.

"Wow, look at that cake. It looks yummy," Tom says.

"Maybe the witch is not so bad. Maybe she likes to bake. Maybe she will share the cake with us," Sue says.

They knock on the door. The door opens. They see a lady. She has a long nose and a pointy hat and a black dress. She smiles. But not a nice smile. A wicked smile.

"Hello, children. I'm so glad you came. I've been waiting for you. Come in, come in. I have a surprise for you," she says.

Tom and Sue are not sure. They think maybe they should go. But they are hungry too. They want a bite of the cake.

They go inside. The lady closes the door. She locks it. She laughs. A loud laugh. A mean laugh.

Tom and Sue are in trouble. They made a mistake. They should have run away. They should have listened to Sue. The lady is a witch. And the cake is a trap.

Once upon a time, a little girl named Lily went for a walk in the park. She was wearing her favorite bracelet that her mommy gave her. As she was walking, she saw a boy crying on the bench.

"Are you okay?" Lily asked the boy.

The boy shook his head and said, "I lost my bracelet. It's unknown where it went."

Lily knew how much the bracelet meant to the boy, so she decided to help him find it. They looked all around the park, but they couldn't find it. Suddenly, the boy shouted, "I found it!" and held up the bracelet.

"Yay!" Lily cheered. "I'm so happy we found it!"

The boy smiled and said, "Thank you for helping me. You're a good friend."

From that day on, Lily and the boy became good friends and they always looked out for each other.

Once upon a time there was an old man. He had a strong steel box. It was very big.

Every day the old man went to his box and opened it. Inside there was a small weak chicken. The old man took care of the chicken. He fed it each day and talked to it softly. The chicken was so happy to have a friend.

One day, the old man could not open the box. It was locked tight. He tried many things but he could not get it open. He was sad and the chicken was too.

Suddenly, a strong young man appeared. He said he could open the box. He used his special tools to get the box open. The old man was so glad! He fed the chicken and went back home.

The old man was happy for the chicken. He was so thankful for the young man who helped him to feed the chicken. They all lived happily ever after.

Sara liked to organize her toys. She had a big box where she put all her dolls, cars, blocks and books. She liked to make them neat and tidy. Sometimes she played with them, but sometimes she just liked to look at them.

One day, her friend Lily came over to play. Lily saw Sara's box and wanted to see what was inside. She opened the lid and started to take out the toys. She threw them on the floor and made a big mess.

"Stop!" Sara cried. "You are ruining my toys! They are delicate and you are breaking them!"

Lily did not listen. She grabbed a doll and pulled its hair. She took a car and smashed it against a block. She tore a page from a book.

Sara was very angry and sad. She ran to her mom and told her what Lily was doing. Her mom came to the room and saw the mess. She scolded Lily and told her to apologize to Sara. She also told her to help Sara organize her toys again.

Lily felt sorry for what she did. She said she was sorry to Sara and her mom. She helped Sara pick up the toys and put them back in the box. She was careful not to hurt them. She saw a palm toy that looked like a hand. She gave it to Sara and said it was a gift.

Sara smiled and thanked Lily. She said she forgave her and they could still be friends. She gave Lily a hug and they played with the palm toy. They pretended it was a puppet and made funny voices. They laughed and had fun. Sara's mom was happy to see them get along. She gave them some cookies and milk and praised them for being good.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to run and play outside in the warm sunshine. One day, Lily's mommy told her that they were going to get a special massage. Lily didn't understand what that meant, but she was excited to try something new.

When they arrived at the massage place, Lily saw a big, comfy chair and lots of soft pillows. Her mommy explained that a massage is when someone uses their hands to make your muscles feel good. Lily was a little nervous at first, but as soon as the massage started, she felt so relaxed and happy.

After the massage was over, Lily's mommy told her that they would come back again soon. Lily understood now why massages are so nice and warm, and she couldn't wait to go back for another one.

Once upon a time, there was a brave little bird named Pip. Pip lived in a big tree with his family. One day, Pip saw a big crane walking near the tree. Pip knew that the crane liked to eat little birds like him. So, Pip told his family to be careful.

The next day, Pip saw the crane again. This time, the crane had a big bucket in its beak. Pip wondered what was in the bucket. He thought it might be water. The crane walked over to the tree and started to pour the water on the roots. Pip realized that the crane was helping the tree grow.

Pip was happy that the crane was not there to eat him. He thanked the crane for helping the tree. From that day on, Pip and the crane became friends. Pip learned that sometimes things are not always what they seem.

Once there was a yellow bird. He was so happy in the sky and he loved to fly around. But one day he saw something new. Smoke was coming from the ground. He flew closer and saw some people around a campfire. He flew around them, enjoying his yellow wings in the sky.

Then suddenly, the bird heard a loud noise. It was so sudden that he had to stop in the sky. He looked down and saw that the people were shooting their guns up in the sky. So, the bird quickly flew away.

He kept flying away, but the smoke kept following him. He kept going and going until he could not see the smoke anymore. He flew so high in the sky, until he felt free and happy again. The bird was so relieved that he had stopped the smoke from following him.

One day, a little girl went to the park with her dog. She was feeling calm and wanted to explore. She spotted an apple tree and noticed there was an apple on a branch that was just out of reach. The girl made the brave decision to try and twist the branch and get the apple. She pulled and pulled, but no matter how hard she tried it wouldn't twist. The girl was starting to get frustrated and was not sure what to do. Just then her dog jumped up and it was able to twist the branch! With one big tug, the branch moved and the apple fell right down into the little girl's hands. She was so excited! The little girl and her dog shared the apple and were so happy that they were able to get the delicious treat.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim wanted to play with a sword, but he did not have one. He looked around for something to use as a sword. He found a long stick that was available. Tim was very happy.

Tim asked his dad to help him make the stick look like a real sword. His dad said, "We can attach a handle to the stick, so it will be easier for you to hold." Tim liked the idea. They found some tape and used it to attach a small piece of wood to the stick. Now, Tim had a sword!

Tim played with his sword all day. He pretended to be a brave knight, fighting dragons and saving people. His mom and dad watched him play and smiled. They were proud of their little knight.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play outside in the sun. One day, Timmy saw a lovely cactus in his backyard. He wanted to touch it, but his mom said no because it was prickly and could hurt him.

But Timmy didn't listen to his mom. He went outside when she wasn't looking and touched the cactus. It was prickly, but he thought it was fun. However, the next day, Timmy's finger started to hurt and turn red. His mom took him to the doctor and they found out that the cactus had spoiled and had something harmful on it.

Timmy had to go to the hospital and get a shot to make him better. He learned that he should always listen to his mom and not touch things that could hurt him.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Jack. One day, Jack went to the park, which was filled with his favorite thing to do--swing. He hopped off the swing and noticed some mud, which he thought looked really fun.

"Can I jump in the mud?" Jack asked his mom.

Mom shook her head. "No, Jack. That might be too messy," she said.

Jack frowned. He really wanted to swing in the mud. But he followed his mom anyway and left the park.

That night, Jack couldn't control his curiosity. He told his mom he was going back to the park, so she gave him a hug and said, "Be careful, Jack".

Jack ran back to the park. When he arrived, he spotted the mud and smiled. He opened the gate and saw that it was just as fun as he had thought. The mud was easy to move in and soon he was swinging around with ease.

Suddenly, it started to rain. Jack saw the rain and realized he was going to get very messy. He started to cry, but then he remembered his mom's warning. He quickly ran back home and managed to make it just before the rain started coming down.

The next day, Jack put on his muddy clothes and showed his mom. She shook her head and said, "I told you it was too messy, Jack!".

Jack smiled

Once upon a time there was a nice boy called Sam. He was very honest and loved to follow the things around him.

One day, Sam was walking around when he saw a strip of yellow. He started to wonder where it came from and why it was so long and thin.

He decided to follow the strip and see where it went. He walked around for a while and then he saw a very big tree. He followed the strip around the tree and it went all the way to the top!

When he got to the top, he saw a very big surprise. There was a big nest with four little baby birds inside. They were all chirping and happy.

Sam was so excited to see the baby birds and he was very honest with them. He said he would follow them wherever they wanted to go.

So the little birds flew away and Sam followed them. They flew around the park and then back to their nest. They were very happy to be home again.

So Sam followed the strip all the way home. He knew that being honest was the right thing to do.

Once there was a man. He wanted to go for a ride, so he secured a permit. The permit gave him permission to use a cart. So he got a cart and he set off. But the road was icy. The icy road made it very difficult to control the cart. The man kept slipping and sliding on the ice. He pushed the cart carefully. After a long struggle, he finally made it to his destination.

One day, Jane and her daddy were at the park. Jane saw something very special - a big green tree with green powder around it. Jane walked closer to the tree and saw that the powder was made of tiny green pieces.

"What is that Daddy?" Jane asked.

"That's special powder, Jane," her daddy replied. "Let's gather some of it together and take it home with us."

So Jane and her daddy started gathering the powder into a bucket. They filled the bucket up with the powder and started walking home.

When they got home, Daddy asked Jane what she wanted to do with the green powder.

"Let's make a special cake with it," she said.

So, Jane and her daddy used the green powder to make a special cake. They cut it up and shared it between them. Jane smiled, as it was the yummiest cake she had ever tasted.

The end.

Once there was a little boy named Timmy. He was 3 years old and very curious. He wanted to understand the world around him.

One day Timmy was looking at an old mural his Grandma had created. It had lots of symbols painted on it. One of the symbols was a big blue circle.

Timmy asked his Grandma, "What does this symbol mean?" She explained to him that this symbol was the symbol of understanding. It meant that if you understand something, it will be easier to learn.

Timmy felt happy to know what this blue symbol meant. He was now one step closer to understanding the world around him.

Once upon a time there was a famous film about a little girl. Everyone loved it so much! But the girl was always complaining about the film. She said it didn't give her enough time in the spotlight.

One day, the girl decided to make her own film. This time it would be all about her! She spent days making the film and when it was done, she invited all her friends to watch it. Everyone loved it!

But soon an even more famous film came out and became the new favorite. The girl was so upset and started to complain even more. She wished people would love her film as much as they loved the other one.

But her complaining went too far. One day a huge storm came and destroyed all of the girl's film. They were all washed away, never to be seen again.

The little girl was so sad. No matter how much she complained, nobody would ever watch her film again.

Once upon a time there was a yellow caterpillar. He was very small and liked to crawl around the garden. One day he was taken by the wind to a big house with a white garden.

The caterpillar was so excited! He crawled around the garden, looking to explore and see what was around. Suddenly a voice said, "Welcome to my garden!" He saw an old man standing there, smiling.

The caterpillar replied, "Hello! I'm so glad to be here!" The old man's smile got bigger, and he said, "Come with me inside the house!"

The caterpillar was so happy, but when he followed the old man into the house, he suddenly felt scared. The man put the caterpillar into a jar and put it on the window sill with a tight lid.

The caterpillar tried to get out but he couldn't. He was so scared he cried and screamed, but no one could hear him. Eventually he stopped and resigned himself to his horrible fate.

The End.

Tom and Mia were best friends. They liked to play in the park every day. They liked to swing, slide and run. But their favorite thing was to climb the pole. The pole was tall and shiny. It was fun to go up and down.

One day, Tom and Mia went to the park as usual. They ran to the pole and started to climb. Tom was faster than Mia. He reached the top of the pole and shouted, "Look at me! I am the king of the pole!"

Mia was still halfway up the pole. She wanted to reach the top too. But she felt scared. The pole was very high and she could not see the ground. She started to cry. "Tom, help me! I want to go down!"

Tom heard Mia cry. He looked down and saw her. He felt sorry for her. He was her best friend. He said, "Don't worry, Mia. I will help you. Stay where you are. I will come down and hold your hand."

Tom climbed down the pole carefully. He reached Mia and held her hand. He said, "It's okay, Mia. You are brave. We will go down together. I will not let go of your hand. I am dependable."

Mia felt better. She trusted Tom. She said, "Thank you, Tom. You are a good friend. You are dependable."

Tom and Mia climbed down the pole slowly. They reached the ground and hugged. They were happy. They learned that friends should help each other and be dependable. They decided to play something else. They did not want to climb the pole again. They had enough of the pole.

Once upon a time there was a little girl who tried to build something very tall with blocks. She had lots of blue and red blocks, but she just could not make it higher. She was sad.

Then she saw an angel who was very kind. The angel said: "Let me help you. If you trust me, I can build something very tall and deep."

The little girl trusted the angel, and so the angel began to build. He made a tall tower with the blocks, and it was so high it went up to the sky. It was very deep and beautiful too.

The little girl was very happy, and she thanked the angel with a big hug. The angel smiled and flew away.

From then on, the little girl knew that when she was sad, she could trust her friends to help her.

Once there was a man named Joe who liked to swim. Every week he got in the water and swam. He enjoyed the feeling of the cold water against his skin on those hot summer days.

One day he decided to swim further out than usual. The water was rough and it took him a while to make it to the other side. Joe was out of breath when he reached the shore.

He looked around, but he couldn't recognize the place. Joe felt scared and confused. He shouted for help, but no one answered.

Joe started to panic. He looked around and saw a shark coming closer and closer towards him. Fearing for his life, Joe quickly jumped back in the water and tried to swim away.

Unfortunately, the shark was too fast. Joe didn't make it back to shore and was eaten. Joe was never seen again.

Sam was a bald man. Every day he would put on his special jacket. The jacket was very important to Sam. It had lots of pockets, and in them was all the things he needed to record the day. He had a very special recording device that would help him remember everything he had seen and done during the day.

Sam liked to take walks and look at the things around him. He would record the colors of the trees, the shapes of the clouds, the sound of the birds, and all sorts of other things. He was very curious and enjoyed recording the world.

Today, he went to the park to record things he hadn't seen before. He recorded the colors of the flowers, the speed of a squirrel running across the grass, and the sound of children playing.

At the end of the day, Sam took off his special jacket and carefully put away his recording device. He smiled, happy to remember the things he had seen and heard. From now on, he would keep the recording in his memory and enjoy the world around him.

Once upon a time, a little girl named Lydia lived in a big yellow house. One day, a big scary earthquake shook the ground and Lydia was afraid. She started to cry and ran to her mom, who was very kind and comforting.

Her mom gently held her and spoke soft words. "Don't be scared," her mom said. "Earthquakes are just nature, and nothing can hurt us."

Lydia felt better and was glad, but she would never forget the fear of the earthquake. After, Lydia's mom told her an important lesson. "Anytime you are scared or uncomfortable," her mom said, "just remember that everything will be okay. That comforting thought will help you through anything."

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a large barrel in a small town. The people in the town loved the barrel because it was always full of yummy food. One day, a little boy named Tim went to the barrel to get some food.

But when Tim got to the barrel, it was empty! He was very sad and said, "Oh no! What will we do now?" Tim's friend, Lily, heard him and came over. She said, "Don't worry, Tim. We can pray for more food to fill the barrel."

So, Tim and Lily held hands and prayed together. They asked for the barrel to be full of food again. Suddenly, the barrel was full of food! They were so happy and told everyone in the town. From that day on, the people in the town always prayed when they needed help. And they all lived happily ever after.

Tom and Sam were brothers. They liked to play with their toys. But they did not like to share. They always fought over who got the best toy.

One day, they found a big red truck in the yard. It was shiny and had four wheels. They both wanted to play with it. They ran to the truck and grabbed it.

"Mine!" Tom shouted.

"No, mine!" Sam shouted.

They pulled and pushed and yelled. The truck broke in two. They both cried.

A man came to the yard. He was their dad. He was mighty. He could fix anything. He saw the broken truck and the sad boys.

"What happened here?" he asked.

"We wanted the truck, but we did not share. Now it is broken," Tom said.

"We are sorry, dad," Sam said.

Dad shook his head. He took the truck and went to his workshop. He came back with a new truck. It was bigger and better than the old one. It had six wheels and a horn.

"Look what I made for you," he said. "But you have to share it. Or it will break again."

Tom and Sam smiled. They hugged their dad and thanked him. They learned to share. They played with the new truck and had fun. They were happy.

Teddy and Peter were best friends. They were always playing together and having fun. But one day they began to quarrel. They did not mean to, but their tempers got the better of them.

Soon it got so loud that their parents had to come into the room and tell them to stop. Teddy and Peter knew better and felt very sorry for what had happened.

That night, Teddy had a nightmare. In it he and Peter kept fighting and shouting. Even though he knew it was just a dream, it still made Teddy very scared. He was relieved to find that Peter wasn't mad at him the next day; he was still his old friend just like before.

It was a quiet day after that. Teddy and Peter understood the importance of not getting into quarrels, and so stayed quiet for the rest of the day. They played together and talked, but not too loudly.

And so, Teddy and Peter stayed best friends, learning to be quiet and not quarrel, and never having any more nightmares.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside and explore the world around her. One day, she went on an adventure to the east, where she saw a big mountain. She wanted to climb it, but her mommy said it was too sharp and dangerous.

Lily was sad, but she didn't give up. She decided to find a way to climb the mountain safely. She asked her friends for help, and they came up with a plan. They found some cool tools and rope to help them climb up the mountain.

Finally, they made it to the top! Lily was so happy and proud of herself. She looked out at the beautiful view and saw the sun setting in the east. She knew that the journey was worth it and that she could do anything if she tried hard enough.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Tim. He had a map that he loved to look at. One day, Tim wanted to go on an adventure. He asked his friend, Sue, to come with him.

"Let's follow the map," Tim said to Sue. "We can find something fun!" Sue liked the idea, so they started to walk. They saw a big tree, some birds, and a small dog. They were having a regular day.

As they walked, they found a door in a hill. Tim said, "Let's pull the door and see what's inside!" Sue was a little scared, but she pulled the door with Tim. Inside, they found a room full of toys and games.

They played for hours and had a lot of fun. When it was time to go home, they closed the door and said goodbye to the secret room. They promised to come back soon for more adventures.

Molly and her brother, Sam, were exploring in the woods. Suddenly, they saw a mule. Sam wanted to examine the mule and see what it was like. Molly was a bit hesitant, so they approached it very slowly.

When they got close, the mule was very calm and mild. Molly moved a bit closer and the mule didn't seem to mind. She pet the mule on its back while Sam examined its hooves. He was amazed at how gentle the mule was.

After a while, they said goodbye to the mule and went back on their journey. It had been a fun adventure and they were excited to tell their parents all about it.

Once upon a time there were two friends, an ostrich and a goat. They were the best of friends and did everything together. One day they decided to take a walk in the woods.

As they were walking down the path they suddenly heard clapping. They looked around and saw a group of people applauding. The goat was so excited and asked the ostrich what was happening.

The ostrich explained that the people were applauding because a performer had done something amazing. The goat was so excited that he decided to join them and start clapping too!

Suddenly the performer got angry and started to say rude things to the little goat. The goat was so shocked, but the ostrich stood up for her friend and said that it was his right to applaud. Everyone agreed and started applauding louder. The performer was so embarrassed that he ran away.

The little goat and his ostrich best friend were so proud of themselves and walked home feeling happy and content.

Tommy saw a peanut. He was so excited! He wanted to try it and see what it tasted like. But it was bitter. He didn't like the way the peanut tasted. He made a sour face and stuck his tongue out. Tommy decided to leave the peanut alone and keep looking around. He kept on exploring and soon he forgot all about the peanut.

Once upon a time, little Suzy asked her Mom what a birdcage was.

"All right, Suzy," said Mom, with a smile. "I'll explain it to you." She pointed at their window. "See that birdcage outside? That's a birdcage."

Suzy stared out the window at the birdcage. It was colorful, with a playful design.

Just then, there was a little chirp. Mom smiled. "Look! A bird is sitting in the birdcage. That's why it's called a birdcage."

Suzy smiled. She went to the window and looked at the bird. "It's so pretty," she said.

Mom nodded. "Yes, it is! Now, why don't you play with your toys so the bird can stay in the birdcage?"

Suzy happily agreed and ran off to play. Mom watched Suzy with a proud smile. She was glad she was able to explain the birdcage to her daughter.

Once upon a time, there was a factory. It was home to five special robots. Every day, the robots would bathe so they were clean and sparkly. The robots were so perfect! They were always very kind, too.

The robots did all kinds of things at the factory; they swept the floors, peeked inside machines, and even made funny faces at each other. They were always so busy!

When it was time to go home, the robots bathed one last time. They all smiled, for they were so happy to be so clean and perfect. Then, they each said goodbye and went their separate ways.

And that was the story of the five special robots who lived in the factory! They had lots of fun, but always remembered to bathe and stay perfect.

Once upon a time there was a rocket. It was very big and shiny. It was so shiny that it could be seen from far away. Every day the rocket flew up very high in the sky.

One day, the rocket needed some help. It wanted to finish its journey. So it flew down to the ground and asked a little boy for help. The little boy was very excited to help the rocket.

The boy gave the rocket some healthy food. The food made the rocket strong and happy. With the boy's help, the rocket was ready to finish its journey.

The rocket said goodbye and thanked the little boy. Then the rocket flew up in the sky and finished its journey.

The little boy waved goodbye. He was very happy and proud that he helped the rocket finish its journey.

Once there was a wealthy farmer. He had lots of animals. One day he wanted to test how sharp his tools were, so he took his sharp knife and tried to cut a branch off a tree. He tested the knife and it was very sharp. He was so pleased.

The farmer then decided to cut the grass that was around his animals. So, the farmer tested the knife again, and it was still very sharp. He was so pleased. He then started to cut the grass with the knife. The animals were happy to have a tidy place to play.

The farmer was very happy with his knife. It had passed the test and had made his animals very happy. He was now sure that all his tools were strong and sharp. He was a very savvy and wealthy farmer.

Once there was a kind little puppy. He was small and white, and his name was Spot. He loved to explore and play outside.

One day, Spot wanted to go out on an adventure. He tried to run away, but there was a leash around his collar. He looked down and frowned.

Spot's mom saw him and she was very kind. She said, "Let's go for a walk instead!" She took the leash off of Spot and they went for a nice walk in the sunshine.

Spot felt so happy. He wagged his tail and looked up at his mom with a big smile on his face. He was so glad that his mom was so kind.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to go to the beach with her family. One day, they went to the beach and Lily saw a big wave in the distance. She was scared but her dad held her hand and told her not to be afraid.

As they got closer to the wave, Lily saw that it wasn't as big as she thought. She felt better and started to play in the water. She noticed that she was getting better at swimming and her dad said she was improving.

Lily was so happy to be at the beach with her family. She loved the sound of the waves and the feeling of the sand between her toes. She knew that she would always remember this day at the beach.

Once upon a time, there was a yellow book. It was very special, and everyone wanted it. One day, a girl named Sally wanted to find the book, so she set out on a long journey. She arrived at a big tree and saw the book at the top. After a lot of trying, Sally was able to get the book. She was so happy that she had finally arrived at the book. She opened the book and made lots of friends. Every day, Sally and her friends played and learned new things until the sun went down. It was a very happy time, and they all had lots of fun.

Mandy and Jane were walking through the park. Jane had a cart. Mandy asked, "What's in your cart Jane?" Jane smiled and said, "We're going to the market! It's a long way away and I need to get some food."

Mandy said, "Wow, can I come with you?" Jane nodded and said, "Sure!" The two friends started walking. They talked and sang songs along the way.

When they arrived at the market, Jane put some food in her cart. After they finished, they started to return home.

They walked a long way. When they finally got home, Jane put away the food from her cart. Mandy said, "That was a great day Jane!" Jane smiled and nodded. They had lots of fun together!

Tom and Lily were playing with their toys in the living room. Tom had a big truck and Lily had a doll. They were having fun until Tom saw a sticker on Lily's doll.

"Hey, what is that?" Tom asked, pointing at the sticker.

"It is a label," Lily said. "It says her name is Anna. She is my friend."

Tom did not like the label. He wanted to take it off. He reached for the doll and tried to pull the label.

"Stop it!" Lily shouted. "You are hurting Anna! Give her back to me!"

Tom did not listen. He kept pulling the label. Lily got upset. She started to cry and hit Tom with her hand.

"Ow!" Tom said. "That hurts! Why are you hitting me?"

"Because you are mean!" Lily replied. "You are not my friend anymore!"

Tom felt sorry. He did not want to make Lily cry. He did not want to lose his friend. He let go of the doll and the label.

"I am sorry, Lily," Tom said. "I was just curious. I did not mean to hurt Anna or you. Can we still be friends?"

Lily looked at Tom. She saw that he was sorry. She wiped her tears and hugged her doll.

"Okay, Tom," Lily said. "We can still be friends. But you have to be nice to Anna. She is my friend too."

Tom nodded. He smiled and hugged Lily.

"I will be nice to Anna," Tom said. "And to you. You are my best friend."

Lily smiled back. She and Tom went back to playing with their toys. They were happy again.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. He loved playing with his toy cars and trucks. One day, he was playing with his red car when he accidentally drove it into a tree.

"Oh no!" he said, feeling impatient. "My car is stuck!"

Just then, his dad came outside and saw what happened. "Don't worry, Timmy," his dad said. "I'll help you."

His dad picked up the car and showed Timmy how to reverse it out of the tree. Timmy was so happy and gave his dad a big hug.

"Thanks, Dad!" Timmy said, with a big smile on his face.

As they walked back inside, Timmy noticed a small scratch on the palm of his hand. "Ouch!" he said, showing his dad.

"It's okay," his dad said. "We'll put a band-aid on it."

And so, Timmy's car was saved and his hand was bandaged. He was grateful for his dad's help and went back to playing with his toys.

Once there was a furry flea. He was very small, but he wanted to make some friends. He knew it would be hard, because he was so tiny. But he decided to try.

He started to jump around and call out. He said, "Come to me, friends! I want to play!" But nobody answered.

The flea was so unhappy. He didn't know what to do. Suddenly, he heard a tiny voice say, "Hello, I'm here!"

The little flea was so excited! He looked around and he saw a group of furry fleas, just like him. He was so happy and he called again, "Come and play with me!"

The furry fleas jumped around and played together. They had so much fun! They called out to each other and laughed. From then on, the furry flea had lots of friends to play with.

Once upon a time, a little boy named Timmy went to the park with his mommy. They saw a big red motor in the distance. Timmy asked his mommy, "What's that?" His mommy said, "That's a motor. It can make things move."

Suddenly, they heard a loud noise. It was a man trying to raise a flag on a tall pole. Timmy asked the man, "Why are you raising the flag?" The man said, "I'm raising the flag to show that we love our country."

Timmy was happy to learn new things and see new things in the park. He and his mommy went home, and Timmy told his daddy all about the motor and the man raising the flag. Timmy loved going to the park and learning new things every day.

Once upon a time there was a little girl who loved to play with her jug. One day she noticed something strange. The jug was shrinking! She couldn’t understand why and started to feel a little bit scared.

The little girl went up to her mum and asked, ‘Mummy, why is my jug shrinking?’ But her mum didn’t know.

So the little girl asked her dad. He said, ‘Your jug is shrinking because a monster made it do that.’ The little girl was scared. What would happen next?

The little girl asked, ‘What can I do?’ Her dad replied, ‘There is nothing you can do. The jug will keep shrinking until it disappears.’

The little girl was so fearful. She hugged her jug tightly and said goodbye.

And then the jug disappeared. The little girl never saw it again.

Jimmy was so lucky! He had a new friend named Sammy. One day they went on a special adventure. Sammy asked to go to the ice cream store. So they went and they had fun choosing flavors.

At the store, Jimmy said, "I want to order vanilla!" So Sammy said, "Okay, let's do it!" They ordered the vanilla ice cream and two spoons.

When they had finished eating, Jimmy said, "You're the best friend ever, Sammy!" Sammy smiled and said, "You're lucky for having such a great friend!"

They both laughed together. It was a lucky day after all!

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim had a brown dog named Max. Max loved to slide down the hill in the park. One day, Tim and Max went to the park to play. They went to the slide and Max climbed up to the top. Tim watched as Max slide down the slide. It was so much fun!

After they were done sliding, Tim noticed that a screw was loose on the slide. He told his mom, who called the park worker to fix it. The park worker came and fixed the screw so that no one would get hurt. Tim was happy that he helped keep the park safe for everyone to play. He and Max went home, tired but happy from their fun day at the park.

Once upon a time there was a patient elephant. He was very slow and always like to take his time. One day the elephant was walking in the forest with his friend the mouse. The mouse was in a hurry so he asked the elephant what was taking so long.

The elephant said,"You know, my good friend, it's important to stop and smell the roses. Patience is important."

The mouse agreed and said,"I know, but I just have to find this pin. I've been looking for it for hours!"

The elephant smiled and said,"Well, let me help you look. Who knows - maybe we'll find it together!"

So they both looked and sure enough, after a while, the mouse found his pin! He was so happy and thanked the elephant for being so patient.

The mouse said with a smile,"Thanks for being so kind. You know, sometimes a little patience goes a long way!"

Once upon a time, there was a small island. On the island, there was a big house made from hard rocks. One day, a little girl who visited the island decided to explore the house. She opened the big door and walked inside.

She saw lots of things and she wanted to see more. But then she heard a loud noise. It was the sound of the door shutting. The little girl was scared, so she started to run. But the door was so hard that she couldn't open it again.

The little girl was now stuck inside the big house on the island. She even tried to climb out of the windows, but they were high up and she couldn't reach them.

She was stuck, so she decided to yell for help. Finally, someone heard her and the door was opened from the outside. The little girl was glad that the door was shut, she never wanted to get stuck inside again.

The end.

Sara liked to fold paper. She could make many shapes with paper. She could make a hat, a boat, a bird, and a star. She was proud of her paper shapes. She showed them to her mom and dad. They smiled and clapped.

One day, Sara had a new baby brother. His name was Ben. Sara wanted to show Ben her paper shapes. She went to his crib with a paper hat. She put the hat on his head. But Ben did not like the hat. He cried and kicked. He tore the hat with his hands. Sara was sad and angry. She said, "Ben is rude! He broke my hat!"

Mom heard Sara and Ben. She came to the crib. She saw the torn hat and the crying baby. She said, "Sara, Ben is just an infant. He does not know how to play with paper. He did not mean to be rude. He was scared of the hat. You have to be gentle and patient with him. He will learn to like your paper shapes when he is older."

Sara felt sorry for Ben. She said, "I'm sorry, Ben. I did not want to scare you. I wanted to share my hat with you." She gave him a hug and a kiss. She took another paper and folded a boat. She said, "Look, Ben. This is a boat. It can float on water. Do you want to see?" Ben stopped crying and looked at the boat. He smiled and reached for it. Sara smiled too. She said, "Maybe Ben is not so rude after all. Maybe he is just curious." Mom smiled and said, "That's right, Sara. You are a good big sister. You can teach Ben many things with your paper shapes." Sara and Ben played with the paper boat. They were happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play outside with his friends. One day, Timmy and his friends were playing soccer. Timmy kicked the ball so hard that it went over the fence and into the neighbor's yard.

Timmy went to get the ball and found a mint plant growing in the neighbor's yard. He picked a mint leaf and smelled it. It smelled so good! Timmy decided to take some mint leaves home to show his mom.

When Timmy got home, his mom noticed that his shirt was rough and dirty. She asked him what happened. Timmy told her about kicking the ball over the fence and finding the mint plant. His mom was happy to see the mint and thanked Timmy for bringing it home.

Timmy and his mom made some mint tea and enjoyed it together. Timmy was happy that he found the mint plant and got to share it with his mom.

Tim and Mia are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big truck. The truck has ice-cream. Tim and Mia love ice-cream. They run to the truck.

"Hello, can we have ice-cream, please?" Tim asks the man in the truck.

"Sure, what flavor do you want?" the man says.

"I want chocolate," Tim says.

"I want strawberry," Mia says.

The man gives them ice-cream. Tim and Mia are happy. They lick their ice-cream.

But then, a big dog comes. The dog is hungry. The dog sees the ice-cream. The dog wants the ice-cream. The dog barks and runs to Tim and Mia.

"Go away, dog!" Tim says. He tries to move away from the dog.

"Help, help!" Mia says. She is scared of the dog.

The man in the truck sees the dog. He is not happy. He does not like the dog. He shouts at the dog.

"Hey, bad dog! Leave the kids alone! Go back to your owner!" the man says.

The dog hears the man. The dog is afraid of the man. The dog runs away from the truck.

Tim and Mia are safe. They hug each other. They thank the man.

"Thank you, mister, for saving us from the dog," Tim says.

"Thank you, mister, for the ice-cream," Mia says.

"You're welcome, kids. Enjoy your ice-cream. And be careful of dogs," the man says.

Tim and Mia smile. They finish their ice-cream. They go back to the park. They play like normal. They are happy. They are friends.

One day, an ant wanted to make some nice art. But he didn't know how! So he asked his friendly friends for help.

"How can I make nice art?" he asked.

The rabbit smiled and said, "You can print it!".

The ant was so excited! He thanked his friend and said goodbye.

He went to the store and bought some printing paper. He put it on the ground, and with a special machine, he printed the prettiest picture he had ever seen! All his friends came over to see it, and they were amazed.

"That looks so nice!" shouted the mouse.

The ant beamed with pride. He had made something beautiful, all by himself. He thanked his friendly friends for the help. They all smiled and said, "You did a great job!"

Together, they enjoyed the beautiful art the ant had printed.

Once there was a good lime named Lanny. One day, Lanny wanted to settle down and find a place to call home.

So, Lanny set off on a long journey to find a place to settle. She looked high and low, but could not find a good place. Finally, Lanny came upon a warm spot in the sunshine. It was just right, so Lanny decided to settle there.

Lanny made herself comfortable, and soon she was all settled in. She was so happy with her new home, and she decided she would stay there forever.

Lanny smiled and enjoyed the sunshine, and she hugged her good lime tightly. She was so happy to have finally found the perfect place to settle down.

Once upon a time, there was a hungry boy named Tim. Tim wanted to find food. He saw a kayak by the river. Tim thought, "I can use the kayak to find food across the river."

Tim got in the kayak and rowed across the river. He saw a big tree with red fruit. Tim thought, "I can eat the red fruit and not be hungry anymore." But Tim did not know how to get the fruit from the tree.

Tim tried to solve his problem. He found a long stick and tried to hit the fruit with the stick. But the stick was too short. Tim was sad and still hungry.

Then, a big wind came and pushed the kayak away. Tim was scared. He could not swim. The wind took the kayak far away, and Tim was lost. The hungry boy did not find food, and he did not get back home.

Once upon a time, there was a little dog named Max. Max loved to play and run around, but he didn't like wearing his collar. His collar was hard and stiff, and it hurt his neck.

One day, Max's owner took him to the park. Max was having so much fun playing with his ball that he didn't even notice when his collar fell off. Max's owner didn't notice either.

As they were leaving the park, Max's owner realized that Max's collar was missing. They searched and searched, but they couldn't find it. Max was sad because he knew he needed his collar to be safe.

That night, Max's owner prayed for a solution. The next day, a package arrived in the mail. Inside was a new collar for Max. This collar was different though. It was soft and flexible, and Max loved it. He never wanted to take it off again.

Once upon a time, there was a girl who was very excited about getting a stamp. She asked her mom if she could have one, but her mom shook her head. "I'm sorry, sweetheart," her mom said. "Stamps aren't available now."

The girl was very disappointed, so she went to her dad and asked him the same question. Her dad thought for a moment and said, "Let's see if we can make it happen." He called a few people and soon it was arranged for the girl to get a stamp.

The girl was very excited, but she soon found out that someone else also wanted the stamp. A boy tried to get it first, and the girl was very upset. She didn't want the boy to have her stamp!

The girl and the boy argued and argued, until finally they both said the same thing at the same time, "We can share!" The two shared the stamp and were happy they could make it happen. They hugged and smiled and enjoyed their stamp together.

Anna and Ben are friends. They like to play together. One day, they visit Ben's grandma. She lives in a small house with a big garden. She has many flowers and birds.

"Hello, Anna and Ben. I am happy to see you. Do you want some cookies?" Grandma says.

"Yes, please. Thank you, Grandma. Your cookies are yummy," Anna says.

"Can we play in the garden, Grandma?" Ben asks.

"Of course, you can. But be careful. Don't touch the roses. They have thorns. They can hurt you," Grandma says.

Anna and Ben go to the garden. They see a ball and a rag. The rag is old and dirty. It has holes and stains.

"Look, a ball. Let's play catch," Ben says.

"OK. But what is this rag for?" Anna asks.

"I don't know. Maybe Grandma uses it to clean something," Ben says.

He picks up the rag and throws it to Anna. Anna catches it and throws it back. They have fun.

But they are careless. They don't see where they throw the rag. They throw it too far. They throw it over the fence. They throw it into the street.

"Oh no! The rag is gone. What if Grandma needs it?" Anna says.

"Let's go and get it. Come on," Ben says.

They run to the fence. They look at the street. They see a car. The car is fast. The car runs over the rag. The rag is torn and flat.

"Oh no! The car broke the rag. Grandma will be sad. What can we do?" Ben says.

"I don't know. Maybe we can say sorry. Maybe we can give her a new rag," Anna says.

They go back to the house. They tell Grandma what happened. They say sorry. They hug Grandma.

"It's OK, Anna and Ben. I'm not sad. I'm not angry. The rag was old and useless. I don't need it. I have many other rags. But I'm glad you are safe. You should not go to the street. The street is dangerous. You should stay in the garden. The garden is safe. The garden is beautiful. Do you want to see my flowers and birds?" Grandma says.

"Yes, please. We want to see your flowers and birds. We love your garden. We love you, Grandma," Anna and Ben say.

They go to the garden with Grandma. They see the roses and the thorns. They don't touch them. They see the sun and the sky. They smile. They are happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little bird who loved to sing. Every day, he would fly around the forest and sing his heart out. One day, he heard a loud noise coming from the nearby nation. The little bird was scared, but he didn't know why.

The next day, the little bird woke up to a bright sun shining in the sky. He decided to fly over to the nation to see what was going on. As he got closer, he saw that the people in the nation were all singing together. The little bird was amazed by the beautiful sound they made.

From that day on, the little bird would fly over to the nation every morning to listen to the people sing. He realized that the loud noise he heard before was just them practicing for their big performance. The little bird was happy that he had faced his fear and discovered something new.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved dessert, especially ice cream. One day, Lily went to a party and ate too much dessert. She felt sick and didn't feel graceful anymore.

The next day, Lily's mom asked her if she remembered what happened at the party. Lily told her mom about eating too much dessert and feeling sick. Her mom reminded her to only eat a little bit of dessert next time.

Lily felt better and remembered her mom's advice. From then on, she only ate a small amount of dessert at parties and felt graceful again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to eat candy and chips all day long. Her mom always told her to eat fruits and veggies, but Lily thought they were yucky.

One day, Lily's mom showed her a big pile of waste. It was disgusting and smelled bad. Her mom explained that all the candy and chips she ate made her body produce waste that was not good for the earth.

Lily felt sad and decided to change her ways. She started to eat more fruits and veggies and less candy and chips. She even asked her mom to deliver her some fresh fruits and veggies every day.

In the end, Lily felt healthier and happier. She learned that taking care of her body and the earth was important. The moral of the story is that we should eat healthy and not waste our food.

Once upon a time there was a little green frog. He lived in a big pond with lots of other frogs, but he was special.

One day, the little green frog found a handle lying in the bottom of the pond. He never saw something like it before, so he picked it up and started to play with it.

Suddenly, a big mean fish came up from the deep water and said in a sharp voice, "Hey, that's mine! Give it back to me!"

The little green frog was so scared, but he wanted to keep the handle, so he held onto it tightly. "No," he said. "This is mine now!"

The mean fish swam back and forth, hissing and snarling. He tried to take the handle back, but the little green frog held on tight.

The fish soon gave up, and the little green frog was saved. From then on, the little green frog was always careful to watch out for the mean fish. He played with his handle often, enjoying the feeling of having something all to himself.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a pet rabbit named Snowy. Lily loved to feed Snowy carrots and lettuce. Snowy would hop around happily when Lily fed him.

One day, Lily's mom made some cookies. They smelled delicious! Lily asked her mom if she could taste one. Her mom said, "Sure, but just one for now." Lily took a bite and said, "Mmm, this cookie is delicious!"

Snowy hopped over to Lily and looked up at her with big eyes. Lily giggled and said, "Sorry Snowy, cookies are not for rabbits. But I will feed you some more carrots later!"

Lily liked to use her crayons to draw pictures. She had many colors, but her favorite was peach. She liked how it looked like the fruit she ate with her mom. One day, she wanted to draw a peach on a big paper. She looked for her peach crayon, but she could not find it. She asked her brother Max if he had seen it.

Max was playing with his cars on the floor. He did not like to draw. He said he did not know where the peach crayon was. But Lily saw something in his hand. It was her peach crayon! She ran to him and tried to get it back. But Max was faster. He put the crayon in his mouth and bit it.

Lily was very angry and sad. She yelled at Max and told him to spit out the crayon. Max made a face and spit out the crayon. It was broken and wet. He said it was disgusting. He did not like how it tasted. He threw it on the floor and went back to his cars.

Lily picked up the crayon and looked at it. It was ruined. She could not use it to draw anymore. She felt like crying. She did not understand why Max did that. She wished he was nicer to her. She decided to tell her mom what happened. Maybe she could get a new peach crayon. She hoped so. She loved her peach crayon.

Once there was a pretty little girl named Lucy. Every night, she looked up at the sky and thanked the stars for all the light they gave her. She loved looking at their twinkling and smiled.

One time, she found a special ornament in the garden. It was made of glass and had a sparkly light inside. She thanked the stars again for the wonderful thing she had found. The little girl was so happy for the gift.

Every night, Lucy put the special ornament up in her bedroom window. The glass was like a tiny star, and shone brightly in the night. She loved how it looked and would thank the stars again for their beautiful light.

Lucy kept that special ornament her whole life and always thanked the stars for the light it brought. Every night, she would remember the sparkly star in her window and smile with joy.

Anna and Ben were twins who liked to play in the forest. They were eager to find new things and have fun. One day, they saw a big mushroom with red spots on it. It looked like a hat.

"Wow, look at that mushroom!" Anna said. "Can we pick it?"

"I don't know," Ben said. "Maybe it is not good to eat. Maybe it is bad."

They went closer to the mushroom and touched it. It felt soft and wet. They smelled it. It smelled like dirt and grass.

"Maybe we can ask Mommy if we can eat it," Anna said. "She knows a lot about food."

"Okay," Ben said. "But how can we take it home? It is too big for our hands."

They looked around and saw a big leaf on the ground. They put the mushroom on the leaf and lifted it together. It was heavy, but they were strong.

They walked back to their house, holding the leaf with the mushroom. They were happy and proud of their find.

When they got home, they saw Mommy in the kitchen. She was making soup for lunch.

"Mommy, Mommy, look what we found!" Anna said.

"A mushroom!" Ben said.

They showed Mommy the mushroom on the leaf. Mommy looked surprised and scared.

"Oh, no, no, no!" Mommy said. "That is a very bad mushroom! It can make you very sick! You must never eat it or touch it!"

She took the leaf with the mushroom and threw it in the trash. She washed Anna and Ben's hands with soap and water. She hugged them and kissed them.

"I'm so glad you are okay," Mommy said. "You are very lucky. God was watching over you. You should pray and thank Him for keeping you safe."

Anna and Ben nodded. They did not understand why the mushroom was bad, but they trusted Mommy. They prayed and thanked God for their Mommy and their life. They ate the soup and forgot about the mushroom. They decided to play with their toys instead.

Once upon a time, there was a mother and her child. The mother was so amazing at making fun things.

Every day, the mother and her child would work on craft projects together. They would paint images and make necklaces together.

Today, the mother and her child were making a special treat. They worked hard to mix the ingredients, stir the batter and fill a pan with the batter.

When their treat was finished, the mother put it in the oven. A few minutes later, their treat was finished and it looked so yummy!

The mother and her child laughed as they ate it all up. They had so much fun making the treat and it was delicious!

The mother was so amazing and it was a great day for both of them!

Mum and Dad were very excited. They had planned a picnic for the whole family! Everybody was getting ready. Mum and Dad packed some modest snacks and drinks, and put them in a bag.

When everything was ready, the family went to the park. They spread out a blanket and set up their picnic. They put out the snacks and drinks, and the children started to play.

When the food was ready, the family started eating. After lunch, everybody went to explore the park. They clapped their hands as they watched the birds fly, and laughed as they chased each other around the trees.

It was such a wonderful day! Everyone was so excited. They wanted to stay much longer, but it was time to go home. On the way, Mum and Dad discussed how much fun they had and how they wished they could go on a picnic again soon!

Mandy yawned as she watched her mum unload the van. It was late, but they had to move all the things out of the old house. Everyone was ready to start living in the new house.

The van was so full that Mandy's mum needed help. So Mandy said she would help as best she could. She was so popular with all the adults that they let her!

Mandy yawned again as she grabbed boxes and put them in the house. She was so tired and wished the moving was finished. Suddenly, her dad said it was time to go. Hooray!

Mandy hopped in the van and waved goodbye to the old house. They were all so excited to start thinking about how to decorate their new house. Mandy couldn't wait to get started in the popular new home!

Once upon a time, there was a tiny bird who was searching for wisdom. Everyday, it looked high and low for just a bit of knowledge.

One day, it found an old wise tree. The tree said to the bird, "Greeting, little one. What are you looking for?"

The bird replied, "I am looking for wisdom!"

The wise tree said, "Come closer and clean your eyes with my leaves. Then you will see."

The bird wore the clean leaves and sure enough, a little bit of wisdom began to appear. The bird asked, "How can I get more wisdom?"

The wise tree said, "You must go on a journey and never give up. Sometimes wisdom will appear and then it will disappear, but it will always come back if you keep searching."

The bird thanked the wise tree and flew away. It kept searching for wisdom, never giving up. Whenever the wisdom disappeared, the bird would come back and search again. Eventually, the bird found more and more wisdom and became very wise.

Lily and Tom were playing hide and seek in the park. Lily was the seeker and Tom was the hider. Lily counted to ten and then opened her eyes. She looked around for Tom, but she could not see him. Where did he go?

She walked to the big tree and looked behind it. No Tom. She walked to the slide and looked under it. No Tom. She walked to the bench and looked on it. No Tom. She started to feel sad and scared. Where was Tom? Did he vanish?

She called out, "Tom, where are you? I can't find you. Come out, come out, please!"

She heard a giggle from behind the bushes. She ran to the bushes and pushed them aside. There was Tom, hiding and smiling. He jumped out and said, "Boo! I scared you, Lily!"

Lily felt a mix of feelings. She was angry that Tom tricked her, but she was also glad that he was safe and not vanished. She said, "Tom, that was not nice. You made me worry. Don't do that again, okay?"

Tom felt sorry for Lily. He said, "I'm sorry, Lily. I was just having fun. I didn't mean to make you worry. I won't do that again, okay?"

Lily and Tom hugged and made up. They decided to play another game, but this time, they would stay close to each other. They heard a loud sound from the park gate. It was their mom, calling them. It was time to go home. They ran to their mom, holding hands. Their mom was happy to see them. She said, "Did you have fun, kids?"

They said, "Yes, mom, we had fun. But Tom vanished and I couldn't find him. He scared me, but then he said sorry. We are friends again."

Their mom said, "I'm glad you are friends again, but don't vanish like that, Tom. It's not safe. You have to stay where I can see you, okay?"

Tom said, "Okay, mom. I'm sorry. I won't vanish again."

Lily said, "Me too, mom. I won't vanish either."

Their mom said, "Good. Now let's go home. I have a surprise for you. It's your favorite cake!"

Lily and Tom cheered and followed their mom. They were happy and hungry. They forgot about the alarm that they heard in the park. It was just a fire truck passing by. They didn't know that it was going to a house that was on fire. They didn't know that someone had vanished in the fire. They didn't know that someone was not glad at all.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to draw and write on paper. One day, she found a fancy pen that her mom gave her. She was so happy and started to write her name on the paper.

Suddenly, she saw a tiny hole in the paper. She wondered how it got there. She looked around and saw her little brother playing with a pencil. She smiled and continued to write her name.
