Her mommy said, "We can't keep buying toys every time we come to the mall, but we can play with it here." Lily was sad but understood. She started bouncing the ball and found out it was very flexible.

A boy came up to Lily and said, "Can I play too?" Lily said, "Yes, you can play with us." They played together for a long time and had lots of fun. When it was time to go home, Lily was happy because she made a new friend and had a great time at the mall.

Tom and Sue are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big tree with green fruits. Tom says, "Look, Sue, pears! I like pears. Do you want to try one?"

Sue says, "Yes, I want to try one. But how can we get them? They are too high."

Tom says, "I have an idea. I can climb the tree and pick some pears for us. You can wait here and catch them."

Sue says, "OK, Tom, be careful. Don't fall."

Tom climbs the tree. He is brave and strong. He reaches a branch with some pears. He picks one and throws it to Sue. Sue tries to catch it, but it is too fast. It hits the ground and rolls away.

Tom says, "Sorry, Sue, I threw it too hard. Let me try again."

He picks another pear and throws it more gently. Sue catches it with her hands. She is happy and proud. She says, "Thank you, Tom, you are a good friend. Now I can try the pear."

She bites the pear. But it is not sweet and juicy. It is tough and sour. She makes a face and spits it out. She says, "Yuck, this pear is bad. It tastes like dirt. I don't like it."

Tom says, "Really? Let me try." He picks another pear and bites it. He also makes a face and spits it out. He says, "You are right, Sue, this pear is bad. It tastes like soap. I don't like it either."

They look at the tree. They see a sign that says, "Do not eat. These are not pears. These are soap fruits. They are for making soap, not for eating."

Tom and Sue feel silly and laugh. They say, "Oops, we made a mistake. These are not pears. These are soap fruits. We should have read the sign first."

They throw the soap fruits away and go to find something else to play with. They learn a lesson. They should always check before they try something new.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily loved to dress up in her princess costume and play with her dolls. One day, Lily's mom mentioned that they were going to a costume party. Lily was so excited! She wanted to wear her princess costume to the party.

But when Lily's mom tried to put the costume on her, it was too hard to get on. Lily started to cry because she really wanted to wear her princess costume to the party. Her mom said not to worry, they could find another costume for her to wear.

At the party, Lily saw all kinds of costumes. There were witches, pirates, and even a superhero! But Lily didn't mind that she wasn't wearing her princess costume. She was just happy to be at the party and have fun with her friends.

Nelly was in class with her friends. She was singing a song that her parents had taught her, and it made her feel very happy. But something surprising was about to happen.

The door opened and a famous man walked in! Everyone was surprised. They thought it was strange that a famous man would walk into their classroom. Nelly wanted to guess who it was, but she couldn't figure it out.

The famous man smiled. Then he said something peculiar - he said he was Nelly's dad! Suddenly it all made sense. This was the surprise her mom had promised her.

Nelly felt surprised and happy. She hugged her dad and giggled. All of her friends were so impressed that Nelly had such a famous dad. Nelly was proud, and she knew that her mom had been planning this special moment for a long time.

One day, a bald man named Tom went to the park. Tom had a big sack. In the sack, there were many toys. Tom liked to play with the toys. He saw a seat near the trees and put his sack on it.

A little girl named Sue came to the park too. She saw Tom's toys and wanted to play. Sue asked Tom, "Can I play with your toys too?" Tom said, "Yes, we can play together."

Tom and Sue played with the toys near the seat. They laughed and had fun. When they were done, they put the toys back in the sack. Tom and Sue became good friends and played at the park every day.

Jim and Dad were in the garden. Dad was tidying up. Jim was watching him and bouncing with excitement.

“What are you doing, Dad?” asked Jim.

“I’m making the garden nice,” Dad said. “I’m making it tidy.”

Jim watched and asked questions while Dad worked. He went around picking up leaves and twigs. He swept the stones too.

After a while Dad had finished. Everything was tidy.

“Look, Jim! The garden is tidy!” Dad said.

Jim clapped his hands and smiled.

“Mmmm,” he said. “It looks nice.”

Dad nodded and smiled. Then he put his tools away.

“The garden looks good,” he said. “Now the job is done. We can end here.”

Jim looked around the tidy garden and nodded. Then he ran away to play. Dad smiled and watched him go.

Once there was a little girl who was very curious. Every day she wanted to learn something new and exciting. One day, her parents gave her a special key that would unlock a door in their house.

The little girl was very eager to find out what was behind the door. She put the key gently in the keyhole and slowly turned it. The door opened and she discovered a cozy room with a pretty tutoring desk.

The little girl ran inside the room and started to explore. She found some interesting books and colorful pencils. She also discovered a box of puzzles and a friendly looking stuffed animal.

The little girl was delighted at what she found. She began to take out the books, pencils and puzzles and arranged them nicely on the tutoring desk. She knew she had found her perfect place to learn and explore new things.

Finally, she gave her stuffed animal a big hug and said “Let’s start learning something new today.” She was so excited to unlock a world full of knowledge!

One day, a group of children were playing together. They were all very silly and would laugh and giggle at even small things. One of the children had a question. He wanted to know why they were all playing together.

The group of children all stopped to think. They thought and thought until finally one of the children offered a solution. He said that they were playing together because it was a lot of fun! Everyone was happy with that answer and started to play again.

Then the same child had another question. He asked why the group was so silly. Everyone laughed and one of the children suggested that it was because they were all so happy. Everyone nodded and agreed.

Again, the group went back to having fun. The silly games and laughing were so much fun that the children kept playing for a long time. They enjoyed the silly games and never stopped having fun!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the park with her friends. One day, Lily saw a big brown dog and she wanted to pet him. She asked the owner if she could, but he said no.

Suddenly, a storm came and everyone had to go home. Lily's mom picked her up and they went home. But when they got there, they saw that their house had been destroyed by the storm. Lily was sad because she lost all her toys and her favorite blanket.

Lily asked her mom if they could fix the house, but her mom said it was too expensive. They had to move to a new house and Lily had to say goodbye to all her friends. She missed her old house and her old life. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lucy. She liked to gaze at the stars at night. One day, her mommy and daddy went to a marriage. They left Lucy with a harmless cat named Whiskers.

While they were gone, Lucy and Whiskers played in the house. Lucy said, "Whiskers, let's play hide and seek!" Whiskers meowed and they started to play. Lucy hid under the bed and Whiskers looked for her.

But then, Lucy saw a big spider on the floor. She screamed and ran out of the room. Whiskers tried to catch the spider, but it was too fast. The spider bit Lucy on the leg. Lucy cried and cried. When her mommy and daddy came home, they saw Lucy crying and took her to the doctor. The doctor said that the spider was not harmless and Lucy had to stay in the hospital for a few days.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her dolls and teddy bears, but she was always alone. One day, she decided to go on a journey to find some friends to play with. She packed her backpack with some snacks and toys, and set off on her adventure.

As she walked, she met a kind dog named Max. Max asked her where she was going, and Lily told him about her journey to find friends. Max offered to join her on her journey, and Lily was happy to have a reliable friend by her side.

They walked and walked until they came across a group of children playing in a park. Lily was shy at first, but Max encouraged her to go and play with them. The children welcomed Lily and Max, and they all played together happily.

Lily learned that sometimes, it's scary to go on a journey alone, but when you have a reliable friend like Max, it's not so scary anymore. She also learned that when you meet new friends, it's important to be brave and say hello. From that day on, Lily and Max went on many adventures together, always with a smile on their faces.

Once upon a time there was a girl called Mary. Mary was 3 years old and was very brave. She wanted to try something new every day and never gave up. One day, Mary decided to try and make a cake. She urged herself to give it a go and try it out.

Mary got all the ingredients and bowls out of the cupboard. She added the ingredients together and stirred it carefully. She put the cake in the oven and waited. Suddenly, an alarm went off and Mary ran to the oven. She opened the oven door, and to her delight, saw a beautiful cake!

Mary was so pleased to see the success of her cake. Everyone was amazed and said it looked very normal. Mary was very proud and excited to have made it. She looked at her cake and said, "I did it, I did it!”

From then on, Mary made cakes whenever she was urged to try something new.

Lily and Ben are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a new boy in the park. He has a big bike and a shiny medal.

"Who is he?" Lily asks Ben.

"I don't know. Let's go and say hello," Ben says.

They run to the new boy and smile.

"Hi, I'm Lily and this is Ben. We are friends. What is your name?" Lily says.

"Hi, I'm Max. I'm new here. I just moved with my mom and dad. This is my bike and this is my medal. I won it in a race," Max says.

"Wow, your bike is cool and your medal is shiny. Can we see it?" Ben says.

"Sure, here you go. But be careful, it's heavy," Max says. He gives them his medal.

Lily and Ben hold the medal and look at it. It has a picture of a bike and some words.

"What does it say?" Lily asks.

"It says 'First Place in the Bike Challenge'. I had to ride my bike very fast and do some tricks. It was fun but also dangerous. I fell down once and hurt my knee," Max says.

"Ouch, that sounds scary. Are you okay?" Ben asks.

"I'm okay. It was just a scratch. My mom put a band-aid on it. Do you want to see?" Max says.

He lifts his pant leg and shows them his band-aid. It has a star on it.

"Wow, that's a nice band-aid. You are brave," Lily says.

"Thank you. You are nice. Do you want to be my friends?" Max says.

"Yes, we want to be your friends. We can play together in the park. Do you want to try the slide?" Ben says.

"Yes, I love the slide. Let's go," Max says.

They give back his medal and run to the slide. They take turns sliding down and laughing. They have a lot of fun. They are happy. They are friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little baby named Max. Max loved to sleep in his crib. He had a yummy bottle of milk before he went to bed every night.

One day, Max's mommy came into his room and said, "Max, do you want to order some yummy pizza for dinner tonight?" Max smiled and said, "Yes, please!"

Mommy called the pizza place and ordered a big pizza with lots of cheese and pepperoni. When the pizza arrived, Max's mommy cut it into tiny pieces so that Max could eat it easily. Max took a bite and said, "Yummy!"

After dinner, Max's mommy put him in his crib and gave him his bottle of milk. Max drank his milk and fell asleep with a happy tummy. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside with her friends. One day, she found a tough piece of candy on the ground. She picked it up and showed it to her friend, Timmy.

"Look, Timmy! I found a tough candy piece!" Lily said.

Timmy peeked at the candy and said, "Wow! That's cool! Can I have a piece?"

Lily broke the candy into two pieces and gave one to Timmy. They both ate the candy and it was very yummy. From that day on, they always looked for candy pieces when they played outside.

Once upon a time, there was a brave little player. One day, the wind blew and he decided to go on an adventure. He was very excited to explore the new land.

Suddenly, something bad happened. He heard a noise and looked around, but he couldn't see anything. Much to his surprise, he noticed something vanishing in the air.

The player asked a nearby bird, "What is happening?" The bird answered, "Bad things happen in this land. You need to be careful."

The player got frightened and quickly ran away. However, it was too late. The bad thing had already vanished, taking him with it. And he never returned. The end.

Once upon a time, there lived a little girl called Mandy. She liked to play dress-up and loved having parties. One day, she decided it was time to have the best dress-up party ever.

Mandy had lots of costumes and even sparkles, but she needed something special to tie it all together. She remembered that she had seen a beautiful yellow needle in her mum's sewing box. She was sure it would match her yellow dress perfectly.

Mandy asked her mum for permission to borrow the needle. Her mum said yes, and Mandy was very excited. She ran to her dresser to get the dress ready for the party. She carefully slipped the needle through the fabric and soon it was finished!

It was perfect! Everyone loved Mandy's dress and she felt like the most special girl at the party. She thanked her mum for letting her borrow the needle and the party guests praised her fabulous costume.

From that day on, Mandy knew that with a little imagination and a sunny yellow needle, she could make any party special.

Once upon a time there was a silly musician. He was walking in the woods one day when he noticed a big tree. Suddenly, he saw a big brown worm on the ground so he bent down and picked it up.

The musician smiled and said, "Hi there, little worm. Would you like to come with me?" The musician was surprised when the worm replied, "Yes, I would love to go with you."

The musician was so excited to have a new friend that he started to jump and dance around. The worm laughed at the musician's silly moves!

Then all of a sudden the musician got too close to the worm and it bit him! The musician screamed and shook his arm. He said, "That was not nice. Why did you bite me?"

The worm replied, "I'm sorry I bit you. I only bit you because I was scared... I just wanted to be friends."

The musician was still a bit angry but he said "It's ok. I forgive you, little worm. Friends should never hurt each other."

The musician and the worm became best friends and went on lots of adventures together.

Once upon a time there lived a boy named Max. He was 3 years old and he loved to make things out of pieces of paper.

One day Max was trying to cut a paper bird with his scissors, but the scissors kept slipping. He was getting very frustrated.

"This is no fun," he said, feeling very miserable.

Just then, Max's mom walked in. She smiled at him and said, "Hey Max, why don't you take a break and come put your scissors away?"

Max sighed and nodded. He put his scissors away in the drawer and carefully went to find his mom.

When he found her, they hugged and she said, "I know it's hard to do things sometimes, but don't ever feel awful about it. You can always try again later."

Max knew she was right, and he smiled. He felt much better.

The end.

Once upon a time, a young boy named Tim liked to study his toys. One day, he found a long chain in his toy box. He looked at it and thought it was very interesting.

Tim showed the chain to his friend, Sally. "Look at my chain," he said. Sally looked at it and said, "Wow, that's a big chain!" Tim and Sally played with the chain all day. They made it into a big circle and pretended it was a race track for their toy cars.

As the sun went down, Tim and Sally knew it was time to go home. They put the chain back in the toy box and said goodbye. Tim was happy that he had a fun day with his friend and the chain. He knew he would study it more tomorrow.

Once there was a girl named Jane. She was three years old and loved playing. Every day she would go to the gym with her family. There she would meet lots of friends.

At the gym she would jump on the trampoline and swing on the swing. It was so much fun! She liked to wear her ordinary t-shirt and pair of shorts when she went.

Sometimes at the gym, she would play with the balls. It was really exciting to toss the balls in the air and make them bounce around.

Everyone in the gym thought Jane was so special. She was so happy to meet all her friends in the gym. Every day when she left she said goodbye to all of them.

She was an ordinary three year old, but the hours spent in the gym were so extraordinary.

John was so excited to start painting! He grabbed his brush and some paints and went outside with his mom.

John's mom showed him a big white wall and she asked him to paint it. John was so amazed. He was ready to start painting the wall and the paints made it look so beautiful!

After painting, John heard a music coming from nearby. He looked around and saw a man playing a flute. John liked the music so much and asked his mom if he could play it. John's mom said that it was available for him to play.

John was so happy to learn how to play the flute. He practiced playing it every day till he got very good. John's mom was so proud of him!

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy liked to play with his toys, especially his toy cars. One day, Timmy's friend Billy came over to play. Billy had a toy weapon that he wanted to show Timmy. Timmy got nervous when he saw the weapon because he didn't like scary things.

Billy noticed that Timmy was nervous, so he put the weapon away and they decided to play with Timmy's toy cars instead. They pretended that the cars were racing and they even tried to number the cars in order from 1 to 10. Timmy was happy that they were playing with his cars and not the scary weapon.

After they finished playing, Timmy's mom gave them some cookies and milk. They sat at the table and talked about their favorite toys. Timmy told Billy that he liked his toy cars the best and Billy said that he liked his toy weapon, but he promised not to bring it over again if it made Timmy nervous. From that day on, they had fun playing together without any scary weapons. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a 3 year old boy who lived in a small town. He was always hungry for adventure and wanted to explore the world around him.

One day, his mom decided to lend him some money so he could go buy some fun junk like candy and toys. He was so excited and immediately ran out to find the perfect items.

He returned home with his junk and handed it to his mother. She was not happy and told him that he should not use money on junk, and that he should always be ready to do something more meaningful with it.

But the 3 year old didn't understand and kept buying junk with his mom's money. After a while, she ran out of money and could no longer lend him any.

The moral of the story is that if you borrow something, you should use it wisely and be ready to take responsibility for it. If you don't, you will eventually run out of the resources you need.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Jane. Jane was always very lonely and did not have any friends. One day, she decided to kneel down and prayed for a friend. Jane believed that if she asked God, he would send her a friend.

The next day, an angel appeared in Jane's room holding a calendar and said: "Little girl, God has heard your prayer. He is sending you a friend. Look in the calendar every day until your friend comes." With that, the angel disappeared.

Jane was so excited! Every day she looked in the calendar but saw only birthday parties and school events. She started to feel very lonely again.

One week later, Jane was feeling sad when suddenly a loud voice said "Hi!" It was a little bunny! Jane was so surprised, she couldn't believe her eyes. The bunny said: "God sent me to be your friend."

The bunny spent all day with Jane, helping her with her chores and playing games with her. From that day on, Jane was never lonely again.

The End.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play outside in his backyard. One day, he saw a long snake slithering around. Timmy was scared of the snake, but he knew he had to be brave. He went inside to get his dad, who helped him organize a plan to safely remove the snake from the backyard. They used a long stick to gently guide the snake into a box, and then they took it to a nearby field where it could live safely. Timmy felt proud that he was able to help organize the snake's relocation. From that day on, Timmy wasn't afraid of snakes anymore.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, Lily and her mom went outside to play. It was very cold outside, and Lily's mom told her to wear a warm coat. Lily didn't want to wear a coat because she didn't like how it felt.

Lily's mom said, "You have to wear a coat, or you will get sick." Lily didn't want to get sick, so she put on her coat. They played outside for a little while, but then Lily got tired and wanted to go inside.

When they went inside, Lily's mom had to work on some things. Lily asked her mom, "Can we play?" Her mom said, "I have to work now, but we can play later." Lily said, "Okay, I hope we can play soon!"

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. He loved to play with his ball and kick it around all day. One day, his mom made him a yummy meal of macaroni and cheese. Timmy gobbled it up quickly and went back to playing.

As he was kicking his ball around, he accidentally kicked it too hard and it went into the street. Timmy ran after it without looking both ways and a car hit him. His mom came running outside, worried and crying.

The ambulance came and took Timmy to the hospital, but unfortunately, he didn't make it. His mom was very sad and wished she had told him to be more careful. The moral of the story is to always look both ways before crossing the street.

Once upon a time, a little girl had a special bag. She kept all her favourite things inside it. She played with her bag every day. One day, she wanted to show her bag to her friends. She decided to take it to the park.

When she got to the park, she was so excited that she jumped and dived into the grass. Her bag flew out of her hands and landed in a big, messy pile of leaves. She was so sad. She carefully looked through the pile of leaves but she couldn't find it.

Suddenly, she heard a funny noise coming from one of the bushes. She looked closer and saw that her bag was hiding under the leaves! She was so happy and carefully picked it up. She quickly opened it and all of her favourite things were inside, safe and sound.

She put the bag back on her shoulder and gave it a big hug. The little girl never let it out of her sight again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Sarah. She was three years old. Everyday Sarah would set her pillow on the bed.

But one day, when Sarah went to set her pillow she noticed it felt different - it was cold.

She went over to her mommy and said “Mama, something is wrong with my pillow. It’s cold.”

Her mommy replied, “It’s ok Sarah. I’ll fix it.”

So Mama got a blanket and set it on top of the pillow.

Sarah smiled and said, “Oh, that’s much better. Now it’s nice and warm. Thank you, Mama!”

Mama smiled and said, “You’re welcome, Sarah. Now you can have a nice rest!”

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play golf with his dad. One day, Timmy's dad was very impatient and didn't want to play golf with Timmy. Timmy felt sad because he wanted to play with his dad.

Timmy's older brother saw that Timmy was sad and decided to tease him. He took Timmy's golf club and started playing with it himself. Timmy didn't like it and started crying.

Timmy's dad saw what was happening and told his older son to stop teasing Timmy. He then apologized to Timmy and promised to play golf with him. Timmy was happy again and they all went to play golf together.

Little Timmy was very curious. Everywhere he looked, he saw symbols. From circles and stars to squares and triangles, they were all around! He couldn't help but wonder what the symbols meant.

One day, Timmy heard a whisper in the wind. At first he was scared but he soon realised it was just a small request calling. He listened closely and he soon realised it was asking him to come closer.

Timmy followed the voice and discovered a large symbol. He wasn't sure what it was but he knew it was special. The voice asked him to use the symbol but Timmy didn't know what it did. He was curious and excited.

Timmy waited for hours until a mysterious figure appeared. They explained to Timmy that the symbol was special and that it held an amazing power. They told him that if he requested it, the power would become available.

Timmy was hesitant but he decided to take a chance and make the request. Suddenly, the symbol lit up and a remarkable energy filled the air! Timmy was amazed and couldn't believe what had just happened. He was grateful to learn that an adventure was just around the corner.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Hannah. Hannah was very naughty and often broke things in the house. But today, Hannah was in a good mood and decided to try and be helpful. She noticed that her mum's alarm was not working and she decided to try and fix it.

Hannah went to the kitchen, opened a drawer and started to look for tools. She found a screwdriver and a hammer and started to look at the alarm. After some time, she managed to fix it. She was so proud of herself for helping her mum.

The next morning, the alarm started ringing and Hannah's mum was so happy. She praised Hannah and made her yummy pancakes for breakfast as a reward. Hannah felt so good knowing that she had done something helpful.

From then on, Hannah learned the importance of helping others. She understood how proud she felt when she managed to fix the alarm and how happy her mum was. She realised that doing good deeds and helping others always brings happiness!

One day, Mommy gave Little Jimmy a very special job. "Can you help me clean up the garage?" she asked. Little Jimmy was very obedient and immediately said yes. He began to look around for something to clean. He spotted something shiny on the floor. It was a screw!

He picked it up and took it to Mommy. "What is this?" Little Jimmy asked.

Mommy smiled. "That's a screw," she said. "Thank you for picking it up! That was a very obedient thing to do."

Little Jimmy was so proud that he had done something helpful. He stuck the screw in his pocket and continued cleaning the garage. In no time, the garage was all nice and neat!

Mommy hugged Little Jimmy and said, "I am so proud of you. You did a wonderful job cleaning the garage." Little Jimmy smiled. He had been so obedient and he felt very proud.

Lily likes apples. She likes red apples and green apples and yellow apples. She likes to eat them and to play with them. She likes to roll them and toss them and catch them.

One day, Lily sees a big tree with many apples. She runs to the tree and looks up. She sees red apples and green apples and yellow apples. She wants to pick one and eat it. But the apples are too high. She cannot reach them.

She sees a stool near the tree. She thinks it can help her. She drags the stool to the tree and climbs on it. She stands on the stool and stretches her arms. She can reach some apples now. She grabs a red apple and pulls it. It is hard and shiny and sweet.

She sees another apple. It is not red or green or yellow. It is different. It is brown and soft and wrinkled. She wonders what it is. She reaches for it and touches it. It is squishy and sticky and yucky. She does not like it. She drops it and makes a face.

She decides to eat the red apple instead. She bites it and smiles. It is crunchy and juicy and yummy. She likes apples. She likes red apples and green apples and yellow apples. But she does not like different apples. She thinks they are bad. She throws the different apple away and picks another red apple. She is happy.

One day a little girl named Emma wanted to go to the pool. It was a hot summer day and she was excited to go. She got her floaties on and turned to her mom, "Can I dive in?" Mom nodded and Emma ran to the side. She looked down into the pool and saw a long, pink thing floating at the bottom.

Mom said, "What is that?" Emma bent over the side and said, "I don't know, but I want to dive and get it!" She told her mom, "I'm gonna get it!" Mom said, "Be careful."

So Emma took a deep breath and dove in. She went as deep as she could and grabbed the long, pink thing. She hurried to the surface and brought it to the side.

But as soon as she saw it, she knew it was a snake! It was a long, pink snake. Emma screamed and jumped back. The snake hissed and slithered away. Emma was so scared and her mom had to take her home.

The bad ending ruined her day!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the sunshine with her friends. One day, they decided to play a game of tag. Lily was scared to be "it" because she didn't dare to run fast enough to catch her friends.

As they were playing, Lily noticed her shadow on the ground. She thought it was funny how her shadow followed her every move. She tried to run away from it, but it always stayed close by.

Suddenly, Lily tripped and fell down. She scraped her knee and started to cry. Her friends quickly came to her side and asked if they could be helpful. They gave her a band-aid and helped her stand up. Lily felt grateful for her helpful friends and knew she was lucky to have them.

There was a young boy named Tim. Tim loved to play basketball. One day, he wanted to go to the park to play with his friends.

Before he left, his mom said, "Tim, pack a bag with snacks and water." So Tim packed a bag with yummy treats and a big bottle of water.

At the park, Tim and his friends played basketball. They were having so much fun. But then, it started to rain. The rain was heavy and the wind was strong. Tim and his friends had to stop playing and go home. Tim was sad because he couldn't play basketball anymore.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Jane. She liked to spend time outdoors, especially on a sunny day. One morning, she decided to go for a walk with her brother Joe.

On the way, they heard lots of noisy birds singing in the trees. Jane and Joe began to laugh with delight!

When they arrived at the park, they saw some children playing and having fun. Joe asked Jane, “Aren't they noisy?”

“Yes,” said Jane, “But this is still a nice place to spend time.”

So, Jane and Joe decided to spend the day at the park. They played tag, climbed a tree and enjoyed the sunny day!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, Lily's mom asked her to clean up her room. Lily didn't want to do it, but her mom said it was important to be organized. So Lily started to pick up her toys and put them away.

As Lily was cleaning, her friend Sarah came over to play. Sarah saw Lily cleaning and said, "What are you doing?" Lily replied, "I'm cleaning my room. My mom said it's important to be organized."

Sarah thought for a moment and said, "That's a good idea. I should do that too." So Sarah helped Lily clean up her room. When they were finished, Lily's mom came in and said, "Wow, you two did a great job! Your room looks so nice and organized now." Lily and Sarah smiled proudly at each other, happy that they had started the day by doing something helpful.

Tom is a big boy who likes to work. He helps his dad with the farm. He feeds the cows, he waters the plants, he picks the eggs. He is strong and fast and happy.

One day, Tom sees a big hill behind the farm. He wants to see what is on the other side. He asks his dad if he can go. His dad says yes, but be careful and come back soon. Tom says okay and runs to the hill.

Tom climbs the hill. It is hard and steep and long. He gets tired and sweaty and thirsty. But he does not give up. He wants to see the view. He reaches the top and looks around. He sees the farm, the cows, the plants, the eggs. He sees the road, the cars, the people, the shops. He sees the sky, the sun, the clouds, the birds. He sees a lot of things he has never seen before. He is amazed and happy.

Tom stays on the hill for a while. He enjoys the view. He feels proud of himself. He did a good work. He is strong and fast and happy. He decides to go back to the farm. He runs down the hill. He sees his dad waiting for him. His dad smiles and hugs him. He tells him he is proud of him too. He asks him what he saw. Tom tells him everything. They go back to the farm together. They are strong and fast and happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy was always busy playing with his toys and never had time to talk to his friends. One day, Timmy's friend Sarah came to visit him, but Timmy was too busy playing to talk to her. Sarah felt sad and left.

That night, Timmy felt lonely and wished he had talked to Sarah. He regretted not spending time with her. The next day, Timmy went to Sarah's house to apologize, but it was too late. Sarah had moved away.

Timmy felt very sad and realized that he had lost a good friend because he was always too busy. He wished he had made time for Sarah and regretted not doing so. From that day on, Timmy promised to make time for his friends and not be too busy playing with his toys.

Once upon a time, there was a very lonely little girl. Each day, she would go outside and fold origami animals in her garden. She was always very careful with each fold, feeling the paper between her tiny fingers. Every time she looked up, she would catch her reflection in the neighbour's mirror.

Later that afternoon, the little girl decided to go explore the neighbour's garden. She went around the corner and saw the mirror reflecting the sun's rays. She approached it slowly with her arms wide open.

Suddenly, the little girl heard a voice coming from behind the mirror.

"Why do you look so lonely today?" The voice asked, crinkling its nose.

The little girl was so excited. She said she was looking for someone to share her origami animals with.

The voice replied with a smile "Come closer and see what I can do..."

The little girl stepped closer and the mirror slowly started to open up. Behind it was a tiny fairy!

The little girl gasped in delight and carefully took the origami animals out of her pocket. As the fairy picked each one up, the animals started to come to life!

From that day on, the little girl was no longer lonely. She and the fairy spent all their time playing together. The fairy even taught her how to fold origami animals even more complicated and beautiful than the ones she was used to making.

Mary and her Dad were in the garden. Dad took out a rake and smiled at Mary.

"What are you doing?" Mary asked.

"I'm going to help the birds to make their home," Dad said.

He started raking and stirring the leaves on the ground in a big circle.

Mary helped too. She was feeling happy and smiley. Soon the circle was just the right size.

"Now let's put something soft and pink in the middle so the birds can settle," said Dad.

He found some pretty pink flowers and he and Mary carefully put them in the middle of the circle.

Soon two birds flew in! They hopped over to the pink flowers and settled down into the middle of the circle.

Mary felt proud and smiled. Dad said quietly, "Now we have a happy bird home!"

Once upon a time there was a kind boy who lived near a big forest. Every day, he liked to go to the forest to explore and play.

One day, as he was walking in the forest, the boy saw something that made him very happy. It was a big, bright butterfly. He wanted to grab it and show his mom.

The boy reached out to grab the butterfly but it flew away! He tried over and over but it wouldn’t stay still. The butterfly went higher and higher until it was out of sight.

The kind boy was sad that he couldn’t grab the butterfly, but he still had a fun day in the forest playing. He smiled and continued his journey.

THE

Lily and Max were hungry. They wanted a snack. They went to the kitchen and looked at the fridge. The fridge was big and white and cold. It had many good things inside.

Lily opened the fridge and saw a bowl of grapes. She liked grapes. They were sweet and juicy. She took the bowl and said, "I want grapes, Max. Do you want some?"

Max looked at the fridge and saw a jar of cookies. He liked cookies. They were crunchy and yummy. He took the jar and said, "I want cookies, Lily. Do you want some?"

Lily and Max sat on the floor and ate their snacks. They did not ask Mom or Dad if they could have them. They did not think they needed to ask. They were happy.

But then Mom came into the kitchen. She saw Lily and Max and the empty bowl and jar. She was not happy. She said, "Lily and Max, what are you doing? Why did you take the grapes and the cookies without asking me or Dad? Those were for later. You should not take things without asking. That is not nice. That is not dependable."

Lily and Max felt bad. They did not want to make Mom unhappy. They did not know they had to ask. They said, "We are sorry, Mom. We were hungry. We wanted a snack. We did not know we had to ask. We will ask next time. We want to be nice. We want to be dependable."

Mom hugged Lily and Max. She said, "I forgive you, Lily and Max. I know you did not mean to be bad. But you have to learn to ask before you take things. That is the polite thing to do. That is the dependable thing to do. Then we can share and be happy together. Do you understand?"

Lily and Max nodded. They said, "We understand, Mom. We will ask next time. We love you, Mom. You are nice. You are dependable."

Mom smiled. She said, "I love you too, Lily and Max. You are nice. You are dependable. Now let's go and find something else to eat. Something healthy and tasty. And we will ask Dad if he wants some too."

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She was playing with her toys when she saw her friend Timmy coming towards her.

"Hi Lily!" Timmy said.

"Hi Timmy!" Lily replied.

Timmy saw that Lily had a triangle toy and he wanted to play with it. "Can I play with your triangle?" he asked.

Lily didn't want to share her toy. "No, it's mine," she said.

Timmy got upset and said, "That's not fair! You always own everything!"

Lily felt bad and thought about it. She realized that she should share her toys with her friends. "Okay, you can play with it," she said.

Timmy was happy and they played together. They both had fun and enjoyed playing with the thick triangle toy.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Sam. One day Sam was playing in the park with her mom. Suddenly, Sam's mom urged Sam to come have a picture taken with her.

But Sam was feeling frustrated and angry. She didn't want to pose for the photo. She wanted to keep playing.

Mom said to Sam, "Come on, we need to take this photo! It would make me so happy!"

But Sam didn't budge, she was still feeling angry. Mom looked at Sam and gently said, "Please, take this photo with me. I want us to have this special moment forever."

Finally, Sam said yes. She and her mom smiled and posed for the photo. And this way, the two of them were able to keep the memory forever.

Lily was a girl who liked to play with her blue cap. She wore it every day, even when it was hot or cold. She liked how it made her feel happy and cool.

One day, she went to the park with her mom and saw a boy who had no cap. He looked sad and lonely. Lily wanted to be his friend, so she ran to him and said, "Hi, I'm Lily. Do you want to play with me?"

The boy looked up and smiled. He said, "Hi, I'm Ben. I would like to play with you, but I have no cap. The sun hurts my eyes and head."

Lily felt sorry for Ben. She thought of a way to help him. She took off her blue cap and put it on his head. She said, "Here, you can have my cap. It will make you feel better. We can share it and play together."

Ben was surprised and happy. He said, "Thank you, Lily. You are very kind and generous. Your cap is very nice and blue. It makes me feel happy and cool too."

Lily and Ben became friends and played in the park. They took turns wearing the blue cap and had fun. Lily's mom saw them and smiled. She was proud of Lily for sharing her cap and making a new friend.

The moral of the story is: Sharing is caring. When we share what we have with others, we can make them happy and ourselves happy too.

Harry was very hungry. He wanted to eat a potato for dinner. But he was nervous about cooking it. He had never cooked a potato before.

His mom saw him looking nervous and said, "Don't worry Harry. Cooking a potato isn't hard. Let me show you how."

Harry was very excited. He watched as his mom put the potato in the pot and filled it up with water. She then put the pot on the stove and turned it on.

After a few minutes, his mom checked the potato. "It's ready!", she said. But Harry wanted to wait a little bit. He wanted the potato to be extra cooked.

His mom smiled and said, "Ok, no problem. We can delay a bit longer to cook the potato."

Harry was so happy. Before he knew it, dinner was ready. It was the best potato he ever tasted.

Once upon a time, there was a graceful cat. Her name was Paw. She had a big box with her.

One day, Paw decided to unpack it. She opened the box and took out all the things inside. First, she took out a toy mouse. Then she took out a fluffy blanket. Finally she took out a ball of yarn.

Paw was very happy with all her new things. She played with the mouse and the yarn, and curled up inside the blanket. Every day she enjoyed the things she had unpacked from the box.

The end.

Once upon a time there was a girl called Jill. She was very helpful and often helped her mom with doing the washing and cooking. One day, when Jill was helping her mom she noticed something very shiny on the kitchen table. It was a knife! She was very interested in the shiny object so she picked it up and showed her mom.

"Jill, be careful with that. That is a knife and it can be dangerous," her mom said.

"Ok mommy, I won't touch it," said Jill.

Jill's mom was very relieved and thanked Jill for being so helpful.

The next day, Jill was in the kitchen and she noticed the same shiny object. She quickly realized that it was the same knife from the day before. But this time she didn't need to ask her mom what it was. She had recognized it and knew it was a knife. From that day on, she was always careful when she saw the shiny knife. She had learned to recognize the knife and to respect it.

The end.

Jan and her mom got to the park. It was very sunny, so Jan's mom got an umbrella for them to share. They played for a while, and then Jan got busy. She was making a masterpiece with sticks and leaves. When she was all done, she got a big surprise! There were tiny bugs walking around in the leaves. Jan and her mom got so excited and they laughed and laughed.

Soon it was time to go home, and they got an umbrella to keep them dry. Jan loved getting an umbrella to use, and they laughed some more as they went on their way. When they got back home, Jan's mom was very busy. She made Jan lunch and made sure she had everything she needed for the day. Jan was happy to get a break from the busy day and rested for a while before she got ready for bed.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Emmy. She was three years old. Emmy watched her dad record a song on his computer. She asked him what he was doing.

"I'm recording a song," he said.

Emmy asked, "What's recording?"

"It means I'm making a copy of the song," he explained.

After the recording was done, Emmy smiled and asked, "Can I record a song, too?"

Her dad said, "Sure!"

They searched around until they found Emmy's old toy recorder and she put a tooth in the recorder to make it work. The sound was a bit strange and bitter, but Emmy sang along and her dad danced and they laughed together.

After a while, Emmy took out the tooth and recorded a copy of the song.

"See, I recorded a song too!" Emmy said excitedly.

Her dad smiled. "I think you just made a lifelong memory!" he said.

Emmy smiled back, happy to have recorded a song.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She liked to go to the shop with her mommy. One day, as they were walking to the shop, Lily saw a little bird on a tree. The bird was singing a beautiful song.

"Listen, mommy, the bird is singing!" Lily said.

"Yes, it's a lovely song," her mommy replied.

At the shop, Lily saw a toy she wanted. She asked her mommy if she could have it, but her mommy said no.

"You can save your money and buy it yourself," her mommy said.

Lily was sad at first, but then she remembered that she wanted to be independent. She decided to save her money and buy the toy on her own.

A few weeks later, Lily went back to the shop with her saved money. She bought the toy and felt very proud of herself. "I did it all by myself!" she said.

From that day on, Lily learned that if she listened to her mommy and saved her money, she could be an independent girl who could buy the things she wanted.

Once, there was a farmer who had to make a long journey. To make sure he was ready for the adventure, he packed his bag. He put in food, clothes and more. He even packed a shovel - it was deep and heavy!

The farmer began his journey and walked a very long way. He crossed rivers, walked through a deep forest and climbed a mountain. Finally, he arrived at his destination.

The farmer was so happy he had packed all the things he needed. Without them, he wouldn't have been able to complete his journey! He looked deep into the horizon and grinned. His adventure had officially begun.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys, especially her dollhouse. One day, Lily's mom gave her a big box of toys to play with.

Lily was excited to play with her new toys, but she didn't know where to put them. She decided to sort them into different piles. She put all the dolls in one pile, the cars in another, and the blocks in a third.

As Lily was sorting her toys, she noticed a strange cell in the bottom of the box. It looked like a small room with metal bars on the front. Lily didn't know what it was for, but it made her feel uncomfortable.

Later that day, Lily's mom told her that the cell was actually a cage for a pet hamster. Lily was surprised and excited to have a new pet. She named him Hammy and made him a cozy bed in the cell. From that day on, Lily loved playing with her toys and taking care of her new pet.

Lily likes to look at magazines. She likes the pictures of animals and people and things. She has a lot of magazines in her room. She keeps them in a big box.

One day, Lily finds a new magazine in the box. It is different from the others. It has a shiny cover and a lot of colors. It says "Unique" on the top. Lily thinks it is a special magazine. She wants to see what is inside.

She opens the magazine and sees more pictures. She sees a picture of a snake. It is long and green and has a forked tongue. Lily is curious. She touches the snake with her finger. It feels smooth and cold.

She moves her finger closer to the snake's mouth. She wonders what it would do. She does not know that the snake is not real. It is a sticker. It has a spring inside. It can bite.

The snake bites Lily's finger. It makes a snapping sound. Lily feels a pinch. She is scared and surprised. She drops the magazine and cries. She runs to her mom.

Mom hears Lily's cry and comes to her room. She sees the magazine on the floor and the snake sticker on Lily's finger. She understands what happened. She hugs Lily and takes off the sticker. She kisses Lily's finger and makes it better.

She tells Lily that the snake is not real. It is a toy. It is meant to be funny, not scary. She tells Lily that she is brave and smart. She tells Lily that she is unique, just like the magazine. Lily smiles and hugs her mom. She feels better. She still likes magazines, but she does not like snakes.

Once upon a time, there was a little birdie who loved to fly high in the sky. One day, the little birdie was flying around when he saw a big, scary hawk. The little birdie started to panic and tried to fly away, but the hawk was too fast.

The little birdie's mother was watching from a nearby tree and saw what was happening. She tried to fly over to help, but she wasn't very graceful and bumped into some branches. The little birdie was getting closer and closer to the hawk, and his mother knew she had to do something.

Suddenly, the mother bird saw a big gust of wind coming. She knew it was her chance to save her little birdie. She flew as fast as she could and pushed her little birdie out of the way just in time. But the hawk caught the mother bird instead and flew away with her. The little birdie was sad and missed his mother very much.

Once there was a girl named Mary. Mary loved to draw in her notebook. One day, Mary was drawing in her notebook when she heard a loud scream coming from outside her window. She was scared and dropped the thin notebook on the ground. Mary quickly ran to the window to see what had made the loud noise. It was a little bird with an injured wing. Mary felt sorry for the bird, so she grabbed her thin notebook and raced outside to help it. She carefully placed the bird on the notebook and took it to a nearby vet. The bird was taken care of and eventually flew away. Mary was so happy and she waved goodbye to the bird with her thin notebook in hand.

Once upon a time, there was a puppy called Misty. Misty was very happy and she liked to sing.

One day, Misty went to a singing contest. She was a little bit nervous, so she looked around and saw some other puppies singing.

Suddenly the judges said "Misty, it is your turn now!". So Misty began to sing. Everyone in the crowd got very excited.

When Misty finished singing, the judges announced that she was the most successful puppy! Misty was very happy and she started to sing a new song. Everyone clapped and cheered.

In the end, Misty was very proud of herself. She sang a happy song all the way home.

Once there was a little girl named Stacy who loved exploring. She had a big backyard that was full of exciting places to adventure to. One sunny day, she decided that it was time to explore and began her journey.

As she was walking around, Stacy heard a strange noise coming from behind a bush. She decided to take a closer look. She moved a few leaves aside, and there sat a tiny frog. It made her smile.

"Hello, Frog!" Stacy said happily.

The frog was quiet. It just looked at Stacy with its big, shiny eyes.

Stacy reached out to pinch the frog's back and it suddenly began to hop away. She laughed and ran to keep up with it. As they ran, Stacy could feel the warm sun on her head and she smiled, happy to be outside in the quiet backyard.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Peter. Peter was three years old. He was a very helpful person, always looking for ways to organize things.

One day, Peter was given a box of masks. He was so delighted! He quickly took out all of the masks, and tried to organize them in the box.

But Peter was having trouble. He just couldn't quite get them to fit. Suddenly, he heard a very rude voice. It was an old man who said, "What do you think you're doing, young man? You'll never get them to fit like that! Get out of my way!"

Peter was very embarrassed, but he decided he could still organize the masks. He rearranged them in neat piles, and soon the box was full. He was so proud of himself.

The old man, who wasn't so old anymore, was very impressed. He said, "Good job, young man! That's how all masks should be organized."

And that's how Peter learned to organize masks in the most helpful way possible.

Anna and Ben are playing in the park. They like to swing, slide and run. They are having fun.

But it is a hot day. The sun is very bright and makes them sweat. They need to drink water.

"Anna, Ben, come here!" Mom calls. "You need to drink some water. It is good for you."

Anna and Ben run to Mom. She has a bottle of water for each of them. She gives them the bottles.

"Thank you, Mom!" Anna says. She opens her bottle and drinks some water. It is cold and fresh. She feels better.

But Ben does not want to drink water. He thinks water is boring. He wants juice or soda. He refuses to open his bottle.

"No, thank you, Mom!" Ben says. "I don't want water. Water is boring. I want juice or soda. They are yummy and fun."

Mom shakes her head. She is not happy. She knows juice and soda have too much sugar. They are not good for Ben.

"Ben, you need to drink water. Water is not boring. Water is healthy and important. It helps you stay cool and strong. Juice and soda have too much sugar. They can make you sick and tired. Please drink some water."

But Ben still refuses to drink water. He puts his bottle down and runs away. He wants to play more.

Mom sighs. She hopes Ben will change his mind. She does not want him to get thirsty or sick. She loves him very much.

Jimbo was a happy little boy that enjoyed playing with his friends. One day Jimbo was playing in the park when he noticed his friends were worried. They were pointing to the sky and telling Jimbo they were scared of the dark clouds.

Jimbo was worried too but he wanted his friends to feel better. He remembered his father once told him that being brave was the best way to solve a problem. So Jimbo got an idea. Jimbo ran to the toy store and bought a few cheap kites with his allowance.

He ran back to the park and handed one kite to each of his friends. Jimbo showed them how to fly the kite and soon enough the dark clouds were replaced with bright colors. His friends laughed and cheered.

Jimbo was proud that he helped his friends not worry anymore. He was glad that kite flying was an easy and cheap way to make them smile again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her dolls and toys. One day, she went to her mom and said, "Mommy, I don't know what to do. I'm bored."

Her mom said, "Why don't you make a pattern with your toys? You can put them in a line or a circle."

Lily thought this was a good idea and started to make a pattern with her dolls and toys. She put them in a circle and then in a line. It was fun!

After a while, Lily's dad came home and saw the pattern. He said, "Wow, Lily! That's really cool. You're so creative."

Lily felt happy and proud. She knew that making a pattern was normal for her, but it was still fun to hear her dad say it.

Once upon a time, there was a girl. Her name was Lucy. She was three years old.

One day, Lucy wanted to go for an adventure. She put on her shoes and went for a walk in the park.

As she was walking, Lucy found something huge. It was a navy thing! She looked closer and saw it was the biggest ship she had ever seen.

Lucy was so excited that she had found the huge navy ship. She ran around it, touching its sides and wondeirng how it got so big.

When her mom came to pick her up, Lucy was bursting with excitement. She told her mom all about her big discovery.

That day, Lucy felt so proud of herself. She was so happy to find the huge navy ship. The end.

Once upon a time there were two friends, Tom and Sally. Tom had a very special surprise for Sally - a maze!

Tom said to Sally, "Hey Sally, do you want to play a funny game?"

Sally replied, "Yeah, what game?"

Tom said, "Let's play in the maze! I'll lead you through it!"

Sally got very excited and said, "Yes, let's go!"

Tom led Sally through the maze, and they had a lot of fun. They laughed and ran from room to room, going around corners and up and down stairs.

At the end of the maze, Sally said, "This was so much fun! Can we do it again?"

Tom smiled and said, "Of course! Let's go again!"

So, Tom and Sally went back into the maze and had a lot more fun. They laughed and ran, discovering new places as Tom led the way.

Lily and Tom were twins who liked to travel with their mom and dad. They went to many places and saw many things. They always had fun and learned new words.

One day, they went to a big park with many animals. They saw lions, monkeys, elephants, and more. They also saw a big sign that said "Mystery House". Lily and Tom were curious and wanted to go inside.

"Can we go, mom? Can we go, dad?" they asked.

"Sure, why not?" mom said. "But be careful, it might be scary."

Lily and Tom nodded and followed mom and dad to the Mystery House. They paid some coins and entered a dark room. There were many strange sounds and lights. Lily and Tom felt nervous but excited.

They walked around and saw many things that made them wonder. They saw a big snake that could talk, a mirror that showed different faces, a clock that went backwards, and a door that led to nowhere.

"Wow, this is so unique!" Lily said.

"I know, right?" Tom said. "But how do they do it?"

They wanted to find out, so they looked for clues. They saw some wires, some buttons, some speakers, and some masks. They realized that the Mystery House was not real, but a trick.

They felt smart and happy. They told mom and dad what they found. Mom and dad smiled and praised them.

"You are very clever, Lily and Tom," mom said. "You solved the mystery."

"Yes, you did," dad said. "You are great travelers."

Lily and Tom hugged mom and dad. They felt proud and loved. They had a wonderful day at the park.

Once upon a time, there was a hungry little boy who loved exploring. On his way to the woods, he stopped to observe a small inchworm on the ground. He thought it was fascinating, and wanted to take it home to feed it. He carefully picked up the inchworm and started walking towards the woods.

Suddenly, a large bear appeared from behind a tree. The bear seemed very hungry, and started to sniff the inchworm in the boy's hands. The boy started to tremble, not knowing what to do. He tried to back away, but the bear stopped him.

The bear said, "I'm so hungry. Give me the inchworm and I'll go away!" The little boy was so scared. He tried to ask the bear to leave, but the bear kept snarling. He had no choice but to give the bear the inchworm.

As the bear left with his food, the sad little boy started to get angry. He couldn't believe that his inchworm was gone and he would never see it again. He knew then that he must always be careful when observing animals in the forest. The End.

Anna and Ben were adventurous kids. They liked to play in the park and explore new things. One day, they saw a big tree with a rope hanging from a branch. They wanted to swing on the rope and have fun.

"Look, Ben, a rope!" Anna said. "Let's try it!"

"OK, Anna, but be careful!" Ben said. He helped Anna climb the tree and hold the rope. Anna was excited and scared at the same time. She swung on the rope and felt the wind in her hair.

"Wow, this is fun!" Anna shouted. "Come on, Ben, you try it too!"

Ben climbed the tree and grabbed the rope. He swung on the rope and felt happy. He smiled at Anna and said, "This is awesome!"

But then, something bad happened. The rope broke and Ben fell to the ground. He landed on some leaves and grass, but he still hurt his arm. He cried out loud and said, "Ow, ow, ow!"

Anna saw Ben fall and panic. She was afraid that Ben was hurt badly. She climbed down the tree and ran to Ben. She hugged him and said, "Ben, are you OK? I'm sorry, I'm sorry!"

Ben looked at Anna and said, "It's OK, Anna, don't worry. It's not your fault. The rope was old and weak. I just have a scratch on my arm. It's not a big deal."

Anna felt relieved and said, "I'm glad you're OK, Ben. You're brave and strong. But maybe we should go home and tell Mom and Dad. They can help you with your arm and give you a hug."

Ben nodded and said, "OK, Anna, let's go home. But can we come back to the park another day? There are still many things to explore and have fun with."

Anna smiled and said, "Sure, Ben, we can come back another day. We are adventurous kids, after all. But next time, let's be more careful and check the rope first."

They held hands and walked home. They learned a lesson and still had a good day. They were adventurous kids, but they also loved each other.

Once upon a time there was a girl called Tina. She was a very troubled girl because she was looking for something very special. Every day she went to different places and searched high and low.

One day, she stumbled across an old safe. She was so excited, but knew she needed help to get inside. She searched for somebody who could help her and eventually found a friendly man nearby. He was happy to help and agreed to open the safe up for her.

Once the safe was opened, Tina couldn't believe her eyes! Inside was a beautiful sparkling jewel which had been lost for many years. She was overjoyed and suddenly didn't feel so troubled anymore. She thanked the man and ran home as quickly as she could to share the wonderful news.

And that's how Tina found her precious jewel inside the safe. She was so happy she could hardly believe it was true! Together with her family, Tina celebrated the joyous occasion and that's how the story ends.

Once upon a time, there was a soft, little cat named Fluffy. Fluffy had lots of fur. It was very soft and nice to touch. Fluffy lived in a small house with a girl named Lily. They were best friends.

One day, Fluffy lost her toy mouse. She looked everywhere, but she could not find it. Fluffy was very sad. She went to Lily and said, "I can't remember where my toy mouse is. Can you help me find it?"

Lily said, "Of course, Fluffy! Let's look together." They looked in the living room, the kitchen, and the garden. Finally, they found the toy mouse under Lily's bed. Fluffy was so happy and thanked Lily for helping her.

From that day on, Fluffy always remembered to keep her toy mouse safe. And Lily and Fluffy played together every day, with the soft fur of Fluffy and her toy mouse. They lived happily ever after.

Once there was a little boy. He loved to peek around. Every day he would explore and look in new places. One day the little boy wanted to find something special. He went to the garden to peek around. He saw something red and round. It was an apple! He reached out and picked it up. The apple felt tough. He knew he needed to work to get it. The little boy put the apple in his pocket and started to run. He ran all the way to his house and showed the apple to his family. Everyone was excited! The little boy smiled and felt so proud of his apple. He had done it himself. He had found a tough apple. It made him feel brave.

Lily was grumpy today. She did not want to get up from her bed. She did not want to eat her breakfast. She did not want to play with her toys. She only wanted to watch her favorite show on the TV.

But Mommy said no. Mommy said Lily had to get ready for school. Mommy said Lily had to eat her breakfast. Mommy said Lily had to play with her toys. Mommy said Lily could not watch TV all day.

Lily sighed. She did not like what Mommy said. She crossed her arms and pouted. She said, "I don't want to go to school. I don't want to eat. I don't want to play. I want to watch TV."

Mommy sighed too. She did not like what Lily said. She bent down and hugged Lily. She said, "I know you are grumpy today, but school is fun. Breakfast is yummy. Toys are fun. TV is not good for you all day. You can watch TV later, after school, if you are good."

Lily sighed again. She did not want to hug Mommy. She did not want to listen to Mommy. She wanted to watch TV. But she saw Mommy's face. Mommy looked sad. Lily did not want to make Mommy sad. She loved Mommy. She said, "OK, Mommy. I will go to school. I will eat. I will play. I will watch TV later. But can I have a cookie?"

Mommy smiled. She was happy that Lily changed her mind. She loved Lily. She said, "Yes, you can have a cookie. But only one. And only after you brush your teeth. Now, let's go to school. Maybe you will feel less grumpy there."

Lily smiled too. She was still a little grumpy, but she felt better. She hugged Mommy back. She said, "OK, Mommy. I love you. Let's go to school. Maybe I will have fun there."

Once upon a time there was a little boy named Jack. Jack liked playing outside in the sun.

One day Jack was playing in the garden. Suddenly he started to sneeze loudly! He kept sneezing and sneezing. His skin began to feel itchy!

Jack's mum came outside and saw him. She said, "Jack, why did you keep sneezing so loudly?"

Jack said, "My skin got itchy and I couldn't help it!"

Mum smiled and said, "Always remember to put sun cream on your skin if you're playing outside for a long time. Your skin needs to be protected from the sun."

Jack nodded, smiling. From then on, whenever Jack went out to play, he made sure to put sun cream on his skin - and he never sneezed so loudly again!

Once upon a time, there was a naughty little mouse. His name was Peter. Peter liked to play all day and never listen to his mom.

One day, Peter took a walk in the forest. Suddenly, he saw something that made him blink - a secret door! He ran quickly to the door and peeked inside.

"Oh wow!" Peter said.

"Who goes there?" a voice said from inside.

Peter was so scared that he couldn't say a word. After a few moments, the voice spoke again.

"If you want to enter this secret door, you must answer a riddle. If you can't answer it, you must go away."

Peter thought for a minute and then asked, "What is the answer?"

The voice replied, "Beware the naughty ones!"

Peter smiled and said, "I know the answer! I'm naughty, but I'm also very curious! May I enter please?"

The voice laughed and said, "Yes, you may come in and explore the secret door!"

And so, Peter did. He explored the secret door with great curiosity and had many adventures!

Once upon a time, there was a chubby little kid called Tom. Tom was three years old and he loved looking at photos. He looked at photos of his best friends, himself, animals and his family.

One particular day, Tom was looking at a photo of his cousin who was visiting from abroad. He asked his mom, "Why isn't my cousin in this photo?". His mom replied, "She is far away, so she couldn't be in the photo". Tom felt very sad that his cousin couldn't be in the photo.

The next day, Tom wanted to look at the same photo again. But when he tried to find the photo, it had gone missing! Tom looked everywhere but couldn't find it. He asked his mom, "Where's the photo?". His mom replied, "I don't know, it's gone missing".

Tom was very angry and he started crying. He loudly shouted, "Where's the photo?!". His mom thought for a while and then she remembered that she had put it in the kitchen drawer. She told Tom, "I think I put it in the kitchen drawer".

Tom ran to the kitchen and he found the photo in the drawer! He was so relieved and happy to find the photo. He hugged the photo tightly and said, "Yes! I found it!".

Once upon a time there were two friends, Sam and Max. Sam and Max liked to have fun together. One day they decided to prepare a jolly fire. Sam and Max found some sticks and small logs and laid them carefully in a pile. Max used a match to light the fire. Soon the small logs were burning brightly. The two friends loved to watch the flame dance around the wood.

Sam and Max were having so much fun that they decided to roast marshmallows. They put the marshmallows on sticks and held them over the fire. The marshmallows became all warm and gooey. The two friends ate the melted marshmallows and laughed. It was a jolly time for Sam and Max.

They enjoyed the fire until it got dark. Sam and Max tidied everything up and went home happy.

Once upon a time, there was a boy who lived in a big house. He wanted to make something new, so he ran to the kitchen to look for ingredients. He found some flour and eggs, so he made a yummy cake.

He added lots of sprinkles and a bit of sugar, and he was really happy with how the cake looked. He brought the cake to the living room and started to dance around it.

Suddenly, he remembered the waist. He was wearing a big white waist and he thought that it would look funny on the cake. He put it on top, and it made the cake look even sweeter. He smiled and sang a happy tune as he looked at his funny waist cake.

Once upon a time, there was a big boat on the sea. The boat had a captain who was very wise. He knew how to sail the boat and keep everyone safe. One day, the captain stopped the boat at a place called a port. At the port, there were many other boats and people who were happy to see the captain. They gave him a drink of water because it was a hot day. The captain drank the water and felt refreshed. After a while, he sailed the boat away from the port and continued his journey on the sea.

Once upon a time, there was a kind man who had a special delivery to make. The man was carrying a soft, brown package and he had to take it to the hall. The hall was far away, but the man had to get there in time.

The man started off with a big smile and the package under his arm. He followed the winding road that took him closer to his destination. After walking for a while, he finally made it to the hall.

The man was so happy to have arrived. He quickly walked up the stairs and into the hall. He found the people he was looking for and he handed them the package. Everyone thanked the man for making the delivery.

The man smiled and started his long journey home. He knew he had done a good job, and he felt proud. With a lighter step and a song in his heart, the man made it home safely.

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a dull jungle. In this jungle there lived an elephant who loved to move around. Every day, the elephant would move around in her jungle looking for new things. One day as the elephant was moving around, she saw something strange. It was a deep hole in the ground.

The elephant was curious and wanted to know what was inside. She moved closer to take a look. As soon as she moved closer, the ground started to shake and rumble. The elephant felt scared and tried to move away, but it was too late. The ground opened up and the elephant fell into the deep, dark hole.

The elephant tried and tried to get out, but she could not move. She was stuck in the deep, dark hole and she stayed there forever, never to be seen again.

The end.

Once upon a time there was a big ship. It was a heavy ship and it had lots of stuff inside. There were lots of packages and boxes.

One day the ship got stuck. It was stuck in the sand on the beach. All the packages and boxes were at the top of the ship and none of them could move.

Suddenly, a knight on a horse came to the rescue. He rode around the ship and tried to help it move. But the ship was too heavy and it wouldn't move.

The knight thought hard and then he had an idea. He got his friends to come and help him. They all pulled on the ship and pushed it out of the sand. The packages and boxes stayed at the top of the ship and they were safe.

The knight and his friends had rescued the ship! They all cheered and they were very happy.

Once upon a time, there was a clever hippo. His name was Jack. One day, Jack wanted to play a game. He decided to scatter balloons of all different colors around the forest. He wanted all of the animals to join him in the game. All of the animals came to play and were very excited. They laughed and jumped around as they tried to gather the balloons in their mouths. Even the hippos were jumping around! Jack was so happy to see everyone enjoying his game. The game went on until the sun set, and then everyone said goodbye and scattered off into the night. Jack was very pleased with his game and smiled at what a great time they had all had.

Mummy had a big jar of jam. It was big and messy. Little Jack wanted the jam. He asked mum, she said no but he didn't listen. He tried to carry the jam to his bedroom but he was too little and he dropped it. The jam went everywhere. It was a big, messy mess!

Mummy was very mad. She said no more jam for Jack. Jack was very sad, but he understood why mummy was mad.

So mummy cleaned up the mess and gave Jack a big hug. She said if Jack ever wanted jam again he had to ask first. Jack said he would never try to carry the jam on his own again.

Once upon a time there were two bears. Their names were Jax and Jill. Jax and Jill loved to go for walks in the forest. They were very happy together.

One day Jax said to Jill, "Hey Jill, let's count the trees!" Jill replied, "OK!"

So the two bears started to count the trees. When they got to ten, they decided to have a dance. Jax and Jill held hands and spun around and around in a circle. They twirled their fur and shouted, "Wheee! That was so fun!"

They continued counting until they reached twenty. Then they wrestled each other, tickling and laughing. They were so tight until they fell asleep.

The two bears spent many days counting and dancing in the forest. And they were always happy when they played together.

Anna and Ben went to the zoo with Mom and Dad. They saw many animals, like monkeys, lions, and elephants. Anna liked the elephants best. They had big ears and long noses. Ben liked the lions best. They had loud roars and sharp teeth.

They walked to the next place. There was a big sign that said "Rhinoceros". Anna and Ben did not know what a rhinoceros was. They looked around, but they did not see any animal. They only saw a big rock and some grass.

"Where is the rhinoceros?" Anna asked Mom.

"Maybe it is hiding behind the rock," Mom said.

"Can we go closer and see?" Ben asked Dad.

"No, we have to stay behind the fence," Dad said. "The rhinoceros is very big and strong. It can hurt us with its horn."

Anna and Ben were impatient. They wanted to see the rhinoceros. They waited and waited, but the rhinoceros did not come out.

"Maybe it is sleeping," Anna said.

"Maybe it is shy," Ben said.

"Maybe it is hungry," Mom said.

"Maybe it is bored," Dad said.

Just then, they heard a loud snort. The rock moved. It was not a rock. It was the rhinoceros. It lifted its head and looked at them. It had a big horn on its nose and a thick skin. It was gray and brown.

"Wow!" Anna and Ben said. "It is the rhinoceros!"

The rhinoceros walked to the fence. It sniffed the air. It saw Anna and Ben. It opened its mouth and made a noise.

"Hello, rhinoceros!" Anna and Ben said.

The rhinoceros nodded its head. It seemed to say hello back. It was not hiding anymore. It was not sleeping, shy, hungry, or bored. It was curious.

Anna and Ben were happy. They saw the rhinoceros. They thanked Mom and Dad for taking them to the zoo. They learned a new word and a new animal. They had a fun day.

One day, a little boy named Tom had a surprise for his family. He had learned to sew by using a special stitch! He proudly showed off his work and his family gathered around, amazed. He had created a thick, warm blanket!

They all hugged Tom, proud of what he had achieved. His mom asked him what he was going to do with his new skill. Tom explained he wanted to help those in need. He decided to use the blanket to serve people who were feeling cold.

So, Tom went out in the world with his blanket and whenever he found someone who needed it, he gave it to them with a smile. People were so thankful for the blanket. Especially because it was thick and warm.

Tom was so glad that his special stitch could serve others and make them happy. So, Tom kept doing it, every day for a long time with a big smile on his face.

One day, Tommy and his friend were in the park. They were playing all sorts of games. Suddenly, Tommy started to feel restless. He wanted to do something more exciting.

He looked around, and saw a big hill. "Let's hurry to the top," he shouted. His friend nodded, and off they went.

The hill was steep and long, but Tommy was determined. He ran and ran, and soon he was at the top. He looked down, and saw the park below.

Tommy was glad he was with his friend. They had a lot of fun, and they made it to the top of the hill. It was a pleasant surprise, and a great feeling. Now they were ready to play some more.

Sam is a big boy who likes to help his mom. His mom works on her computer and has many files. Files are papers with words and pictures on them. Sam wants to see the files, but his mom says they are not for him. She says he can hold one file and look at it, but he must be careful.

Sam is happy and holds the file. He sees a picture of a cat on the file. He likes cats. He wants to show the cat to his mom, but she is busy. She says she has to finish her work. Sam feels restless. He wants to play with the cat. He thinks the cat is lonely. He tries to take the file off the computer, but it is stuck. He pulls harder and harder.

The file comes off, but so does the computer. The computer falls on the floor and makes a loud noise. Sam is scared. His mom is angry. She says he broke the computer and the file. She says he is a bad boy. Sam feels sad. He says he is sorry. He says he just wanted to play with the cat. He hugs his mom and cries. His mom hugs him back and says she loves him. She says he is a good boy, but he must not touch her files. She says they can play with a real cat later. Sam smiles and says okay. He says he will be good and wait. He holds his mom's hand and sits with her. He is not restless anymore.

Once upon a time, there was a big tree in the forest. The tree was very tall and had lots of branches. One day, a lumberjack came to cut the tree down. He had an axe and started to chop the tree. Suddenly, the tree made a loud snap sound and fell down. The lumberjack was happy and took the tree away.

After the tree was gone, the forest was very calm. The animals who lived there were sad because they lost their friend, the tree. But then, they saw something amazing. A new tree started to grow where the old tree used to be. It was small at first, but it grew bigger and bigger every day. Now, the animals have a new friend and they are happy again.

Once there was a sunflower who was always looking for someone to play with. She tried to find a friend but it seemed that no one wanted to join her. As she sat all alone, suddenly a clear voice pierced the air. It was a voice full of joy and excitement.

The sunflower looked up to see a little girl jumping up and down and clapping her hands. She was smiling from ear to ear. The sunflower couldn't help but smile back.

The little girl said, "Come and play with me now! I'm having so much fun! Please join me!"
