Next, she suggested that he help collect the leaves to build a little camp. Billy loved to find the biggest and brownest leaves to make their very own little camp.

Billy's mom was so happy that he was helping and soon enough they had a big campfire and lots of little camp homes! Billy was so excited to play in the camp and he couldn't wait to come back the next day.

Ben and Mia liked to paint. They had many colors and brushes. They painted animals and trees and flowers. They painted on paper and on the wall. Sometimes they painted on each other.

One day, they went to visit their grandma. She lived on a big ranch. There were many cows and horses and chickens. Ben and Mia wanted to paint them. They took their paints and brushes and ran outside.

They saw a brown cow. They painted it blue and yellow. They saw a black horse. They painted it pink and green. They saw a white chicken. They painted it red and orange. They had fun.

But then, they heard a loud moo. It was the cow. It was angry. It did not like the colors. It chased Ben and Mia. They ran away. They were scared.

They ran to their grandma. She saw them and the cow. She was shocked. She said, "What did you do? You hurt the cow. You hurt its feelings. You have to say sorry and wash it."

Ben and Mia felt bad. They said sorry to the cow. They took a bucket and a sponge and washed it. They washed the horse and the chicken too. They said sorry to them.

Their grandma hugged them. She said, "I love you, but you have to be careful. You can paint on paper and on the wall, but not on the animals. They are alive. They have feelings. They do not like to be painted."

Ben and Mia nodded. They said, "We understand. We are sorry. We will not paint on the animals again."

They went inside. They painted on paper. They painted their grandma and the ranch. They used nice colors. They gave their paintings to their grandma. She smiled. She said, "Thank you. These are beautiful. You are good painters."

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved his fridge magnets. He had many different magnets with pictures of animals, fruits and shapes. One day, Timmy noticed that one of his magnets was missing. He looked everywhere for it but couldn't find it.

Timmy's mom saw him looking sad and asked him what was wrong. Timmy told her about his missing magnet. His mom said, "Don't worry Timmy, we can replace it with a new magnet." Timmy's face lit up with excitement. He couldn't wait to pick out a new magnet.

They went to the store and Timmy picked out a magnet with a different animal on it. He was so happy to have a new magnet on his fridge. From that day on, Timmy made sure to keep all his magnets in a safe place so he wouldn't lose any more.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy who wanted to do something he'd never tried before. It was a great adventure! He started by standing on his knees and put his hands up in the air. He was so excited he couldn't help but start hopping from one foot to the other.

He knew he had to be careful, because it was a different kind of adventure. After a few moments, he steadied himself and continued. He did it - he was doing something he'd never done before! He felt brave and powerful and he couldn't wait to finish.

Just then, an unexpected feeling came over him. It was like something was waiting for him, something he hadn't expected.

He continued, even though he was feeling a little afraid. Suddenly, he felt something at his feet - a surprise! It was a big, soft pillow. He had finished his adventure and it felt amazing! He had done something different and proved he could do it!

Once upon a time, there was a big horse named Max. Max lived in a big house called a stable. The stable was enormous and had lots of hay for Max to eat.

One day, Max's owner asked him to serve as a helper. Max was happy to help and followed his owner to a nearby farm. At the farm, Max saw many animals that he had never seen before.

Max's job was to carry big bags of food for the other animals. He was strong and could carry the bags easily. The other animals were grateful for Max's help and thanked him.

After a long day of serving, Max was tired. He went back to his stable and ate some hay before going to sleep. Max was happy to have helped the other animals and couldn't wait to serve again.

Once upon a time, there was a strong bull. He loved to play with the other animals in the countryside. One day, he saw an interesting attach and wanted to give it a try. He thought it looked like it would be fun. He worked and worked, attaching it to the ground with his strong hooves. After a few tries, he finally succeeded.

The bull was so excited and ran back to tell all the other animals. He couldn't believe the attach worked. As they all watched, the bull had fun playing with the attach. He twirled it around, jumped over it and ran alongside it. Everyone was amazed by the strong bull's strength and skill.

The other animals started to attach their own attaches to the ground. They laughed and cheered, playing for hours on end. The strong bull smiled, proud of himself for inventing such a fun game.

The End.

Sara and Ben like to draw pictures for their grandma. Grandma lives far away, so they cannot see her often. But they can mail her their pictures and make her happy.

One day, Sara and Ben draw many circles on their papers. They use different colors and make big and small circles. They think circles are fun and pretty. They write their names and "I love you" on their pictures.

"Let's mail our pictures to grandma!" Sara says. "She will like them a lot!"

"OK!" Ben agrees. "But how do we mail them?"

They ask their mom for help. Mom puts their pictures in a big envelope and writes grandma's address on it. She gives them some stamps and stickers to decorate the envelope.

"Be gentle with the stamps and stickers," Mom says. "They are sticky and can tear the envelope."

Sara and Ben are gentle. They stick the stamps and stickers on the envelope carefully. They make it look nice and colorful.

"Good job!" Mom says. "Now we can go to the mailbox and mail your pictures to grandma."

Sara and Ben are excited. They hold Mom's hand and walk to the mailbox. They take turns to put the envelope in the slot. They wave goodbye to their pictures and hope grandma will get them soon.

"Grandma will love our pictures!" Sara says.

"Yes, she will!" Ben says.

They smile and hug Mom. They are happy to mail their pictures to grandma.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl. The little girl loved wearing pretty and cozy clothes. Her favourite thing to wear was her comfortable bathrobe. Every day, the little girl would put on her soft bathrobe and feel so happy.

One day, the little girl noticed that her bathrobe had become too small. It didn't fit her anymore. She felt so sad and wondered what she would do.

Her mom was very nice. She wanted to make her little girl happy again. Mom decided to go to the store to buy a new bathrobe. She found the perfect one. The new bathrobe was very soft and fit the little girl perfectly!

The little girl put on the new bathrobe and it was a perfect fit. She was so happy and ran around twirling and feeling so cosy. Mom smiled to see her daughter so happy. She was glad she could make her happy again.

The little girl was very thankful. Every day, she would put on her lovely bathrobe and feel so fit and comfy.

Lily was going to visit her aunt for the first time. She was very excited, but also a little frightened. She did not know what her aunt looked like, or what she liked to do. She hoped her aunt would be nice and have fun toys.

When they got to the house, Lily's mom knocked on the door. Lily held her mom's hand and gazed at the door. She wondered who would open it. She heard a voice say, "Come in, come in!" It was her aunt. She opened the door and smiled.

Lily's aunt was very tall and had long red hair. She wore a big hat and a colorful dress. She looked different from Lily's mom, but she had the same eyes. She bent down and hugged Lily. She said, "Hello, Lily, I'm so happy to meet you. You are so cute and smart. Come, I have something to show you."

Lily's aunt took her by the hand and led her to the living room. There, on the couch, was a big fluffy cat. It was white and gray and had green eyes. It looked at Lily and meowed. Lily's aunt said, "This is my cat, Fluffy. He is very friendly and loves to play. Do you want to pet him?"

Lily was not sure. She liked animals, but she had never seen a cat like this. She was a little frightened. She looked at her mom, who nodded and smiled. She looked at her aunt, who stroked the cat and said, "Don't be afraid, Lily. Fluffy won't hurt you. He is very gentle and soft. Come, try it."

Lily took a deep breath and moved closer to the couch. She reached out her hand and touched the cat's fur. It was warm and soft. The cat purred and rubbed his head against her hand. Lily felt a tickle and giggled. She liked the cat. She looked at her aunt and smiled. She was not frightened anymore. She was happy. She said, "Thank you, aunt. Fluffy is very nice. I like him. I like you too."

Once there was a jolly boy called Tom. Tom lived next to the mill. Every day he would watch the mill from his window. One day Tom saw some people frowning at the mill. He wondered what was wrong.

Tom decided to go and find out. He found that the mill had broken and nobody could fix it. Everyone was very sad and they all frowned.

Tom wanted to make them all smile again. He had a bright idea and he ran home to get some tools. He fixed the mill and the people were so happy! Everyone was jolly and they thanked Tom for fixing the mill.

Tom was very proud that he could make the people smile again. He waved goodbye to them and went home, knowing that he had done good.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She was very eager to go to the store with her mommy. They walked together and saw lots of things in the store. Lily wanted to buy a toy, but her mommy said they had to close the store soon.

Lily was sad because she couldn't get the toy she wanted. But her mommy told her they could come back another day. Lily felt happy again and they left the store together. As they walked home, Lily saw a butterfly and ran to catch it. Her mommy laughed and said Lily was very fast.

When they got home, Lily was tired from all the excitement. She closed her eyes and fell asleep, dreaming of the toy she would get on their next trip to the store.

Once upon a time there was a mom and a 3 year old. The 3 year old wanted juice, but it was too expensive. So the 3 year old asked his mom if he could have juice. The mom decided that it would be better to make juice instead of buying it.

So the mom and the 3 year old went to the store. They bought some fruit and a blender. When they got home, the 3 year old helped his mom make the juice. They blended up the fruit and added some water.

The 3 year old tasted it. He liked the juice a lot. It was sweet and cheap. He smiled and decided that it was the best juice ever! From then on, the 3 year old and his mom made juice every week. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a brother named Max. One day, they went outside to play in the snow. The snow was very icy and cold.

Lily said, "Max, I see your leg is turning red. Are you okay?"

Max said, "No, it's too cold. I want to go inside and warm up."

Lily said, "Okay, let's go inside and have some hot chocolate."

They went inside and their mom made them hot chocolate. They sat by the fire and warmed up their legs. They were happy to be inside where it was warm.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a large key that she loved to play with. One day, Lily went to the park to play. She put her key in her pocket and started to play on the swings.

While she was swinging, she saw a little boy crying. She asked him, "Why are you crying?" The little boy said, "I lost my mommy and I don't know how to find her." Lily knew what to do. She took out her key and called her mommy. Her mommy answered and Lily told her about the little boy. Her mommy came to the park and helped the little boy find his mommy.

The moral of the story is that it's important to help others when they need it. Even if you have a toy you love, like Lily's large key, you can still use it to help someone else.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his toy cars and trucks. One day, Timmy's mom took him to the store to buy some groceries. Timmy saw a big cart in the store and asked his mom if he could ride in it.

As they walked through the store, Timmy saw a toy truck that he really wanted. He told his mom that he hoped she would buy it for him. His mom said maybe if he was good, she would buy it for him later.

After they finished shopping, Timmy's mom put all the groceries in the cart and pushed it to the car. Timmy was so proud of his mom for carrying all the heavy bags and pushing the cart all by herself. They drove home and Timmy helped his mom unload the groceries. They had a great day together!

One day, two children decided to have a race. One child was called Olivia and the other one was called Dave. Olivia said: "Let's have a race and run to the tree!" Dave said: "Yes, let's do it!"

They started the race and were running very fast. Soon, Olivia was in the lead. She said: "I'm winning! I'm going to win!" Dave got very busy and started to run faster. He said: "I'm catching up with you. I'll win this race!"

They kept running until they got to the tree. Dave was just a few steps behind Olivia. Both of them jumped to the tree, trying to get there first.

Suddenly, Dave heard a loud sound and he fell off the tree. Dave was hurt and he started to cry. Olivia quickly ran to him and asked: "Are you ok?" Dave said: "No, I'm not ok. I think I hurt my arm."

Olivia helped Dave to walk back home. She said: "I recommend you to rest. You should not race anymore."

Dave sadly agreed. He had learnt that sometimes it's better to be careful and not do something too risky.

Once upon a time, there was a unique cat named Bob. Bob was not like other cats. He liked to help his friends get better when they were sick. Bob was a patient cat who wanted to improve the lives of his friends.

One day, Bob's friend, a little bird named Sue, was not feeling well. Sue said, "Bob, I don't feel good. Can you help me improve?" Bob thought for a moment and said, "Yes, Sue. I will be patient and help you feel better."

Bob and Sue tried many things to help Sue feel better. They tried resting, eating yummy food, and drinking water. But nothing seemed to work. Sue was still not feeling well. Bob started to feel sad because he could not help his friend. But then, he had an idea. "Sue, let's try singing a happy song. Maybe that will help you feel better."

Sue and Bob sang the happy song together. Slowly, Sue started to feel better. The happy song had worked! Bob was so happy that he could help his friend improve. From that day on, Bob and Sue knew that their unique friendship could help them face any problem.

Sara and Ben are friends. They like to play in the park. They like to swing, slide and run. But today, the park is closed. There is a big sign that says "No play. Wait for fix."

Sara and Ben are sad. They want to play. They look at the sign and frown.

"Can we play somewhere else?" Sara asks.

Ben thinks. He sees a big tree near the park. The tree has many leaves and branches. He has an idea.

"Let's play in the tree!" Ben says. "We can climb, hide and pretend. It will be fun!"

Sara smiles. She likes Ben's idea. She nods and follows him to the tree.

They climb the tree carefully. They find a cozy spot between the branches. They can see the park and the sky. They feel the warm sun on their faces.

They pretend they are birds. They sing, flap and hop. They make a nest with leaves and sticks. They share a snack of crackers and juice. They giggle and chatter.

They have a lot of fun in the tree. They forget about the sign and the park. They are happy. They smile.

Once upon a time, there was a small red bird who liked to visit nature. Every day, the bird would flock to the big green meadow and see all the beautiful things nature has to offer.

The bird loved how the air was clean, how the grass was green, and all the colorful flowers that were growing around the meadow. The bird could happily spend hours exploring the meadow and taking in the sights.

One day, the bird came across a baby rabbit in need of food. The bird knew that it was only right to feed the baby rabbit, so it quickly picked some fresh grass to give the rabbit.

The rabbit was so happy that he got food and thanked the bird with a big smile. Seeing the beauty of nature and how the bird fed the rabbit with kindness, the bird decided to make the meadow his home so he could continue to observe and appreciate the beauty of nature. The bird was so happy living in this clean and peaceful meadow!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily loved to play outside and explore the world around her. One day, she went for a walk in the forest and noticed a little squirrel with a wink in its eye. The squirrel seemed to be trying to tell her something.

Lily followed the squirrel deep into the forest, but as she went further and further, she noticed that she was getting lost. She tried to find her way back home, but she couldn't. Suddenly, she heard a loud noise and saw a big, scary bear coming towards her.

Lily tried to run away, but she tripped and fell. The bear came closer and closer, and Lily knew she was in trouble. She closed her eyes and wished she had listened to her parents when they told her not to wander too far from home. The moral of the story is to always listen to your parents and not do stupid things, or you might end up in danger.

One day, a boy named Tim was watching his favorite cartoon on TV. He loved the funny animals and the bright colors. His friend, Sam, came over to play with him. Sam saw the cartoon and thought it was very funny too.

"Can I watch the cartoon with you?" Sam asked. Tim said, "Yes, but don't steal my toy while I'm not looking!" Sam promised he wouldn't steal anything.

While they were watching the cartoon, a big, rough dog came into the room. The dog saw Tim's toy on the floor and took it in his mouth. Tim and Sam were so busy watching the cartoon that they didn't see the dog steal the toy.

When the cartoon was over, Tim looked for his toy but couldn't find it. He said, "Sam, did you steal my toy?" Sam said, "No, I didn't! I promised I wouldn't!" They looked around the room and saw the rough dog with the toy in its mouth.

Tim and Sam ran to the dog and said, "Give back the toy, dog!" The dog dropped the toy and ran away. Tim and Sam were happy that they got the toy back, and they continued to watch cartoons and play together.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his toys in the backyard. One day, he found a spear on the ground. He thought it was cool and picked it up.

Timmy's mom saw him with the spear and said, "Timmy, put that down! Spears are dangerous!"

Timmy replied, "But Mom, I love it! It's not stupid, it's awesome!"

His mom sighed and said, "Okay, but be careful with it. It's still dangerous." Timmy promised to be careful and continued to play with his new toy.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a big brother named Max. One day, Lily and Max went outside to play. It was very cold outside and the ground was icy. Max slipped and fell down, but he was okay.

Lily and Max decided to pretend they were in a magic land. Max pretended to be a brave knight and Lily pretended to be a fairy. They walked around the icy land and looked for treasure. They found a big rock that looked like a castle. Max pretended that the castle was his home and Lily pretended to be his guest.

After a while, Lily and Max got tired and went back inside. They had so much fun pretending to be in a magic land. Lily was happy to have a big brother to play with.

Once upon a time, there was a nice lady who had to borrow something from a big hill. She asked a fair boy to help her. The fair boy said, "Yes! I can help."

The nice lady and fair boy walked to the top of the big hill. The hill was so tall and the nice lady was so small! But finally, they got to the top. The nice lady saw lots of things she wanted to borrow. She chose a big wheel and a little wheel.

The nice lady and fair boy took the wheels back down the hill. On the way, the nice lady asked the fair boy, "Would you like to play with these wheels?" The fair boy said, "Yes! Let's have some fun!"

They played with the wheels at the bottom of the hill. They went in circles and laughed a lot. When it was time to go, the nice lady gave the fair boy one of the wheels to keep. "Thank you for helping me borrow this wheel," the nice lady said.

And the fair boy said, "You are very welcome!"

Once upon a time, there was a long road that led to a big house. One day, a little boy named Timmy was walking down the road when he saw a cat stuck in a tree.

"Meow! Help me!" cried the cat.

Timmy knew it was an emergency, so he ran to the big house to ask for help. He knocked on the door and a kind lady answered.

"Please help! There's a cat stuck in a tree!" Timmy said.

The lady revealed that she was a firefighter and she knew just what to do. She quickly got her long ladder and went to rescue the cat. Timmy was so happy to see the cat safe and sound. "Thank you for helping!" he said.

The lady smiled and said, "No problem, helping others is what we do in an emergency."

Once upon a time, there was a small bird. He wanted to travel to new places, so he decided to fly to the highest roof he could find. As he flew, he saw the roof getting closer and closer. It looked very fragile, so he was careful as he landed. He felt happy that he had reached the top of the roof, and he decided to stay there for a little while to look around. He enjoyed the view and then continued his journey. The bird was so excited to travel around and explore new places.

One day, Jack saw a trumpet. It was shiny and green.

Jack asked his dad, "What is that?"

His dad replied, "That is a trumpet, and it makes loud music. Music is like sounds and songs."

Jack was excited. He looked at the trumpet with bright eyes.

The dad said, "Let's try it. Blow into this end."

Jack did as his dad said. He tried to blow into the trumpet but it made no sound.

Jack's dad laughed. He said, "Let's practice a bit more. You'll get it soon."

Jack nodded and smiled. He couldn't wait to hear the green trumpet make some loud music.

Once there was a girl called Emma. She was very excited because she was going to the cinema. Emma had a big bag full of snacks to eat during the film.

Emma sat down in her seat and waited for the film to start. When it did start, it was very exciting! There were lots of funny characters, loud noises and bright colours.

Emma really enjoyed the film, but she also really wanted to eat her snacks. She started to feel hungry so she opened her bag and took out a big bag of popcorn. She opened the bag and squeezed it tight in her hands.

The popcorn was so tasty that Emma could not stop squeezing it. She squeezed and squeezed until the entire bag was finished!

Emma was happy that she was able to enjoy her snacks during the film. She had a great time at the cinema and she looked forward to going again soon.

Lily and Tom were twins who liked to play in the park. One day, they saw a big poster of a famous clown. The clown had a red nose, a big smile and curly hair. Lily thought the clown was funny and wanted to see him. Tom thought the clown was scary and wanted to run away.

"Look, Lily, it's the famous clown! He is coming to our town soon. Do you want to go and see him?" Lily asked Tom.

"No, Lily, I don't want to go. The clown is scary. He has a big nose and a big mouth. He might scare me or make me laugh too much. I don't like clowns," Tom said.

"But, Tom, the clown is not scary. He is funny and nice. He makes jokes and gives balloons. He might make you happy and not scared. Please, Tom, let's go and see him," Lily said.

Lily and Tom argued for a while. They could not agree on whether to see the clown or not. Then, they saw an old man walking by. The old man had a long beard, a hat and a cane. He looked at the poster and smiled.

"Hello, children. Do you like the famous clown?" the old man asked.

Lily and Tom looked at the old man. They did not know him. They felt shy.

"Hello, sir. I like the clown, but my brother doesn't. He thinks the clown is scary," Lily said.

"Is that so? Well, I have a secret to tell you. Do you want to hear it?" the old man said.

Lily and Tom nodded. They liked secrets.

The old man leaned closer and whispered in their ears.

"I am the famous clown. I just wear this old clothes and beard to hide. But when I go on stage, I put on my nose, my smile and my hair. And I make everyone laugh and have fun. Do you want to come and see me?" the old man said.

Lily and Tom gasped. They could not believe it. The old man was the famous clown. They looked at his eyes and saw they were twinkling. They looked at his mouth and saw it was smiling. They looked at his nose and saw it was red.

Lily and Tom laughed. They were not scared anymore. They were happy.

"Yes, yes, we want to see you. You are not scary. You are funny and nice. You are the famous clown. Thank you for telling us your secret," Lily and Tom said.

The old man hugged them and gave them each a balloon. He winked at them and walked away.

Lily and Tom ran to their mom and dad. They told them the secret. They asked them to take them to see the famous clown. They were excited and curious.

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside and collect pebbles. One day, she found a shiny pebble that she wanted to give to her friend, Max. So, she put it in a small box and asked her mom to deliver it to Max's house.

But when Max received the box, he was angry because he thought it was a prank from Lily. He threw the box on the ground and the pebble fell out. Lily's mom saw what happened and explained that Lily just wanted to give him a present. Max felt bad and went to apologize to Lily.

From that day on, Lily and Max played together every day and collected pebbles together. They never got angry at each other again.

Once upon a time, there was a little black mole. He lived in a hole in the ground. The mole loved to dig and play all day.

One day, the mole saw a big yawn. It was a big hole in the ground. The mole was scared. He did not know what to do. He wanted to go back to his little hole.

The mole was brave. He went to the big yawn. He saw it was just another mole hole. The mole was happy. He made a new friend. They played and dug in the dirt all day.

Once upon a time, there was a worm. He was a very special worm because he was unique. One day, the worm was picking some food from the ground. He was eating some yummy leaves and grass.

Suddenly, something special caught the worm's eye. He noticed a bright, sparkly rock nearby. It was so beautiful that he had to pick it up. He was so excited! He held it in his hand for a few moments, then he carefully put it safely in a little hole in the ground.

The worm liked the sparkly rock so much, that he went back every day to pick it up again. He would lay down in the grass and he'd look at it and enjoy its beauty. He thought it was the most special thing in the world.

The friends of the worm were so impressed by the unique rock, that they started picking up special objects of their own. They kept their special objects in the same hole in the ground as the sparkly rock.

The worm was very proud of his special rock and he liked that he could share this unique treasure with his friends. They all enjoyed picking up new things, looking at them and having fun.

Lila and Ben are twins who love to play with their toy trains. They have a long track that goes around their room and many different trains to choose from. They like to polish their trains every day to make them shiny and smooth.

One day, Lila and Ben have a big fight. Lila wants to use the red train, but Ben says it is his and he won't share. Lila says she polished it yesterday, so it is hers today. Ben says he polished it this morning, so it is his all day. They pull and tug on the red train, but neither of them will let go.

They are so busy fighting that they don't notice their little brother, Sam, who is crawling into their room. Sam sees the long track and the shiny trains and thinks they are fun to play with. He grabs the blue train and puts it in his mouth. He chews and bites on it, making it dirty and broken.

Lila and Ben hear Sam's noise and look at him. They are shocked and angry to see what he has done to their blue train. They run to him and try to take it away, but Sam cries and holds on. Lila and Ben forget about their fight and work together to calm Sam down. They explain to him that the trains are not for eating, but for rolling on the track. They show him how to play with them gently and safely.

Lila and Ben learn their lesson. They realize that fighting over the red train was silly and selfish. They decide to share their trains and their track with each other and with Sam. They also remember to polish their trains every day, but not too much, so they don't get too attached to them. They are happy and grateful for their toys and their family.

The moral value of the story is: Sharing is caring, and fighting is not nice.

Once upon a time there lived two brothers, Jack and Tony. They were best friends, but Jack was sometimes jealous of Tony's things.

Today, Tony had something extra special! He had two tickets to the circus and Jack didn't. Tony was excited to go and even before the show started, he was clapping along to the music.

Jack was so jealous. He asked Tony, "Why can't I go too?".

"The tickets don't have enough space to fit us both. We'll just have to find something else to do," answered Tony.

Suddenly, a voice came from outside. "The circus tent is open! Would you like to come in?" it asked.

The two brothers looked at each other and smiled. They couldn't believe it. Jack and Tony ran up to the circus tent, clapping their hands together.

They were finally able to go to the circus! They had the best time and Tony was glad to give Jack the extra ticket.

Jack was no longer jealous and they both agreed that the day was wonderful.

Once upon a time there was a brave penny. She wanted to try something new, so she decided to go on an adventure. She hopped on her bicycle and started to speed away.

She pedalled faster and faster, zooming down the street. The wind swooshed through her hair. She felt so happy, and excited to see what lay ahead.

Soon she came across a giant hill. She was a little scared, but she was brave. She kept pedalling as fast as she could; faster and faster she went up the hill.

At the top, she stopped and looked around. The view was amazing! She felt so free and alive.

The brave penny smiled, feeling proud of herself. She knew she had been brave, and had accomplished something great. She sped back home, knowing that she had had a wonderful adventure.

Once upon a time, in a big pond, there was a yellow alligator. He had many friends. They liked to play together.

One day, the yellow alligator and his friends wanted to choose a game. Some friends wanted to play hide and seek. Other friends wanted to play tag.

The yellow alligator thought hard. He wanted to make everyone happy. So, he chose to play both games. First, they played hide and seek. Then, they played tag. All the friends had fun and were happy.

Once upon a time, there was a purple phone. It was a very special phone because it could talk to animals. One day, a little girl named Lily found the phone and decided to try it out. She dialed the number and to her surprise, a friendly voice answered.

The phone told Lily that she could talk to any animal she wanted by pressing a special button. Lily was so excited that she pressed the button right away. Suddenly, she heard a loud noise and saw a banana rotting on her kitchen table.

Lily was confused but the phone explained that sometimes when you talk to animals, strange things can happen. From that day on, Lily had lots of fun talking to animals with her purple telephone, even if sometimes things got a little bit weird.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy. He loved to spin and have fun. One day, he heard an amazing noise outside. It sounded like thunder! He was a bit scared, but he decided to go out to explore.

The little boy bravely stepped outside and saw a huge spinning storm. The thunder was roaring and the lightning was flashing around him. The little boy was so amazed that he started to spin and dance around the storm.

The storm was so powerful and beautiful, the little boy stayed spinning and playing in the storm for hours. When it was over, the little boy felt happy and excited. He had just experienced an amazing and wonderful storm!

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play basketball with his friends. One day, Timmy's friend Johnny came over to play. "Let's play basketball!" said Timmy. "Okay!" said Johnny.

They went outside to play basketball. Timmy dribbled the ball slowly down the court. Johnny tried to steal the ball, but Timmy was too good. "You're a great basketball player!" said Johnny. "Thanks!" said Timmy.

After they finished playing basketball, Timmy's mom called them inside. "I'm making cookies!" she said. Timmy and Johnny went into the kitchen. Timmy's mom gave them a big bowl and a spoon. "Stir the cookie dough!" she said. Timmy and Johnny stirred the cookie dough slowly. It smelled delicious!

Jill and Lucas were best friends. They did lots of things together and played in the garden all day.

Then one day, Jill suggested a new game. She said, "Let's clean the network in the garden!" Lucas looked confused and asked, "What is a network?" Jill explained that the network was an attractive garden full of flowers.

Lucas agreed and they quickly got to work. They picked up the fallen leaves and flowers and put them back in the flowerbed. Lucas held the basket while Jill tidied the garden path.

They worked really hard and soon the garden was beautiful again. Jill said, "Thank you, Lucas. You helped make the network look attractive!" Lucas was so proud of himself and they hugged each other in celebration.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to walk with her mommy on the street. One day, they saw something unusual on the street. It was a big, red balloon floating in the sky!

Lily was so happy to see it and she pointed at it, saying "Mommy, look!" Her mommy observed the balloon too and smiled at Lily. They walked closer to the balloon and saw that it had a smiley face on it.

Lily and her mommy watched the balloon for a long time, until it floated away in the wind. Lily was sad to see it go, but she was happy that she got to observe something so special on the street.

Once upon a time there was a family with a mummy, a daddy and a little boy. The little boy's favourite thing to do was to go to the park. One summer's evening, he went to the park with his mummy and daddy.

The little boy was so excited when he saw the park. He ran towards the swings and sat down. He giggled and asked his mummy to push him high. He laughed out loud each time he went around in a circle.

After a few minutes, it was time for the little boy to have a snack. He opened his lunch box and he saw some tasty food: sandwiches, fruits and a cake. He clapped his hands and said: "Yay, yummy food!"

But then the little boy saw something else in the corner of his box. It was a little toy turtle! He cried "Oh no, I left my turtle at home!" and started to weep. His mummy and daddy felt so sorry for him that they gave him a hug and tickled his waist to make him laugh.

The little boy felt better after that. He finished his tasty snack, played some more and then it was time to go home. His parents held his hands and he waved good-bye to the park. From then on, he never forgot to bring his turtle with him!

Once upon a time, there were two friends, John and Mama. Mama wanted to become successful, so she decided to study. John wanted to help her and asked, "What are you doing, Mama?"

Mama replied, "I'm studying so I can make money. Then I will be successful!"

John was amazed and asked, "What can I do to help?" But Mama said she just needed to work hard and study.

Soon, their friendship was tested. Mama wanted to spend all her time studying, without spending any time with John! He was sad and asked her to spend time with him too.

Mama felt torn. She really wanted to be successful, but she also wanted to keep her friendship with John. Finally, she decided to study and spend time with John, and both of them were happy.

Mama worked hard and eventually became successful. John was so proud of her and they continued to be great friends. In the end, it was a happy ending!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, Lily's mom made her favorite food, spaghetti. Lily loved spaghetti so much that she ate it all up. But then, Lily wanted to go play at the park.

At the park, Lily saw a big slide. She wanted to slide down it, but she was scared. Her friend Jack said, "Come on, Lily! It's fun!" But Lily was stubborn and didn't want to try.

Then, a little boy named Timmy came up to Lily and said, "I used to be scared too, but I tried and now I love it!" Lily thought about what Timmy said and decided to give it a try. She climbed up the slide and slid down. It was so much fun!

The moral of the story is to not be stubborn and to try new things, even if they seem scary at first.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the sun and rain. One day, she saw a big rainbow in the sky.

Lily: "Mommy, look! A rainbow!"

Mommy: "Yes, it's very pretty. Do you want to draw a picture of it?"

Lily: "Yes, please!"

So, Lily ran inside to get some paper and crayons. She tried hard to draw the rainbow, but it was difficult.

Lily: "Mommy, can you help me wrap the colors of the rainbow in my picture?"

Mommy: "Of course, sweetie. Let's start with red."

Together, they wrapped the colors of the rainbow in Lily's picture. It was the most beautiful rainbow Lily had ever seen.

Once upon a time, there were two friends named Tom and Sam. Tom liked exploring and finding new stuff, while Sam liked helping his friends. One day, Tom said, “Let’s go explore and find new stuff.” Sam replied, “Let’s go. I will follow you and help.”

So, they followed a dirt road and soon they came to a big forest. Tom said, “Let’s go and explore the forest.” Sam said, “OK.”

Soon, they were deep in the forest. As they were looking around, they saw a big hill. Tom said, “Let’s climb up the hill and see what’s on the other side.” Sam was excited and said, “OK, let’s go!”

But then, as they were climbing the hill, Tom slipped and started to slide down. Sam quickly ran to him and caught him so he wouldn’t get hurt. Tom said, “Thanks for being so helpful, Sam.” Then, when they got to the top of the hill, they saw a wonderful surprise! There were lots and lots of shiny, glittering stuff. “Wow!” exclaimed Tom, “We’re going to be rich from all this stuff!”

Lily and her mom went to a big restaurant for lunch. Lily liked the restaurant because it had many colors and pictures on the walls. She also liked the food, especially the fries and the juice.

When they finished eating, Lily saw a man with a funny hat and a big smile. He was the chef, and he was making food in the kitchen. Lily wanted to say hello to him, so she asked her mom.

"Mom, can I wave to the chef?" Lily said.

"Sure, honey, you can wave to the chef. He likes to see happy customers," her mom said.

Lily got up from her chair and walked to the window where she could see the chef. She waved her hand and said, "Hi, chef! Thank you for the food!"

The chef saw Lily and waved back. He said, "Hi, little girl! You're welcome for the food! I'm glad you liked it!"

Lily smiled and ran back to her mom. She gave her mom a hug and said, "I like the chef, mom. He is nice and funny."

"I like him too, Lily. He is a good chef and a good friend," her mom said.

They paid for their lunch and left the restaurant. Lily waved to the chef again and said, "Bye, chef! See you soon!"

The chef waved to Lily and said, "Bye, little girl! See you soon!"

Tim and Jen are twins. They like to play with their toys in their room. One day, they find a big box in the closet. They open the box and see many things inside. They see a hat, a scarf, a coat, and a pin.

"Look, Jen, a pin!" Tim says. He picks up the pin and shows it to Jen. The pin is shiny and has a star on it.

"Wow, Tim, it is pretty!" Jen says. She wants to see the pin too. She reaches for the pin, but Tim pulls it away.

"No, Jen, it is mine!" Tim says. He puts the pin on his coat. He zips up his coat and puts on the hat and the scarf. He looks at himself in the mirror. He thinks he looks cool.

"Tim, share with me!" Jen says. She is sad and angry. She does not like it when Tim does not share. She looks around the box and sees a dull knife. She picks up the knife and runs to Tim.

"Jen, what are you doing?" Tim says. He sees Jen with the knife and gets scared. He thinks Jen wants to hurt him.

"Give me the pin, Tim, or I will cut your coat!" Jen says. She waves the knife at Tim.

"Jen, no, stop!" Tim says. He tries to back away, but he trips on the scarf. He falls to the floor and the pin falls off his coat.

Jen sees the pin and grabs it. She is happy and puts it on her hat. She does not see that the knife has cut Tim's coat and made a big hole.

"Look, Tim, I have the pin!" Jen says. She shows Tim the pin and smiles.

Tim looks at Jen and then at his coat. He sees the hole and starts to cry. He does not care about the pin anymore. He only cares about his coat.

"Jen, you are mean!" Tim says. He cries louder and louder.

Mom hears Tim and Jen and comes to their room. She sees the mess and the knife and the hole. She is angry and shocked.

"Tim, Jen, what have you done?" Mom says. She takes the knife and the pin away from them. She scolds them and makes them say sorry to each other. She tells them to never play with sharp things again. She hugs them and tries to fix the coat.

Tim and Jen feel bad and hug Mom. They say sorry to Mom and to each other. They learn to share and to be careful. They do not play with the box anymore. They play with their other toys and have fun.

Johnny was outside playing with his truck when a tornado came. He was careless and didn't run away. He was sucked up in the tornado and felt scared. He wished he had been more careful.

The tornado carried Johnny over the town and his truck fell and broke. Johnny felt very sad and regretted not listening to his mom.

The tornado eventually stopped and Johnny landed gently in a tree. He was thankful to be safe and sound. He looked around him and all the damage the tornado had done. He was sorry for his carelessness and knew to be more careful in the future.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Beth. Beth was nice, but sometimes she was spoiled.

One day, Beth was playing in her backyard. Suddenly, a cop appeared. He was very big and Beth was scared.

The cop said, "Don't worry, Beth. I'm here to help you."

Beth was still scared, but she nodded. The cop gave Beth a big hug and said, "Everything will be alright."

Beth smiled and felt better. She hugged the cop and thanked him. The cop smiled and waved goodbye.

Beth waved goodbye as the cop disappeared. She was glad he had appeared.

One day, a little boy named Tim went with his mom to the park. It was a cold day, and there was ice on the ground. Tim saw his friend, Sam, playing near the ice. Sam was being very noisy and laughing.

Tim went to Sam and said, "Sam, be careful on the ice. It is slippery, and you can fall." Sam did not listen to Tim and kept playing. Tim tried to learn how to play on the ice too, but he was scared.

Soon, Sam slipped on the ice and fell down. He cried loudly. Tim's mom came and helped Sam. She told both boys, "You should listen to your friends when they tell you to be careful." The moral of the story is to always listen to good advice from friends.

Anna and Ben are playing with blocks in the living room. They like to build towers and houses and bridges with the blocks. They have many colors of blocks: red, blue, yellow, green, and more.

"Look, Anna, I made a big tower!" Ben says, showing his blocks to his sister. "It is very high and strong!"

Anna looks at Ben's tower and smiles. She likes his tower, but she also wants to make her own. She picks up some blocks and starts to build next to Ben.

"Can I have some of your blocks, Ben?" Anna asks. "I need more to make my tower."

Ben shakes his head. "No, Anna, these are my blocks. You have your own blocks. Go away!"

Anna feels sad and angry. She does not like Ben's answer. She wants to share the blocks with him. She thinks he is being mean and selfish.

She decides to do something bad. She pushes Ben's tower with her hand. The blocks fall down and break. They make a loud noise.

"Anna, why did you do that?" Ben cries. "You broke my tower! You are a bad sister!"

Anna feels sorry for what she did. She sees Ben's tears and hears his cry. She knows she made a mistake.

"I'm sorry, Ben, I'm sorry!" Anna says. "I did not mean to break your tower. I was mad at you, but I should not have pushed your blocks. Can you forgive me?"

Ben looks at Anna and sees her face. She looks sad and sorry too. He remembers that she is his sister and he loves her.

"It's okay, Anna, I forgive you," Ben says. "But don't do that again, okay? It is not nice to break other people's things."

Anna nods and hugs Ben. "Okay, Ben, I won't do that again. I love you, brother."

They hug and make up. They decide to share the blocks and build a new tower together. They have fun and play nicely.

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a crocodile who had a broken toy. The crocodile was sad and frustrated. He wanted to fix his toy, but he didn't know how.

One day, a kind bird saw the crocodile and asked, "Why are you sad, Mr. Crocodile?" The crocodile said, "My toy is broken, and I don't know how to fix it." The bird wanted to help the crocodile, so they both worked together to fix the toy.

After some time, they fixed the toy, and the crocodile was very happy. He said, "Thank you, kind bird, for helping me fix my toy." The bird was happy too, because he made a new friend. From that day on, the crocodile and the bird played together every day, and they were never frustrated again.

Once upon a time there was a factory. It was very busy with lots of machinery spraying and making things.

One day, two three-year-olds ran into the factory. They were curious to see the machines spraying and all the activity.

The manager saw them and told them not to touch anything.

The little boy replied, "Why not? We want to help out!"

The manager smiled and told them, "It's nice to offer help, but this factory is a very busy place. It needs adults to help, not little kids."

The two children nodded and left the factory.

The moral of this story is that children should be careful when they try to help out. It's important to know when help is needed and when it is not.

It was a sunny day and the birds were chirping. Little Peter was in the garden playing with his toy truck. He was having lots of fun.

Suddenly he heard a loud noise and he looked up. There was a trouble balloon flying in the sky. It was making noises and going round and round.

Peter watched the balloon for a long time but he started to get bored. Then he spotted a big white cream coming out of the balloon. He got excited and ran to get a bowl.

When Peter came back he saw the balloon had landed in front of him. He looked inside and was surprised to see a little bird. The bird was looking very troubled.

"Can I help you?" Peter asked. The bird was too afraid to answer. Peter slowly slowly reached out and petted the bird gently. The bird started to calm down and eventually it hopped on his shoulder.

Peter took the bird to the kitchen and gave it some cream. The bird enjoyed the cream and soon it started to feel comforted.

Peter and the bird watched the sunset together and they both felt happy.

Every day, Jane goes to a veterinarian's office with her mom. She loves visiting the veterinarian because the veterinarian gives her treats for being a good girl. On this day, the veterinarian had an extra special surprise for Jane. She was given a puppy! Jane was delighted!

The veterinarian showed them many important things to do with the puppy. She taught Jane how to feed and take care of it. Jane completed these tasks with ease and her mom was so proud.

The veterinarian showed them to the store to buy all the things the puppy needed. Jane was so excited to pick out toys for it. When they arrived back home, Jane settled in with her new puppy. She was determined to make sure her puppy got regular walks and brushing. Jane was happy that she could take care of her new puppy so easily.

Every day, Jane and her puppy would explore and have so much fun. And, of course, every day Jane would complete her tasks with the puppy so that it was healthy and happy!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to eat spicy food, especially spicy turkey. One day, her mommy took her to the store to buy some turkey for dinner.

At the store, Lily saw a big turkey and asked her mommy if they could buy it. "Mommy, can we pay for that turkey?" she asked. Her mommy said yes, and they put the turkey in their cart.

When they got home, Lily's daddy cooked the turkey and it smelled so good. Lily took a bite and said, "Mmm, this spicy turkey is so yummy!" Her mommy and daddy smiled and said they were happy she liked it. From that day on, Lily always asked for spicy turkey for dinner.

Once upon a time there was a silly country. The people in the country were silly too.

One day they decided to play a game. The game was to stand in a circle and pass a ball around. It was lots of fun!

But then the sun started to set and it was time to end the game. Everyone said goodbye and went their separate ways.

The people went home and the country was quiet. Even though it was silly, it was also peaceful. And so the day ended peacefully in the silly country.

Once upon a time there were two bears, one small and one big. The little bear asked the big bear, "Can I stay with you?" The big bear replied, "Yes, come with me and we'll have some fun!" So the little bear followed the big bear.

They roamed around the forest, looking for food and playing games together. The big bear showed the little bear where to find the best berries and how to look for wild mushrooms. On the way, the little bear felt a bit scared about the thick forest.

The big bear sensed that the little bear was afraid and said, "My friend, stay close to me so that you won't be scared. Together, we can make our way through this thick forest."

The little bear thanked the big bear and stayed close to him. Together they made it back home to their den in the forest.

Moral of the story: It's often easier to do something when you have a friend by your side!

Sam and Anna were helping Mom make dinner. They liked to help Mom in the kitchen. Mom gave them each a spoon and a bowl. She said, "You can stir the cheese sauce for the broccoli. Be careful, it is hot."

Sam and Anna took their spoons and bowls and went to the stove. They saw a big pot with cheese sauce. It smelled good. They each scooped some sauce into their bowls. Then they started to stir.

"I can stir faster than you," Sam said. He stirred his sauce very fast. He wanted to show Anna that he was strong.

"No, I can stir faster than you," Anna said. She stirred her sauce very fast too. She wanted to show Sam that she was strong.

They stirred and stirred until their sauce was smooth and bubbly. But they stirred so fast that some sauce spilled out of their bowls. It splashed on the stove and on the floor.

"Oh no!" Sam and Anna said. They looked at the mess. They felt bad.

Mom came over and saw the sauce. She was not angry. She smiled and said, "You are both very good helpers. And very strong stirrers. But sometimes you need to stir slowly and gently. That way, you won't make a mess. And the sauce will stay in the bowl."

Sam and Anna nodded. They said, "Sorry, Mom. We will stir slowly and gently next time."

Mom hugged them and said, "That's okay. I love you both. Now, let's put the sauce on the broccoli and eat dinner."

One day, a little girl named Mia went to the beach with her mom. They saw many things like sand, shells, and water. Mia liked to play in the sand and make castles. She felt happy and peaceful at the beach.

Then, Mia saw a jellyfish in the water. It was big and pretty. Mia asked her mom, "What is that?" Her mom said, "That is a jellyfish. We can look, but we should not touch it." Mia admired the jellyfish from far away.

Later, Mia and her mom sat on the sand and ate a snack. They talked about the jellyfish and how nice the day was. Mia loved the beach and the jellyfish, and she felt very peaceful.

Once upon a time, there was a princess named Emma. She loved to play dress-up, and she owned lots of pretty clothes and accessories. Her favorite color was pink.

One day, Emma wanted to organize all of her clothes. But it was so hard to do by herself. "Please can someone help me organize my clothes?" said Emma.

Then her mom came over to help her. "Of course Emma", smiled her mom.

They worked together to make all the clothes look organized and neat. When they were done, Emma saw a sparkly pink dress.

Good job! exclaimed her mom. Emma smiled and said, "Thanks for helping me. I'm so happy!"

Once upon a time, there was a real big yellow flower. She bloomed and sparkled like the sun. Every day, a funny tiny mosquito came to visit the flower. He would fly around the sparkling petals and tell her funny stories. The flower was always happy to listen.

One day, the flower got sleepy. She started to droop down, until she was almost on the ground. The little mosquito was very worried. He wanted to help the flower to bloom again.

So, the mosquito started to hum a sweet song. He was singing so loudly, and so happily. The flower felt the songs vibrations. She started to move and sway. Her petals opened up until she bloomed bigger than ever before.

The mosquito was so happy! The flower was back to shining yellow in the sun. And they both live happily ever after.

Sam was a brave little boy. He loved playing in the park and exploring new places. One night, he decided to take a walk on a dark path. Sam was a bit fearful, but he kept walking.

Suddenly, Sam heard a loud noise coming from behind a nearby bush. He moved closer to get a better look and found a chocolate wrapper. He was curious, so he stepped closer and closer.

At that moment, there was a loud roar and a huge bear jumped out of the bush! Sam was so scared he screamed and ran away. The bear chased after him, but Sam was too quick.

He ran until he reached a gate. He quickly shut the gate and the bear was locked outside. He was very relieved, but his heart was still pounding. Sam was happy he was safe and he thanked his strength and courage.

Once upon a time, there was a little dog named Max. Max loved to play and run around in the park. One day, Max saw a big bone on the ground. He wanted to take it home and show it to his family. But when he tried to pick it up, he saw another dog coming towards him. The other dog was much bigger than Max and growled at him. Max was scared and ran away without the bone.

Max went home without the bone and felt sad. His family asked him what was wrong and he told them the story. His family told him that sometimes in life, we have to be obedient and not take things that don't belong to us. They also told him that it's important to stand up for ourselves, but not to be mean to others.

From that day on, Max was more obedient and didn't take things that didn't belong to him. He still loved to play and run around in the park, but he knew that he had to be careful and respectful to others. And when he saw the big bone again, he didn't take it. Instead, he showed it to his family and they all had a good laugh.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a white dress that she loved to wear. It was soft like a pillow and made of a special fabric called velvet.

One day, Lily went for a walk in the park. She saw a beautiful flower with petals as soft as velvet. She admired the flower and thought it was the prettiest thing she had ever seen.

Lily picked the flower and put it in her hair. She felt happy and proud to wear the flower. She showed it to everyone she met and they all admired it too.

From that day on, Lily always looked for pretty things to admire. She loved the feeling of joy it brought her. And she always remembered the beautiful white velvet flower that made her so happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little beetle named Benny. Benny was a friendly beetle who loved to play with his friends in the garden. One day, Benny saw a strange light glowing in the distance. He asked his friend, "What's that light?"

His friend replied, "I don't know, but it looks troubled."

Benny was curious and wanted to investigate. As he got closer, he saw that the light was coming from a jar. Inside the jar was a firefly who was trapped and couldn't get out. Benny knew he had to help the firefly. He used his strong beetle legs to push the jar over, and the firefly was free.

The firefly thanked Benny and said, "You are a kind beetle. You saved me from being trapped forever in that jar."

From that day on, Benny and the firefly became the best of friends. They would play together in the garden, and the firefly's glow would light up the night sky. Benny was happy that he could help his new friend and make the garden a happier place.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy who loved to play with his toys. One day, he went to the park to play with his friend, Sammy. They were having a great time until Timmy's favorite toy car got stuck in the mud. He tried to pull it out, but it wouldn't budge.

Sammy said, "Let's ask the big kids for help!"

Timmy replied, "No, they always make fun of me because I'm little."

Sammy said, "Don't worry, I'll go ask them for you."

Sammy went over to the big kids and said, "Can you help my friend Timmy? His toy car is stuck in the mud."

The big kids said, "Sure, we'll help him."

Timmy was surprised and happy that the big kids helped him. He surrendered his toy car to them and they pulled it out of the mud. Timmy thanked them and they all played together. The gloomy feeling Timmy had before was gone and he had a great day with his friends.

Once upon a time, there lived a little girl called Daisy. Daisy loved going to the hospital and visiting all the patients. She saw them as her friends and made sure they were happy.

One day, Daisy decided to make a special treat for the patients. She baked a yummy cake with lots of sprinkles and frosting. Everyone was so excited when they saw it!

The patients separated into two lines so that each one could have a slice of cake. Daisy made sure to give them all equal cuts; so that everyone had the same size slice.

After eating, the patients thanked Daisy for the yummy cake. They said it made them feel better, like they were in a world of happiness.

Daisy was happy to help the patients, and they were all very grateful. They were excited to see her whenever she visited the hospital.

Sara and Ben were best friends. They liked to play in the park every day. They had a ball, a bike and a kite. They shared their toys and had fun.

One day, they saw a big sign in the park. It said: "Keep the park tidy. Put your trash in the bin." Sara and Ben nodded. They wanted to help keep the park clean.

They played with their ball for a while. They kicked it, threw it and caught it. Then they wanted to play with their bike. Sara said: "Let's skip to the bike. Skipping is fun." Ben agreed. They skipped to the bike, holding hands.

But when they got to the bike, they saw something bad. Someone had left a lot of trash on the grass. There were cans, wrappers and bottles. Sara and Ben felt sad and angry. They said: "Who did this? This is not tidy. This is not nice."

They looked around and saw a boy. He was holding a can of soda. He was about to throw it on the ground. Sara and Ben ran to him. They said: "Stop! Don't do that. You have to put your trash in the bin. That's the rule. If you don't, the park will be dirty and the animals will be sick."

The boy looked at them. He felt ashamed. He said: "I'm sorry. I didn't know. I was just lazy. I won't do it again." He took his can and walked to the bin. He threw it inside. He said: "Thank you for telling me. Can I play with you?"

Sara and Ben smiled. They said: "Sure. You can play with us. But you have to be tidy and share." The boy nodded. He said: "OK. I will. What do you want to play?"

Sara said: "How about kite? We have a nice kite. We can take turns to fly it." Ben said: "Good idea. Let's go." They gave the boy a pass to join their group. They skipped to the kite, holding hands. They flew the kite high in the sky. They were happy and proud. They had made a new friend and kept the park tidy.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, Lily went to the park with her mommy and daddy. They had a picnic and ate yummy sandwiches. After they finished eating, Lily's daddy took out a knife and cut some fruit for dessert.

As they were eating the fruit, Lily noticed the sky was turning orange and pink. She pointed to the sunset and said, "Look, mommy, pretty colors!" They all watched the sunset together and it was so beautiful.

After the sunset, they packed up their things and went home. Lily was tired from playing at the park, so she went to bed early. She dreamed about the yummy fruit and the pretty sunset.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Sally. Sally was nervous because she had to dress up for a big party. The party was for the whole nation, and everyone was going to be there.

Sally's mom said, "Don't worry, Sally. I will help you dress up nice and pretty for the party." They picked out a pretty dress with flowers on it. Sally felt a little better, but she was still nervous.

At the party, everyone was happy and having fun. Sally saw her friend Tim. Tim said, "Wow, Sally! You look so pretty in your dress!" Sally smiled and felt much better. She was not nervous anymore. She had a great time at the party with her friends and family. And the nation had a wonderful celebration.

Once there was a little girl named Sue. She was only three and she wanted to be able to communicate with her family. She started to think of different ways she could let her family know what she wanted.

Her parents suggested that she should learn some signs. They showed her some useful sign language and she liked it very much. Every night before bed, Sue practiced signing the words she had learned.

Sign language was very useful for Sue. She was able to tell her family what she wanted and what she didn’t want. Her family was very proud of her for learning sign language.

Sue was very happy she had learned sign language. She was able to understand her family and let them know what she wanted.

Once upon a time, there was a little frog. He was very dirty and needed a bath. His mom said, "Let's go to the pond and clean you up." They hopped to the pond and the mom helped the little frog turn over a leaf. The leaf was big and clean, perfect for a bath. The little frog was happy and splashed around in the water. When they were done, the little frog was clean and shiny. He was so happy he turned around and gave his mom a big hug. From then on, the little frog always remembered to stay clean.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to whistle while she played with her toys. One day, while she was walking in the park, she met a kind old man who winked at her. "Hello, little one," he said. "Why are you so thoughtful?"

Lily thought for a moment and then replied, "I like to think about how I can make others happy." The old man smiled and said, "That's very kind of you. Did you know that when you whistle, it makes others happy too?"

Lily was surprised and asked, "Really?" The old man nodded and said, "Yes, it's true. You have a special talent that can bring joy to others."

From that day on, Lily made it her mission to whistle whenever she could. She even taught her friends how to whistle too. And whenever they did, they saw how it made others smile. Lily learned that even the smallest things, like whistling, can make a big difference in someone's day.

Once upon a time, there was a girl called Lucy. One day Lucy went for a walk in a park. As she walked, she saw a huge spot on a tree. It was a terrible spot.

Lucy was worried. She thought the spot would ruin the tree. She didn't know what to do.

Suddenly, she had an idea. She took a cloth from her pocket and carefully wiped the spot until it was gone.

Lucy was no longer worried. She smiled and happily walked away. The tree was safe and the spot was gone.

Once upon a time, there was a dragon. It was big and strong. It had wings and a long neck. Every day, the dragon would fly over the hills and forests. One day, it saw something special in the distance. It was a flame! It flew closer and saw that the flame was very big and hot.

The dragon thought the flame was impressive. It used its long neck to pull the flame towards it. The dragon was so happy and held the flame close. The flame was warm and made the dragon feel safe.

The dragon flew back to its home with the flame. It put the flame in a special place in the cave. Now the dragon had a home for its flame. Whenever it wanted to feel safe it would look at the flame and smile.

The end.

Lily loved to swing. She liked to feel the wind in her hair and the sun on her face. She liked to go high and fast and pretend she was flying. She had a swing in her backyard, but it was small and old. She wished she had a large swing, like the one in the park.

One night, Lily had a dream. She dreamed that she was in the park, and there was a large swing waiting for her. It was blue and shiny and had a soft seat. Lily ran to the swing and climbed on. She pushed with her feet and swung higher and higher. She felt happy and free.

But then, she heard a loud noise. It was her mom, waking her up. "Lily, it's time to get up. You have to go to school today." Lily opened her eyes and saw her mom smiling at her. She felt sad and wanted to stay in her dream. She said, "Mom, can we go to the park today? I want to swing on the large swing."

Her mom hugged her and said, "Maybe we can go after school, if you are good. But first, you have to get ready and eat your breakfast. Come on, let's go." Lily got out of bed and followed her mom. She hoped that her dream would come true. She still loved to swing.

Sammy was a very happy boy. He had a pet cat that he loved very much. Every morning they would go outside together and play.

One day Sammy's mom gave him a surprise. She gave him a special toy that could print. Sammy was very excited and he immediately hugged his mom.

Sammy started playing with the toy. He loved watching it print pictures. He would pick pictures of his pet cat, and it would come out looking very comfortable. Sammy thought it was so much fun that he printed lots of pictures of his pet.

His mom was so happy that Sammy was having so much fun. She was glad she had given him the toy. Sammy and his pet cat were best friends forever, and the toy made it even more special for them.

Once upon a time, a grumpy old man named Jack had a bag full of worries. Whenever Jack opened the bag, new worries came out to play.

One day, Jack found himself feeling a bit down, so he decided to take a walk. On his way, he passed by a beautiful garden filled with flowers and a pond full of happy ducks. As he admired the garden, he heard a voice say, "Come learn the way to heal your worries. Let me show you."

It was a wise little old man sitting on a rock near the pond. Jack was curious and asked, "How can I heal my worries?"

The old man said, "Just learn how to leave your worries in the bag and carry on with a smile. That's the secret to healing!"

Jack thanked the old man and slowly the worries lifted from his bag. With each step, Jack felt lighter and more carefree. When he finally reached home, he was no longer grumpy - he was free.

Once there was a little dog named Timmy. Timmy was a very modest dog, he loved to take naps, and play around in the garden. One day, Timmy decided he wanted to try something new. He wanted to go for a walk in the forest and find a wolf! He thought it would be fun to explore and find a new friend.

So, off he went! He followed a path through the trees, looking for a wolf. He could hear birds singing and the wind rustling through the leaves. Timmy was feeling brave and excited.

He came to a clearing and spotted a big gray wolf! Timmy was scared, but he stepped closer. The wolf looked at Timmy with big, friendly eyes. Timmy felt a bit more brave, so he tried to talk to the wolf. He said "Hi! I'm Timmy and I wanted to be friends."

The wolf understood and bowed his head in response. After that, Timmy and the wolf became the best of friends! They went on new adventures in the forest, played chase and even had snack together!

Every time Timmy went for a visit, the wolf was always there, and they both appreciated their time together. Timmy was so glad he had the courage to try something new and make a new friend!

Jimmy was looking at the wall. He saw a print of a strange creature with funny eyes. He was stunned and he just stared at it. His mom heard him and came to see what was happening. She saw the print and said “This is a very mild creature, Jimmy. We don't need to be scared of it.” Jimmy was still staring at it and didn’t say anything.

His mom got closer. Suddenly, the creature jumped out of the print. Jimmy screamed and ran away. His mom yelled at the creature but it was too late. The creature ran away and was never seen again.

Jimmy was very scared and his mom was sad. They both stared at the print but this time, they were scared and worried. They never saw that creature again.

Once there was a little girl called Amy. She was very curious and loved exploring. One day she asked her mummy, "What's a stadium?"

Mummy replied, "Well, a stadium is a very busy place where people supply food and drinks to watch sports. Do you want to go to one?"

Amy was so excited, so she and mummy travelled to the stadium. When they arrived, Amy was amazed by how big it was. It was full of people, and she could hear music playing in the background.

Mummy took her inside and showed her around. Amy was amazed at all the busy places there were to explore. She was given food and drinks to try and people were supplying a lot of different types of items.

Amy had a wonderful time and she will never forget her first visit to the stadium.

Lily was a curious girl who liked to explore. One day, she saw a big puddle in the park. She wanted to know what it felt like to splash in it. She ran to the puddle and jumped in with both feet. She laughed as the water splashed on her legs and shoes.

But she did not see that her scarf was dragging behind her. Her scarf dipped into the puddle and got very wet. It soaked up the water like a sponge. Lily did not notice until she felt something heavy and cold around her neck. She pulled on her scarf and saw that it was dripping with water.

She was surprised and a little sad. She liked her scarf. It was pink and soft and warm. She did not want it to be wet and cold and heavy. She wondered if it would ever be dry and fluffy again. She took off her scarf and wrung out the water. She looked for a sunny spot to lay it down.

She found a bench near a flower bed. She spread her scarf on the bench and hoped that the sun would dry it soon. She decided to wait and watch her scarf. She was curious to see how it would change. She hoped it would be pink and soft and warm again. She smiled and hummed a song. She was happy to have a scarf and a puddle and a sunny day.

Lily wanted to buy a new toy. She saw a big doll with long hair and a pink dress in the shop window. She asked her mom to buy it for her.

"Maybe later, sweetie. We have to go to the bank first. It won't take long, I promise." Mom said.

Lily was impatient. She did not want to go to the bank. She wanted to play with the doll. She pulled mom's hand and said, "Please, mom, please. I want the doll now."

Mom sighed. She looked at her watch. She had to pay some bills at the bank. She did not have much time. She said, "Okay, okay. We'll buy the doll first. But you have to be good and stay with me. The bank is not a safe place for little girls."

Lily was happy. She smiled and hugged mom. She said, "Thank you, mom, thank you. You are the best mom ever."

Mom and Lily went into the shop. Mom paid for the doll and gave it to Lily. Lily hugged the doll and said, "Hello, doll. I'm Lily. You are my new friend."

Mom and Lily left the shop. They walked to the bank. Lily held the doll in her arms. She did not notice the man who followed them. He had a mask and a gun. He wanted to rob the bank. He saw mom's purse. He thought it had a lot of money. He decided to take it.

He ran after mom and Lily. He grabbed mom's purse. He said, "Give me that. It's mine now."

Mom screamed. She tried to get her purse back. She said, "No, no. Leave us alone. Help, help."

Lily was scared. She dropped the doll. She cried. She said, "Mom, mom. What's happening?"

The man pushed mom to the ground. He ran away with the purse. He did not see the police car that was coming. The police saw him. They chased him. They caught him. They took him to jail.

Mom and Lily were safe. The police gave mom her purse back. They said, "Are you okay, ma'am? We're sorry this happened to you. He's a bad man. He won't hurt you anymore."

Mom thanked the police. She hugged Lily. She said, "We're okay, sweetie. We're okay. Don't worry. He's gone now."

Lily looked for her doll. She saw it on the sidewalk. She ran to get it. She said, "Doll, doll. I'm sorry I dropped you. Are you okay?"

The doll was okay. It had a small tear on its dress. Lily did not mind. She said, "It's okay, doll. You are still pretty. I love you."

Mom and Lily went home. They did not go to the bank. They did not need to. They had each other. They were happy.

Lily and Ben were friends who liked to play sport. They had a ball and a net in the backyard. They took turns to shoot the ball into the net. They had fun and cheered for each other.

One day, a new boy moved in next door. His name was Sam. He had a big toy gun that made loud noises. He saw Lily and Ben playing sport and wanted to join them. He said, "Can I play with you? I have a gun. We can shoot the ball and make it explode."

Lily and Ben did not like the idea. They said, "No, thank you. We like to play sport. We do not like to shoot things. Shooting is not a sport. It is dangerous and scary. You can hurt someone or break something."

Sam did not listen. He said, "You are boring. I am adventurous. I like to shoot things. It is fun and exciting. Watch me." He aimed his gun at the ball and pulled the trigger. The gun made a loud bang and the ball popped. Lily and Ben were shocked and sad. They liked their ball. It was their favorite toy.

Sam laughed and said, "See? I told you it was fun. Do you want to try?" Lily and Ben shook their heads. They said, "No, we do not. You are not adventurous. You are mean and rude. You ruined our game and our ball. You are not our friend. Go away."

Sam felt sorry. He realized he had made a mistake. He said, "I am sorry. I did not mean to hurt you or your ball. I just wanted to play with you. I thought shooting was a sport. I did not know it was bad. Can you forgive me? Can we be friends?"

Lily and Ben thought for a moment. They said, "We forgive you. But you have to promise to never shoot things again. Shooting is not a sport. It is not fun. It is wrong. You have to learn to play nice and respect others. Then we can be friends."

Sam nodded. He said, "I promise. I will never shoot things again. I will learn to play nice and respect others. Thank you for forgiving me. Can we play sport together?"

Lily and Ben smiled. They said, "Yes, we can. We have another ball. We can share it with you. Come on, let's play sport together."

They gave Sam their ball and their net. They taught him how to shoot the ball into the net. They had fun and cheered for each other. They became friends who liked to play sport. They learned that shooting is not a sport. It is a bad thing. They learned that being adventurous is not about being dangerous. It is about being curious and trying new things. They learned that being friends is about being kind and caring. They learned a valuable lesson.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys and explore the world around her. One day, she went to the park with her elderly grandmother. They had a lot of fun playing together, but when it was time to go home, Lily couldn't find her favorite toy.

She looked everywhere, but it was nowhere to be found. Her grandmother told her that sometimes things get lost and we need to let them go. Lily was sad, but then her grandmother showed her an anchor. She explained that just like an anchor keeps a boat from drifting away, we need to anchor our feelings and not let them drift away.

Lily didn't quite understand, but then her grandmother showed her how to lock her feelings inside and not let them get away. She told her that it's okay to feel sad, but we shouldn't let it take over our happiness. Lily learned that it's important to anchor our feelings and lock them in, so we can always find them when we need them. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to draw pictures with her crayons. One day, Lily drew an amazing picture of a rainbow with lots of colors.

Her mom came in and said, "Wow, Lily! That's an amazing picture! Can you tell me about it?"

Lily replied, "I drew a rainbow with red, orange, yellow, green, blue, and purple colors."

Her mom smiled and said, "That's wonderful! Let's hang it up on the wall so everyone can see it."

As they hung up the picture, Lily's mom reminded her, "Remember, Lily, it's important to always stir your imagination and keep creating amazing things."

One morning, Jack woke up feeling excited. He sensed something was different.

Jack asked his mum, "Mum, what is today?"

His mum replied, "Today is a special day, Jack. We are going to measure the dead tree in the backyard!"

Jack was so happy he jumped up and down. He asked, "How will we measure it?"

His mum said, "We will measure it with a tape measure. We will measure the height and width of the tree!"
