Jack enjoyed measuring the dead tree. He stretched out the long tape measure from the top of the tree trunk to the ground, and then around the trunk. In the end, Jack was proud of the measurements he made on that special morning!

Anna and Ben are playing with wool. They have many colors of wool. They like to make things with wool. They can tie wool together and make shapes.

"Look, I made a flower with pink wool!" Anna says. She shows Ben her wool flower. She ties it to her hair.

"That is pretty, Anna. Can you make one for me?" Ben asks. He likes flowers too.

"Sure, Ben. What color do you want?" Anna asks. She has blue, green, yellow, and purple wool.

"I want a blue flower, please. Blue is my favorite color." Ben says. He gives Anna some blue wool.

Anna ties the blue wool together and makes a flower for Ben. She ties it to his shirt. "There, now you have a flower too!" Anna says. She smiles at Ben.

"Thank you, Anna. You are very good at making flowers." Ben says. He hugs Anna. They are happy.

They hear Mom calling them. "Anna, Ben, come inside. It is time for lunch. I made some delicious soup for you." Mom says.

Anna and Ben run to the kitchen. They smell the soup. It smells good. They wash their hands and sit at the table. Mom gives them each a bowl of soup and a spoon.

"Enjoy your soup, my little flowers." Mom says. She kisses them on their heads.

Anna and Ben eat their soup. It is warm and tasty. They like the soup. They say, "Mmm, this is delicious, Mom. Thank you."

Mom smiles at them. She is proud of them. They are good children. They love wool, flowers, and soup.

Tom and Lily are twins. They like to play outside. One day, they see a trail in the woods. They want to see where it goes.

"Let's go, Tom!" Lily says. She runs on the trail. Tom is lazy. He does not want to run. He walks slowly.

"Wait for me, Lily!" Tom says. He hopes Lily will stop. But Lily does not stop. She runs faster and faster. She sees a big hill. She wants to climb it.

"Look, Tom! A hill!" Lily says. She climbs the hill. Tom is tired. He does not want to climb. He sits on the trail.

"Come on, Tom! It's fun!" Lily says. She is on top of the hill. She sees a lake. She wants to swim.

"Look, Tom! A lake!" Lily says. She runs down the hill. Tom is bored. He does not want to swim. He lies on the trail.

"Have fun, Lily!" Tom says. He hopes Lily will come back soon. But Lily does not come back soon. She swims and swims. She sees a boat. She wants to ride it.

"Look, Tom! A boat!" Lily says. She swims to the boat. Tom is lonely. He does not want to ride. He cries on the trail.

"Where are you, Lily?" Tom says. He hopes Lily will hear him. But Lily does not hear him. She rides the boat. She sees an island. She wants to explore it.

"Look, Tom! An island!" Lily says. She jumps off the boat. Tom is sad. He does not want to explore. He misses Lily.

"Please come back, Lily!" Tom says. He hopes Lily will see him. But Lily does not see him. She explores the island. She sees a cave. She wants to enter it.

"Look, Tom! A cave!" Lily says. She enters the cave. Tom is scared. He does not want to enter. He wants Lily.

"Lily, Lily, where are you?" Tom says. He hopes Lily will answer him. But Lily does not answer him. She is lost in the cave. She is scared too.

"Tom, Tom, where are you?" Lily says. She hopes Tom will find her. But Tom does not find her. He is still on the trail. He is crying.

They both wish they had stayed together. They both want to go home. They both need each other. They both love each other.

Once there was an egg. It was gentle, but it had a hard job. It had to balance on a wall. At first, it was okay. The egg would just sit there, and the wall would hold it up. But one day, the wind blew. It was strong and harsh. It was so strong, that the egg started to tilt and it almost fell off the wall. But the egg was brave. It grabbed the sides of the wall with its body, and balanced itself back up again. The egg felt proud. Even in the harshest of winds, it stayed strong and balanced.

Lilly was eager to explore her new house. She ran from room to room until she found the living room. In the middle of the room was a big couch. Lilly saw that the couch was very colorful, but it looked a bit fake. She was excited to sit on it and explore!

Lilly looked around the couch to see if she could find anything special. Suddenly, she spotted a sparkly button on the side. She pushed it and the couch slowly started to move away from the wall! Lilly was amazed! Behind the couch, she found a secret door! She couldn't open it, but she was curious to know what was inside.

Lilly ran to find her mom and dad. She was sure that they would be able to open the door. When they all came back to the living room, they saw that Lilly had discovered a secret door. Her father pushed the door open and they all could quickly see what was behind it. It was Lilly’s very own mini theater! It was filled with fun decorations, real theater chairs and a mini stage. Lilly couldn’t believe her eyes! Her parents had revealed the perfect secret playroom for her! She was so excited, she could hardly contain her smile.

Once there was a little boy named Sam. He was only three years old and he was always curious and adventurous. One day, he was playing at the beach when he saw something unusual in the sand. He bent down and carefully plucked it out of the sand. It was an incredible oyster!

Sam was so excited. He had never seen an oyster before. He looked at it with amazement and wanted to see what was inside. So he slowly turned it over and opened it. Inside was a beautiful pearl!

Sam's eyes widened in surprise. He couldn't believe his luck. He ran home to show his mum the incredible pearl he had found in the oyster. When she saw the pearl, she gasped in amazement.

Mum: "Wow, Sam, that's incredible! You found this in the sand?"

Sam beamed with pride.

Sam: "Yes! I turned the oyster over and there it was!"

Mum smiled and gave Sam a big hug. She was so proud of her little explorer.

They both knew that this would be an amazing keepsake from this special day.

Once upon a time, there was a girl who loved to count. She had a shiny green notebook in which she kept track of all her tallies. Every morning, she'd take out her notebook and count how many sweet things she had.

One day, she found a basket of fresh apples in her garden. She counted how many were in the basket and wrote the number down in her notebook. Then, she counted how many sweet strawberries were growing in her backyard. Once the tally was done, she wrote the number in her notebook too.

Next, the girl counted the birds that were flying in the sky. There were so many, it took her a little while to count them all! When she was finished, she wrote down the number of birds in her notebook.

At the end of the day, the girl felt so proud of herself for all the counting she'd done. She looked through her notebook and smiled as she read the numbers written in its pages.

Anna loved her kitten, Luna. Luna was small and soft and had blue eyes. Anna liked to play with Luna and cuddle her. Sometimes, Anna wondered how much Luna weighed. She wanted to know if Luna was growing well.

One day, Anna had an idea. She asked her mom, "Mom, can I weigh Luna?"

Her mom smiled and said, "Sure, honey. Let's go to the bathroom. There is a scale there."

Anna picked up Luna and followed her mom. She put Luna on the scale and looked at the numbers. She did not know what they meant, but her mom told her.

"Luna weighs four pounds. That's very good for a kitten. She is healthy and strong."

Anna was happy and gave Luna a hug. Luna purred and licked Anna's face. Anna said, "I love you, Luna. You are my best friend."

Her mom said, "You are very thoughtful, Anna. You care about Luna a lot. She is lucky to have you."

Anna and Luna smiled and went back to their room. They played with a ball of yarn and had a lot of fun.

Once upon a time, there was a charming dog named Max. Max loved to play with his ball in the park. One day, Max saw a box with a label on it. He did not know what the label said.

Max wanted to find out what was in the box, so he asked his friend, a cat named Tom. Tom didn't know what the label said either. He just gave a shrug. Max and Tom decided to open the box.

When they opened the box, they found a big cake inside. Max and Tom were very happy and started to eat the cake. But, the cake was not good. It made Max and Tom feel sick. They should not have eaten the cake.

Sara likes to eat avocado. She likes to cut it with a knife and scoop it with a spoon. She likes to share it with her cat, Luna. Luna likes to lick the avocado from Sara's spoon.

One day, Sara finds a big avocado in the kitchen. She is very happy. She takes the knife and the spoon and goes to the table. She wants to cut the avocado and eat it with Luna.

But when she tries to cut the avocado, it is very hard. She cannot cut it. She pushes harder with the knife, but it does not work. She feels sad and angry.

She sees her brother, Tom, sitting on the couch. He is watching TV. He has a remote in his hand. He is changing the channels.

"Tom, help me!" Sara says. "I want to eat this avocado, but I cannot cut it. It is too hard."

Tom looks at Sara. He sees the avocado and the knife and the spoon. He laughs.

"That is not an avocado, silly," he says. "That is a coconut. You cannot eat a coconut like that. You need a hammer and a nail to open it."

Sara feels more sad and angry. She thinks Tom is very rude. He is not nice to her. He does not help her. He only laughs at her.

She picks up the coconut and throws it at Tom. It hits him on the head. He drops the remote. He says "Ow!"

Sara runs to her room. She slams the door. She closes it very hard. She does not want to talk to Tom. She does not want to see him. She only wants to eat avocado with Luna.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Jane. She loved to explore and had lots of adventures.

One day, Jane decided to walk to the park. On the way, she began to stumble. She fell over and hurt her knee. She started to cry.

All of a sudden, Jane stoped crying when she saw something. It was a prioe on the ground! It was sparkly and made of gold. Jane was so happy and picked it up.

She looked around, but she couldn't see who owned the prize. Jane was very curious, but the story of the prize was unknown.

Jane took the prize and went back home. That night, Jane put it on the mantelpiece where she could always see it. Jane was very happy with her special unknown prize.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Ruby. Ruby was three years old and she loved playing with her toys. One day, her mommy called her name.

“Ruby! Come here,” said her mommy. Ruby came running into the kitchen. Her mommy was at the sink, washing something green and leafy.

“Mommy, what's that?” asked Ruby.

“It's broccoli,” said her mommy.

Ruby crinkled up her face. She wasn't sure that she liked broccoli.

Her mommy looked worried. “You have to eat some broccoli, okay, Ruby?”

Ruby nodded nervously. She didn't want to make her mommy mad.

So Ruby ate the broccoli. To her surprise, it wasn’t so bad after all! Ruby smiled and hugged her mommy.

“Thanks for calling me, Mommy!” said Ruby.

Once upon a time there lived a young girl called Lucy. She was only three years old and loved to explore the world. One day, she decided to take a walk in the nearby forest. As she walked, Lucy heard a noise coming from a temple in the distance. She had never seen a temple before, so Lucy decided to find out what it was.

When she arrived at the temple, Lucy opened the door slowly. Inside, she saw a gentle giant. The giant was so big that Lucy was scared, so she screamed.

The gentle giant then said in a kind voice, “Don’t be scared, little one. I’m not here to hurt you.”

Lucy was relieved and stepped closer to the giant. She sighed with relief and said, “Thank you for being so gentle.”

The giant smiled and asked if Lucy wanted to explore the temple. Lucy couldn’t believe her luck and eagerly nodded her head. The giant helped her explore the temple and showed her all the secret places. Together, they had a wonderful adventure and Lucy never forgot the day she met the gentle giant.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Emmy. Emmy loved to explore. She went on a hike with her family to find something unique.

As they walked down the trail, Emmy came upon a round rock that fit perfectly in her tiny hand. It was a unique rock!

"Mommy!" she shouted. "What do you think of my rock?"

"That's wonderful, Emmy!" said her mom. "That rock is one-of-a-kind!"

Emmy beamed with pride. She kept on walking down the trail, looking for more unique things.

Soon, she found a shell that fit perfectly in her pocket. It was beautiful and special.

Emmy ran back to her family, showing off her new discovery.

"Look what I found!" She said.

Her parents smiled and told Emmy how lucky she was.

Emmy was happy, she had found something truly unique on her family trail.

Anna loves roses. She likes to smell them and touch them. She has a rose garden in her backyard. She waters the roses every day.

One day, Anna sees a new rose in her garden. It is big and red and shiny. It is the most beautiful rose she has ever seen. She runs to it and says, "Hello, rose! You are so great! Can I be your friend?"

The rose does not say anything. It just stands there. Anna feels sad. She thinks the rose does not like her. She says, "Please, rose, talk to me. I want to play with you."

Then, she hears a voice. It is not the rose. It is her mom. She says, "Anna, what are you doing? Come inside, it is time for lunch."

Anna turns around and sees her mom. She says, "Mom, look at this rose! It is so great! But it does not talk to me. Why not?"

Her mom smiles and hugs her. She says, "Anna, roses do not talk. They are plants. They can only show their beauty and their smell. But they can still be your friends. You can admire them and take care of them. And they will make you happy."

Anna nods and smiles. She says, "Okay, mom. I understand. I love roses. They are my friends. Can I bring this rose inside?"

Her mom says, "Sure, you can. But be careful. It has thorns. They can hurt you."

Anna says, "I will be careful. Thank you, mom." She picks the rose gently and holds it in her hand. She says, "Come on, rose. Let's go inside. You are so great!"

Tom and Lily liked to play in the pool. They had many toys to swim with, like balls and rings and ducks. But their favorite toy was a big whale that could squirt water from its mouth. They called it Wally.

One day, Tom had an idea. He wanted to see how much Wally weighed. He asked Lily to help him. "Let's take Wally out of the pool and put him on the scale," he said. "Then we can see how big he is."

Lily agreed. She thought it was a fun game. They both grabbed Wally and lifted him out of the water. He was very heavy and wet. They carried him to the scale and put him on it. The scale made a loud beep and showed a number.

"Wow, Wally is 20 pounds!" Tom exclaimed. "He is the heaviest toy we have."

Lily nodded. She was proud of Wally. He was their original toy. They had made him from an old pillow and some fabric. They had painted him blue and white and glued a plastic bottle on his head. He was very special to them.

They decided to put Wally back in the pool. They lifted him again and walked towards the water. But they did not see the hose that was lying on the ground. They tripped over it and fell down. Wally flew out of their hands and landed on the grass.

"Oh no, Wally!" they cried. They ran to him and picked him up. He was dirty and torn. His bottle was broken and his water was gone. He looked very sad.

They hugged him and said they were sorry. They tried to fix him, but they could not. They felt very bad. They had lost their favorite toy.

They did not know what to do. They wished they had never taken Wally out of the pool. They wished they had just played with him and enjoyed him. They learned a lesson. They learned that some things are better left alone. They learned that some things are too precious to weigh.

Mary was very tidy. She liked to keep her room clean and her toys in the correct places. One day, Mary had the idea to build a castle. She found some boxes and a big blanket and pushed them into the corner of her room.

Then she went to find her mother. "Mama, can you help me build my castle?" she asked.

"Of course I can," said her mother. She found some tape and they worked together to make the castle.

"I'm going to put a door on the castle," said Mary gleefully.

"Ok," said her mother.

It was almost finished when Mary heard a rumble in the sky. "What's that?" she asked.

"That's the rain, sweetheart," her mother said. Suddenly, the room was filled with the sound of rain. "Oh no!" said Mary.

But, with the help of her mother, Mary found an old umbrella. She pushed it over her castle, to keep it safe from the rain.

"All done!" said Mary's mother.

Mary smiled with pride. Her castle was safe and the rain had stopped. "Thank you," she said.

Mary's mother handed her an old toy soldier. "Here," she said, "to guard your castle."

Once upon a time, there was a child who was always busy. One day, the child wanted to travel. So, they set off in search of adventure.

On the way, they met a stranger. The child's heart sank because they were scared. But even though the child felt scared, they decided not to turn back.

After walking for some time, the child arrived in a far away place. Everything seemed strange and unfamiliar. The child felt lost and confused. But, the stranger kept talking and so the child followed them.

Suddenly, the stranger grabbed the child. There was nowhere to run! The child screamed but no one helped. The stranger took the child away to a busy place.

The end. Unfortunately, the child's travels didn't end well. The stranger took the child away and never returned. The child was never seen again.

Jake and Jane were best friends. Every day when school finished they liked to swing together on the swing in the park. One day when they were swinging, they saw an old station.

"Let's explore the station," said Jane.

Jake smiled in agreement and they both ran towards the station. Inside, there was a big room with a light coming from the ceiling.

"Wow, this is so cool," squealed Jane.

The two friends stepped into the light and started to explore the station. They had a lot of fun, swinging and playing games all around the place.

When the two friends arrived back at the park, they couldn't wait to tell their friends all about the fun they had inside the old station.

Once upon a time there was a boat that loved to sail. It went out on the big blue sea every day and had lots of fun. One day, the boat saw a big square. The boat was curious and wanted to explore.

The boat sailed closer, and saw that it was an island. On the island, there were lots of friendly animals, like cats and dogs. The boat was so happy, it wanted to meet the animals and have some fun.

The animals were so helpful. They showed the boat all the best places to swim and play. They even took the boat for a sail around the island. The animals and the boat had so much fun together.

At the end of the day, the boat had to leave. It said goodbye to the animals and thanked them for being so helpful. Then, the boat sailed away and was back on the big blue sea before long.

Dog and Cat were best friends. One day they were playing in the garden when they spotted something strange. It was a smelly old box. Curiosity got the better of them and the two pets decided to take a closer look.

Dog pricked up his ears and said, "I think I can hear something inside." Cat carefully used her claws to cut open the top of the box and out popped a little purple mouse! It was holding a shiny golden key in its paws.

The mouse saw the two pets and started to shiver. It had been trying to steal the key when they found it! Dog and Cat quickly scooped it up and set it free.

The mouse thanked them and scurried away, leaving the wonderful golden key behind. Dog and Cat looked at each other in surprise and couldn't help but laugh. They had caught the thief and saved the day!

Lily and Tom were playing in the park. They saw a big truck with many pictures of candy on it. They were curious and wanted to see the candy.

"Look, Tom, candy truck!" Lily said. "Let's go and get some."

They ran to the truck and knocked on the door. No one answered. They tried to open the door, but it was locked. They looked around and saw a window. They climbed on a box and peeked inside.

They saw many bags of candy in the truck. They also saw a man sleeping on a chair. He had a big hat and a long beard. He looked scary.

"Wow, so much candy!" Tom said. "Let's take some and run away."

He reached his hand inside the window and grabbed a bag of candy. He pulled it out and smiled. He gave it to Lily and took another one.

Suddenly, the man woke up and saw them. He was angry and shouted. "Hey, you little thieves! Stop stealing my candy!"

He got up and ran to the door. He opened it and jumped out. He chased Lily and Tom, who dropped the candy and ran away.

But they were not fast enough. The man caught them and grabbed them by their arms. He dragged them to the truck and threw them inside. He locked the door and drove away.

Lily and Tom were scared and cried. They wished they had never been curious about the candy truck. They did not know where the man was taking them or what he would do to them. They had a bad ending.

Once there was a little boy who was very sleepy. He yawned and rubbed his eyes. He was scared of the dark. He looked around, but all he could see were shadows. Suddenly, he heard something. It was an oyster! He got very excited and ran towards it. The oyster was big and wide open. The little boy smiled and looked inside. He could see it was full of sparkly pearls. He wanted to take them all but he was too scared. He still remembered it was dark outside. So, he decided to take just one pearl, put it in his pocket, and go back home. As he ran home, he yawned once again. He was a happy boy!

Anna and Ben are twins. They are three years old. Today is their birthday. They are very happy. They want to celebrate with their friends.

They help their mom make a big cake. The cake is chocolate. It has pink and blue frosting. It has candles on top. Anna and Ben like chocolate. They think the cake will taste good.

Mom invites their friends over. They come with gifts and balloons. They play games and sing songs. They have fun. Anna and Ben share their toys. They are fair.

Then it is time to cut the cake. Mom lights the candles. She tells Anna and Ben to make a wish. They close their eyes and think hard. They wish for more fun and more cake.

They blow out the candles together. Everyone claps and cheers. Mom gives them each a big slice of cake. They take a bite. They smile. The cake tastes very good. They say, "Thank you, mom!"

They share their cake with their friends. They enjoy their birthday. They celebrate. They are very happy. They hug their mom. They love their mom. Mom loves them too.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved to play in the garden. One day, she found a spade and started digging in the dirt. She dug and dug until she found a little worm. "Hello, little worm," she said. "What are you doing?"

"I'm trying to find my way home," said the worm.

Lily became very compassionate and said, "Don't worry, little worm. I'll help you find your way home." So, she picked up the worm and put him back in the dirt. "There you go," she said. "Now you can find your way home."

The worm said, "Thank you, Lily. You're very kind."

Lily smiled and continued playing in the garden, knowing that she had helped someone in need. From that day on, Lily became known as the girl who was always kind and compassionate to others.

Sam was a curious 3 year old. One day, he was in the playground with his mom. He saw a black bicycle sitting in the corner. His mom saw too and she pointed at it. Sam was excited and ran over to it. He wanted to try it out. So he got on the seat and started pedaling. He found it was harder to pedal than it looked. But he kept trying until he was riding around. He had a lot of fun and couldn't wait to ride the black bicycle again.

The Dolphin was swimming in the big blue ocean. He looked happy and excited as he swam around.

But then he noticed someone was staring at him. He looked over, and saw a little girl standing on the beach. She was wearing a blue dress and she was staring right at him.

The Dolphin looked very sad. He felt so miserable. He wanted to be alone.

He tried to swim away, but the little girl kept on staring at him. He wanted to make her go away, but he didn't know how.

Suddenly, the little girl smiled. She waved at the Dolphin and he felt much happier. He stared back at her, and smiled too. Then he swam away, feeling much less miserable.

Max was a 3-year-old boy who loved puzzles. His mum was always looking out for new ones for him to enjoy.

One afternoon, Max's mum said to him, "Max, I have something special for you." She then offered him a new puzzle.

Max was so excited! He thanked his mum and said "Thanks, Mum!"

Max started to play with the puzzle. His mum asked if he was hungry and he nodded. She then offered Max a tasty snack.

Max said, "Yum! This is so tasty!"

He ate his snack and continued to play with his new puzzle. Max was very happy that his mum had offered him such a fun gift.

One day, Tom found a piece of paper. He wanted to make an ordinary aeroplane. He asked his mom, "Can you help me fold this paper?" Mom said, "Yes, I can help you."

They started to fold the paper. But Tom's little sister, Jane, wanted to play with the aeroplane too. Tom said, "No, it's mine!" Jane started to cry. Mom said, "Tom, you should share with your sister."

Tom thought for a moment. He said, "Okay, I will share." Jane stopped crying. They played with the aeroplane together. They had a lot of fun. The moral of the story is to share with others.

Lily got a new bucket for her birthday. She was very happy. She wanted to play with it in the sand. She took her bucket and her shovel and ran to the sandbox.

She saw Tom there. Tom was her friend. He had a red bucket and a blue shovel. He was making a big hill of sand. Lily said hello to Tom and showed him her new bucket. Tom liked her bucket. He said it was pretty.

Lily wanted to make a hill of sand too. She dug with her shovel and filled her bucket. She turned it over and lifted it up. She made a nice hill of sand. She was proud of her hill. She poked it with her finger to make a hole. She said it was a door for a mouse.

Tom saw her hill of sand. He thought it was funny. He wanted to poke it too. He ran to her hill and poked it with his shovel. He made a big hole. He said it was a door for a cat.

Lily was angry. She did not like what Tom did. She said he was mean. She grabbed her bucket and hit his hill of sand. She made it fall down. She said it was a mess.

Tom was angry too. He did not like what Lily did. He said she was rude. He grabbed his shovel and hit her hill of sand. He made it fall down too. He said it was a mess.

Lily and Tom were both very angry. They yelled at each other. They threw sand at each other. They made a big mess.

Mom saw them. She was not happy. She said they were naughty. She said they had to stop fighting. She said they had to share and be nice. She said they had to clean up the mess.

Lily and Tom felt sorry. They said they were sorry. They said they were friends. They hugged each other. They picked up their buckets and shovels. They cleaned up the mess. They made new hills of sand. They poked them with their fingers. They said they were doors for mice and cats. They smiled and laughed. They had fun.

Once upon a time, there was a big bird. He loved to whistle all day long. Every morning he would find a fresh stalk of celery and begin to whistle. The bird's whistle was so high and sweet that all of the other birds would chirp along.

One day, the bird spotted an extra-big stalk of celery in the garden. He immediately started to whistle with joy. He quickly ran over to the celery and began chomping on it. He was so delighted by the sweet taste that he whistled even louder.

Soon, he had finished the entire stalk of celery, and he was feeling very satisfied. He decided to take a nap in the sun and continue to whistle. Every so often, he would poke his head up to whistle a happy tune at the sky.

The bird felt so content that he stayed in the garden all day and whistled until the sun fell asleep. He thanked the sky for the big stalk of celery and snuggled into bed for the night.

Once upon a time, there lived a tidy little rabbit. One day, the rabbit's mommy asked the rabbit to help her make a spell. The rabbit happily agreed and watched carefully. Mommy waved her wand and said the magical words. The spell worked and the door locked.

The rabbit clapped her hands and said, “Mommy, can I make a spell too?” Mommy chuckled and replied, “Yes! But you need to be very careful and tidy when making a spell. Can you do that?”

The rabbit nodded her head, eager to try. She carefully waved her wand and said the words. Amazingly, the spell worked! The rabbit was so proud of herself and hugged her mommy.

From then on, the rabbit made many more spells. She always remembered to be tidy and careful. She even taught her friends how to make spells too. The rabbit was very happy whenever she cast a spell.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She was very sleepy and wanted to take a nap. Her mommy put her in bed and told her to close her eyes. After a minute, Lily fell asleep.

When she woke up, she was very hungry. She wanted to eat something yummy. Her mommy made her a sandwich with peanut butter and jelly. Lily loved it and ate it all up.

After she ate, she felt better and not so sleepy anymore. She played with her toys and had a lot of fun. But when it was time for bed, she was sleepy again. So, she went to bed and fell asleep in just a minute.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved going outside to play with his toys. One day, Timmy's mom took him to the park. They had to cross the street with lots of cars. Timmy's mom said, "Be careful, Timmy. We have to watch for traffic."

As they were crossing the street, a car came too close to them. Timmy's mom shouted, "Stop!" The car stopped just in time. Timmy's mom thanked the driver for being careful.

After they crossed the street, Timmy's mom bought him an ice cream cone. Timmy was very happy and ate his ice cream while playing with his toys in the park. He remembered to always be careful around traffic and never forget how his mom shouted to keep him safe. The end.

Ben and Lily like to play in the park. They like to slide, swing, and run. But today, they see something new. It is a big seat with wheels and a belt. It looks like fun.

"Let's try it!" Ben says. He runs to the seat and climbs in. He puts on the belt and holds the wheel. "Vroom, vroom!" he says.

Lily follows him. She wants to try it too. But she sees a sign. It has a picture of a seat with wheels and a belt, and a big red X. It says "No, no, no!"

"Lily, come on!" Ben says. He pushes a button. The seat makes a loud noise. It starts to move.

Lily is scared. She knows the seat is dangerous. She shouts, "Ben, stop! Get out! It is not a toy!"

But Ben does not hear her. He is too busy driving. He thinks he is having fun. He does not see the road. He does not see the cars. He does not see the trouble.

One day, there was a boy named Happy. Happy was three years old and very excited to explore the world. He asked his mother, "Where can I go today?" She smiled and suggested they go to the park.

Happy skipped along the path and admired the many trees, flowers and birds. He also noticed a quiet lake. Happy looked at the lake and sighed with contentment. He asked his mother, "What's this place called?" She replied, "It's called Peace Park. It's a place of peace and tranquility."

Happy were amazed by the beauty and calmness of the park. He thought it was the perfect place to relax. He asked his mother, "Can we come here again tomorrow?" She smiled and said, "Yes, we can come here as often as you want."

Happy smiled and thought to himself how nice it was to be wealthy and live in a peaceful place. That night, Happy dreamt of the park and how peaceful it made him feel. He also thought of how he wanted everyone in the world to know about Peace Park. He suggested to his mother, "Let's tell our friends about this place so they can come here and feel the peace, too."

His mother smiled and ruffled Happy's hair. She said, "That's a wonderful suggestion, Happy."

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his toys all day long. One day, his sister Sarah came to play with him. Timmy was happy to see her, but Sarah didn't want to play with Timmy's toys. She wanted to play with her own toys instead.

Timmy's face turned sad when he heard this. He didn't know what to do. But then he had an idea. He was a helpful boy, so he went to his room and got some of his own toys to share with Sarah. They played together and had lots of fun.

After a while, Sarah's face turned happy and she thanked Timmy for being so helpful. They continued to play together and had a great time. Timmy learned that sharing his toys was a good thing to do and it made him feel happy too.

Once there was a thin girl named Claire. Claire always wanted to feel relaxed, but couldn't find a way. She was too weighed down by her worries. She wanted to feel as light as a feather, so she could float away.

One day she decided to go find a way to relax. She ran and ran until she stumbled upon a beautiful pond. It sparkled in the sun, like a thousand diamonds. She stepped in and felt the cool water wrap around her feet.

Slowly, she relaxed. She walked deeper into the middle of the pond, feeling the weight from her worries slowly wash away. Claire let out a deep breath and smiled as she felt the water kiss her skin.

The gentle sway of the water seemed to help her mind feel better as she floated on top. Her worries seemed weightless, and she felt free and happy for the first time in a long time.

Claire stayed there for a while and enjoyed the peace, until she was ready to go home. She emerged from the pond feeling thin and relaxed. She could never forget the magic of the pond, and still visits it whenever she needs to feel the weightless freedom it brings.

Ben likes to fish with his dad. They have a rod and a hook and a worm. They go to the lake and sit on a boat. Ben sees the water and the fish and the birds. He is happy.

Dad shows Ben how to open the rod and put the worm on the hook. He says, "Be careful, the hook is sharp. Don't touch it." Ben nods and listens. He wants to be a smart fisher like his dad.

They throw the rod in the water and wait. Ben watches the bobber. It goes up and down. He asks, "Dad, when will the fish come?" Dad says, "Be patient, son. Sometimes it takes time. The fish are shy."

Ben waits and waits. He feels bored. He looks at the sky and the trees and the ducks. He sees a big duck with a green head. He says, "Dad, look, a duck!" Dad says, "Yes, that's a mallard. He's very pretty."

Suddenly, the bobber goes under the water. Ben feels a tug on the rod. He says, "Dad, I got one! I got one!" Dad says, "Good job, Ben! Pull the rod, pull the rod!" Ben pulls the rod with all his might. He sees a shiny fish on the hook. He says, "Wow, it's a big one! It's a big one!" Dad says, "You did it, Ben! You caught a fish! You're a smart fisher!" Ben smiles and hugs his dad. He is proud.

Once upon a time, there was a little penguin named Puddles. Puddles loved to visit his friends who lived on the other side of the icy mountain. He would waddle and slide his way through the snow to get there.

One day, Puddles felt a rumble in his tummy while he was on his way to visit his friends. He knew he had to go to the toilet soon. But he didn't want to stop his journey to the other side of the mountain.

As he continued walking, Puddles saw a small igloo. He thought he could go inside and use the toilet. He went in, but the toilet was very icy and cold! Puddles quickly finished his business and left the igloo.

When Puddles finally arrived at his friends' home, they had a surprise for him - a warm and cozy toilet! Puddles was so happy and relieved that he could use the toilet comfortably. From that day on, Puddles always made sure to go to the toilet before he went on his visits.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with blocks and make a big stack. One day, Lily's mom asked her to stay in her room while she went to the store. Lily was sad, but she knew she had to listen to her mom.

As she played with her blocks, Lily made a pretty tower. She was so proud of it! But then, her little brother came in and knocked it down. Lily was upset, but she didn't get mad. She just started to stack the blocks again.

When Lily's mom came back, she saw the pretty tower and was so happy. She was proud of Lily for being patient and staying in her room. From then on, Lily knew that even if things got knocked down, she could always stack them up again.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim had a big box of yummy snacks. He loved to share his snacks with his friends. One day, Tim found a small eraser in his box. The eraser was very cute and looked like a little animal.

Tim thought the eraser was hungry, so he decided to feed it. He gave the eraser some of his yummy snacks. The eraser did not eat the snacks, but Tim believed it was happy. Tim and the eraser became good friends.

Every day, Tim would play with the eraser and pretend to feed it yummy snacks. They had lots of fun together. Tim's friends also liked the eraser and would play with it too. Tim and the eraser were very happy and had many adventures together.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to bake with her mommy. One day, they decided to make cookies. They mixed flour, sugar, and eggs together. Lily loved to mix the ingredients with a big spoon. She giggled as she stirred.

But then, they realized they didn't have enough butter. Lily's mommy had to go to the store to get more. Lily was sad because she wanted to keep mixing. She waited patiently for her mommy to come back.

When her mommy returned, they finished making the cookies. They put the dough in the oven and waited for them to bake. When the cookies were done, they had a happy texture. Lily was so happy she could share them with her friends.

Lily and Ben were bored. It was a gloomy day and they could not go outside. They looked at their toys, but they did not want to play with them. They wanted to do something new and fun.

"Let's gather some things and make a fort!" Lily said. She liked to build things with pillows and blankets. Ben nodded. He liked to pretend he was a knight or a pirate. They ran to their rooms and gathered some things. They brought pillows, blankets, books, and a flashlight.

They went to the living room and started to build their fort. They used the couch and the chairs as walls. They covered them with blankets. They made a door with a pillow. They put books inside as treasures. They turned on the flashlight as a lantern.

They crawled inside their fort and felt cozy and warm. They pretended they were in a castle or a cave. They told each other stories and jokes. They laughed and had fun.

But they did not know that their mom was watching them. She smiled and was happy to see them playing. She had a surprise for them. She went to the kitchen and made some hot chocolate and cookies. She put them on a tray and walked to the living room.

She knocked on the pillow door and said, "Hello, is anyone home?" Lily and Ben opened the door and saw their mom. They saw the tray and smelled the chocolate and cookies. They were excited and happy. They said, "Thank you, mom! You are the best!" They invited their mom to join them in their fort. They shared the hot chocolate and cookies and enjoyed their gloomy day.

Once there was a girl called Daisy. She loved to skip along the beach. One day, Daisy looked out across the big ocean and saw a sailboat. She skipped over to take a closer look.

The sailboat was reliable and white, with blue and yellow stripes. Daisy wanted to go on-board, so she asked the captain if she could join them. The captain smiled and said yes.

For hours Daisy skipped around the boat as it sailed over the ocean. When the coast came into sight, Daisy had to say goodbye to the captain and crew. But she knew she would be back again soon.

Daisy loved to explore the ocean and skip around the beach with her friends. Anything was possible when she was sailing out on the reliable ocean.

Once upon a time there was a happy boy named Tim. He loved to run outside and play in the sunshine. One day he thought it would be fun to make some cocoa. He gathered the things he needed and set to work.

Once all the ingredients were mixed, Tim put them in a pot on the stove to cook. He waited and waited, stirring the cocoa with a spoon. Finally, the cocoa was ready to drink.

Tim took a sip and was so happy! It was the best cocoa he had ever had! He decided to make cocoa every day and share with his friends.

Day after day, Tim made more cocoa. Soon, everyone in the village was drinking cocoa. Even the adults were enjoying it!

Thanks to Tim's hard work and successful cocoa-making, everyone was happier and healthier. Everyone cheered for Tim and all agreed, cocoa was a wonderful thing!

Toby was an independent kid. He loved to drive his car everywhere. One day he decided to take a trip to a hotel. He put on his seatbelt and drove down the road.

When he arrived at the hotel, he was amazed. It looked so big and tall, and there were so many people around. He found a parking spot and parked his car.

He went inside and was very excited. He saw all the funny decorations and different types of snacks. He wanted to explore the hotel, so he started walking around. He even got to take the elevator which was so much fun!

He made new friends in the hotel. They laughed and played all day. At the end of the day, Toby was so tired that he fell asleep in his car. After a long day, he drove back home to his house.

One day in the river, an otter named Jack was swimming. As he looked around, he noticed a wide beach. Wanting to explore further, Jack began to swim towards it.

As he got closer to the beach, something strange happened. He felt an urge to explore it. Jack swam closer and closer and soon found himself on the beach. He was amazed to see how wide it was.

As he looked around, another otter appeared. "Hi Jack, why are you here?" the otter asked.

Jack replied, "I felt an urge to explore this wide beach. What about you?"

The otter said, "I felt the same urge. We should explore this beach together!"

Jack and the other otter had a great time exploring the beach and finding new things. They were both very happy that they had followed their urge.

Once upon a time, there was a brave little girl named Jane. Jane loved climbing mountains and exploring the countryside. One day, she asked her mum if she could go exploring a very high mountain, but her mum refused. Jane was disappointed.

But then, Jane had an idea. She asked her mum if she could go exploring a much smaller mountain nearby. This time, her mum said yes!

Jane was so excited that she set off on her adventure straight away. She climbed the mountain, and as soon as she got to the summit, she noticed something unusual. It was a cave! She had never been inside a cave before!

However, her mum had warned her not to do anything dangerous, so instead of going inside the cave, Jane decided to look around it instead. She explored the area around the cave and had a wonderful adventure.

At the end of the day, Jane was really proud of herself. She had listened to her mum and didn't do anything risky. Even though it was hard to refuse the exciting opportunity to explore the cave, Jane had stuck to what her mum told her. Sticking to the important rules in life can be hard, but it's always better in the long run.

Tom was a boy who liked to play with keys. He had many keys of different shapes and colors. He liked to try them on different doors and locks. He wanted to see what was behind them.

One day, he found a big orange key in his dad's drawer. He wondered what it could unlock. He took the key and went around the house. He tried it on the front door, the back door, the garage door, but none of them opened. He was disappointed.

Then he saw a small door under the stairs. He had never noticed it before. He was curious. He put the orange key in the lock and turned it. The door opened with a click. He saw a dark and dusty room. He stepped inside.

He saw many old things, like books, toys, clothes, and pictures. He wanted to touch them and play with them. He did not see a sign that said "Do not enter". He did not hear his dad calling him.

Suddenly, he heard a loud bang. The door had closed behind him. He was scared. He ran to the door and tried to open it. But the orange key was gone. He had dropped it somewhere. He could not find it. He could not unlock the door. He was trapped.

He cried and shouted for help. He wished he had not taken the key. He wished he had listened to his dad. He learned a lesson. He should not play with things that are not his. He should not go to places that are not safe. He should be careful and obedient. He hoped someone would find him soon.

Once upon a time, there were two friends named John and Jane. They both loved to play outdoors, and they spent all of their free time together. One sunny day, they decided to go explore the forest nearby. They were having so much fun, but as they went deeper and deeper into the forest, they started to get scared.

Suddenly they saw something very strange. It was a big hole in the ground, and they could see three different-colored toes sticking out from the bottom. John and Jane stepped closer with curiosity, but then a loud voice said "Stay away from the hole!"

John and Jane were so frightened that they ran away as fast as they could. Later, they learned that the three toes belonged to a child who had gotten lost in the forest and fallen into the deep hole. They were heartbroken to learn that the child was never found.

The moral of this story is to always be careful where you step, even when you're out having fun. If you ever find yourself in a dangerous situation, it's important to stay away and get help right away.

Once there was a brave knight. He was on a hunt for a very special treasure. So he got on his horse, and rode off into the forest. He knew he had to be brave and strong.

He searched for days and days, until he came to a cave. He was sure this must be the home of the treasure! He took a deep breath and entered the cave. To his surprise, he found an incredible sight. There were golden coins, precious gems, and all kinds of amazing things. He had found the treasure!

The knight was so happy that he bowed down to show his respect. He gathered all of the treasure and put it into a big sack. He hopped onto his horse and rode back to his kingdom. He gave the treasure to the king and said he was thankful.

The king was so pleased that he declared the knight a hero. He made a big celebration and said the knight was incredible. Everyone cheered and hugged the knight as he bowed one last time. The knight now had a treasure of his own to show for all his hard work!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved playing outside with her friends. One day, she was playing in the park when her tummy started to rumble. She knew it was noon and time for lunch.

Lily went to her mom and requested a sandwich. Her mom made her a peanut butter and jelly sandwich. Lily sat down on a comfortable blanket and ate her sandwich.

After lunch, Lily and her friends played on the swings. One of her friends said, "I'm not comfortable on the swing." Lily replied, "Let's play something else then." They played hide-and-seek and had so much fun. When it was time to go home, Lily hugged her friends and said, "Thanks for playing with me today!"

Once upon a time, there was a king who lived in a big castle. The king was very rich and had many servants. One day, the king was walking in his garden and he saw a small bird on the ground. The bird was very hot and thirsty.

The king asked the bird, "Are you okay?" The bird did not answer. The king picked up the bird and took it to his castle. He gave the bird some water and some food. The bird felt better and started to sing.

The king was very happy that he helped the bird. He realized that it is important to help others when they need it. The king learned that even though he was a king, he should always be kind to everyone, no matter how big or small.

Once upon a time, there was a little bean. The bean lived in a big garden with lots of other beans. They all grew on tall, green plants that reached up to the sky. The little bean loved living in the garden with his bean friends.

One day, a big spray of water came to the garden. The little bean and his friends loved the water. They drank it up and grew taller and taller. The little bean was so happy when the water came to visit.

But one day, the little bean saw something disgusting. A big, slimy bug was eating his friend. The little bean was scared and sad. He did not want the bug to eat him too. So, the little bean asked the water to help. The water came and sprayed the bug away. The little bean was safe and happy again. And he grew bigger and bigger, just like his friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to jog around her garden and play with her toys. One day, she found a brilliant ornament on the ground. She picked it up and showed it to her mom.

"Mommy, look what I found!" Lily said, holding up the ornament.

"That's beautiful, Lily," her mom said. "Where did you find it?"

"I found it while I was jogging in the garden," Lily replied.

"That's very impressive, Lily. You're such a good jogger!" her mom said with a smile.

Lily felt proud of herself and continued to jog around the garden with her new ornament in her hand. She knew that she was a brilliant jogger and that she could find more treasures if she kept looking.

Lily liked to play with her mom's large vase. It was blue and shiny and had flowers on it. She would fill it with water and pretend it was a lake for her toy ducks. Sometimes she would put her hand inside and feel the cold water.

One day, mom told Lily to stay in the living room while she went to the kitchen. "Don't touch the vase, Lily. It can break and hurt you," mom said. Lily nodded, but she was curious. She wanted to see how the vase looked from the top. She dragged a chair to the table and climbed on it. She reached for the vase and lifted it up.

But the vase was too heavy for Lily. She lost her balance and the vase slipped from her hands. It fell to the floor and smashed into pieces. Water and flowers spilled everywhere. Lily was scared and started to cry.

Mom heard the noise and ran to the living room. She saw the mess and Lily on the chair. She was angry and worried. "Lily, what did you do? I told you not to touch the vase!" mom said. She picked up Lily and hugged her. "Are you hurt, sweetie?"

Lily shook her head and sobbed. "I'm sorry, mom. I wanted to see the vase. It was so pretty. I didn't mean to break it," Lily said. Mom sighed and kissed her. "I know, Lily. But you have to listen to me. The vase was not a toy. It was fragile and dangerous. You could have cut yourself or fallen off the chair. You have to be careful, okay?"

Lily nodded and hugged mom. "Okay, mom. I'm sorry. I love you," Lily said. Mom smiled and said, "I love you too, Lily. Now let's clean up this mess and find a new place for your toy ducks."

Once there was a silly woodpecker who wanted to mail something. So he picked up a big piece of wood and took it to the post office. He asked the mailman if he could mail it. But the mailman said it was too big. The woodpecker was sad. Then he had an idea! He got out his hammer and started hammering the wood into lots of little pieces. When he finished, he took the pieces of wood to the mailman and asked if he could mail them. The mailman smiled and said, "Yes, of course!" So the woodpecker mailed all the small pieces of wood and was happy.

Once upon a time there was a great nation. In this nation lived a very brave king. The king was loved by all his people.

One day the king made an announcement to the nation. He said, "My people, I have decided to send out a team to explore the wider world." Everyone cheered and celebrated the king's great decision.

Unfortunately, the journey was too much for the explorers. They got lost and never returned. One of the people said to the king, "Your Majesty, it has been too long since we last saw the explorers. I fear they must have been lost."

The king was very sad and felt like he had let his nation down. He knew he had made a mistake by sending the explorers and realised he should have heeded the warnings of the soothsayer. The king never recovered from this tragedy, and the nation never got the explorers back.

"Come on, let's go collect the bookshelf," said Tim. Tim and his sister Sam were excited to pick up the colourful, cheerful bookshelf.

When they arrived at the store, they saw it and were overjoyed. It was bigger than they had expected.

They carefully put the bookshelf in their car and rushed home.

When they opened the door, they saw the empty corner where the bookshelf should go.

They started to unpack the pieces, and Tim said to Sam, "Let's build it!"

They started to assemble the bookshelf, but suddenly, Tim's hand got stuck.

The bookshelf came crashing down on him and they were so shocked.

Tim was rushed to the hospital and Sam was left alone and sad.

The bookshelf was ruined, and the cheerful feeling was gone.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy who loved going to the zoo. He always went with his mom and dad, but this time he wanted to go alone. His mom and dad were worried, but Timmy was determined to go by himself.

As Timmy was walking around the zoo, he saw a big rhinoceros. The rhinoceros looked very scary and Timmy wanted to run away, but he remembered what his mom and dad always told him - "if you need help, ask for it." So, Timmy went to the zookeeper and asked for help.

The zookeeper came and helped Timmy see the rhinoceros up close. Timmy realized that the rhinoceros wasn't scary at all, it was just big and had a horn on its nose. As Timmy was walking away, he slipped on some icy ground. He was scared and didn't know what to do. But then, the zookeeper came to help him up and Timmy realized that it's always okay to ask for help when you need it.

Once there was a boy named Tommy who always wanted to explore. He had a special texture blanket that he loved to carry around with him wherever he went.

One day, he wanted to walk outside in the sunshine. So he grabbed his blanket and ran out the door. But when he got outside, he saw that it was raining. Tommy complained and stomped his feet. He was very confused, because he didn't understand why it didn't want to be sunny.

He sniffled and stood in the rain. Suddenly, Tommy had an idea! He yelled, "Let's make our own sunshine!" He wrapped himself in his special texture blanket, and just like that, he was warm and cozy. He giggled with joy and decided he didn't need the sunshine after all.

One day, a little girl was outside looking around. She thought she saw something in the grass. She went a little closer and saw a bug. It was pale and she was curious. She bent down to look at it more carefully. The bug was scared and tried to fly away. But the little girl was gentle and careful. She reached out a finger and it let her touch it. She was very happy and started to think about the bug.

Suddenly the bug flew away and she thought about what it was doing. She was sure that it had a special job to do that day. She smiled and watched it go until it was out of sight. She stood up and started to go back home. She knew that even thought the bug was pale, it was still a special bug.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a bedroom with a big bed and lots of toys. One day, Lily's mommy came into her bedroom and said, "Lily, we need to replace your old bed with a new one."

Lily looked at her mommy and asked, "Why do we need to replace my bed?"

Her mommy replied, "Because your old bed is broken and it's not safe for you to sleep in anymore."

Lily was a little bit angry because she loved her old bed, but her mommy promised to buy her a new one that was just as comfortable. And so, they went to the store together to pick out a new bed for Lily's bedroom. When they got home, Lily was so happy with her new bed that she forgot all about her old one.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Emily. She was three years old, and she liked finding new things.

One day, Emily went on a walk with her mom. They were in the garden, and Mom said, "Look, Emily! What do you see?"

"I see a zipper!" said Emily excitedly. Emily was very curious about the zipper, so she decided to be polite and ask.

"Mommy, what is that?"

"It's a zipper," replied Mom.

Emily then discovered she could open the zipper. She carefully opened it and found a box inside. She was so excited to open the box!

The box was full of fun toys! Emily had a great time playing with them. She and Mom played hide and seek with the toys for the rest of the day.

At the end, Emily was happy and tired. She had a wonderful day discovering new things.

Stephen was a delivery man. Every day he would deliver packages. One day, he had to deliver a special package. It was a diamond! The diamond was big and sparkly.

Stephen was excited, but he didn't know where to take it. Eventually he found the right address. But when he got there, the person he was supposed to deliver to was very rude. They didn't say thank you, or even smile.

Stephen wanted to leave, but he remembered why he was there. So he handed the diamond to the rude person and said goodbye. The person grumbled a small thank you, but Stephen was glad he delivered the diamond. He was happy to have done a good job.

Once upon a time, there was a strong man named Bill. But one day, he was feeling very weak. He went for a walk in the park to try and feel better.

But then he saw a bad man named Frank. Frank was trying to steal something. He was trying to steal a white sheet from a little girl.

Bill saw this and he felt brave. He ran up to Frank and shouted. He shouted, "Stop! You stop stealing that sheet!"

Frank was scared and he ran away. The little girl was so happy! Bill had saved her sheet.

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the park and feed the pigeons. One day, she noticed that some of the pigeons were sick and had a hard time flying.

Lily was worried about the sick pigeons, so she asked her mommy what she could do to help. Her mommy told her that she could prevent the pigeons from getting sick by not feeding them bread, which can be bad for their tummies.

Lily listened to her mommy's advice and started feeding the pigeons birdseed instead. The sick pigeons started to get better and Lily was happy that she was able to help them. From that day on, Lily always made sure to prevent the pigeons from getting sick by only feeding them healthy food.

Once upon a time, there lived an ancient hero. He was so brave that everyone in the village admired him greatly.

One day, the hero was travelling through the forest when he heard a strange noise. He went to investigate and realized it was a small creature in distress. The creature said, “Please help me! I am stuck in this big tree and can’t get out!”

The hero immediately acted. He used all his strength to squeeze the trunk of the tree, until the creature was released!

The creature thanked the hero enthusiastically, and then ran off into the forest. The hero was very pleased that he had been able to help the creature.

He smiled and said to himself, “I am glad to be a hero today!”

Tommy was so excited. He was getting a great invitation! His mom had told him it was special, so he was very excited to see what he was invited to. He opened the envelope and looked inside. It was a beautiful party invitation!

"Mom!" he said. "Can I go to the party?"

His mom smiled. "Yes, you can," she replied. "But you will need to go to the store and buy a gift for the birthday girl."

Tommy was so happy he jumped up and down. He couldn't wait to go the store and pick out a great present.

When Tommy got to the store, he asked the clerk for help and found the most wonderful present. He couldn't wait to give it to the birthday girl!

When his mom opened the invitation, she couldn't believe how excited Tommy was. "That was a great choice Tommy! I'm sure she will love it!"

Tommy smiled. He was so happy and couldn't wait to give the present at the party!

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved trains. He had a big train set in his room and he played with it every day. One day, Timmy's friend Billy came over to play. Billy thought trains were boring and he didn't want to play with Timmy's train set.

Timmy was sad and didn't know what to do. He asked Billy why he didn't like trains. Billy said, "Trains are boring. I like things that can destroy things." Timmy didn't understand why anyone would want to destroy things.

Later that day, Timmy and Billy went outside to play. Billy found some rocks and started throwing them at a tree. Timmy told Billy to stop because it was not nice to destroy things. Billy didn't listen and kept throwing rocks. Suddenly, a branch from the tree fell and hit Billy on the head.

Timmy helped Billy up and asked him if he was okay. Billy said he was sorry for trying to destroy things and promised to never do it again. Timmy forgave Billy and they went back to playing with the train set. The moral of the story is that it's important to be kind and not destroy things.

John was out walking with his mom when they stopped at a road. "This is a lovely road," said John's mom. John was very excited and asked, "Can I paint it?" His mom smiled and said, "Sure, let's get some paint and brushes."

They quickly found some paint and brushes and John got to work. He was painting the road in bright colors and shapes. He carefully worked in the details.

John's mom watched proudly as he worked. "That's lovely," she said. His mom had to help him a little, but he was determined to do it all himself.

Finally, with help from his mom, John finished the painting. "This is the best road I have ever seen," said John's mom. She gave him a big hug and said, "I am so proud of you, it is a lovely painting." John was so happy and said, "I love painting!"

Once upon a time, there was a little boy who was very thirsty. He went to the kitchen to get a drink. He saw a jug full of cold water, so he took it and tried to pour some into his cup. But he couldn't make it work - the water wouldn't separate from the jug! The little boy was feeling very miserable because he was so thirsty.

So he asked his mummy for help. She said, "Oh darling, don't worry. Let me show you how it works." She picked up the jug and with a little twist and turn, the water came out slowly into the cup. "See, it's so easy!" said the mummy. The little boy was so happy now.

He thanked his mummy and drank the water. It was so refreshing! From then on he knew how to separate the water from the jug and fill his cup with cold water whenever he was thirsty.

Once there was a jolly bull walking in the woods. He was so happy to explore his new surroundings. Suddenly, he saw something shining ahead. He slowly walked towards it and suddenly he realized it was a pot of gold! He was so excited and he couldn't believe his luck.

He imagined what he could do with all that gold. He thought of buying lots of sweets and treats with it. The bull was so happy that he started to jump and dance. Suddenly, he heard a loud roar. He turned around to see a big and angry bear.

The bear wanted the pot of gold and he wasn't happy to see the bull. Before the bull could do anything, the bear charged at him with full force. Sadly, the bull was no match for the bear and he got hurt pretty badly.

The bull limped back home without any golden pot. He was heartbroken, but he was also very wise. He learned never to imagine too much, or it may lead to a bad ending.

Once upon a time, there was a little squirrel named Nutty. Nutty lived in a big white tree in the forest. One day, Nutty saw a big pile of sticks on the ground. "I want to build a house with these sticks," Nutty said.

But then, a big bird named Tweetie came and said, "Those sticks are mine! I was going to build a nest with them." Nutty got sad because she really wanted to build a house. "Please let me use some sticks too," Nutty said.

Tweetie thought about it and said, "Okay, we can share the sticks. I'll help you build your house." Nutty was happy and together they built a little house with the sticks. It was a small white house with a door and a window. Nutty thanked Tweetie for helping her and they became good friends. The end.

Tommy was an alert little boy. He was always looking around and noticed everything. One day, he was in the kitchen, and saw something on the counter. It was a round yellow thing - it was cheese! He wanted to try it.

He reached for it, but just then his mummy turned around. She saw what he was doing and said no. Tommy was disappointed and turned away.

But his mummy was kind, and gave him a piece of cheese. Tommy was so excited, he couldn't help but smile. He eagerly took a bite. It tasted delicious! Tommy was pleased - he knew he had made the right choice!

Once there was a little girl called Sarah. She loved to make things! One day she wanted to make something special, so she went outside to pick some vegetables. She picked some carrots, potatoes and peas.

When she came back inside she washed the vegetables and got out her big pot. Carefully she started to put the vegetables in. Then she added some cool water, and a spoonful of salt.

She took the pot over to the stove and turned on the heat. The pot began to bubble and sizzle. After a few minutes she turned down the heat and left the vegetables to cook.

When they were ready the vegetables looked really cool. She added some butter and sprinkled on some pepper. Then with a smile on her face she served the vegetables for dinner.

It was the best dinner ever! Sarah was so proud of her yummy vegetable dish.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy had a big foot and he loved to run and jump with it. One day, Timmy accidentally stepped on his friend's toy and broke it. Timmy felt guilty and didn't know what to do.

So, Timmy went to talk to his mom about what happened. He told her about his big foot and how he accidentally broke his friend's toy. His mom listened and told him that it was important to say sorry and make things right.

Timmy went to his friend's house and said sorry for breaking the toy. His friend forgave him and they played together again. Timmy felt happy that he talked to his mom and made things right with his friend.

Once upon a time there was a girl who wanted to try something new. She wanted to explore a new space. She found a very big door and wanted to open it. But it was locked!

Then she looked around and noticed a key on the floor. She was so happy because the key would unlock the door! She grabbed the key and put it in the door's lock. Then with a click the door opened!

The girl excitedly stepped into the new space. She saw lots of yummy things all around her! There were yummy snacks and yummy ice-creams. She was so happy!

She spent the whole day exploring and eating yummy sweets. She had lots of fun and when it was time to go home, she took one extra yummy treat with her. She said goodbye to the exciting space and unlocked the door.

Once there was a little girl named Jacky. She loved to play outside, but one day she was sad because she couldn't find anything to play with. Suddenly, she saw a big, red ball. She jumped and kicked it with her leg. The ball went flying and Jacky went running after it. As it rolled away, it got spicier and spicier.

Jacky chased the ball until finally it stopped. Right when she was about to kick it again, a big dog came out of nowhere and tried to eat the ball. Jacky was scared, but she kicked the ball away with her little leg. The dog started to bark and run away.

Jacky was relieved, but she was also excited. She ran over to the ball and kicked it as hard as she could. It went flying off and Jacky went running after it again. She played with the ball until it was time to go home.

Jacky was feeling excited, happy and a little bit spicy!

Ben likes to listen to cars. He likes the sound they make when they go fast. He likes to see the colors and shapes of different cars. He has many toy cars that he plays with at home.

One day, Ben goes to the park with his mom. He sees a big car with a loud noise. It is a fire truck. It has red and yellow and white on it. It has a long ladder and a hose. It has a siren that goes woo-woo-woo. Ben thinks it is cool.

The fire truck stops near the park. Some men get out of the car. They wear big hats and coats. They have a dog with them. The dog has black and white spots. It is a dalmatian. The dog barks and wags its tail.

Ben wants to see the fire truck and the dog. He runs to them. He forgets to hold his mom's hand. He forgets to look both ways. He does not see another car coming. The car is going fast. It has a lot of speed.

The driver of the car sees Ben. He honks his horn. He tries to stop. But it is too late. He hits Ben. Ben falls down. He feels pain. He cries.

His mom hears him. She runs to him. She hugs him. She is scared. She is sad. She calls for help.

The men from the fire truck hear her. They come to help. They check on Ben. They say he is hurt. They say he needs to go to the hospital. They put him on a stretcher. They put him in the fire truck. They turn on the siren. They drive away.

Ben's mom goes with him. She holds his hand. She tells him she loves him. She tells him he will be okay. She tells him he was brave. She tells him he should always listen to her. She tells him he should always be careful. She tells him he should always watch for cars. She tells him cars can be dangerous. She tells him cars can be different. She tells him some cars are good. She tells him some cars are bad. She tells him he should always be safe.

Lila loves dolphins. She has a big toy dolphin that she sleeps with every night. She hugs it and squeezes it tight. She likes to pretend that she is swimming with dolphins in the sea.

One day, Lila goes to the zoo with her mom and dad. They see many animals, but Lila is most excited to see the dolphins. They are gray and shiny and jump out of the water. Lila claps and laughs. She wants to touch them and squeeze them.

Lila's mom and dad buy her a ticket to feed the dolphins. Lila is very happy. She holds a fish in her hand and walks to the edge of the pool. A dolphin comes close and opens its mouth. Lila throws the fish and the dolphin catches it. Lila smiles.

The dolphin comes back and nudges Lila's hand with its nose. Lila feels its skin. It is smooth and wet. Lila gently strokes the dolphin and says, "Hello, dolphin. You are so nice. I love you." The dolphin makes a squeaky sound and wags its tail.

Lila leans over and gives the dolphin a kiss. She wraps her arms around its head and squeezes it tight. The dolphin hugs her back with its flippers. Lila feels warm and happy. She thinks, "This is the best day ever. I wish I could stay with the dolphin forever."

Once there was a guard who was feeling very anxious. He had an important job to do, which was to look after the park. But one day something unexpected happened. A big, green car came zooming into the park at top speed! The guard was terrified and ran to tell the mayor.

The mayor was very worried and they quickly got out their fastest police car to try and capture the driver. The police car zoomed after the big, green car, but it was too fast. Eventually the car disappeared in the distance and the mayor was very sad.

The guard was very relieved that the car had gone and no harm had been done. He was also very thankful that he could get back to work and guard the park again. From then on, he was always ready and alert, and never let anything near the park go unnoticed.

Once upon a time, there was a rat who wanted to taste something delicious. He saw a big fire and said, "That looks yummy!" He came to the fire and put his paw over the flames.

It was hot! The rat felt a burning sensation on his paw and quickly pulled it away. He felt pain as the wetness from his tears ran down his face.

He was sad and thought he would never taste something delicious again. But then a smell filled the air. It was sweet and it was coming from the fire.

The rat looked closer and saw a delicious apple pie baking in the flames. He quickly took the pie and ran away. He ate the delicious pie and was so full and happy that he forgot all about the burning pain.

Once upon a time there was a girl. She had a secret that made her feel hurt. It was like a big weight she had to carry in her heart. The secret was so big and so sad she was afraid to tell anyone.

Every time she wanted to share she stopped and stayed quiet. She leaned against the wall in her room and hugged herself. Nobody knew the secret but she felt all alone. There was too much silence.

Then one day she made a wish. She wished that she could get rid of the hurt. A magic wind came and blew away the secret. She could feel the hurt lifting away with it. When it was all gone she opened her eyes and felt a warm feeling in her heart.

The girl had learned that it is ok to talk about your feelings and that you don't have to carry around secrets that make you feel hurt.

The End

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to go on adventures in the forest near her house. One day, while she was walking, she saw an owl sitting on a branch.

"Hello, owl!" she said.

"Who are you?" asked the owl.

"I'm Lily," she said. "What's your name?"

"My name is unknown," said the owl. "But you can call me Ollie."

Lily and Ollie became friends and went on many adventures together. One day, they were walking and got lost. Ollie said, "Let's reverse and go back the way we came."

They followed Ollie's advice and found their way back home. From then on, they always made sure to bring a map on their adventures.

Once upon a time, there was a brave young boy named Mike. Mike had a very special team - his family! He loved spending time with them and playing games together.

One day, his family decided to send Mike and his team on an adventure. On their journey, they came across a dangerous cave. Mike was scared to explore the cave, but his team was there to encourage him and make sure he stayed safe.

When they reached the cave, Mike's dad said “Be careful, it’s dangerous in there. Let’s stay together and explore carefully!” Mike nodded and he and his team ventured inside.

Inside, they found a magical place with amazing creatures and treasures. They also found a message that said “Loyalty and courage are rewarded in dangerous places”.

The moral of the story is – if you stay together and remain courageous, even the most dangerous places can offer amazing rewards!

Lily and Max were best friends. They liked to play in the park and share their toys. One day, they saw a shiny thing on the ground. It was a diamond. Lily and Max both wanted it.

"I saw it first!" Lily said.

"No, I saw it first!" Max said.

They started to pull the diamond and shout at each other. They were not nice to each other. They forgot to be friends.

A lady saw them and came over. She asked them what was wrong. Lily and Max told her about the diamond. The lady smiled and said, "Do you know what this is? It is not a diamond. It is a glass bead. It is not worth anything. But your friendship is worth a lot. You should not fight over a glass bead. You should be kind and share."

Lily and Max felt embarrassed. They realized they were silly. They said sorry to each other and hugged. They gave the glass bead to the lady and thanked her. They decided to be good friends again. They learned that friendship is more important than things.

Ben and Lily were playing with blocks in the living room. They liked to build towers and houses with the blocks. They had many blocks of different colors and shapes.

"Look, I made a big building!" Ben said, showing his block tower to Lily. "It is taller than you!"

Lily was not happy. She wanted to make a big building too, but she had fewer blocks than Ben. She thought Ben was not generous. He did not share his blocks with her.

"I want some of your blocks!" Lily said, reaching for Ben's tower. "Give me some!"

"No, they are mine!" Ben said, pulling his tower away. "You have your own blocks!"

Lily was angry. She pushed Ben's tower and made it fall. The blocks scattered on the floor. Ben was sad. He had worked hard to make his tower. He started to cry.

"Mama, mama, Lily broke my building!" Ben shouted.

Mama came to the living room. She saw the mess and the crying children. She was not happy.

"Lily, why did you break Ben's building?" Mama asked.

"Because he did not share his blocks with me!" Lily said.

"That is not a good reason, Lily. You should not break things that belong to others. That is not nice. You need to say sorry to Ben and help him pick up the blocks. That is your punishment." Mama said.

Lily felt sorry. She knew she had done something bad. She said sorry to Ben and helped him pick up the blocks. Ben forgave her and gave her some of his blocks. They decided to build a new tower together. Mama was proud of them. She said they were generous and kind. She gave them a hug and a cookie.

One day, an adventurous penguin named Pippa wanted to explore the big ice land. She said to her mama, "Mama, can I go and see what is over there?" She pointed to a hill far away.

Her mama said, "No, Pippa, it is too dangerous. You might get lost or meet a scary animal. You should stay with me and the other penguins."

But Pippa did not listen. She ignored her mama and sneaked away when she was not looking. She waddled and slid on the ice, feeling happy and curious. She saw many new things, like shiny rocks, fluffy snowflakes and colorful fish.

Soon, she reached the hill and climbed up. She wanted to see what was on the other side. But when she got to the top, she saw something that made her very afraid. It was a big, furry, growling bear! The bear saw her too and started to run towards her.

Pippa was so scared that she forgot how to move. She wished she had listened to her mama. She closed her eyes and hoped the bear would go away. But then, she heard a loud honk and felt a warm wing around her. It was her mama! Her mama had followed her and scared the bear away. She hugged Pippa and said, "Pippa, I am so glad you are safe. But you should never ignore me again. I only want to protect you and love you."
