Mama smiled and said, "Okay, count the yellow taxi." So the little girl counted, "One, two, three, four....Taxi!" And they both giggled.

The little girl was so happy that she could count the taxis. She had a huge smile on her face as they walked home.

Once upon a time, there was a friendly bear. He loved to organize things and make sure that everything was neat and tidy. He had a little door in his house that he liked to take care of.

One day, the bear decided to organize the door in his house. He cleaned it and made sure it was nice and tidy. He even put a shiny doorknob on it.

He had a lot of fun organizing the door. So much so that he decided to organize the whole house. He cleaned and tidied everything in it.

When he finished, he opened his door and said hello to all the friendly people who were outside. They were so happy to see a tidy house that they all waved and said hello back.

The bear was glad that he had taken the time to organize his house because it made everyone around him so happy. From that day forward, he was always sure to organize his house and make it a friendly place.

Once upon a time, in a small village, there lived a beautiful little girl called Mia. Mia loved animals, especially ducks. Every morning, Mia would come to the pond and sit with her favorite duck. Together they would talk, laugh and play.

One day, Mia noticed something shiny and wonderful near the edge of the pond. She bent down and picked up a metal sign. She couldn't believe her eyes! It was the most beautiful sign she had ever seen.

Mia asked her duck: "What do you think the sign says?" But, alas, the duck couldn't answer. So Mia decided to take the sign home with her, and ask her family what it meant.

When Mia reached home, she showed the sign to her mom and dad. They were both so happy that she had found it! They had been looking for this exact sign for weeks. Mia asked, "What does it say?". Her mom and dad smiled at each other and said: "It says, 'This pond is now a duck sanctuary!'"

The next morning, Mia returned to the pond with her duck to find out that it had been transformed. Beautiful metal bars had been placed around the pond and ducks of all kinds had started to take refuge in it.

Mia couldn't believe her eyes! Thanks to the sign, the pond had become a safe haven for ducks. Mia was so proud.

Once upon a time there was a bald man named Jack. He was bouncing along the street with a big smile on his face.

As he bounced, he saw a bright colourful ornament twinkling in a shop window. He went in and asked the shop keeper how much the ornament cost.

The shop keeper smiled and said, "It's free, but you have to do a special task first!"

Excitedly Jack said, "What can I do?"

The shopkeeper chuckled and replied, "You must bounce up and down ten times!"

Jack beamed and started to bounce. He bounced up and down and round and round, until he had bounced ten times!

The shop keeper said, "Well done Jack! Here is the ornament for you."

Jack thanked the shop keeper, grabbed the ornament and held it proudly in his hands as he bounced away with a big smile on his face.

Once upon a time, there was a tough car. Every day, it drove around the town, taking people here and there. People love the car and always gave it big smiles and waves as it went past.

One day, while driving along, the car noticed something strange. It was a mask! It was lying on the ground and it was bright and colourful. The car was curious so it stopped to take a closer look.

As the car approached, the mask started to move! It was alive! The car was surprised. The mask said it was looking for a tough car to take it on a drive. The car thought it sounded like fun, so it offered to take the mask for a ride.

So off they went, driving through the town. They saw the birds in the sky, the trees in the forest and all the fun things in the town. The car was so happy to have a new friend.

At the end of the drive, the car promised to take the mask for a drive again. The car drove away feeling tough and happy. And the mask smiled knowing it had just made a new best friend.

Lily and Ben were having lunch with their mum. They had cheese and bread and grapes on their plates. Lily liked cheese and bread, but she did not like grapes. She pushed them away with her fork.

"Can I have more cheese, please?" she asked her mum.

"Of course, dear. But you should also eat some grapes. They are good for you and they are sweet and juicy," mum said.

Lily made a face. She did not want to eat grapes. She wanted to eat cheese and bread and play with her toys.

Ben saw Lily's face and smiled. He liked grapes. He liked all fruits. He reached for Lily's plate and took some grapes.

"Hey, that's mine!" Lily shouted. She grabbed her plate back and glared at Ben.

Ben laughed. He thought it was funny to tease Lily. He was a jolly boy. He liked to make jokes and have fun.

Mum saw what happened and shook her head. She did not like it when Lily and Ben fought. She wanted them to share and be kind.

"Ben, that was not nice. You should ask Lily before you take her grapes. And Lily, you should not yell at Ben. You should try to eat some grapes. They are yummy and healthy," mum said.

Lily and Ben looked at each other. They knew mum was right. They said sorry to each other and hugged.

"Can we have some cake after lunch?" Ben asked.

"Only if you finish your plates," mum said.

Lily and Ben nodded. They ate their cheese and bread and grapes. They even liked the grapes a little bit. They were happy and full. They could not wait to have cake and play with their toys.

Once upon a time, there was a funny triangle. It was big and thick. Every day the triangle would follow the sun. It was so happy! The triangle would look for the sun and the sun would always be in a different place.

The triangle kept following the sun. It wanted to be happy, so it followed the sun everywhere it went. It followed the sun in the morning and evening. It followed the sun up high in the sky, and down low behind the clouds.

The sun was getting tired of the triangle. One day, the sun said, "I'm tired of you following me! I'm going to hide. If you can find me, I'll let you follow me again.

The triangle was so excited! It looked and looked, but the sun was nowhere to be seen. Then, the triangle heard a little voice. It was the sun, calling from over behind the clouds. The triangle smiled and followed the sun again. They followed the sun up high in the sky and down low behind the clouds. They were happy and laughed and sang songs.

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a small boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play outside in the snow. One day, Timmy's mom gave him a small bag of salt to sprinkle on the icy sidewalk.

As Timmy was sprinkling the salt, he saw a small snowman that he had made the day before. "Hello, little snowman," said Timmy. "You look small today."

The snowman replied, "Yes, I am melting because of the salt. It makes the snow melt faster."

"Oh no!" cried Timmy. "I don't want you to melt. Let's move you to a shady spot where the sun can't reach you."

So, Timmy carefully picked up the small snowman and moved him to a shady spot. The snowman was happy because he didn't melt anymore. Timmy was happy because he saved his small snowman from melting. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who lived in a big house. She was happy and loved to smile. One lazy afternoon, she decided to take a walk outside.

As she walked along, she stumbled on a rock and fell down. She was so sad but then she heard a lovely sound. It was her friend the butterfly who had come to visit. He was so soft and gentle and he made her smile.

The butterfly was so friendly that he offered to help her back up. He flew around her, tickling her face with his wings. Making it difficult for her to keep from smiling.

He flew away and the little girl continued her walk. She still felt a bit wobbly, so she was more careful where she stepped. Eventually she reached her house again, feeling happy and relaxed, with a big smile on her face.

Once upon a time, there was a thoughtful boy named Tim. He loved to march and play with his toys. One day, Tim went on an adventure to find a treasure.

Tim marched through the living room, the kitchen, and the garden. He looked under the chairs and behind the trees, but he could not find the treasure. Tim did not give up. He kept marching and looking.

Finally, Tim found the treasure under his bed. It was a box filled with his favorite toys and treats. He was so happy and proud of himself. Tim learned that being thoughtful and never giving up can lead to great things.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to draw with chalk on the sidewalk outside her house. One day, she was drawing a big sun with yellow chalk when her little brother came over.

"Can I draw too?" he asked.

"Sure!" said Lily, handing him some blue chalk.

But her brother was careless and accidentally drew all over Lily's sun. Lily was upset and said, "You ruined my drawing!"

"I'm sorry," said her brother. "I didn't mean to."

Lily forgave him and they continued to draw together. The sun got bigger and the colors increased until they had drawn a beautiful rainbow. They were both very proud of their artwork and showed it to their parents when they came outside to see what they were up to.

Tommy was very frustrated. His favorite toy was stuck in the jug, and he couldn't get it out. He tried and tried, but it wouldn't come out. He cried and told his mommy, who came to the rescue. She took a deep breath, grabbed something sharp, and started to cut the jug open. Suddenly, the toy came flying out at high speed, and Tommy was so excited! He smiled and thanked his mommy for helping him, and all was well.

Sara and Tom were going on a journey with their mom and dad. They packed their bags and got in the car. Sara was happy because she liked to see new things. Tom was sad because he did not want to leave his toys and his friends.

"Tom, why are you frowning?" Sara asked. "Don't you want to go on a journey?"

"No, I don't," Tom said. "I want to stay home and play. I don't like journeys. They are long and boring."

"But journeys are fun," Sara said. "You can see new places and meet new people. And you can play with me and mom and dad. We can sing songs and tell stories and play games in the car."

Tom shook his head. He did not want to sing or tell stories or play games. He wanted to play with his toys and his friends. He crossed his arms and looked out the window.

The car drove for a long time. Sara saw many things. She saw cows and horses and sheep. She saw trees and flowers and hills. She saw houses and shops and signs. She pointed and asked mom and dad what they were. Mom and dad told her and she learned new words.

Tom did not see anything. He closed his eyes and pretended to sleep. He did not want to learn new words. He knew enough words already.

The car stopped at a big house. Mom and dad said it was their aunt's house. They got out of the car and took their bags. Sara ran to the door and knocked. She was excited to meet her aunt and her cousins.

Tom walked slowly behind mom and dad. He did not want to meet his aunt and his cousins. He did not want to share his room and his toys. He did not want to make new friends.

The door opened and a lady with a big smile came out. She hugged mom and dad and said hello. She looked at Sara and Tom and said, "You must be Sara and Tom. I'm your aunt Lucy. I'm so happy to see you. Come in, come in. I have a surprise for you."

Sara smiled and said hello. She followed her aunt into the house. She wondered what the surprise was.

Tom frowned and said nothing. He followed mom and dad into the house. He did not care about the surprise. He wanted to go home.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Lily. She always wanted to help her mom in the kitchen. So one day, Mommy gave her an apron to put on before they started cooking. Lily put on the apron and she was so excited.

Mommy said, "Lily, can you help me by stirring the beans?"

Lily said, "Yes Mommy! I can do it!"

So Lily started stirring the beans with a big spoon and she did a good job. Mommy smiled at Lily and said, "You did a very good job, Lily."

Lily was so happy that she ran over to Mommy and hugged her. "Thank you Mommy for letting me help," said Lily.

Mommy said, "Anytime, my sweet little girl! It's always nice to help."

The moral of the story is that helping people can make you feel good, and be nice to show appreciation to those that help you.

John and his mum were always very curious. They loved exploring new places and wanted to record everything they saw. One day, they went to an old, small room. It was filled with interesting things and they just had to have a closer look.

John's mum said, "John, I'm going to record this room. Why don't you go and explore?"

John was very excited, but he only saw small things. He saw a tiny mouse, a little spider and a few small flowers. He walked around and examined every corner of the room.

Suddenly, he heard his mum say, "John, come here, I've recorded everything!" John ran to her side, eager to see the recording of their amazing adventure.

His mum showed him the recording and he was amazed. He couldn't believe how much he had seen in the small room! He wanted to watch it over and over again.

But for now, it was time to go home and plan the next place to explore and record together. That was the best part of all - exploring new places with his favourite person.

Ben looked out the window and what did he see? A rock! He wanted to pick it up so he ran outside. He turned it over and saw some writing. Ben asked his mom what it said. She read it out loud.

“Be flexible.”

Ben thought hard about this. He knew he was flexible when he would push his body into fun shapes. He jumped up and down trying all sorts of movements. He wiggled his body and even bent over backwards. Ben was so flexible!

The next day, Ben saw the rock again. He wondered what new message it had for him this time. Ben asked his mom to read it to him.

“Be brave.”

Ben smiled. He knew he was brave. He climbed the monkey bars, made funny faces in the mirror, and told jokes to his friends. Ben was brave!

He picked up the rock and put it in his pocket. He wanted to remember the messages it gave him and carry it with him everywhere. He didn’t need to wait for the rock to tell him to be flexible and brave; Ben already knew he was!

Lila and Ben are friends. They like to play in the sand. They make castles and hills and tunnels. They have fun.

One day, a big wave comes. It is powerful. It breaks their sand castles and hills and tunnels. Lila and Ben are sad. They cry.

A man sees them. He has a bag. He says, "Do not cry. I have something for you." He opens his bag. He takes out some powder. It is colorful. It is magic.

He says, "This powder can make anything you want. Just sprinkle it on the sand and say what you want." He gives some powder to Lila and Ben. They smile.

Lila sprinkles some powder on the sand. She says, "I want a princess castle." The powder glows. A princess castle appears. It is pink and shiny. Lila is happy.

Ben sprinkles some powder on the sand. He says, "I want a pirate ship." The powder glows. A pirate ship appears. It is black and scary. Ben is happy.

Lila and Ben play with their new toys. They thank the man. He says, "You are welcome. But be careful. The powder does not last long. When the sun sets, it will disappear." He leaves.

Lila and Ben do not care. They have fun. They forget about the wave. They are friends.

Tom and Lily are young. They like to play with toys and books. But today, they have to pack. They are going to visit Grandma and Grandpa.

"Tom, help me pack this bear," Lily says. She holds a big, brown bear. She loves the bear very much.

"OK, Lily," Tom says. He takes the bear and puts it in a big, blue bag. The bag is empty. They have to fill it with things they need.

"What else do we need, Lily?" Tom asks.

"We need clothes, and toothbrushes, and snacks," Lily says. She looks around the room. She sees a lot of things she likes. She wants to take them all.

"But we can't take everything, Lily," Tom says. "The bag will be too heavy. And Grandma and Grandpa have toys and books, too."

Lily thinks for a moment. She knows Tom is right. She picks up a few things she really wants. She puts them in the bag. Tom does the same.

"Are we done, Tom?" Lily asks.

"I think so, Lily," Tom says. He zips the bag. It is full, but not too heavy.

They take the bag to the door. Mom and Dad are waiting for them. They are ready to go.

"Come on, Tom and Lily," Mom says. "Let's go see Grandma and Grandpa. They are very happy to see you."

Tom and Lily smile. They hug Mom and Dad. They take the bag. They are excited to go. They love Grandma and Grandpa. They hope they have fun.

Tommy was a little boy and he was worried. He was lost and he wanted to find his way home.

Tommy started walking. As he walked he heard a funny noise. It was a whistling sound. Tommy followed the sound and he came to a tunnel. He was scared, but he was also curious.

Tommy walked closer to the tunnel and he heard the whistling get louder. He felt a little braver and so he walked into the tunnel. The tunnel was dark, but it was also warm.

At the end of tunnel Tommy saw a man. The man was whistling and Tommy knew that he was friendly. Tommy walked over and the man gave him a big smile.

The man was Tommy's dad! Tommy was so happy that he ran and gave his dad a big hug. His dad was worried, but he was also relieved.

Tommy and his dad left the tunnel, with Tommy holding his dad's hand. They both whistled, happy to be on their way home.

Anna and Ben are friends. They like to play with toys and books. One day, Anna finds a telephone in her mom's room. It is big and heavy and has many buttons.

"Look, Ben, I have a telephone!" Anna says. "We can talk to anyone we want!"

"Wow, that is cool!" Ben says. "Can I try it?"

"Okay, but be careful. It is my mom's telephone. She will be angry if we break it. Promise you will not drop it or hit it."

"I promise, Anna. I will be gentle." Ben says.

Anna gives Ben the telephone. He holds it with both hands and puts it to his ear. He presses some buttons and hears a beep.

"Hello, hello, is anyone there?" Ben says.

Suddenly, he hears a loud voice from the telephone. It is not a nice voice. It is a scary voice.

"Who is this? How did you get this number? Stop calling me or I will call the police!" the voice says.

Ben is afraid. He drops the telephone on the floor. It breaks into many pieces. Anna sees what happens and starts to cry.

"Ben, you broke my mom's telephone! You promised you would not do that! Now she will be very angry and we will be in trouble!" Anna says.

"I'm sorry, Anna, I'm sorry! I did not mean to do that! The voice was scary and I got scared!" Ben says.

But it is too late. Anna's mom hears the noise and comes to the room. She sees the broken telephone and the crying children. She is very angry and sad.

"Anna, Ben, what have you done? This was my special telephone! It was a gift from your grandma! How could you be so careless and naughty?" Anna's mom says.

She takes away the telephone and the toys. She sends Anna and Ben to their rooms. She does not talk to them for a long time. Anna and Ben are very sorry and sad. They wish they had not played with the telephone. They wish they had kept their promise.

Once upon a time there was a rabbit named Bob. Bob was a brave little rabbit who loved to hop in the grass. One day Bob decided to explore the woods near his home. As he hopped through the trees he heard a strange noise. He stopped to listen and blinking his eyes he saw a big animal.

It was a bear! Bob was scared but he stayed still. The bear growled and bared its teeth. Bob knew it was a threat! But then the bear blinked, shook its head and lumbered off into the woods. Bob was so relieved.

The sky opened and a heavy rain started to pour. Bob felt wet but he smiled. Now he knew that the bear was only trying to keep him safe from the rain. Bob hopped all the way home and never forgot the day the bear blinked.

John and Mandy were best friends. Every day they would walk together to John's house. One day, John had a special surprise for Mandy. He was going to make her tea!

Mandy was very excited. She ran ahead and waited for John on the front steps. John came soon after with his special tea. He handed it to Mandy and she smiled.

They sat down to talk and share their tea. As they talked, Mandy told John how honest he was. John was so happy that he jumped for joy.

When the tea was gone, John and Mandy said goodbye and went on their way. They always felt very special when they spent time together.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy had a meeting with his friends at the park. He was very excited to play with them.

When Timmy got to the park, he saw that his friends were on the other side of the playground. He tried to reach them, but they were too far away.

Timmy felt sad because he couldn't play with his friends. But then, he saw a swing that was available. He ran over to it and started swinging. Soon, his friends saw him and ran over to play with him.

They had a fun meeting at the park and played together until it was time to go home. Timmy was happy that he was able to play with his friends, even though they were far away at first.

Once upon a time there was a boy whose name was Bob. Bob liked to go on walks in the park.

One day as he was walking, Bob saw something that looked interesting. He ran to where he saw it and stopped in front of some broken ice.

"What is that?" Bob asked. He didn't know what it was, but he wanted to find out.

Suddenly, Bob thought of a good idea to remove the ice. He ran back home and grabbed a shovel from the garage. He came back to the park and started to dig around the ice. After a few minutes, he was able to carefully remove the ice.

Bob was so happy that he could take the ice home with him. He carefully put it in a bucket and took it home.

He showed his mom and dad the ice and they were so impressed with what Bob had done. They put the ice in the freezer and now Bob can show his friends the broken ice that he removed from the park.

Once there was a little girl named Jane. She was three years old and very intelligent. She liked to visit new places. One day, her parents took her to an opera. At the opera, Jane loved the music and clapped her hands. She watched the performers in their fancy costumes and she even sang along with the songs. After the show, Jane was so excited. She talked about it for days. She said it was the most fun she ever had. Jane loves to visit the opera and looks forward to it every time.

Mama was very weak. She was feeling sick and couldn't do anything. Papa put a rug on the floor to help her rest and be comfortable.

Mama was so weak that she couldn't get out of bed. But Papa was there to help. He brought a big soft rug and laid it near the bed. He snuggled the rug up around her so that it supported her back.

When Mama felt strong enough, she got up and took a few steps on the rug. Mama smiled at Papa and thanked him for helping her.

He smiled back and said, “Anything for you, Mama.” He stayed with her until she felt better, rubbing her back and bringing her snacks. Mama was so grateful to have such a wonderful and supportive husband.

Once upon a time, there were two friends named Ben and Jane. They were playing together in the park when suddenly, it started to rain.

"Oh no!" shouted Jane, "We're getting very wet!".

Ben looked around and saw a sign which said "Film Today".

"Let's go inside and watch a film," he said.

The two friends ran over to the building and they found a man standing at the door.

"Can we watch the film?" asked Ben.

The man smiled and said, "That's why I'm here. Please sign this paper and then you can come in."

Ben and Jane both signed the paper and the man opened the door. They walked inside and found a big screen showing a film. They sat down and watched the movie, forgetting about being wet outside.

When the film was over, the sun was shining in the sky. Ben and Jane walked back to the park, happy to be dry and have had such a fun time.

Ben and Lily were playing with their toy cars in the garden. They liked to make them zoom on the grass and the dirt. They had many cars of different colors and sizes.

"Look at my orange car!" Ben said. "It is very fast and loud. Zoom, zoom, zoom!"

Lily looked at Ben's car and wanted to play with it. She reached out her hand and grabbed it. "I want to play with the orange car!" she said.

Ben was angry. He did not like to share his car. He pulled it back and shouted. "No, it is my car! You have your own car. Give it back!"

Lily was angry too. She did not want to give back the car. She held it tight and cried. "No, it is mine now! You have many cars. I only have one!"

They both started to tug and yell. They did not hear their mom calling them from the house.

"Ben, Lily, what is going on?" mom said. She came to the garden and saw them fighting over the car. She was not happy. She took the car from them and put it on the table. "You two need to learn to share and be nice. No one can play with the car until you say sorry to each other."

Ben and Lily looked at each other. They felt bad for making mom angry and for hurting each other. They said sorry and hugged. Mom smiled and gave them a hug too. She gave them each a cookie and a glass of milk. She said they could play with the car together if they promised to take turns and be kind.

Ben and Lily agreed. They thanked mom and went back to the garden. They played with the car and their other toys. They made them zoom and laugh. They were happy and had fun.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved playing with her toys, especially her dolls. One day, Lily's mom gave her a special toy. It was a fragile glass ball that had numbers on it. It was a math toy!

Lily was so excited to play with it, but her mom warned her to be careful and not drop it. Lily promised to be careful and started playing with the toy. Suddenly, her little brother came running into the room and accidentally bumped into her. The glass ball fell from Lily's hand and started rolling on the floor.

Lily was scared that the toy would break, so she shouted "Stop!" Her little brother stopped running and looked at her. Lily explained that the toy was fragile and they needed to be careful. Her brother understood and helped her pick up the toy. From that day on, Lily and her brother played with the math toy together, but always made sure to be careful and not let it break.

Once there was a dependable horse named Jack. He was always so happy to run and play with his friends. One day, he wanted to go on an adventure, so he asked his friend George to come with him.

They ran and ran, until they found a cardboard box. They were so excited to explore it, they opened the box up. Inside was a bell! It was ringing loudly. The ringing made them laugh and smile.

They decided to use the bell to follow a trail, so they put it around Jack's neck and held onto the rope. The bell led them to a big open field where they could see the sun shining down.

Jack and George had so much fun playing all day in the field. They met new friends and ran around until it was time to go back home. Before they left, they tied the bell to the box so it would be safe, so it could ring for many more adventures.

Suzie was playing in her room. She had lots of toys and she was having lots of fun. She had some blocks, a doll, and two magnets. She was playing with the magnets, and she made them stick together.

"Look, the magnets stick together!" Suzie said. She was so excited.

Suzie's dad saw what she was doing and said, "Wow, that's so cool!" Suzie was happy, and she couldn't stop smiling.

Suzie decided to try something. She picked up the magnets and held them in her hands. She shook them up, then clapped. When she clapped, the magnets stuck to her hands.

"Oh wow!" Suzie said. She couldn't believe it. She clapped her hands again and the magnets stayed put.

Suzie tried again and again, and each time, the magnets stayed stuck. "Wow, the magnets are really heavy!" Suzie said.

Suzie's dad smiled and said, "Yes, they are. Magnets are really strong!"

Suzie was so happy. She clapped her hands and laughed, then looked at the magnets again. Now she loved magnets, and she was happy to know how strong they were.

Once upon a time, there was a red bird named Ruby. She lived in a big tree with a beautiful view of the park. Ruby loved to fly around and play with her friends.

One sunny day, Ruby met a little boy named Tim. Tim looked up at the sky and said, "Ruby, I believe I can fly like you!" Ruby smiled and said, "Tim, you can't fly, but we can still play together."

So, Tim and Ruby played all day long in the park with the pretty view. They laughed and had fun. At the end of the day, they both knew they would be best friends forever.

Anna and Ben were twins. They liked to play outside in the sun. One day, they saw a big, fluffy dog near their house. The dog had a red collar and a long tail. It looked friendly and happy.

"Let's follow the dog!" Anna said. "Maybe it will show us something fun."

"OK!" Ben said. "But we have to be careful. Mom said we can't go too far from home."

They ran after the dog, who wagged its tail and barked. The dog led them to a park with a pond. There were ducks and fish in the water. The dog jumped into the pond and splashed around.

"Wow, look at the dog!" Anna said. "It likes the water. Can we go in too?"

"No, we can't," Ben said. "We don't have our swimsuits. And the water is dirty. We will get wet and sick."

"But the dog is having so much fun," Anna said. "Maybe we can just touch the water with our hands."

She walked closer to the pond and reached out her hand. But she slipped on a wet rock and fell into the water. She screamed and cried. The water was cold and deep. She couldn't swim.

"Anna, Anna!" Ben shouted. He ran to the pond and tried to help her. But he was too small and scared. He didn't know what to do.

The dog heard Anna's scream and saw her in the water. It swam to her and grabbed her by the collar. It pulled her out of the pond and onto the grass. Anna was wet and shivering. She hugged the dog and thanked it.

"Thank you, thank you, dog!" she said. "You saved me. You are a good dog."

The dog licked her face and wagged its tail. It barked and ran to Ben. It licked his face too and wagged its tail. It barked and ran back to Anna. It wanted them to play with it.

"Ben, are you OK?" Anna asked. She was still scared and cold.

"I'm OK," Ben said. He was glad that his sister was safe. He was also wet and cold. He was angry at himself for following the dog.

"Let's go home," he said. "We have to tell Mom what happened. She will be worried and mad."

"OK," Anna said. She was sorry for being naughty. She wanted to dry off and warm up.

They got up and followed the dog. The dog followed them. It didn't want to leave them. It wanted to be their friend.

They walked back to their house. They saw Mom waiting for them at the door. She looked worried and mad.

"Where have you been?" she asked. "I've been looking for you. You didn't stay where I told you to. You are wet and dirty. What did you do?"

They looked at each other and at the dog. They didn't know how to explain. They felt bad and ashamed.

They opened their mouths to speak. But before they could say anything, the dog barked and ran to Mom. It licked her face and wagged its tail. It barked and ran back to them. It wanted them to stay with it.

Mom looked at the dog and at them. She saw the red collar and the long tail. She recognized the dog.

"Oh, I see," she said. "You followed the dog. The dog belongs to our neighbor, Mr. Lee. He lost his dog this morning. He was very sad and worried. He asked me to help him find his dog. He will be very happy to see his dog again."

She smiled and hugged them. She was relieved and glad.

"I'm sorry, Mom," they said. "We were curious and silly. We won't do it again. We love you, Mom."

"I love you too, my darlings," she said. "But you have to be careful and listen to me. You could have been hurt or lost. You are lucky that the dog was nice and smart. It saved you and brought you back. You owe the dog a big thank you."

They nodded and hugged the dog. They thanked it and said goodbye. They watched as Mom took the dog to Mr. Lee's house. They saw Mr. Lee hug the dog and thank Mom. They saw the dog lick Mr. Lee's face and wag its tail. They saw the dog look at them and bark. It wanted them to visit it.

They waved at the dog and smiled. They liked the dog. They wanted to visit it too.

They went inside the house. They changed their clothes and drank some hot chocolate. They felt warm and cozy. They told Mom their story. They learned their lesson.

They never followed a dog again. But they made a new friend

Once there was a funny bounce. It was so happy and fun. The bounce loved the sunshine. It would laugh and jump in the warm sunshine and feel so happy.

Every morning the bounce would wake up and splash in the sunshine. The bounce would laugh so much and have so much fun. It was full of joy, bouncing around in the sunshine.

The bounce was so happy! It loved the sunshine and the feeling of joy it brought. Everyone who saw the bounce bouncing around in the sunshine couldn't help but smile too. The bounce stayed happy, bouncing around in the sunshine. Day after day it could enjoy the warmth of the sunshine, and the joy of the bouncing.

Lily and Ben were playing in the park with their mom. They saw an elderly man walking with a big bag. He stopped at a red box and put some letters inside.

"What is he doing, mom?" Lily asked.

"He is sending post, sweetie. That means he is giving messages to people who live far away. The red box is where he puts the post, and then someone comes and takes it to the people," mom explained.

"Wow, that is cool! Can we send post too, mom?" Ben asked.

"Sure, we can. Do you have someone you want to send a message to?" mom asked.

Lily and Ben thought for a moment. Then they both said, "Grandma!"

"Grandma would love to hear from you. Let's go home and make some cards for her. You can draw and write whatever you want," mom said.

They went home and got some paper, crayons, and stickers. They made beautiful cards for grandma, telling her how much they loved her and missed her. They put their names and kisses on the cards. Mom helped them put the cards in envelopes and write grandma's address.

The next day, they went back to the park with their mom. They saw the same elderly man with his big bag. He smiled at them and said hello.

"Hello, sir. We are sending post too. We made cards for our grandma. She lives far away and we can't see her now," Lily said.

"That is very nice of you, children. I'm sure your grandma will be very happy to receive your cards. I admire you for being so thoughtful and creative," the man said.

He helped them put their cards in the red box. He gave them a wink and said, "There you go. Your post is on its way. Have a wonderful day!"

Lily and Ben thanked him and waved goodbye. They felt proud and happy. They hoped grandma would get their cards soon and smile. They loved sending post.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved playing outside with his friends. One day, Timmy's mom gave him a new gear to wear when he played outside. The gear was warm and cozy, and Timmy loved it.

Timmy and his friends played outside for hours, but then it started to get dark. Timmy's mom called him inside for dinner, but he didn't want to go. He was having too much fun with his friends.

But then, Timmy remembered his warm gear and how much he loved it. He knew he had to go inside to eat dinner and put his gear away. So, Timmy called to his friends, "I have to go inside now, but I'll see you tomorrow!"

Timmy went inside and had a yummy dinner with his family. He felt happy and warm in his gear, and he couldn't wait to play outside with his friends again tomorrow. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to draw with her favorite ink pen, which was pink and sparkly. One day, while she was drawing a picture of a flower, her little brother came over and accidentally knocked her ink pen off the table.

Lily was very upset and started to cry. Her brother felt stupid for making her cry and said, "I'm sorry, Lily. I didn't mean to knock over your pen."

Lily's mom came over and saw what happened. She said, "It's okay, Lily. Don't cry. We can support you by getting you a new ink pen."

Lily stopped crying and smiled. She hugged her mom and said, "Thank you for supporting me."

Once upon a time, there was a cute little girl named Mia. Mia loved to mix things together.

One day, Mia's mommy took her to the opera. At the opera, Mia saw all sorts of interesting things. One of them was two singers mixing their voices.

Mia was so amazed by their mix that she started to mix some things herself. She mixed a few colorful cushions and a doll. Mia was so pleased with the mix she made.

Mia's mommy was so happy to see Mia so happy. It was a wonderful day at the opera.

Once upon a time, there was a lovely prince. He was brave and daring. One day he decided to go on a journey. He put on his armour and got on his horse. All of a sudden, he heard a loud noise. He looked around and noticed a dragon! The dragon asked the prince, "Do you dare to fight me?". Without hesitation, the prince said yes. The prince was brave and strong. He fought the dragon and eventually he won! Everyone cheered and praised the prince! The prince felt proud and happy knowing he was loved by many people.

He went back to the kingdom and everyone there welcomed him with open arms. The prince was proud of his courage and bravery and vowed to protect the kingdom from any harm. And so, he lived happily ever after with his lovely kingdom. This is the tale of the daring prince!

Once upon a time, there was a boy who had a round, soft rug. He loved to play on it. One day he wanted to do something different. He decided to number the rug. So, the boy got his markers and carefully he started to number each side of the rug. The boy was slow and precise. He must make sure that the numbers were neat and even. Finally, the number rug was complete and the boy was very happy. Every day he wakes up, jumps onto the rug and counts the numbers. It was so much fun to sit and relax on his special number rug!

Ben and Lily were two camels who lived in the desert. They liked to walk and look for food and water. Sometimes they found an oasis, a place with green plants and a pond. They were happy when they found an oasis, because they could drink and rest.

One day, they saw a big oasis far away. They wanted to go there, but it was very hot and they were tired. Ben said, "Let's roll on the sand. It will make us cool and comfortable." Lily said, "No, let's keep walking. The oasis is important. We need water and shade."

Ben did not listen to Lily. He rolled on the sand and closed his eyes. He felt good, but he did not see the sandstorm coming. The sandstorm was strong and loud. It covered Ben with sand and made him lose his way. He could not see the oasis or Lily.

Lily kept walking. She reached the oasis and drank from the pond. She looked for Ben, but she could not find him. She was worried and sad. She said, "Where is Ben? I hope he is safe. I wish he listened to me."

Ben was scared and thirsty. He tried to find the oasis, but he could not. He said, "Help! Help! Where is Lily? Where is the oasis? I made a mistake. I should have listened to Lily. The oasis was important."

The moral of the story is: Listen to your friends who care about you. They can help you make good choices. Do not be lazy or careless. You might miss something important.

Once there was a pale girl called Ella. She was three years old and loved to do sports. One day, Ella's mommy said it was time for a game. Ella was so excited!

They went to Ella's room and her mommy told her to sit on the bed. Then she showed Ella a special surprise - some cloth that was brightly coloured. Ella watched as her mommy bent the cloth carefully and wrapped it around her. She felt so snug and warm!

Afterwards, Ella and her mommy went outside to play. They ran to the park and Ella saw so many other kids playing different sports. She chose running and soon was chasing her mommy around the field. It was so much fun!

When they went home, Ella's mommy hugged her and said she did a great job with the sport. Then they had a drink and sat together in Ella's room. Ella's mommy said she was proud of her and hugged her again. Ella felt so happy and sleepy, so she snuggled with her mommy and went to sleep.

A human was walking through a field, looking around and seeing the world around them. Suddenly, they saw something in the grass. It was big and bright and seemed harmless. The human reached down to pick it up and saw that it was a butterfly!

The butterfly flew around in front of them and the human smiled. It was so pretty and harmless. Suddenly, the butterfly landed on the human’s shoulder and stayed there. The human was so happy to have a new friend.

Then, something even better happened. The human heard a rustling in the grass and saw two more butterflies fly out! They were just as pretty and harmless as the first one. The three butterflies flew around for a few minutes before flying off into the sunset.

The human watched them fly away and smiled. It was a beautiful sight to see!

Ben and Lily liked to play freeze tag in the living room. They ran around the furniture and tried to touch each other. If Ben touched Lily, she had to freeze and not move. If Lily touched Ben, he had to freeze and not move. They were very competitive and wanted to win.

One day, they played freeze tag when their mom was not home. They did not listen to their dad, who told them to be careful and not break anything. They ran faster and faster, and did not watch where they were going. They bumped into the table, the lamp, the sofa, and the bookshelf. They made a big mess and a lot of noise.

Their dad heard the noise and came to the living room. He saw the mess and was very angry. He said, "Stop! What are you doing? Look at what you have done! You have broken the lamp and the vase, and you have knocked down the books and the pictures. You are in big trouble!"

Ben and Lily stopped and looked at their dad. They felt sorry and scared. They said, "We are sorry, dad. We were just playing freeze tag. We did not mean to break anything. Please don't be mad at us."

Their dad sighed and said, "I know you were just playing, but you have to be more careful and respectful. You have to clean up this mess and apologize to your mom when she comes home. And no more freeze tag in the living room. Do you understand?"

Ben and Lily nodded and said, "We understand, dad. We are sorry. We will clean up and say sorry to mom. And we will play freeze tag outside next time."

Their dad hugged them and said, "I love you, but you have to learn from your mistakes. Now, let's get to work and fix this mess."

One day, there was a little girl, who was just three years old. She saw something that made her really happy. It was a pot of cream! She was so excited she picked it up and starting pointing at it.

The little girl could tell that the cream was smelly because the smell was very strong. She wanted to know what it was so she asked her daddy, "What's in the pot?"

Daddy told her that it was something very special. It was ice cream. He said it was something special that she could eat.

The little girl was very excited and wanted to eat it right away. Daddy said that she had to wait until it was ready. He put it in the freezer and they both waited.

Finally, after an hour the ice cream had frozen and was ready to eat. Daddy said it was delicious! The little girl couldn't agree more. Together they ate the creamy, smelly, delicious ice cream.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy who lived near a hedge. He liked to explore the hedge and have adventures. One day, he heard something delicate. It was so quiet he almost didn't hear it. He followed the sound to see what it was, and he found a tiny bird with a beautiful voice. The song was so beautiful that the boy wanted to stay and listen forever! The little boy was so happy to hear the delicate sound and he tried to memorize every note. After that, the little boy returned home with a big smile on his face because he had heard something so magical!

Once upon a time there was a special boy named Joe. Joe loved to design things. One day he decided to design a monster. Joe sketched and painted the monster. He made it high, with tall legs and big eyes.

After the monster was finished, Joe put it in the garden. He was so proud of his masterpiece.

A few days later, Joe's dad saw the monster while he was gardening. Joe's dad was so surprised, he said, "Wow, this is an amazing monster Joe! What are you going to do with it?"

Joe smiled and said, "I'm going to have a party and let the monster out!"

Joe's dad was curious. He knew the monster was special. That night, Joe made a plan. He invited all his friends to his house. When they arrived, Joe opened the door to the garden. Everyone was so amazed when they saw the monster. Joe said, "Let's all have fun and play together."

The next day, everyone had a great time playing with the monster. Joe was so proud of how his design had come to life. He had created a monster that brought everyone joy.

Anna liked to study flowers. She had a book with pictures of many flowers. She learned their names and colors. She wanted to see them in real life.

One day, she went to the park with her mom. She saw a lot of flowers there. She ran to them and looked at them closely. She saw roses, daisies, tulips and more. She was very happy.

She saw one flower that was different. It was big and bright. It had many petals that looked like flames. It was brilliant. She pointed to it and asked her mom, "What is that flower?"

Her mom smiled and said, "That is a sunflower. It is called that because it looks like the sun. It is very beautiful, just like you."

Anna smiled and said, "I like sunflowers. They are my favorite now. Can I study them more?"

Her mom nodded and said, "Of course. You can study anything you want. You are a smart and curious girl. I am proud of you."

Anna hugged her mom and said, "Thank you, mom. I love you. And I love flowers."

Once there was a little girl named Bea. She was adventurous and loved to explore. One day, Bea noticed two squirrels running around outside. She wanted to race them, so she put on her running shoes and dashed out the door.

Bea ran as fast as she could, but the squirrels were way too quick for her. They zigzagged around trees and hopped over rocks with ease. After a few minutes, Bea was exhausted.

Luckily, Bea wasn't alone. Her tutor saw what was going on and decided to join the race. His long legs enabled him to run faster than the squirrels, so he was able to pass them. When he reached the end, the tutor waited for Bea to finish. Even though she wasn't the winner, Bea was proud of how fast she had been running. All in all, it was a very adventurous race!

Lila liked to polish her sunflower. She had a yellow cloth and some water. She would wet the cloth and rub it on the sunflower. She wanted it to shine like the sun.

One day, she saw a bee on the sunflower. She thought the bee was dirty. She tried to polish the bee with her cloth. The bee did not like that. It buzzed and stung her hand. Lila cried out loud.

Her mom heard her and came to see. She saw the bee and the cloth and the sunflower. She hugged Lila and took her inside. She put some ice on her hand and gave her some juice. She said, "Lila, you are foolish. You cannot polish a bee. Bees are not dirty. They help the sunflowers grow. You should leave them alone."

Lila felt sorry and said, "I'm sorry, mom. I did not know. I just wanted to polish my sunflower." Her mom smiled and said, "I know, Lila. You love your sunflower. But you have to be careful. Some things are not for polishing. They are for looking and learning."

Lila nodded and said, "OK, mom. I will look and learn. And I will not polish bees anymore." Her mom kissed her and said, "That's good, Lila. Now, let's go and see your sunflower. Maybe it has a new friend." They went outside and saw a butterfly on the sunflower. Lila smiled and said, "Look, mom. A butterfly. It is pretty. Can I polish it?" Her mom laughed and said, "No, Lila. You cannot polish a butterfly. But you can watch it and enjoy it." Lila agreed and said, "OK, mom. I will watch and enjoy. And I will not be foolish." They sat down and watched the butterfly and the sunflower. They were happy.

Mummy was in the supermarket. She needs to buy lots of things for dinner. She saw a big board with some chunky carrots on it. She wanted to buy them, but it was very heavy.

Mummy looked around and saw Pete. He was a clumsy boy. He was having a lot of trouble trying to pick up the board. Mummy smiled and asked him:

"Can I help you with the board, Pete?"

Pete was so pleased.

"Yes please!" he said.

Mummy picked up the board and put it in her trolley. Then she bought the carrots.

Back at home, Mummy put the carrots on the table.

"Thank you for helping me buy the carrots, Pete," she said.

Pete smiled. He was glad he could help.

Mummy and Pete enjoyed dinner together.

Lily and Ben liked to play in the forest. They liked to look for animals and flowers and rocks. One day, they saw a big mushroom. It was red and white and high. Lily wanted to pick it.

"Look, Ben, a mushroom! Can I have it?" Lily asked.

Ben shook his head. "No, Lily, you can't. That mushroom is not good. It can make you sick. We have to keep away from it."

Lily frowned. "But it is so pretty. I want to touch it."

Ben grabbed Lily's hand. "No, Lily, don't. Come with me. I will show you something better."

He led her to a sunny spot. There were many yellow flowers. They smelled nice. Ben picked one and gave it to Lily.

"Here, Lily, this is for you. A flower. You can keep it. It is good. It will make you happy."

Lily smiled. She took the flower and smelled it. She hugged Ben.

"Thank you, Ben. You are a good brother. I like the flower. It is better than the mushroom."

They played with the flowers and forgot about the mushroom. They were happy.

One day, a little girl named Susie was playing in her garden with bubbles. She eagerly waited for the sun to shine and to bring the bubbles to life.

When the sun came out, Susie was cheered. She eagerly watched as the bubble she blew began to sparkle and shine in the sunlight. It was beautiful.

In her excitement, she shouted with joy: “Look, my bubble is shining!”

Her mother, who was nearby, smiled and replied, “Yes, Susie. It looks so pretty!”

Susie had so much fun that day playing with her bubble and watching it shine in the sun. After several hours, the sun disappeared and the bubbles began to disappear too. But Susie did not worry, she knew that the sun was dependable and would be back tomorrow.

Once upon a time, a cap was having a fun day playing in the sun. Suddenly, the cap noticed a funny figure in the distance. After a few minutes, the figure came closer and the cap realized it was a monster! The cap quickly covered his eyes so he didn't have to look at it.

The monster was getting nearer and nearer. The cap started to panic, but then he remembered that he was wearing a cap! He covered his face with the cap, and soon the monster was gone.

The cap was so relieved, and he was very thankful for his cap. After that, he made sure to always wear a cap so he wouldn't have to be scared of monsters again.

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a kind girl named Lily. She loved to play with her hoop in the park. One day, she found a marker on the ground. She picked it up and started to mark on the hoop. She drew a smiley face and some stars.

Suddenly, a boy came over and asked if he could play too. Lily was happy to share her hoop with him. They played together and had so much fun. When it was time to go home, Lily gave the boy the hoop as a gift. He was so happy and thanked her with a big smile.

From that day on, Lily and the boy became good friends and played together often. They always remembered the day they marked on the hoop and how it brought them together. The end.

Jenny was getting ready for her big trip. She was so excited and enthusiastic to go. She had been counting down the days until she could leave.

Jenny's mom came into her room and asked her what she was doing. Jenny told her she was trying to pack. Her mom smiled and gave her a hug.

Then, Jenny's dad said, "Let me give you a rub before you go." Jenny smiled and said yes. Her dad gave her a nice long rub on her back. She felt so relaxed.

Finally, Jenny finished packing and was ready to go. She was so full of joy and enthusiasm that she almost forgot her suitcase. She was finally off on her big adventure.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys and her dog named Max. One day, Lily's mommy turned on the TV to watch the news. The news talked about a big storm coming to their town. Lily got scared and asked her mommy, "What should we do?" Her mommy said, "We should pray that the storm doesn't hurt us."

Lily didn't know how to pray, so her mommy taught her. They held hands and closed their eyes. Lily repeated after her mommy, "Dear God, please keep us safe from the storm." After they finished praying, Lily felt better.

The storm came, but it wasn't as bad as they thought it would be. After the storm, Lily and Max went outside to play. They found a charming butterfly in the garden. Lily said, "Look, Max! A pretty butterfly!" Max barked happily. Lily smiled and felt grateful that they were safe.

Once upon a time, there was a mommy and a baby who loved to play. Mommy was very impressive and always lent an ear to her baby's stories. One day, mommy decided to play a game. She took a large stick and placed it so that it went from the ground, up to the sky. She asked the baby to take a turn and the baby smiled big!

The baby grabbed a big rock and tried to lift it up to the sky. Mommy saw how hard the baby was working and she felt proud. The baby kept trying, but the rock was too heavy. Mommy saw how determined the baby was and she smiled. She walked over and lent a hand to help the baby with the rock. Finally, they managed to get the rock up to the sky together.

Mommy and the baby hugged each other, feeling so happy. They had done an impressive job working together. It was a great game, full of fun and adventure. Mommy and the baby were the best of friends and they couldn't wait to create more memories together.

Once upon a time, there was a charming little frog. He lived near a small pond. He liked to jump and play all day long. He had many friends who lived there too. They all had fun together.

One day, the frog saw a big mess near the pond. It was very dirty. The frog wanted to help, so he started to wipe the mess with his small hands. He worked very hard. His friends saw him and they all came to help.

But the mess was too big for them. They wiped and wiped, but it did not go away. The pond became dirty too. The charming little frog and his friends could not play there anymore. They were very sad. The bad mess had changed their fun pond forever.

One day, a girl named Sue wanted to make a new friend. She went to the park and saw a boy named Tim. Tim was playing with a big, scary bug. Sue was scared, but she wanted to be brave and make friends with Tim.

Sue went to her house and found a big jug. She had an idea. She would catch a bug in the jug and show it to Tim. Then, maybe Tim would want to be her friend. Sue went outside and looked for a bug to catch.

Sue found a bug and put it in the jug. She went back to the park and showed Tim the bug in the jug. Tim was happy to see the bug and they both played with it. Sue was not scared anymore. Sue and Tim became good friends, and they had fun playing with bugs together.

Once upon a time, there was a curious lion. She was so curious that she wanted to fly.

She said to a bird, "Can I fly too?" The bird said, "No, only I can fly."

The lion did not want to accept the answer, so she kept asking different animals if she could fly. Everyone said no, but the lion kept trying to find a way to fly.

Suddenly, a magical fairy appeared in the sky! She said, "You can come fly with me!" The lion was so happy that she hopped and cheered.

But when they flew higher and higher, something terrible happened. The lion got too close to the sun and its bright heat made the lion start to fall!

The lion said, "I'm scared!" She flew faster and faster, but it was too late. The lion hit the ground with a loud crash and she was never seen again.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy liked to play chess with his grandpa. One day, Timmy's grandpa said, "Timmy, it's time to bathe before dinner." Timmy said, "Okay, grandpa."

Timmy went to the bathroom and filled the tub with nice warm water. He put bubbles in the water and got in. Timmy splashed around and had fun. After he was done, he got out and dried off.

When Timmy went back to his grandpa, he said, "Grandpa, I'm clean now. Can we play chess?" His grandpa said, "Sure, Timmy. Let's play." Timmy and his grandpa played chess for a long time. It was a nice day.

Once upon a time, there was a small mouse who wanted to succeed. He looked up to the sky and said to himself, "I can do it!". He then turned and started to run. He ran faster and faster, until he was so fast that he could fly! He flew up high into the sky. He felt so small under the big sky, but he kept going. Finally, he reached his goal and was very proud of himself! He had succeeded!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a mighty red ball that she loved to play with. One day, she went to the park with her mommy and daddy. At the park, she saw a big slide that she wanted to go on.

Lily climbed up the steps and when she got to the top, she felt scared. But her daddy held her hand and said, "Don't worry, I'll catch you." So, Lily slid down the slide and it was so much fun!

After playing at the park, Lily's mommy gave her a bottle of water to drink. Lily was thirsty and drank all the water from the bottle. She felt happy and so grateful to have such a fun day with her mommy and daddy. The end.

Ben and Sam are brothers. They like to play with their toy cars and trucks. They make noises like engines and horns. They pretend to drive fast and have races.

One day, they find a big box in the garage. It has a picture of a real car on it. They are very excited. They think it is a gift for them. They open the box and see a shiny red car inside. It has four wheels, a steering wheel, and a key.

"Wow, look at this!" Ben says. "It is a real car! Let's try it!"

"OK, but I want to drive first!" Sam says. "You always get to do everything first. It is not fair!"

"No, I want to drive first!" Ben says. "You are too little. You don't know how to drive. It is my turn!"

They start to fight over the car. They pull and push and shout. They do not listen to each other. They do not listen to their mom, who calls them from the house.

"Ben! Sam! Come inside! It is time for lunch!" Mom says. "Stop fighting and share the car!"

But they do not hear her. They are too busy fighting. They do not see the car key fall out of the box. They do not see the cat, who is curious and playful. The cat sees the shiny key and thinks it is a toy. The cat grabs the key with its paw and runs away.

Ben and Sam finally stop fighting. They are tired and hungry. They look for the key to start the car. But they cannot find it. They look in the box, under the car, around the garage. But the key is gone.

"Where is the key?" Ben asks.

"I don't know!" Sam says.

They start to cry. They have a real car, but they cannot drive it. They have ruined their fun. They have been bad brothers. They wish they had listened to their mom. They wish they had shared the car. They wish they had been fair. But it is too late. The end.

Once there was a little boy named Josh. He was three years old and he loved to explore the world. He loved to follow the birds, explore the garden and run around in the park.

One day, Josh saw a brown rabbit. He wanted to follow the rabbit and see where it went. So he slowly walked after the rabbit, being careful not to scare it away. The rabbit hopped away until it came to a burrow in the ground.

Josh wanted to give the rabbit a name, so he called out, "Hello, Mr Brown Rabbit!" He smiled as he said the name and the rabbit turned around and hopped off, disappearing into the burrow. Josh laughed and waved goodbye to his new friend.

Josh followed the rabbit's tracks back home, where he told his parents all about his adventure. His parents were so proud of him - Josh had made a new friend and seen what amazing things he could find when he followed his curiosity.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a strong desire to help her mom in the kitchen. One day, her mom asked her to spread the butter on the bread. Lily tried her best but found it hard to spread the butter evenly.

Her mom then gave her a key to unlock a secret drawer in the kitchen. Inside the drawer, Lily found a special butter knife that was easy to use. She happily spread the butter on the bread and showed her mom.

But then, her little brother came along and wanted to eat the bread too. He tried to take it away from Lily, causing a conflict between them. Lily said, "No, this is mine!" Her brother started crying, and Lily felt bad. She decided to share the bread with him, and they both enjoyed it together.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Molly. She was very worried, because she had lost her favorite toy. One night, while she was crying in bed, she heard a gentle hooting sound. Molly opened her window and a friendly owl flew in.

Molly was surprised, but the owl only wanted to help. It flew around the room, searching until it found Molly's toy. It bowed its wings and dropped the toy in Molly's lap.

Molly was amazed and asked the owl, “What are you?”

The owl hooted again and said, “I'm an owl! I saw that you were worried so I wanted to come and restore your toy. Now, please have a good night's sleep.”

Molly thanked the owl and fell asleep with a smile on her face. From that day on, Molly was sure that owls were magical creatures who could make any worries go away.

Once upon a time there was a lady who had the biggest backyard around! It was filled with flowers, trees and a little pond. She wanted to keep her backyard nice and beautiful so she decided to keep it very fragile.

One day, a naughty neighbourhood boy heard about the lady's backyard and decided to come and have a look. He came to the backyard and started picking flowers, breaking branches and throwing stones in the pond. The lady was very unhappy and shouted at the boy to leave.

"No! I won't leave," shouted the naughty boy. "This is my backyard now!"

The lady was so angry she had no choice but to call the police. When the police arrived, the naughty boy had no choice but to leave the backyard. He was very sad but had no other choice.

The lady was very sad too. She had hoped the boy would learn to be gentle and careful, but instead he decided to do bad things and ruined her backyard. From then on, she made sure her backyard was locked so no one else could get in.

The end.

Jim was walking in the park when he noticed a bottle lying on the ground. He picked it up to look for a label and saw it said 'juice'. Instantly, Jim felt really thirsty, so he nodded, opened the bottle and took a big drink.

The juice was thick and sweet and made Jim's throat feel all tingly and warm. He had just taken another sip when he heard a small voice from behind him say,

"My bottle, please."

Jim spun around to find a little girl, about three years old, standing there holding out her arms and looking really thirsty. She had big, sleepy eyes and long, golden hair.

Jim smiled at her and nodded. He handed her the bottle, and she gave him a big smile and took a tiny sip. Then she said,

"Thanks!"

Jim smiled back and nodded. He said,

"You're welcome."

Then he watched as she ran off, sipping her juice as she went. Jim smiled to himself. He was happy he had been able to give the little girl a drink.

Tiny was walking in the park when she noticed a big spring. It was so big and shiny, it made her jump! She ran over to it and touched it with her finger. The spring moved, so she touched it again. She laughed and started to bounce up and down on it.

When she looked up, she saw a boy. He was a little older than her, around five or six.

"Hi!" said Tiny.

"Hello," said the boy.

"What are you doing?" asked Tiny.

"I'm looking for something important," said the boy.

"What is it?" asked Tiny.

"It's a special spring," said the boy. "It's magic and it can make wishes come true."

Tiny was excited. "Do you think this is it?" she said, pointing to the big spring.

The boy smiled and nodded. "Yes, I think this is the one. Thank you so much for finding it," he said.

Tiny beamed. She was so happy to have helped the boy find something important. Then, she watched as the boy started to make his wish on the spring. When he was done, the spring glowed and a puff of magic sparkled in the air.

Tiny smiled. She was so glad she had helped the boy find such an important spring.

Once upon a time, there was a lovely monster called Jack. He loved to dance whenever he felt happy. Everyone around could see how he moved his body so gracefully.

He hopped and jumped and twirled around the meadow to the beat of the music. Even when his feet were so tired, he kept on dancing. He loved it that much.

He quickly learnt lots of different dances like the tango, the salsa and the foxtrot. Everyone was astonished at how fast his dancing had improved in such a short time.

One day, Jack was invited to a big dance party. He was so excited and couldn't wait to show off his new moves.

At the party, everyone was amazed at how he moved. He was having so much fun, he didn't want to stop.

The night ended with Jack giving a big bow and everyone giving him a round of applause. Jack danced and smiled all the way home because it had been such a lovely night.

Once upon a time, there was a little bunny named Bobo. He lived in a small hole near a big tree. Bobo loved to play with his friends in the grass. They liked to jump, run, and have fun in the sun.

One day, Bobo saw a new bunny near the tree. The new bunny was shy and did not have any friends. Bobo wanted to help, so he went to the new bunny and said, "Hi! I am Bobo. Do you want to play with us?" The new bunny smiled and said, "Yes, I am Lulu. I want to play too."

Bobo and his friends included Lulu in their games. They all played in the grass together. They were very happy. The little bunnies learned that it is good to be kind and include others. When you are kind and include others, you make new friends and have more fun. And that is the moral of the story.

Once upon a time, there was a thin parrot. The parrot liked to fly around, exploring the world around him. One day he decided to go a little too far and got lost. He was scared and didn't know what to do.

So he flew and he flew, searching and searching until he couldn't fly anymore. Finally he found his home, and he was so happy. He returned to his family, and he was never so happy to be home!

The parrot's friends were very excited to see him. They all gave him a big hug and he felt so loved. After that, he enjoyed his adventures a lot more, but he still made sure that he didn't go too far away so he wouldn't get lost again.

The parrot was happy to be home once again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. Today was a special day because it was her birthday! She was so excited and ready to celebrate.

Lily's mommy made her a big cake with lots of frosting and candles. She counted the candles on the cake and said, "There are five candles, Lily! Can you say the number five?"

Lily giggled and said, "Five!" She was so happy to be five years old now. She blew out the candles and made a wish. She wished for lots of toys and candy.

After the cake, Lily's friends came over to play. They had a fun time playing with toys and games. Lily was so happy to have her friends with her on her special day. She felt loved and ready for another year of adventures.

Sara and Ben were playing in the backyard. They liked to dig holes and look for bugs. Sara found a big worm and put it in a jar. She wanted to show it to Mom.

"Look, Ben, I have a worm!" Sara said. "It is very long and wiggly. Maybe it is an inch long."

Ben came closer and looked at the jar. He saw the worm moving inside. He wanted to touch it.

"Can I hold it, Sara?" Ben asked. "Please?"

Sara shook her head. "No, Ben, it is mine. You have to find your own worm."

Ben felt sad and angry. He was impatient. He did not want to dig anymore. He wanted Sara's worm.

He waited until Sara was not looking. Then he grabbed the jar and opened the lid. He reached inside and tried to catch the worm.

But the worm was fast and slippery. It escaped from Ben's hand and fell on the ground. It crawled away into the grass.

"Hey, Ben, what are you doing?" Sara shouted. "You let my worm go! That was not nice!"

Ben felt sorry and scared. He dropped the jar and ran away. He hoped Sara would not be mad at him for too long. He wished he had not taken her worm.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who loved to explore. One day, she wanted to find out how heavy an armchair was.

“Mommy, can we weigh the armchair?” she asked with a smile.

“No, sweetheart,” her mommy said. “It’s too big.” The little girl thought for a moment. “What about the empty cardboard box in the garage?”

Her mommy nodded. “That can work. Let’s go take a look.”

They went to the garage and found the empty cardboard box. Her mommy left the little girl alone with the box while she went to look for something to weigh it with.

The little girl touched the empty box and said to herself, “This box is probably too light to weigh an armchair.” She smiled.

A few minutes later, her mommy came back with a scale. They weighed the box and found that it was just enough to weigh the armchair.

The little girl was so happy that she hugged her mommy. “See? I knew it could work.”

The end.

Polly was a happy girl. She had a lot of energy, so each day she would dance. Everywhere Polly went, she brought her horn with her.

Today she was feeling particularly restless. She wanted to dance even more than usual. Polly went to a big field and shouted, "This is my dance floor!" Then she blew her horn and waved her arms up above her head.

She kept dancing and dancing until her feet got tired. She finally stopped and rested in the cool grass. Polly was exhausted and happily out of breath. But she made sure to keep her horn close.

Polly was happy and content. She cooled down and then, when she was ready, it was time to dance again. And that's what Polly did, until it was time for bed.

Anna loves cream. She likes to eat it with cake, or fruit, or just by itself. She thinks cream is very yummy and sweet. But cream is expensive. Her mom and dad do not have a lot of money. They can only buy cream sometimes, as a treat.

One day, Anna sees a big jar of cream in the fridge. She is very happy. She thinks her mom and dad bought it for her. She wants to eat some right away. She takes a spoon and opens the jar. She scoops some cream and puts it in her mouth. It is delicious.

But then she hears her mom's voice. "Anna, what are you doing?" Her mom is angry. She says, "That cream is not for you. That cream is for grandma. She is sick and we want to give her something nice. You are very naughty. You wasted the expensive cream."

Anna feels bad. She did not know the cream was for grandma. She loves grandma. She does not want to make her mom or grandma sad. She says, "I'm sorry, mom. I did not know. I like cream, but I like grandma more. Can I give her some cream too?"

Her mom sighs. She is still angry, but she loves Anna. She says, "Yes, you can give her some cream. But only a little bit. And you have to say sorry to grandma. And no more cream for you today. You have to learn to share and to ask before you take something."

Anna nods. She says, "OK, mom. I will do that. I will be good." She hugs her mom and says, "I love you, mom. And I love grandma. And I love cream. But not as much as you and grandma." Her mom smiles and hugs her back. She says, "I love you too, Anna. And I love grandma. And I love cream. But not as much as you and grandma." They go to see grandma and give her some cream. Grandma is happy. She says, "Thank you, Anna. And thank you, mom. You are very kind. I love you both. And I love cream. But not as much as you both." They all laugh and hug. They are a happy family. They all love cream. But not as much as each other.

Lily and Ben were playing soccer with their team. They liked to kick the ball and run fast. They wanted to win the game and have fun.

But Sam was on their team too. Sam was selfish. He did not like to share the ball. He always wanted to score by himself. He did not care about his team.

One time, Sam had the ball and ran to the goal. He saw Lily and Ben open, but he did not pass to them. He tried to shoot, but the other team blocked him. The other team got the ball and ran to the other goal.

Lily and Ben ran after them. They wanted to save the goal. They saw Sam standing and pouting. They shouted at him.

"Sam, help us! We are a team! We need you!" Lily said.

"Stop being selfish! Pass the ball next time!" Ben said.

But Sam did not listen. He did not move. He did not care.

Lily and Ben reached the other goal. They saw the other team about to shoot. They jumped and blocked the ball. They saved the goal!

Their team cheered for them. They were happy and proud. They hugged each other.

But Sam was not happy. He was alone and sad. He realized he was wrong. He wished he had helped his team. He wished he had not been selfish. He learned a lesson.

Once upon a time, in an ordinary little town, there lived a boy named Tim. Tim loved to make people laugh. Every day, he would tell a joke to his friends and family. They would all laugh and clap, and it made Tim very happy.

One day, Tim met a new friend named Sam. Sam was very shy and did not trust people easily. Tim wanted to make Sam laugh, so he told him a funny joke. At first, Sam did not laugh. But Tim did not give up. He told another joke, and this time, Sam laughed a little bit.

As they spent more time together, Sam started to trust Tim more and more. They became best friends and shared many jokes and laughs. Tim learned that sometimes, people need time to trust, and Sam learned that laughter can help make friends. And they lived happily ever after in their ordinary little town.

Once upon a time, there was a generous lady who had an important job. Her job was to remind the people in her town to be kind. She helped people who were in jail and made sure they had enough to eat. She always gave them a big smile when she visited.

One day, the generous lady decided she wanted to do something more for the people in jail. She went to the local store and bought lots of treats. Then she went back to the jail and shared them out. Everyone was so happy and thanked her.

The generous lady's job was to remind them to be kind, but she was also reminding them of how good it is to be generous. Her generous actions made the people in jail feel good, and the people in town very proud.

At the end of the day, the generous lady smiled. She was happy that she could help make people's day a little brighter.

One day, a wise old man had to go to a special suit-making shop. He wanted to get a very special suit that nobody had ever seen before. He brought some money with him but he noticed something was missing when he arrived. He had forgotten to take the tiny blue feathers he needed for the suit!

He started to worry about what to do, but then he had a clever idea. He picked up a feather from the floor and scattered it around the shop. Soon, many more feathers were appearing from thin air. Everyone in the shop was amazed as the wise man filled his pockets with the beautiful blue feathers.

The old man took the feathers to the suit-maker and the man was very pleased. With the feathers, he made an incredible suit like nobody had ever seen before. The old man was very proud of his new suit and he went out into the world to show it off.

Everyone admired the old man's new suit and they thought he was very wise. He smiled and gave thanks to the method he had used to get the feathers: the scatter!

Once upon a time there was a green frog. He lived in pond, right in the middle of a field. Every day he would hop around the pond and make a sound. This sound made everyone nearby very happy.

One day, while the green frog was sitting on his rock, he heard something big coming closer. He knew this thing was not normal. Suddenly, he heard a loud noise, it was coming from the sky. It disturbed the peace of the field.

The frog was so scared that he hopped away to hide. He didn't know what to do, or who was making that sound. He asked the bird who was flying overhead if he had seen anything strange.

The bird told him he had seen a big, green machine. It was making loud noises as it flew up to the sky. He said it was disturbing the quietness of the field.

The green frog was so surprised. He had never seen anything like this before. He hopped away and told all his friends about the big, green machine that he had seen. All of them agreed that it was a very strange sight.

Once upon a time, there was a dog named Spot. Spot had a flea on his back that he could not catch. The flea was very fast and Spot was very sad.

One day, Spot's friend, a cat named Mittens, saw Spot scratching and feeling bad. Mittens said, "Let me help you, Spot!" Mittens chased the flea and caught it with her sharp claws.

Spot was so happy and said, "Thank you, Mittens! You are such a fine friend!" From that day on, Spot and Mittens played together every day and had lots of fun. The end.

Once there was a turtle who loved to laugh. He travelled through a big garden which had many colourful flowers and big trees. One day, he met a bunny rabbit and they started talking.

Turtle: "Hi, I'm the turtle. What is your name?"

Bunny: "My name is Bunny. What do you like to do?"

Turtle: "I love to play and laugh. It's so much fun!"

Bunny: "That sounds really nice. Did you know that some animals value results? We like to think before we act and then try to do things well."

Turtle: "Yes, that makes sense. I don't always get the results I want, but it's still funny to try!"

The turtle and the bunny rabbit enjoyed playing together and had lots of fun. They valued each other's efforts and appreciated the results.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a teddy bear named Teddy. One day, Lily was playing with Teddy when she saw a spider on the wall. She was scared and didn't know what to do.
