Her mom noticed that Lily was troubled and asked her what was wrong. Lily explained that there was a spider on the wall and she was scared of it. Her mom told her not to worry and that she had the power to make the spider go away.

Lily didn't understand how she had the power, so her mom explained that she could ask her dad to come and take the spider outside. Lily was happy and thanked her mom for explaining how to make the spider go away. From that day on, Lily knew that she had the power to ask for help when she was troubled.

Cookie wanted to stretch, so she got up from her bed. She looked around the room, and saw her watch on the dresser. She went over and grabbed it, then went back to her bed.

She put on the watch and then stretched out her arms and legs. She felt so much better! Suddenly, she heard a loud noise outside. It made her feel scared.

Cookie didn't know what the noise was, so she ran and hid under her bed. She pulled the blanket over her head and looked at her watch. It ticked, ticked, ticked, but the noise outside kept going.

Eventually, the noise stopped, but Cookie stayed under her bed for a few more minutes. When she was sure it was safe, she slowly peeked out from under the blanket.

She looked around the room, then put on her watch and went back to stretching. All was quiet, and she felt much better.

Once upon a time, a little girl named Lucy went for a walk in the park. She saw a bike with a red pedal. She wanted to try it, so she put her small foot on the pedal and started to ride. The path was rough, but Lucy was brave and kept going.

As she rode her bike, she met a boy named Tim. Tim said, "Hi, I like your bike! Can I try it?" Lucy said, "Yes, but be careful. The path is rough." Tim got on the bike and started to ride. He felt the rough path but kept going, just like Lucy.

Together, Lucy and Tim rode their bike on the rough path. They went fast and slow, up and down. Then, they discovered a beautiful flower garden. They stopped and looked at the pretty flowers. They smiled and said, "We found a nice place!" They played in the garden and had fun.

Once there was a little girl called Sarah who was adorable. She loved to play in her garden and have fun with her family and friends. One day, she went to the park with her mum. As they sat by the drain, Sarah started to weep.

Mum: "What's wrong Sarah? Why are you crying?"

Sarah: "I don't know."

Mum: "It's okay, don't worry. Why don't we get some ice cream? That will make you feel better!"

Sarah smiled as they walked to get some ice cream. She was so happy that she was not crying anymore. Later, she went back to the park with her mum to play. She was having so much fun that she completely forgot why she was crying at the drain.

Sarah's mum was so proud of her daughter and know that even when she was feeling sad Sarah could find a way to make it better. And that was how adorable Sarah overcame a bad day.

Once, there was a puppy called Bob. He loved to run and play in the park, but sometimes he needed to rest. One day, Bob was playing near a pond and he found a stick. He was so excited to play with it! But then, he heard a rude voice.

It belonged to a big dog. He growled at Bob and said he was not allowed to touch the stick. Bob was scared. He had never seen the big dog before and he didn't know what to do.

Bob wanted to take the stick, but he did not want to be rude. So he tried to think of a way to get the stick without making the big dog angry.

He decided to run away and have a rest. When he came back he saw the stick was still there. So he grabbed it quickly and ran away again.

The big dog was confused and thought Bob was the rudest pup he had ever met! But Bob was just clever and he made sure he got to keep the stick.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, Lily went to the park with her mom. She saw a big swing and asked her mom if she could play on it. Her mom said yes, so Lily ran over to the swing and started swinging back and forth.

Suddenly, Lily heard a loud noise and looked up. She saw a big bird flying towards her, and it looked very angry. Lily got scared and jumped off the swing. She ran over to her mom and told her what happened.

Her mom hugged her and said it was okay. They decided to go for a walk and explore the park. They walked up to a cliff and looked out at the beautiful view. Lily forgot all about the angry bird and was happy again.

John wanted to behave, but he couldn't. He wanted a banana, but he could not get it. His parent said he had to wait, but he did not know what waiting was. He got angry and shouted and yelled. He was not calm. John's parent got angry too, and said he needed to go to his room. He was sent away, and he was all alone. He was very sad and did not know what to do. He tried to be calm, but it was not working. He wanted to have a banana and be happy. But he did not get the banana, and he was still very angry. He was not allowed to act this way and the banana was not for him. It was a bad ending for John.

Once there was a little girl who wanted to make her mommy very happy. So she went to the kitchen and found a big box of coloured pencils and paper. She wanted to make something special.

The girl drew a big smile on the paper and coloured it in, making sure that all the colours were bright and colourful. Then she made messy scribbles in the background and added lots of different shapes and sizes.

When she was done, the little girl proudly took her masterpiece to her mommy and said, "Look Mommy, I made this special picture just for you!"

Mommy smiled and said, "What a beautiful picture! You made it all by yourself. I love it!" She gave her daughter a big hug.

The little girl was so happy to make her mommy smile that she danced around the kitchen. When she was done, the kitchen was a big, messy mess. But it was the best kind of mess the little girl ever made.

Anna and Ben are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they find a big bag of money under a tree. They are very happy.

"Wow, look at all this money!" Anna says. "We can buy many toys and candy!"

"Yes, we can!" Ben says. "But we have to be careful. Maybe someone is looking for this money."

They look around. They do not see anyone. They decide to take the money and run to the store.

But on the way, they meet a man. He is angry. He has a gun. He says, "Stop! That is my money! Give it back or I will shoot you!"

Anna and Ben are scared. They do not want to get hurt. They do not know what to do.

Then, Anna has an idea. She says, "Ben, throw the money at him!"

Ben nods. He throws the money at the man. The money flies in the air. The man is surprised. He drops his gun. He tries to catch the money.

Anna and Ben use this chance. They run away. They find a police officer. They tell him what happened. The police officer says, "You did the right thing. That man is a robber. He stole the money from a bank. You are very brave and smart."

Anna and Ben are happy. They are safe. They do not need the money. They have each other. They hug and smile.

Anna and Ben wanted to bake a cake for their mom. They found a big bowl, some eggs, some flour, some sugar, and some milk. They also saw a bottle of green stuff on the counter. They did not know what it was, but it looked yummy.

"Let's put some of this in the cake," Ben said, and poured some of the green stuff into the bowl.

"Are you sure?" Anna asked. "Maybe it is not for cakes."

"Don't be silly," Ben said. "It will make the cake taste good."

They mixed everything together and put it in a pan. Then they put the pan in the oven and waited.

Soon, the cake was done. It smelled funny, but they did not care. They took it out of the oven and put it on a plate. They were very proud of their cake.

"Mom will love it," Anna said.

They ran to find their mom and showed her the cake. Mom looked at the cake and smiled.

"Wow, you made a cake for me?" she said. "That is very sweet of you. What did you put in it?"

"We put eggs, flour, sugar, milk, and some green stuff," Ben said.

"Green stuff?" Mom asked. "What green stuff?"

Ben pointed to the bottle on the counter. Mom looked at the bottle and gasped.

"That is not green stuff, that is vinegar!" she said. "You put vinegar in the cake?"

Anna and Ben looked at each other. They did not know what vinegar was, but they guessed it was not good.

"Oops," they said.

Mom hugged them and said, "It's okay, you did not know. But next time, ask me before you use something you don't know. Vinegar is for salads, not for cakes. It makes cakes sour and yucky."

Anna and Ben felt foolish. They said they were sorry and asked Mom to help them bake a new cake. Mom agreed and said she loved them anyway. They threw away the vinegar cake and baked a new one with chocolate and sprinkles. It was delicious and Mom was happy.

Once there was a little girl named Mira. She was very excited because a festival was coming soon. Mira asked her dad, "Can we go?"

Dad smiled and said, "Yes, lets go to the festival together."

Mira was so happy she jumped up and hugged her dad. When they arrived at the festival, Mira saw so many people gathering to celebrate. She saw lots of little things like food, balloons, and toys. She ran around with excitement.

But then she saw a little old man all alone. He was sitting on a bench and looked very sad. Mira asked, "Why don't you join us? Come join our fun!"

The old man smiled and said, "Thank you, but I'm all alone. I don't have anyone to celebrate with."

Mira thought for a moment and then said, "We can be your friends. Come have fun with us."

The old man was so happy he hugged Mira. Together, they all celebrated the festival.

The moral of the story is that it doesn't matter who you are or where you come from. Everyone should be included in celebrations and given the opportunity to have fun.

Once, there was a little girl who loved to play the flute. She would put on her pretty dress and run to the park, her favorite spot to perform.

One day, she was playing her flute, when she heard a strange noise. She saw a pale cat stuck in a bush. She quickly put down her flute and ran to rescue the cat.

The girl stuck her arm in the bush, and the cat jumped out, into her arms. She said to the cat, "Are you ok?" The cat purred and rubbed against her neck.

The little girl was so happy to have rescued the cat. She hugged the cat and thanked it for joining her for a flute performance in the park. The cat meowed and seemed to understand. From then on, the little girl was never alone when she went to play her flute in the park.

Once upon a time, there was a little dog named Spot. Spot loved to play outside in the sunshine. One day, while Spot was playing, he saw a butterfly. The butterfly had pretty colors and Spot thought it was interesting.

Spot followed the butterfly and found a big box. The box had a label on it that said "Fragile." Spot didn't know what that meant, but he could see that the box was shaking and starting to tremble.

Suddenly, the box opened and out popped a little kitten! The kitten was scared and shivering, but Spot knew just what to do. He cuddled up next to the kitten and made her feel safe. From that day on, Spot and the kitten were best friends and they played together in the sunshine every day. The end.

One day, Jim went on an adventure. He was looking for something special. He put on his hat and grabbed his coat. He was ready to go.

Jim walked and walked. He passed lots of trees and houses. Then, he discovered something special. It was a big, blue jug. Jim was very excited! He touched the jug and shook it. It was very noisy.

Jim looked inside the jug. He saw some fun toys and candy. He wanted to take the jug with him. So, he dragged it home. When he got there, he showed his friends the jug. They played with the toys and ate the candy.

It was the best adventure for Jim. He discovered something special and he had lots of fun.

Jim was a three year old boy with a big backyard. He liked to spend hours playing in the yard. Every morning, Jim would jump out of bed, eager to get to the yard.

Today he decided to do something special. He stood at the entrance of the yard and looked around. It seemed very interesting. He saw some colorful flowers, tall grass and some big trees. He couldn't wait to explore it all.

He ran around and saw so many things. He especially loved the pond and the swings. Jim stood in the middle of the yard admiring it all. It was the most interesting place he had ever seen.

Jim spent many days exploring his backyard. He loved the adventures he discovered and the stories he made up. He often stood in the yard and admired its beauty. Jim's backyard was his favorite place.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to eat spaghetti with a fork. One day, she went to a restaurant with her mommy and daddy.

When the waiter came to their table, Lily said, "Hi, Mr. Waiter. Can I please have a fork?" The waiter smiled and gave her a fork. Lily was happy and said, "Thank you, Mr. Waiter. You are very polite."

But when Lily started eating her spaghetti, she noticed it didn't taste good. She made a frown and said, "Mommy, this spaghetti doesn't taste good." Her mommy told the waiter and he brought her a new plate of spaghetti. This time, it tasted delicious!

Lily smiled and said, "Yummy! Thank you, Mr. Waiter, for bringing me a new plate of spaghetti. You are very polite." The waiter smiled and said, "You're welcome, Lily. I'm glad you like it." And Lily ate her spaghetti happily ever after.

Heidi was a young girl who loved to play and explore. She wanted to know why her mommy would kneel in the bathroom every day. So one day, when her mommy was in the bathroom, Heidi decided to kneel too!

At first, Heidi felt silly and foolish. But then she noticed that her mommy smiled and looked happy. Heidi was so glad to make her mommy happy.

Heidi spent more and more time kneeling in the bathroom with her mommy. She would sing her favorite silly songs and ask her mommy questions.

Heidi and her mommy spent many precious moments together. Now whenever Heidi sees someone kneeling, she smiles and remembers the wonderful time when they were together.

Once there were two friends, Sarah and Tony. They both wanted a shelter. So they worked together to build one.

Tony and Sarah gathered wood and nails. They used a hammer to build the walls and a saw to make the roof. Sarah cut the roof panels and Tony nailed them together.

When the walls and roof were ready, Sarah used a paintbrush to paint the outside. Tony helped her. They painted it green and blue.

Finally, the shelter was ready! Tony and Sarah were so proud of their shelter that they hugged each other. They were so happy to have a shelter of their own. They went inside, happy and ready to stay inside their shelter.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Anna. She was three years old and she loved to explore her garden. One day, Anna was playing in the garden when she saw something fancy. It was a big lizard! Anna was so excited and she wanted to get closer. She took one step forward and the lizard started to stare. Anna was a bit scared, but she took another step forward. The lizard suddenly jumped away! Anna was sad because she wanted to explore the lizard.

Anna decided to go back home and get her dad. When her dad saw the lizard, he said: "Let's see if we can catch it!" Anna was very excited, so she started to follow it. She followed the lizard until they arrived at a lake.

Anna's dad started to stretch out his net, but then something unexpected happened. A big bird came flying out of the bushes! He was so fast that he scooped up the lizard and flew away. Anna felt very sad because she was not able to explore the fancy lizard. She started to cry and she vowed never to go exploring again.

Once upon a time, there was a smelly goat. He had a big horn on his head. The goat lived in a little house near a big tree.

One day, the goat went to find some food. He saw a big, round fruit on the ground. The goat wanted to eat it. He tried to squeeze the fruit with his horn, but it was too hard.

The goat tried again and again. At last, the fruit burst open. The goat was happy. He ate the fruit and went back to his little house. The goat was not smelly anymore. He was a happy goat with a big horn.

Tom and Ann like to play with their toys. They have many toys, but their favorite is a big red car. The car can make noises and move by itself. Tom and Ann like to pretend they are driving the car to different places.

One day, their mom says they have to go to the store with her. She says they need to buy some food for dinner. She says they can bring one toy each. Tom and Ann both want to bring the car, but they cannot share it. They start to fight over the car. They pull and push and yell.

Their mom is angry. She says they are being naughty and selfish. She says they cannot bring any toys. She takes the car away from them and puts it on the shelf. She says they have to go to the store now. Tom and Ann are sad and mad. They do not want to go to the store. They want to play with the car.

At the store, their mom buys some things. She buys bread and cheese and milk and eggs. She also buys some potatoes. She says potatoes are good for them. She says they are not expensive. She puts the potatoes in a big bag.

Tom and Ann are bored. They do not like the store. They do not like potatoes. They want to go home and play with the car. They have an idea. They think they can prevent their mom from buying potatoes. They think they can make the potatoes go away.

They wait until their mom is not looking. They sneak to the bag of potatoes. They take the potatoes out of the bag. They throw the potatoes on the floor. They kick the potatoes. They smash the potatoes. They make a big mess.

Their mom sees what they are doing. She is very angry. She says they are being naughty and wasteful. She says they have to pay for the potatoes. She says the potatoes are expensive now. She says they have to use their money to pay for the potatoes. She says they have no money left to buy toys. She says they have to go home now. She says they have to go to bed early. She says they cannot play with the car for a long time.

Tom and Ann are sad and mad. They do not want to pay for the potatoes. They do not want to go home. They do not want to go to bed. They want to play with the car. But they cannot. They have no choice. They have to do what their mom says. They have to learn their lesson. They have a bad ending.

Lily and Ben were playing with their board. It had many colors and shapes that they could stick on it. They liked to make pictures and stories with the board.

"Look, I made a house with a red roof and a yellow door," Lily said, showing Ben her board.

"That is impressive, Lily. I made a car with four wheels and a blue window," Ben said, showing Lily his board.

They were having fun, but then they heard their mom calling them.

"Lily, Ben, it's time for lunch. Come to the kitchen, please," Mom said.

Lily and Ben ran to the kitchen, leaving their board on the floor. They forgot to put it away.

After lunch, they wanted to play with their board again. But they could not find it.

"Where is our board, Lily?" Ben asked.

"I don't know, Ben. Maybe we left it in the living room," Lily said.

They looked in the living room, but they did not see their board. They looked in their bedroom, but they did not see their board. They looked in the bathroom, but they did not see their board.

They were sad and confused. Where was their board?

Then they heard a noise from the backyard. They went outside and saw their dog, Max, chewing on their board. He had taken it from the floor and brought it to his favorite spot.

"Max, no! That is our board!" Lily and Ben shouted.

Max looked at them with his big brown eyes and wagged his tail. He did not understand why they were angry. He thought he had found a new toy.

Lily and Ben ran to Max and took their board from him. It was all wet and torn. Some of the colors and shapes were missing.

They were very upset. Their board was ruined.

"Bad dog, Max. You should not take our things," Lily said.

"Sorry, Lily, Ben. I did not know. I just wanted to play," Max said in his doggy way.

Lily and Ben sighed. They knew Max did not mean to be bad. He was just a curious and playful dog.

They hugged Max and forgave him. They decided to share their board with him. They could still make some pictures and stories with the remaining colors and shapes.

They learned to be more careful with their things and to put them away when they were done. They also learned to love and understand their dog, even when he made mistakes.

Once upon a time there was a little girl. She was three and her name was Anna. Every day, Anna would go to the kitchen and open the drawer. Inside the drawer she found lots of fun things to play with.

One day, Anna opened the drawer and inside she saw a gloomy bug. She was scared and tried to pinch it. But when she did, the bug flew away! Anna felt sad and closed the drawer.

But then, something magical happened! The drawer opened on its own and the gloomy bug came back, but this time with some friends. They flew around Anna, laughing and playing. Anna was so happy!

From then on, Anna always kept the drawer open so her new friends could come and go whenever they wanted. And the kitchen was never gloomy anymore.

Once upon a time, there was a little rabbit named Benny. Benny loved to wander around the forest, looking for tasty carrots to nibble on. One day, as he was wandering, he saw something incredible in the distance. It was a big, shiny rock that sparkled in the sunlight.

Benny was so excited to see the incredible rock that he hopped as fast as he could towards it. But as he got closer, he noticed something strange. There was a big, scary fox sleeping next to the rock! Benny knew he had to be careful, so he tiptoed closer and closer.

Suddenly, the fox woke up and started chasing Benny! Benny ran as fast as he could, but he knew he couldn't outrun the fox for long. Just when he thought he was done for, he remembered something. He had seen a big hole earlier that day, and he knew he could hide in it. So he ran towards the hole and jumped inside, safe and sound. From that day on, Benny learned to be more careful when he wandered around the forest.

Piggy was a proud duck. Every day, she would stand tall and look around the farm. One day, something dropped on the floor near Piggy's pond. She was curious, so she moved closer to get a better look.

When she arrived, she saw a shiny red ball. It must have dropped from the sky! Proudly, Piggy picked up the ball and started to play with it. Around and around she went, kicking it and giggling.

Suddenly, the ball got away from Piggy and raced across the farm. Piggy tried to chase it, but she just couldn't catch up! The ball flew off the farm and dropped on the floor far away.

Piggy was sad. She missed her shiny red ball. She looked around, but it was gone. She sadly went back to her pond and waited.

But then something wonderful happened. The shiny red ball came flying back and dropped on the floor in front of Piggy. She was so happy! Piggy held the ball tightly and smiled proudly.

Once upon a time, there was a young boy named Jack. He was only three years old, but he was very brave. One day, Jack was walking through a park and he saw an elderly woman. The woman was holding a toy in her hands. Jack wanted the toy, so he ran over to the woman and grabbed it. The elderly woman screamed.

Jack was so scared he dropped the toy and started to run away. He ran so fast that he could hardly breathe. Suddenly, Jack heard the woman screaming again. He stopped and looked back. The elderly woman was not angry. She was laughing!

Turns out, the toy the woman had was a funny noise maker. When Jack grabbed it, the noise maker had made the screaming noise. Jack laughed too. He took the toy back to the woman with a big smile on his face. The elderly woman thanked him and gave him a hug.

Jack was so happy he could hardly contain himself. The toy had made him laugh and the woman had been so kind. From that day on, Jack always looked forward to taking a walk in the park!

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. He had a toy hammer that he loved to play with. One day, he accidentally struck his little sister's toy and it broke. His sister cried and Timmy felt very bad.

The next day, Timmy's mom had to go to the hospital for an operation. Timmy didn't understand what that meant, but he knew it was important. He wanted to help his mom feel better, so he drew her a picture of a happy sun and gave it to her.

When they got home, Timmy's dad was trying to fix a lamp but he couldn't figure it out. Timmy thought it was stupid that his dad couldn't fix it, so he grabbed his toy hammer and tried to help. He ended up accidentally striking the lamp and it broke. Timmy's dad wasn't mad though, he just laughed and hugged Timmy.

Sara and Ben are twins. They like to play with their toys. But sometimes they fight over them. One day, Sara wants to play with the orange car. But Ben has it. He says it is his turn. Sara gets angry. She grabs the car from Ben. Ben cries. He hits Sara. Sara cries too.

Mom hears them. She comes to their room. She sees the car on the floor and the twins crying. She is not happy. She says, "Sara, Ben, why are you fighting? You have to share your toys. And you have to be kind to each other. You are brother and sister. You have to love each other." She hugs them both. She says, "Now, say sorry to each other. And forgive each other. Can you do that?"

Sara and Ben look at each other. They feel sorry. They say, "Sorry, Sara. Sorry, Ben." They hug each other. They say, "I forgive you, Sara. I forgive you, Ben." They smile. They feel better.

Mom smiles too. She says, "That's good. I'm proud of you. Now, let's go to the kitchen. Dinner is ready. We have chicken and rice and carrots. And for dessert, we have orange cake. Do you like orange cake?"

Sara and Ben nod. They love orange cake. They say, "Yes, Mom. We like orange cake. Thank you, Mom." They hold Mom's hand. They go to the kitchen. They have a nice dinner. They share the orange cake. They are happy. They are a family.

Once there was a loyal dog who loved his master very much. Every night before bed, the dog would curl up in a warm sheet and wait for his master to come and snuggle him.

One night, the master did not come. Instead, a robber came and tried to steal the sheets. He demanded that the dog give up the sheets. But the dog insisted that he would not give up the sheets.

The robber became angry. He decided to punish the dog with violence. He kicked and hit the dog until it was too injured to move. After the robber left, the master arrived to find his loyal pup in pain. Even though he tried very hard, the master was unable to save his pup from the injuries and the pup died soon after.

The master was very sad to lose his loyal pup. He was even more angry about the robber who had caused so much pain and heartache. From that day onward, the master promised himself to always be loyal to his friends and family, just as his pup had been loyal to him.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved tea parties with his friends. One day, Timmy's mommy made him a special tea party. She hid some cookies for Timmy and his friends to find. Timmy's friends looked everywhere, but they couldn't find the cookies. Timmy knew where they were hidden, but he didn't tell his friends.

Timmy's friends were sad they couldn't find the cookies. Timmy felt bad for not telling them where they were hidden. He knew it wasn't nice to keep the cookies a secret. So, Timmy said sorry to his friends and thanked them for coming to his tea party. He also showed them where the cookies were hidden. Timmy learned that it's always better to share and be kind to others.

Once there was a little girl named Daisy who was very lonely. One day, Daisy was playing in her garden when suddenly she started to tremble.

She looked around, but she couldn't see anything that would make her afraid. But then she noticed something sparkling on the ground. It was a beautiful bracelet! She was so excited; she picked it up and put it on her wrist.

But then, to Daisy's surprise, the bracelet started to tremble. At first, Daisy was scared. But then she realised that the bracelet was shaking because it was lonely and wanted a friend too.

So Daisy held the bracelet and both of them stopped trembling. Daisy was so happy, she had a friend! From then on, Daisy and her bracelet were the best of friends, and neither of them ever felt lonely again.

Tom and Lily wanted to buy a flashlight. They liked to play with flashlights in the dark. They had some money from their piggy bank. They asked their mom if they could go to the store.

Mom said yes, but they had to be careful and come back soon. She gave them a big hug and a kiss. Tom and Lily put on their coats and shoes. They took their money and walked to the store.

At the store, they saw many flashlights. Some were big, some were small, some were red, some were blue. They looked at all of them. They liked a small yellow flashlight. It was shiny and bright. They asked the store lady how much it was.

The store lady said it was five dollars. Tom and Lily counted their money. They had four dollars and fifty cents. They were sad. They did not have enough money.

Then they saw a naughty boy. He was sneaking behind the store lady. He grabbed a big green flashlight and ran away. He did not pay for it. He was stealing.

Tom and Lily saw what he did. They were shocked. They knew stealing was very bad. They decided to tell the store lady.

They ran to the store lady and said, "Excuse us, miss. We saw a naughty boy. He took a flashlight and ran away. He did not give you any money. He was stealing."

The store lady was surprised and angry. She thanked Tom and Lily for telling her. She said they were very good and honest. She said she would call the police and find the naughty boy.

Then she said, "You know what? You can have the yellow flashlight for free. You deserve it. You are very brave and kind."

Tom and Lily were very happy. They thanked the store lady and hugged her. They took the yellow flashlight and ran back home. They showed their mom their new flashlight. They told her what happened at the store.

Mom was very proud of them. She said they did the right thing. She said they could play with the flashlight in the dark. She said she loved them very much. Tom and Lily smiled and hugged her. They said they loved her too. They turned on the flashlight and had fun.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a sister named Lucy. One day, Lily was playing with her toys and her sister was reading a book. Suddenly, the phone rang and it scared Lily. She felt upset and started to cry.

Lucy saw her sister crying and went to her. She hugged her and asked what was wrong. Lily told her that the phone ringing scared her. Lucy explained that it was just the phone and it wasn't anything to be scared of.

Lily felt better and stopped crying. She hugged her sister and thanked her for making her feel better. From that day on, whenever the phone rang, Lily wasn't scared anymore because she knew it was just the phone and nothing to be upset about.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who was very clever. She wanted to try new things, but unfortunately, her mom didn't always permit it.

One day, her mom decided to permit her to get a start on exploring the world. She was so excited! She put on her shoes and ran outside.

The little girl wanted to explore her neighborhood, but it was a very big place. She was a bit scared, so she looked for ways to stay safe.

She soon had a clever plan - she would find a buddy. She got permission from her mom to find a friend and they went all around the neighborhood, playing and learning together!

They explored every nook and cranny. The little girl gained so much knowledge and confidence that day. She even came up with new ideas on how to explore the world.

The little girl's mom was happy and proud of her and she always let the little girl go out and explore with her buddy.

The End.

Once upon a time there was a mighty reef. It was full of amazing animals and plants. Three year old Amy was on a boat with her parents, sailing over the reef. Suddenly, Amy started to feel something special. She recognized that the reef was really special and would stay in her heart forever. As her parents looked at her with love, Amy smiled and said, "I recognize this reef. It's so mighty!" Amy and her parents were happy to recognize the beautiful reef, and Amy vowed to always remember how special it was.

Once upon a time, there was a prince. He lived in a big castle with his mommy and daddy. The prince had lots of toys, which include a big red ball and a soft teddy bear.

One day, the prince found a little bird outside. The bird was harmless and looked very sad. The prince picked up the bird and brought it inside the castle. He gave the bird some water and some seeds to eat.

The prince loved having the bird as his new friend. He played with it every day and even let it sleep in his bed. The bird was very happy and the prince was happy too. They had lots of fun together and the prince knew that he had made a new friend for life.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to drink coffee with her mommy in the morning. One day, Lily spilled her coffee all over the clean kitchen floor. She was sad because she made a mess.

Her mommy said, "Don't worry, Lily. We can clean it up together." They got a towel and started to clean the floor. Lily saw a little ant crawling on the floor and said, "Mommy, can the ant join us?"

Her mommy said, "Sure, Lily. The ant can join us." So, they cleaned the floor with the ant and finished their coffee together. From that day on, Lily always made sure to hold her coffee cup carefully.

Once there was a bald man named Bob. Bob had no hair on his head. He was sad because people would laugh at him. One day, he went to the park and saw a little boy crying. The boy had a big bag of candy but he could not open it.

Bob walked to the boy and asked, "Why are you crying?" The boy said, "I can't open my candy bag." Bob helped the boy open the candy bag. The boy was very happy. He said, "Thank you, Bob!" Then, the boy gave Bob a piece of candy.

Bob felt happy too. He learned that when you help others, they will be kind to you. The people at the park saw Bob's kindness and stopped laughing at him. They all became friends. The moral of the story is to always be kind and help others.

Once upon a time, there were two friends - Tim and Jill. They liked to wander around in the same forest every day. One day, when the two of them were walking, they noticed a big chest in the middle of the forest.

"Let's open it," suggested Tim excitedly.

Jill shook her head and told him, "Let's not, Tim. It might be someone else's chest, and it wouldn't be nice to open it without permission."

But Tim insisted and started to open it.

In the chest, the two friends found a lot of money.

Tim said excitedly, "Let's take the money. It's going to help us a lot!"

But Jill said sadly, "No, let's not. We have no right to take their money. It's not ours."

In the end, Tim realised Jill was right and the two friends put back the money. The moral of this story is that it is never right to be selfish. We must always act with kindness and respect towards others.

Once upon a time, there was a wet frog named Bob. Bob loved to jump and play in the rain. He liked the rhythm of the raindrops falling on the leaves. It made him very happy.

One day, Bob met a new friend named Sally. Sally was a wet cat who also liked the rain. They decided to play a game together. They took turns counting the number of raindrops that fell on their heads.

Bob counted one, two, three raindrops on his head. Sally counted one, two, three, four raindrops on her head. They laughed and danced in the rain, enjoying the wet fun and the rhythm of the raindrops.

As the rain stopped, Bob and Sally said goodbye. They promised to play together again the next time it rained. Bob hopped away, and Sally ran home, both happy to have made a new friend who loved the wet rain and the rhythm of the raindrops just like they did.

Once upon a time, there was a happy chubby bunny named Bubbles. Bubbles loved to hop around the meadow and eat carrots all day long. One day, Bubbles met a sad little bird named Tweetie. Tweetie had lost her nest and didn't know where to go. Bubbles felt sad for Tweetie and wanted to help.

Bubbles had an idea! She thought if they worked together, they could improve Tweetie's situation. Bubbles and Tweetie started to build a new nest together. They found some twigs and some soft grass to make the nest cozy. While they worked, Bubbles made sure to smile and encourage Tweetie.

After a while, the nest was finished and Tweetie was so happy! She thanked Bubbles for helping her and they became friends. Bubbles was happy too, knowing that she had helped someone in need. From that day on, Bubbles and Tweetie played together in the meadow and Bubbles always had a big smile on her face.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a doll that she loved very much. One day, Lily's little brother came into her room and accidentally destroyed her doll. Lily was very sad and cried a lot.

Her mom came into the room and asked her why she was crying. Lily told her that her brother destroyed her doll. Her mom hugged her and said, "I know you loved your doll, but don't worry, we can get you a new one."

Lily was very excited to hear that she could get a new doll. She stopped crying and smiled. Her mom took her to the store and they picked out a new doll together. Lily was so happy and hugged her new doll tightly. She promised to take good care of her so that she wouldn't get destroyed like her old one.

Once upon a time, there was a little bird named Tim. Tim loved to fly and soar high in the sky. He had many bird friends, but he was very competitive. Tim always wanted to be the best at flying.

One day, Tim heard about a big race. The winner would get a shiny trophy. Tim wanted that trophy very much. He practiced flying every day to get ready for the race. His friends cheered for him and said, "Go, Tim, go!"

The day of the race came, and all the birds lined up to start. The race began, and Tim soared high and fast. He flew faster than all the other birds. At the end of the race, Tim won! His friends were so happy for him. They said, "You did it, Tim! You won the trophy!"

Tim felt proud but also learned that being the best was not the most important thing. Having fun and being with friends was what truly mattered. From that day on, Tim shared his trophy with his friends and enjoyed flying together, high in the sky.

Mama and Michael were in the kitchen. Mama was cooking on the stove and Michael was watching. "What are you making, Mama?" asked Michael. Mama smiled. "I'm making a delicate soup," she said. "It's for supper." "Can I help?" asked Michael. Mama said, "Yes, you can help." She showed him how to stir the soup on the stove. Michael was careful to be gentle and gentle. He stirred with a wooden spoon.

Mama smiled. "You know how to be delicate," she said. "Yes," said Michael. "I know how to be delicate with the stove." He kept stirring. After a little while, Mama said, "That's enough. Let's eat!" They ate the soup together. It was delicious! Michael was happy that he had helped make it.

Once upon a time there were two sisters. The sisters wanted an ice cream but couldn't decide which one to get.

The first sister wanted to choose a luxury ice cream that she had never had before. She said she wanted to pick something special.

The second sister wanted to choose a cheap ice cream that she knew she loved. She said it was her favourite.

The sisters decided to share the ice cream. They chose the cheap ice cream that the second sister wanted and took the luxury ice cream home to share with their parents.

They loved their ice cream and were very happy with the choice they made.

Lily was walking in the park when she saw something huge. It was an avocado! She had never seen something so big before in her life. She couldn't believe it.

Excitedly, she ran to it and said, "Hello! What are you doing here?"

The avocado answered, "I'm here to meet you, Lily! I've come all the way from far away to say hello."

Lily smiled. "That's so nice of you! What do you like to do?"

The avocado replied, "I love to play in the sun, and I love to eat fruits and veggies. I'm so happy to meet you."

Lily laughed and said, "It's so nice to meet you, avocado! Maybe we can play together tomorrow."

The avocado smiled and said, "I'd love to! See you soon."

And then the avocado went off to enjoy the rest of his day in the park, and Lily went home, excited to meet her new friend.

Once upon a time, there was a smart cat named Kiki. Kiki loved to teach her friends how to do new things. One day, Kiki saw her friend, a little bird named Toto, trying to fly. Toto was sad because he could not fly like the other birds.

Kiki went to Toto and said, "I will teach you how to fly." Toto was very happy. Kiki told Toto to push his wings up and down, up and down. Toto did what Kiki said and soon, he started to fly a little bit.

Every day, Kiki would teach Toto how to push his wings better. Toto became very good at flying. All the other birds were happy for Toto. Toto thanked Kiki for being a good friend and a smart teacher. They played and flew together all day long.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to draw and color with her pen. But one day, her pen became very dull and didn't work well anymore. Lily was sad and didn't know what to do.

She went to her mom and asked for a new pen, but her mom said they didn't have any. Lily suffered because she couldn't draw or color anymore.

Days passed and Lily tried to sharpen her pen with a knife, but it didn't work. One day, she accidentally cut herself with the knife and got hurt. Her mom took her to the hospital, but it was too late. Lily had lost too much blood and passed away.

Her mom was very sad and regretted not buying her a new pen. She learned that sometimes, even small things like a dull pen can have a big impact on someone's life.

Once upon a time there was a mysterious veil. It was special because it had a lock on it. Every day the little girl wanted to open it and see what was inside. She asked her mom if she could unlock it, but her mom said no.

One night when everybody was asleep, the little girl tiptoed to the veil and tried to open it. But, the lock was too hard for her to open. She couldn't figure it out. Finally, she gave up and went back to bed.

The next day, the little girl's mom said that she finally knew how to open the mysterious veil. She got a key, put it in the lock, and the veil opened up. When the little girl looked inside, she saw a beautiful surprise!

The little girl was very happy that she could finally open the mysterious veil and see the surprise her mom had been hiding. She hugged her mom tight and thanked her for unlocking it. From that day forward, the little girl knew that fun surprises can come with a little bit of mystery.

Once upon a time, there was a man who loved to play hide and seek. One day, he was hiding behind a tree when he saw a little girl walking by. The man was feeling healthy and happy, so he decided to say hello.

"Hi there, little girl! Do you want to play hide and seek with me?" the man asked.

The little girl was excited and said, "Yes, please! I love to play hide and seek!"

So the man and the little girl played hide and seek together. They had so much fun hiding and finding each other. The man felt even more healthy and happy because he made a new friend.

Once upon a time, there was a person who had a very important meeting. They wanted to be sure to be on time, so they followed their schedule very exactly. They made sure to have a nap in the morning before the meeting and went to bed early.

On the day of the meeting, the person woke up feeling tired. They remembered the meeting and tried to stay awake, but they were so tired that they soon fell back to sleep. The next thing they knew, the clock was ticking away and it was almost time for the meeting.

The person quickly got ready and tried to rush to the meeting, but they had slept too long and they were still late. As they hurried, they felt very impatient and wished they hadn't taken a nap. When they arrived at the meeting, everyone was already there and all eyes were on them.

The person apologized and explained why they were late, and soon the meeting began. From then on, the person was extra careful to avoid taking a nap before any important meetings.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy had a toy car that he loved to play with. One day, Timmy's car got stuck under the couch and he couldn't reach it. Timmy's mom tried to get the car out, but it was too far away.

"I don't know what to do," said Timmy's mom.

Timmy shrugged his shoulders and said, "I'm lonely without my car."

Suddenly, Timmy's mom had an idea. She took a magnet and used it to pull the car out from under the couch. Timmy was so happy to have his car back and he gave his mom a big hug. From that day on, Timmy always kept his magnet nearby, just in case his car got stuck again.

Once upon a time, there was a big ocean. It was so big, it went on and on. In the ocean, there was a little fish named Fin. Fin was a fine little fish who liked to swim and play with his friends.

One day, Fin and his friends found a big, shiny thing in the ocean. They did not know what it was, but they all wanted to take it home. Fin's best friend, Gilly, said, "Let's promise to take turns with the shiny thing." Fin and his friends all said, "We promise!"

So, Fin and his friends took turns with the shiny thing. They played with it and had lots of fun. The ocean was a happy place, and Fin and his friends were happy too. They kept their promise, and they all stayed best friends forever.

Once upon a time, there was a kind man who lived in the forest. He loved to give food to the animals, especially the deer. One day, he saw a baby deer who was lost and scared. The man knew he had to do something to help the deer feel safe.

He gently picked up the baby deer and carried it to his home. He gave the deer some food and water to drink. The baby deer felt safe and happy with the kind man.

From that day on, the man took care of the baby deer and they became best friends. They would play together in the forest and the man would always make sure the deer was safe. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the garden. One day, while she was playing, she noticed a fairy sitting on a flower. The fairy had unusual wings that sparkled in the sun.

Lily ran to her mommy and said, "Mommy, look! A fairy with pretty wings!" Her mommy smiled and said, "That's nice, Lily."

Lily went back to the garden to play, but she accidentally stepped on the fairy's flower. The fairy got angry and said, "You ruined my home! Now I will curse you!" Lily didn't know what a curse was, but she could tell it wasn't good.

The next day, Lily woke up with a rash all over her body. Her mommy took her to the doctor, but they couldn't find a cure. Lily felt very sad and wished she hadn't stepped on the fairy's flower.

Bap was walking out the door with his boots on and his coat zipped up. He was feeling impatient, wanting to go out and make a puddle. He stepped outside and realised it had recently rained. He saw all the puddles around him and smiled.

Bap knelt down alongside one of the puddles and watched as the raindrops made tiny circles on the surface of the water. He said out loud, "I can make a puddle too!" so he picked up a stick and made a big circle in the dirt next to the puddle.

Next, he went around collecting all of the small leaves and twigs he could find and made a tiny pile in the middle of his circle. He smiled and said "Now I just need some water!" Then he heard a voice calling to him.

It was his mother, standing in the doorway. "What are you doing, Bap?" she asked.

He smiled and said, "I'm making my own puddle! Just like the one over there."

His mother nodded and said, "Then let's get you some water so you can finish it." She filled up a bucket and Bap poured it into his tiny puddle, filling it up until it reached the edges of the circle.

He was so happy with his work that he jumped in, splashing around and making a big splash. His mother smiled and said

Once upon a time, there was a fox. The fox was a slow creature but it was very clever. Every night, when it went to sleep, it would attach a wink to its tail. Every morning when it would wake up, it could feel its tail twinkle and that made the fox happy.

One day, the fox wanted to use its tail to show its friends how clever it was. It started to attach larger and larger winks to the end of its tail. Pretty soon the tail was so big, that the fox could barely move.

But the fox didn’t care. As it wiggled through the forest, the winks on its tail caught the attention of all the animals. They stopped to look and admire the sparkles of the fox’s tail.

The fox was so happy! And even though it was very slow, it was proud of its tail and the wink it was able to attach.

Once upon a time there was a jolly little girl. She was only three years old and very excited for the day. She woke up early and ran outside to play in the sunshine.

"Where should I go?" she said to herself. She decided to head to the toyshop. When she got there, she saw lots of wonderful things. She saw dolls, bikes and games. She wanted to buy them all.

But then something else caught her eye, it was a plastic bottle full of medicine. She wanted it. She thought it would make her very strong.

"I want the medicine, please give it to me," she said to the shopkeeper.

But the shopkeeper did not listen. He struck her with his fist and kicked her out of the shop.

The poor little girl felt sad. She returned home without the medicine and cried until she fell asleep. Her dream of being strong was over. Thankfully, her parents found her and the nightmare ended.

Once upon a time there was a small boy who loved jam. His mum would make it for him every day. One day, he asked her if he could have some extra jam and she said “No”. The little boy was upset, so he quit and pouted all day.

When dinner time came, the little boy came to the dinner table, but he didn’t feel like eating. His mum asked him why and he told her he was mad because she wouldn’t give him extra jam.

His mum then took a deep breath and said in an understanding voice “People can be ignorant sometimes, but it’s important to not quit when something doesn’t go your way, even if it is really hard.”

The little boy thought about his mum’s words and he realised that she was right. He finished his dinner and was a bit happier.

His mum then brought out a big jar of his favourite jam, and said “This jam is for you, no matter what.” The little boy could not believe his eyes. He hugged his mum and thanked her for her wise words, and for the jam.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play dress-up and wear pretty clothes. One day, she saw her friend Emma wearing a dress that was very old. Lily didn't like it and told Emma she disagreed with her style. Emma felt sad and didn't understand why Lily didn't like her dress.

Lily realized she hurt her friend's feelings and decided to apologize. She told Emma that even though she didn't like the dress, it was still special because it was ancient and had a lot of history. Emma felt better and forgave Lily.

From that day on, Lily learned that everyone has their own style and it's okay to disagree, but it's important to be kind and understanding. And Emma taught Lily that even ancient things can be beautiful and special. They continued to play dress-up together and had lots of fun. The end.

Once there was a little girl named Ella who wanted to climb a tall tree in her backyard. Her mom said she could use a rope to help pull herself up. Ella was excited to try, so she grabbed the rope and started climbing. She was graceful and determined as she made her way higher and higher. But soon, it became too hard. Her arms were tired and she couldn't keep going.

Ella wanted to keep trying, but she started to get discouraged. She decided to quit. Then, something amazing happened. As she said goodbye to the tree, she felt a sudden burst of strength. She kept hold of the rope and pulled herself up even higher.

When Ella reached the top, she felt a sense of accomplishment and pride. She learned that had she just persevered a little bit longer, she could have made it to the top. Ella taught herself an important lesson that day: Never quit, even when things get hard!

Once upon a time there was a girl named Jenny. She was three years old and loved playing in her backyard. Every day she would play outside with her toys and have a great time.

One day, Jenny noticed something new in her backyard. It was a big pile of dirt. Jenny wasn't sure what it was or where it had come from. But it looked like something fun to play with.

So Jenny started to add some of the dirt to her toy cars and animals. She made towers, roads and even a big castle. It didn't take her long to make the dirt pile disappear.

But when Jenny was done playing, she noticed something strange. Her backyard was filthy! The dirt she had added had made a mess and spread everywhere. Jenny was sad and started to clean up her backyard.

It took her a long time but with some help from her mom, Jenny was able to get the backyard clean again. After everything was nice and tidy, Jenny made sure to be more careful when adding dirt in the future.

Once upon a time, there was a chubby panda named Benny. He loved to explore and often roamed around his neighborhood. On one of his adventures, Benny noticed a nearby cave. He wanted to go in and explore, so he decided to bravely step inside.

Once inside, Benny noticed a dark, mysterious chamber. As he walked closer and closer, the cave started to shake and tremble. Suddenly, the ceiling started to collapse and Benny had to run away as fast as he could!

Outside the cave, Benny was shaking and afraid. He was also sad because he couldn't explore the cave like he wanted to. As he was walking back home, Benny noticed something unusual. It was an old man walking towards him with a long, pointed stick. Benny felt scared and his heart started to beat faster.

Unfortunately, the old man turned out to be a hunter who was searching for a chubby panda like Benny. After a few minutes of chasing, Benny was captured and taken away. Sadly, Benny never returned home.

Once there was a group of brave children. They were playing together in the garden when they saw something interesting in the sky. It was a big, colorful bird.

The kids were all excited and jumped around, pointing at the bird. Suddenly, one brave little girl said, "Let's catch the bird!" and started running.

The others followed. But the bird was too fast. They ran and ran but the bird was too quick. Suddenly, the little girl stopped and said, "Let's throw something at it". She grabbed a big stick and threw it at the bird.

The group cheered when the stick hit the bird. The bird flew away and the kids were happy. Then the brave little girl said, "Let's do it again!" and everyone ran off to find more sticks.

The brave little girl led the group and soon they found some stones. She said, "Let's throw these stones and see what happens!" Everyone started throwing the stones. One of the stones hit the bird and the bird flew away again.

The group cheered again and the brave little girl clapped her hands together. She said, "That was fun and interesting!" The others agreed and then she said, "Let's do it again! I have an idea. Let's try to slap the bird!"

The group laughed and then ran after the bird. Everyone took turns trying to slap the bird, but none of them

Once upon a time, there was a small girl named Lily who loved to play outside. One day, she found a small rock on the ground. She picked it up and showed it to her friend, Timmy.

"Look at this small rock I found," said Lily.

Timmy looked at the rock and said, "It's so small! But it's still a rock."

Lily smiled and said, "Yes, it's a small rock, but it's still special to me."

They played with the small rock for a while, tossing it back and forth. Then, Lily's mom called for them to come inside.

Lily put the small rock in her pocket and said, "I'll keep this rock with me always."

And from that day on, Lily kept the small rock with her wherever she went.

Once upon a time, there lived a big, enormous elephant. Everywhere the elephant went, he would wink and make all of his friends laugh and smile. One day, the elephant noticed a big, shiny machine near his pond. He walked over to it and noticed it had a big button. He pushed the button and saw something very exciting. The machine had printed an enormous wink! He couldn't believe his eyes and started to laugh. The elephant showed the wink to all of his friends. They thought it was so funny and laughed along with the elephant. Everyone was so happy and enjoyed the enormous wink that was printed. The end!

Once upon a time there was a friendly beach. Every day a little girl went to the beach to play. She loved it! She built sandcastles and ran along the shore.

One day on her way to the beach, the little girl dropped her bucket and shovel. She was so sad! She didn't know how she would get back to the beach without them.

But then something wonderful happened. Two friendly seagulls offered to help her. The birds picked up her bucket and shovel and flew her to the beach.

The little girl thanked the seagulls and had a wonderful day at the beach playing with her bucket and shovel. She was very thankful for their help.

Once upon a time there was a little boy. His name was Tim and he was three years old.

One day Tim's mom said, "Tim, listen carefully. Don't eat anything until mommy and daddy come back, okay?"

Tim nodded in agreement but he was very curious. Finally he couldn't take it anymore and he reached for the forbidden food. He took one bite and swallowed it quickly.

When mom and dad came back, mom noticed the empty plate. She yelled at Tim, "Why didn't you listen? You were so stupid!"

Tim felt really bad and started to cry. Then he felt a strange feeling in his stomach. Very soon, he was throwing up all over the kitchen floor.

Mom and dad were very disappointed. They scolded Tim and sent him to bed. Tim learned his lesson but it was too late.

Moral of the Story: Listen to your parents or else you might be sorry!

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Sarah. She was very sad and her parents wanted to help her cheer up. They asked her why she was so sad and she had trouble explaining. Then her mom had an idea and said, "Let's do a puzzle!" Sarah was interested and they got the puzzle out.

While they were doing the puzzle pieces, Sarah noticed a funny powder all over the table. She asked her parents what it was and they explained to her that it was a special powder that helped solve puzzles! Sarah was so excited to find out that she could use powder to help solve the puzzle. She quickly grabbed the powder and sprinkled it all over the puzzle.

The powder worked like magic! The puzzle was solved in no time. Sarah was so happy that she had been able to solve the puzzle with the help of the powder. She was no longer sad.

Moral of the story: Problems can be solved with patience and creativity.

Once upon a time, there was a farmer. He had a big red barn where he kept all his animals. The barn was very important to him because it kept his animals safe and dry.

One day, the farmer decided to make some changes to the barn. He added some new windows and painted the doors blue. The animals were very curious and watched as the farmer worked.

When the farmer was finished, he called all the animals inside to show them the new changes. They were very happy and wagged their tails. The farmer was proud of his work and felt happy too. From that day on, the barn looked even more important to the farmer and his animals.

Alice was very excited. She was going to play a game and try to win a pin. She couldn't wait to see what kind of pin it was.

Alice lined up with the other children and it was time to start the game. She followed all of the rules and listened very carefully. When it was time to see who won, Alice couldn't believe it! She had won an amazing pin.

Alice jumped for joy. She had never seen a pin like this before. It was so special and sparkly. She couldn't wait to show it to her mom.

Alice put the pin carefully in her pocket and ran home to show her mom. Her mom was so proud of her and said she had done an amazing job.

Alice was so happy that she had won the pin. It was an amazing day and she will never forget it.

Once upon a time, there was a big tree with lots of leaves. A little bird lived in the tree and loved to sing all day. One day, the bird fell out of the tree and hurt its wing. The bird's mommy took it to the doctor who took an x-ray of the wing. The x-ray showed that the wing was broken.

The doctor put a bandage on the bird's wing and told it to rest. The little bird felt sad because it couldn't fly anymore. But the bird's mommy said that it was still rich because it had a loving family and lots of friends who cared about it. The bird felt better and knew that it would fly again one day.

Lily and Ben were bored. They wanted to play, but they had no toys. All their toys were old and broken. They were cheap toys that their mom got from the store.

"Let's make our own toys!" Lily said. She had an idea. She ran to the kitchen and got some paper cups and a spoon. Ben followed her.

"What are you doing?" Ben asked.

"Watch!" Lily said. She filled the cups with water from the tap. Then she banged the spoon on the cups. They made different sounds. "See? We have drums!"

Ben smiled. He liked the sounds. He got another spoon and joined Lily. They banged the cups and made music.

"Let's march!" Lily said. She picked up two cups and held them like a drum. Ben did the same. They marched around the house, banging their cups and singing. They felt happy.

Their mom heard the noise and came to see. She saw Lily and Ben marching with their cups. She smiled. She was proud of them. They were creative and fun.

"That's a nice march!" she said. "Can I join you?"

"Yes, mom!" Lily and Ben said. They gave her a cup and a spoon. They marched together, making music and laughing. They had a lot of fun. They did not need cheap toys. They had each other.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the garden with her hose. She would water the flowers and the grass every day. But one day, she couldn't find her hose. She looked everywhere but it was nowhere to be found. She started to feel nervous because she loved her hose and didn't want to lose it.

Lily's mom saw that she was upset and asked her what was wrong. Lily told her about her missing hose. Her mom promised to help her find it. They looked in the shed, under the bushes, and in the garage, but they couldn't find it. They had to delay their gardening until they found the hose.

Finally, after searching for a long time, they found the hose behind a big rock. Lily was so happy and relieved to have her hose back. She watered the flowers and the grass with a big smile on her face. From that day on, she made sure to put her hose away in a safe place so she wouldn't lose it again.

Once there was a squirrel. He was very fine. He decided to explore the big world around him. He ran into a forest with lots of trees. The squirrel climbed to the top of the tallest tree and he could see for miles and miles.

He stayed in the tree for a long time, looking at all the sights. He thought it was fun. But, after a while, he got very tired. So, he decided it was time to return home.

On the way, back he saw some of his friends. They were very excited to see him. One of them asked, "Where have you been?" The squirrel replied, "I've been exploring the world. It's very big and very exciting!"

The squirrel's friends were so happy to see him. They all returned home together. The squirrel was so happy he'd had such a fine adventure!

One day Sally was helping in the garden. She saw a beautiful radish growing. She was amazed and asked her dad, "What is that?"

Her dad smiled and said, "It's a radish, Sally! It's a root vegetable. We can eat it!"

Sally was curious and asked, "How does it grow?"

Her dad said, "We can study it together if you like."

So the two of them sat down in the garden and studied the radish. Sally was amazed at how humble the plant was. It grew slowly and steadily, never stopping or complaining.

After a while, her dad said, "I think we've studied enough for today. Let's take a break! Maybe we can cook up the radish for lunch."

And so they did.

Sally enjoyed her first radish and learned a valuable lesson: with hard work and humble study, anything is possible.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play outside in the park. One day, Timmy saw a big tree with lots of leaves on it. Timmy thought it would be fun to climb the tree and play in the leaves.

Timmy climbed up the tree and played in the leaves for a while. But then, he heard a loud noise. It was the sound of the park closing. Timmy knew he had to get down from the tree and go home. But he was scared because it was getting dark and cold outside.

Timmy remembered his mommy telling him that he needed to be careful when he played outside. So, he took a deep breath and slowly climbed down the tree. He picked up a leaf and held it tightly in his hand. When he got home, he showed the leaf to his mommy and said, "I was brave and shut my eyes tight when I climbed down the tree." His mommy hugged him and said, "Good job, Timmy. You are a brave boy."

Jill and Ben were twins who liked to play together. They had many toys, but their favorite was a big teddy bear. They always wanted to hold the teddy bear and hug it. Sometimes they fought over who could hold it first.

One day, their mom told them she had a surprise for them. She said it was something very important and they had to wait until after dinner. Jill and Ben were very curious and excited. They wondered what the surprise could be.

While their mom was cooking, they decided to look for the surprise. They searched the whole house, but they could not find it. Then they remembered there was a closet in their mom's room that they never opened. Maybe the surprise was in there.

They ran to their mom's room and opened the closet. They saw many boxes and bags, but they did not see the surprise. They started to take out the boxes and bags and look inside them. They made a big mess in the closet and on the floor.

Suddenly, they heard their mom calling them for dinner. They were scared that their mom would be angry with them for making a mess. They quickly put the boxes and bags back in the closet, but they forgot to put the teddy bear back. They left the teddy bear on the floor and ran to the kitchen.

Their mom was waiting for them with a big smile. She said she had a surprise for them. She gave them each a small box wrapped in colorful paper. Jill and Ben opened the boxes and gasped. Inside each box was a new teddy bear, just like their old one, but in a different color.

Their mom said she knew how much they loved their teddy bear, so she bought them each a new one. She said they could share their teddy bears and play together nicely. She said she hoped they would always be kind and generous to each other.

Jill and Ben felt happy and ashamed at the same time. They hugged their mom and thanked her for the surprise. They also said they were sorry for making a mess in her closet. They told her they would clean it up after dinner.

Their mom said she was glad they were honest and sorry. She said she loved them very much and she was proud of them. She said the surprise was not only the new teddy bears, but also a lesson. She said the lesson was that the most important thing to hold was not a toy, but each other's hand.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One evening, Lily went to take a bath before bed. She liked to soak in the warm water and play with her rubber duck.

As she was getting ready for bed, Lily's mom noticed that her pajamas didn't fit anymore. "Oh no, these pajamas are too small," said Lily's mom. "We'll have to get you some new ones tomorrow."

The next day, Lily and her mom went to the store to buy new pajamas. Lily picked out a pair with her favorite cartoon character on them. When they got home, Lily put on her new pajamas and showed them to her dad. "Wow, those look great on you!" her dad said.

Later that evening, Lily was getting ready for bed again. This time, her new pajamas fit perfectly. "I love my new pajamas," said Lily. "I'm so glad we got them." And with that, she climbed into bed and fell asleep, dreaming of all the adventures she would have in her new pajamas.

Once there was a little boy called Jake. Jake loved playing outside in the garden. One day, Jake saw a big motorcycle! It was red, shiny, and it had two wheels. Jake thought it was exciting. He wanted to ride it.

Suddenly a man ran up to Jake and said, "What are you doing? Hurry!" Jake was a bit scared. The man looked very serious. Jake thought it was time to go back inside.

He scampered off but he kept glancing back at the big red motorcycle. The man shouted again, "Come on! Hurry up!"

Jake ran inside and wondered what the man wanted with the motorcycle. He wanted to know why he was in such a hurry.

Moments later, the man zoomed off on the motorcycle. Jake thought the man looked so cool and he wanted to ride the motorcycle too! But for now, he stayed inside, hoping to ride the big red motorcycle one day!

Once upon a time there were two best friends, Anna and Dave. They were so excited together because they were going on an incredible journey. Anna and Dave hopped on a big pink bus that took them to the most beautiful park they had ever seen.

At the park, they found a big, fancy swing just for them. Anna and Dave jumped onto the swing and began to swing higher and higher. They laughed and giggled with joy as the wind blew through their hair.

Soon, Anna and Dave felt like they were in the sky! They felt like they were flying and for a moment, it was as if there was no time at all.

Eventually, Anna and Dave had to go home. But they both knew that this special journey and their fancy swing would stay in their memories forever.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to march around the house like a soldier. One day, Timmy's mom gave him a map to play with. Timmy was glad to have a new toy.

Timmy's friend Billy came over to play. Billy saw the map and said, "Let's go on an adventure!" Timmy and Billy followed the map to a big tree in the park. They dug under the tree and found a treasure chest!

But when they opened the chest, they saw that it was full of spiders. Timmy and Billy were scared and ran away. Timmy's mom told him that sometimes things that look good can be bad. Timmy learned to be careful and not trust everything he sees on a map.

Once upon a time, there was a naughty band. It was made up of four mischievous kids, who loved to make a lot of noise.

They would all get together in a room and start to work. They made music with their hands, feet and lots of singing. It sounded like a joyful melody.

Everyday, the naughty band worked hard, trying to make their music louder and better than before. The more they practised the better the music became. Finally, one day, their music was so good, it made everyone on the street stop and listen.

When the naughty band finished their work, everyone clapped and cheered for them. The band felt so proud of what they had achieved. From that day forwards they had a special place in everyone's heart.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to eat candy and cake, but he did not like vegetables. His mommy always told him that vegetables were good for him, but he did not listen.

One day, Timmy's friend Tommy came over for a playdate. Tommy loved vegetables and always had them for snacks. Timmy felt envious of Tommy's love for vegetables and wished he could like them too.

Tommy offered Timmy some carrots and cucumbers, but Timmy refused. He only wanted candy and cake. Later that day, Timmy felt sick and had to go to the hospital. The doctor said that Timmy's tummy was upset because he did not eat enough vegetables.

Timmy learned his lesson and promised to eat more vegetables from then on. But unfortunately, he was too sick to keep his promise and he never got better. The moral of the story is that we should listen to our parents and eat our vegetables, or we might get sick and never get better.

One day, Jack decided he wanted to go to the hospital. His mom drove him there, and he was feeling both scared and excited.

When they arrived, they went to the room where the operation was going to take place. Jack felt scared, but his mom held his hand and said, "Don't be scared, Jack. Just stay here and I'll be right back."

Jack nodded, and his mom left. But when she left, Jack started to feel really miserable. He was so alone, and he wished his mom would come back soon.

Suddenly, the door opened and Doctor Lucy walked in. She said, "Hello there Jack, I just wanted to make sure you were feeling okay."

Jack sighed and said, "I'm really miserable. I just want my mom to come back."

Doctor Lucy smiled and said, "I know it's hard, but you'll be safe here. Just stay here, and I'm sure your mom will be back soon."

Jack nodded and hugged Doctor Lucy. After that, he felt a little bit better.

Jack waited in the hospital room, but eventually his mom came back. He was so happy to see her, he hugged her tight. Jack and his mom then drove home, safe and sound.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Tim. Tim had a bag of marbles that he loved to play with. One day, Tim's friend came over and they played with the marbles together. Tim felt happy when he played with his friend.

Tim's marbles were all different colors and sizes. Some were big and some were small. Tim's favorite marble was a thick blue one. He liked how it felt in his hand.

As they played, Tim's friend accidentally knocked over the bag of marbles. They went rolling all over the floor. Tim felt sad because he thought he lost his favorite marble. But then, his friend found it and gave it back to him. Tim felt happy again and they continued to play with the marbles together. The end.

Once there was a little girl named Jane. She was three years old. Every day, Jane would help her mom in the kitchen.

Today was no exception. Her mom was making a delicious dinner. She said to Jane, "I need help. Can you put two cups of rice in this bowl?"

Jane smiled and said, "Yes, mommy!" She opened the cupboard and grabbed two cups of rice. She gently poured them into the bowl.

But when she was done, the rice was all over the floor! Jane's mom said, "Oh no! Now the rice is broken!"

Jane stared at the mess for a few seconds and then she smiled. She said, "Don't worry, Mommy! I know what to do." Jane grabbed the broom and started to shake the rice into a pile.

After a few minutes, all the rice was cleaned up. Jane's mom smiled and said, "Thank you, Jane! You did a great job."

Jane was so proud and she smiled. She said, "That's what friends are for!"

Once there was a little girl named Alice. She was three years old and loved to go visit her family. One day, she went to visit her aunt's house with her mom.

When they arrived, Alice couldn't help but noticed the big house. She had never been there before and it was full of unknown things. Her mom asked her to go upstairs to look for the toilet.

Alice went up the stairs, but she was scared! Before she knew it, she was standing in front of a small room. She poked her head inside and what do you think she saw? The toilet!

Alice smiled and shivered with joy. She quickly ran back to her mom and said, "I found the toilet!" Her mom was so proud of her.

Alice came to visit her aunt's house many times in the future and she was never afraid of the unknown again.

Tom was a little boy who liked to play with his toy monkey. He named his monkey Max and took him everywhere. One day, Tom and Max went to the park with Mom and Dad. They saw a big band playing music and people marching with flags and drums.

Tom wanted to march too, so he held Max by the hand and followed the band. He tried to copy their steps and sounds, but he was too small and slow. He bumped into a man who was carrying a big tuba. The man got angry and shouted at Tom. He said, "Get out of the way, you terrible kid! You are ruining the parade!"

Tom was scared and sad. He ran back to Mom and Dad, who hugged him and comforted him. They told him that the man was rude and mean, and that Tom was not terrible at all. They said, "You are a good boy, and we love you and your monkey. You can march with us anytime you want."

Tom smiled and hugged them back. He felt better and said, "Thank you, Mom and Dad. I love you too. And I love Max. He is my best friend." He kissed his monkey and held him tight. He decided that he did not need to march with the band. He was happy to march with his family and his monkey.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Sue. Sue had a fancy dress that she loved to wear. One sunny day, she decided to go on a walk in the park.

While walking, Sue saw a big knot in a tree. She thought it was so interesting. Sue wanted to touch the knot, but she tripped and fell into a puddle. Her fancy dress was all wet and muddy.

Sue was sad, but her mom told her to soak her dress in water to make it clean again. Sue learned that it's important to be careful and look where you're going. And even when things go wrong, there's always a way to fix them.

Once upon a time, there was a nice boy named Tim. He had a toy rocket that he loved very much. Every day, he would play with his rocket and make it fly high in the sky.

One day, Tim was playing with his rocket in the park. He threw it up in the sky and it went very high. But, the wind blew it far away. Tim looked and looked for his rocket, but he could not find it. He started to weep because he was very sad.

A big girl named Sue saw Tim weep and asked, "Why are you sad?" Tim told her about his lost rocket. Sue said, "I saw a rocket near the big tree." They went to the big tree and found the rocket. But, it was broken. Tim wept more because his rocket was not nice anymore. The moral of the story is to be careful with the things you love, or they might get broken.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lucy. She was very naughty and had a spade she used in the sand. On this day she was outside playing in the sand. She loved to be naughty and decided to make bigger and bigger splashes in the nearby pond.

"Look mom,” Lucy shouted, “I'm making a big splash!"
