Soon enough, Suzy was able to draw an amazing picture. She was so proud of her work and showed her mom. Her mom was very proud too and said, "You did it! You learned how to draw!"

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a small, clever boy. He had a dream. He wanted to succeed at something big and special.

He decided he would try to move a very big barrel. He couldn't lift it, so he had to think of a clever plan. He looked around until he found some small sticks. He carefully put the sticks underneath the barrel and then used them to push the barrel up until it was off the ground.

He kept pushing until the barrel was moving. He was very proud of himself that he managed to succeed at this difficult task. He smiled with joy, knowing that he had been very clever and achieved his goal.

The end.

Tom was a curious boy who liked to examine everything. He liked to look at the pictures in his books, the toys in his room, and the bugs in the garden. One day, he found something new to examine on the floor. It was a small, shiny box with a lid.

Tom picked up the box and shook it. He heard a rattling sound inside. He wondered what was in the box. He tried to open the lid, but it was stuck. He pulled and pushed, but it did not move. He felt frustrated and angry. He wanted to see what was in the box.

He decided to ask his mom for help. He ran to the kitchen, where his mom was making lunch. He showed her the box and said, "Mom, can you open this?" His mom smiled and took the box from him. She examined it and said, "This is a music box, Tom. It plays a song when you open it. But it is very old and rusty, so it might be hard to open. Let me try."

She used a knife to pry open the lid. Tom heard a click and then a beautiful melody. He saw a tiny dancer spinning on a platform. He was amazed and delighted. He clapped his hands and said, "Wow, mom, thank you! This is so pretty! Where did you find it?"

His mom hugged him and said, "This was my grandma's music box, Tom. She gave it to me when I was a little girl. She told me it was very special and I should take good care of it. And now I want to give it to you, because you are very special to me. Do you like it?"

Tom nodded and said, "Yes, mom, I love it! It is the best thing I ever examined!" He kissed his mom and said, "You are the best mom ever!" He took the music box and ran back to his room. He put it on his shelf and opened and closed it again and again. He listened to the song and watched the dancer. He felt happy and proud. He had a new treasure to examine.

Once upon a time there was a thin cat called Connie. She was very lazy, and liked to sleep in the sun all day.

Every day, Connie would gaze at the flowers and the birds that flew by. One day, she spotted a magnificent flower with a unique style. She wanted to make the flower her own, but it was too far away to reach.

So Connie asked the bird, “Can you help me? I want the flower!”

The bird said, “Sure, I can help. I will restore it for you!”

The bird flew up to the flower, and lifted it gently with its beak. It brought the flower back to Connie, who thanked the bird for its help.

Connie carefully planted the flower in her garden, and it bloomed brightly. From then on, Connie’s garden had the same thin style as the flower she found.

Once upon a time there was a little girl who was so playful. She stumbled here, there and everywhere! One day, she stumbled into a mysterious place. It was filled with magical power! She had never seen anything like it before.

The little girl was so curious. She knew she had to explore! She stumbled around the room looking at all the things that glowed. She walked up to a big box and saw it had so many colours. She pressed a few buttons and suddenly the room lit up!

The little girl couldn't believe her eyes. She felt so much power inside her. She stumbled back and forth, laughing and having a great time. She was filled with joy and felt like anything was possible.

The little girl stumbled around until it was time to go home. She had an amazing day and she thanked the mysterious place for giving her so much power. With a skip in her step, she walked back home filled with a playful energy.

Once upon a time, there were two best friends, Jack and Emily.

Jack was very organized. He always kept his toys tidy.

Emily was not so organized. She had a big pile of toys she would move around, but it was always a mess.

One day, Jack asked Emily, "Why don't you become more organized?"

Emily thought for a minute, and then she had an idea. "Let's ride the train!"

So, Jack and Emily went to the train station. They found an old, empty train, and Jack began organizing it. He put the seats in neat rows and made sure the windows were clean.

Then, Jack and Emily became the train driver and conductor. They drove the train all around town, picking up passengers and stopping at stations.

At the end of the day, Emily was so proud of how organized everything had become. She smiled at Jack and said, "I'm so glad I listened to you!".

Once upon a time, there was a shy little bunny. He had big floppy ears and a furry tail. Every day, he would hop around looking for a home. He wanted to make a home that was his very own.

One day, he hopped into a meadow filled with daisies. He looked around and saw a hollow log. He thought, "This is the perfect place to make my home."

He hopped inside and made some extra fluffy leaves for a bed. He made some sticks into a cozy nest and he had a little home of his own.

The shy little bunny was so happy. He was no longer alone and he had a place to keep him warm. From then on, he was never shy and he always had a place to call home.

Once there was a dish. The dish was very wet. It felt very heavy in her small hands. She wanted to know how heavy the dish was, so she put it on the scales. She watched as the needle moved and stopped. She had weighed the dish! It weighed a lot! She smiled and took the dish carefully off the scales. That way she knew how heavy her dish was.

Once upon a time there was a little boy. His name was Jack and he wanted to learn how to play the flute. His parents bought him a fake flute, but Jack was not sure how to play it. He tried to put the fake flute to his lips, but the sound was terrible. Jack struggled every day to learn how to make real music with his flute.

One day, he heard his neighbor playing beautiful notes with her flute. He didn't know what they were, but he wanted to learn how to make them too. He stared at her and listened carefully, trying his best to remember what she was doing.

Jack spent hours and hours practicing to make the same notes. He used the fake flute, but he could not make real music. He was getting so frustrated, he wanted to give up. Then something happened. On one particular day, he finally made a real music! He couldn't believe it!

Jack was so happy and proud of himself. It wasn't easy, but he had finally done it. Now, Jack has become a great flute player! And all it took was hard work and a little bit of struggle!

One day, a nice fish named Tim wanted to organize a fun swim race for his friends in the sea. He told all his friends about the race. They were all very excited. But there was a big jellyfish named Bob who wanted to join too. Tim was worried because jellyfish can sometimes hurt other fish.

The day of the race came, and all the fish were ready to swim. Tim told Bob the jellyfish to be very careful not to hurt anyone. Bob promised to be nice and not hurt his friends. The race started, and all the fish swam as fast as they could.

As they swam, Tim saw that Bob the jellyfish was getting too close to a little fish named Sue. Tim swam very fast to help Sue. He told Sue to swim away from Bob. Sue swam away just in time, and Bob didn't hurt her. In the end, Tim won the race and everyone was happy. They all learned that it is important to be nice and help each other.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy who loved dinosaurs. He had a toy dinosaur that he played with every day. One day, Timmy took his dinosaur to the park to play.

At the park, Timmy met a girl named Lily who also loved dinosaurs. She had a toy dinosaur too, but hers was bigger and smarter than Timmy's. "Wow, your dinosaur is so intelligent!" said Timmy.

Lily smiled and replied, "Thank you! I taught him how to bow." And with that, her dinosaur bowed down to Timmy's dinosaur. Timmy was amazed and said, "That's so cool! Can you teach my dinosaur to bow too?"

Lily nodded and showed Timmy how to teach his dinosaur to bow. From then on, Timmy's dinosaur was just as smart as Lily's and they all played together happily ever after.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Katy. Katy lived in a big house with her grandma. One summer day, Katy wanted to explore the garden, but grandma said she had to stay inside.

"No, I won't let you go out there!" Said grandma

Katy was very sad, but she decided to listen to her grandma. After a while, Katy heard something coming from outside. She got curious and went to the window to have a peak. She saw the wind was blowing gently and the leaves were falling from the trees.

"Look Katy, the leaves are hidden in the garden! Can you collect them?" Asked grandma.

Katy was so happy about it. She grabbed a basket and went to the garden. Katy collected all the leaves she could find, and she arranged them in different shapes.

The moral of the story is that if we listen to our elders, we can discover ideas and find joy in something as simple as leaves falling from the trees.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside and explore the world around her. One day, she wandered too far into the woods and got lost.

She started to cry and felt very scared. Suddenly, she heard a voice calling out to her. It was her mom's voice! She felt so grateful that her mom found her.

Her mom reminded her to always stay close and not wander too far. Lily promised to listen and be more careful. From that day on, Lily always stayed close to her mom when they went on adventures together.

One day, Dad went to the garden to observe all of the flowers. He thought one particular flower was very beautiful. His three year old daughter followed Dad, running around, and wanted to pick the flower too.

"Please don't pick the flower," Dad said. He didn't want her to ruin the flower.

She smiled and said, "But why Dad? It looks so pretty."

"I know, but if you pick it, it won't look so pretty anymore," said Dad.

Suddenly, a crazy wind blew and picked the flower all by itself. The three year old looked in amazement, and said, "Look Dad! It's a magical flower."

Dad smiled and said, "Yes, amazing isn't it? That's why I wanted you not to pick the flower."

The little girl learned her lesson that day and knew never to pick the flowers in the garden.

Once there was a blue car. It had a driver that could permit it to go anywhere. The car drove to the park and stopped. Then the driver opened up the door and a little girl stepped out of the car. The driver permitted her to run around and play. The little girl ran around the park, skipping and laughing. She saw lots of other people and waved to them. Then the blue car started to move. The driver had permitted the car to take the little girl home. The little girl said goodbye to all her new friends and hopped back in the car. The driver permitted the car to drive away and soon the little girl was home. The driver had permitted the car to take her back home safely.

One day, a girl named Sue went to a small cabin in the woods with her mom. The cabin was a nice place to play and have fun. It was a harmless place where Sue felt happy.

While they were inside the cabin, Sue saw a big box. She asked her mom, "Can I remove the box, please?" Her mom said, "Yes, Sue, you can remove the box."

Sue removed the box and found many toys inside. She played with the toys all day long. Sue and her mom had a great time in the harmless cabin. And they knew they would come back to the cabin again soon.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy called Max. Max was three years old and always wanted to find new things to do. One day, his dad told him he could go and play in the park.

Max was so excited! He quickly put on his shoes and ran out the door. The park was far away, so Max had to manage the long walk there. After what seemed like forever, Max finally arrived at the park. He felt very happy.

The park was full of amazing things to do – there was a big slide and a big swing! He was about to start playing when he noticed something strange. The sky was dark and full of thick ash. Suddenly, he heard a loud sound - like a distant thunder - and he started to feel scared.

But Max was brave and he managed to stay brave. After playing for a while he decided it was time to go home. Even though the sky was still dark and the thunder was still distant, Max was happy to have gone to the park. He couldn't wait to go back again!

One day, a little guard dog was in his yard. He liked to get his ball and play. He was happy and did not know many things. This guard dog was not smart, but he was a good friend.

A big bird came to the yard. The bird wanted to play with the guard dog. The bird was not nice, but the guard dog did not know. The guard dog got his ball and gave it to the bird.

The bird took the ball and flew away. The guard dog was sad. He did not understand why the bird did that. But, a nice cat saw everything. The cat got a new ball and gave it to the guard dog. They played together and became good friends.

Once upon a time, there was a pink bunny. The bunny liked to stay in the garden and eat carrots. One day, the bunny saw a butterfly. The butterfly flew away, but then it disappeared! The bunny looked around and couldn't find the butterfly. The bunny was sad because it wanted to play with the butterfly. But then, the butterfly appeared again and the bunny was happy! They played together and had fun. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little dog named Spot. Spot was a very playful dog. Today, he wanted to be a good dog and behave. Spot's mom said, "Spot, if you behave today, you will get a big treat!"

Spot played with his ball in the yard. He saw a big, red ball near the fence. Spot wanted to play with the red ball, but he knew it belonged to the neighbor. Spot remembered what his mom said about being good and behaving today. So, he did not take the red ball.

Later that day, Spot's mom came outside. She saw that Spot had behaved and was a good dog today. She gave him a big treat, just like she promised. Spot was very happy that he listened to his mom and behaved. From that day on, Spot knew that being good and behaving would make his mom happy and bring him treats.

One day, Anna noticed something shiny in the sand. She bent down to see what it was and found a cap. It was a nice cap with a shiny buckle on the front! Anna was so excited that she put the cap on her head.

Anna decided to take a walk around the park to show everyone her new cap. As Anna walked, she noticed a group of wealthy people, wearing their fancy clothes. She wanted to be like them and be wealthy too.

Anna kept walking until she came to a patch of grass. She noticed a shiny penny in the grass and picked it up. Anna smiled and thought to herself; if I find some more of these pennies, I can be rich just like the people I saw earlier!

So, from then on, Anna went on walks around the park, hoping to find more pennies. She had noticed that the more of them she found, the closer she was to becoming wealthy like her new friends.

Josie wanted to pack her life. She had unusual things that meant a lot to her. She wanted to take it all with her and make a fresh start.

“Do you want to help me pack, Mommy?” Josie asked.

“Of course I do,” Mommy answered. “We will make sure nothing is left behind.”

They started to pack all of Josie’s things. She had some unusual objects she wanted to bring with her. But when they finished, something was missing. Josie couldn’t find her favourite toy.

“Where is my toy, Mommy?” she asked with tears in her eyes.

“I don’t know. We have to look again.”

But it was too late, the toy was nowhere to be found and Josie had to leave without it. It was a sad ending to her packing her life.

Once upon a time, there lived a little girl. She was 3 years old and loved to play. One night, the little girl wanted to explore. So she took her flashlight and began to look around.

Suddenly she saw something. It was a delicious cake! She knew she should not, but something inside her wanted to eat it. So she did. She was feeling guilty, but the cake was very yummy!

After she finished the cake, the little girl decided to go back home. She followed the light of her flashlight, and soon she was safe and sound in her bedroom.

The end!

Once upon a time, there was a special bird that could soar. One day, the bird went on a journey. To get ready for the journey, it pumped its wings with gas. When the bird was ready, it opened his wings wide, and flew up in the sky.

The bird soared high and its wings felt so free. It flew over the hills, the trees, and the rivers. It even saw some farms! Pretty soon, the bird was so high that it saw the clouds.

The bird flew faster and faster, and soon it felt like it was flying very fast! At one point, the bird could almost touch the sky. But, the bird realized it had to go home.

So, the bird started to fly back down to the ground. It felt so good to glide through the clouds! After all of its soaring, the bird was back in its nest, safe and sound.

Once there was a clumsy bear. The bear was always moving from one place to another. One day the bear came to a clearing with a big rock. The bear was very curious about the rock so it moved closer to take a look. The clumsy bear got too close and tripped, tumbling over the rock. The bear was unharmed and the rock stayed exactly where it was the whole time.

The bear was happy to find a big rock to sit on and it quickly made the rock its fun spot. The clumsy bear liked to move around the rock, jumping and twirling and dancing as it went. The bear was having lots of fun when it noticed an opening beneath the rock.

The bear moved closer to investigate and found that the rock was sitting on top of a tiny cave. Inside the cave were lots of treasures the clumsy bear had never seen before. So the bear gathered up all of the sparkly objects and moved them somewhere safe. After that, the clumsy bear continued to dance, jump and twirl around the rock.

Sam and Lily were twins who liked to play together. One day, they found an ancient book in the attic. It had pictures of knights and dragons and castles. They decided to pretend they were in the book.

"I am a brave knight and you are a princess," Sam said to Lily. "We have to save the kingdom from the evil dragon."

"Okay," Lily nodded. She put on a dress and a crown. Sam took a sword and a shield. They ran down the stairs and into the garden.

They saw a big tree that looked like a castle. They climbed up the branches and pretended it was their home. They looked around and saw a red car that looked like a dragon. They decided to fight it.

"Roar!" Sam shouted. He swung his sword at the car. "Take that, dragon!"

"Help!" Lily cried. She pretended the car caught her. "Save me, knight!"

Sam ran to the car and tried to free Lily. But he slipped and fell. He hit his head on a rock. He felt a lot of pain and started to cry.

Lily saw that Sam was hurt. She was scared and sorry. She ran to him and hugged him. She called for their mom.

Mom heard their cries and came to the garden. She saw Sam's head bleeding. She was worried and angry. She took Sam and Lily to the hospital.

At the hospital, a nice doctor looked at Sam's head. He cleaned the wound and put a bandage on it. He said Sam would be okay, but he had to rest.

"Thank you, doctor," Mom said. She hugged Sam and Lily. "I'm glad you're both safe. But you should never play with the car or the sword. They are dangerous. And you should never go to the attic. It is old and dusty. Do you understand?"

"Yes, Mom," Sam and Lily nodded. They felt sorry and ashamed. They learned their lesson. They decided to play with safer toys and stay away from the attic. They also decided to read the ancient book together and learn more about knights and dragons and castles. They thought it was more fun and less risky.

Bob was a little boy who had a new neighbor. He was excited to meet them but he was also a bit scared. Bob's neighbor was very big and he was speaking with a deep, rough voice. Bob didn't know what to do, so he decided to rest for a bit. He sat down on the porch and closed his eyes.

The neighbor saw Bob and he smiled. He came close and Bob was surprised, but he felt safe. The neighbor asked Bob if he wanted to play a game and Bob said yes!

They played all afternoon and Bob was getting tired. The neighbor said that it was time to rest and Bob happily agreed. He said goodbye and went back home.

Bob was now sure that his new neighbor was very nice, even if his voice had been a bit scary and rough before. He was grateful that they were friends.

Once upon a time, there was a family who lived together in a small house. Every Sunday, they would lay out a big table cloth in the garden to have a picnic together. They would eat their lunch and play lots of games together, laughing and giggling.

One Sunday, the mother was feeling very angry. As soon as the family lay out the table cloth, she began yelling and scolding her children. No one knew why she was so angry, but there were lots of angry words and no one was having fun anymore.

The children, who were sad and frightened, ran away from the angry mother and stayed away from her the rest of the day. The father was also unhappy, but was patient with the children and said nothing.

The next day, the father took the children for a walk and told them a story about the meaning of the word "anger". He explained that it is ok to feel angry sometimes, but it is important not to let it stay for too long. People should always try to let anger go and to find ways to be happy again.

The children learnt a great lesson from their father and from that day forward, they made sure to always be patient and kind to each other, even when they were feeling angry.

Once upon a time there was a special day. On that day the sun shone brightly and the birds sang happily. A little girl called Sara was very excited because it was her birthday.

Sara opened her presents, one by one. One of the presents was very special. It was a squishy, smelly gift—it was a hug from her mommy! Sara smiled and hugged the gift back.

Mommy was so happy that Sara liked the special hug-gift. She hugged Sara tight and whispered "Happy Birthday". Sara giggled and hugged her mommy.

Mommy and Sara stayed together, hugging and laughing. It was a very special moment that they would never forget.

Ben and Lily went to the zoo with Mom and Dad. They saw many animals, like lions, monkeys, and birds. But Ben and Lily liked the zebras the best. They had black and white stripes and long tails.

"Can we feed the zebras, Mom?" Lily asked.

"Sorry, honey, we can't. The zebras have their own food. We can only look at them," Mom said.

Ben and Lily looked at the zebras through the fence. They saw one zebra that was very hungry. It was trying to reach some leaves on a tall tree. But the tree was too high for the zebra. The zebra stretched its neck and legs, but it could not get the leaves.

"Look, Lily, that zebra is hungry. It wants the leaves," Ben said.

"I know, Ben. I wish we could help it," Lily said.

They felt sorry for the hungry zebra. They wanted to give it some of their snacks. But they knew they could not. They had to follow the rules of the zoo.

"Maybe the zookeeper will come and give the zebra some food," Mom said.

"I hope so, Mom. The zebra looks sad," Ben said.

Lily nodded. She hoped the zebra would get some food soon. She and Ben waved goodbye to the zebra and went to see the other animals. They hoped the zebra would be happy.

Tom and Lily are twins. They like to play with their dog, Spot. Spot is a big, brown dog. He can do many tricks. He can sit, roll, and fetch.

One day, Tom and Lily want to show their mom and dad what Spot can do. They take Spot to the backyard. They say, "Spot, perform for us!"

Spot is happy. He wags his tail. He sits when Tom says "sit". He rolls when Lily says "roll". He fetches a ball when Tom throws it.

Mom and dad clap their hands. They say, "Good boy, Spot! You are very smart!"

Spot is proud. He wants to do more tricks. He sees a lemon on the table. He thinks it is a ball. He jumps and grabs it with his mouth.

But the lemon is not a ball. It is sour. Spot makes a funny face. He spits out the lemon. He barks.

Tom and Lily laugh. They say, "Spot, that is not a ball. That is a lemon. Lemons are sour. They are not for dogs."

Spot is confused. He does not like lemons. He runs to Tom and Lily. He licks their faces. He wants to play with them.

Mom and dad smile. They say, "Spot, you are a silly dog. But we love you. You are part of our family."

They hug Spot. They give him a treat. They say, "Spot, you are the best dog ever!"

One day, a little girl named Lily went to the park. She saw an attractive structure with many colors. It was a big playhouse. She wanted to gather her friends to play with her.

Lily found her friend Tom. "Tom, come see the pretty playhouse!" she said. Tom looked at the structure and smiled. "Wow! It's so nice, Lily! Let's go play!" They ran to the playhouse together.

Inside the playhouse, Lily and Tom laughed and played. They gathered more friends to join them. Everyone had a fun time. The pretty playhouse made their day special.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved playing outside in the garden. One day, she saw a caterpillar crawling on the ground. She picked it up gently and held it in her hand.

"Hello, little caterpillar," said Lily. "You are so cute and fuzzy!"

The caterpillar wiggled and Lily giggled. She squeezed her hand a little bit, but not too hard. Suddenly, she felt dizzy and had to sit down.

"Are you okay, Lily?" asked her mom.

"I'm okay, Mommy," said Lily. "I just got a little dizzy from squeezing the caterpillar too much."

From that day on, Lily was more careful when holding the caterpillar and never squeezed it too hard again.

Once upon a time, there were two friends, Bob and Jo. One day, Bob and Jo were playing at the park and they both had a plan. Bob's plan was to climb up to the top of the tallest tree in the park. Jo's plan was to sit by the pond and watch the empty sky.

Bob started to climb the tree and said to Jo, "Look at me, I'm almost at the top!" When Bob reached the top, he shouted, "I did it!"

Jo noticed that the sky had gotten a little dark and said, "You better come down, Bob, or the storm will ruin our plans!"

But Bob refused and stayed at the top of the tree, shouting, "You can't make me come down!"

Both Bob and Jo were getting scared and worried about the storm. Jo pleaded, "Please come down Bob, it's not safe!"

Bob looked down and sighed. He started to climb down from the top of the tree, and once he was safely back on the ground, both Bob and Jo ran to the empty pond and waited for the storm to pass.

Once there was a skin. It was the color of the sun, shiny and bright. But it was hard - so difficult that it hurt if someone touched it.

The skin lay all alone, until one day a little bug came and made a home. The bug loved the skin, and rested their tired legs. But the skin was sad. It wished for someone else to lie with it.

One day, a spider came and saw the skin lying all alone. The spider asked the skin if it could lie with it. The skin was too scared to say yes, so it stayed quiet.

But the spider was brave and went ahead and lay down next to the skin. Together they rested in the sun, happy and content.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy wanted to have a toy he could rely on all the time. He asked his mommy and daddy if they could provide him with one. His mommy and daddy smiled and said they would try their best.

A few days later, Timmy’s parents gave him a present. When Timmy opened the present he felt so excited! It was a toy car with a bright red button. Timmy pressed the button and the car beeped and drove away! Timmy was delighted.

Timmy played with his toy car every day. Everywhere he went, the car followed him. Timmy was so happy because he had a toy that was reliable. He knew his car was always there for him.

One day, Timmy got stuck in the mud. No matter how hard he tried, he couldn’t get out. He was about to give up, when suddenly he remembered his bright red button. He pressed the button and the toy car started to pull him out of the mud!

Timmy was so relieved. He realised that his toy car really was reliable! He hugged his car and thanked it for providing him with help when he needed it the most.

Once upon a time, there was a wise owl who lived in a big tree in the forest. He loved to watch the animals play and lumber around in the woods. One day, a little rabbit came to him and said, "I lost my carrot, can you help me find it?" The owl said, "Sure, let's go look for it."

As they were searching, they heard a loud noise. The owl said, "I think that's a storm coming, we need to hurry." The rabbit started to panic and said, "I don't want to get wet!" The owl said, "Don't worry, I know a place where we can stay dry."

They followed the owl to a small cave and waited out the storm. When it was over, the rabbit found his carrot and thanked the wise owl for his help. From that day on, the rabbit and the owl were good friends and would often go on adventures together in the forest.

Once upon a time, there was a perfect church. It was so pretty that people from far away would often come to peek at it. Every day, the church looked more perfect.

One day, a little girl came to peek at the church. She was only three years old, but something about the church looked so magical. She wanted to explore it.

The little girl slowly opened the big door of the church and peeped inside. It was like a dream come true! Everything looked so perfect. From the big windows to the tall columns.

The little girl stayed and peeked around until she was too tired to stay. Then she left, happy to have found the perfect church.

John and his mom went to the park. He was so excited! It was full of colors, like green grass and blue sky. John ran around, playing games with the other kids. But then it was time to go home. John didn't want to surrender and leave the park. He felt embarrassed that the other kids were staying and he had to go. John's mom gently held his hand, and told him it was time to go. Knowing he had to surrender, John slowly said goodbye to the park. His mom hugged him and they began walking home. As they walked, John danced and twirled, ending the day with a smile, surrounded by the colors of the park.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a white couch in her room that she loved to jump on. One day, Lily's mom told her to behave and not jump on the couch anymore. Lily was sad, but she knew she had to listen to her mom.

Later that day, Lily's friend came over to play. They decided to have a tea party on the couch. Lily remembered what her mom said and told her friend to be careful and not jump on the couch. They had a fun tea party and the couch stayed clean and white.

Lily was proud of herself for behaving and keeping her couch clean. She knew that listening to her mom was important and she wanted to make her proud too. From that day on, Lily always made sure to take good care of her couch and never jumped on it again.

Once upon a time, there was an old man who lived in a small house. He loved to whistle all day long. His whistling was so loud that it could be heard from miles away. People in the village thought he was crazy.

One day, a little girl named Lily went to visit the old man. She asked him why he whistled so much. The old man smiled and said, "I whistle to keep my heart happy."

Lily loved to listen to the old man's whistling. She even learned how to whistle herself. Every day, she would visit the old man and they would whistle together.

One day, the old man stopped whistling. Lily was sad and asked him why he had stopped. The old man smiled and said, "I have taught you how to whistle. Now it's your turn to make the world happy with your whistling." From that day on, Lily whistled every day and made the world a happier place, just like the old man had done.

Tim and Sue are friends. They like to play outside. One day, they see a big hill with smoke. Tim says, "Look, a volcano!" Sue says, "Wow, can we go there?" Tim says, "Yes, let's go!"

They run to the hill. They see rocks and fire. They hear a loud noise. Tim says, "This is fun!" Sue says, "This is scary!" Tim says, "Don't be scared, it's just a volcano!"

They go closer to the volcano. They see a hole. Tim says, "I want to see what's inside!" Sue says, "No, don't go there, it's dangerous!" Tim says, "No, it's not, it's cool!" He points to the hole. He says, "Look, there's something shiny!"

He runs to the hole. He tries to grab the shiny thing. But it's too hot. He burns his hand. He screams. Sue screams. The volcano screams. It spits fire and rocks. Tim and Sue are too close. They can't run away. They get hit by fire and rocks. They fall down. They don't get up. The volcano is quiet. The shiny thing is still there. But Tim and Sue can't see it. They can't see anything. They are gone. The volcano is not fun. It's bad. Tim and Sue made a big mistake. They didn't listen to Sue. They didn't stay away from the volcano. They didn't do what was important. They did what was silly. And they paid a big price. The end.

One day, a boy named Tim found a toy motorcycle. It was red and shiny. He liked it very much. Tim wanted to play with it outside. So, he put on his shoes and went out to the yard.

Tim saw a big rock. It was hard and gray. He wanted to make the motorcycle go up the rock. He pushed the motorcycle up, but it was too hard. Tim felt sad.

Then, Tim had an idea. He would skip with the motorcycle. He held the motorcycle in his hand and skipped around the yard. The motorcycle went up and down as he skipped. Tim was happy. He played with his motorcycle all day long.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to go to the museum with her family. The museum was full of toys, animals, and pretty things to see.

One day, Lily went to the museum and saw a big lion. The lion looked so real and Lily thought it was very attractive. She wanted to touch it, but her mom said no.

Lily got tired and started to yawn. She wanted to go home and take a nap. But before she left, she said goodbye to the lion and promised to come back and see him again.

Once upon a time, there were two friends named Jack and Jill. They were very intelligent and liked to play together.

One day, Jack wanted to try something fun. He decided to make a huge pile of sand and destroy it. When Jill saw Jack, she laughed and said it was silly.

Soon, some other friends came to join the fun. They all had a great time throwing sand and destroying it.

Then, a judge came by and saw what they were doing. He was very angry and said they had to clean up. Jack and Jill looked sad and wanted to keep playing.

The judge saw how intelligent they were and decided to be nice. He said they could keep playing if they cleaned up first.

Jack and Jill were so happy! They quickly cleaned up the sand and went back to have fun. They all agreed that intelligent people can find a way to have fun and keep it neat.

Once upon a time, there was a magic tree. Everyday the tree would glow with a special power.

One day, a little boy named Tom noticed the tree and thought it was beautiful. He asked his mum, "What is this tree, mum? It is so sparkly and special!"

"That is a magic tree, Tom. It glows with special power," his mum replied.

Tom was so excited to see the magic tree! He asked if he could go closer to see it better. "Please, mum, can I go near the magic tree?"

His mum said, "Yes, but be careful. You must be very gentle with the tree. It is very special."

So Tom carefully and gently went closer to the tree. He looked and looked, and the tree glowed brighter and brighter! Tom was amazed, and he said, "Wow, the tree is magical!"

The tree was so special and Tom knew he had to be careful to not hurt it. He gave the tree a gentle hug and the tree glowed even brighter!

That night, Tom was sure the tree had magical power and said, "Thank you, tree, for being so special!"

Once upon a time, there was a candle. It was a regular candle, just like any other candle. It was big and tall and stood on a table.

One day, something strange happened to the candle. It started to shrink! It became smaller and smaller until it was just a tiny candle.

The people in the room were surprised to see the candle shrink. They didn't know what to do. But then they decided to light the tiny candle anyway. And even though it was small, it still gave off a warm and cozy glow. The end.

Lily and Max were playing in the garden. They liked to dig holes and fill them with water, stones and leaves. They pretended they were making ponds for frogs and fish.

"Look, Lily, I made a big hole!" Max said, showing his sister his work.

"That's nice, Max, but don't make it too close to the fence. Mom said we have to behave and not make a mess," Lily said, digging her own hole.

Max did not listen. He wanted to make his hole bigger and deeper. He dug and dug until he hit something hard. He tried to pull it out, but it was stuck.

"What is that, Max?" Lily asked, coming over to see.

"I don't know, Lily. It looks like a metal box. Maybe it has treasure inside!" Max said, excited.

He pulled harder, but the box did not move. Instead, he heard a loud creak and saw the fence start to fall.

"Max, stop! You're breaking the fence!" Lily shouted.

But it was too late. The fence collapsed and landed on the box, making a loud bang. Max and Lily were scared and ran inside the house.

Mom heard the noise and came out to see what happened. She saw the broken fence, the hole, the box and the mess. She was very angry and frustrated.

"Max and Lily, what have you done? You did not behave at all! You have to fix the fence and clean the garden. And no more digging holes!" Mom said, sternly.

Max and Lily felt sorry and ashamed. They said they were sorry and helped Mom fix the fence and clean the garden. They learned their lesson and never dug holes near the fence again.

Once upon a time, there was a grumpy old man who lived in a big house. He had lots of gold coins, but he never shared them with anyone. One day, a little girl came to his house and knocked on the door. The old man opened the door and looked at her with his grumpy face.

The little girl asked him if she could observe his garden. The old man didn't want to let her in, but she was so polite that he finally said yes. They went to the garden and the little girl saw a beautiful flower. She picked it up and gave it to the old man. He was so surprised that he smiled for the first time in years.

The old man realized that sharing is better than keeping everything to himself. He gave the little girl a gold coin as a thank you gift. From that day on, he was no longer grumpy and he shared his gold with everyone who needed it. The little girl had taught him a valuable lesson about kindness and generosity.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy had a fan in his room that he loved to use when he slept. One day, the fan stopped working and Timmy was sad.

Timmy asked his mom, "Can you fix my fan? It's not working." His mom said, "Sure, I will try to repair it." She opened the fan and saw that a part was broken. She said, "This is a heavy fan. It will take some time to fix."

A few hours later, Timmy's mom came back with the fan. She said, "I repaired it! Now it's working again." Timmy was happy and said, "Thank you, Mommy! You fixed my fan!" From that day on, Timmy slept with his fan on every night.

Once upon a time, there was a purple couch. It was big and comfy. While sitting on it, a girl and her brother liked to make silly faces together. One day, they were on the purple couch, playing a silly game. But then something happened! All of a sudden, there was a big noise and the couch split right in the middle! The girl and her brother were so surprised! They screamed and laughed at the same time. Then, the girl said she was gonna fix the couch. She got some glue and a special tool. After a few tries, the couch was all patched up and good as new. It was just like nothing ever happened. The girl and her brother were so happy! From then on, they always made sure to be a bit more gentle with the purple couch. The End.

One day, a boy was playing with his football in the garden. He was very gentle with the ball and touched it with delicate hands. He wore a special top and shorts which sparkled in the sunlight.

Suddenly, the football flew up into the air. It went higher and higher until it landed on top of the house! He couldn't reach it. He called out and asked his dad to help.

Dad came out with a long stick. He held it up and nudged the football down. The boy put out his delicate hands and caught the football.

He thanked his dad and ran around the garden with the football. He looked so happy wearing his sparkly clothes as he played. The football never flew away again.

Robbie was a three year old boy who liked to explore. One day, he decided to explore the park near his house. He skipped over to one of the benches and saw a distant woman sitting there. She was frowning and looked worried. He walked over to her and said, "Hello."

The woman looked surprised and smiled. "Hello there," she said. She seemed very friendly.

Robbie asked her why she was frowning. The woman told him that she was waiting for someone and they were late. Robbie thought that was sad. He asked if he could wait with her. She smiled and nodded.

They waited together for a few moments until the distant person the woman was waiting for finally came. Robbie waved goodbye to her, and they were on their way. As he went home, Robbie smiled to himself, feeling a little less distant from the world around him.

Jack was feeling generous today. He saw a lady in the shade who was very dirty. He offered to help her clean.

The lady was very happy and said, "Thank you so much! I really appreciate it."

Jack set to work. He scrubbed and washed the lady until she was nice and clean.

The lady gave Jack a big hug and said, "Thank you, you are so generous!"

But then, as the lady was walking away, she took a silver necklace that belonged to Jack. She ran away, never to be seen again.

Jack was not happy. He had been nice to the lady, but she had stolen from him instead of being thankful. He learned an important lesson that day.

Lily and Ben are friends. They like to play with a ball in the park. One day, they see a big sign. The sign says: "Fun Event Today! Games, Prizes, Music and More!"

"Wow, look at that!" Lily says. "Can we go, please?"

"Yes, let's go!" Ben says. "Maybe we can win a prize!"

They run to the event. There are many people and many things to do. They see a big tent with a clown. They see a table with cakes and juice. They see a stage with a band. They see a field with a goal.

"Look, a soccer game!" Ben says. "I want to play!"

"Me too!" Lily says. "Let's join a team!"

They find a team with other kids. They wear red shirts. The other team wears blue shirts. The game starts. Ben and Lily try to kick the ball to the goal. They have fun.

But then, a big boy from the blue team kicks the ball very hard. The ball hits Lily in the face. Lily falls down. She cries.

"Ow, ow, ow!" Lily says. "That hurts!"

Ben runs to Lily. He helps her get up. He hugs her.

"I'm sorry, Lily," Ben says. "Are you okay?"

Lily wipes her tears. She nods.

"I'm okay, Ben," Lily says. "Thank you for being my friend."

They smile at each other. They decide to leave the game. They go to the tent with the clown. The clown makes them laugh. He gives them a balloon. They are happy.

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She lived with her mom, dad, and aunt. Lily loved her aunt very much. Her aunt was kind and always played with her.

One day, Lily's aunt was going to the store. She asked Lily, "Do you want to come with me?" Lily was very happy and said, "Yes, please!" They both put on their coats and went outside.

As they walked to the store, Lily saw a cat stuck in a tree. "Oh no!" she said. Lily's aunt saw the cat too. She knew they had to help. "Let's rush and get help," said her aunt. They ran to a big, strong man who helped get the cat down. The cat was grateful and purred. Lily and her aunt were happy they could help. They continued to the store and had a great day together.

Once upon a time there was a brave little girl named Daniella who loved to explore.

One day Daniella was walking in a forest and came across a strange old structure. She wanted to explore it, but she had to be careful.

Daniella went up to the structure and started to climb it. As she was climbing, she stumbled but she was able to catch herself before she fell down.

"Oh no! I almost fell," Daniella said to herself.

Then she remembered that she had to be careful and continued to climb up the structure.

When she reached the top, Daniella looked around and saw all sorts of amazing things. She was so excited to have found this structure.

From that day forward, Daniella explored the structure almost every day. She was so careful and she never stumbled again!

Once upon a time, there was a healthy boy named Tim. Tim had a red rose that he loved very much. Every day, he would water the rose and watch it grow. One day, a little bug came to live on the rose.

"Hi, I am Zip!" said the bug. "I like your rose. Can I stay here?"

"Yes, you can," said Tim. "But you must be nice to my rose."

Zip and Tim became good friends. They played and talked every day. Zip would tell Tim stories about other bugs and flowers. Tim would laugh and tell Zip stories about his life.

One day, Tim saw that his rose was not looking so good. He asked Zip, "What is wrong with my rose? It looks sad."

Zip said, "Don't worry, Tim. I will help you. We just need to give it more water and love."

So, Tim and Zip worked together to make the rose healthy again. They watered it, talked to it, and even sang to it. Soon, the rose was happy and healthy, just like before. Tim and Zip were very happy, and they knew that they would be friends forever.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved to play with her dolls. One day, Lily's mom said, "Lily, we have to go to the store to buy a new board for our kitchen." Lily didn't want to go to the store because she wanted to keep playing with her dolls. But, she went anyway.

At the store, Lily saw a big candy bar and asked her mom if she could have it. Her mom said no because it was too big and would make her sick. Lily felt sad and said, "I regret not listening to you, Mommy."

On the way home, Lily accidentally dropped the board and it broke into pieces. She felt terrible and started to cry. Her mom told her it was okay and they could buy a new one. They went back to the store and got a new board.

When they got home, Lily's dad fixed the board and they all sat down for dinner. Lily said, "I'm sorry for dropping the board. I promise to be more careful next time." Her parents smiled and told her it was okay. From that day on, Lily always listened to her parents and never regretted it.

There was a little girl called Lily. She loved to ride her tricycle around the garden. She had a pocket too, which she kept all her most special treasures in.

One day, she decided to take her tricycle on a slow ride around the block. She put on her hat, and filled her pocket with shells and leaves.

Lily pedaled slowly, so she could admire the flowers in the park and say hello to the friendly animals. She waved at all the people in the streets as she rode along.

When she had completed the ride, Lily was so happy. She took out all the treasures she had collected and put them back into her pocket. She knew they would make her smile when she saw them again.

Once there was a purple candy. It was so small that everyone wanted to eat it. Every day it would grow bigger and bigger until it was the size of a basketball.

One day, a small girl named Rose saw the candy and said, "Wow, that candy looks delicious!" She wanted to eat it but couldn't get to it because it was too high.

Rose asked her mom for help. Her mom said, "Let's build a ladder so you can reach the candy". So, mom and Rose worked together, and soon enough there was a long, purple ladder reaching up to the candy.

Rose climbed the ladder, grabbed the candy, and said, "Yummy, I could eat this all by myself!". Her mom smiled and said, "Just don't forget to share!"

Once upon a time there was a vine who loved to print things. No matter what anyone said he liked to print things all by himself. He was very independent.

One day, he invited a friend to his house for a play date. His friend was so excited about the visit. When he arrived, the vine showed him all the things he had printed. The friend asked, "What is this?"

The vine replied, "It's my very own print. I made it all by myself. I love to be independent and print things!"

The friend thought it was so neat and asked, "Can I print something too?" The vine said "Yes!" Then the vine and his friend spent the whole day printing together. They were so happy.

The end.

Lila was a little girl who liked to play outside. She had a big yard with many trees and flowers. She also had a friend who lived near her. His name was Ben and he had a red bike.

One day, Lila and Ben decided to go for a ride in the woods. They put on their hats and gloves because it was cold. They rode their bikes along the path and saw many animals. They saw birds, squirrels, rabbits and deer. They said hello to them and smiled.

As they rode deeper into the woods, they saw something different. It was a fox. The fox was orange and white and had a long tail. It looked at them with bright eyes and tilted its head.

"Hello, fox!" Lila said. "Do you want to play with us?"

The fox did not answer. It ran away into the bushes.

"Where are you going, fox?" Ben asked. "Don't be scared. We are nice."

The fox did not come back. Lila and Ben felt sad. They wanted to be friends with the fox.

They decided to leave a gift for the fox. They looked around and found some nuts and berries. They put them in a basket and left it near the bushes where the fox had disappeared.

"Maybe the fox will come back and see our gift," Lila said. "Maybe it will like it and want to play with us."

They rode their bikes back to their homes. They hoped the fox would receive their gift and be happy.

The next day, they went back to the woods. They looked for the basket. It was gone.

"Look!" Ben said. "There are some paw prints on the ground. And some fur on the branch. And some nut shells and berry seeds."

Lila and Ben smiled. They knew the fox had received their gift and enjoyed it.

They heard a rustle in the bushes. They saw the fox peeking out. It wagged its tail and made a soft sound.

"Hello, fox!" Lila and Ben said. "Thank you for coming back. Do you want to play with us?"

The fox nodded and came out of the bushes. It ran around them and licked their hands. It was not scared anymore. It was happy.

Lila and Ben were happy too. They had made a new friend. They played with the fox until it was time to go home. They hugged the fox and said goodbye.

"See you soon, fox!" Lila and Ben said. "We will bring you more gifts."

The fox smiled and waved its tail. It watched them ride away. It was not cold anymore. It was warm.

Once upon a time, there was a little rabbit called Jack. Jack was feeling upset because he couldn't find his friends. He was searching everywhere, but they just weren't turning up.

Jack's mother said: "If you want to find your friends, you must search carefully". So, Jack decided to search the nearby woods carefully. He stepped among the trees, and then noticed a big yellow cushion. He thought that his friends might have been there, so he started to look around it. And then, he heard his friends' voices coming from the cushion!

Turns out, Jack's two friends Sam and Joe were hiding inside the cushion. They had found a nice, warm spot to hide from the cold weather. Jack was so glad to find his friends, and thanked his mother for the advice.

The moral of the story is that you should always search carefully when looking for something important. Even though Jack's friends were really close to him, he still had to look carefully to find them.

Once upon a time there were two friends, Mandy and Jane. Mandy had a pale perfume bottle and was very proud of it. Every day she would take it out and store it in a safe place.

One day, Jane saw the pale perfume bottle and asked Mandy if she could hold it. Mandy said no, and Jane became very sad. She wanted to play with the perfume and smell it.

Mandy tried to explain to Jane why she was not allowed to touch the perfume. She said, “I need to store the perfume in a safe place because it is very special to me.”

Jane was still sad, but she started to understand. She promised to never ask for the perfume again. Mandy was happy and gave Jane a hug. They both smiled, and their friendship was strong again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play in her room with her toys. But sometimes, when it was dark outside, she felt scared. She thought there might be a monster under her bed.

One night, Lily's mom came to tuck her in. She said, "Don't worry, Lily. There are no monsters here. Let's check under the bed together." They looked, but there was nothing there.

Lily felt peaceful and safe. She went to sleep with a smile on her face. But then, in the middle of the night, she heard a strange noise. She got scared again. But this time, she remembered what her mom said. She let herself be brave and looked under the bed. And there it was - a little toy monster that had fallen off the shelf. Lily laughed and went back to sleep, feeling proud of herself for being brave.

Once there was a little boy named Tim who loved to dance. He would always practice a lot and then one day his dream became true. He was going on a big stage to show everyone his moves. When he stepped onto the stage he could feel his heart beating in excitement, and he heard clapping from the people all around. His moves were so soft and graceful that everyone cheered for him.

After a few minutes he was finished dancing, but he wanted to do it all over again. He asked the people if he could come back to the stage soon. Everyone said yes!

So Tim kept practicing and soon it was time to return to the stage. He was more confident this time and his moves were even smoother. Again, the people praised him with thunderous clapping and cheers. This time young Tim was also given a big round of applause as he left the stage.

He went back home knowing that dancing was his true passion, and he couldn't wait to return to the stage again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who was very upset. She had to go to the stadium, but she was sad and didn't want to go.

So she prayed. She prayed for help. She prayed for strength. She prayed for courage.

When she finished praying, she felt better. She was no longer upset. She took a deep breath and walked into the stadium.

Inside, she saw a lot of people cheering and smiling. It made her feel so happy! She knew that if she had stayed upset, she would have missed out on the fun.

So she said a Prayer of thanks and ran off to join the fun!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Sue. Sue was very tired. She had a bucket that she loved very much. Sue would carry her bucket everywhere she went.

One day, Sue was playing with her bucket when a boy named Tom came up to her. Tom wanted to play with the bucket too. He said, "Can I play with your bucket, please?" Sue did not want to share her bucket. She said, "No, this is my bucket!"

Sue and Tom were both sad. Sue's mom saw them and said, "Why don't you both pray and ask for help?" So, Sue and Tom prayed. They asked for a way to play together and be happy.

After they prayed, Sue had an idea. She said, "We can both play with the bucket! We can take turns!" Tom was happy, and they played with the bucket all day. Sue and Tom became good friends and shared the bucket. They were not tired anymore. They had lots of fun together.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to eat vegetables, especially carrots. He would always ask his mom for more carrots.

One day, Timmy went to the garden to pick some carrots. He saw a rough-looking carrot and decided to pick it. As he was picking it, he accidentally blinked and the carrot fell into a hole.

Timmy tried to reach for the carrot, but he couldn't. He then heard a voice from the hole saying, "I warned you not to pick me, now you will never see the light of day again." Timmy was frightened and ran back to his mom.

From that day on, Timmy learned to always listen to warnings and not to pick rough-looking vegetables. The moral of the story is to always be careful and listen to warnings.

Once there was a cool yellow bird who lived in a tree. Every day he would pass by the trees looking for food. One day while he was passing by, he heard a loud noise. He quickly flew over to see what was happening. He saw another yellow bird chasing a bug. The other yellow bird wanted to pass right where the bug was, but the bug wasn't happy about it.

The cool yellow bird quickly flew over to help the bug. He flapped his wings and shouted at the other bird to stop. The other bird got scared and flew away. The cool yellow bird saved the bug and they both thanked him.

The cool yellow bird was happy he could help the bug. From then on, every day he passed by the same tree. The bug was always there to say hello.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys and draw pictures. One day, Lily's mom told her that they were going to visit her aunt who lived far away. Lily was excited because she loved her aunt and always had fun playing with her.

Before leaving, Lily's mom told her to get ready and pack her bag. Lily quickly ran to her room and put her favorite toys and books inside. "Are you ready, Lily?" her mom asked. "Yes, I have my bag," Lily replied.

When they arrived at her aunt's house, Lily ran to give her a big hug. "I'm so happy to see you, Auntie!" Lily exclaimed. They spent the day playing games and having fun. Later that night, when it was time to go to bed, Lily's aunt told her a bedtime story. "Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily," her aunt began.

Lily smiled, knowing that her aunt was talking about her. She listened to the story and fell asleep with a big smile on her face, happy to be with her aunt.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a toy that she loved so much. It was a cute and adorable teddy bear. She played with it every day and took it everywhere she went.

One day, Lily went to a park with her friends. She saw a little boy who didn't have any toys to play with. She felt sad for him and wanted to share her teddy bear with him. But she was too shy to ask him to play with it.

When she got home that day, Lily felt regret for not sharing her toy with the little boy. She realized that it would have made him happy and that it was the right thing to do. From that day on, Lily learned to share her toys with others, and she felt happy knowing that she could make someone else happy too. The moral of the story is that sharing is caring.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to wear her pink cap everywhere she went. One day, she went to the park and met a little boy named Max. Max had a red cap on his head.

"Hi Max, I like your cap," said Lily.

"Thank you, Lily. I like your pink cap too," replied Max.

Lily smiled and they started to play together. They played on the slide, swings and monkey bars. They had so much fun that they didn't even notice the time passing.

When it was time for Lily to go home, Max said, "Goodbye Lily, let's play again tomorrow."

Lily replied, "Yes, let's play again tomorrow. I had so much fun with you today."

Lily went home with a big smile on her face, happy to have made a new friend.

Once upon a time there was a boy who wanted to discover something. He looked everywhere and he found a cat! The cat was so soft and he was so happy. The cat was not scared at all.

The boy went for a walk with the cat. He wanted to show the cat to his friends. But the cat was so curious he ran away and soon the boy lost him.

The boy was sad, but he didn't give up. He kept looking for the cat and he was very determined. Soon he discovered something. It was the cat! He picked him up and he was so relieved.

Now the boy knew that cats can be easy to find with determination. He was so glad he found the cat and they had a happy day together.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved cake and would eat it every day. One day, her mom made a cake for her birthday. It was a big cake with lots of frosting and sprinkles. Lily was very happy and ate a big piece of cake. But when she went to get more, the cake had disappeared! Lily was very sad because she wanted more cake. Her mom told her not to be sad and that they could make more cake together. So, they made another cake and it was even better than the first one. Lily was very happy and ate a big piece of cake again.

One day, a little dog named Max wanted to relax. He saw a big stage in the park. Max thought it looked fun to play on. He jumped on the stage and started to run around.

A dull cat named Tom saw Max on the stage. Tom said, "Max, why are you running on the stage? It is not for playing." Max stopped and looked at Tom. "I just wanted to have fun and relax," Max said.

Tom told Max, "We can relax and have fun without going on the stage. Let's play together in the park instead." Max and Tom played in the park and had a great time. They learned that it is important to respect rules and have fun together.

Once upon a time, there was a little goat who lived on a farm. All the animals on the farm were very happy. One day, the little goat found something special. It was a shiny red chilli! It looked so tasty and spicy!

The little goat was so excited. He couldn't wait to try it. But deep down he was afraid. He nervously put the chilli close to his nose, and took a small sniff. Suddenly, he started to tremble, and quickly put it back down.

The goat's friend, a pig, noticed and waved his hoof. "Why don't you try it?" he said. The goat had an idea. He picked up the chilli again and put it in his mouth, then stuck his thumb out to stop it from going any further.

The pig smiled. "Go on, try it!" The goat hesitated, then mustered all his courage and took a brave little bite. Surprisingly, it wasn't as spicy as he'd thought it would be!

The little goat smiled and jumped around with joy. He'd put his fears aside and found out that there was nothing to be so scared of! He had discovered something incredible. He was now brave and happy, thanks to the tasty spicy chilli!

One day, Ben and Lily went to the zoo with their mom. They saw many animals, like monkeys, elephants, and giraffes. But their favorite was the lion. The lion was big and strong, and had a long mane of hair. He was lying on a rock, looking bored.

"Can we raise a lion, mom?" Ben asked. He wanted to play with the lion and hear him roar.

"No, honey, we can't raise a lion," mom said. "Lions are wild animals, not pets. They need a lot of space and meat, and they can be dangerous."

"But he looks so gloomy," Lily said. She felt sorry for the lion. He had no friends and no toys.

"Maybe he is gloomy because he misses his home," mom said. "Lions live in Africa, where it is warm and sunny, and they have a family called a pride. They hunt and play together."

"Can we go to Africa and see the lions there?" Ben asked.

"Maybe someday, when you are older," mom said. "But for now, we can do something to cheer up the lion here. Do you have any ideas?"

Ben and Lily thought for a moment. Then they had an idea. They ran to the gift shop and bought a big yellow ball. They went back to the lion's cage and threw the ball over the fence. The ball bounced and rolled near the lion. The lion looked at the ball with curiosity. He got up from his rock and walked towards the ball. He sniffed it, then pawed it, then bit it. The ball squeaked and made a funny noise. The lion liked the noise. He started to play with the ball, tossing it and chasing it. He even roared a few times.

Ben and Lily clapped and laughed. They were happy to see the lion having fun. The lion looked at them and smiled. He was not so gloomy anymore.

"See, mom, we made the lion happy," Ben said.

"Yes, you did," mom said. "You were very kind and thoughtful. But remember, he is still a wild animal, not a pet. We can't raise a lion, but we can respect and admire him."

Ben and Lily nodded. They waved goodbye to the lion and thanked him for the show. They left the zoo feeling proud and happy. They had learned a lot about lions and how to care for them.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys, but she always left them on the floor when she was done. One day, her mom told her that she needed to start cleaning up after herself.

Lily didn't want to clean up, but she knew it was the right thing to do. So, she started to lift her toys and put them away. It was hard work, but she felt proud of herself when she was done.

Later that day, Lily's family gathered around the fireplace to tell stories and drink hot cocoa. But, they couldn't start the fire because there was no wood available. Lily remembered that she had some sticks outside that she could use. She went outside, gathered the sticks, and brought them back to the fireplace.

Everyone was so happy that Lily had helped out. They all learned that it's important to clean up after yourself and to help others when you can.

Mum and Dad were in a hurry. They were going to the garden to do some work. When they arrived, the garden was very untidy. There were weeds everywhere and the grass was too long. Mum and Dad started to work. They trimmed the hedges and cut the grass. They tidied up the flower beds, and they thinned out the weeds.

When they finished, the garden looked much better. It was tidy and neat. Mum and Dad were happy with their work. They smiled and sat down to rest. They enjoyed the sun and the quiet of the garden. They were glad that they had hurried so much.

Lily liked to fix things. She had a box of tools and some old toys that she could take apart and put back together. She was very creative and made new things from the parts. She made a car with wings, a robot with a hat, and a doll with a flashlight.

One day, Lily wanted to fix her brother's bike. It had a flat tire and a broken bell. Lily thought she could make it better. She took her tools and went to the garage. She did not ask her brother if she could fix his bike. She thought it was a surprise.

But her brother was not happy when he saw what Lily did. She had taken off the tire and the bell and put them on her car with wings. She had also painted the bike pink and put stickers on it. Her brother was angry and yelled at her. He said she ruined his bike and he did not want it anymore.

Lily was sad and sorry. She did not mean to make her brother mad. She wanted to help him. She realized she should have asked him first. She said she was sorry and asked him if they could fix the bike together. Her brother calmed down and said yes. He said he liked some of her ideas, but not all of them. He said they could share some of the parts and make both the bike and the car with wings better.

Lily and her brother worked together to fix the bike and the car with wings. They used some of Lily's tools and some of her brother's tools. They were both creative and had fun. They learned to respect each other's things and to ask before they fix them. They also learned to cooperate and to appreciate each other's skills. They hugged and thanked each other. They rode the bike and the car with wings around the yard. They were happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. He loved to play outside with his friends. One day, they all went to the park to have fun.

While playing, Tim saw a small pebble in his shoe. He sat down and tried to remove it. His friends watched and were envious because the pebble was so pretty. It was shiny and smooth, just like a little treasure.

Tim shared the pebble with his friends, and they all took turns looking at it. They played with the pebble in the park all day, and had lots of fun. In the end, they all went home with big smiles on their faces.

Once upon a time there was a snowman. Every day the snowman would dance and play in the snow. One day, a little girl saw the snowman. She was so delighted that she began to applaud.

The Snowman felt so happy! He looked around and thanked the little girl with a smile.

The Snowman was so excited, he started to dance in circles. But suddenly, he started to feel strange. A nasty problem had been created - the snow had turned into a disgusting slime.

The little girl was sad. She said, "Oh no, the snowman's snow has turned bad. Now he won't be able to play."

The Snowman tried his best to keep dancing, but soon he became too tired. Sadly, the snowman melted away.

The little girl knew that this was the end for the snowman. She said goodbye to him and sadly walked away.

Lisa loved spaghetti. She liked to eat it with cheese and sauce. She also liked to play with it. She made long strings with her fork and twirled them around. She made funny shapes and faces with the noodles. She had fun with spaghetti.

But Mom did not like it when Lisa played with her food. She said it was messy and wasteful. She said Lisa had to eat her spaghetti, not play with it. She said Lisa could play with her toys after dinner. She did not permit Lisa to play with her food.

One day, Lisa had a new idea. She asked Mom if she could make a picture with her spaghetti. She said she would eat it after she finished. She said it was like art. She said it would be fine.

Mom thought about it. She liked art. She liked Lisa. She wanted Lisa to be happy and creative. She also wanted Lisa to eat her spaghetti. She decided to give Lisa a chance. She said yes, Lisa could make a picture with her spaghetti. But she had to eat it after she finished. She said it was a deal.

Lisa was happy. She thanked Mom and started to make her picture. She used spaghetti for the hair, cheese for the eyes, sauce for the mouth, and peas for the nose. She made a face that looked like Mom. She showed it to Mom and said, "Look, Mom, it's you!"

Mom smiled. She said, "That's very nice, Lisa. You are a good artist. And now, you are a good eater. Let's eat your picture together." She helped Lisa cut the spaghetti and put it on their plates. They ate the spaghetti and said it was yummy. They both had fun with spaghetti.

Once upon a time there were two best friends, Chris and Jane. Chris was a small boy and Jane was a brave girl. They always wanted to fight and play together.

One day they went to the market, and there they saw a beautiful flute. They both wanted it, so they began to fight over it.

Chris said, “I should get the flute, because I am the strongest. ”

But Jane was determined and said, “No, I should get it, because I am the most brave.”

They argued until an old man said, “Why don't you share the flute? That way, you can both be proud.”

Chris and Jane looked at each other and smiled. They decided to share the flute, and became even better friends!

Once upon a time, there was a young boy who wanted to win the biggest race in the country. He worked very hard for many weeks and practised every day. On the day of the race, the boy arrived but he was shocked when he saw the track. It was so filthy that he almost didn't want to race! But the boy was determined to win, so he started the race. He ran as fast as he could and soon he was in the lead. Everyone was cheering for him and he crossed the finish line first! He had won the race and the country was so happy! The boy was overjoyed and happy to have won.

Once upon a time there was a girl named Polly. She was only three years old and she liked to make something special. She had a big pot filled with dough. She mixed the dough with some other stuff and then she put it in the oven.

When it was done, Polly was very excited. She was nervous too. She wanted to make sure she kept her dough safe. So she kept her eye on it all the time. She watched it, she waited, and then finally it was done.

Polly was so happy. She took it out of the oven and it smelled so good. She put it on a plate and smiled. She was proud that she was able to keep her dough safe.

Once upon a time, there was a bunny named Sam. Sam lived in a small house in the forest with his paw, who loved him very much.

One day, Sam did something wrong and his paw was angry. Sam was very upset, he wanted to make it right, but he didn’t know how. He wanted to say sorry to his paw, but he was too scared.

So Sam decided to do something special. He asked the birds to bring him some brightly coloured flowers. He made a big bouquet and gave it to his paw, who was very happy.

His paw was so happy, he said he was going to forgive Sam. He said that sometimes it was difficult to say sorry, but it was important to do so. Sam was so happy - his paw accepted his apology and he was forgiven!

From then on, Sam and his paw never had a disagreement. They were always happy and enjoyed spending time together. Sam had learned a valuable lesson about forgiveness.

Once upon a time, there was a ghost. He was busy all day, acting like a ghost. He was busy scaring people and making scary noises. He liked waking up early in the morning and playing his ghost games.

At night he would act even more silly. He would fly around from place to place and laugh as he flew. He thought it was so fun to see people run away when they saw him! He acted so silly that many people were scared of him.

One day, he decided to take a break and have some fun. He decided to play hide and seek! He hid behind a tree and waited to be found. After a while, some children found him and they were so excited. They laughed and ran around playing with him.

When it was time to go home, the children said their goodbyes. The ghost smiled as they waved goodbye and he wished they could stay. He knew that it was time for them to go, but he was still happy they took the time to have some fun with him.

The busy ghost was glad that he got to act silly and have a good time. He knew that he couldn't stay out too late or people would be scared. But for today he was happy just acting like a ghost with the children.

Sammy was getting ready for bed. He went into his room, which was modern and very nice. Then he remembered his bed-time routine. He brushed his teeth and got into his pajamas. Then he picked up all of his toys and put them in their toy-box. He had completed his cleaning and was happy and ready for bed.

He walked over to his father to say goodnight. His father gave him a hug and told him to have sweet dreams. Sammy said goodnight and went back to his room. He climbed into bed and hugged his favorite stuffed animal.

He whispered goodnight to his room and his stuffed animal and closed his eyes. Now that he had completed all of his bed-time routine, he was sure to have sweet dreams.

Lily and Tom were playing in the garden. They had a little house with a table and chairs. They liked to pretend they were having tea with their toys.

"Would you like some tea, Mr. Bear?" Lily asked, pouring water from a plastic pot.

"Yes, please, Lily. You are very kind," Tom said, making his bear talk.

They sipped their tea and talked about their day. They heard a loud noise from the sky. It was a plane flying very fast.

"Wow, look at that!" Tom said, pointing up.

Lily looked too. She saw the plane leave a white line behind it. She wondered where it was going.

"Maybe it is going to a faraway place," she said.

"Maybe it is going to see the stars," Tom said.

They watched the plane until it was gone. Then they heard their mom call them.

"Lily, Tom, time to come in. It's getting dark and cold," she said.

They put their toys away and ran to the house. Their mom gave them a hug and a kiss.

"Did you have fun in the garden?" she asked.

"Yes, mom. We had tea with Mr. Bear and we saw a plane," Lily said.

"That sounds lovely. Now, let's go inside and settle down for the night. You can have some warm milk and a story before bed," she said.

They followed their mom inside. They felt cozy and happy. They did not mind the harsh wind that blew outside. They had each other and their mom. They had a good day.

Lily and Tom are twins. They like to play together. Today, they want to dress up as cowboys and cowgirls. They find hats, boots, and scarves in their closet. They put them on and look at each other.

"You look good, Lily," Tom says.

"You look good, too, Tom," Lily says.

They go to the living room and pretend to ride horses. They make noises like "yee-haw" and "giddy-up". They have fun.

Mom calls them from the kitchen. "Lily, Tom, dinner is ready. Come and wash your hands."

They run to the kitchen and see a big steak on the table. They love steak. It is their favorite food.

"Wow, Mom, this steak looks good," Tom says.

"Thank you, Mom, this steak smells good," Lily says.

Mom smiles and cuts the steak for them. They sit down and eat. They say "yum" and "delicious". They are happy.

After dinner, they hug Mom and say "thank you". They go back to their room and take off their hats, boots, and scarves. They put them back in the closet. They brush their teeth and get ready for bed.

Mom comes and tucks them in. She kisses them and says "good night, my cowboys and cowgirls. I love you."

They say "good night, Mom. We love you, too."

They close their eyes and dream of horses and steaks. They are good twins.

Once upon a time there was a boy who liked to wander in the woods. One day he set off, curious and excited to explore the unknown. As he looked around, the boy saw many harmless creatures, all enjoying their day in the sun. The boy was careful and stepped lightly, looking around him the whole time. He stumbled across a meadow with the prettiest flowers he had ever seen. He could have stayed there all day. But soon, the wind started to blow and the boy decided it was time to go. He bid farewell to the birds and the butterflies and gracefully wandered back to his home.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Star. Star was three and loved helping the people in her family prepare dinners.

One day, Star asked her Mum what she was making for dinner. Mum said she was making a very tasty cake. Star was so excited!

"Can I help?" Star asked.

Mum said, "Yes of course, what would you like to do first?"

Star said, "I want to measure the ingredients, I can do that with the scale!"

Mum smiled, "That's a great idea," she said.
