They read the book together and learned more about the thumb-saurus and other dinosaurs. They had fun unpacking their bag and sharing their toys. They were happy to visit their grandma for the weekend.

Anna and Ben were twins who liked to play in the garden. They had a big sandbox where they could dig and make castles. One day, they found a shiny metal thing in the sand. It looked like a door with a handle.

"Let's open it and see what's inside," Ben said.

"Maybe it's a secret underground place," Anna said.

They pulled the handle and the door opened. They saw a dark hole with stairs going down.

"Wow, let's go and explore," Ben said.

He went down the stairs, holding a flashlight. Anna followed him, feeling scared.

They walked for a long time in the dark. They saw pipes and wires and machines. They heard strange noises and smelled bad things.

"This is not fun, this is scary," Anna said. "I want to go back."

"Me too," Ben said. "But I don't know how. We are lost."

They started to cry. They wished they had not opened the door. They regretted being curious.

They heard footsteps and saw a light. A man came towards them. He wore a helmet and a uniform. He looked angry.

"Who are you and what are you doing here?" he asked.

"We are sorry, mister," Ben said. "We were playing in the garden and we found a door and we opened it and we came down and we got lost and we are scared and we want to go home."

The man sighed. He was not angry, he was worried.

"You are very lucky I found you," he said. "This is a dangerous place. It's not for children. It's for workers who fix the water and the electricity. You could have been hurt or trapped. Come with me, I'll take you back to the door."

He took them by the hand and led them up the stairs. He closed the door behind them and locked it.

"Next time, don't touch things that are not yours," he said. "And keep your garden tidy. You never know what you might find."

Anna and Ben nodded. They thanked the man and ran back to their house. They hugged their mom and dad and told them what happened. They were happy to be safe and warm. They learned their lesson. They never opened the door again.

Lily and Tom are friends. They like to play outside. One day, they see a big rain cloud. It is dark and scary. They hear a loud boom. It is thunder.

They run to the big tree. They hide under the leaves. They hope the rain will not find them. They are afraid of the rain. They do not like to get wet.

But the rain is very strong. It falls from the sky. It makes the ground wet and muddy. It makes the leaves wet and heavy. It makes the tree shake and bend.

Lily and Tom see a small bird. It is on a branch. It is wet and cold. It cannot fly. It chirps and cries. It needs help.

Lily and Tom want to help the bird. They are brave and kind. They climb the tree. They are careful and slow. They reach the branch. They take the bird in their hands. It is soft and warm. It stops chirping and crying. It is happy.

They rescue the bird. They bring it down the tree. They find a dry and cozy place. They make a nest for the bird. They give it some seeds and water. They make it feel better.

The rain stops. The sun comes out. It makes a rainbow. It is bright and pretty. Lily and Tom smile. They are proud and happy. They have a new friend. The bird sings and thanks them. It is sweet and grateful.

Once upon a time, there was a smelly cat. The cat loved to play with cardboard. One day, the cat found a big cardboard box in the yard. The cat was very happy and wanted to play with it all day.

But, there was a problem. A dog lived next door. The dog did not like the cat. The dog saw the cat playing with the cardboard and wanted it too. The dog and the cat began to fight over the cardboard box.

The cat had an idea. The cat tried to reverse the box to hide inside. But the dog was too strong. The dog took the cardboard box away from the cat. The cat was very sad and had no more cardboard to play with. The end.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Lucy. She was 3 years old and very curious. One day, she was in the house when she realized that she needed to go to the toilet. She got up and walked to the toilet, looking around curiously. When she got there she was so amazed. She had never seen such a big, shiny toilet before! She couldn't believe how big and colorful it was. She was so excited, she ran to tell her mom. She was so happy that she had realized she needed to use the toilet. She was so proud of herself.

Once upon a time there was a bunny called Furry. Furry was very excited and couldn't wait to explore the forest.

Furry hopped and hopped until he found a pond. He settled near the edge and started to drink the cool, clear water. Suddenly, Furry saw something oily floating on top of the water. He nibbled the oily thing and it tasted really bad. Furry felt sick and he went to settle on the grass to rest.

Unfortunately, the oil had made Furry very sick. As the hours went by, he felt worse and worse. Furry sadly passed away surrounded by the forest he had been so excited about exploring.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the bright sunshine. One day, she went on an adventure in the forest and got her dress all dirty.

When she got home, her mom saw her dress and said, "Oh no, Lily! Your dress is dirty. Let's wipe it clean."

Lily's mom got a wet cloth and wiped the dirt off her dress. Then, she tied a pretty bow around Lily's waist.

Lily looked at herself in the mirror and said, "Wow, I look so pretty! Thank you, Mom!"

Her mom smiled and said, "You're welcome, Lily. Now go outside and play some more!"

Lily ran outside, feeling happy and clean in her bright dress. She played until the sun went down and it was time for bed.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Jane. Jane's mommy always read her stories at night before she went to sleep. But sometimes, scary dreams came to her, like a big nightmare. Jane was very afraid.

One night Jane told her mommy that she had a scary dream with a nightmare in it. Then, her mommy said, "Don't be scared, sweetheart. I have a special thing that can make your scary dream go away."

Jane was curious, so she asked, "What is it?" Her mommy answered, "A nice spin! Just close your eyes and think nice thoughts, and spin around slowly. Your nightmare will go away like magic."

So Jane gave it a try. She closed her eyes and thought nice thoughts, and then she spun around very slowly. And it worked! All of a sudden, her nightmare was gone!

Jane smiled and said to her mommy, "That was nice! I'll never forget my special spin."

Once upon a time, there were two best friends who loved to play. Their names were Toni and Jack. One day, when Toni and Jack were playing in the park, Toni saw something shiny near a tall tree. She ran over to it, but Jack followed her and said, "What is it?" Toni looked down and saw a bag of sugar. She smiled and said, "Let's take it home." Jack was very shy and he shook his head no. He said, "We can't steal it. That's not nice." Toni picked up the sugar and said, "Come on. Nobody will know!" But Jack still said no, and even though Toni was sad, she knew Jack was right. So they left the bag of sugar behind and went back to playing.

Once upon a time there was a little boy called Peter. One day Peter went for a walk in the countryside. He walked and walked and soon he saw something strange. There were lots of peppers growing on a bush! So Peter decided to pick some and he filled his pockets with as many as he could.

On his way home he heard a noise. It was a strange sound and it made Peter panic. He started to run but the peppers kept bouncing out of his pockets. Before long he had lost them all!

Peter was very sad that he had lost his peppers but then he noticed something useful. There were lots of pepper plants growing near where the peppers had bounced out of his pocket. Peter was very happy! He picked some more peppers and made his way home with a pocket full of peppers.

He was so relieved he had found more peppers, he never wanted to panic like that again! So from then on, he always remembered to be careful when he was picking peppers.

Once there was a ghost. He liked to mail things. Every day he put things in envelopes, sealed them up and posted them to far away places. But one day he got very worried. He weren't sure if his letter would make it to its destination. He had put something very special in the envelope but he weren't sure if his mailman friend would be able to deliver it.

He sat and waited by the mailbox for what felt like forever. But then finally he saw his mailman friend walking down the road and waving his mailbag. He was so relieved! He had been worried for so long.

He waved to his mailman friend and watched as he walked towards him. His mailman friend smiled and said ‘hello.’ He handed the ghost an envelope and said ‘here it is!’ The ghost was so happy to see it. He smiled and said ‘thank you!’

The ghost opened the envelope and inside was the special thing he had been worried about. He was so happy that the mailman had delivered it safely. ‘Thank you!’ he said again. The ghost waved goodbye to the mailman and hugged the envelope. He was so relieved!

Sam and Mia were hungry. They wanted to eat pizza for dinner. But Mom said no. She said pizza was not good for them. She said they had to eat soup and salad.

Sam and Mia did not like soup and salad. They made faces and said yuck. They did not want to eat their dinner. They wanted to eat pizza.

Mom was tired. She had a long day at work. She did not want to argue with Sam and Mia. She said they had to eat what she made or go to bed hungry.

Sam and Mia were angry. They did not listen to Mom. They sneaked out of the kitchen and went to the living room. They saw a box of pizza on the table. It was from last night. Mom had forgotten to put it away.

Sam and Mia smiled. They opened the box and saw four slices of pizza. They grabbed two slices each and ran to their room. They closed the door and locked it. They bit into the pizza and said yum.

Mom heard a noise. She went to the living room and saw the empty box of pizza. She knew what Sam and Mia had done. She was very mad. She went to their room and knocked on the door. She said, "Open the door right now! You are in big trouble!"

Sam and Mia heard Mom. They were scared. They did not want to face Mom. They hid under the bed and squeezed each other. They hoped Mom would go away. But Mom did not go away. She had a key. She opened the door and saw Sam and Mia under the bed. She said, "Come out of there! You have to say sorry and go to bed without dessert!"

Sam and Mia came out of the bed. They looked at Mom. They felt bad. They said sorry to Mom. They gave her a hug and a kiss. They said they loved her. Mom said she loved them too. She said they had to learn to eat healthy and listen to her. She said she was sorry for being tired and grumpy. She said they could have pizza once in a while, but not every night.

Sam and Mia nodded. They understood. They said they would try to eat better and obey Mom. They said they were sorry for making Mom mad. They said they were tired too. They asked Mom if they could go to bed.

Mom said yes. She said good night to Sam and Mia. She tucked them in and kissed them. She turned off the light and closed the door. She smiled and said to herself, "They are good kids. They just need some guidance. And maybe some pizza once in a while."

Anna and Ben were twins who liked to travel. They had a big suitcase with wheels that they could pull around. One day, they decided to travel to the attic, where they had never been before.

"Let's go and see what's up there," said Anna, who was brave and curious.

"OK, but be careful," said Ben, who was shy and cautious.

They climbed the stairs and opened the door. The attic was dark and dusty. They saw many old things, like boxes, books, and clothes. They also saw many cobwebs, which were sticky and white.

"Look, a cobweb!" said Anna, and touched one with her finger.

"Yuck, don't touch that!" said Ben, and pulled her hand away.

But it was too late. The cobweb was not empty. It had a big, furry spider inside, who was angry and scared. The spider jumped out of the cobweb and landed on Anna's hair.

"Aaaah!" screamed Anna, and shook her head.

"Aaaah!" screamed Ben, and ran to help her.

They tried to get the spider off, but it was too fast and too furry. It crawled all over Anna's face and neck, and bit her ear.

"Ow, ow, ow!" cried Anna, and fell to the floor.

"Get off, get off, get off!" yelled Ben, and slapped the spider with his hand.

The spider finally let go and ran away. Anna and Ben hugged each other and cried. They had never been so scared in their lives.

They decided to never travel to the attic again. They ran down the stairs and told their mom what happened. She gave them a hug and a band-aid and a cookie.

"Next time, don't touch the cobwebs," she said.

"We won't, we promise," they said.

They learned their lesson. They still liked to travel, but only to nice and safe places.

Once there was a little girl named Jenny who loved to go for car rides with her mom. She always asked to go fast, but her mom said it was too dangerous.

One special day, Jenny and her mom went for a ride. As the car started to go, Jenny said "Faster! Faster!" Her mom smiled and said, "Okay, but just a little bit, okay?"

Jenny watched as the car started to pour on speed. She could feel the orange wind blowing through her hair. The car was going so fast that Jenny almost forgot to be scared.

Soon they reached a hill and Jenny's mom slowed the car down. Jenny smiled, feeling the wind and speed in her cheeks. She said, "Let's do that again!" Her mom was so proud of Jenny.

The two turned around the car and Jenny watched in amazement as her mom poured on the speed again. Jenny felt so happy and they drove back home laughing.

One day, an Elephant and his friend Wolf went on a walk in the forest. Wolf said, “I bet I can stand on the biggest log.” Elephant said, “I don’t think so. It looks too big!”

They looked around and found a very pretty log near some tall grass. Wolf said, “I can do it!” Elephant watched as his friend stood on both feet on top of the log. Wolf beamed. Elephant cheered.

After that, they continued their walk through the forest. But they still stopped to look at the pretty log every time they passed by.

One day, Peter went on a journey. As he walked, he discovered some birds singing in a tree. Their song filled the air with peace and he smiled.

Next, he met a dog playing in the grass. It was reliable and kind, and Peter was so happy.

As he kept walking, he saw a beautiful lake. It was so peaceful that Peter wanted to stay and explore. He looked around and saw lots of animals living happily.

Peter was glad to have discovered so much peace. He knew it would be a place he could always rely on.

Once there was a little girl named Sarah. She had long brown hair and big blue eyes. She was sad one day because she had scraped her leg. It hurt when she walked so Sarah stayed in her room.

Then, Sarah's mom came into the room and said "Let me spray your leg." Sarah was scared but her mom told her it would make her leg feel better. So Sarah said ok.

Mom took out a spray bottle and sprayed the scraped leg. Sarah's leg felt cool and it made the scraped area less sore. Sarah smiled and said thank you to her mom.

The next day her leg felt much better and Sarah was no longer sad. She could walk around and play. Mom smiled and said "I'm glad the spray helped your leg to feel better." Sarah agreed, and she was glad that the spray had made her leg feel better too.

Jill and Ben were twins who liked to play outside. One day, they saw a big pit in the ground. It looked like fun, so they ran to it and jumped in. They laughed and rolled in the dirt.

"Look, I found a shiny rock!" Jill said, holding up a glittery stone.

"Wow, that's so fancy!" Ben said, admiring the rock. "Can I see it?"

"Sure, here you go," Jill said, handing him the rock.

But as Ben took the rock, he slipped and fell. He hurt his knee and started to cry.

"Ow, ow, ow!" he wailed. "It hurts!"

Jill felt sorry for her brother. She climbed out of the pit and ran to get their mom.

"Mom, mom, Ben fell and hurt his knee!" she shouted.

Mom came quickly and saw Ben in the pit. She picked him up and hugged him.

"Shh, shh, it's okay, Ben," she said. "Let me see your knee."

She looked at his knee and saw a small cut. She cleaned it with a cloth and put a band-aid on it.

"There, all better," she said. "Now, relax and stop crying."

Ben sniffled and nodded. He felt better with mom's hug and band-aid.

"Thank you, mom," he said.

Mom smiled and kissed him.

"You're welcome, Ben," she said. "And thank you, Jill, for being a good sister and getting me."

Jill smiled too. She was glad Ben was okay.

"Can I keep the shiny rock?" she asked.

"Of course, you can," mom said. "But next time, be careful when you play in the pit. It can be dangerous."

Jill and Ben agreed. They learned that playing in the pit was fun, but they had to be safe and help each other. They also learned that mom was always there to make them feel better. They hugged mom and each other and went home with the fancy rock.

Once upon a time, there was an old man who loved to pass his time fishing by the river. One day, he caught a big fish, but it was too strong for him to handle. He tried and tried, but the fish wouldn't surrender.

Suddenly, a little boy came by and saw the old man struggling. "Can I help you?" asked the boy. "Yes, please," said the old man. The boy took the fishing rod and pulled the fish out of the water.

"Wow, you're strong!" said the old man. "Thank you," said the boy. "I like to help people." The old man smiled and gave the boy the fish as a reward. "You can have this fish for dinner," he said. The boy was very happy and said, "Thank you, I love fish!"

From that day on, the old man and the boy became good friends. They would often pass their time fishing together by the river, and the old man would tell the boy stories about his adventures when he was young. The boy loved listening to the old man's stories, and the old man loved having someone to share them with.

Once upon a time, there was a girl with magical powers. She was very independent and could do anything she wanted on her own.

One day, the girl wanted to go on an adventure. She set off in search of a special jewel.

She explored the forest and fields until she came upon a magical cave. She crept inside and discovered the jewel she had been searching for!

Alas, her excitement was short lived as she had forgotten to bring anything to carry the jewel in.

In a moment of independence and cleverness, she used her magical powers to make a basket of leaves appear. She put the jewel safely inside and carried it home.

The girl was delighted to finally have the jewel, and she never forgot to bring something to carry treasures in again!

Tommy liked to watch the fisherman on the lake. He saw him throw his net and pull out many fish. Tommy wanted to catch fish too. He asked his mom if he could go with the fisherman.

"No, Tommy, you are too little to go on the boat. The fisherman is busy and needs to work. You can play with your toys here on the shore," his mom said.

But Tommy did not listen. He ran away from his mom and followed the fisherman. He climbed on the boat when the fisherman was not looking. He hid under a soft blanket.

The fisherman did not know Tommy was on the boat. He sailed away from the shore. He threw his net again and again. He caught many fish. He was happy.

But Tommy was not happy. He was scared. The boat was rocking and the water was loud. He missed his mom and his toys. He wanted to go back. He started to cry.

The fisherman heard Tommy's cry. He lifted the blanket and saw Tommy. He was angry.

"Who are you? What are you doing here? How did you get on my boat?" he shouted.

Tommy was more scared. He sobbed and said, "I'm sorry, mister. I wanted to catch fish with you. But I don't like it. I want my mom. Please take me back."

The fisherman sighed. He felt sorry for Tommy. He said, "You should not have come on my boat without asking. You could have fallen in the water or hurt yourself. You should listen to your mom. She knows what is best for you. Come, I will take you back. But you have to promise me to never do this again."

Tommy nodded. He said, "I promise, mister. I'm sorry. Thank you for taking me back."

The fisherman turned the boat around. He sailed back to the shore. He gave Tommy to his mom. She hugged him and scolded him. She said, "Tommy, you scared me so much. You should never run away from me. You should always stay with me. You could have been lost or in danger. You should be more careful and obedient."

Tommy said, "I'm sorry, mom. I learned my lesson. I will never run away from you again. I love you, mom."

The fisherman smiled and said, "You are a good boy, Tommy. I hope you will remember this day and never forget. Fishing is not for little kids. It is hard work and risky. Maybe when you are older, you can come with me. But for now, you should play with your toys and enjoy your childhood."

Tommy thanked the fisherman and said goodbye. He went to play with his toys. He was happy. He had a new friend and a new story. He also had a new respect for the fisherman and his mom. He learned to settle for what he had and not to be greedy or curious. He learned to be grateful and obedient. He learned a lot that day.

Sandy was a little girl of three. She had a gray teddy bear that she loved very much. One day, Sandy was playing outside in the garden. She saw a bee and decided to catch it. Suddenly, the bee gave Sandy a shock! It stung her and she screamed.

Sandy began to cry. She was scared and angry. She picked up her teddy bear and slapped it hard. She ran inside to her mom. Mom was very surprised to see the bear. She asked Sandy what had happened. Sandy told her about the bee.

Mom hugged Sandy and kissed her forehead. She said that everything was alright. Then she gave the bear a big hug and told Sandy to take care of it.

Sandy had learned a lesson that day. She promised herself that she would never slap her bear again. From then on, Sandy treated her little gray teddy bear with lots of care and love.

Once upon a time, there lived an enthusiastic girl called Daisy. Every morning Daisy would bow to the sun and say a cheery hello. She was always in a very good mood and brightened up everyone's day.

One day however, Daisy started to worry. She had a big test coming up at school and she wanted to do it perfectly. She started to fidget and couldn’t decide what to do. She asked a friend for help.

The friend said, "Daisy, why don't you close your eyes and bow to the sun. Then your worries will wash away."

Daisy listened to her friend, and decided to try it. She closed her eyes and bowed to the sun. She felt a sense of calmness and peace, which replaced her worries.

The next day, she felt more enthusiastic than ever and hosted a party to celebrate. Everyone at the party was impressed with how happy she was and asked her to share her secret. Daisy said, “Just bow to the sun.”

The End.

Once upon a time, there was a little gray mouse named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his friends and go on adventures. One day, Timmy and his friends had a meeting to plan their next adventure. They were all excited and happy.

But then, a big, scary cat came and scattered all of Timmy's friends. Timmy was all alone and scared. He tried to run away, but the cat caught him and ate him.

The moral of the story is that sometimes bad things happen and we can't control them. But we can always try to be brave and do our best, even when things are scary.

Once there was a naughty little bear called Sammy. He loved to print pictures everyday. He always asked his mommy to bring him oil to help him with his printing.

One day, Sammy was feeling really naughty and he used so much oil that the whole bottle was empty. His mommy told him not to use so much oil, but he did not listen.

Suddenly, Sammy heard a strange noise. There was a printer man outside the window. He was carrying a magical backpack full of oil! Sammy was so excited and quickly called for his mommy.

His mommy opened the window and the printer man gave them a new bottle of oil. Sammy thanked the printer man and promised he would use the oil more wisely from now on.

From that day on, Sammy made sure to use the oil responsibly when printing his pictures.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Sally. Sally loved to play outside in the rain. She would jump in puddles and catch raindrops on her tongue. One day, Sally's mom gave her a new coat with shiny buttons. Sally was so happy and couldn't wait to wear it outside.

As Sally was playing in the rain, she noticed a little worm on the ground. Sally wanted to pick up the worm and play with it, but her hands were wet and she couldn't squeeze it. She saw a button on her coat and thought it would be a good idea to use it to pick up the worm.

But when Sally tried to pick up the worm with the button, it didn't work. The button was too small and the worm was too slimy and wet. Sally realized that it was not a good idea to use things for something they were not made for. She learned that it's important to use the right tools for the right job.

Once upon a time, a cute little dog named Spot lived in a small house. Spot loved to play outside in the sun. One hot day, Spot felt very hot and wanted to find some shade. He looked around and saw a big tree with lots of shade under it.

Spot went to the tree and sat down in the cool shade. He felt much better. Then, he saw a little bird named Tweetie. Tweetie was sad because she lost her nest. Spot wanted to help Tweetie solve her problem.

Spot asked Tweetie, "Where did you see your nest last?" Tweetie said, "I saw it near the red flowers." Spot and Tweetie went to the red flowers and found the nest. Tweetie was so happy, she sang a song for Spot. They both played together in the shade for the rest of the day.

Once upon a time, there was a boat. It was empty but the sea was nice and blue.

One day, a little girl got on the boat. She was so happy to be sailing and saw the world around her. Suddenly, the sky changed from blue to grey. Storm clouds were forming and the sea started to move.

The little girl was scared, but she stayed in the boat. It started bouncing up and down and she could feel the wind. The waves got bigger and bigger and the boat continued to rock.

Finally, the storm passed and the little girl was relieved. The sea turned back to blue and she was safe. Now, the boat was not empty anymore: the little girl was inside and the adventure had just begun!

Once upon a time, there was a little bird. She was very happy and loved to play. She had bright purple feathers and loved singing sweet songs.

One day, the bird was out flying in the warm sunshine. Suddenly, she heard a loud noise from the ground below. It was a thief! He was trying to steal some of the other animals' food.

The little bird was scared and flew away quickly. She landed on a branch and cried out for help. "Help, help! someone stop the thief!"

Just then, a big lion came out of the forest. He was strong and brave. "Don't worry bird," he said. "I'll lay him out with one powerful swipe of my paw!"

And with a single powerful swat, the lion scared away the thief. All the animals cheered, and the little bird was so thankful! From that day on, the bird spread the word of the lion's bravery and watched over the other animals.

Lily and Ben liked to play in the park. They liked to run, jump, slide and swing. They also liked to look for things in the grass and under the trees. One day, they found a big oak. It had many branches and leaves. It was very old and strong.

They decided to climb the oak. They used their hands and feet to go up and up. They felt very brave and happy. They saw birds, squirrels and bugs on the oak. They also saw the whole park and the sky. They waved to their mom, who was sitting on a bench.

But then, they heard a loud noise. It was a big truck. It came to the park. It had a long arm with a saw. It stopped near the oak. The man in the truck got out. He put on a helmet and gloves. He looked at the oak. He said, "This oak is too old and sick. It might fall and hurt someone. I have to cut it down."

Lily and Ben were scared and sad. They liked the oak. They did not want it to go. They shouted, "Stop! Stop! Don't cut the oak! It is our friend! It is useful! It gives us shade and fun and homes for animals! Please, stop!"

The man heard them. He looked up and saw them on the oak. He was surprised and worried. He said, "Hey, kids, what are you doing up there? You have to come down. It is not safe. I have to do my job."

Lily and Ben did not want to come down. They hugged the oak. They said, "No, no, we won't come down. We love the oak. We want to save it. Please, don't cut it. Please, please, please."

The man did not know what to do. He called their mom. She came and saw them on the oak. She was also surprised and worried. She said, "Lily, Ben, listen to me. You have to come down. The man is right. The oak is old and sick. It might fall and hurt you or someone else. It is not your fault. It is not his fault. It is just how things are. Sometimes, we have to say goodbye to things we love. But we can always remember them and be thankful for them. Please, come down. I will help you."

Lily and Ben looked at their mom. They looked at the man. They looked at the oak. They felt very sad. But they also knew their mom was right. They slowly came down from the oak. They said, "We are sorry, oak. We will miss you. Thank you for everything. Goodbye, oak."

The man said, "Thank you, kids. You are very brave and kind. I am sorry, too. I don't like to cut trees. But sometimes, I have to. I will try to be gentle and quick. I will also plant a new tree here. Maybe, one day, you can come back and play with it."

Lily and Ben nodded. They hugged their mom. They watched the man cut the oak. They cried a little. But they also smiled a little. They knew the oak had a good life. They knew they had a good memory. They knew they had a good mom. They knew they had each other. They knew they would be okay.

Once upon a time, there were two friends called Happy and Wish. Every day Happy and Wish played together and yesterday was no different. They ran around and laughed a lot but then Wish made a big mistake.

Happy made a toy boat for them to play with and Wish accidentally broke it. Wish wanted to confess that he did it, but was afraid to say sorry. So Happy got angry and chased Wish away.

Wish felt so sad and unhappy, but he knew that he should forgive. So he went back to Happy and said sorry. But Happy was still so angry that he didn't want to forgive.

Happy thought that he was not fit enough to forgive Wish. So he ran away and left Wish all alone. This was very sad and Wish realized that it is very important to forgive if someone makes a mistake. Unfortunately, that was Happy and Wish's last day playing together.

One morning, Mark woke up early. He was excited because he had a new puppy! He was so thoughtful that he knew his puppy needed some breakfast. He ran to the kitchen and grabbed some food for the puppy.

Mark took the food to the puppy and made sure it was eating. The puppy was so happy, it jumped around and gave Mark lots of hugs. Mark thought this was the best way to start the day.

Next, Mark decided to take his puppy for a walk. He thought it was nice to get some fresh air. The puppy ran around and played with the birds and other animals it saw. Mark was so happy to watch his puppy having so much fun.

After their walk, Mark took his puppy back home. He was so tired from their adventure that he let it sleep in his bed. Mark was so pleased with his thoughtful puppy and was excited for tomorrow's adventures.

Once upon a time, there was a painter. The painter was very brave. The painter liked to paint pretty pictures. The painter was happy when he painted.

One day, the painter saw a big hill. The painter wanted to paint on the hill. He was not scared. The painter was brave. So, he went up the hill to paint.

When the painter was on the hill, he painted a big, pretty picture. The picture was of the sun and the sky. The painter was happy. The brave painter went down the hill and showed everyone his pretty picture. Everyone was happy too.

Once upon a time, there was a wealthy person. The person had a very special guitar, and many people wanted it. Everyone recognized it was something special.

One day, a little 3 year old saw the guitar. She liked it very much and asked if she could hold it. The wealthy person said yes.

When the little one held the guitar, she smiled. Then she started strumming it. Everyone recognized that the little one had a special talent with the guitar.

The wealthy person asked the little one if she wanted to keep the guitar. She said yes, and from then on the little one kept it with her. She practiced it every day, and soon became an amazing guitarist. Everyone recognized her talent. The little one thanked the wealthy person for the guitar and said that it had changed her life. The wealthy person smiled and said, “You have changed my life, too.”

One day, a boy named Tim found a big motorcycle. It was red and shiny. He wanted to ride it, but he was too small. Tim felt ashamed that he could not ride the motorcycle. He thought his friends would laugh at him.

Tim had an idea. He would bury the motorcycle so no one could see it. He dug a big hole and pushed the motorcycle into it. Then, he covered it with dirt. "Now no one will know," he said to himself.

Later, his friend Sam came over to play. They were playing near the hole when Sam fell in. He saw the buried motorcycle and asked, "What is this?" Tim was scared and did not want to tell the truth. Sam was angry and left. Tim was sad because he lost his friend and the motorcycle was still buried.

Tom and Mia like to play with cars. They have many cars of different colors and sizes. They make roads with blocks and books and zoom their cars on them. They pretend to be drivers and talk to each other.

"Look at my car, Mia!" Tom says. "It is purple and big and fast. It can zoom past all the other cars. Vroom, vroom!"

"Wow, Tom, your car is nice!" Mia says. "But my car is better. It is red and small and smart. It can zoom under the bridges and around the corners. Beep, beep!"

They zoom their cars together and have fun. But then they hear a loud noise. It is a scary noise. It sounds like a roar. They look up and see a big, black dog. The dog is angry and barks at them. It runs towards them and their cars.

"Help, Mia, help!" Tom cries. "The dog is scary! It wants to bite us and our cars!"

"Run, Tom, run!" Mia shouts. "Grab your car and follow me! We have to hide!"

They pick up their cars and run away from the dog. They find a safe place behind the sofa. They hug each other and their cars. They are scared and sad.

"Tom, Mia, what's wrong?" Mom asks. She hears them crying and comes to see. She sees the dog and shooes it away. She picks up Tom and Mia and hugs them. She is kind and gentle.

"Mom, the dog was scary!" Tom says. "It chased us and our cars!"

"Mom, the dog was mean!" Mia says. "It barked at us and our cars!"

"I'm sorry, Tom and Mia," Mom says. "The dog is not ours. It belongs to the new neighbors. They must have left the gate open. I will talk to them and tell them to keep the dog inside. You are safe now. Don't worry."

She kisses them and their cars. She gives them cookies and milk. She plays with them and their cars. They zoom their cars again and smile. They are happy and brave.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who liked to drive her toy car. One day, she decided to take her car for a drive in the woods.

As she drove around, she saw a gracefully curving snake near a tree. She stopped the car and watched it carefully. The snake moved slowly, and the little girl was mesmerized by its graceful movement.

Suddenly, the snake's tongue shot out and it hissed loudly. The little girl jumped back in fright and quickly drove away. She drove until she found her way back home and never returned to the woods.

The little girl will never forget her experience with the graceful snake!

The pale stair was long. Sally wanted to go up it. But she had to delay. It was too high and too far.

Instead she waited and waited. She watched her mommy go up it. Mommy said she'd wait for Sally at the top. Sally wanted to see what was up there.

Finally, Sally decided she'd try the big pale stair. One slow step at a time, she followed her mommy. It was a long way up the stair!

Soon Sally reached the top. She was very proud of herself. She could see everything from up here. Mommy smiled at her. She said, "I am proud of you, Sally."

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy liked to run around in the park with his friends. They would play tag and race each other.

One day, Timmy went to a restaurant with his family. He spilled some juice on his shirt, but his mommy gave him a napkin to clean it up. Timmy thought the napkin was very useful.

After lunch, Timmy went to take a nap. He slept for a long time and woke up feeling fine. He ran outside to play with his friends again. They had a lot of fun and Timmy was happy he had taken a good nap.

Once upon a time, there was a big bear. He liked to do lots of things like play, eat honey, and sleep. One day, he found a big rock and wanted to lift it. But it was too heavy and he felt uncomfortable.

The bear asked his friends, the birds, for help. They tried to lift the rock but it was still too heavy. Then, the bear had an idea. He went to the river and picked up some big sticks. He put the sticks under the rock and lifted it up.

The bear was so happy that he did it! He lifted the heavy weight! He thanked his bird friends and went back to playing and eating honey. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, Lily and her mom went to a big building with many floors. They got into an elevator and went up to the 10th floor. When the elevator doors opened, Lily peeked out and saw a big office with many people working.

Suddenly, Lily's mom realized that she left her phone in the car. She was worried because she needed her phone for an important call. Lily said, "Mommy, don't worry. I can go get your phone for you." But her mom said no because she didn't want Lily to get lost.

Lily felt sad because she wanted to help her mommy. But then she remembered something her teacher had taught her, "Always ask for help when you need it." So, Lily asked a nice lady in the office to help her find her mommy's car. The lady was happy to help and they found the phone quickly. Lily learned that it's okay to ask for help and that people are usually happy to help when they can.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved going to the toy store with her mom. One day, Lily saw a beautiful doll in the store window. She wanted it so much!

Lily and her mom went inside the store to examine the doll. It had pretty blonde hair and a pink dress. Lily thought it was very attractive. But when they looked at the price tag, it was too expensive for Lily's mom to buy.

Lily felt sad, but her mom told her they could save up to buy the doll another day. Lily was happy to hear that and gave the doll one last look before leaving the store.

Once upon a time, there was a kind and compassionate man named Tom. Tom had a special job. He would listen and hear what people needed, then help them.

One day, Tom met a sad little girl named Lily. "Why are you sad?" asked Tom. Lily said, "I lost my toy bear in the park." Tom knew he had to help Lily find her bear.

Tom and Lily looked all over the park for the bear. They looked under trees, behind bushes, and even in the sandbox. Then, Tom heard a tiny sound coming from a big tree. He looked up and saw the bear stuck in the tree! Tom climbed up and got the bear for Lily. She was so happy and thanked Tom for his help. From that day on, Lily knew Tom would always be there to help her.

Lily and Max liked to race each other in the park. They ran as fast as they could, and laughed when they reached the big tree. Sometimes they raced their bikes, or their scooters, or their balls.

One day, they saw a stranger in the park. He had a big dog with him, and he looked angry. He shouted at Lily and Max, and told them to go away. He said they were making too much noise, and they were bothering his dog.

Lily and Max were scared. They did not like the stranger, or his loud voice, or his big dog. They wanted to go home, but they did not want to pass by the stranger. They did not know what to do.

Then they saw their mom. She was walking towards them, with a smile on her face. She saw the stranger, and she did not like him either. She told Lily and Max to come to her, and she held their hands. She said to the stranger, "Leave my children alone. They are not doing anything wrong. They are just having fun. This is a public park, and they have the right to play here."

The stranger did not say anything. He looked at mom, and he looked at Lily and Max, and he looked at his dog. He saw that mom was not afraid of him, and that Lily and Max were not alone. He turned around, and walked away.

Lily and Max were happy. They hugged their mom, and thanked her for saving them. They said they did not want to race anymore, they just wanted to go home. Mom said that was fine, and that she was proud of them. She said they did a good job of staying away from the stranger, and of calling for her. She said they were brave, and smart, and kind.

They went home, and had some cookies and milk. They told their dad what happened, and he said he was proud of them too. He said they should always be careful of strangers, and always stick together. He said they were a great team, and he loved them very much.

The end.

Lily and Ben are best friends. They like to play in the park with their toys. One day, they see a big dog. The dog is black and has sharp teeth. It barks loud and runs fast.

Lily and Ben are scared. They worry that the dog will bite them. They hold their toys tight and run to the bench. They hide behind the bench and hope the dog will go away.

"Are you okay, Lily?" Ben asks. He sees that Lily is crying. She has a scratch on her arm from the dog's claw.

"No, Ben. It hurts. The dog is mean and tough. I want to go home." Lily says. She hugs her doll and sniffles.

Ben feels sorry for Lily. He wants to make her feel better. He thinks of what his mom does when he is hurt. He remembers that his mom kisses his boo-boos and tells him he is brave.

Ben leans over and kisses Lily's scratch. He says, "There, Lily. You are brave. The dog is gone now. We can go home and tell our moms. They will be proud of us."

Lily smiles. She feels a little better. She says, "Thank you, Ben. You are a good friend. You are brave too."

They hold hands and walk to the gate. They see their moms waiting for them. They run to their moms and hug them. They tell them what happened. Their moms kiss them and say they are proud of them. They say they are sorry for the dog and they will be careful next time.

Lily and Ben are happy. They are best friends. They kiss each other and say goodbye. They go home with their moms and their toys. They are not scared of the dog anymore. They are tough and brave.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys and read books. One day, she went to the park to play with her friends.

While they were playing, Lily saw a big alarm clock on a bench. She picked it up and showed it to her friends. They were amazed by the clock and wanted to play with it too.

Suddenly, the clock started ringing loudly! Lily was embarrassed because everyone was looking at her. She whispered to her friends, "Let's put the clock back on the bench before someone gets mad."

Her friends agreed, and they quickly put the clock back. They continued playing and having fun, but they made sure to stay away from the alarm clock. From that day on, Lily always made sure to be careful with things that didn't belong to her.

Once upon a time, there were two friends, Jane and Sam. Jane was very excited about a new plant she bought and wanted to tell her friend about it. She went to Sam's house and said, "Sam, I got a plant!"

"What kind of plant is it?" asked Sam.

"It's a sweet plant," said Jane.

Sam smiled and asked, "Can I help you take care of it?"

Jane was overjoyed and said, "Yes! That would be great!"

So, together they took care of the plant, watering and writing it. Every day they worked hard to make sure the plant was healthy and growing.

One day, Jane came over and noticed the plant was missing. She asked Sam, "Where is the plant?"

Sam smiled and said, "I wrote it to Grandma. I thought she would enjoy it more than us."

The moral of the story is that it's important to think of others and be kind. With a little bit of effort and kindness, we can make someone else feel special.

Ben and Sam are brothers. They like to play with cars and balls. One day, they find a big gray hat in the closet. It is their dad's hat. Ben wants to wear the hat. He puts it on his head. He says, "Look at me! I am a big man!"

Sam wants to wear the hat too. He says, "No, Ben! It is my turn! Give me the hat!" He tries to pull the hat from Ben's head. Ben holds the hat tight. He says, "No, Sam! It is mine! Go away!"

They start to fight. They push and pull and shout. The hat falls to the floor. They both run to get it. They bump their heads. They cry.

Mom hears the noise. She comes to the closet. She sees the hat and the boys. She says, "What are you doing? Why are you fighting? This is not your hat. This is dad's hat. You should not take his things without asking. You should share and be nice."

She picks up the hat. She puts it on her head. She says, "Now, I am a big man!" She smiles. The boys stop crying. They laugh. They say, "No, mom! You are a big woman! You are funny!"

Mom hugs the boys. She says, "I love you, Ben and Sam. You are my big boys. But you are still little. You have a lot to learn and gain. Now, let's put the hat back and play something else."

Once upon a time, there was a happy little boy. His name was Doug and he loved to play the drum. One day Doug and his mom went for a walk in the park. It was a cold day, and suddenly everything around them began to freeze. Doug's mom was worried, but Doug just smiled and reached for his drum. He started to beat it and the sound echoed across the park. Soon, all of the ice started to melt and the sun came out. It was warm again and Doug and his mom were so happy. They hugged each other and thanked the drum.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy had big, thick sunglasses that he loved to wear. One sunny day, Timmy went outside to play with his friends. They decided to play tag and Timmy was "it". He ran around the yard, trying to tag his friends.

Suddenly, Timmy's sunglasses fell off his face and onto the ground. He stopped running and picked them up. But when he put them back on, he noticed that one of the lenses was cracked. Timmy was sad because he loved his thick sunglasses.

His friends saw that he was sad and decided to help. They all ran to Timmy's house and asked his mom if they could buy him new sunglasses. Timmy was so happy and grateful for his friends. From that day on, he wore his new sunglasses everywhere he went, even when he wasn't outside!

Suzie and her mom were in the park. It was a sunny day, and the birds were chirping cheerfully. Suzie enjoyed the bright sun and soft grass beneath her feet.

They reached the wheat field. The wheat waved in the wind, making a gentle rustling sound. Suzie smiled and said, "Mommy, let's play in the wheat!".

So Mommy and Suzie ran around and enjoyed the wheat. They laughed and hugged each other. The wheat felt soft against their skin and smelled sweet in the air.

But then the wind shifted. Suddenly, a harsh gust blew across the wheat field. The wheat began to whip around Suzie and her mom.

"It's too harsh!" yelled Mommy. She grabbed Suzie's hand and they ran out of the wheat field until the wind calmed down.

Back at home, the two were safe and sound. Suzie hugged her Mommy and said she loved her. Although they had a harsh experience at the wheat field, they both enjoyed the adventure.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Mark. Mark was a thoughtful boy who liked to help others. One day, he saw a small bird with a hurt wing. Mark wanted to help the bird, so he took it home.

At home, Mark made a soft bed for the bird to rest. He gave it food and water. The bird was happy and nodded its head to say thank you. Mark felt good that he could help the bird.

After a few days, the bird felt better. Mark knew it was time to let the bird go. He took the bird outside and opened his hands. The bird flew away, but it looked back and nodded to Mark one more time. Mark smiled and waved goodbye.

Once upon a time there was a small girl called Jane. Jane wanted to go to the top of a tall building but there were so many stairs! Fortunately, the building had a big elevator!

Jane happily went into the elevator and pressed the button. But suddenly, the elevator stopped! Jane was confused but then she heard a noise. It was coming from a box full of dirty, old tools.

Jane had to try and manage the elevator without the tools. She thought hard and she came up with a clever plan! She tied two pieces of string together and used them like a pulley to help the elevator go up.

Jane was very proud of herself. She managed to move the elevator up to the top of the tall building. From the top, she could see all the pretty houses below. Jane was so happy she made it to the top!

Once upon a time, there was a funny monkey who lived on an island. He liked to play with his friends and eat bananas. One day, he saw a beautiful butterfly and wanted to kiss it. But the butterfly flew away and the monkey was sad.

The next day, the monkey went to the beach and saw a big boat. He wanted to go on an adventure and explore new places. But when he got on the boat, he saw a mean pirate who wanted to take his bananas. The monkey was scared and didn't know what to do.

Suddenly, the monkey remembered the butterfly and how it flew away. He used his quick monkey skills to climb up the mast and jump onto the pirate's head. The pirate was so surprised that he fell into the water and swam away. The monkey was a hero and his friends cheered. He realized that sometimes, it's better to be brave than to just kiss a butterfly.

Once upon a time, there was a big, tall giraffe named Gigi. Gigi loved to play in the water and make bubbles. One day, Gigi's mom said, "Gigi, it's time to wash up." Gigi didn't want to wash because she loved playing in the dirt. But her mom said, "You can make bubbles in the water too!"

So Gigi went to the river and started washing herself. She splashed around and made lots of bubbles. Suddenly, she saw a little fish swimming in the water. The fish said, "Can I play with you?" Gigi said yes and they played together, making more bubbles and having fun.

After they finished playing, Gigi's mom said, "You look so clean now, Gigi!" Gigi was happy and proud of herself. From that day on, Gigi loved to wash up and make bubbles in the water.

Jamie was having a picnic with her family. She was so excited to eat the delicious lunch, but she was also a little embarrassed because she was wearing a funny hat.

When it was time to eat, Jamie tried to get some jam, but her hand slipped and the jar of jam hit the ground. It froze and became one big, sticky mess. Jamie was so embarrassed and embarrassed.

Her mom and dad saw how embarrassed Jamie was and they knew what to do. They grabbed the picnic blanket and spread it out on the ground. Then they got a spoon and scooped out the frozen jam.

Jamie was so relieved when they were finished. She was able to eat her lunch without worrying about making a mess. Eating lunch with her family was now more fun than ever, and Jamie was glad she didn't have to be embarrassed anymore.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys, especially her toy car. One day, she noticed that her car was not working properly. She asked her mom to help her fix it.

Her mom said, "Let's examine the car and see what's wrong." They looked at the car and saw that one of the gears was broken. Lily's mom explained that the gear helps the car move.

Lily was sad that her car was broken, but her mom told her not to worry. She said, "We can fix it together. You can be my little helper." Lily was happy to be independent and help her mom fix the car.

They worked together and fixed the gear. Lily was so excited to play with her car again. She thanked her mom for teaching her how to examine and fix things. From that day on, Lily felt more confident and independent.

Once upon a time there was a house. It was a big house and it was very heavy. Inside the house there was a family. They were sad because they had to surrender their house.

The family packed their things and put them into a truck. They said goodbye to the house they once loved then drove away. The house stayed still and felt very lonely.

Suddenly, something magical happened! Clouds in the sky started to float down and hug the house. Suddenly the house didn't feel heavy anymore, it felt light and free!

The family looked out at the house from the truck and smiled. They knew they had made the right decision to surrender the house. They waved goodbye as they drove away until they were out of sight.

The house was happy now and looked forward to a new start in life.

Once there was a little girl called Lucy. She was three years old. She was very curious and loved going on new adventures. One day, her mom gave her a special camera. She was so excited and wanted to take photographs of everything around her.

She held the camera gently and started to investigate. She squeezed the camera and took a picture. She saw the photo and was confused. "Why didn't it turn out nicely?" she wondered.

Her mom explained to her that the camera works best when she uses it gently. She showed Lucy how to hold it lightly and squeeze the button. When Lucy tried it again, she got a beautiful picture. She was so happy she ran outside to show her family the picture.

She kept practicing and exploring with her camera, squeezing the button gently to take the best pictures. She was no longer confused and had lots of fun every day!

Tommy loved to go to the park. One day, he saw a shiny orange truck. He was so excited to ride in it. His mom put him in the truck and loaded him in. He heard a loud noise when his mom turned the engine on. Tommy was so happy! He held on tight and smiled as the truck drove around the park.

Next, he saw some orange flowers growing on the side of the road. He noticed how beautiful they were and he wanted to pick one for his mom. His mom said it was too far away so she loaded him out of the truck and carried him over to the flowers.

Tommy was so excited to pick the orange flower. He felt the petals and smelled the sweet scent. He laughed as he played with the petals and then he handed the flower to his mom. His mom hugged him and thanked him for the orange flower.

Tommy enjoyed the rest of his day in the park. He saw orange butterflies flying around and he heard all sorts of noises. He grinned with joy as he loaded back in the orange truck and his mom drove him home.

Once upon a time, there lived a little boy called Andy. He was an adventurous boy and always liked trying new things. He was especially curious about the world around him.

One day, Andy went to the park with his mom. As he ran around, playing with the other kids, he saw a beautiful butterfly with purple and yellow wings. He watched in amazement as it flew away and shouted with joy.

His mom was so proud of him - she smiled and clapped! This made Andy feel so special. He looked up at her and smiled back with love.

The next day, Andy decided to go on an adventure and explore the park even more. As he ventured through the woods, he heard a loud noise. To his surprise, it was the same butterfly from the day before!

Andy was so happy that he wanted to thank the butterfly. He started to applaud and waved his hands in the air with excitement. The butterfly fluttered around him, enjoying the moment.

Andy's mom was filled with pride. He had been so adventurous that day and she was so proud of him. She said, "You make me so happy Andy!" And they hugged and filled each other with love.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily loved to play outside in the sunshine with her friends. One day, Lily and her friends wanted to play hide and seek, but it was getting dark outside.

Lily said, "I wish we had some light so we could keep playing."

Just then, a jolly man named Mr. Smith walked by and heard Lily's wish. He said, "I can provide some light for you. I have a flashlight in my pocket."

Lily and her friends were very happy and thanked Mr. Smith. They continued playing hide and seek with the light from the flashlight.

But then, a conflict arose when Lily's friend, Timmy, accidentally broke the flashlight. Lily was upset and said, "Now we can't play anymore."

Mr. Smith saw that Lily was upset and said, "Don't worry, I have another flashlight at home. I'll go get it for you."

Lily and her friends were relieved and grateful that Mr. Smith could provide them with more light. They continued playing and had a great time. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play in her yard. Her yard was big and green with lots of flowers. One day, Lily saw a tiny blue seed in her yard. She picked it up and asked her mom, "What is this?" Her mom replied, "It's a seed. If you plant it, it will grow into a beautiful blue flower."

Lily was very excited and quickly planted the seed in the ground. Every day she watered it and waited patiently. Finally, one day she saw a tiny green sprout growing out of the ground. She was so happy and shouted, "Look, look! It's growing!"

Days passed by, and the sprout grew taller and taller until it became a beautiful blue flower. Lily was overjoyed and ran to her mom to show her. "Mommy, look at my flower! It's so pretty and blue!" Her mom smiled and said, "You did a great job growing it, Lily. It's beautiful." From that day on, Lily loved to plant seeds and watch them grow in her yard.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Paul. Paul was playing on the beach. He saw a cool palm tree in the distance. He was so excited! He ran to the tree and tried to climb it. But he couldn't get very far. He tried to pull himself up but he was too little. Then he saw something strange. Right above his head was a big yield sign. But what did it mean?

Paul was confused. He wanted to keep climbing the cool palm tree. He tried to ignore the yield sign and kept climbing it. But the sign started to shake. Suddenly, Paul came tumbling down to the ground. He was so upset!

Luckily, Paul was fine. He just had a few scratches. But he was sad that he couldn't keep climbing the cool palm tree. He still didn't know what the yield sign meant.

Then Paul's dad came over. He said that the yield sign meant that it was time for Paul to take a break. So Paul decided to sit under the palm tree and rest for a bit. He still enjoyed playing at the beach and looking at the cool palm tree from afar.

Once there was a little brown fox called Sam. Sam loved to explore, and one day he decided to venture deep into the forest.

But as Sam walked, he began to struggle. It was dark and he didn’t know which way to turn. Suddenly he heard a voice, “Who's there?”

Sam jumped up and said, “It's me, Sam the fox.”

The voice said, “I'm the judge of the forest. What are you doing here?”

“I'm just exploring,” Sam said. “I'm lost and I'm struggling to find my way home.”

The judge thought for a moment and said, “I know the way. Follow me!”

Sam was so happy and he followed the judge through the forest. After a while, they arrived at Sam’s home.

Sam was very relieved and said, “Thank you so much. I don’t know what I would have done without your help!”

The judge smiled and said, “You’re welcome. Just remember, no matter how lost you feel, I'm always here to help.”

Sam nodded and said goodbye. He knew he would never forget the kind judge with her brown fur.

Lily was a lovely girl who liked to play with her toys and her dog. She had a big box full of toys that she could choose from. She had dolls, cars, blocks, books and more. She loved to make stories with her toys and pretend they were her friends.

One day, she found a toy that she did not remember. It was a soft bear with a red ribbon around its neck. She picked it up and hugged it. It felt warm and cozy. She wondered where it came from and who gave it to her.

She asked her mom, who was in the kitchen. Her mom smiled and said, "That was your grandma's bear. She gave it to you when you were a baby. She loved you very much and wanted you to have it. Do you remember your grandma?"

Lily thought hard. She remembered a nice lady who smelled like flowers and cookies. She remembered her voice, her laugh, her hair. She remembered how she would read her stories and sing her songs. She remembered how she would hug her and kiss her and say, "You are my life, my Lily."

Lily felt a tear in her eye. She missed her grandma. She wished she could see her again. She said, "I remember, mom. I love grandma. And I love her bear. Thank you for keeping it for me."

Her mom hugged her and said, "You're welcome, sweetie. Grandma is always with you in your heart. And so am I. You are my life, too, my Lily. And you are lovely."

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the snow. One day, she saw a reindeer in her yard. The reindeer was very big and had antlers on its head.

"Hello, reindeer!" said Lily. "You're very big and have antlers on your head. Are you an intelligent reindeer?"

"Yes, I am," said the reindeer. "I can help you find your way home if you're lost."

Lily was very happy to hear this. But then, she saw that the reindeer was stuck in the snow. "Oh no!" she said. "You're stuck in the snow. Let me help you step out of it."

Lily pulled and pulled, and finally, the reindeer was free. "Thank you, Lily," said the reindeer. "You're very kind. I'll always remember you."

From that day on, Lily and the intelligent reindeer were the best of friends. They played in the snow together and had lots of fun.

Tom and Sue were playing in the park. They liked to run and jump and slide. But Tom was stubborn. He wanted to go on the big swing, but Sue was scared.

"Come on, Sue, it's fun!" Tom said. "You can hold my hand."

"No, Tom, it's too high!" Sue said. "I want to go on the slide."

Tom was angry. He did not want to go on the slide. He wanted to go on the big swing. He pulled Sue's hand and tried to make her go with him.

"Ow, Tom, you hurt me!" Sue cried. She let go of Tom's hand and fell on the ground. She scraped her knee and it bled. She started to weep.

Tom saw Sue's knee and felt sorry. He did not mean to hurt her. He ran to the bench where his mom was sitting. He asked for a band to put on Sue's knee.

"Mom, can I have a band?" Tom said. "I hurt Sue and she is weeping."

Mom gave Tom a band and a hug. She told him to say sorry to Sue and to be gentle with her.

Tom took the band and went back to Sue. He said sorry and put the band on her knee. He gave her a hug and a kiss.

"I'm sorry, Sue, I was stubborn," Tom said. "Do you want to go on the slide with me?"

Sue smiled and nodded. She wiped her tears and held Tom's hand.

"OK, Tom, let's go on the slide," Sue said. "But next time, you can go on the big swing if you want."

Tom and Sue went on the slide and had fun. They were friends again.

Once upon a time there was a blue whale. The whale lived deep in the beautiful ocean. The ocean was a very safe and happy place for the whale.

Every day the whale would swim around, enjoying the fresh and clean water. But what the whale really loved was the oxygen. The oxygen made it happy and it felt great!

The whale wanted to show its gratitude and so it served the other ocean animals. It shared its oxygen with them, making sure everyone was healthy and happy. The whale was so kind!

The other animals were so grateful to the blue whale. They thanked it and praised it every day. They were happy to have such a noble creature living in their ocean.

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved books and would read them every day. One day, she found a book that was very high up on a shelf. She wanted to read it, but she was too little to reach it. So, she asked her daddy to help her. He kneeled down and picked up the book for her. Lily was very happy and thanked her daddy. She then sat down and read her book until it was time for bed. The end.

One day, a big cat named Tom and a little mouse named Tim were playing in the park. They saw a bell hanging from a tree. Tim said, "I want to ring that bell, but I can't reach it." Tom wanted to help, so he tried to think of a way to get the bell down for Tim.

Tom had an idea. He found a long stick and tried to hit the bell with it. But the stick was too harsh and broke. Tim was sad and said, "Now we can't ring the bell." Tom told Tim not to worry, and he would find another way to help.

Just then, a friendly bird came by and saw the broken stick. She asked what happened. Tom and Tim told her about the bell and how they wanted to ring it. The bird had an idea. She flew up to the tree and rang the bell for them. The sound of the bell made Tom and Tim very happy. They thanked the bird for her help and continued playing in the park, knowing they had a new friend who could help them when they needed it.

Tim and Jen were twins who liked to play with their toys. One day, they found a big box in the living room. It had a sticker that said "Do not open until your birthday". Tim and Jen wondered what was inside the box. They wanted to open it and see.

"Let's open it now," Tim said. "It will be fun."

"No, we can't," Jen said. "Mom and Dad said we have to wait. It is a surprise for our birthday. We have to resist."

"But I'm curious," Tim said. "Maybe it is something we really like. Maybe it is a bike or a doll or a robot."

Jen shook her head. "It is not nice to open presents before the event. We have to be patient and follow the rules. Come on, let's play with our other toys."

Tim was not happy. He waited until Jen was busy with her blocks. Then he sneaked to the box and lifted the lid. He saw a big train set with tracks and cars and a remote control. He smiled and took it out of the box. He wanted to try it.

But he was not careful. He dropped the remote control and it broke. He tried to fix it, but he could not. He heard Jen coming and he panicked. He put the train set back in the box and closed the lid. He hoped Jen would not notice.

But Jen did notice. She saw the broken remote control sticking out of the box. She saw the tear in the wrapping paper. She saw Tim's guilty face. She was angry and sad.

"Tim, what did you do?" she asked. "You opened the box. You broke the remote control. You ruined our birthday surprise."

Tim felt bad. He knew he made a mistake. He wished he listened to Jen. He wished he resisted his curiosity. He said he was sorry, but Jen did not forgive him. She ran to their room and cried.

Mom and Dad came home and saw the mess. They were disappointed and upset. They explained to Tim and Jen that the train set was a special gift from their grandparents. They said they had to call them and tell them what happened. They said they had to take the train set back to the store and see if they could exchange it. They said they had to teach Tim and Jen a lesson about respecting other people's things and waiting for the right time.

Tim and Jen felt worse. They realized they hurt their grandparents and their parents. They realized they spoiled their own birthday. They realized they had to learn to resist temptation and be more careful and grateful. They hugged each other and said they were sorry. They hoped they could still have a happy birthday.

The moral of the story is: Resist the urge to do something wrong, even if you are curious or bored. It can have bad consequences for yourself and others. Be patient and respectful and you will be rewarded.

Once upon a time there was a girl. She loved to play pretend. Every morning, she would find something to pretend with. One day, the girl found something really special. It was a purple mask! She was so excited and showed it to her mom. Her mom told her she could use it for her pretend play. The girl smiled and put the mask on. Now she was ready for adventure. She went on a big pretend adventure. She pretended to be a magical princess and made up a game where she had to find the purple gems. She had a lot of fun with her purple mask. When she was done playing, she showed the mask to her mom. Her mom smiled and said she had done a great job.

The girl thanked her mom and put her purple mask away, waiting for her next fun pretend play adventure.

Once there was a bright girl named Amy. She loved to balance on one foot and do all kinds of fun tricks. One day, Amy decided to take a journey. She hopped on her bike and started pedaling.

On her journey she had to balance her bike on two different bridges. She crossed the first one without any problem. On the second bridge she wobbled a bit and almost fell! Luckily, she was able to balance her bike and make it across.

Soon Amy was having lots of fun! She sped around turns and hopped over bumps. She even tried to balance on top of a picnic table! After a few hours, Amy was ready to head back home.

She pedaled all the way and was very proud of her bright journey.

Once upon a time, a little girl named Mia went to the store with her mom. Mia saw many things in the store. She saw a big blue ball, a funny hat, and a soft teddy bear. Mia's mom said they needed to buy shampoo, and Mia could choose which one they would buy.

Mia looked at all the shampoo bottles. There were many colors and shapes. She saw a red bottle, a green bottle, and a yellow bottle. Then Mia saw a blue bottle of shampoo. She liked the color blue. It was her favorite color, just like the sky and the ocean.

Mia picked up the blue shampoo bottle and showed it to her mom. Her mom smiled and said, "Good choice, Mia!" They bought the blue shampoo and went home. That night, Mia had fun using her new blue shampoo in the bath. She was happy she got to choose the shampoo they used.

Once upon a time, there was a very wise old owl. He lived in a tall tree and liked to look down onto the world below. One day, he saw a tiny mouse trying to scratch a very big itch at the bottom of the tree.

The owl felt sorry for the little mouse, so he flew down to meet her. The mouse was very scared, but the owl promised her he wouldn't hurt her. He asked the mouse why she was trying to scratch such a big itch.

The mouse said she had fallen into an itchy patch of grass on her way home. She tried to scratch it, but it would not get itched away. The wise owl had an idea. He told the mouse to take a bath, and he promised she would feel better after.

The mouse took the advice and had a nice bath with some soap. When she came out, her itch was gone!

From then on, the wise owl taught the little mouse to always listen to advice from wise people and to think about the consequences of her actions.

The moral of the story is to always think before you do things, and to listen to people who are wiser than you. People who have more knowledge than you can often help you in ways you can't help yourself.

One day, Mummy, Daddy, Nana and the little boy went to the park. Daddy pointed to the sky and said, "Look at the birds!" Then he pointed to a tree and said, "Look at the leaves!" Then he pointed to a bench and said, "Let's sit down and have a rest!"

When they sat on the bench, Nana took out a photo from her pocket. Then she pointed to it and said, "This is a photo of Mummy and Daddy when they were young." Then Daddy smiled and pointed to himself and said, "And this is me now."

The little boy looked at the photo and said, "I want a photo too!" Daddy shook his head and said, "Not now, it's too expensive." But Mummy said, "That's being selfish. Let's take a photo of the little boy and keep it forever to remember this happy day."

So they did! They pointed their phones at the little boy, and he made funny faces and smiled. Then they saved the photo and kept it forever to remember their happy day at the park.

Once there was a huge pink elephant. He liked to clap his trunk with glee! One day, he stumbled upon a farmer and his daughter walking through the forest. The farmer was astonished and pointed at the elephant.

“Look at the huge pink animal!” he said.

The daughter clapped with excitement. Then the elephant got angry, because he didn't like the farmer pointing at him. He began to charge at them.

The farmer and the daughter tried to run away but the huge pink elephant was too quick for them. He ran towards them and then attacked them with his trunk.

The farmer and the daughter were so scared that they screamed in terror. The elephant kept clapping his trunk and defending himself from them.

The farmer and the daughter were never seen again. The huge pink elephant continued to roam the forest, always on the lookout for strangers that he could scare away.

Once upon a time, there was a brown dog named Spot. Spot loved to play fetch with his owner, Timmy. One day, Timmy and Spot went to the park to play.

While they were playing, they saw a big airplane in the sky. Timmy pointed and said, "Look, Spot! A pilot is flying that plane!" Spot barked excitedly.

After they finished playing, Timmy and Spot went to get some ice cream. But when they got to the ice cream shop, they saw that it was closed. "Oh no," said Timmy. "We can't get ice cream."

Just then, a kind lady walked up to them and said, "I have extra ice cream at my house. Would you like some?" Timmy and Spot were so happy! The lady supplied them with delicious ice cream. They thanked her and went home, feeling grateful for the kind stranger's help.

Bess was playing in the garden. She had a pan in her hand and she was running around looking for something special. Suddenly, she tripped and the pan slipped out of her hand and rolled down the hill. "Oh no!", Bess cried. She ran as fast as she could to get the pan back, but when she reached the bottom of the hill the pan was gone.

Bess started crying and she just couldn't stop. She had lost her pan. Suddenly, an open door caught her eyes. Bess had found a new room. She went inside and looked around. To her surprise, there was the pan! She was so happy she gave it a big hug.

Bess ran back home to show her parents what she had found. Everyone was really happy and Bess promised to never lose the pan again. She would keep it in a safe place next time.

Once there was a little girl called Lucy. She was only three years old and she loved exploring the world.

One day, Lucy and her parents went for a walk in the park. The sun was shining and birds were everywhere. Lucy saw a pond in the garden and she went to see what creatures were inside it. There she saw many shiny shrimp swimming around. Lucy was so excited.

"Look Dad," Lucy said, pointing to the pond. "I want to get closer and admire them!"

Dad was worried but nodded and said, "Okay, but stay close and be careful".

Lucy took small steps and admired the beautiful shrimp. She was so happy she wanted to smile but instead she just said, "Oh wow!". She was mesmerized by their colours.

After a while, Lucy ran back to her parents. She was so pleased to have seen the shrimp and couldn't wait to tell her best friends the news.

Once there was a naughty dog called Max. He loved to play with his toys and make all sorts of messes. One day, Max decided to spray some water from a hose all over his owner's waffle.

When the owner saw what Max had done, they were angry. "Max, you must not spray water on the waffle!" they said.

But Max did not listen. He just kept jumping around and spraying the hose until everything was wet.

So, his owner took away the hose and said, "No more spraying for you!"

Max was sad for a little bit, but soon he forgot about the hose. Instead, he started playing with his toys again and had lots of fun. He was a naughty dog, but he was also very happy.

Once upon a time, there was a dog named Max. Max had a flea on his back that he couldn't get rid of. The flea troubled Max a lot because it made him itchy. Max tried to scratch the flea off, but it wouldn't go away.

One day, Max's owner saw the flea and decided to help. She got a comb and started to brush Max's fur. The flea tried to keep hiding, but the comb caught it. Max's owner was happy to finally catch the flea.

Max was happy too because he didn't feel itchy anymore. He wagged his tail and licked his owner's face to say thank you. From that day on, Max's owner made sure to keep him flea-free.

One day, Tom and Tim were playing football in the park. They were having a lot of fun. Tom was a little anxious because he wanted to win. He wanted to finish the game fast.

Tom said, "I will win!" Tim said, "No, I will win!" They both ran fast to get the ball. They were not happy with each other.

In the end, Tom and Tim both kicked the ball at the same time. The football went far away. They laughed and were friends again. They learned that playing together was more fun than winning.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Rosie. She had a brilliant new doll. She felt so excited when she saw it. Rosie hugged the doll and it felt so soft and warm in her arms. She snuggled the doll close and felt happy. Rosie decided to take the doll for a walk. Everywhere they went, people smiled and said that the doll was brilliant. When they went home, Rosie put the doll to bed in her room. Now she always feels happy and safe when her doll is with her. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a young boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play outside, but it was raining outside. He put on his raincoat and boots and went outside anyway. Timmy splashed in the puddles and had lots of fun.

After a while, Timmy's mom called him inside for lunch. She asked him what he wanted to eat, and he said he wanted a peanut butter and jelly sandwich. Luckily, there was some bread and peanut butter available, but they were out of jelly.

Timmy was sad he couldn't have a peanut butter and jelly sandwich, but his mom told him they could go to the store later and get some more. Timmy was happy again and went to play with his toys. The rain kept falling outside, but Timmy didn't mind because he was having so much fun inside.

Every day, Bob and his mom had an ordinary idea. Bob would take a nap and then he could play afterwards. He liked this idea very much. So each day, Bob would have his lunch, lay down in his soft bed, and snuggle up under his blankets. He knew his mom was nearby, just in case he needed anything.
