After a few minutes, Bob would fall into a deep sleep. He would dream of all the things he could do once he woke up, like going to the park or visiting his friends. When it was time, Bob’s mom would carefully wake him up, and help him out of bed. He would stretch his arms and legs and feel refreshed.

Before long, he was ready for a day of play and fun. All because of their ordinary, yet special nap idea.

Once upon a time, there was a cute little girl called Anna. Anna had an old boat, but it couldn't float on the water. One day, Anna's dad said he could provide her with a good raft. Anna was very excited and hoped it would help her explore the lake. When it arrived, the raft was red and shiny. Anna and her dad took it down to the lake and it floated perfectly. Now Anna could have lots of fun adventures on her special raft. Whenever she wanted to go explore the lake, she just had to take her raft with her!

Once upon a time, there was a long line of ants marching through the forest. One ant, named Billy, was carrying a big piece of bread. Suddenly, Billy saw a big flame and yelled, "Help! Fire! My bread will burn!"

Another ant, named Sally, heard Billy's cry and ran over to help. Sally said, "Don't worry, Billy. I'll help you save your bread." Sally quickly grabbed the bread and ran away from the fire.

But then, a big bird swooped down and tried to steal the bread from Sally. Sally yelled, "No! That's not yours!" The bird tried to grab the bread with its beak, but Sally held on tight.

Finally, the bird gave up and flew away. Sally and Billy were safe, and they shared the bread together. They were happy and proud that they had saved the bread from burning in the fire. The end.

Once upon a time there was a little girl. She was three years old and her name was Emma. One day, Emma had a great idea. She wanted to help her mom make a delicious dinner for the family. She ran to her mom and asked if she could help. Her mom said yes and gave her a task.

Emma was so excited, she ran to the kitchen and found a light bulb. She didn't know what to do with it. She thought and thought, then she had a brilliant idea. She grabbed a chair, stood on it and carefully unscrewed the bulb. Then, she ran outside to the garden and found a big, juicy carrot. She grabbed the carrot and ran back to the kitchen, put it inside the empty bulb and carefully screwed it back.

Emma felt so proud of her work, she went to show her mom. Her mom was so impressed! She put the bulb in the oven and cooked it. When the dinner was ready, her mom served it and everyone thought it was delicious. Emma was so happy she helped her mom make a yummy dinner!

Once upon a time there was a young boy. He liked to go to a special place every day. It was a place where he could play, laugh and have lots of fun.

One day the young boy went to the special place. There he saw something very special. It was a big box full of toys. He saw lots of things he wanted to play with. Suddenly, a kind voice said, "These toys are for you. I want to give them to you."

The young boy was so excited. He said thank you to the kind voice. He opened the box and looked inside. There were so many toys - cars, robots and dolls. He thanked the kind voice again before he started to play with the toys.

The young boy was so happy that he had been given such a special gift. He enjoyed playing with all the toys - it was the best day ever.

Mia and Ben are playing in the park. They like to slide on the big slide. Mia goes first. She sits on the slide and holds the hand of Ben. Ben counts to three and they slide down together. Whee!

They run back to the top of the slide. They want to slide again. But there is a problem. The slide is wet. It rained last night and the slide is slippery. Mia does not see the water. She sits on the slide and holds the hand of Ben. Ben counts to three and they slide down together. But they slide too fast. They slip off the slide and land on the grass. Ouch!

Mia and Ben are not hurt. They are just wet and dirty. They laugh and get up. They look at the slide. They see the water. They do not want to slide anymore. They want to play something else.

They see a swing. They run to the swing. They take turns to push each other. They swing high and low. They have fun. They forget about the slide.

But there is a boy who wants to slide. He is persistent. He does not care about the water. He does not care about the slip. He runs to the slide. He sits on the slide. He does not hold anyone's hand. He slides down by himself. He slips off the slide and lands on the grass. Ouch!

He cries and gets up. He looks at the slide. He does not want to slide anymore. He wants to play something else.

He sees Mia and Ben on the swing. He runs to the swing. He asks them if he can join them. They say yes. They share the swing. They push each other. They swing high and low. They have fun. They forget about the slide.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who was very excited to go to a museum. She had heard that it was amazing and could not wait to go.

When she arrived, she saw all sorts of interesting things she had never seen before. There were big statues, colourful paintings and funny sculptures. She was amazed by everything she saw.

The little girl stayed at the museum all day. She watched people using a telescope to look at the stars and saw an elephant that had a tiny hat on its head. She saw so many amazing things!

At the end of the day, the little girl was very happy. She had seen so many interesting things. She already couldn't wait to come back to the museum and stay there again.

Once upon a time, there was a little crab named Carl. Carl liked to play in the sand and look for shiny rocks. One day, Carl saw a shrimp that was stuck in a big shell. The shrimp was very sad and confused.

"Can you help me, please?" asked the shrimp.

Carl replied, "Yes, I can fix it!"

Carl used his strong claws to break open the shell and the shrimp was free. The shrimp was very happy and said, "Thank you so much, Carl! You're my hero!"

From that day on, Carl and the shrimp became best friends and they played in the sand together every day. Carl was happy that he could help his friend and fix the problem.

Once upon a time, there was a car. The car had a driver who liked to go fast. One day, the driver saw a sign that said "enter here". The driver got excited and entered the place.

But oh no! The driver was being naughty and didn't see the stop sign. The car hit a tree and the driver got hurt. The car was broken too.

The driver learned a lesson to always be careful when entering new places. And the car got fixed by a kind mechanic. The end.

Once upon a time there was a king who wanted to travel. He was looking for a very easy way to go. He searched high and he searched low. Finally, he found a big boat.

So the king hopped in the boat and started his journey. He waved goodbye to everyone, and he was off! As he sailed, the king saw lots of different things. He saw a seagull and a big fish. He even saw a whale!

Eventually the boat sailed to a new land. The king was so happy and excited. He hopped out of the boat and looked all around. He found many new things to explore.

The king had a great time on his travel. He made lots of new friends and had lots of fun. He was sad when it was time to go home, but he was so happy that he had a wonderful and easy journey!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She went for a walk in the forest with her dad. They saw a big log on the ground. Lily's dad asked her if she wanted to sit on it. She said yes and they sat down.

Lily felt uncomfortable on the log because it was hard and bumpy. But she enjoyed looking at the trees and listening to the birds. Her dad told her stories about the animals that lived in the forest. Lily liked the story about the squirrel who collected nuts for the winter.

After a while, they got up and continued their walk. Lily was happy because she enjoyed spending time with her dad and seeing all the beautiful things in the forest. She even forgot about the uncomfortable log. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside on her swing. She would go back and forth, back and forth, feeling the wind in her hair. One day, her mom called her inside for a snack. Lily was so hungry! She sat down at the table and her mom gave her some crackers and cheese. Yum! But then, Lily started to feel bad. Her tummy hurt and she didn't want to swing anymore. Her mom gave her some medicine and told her to rest. The next day, Lily felt better and went back to swinging on her swing.

Once upon a time, in a big jungle, there was a silly elephant named Ella. Ella loved to play with her friends. She liked to hide behind trees and peek out at them.

One day, Ella was playing with her friend, a little monkey named Momo. Momo said, "Let's play hide and seek!" Ella was very excited and agreed. Momo started to count, and Ella ran to find a place to hide.

Ella tried to hide behind a small tree, but she was too big! Her big ears and long trunk could still be seen. Momo laughed and said, "I see you, Ella! You are too big for that tree!" Ella felt silly and laughed too.

They played all day, taking turns hiding and seeking. They had so much fun, and Ella learned that even though she was big, she could still find good places to hide. At the end of the day, Ella and Momo were happy and tired. They said goodbye and went to their homes, excited to play again the next day.

The pink march was coming and everybody was excited. Today was going to be a special day.

Cindy, a three year old, was running around the house trying to find something to help her get ready. She found an old ribbon from a present and asked her mom if she could tie it around her wrist.

Finally, the day had arrived and Cindy was ready with her ribbon tied firmly around her wrist. Everyone started marching, chanting and singing. Cindy held her mom's hand and joined in the fun.

As they got closer to the end of the march, Cindy noticed something in the air - a smell her mom had in the house the day before. Then, Cindy saw it - a bright pink balloon attached to one of the floats. It was the same ribbon Cindy had tied around her wrist the day before!

Cindy smiled and waved as the pink march went by. It was a special day and Cindy was very proud of her ribbon.

Once upon a time, there was a brown jet. The brown jet could fly very high in the sky. It loved to fly fast and make big loops.

One day, the brown jet was flying very fast. It wanted to see how fast it could go. But then, it hit a big cloud. The brown jet started to break.

The brown jet was sad. It could not fly anymore. It needed help to fix the break. A kind bird saw the brown jet and wanted to help.

The bird found some friends to help fix the brown jet. They all worked together to make the jet better. Soon, the brown jet could fly again. It was so happy and thanked the bird and its friends. From that day on, the brown jet flew with care and always had friends in the sky.

Once upon a time there was a little boy. He was jumping around, waving his hand in the air. He was so happy and excited—he'd just seen a new toy! It was shiny and colourful, and he loved it.

The little boy held his hand up and waved it again. He wanted to show everyone his new toy. He waved it over and over, as high as he could. He just couldn't believe how much he loved his new toy.

Soon after, his mom came over and gave him a hug. She said, "I'm so glad you like your new toy! I can tell you really enjoy it." The little boy smiled and held up his hand to show off his toy once again. He just couldn't stop waving his hand. His new toy made him so happy!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, Lily woke up and found out that her tooth was wiggly. She was very excited because she knew that the tooth fairy would come and leave a surprise for her under her pillow when she lost her tooth.

Lily's mom told her that she needed to keep her tooth organized and safe until it was ready to come out. Lily listened and made sure to brush her teeth extra carefully.

After a few days, Lily's tooth started to hurt and she didn't want to eat her favorite foods anymore. Finally, Lily decided to surrender and let her mom pull out her tooth. It was scary at first, but Lily was very brave and didn't cry.

That night, Lily put her tooth under her pillow and went to sleep. The next morning, she woke up to find a shiny coin from the tooth fairy! Lily was very happy and couldn't wait for her next tooth to fall out.

Once, there was a giant who had a huge space under his arm. It was so big that he could fit all of his friends in it. One day, the giant got sad and wept. Everyone was worried and wondered why he was so sad.

The giant's friends wanted to cheer him up. So they called up a magical unicorn and asked if it could help. The magical unicorn flew over to the giant and said it could help.

The unicorn told the giant that the huge space under his arm was magical. Inside, the giant could hold all of his worries, and soon he would feel much better. So the giant opened the huge space and put all of his worries in it.

It was like a magical trick! The giant stopped weeping and was soon laughing and playing. Everyone was so happy that the giant was back to feeling good again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Amy. She was three years old. She loved playing with her friends, eating ice cream and helping her mommy at home.

One day, Amy was feeling sad. She ran outside into the garden and sat in the grass. She looked around and saw a big, yellow flower. Suddenly, the flower started to grow! Amy was so surprised. The flower grew and grew until it was as big as Amy.

"Hello," said the flower. "My name is Daisy. What's yours?"

"My name is Amy," said Amy. "I'm so happy you can talk!"

"Me too," said Daisy. "Let's be friends forever. We can do lots of fun things together. What would you like to do?"

Amy thought for a moment. "Let's make some ice cream!" she said.

So Daisy and Amy went to the kitchen and made a delicious bowl of ice cream. They laughed and talked as they stirred the cream.

"Thank you for being my friend today," said Amy to Daisy. "I feel happy now."

"It was fun to be your friend, too," said Daisy.

And they both grinned big, happy smiles.

Lila was a shy girl. She did not like to talk to new people. She liked to play with her toys and read her books. One day, her mom said they had to go to the park. Lila did not want to go. She was afraid of the big kids and the loud noises.

At the park, Lila sat on a bench with her mom. She watched the other kids run and play. She saw a boy with a ball. He looked nice. He smiled at her. He threw the ball to her. Lila caught it. She wanted to throw it back, but she was shy.

"Hi, I'm Sam. What's your name?" the boy asked.

Lila did not answer. She looked at her mom. Her mom nodded. She wanted Lila to make a friend.

"Can I play with you?" the boy asked.

Lila nodded. She threw the ball to him. He threw it back. They played catch for a while. Lila started to feel happy. She liked Sam. He was fun.

"Let's go on the slide!" Sam said.

Lila was scared. The slide was high and fast. She had never been on it before.

"Come on, it's fun!" Sam said. He ran to the slide. He climbed the steps. He slid down. He laughed.

Lila watched him. She wanted to try, but she was shy.

"Come on, Lila! You can do it!" Sam said. He waited for her at the bottom.

Lila looked at her mom. Her mom smiled. She wanted Lila to be brave.

Lila took a deep breath. She got up from the bench. She walked to the slide. She climbed the steps. She felt nervous. She reached the top. She saw Sam. He cheered for her.

Lila sat on the slide. She held the sides. She pushed herself. She slid down. She felt the wind in her hair. She felt the thrill in her tummy. She reached the bottom. She smiled.

She did it!

Sam gave her a high-five. He hugged her. He said, "You're awesome, Lila!"

Lila hugged him back. She said, "You're awesome, Sam!"

They became friends. They played some more. They had fun. Lila was not shy anymore. She was happy.

Once upon a time there was a smart fox. He was hopping around in the forest and looking for something to eat. He came to a big river filled with water. He wanted to cross the river but he was stuck.

Then he had an idea! He decided to ask a frog for help. “Please, can you help me get across the river?” he asked. The frog said yes and hopped in the water.

Then the frog swam across the river and came back. “Hop on my back,” said the frog. The fox hopped on the back of the frog and the frog began to swim across the river.

The fox was so excited as they passed the river! He was so happy that he was able to cross with the help of the smart frog. When they reached the other side of the river, the fox thanked the frog and hopped away. The frog smiled and waved goodbye.

Once, there was a girl. She was very popular. Everyone in town liked her a lot. One day, she found a key. She was so excited! She thought she could open some special door with her new key.

The girl asked her mom if she could take the key with her. "No," said her mother. "You can't take it away."

The girl didn't listen. She took the key away, hoping to find something special. But when she returned home, her mom was very angry. She punished the girl for not listening.

The girl was very sad. She had to stay in her room for the whole day, without playing with her friends.

She never saw the key again. And she never opened the mysterious door.

Once upon a time, there was a happy family. The family had a playful dog named Max. Max loved to play with his toys and run around outside. One day, the family decided to go on a trip. They went to a beach far away from their home. They had a lot of fun playing in the sand and swimming in the ocean.

But then, something bad happened. A big hurricane came and destroyed everything in its path. The family was scared and didn't know what to do. They decided to send a message to their friends for help. But the storm was too strong and the message didn't go through. They were stuck on the beach with no food or water.

Days passed and the family grew weaker and weaker. Max tried to find food for them but there was nothing left. Eventually, the family passed away from hunger and thirst. Max was very sad and missed his family very much. He wished he could have done something to save them.

Once there was a black monkey named Joe. He lived high up in a tall tree and loved to climb. One day, he decided to explore and see what he could find.

Joe climbed down the trunk of the tree and scurried along the ground. Soon he found an old tree stump. He climbed it and peered around. There he saw a waist that was lying on the ground.

The waist was black in color and had tiny pockets. Joe was curious and wanted to know what was inside the pockets. He opened the pocket and pulled out a tiny yellow box. He sniffed the box and it made him curious.

Joe opened the box and inside there was an orange cookie. He took the cookie out of the box, licked it and said, “Yum!”

Joe was so excited, he climbed back up the tree as fast as he could. He nibbled on the cookie as he went. When he reached the top of the tree, he opened the box again and ate the rest of the cookie. He was happy and full and ready for his next adventure.

Lily was a cat who liked to explore. She was very curious and always wanted to see new things. One day, she saw a big white box in the kitchen. It was cold and had food inside. Lily wanted to try some of the food, so she jumped on the box and pushed the door open.

Inside the box, there were many yummy things. Lily saw cheese, milk, eggs, and meat. She licked her lips and started to eat. She did not hear her owner coming back from the store. She did not see him put more food in the box and close the door. She was trapped inside the box!

Lily was scared and cold. She meowed and scratched the door, but no one heard her. She felt very sorry for being greedy and sneaky. She wished she had listened to her owner, who always told her not to go near the box. She wondered if she would ever get out.

But Lily was also smart and brave. She remembered that the box had a light inside. She looked for the switch that turned the light on and off. She found it and pushed it with her paw. She hoped that someone would see the light and open the door.

Her plan worked. Her owner saw the light flickering in the kitchen. He wondered what was wrong with the box. He opened the door and saw Lily. He was surprised and angry, but also relieved. He took Lily out of the box and hugged her. He told her not to do that again, or she could get hurt. He gave her some water and a treat.

Lily was happy and grateful. She learned her lesson. She decided not to explore the box anymore, or any other place that was not safe. She thanked her owner and licked his face. She was a graceful cat who knew how to escape, but also how to behave.

The sun peeked over the horizon and the day began. Emily happily gazed out her window at the new day. She saw the trees and birds and felt so full of joy. Emily could not wait to start her day.

She put on her clothes and headed to the kitchen. There she saw a big table filled with all sorts of healthy food. Emily was ready to eat! She scooped a big spoonful of oatmeal and squished it in her mouth. The taste was so delicious!

Emily smiled and started to walk outside. She gazed up with wonder at the bright blue sky and all the birds flying around. Everything was so peaceful and beautiful. Emily took a deep breath and smiled.

She spent the day running around in the park, exploring and playing with her friends. Before Emily knew it, the sun was setting, and it was time to go.

Emily gave one last gaze of the beautiful day, full of sunshine and fresh air, and headed home happy and content.

Tom and Lily are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big truck. The truck has many tools and boxes. Tom and Lily want to see what is inside.

They run to the truck and climb on it. They open a box and find some seeds. They think the seeds are candy. They take some and eat them. They are not candy. They are very spicy. Tom and Lily spit them out. They are not delicious. They are yucky.

The truck driver sees them. He is angry. He says, "What are you doing? Those are not candy. Those are seeds for the wild flowers. I work hard to plant them. You are naughty. Go away!"

Tom and Lily are scared. They jump off the truck and run away. They say sorry to the truck driver. They do not want to eat seeds again. They want to eat ice cream. Ice cream is delicious.

Mama was having a lot of trouble with her car. It wouldn’t start, and the engine made funny noises.

“What’s wrong mama?” asked the 3 year old child.

“My car is broken,” replied mama.

“Can you repair it?”

Mama smiled. “I sure can, with some help.”

The little girl helped mama take the broken pieces of the car to the repair shop. They worked together to get the car fixed.

Finally, after a few days, mama got the car back in working order.

“Hey look mama! The car is fixed!” the little girl said excitedly.

Mama gave her a big hug. “Yes, we fixed it together. Now we can go anywhere we want!”

Anna was a thoughtful girl who liked to help others. She often visited her grandma, who was old and used a cane to walk. Anna liked to talk to her grandma and listen to her stories.

One day, Anna saw a big bag of apples at the market. She thought they would make a nice gift for her grandma, who loved apples. She asked the seller how much they cost. The seller said they cost one coin for each apple.

Anna counted her coins. She had five coins. She could buy five apples, but the bag had more than five apples. She wanted to buy the whole bag for her grandma. She had an idea. She asked the seller if he had a scale to weigh the apples.

The seller nodded and brought out a scale. He put the bag of apples on one side and a weight on the other side. The scale balanced. He said the bag of apples weighed the same as the weight.

Anna looked at the weight. It had a number on it. The number was ten. Anna thought hard. She remembered that her grandma's cane also had a number on it. The number was ten. She wondered if her grandma's cane weighed the same as the bag of apples.

She asked the seller if he would trade the bag of apples for her grandma's cane. The seller was surprised, but he agreed. He gave Anna the bag of apples and took her grandma's cane.

Anna was happy. She ran to her grandma's house with the bag of apples. She knocked on the door and gave her grandma the bag of apples. She said she traded her grandma's cane for the apples.

Her grandma was shocked. She asked Anna why she did that. She said she needed her cane to walk. She said she could not walk without her cane.

Anna felt sad. She did not think of that. She wanted to make her grandma happy, but she made her unhappy. She said she was sorry. She said she would get her cane back.

She ran back to the market with the bag of apples. She looked for the seller, but he was gone. He had left with her grandma's cane. Anna cried. She did not know what to do.

A kind man saw Anna crying. He asked her what was wrong. Anna told him what happened. The kind man felt sorry for Anna. He said he had a spare cane at home. He said he would give it to Anna if she gave him the bag of apples.

Anna was grateful. She thanked the kind man and gave him the bag of apples. He gave her the spare cane. He said it was a good trade. He said he liked apples and he did not need two canes.

Anna smiled. She ran back to her grandma's house with the spare cane. She knocked on the door and gave her grandma the spare cane. She said she got it from a kind man who traded it for the bag of apples.

Her grandma was relieved. She hugged Anna and thanked her. She said she was proud of her. She said she was a thoughtful girl who learned from her mistake. She said she loved her.

Anna was happy. She hugged her grandma and said she loved her too. She said she learned a lesson. She said she would never trade something important for something less important. She said she would always think of the consequences of her actions.

The end.

Tom was a very intelligent boy. He liked to read books and learn new things. He also liked to play with his dog, Spot. Spot was a good friend and a loyal pet.

One day, Tom and Spot went to the park. They saw many flowers and trees and birds. They also saw a big pond with ducks and frogs. Tom wanted to feed the ducks some bread. He took out a slice from his bag and tore it into pieces.

"Here, Spot, you can have some too," he said, and gave some bread to his dog.

Spot wagged his tail and ate the bread. He liked the taste and the smell. He saw more bread on the ground near the pond. He ran to get it, but he did not recognize the danger. There was a big sign that said "Do not feed the ducks. Bread is bad for them."

Tom saw Spot running and shouted, "Spot, come back! That bread is not good for you!"

But it was too late. Spot had already eaten some of the bread. He felt a strange itch in his mouth and throat. He started to cough and sneeze. He ran back to Tom, feeling sick and scared.

Tom saw that Spot was not well. He hugged him and said, "Don't worry, Spot. I will take you to the vet. He will make you better."

He picked up his bag and his dog and ran to the nearest bus stop. He hoped that Spot would be okay. He wished he had read the sign before giving him the bread. He learned a lesson that day. He learned to be more careful and to recognize the signs. He also learned to love his dog even more.

Once upon a time there was a fragile little girl who loved to spin. No matter where she went, she would spin around and around. One day, she told her parents that she was going to spin all the way to the west. Her parents laughed and said she was silly, but the little girl smiled and kept spinning.

Suddenly something magical happened. As the little girl spun faster and faster, the winds pushed her from side to side until she was going so fast that she was flying! She flew and flew until she finally reached the west, where the sunsets are especially beautiful.

The little girl was so happy that she had achieved her goal, and she felt very brave for going so far. From then on, whenever she was feeling scared or fragile, she would just take a deep breath and spin around like she did that day. That would remind her that she can go anywhere, no matter how far, if she just believes in herself.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lily. She loved to wear pretty dresses and play outside. One day, she saw a butterfly and ran after it. She was so excited that she didn't notice the big rock on the ground. She tripped and fell, and her dress got dirty.

Lily was sad because she loved that dress. But then she saw a seesaw and decided to play on it. She tried to balance on one side, but it was too hard. Suddenly, a wild gust of wind blew and made the seesaw go up and down very fast. Lily got scared and wanted to get off, but she couldn't.

Just then, her friend came to play and saw that Lily was in trouble. She helped her get off the seesaw and they both laughed. Lily was happy again, even though her dress was still dirty. She realized that having fun with her friend was more important than her pretty dress.

Ben and Lily were friends who liked to play in the farm. They liked to run in the grass, chase the chickens and watch the cows. Sometimes they helped their dads with the work, like picking corn or feeding the pigs.

One day, Ben and Lily decided to play a game. They wanted to see who could pick more corn from the field. They each took a big basket and ran to the corn plants. They started to pull the yellow ears and put them in their baskets.

"Look, Lily, I have more corn than you!" Ben said, showing his basket.

"No, you don't, Ben, I have more corn than you!" Lily said, showing her basket.

They kept picking corn and arguing, not paying attention to anything else. They did not see the sky getting dark and the wind getting strong. They did not hear the thunder and the rain. They did not notice the corn plants shaking and bending.

Suddenly, a loud noise made them stop and look up. They saw a big, black cloud spinning in the air. It was coming towards them, fast and angry. It was a tornado!

"Ben, Lily, run!" their dads shouted from the barn. "The tornado is coming! It will increase and destroy everything!"

Ben and Lily dropped their baskets and tried to run, but it was too late. The tornado was too close and too strong. It picked them up and threw them in the air, along with the corn, the baskets, the chickens and the cows. They screamed and cried, but no one could hear them or help them.

The tornado carried them far away, to a place where the sky was clear, but the land was empty and cold. There was no farm, no grass, no animals, no dads. There was only corn, scattered and broken. Ben and Lily were alone and scared. They wished they had not played that game. They wished they had listened to their dads. They wished they had been good friends. But it was too late. The end.

Sam and Lily are playing in the park. They like to run, jump and slide. They see a big tree with wide branches. They want to climb the tree.

"Can we climb the tree, Sam?" Lily asks.

"Yes, we can, Lily. But be careful. The tree is very high," Sam says.

They climb the tree, one by one. They hold on to the branches and find a nice spot to sit. They can see the whole park from the tree. They feel happy and proud.

"Look, Sam, I can see our mom and dad. They are sitting on the bench. They have a basket with them. I think they have lunch for us," Lily says.

"Me too, Lily. I can see them. I am hungry. Do you want to go down and eat lunch?" Sam says.

"Yes, Sam. Let's go down and eat lunch. But how do we tell them we are in the tree?" Lily says.

"I know, Lily. We can call them. We can shout their names. They will hear us and look up. Then they will see us in the tree," Sam says.

"OK, Sam. Let's call them. On the count of three. One, two, three," Lily says.

They shout together, "Mom! Dad! We are in the tree!"

Mom and dad hear them and look up. They see Sam and Lily in the tree. They smile and wave.

"Hi, Sam and Lily. You are very brave to climb the tree. Come down and join us for lunch. We have sandwiches, apples and juice for you," mom says.

"OK, mom. We are coming down. We love you," Sam and Lily say.

They climb down the tree, carefully and safely. They run to mom and dad and hug them. They sit on the bench and eat lunch. They share their stories and laugh. They are a happy family.

Once upon a time there was a club. It was a big and special club. Inside was a very expensive toy.

One day, a little boy called Jack was visiting. He was only three years old and was very excited. He asked if he could play with the expensive toy. But his mum said no, it was too expensive.

Jack snuck away from his mum. He ran to the toy and started playing. His mum stopped looking for him and the toy started to disappear. Jack wondered what was happening.

"Mum, where did the toy go?" Jack asked, very confused.

"That was magic," his mum replied. "The toy disappeared. That is why it was so expensive."

Jack nodded his head. He was excited by the magic. He promised himself he would never touch an expensive toy again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to take photos with her camera. One day, she went to the park with her family and took lots of photos of the trees, flowers, and birds.

When they got home, Lily's mom asked her to show the photos she took. Lily remembered that she had saved them on her camera. She quickly found the photos and showed them to her family.

Lily's mom said the photos were very useful because they could use them to remember the fun day they had at the park. Lily was happy that her photos were helpful and made her family happy. From that day on, Lily took photos everywhere she went and loved to share them with her family.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. One day, Timmy and his mom went to the store to buy some food. While they were walking, Timmy saw a cartoon on a TV in the store. He pointed at it and said, "Mommy, can we watch the cartoon?" His mom said, "Sorry, Timmy. We can't watch the cartoon now. It's not available."

Timmy felt sad and started to shiver because he really wanted to watch the cartoon. Suddenly, a man who worked at the store came up to them and said, "Excuse me, ma'am. We have a special room where you can watch cartoons. Would you like to go there?" Timmy and his mom were very happy and followed the man to the room. They watched the cartoon and Timmy laughed and clapped his hands. He said, "Thank you, Mommy. Thank you, man. This is so fun!"

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to dance and sing. One day, Lily wanted to perform in a big show. She practiced every day, but she was very clumsy.

Her mom gave her a powder to help her not slip. Lily put the powder on her feet and practiced even more. She felt better and ready to perform.

On the day of the show, Lily was nervous, but she went on stage and danced her heart out. She wasn't clumsy anymore! Everyone clapped and cheered for her. Lily was so happy and proud of herself.

Susie was skipping down the street when she felt an itch on the back of her neck. Her furry cat had been following her, so she figured it was him.

"Meow," mewed the cat, "why are you skipping?"

"I'm skipping because it's fun," explained Susie.

The cat purred and said, "It's also fun to scratch my furry neck when I have an itch."

The little girl smiled and reached up to scratch her own neck.

"That feels much better!" said Susie.

The cat meowed in agreement and they went back to skipping down the street.

Anna likes to count. She counts her fingers, her toes, her dolls, and her books. She can count up to ten. She is very proud of herself.

One day, Anna finds a comb in her mom's drawer. It is shiny and has many teeth. Anna thinks it is a funny thing. She wonders how many teeth it has. She decides to count them.

She starts from one end and says the numbers out loud. One, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine, ten. She is not done yet. She keeps counting. Eleven, twelve, thirteen, fourteen, fifteen, sixteen, seventeen, eighteen, nineteen, twenty. She is still not done. She counts more. Twenty-one, twenty-two, twenty-three, twenty-four, twenty-five, twenty-six, twenty-seven, twenty-eight, twenty-nine, thirty. She is amazed. The comb has so many teeth.

She wants to show her mom. She runs to the living room, where her mom is reading a book. She holds up the comb and says, "Mom, look! I counted the teeth of the comb. It has thirty teeth. That is a lot of teeth."

Her mom smiles and hugs her. She says, "Wow, Anna, you are so smart. You counted all the way to thirty. That is a big number. I am very proud of you. And you know what? You have a lively mind. You are always curious and eager to learn new things. That is a good thing."

Anna feels happy and warm. She loves her mom. She loves to count. She loves the comb. She says, "Thank you, mom. I love you. Can I keep the comb?"

Her mom says, "Of course, you can. It is yours now. You can use it to comb your hair, or to count, or to play. It is a fun thing. Just be careful not to poke yourself with the teeth. They are sharp."

Anna nods and says, "Okay, mom. I will be careful. Can I count the teeth again?"

Her mom says, "Sure, you can. But first, can you give me a kiss?"

Anna says, "Yes, mom." She gives her mom a kiss and then runs back to her room with the comb. She counts the teeth again and again. She is happy. She likes to count.

Lila and Sam were hungry. They wanted to eat rice for dinner. But Mom said they had to wait. She was cooking the rice in a big pot on the stove.

Lila and Sam did not like to wait. They ran around the house and made a lot of noise. They played with their toys and threw them on the floor. They jumped on the couch and knocked over the lamp.

Mom was not happy. She said, "Lila and Sam, stop! You are making a mess. You need to settle down and be quiet. The rice will be ready soon."

Lila and Sam did not listen. They kept running and playing and making noise. They did not see the cat sleeping on the table. They bumped into the table and the cat woke up. The cat was scared and angry. It hissed and scratched Lila and Sam.

Lila and Sam cried. They ran to Mom and showed her their scratches. Mom said, "Oh, no! You hurt the cat and yourselves. You should have listened to me. Now you need to say sorry to the cat and clean up your mess."

Lila and Sam said sorry to the cat and gave it a hug. They picked up their toys and put them away. They fixed the lamp and the couch. They settled down and waited for the rice.

Mom smiled and said, "Good job, Lila and Sam. You learned your lesson. Now you can have some rice for dinner. But be careful, it is hot and hard. You need to blow on it and chew it well."

Lila and Sam nodded and said, "Thank you, Mom. We love rice. And we love you. And we love the cat." They ate their rice and enjoyed it. They were happy and full. They said good night to Mom and the cat and went to bed. They slept well and dreamed of rice.

Once upon a time there was a young boy named Thomas who really loved baseball. One day he was playing out in the garden when his ball suddenly flew into a tree. Thomas was very sad. He tried to reach for it but he couldn't.

Suddenly, his mom came outside and said, “Don’t worry, Thomas. I’ll help you save your baseball!” She found a ladder and stood on it so she could reach the ball. She grabbed it and handed it back to Thomas.

Thomas was so happy, he hugged his mom and said, “Thank you Mom. You’re very powerful!” His mom smiled and said, “Anything for my little baseball lover.”

Thomas was so excited he ran off to play with his baseball again. He learned that day that even with powerful help, he would never give up on his dreams.

Tom was a restless boy. He did not like to sit still or be quiet. He liked to run and jump and shout and play. He hated when his mom said it was time for a nap. He hated naps more than anything.

One day, Tom's mom had to go to the store. She asked Tom's old grandma to watch him. Tom did not like his old grandma. She was slow and boring and always told him to be good. She said he had to take a nap with her on the couch. Tom hated that idea.

He tried to sneak away, but his old grandma saw him. She grabbed his hand and pulled him to the couch. She said naps were good for him and her. She said they would feel better after a nap. Tom hated that lie.

He lay down on the couch, but he did not close his eyes. He waited for his old grandma to fall asleep. Then he got up and ran to his room. He found his toys and started to play. He made a lot of noise. He was happy.

But his old grandma heard him. She woke up and walked to his room. She was angry. She said he was a bad boy. She said he had to go back to the couch. She said he had to stay there until his mom came back. Tom hated that punishment.

He cried and kicked and screamed. He did not want to nap. He did not want to be with his old grandma. He wanted to play. He wanted his mom. He hated this day.

Once upon a time, there was a tree. It was a nice, harmless tree. On the tree there were lots of yummy peaches. Every day, the tree allowed the birds, bees and other animals to come and eat the peaches. They were so happy because the peaches were so tasty.

One day, a little girl named Lola found the tree. She saw the peaches and wanted to eat one. She asked the tree if she could have one. The tree looked at her and thought about it for a second. Then it said yes and allowed Lola to take one of the peaches.

Lola was so excited! She thanked the tree and carefully picked one of the peaches. It was a bit too big for her so she went back to the tree. She asked nicely if she could have a smaller one. The tree said yes and let her choose a smaller, harmless peach.

Lola was so happy. She thanked the tree and went away with her peach. The tree was glad it had been able to help Lola. It watched her go and smiled, knowing that it had made the little girl happy.

Lily and Max were going to a fancy party with their mom and dad. They wore nice clothes and shiny shoes. They got in the car and drove to the big house where the party was.

"Are we there yet?" Lily asked.

"Soon, sweetie," mom said. "We have to wait for the green light."

Max looked out the window and saw many cars and people. He saw a man with a file in his hand. He wondered what was in the file.

"Look, Lily, that man has a file. Maybe he is a spy," Max said.

Lily giggled. "No, silly, he is not a spy. He is a lawyer. He has papers in his file. Mom told me."

The car stopped and they arrived at the big house. They got out and walked to the door. A lady with a smile greeted them.

"Welcome to the party. Please give me your names and I will check the list," she said.

Mom gave their names and the lady looked at her file. She nodded and let them in.

"Have fun, kids. There are games and snacks in the garden," she said.

Lily and Max ran to the garden. They saw balloons and toys and cake. They were happy. They had arrived at the fancy party.

Sam saw a really big cop. He smiled and waved at him. "Hi, cop!" he said.

The cop smiled and waved back. "Hello, Sam!"

Sam pointed to the lemon tree in his garden. "Would you like some lemons?" he asked. "They're really sour!"

The cop grinned and nodded. "That sounds great!"

Sam got a ladder and carefully picked a few lemons. He handed them to the cop.

"Thanks, Sam!" the cop said. He took a bite of one of the lemons. "Wow, these are really sour!"

Sam smiled. "I recommend eating one with some sugar," he said. "It tastes much better!"

The cop tried it and smiled. "You're right, Sam. This tastes delicious!"

Once upon a time, there was a hairy bear. He loved to eat yummy honey and fish. One day, he wanted to explore the forest. So he went for a walk. He saw big trees, scary birds and he even saw a big river. But then he found some really yummy fruit. He decided to eat it. It was sweet, juicy and delicious. He ate so much that he was full and couldn't eat anymore. After he ate all the fruit, he went back home. He had a great adventure in the forest and he loved it.

Once upon a time, there was a humble dog named Spot. Spot lived in a small house with a fence around it. Spot loved to play with his ball and run around in the yard.

One day, Spot saw a big, red ball outside the fence. He wanted to play with it, but he couldn't get past the fence. Spot's owner, a kind girl named Lily, saw him looking at the ball. She told him to wait and that she would get the ball for him later. This made Spot happy, but he still wanted the ball right away.

A little while later, Lily went outside to get the ball. Spot was so excited that he forgot about the fence. He tried to jump over it, but he couldn't. Lily reminded him that he needed to wait for her to open the gate. When Lily opened the gate, Spot ran out and played with the big, red ball. It was the best day ever for the humble dog named Spot.

One day, Anna had an idea. She wanted to make prints of her creations. She started to work on the project, cutting shapes out of paper and using crayons to make them colorful.

Then she went to get the print. She carried her paper to the print shop and waited in line. When it was her turn, she showed the worker her creations, and he smiled. He put them all in the printer and started to work.

Before long, the prints were ready. Anna was excited. She thanked the worker and returned home with her creations.

When she showed them to her family, they were so excited! Everyone said they were beautiful! Anna was so happy that her project worked out and her family was spoiled with the prints she made.

Sara loves her cat, Max. Max is big and fit. He can run fast and jump high. He likes to play with Sara and her toys. Sara and Max are best friends.

One day, Sara and Max go to the park with Mom. Mom says they can play for a while, but they have to stay close. Sara and Max run and jump on the grass. They see a big tree with many birds. Max wants to catch a bird. He runs to the tree and climbs up.

Sara sees Max on the tree. She is scared. She calls him, "Max, come down! You can fall!" But Max does not listen. He jumps from branch to branch, chasing the birds. The birds fly away. Max is alone on the tree.

Mom sees Sara and Max. She is worried. She says, "Sara, we have to go. It is getting dark. Max, come down now!" But Max does not listen. He is stuck on the tree. He meows loudly. He is scared too.

Sara and Mom hope that Max can come down. They do not want to leave him. They look for a ladder or a rope. They ask other people for help. But no one has a ladder or a rope. No one can help.

Sara starts to cry. She says, "Max, please come down. I love you. I miss you. I need you." Max hears Sara. He loves her too. He misses her too. He needs her too. He looks for a way to come down. He sees a lower branch. He jumps to it. He sees another lower branch. He jumps to it. He does this until he reaches the ground.

Sara and Mom are happy. They hug Max. They say, "Max, you are brave. You are smart. You are safe." Max purrs. He is happy too. He hugs Sara and Mom. He says, "Meow, meow, meow." He means, "I am sorry. I am glad. I am home." Sara and Max go home with Mom. They are best friends.

Once upon a time, there was a furry cat named Mittens. Mittens loved to play with his toys and take naps in the sun. One day, Mittens' owner took him to a new place called "class".

At class, Mittens saw a big dog named Max. Max was very loud and didn't like Mittens. Max would bark and growl at Mittens every time he saw him. Mittens was scared and didn't know what to do.

One day, Mittens decided to be brave and wave at Max. To Mittens' surprise, Max stopped barking and started to wag his tail. They became friends and played together. Mittens learned that sometimes it's good to be brave and say hello, even if you're scared.

Lily and Ben were twins who liked to play together. One day, they found a pack of gum in their mom's purse. They wanted to try it, but they knew they had to ask first.

"Mom, can we have some gum?" Lily asked.

"No, sweeties, gum is not for little kids. It can make you choke or stick to your hair or teeth. You can have some fruit instead," Mom said.

But Lily and Ben did not listen. They were very nosy and curious. They took the gum when Mom was not looking and ran to their room. They opened the pack and each took a piece.

"Mmm, this is yummy!" Ben said. He blew a big bubble with his gum.

"Let me try!" Lily said. She tried to blow a bubble too, but she could not. She was angry and jealous. She wanted Ben's gum.

"Give me your gum!" she said. She tried to grab Ben's gum from his mouth.

"No, it's mine!" Ben said. He pulled away from Lily. They started to fight over the gum.

"Stop it, you two!" Mom said. She heard the noise and came to their room. She saw the gum in their mouths and on their clothes and bed. She was very angry and disappointed.

"What did you do? I told you not to have gum! You were very naughty and disobedient!" she said. She took the gum away from them and threw it in the trash. She made them brush their teeth and wash their clothes. She also gave them a time-out.

Lily and Ben felt very sorry and ashamed. They knew they had made a big mistake. They hugged Mom and said they were sorry.

"We love you, Mom. We won't have gum again," they said.

Mom hugged them back and said she loved them too. She said they had to learn to listen and share. She also said they had to be careful and not be too nosy.

"Sometimes, gum is not as good as it looks," she said. "And sometimes, Mom knows best."

Once upon a time, there was a wealthy man who lived in a big house. He had a lot of food for dinner every day. One day, a little boy came to his house. The boy was hungry and wanted some dinner.

The wealthy man saw the boy and gave him a big plate of food. The boy was very happy and said thank you. But then, the boy accidentally spilled his food on the floor. He was sad and worried the wealthy man would be mad.

The wealthy man saw the spilled food and smiled. He said, "I forgive you, don't worry." He gave the boy another plate of food for dinner. The boy was very thankful and they both ate dinner together. From that day on, they were good friends.

Lily was an adorable girl who loved to pray. Every night, she would kneel by her bed and talk to God. She would thank Him for her family, her friends, and her toys. She would also ask Him to bless the people who were sick, sad, or hungry.

One night, Lily heard a loud noise outside her window. She saw a big storm with rain, wind, and thunder. She was scared and ran to her mom and dad's room. She knocked on the door and said, "Mom, Dad, can I sleep with you? There is a scary storm outside."

Her mom and dad hugged her and said, "Of course, Lily. You can sleep with us. We are not afraid of the storm, because God is with us. He is watching over us and protecting us. Do you want to pray with us?"

Lily nodded and said, "Yes, please. I want to pray with you." She crawled into their bed and held their hands. They closed their eyes and prayed together. They thanked God for His love, His power, and His peace. They asked Him to calm the storm and keep them safe.

Lily felt better after praying. She was not scared anymore. She felt God's presence and love in her heart. She smiled and said, "I love you, Mom and Dad. I love you, God. Good night." She snuggled with them and fell asleep. The storm passed and the sky cleared. God heard their prayers and answered them. He loved them too.

Ben and Lily were playing in the living room. They liked to pretend they were grown-ups and had a fancy party. They had some juice in small cups and some crackers on a plate. They also had a big bottle of wine that they found in the kitchen. They did not know what wine was, but it looked pretty.

"Hello, Lily," Ben said in a deep voice. "Welcome to my party. Would you like some wine?"

"Yes, please, Ben," Lily said in a high voice. "Thank you for inviting me. You have a lovely home."

Ben poured some wine into Lily's cup. He tried to be careful, but he spilled some on the floor. He did not notice. He gave the cup to Lily and took one for himself. They clinked their cups and said, "Cheers!"

They sipped their wine and made faces. It tasted bad. They did not like it at all. They put their cups down and ate some crackers. They felt funny. They started to giggle and talk louder.

Mom came into the living room. She saw the wine bottle and the spilled wine on the floor. She saw Ben and Lily with their cups and their red faces. She was very angry.

"Ben! Lily! What are you doing?" she yelled. "That is not juice, that is wine! Wine is for grown-ups only! You are not allowed to drink wine! You could get sick!"

She took the wine bottle and the cups away. She cleaned the floor with a cloth. She looked at Ben and Lily with a stern face.

"That was very naughty and dangerous," she said. "You should never touch wine or any other drink that is not for you. You should always ask me or Dad before you take anything from the kitchen. Do you understand?"

Ben and Lily nodded. They felt sorry and scared. They did not mean to be bad. They just wanted to have fun.

"I'm sorry, Mom," Ben said.

"Me too, Mom," Lily said.

Mom hugged them and said, "I love you, but you have to be more careful. Now, go to your room and rest. You need to get the wine out of your system."

Ben and Lily went to their room. They lay down on their beds and closed their eyes. They felt sleepy and dizzy. They learned their lesson. They did not want to drink wine ever again. They only wanted juice and water.

The End.

It was time for the lecture to begin. Little Tom was excited to come to the high school and learn something new. When he arrived, he was amazed at the big space filled with many people.

The teacher started his lecture. He spoke with a voice that was calming and wise. Tom listened carefully and learned many new things. He began to feel a strange feeling in his heart.

Tom asked the teacher, "What is this feeling inside my heart?" The teacher smiled and said to him, "It's the feeling of healing. When you learn something new, your heart can heal and grow stronger."

Tom smiled and felt happy. He knew that the lecture would help him to heal and feel better. He thanked the teacher for his wise words and ran off to tell the other children the good news.

Once upon a time, there was a little blue bird. The bird was flying in the sky when suddenly a big storm came. The wind was blowing very hard and the rain was falling heavily. The little bird was scared and didn't know what to do.

Then, the bird saw a tree and decided to land on it. The tree was very tall and had big branches that could keep the bird safe from the storm. The little bird felt happy and safe on the tree.

But then, the storm got stronger and the tree started to shake a lot. The little bird knew that it was time to leave the tree and find another safe place. So, the bird flew away and found a cozy nest in a nearby bush. The little bird felt happy and safe again, and fell asleep.

Once upon a time, there were two friends who were playing together in the park. One day, they saw a stand painted black. They were curious and wanted to see what it was. But when they touched it, they were in trouble!

Their parents heard them and came running. They were very angry and said that they should be punished for touching the stand. The friends felt so scared but they couldn't help it.

The parents decided that the friends should stand in the corner for an hour as punishment. The friends had to stay there for an hour, feeling so sad. They wanted to keep playing but they couldn't.

When the hour was finally over, the friends went back to playing, but they were always extra careful with the stands from then on. They knew it wasn't good to make their parents mad. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim was playing in his room one day when he saw a cable on the floor. He wanted to know what the cable was for. So, he picked it up and took it to his mom.

His mom was in the kitchen making a sandwich. Tim showed her the cable and asked her what it was for. His mom looked at the cable and said, "This is a cable we use to watch TV. But be careful, it can be harsh if you pull on it too hard."

Tim was excited to learn about the cable. He took it back to his room and pretended it was a snake. He played with the cable all day, making sure not to pull on it too hard. And every night, he watched his favorite cartoons on TV with his mom using the cable.

Sara and Ben were playing in the yard. They liked to run and jump and chase each other. Sara saw a big pile of laundry on the porch. She had an idea.

"Let's play freeze tag!" she said to Ben. "You are it. If you touch me, I freeze. If I touch you, you freeze. OK?"

"OK!" Ben said. He ran after Sara. Sara ran away. She ran behind the laundry. She thought Ben could not see her.

But Ben was smart. He saw Sara's feet under the laundry. He sneaked up to her. He touched her arm.

"Freeze!" he shouted. "I got you!"

Sara was surprised. She tried to move, but she had to freeze. She was stuck behind the laundry.

Ben laughed. He was happy. He had won the game.

But then he heard a loud voice. It was Mom.

"Ben! Sara! What are you doing?" Mom said. "That is my clean laundry. You made it dirty and messy. Come here right now!"

Ben and Sara felt bad. They had been clumsy. They had ruined Mom's laundry. They came out from behind the laundry. They looked at Mom. They said sorry.

Mom was angry. She told them to go inside. She told them to help her with the laundry. She told them to not play with the laundry again.

Ben and Sara nodded. They followed Mom inside. They helped her with the laundry. They learned their lesson. They did not play with the laundry again.

Once there was a girl named Anna. She was very polite. Every day she would take her pencil to school. One day in the classroom Anna's teacher asked her to match the pencils. Anna was very excited and got to work. She carefully put one pencil with the same colours and patterns.

Anna was happy with her work. She was so proud that it was a perfect match! Each pencil was with its twin and each set was happy. All her friends were impressed by her matching skills.

When the day finished Anna was happy she had done such a good job. She said goodbye to her teacher and took her pencil home. She was now a pro at matching pencils!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She was very hungry and wanted a lollipop. Her mommy said she could have one if she ate all her dinner. So, Lily ate all her dinner and said "thank you" to her mommy.

Then, her mommy gave her a lollipop. It was red and round and looked very yummy. Lily was so happy and smiled a big smile. She licked the lollipop and it tasted very sweet.

After she finished the lollipop, Lily felt very full and happy. She hugged her mommy and said "thank you" again. Her mommy hugged her back and said she was proud of her for eating all her dinner. From that day on, Lily knew that if she ate all her food, she could have a yummy lollipop.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. He loved to ride his bicycle in the park every day. One day, he saw a big lion in the park. The lion was very scary and Timmy was afraid. The lion started to roar very loudly.

Timmy was very sad because he couldn't ride his bicycle anymore. He was too scared to go back to the park. One day, Timmy saw a circus in town. He wanted to see the circus but he was still scared of the lion. His mom told him that there were no lions in the circus, only clowns and acrobats.

Timmy went to the circus and had a lot of fun. He saw clowns doing funny tricks and acrobats doing amazing flips. He forgot about the lion and was happy again. When he got home, he told his mom that the circus was not disgusting like the lion in the park.

Once upon a time, in a small town, there was a foolish cat named Tom. Tom loved to play music. One day, he found a big red box. He thought, "I will put my music in the box so I won't forget it."

The next day, Tom went to play with his friends. He told them about the big red box and the music inside. His friends were very excited. They wanted to hear the music too. But Tom forgot where he put the box. He and his friends looked everywhere.

At last, they found the big red box under a tree. Tom opened the box and played the music. All his friends danced and had fun. Tom was happy he found the box and didn't forget the music. From that day on, he always remembered where he put his things.

Once upon a time there was a girl named Susie. One day, Susie decided to go for a walk in the park. She was so excited to see all the fun things she could find.

The first thing she noticed was a golf ball. It was a fine golf ball. Susie smiled and picked it up. She thought the golf ball looked so nice that she decided to own it.

After that, Susie got busy trying to find more fun things to own. She found a rock, a stick and some flowers. She was so proud of herself and her new things she got to own.

When it was time to go home, Susie was thrilled to show her new items to her mom and dad. They were so proud of Susie and they were happy that she found some fine things to own.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She lived in a house with a big chimney on the roof. One night, Lily was feeling very sleepy, so she went to bed.

As she lay in bed, she realized that she had forgotten to close the window in her room. She got up and went to close it, but when she looked outside, she saw something strange.

There was a man dressed in red climbing down the chimney! Lily was very surprised and scared, but then she realized that it was just Santa Claus delivering presents. She smiled and went back to bed, dreaming of all the toys she would find under the Christmas tree in the morning.

Lily and Ben were friends who liked to play in the park. One day, they saw a big pond with many ducks and fish. They wanted to swim with them, but their mom said no. She said the water was too cold and dirty, and they could get sick.

"But mom, we have swim suits and towels!" Lily said. "We can be dry and warm after we swim!"

Mom shook her head. "No, Lily, it's not safe. You can watch the ducks and fish, but you have to stay on the grass. Do you understand?"

Lily and Ben nodded, but they were not happy. They sat on the grass and watched the pond. They saw a big fish jump out of the water and splash. They saw a duck with a green head and a yellow beak. They saw a shiny thing in the water that looked like a star.

"What is that?" Ben asked, pointing at the shiny thing.

"I don't know. Maybe it's a coin or a ring. Let's go and see!" Lily said.

She got up and ran to the edge of the pond. She reached out her hand to grab the shiny thing. But as she did, she slipped and fell into the water. She screamed and splashed.

"Lily!" Ben shouted. He ran to help her, but he was too scared to go into the water. He looked around and saw a long stick. He picked it up and tried to attach it to Lily's hand. He hoped she could hold on and pull herself out.

But the stick was too short and Lily was too far. She could not reach it. She was cold and wet and scared. She cried for help.

Mom heard her cry and ran to the pond. She saw Lily in the water and Ben with the stick. She was angry and worried. She jumped into the water and swam to Lily. She grabbed her and lifted her out of the water. She hugged her and checked if she was okay.

"Lily, what were you doing? You could have drowned! You disobeyed me and went to the pond. That was very naughty and dangerous!" Mom said.

"I'm sorry, mom. I wanted to see the shiny thing. It looked like a star. But I slipped and fell. I was so scared. I'm sorry, mom." Lily said.

Mom sighed and kissed her. "It's okay, Lily. I'm glad you're safe. But you have to listen to me and stay away from the pond. The shiny thing was not a star. It was a bottle cap. It's not worth risking your life for. Do you understand?"

Lily nodded. She felt sorry and ashamed. She hugged mom and said, "I love you, mom. Thank you for saving me."

Mom smiled and said, "I love you too, Lily. Come on, let's go home and get you dry and warm. And you too, Ben. You were a good friend for trying to help Lily. But next time, call me if something happens. Okay?"

Ben nodded. He felt sorry and relieved. He hugged mom and said, "I love you, mom. Thank you for being here."

Mom took Lily and Ben by the hand and walked to the car. They left the pond and the ducks and the fish and the shiny thing behind. They learned a lesson that day. They learned to obey mom and to be careful near the water. They learned that swim is fun, but only in a safe place. And they learned that dry is better than wet.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved to spell words. She would sit in her room and spell words all day long. One day, Lily's friend Timmy came to visit her. "Hi Lily," Timmy said with a kind smile. "What are you doing?"

"I'm spelling words," replied Lily. "Do you want to spell with me?"

"Sure!" said Timmy happily. They spelled words together for a while, but Timmy was having trouble with some of the harder words. "I can't spell this word," he said sadly.

"Don't worry," said Lily kindly. "You will gain the ability to spell harder words with practice. Let's keep trying together!" And they continued to spell words together, happy to have each other's company.

Once upon a time, there was a big, friendly bear. He had a handle in his paw. He wanted to push it, to explore the world. As he was about to push the handle, he noticed a little mouse near him.

The bear said, "Why don't you come and help me push the handle? We can explore together." The little mouse looked very scared.

The bear said, "Don't be scared. I'm a very kind bear. Come, let's go and explore together."

The mouse said, "Oh, ok. Thank you for being so kind."

So the bear and the mouse pushed the handle together. They explored places that neither of them had ever seen before.

The moral of the story is that being kind to others will make them feel safe. Everyone can explore and do amazing things if we all work together.

Once upon a time there was a princess. She lived in an amazing palace. Every night she looked out of her window and wished she could explore the world outside.

One day, something magical happened - a giant appeared, like out of a storybook. He had a big smile and said he wanted to take the princess out of the palace. She nodded with excitement!

The giant took the princess on an adventure around the world - they explored snowy mountains, deep oceans, and dense forests. Everywhere they went was more amazing than the last.

At the end of the day, the giant took the princess back to the palace. He said goodbye and thanked her for such a fun adventure. She smiled and nodded happily.

Every night the princess looked at the stars and remembered her amazing adventure with the giant. She would never forget it!

Two friends were walking in a wild field. They came across a big dinner. One wanted to eat it, but the other disagreed. The one who wanted to eat it got very mad. He picked the other one up and threw him across the field. The friend was very scared and ran away. The other was left alone and very sad not to have a friend anymore. He tried to find a way to make it right but it was too late. Unfortunately, the bad ending was finally there.

Once upon a time, there was a small boy. He had an exciting day ahead of him and was ready to explore. He started out looking in his bedroom, examining his toys on the carpet. He carefully examined a dump truck and a teddy bear.

Next, he walked into the bathroom and wanted to see what was inside the sink. His eyes lit up as he saw lots of bubbles in the sink! He touched the bubbles and they felt so squishy and slimy. He was amazed and kept examining each bubble.

He then moved onto the kitchen. It was full of fancy plates and cups. He took a look inside the fridge, it was full of nice food. The smell of ice cream made his nose tickle. He then turned his attention to the oven - he could just see the top of a modest cake!

Once upon a time, there was a big ball. The ball was red and round. A little girl saw the ball and wanted to play with it. She rolled the ball on the grass and it was so much fun!

One day, the little girl went for a walk and saw a beautiful bridge. She walked on the bridge and saw the water underneath. The water was blue and sparkly. She thought the bridge was so pretty.

After walking on the bridge, the little girl found her red ball again. She rolled it on the bridge and watched it go up and down. It was a lot of fun to play with her ball on the beautiful bridge.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a blue toy car that she loved to play with. One day, Lily went to the park with her mom and forgot to bring her toy car. She was sad because she wanted to play with it.

When they got home, Lily remembered that she forgot her toy car at the park. Her mom told her not to worry and that they could go back to the park to get it. Lily was happy again.

When they got to the park, Lily found her blue toy car right where she left it. She was so happy to have it back and played with it all day long. From that day on, Lily never forgot to bring her toy car with her again.

One day, Maria and her mom went to the park. When they got there, Maria hugged her mom and said, "Mommy, I'm so happy you took me to the park!"

Her mom smiled and said, "It's so nice to spend some time together, honey."

Maria looked around and saw lots of children playing. She saw a group of kids playing tag and said, "Mommy, can I play tag with them?"

Her mom said, "That looks like a fair game, yes. Go ahead."

Maria ran over to the group and admired their fair play. She asked if she could join, and they said yes.

Maria and the kids had a great time playing. They laughed and chased each other around the park. When it was time to go home, Maria said goodbye to her new friends and thanked her mom for taking her to the park.

Lisa and Ben are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, Lisa falls from the swing and hurts her knee. It bleeds a lot. Ben runs to get help.

"Lisa, are you okay?" Ben asks. He is scared.

"It hurts, Ben. It hurts a lot," Lisa cries. She holds her knee.

A lady comes with a bandage. She is a nurse. She cleans Lisa's knee and puts the bandage on it.

"There, there. You'll be fine, Lisa. The bandage will help your knee heal," the nurse says. She is kind.

"Thank you, nurse. You are nice," Lisa says. She feels better.

"Can I go play with Ben now?" Lisa asks.

"Sure, but be careful. Don't run too fast or jump too high. And change your bandage every day," the nurse says.

Lisa and Ben hug the nurse and go back to the park. They play with the slide and the sandbox. They are happy.

The next day, Lisa and Ben go to school. They are in the same class. Their teacher is Miss Amy. She is organized. She has a plan for every day. She teaches them letters and numbers and colors and shapes.

"Today, we are going to learn about animals. Do you like animals?" Miss Amy asks.

"Yes, we do!" Lisa and Ben say.

"Good. Let's name some animals. Who wants to start?" Miss Amy says.

Lisa raises her hand. She wants to start.

"Okay, Lisa. What animal do you want to name?" Miss Amy says.

Lisa thinks for a moment. She remembers the nurse who helped her. She smiles.

"I want to name a nurse," Lisa says.

Miss Amy laughs. She thinks Lisa is funny.

"A nurse is not an animal, Lisa. A nurse is a person who helps people who are hurt or sick. Do you know why Lisa said a nurse?" Miss Amy asks.

Ben raises his hand. He knows why Lisa said a nurse.

"Because Lisa has a bandage on her knee. She fell from the swing and the nurse helped her. She is a good nurse. Lisa likes her," Ben says.

Miss Amy nods. She is proud of Ben.

"That's right, Ben. Lisa has a bandage on her knee. And she likes the nurse who helped her. That's very sweet of Lisa. Do you know what that means? It means Lisa misses the nurse. She wants to see her again. Do you ever miss someone?" Miss Amy asks.

Lisa and Ben nod. They miss their parents when they are at school. They miss their grandparents when they are far away. They miss their friends when they are sick.

"Sometimes, we miss people who are not with us. That's okay. It means we love them and care about them. And we can always call them or write to them or draw them a picture. That makes them happy. And it makes us happy too. Do you want to draw a picture for someone you miss?" Miss Amy asks.

Lisa and Ben say yes. They want to draw a picture for someone they miss. They get their crayons and paper. They draw a picture for the nurse. They write "Thank you" and "We miss you" on it. They are proud of their picture.

They give their picture to Miss Amy. She likes it. She says she will give it to the nurse the next time she sees her. She says the nurse will be very happy.

Lisa and Ben smile. They are happy too. They don't feel sad anymore. They have each other. And they have Miss Amy. And they have the nurse. They have many people who love them and help them. They are lucky.

Once upon a time, there was a dancer named Lily. She loved to dance in the rain. One day, Lily went outside to dance, but it started to rain really hard. She got wet and cold.

Lily's friend, Timmy, saw her dancing in the rain and asked, "Lily, why don't you go inside? You're getting wet!"

Lily replied, "I want to stay outside and dance in the rain. It's fun!"

Timmy thought about it and said, "Okay, I'll stay with you and dance too!"

So, Lily and Timmy danced together in the rain until they were both soaking wet. They had so much fun and laughed the whole time. The end.

Tom and Mia are twins. They like to play outside in the sun. One day, they see a big hill with many trees. They want to climb the hill and see what is on the other side.

They hold hands and start to walk up the hill. They see many birds and flowers and bugs. They are happy and curious. They talk to each other and laugh.

"Look, Tom, a red bird!" Mia says, pointing to the sky.

"Wow, it is so pretty!" Tom says, looking up.

But as they look up, they do not see where they are going. They stumble on a rock and fall down. They hurt their knees and elbows. They cry and hug each other.

"Ow, ow, ow!" Mia says, rubbing her knee.

"Are you okay, Mia?" Tom says, wiping his tears.

"I think so, Tom. Are you okay?" Mia says, looking at his elbow.

"I think so, too. But look, what is that?" Tom says, pointing to something black and gray on the ground.

They see a pile of ash. It is from a fire that burned some of the trees. It is still warm and smoky. They are scared and curious.

"What is it, Tom?" Mia says, touching the ash.

"It is ash, Mia. It is what is left after something burns. It is not good to touch. It can hurt you." Tom says, pulling her hand away.

"Who burned the trees, Tom?" Mia says, looking around.

"I don't know, Mia. Maybe someone who is lazy and does not care about the trees. Or maybe it was an accident. But we should not stay here. It is not safe. Let's go back." Tom says, holding her hand.

"Okay, Tom. Let's go back. Maybe we can find another hill to climb. One that is green and happy." Mia says, nodding.

They get up and walk back down the hill. They are careful and watch where they are going. They see the red bird again and wave to it. They are happy and curious. They talk to each other and laugh.

One day, a little girl wanted to go to the zoo. She was very excited and could not wait to see all the animals.

So her mum took her to the zoo. When they got there, they had to get a ticket. The mum said to the girl, "We need to print a ticket before we can go in."

So they went to the ticket machine and the mum inserted some money and pressed the print button. Out came two tickets! The mum gave one to the little girl and one to herself.

The girl was very serious as she held her ticket in her hand, and with a big smile she said, "Let's go see the animals!" The mum and the little girl went inside the zoo and had a wonderful time.

One day, a little girl named Lily went on a walk with her mommy. They saw a big tree that was starting to rot. "Mommy, what does rot mean?" asked Lily. "It means that the tree is getting old and weak," her mommy explained.

As they kept walking, they saw a car that needed fuel. "Mommy, what is fuel?" asked Lily. "It's like food for the car. It helps it go," her mommy answered.

Suddenly, they heard a noise coming from a nearby bush. "What was that?" asked Lily. "I don't know, let's go check," said her mommy. As they got closer, they saw a little bird who looked very weak. "Oh no, we need to help it," said Lily. They brought the bird to a nearby vet who gave it some medicine. The bird got better and flew away happily.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy had a thermometer, which he used to check his temperature when he was sick. One day, Timmy accidentally dropped his thermometer and it broke.

Timmy's mom asked him why he looked sad. Timmy replied, "My thermometer is broken." His mom said, "Oh no! Let's go to the store and get a new one."

At the store, Timmy and his mom found a new thermometer. The store worker asked Timmy if he needed help finding anything else. Timmy said, "No thank you, we just need a thermometer to part with the old one."

With his new thermometer, Timmy felt happy again. He knew he could use it to check his temperature whenever he felt sick.

Lily was a big girl. She wanted to learn how to use the toilet by herself. She asked her mom to teach her.

"Okay, Lily, I will teach you how to use the toilet," her mom said. "But you have to be humble and listen to me."

Lily nodded. She followed her mom to the bathroom. Her mom showed her how to pull down her pants and sit on the toilet. She told her to wait until she felt the pee or the poop come out. Then she showed her how to wipe herself and flush the toilet. She also told her to wash her hands with soap and water.

Lily tried to do everything her mom taught her. She was happy when she peed on the toilet. She was proud when she pooped on the toilet. She smiled when she wiped herself and flushed the toilet. She giggled when she washed her hands.

"Good job, Lily! You are a big girl now!" her mom said. "You learned how to use the toilet by yourself. You were humble and listened to me. I am so proud of you!"

Lily hugged her mom. She said, "Thank you, mom! You are the best teacher! I love you!"

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Jake. Jake was very excited because he was going on a special safari. He got to wear a new outfit and he couldn't wait to explore the wild jungle. He had never been on a safari before and he was very excited.

On the safari, Jake started to notice that something wasn't right. He started to frown as he looked around. Everywhere he looked, he could see old and dirty animals. He thought they were supposed to be new and unique ones.
