Then suddenly, he heard some strange noises coming from the bushes. He walked closer and noticed two beautiful new tigers! He was so happy! He couldn't believe it. He let out a huge smile and the tigers ran away.

After that, Jake continued to explore the safari, and he found more amazing new animals. Finally, it was time to go home, and Jake was so excited about what he had seen. He knew he would never forget his safari adventure.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Jack. Jack loved to eat cookies, especially the ones his mommy made. They were so delicious!

One day, Jack's mommy asked him to help her file some papers. Jack didn't want to do it because he wanted to eat cookies instead. His mommy told him he needed to behave and help her, or else he wouldn't get any cookies.

Jack decided to be a good boy and help his mommy file the papers. After they finished, his mommy gave him a big plate of delicious cookies as a reward for behaving. Jack was so happy and proud of himself for being a good helper.

Tom and Lily are twins. They like to play together and observe things. They observe birds, flowers, cars, and people. Sometimes they observe things that are not nice, like bugs, trash, or smoke.

One day, Tom and Lily observe a big, ugly dog. The dog is black and brown, and has a lot of hair. The dog is angry and barks loud. The dog chases a cat and bites it. The cat cries and runs away. Tom and Lily are scared and run away too.

They run to their mom, who is in the kitchen. They tell her what they observe. Mom is sad and worried. She says, "That is a bad dog. He needs medicine. Medicine can make him calm and nice. Maybe he is sick or hurt. We should call the animal doctor."

Tom and Lily nod. They understand. They love animals, even ugly ones. They hope the cat is okay. They hope the dog gets medicine. They hug their mom and go to their room. They play with their stuffed animals and observe them. They are soft and cute. They make them happy.

Once there was a famous girl. Her name was Mary. Mary was very smart. She liked to play with math. Every day she practised her math. She learnt new things and she repeated them again and again. She did this everyday and soon she was really good at math. Everyone was so surprised that a small girl like her was so famous for her math. Mary was so happy. She used to repeat her math and everyone would clap and cheer. It was fun and Mary liked it. So she kept practising, repeating her math every day. And soon she was famous for her math.

Once upon a time, there was a mommy and a little girl. The mommy was cooking dinner, and the little girl wanted to help.

The mommy said, "Go to the pantry and get the potatoes." The little girl said, "Ok! I'll put the potatoes in the pot." So she put the potatoes into the pot and the mommy said, "Thank you, sweetheart!"

The mommy said, "Now, let's put in some carrots, too." So the little girl put the carrots in the pot with the rest of the dinner, and the mommy said, "Excellent job!"

The little girl said, "Can I stir the dinner too?" The mommy said, "Sure, go ahead!" So the little girl stirred and stirred and stirred, until the dinner was all mixed up. The mommy said, "What a crazy dinner!"

The little girl said, "It looks yummy!" The mommy said, "Yes, it sure does!"

So they served up their dinner, and ate until their bellies were full. The end.

Once upon a time there was a little girl who wanted to manage a very special magnet. She looked and looked, but she couldn't find it. One day she asked her mom, "Can you help me manage my magnet?"

Her mom smiled and said, "Yes, of course I can. Where did you see it last?"

The little girl thought for a moment, then said, "I think I saw it in my quiet room yesterday."

So the mom and the little girl went off to the quiet room and sure enough, there was the special magnet. The little girl was so happy. She picked it up and hugged it tightly.

"Thank you mom," she said. "I managed to find my magnet."

Her mom smiled and said, "You did it! You managed to find it yourself. You did a great job."

The little girl was so proud she hugged her mom tightly. From then on she was very careful to manage her special magnet and make sure it was always in the right place.

Once upon a time, there was a hungry boy walking in the hot desert. He was looking for an oasis so he could have something to eat and drink. After a long time walking, the boy started to get tired and thirsty.

Suddenly, the boy saw an oasis nearby! He was so excited and ran quickly towards it. When he arrived, he saw there were two parts.

The hungry boy was so thirsty, he went to the first part and started to drink from the water. He had been walking for so long, he drank and drank until he was not thirsty anymore.

Then, he walked to the second part of the oasis and there were lots of delicious fruits. He quickly ate as many as he could. The boy was so happy!

After he was finished, the boy looked around and realized the oasis was separated into two parts. He smiled and was so thankful to find such a wonderful oasis.

Sara was very sick. She had a bad cough and a hot head. Mom took her to the doctor. Sara did not like the doctor. He had a white coat and a big bag. He looked at Sara with a light and a stick. He said, "You have a fever and a sore throat. You need some medicine and some rest."

Sara did not want medicine. She did not want rest. She wanted to play with her toys and watch TV. She said, "No, no, no! I don't want medicine. I don't want rest. I want to go home!"

Mom said, "Sara, you have to take the medicine. It will make you feel better. And you have to rest. It will help you heal. The doctor knows what is best for you."

The doctor said, "Don't worry, Sara. The medicine is not bad. It is a little needle. It will only hurt for a second. Then you will feel cool and calm. You can have a sticker and a lollipop after."

Sara was scared of the needle. She cried and kicked. She said, "No, no, no! I don't want the needle. I don't want the sticker. I don't want the lollipop. I want to go home!"

Mom hugged Sara and said, "Sara, I know you are scared. But the needle is not so bad. I will hold your hand and sing to you. It will be over soon. Then we can go home and rest. You will feel better tomorrow."

Sara looked at Mom and said, "Really? You will hold my hand and sing to me?"

Mom said, "Yes, really. I love you, Sara. I want you to be well."

Sara said, "I love you, Mom. I will try to be brave."

The doctor gave Sara the needle. It hurt for a second. Then Sara felt cool and calm. She got a sticker and a lollipop. She said, "Thank you, doctor. I'm sorry I was naughty."

The doctor said, "You're welcome, Sara. You were very brave. Now you can go home and rest. You will be fine soon."

Mom and Sara went home. Sara rested on the couch with her toys and TV. She felt better the next day. She said, "Mom, you were right. The medicine and the rest helped me. I'm sorry I was naughty."

Mom said, "I'm glad you're better, Sara. You don't have to be sorry. You were sick and scared. I understand. I'm proud of you, Sara. You are a good girl."

Ben and Mia are at the beach with their mom and dad. They like to play in the sand and splash in the water. They see many fish and shells and crabs. They are very happy.

One day, they find a big shark tooth in the sand. It is white and sharp and shiny. Ben and Mia are very excited. They show it to their mom and dad.

"Wow, that is a very original shark tooth!" mom says. "It must be from a very old and big shark. Maybe it lived here a long time ago."

"Can we keep it?" Ben asks.

"Of course, you can keep it. It is a very special find. But you have to be careful with it. It is very sharp and it can hurt you or someone else." dad says.

Ben and Mia nod. They wrap the shark tooth in a towel and put it in their bag. They want to show it to their friends when they go back home.

They play some more in the water and then they go to dry themselves with another towel. They are very hungry and thirsty. They go to have a picnic with their mom and dad. They have sandwiches and juice and cookies. They are very yummy.

They have a lot of fun at the beach. They love their shark tooth. They think it is the best thing they ever found. They are very proud.

Tommy was playing with his toys in his room when he heard a knock on the door. He ran to open it and saw his mom holding a big envelope. She smiled and said, "Look, Tommy, this is a letter from your grandma. She sent you a present for your birthday. Do you want to open it?"

Tommy nodded and took the envelope from his mom. He ripped it open and saw a card with a picture of a cake and a balloon. He opened the card and saw a shiny coin inside. He gasped and said, "Wow, a coin! Thank you, grandma!"

His mom hugged him and said, "You're welcome, sweetie. Grandma loves you very much. She said you can use the coin to buy something you like. What do you want to buy?"

Tommy thought for a moment and said, "I want to buy a candy. Can we go to the store now?"

His mom checked her watch and said, "Sure, we can go to the store. But first, you have to put on your shoes and coat. It's cold outside."

Tommy ran to his closet and grabbed his shoes and coat. He put them on and followed his mom to the door. He was so excited to buy a candy with his coin. He forgot to put the envelope and the card in his toy box.

When they came back from the store, Tommy saw his little sister, Lily, sitting on his bed. She was holding the envelope and the card. She looked at Tommy with a guilty face and said, "I'm sorry, Tommy. I was curious. I wanted to see what grandma sent you. I didn't mean to take your coin."

Tommy felt angry and sad. He said, "You took my coin? That was my present from grandma. That was not nice, Lily. You have to give it back to me."

Lily started to cry and said, "I'm sorry, Tommy. I don't have it. I lost it. I was playing with it and it rolled under the bed. I tried to find it, but I couldn't. I'm sorry, Tommy. Please don't be mad at me."

Tommy looked under the bed and saw the coin shining in the corner. He reached for it and grabbed it. He felt happy and relieved. He said, "It's okay, Lily. I found it. I'm not mad at you. But you have to ask me before you touch my things. And you have to say thank you to grandma for the coin. She was very nice to send it to us."

Lily nodded and said, "Thank you, grandma. And thank you, Tommy. You are a good brother. Can I have a candy, too?"

Tommy smiled and said, "Sure, you can have a candy. But only one. We have to save some for later. And we have to brush our teeth after. Mom said too much candy can increase the germs in our mouth. And we don't want that, right?"

Lily shook her head and said, "No, we don't want that. We want to have healthy teeth and happy smiles. Come on, Tommy. Let's go and share our candy."

Once upon a time, there was a big red car. The car had a new rope. The car wanted to work and help people.

One day, the car saw a little cat stuck in a tree. The cat was sad and scared. The car wanted to help the cat. So, the car used the new rope to work and save the cat.

The car tied the rope to the tree and pulled it. The tree bent down and the cat jumped onto the car. The cat was happy and safe. The car was proud of its work. Everyone cheered for the big red car and its new rope.

Once upon a time there was a grumpy skeleton. He was so grumpy all day long that he never spoke a word. He even refused to smile!

One day, clouds gathered in the sky and it began to rain. The skeleton thought the rain was very annoying, but he didn’t want to complain. He just sat there and watched as the rain came down.

Suddenly, a small voice said “Why don’t you come with me and we’ll find some fun?” The skeleton looked down and saw a little girl. She smiled and said “Come on! Let’s find somewhere dry!”

The skeleton was quite amazed at the little girl’s kindness. He said “Yes, ok!” He took the little girl’s hand and they ran in search of a dry place.

Finally, they found a dry spot under a bridge. The skeleton even smiled! He thanked the little girl and said “That was fun! Thank you for helping me have some fun!” The little girl smiled and said “You’re welcome!” They both laughed and went on their way.

Lily liked to play the flute. She had a small flute that made nice sounds when she blew into it. She played the flute every day in her room. She felt happy and peaceful when she played.

One day, her brother Tom came into her room. He was bored and wanted to play with Lily. He saw her flute and grabbed it. He said, "Let me play with this. It looks fun."

Lily was angry and scared. She did not want Tom to take her flute. She said, "No, Tom, that is mine. Give it back. You don't know how to play it. You will break it."

Tom did not listen. He blew into the flute very hard. He made a loud and ugly noise. He laughed and said, "This is easy. I can play better than you."

Lily started to cry. She wanted her flute back. She said, "Tom, please, stop. You are hurting my flute. You are hurting my ears. You are hurting my feelings."

Tom saw that Lily was crying. He felt sorry and ashamed. He realized that he was being mean and selfish. He said, "I'm sorry, Lily. I was wrong. Here, take your flute. I won't touch it again."

He gave the flute back to Lily. Lily stopped crying. She looked at her flute and saw that it was not broken. She was relieved and grateful. She said, "Thank you, Tom. I forgive you. Do you want to play something else with me?"

Tom nodded and smiled. He said, "Yes, Lily. I want to play with you. You are my sister and I love you."

They hugged each other and went to play with their toys. They felt happy and peaceful again. They learned to share and respect each other's things. They played the flute together and made nice sounds.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a very helpful mom who always helped her with everything. One day, Lily and her mom were playing in their room. They were having so much fun! Then, Lily's tummy started to rumble. She was hungry!

"Mommy, I want to eat something," said Lily.

"Okay, let's go to the kitchen and find something yummy to eat," said her mom.

So, they went to the kitchen and found some cookies. They were so delicious! Lily ate them all up and felt very happy. After that, they went back to their room and continued playing. Lily was so grateful for her helpful mom and the yummy cookies they ate together.

Jake had a busy day. He was busy lifting things. Suddenly, he heard a noise. He looked around and saw a small rail. Jake went to it and tried to lift it with all his might, but it was too heavy.

"I can't lift it all by myself," he said sadly. He looked around and saw a few people nearby.

"Can you help me lift this rail?" he asked.

One of the people smiled. "Yes, of course we can help you," they said.

Soon, they all worked together and managed to lift the rail. Jake was so happy! They put the rail down and Jake gave them a big thank-you hug.

The people smiled and said goodbye. Jake went home feeling happy and satisfied from all the busy work he had done.

One day, a boy named Tim went to the park. He played with his ball and had fun. But then, he saw a big spike on the ground. Tim was upset. He didn't want anyone to get hurt.

Tim saw his friend, Sue. He ran to her and said, "Sue, look! There's a big spike on the ground. We need to tell someone so they can take it away."

Sue looked at the spike and said, "You're right, Tim. Let's go tell my mom. She can help us."

They found Sue's mom and told her about the spike. She was happy they told her. She picked up the spike and threw it away. Tim and Sue realized they did a good thing. They went back to play and had more fun at the park.

Ben and Lily were playing with their toy cars on the floor. They liked to make them speed and crash and honk. They pretended they were drivers in a big race.

"Look at my car, it's so fast!" Ben said, zooming his red car past Lily's blue one.

"But my car is smarter, it can go around the knot!" Lily said, pointing to a big knot in the rug. She made her car swerve and dodge the knot.

They raced and raced, until they heard their mom call them for lunch.

"Who won the race?" Mom asked, as they ran to the kitchen.

"We both did!" Ben and Lily said, smiling. "We are successful drivers!"

Mom hugged them and gave them sandwiches and juice. She was proud of their imagination and fun.

Once upon a time, there was a big dog. He had a very charming smile and loved to play with his toys. One day, he found a tie on the ground and decided to wear it around his neck. He thought it made him look very handsome.

As he was playing with his toys, a little boy came by. The dog wanted to say hello, but he accidentally bit the boy's hand. The boy started to cry and the dog felt very sorry. He licked the boy's hand to make it feel better.

From that day on, the dog decided to never wear a tie again. He realized that it was more important to be friendly and kind to others than to look charming.

Once there was a girl who was very curious and wanted to weigh everything! Every time she found something small enough to pick up she would put it on the scales to see how much it weighed. Her parents would laugh at her curiosity and say she was being very funny!

One day she found a little box in her backyard. She was so excited and quickly ran to get the scales to see how much it weighed. Her parents shook their heads and smiled as she tried to figure out how much the box weighed.

The girl carefully placed the box on the scales, and it weighed three ounces! She was so proud and jumped for joy. Then she carefully put the box back where she had found it.

From then on, whenever she found something small enough to pick up, she would take it over to the scales to see how much it weighed. She was having so much fun and her parents couldn't help but smile!

Once upon a time there was a monkey. He was very creative and he loved to clap. Everywhere the monkey went he was clapping his hands.

One day, the monkey was in the park. He was clapping and having fun with the other animals. Even the birds were joining in and singing with him.

Suddenly, a little boy came along. He was only three years old. When the little boy saw the monkey, he began clapping too! He and the monkey clapped together.

The little boy and the monkey had so much fun clapping together. They did it for a long time and it was very magical. They were like best friends.

The little boy went away at the end of the day, but he never forgot his magical time clapping with the monkey.

Lily and Ben are twins. They like to play pretend. Today, they pretend to drive a big car. They use two chairs and a box. Lily sits on one chair and holds the box. She says, "I am the driver. I go fast and slow. Beep beep!" Ben sits on the other chair and says, "I am the passenger. I look out the window. Wow, I see a dog and a bird and a tree!"

They have fun driving around the room. But then, they hear a knock on the door. It is their mom. She is nosy. She wants to see what they are doing. She opens the door and says, "Hello, Lily and Ben. What are you playing?" Lily and Ben stop driving. They look at their mom. They do not want to tell her. They think she will laugh at them or tell them to stop.

Lily says, "We are playing nothing. Go away, mom." Ben says, "Yes, go away. We are busy." Their mom is surprised. She says, "Why are you so rude? I just want to see your game. It looks fun. Can I play too?" Lily and Ben shake their heads. They say, "No, mom. You are too big. You cannot fit in our car. And you are too nosy. You ask too many questions. Go away, mom."

Their mom is sad. She says, "Okay, okay. I will go away. But I love you, Lily and Ben. And I think your car is very cool. Maybe you can show me later." She closes the door and leaves. Lily and Ben look at each other. They feel a little bad. They love their mom too. But they also love their car. They decide to drive a little more. Then, they will say sorry to their mom and show her their car. They hope she will like it. They say, "Beep beep!" and drive away.

Once upon a time, there was a delicate mushroom. It wanted to win the race, so it started running. But the mushroom was too delicate and it couldn't move fast enough. Suddenly, a big gust of wind blew it away and it couldn't get back.

The mushroom flew and flew until it reached a dark cave. The mushroom was scared and it started to cry. It wanted to go home, but it was stuck.

Soon, a big monster came in the cave. He was very angry and he grabbed the delicate mushroom. He started to eat it and the mushroom could not win.

When the monster finished eating the mushroom, he felt bad. The poor mushroom had lost the race and would never be seen again.

Once upon a time, there was a little puppy named Max. Max had a big bossy sister named Bella. Bella always told Max what to do.

One day, Max was playing with his favorite toy, a ball. Suddenly, a big dog came and stole Max's ball. Max was sad and didn't know what to do.

Bella saw what happened and said, "Don't worry, Max. I'll help you get your ball back." Bella ran after the big dog and barked loudly. The big dog got scared and dropped the ball. Bella picked up the ball with her paw and brought it back to Max.

Max was so happy to have his ball back. He said to Bella, "Thank you for helping me. You're not so bossy after all." Bella smiled and said, "I just want to help my little brother." From that day on, Max and Bella played together and shared their toys.

Once upon a time there was a girl who was trying to do something special. She wanted to be strong and healthy and she set off on a journey to succeed.

Every day she exercised, running and jumping and stretching. She worked hard to get stronger and fitter.

As she kept on exercising, she felt more and more comfortable. She worked harder and eventually she achieved her goal. She succeeded in becoming fit and healthy and felt so proud of herself.

The girl was now happy and felt amazing. She had achieved something special and she was so pleased with herself.

She kept on exercising, and she continued to feel good and comfortable. She smiled, knowing that she had succeeded in her mission.

Once upon a time there was a young girl who wanted more money. One day she decided to kneel down and pray for money. The young girl prayed with all her heart and asked for a modest amount. Suddenly, a magical fairy appeared! She handed the girl some money and said, "Your wish has been granted. Be sure to always be kind and generous."

The girl thanked the fairy and smiled. She was so excited to have more money! She held the money tightly in her hands and ran to purchase small gifts for her family. She was so happy that her prayers had been answered.

The young girl never forgot the gift of money she had been given. From that day on, she was always careful to be kind and generous with whatever money she had.

A parent was really glad. She saw that her three year old was playing in the garden. She wanted to say 'hello' to her child but her child decided to ignore her.

The parent felt sad. She called out to her child again but she still ignored her. The parent smiled and went over to her anyway. She hugged her little one and asked why she was ignoring her.

The little one said that she wanted to play all by herself. The parent said that was ok and gave her a hug. She said she was glad to see her and asked her if she wanted to play together.

The little one was excited and ran off to the swing. The parent followed and they had a wonderful time together. They laughed and smiled and played until it was time to go inside.

The parent was really glad that her child had chosen not to ignore her. She was filled with happiness. The little one had taught the parent a valuable lesson - even when it seems like someone is ignoring you, it's still ok to provide an opportunity for them to come back.

Once there was a little girl called Jane. She wanted to collect some happy feelings. So she went to the park with her mom. The sun was shining and she felt excited.

Jane ran to the slide and climbed up the steps. She sat on the top and looked around. There were birds flying high in the sky and Jane smiled. She slid down to the bottom and clapped her hands.

Suddenly, Jane felt an empty feeling in her stomach. But she couldn't remember why. She thought and thought until she remembered - she wanted a snack!

Jane's mom was patient, but Jane was impatient. She wanted the snack now! So Jane and her mom went to the shop near the park to buy some food.

Jane chose some cookies, and her mom bought her a drink too. She was happy now, and the empty feeling in her stomach was gone. Jane was content and enjoyed the rest of the day in the park.

Once, there was a little girl named Jane. Jane really wanted to win the spelling contest that was being held in school. But she was scared that she wouldn't be able to spell the big words that the other kids could.

So she practiced really hard and asked her parents to help her. Every night they helped her with her spellings and encouraged her to try her best.

On the day of the contest, Jane was very nervous. But when it was her turn, she closed her eyes, took a deep breath and spelled the word. It was an expensive word and she was sure she had finished it correctly.

Everyone waited to see who had won the spelling contest. And it was Jane! The other kids were so proud of her and congratulated her for the win. Jane was overjoyed!

Jane and Tim visited their grandparent's house. Jane was so excited to visit. Tim was happy too, but he was a little bit scared because he had never been there before.

They rang the doorbell and soon heard their grandmother's friendly voice. Grandmother opened the door and greeted them with a hug.

Jane and Tim asked Grandmother to show them around the house. They looked around and saw the garden. Jane said that the garden looked harmless, and Tim agreed.

Grandmother gave the children a note. She said, “This is a note from your grandfather. He said that he wanted to visit you, but he is a little bit sick. He loves you very much and he hopes you visit him soon!”

Jane and Tim were sad they couldn't visit Grandfather, but they knew that he was taking care of himself. They hugged Grandmother goodbye and promised to return soon and visit Grandfather.

Once there was a little girl named Ellie. Ellie had a pin. She was very happy to have the pin and always wore it on her shirt.

One day, Ellie was feeling a little bit sick. She sneezed several times. Her mom and dad said that she should take some medicine to help her become healthy again.

So, Ellie took the medicine and she felt much better. She put back on her pin and went out to play. Ellie was very happy to be healthy again!

One day, a boy named Tim went to the store with his mom. They wanted to buy ice cream from the big freezer. Tim walked slow because he was very excited. He could not wait to eat the ice cream.

When they got to the store, Tim saw his friend, Sam. Sam said, "Hi, Tim! Do you want to skip with me?" Tim said, "Yes, but first I need to get ice cream from the freezer with my mom."

Tim and his mom opened the freezer and picked their favorite ice cream. Then, Tim and Sam skipped all the way home. They were happy to eat the ice cream and play together.

Once upon a time, there was a little dog named Max. Max loved to run and play outside. One day, Max saw a big tree and decided to go say hello. As Max got closer, he saw a squirrel in the tree. The squirrel looked down at Max and said, "Hello, Max! I am so happy to see you. You are a very dependable friend." Max wagged his tail happily and barked, "Thank you, squirrel!"

Suddenly, the squirrel jumped down from the tree and ran away. Max was confused and wondered where his friend had gone. Just then, Max felt a sharp pain in his tail. He turned around and saw the squirrel biting him! Max yelped and ran away as fast as he could.

From that day on, Max learned to be careful around squirrels and to always watch his tail. But he still loved playing outside and visiting his tree friends.

Anna liked to play with her hair. She had long hair that was brown and soft. She liked to make braids and bows and clips. She liked to look at herself in the mirror and smile.

One day, Anna went with her mom to the barber. The barber was a nice man who cut hair. He had scissors and a comb and a cape. He said hello to Anna and her mom and asked them to sit down.

"Anna, do you want to cut your hair?" the barber asked.

Anna shook her head. She did not want to cut her hair. She liked her long hair.

"But your hair is very long, Anna. It is almost touching the floor. Don't you want to make it shorter and neater?" the barber said.

Anna shook her head again. She did not want to make it shorter and neater. She liked her long hair.

The barber looked at Anna's mom. Anna's mom nodded. She wanted Anna to cut her hair. She said it was too hard to wash and comb and dry.

"Anna, please listen to your mom. She knows what is best for you. If you cut your hair, you will look very pretty and fresh. And you can still play with your hair and make braids and bows and clips. You will also have more time to do other things, like read and draw and play with your toys. And you know what? Your hair will grow back. It will not stay short forever. It will bloom like a flower in the spring. Do you like flowers, Anna?" the barber said.

Anna thought for a moment. She liked flowers. She liked how they smelled and looked and felt. She liked how they bloomed in different colors and shapes. She wondered if her hair could bloom like a flower.

"Okay, I will cut my hair," Anna said.

The barber smiled. He put the cape around Anna and combed her hair. He took the scissors and cut a little bit of her hair. He showed Anna the hair that he cut. It was long and brown and soft.

"See, Anna? This is your hair. It is still your hair. It is just shorter. Do you like it?" the barber asked.

Anna looked at the hair. She touched it. It was still her hair. It was just shorter. She nodded. She liked it.

The barber cut more of her hair. He made it even and tidy. He blew away the hair that fell on her face. He showed Anna the mirror. Anna saw herself. She had short hair that was brown and soft. She looked very pretty and fresh.

"Do you like your hair, Anna?" the barber asked.

Anna smiled. She liked her hair. She thanked the barber and gave him a hug. She thanked her mom and gave her a hug. She took her hair that he cut and put it in a bag. She wanted to keep it. She wanted to see if it would bloom like a flower.

Once there was a man. He was bald. He liked to play with a square. He put the square on the ground and rolled it. He laughed and smiled when it rolled away. He was happy.

Then the man saw a bird. The bird had a square in its beak. The man wanted the square. The bird flew away with the square.

The man chased the bird but the bird was too fast. The man could not catch it. The man was sad.

He looked around and then he saw another square. It was lying on the ground. He was happy again and he picked it up. Now he had a square. He played with it. He was very happy.

Once upon a time there was a girl named Grace and her mom. They were going on a walk together. Grace was very stubborn and wanted to go a certain way. Her mom wanted to go another way, but Grace would not listen.

"Grace, this way is better," her mom said. "No, my way is better," Grace said.

So they kept walking, but then Grace saw something. It was the biggest secret she ever saw! It was a beautiful bush with big yellow flowers.

"Mom, what is this?" Grace asked excitedly.

Her mom knew the answer but wanted to prevent Grace from discovering the secret. "Grace, it is nothing special," her mom said.

But Grace kept asking her mom about the secret and would not take no for an answer. She was so stubborn.

Finally, her mom had to tell her. "Grace, it's a fairy bush. It is something special and it's a secret."

Grace was amazed. From that day on, Grace and her mom always looked for the secret fairy bush when they went walking.

Once there was a little girl called Mandy. She had a wonderful model plane. Every day after school, she would take it out and throw it high into the sky. She loved to watch it soar up high, faster and faster.

One day, Mandy was practising throwing her model plane, when suddenly she saw an eagle soaring in the sky. It was so beautiful, she decided she wanted to throw her plane higher so she could be like the eagle.

But this time, her plane flew too high and too far away. Mandy began to worry. She searched everywhere, but the plane was gone. She was sad and upset.

Suddenly, she heard a rustling sound in the nearby bushes. She looked over and saw her plane was safely perched on a branch. She was so relieved and quickly ran over to retrieve it.

From then on, Mandy was very careful when throwing her model plane. She wanted to make sure it was safe and she never wanted to lose it again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a furry cat named Mittens. Lily loved to watch Mittens play with yarn. One day, Lily lost her watch while playing outside. She searched and searched but couldn't find it. Mittens saw Lily looking sad and knew something was wrong. Mittens went outside and found the watch! Lily was so happy and gave Mittens a big hug. From that day on, Lily and Mittens were best friends forever.

Once there was a ant who decided to have a nap. The ant wiggled and twisted until it was comfortable to sleep. But while the ant was sleeping, it heard a loud noise. The ant was scared and quickly looked around. Its eyes widened with shock.

The ant saw a huge sack with curious words written on it. The ant quickly hopped away, but the sack followed it. The ant ran faster and faster, but the sack was always behind it.

The ant ran up a tree and scrambled up to the top branches. The sack soon followed and the ant looked down at it, feeling scared and confused. Suddenly, a voice came from the sack.

"Hey there, little ant!" the voice said in a harsh tone. "I'm here to take you away!"

The ant was surprised. It knew that it could not get away. The sack was too strong and the voice was too harsh. The ant sadly stepped into the sack and was taken away.

The ant never saw its friends again. But it never forgot the harsh voice and the huge sack.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a teddy bear named Teddy, who she loved very much. One day, Lily went to the park to play with her friends. They played on the swings and the slide, but Lily fell down and hurt her knee. She started to cry, but Teddy was there to comfort her.

Lily's friends came over to ask how she was feeling. They all gave their opinion on what she should do to feel better. Some said she should put a band-aid on her knee, while others said she should rest for a little while. Lily listened to their opinions, but she decided to do what Teddy thought was best.

Teddy suggested they sit down and have a snack. Lily thought that was a great idea, so they all sat down and ate some crackers. Soon, Lily's knee started to feel better. Her friends thought Teddy's idea was really popular, and they all wanted to have a snack too. They all had a great time together, and Lily was happy that Teddy was there to comfort her when she needed it.

Once upon a time, there was a yacht. It was very spoiled. A little boy wanted to go on a journey with the yacht. The daddy warned him not to go.

The little boy was very sad. He wanted to go and have a great time on the yacht. The daddy said that it wasn't safe. He said that all the creatures in the sea were very sneaky. They would try to make the little boy's journey very difficult.

The little boy knew that his daddy was right, so he didn't go on the yacht. He was disappointed, but he knew it was safer to stay close.

The daddy was very happy that his son heeded his warning and was safe. The dad was glad that his little boy was a smart cookie. He knew that one day, when the little boy was older, he could go for interesting adventures on the yacht.

Once upon a time, there was a mom and a little boy. The mom had a plan to go to the park. "Let's make popcorn and go to the park," said the mom.

The little boy was happy and they began to make popcorn. The boy warned his mom,"Be careful with the fire. Don't touch it."

The mom listened and made sure the fire was safe. Soon, the popcorn was ready and it smelled yummy. The little boy took a big sniff and laughed.

At the park, they put the popcorn on a picnic blanket and the little boy noticed some people nearby had some food that smelled disgusting. He warned his mom, "Don't eat that, it looks yucky."

The mom smiled at her little boy, then they shared their popcorn and had a fun day. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play in the park and watch the birds fly in the sky. One day, she saw a scary spirit in the park. It had big eyes and a ghostly face. Lily was afraid, but she wanted to be brave.

She decided to choose to go closer to the spirit to see if it was real. As she got closer, the spirit started to move and make spooky sounds. Lily was scared and tried to run away, but the spirit caught her. The spirit took her away to a dark place and she never came back.

The end.

Once there was a little girl named Sue. She liked to go on adventures. One day, Sue decided to go berry picking in the forest. She wanted to find some of the biggest, juiciest berries in the woods.

Sue found a huge berry bush, and she began to pick berries. She had almost filled her bucket when she heard a strange noise. It was coming from behind a big tree.

Sue was a bit scared, but she was also curious. She slowly walked to the tree and peeked around it. There she saw a rabbit sitting and looking at her. The rabbit looked quite serious. Sue thought he might be a guardian of the berry bush!

The rabbit and Sue stared at each other for a few moments. Then the rabbit hopped away. Sue smiled, and continued to pick the berries. She had a great time in the forest that day.

Once upon a time there was a great race. The racers were ready and waited for the flag to drop. When it did, off they went. Some went faster than others. As they went around the track, some were ahead and some were behind.

The racer with the new car stayed ahead the whole way. He knew he had a good chance to win. He was the fastest one there.

Then a terrible thing happened. The new racer's car hit a rock and his car stopped. He tried really hard to push it, but it would not start again. He was so disappointed.

The other racers went on. One of them went really fast and took the lead. He shouted out, "I'm gonna win this race!"

But when he crossed the finish line, he saw that the racer with the new car had stayed ahead and he had won the race.

The other racers were so disappointed, but the racer with the new car was so happy. He had remained in the lead and won the race.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved playing with cards, especially the ones with princesses on them. One day, she went for a walk in the park, but it started to get dark. She was scared, but then a nice man introduced himself and offered to walk her home.

Lily was happy to have found a new friend. The man gave her a card with a picture of a puppy on it, and she smiled. But when they arrived at her house, the man tried to take Lily inside with him. She screamed and her parents came to the door. They called the police and the man was taken away.

Lily never forgot that scary night. She threw away the card with the puppy on it and never played with cards again. She learned to always be careful around strangers and to never trust someone she didn't know.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, she asked her mom if she could have a massage. Her mom said yes and told her to lie down on the bed. Lily's mom rubbed her back gently, making her feel relaxed.

After the massage, Lily asked if she could go outside to play. Her mom said yes, but reminded her to wear her tough shoes because the ground was rocky. Lily put on her shoes and went outside to play with her friends.

While playing, Lily's friend asked if she could borrow her toy. Lily said no because it was her favorite toy and she didn't want it to get broken. Her friend asked again, but Lily still didn't permit her to borrow it. Instead, Lily suggested they play with a different toy together. Her friend agreed and they had fun playing together.

Once there was a family who lived in a big house. The house had an attic, which was full of things. One day the family found that some of the things in the attic were old and broken. The family was very generous and wanted to replace the broken things with new, better things. So, they decided to go shopping to buy the new, better things to put in the attic.

The family went to the store and bought many new things. The store keeper was very generous and gave them some extra items for free. The family was so happy! When they got home, they went to the attic and replaced all the old things. Now the attic was full of new, better things that looked nicer and worked better.

The family was so pleased with the new, better items in the attic that they threw a party to celebrate. Everyone was so happy because of their generous and kind deed. The family smiled, laughed and danced the night away. And that is how the attic was replaced!

Once upon a time, there was a little dog named Spot. Spot liked to play outside. One day, he saw a big wall made of bricks. He wanted to see what was on the other side of the wall.

Spot tried to climb the wall. He put his paws on the bricks and pushed up. He climbed higher and higher. But he got tired. Spot was not used to climbing so high.

Spot was very tired, but he did not give up. He took a rest and then tried again. This time, he climbed all the way to the top of the wall. Spot was happy he did not give up. On the other side of the wall, he found a big park to play in.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Rose. Rose was playing in the park when she saw a big bubble floating in the air. She wanted to catch it so she chased after it! But when the bubble got close, Rose's friend Tommy called to her, saying the bubble wasn't real.

Rose was very sad. She was so ignorant that she didn't believe Tommy. She kept chasing the bubble even when Tommy said it was impossible to catch. But eventually, Tommy's words sank in, and Rose stopped chasing the bubble, quitting her pursuit.

Rose was very disappointed that the bubble wasn't real. But as she thought about it, it made her realise she should listen to Tommy next time. It was a lesson for her, so she would never be ignorant again. Rose was happy and thanked Tommy for being a great friend.

Once upon a time, there was an elderly lady named Granny. Granny loved to take long walks in the park. One day, while she was walking, she tripped and fell.

A little girl named Lily saw Granny fall and ran to help her. "Are you okay, Granny?" asked Lily.

Granny said, "No, I hurt my arm. I need some medicine to make it feel better."

Lily ran to get Granny some medicine and helped her put it on her arm. Granny felt much better and thanked Lily for her help. From that day on, Granny and Lily became good friends and went for walks in the park together.

The sun was shining brightly and Billy was out playing in the park. He saw a tall tree and some waste lying around. He thought "What a shame they left waste here. I must clean it up".

He looked around and saw a little girl looking at the big tree. "Hello," said Billy. "What are you looking at?"

The girl replied, "I'm looking at the the tall tree. I hope it will grow even taller!"

Billy said "I hope so too!" He gathered up the waste and put it in a bin. Then Billy and the girl played tag underneath the tall tree, laughing and enjoying the sunshine.

Once upon a time, in a thick forest, there lived a little bird. The bird loved to sing and play with his friends. One day, a big fire started in the forest. The bird was scared, but his friends encouraged him to help them put the fire out.

The little bird and his friends flew to the river to get water. They used their wings to splash water on the fire. They worked very hard, but the fire kept getting bigger and bigger. The little bird was tired, but his friends kept encouraging him to keep going.

In the end, the fire was too big, and the little bird and his friends could not stop it. The forest burned down, and the animals lost their homes. The little bird was sad and learned that sometimes, even when you try your best and encourage each other, things can still have a bad ending. The moral of the story is that sometimes, we cannot control everything, and we must accept the things we cannot change.

Harry was three years old, and he was excited to unpack his new box. Inside, he found a weird cactus with bright yellow flowers. “Wow! What is this?” Harry said out loud.

His mom walked into the room.

“That’s a cactus, Harry,” she said. “It’s a plant, and it’s a bit weird but it's very cool.”

Harry looked at the cactus and smiled. He liked weird things and thought the cactus was the coolest. He took it and put it on the shelf.

Every morning, Harry would unpack one of the boxes he had, and he was happy to have the cactus around. He talked to it, he sang to it, and he even pretended to fly around it like it was a rocket!

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play hockey with his friends. They would skate on the ice and try to score goals. One day, Timmy's mom came to watch him play. She said, "Timmy, you smell smelly. Did you forget to take a bath?" Timmy didn't know what smelly meant, so his mom had to explain it to him. She said, "Smelly means you have a bad smell. You need to take a bath to smell good." Timmy felt embarrassed, but he was happy his mom explained what smelly meant. From then on, he made sure to take a bath before playing hockey with his friends.

One day, a boy named Tom and a girl named Anna went for a walk. They liked to explore new places and see new things. They saw a big hill and wanted to climb it. They walked and walked until they reached the top.

"Wow, look at that!" Tom said, pointing to the other side of the hill. "There is a village!"

Anna looked and saw many small houses and people. The houses were yellow and had red roofs. The people wore colorful clothes and smiled. They looked happy and friendly.

"Let's go and meet them!" Anna said, excited. "Maybe they have toys or games or stories to share!"

Tom nodded and they ran down the hill. They reached the village and saw a woman with a basket of fruit. She saw them and waved.

"Hello, little ones!" she said. "Where are you from?"

"We are from the other side of the hill," Tom said. "We came to see your village. It is very pretty and yellow."

"Thank you," the woman said. "We like our village. It is our home. Do you want some fruit? They are sweet and juicy."

"Yes, please!" Anna said. "We are hungry and thirsty."

The woman gave them some fruit and invited them to sit with her. She told them stories about the village and the people. Tom and Anna listened and asked questions. They learned a lot and had fun.

They liked the woman and the village. They made new friends and had a good time. They were glad they went for a walk and met them.

Bob and his mom went to the store. They wanted to pack for a trip. Mom bought a journal for Bob.

Bob was so excited and started to pack. He put his toys and games in the bag. He thought it was so fun!

But then, he tried to pack the journal. It was too big and he couldn't fit it in the bag. He tried and tried, but it was no use. He was getting so frustrated!

Mom saw that he was feeling stupid and helped him pack the journal. She put it carefully in the bag. Now Bob's bag was ready for their trip!

Bob was so happy that he couldn't stop smiling. He knew that he was going to have an amazing trip with his mom.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside with her friends. One day, they found an olive tree with lots of olives on it. They picked some and ate them. They were very tasty!

Suddenly, Lily heard a loud noise. She became very fearful and didn't know what to do. Her friends came over and told her to surrender her fear. They said there was nothing to be afraid of.

Lily listened to her friends and slowly felt better. They continued to play and have fun under the olive tree. From that day on, Lily learned that surrendering her fear was the best thing to do when she felt scared.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Sarah. She was three years old and loved nothing more than playing outside in the sun.

One day, Sarah's dad said to her, "Let's play bury the flower!" Sarah smiled and ran to get the flower. Together, they put the flower in a hole and Sarah started to cover it with dirt.

When Sarah was done, her dad said, "It's time to have a cookout! Let's go see if we can find something to cook on the grill." They searched around the garden and found a regular grill.

Sarah helped her dad light the fire and they put the food on the grill. Soon the food was cooked and they ate it together. Sarah said,"That was yummy! Can we bury a flower every day?"

Her dad laughed and said, "No, but maybe we can play bury the flower every few weeks!" Sarah smiled and said, "Okay!"

Once there was a little girl who was very obedient. She wanted to play outside but her mum had said it was time to come in. So she obeyed and went inside the house.

Just then the doorbell rang. The girl ran to open the door and saw a lady with a big box. The lady smiled and said she had something inside the box to show her.

The little girl was so excited. She clapped her hands and waited as the lady opened the box. Inside were lots of colourful toys that made the girl's eyes widen in delight.

The toys were amazing and soon the little girl was playing with them. All the while the lady was watching her. When the girl had finished playing the lady put the toys back in the box and said goodbye.

The little girl said goodbye in return and followed her mother to the exit. Even though she was sad to leave the toy display she remembered to be obedient and walk to the exit with her mummy.

Lily and Sam were bored. They had played with all their toys and read all their books. They wanted to do something new and fun.

"Let's decorate the plant!" Lily said. She pointed to the big green plant in the corner of the living room. It had long leaves and a brown pot.

"Okay!" Sam said. He liked the plant. It smelled nice and made the room cozy. He ran to get some paper and crayons. Lily got some scissors and glue.

They cut out different shapes and colors from the paper. They drew faces and patterns on them. They glued them to the leaves and the pot. They made the plant look very funny and pretty.

"Wow, it's brilliant!" Lily said. She admired their work. The plant had paper flowers, stars, hearts, and animals on it. It looked like a rainbow.

"Brilliant!" Sam agreed. He smiled. He was proud of their decoration. He thought the plant liked it too.

"Look, Mommy!" they shouted. They ran to get their mommy. They wanted to show her their brilliant plant. Mommy came and saw their decoration. She was surprised and happy.

"What a lovely plant!" Mommy said. She hugged them and kissed them. "You are very creative and clever. I love your decoration. And I'm sure the plant does too."

Lily and Sam were happy. They had done something new and fun. They had decorated the plant. They had made Mommy smile. They had had a brilliant day.

Once upon a time there was a cheerful dog named Fido. Fido loved learning new things. One day Fido was out on a walk and he came across a wire. Fido had never seen a wire before, so he decided to lean closer and take a look. Before long Fido was playing with it and learning all about this new thing. He had a lot of fun.

But then something terrible happened. Fido accidentally stepped on the wire and he got a nasty shock. He felt scared and very sad.

Fido learned an important lesson that day. He vowed never to touch wires again. He was no longer cheerful, but he was wiser.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy liked to play outside. One day, he saw a weird bug on the ground. It had a lot of legs and was very small. Timmy wanted to touch it, but he was scared it would bite him. Suddenly, the bug started to move and Timmy got scared. He kicked the bug away and ran back to his house.

Once upon a time, there was a poor man. Every day, the poor man worked in the fields to make enough money to feed his family. One day, he wanted to put his books on a shelf, but he didn't have one.

The poor man was sad when he realized he couldn't get a shelf because he had no money. He decided to ask his neighbour if he could borrow a shelf. The neighbour said, "Yes, you can have this old shelf, but you must attach it to the wall yourself."

The poor man was very grateful and he thanked his neighbour. He took the shelf home and attached it to the wall, and thanked his neighbour again. He put all his books in the shelf and was happy to have a place to store them.

From this story, we learn that giving helps more than receiving. When we help people in need, we can make their lives better.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a toy bunny named Bun-Bun that she loved very much. One day, she accidentally dropped Bun-Bun and his ear fell off. Lily was very sad and didn't know what to do.

Lily's mommy saw her daughter was frustrated and asked her what was wrong. Lily showed her mommy Bun-Bun's broken ear. Her mommy said, "Don't worry, we can replace his ear with some glue." Lily was happy to hear that and gave her mommy a big hug.

Later that day, Lily's daddy came home from work and brought a message for her mommy. Lily asked, "What's a message?" Her mommy explained that it was like a letter that someone sends to tell you something important. Lily thought that was cool and asked if she could get a message too. Her mommy smiled and said, "Of course, Lily. You are my special little girl."

The day was cold and the nation was marching. The children had wrapped up warm and their parents cheered them on with joy.

“Come on, everyone,” shouted the mum. “Let’s march!”

The little girl, who was only three years old, jumped up and down and clapped her hands. “Yes! Let’s march!” she cried.

The little girl marched along with the others with a big grin on her face. Suddenly, the cold wind blew, blowing her hat away. She stopped and looked around.

“Where’s my hat?” she exclaimed.

Her mum stopped and looked around too. Then she spotted the hat lying in the grass.

“There it is,” she said, pointing at the hat. “Let’s go and get it.”

The little girl ran over to get her hat, but when she reached it, she stopped and looked up.

“What is it?” asked her mum.

The little girl pointed at the sky. “Look at the sky,” she said.

Above them, the sky was full of colourful balloons, floating away in the wind. The little girl smiled. “That’s so pretty,” she said.

The mum smiled too. “

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play outside with his friends. One day, Timmy and his friends were playing hide-and-seek. Timmy was hiding behind a tree when he suddenly fell down and ripped his pants.

Timmy's friend Billy saw what happened and said, "Oh no, Timmy! Your pants are ripped! Are you okay?"

Timmy started to cry because he was embarrassed about his ripped pants. His friends tried to make him feel better by telling him that it was okay and that they wouldn't laugh at him.

After a little while, Timmy stopped crying and his friends suggested they play a quiet game of Simon Says. Timmy felt better and joined in the game. They had so much fun playing quietly and Timmy forgot all about his ripped pants. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his toys. One day, he saw a rocket toy in the store. It was big and red with a thick body. Timmy wanted it, so he asked his mom to buy it for him.

When they got home, Timmy grabbed the rocket and started to play with it. He pretended that he was flying through space and exploring new planets. The rocket was so much fun to play with that Timmy played with it all day long.

At night, Timmy went to bed with the rocket by his side. He dreamed that he was flying through space and having the best adventure ever. When he woke up in the morning, he grabbed the rocket again and continued his adventure. Timmy was so happy that he had his new toy rocket to play with.

One day it was raining outside. Mandy and her mom were inside biking. "I want to go outside and play in the rain," said Mandy.

Mandy's mom said, "No, it's too dangerous." But Mandy was very stubborn.

She said, "I want to go outside! Please!"

Mandy's mom sighed and said, "Okay, but stay close."

Mandy put on her rain coat and ran outside. She stepped into the deep puddle and splashed around. She loved the feeling of the rain on her skin.

Suddenly, Mandy heard a loud roar. She looked up and saw a big black cloud. It started to rain harder and the puddle grew even deeper.

Mandy ran inside the house. Her mom was waiting in the kitchen with a salad. "You're soaked," said her mom.

Mandy looked sadly at the floor. She knew she should have listened to her mom.

The End.

Tom and Lily were twins who loved to play in the water. One day, their dad took them to the lake and gave them a big surprise. He had a kayak for them to ride in. A kayak is a long boat that you sit inside and move with a stick that has a paddle on each end.

"Wow, a kayak!" Tom and Lily shouted. They put on their life jackets and helmets and climbed into the kayak with their dad. He showed them how to hold the stick and paddle together. "Are you ready for some fun?" he asked.

"Yes, dad!" they said. They were very jolly and excited. They paddled around the lake, looking at the fish, the ducks, and the trees. They sang songs and made funny noises. They felt the sun on their faces and the breeze in their hair.

Suddenly, they saw a big splash in the water. It was a frog that had jumped out of a lily pad. Tom and Lily laughed and tried to catch the frog. But the frog was too fast and slippery. It jumped back into the water and swam away.

"Bye, frog!" Tom and Lily shouted. They waved their sticks and smiled. They had so much fun in the kayak. They thanked their dad for the surprise and hugged him. They were very happy and tired. They went back to the shore and had a picnic. They ate sandwiches, cookies, and juice. They told their mom about their adventure in the kayak. They said it was the best day ever.

One day, a weak little boy named Tim went for a walk. He saw a bright light in the sky. It was so pretty! Tim wanted to grab the light and keep it.

He asked his mom, "Can I grab the light, please?" His mom said, "No, Tim. The light is too far away. But we can look at it together."

So, Tim and his mom sat and looked at the light. They had a nice time. The light made them both feel happy and warm.

Mummy and Daddy were talking one night, and they thought it was time for Ben to act more dependable. They decided to give him a job to do the next morning. Mummy set the vase on the table and told Ben that he had to take it to Grandma's house without dropping it. Ben was not sure he would be able to do this, but he was excited to try.

The next morning, Ben got dressed and carefully picked up the vase. His daddy said, "Good luck, son!" as Ben walked out the door. Ben was nervous, but determined. He slowly made his way down the street.

Suddenly, a loud noise startled Ben and made him jolt. He accidentally struck the vase, and it nearly fell to the ground. With all his might, Ben was able to save it! He continued walking, carefully holding the vase close.

Finally, Ben reached Grandma's house and proudly presented her with the vase. Grandma was so happy, and she said with a smile, "Well done, Ben. You are so dependable." Ben beamed with joy and proudly walked back home.

Once upon a time, there were two friends, Jack and Jill. Jack wanted to go fill their pot with water from the stream. So off they went, carrying their pot between them.

But oh dear, the stream was so far away. Jack and Jill got so tired. Soon, Jill was feeling a bit dizzy from walking so much.

Jack said to Jill, "Come on Jill, just a little bit more and we can fill our pot."

So with a big push, Jack and Jill finally reached the stream. Jack grabbed the pot and filled it with water. He said to Jill "We did it, now let's go home!" They carried the heavy pot back home. When they got there, Jack and Jill realized their pot was so full that some water spilled out. They both laughed and ran away, feeling so proud of their pot!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her colorful toys and run around outside. One day, she saw some other children playing together and wanted to join in. But they said she couldn't play because she didn't have a mother to unite with them.

Lily felt sad because she missed her mother who had passed away. She went to her room and cried. Suddenly, she heard a knock on the door. It was her grandmother who came to visit her. Lily's grandmother told her that she could be her mother for the day and they could unite with the other children.

Lily was so happy and ran outside to play with her grandmother and the other children. They all had so much fun playing together and Lily felt like she had a new family. She realized that even though her mother was gone, she still had people who loved her and would unite with her.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Amy. She liked to wonder about the world around her. One day, she saw a big box with an open top. Amy walked slow to the box and looked inside.

Inside the box, there was a small cat. The cat said, "Hello, Amy! I am a magic cat. I can talk!" Amy was very happy to meet the cat. They became good friends.

Every day, Amy and the cat played together. They ran, jumped, and laughed. They were always happy. And when they were tired, they sat by the open box and talked about their fun day.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys all day long. One day, Lily went to the store with her mommy. She saw a big, expensive toy that she really wanted.

Lily said to her mommy, "Mommy, can we buy this toy? It's so pretty!"

Her mommy replied, "Sorry, sweetie. It costs too much money. We have zero money left to buy it."

Lily was sad, but her mommy said, "Don't worry, we can still have fun without it." They went home and Lily carried her favorite toy, a stuffed bear, with her. She played with it all day long and had a great time. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. He had a big dream. He wanted to play in a kayak on the river. Every day, he would ask his mom and dad if he could try it. Tim was very persistent.

One sunny day, Tim's mom and dad took him to the river. They showed him a small, red kayak. Tim was so happy! He got in the kayak and started to paddle. He splashed water and laughed. The fish in the river jumped and played too.

After a fun day in the kayak, Tim went home. He told his friends about his adventure. They all wanted to try the kayak too. Tim's dream came true, and he couldn't wait to go back to the river again.

Once there was a very graceful girl called Lucy. She liked to kneel on the floor and make special patterns with her hands and feet. Every week she went to a place called school. There, her teachers taught her how to move to music in a graceful way. Lucy loved it. Every morning she would kneel on the floor and practise what she had learned.

One day, her teacher asked her to demonstrate her graceful kneeling to the class. Lucy felt shy, so she closed her eyes and used her feet to move in a special pattern. Everyone clapped when she finished. Lucy was so proud.

The teacher said to her "That was extremely graceful. You should be very proud of yourself". Lucy smiled because she was. She felt like she was floating on air. From that moment on she kept kneeling and practising, always in a graceful way.

Once upon a time there was a new family. They had a home and it was full of light. Next door was a smart kitty. Every morning, the kitty would sit in the sun.

One afternoon, the family decided to go for a walk. The kitty saw that they were leaving and decided to join them. The family was so happy to have the smart kitty with them!

Along the way, the kitty showed them lots of fun things. They played games, looked for bugs and marveled at the wonderful sights.

In the evening, the family and kitty were very tired. They made a cozy spot in the grass and sat down together. As the sun began to set, the family watched the beautiful sunset with the smart kitty by their side.

The family was so happy to have a smart kitty as a friend. They all enjoyed the light, laughter and love that the kitty brought. From that day forward, the kitty was a part of their family and they were very fond of each other!

Once upon a time, there was a furry bunny named Benny. Benny loved to whistle while he hopped around. One day, Benny met a little girl named Lily.

"Hi, Benny! Can you whistle a song for me?" asked Lily.

"Sure, I can whistle a happy story for you," replied Benny.

Benny hopped around and whistled a happy tune. Lily clapped her hands and smiled. "That was a great story, Benny. Thank you!" she said.

Benny felt happy that he could make Lily smile. From that day on, Benny and Lily became good friends and Benny would always whistle a happy story for her.

Once upon a time, there was a brave girl called Lucy. Everyday Lucy would go to the park and bow to all the animals she saw. One day, Lucy found a beautiful key on the floor of the park. She had never seen a key like this before and got very excited. She wanted to try the key in the park gate, as she thought it might open it!

But when she tried to open the gate, the key did not fit. It wasn't the right key for that gate. Lucy was very upset. She wanted to get inside the park, but she couldn't find the right key.

Just then, Lucy remembered how brave she was. She decided to try a different key in the gate. She looked around the park and found a small key lying on a bench. She quickly tried the key in the gate and was overjoyed when it opened! Lucy was so happy and proud of herself for being so brave.

From then on, whenever Lucy went to the park, she would bow to all the animals and use the special key to open the gate.

One day, a 3 year old was playing in the park. Suddenly, the 3 year old noticed an old bottle on the ground. He became curious and picked it up. When he looked inside the bottle he could see lots of coins. He was very happy and started counting the coins.

But then, a big man came and snatched the bottle away. The 3 year old tried to get the bottle back, but the big man said "This is mine!"

The 3 year old was very upset but he knew that he wouldn't be able to take the bottle away from the big man. All he could do was go home and tell his mum about it.

When the 3 year old explained what happened to his mum, she felt sorry for him. She said that even though he couldn't have the bottle, there were still things he could be thankful for. She suggested that he say 'thanks' for all the little things that make life fun, like playing in the park.

The 3 year old decided to take his mum's advice. He thanked her for being so kind, thanked the birds for singing, and thanked the clouds for the rain. He was very happy and content with the world around him.

Once there was a wise old owl who loved to stitch. He had been stitching forever, and he was very good at it too! But now it was time to celebrate.

So, the wise owl started to look for someone to join him. Everywhere he looked, he couldn’t find anyone. He even asked the birds, bees, and bugs, but no one wanted to join him.

The owl was getting very sad. Then, he looked up and saw some friends flying around. They cheered for the owl and said, “Let’s celebrate!”

The owl was so happy that he started to stitch with all of his friends around him. He stitched a quilt with beautiful colors and patterns. Everyone loved it!

The owl smiled and said, “It’s time to celebrate!” And everyone celebrated with music, dancing, and a big feast. It was the best celebration ever!

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lily. She went to the store with her mom to buy some candy. Lily saw a big red lollipop and asked her mom if she could have it. Her mom said she could only have it if she answered a question. The question was, "What is your favorite color?" Lily thought for a moment and said, "Pink!" Her mom smiled and said she did a good job answering the question.

Lily was so happy to get the lollipop. She told her mom it tasted really good. They walked around the store and saw lots of toys and clothes. Lily wanted to buy everything, but her mom said they had to be careful with their money. They left the store with just the lollipop, but Lily was still happy because it was a good day.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, she saw her brother playing with his toys and she wanted to play too. "Can I join you?" she asked. But her brother said no and kept playing alone. This made Lily sad.

Later that day, Lily's mom asked her to help clean the attic. When they went up there, they found an old box of lemons. "These lemons are sour," said Lily's mom. "But we can make lemonade with them." They went to the kitchen to make the lemonade.

While they were making lemonade, Lily's brother came in and said he was thirsty. "Can I have some lemonade?" he asked. Lily remembered how sad she felt when he didn't let her join his game earlier. "No," she said. "You said I couldn't join you earlier. Now you can't join us."

Her brother realized he was being mean and apologized. They all drank the lemonade together and had fun. The moral of the story is that it's always better to include others and be kind.

John and Tina were best friends. They liked to play with their modern toys but one day, John had an idea. He said to Tina, “Hey! Let’s have a match and the winner will get a prize!” Tina was excited and they both agreed to it.

But when it was time for the match, John lied to Tina. He said, “It looks like it’s going to rain, so we can’t have the match today.” Tina was sad, but she trusted John and went home.

The next day, John went to the playground without Tina. She was there, playing with her modern toys. John said, “Hey! Let’s have our match now, Tina!” But Tina was mad because she knew John had lied to her. She said, “No way! You lied to me yesterday. I don’t want to play with you."

John never got his prize and Tina never got to have the match. Their friendship was never the same and they stopped being best friends.

Ben and Lily are twins. They like to play in the garden. They have a big red ball. They kick the ball to each other.

One day, they see a tomato plant in the garden. It has many green and red tomatoes. Ben and Lily want to pick some tomatoes. They think they are yummy.

They run to the tomato plant. They rush to grab the tomatoes. They do not see Mom and Dad. Mom and Dad are working in the garden. They are not happy.

"Stop!" Mom shouts. "Those are not your tomatoes. They are ours. We planted them. We watered them. We waited for them to grow. You cannot take them."

Ben and Lily are scared. They drop the tomatoes. Some tomatoes fall on the ground. Some tomatoes break. They make a mess.

"Sorry, Mom. Sorry, Dad." Ben and Lily say. "We did not know. We just wanted to eat them. We like tomatoes."

Mom and Dad are still angry. But they are also kind. They pick up the tomatoes. They see some bad tomatoes. They are rotten. They have worms. They throw them away.

"Look, Ben and Lily." Mom says. "These are bad tomatoes. They are not good to eat. They can make you sick. You have to be careful. You have to ask before you pick anything from the garden."

Ben and Lily nod. They understand. They feel sorry. They hug Mom and Dad. They say they are sorry again.

Mom and Dad smile. They forgive Ben and Lily. They give them some good tomatoes. They are ripe. They are juicy. They are delicious.

Ben and Lily thank Mom and Dad. They eat the tomatoes. They share the ball. They play in the garden. They are happy.

Once upon a time there was a girl called Kim. She was three years old. One day, she was playing with some blocks, when she saw a strange square. She wanted to know what was inside, so she picked it up and opened it. Inside, there was a toy that she had never seen before. She knew she shouldn't take it, so she told a little lie, and said that she hadn't taken it.

But a few minutes later her mum came in and saw the toy. Kim felt guilty and said she was sorry. Her mum said that she should have been truthful and not lied. Kim said she was sorry again, and promised to never do it again.

From then on, Kim was a good girl and always told the truth. She learnt her lesson and never felt guilty again.

Once upon a time there was a wise old fox who lived near by a big forest. The fox had a beautiful coat of bright red fur. All the other animals of the forest admired the fox for his wise ways.

One day, a small rabbit hopped into the fox's den, hopped right up to the fox, and started to yell.

"Why are you yelling, little one?" asked the fox.

"I'm lost! I don't know how to get home," the rabbit said, between sobs.

The fox looked at the rabbit and thought for a moment. "Now listen to me, little one. I can help you find a way home. Follow my directions and you'll find your way back safe and sound," the wise fox said.

The rabbit followed the fox's directions and soon enough, he had found his way home. From that day on, the rabbit always looked out for the wise old fox and thanked him for helping him find his way home.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a white bunny named Snowy. One day, Lily and Snowy went for a walk in the forest. It was very cold outside, and Snowy was shivering.

Lily said, "Snowy, are you cold? Let's go home and get you warm." Snowy nodded his head and they started to walk back home. As they were walking, Lily saw a bird sitting on a tree branch. The bird was whistling a sweet tune.

Lily said, "Snowy, listen to the bird! He is whistling a pretty song." Snowy looked up and listened to the bird. They both enjoyed the bird's song on their way back home. When they got home, Lily gave Snowy a warm blanket to snuggle in. They both felt happy and cozy.

Once upon a time, in a small village, there was a tiny fly. This fly was unknown to others. It had no friends. The fly was sad.

One sunny day, the fly met a friendly bee. The bee said, "Hi, I'm Bee. Do you want to be my friend?" The fly was happy and said, "Yes, I want to be your friend. My name is Fly."

Fly and Bee became good friends. They played together every day. One day, Bee said, "Fly, I want to marry you." Fly was very happy and said, "Yes, I want to marry you too."

They told their families and everyone in the village. The village people were happy for them. Fly and Bee got married and lived happily ever after. And Fly was not unknown anymore.

Once upon a time, there was an old man who lived in a high tower. He loved to display his beautiful paintings on the walls. One day, a naughty bird flew into the tower and knocked down all the paintings. The old man was very sad and couldn't fix them. He felt so upset that he wanted to cry.

The next day, a big storm came and blew the tower down. The old man was hurt and couldn't move. He called for help, but no one came. He was all alone and very scared. The storm was too strong, and the old man couldn't survive. He passed away, and his beautiful paintings were lost forever.

Tom and Sam are friends. They like to ride bikes in the park. Tom has a new bike. It is red and shiny. Sam has an old bike. It is blue and rusty.

"Look at my new bike!" Tom says. "It is fast and cool. Do you want to try it?"

Sam nods. He wants to try Tom's new bike. He puts on Tom's helmet. It is big and yellow. It has a light on the front. The light can blink.

"Be careful!" Tom says. "My bike is not easy to ride. You have to balance and steer."

Sam gets on the bike. He pedals hard. He feels the wind in his hair. He smiles. He likes Tom's new bike.

But Sam is clumsy. He does not see the rock on the path. He hits the rock with his wheel. He loses his balance. He falls off the bike.

"Ouch!" Sam cries. He scrapes his knee. He drops the helmet. The light stops blinking.

Tom runs to Sam. He helps him up. He checks the bike. It is not broken.

"Are you okay?" Tom asks. He is worried.

Sam nods. He is okay. He is sorry. He gives Tom his helmet.

"I'm sorry, Tom," Sam says. "I was clumsy. I broke your helmet."

Tom hugs Sam. He is not angry.

"It's okay, Sam," Tom says. "You are my friend. The helmet is not important. The light can be fixed. Do you want to ride my bike again?"

Sam shakes his head. He does not want to ride Tom's bike again. He likes his old bike. It is blue and rusty.

"Can we ride your bike?" Sam asks. "It is easy and fun."

Tom nods. He agrees. He likes Sam's old bike. It is blue and rusty.

They swap bikes. They put on their helmets. They ride together in the park. They are happy. They are friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to draw pictures of animals and flowers. One day, she drew a picture of a big yellow sun and a green tree with lots of leaves. She wanted to show her picture to her grandma, who lived far away.

Lily's mom told her she could mail the picture to her grandma. Lily was careful not to rip the picture as she put it in an envelope. She wrote a note to her grandma and put it in the envelope too. The note said, "I love you grandma. Here is a picture for you."

Lily's mom helped her put a stamp on the envelope and they walked to the mailbox. Lily put the envelope in the mailbox and closed the door. She felt happy and excited to think about her grandma getting the picture. A few days later, Lily's grandma called to say thank you for the picture. Lily felt proud and happy that she could make her grandma smile.

Once upon a time there was a boy called Joe. He was an ordinary boy who lived in a regular house. One day, Joe asked his mom for a note.

“What do you need the note for, Joe?” his mom asked.

“My friend Sarah lent me some money and I want to write her a thank you note,” Joe answered.

“That’s very thoughtful of you, Joe,” his mom said with a smile.

Then she gave Joe a piece of paper and a pencil so he could write the note. Joe carefully wrote the words, “Thank you for lending me money.”

When he was done, Joe took the note over to Sarah and gave it to her. Sarah read the note and smiled.

“You didn’t have to say thank you, Joe,” she said. “But I’m glad you did.” From then on, Joe wrote thank you notes to people whenever they lent him things. Soon, his mom, dad and friends started to write thank you notes too. And it was all because of Joe’s ordinary act of kindness.
