Bobby had a great time at the theater. He saw the moving pictures, ate popcorn and drank his favorite drink.

When it was time to go home, Bobby was so happy and thankful that he resisted his Mom's no.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved going to school every day because she had lots of friends there. One day, she woke up and saw that the sun was shining bright and the grass outside was very green. She knew it was going to be a great day.

When Lily got to school, she saw that her teacher had set up a surprise for the class. She had scattered lots of green balloons all around the room. Lily was so excited to play with them during recess.

After class, Lily and her friends ran outside to play. They were having so much fun with the balloons, but then the wind started to pick up. Suddenly, all the balloons started to scatter in different directions. Lily and her friends tried to catch them, but they were too fast.

Just when they thought they had lost all the balloons, they saw a little boy walking towards them with a big smile on his face. He had found all the balloons and brought them back to Lily and her friends. They were so happy and grateful to the little boy for helping them. From that day on, Lily knew that good things can happen when you least expect them.

Today, Jake and Anny were playing in the garden. Jake had a rough toy train that he liked to push around. Suddenly, when they weren't looking, the toy train vanished! Jake and Anny were very surprised. They looked all around and couldn't find the train anywhere. They asked mum, but she said she didn't know what had happened to it.

Jake and Anny decided to look for the train. They searched high and low and still couldn't find it. They looked inside the shed, around the trees, and all over the garden, but it was nowhere to be seen. They were so disapointed.

Suddenly they heard a noise coming from the sky. They looked up and saw the train flying above them! It was circling around in the sky. Anny laughed and clapped her hands. Jake shouted for excitement. Then, the toy train vanished and flew away.

They said goodbye to their train and waved. Jake and Anny looked at each other with a big smile, and knew that their toy train was having an adventure in the sky. What an exciting day!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the woods by her house. One day, she found a big log and decided to sit on it.

As she sat there, she saw a squirrel running up a tree. She imagined what it would be like to climb up the tree like the squirrel.

Suddenly, Lily's mom called out to her from the house. "Lily, it's time to come inside for lunch!"

Lily got up from the log and went inside. "Mom, can we come back to the woods later?" she asked.

"Of course, Lily. The woods are a dependable place for us to play," her mom replied with a smile.

Bob was walking in the park one day with his mom. He saw a yellow apple on the ground and he was really excited.

"Mom, look, there's an apple!" Bob said.

"Yes, it's a yellow apple Bob," said his mom.

Bob picked up the apple and he counted the number of bumps on it.

"Mom, there are five bumps on the apple!" he shouted.

"That's right Bob, you counted the number of bumps correctly," said his mom.

Bob was so happy. He took the apple home and had a big snack. It tasted so sweet!

Once upon a time, there lived two friends who loved to dance. Every day the two friends would go to the subway and dance together. They were so happy and their movements were as smooth as silk.

One day, the friends decided to dress up in blue clothes for their dance. They felt so cool and spun around in circles. Suddenly, the ground started to rumble and the walls began to shake.

The two friends started to panic and quickly ran away, but it was too late. The subway was crumbling and clouds of dust filled the air. The friends had to quickly leap out the windows.

The friends made it out of the subway alive, but they were never able to dance inside it again. The terrible experience stayed with them forever and they vowed to never go back.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Mary. Mary loved to explore and she did it every day. On this day, she found a special powder. It was like nothing she had ever seen before.

She decided to try it out, so she sprinkled the delicious powder on top of a big hill. Suddenly, the hill started to shake and move around. Then, the hill began to reverse! Mary watched in wonder as the hill went backwards in a strange and magical way.

When the hill was gone, there was a surprise in its place. Instead of dirt and stones, the hill had become a giant delicious cake! Mary was very excited and she quickly ran to get her friends. Together, they shared the tasty treat and celebrated their magical find.

Little Thomas loved school. He was so happy every morning when he got ready to go. He got to play, learn new things, and have fun with his friends.

But one day, when Thomas got to school, he noticed the air was cold. He couldn't understand why everyone else didn't seem to mind. He tried to ignore it and soon he was having fun.

Then, something happened that made Thomas shiver. The teacher had announced that something very rare was in the school. Every student was excited and Thomas quickly forgot about the cold.

The next day, when Thomas arrived at school, he was surprised to find that the whole school had been decorated with snowflakes. Thomas couldn't believe his eyes! It must be something very rare indeed.

Now he knew why he had shivered the day before - it was from the cold and from the anticipation of something special.

Once upon a time there was a stubborn fox who loved to jump. He would jump over rocks and through bushes. One day he came across a trail he had never seen before. He followed the trail, jumping over logs and ducking under branches.

As he continued on the trail, it got narrower and narrower. Soon, he had to jump even higher to move forward. He was getting tired from all the jumping, but he was too stubborn to quit.

He kept jumping, until he saw a clearing. He was so happy that he jumped right into the middle.

Suddenly, a rabbit popped out from the bushes.

"Why are you jumping around like that?" asked the rabbit.

The fox stopped jumping and said, "I'm following this trail and I had to jump to get here. Now I just need to figure out where it leads."

The rabbit smiled and said, "I know exactly where it goes. Come on, I'll show you."

The fox was so glad that he followed the stubborn trail. Together they jumped down the trail, until it led them to a beautiful meadow.

Ben and Mia are twins. They like to play with their toys and eat spaghetti. But Ben is deaf. He cannot hear what Mia says. He can only see her mouth and hands.

One day, Mia has a new idea. She wants to play a game with Ben. She says, "Let's move the spaghetti like snakes. We can make them wiggle and hiss." She shows Ben how to do it. Ben nods and smiles. He likes snakes.

They take some spaghetti from their plates and put them on the table. They move them with their fingers. They make funny faces and noises. They have fun.

But Mom does not see them. She is busy in the kitchen. She does not know they are playing with their food. She thinks they are eating.

She comes to the table with a big bowl of sauce. She says, "Who wants more spaghetti?" She does not see the spaghetti snakes on the table. She pours the sauce on them.

Ben and Mia scream. They are scared and sad. Their spaghetti snakes are gone. They are covered with sauce. They look at Mom. Mom looks at them. She is shocked and angry.

She says, "What are you doing? Why are you playing with your food? That is not nice. That is wasteful. You have to eat your spaghetti, not move it like snakes."

Ben and Mia cry. They do not understand. They were just having fun. They did not mean to make Mom mad. They try to explain. But Mom does not listen. She does not see their mouth and hands. She only hears their cries.

She says, "No more games. No more spaghetti. Go to your room. Now."

Ben and Mia go to their room. They are sad and hungry. They hug each other. They wish Mom could understand. They wish they could hear and speak like her. They wish they could move the spaghetti like snakes again.

A little boy named Jack was walking through the woods. He could hear a strange voice echoing through the forest. Jack got closer and closer, and noticed the voice was coming from a fat tree at the center of the woods. As he looked closer Jack could see the tree was shaking and its branches were waving around. He was so curious he wanted to climb it.

Jack hesitated for a moment, but then decided to make his way up the fat tree. He finally made it to the top and he saw what was making the voice. It was an old, rusty birdhouse with a strange opening in the back. Jack stuck his finger in the opening, but suddenly the birdhouse started to shake and he lost his grip. He watched as the birdhouse started to fall from the tree.

Jack was terrified, but then he heard the voice again. It was the same one he had heard before. He looked around and he was surprised to see an owl perched on top of a nearby branch. The owl was shaking its head and Jack could see it was warning him. The voice was saying: "Fall, fall!"

Jack was so grateful to the owl. It had saved him just in time! He waved goodbye to the owl and thanked it before running back home. He would never forget the wise owl's voice.

Lily and Ben were playing a game with their cards. They had to match the cards with the same pictures. Lily had many cards, but Ben had only a few. Lily was happy, but Ben was miserable.

"Look, I have more cards than you!" Lily said. "I am winning the game!"

Ben felt sad. He wanted to have more cards too. He wanted to win the game. He looked at Lily's cards and saw one that he liked. It had a picture of a big red car. Ben loved cars.

"Can I have that card, please?" Ben asked. "It is my favorite."

"No, you can't!" Lily said. "It is my card. You have to find your own."

Ben felt angry. He thought Lily was not nice. He wanted to take the card from her. He reached out his hand and grabbed the card.

"Hey, give it back!" Lily shouted. "That is not fair!"

They both pulled the card and it tore in half. They both dropped the pieces and started to cry.

Mom heard the noise and came to see what was wrong. She saw the torn card and the unhappy children.

"What happened here?" Mom asked. "Why are you crying?"

"Lily and Ben told Mom what happened. They both said sorry for tearing the card. Mom hugged them and said it was okay.

"I have an idea," Mom said. "Why don't we play a different game? A game that includes everyone and has a prize for the winner."

"What game?" Lily and Ben asked.

Mom smiled and said, "How about a treasure hunt? I will hide some clues around the house and you have to find them. The clues will lead you to a prize. Do you want to play?"

Lily and Ben nodded. They liked treasure hunts. They forgot about the card and the game. They dried their tears and smiled.

"Okay, let's play!" Mom said. "The first clue is in the kitchen. Go and find it!"

Lily and Ben ran to the kitchen. They were excited to play the new game. They hoped to find the prize. They hoped it was something good. They hoped it was a car.

Today was the first day Sammy's family had decided to go down to the beach. Sammy was so excited. He loved the beach. But then, he started to worry.

He noticed the rock pool across from them and thought about the creatures living inside it. He had never seen them before and he wasn't sure if he was ready.

Suddenly, Sammy felt very scared. He wanted to get away from the rock pool and he started to feel uneasy. His dad sensed a change in him and asked him what was wrong.

Sammy explained his worries and his dad comforted him. He calmly explained that the creatures in the rock pool would not hurt them and were just as curious of Sammy as Sammy was of them.

Sammy felt reassured and excited to explore the rock pool with his dad. Together, they got close enough to spot the creatures. Sammy couldn't believe it when he saw them - he was so excited!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in her backyard, where there was a big slide. One day, Lily saw a pretty flower growing next to the slide. She wanted to pick it, but her mom had told her to leave the flowers alone so they could stay healthy.

Lily was sad because she really wanted the flower. She thought about it all day and decided to sneak out to the backyard at night to get it. But when she got there, she saw that the flower was gone! She looked around and saw that her little brother had picked it and accidentally dropped it on the slide, where it got all squished.

Lily was angry at her brother for ruining the flower, but then she remembered what her mom had said about keeping the flowers healthy. She decided to forgive her brother and help him plant some new flowers so they could all be healthy and pretty again.

Once upon a time, there was a big, brown bear named Benny. Benny loved to play in the forest and eat honey from the beehives. One day, Benny received a message from his friend, the squirrel. The message said that there was a big, juicy watermelon in the field.

Benny couldn't resist the urge to go and find the watermelon. He ran through the forest, following the squirrel's directions. But when he got to the field, he saw that the watermelon was being guarded by a mean, old farmer.

Benny knew he had to be careful. He waited until the farmer was asleep before sneaking into the field. But just as he was about to take a bite of the watermelon, he heard the farmer waking up. Benny quickly ran back into the forest, feeling sad that he didn't get to eat the watermelon. But he knew he had to be patient and wait for another chance to get it.

Jack was very frustrated. He wanted to go faster than anyone else. He saw a plastic toy car and he knew it would help him speed.

So Jack grabbed the car and sped off. He drove it so fast that he almost lost control. But then, he put his foot on the brakes and stopped.

He was so happy that he had been able to speed. It had made him feel better. From then on, he played with the toy car every day and tried to be the fastest one.

Once there was a very small mouse living in a big forest. Every day the mouse would run around and look for food and adventures. One day, when the mouse was out exploring, she found a shiny coin. She was so excited and couldn't believe her luck. She held it tightly in her hands so it couldn't get away.

But suddenly, in a blink of an eye, the coin vanished! The mouse was worried because she had found something so valuable and it had disappeared so quickly. She looked and looked for the coin but it was impossible to find.

The mouse was sad but she learned an important lesson about treasure. She realized that it wasn't right to try to hold things that don't belong to her. In the end, it's better to leave it alone and let it be.

Lily and Tom were friends who liked to play near the water. They saw many things on the shore, like shells, rocks, and crabs. One day, they found a green bottle with a paper inside. They were curious and wanted to see what it said.

They opened the bottle and pulled out the paper. It had some words on it, but they could not read them. They only knew some letters, like A, B, and C. They tried to guess what the words meant.

"Maybe it is a map to a treasure," Lily said.

"Or a message from a pirate," Tom said.

"Or a magic spell," Lily said.

They decided to whisper the words and see what would happen. They thought it would be fun and exciting. They did not know that the words were a curse.

They whispered the words together, holding the paper. As soon as they finished, they felt a strange pain in their bodies. They looked at each other and screamed. They were turning into fish!

They dropped the paper and the bottle and tried to run, but it was too late. Their legs became fins and their arms became scales. They could not breathe the air anymore. They had to jump into the water to survive.

They swam away from the shore, scared and sad. They could not talk to each other or to anyone else. They had lost their friends, their families, and their lives. They had made a big mistake. They wished they had never found the green bottle.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Daisy. Daisy wanted to do something special, so she decided to decorate her room. She chose lots of pretty colors and shapes. Everyone in the family was so impressed by her hard work!

One day, Daisy made a surprise for her family. She created an icy trap on the floor. She used a sheet of paper and different types of decorations. When someone stepped on it, it made a fantastic noise. She laughed when her family tried to avoid her trap!

The next day, Daisy put the trap in the front yard. She wanted to play with her friends. She thought it would be fun to surprise them. When her friends arrived, they could not believe their eyes. The icy trap made the most wonderful sound when they stepped on it.

Daisy was so glad that she decorated her room and made the icy trap. She had so much fun playing with her friends. They all laughed in joy. It was the best day ever!

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy who loved to play outside. One day, he found an orange beetle crawling on a leaf. He picked it up and showed it to his friend, Lily.

"Look, Lily! I found an orange beetle!" Timmy exclaimed.

Lily looked at the beetle and said, "It's so pretty! Can I hold it?"

Timmy handed the beetle to Lily, but as soon as she touched it, the beetle started to tremble. Lily got scared and dropped the beetle.

"Oh no! I think I hurt it," Lily said, feeling sad.

Timmy picked up the beetle and saw that it had a broken leg. He knew he had to help the beetle, so he gently put it on a leaf and brought it to his mom.

"Mom, can you help the beetle with the broken leg?" Timmy asked.

His mom took the beetle and fixed its leg with a tiny bandage. Timmy and Lily were so happy to see the beetle healthy again. From that day on, they made sure to be extra careful with the little creatures they found outside.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily loved to play outside on the ground. One day, her mom told her it was time to come inside for dinner. Lily insisted she wanted to stay outside a little longer.

Her mom worried that Lily would get too hungry, but Lily kept playing. Eventually, Lily's mom came outside and said, "Lily, it's time to come inside now." Lily replied, "But I'm having so much fun playing on the ground!"

Her mom smiled and said, "I know you are, but we need to eat dinner now." Lily finally agreed and went inside, happy and full of energy from her fun day outside.

Once upon a time there was a fit girl who loved to explore. She went to discover a river one sunny day, and she loved it. The water was so sparkly and the birdsong made it so peaceful.

The girl was so happy! She wanted to complete a special project, so she gathered white stones in the river and made a path in the water. She arranged the stones to make a pattern, and when she was done it was so pretty.

The girl was so proud of her work and watched the river each day to make sure that the stones were in the same place. She was happy to see that the river and stones fit together so well.

The little girl's project was complete, and she was so pleased with her successful adventure.

Tom and Jen are friends. They like to travel and see new things. One day, they find a big box in the park. The box is cheap. It has holes and dirt on it. But Tom and Jen think it is fun. They say, "This is our car. We can travel in it."

They push the box to the road. They see a big truck. The truck is loud and fast. Tom and Jen are scared. They say, "We need a roof. The roof will keep us safe." They look around. They see a big tree. The tree has leaves and branches. They say, "This is our roof. We can hide under it."

They pull the box to the tree. They climb inside the box. They pretend they are in a car. They say, "We are traveling to the zoo. We will see lions and monkeys and bears." They make noises like animals. They laugh and have fun. They forget about the truck and the road. They are happy under their roof.

Once upon a time there was a little girl. She liked to dress in a very pretty dress with lots of colors.

One day, the girl decided to go to the shore. As she ran, she felt a little dizzy. But she kept running until she got to the shore.

She liked the shore very much. The sand was so soft and the water was so blue. She started to play in the sand and splash in the water. She was having so much fun!

But then she started to feel a little dizzy again. So she got out of the water, put on her dress and went home.

The End.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. He loved going to the park with his mommy. One day, while they were walking, Timmy saw a tree with some unusual fruit.

"Mommy, look! What's that?" Timmy asked, pointing at the fruit.

"That's a persimmon, Timmy. It's a type of fruit," his mommy explained.

Suddenly, a friendly squirrel appeared. "Hello there! I'm Sammy the squirrel. Nice to meet you," Sammy said to Timmy.

Timmy was so happy to meet Sammy. They all had a great time together, picking the persimmons and sharing them with Sammy. From that day on, Timmy and Sammy would often meet in the park to play together and eat more fruit.

Once upon a time there was a curious elephant called Jojo. Jojo wanted to go to university but didn't know how. One day, while walking in the jungle, he happened to meet a wise monkey. The monkey asked Jojo: "What are you doing here?". Jojo replied: "I want to go to university but I don't know how." The monkey smiled and said: "Go to that big building and wipe your feet before entering. You will then find out what you need to do." So Jojo went to the big building and wiped his feet before entering. He was amazed to find a lot of students inside, all busy studying and learning. Jojo was very interested so he started to explore the university. With the help of the people inside he finally had the chance to achieve his dream and go to university. The moral of the story is that you don't need to know it all. With curiosity and hard work, anyone can achieve their dreams.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her round ball in the park. One day, she met a boy named Timmy who also loved to play with his round ball. They played and laughed together, and Lily felt very happy.

As they were playing, Lily's ball rolled away and got stuck in a bush. Lily started to weep because she thought she had lost her ball forever. Timmy saw her crying and asked what was wrong. Lily told him about her ball and Timmy said, "Don't worry, I'll help you get it back!"

Timmy climbed into the bush and found the ball. He gave it back to Lily and she was so happy that she gave him a big hug. From that day on, Lily and Timmy played together every day in the park with their round balls. They never forgot the time Timmy helped Lily when she was weeping.

Once upon a time, there was a big, black and white panda. His name was Bob. Bob was very cool because he always wore sunglasses. Bob lived in a big forest with lots of trees and flowers.

One night, Bob went to sleep and started to dream. In his dream, he was flying like a bird. He flew over the trees and saw lots of animals. He saw lions, tigers, and even monkeys swinging on vines. It was a very cool dream.

When Bob woke up, he felt happy. He stretched his arms and legs and went outside to play. He saw his friends, the rabbits and the squirrels. Bob told them about his dream and they thought it was very cool too. They played together all day and had lots of fun.

One day, a boy named Tim found an empty box. He had an idea. He wanted to make music with the box. He called his friend, Sue, to help him.

Tim said to Sue, "Let's make a rhythm with this box." Sue was happy and said, "Yes, let's do it!" They tapped on the box and made a fun rhythm. They laughed and played together.

Tim's mom came and saw them playing. She said, "I can record your music with my phone." Tim and Sue were excited. They played the rhythm again, and Tim's mom recorded it. They listened to their music and danced. It was a fun day.

Once upon a time, there were two friends named Joe and Mary. Joe liked to mix things together and Mary liked to draw a line. But one day, they had a disagreement because Joe wanted to mix the line Mary had drawn together. Mary didn't want to do that and said no, but Joe was very stubborn and tried to mix the line anyway. Mary got very angry and ran away.

Joe didn't want to give up and drew a hidden line. Then he used a big spoon and tried to mix it with the other things in the room. But it didn't work very well and the line was still very much in plain sight.

Joe felt sorry for not listening to Mary, and decided to ask her for help. He was surprised to find her in a corner, crying to herself. Joe thanked Mary for not giving up on him and said that he learned an important lesson: when it comes to friendship, it is important to listen and accept the opinion of others.

From then on, Joe and Mary worked together to create beautiful things and they were very happy. They never forgot the lesson they had learned and they remained the best of friends forever.

Lily and Ben are best friends. They like to play outside in the sun. They have a big yard with a swing, a slide and a sandbox. They also have a red wagon that they can pull or ride.

One day, they decide to have a race with their wagon. They take turns to pull each other around the yard. They laugh and shout as they go fast and slow, left and right, up and down. They are very jolly.

"Look, Lily, I can pull you faster than you can pull me!" Ben says.

"No, Ben, I can pull you faster than you can pull me!" Lily says.

They keep racing until they hear a loud boom. They look up and see dark clouds in the sky. They hear another boom and see a flash of light. They feel drops of water on their faces. It is a storm.

"Oh no, Lily, we have to go inside!" Ben says.

"Yes, Ben, we have to go inside!" Lily says.

They quickly jump off the wagon and run to the house. They leave the wagon in the yard. They hope it will be okay.

They go inside and find their mom. She gives them a hug and a cookie. She tells them not to be scared of the storm. She says it will be over soon.

They sit on the couch and watch the storm through the window. They see the rain, the wind, the thunder and the lightning. They are not jolly anymore. They are a little bit scared.

But they are also a little bit curious. They wonder how the storm makes all the noise and light. They wonder how the rain falls from the sky. They wonder when the sun will come back.

They ask their mom many questions. She tries to answer them with simple words. She tells them that the storm is part of nature. She tells them that the sun will come back when the storm is gone. She tells them that they are safe and warm inside.

They listen to their mom and feel better. They snuggle with her and each other. They are not scared anymore. They are a little bit jolly again. They wait for the storm to end and the sun to shine. They hope to race with their wagon again tomorrow.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the rain and jump in puddles. One day, she got very muddy and her mom said, "Lily, you need to take a shower."

Lily didn't want to take a shower because she liked being muddy. But her mom said, "You can't go to bed all dirty. You need to get clean." So Lily took a shower and it was so much fun! She splashed and played with the water.

After her shower, Lily's mom gave her a big towel to dry off with. Lily wrapped herself up in the towel and said, "I love showers! They make me feel ancient!" Her mom laughed and said, "You mean refreshed, Lily. Showers make you feel refreshed." And Lily smiled and said, "Yes, refreshed!"

Mum was feeling tired, so she opened the bathtub, filled it with warm water and got into it. She closed her eyes and felt the warmth comfort her.

Suddenly, she heard the sound of little feet running into the bathroom. It was her 3-year-old daughter Isla, who shouted, "Mummy, can I join you?"

Mum said, "Of course, my darling."

Isla clapped her hands and quickly took off her clothes. She jumped into the bathtub and cuddled up next to Mum. They stayed like that for a while, feeling the warmth of the water comfort them.

When they finished their bath, Mum hugged Isla tight and kissed her forehead. Isla smiled and said, "I love you, Mummy."

Mum smiled back and said, "I love you too."

Once upon a time, there was a warm, fuzzy cat named Fluffy. Fluffy loved to play in the sun all day. One day, Fluffy found a ball. The ball was big and red. Fluffy liked the ball a lot.

Fluffy played with the ball all day. Fluffy would drop the ball and then run after it. The ball would roll and roll, and Fluffy would chase it. Fluffy was so happy to have a new toy to play with.

But then, Fluffy got an itch. The itch was on Fluffy's ear. Fluffy tried to scratch the itch, but it was hard to reach. Fluffy dropped the ball and rubbed the ear on the ground. The itch went away, and Fluffy was happy again. Fluffy picked up the ball and went back to playing in the warm sun.

Once upon a time, a little baby slept in a lovely crib. The baby was happy and cozy in the crib. One day, the baby woke up and saw a toy on the floor. The baby wanted to play with the toy, so the baby reached out and poked it with a chubby finger. The toy made a funny noise and the baby giggled. The baby loved playing with toys in the lovely crib.

Once upon a time there was a girl named Sarah. She loved going up to the attic and playing with all the unknown things stored up there. One day, she went to the attic and found a big pot. It was unknown to her, so she wondered what she could make.

Sarah thought, "Maybe I can cook something in it". She went downstairs to the kitchen and found ingredients to cook with. She put them in the pot and stirred them around. The smell was delicious!

Her mom came in and said, "What have you been cooking?" Sarah replied with a smile, "Look what I made in the attic!" Her mom took a look and smiled too, "It looks delicious!"

So Sarah and her mom sat down to enjoy the meal she had cooked in the attic with the unknown pot. Together they laughed and enjoyed their tasty food. The end.

Jacky was very loyal to his friend Bobby. Bobby had a big, bushy mustache and Jacky thought it was very funny. One day, Bobby asked Jacky to help him manage his mustache.

Jacky said, "I'll try! How can I help?"

Bobby replied, "Just hold it while I cut it."

So Jacky held Bobby's mustache as he cut it and managed it as best he could. Bobby thanked Jacky for his help and promised to take better care of his mustache from now on.

Jacky smiled and said, "You're welcome. I'll always be here for you to help manage your mustache."

And so Jacky remained loyal to his friend and always helped him manage his big, bushy mustache.

Once upon a time there lived a little girl. She was very adventurous and liked to travel. One day she decided that she wanted to plan a trip. She found a pretty calendar and started to plan each day.

The little girl asked her mom, "Can I travel far away today?" Her mom nodded and said, "Yes you can travel wherever you would like to go."

The little girl was so excited to go on her trip. She started packing her bag full of fun things and decided to go on a boat. When she arrived on the boat, the little girl was so happy. She got to explore the waves and see the sun set in the sky.

The little girl was pleased with her travels and was glad to be back home. She hung her pretty calendar on the wall, so she could plan more travel adventures in the future.

Lily and Ben were playing in the dark. They had a flashlight and a tent. They liked to pretend they were explorers in a jungle. They saw many animals and plants with the flashlight.

But then they heard a loud noise. It was a big bear. The bear was hungry and angry. It wanted to eat Lily and Ben. Lily and Ben were scared. They did not want to be eaten.

They decided to fight the bear. They used the flashlight to make the bear blind. They shone the light in the bear's eyes. The bear roared and covered its eyes. Lily and Ben ran fast to the tent. They zipped it up and hid inside.

The bear tried to find them. It sniffed and scratched the tent. But it could not see them. It was still blind from the flashlight. Lily and Ben held each other and hoped the bear would go away.

After a while, the bear gave up. It was too tired and sore. It walked away to find another food. Lily and Ben heard the bear leave. They were happy and relieved. They had fought the bear and won. They hugged the flashlight and thanked it for saving them. They were brave explorers.

Lily and Ben are friends. They like to play with cars and trucks. They have many cars and trucks, but they have one big truck that they both love. It is red and shiny and makes loud noises.

One day, they want to play with the big truck on the road. The road is not busy, but they have to be careful. They take turns to drive the big truck and make it go fast and slow and beep the horn. They have fun and laugh.

But then, a big dog comes to the road. It is black and furry and has sharp teeth. It sees the big truck and wants to play with it too. It runs to the truck and barks and tries to bite it. Lily and Ben are scared. They do not want the dog to hurt their big truck or them.

They run to their house and call for help. Their mom and dad come out and see the dog. They are not happy. They tell the dog to go away and leave the big truck alone. The dog is not loyal. It does not listen. It keeps barking and biting.

Lily and Ben are sad. They think they have lost their big truck. But then, they see something. Their cat, Max, is on the road. He is small and orange and has soft fur. He is loyal. He likes Lily and Ben and their big truck. He sees the dog and does not like it. He hisses and scratches and chases the dog away. The dog is scared. It runs away and does not come back.

Lily and Ben are happy. They hug Max and thank him. They get their big truck and bring it to their house. They share it with Max and let him sit on it. They play with their cars and trucks and their cat. They are loyal friends. They have fun and laugh.

Once upon a time there was a girl called Amy. She was three. Amy liked to relax and have fun.

One day, Amy went to the park by herself. She wanted to relax and enjoy the sunshine.

In the park, Amy looked around. Suddenly, she saw something hidden: a needle! She was scared. She didn't know what it was.

Amy decided to tell her mummy. She ran all the way home. When she got there, she told mummy what she had seen.

Mummy explained that the needle was sharp. That meant it could hurt you. Mummy said: "Now you know why it is a good idea to tell me if you see something dangerous".

Amy was very glad she had spoken to mummy. Now she could relax and have fun in the park again.

Once upon a time, there was a bunny named Benny. Benny was a regular bunny who loved to eat carrots. One day, Benny was walking through the woods and saw a delicious looking apple. He couldn't help himself, so he decided to take a bite.

After he bit into the apple, Benny felt a strange tingling sensation. He asked the apple, "What was that?".

The apple answered, "I am magical and I give special powers to whoever bites me!"

Benny was so excited. He took another bite and sure enough, he felt the tingling again. This time, it was stronger and he began to feel really powerful. He shouted, "Wow, this is amazing!"

The result of Benny's two bites was a super power! Now, Benny could fly and do amazing things! Benny was happy every day because of his new power. He was grateful for what he got from the magical apple.

The End.

The bell be ringing. It be loud and happy. The bird be singing too. The children be so excited, running to the door. They want to see what be outside. One of them opened the door. It be disgusting. There be a big fly buzzing around, and it be carrying a big bell. Disgusting! No one wants to touch it, so they all just be shouting and waving their hands until the fly flew away. At last, the bell be gone. Everyone be happy again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys and her friends. One day, Lily and her friends decided to have a race. They ran and ran, but Lily fell down and hurt her knee. She started to cry.

Lily's friends tried to help her, but she was too upset. She felt like she was going to miss the victory. But then, her friend Sarah had an idea. She told Lily that they could be flexible and make the race fair. They could start over and everyone could win.

Lily smiled and wiped away her tears. She realized that being flexible was important and that winning wasn't everything. She was happy to have such kind friends who cared about her. From then on, Lily knew that even if she didn't win, she could still have fun and enjoy playing with her friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, Lily's mom asked her to get some milk from the refrigerator. Lily went to the kitchen and opened the fridge. She saw a cute little mouse inside. The mouse was harmless and didn't do anything to Lily.

Lily said, "Hi little mouse, what are you doing in my refrigerator?" The mouse replied, "I'm just looking for some cheese to eat." Lily realized that the mouse was just hungry and wanted some food.

Lily said, "I have some cheese in the fridge. You can have it." The mouse was very happy and thanked Lily. From that day on, the mouse and Lily became friends. Lily learned that even though something might seem scary at first, it can be harmless and friendly.

The moral of the story is to be kind to others, even if they are different from us. We should always try to understand and help others, just like Lily helped the little mouse.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. He loved to play outside in the big green grassy field. One day, Timmy found an axe under a tree. He believed it was a magic axe that could make trees fall down. So, he swung the axe and chopped down a tree.

Suddenly, a group of lively squirrels came out of the tree. They were angry with Timmy for chopping down their home. Timmy felt bad and promised to never chop down a tree again. He apologized to the squirrels and promised to plant new trees for them to live in. From that day on, Timmy became a friend to all the animals in the field.

Once upon a time, there was a man named Tom. Tom had a long wallet. One day, Tom wanted to buy a toy car for his son. But when he looked for his wallet, it was gone! Tom was sad and did not know what to do.

Tom began to look for his wallet everywhere. He looked under his bed, behind the door, and on the table. As the sun began to rise, Tom still could not find his wallet. He felt very upset because he wanted to make his son happy.

Then, Tom saw his little dog, Spot, playing with something. It was his long wallet! Tom was so happy and thanked Spot for finding it. Now, Tom could go buy the toy car for his son. They played with the toy car all day and had lots of fun.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to go camping with his family. They always brought a big tent that they could sleep in. Timmy thought it was the best tent in the world because it kept them dry when it rained.

One day, Timmy and his family went on a hike. They saw a big mountain in the distance and Timmy wanted to climb it. His mom said they could try, but only if they had a reliable map to follow. Timmy's dad said he had a map that would help them find the way.

They started to climb the mountain and it was very hard. But with the help of the map, they were able to find the right path. When they got to the top, Timmy felt very proud. He had gained a lot of confidence and he knew he could do anything he set his mind to.

Claire was playing in the garden when she saw a red truck. It was so fast! She couldn't take her eyes off it. Claire wanted to drive a truck like that one!

She ran to her big brother and asked him if she could get one too. The big brother told her there was something special inside the truck.

Claire was so excited to find out what it was. She opened the door and saw a bowl of special oatmeal. It looked so good! On the side was a spoon that her brother had put there.

Claire picked up the spoon and started to stir the oatmeal. She added some cream and sugar and stirred it some more. Then she closed the door and went to the truck. She pretended it was her own.

Claire got inside and pretended to drive. She stepped on the pedal and off she went, feeling very proud. She took her imaginary truck for a spin around the garden, imagining it was very fast.

It was the best time ever. Claire was very happy that she had found something so special in the truck.

Once upon a time, there was a very adorable comet. It liked to skip in the night sky. It would twinkle and spin and have lots of fun.

One night, the comet saw a little girl. She was outside playing in her backyard. The comet skipped over to her and smiled.

The little girl was so happy to see the adorable comet. She waved and skipped around with the comet. They laughed and laughed and had a great time together.

The little girl and the comet skipped through the night sky until the morning came. The little girl had to go inside, so the comet waved goodbye.

The girl smiled and waved goodbye to the comet. She was sad that they had to part, but she knew the comet would always be back in the night sky.

Jimmy was a very curious three year old. Everywhere he went he wanted to learn new things. One day he was walking with his mom and he saw a beautiful flower beside some bushes. "Mama, what's that?" He asked pointing at the flower.

"That's a flower, Jim," said his mother, "Flowers are very special, they grow everywhere."

Jimmy couldn't take his eyes off the flower. He reached his hand out to touch it, but before he could, his mom stopped him and said, "Jimmy, it is rude to take something that doesn't belong to you without asking first."

Jimmy looked down, embarrassed. "I'm sorry mom," he said softly.

His mom said kindly, "It's okay, Jim, but you should always remember to be polite and ask before you touch something that isn't yours! You can learn a lot if you remember to be respectful."

Jimmy smiled and nodded. He learned a valuable lesson that day, that being polite and respectful can help him learn even more. From then on, Jimmy remembered to always keep his manners in mind when exploring the world around him.

Lily and Ben are friends. They like to play in the park. They have a ball and a kite. They have fun.

One day, a big dog appears. The dog is black and loud. It runs to Lily and Ben. It wants the ball. Lily and Ben are scared. They hold the kite and run away.

"Go away, dog!" Lily shouts. "This is our ball!"

The dog does not listen. It chases Lily and Ben. It barks and growls. Lily and Ben are very scared.

They see a man. The man has a guitar. He plays a song. The song is nice and soft. Lily and Ben like the song. They stop running. They listen to the song.

The dog hears the song too. The dog stops chasing. The dog is quiet. The dog is weak. The song makes the dog weak. The dog lies down. The dog sleeps.

The man smiles. He says, "Don't be afraid. The dog is not bad. The dog is just playful. But the dog does not like loud noises. The song calms the dog down."

Lily and Ben are happy. They say, "Thank you, man. You are kind. You have a good song."

The man says, "You are welcome, kids. You are brave. You have a nice kite."

Lily and Ben give the ball to the dog. The dog wakes up. The dog is happy. The dog plays with the ball.

Lily and Ben play with the kite. They fly the kite high. They sing the song. They have fun.

Mum and Dad sat at the table and talked. "We need to prepare some mail," said Mum. Dad got up and fetched some paper and a pen. He wrote something and put it in an envelope.

The next day, the family went to the post office. They posted the envelope. Dad looked very sad.

A few days later, a letter arrived for the family. As Mum opened the letter, her face went very pale. Dad felt a bitter feeling in his heart.

The letter said that the family could not go on their holiday. They had not planned it properly and now they would have to stay at home.

The moral of this story is that it is important to plan carefully before taking any action. When things are not planned properly, it can lead to bad results.

Once upon a time there was a little bird who wanted to fly. Every morning he would look up at the sky and wish he could soar. Everyday he would try his hardest to fly, but he never seemed to be able to.

One day, he heard about a law that said he could fly. He was so excited! He hopped and flapped his wings until he finally rose up into the air and began to soar. He felt so free.

The little bird was able to visit many wonderful places. Everywhere he went, he brought joy and happiness to everyone he met. People laughed as they watched him soar.

The little bird was so happy that he could finally fly. He was thankful for the law that made it available for him to soar.

The little bird had the best time ever in the sky and still visits all the places he could find. Now, everyone can watch the little bird soar in the sky!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside and look for bugs. One day, she found a funny looking spider crawling on a leaf.

Lily said, "Hello little spider! What are you doing?"

The spider replied, "I'm thirsty. I need a drink of water."

Lily said, "I can help you! Come with me."

Lily took the spider to a puddle of water and the spider drank and drank until he was no longer thirsty.

The spider said, "Thank you, Lily! You are very kind."

Lily smiled and said, "You're welcome, spider. Now let's go have more fun outside!"

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved watching dancers twirl and spin around. One day, she saw a very difficult dance on TV and said to her mom, "I admire that dancer, she's so good!"

Her mom smiled and said, "Would you like to try dancing like her?"

Lily nodded excitedly and her mom put on some music. Lily tried to copy the dancer's moves, but it was very difficult. She got frustrated and said to her mom, "This is so hard!"

Her mom hugged her and said, "Don't worry, it takes practice to be a good dancer. You'll get better with time."

Lily smiled and kept trying. Even though it was difficult, she admired the dancer's talent and was determined to keep practicing.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy who had a shiny shoe. It was clear, like the sky in summer. He loved to wear it and twirled around in circles. One day, he wanted to fly with the shoe. So he jumped off his bed and tried to take off. But he fell down and the shoe fell off his foot. He looked everywhere for it, but it was gone. He was sad but kept looking. After a while, he spotted it; it had fallen under the bed. He reached down, grabbed his shoe, and hugged it tight. Then he smiled and put it back on his foot. The little boy was so happy to have his shoe again. They twirled around the room together. The end.

One day Emma was at the beach. She was pushing her toy car in the sand. She liked to push the car back and forth in the soft, sandy ground. Then, she saw something gracefully swimming in the ocean. It was a majestic dolphin. She stood and watched it for a long time. She thought it was so beautiful and graceful. Emma was sad when it eventually disappeared. She got back to playing in the sand, pushing her toy car around. She had lots of fun in the sand that day!

Once there was a little girl who really wanted a pet. But she had nowhere to keep it. One day, she found a green image in a box. It was a picture of a dog - the little girl's dream pet! She was so happy she began to weep with joy.

The little girl kept the image with her wherever she went. When she was sad, she looked at the image and felt happy. Whenever she was happy, she cried tears of joy.

The little girl decided to keep the image forever and make it the pet she had always wanted. And that is how the little girl got her very own pet.

Once upon a time there was a nice dog called Stan. He had a very nice owner who always looked after him.

One day, the owner took Stan for a walk in the park. He wanted to make sure Stan was fit and healthy, so he said "Stan, let's stretch your legs." Stan was very excited and stretched his legs as far as he could go.

Stan enjoyed the walk, running and stretching his legs until it was time to go home. The nice owner said "Well done Stan. You have stretched your legs really well." Stan was very happy and wagged his tail with joy.

The next day, the owner took Stan back to the park and Stan was ready to stretch his legs again. He ran and ran, stretching his legs and having lots of fun.

The owner was very proud of Stan and said "Good boy. You have been stretching your legs nicely." Stan was so proud and happy to hear his owner's kind words, and he knew that he had another great day in the park.

Sara and Ben were playing in the park. They saw a big slide and ran to it. Sara climbed up the ladder and sat on the slide. Ben followed her and sat behind her.

"Ready, Sara?" Ben asked.

"Yes, Ben!" Sara said.

Ben pushed Sara and they slid down together. They went very fast and felt the wind in their hair. They laughed and screamed.

At the bottom of the slide, they saw a feather on the ground. It was white and soft. Sara picked it up and tickled Ben's nose with it.

"Stop, Sara, stop!" Ben said. "That tickles!"

Sara giggled and tickled him more. Ben tried to grab the feather, but Sara was too quick. She ran away and Ben chased her.

They ran around the park, holding the feather. They felt happy and dizzy. They did not see the big tree in front of them. They bumped into it and fell down.

"Ouch!" Sara said.

"Ouch!" Ben said.

They rubbed their heads and looked at each other. They still had the feather in their hands. They smiled and hugged.

"Are you okay, Sara?" Ben asked.

"Are you okay, Ben?" Sara asked.

They nodded and kissed each other's cheeks. They got up and ran to the slide again. They wanted to play more. They loved the slide and the feather and each other.

Once there was a small bird called Copper. Copper was thick and strong and could fly very fast. One day, Copper was flying very high and not paying attention and flew into a tree.

Copper couldn't fly away and was very scared. Suddenly she heard a voice, it was an old bird who lived in the tree. He asked, "Why are you afraid little bird?"

"I flew too close and now I can't move," Copper said, tears filling her eyes. The old bird said, "It looks like you were going too fast, maybe you should pause more often".

Copper thanked the old bird and understood his lesson. She paused to fly beside the tree, testing her wings before going higher. She was grateful for the wise words the old bird had given her.

The moral of the story is that it’s important to take time to think before making decisions. Taking a pause can help us see things more clearly and can even save us from danger.

Lily likes to see the birds on the porch. She has a cute bird feeder that she fills with seeds. She sits on the porch with her mom and watches the birds eat and sing.

One day, she sees a new bird on the porch. It is small and brown and has a red spot on its head. Lily thinks it is very cute. She wants to give it a name. She asks her mom what kind of bird it is.

Her mom says it is a woodpecker. She says woodpeckers like to peck on trees and make holes. She says they also make a loud noise when they peck.

Lily listens and hears the woodpecker peck on the porch railing. It sounds like a drum. Lily likes the sound. She claps her hands and says, "I like the woodpecker. I will call him Woody."

Her mom smiles and says, "That is a good name for him. Maybe he will come back and visit us again." Lily hopes so. She likes to see Woody on the porch. He is her new friend.

Lily and Ben were twins, but they were very different. Lily liked to play with dolls and draw pictures. Ben liked to run and jump and make noise. One day, they went to the park with their mom. Lily found a bench and sat down with her doll. Ben ran to the slide and climbed up and down.

"Ben, come and rest with me," Lily called. "You look tired."

"No, I'm not tired," Ben said. "I want to play more."

He ran to the swings and pushed them hard. Lily shook her head and hugged her doll. She wished Ben would be more like her.

Soon, it was time to go home. Mom gave them each a cup of cocoa. Lily sipped hers slowly and smiled. She liked cocoa. It was warm and sweet. Ben gulped his down and asked for more. He liked cocoa too. It gave him more energy.

"Ben, you should rest now," Mom said. "You had a long day."

"No, I'm not tired," Ben said. "I want to play more."

He ran to his room and took out his cars. He made them zoom and crash on the floor. Lily followed him and watched. She wished Ben would be more quiet.

"Ben, can you play something else?" Lily asked. "Something more calm?"

"No, I like cars," Ben said. "They are fun and fast."

He made more noise with his cars. Lily sighed and left. She went to her room and took out her crayons. She drew a picture of her doll and herself. She liked drawing. It was quiet and pretty.

Lily and Ben were twins, but they were very different. They liked different things and played different ways. But they still loved each other. And sometimes, they would rest and share their cocoa.

Once upon a time, there were two friends who liked to sit and talk.

One day, they went to the cafe and saw a big, steaming cup of coffee. It looked yummy, but it had a smelly smell.

One friend asked, "Do you want to try it?"

The other friend said, "No, it smells too smelly. I don't want to drink it."

So, the two friends just sat and talked. They laughed, smiled, and had a good time.

Eventually, they decided it was time to go. They said goodbye and left the cafe.

The two friends never tried the smelly coffee, but they had a lot of fun just sitting and talking.

Once upon a time there was a baby shark. She wanted to be brave, and go on an adventure. So she swam out of the safety of the sea, and she carried with her a brand new net she had made.

As she went, she soon found herself in the middle of a big open ocean. All around her were other clever fishes, with special powers. The baby shark felt a little scared, lost in the middle of the sea, until she bumped into a giant whale!

“Hello! Where are you going?” said the whale.

The baby shark took a deep breath, and replied “I am going on an adventure. I am going to catch some crazy fish in this net I made. Just wait and see!”

The whale laughed, and said “Well make sure you’re careful, and have lots of fun. Make sure you carry your net so you don’t lose it!”

So the baby shark carried her net, and swam further out into the deep ocean. Sure enough, she found some crazy fish, and she caught them gleefully in her net. And so the baby shark had a great adventure, and a really fun day in the big blue sea!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the rain with her yellow raincoat and boots. One day, she was playing outside when she saw a little bird that was wet and cold.

"Hi little birdie, are you okay?" asked Lily.

"No, I'm not okay. I'm cold and wet," replied the birdie.

"I can help you! Let me take you inside my house so you can get warm and dry," said Lily.

Lily took the birdie inside and gave it a towel to dry off. She also gave it some seeds to eat. The birdie felt much better and thanked Lily for being so kind.

From that day on, the birdie would visit Lily every day and they became famous friends in the neighborhood. Lily learned that it's important to help others and be kind, and in return, she received a new friend.

The little girl felt gloomy on a cold, grey morning. But then she spun around, faster and faster and the wind blew against her face. Her spirits lifted, and she felt happy. Suddenly, she remembered that her mum did yoga each morning. Suddenly, if felt like a great idea. So she spun over to the living room and watched as her mum did some amazing poses. She felt the joy and energy light up her body. Then she spun back to her room and carried on with her day, feeling happy and energized.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to eat peanuts. One day, Lily's mom gave her a big bag of peanuts. Lily was so happy and said, "I enjoy eating peanuts!"

As Lily was eating her peanuts, a little boy named Timmy came by. Timmy had never seen peanuts before and he asked, "What are those?" Lily replied, "These are peanuts. They are interesting because they grow underground!"

Timmy wanted to try a peanut, but he was allergic to them. Lily remembered that her friend Sarah was also allergic to peanuts. She learned from her mom that some people can't eat peanuts because it makes them sick.

Lily decided to share her peanuts with her friends who could eat them. She said, "I have lots of peanuts, but some of my friends can't eat them. So, I will share with my friends who can enjoy them too!"

The moral of the story is that it's important to share with others and be considerate of their needs.

Fred was ready for his big day. He was finally going to the stadium. He had been waiting for so long to be able to gaze upon the stadium and now the time had come. He was so excited as he rushed to the gates ready to get a glimpse of what was inside.

But when Fred got there he saw that the stadium was closed. He quickly realized that the stadium wasn't ready yet. Fred was so disappointed. He had been dreaming of this day and now he was not able to see it. His excitement had been replaced with frustration.

Fred knew he would have to come back again when the stadium was ready. He looked up to the sky and sighed. He turned around and slowly walked away, but he was determined to come back and gaze upon the stadium when it was open. He knew it was only a matter of time.

Once upon a time, there was a young boy named Timmy. Timmy was very lonely because he didn't have any friends to play with. One day, Timmy's mom asked him to help organize his toys.

Timmy replied, "Sure mom, I can help. Organize means to put things in their right places, right?"

"Yes, Timmy, that's right," his mom said with a smile.

As Timmy started organizing his toys, he found a small teddy bear that he had forgotten about. "Look, mom! I found my teddy bear. He was all alone under my bed. Now he won't be lonely anymore," Timmy said happily.

"Good job, Timmy. You not only organized your toys but also made your teddy bear happy," his mom said proudly.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to ride the bus with her mom to go to the park. One day, Lily's mom said, "Lily, can you count how many people are on the bus?" Lily counted all the people and said, "There are ten people on the bus."

The next day, Lily's mom said, "Lily, can you count how many red cars we see on the way to the park?" Lily counted all the red cars and said, "We saw three red cars on the way to the park."

One day, Lily's mom said, "Lily, you are a big girl now. You can ride the bus by yourself to go to the park." Lily felt scared at first, but then she felt proud because she was independent. She counted all the people on the bus, just like her mom had taught her. When she got off the bus, she saw her mom waiting for her at the park. Lily felt happy because she had learned how to be independent and count all by herself.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys all day long. One day, her mom gave her a yummy snack to eat. Lily was so happy and ate it all up.

After she finished her snack, she felt playful and wanted to run around. But her mom told her to clean up her toys first. Lily didn't want to clean up, so she started to cry.

Her mom told her that it's important to clean up after playing, so that she can find her toys easily next time she wants to play. Lily understood and stood up to clean up her toys. From that day on, Lily always cleaned up after playing and never had trouble finding her toys.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved to play with her toys. One day, her favorite toy, a little orange car, broke. Lily was very sad and didn't know what to do.

Her mom saw how sad she was and asked her what was wrong. Lily told her that her car was broken and she didn't know how to fix it. Her mom said, "Don't worry, we can repair it together."

Lily was so happy and helped her mom fix the car. After they were done, her mom gave her a medal for being such a good helper. Lily was so proud of herself and her shiny new medal.

She showed it to her dad and said, "Look! Mom and I repair my car and now I have a medal!" Her dad was so impressed and gave her a big hug. Lily was so happy that her car was fixed and that she got a medal for helping.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who loved cauliflower. Whenever she went to the grocery store, she wanted to buy the biggest cauliflower she could find.

One time, the girl found an enormous cauliflower and she was so excited. She showed it to her friend, who seemed envious. But the girl didn't care, she wanted this cauliflower more than anything.

So, the girl took the cauliflower home and ate it with her family. It was bigger than she had imagined and they all had so much cauliflower that night.

When the girl and her friend met up the next day, the girl showed the friend the photos of the big cauliflower she'd eaten. The friend was still envious, but the little girl didn't mind. She was just so proud and excited that she had found such a big cauliflower.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily lived with her family in a big house. Lily loved her family very much. She liked to play with them and talk to them.

One day, Lily's family went out to play without her. Lily felt lonely and sad. She wanted to play with them too. But they didn't take her with them.

Lily went to her mommy and said, "Mommy, I feel lonely. I want to play with my family." Her mommy said, "Don't worry, Lily. They didn't mean to ignore you. They just forgot. Let's call them and ask them to come back home and play with us." And so they did. Lily was happy again, and her family played with her all day long.

Once there was a little girl named Sarah. She was so excited one day to go to the playground. She saw a huge slide and ran right over to it. She was so happy when she saw it!

When she got to the top of the slide, Sarah could barely hang on. She was so excited to slide down. She wiggled until she was ready, then let go and went sliding down. She laughed and laughed as she flew down the slide.

When she got to the bottom, she didn't want to stop. She ran around the whole play area, looking for something else to hang on. She saw a huge swing and ran straight over to it.

She pulled herself up, and she began to swing back and forth. The wind blew through her hair and she smiled and laughed as she went higher and higher. Sarah had so much fun at the park!

Once upon a time, there was a dog with an ugly collar. The collar was too big for the dog and it was not pretty. One day, the dog's friend saw the collar and urged the dog to take it off. The dog did not like the collar either, so he took it off and threw it away. The dog was happy without the ugly collar. The end.

One day, a boy named Tom found a basketball. He wanted to play with it. Tom saw his friends playing in the park. He ran to them with the basketball.

Tom tried to play with his friends, but he did not know how. He threw the ball and it hit a girl. The girl was angry. Tom was embarrass.

Tom's friends did not want to play with him. They took the basketball and left him alone. Tom was sad and went home.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play in his garden. One day, Timmy's mom gave him a spade to dig in the dirt. Timmy was so happy and started to dig.

As he dug, he found a little seed. Timmy planted the seed and watered it every day. Slowly, the seed started to grow into a big tree. Timmy loved to play under the tree because it was so peaceful.

One day, Timmy's little sister came to play with him. They had so much fun playing together. Timmy showed his sister the big tree and they both sat under it. Suddenly, the wind started to blow and the leaves on the tree started to turn. Timmy and his sister laughed and played in the falling leaves. They were so happy to be together and have fun.

"Mum! I want to finish!" yelled Sam. His mum smiled and handed him a roll of tape. Sam carefully tore off a piece and stuck it onto the corner of the big box. He beamed with satisfaction.

"Good job, Sam. Your box is almost finished," said his mum.

Sam grabbed the tape again, and this time, he taped the lid of the box closed.

"I finished!" Sam shouted in delight.

His mum patted him on the head. "See, you can do anything when you try, Sam. That was a normal tape job," she said with a smile.

Sam looked at his finished box and smiled. He was proud of what he had done.

Once upon a time, there was a little bunny named Benny. Benny was very lonely because he didn't have any friends to play with. One day, Benny found an old frame in the woods. He thought it was pretty and decided to take it home.

When Benny got home, he showed the frame to his mom. She thought it was nice too, and they decided to test it out by putting a picture inside. They found a picture of Benny's family and put it in the frame.

Benny was so happy with his new frame and picture. He didn't feel as lonely anymore because he had his family with him all the time. From then on, Benny always looked for things to put in his frame and he knew that he would never be lonely again.

Once there was a little girl named Nancy. Nancy had a dream. She wanted to have a blue battery to make her day perfect.

She asked her mom for the blue battery that she wanted and said, "Mom, can I please have a blue battery?" Her mom smiled and said, "I'm sorry, sweetie. We don't have a blue battery."

Nancy was very disappointed but then she had an idea. She asked her mom, "Can I go outside and try to find a blue battery?"

Her mom said, "Of course, you can go outside and have a look. You never know what you might find!"

So Nancy went outside to look. She looked near the trees and under the rocks. She looked in the bushes and even in the sky. All of a sudden, she saw something shining: a blue battery! Nancy was so happy, she ran home and gave it to her mom.

Mom was so proud of Nancy for finding the battery and said, "You can always make your dreams come true if you work hard enough!"

Once upon a time, there was a purple peanut. It was so pretty and everyone wanted to have it. One day, a couple of kids saw the purple peanut and decided to take it. They ran away with it and the peanut disappeared. No one knew where it went. Everyone looked everywhere but couldn't find it. They were sad and wondered what happened.

Suddenly a big bird flew over the sky and it had something purple in its beak. It was the purple peanut! The kids were so excited and ran to the bird. But the bird flew away with the peanut in its beak and it disappeared. No one saw it again!

The kids never found the purple peanut again. But they always remembered it and talked about the wonderful thing that had disappeared.

Jill was a 3 year old girl who loved playing with her friends. Today, she was part of a team. She was so excited! Every member of the team was wearing a noisy shirt and a funny hat. Jill couldn't wait to get started.

Suddenly, Jill started to frown. She noticed that one of her teammates was not wearing a noisy shirt or funny hat like the others. She was worried that the team would not look the same when they played together.

Then, one of her teammates noticed the problem and shouted out a big idea. Everyone started to cheer.Everyone went home and the next day, all of the members of the team had matching, noisy shirts and funny hats. Jill was very happy. She smiled from ear to ear and was so excited to be part of the team.

Ben was sad. He wanted to go to the park with Mom and Dad, but they said no. They said it was too cold and wet outside. Ben did not like cold and wet. He liked sun and fun.

Ben looked out the window. He saw a little bug on the glass. It was an inch. It had six legs and a long body. It was brown and black. Ben liked inch. He wanted to play with it.

Ben opened the window. He put his hand out. He said, "Hello, inch. Do you want to be my friend?" The inch did not say anything. It just walked on the glass. Ben tried to touch it, but it was too fast. It walked away from Ben's hand.

Ben was sad again. He said, "Please, inch. Don't go. Stay with me. We can have fun." The inch did not listen. It walked to the edge of the window. It found a small hole. It crawled through the hole. It was gone.

Ben cried. He said, "Bye, inch. I miss you. Come back soon." He closed the window. He went to his bed. He hugged his teddy bear. He hoped the inch would come back. He hoped the sun would come out. He hoped he could go to the park. He hoped he would be happy.

John and his mom were in the garden. The sun was high in the sky, it was almost noon. John looked up and grinned. His mom smiled and said: "Let's explore this garden, what do you say?".

John nodded eagerly and they both walked around the garden. They saw many trees and flowers and butterflies. They picked some apples from a tree and shared it.

John smiled and said: "I'm grateful for this garden, it's so nice". His mom nodded in agreement and said: "Yes, the garden is lovely. Let's come back here when the sun sets".

They said goodbye to the garden and walked home. When they arrived, John was so happy. He was grateful for his mom who let him explore the garden. His mom smiled and gave him a hug.

Once upon a time there was a little puppy. His name was Chris. One day Chris was playing in the garden when he saw something on the ground. It was a collar! It was a very pretty collar with sparkles on it.

Chris was happy and he put the collar around his neck. He rubbed the sparkles to make them shine. But then he felt something strange - he felt sad. He didn't know why but there it was.

Chris looked around but there was no one there. He lay down in the sunshine and rubbed his collar. He didn't know why he was so sad, but he wanted to make the sadness go away. He kept rubbing his collar until he felt better.

The sun went down, and Chris went to bed. He was a little bit happier, but he still wasn't sure why he was so sad. He hugged his collar and went to sleep.

The next morning he was feeling much better. He was happy and excited to wear his new collar. He rubs it and smiles - the sparkles still make him happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to hug her mommy and daddy. One day, Lily's heart felt sad because her best friend moved away. She missed her friend so much that her heart felt bitter.

Lily's mommy saw that her little girl was sad and gave her a big hug. She told Lily that it's okay to feel sad sometimes, but that her heart will feel better soon. Lily hugged her mommy back and felt a little better.

Later that day, Lily's daddy came home from work and gave her a big hug too. He told her that he loved her and that she always had him and mommy to hug whenever she needed it. Lily hugged her daddy back and felt happy again. From that day on, Lily knew that whenever her heart felt bitter, she could always hug her mommy and daddy to make it feel better.

Once upon a time, there was a honest boy. His name was Jake. Every morning he loved to bathe in the river. He had a boat to help him float around.

One morning, Jake was out on his boat, but he couldn't find any fish to catch! He got so frustrated that he wanted to run away.

Suddenly, Jake heard a voice. It was his friend Abigail. "What are you doing out here, Jake?" she asked.

Jake sighed. "It's no use. I can't even catch one fish!"

"Well don't give up," Abigail said. "Why don't you try again in the evening?"

So that night, Jake went back to the river. He was honest and tried his best. To his surprise, he caught five fish! He was so happy and he thanked Abigail for helping him.

From that day on, Jake and Abigail would go out every day on Jake's boat to bathe and fish together. They had lots of fun and created wonderful memories.

One day, there was a lonely sunflower who was feeling very sad. He was alone in the middle of a field with no one to talk to. Suddenly, he heard a voice calling out. He looked up and saw a kind gentleman who was smiling at him. The gentleman said he would rescue the poor sunflower and take him home.

The sunflower was happy and followed the man back to his house. There he found a whole garden full of colourful flowers. His new friends were excited to meet him and welcomed the sunflower with open arms.

The sunflower was so happy that he could join his new friends in the garden. He was no longer lonely and had someone to play with. From that day on, the sunflower never felt lonely or sad again. He was very grateful to the kind gentleman who rescued him from the field.

Once upon a time, there was a frog named Freddy. Freddy lived in a pond with his friends. The pond was big and had lots of lily pads. Freddy was famous in the pond because he could jump really high.

One day, Freddy's friend asked him a question. "Freddy, how do you jump so high?" his friend asked. Freddy replied, "I practice every day!" His friend was impressed and wanted to be famous like Freddy.

So, his friend started practicing every day too. Soon, he could jump high just like Freddy. Now, they were both famous in the pond for their jumping skills. And they lived happily ever after, jumping and playing with their friends.

Once upon a time there was a little girl. She was young and strong and loved to use her imagination. One day she was playing in her room when she came across a black box. It was a mysterious box and she was so curious to know what was inside, so she opened the box. Inside she found a shiny silver star. She was so surprised and excited to find such an incredible thing!

She smiled and decided to take the star outside. On her way outside she met her best friend. Her friend saw the star and suggested that they take it to the park and throw it up in the sky. She agreed and they soon found themselves in the park throwing the star up in the air. As the star was up in the night sky, the two friends looked up in awe.

They had never seen anything so magical! Suddenly, the little girl had an idea. She suggested that they keep the star in her black box for safe keeping and bring it out for special occasions. Her friend thought this was a wonderful idea and soon the star was placed safely inside the black box and the two friends walked away with a smile.

Tom and Mia were best friends. They liked to play in the park with their toys. One day, they found a big box under a tree. It was heavy and had a lock on it.

"Maybe there is something good inside," Tom said. "Let's lift it and take it home."

Mia nodded. "But we have to make a promise. We will only open it together, okay?"

Tom agreed. They made a pinky promise and lifted the box. It was hard, but they carried it all the way to Tom's house.

They put the box in Tom's room and waited for his mom to go out. Then they ran to the box and tried to open it. But the lock was too strong. They looked for something to break it.

Tom saw a hammer in his dad's toolbox. He grabbed it and ran back to the box. He hit the lock with the hammer. It made a loud noise.

"Be careful, Tom," Mia said. "You might break something inside."

Tom did not listen. He hit the lock again and again. Finally, it broke. He opened the box and looked inside.

He screamed. Mia screamed too. Inside the box, there was a rare snake. It was big and angry. It jumped out of the box and bit Tom on his arm. Tom felt a sharp pain and fell to the floor. Mia ran to him and cried.

The snake slithered out of the window and disappeared. Tom's mom came back and saw what happened. She called an ambulance and tried to help Tom. But it was too late. The snake was poisonous and Tom did not survive. Mia lost her best friend because of a bad promise and a bad box. She wished they never lifted it.

Jill and Jack were the best of friends, always ready to explore the world together. They loved to run about and skip with joy. On one bright day, the two friends decided to embroider a beautiful dress for Jill. They diligently placed each colourful stitch together with care, until at last the dress was complete.

Jack thought the dress was perfect, but Jill suddenly noticed that one of the stitches was missing. She scrunched up her face and declared that the dress was ruined.

Jack thought quickly and told Jill to come outside with him. He picked a bright yellow flower and told her to stitch it onto her dress. Jill laughed and was delighted. She thanked Jack and sang a happy song, as the two friends skipped around the yard.

Mary had a secret. She wanted to peek, but she was scared. Everyday she saw the lawyer who lived next door. He was a pale man with a serious look on his face. One day, when Mary walked past his window, she saw him looking at something very closely. He asked "What do you see?"

Mary felt a bit scared, but the lawyer smiled and said "It's alright. I just want to know what you see." Mary stepped closer and saw that the lawyer had a treasure map! She whispered "I see a map!"

The lawyer smiled and said "Yes, it is a map. I need help finding the treasure. Will you help me find it?" Mary was so excited, she couldn't speak. The lawyer put the map in Mary's pocket and said "Come back tomorrow and we can go on our adventure!"

The next day, Mary returned and the lawyer said "Let's go. Follow my lead." They went on a long journey until they finally arrived at a beach. The lawyer smiled and said "Here we are, ready to find the treasure!"

Mary was so excited - she couldn’t believe they had made it to the beach. What kind of treasure were they going to find? Would they uncover something amazing? The beach looked beautiful and peaceful, and they couldn’t wait to begin their search!

Once upon a time there was a girl who loved to skip. She could skip so high that she could jump over the family's house. One day she wanted to do something different. She said, "I want to skip and do something cool".

So she went outside and saw a big cube. It was yellow and green and looked really fun. She said, "I'm gonna skip over this cube".

So she skipped and skipped until she got all the way over the cube. She felt so good that she did it and she said, "I can do anything I want".

From then on she decided to skip every day. She was so happy and had so much fun. She smiled and said, "I love to skip, it makes me feel so good".
