Lily and Ben were playing with their toys in the living room. Lily had a doll with long hair and a dress. Ben had a car with wheels and a horn. They liked to share their toys and make stories with them.

"Look, Ben, I made a hat for my doll with this paper and this pin," Lily said, showing him her craft. "Do you like it?"

"Yes, Lily, it is very beautiful," Ben said, admiring the hat. "But be careful with the pin. It can hurt you if you touch it."

"I know, Ben, I am careful," Lily said. "Do you want to make a hat for your car too? I have more paper and pins."

"Thank you, Lily, but no," Ben said. "I like my car as it is. It is fast and loud. But I recommend you to make more hats for your doll. You are very good at it."

Lily smiled and hugged Ben. "You are very nice, Ben. You are my best friend."

They continued to play with their toys and have fun. They were happy and loved each other.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved to eat treats. One day, she went to the store with her mom and saw a man selling candy. She asked her mom if she could buy one, but her mom said no because she had already eaten too many treats that day.

Lily was sad, but then she saw a dirty dog walking by. She felt bad for the dog and asked her mom if they could give him a treat. Her mom said yes, so Lily gave the dog a yummy treat.

The man selling candy saw what Lily did and said, "You are a kind girl. I will give you a treat for free." Lily was so happy and thanked the man. From that day on, Lily always remembered to be kind to animals and people, and sometimes she even got free treats!

One day, 2 friends were playing near a line. The line was very long and tough. The friends were smiling and having fun. Suddenly, they saw a large gust of wind. The gust of wind was so strong that it separated the line! The friends had never seen anything like it before.

The friends looked around trying to figure out what to do. Then, they realized that they needed to put the line back together. They worked together and pulled really hard. It took them a long time, but eventually they got the line back to the way it was before.

The friends smiled at each other and hugged. They were so proud of themselves. They had worked together and shown that even tough lines can be separated and put back together.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved the holiday because he got to eat lots of candy. He had a hard time waiting for the holiday to come.

Finally, the holiday came and Timmy got lots of candy. He was so happy that he ate all the candy in one day. The next day, Timmy got a tummy ache. He felt very sick and his tummy hurt so much.

Timmy's mom gave him some medicine and put him to bed. But, while Timmy was sleeping, his candy melted in the hot sun. When he woke up, all his candy was gone. Timmy felt sad and learned that eating too much candy can make you sick and cause bad things to happen.

Once upon a time there was an ancient tree. Every day it would grow bigger and bigger. One day, the tree took an special trip. It was so excited!

It flew high in to the sky and looked out over the world below. The tree felt so small compared to everything else around it. Suddenly, the tree grew and grew until it was the tallest tree in the whole world!

The tree looked down and it could see the whole world. It could see all the beautiful places below it. Everywhere the tree looked it could see wonderful things.

The tree was so happy that it took a trip every day. It saw so many wonderful things every day and grew taller and taller. And so, the tree stayed the tallest tree in the world for many years.

Once upon a time there was a mighty hat. It was so grand and shiny, the colour of the sun. Everyone who saw the hat wanted to wear it.

One day a little boy named Jack saw the hat and decided he wanted it for himself. He asked his parents if he could have it. His dad said "No, this is too mighty for you!"

Jack was angry. He grabbed the hat and ran away with it. He ran and ran until he found a nice spot outside in the woods. He put the hat on and looked so happy.

The sun shone brightly and the air felt warm. But unfortunately, the sun was too strong. Before Jack knew what was happening, the hat had begun to burn!

Jack screamed to his parents, "Help me! The hat is burning!" But it was too late. The hat was burned to ashes and all that was left was a smokey smell.

Jack was very sad. He had lost his mighty hat. He never would get it back.

Once upon a time, there was a king. The king was fair and kind. He loved to play with his friends in the big blue sea.

One day, the king saw a big rock far away in the sea. He thought it would be fun to dive off the rock. He told his friends, "I want to dive off the big rock!" His friends were scared, but the king was brave.

The king swam to the big rock with his friends. He climbed up and stood on the top. He looked down at the water and took a deep breath. Then, the king jumped and dove into the sea. His friends clapped and cheered. The king was happy and proud. From that day on, the king and his friends loved to dive off the big rock together.

Once upon a time there was a big sister. She was enormous! One day she decided to take a nap. She laid down in her cozy bed and closed her eyes. She snuggled under the soft blanket and went to sleep.

Her little sister watched in amazement. She climbed up the enormous bed and laid down beside her sister. She curled up in the warm blanket and closed her eyes. Together they took a long nap.

When they awoke they were refreshed and happy. The sisters hugged and laughed. They thanked each other for taking such a special nap together.

The end.

Once upon a time, there was an old tree. The old tree was very compassionate. It loved to help others. One day, a little bird came to the old tree. The little bird was sad.

"Old tree, I can't balance on my nest," said the little bird. "Can you help me?"

The old tree wanted to help the little bird. So, the old tree thought of a plan. The old tree would teach the little bird to balance. But, there was a problem. The wind was very strong. The wind made it hard for the little bird to balance.

The old tree and the little bird tried hard. They practiced balancing together. The wind was still strong, but the little bird was getting better. The old tree was happy to see the little bird learn to balance.

In the end, the little bird could balance on its nest. The old tree was proud of the little bird. The little bird thanked the old tree for its help. The old tree and the little bird became good friends. They lived happily ever after.

Ben and Mia are playing with their toys in the living room. Ben has a big truck and Mia has a doll. They are having fun and making noises.

Then, a new boy comes in. His name is Sam and he is their mom's friend's son. He looks at Ben and Mia and their toys. He does not say hello. He does not smile. He just stares. He stares at Ben's truck. He stares at Mia's doll. He stares and stares.

Ben and Mia do not like Sam. They think he is rude. They want him to go away. They try to ignore him and keep playing. But Sam does not stop staring. He walks closer and closer. He reaches out his hand and grabs Mia's doll. He pulls it away from her.

"Hey!" Mia shouts. "That is my doll! Give it back!"

Sam does not listen. He holds the doll and laughs. He says, "This is a silly thing. It is not a real baby. It is just a toy. I want it. It is mine now."

Mia is very angry and sad. She tries to get her doll back. She pushes Sam and cries. Ben is angry too. He loves his sister and he does not like Sam. He drops his truck and runs to help Mia. He says, "No, it is not yours. It is Mia's. You are a bad boy. You are not nice. You are not our friend. Give the doll back or we will tell mom."

Sam does not care. He thinks he is stronger and smarter than Ben and Mia. He says, "No, I will not. You can't make me. You are both stupid and boring. I will keep the doll and I will take your truck too."

He tries to grab Ben's truck, but Ben is faster. He picks up his truck and hits Sam on the head. Sam drops the doll and screams. He holds his head and cries. He says, "Ow, ow, ow! That hurts! You are mean! You are mean!"

Mom hears the noise and comes in. She sees Sam crying and Ben and Mia holding their toys. She asks, "What is going on here? What happened?"

Ben and Mia tell mom what Sam did. They say, "He was rude. He stared at our toys. He took Mia's doll. He said bad things. He did not share. He did not play nice. We did not like him."

Mom is shocked and angry. She says, "That is not okay. That is not how we treat our guests and our toys. Sam, you need to apologize to Ben and Mia. You need to give back the doll. You need to say sorry."

Sam does not want to apologize. He does not think he did anything wrong. He says, "No, I don't. They started it. They hit me. They are mean. I don't like them."

Mom does not accept Sam's answer. She says, "That is not true. You started it. You were rude and selfish. You need to learn how to be polite and kind. If you don't apologize, you will have to go home. You will not be welcome here anymore."

Sam does not want to go home. He does not want to lose his mom's friend. He does not want to be alone. He realizes he made a mistake. He says, "Okay, okay. I'm sorry. I'm sorry, Ben. I'm sorry, Mia. I was wrong. I should not have taken your doll. I should not have said those things. I should have asked to play with you. Can we be friends?"

Ben and Mia are still upset, but they are also forgiving. They say, "Okay, we accept your apology. We can be friends. But you have to be nice. You have to share. You have to play fair. Do you promise?"

Sam promises. He gives back the doll to Mia. He says, "Here, this is your doll. She is pretty. Can I hold her for a minute?"

Mia says, "Yes, you can. But be gentle. She is my baby. Can I see your truck for a minute?"

Ben says, "Yes, you can. But be careful. It is my truck. It is fast and strong. Can I show you how it works?"

Sam says, "Yes, please. That sounds fun. Can we play together?"

Ben and Mia say, "Yes, we can. Let's play together."

Mom smiles and says, "That's better. That's how we make friends. That's how we have fun. I'm proud of you, Ben and Mia. And I'm glad you said sorry, Sam. Now, why don't you all play nicely and share your toys?"

Once upon a time, there was a little bear who lived in a big forest. He loved to explore, and one day he saw something he had never seen before – an object. It was shiny and round, and very strange. The little bear wanted to take the object, but he was scared. He didn't know what would happen if he touched it.

The little bear stood still and thought. He thought and he thought and he thought some more. Finally, he plucked up the courage to dare himself to pick up the object. He was very scared, but very brave. He reached out his paw and cautiously grabbed the object.

Nothing happened! He inspected the object and saw that it was nothing to be scared of. It was just a shiny round object. He was so pleased he had been brave enough to dare himself to pick it up. It was his special treasure! He took the object with him back to the forest and he never was so scared again.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Sarah. She liked to try new things and always looked forward to dessert. One day Sarah saw a yummy dessert on the table. She was excited to have it but her parents said she was too young to accept it. Sarah was sad and she started crying. She really wanted the yummy dessert but her parents wouldn't accept it. So Sarah had to go without any dessert. She felt bad and ended up going to bed without having any yummy dessert.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to walk in the forest, where she found many pine trees. She liked the smell of the pine trees and thought they were very pretty. One day, Lily was walking when she discovered a small rabbit. The rabbit was very cute and Lily wanted to keep it as a pet.

Lily took the rabbit home and showed it to her mom. "Mommy, look what I found in the forest!" she said. "It's a bunny!" Her mom looked at the rabbit and said, "Lily, that rabbit belongs in the forest. We have to let it go."

Lily was sad, but she knew her mom was right. So, they took the rabbit back to the forest and let it go. As they were walking back home, Lily saw a pine cone on the ground. She picked it up and took a bite. "Mmm, this pine cone is tasty!" she said.

But little did she know, pine cones are not meant for eating. Lily got very sick and had to go to the hospital. She learned her lesson and promised to never eat anything she found in the forest again. The end.

Sam and Mia are friends. They like to play together. Sometimes they play with toys, sometimes they play with balls, sometimes they run and jump.

One day, they decide to play exercise. They want to be strong and healthy. They find a big rope in the yard. They think it is fun to pull the rope.

Sam says, "I will pull this end, and you pull that end. We will see who is stronger."

Mia says, "OK, let's do it. But be careful, don't pull too hard."

They start to pull the rope. They pull and pull and pull. They feel their arms and legs working. They laugh and smile.

But then, something happens. The rope breaks. It snaps in the middle. Sam and Mia fall down. They are surprised and scared.

They look at the rope. It is old and thin. It is not reliable. It is not good for exercise.

Sam says, "Oh no, the rope is broken. It is not a good rope. It is a bad rope."

Mia says, "Yes, it is a bad rope. But we are OK. We are not hurt. We are still friends."

They hug each other. They are happy. They decide to find another game to play. They look for a reliable toy. They find a ball. They think it is fun to kick the ball. They play exercise with the ball. They are strong and healthy.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily loved to play with clay and create things with her hands. She would spend hours molding and shaping the clay into different shapes and objects.

One day, Lily decided to make a vase. She worked hard on it, making sure it was just the right size and shape. When she was finished, she put it in the oven to bake.

After it was done, Lily took the vase out of the oven and admired her creation. But as she looked at it, she noticed that it was very dark inside. She couldn't see the bottom of the vase at all.

Lily decided to put some flowers in the vase to brighten it up. But when she did, she realized that the dark inside of the vase made the flowers look even more beautiful. From that day on, Lily loved to create vases with dark insides, because they made everything inside them look even more special.

Once upon a time, there was a little mouse named Timmy. Timmy loved to explore the world outside his cozy home. One day, he met a big rat named Remy. Remy was very cool and had lots of stories to tell. Remy mentioned that he knew of a secret place where they could find lots of yummy cheese.

Timmy was very excited and followed Remy to the secret place. But when they got there, Timmy realized it was a trap! They were caught by a mean cat who wanted to eat them for dinner. Timmy was very scared and tried to run away, but he couldn't escape the trap.

In the end, the cat caught both Timmy and Remy and they were never seen again. The moral of the story is to be careful of strangers and always be aware of traps.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to watch the birds flying in the sky. One day, while she was looking up, she saw a big, fluffy cloud that looked like a bunny. Lily was very curious and wondered how the cloud could look like a bunny.

The next day, Lily went to the park to play. She saw a group of kids playing a game. One of the kids was being mean to the others and judging them for not playing well. Lily didn't like that and decided to play with the other kids. They had a lot of fun together.

As Lily was leaving the park, she saw the same big, fluffy cloud that looked like a bunny. She remembered how curious she was about it and realized that sometimes things can be different than they seem. Just like the cloud that looked like a bunny, people can also be different than they seem. She felt happy that she made new friends at the park and didn't judge them for not playing well.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy who loved to play with his toys. One day, he found a big cabinet in his house. He opened it and saw a lot of colorful jars inside. Timmy wanted to touch them, but his mom told him to be careful.

Timmy tried to be careful, but he accidentally knocked over one of the jars. It made a loud sound and his mom came running. She was very angry and told Timmy to go to his room. Timmy felt sad and wished he had been more careful.

The lesson Timmy learned was to always listen to his mom and be careful. He promised to be more careful in the future. From that day on, Timmy would clap his hands whenever he remembered to be careful.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, Lily and her mom went to the park. They saw a big, amazing tree. Lily said, "Mom, look at the tree! It's so big and pretty!" Her mom said, "Yes, it is amazing. Let's go closer and take a better look."

As they walked closer to the tree, they saw a little bird sitting on a branch. Lily said, "Mom, look at the bird! It's so cute!" But then, a big dog came running towards the tree. The little bird got scared and flew away. Lily said, "Mom, the bird is gone! I wanted to see it more." Her mom said, "I'm sorry, Lily. Sometimes things don't go the way we want them to."

Lily looked sad, but then her mom said, "But we can still enjoy the sight of this amazing tree. Let's sit down and gaze at it for a while." So, they sat down on a bench and looked at the tree. Lily said, "Mom, thank you for bringing me here. This is a nice sight." Her mom smiled and said, "You're welcome, Lily. I love spending time with you."

Once upon a time, there lived a skeleton. He wanted to stay in one place. He looked around, but could not find anywhere that would be good to stay.

He looked up in the sky and saw a big castle with pointy towers. "That would be a good place to stay!" The skeleton thought. He hopped up the tower and when he got to the top of the castle, he saw the most beautiful view.

He decided to stay at the castle forever. Every day the skeleton watched over the castle and saw the sun, the clouds and the stars. He had a good time there.

The skeleton lived at the castle for many years, and the people around him were nice to him. He was happy to stay at the castle forever.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved going to the festival every year. This year, she saw a man selling a big, red apple. She wanted it so badly, but her mom said no. Lily felt sad and foolish for wanting something so much.

As she walked around the festival, she saw a group of kids playing a game. They were taking turns spinning a wheel and doing silly things like hopping on one foot or singing a song. Lily joined in and had so much fun.

When she got home, she told her mom about the game and how much fun she had. Her mom smiled and said, "See, Lily, sometimes the things we think we want aren't really important. It's the fun we have with others that matters." Lily realized her mom was right and felt happy. From that day on, she knew that having fun with her friends was more important than any toy or treat that might rot away.

Molly was very excited, as she was ready to explore the maze. She was with her parents, holding their hands and wondering what secrets the maze held. Molly's parents had been talking about mazes for days and Molly was eager to see one in real life.

Molly went further and further into the maze, taking each turn and discovering more and more twists and turns. Each corner was an adventure. Eventually, after a few turns, Molly became tired and a bit scared - she had been in the maze for what seemed like forever.

Molly's dad saw the tired look on her face and said, "Don't worry Molly, we'll surrender and go home."

Molly was relieved. She grabbed her parent's hands and they left the maze. Molly felt sure that one day she'd be brave enough to explore a maze again.

As they left, Molly took one last look back. She felt excited to explore the maze one day and find out where each turn would lead her.

Tom and Sue are twins. They share a room and a crib. They like to play with their toys and books. But when it is night, they have to go to sleep.

One night, Tom does not want to sleep. He wants to stay up and read his book. He says to Sue, "Sue, let us sack the crib. We can make a tent with the blanket. Then we can read under the light."

Sue thinks this is a fun idea. She says, "OK, Tom, let us sack the crib. But we have to be quiet. Mom and Dad will be mad if they hear us."

They sack the crib. They pull the blanket over the bars. They crawl under the blanket. They turn on the light. They read their book.

But they do not hear Mom and Dad coming. Mom and Dad open the door. They see the tent. They see the light. They are not happy.

They say, "Tom and Sue, what are you doing? You should be sleeping. It is late. You have to go to school tomorrow. Sack the crib right now. Turn off the light. Go to sleep."

Tom and Sue are scared. They say, "Sorry, Mom and Dad. We just wanted to read. We will sack the crib. We will turn off the light. We will go to sleep."

They sack the crib. They turn off the light. They go to sleep. They dream of books and tents.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Jenny. She was only three years old and very eager to explore the world. One day while her mom was busy in the kitchen Jenny entered the living room. She was excited to see what was there.

Jenny saw a big shiny floor. She had never seen a floor so big and shiny before. She said "Wow!" and eagerly walked to the center of the room. She closed her eyes and spun around until she felt dizzy.

Suddenly she heard a noise. It was her mom's voice. "Jenny, what are you doing? she asked. Jenny answered, "I'm exploring the floor!" Jenny's mom smiled. She was happy to see her daughter so eager to explore. She said, "Then keep exploring, my little explorer!"

John was eating his yummy lunch when he saw something sparkly on the ground. He picked it up and it was a diamond! He wanted to keep it for himself, but his mother told him to put it back. John didn't want to and he tried to resist.

John's mother said, "We can't keep it, John. We need to put it back".

John refused and began to cry. His mother was starting to become angry.

John kept saying he wanted to keep the diamond, so his mother finally told him he would be in big trouble if he didn't put it back. She told him that if he didn't, he wouldn't get any treats for a month.

John was so sad but he knew he had to listen. He put the diamond back where he found it, and his mother smiled.

But when John went to get his treat, there was nothing. His mother said she was serious and he had to learn to resist.

Once upon a time there was a prince who lived in a big castle. He was so graceful that everyone in the kingdom thought he was the most handsome prince ever! The prince was looking for somebody to love.

One day, a beautiful princess came to the castle. She had a very kind heart and wonderful hair. She wanted Prince to guess what she had brought.

The princess opened her bag and took out a majestic rose. Its petals were so soft, and the scent was so sweet. The prince was amazed. He held the rose and said, "I can't guess what you have brought me. Please tell me!"

The princess smiled, and told the prince, "This flower is a symbol of my love for you. I want you to have it." The prince was so happy. He thanked the princess and promised to love her forever.

They both knew this was meant to be, and from then on their love grew stronger every day. The graceful prince and the kind princess lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a yummy cake. It was so pretty and made of the best ingredients. Everyone wanted to try it, but it was a special cake. It was reserved for special celebrations.

One day, the family was having a big celebration. Everyone was excited. They had the luxury to eat the yummy cake! As they cut into the cake, everyone was delighted to get a piece.

They ate the cake and it was even more delicious than anyone had imagined. The kids were dancing with joy. They were so happy to celebrate with such an amazing cake.

Everyone had fun that day. They laughed until their sides hurt. It was a day of luxury and yummy treats! All because of the special celebration and the yummy cake. The family will remember it forever!

One day, a little girl named Lily went for a walk. She wanted to see something new. She walked and walked until she saw a big tree. Under the tree, she saw a box. The box had a big zero on it. Lily was very curious about what was inside the box.

Lily opened the box and found a small, scary toy. The toy looked like a monster with big eyes and sharp teeth. Lily was scared at first, but then she thought the toy was funny. She decided to take the toy home with her.

When Lily got home, she showed the toy to her mom. Her mom said, "Oh, that's not scary at all! It's just a silly toy!" Lily and her mom laughed together. Lily put the toy in her room and played with it every day. And from that day on, the scary toy with the big zero on its box became Lily's favorite toy.

Once upon a time, there lived a family of three. Mom, Dad and their little three-year-old daughter, Millie.

Millie was a very strong-willed and determined girl who would always insist on getting her own way. One day, Millie and her Dad were playing a game in the garden when Millie became insistent that she wanted to play instead of Dad.

Dad was patient, but he knew he had to explain why it wasn't a good idea to always insist on her own way. He knelt down to talk to her and said, "Millie, if you insist on getting all your own way, it could lead to an argument, like a fight. A fight can be loud and nobody likes that."

Millie nodded her head, understanding what her Dad meant. As time passed, Millie learned to be patient and would talk to her Dad rather than just insist on things. As it was, Mom and Dad were really proud.

The moral of this story is that it's better to talk to people than to just insist on getting your own way. Communication and understanding can go a long way.

Sam and Sue were best friends. One day, they went to play outside. Sam had a pale folder with him that he was excited to show to Sue.

Sue looked at the folder and said, "Oh, it's broken! I'm sorry Sam."

Sam frowned and replied, "I know. I want to repair it but I don't know how to."

Sue thought for a moment and said, "Let's go ask Mr. Michael. He knows how to fix everything."

So, Sam and Sue went to Mr. Michael's house. He welcomed them and took a look at the folder. He told them that he could repair it and asked them to wait in the garden while he was doing his work.

After sometime, Mr. Michael called them back and showed them his work. Sam was so happy to see his folder looking like new again. He thanked Mr. Michael and went home with Sue. Sam never forgot the day when his friend helped him repair his pale folder!

Once upon a time, in an ancient house, there was a big drain. The drain was very old and dirty. One day, a little boy named Tim wanted to wash the drain. He thought it would make the house look nice and clean.

Tim took a big bucket of water and a brush to wash the drain. But when he started to wash, a mean and angry cat jumped out of the drain. The cat did not like Tim washing its home. The cat hissed at Tim and tried to scratch him.

Tim was very scared and ran away from the angry cat. He could not wash the drain. The ancient house stayed dirty and the cat kept living in the drain. Tim was sad because he could not make the house clean and pretty. And so, the story has a bad ending.

Once upon a time, there was a kind rabbit named Benny. He lived in a cozy hole with his family. One day, Benny's friend, a mouse named Mickey, visited him.

Mickey said, "Benny, I need your helpful hands. I lost my luxury cheese and I can't find it."

Benny replied, "Don't worry, Mickey. I will help you find it. Let's shut our eyes and imagine where it could be."

They closed their eyes and imagined the cheese. Suddenly, Benny opened his eyes and saw it behind the bookshelf. He grabbed it and gave it to Mickey.

Mickey was very happy and said, "Thank you, Benny. You are the most helpful friend I have ever had."

Benny smiled and said, "It's my pleasure to help you, Mickey. Let's have some cheese together now." They ate the cheese and enjoyed their time together.

Once upon a time, there was a little bird named Blue. Blue loved to fly around and sing songs. One day, Blue saw some other birds who were ignorant and mean. They didn't want to play with Blue because Blue was different. Blue felt sad.

Winter came and it was very cold outside. Blue was all alone and didn't have any friends to keep warm with. Blue remembered the other birds and wished they were nicer.

One day, Blue saw a group of animals trying to separate a big log. They were having trouble because the log was too heavy. Blue flew over and helped them. The animals were grateful and became Blue's friends.

Blue learned that it's important to be kind to others, even if they are different. And sometimes, helping others can lead to new friendships.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Lucy. She loved to play in the rain and today it was her favourite - there was thunder and lightning too!

Lucy was wearing a pretty pink dress and had a special veil on her head which caught the rain. She twirled and twirled, feeling so happy and excited.

The rain was heavy and soon Lucy was feeling very wet. She wanted to relax, so she found a big tree with lots of leaves and climbed up into the branches.

The leaves kept her dry and the thunder made her feel safe. She curled up and closed her eyes, feeling the rain on her veil. Lucy was so relaxed, she fell asleep in the tree, sleeping for a long time until the sun came out and dried up all the rain.

Anna and Ben are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a new animal in the park. It is big and brown and has long legs. It can jump very high.

"What is that?" Anna asks.

"It is a kangaroo," Ben says. He knows a lot of things.

"Can we play with it?" Anna asks.

"I don't know. Maybe it is shy," Ben says.

They walk closer to the kangaroo. The kangaroo looks at them. It has big ears and a long tail. It makes a funny noise.

"Hello, kangaroo," Anna says. "Do you want to play with us?"

The kangaroo nods. It hops towards them. It is friendly.

"Wow, it likes us," Ben says. "Can we touch it?"

They pet the kangaroo. It feels soft and warm. The kangaroo licks their hands. It is hungry.

"Do you want to eat something, kangaroo?" Anna asks.

The kangaroo nods again. It looks around. It sees some grass and some flowers.

"Can we give it some grass and some flowers?" Ben asks.

"Sure, let's do that," Anna says.

They pick some grass and some flowers. They give them to the kangaroo. The kangaroo eats them. It makes a happy noise.

"Yum, yum, yum," the kangaroo says.

"Yum, yum, yum," Anna and Ben say.

They laugh and play with the kangaroo. They have a lot of fun. They make a new friend.

One morning, a deep sound arrived. It was loud and filled the air. All the animals came out from their homes. They were curious, what was that sound? Soon, all the animals saw a bright sun, rising in the sky above them. It was the morning.

The animals were excited and started running around, playing together and having fun. Suddenly, the deep sound arrived again, but this time it was louder and closer. Something was coming. Everybody stopped and looked in the same direction.

Out of the trees, a big black bear appeared. He had long sharp claws and big pointy teeth. All the animals were scared! But much to their surprise, the bear looked friendly. He was just happy to see all the animals out playing on the morning. The bear smiled and waved at everyone.

The animals slowly gained courage and started to walk closer to the bear. Soon, they were all playing together, having a deep and wonderful time on the morning.

Once upon a time, there was a young girl named Jessica. She loved to rock in her special seat. Every day, she would sit down and rock back and forth, feeling the amazing movement of her seat.

One day, Jessica's mommy asked her to come over. "Jessica, come here! I have something special to show you!" Jessica ran over, excited to see what it was.

When Jessica came close, she saw an even bigger seat. It was like her own seat, but much bigger. Her mommy said, "This is a rocking chair! It rocks better than your seat. Do you want to try it?"

Jessica was amazed! She said, "Yes! I want to rock it!" She quickly hopped into the chair and started rocking back and forth. It was so much fun! She rocked and rocked, back and forth, feeling the gentle movement of the chair.

Jessica's mommy said, "That looks like you're having fun! Keep rocking, Jessica!" So Jessica rocked and rocked, until it was finally time to go to bed.

She said goodbye to her rocking chair, then went off to bed with a big smile on her face. She had had an amazing rocking adventure!

One day, a big bird called an ostrich was walking in the rain. The ostrich was wet from the raindrops falling on him. He was looking for food to eat.

The ostrich saw a tree with yummy fruit. But the tree was tall, and the ostrich could not reach the fruit. He tried to jump, but the fruit did not yield.

Then, a kind friend came to help. The friend climbed the tree and got the fruit for the ostrich. Now, the wet ostrich was happy. He ate the fruit and thanked his friend. They played together in the rain until the sun came out.

Once upon a time, there was a little bee. The bee was very filthy. It did not like to be clean. The bee had many friends, but they did not like how dirty it was.

One day, the bee went to play with its friends. The friends said, "We hate how filthy you are! We don't want to play with you." The bee felt very sad but did not want to be clean.

The bee went to find new friends. It found a big spider. The spider said, "I like how filthy you are. We can be friends." The bee was happy to have a new friend. But the spider was not a good friend. It wanted to eat the bee.

In the end, the spider ate the bee. The bee's old friends were sad. They wished they had been kinder to the filthy bee.

Once upon a time, there was a little fish named Nemo. Nemo loved to swim in the deep blue sea with his fish friends. One day, Nemo saw a shiny object in the water and he wanted to investigate. He swam closer and closer until he saw that it was a big wrecked ship.

Nemo got excited and wanted to explore the ship. He swam inside and saw many interesting things. But suddenly, he heard a loud noise and felt something push him. It was a big wave that had hit the ship. Nemo tried to swim away, but he was stuck inside the wreck.

Nemo's fish friends tried to rescue him, but it was too late. Nemo was trapped and couldn't escape. His fish friends were very sad and missed him very much. From that day on, they never went near the wreck again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved to sing. She sang all day long, even when she was brushing her teeth or eating her breakfast.

One day, while she was singing in the park, she saw a beautiful angel sitting on a bench. The angel had big white wings and a shiny halo on her head.

"Wow, you're so beautiful!" said Lily.

"Thank you, little one," replied the angel. "I love to hear you sing. Would you like to sing a song with me?"

Lily was so happy that she sang a beautiful song with the angel. From that day on, they became good friends and sang together every day in the park.

Once upon a time, there was a kind princess. She lived in a big castle with her family. She had a lot of friends, but her best friend was a little cat named Fluffy. Fluffy was very weak and small, but the princess loved her a lot.

One day, the princess and Fluffy were playing in the garden. They were having a lot of fun. Suddenly, Fluffy saw a big butterfly and started to chase it. Fluffy ran so fast that the princess couldn't see her anymore. The princess was sad and started to cry.

A nice lady saw the princess crying and asked, "Why are you crying, little princess?" The princess said, "I lost my cat Fluffy. She is weak and I am worried." The lady helped the princess look for Fluffy. They found her under a big tree. The princess was so happy that she gave Fluffy a big hug. From that day on, the princess, Fluffy, and the nice lady became best friends and played together every day.

Once upon a time, there was a big taxi. It was blue, with yellow wheels. Every morning it would go split, split, split down the street. One morning, it stopped at a red light. Then it split right, then left, to go around the corner. It was going to pick up someone very special.

The taxi stopped in front of a tall building. Out came a little girl. She was wearing red shoes and had a big smile on her face. She said hello to the driver and hopped in the back seat.

The driver split off down the road. He split left, then split right, then he sped up. The little girl laughed and waved at everyone they passed.

Soon the taxi stopped in front of a big park. The driver helped the little girl out of the car. She thanked him, waved goodbye, and ran off to join her friends. The big taxi split off and drove away.

One day, there was a fast lady. She had a sharp knife in her hand. She wanted to use the knife to cut a cake. She worked very hard and cut the cake quickly. Suddenly, the lady felt something sharp on her finger. She had cut it with the knife! She was very surprised. She quickly put a bandage on her finger and smiled. The cake was cut and she was happy.

Once upon a time, there was a young boy named Timmy. Timmy was very bored one day and didn't know what to do. He looked around his room and saw his toy cars, but they didn't interest him. He looked out the window and saw the trees, but they were just green and boring.

Suddenly, Timmy's mom came into the room with a book. She showed Timmy the pictures in the book and told him about all the animals in the pictures. Timmy was amazed and admired the colorful birds and furry animals. He asked his mom to read the book to him, and she happily obliged.

Timmy was no longer bored and spent the rest of the day looking at the pictures and learning about the animals. From that day on, Timmy loved learning about new things and admired the beauty of the world around him.

Once upon a time, there was a farmer. He had many animals on his farm like cows, pigs, and chickens. The farmer was very kind and generous. He always shared his crops with his neighbors.

One day, a little girl came to the farmer and asked him a question. "Can I have some apples from your tree?" she asked. The farmer smiled and answered, "Of course, you can have some apples. I have plenty." The little girl was very happy and thanked the generous farmer.

From that day on, the little girl would visit the farmer often and they would talk about the animals and the crops. The farmer was always happy to answer her questions and share his knowledge. The little girl loved visiting the farmer and his farm, and she always left with a big smile on her face.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Lily. Lily liked to skip everywhere. One day, she wanted to go skipping in the garden and she grabbed her mum’s cane to help her balance.

As Lily skipped around the garden, she saw something weird. There was a very big, slimy monster in the garden! Lily couldn’t believe her eyes. She was scared and started to run away. But the monster went faster and caught Lily. She started to scream and cry. But then she remembered her mum’s cane, and started to wave it at the monster. The monster became scared and ran away!

Lily was relieved and happy, and she skipped all the way back home. She was happy that she had been brave and faced the monster.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved motorcycles and dreamed of riding one someday. One day, Timmy saw a tough-looking motorcycle parked outside the candy store. He ran over to it and touched it, feeling the cold metal.

Suddenly, a big man with a beard came out of the store and asked Timmy, "Do you like my motorcycle?" Timmy nodded his head and said, "Yes! It's tough!" The man smiled and said, "Do you want to sit on it?" Timmy's eyes widened with excitement and he nodded his head again.

As Timmy sat on the motorcycle, he looked up at the big man and asked, "Can I chew gum while riding it?" The man laughed and said, "Sure, but don't chew too hard or you might swallow it!" Timmy giggled and promised to be careful. From that day on, Timmy never forgot the fun he had on the tough motorcycle and always remembered to be careful when chewing gum.

Once upon a time, there was a little dog. The dog had a long tail. He liked to wag his tail when he was happy. One day, he saw a big ball in the distant. He wanted to get the ball and play with it.

The little dog ran and ran to get the big ball. His tail wagged so fast. As he ran, he did not see a big hole in the ground. The little dog fell into the hole. He tried to get out, but the hole was too deep.

The little dog was very sad. He could not get the ball or get out of the hole. His tail did not wag anymore. The little dog stayed in the hole and never got the big ball from the distant.

Once upon a time, there was a bald man named Bob. He lived in a small house with his cat, Mittens. One day, Bob decided to change his postbox.

He walked to the store and picked a new postbox. It was red and shiny. Bob was happy with his new postbox.

When he got home, Mittens was waiting for him. She meowed happily when she saw the new postbox. Bob smiled and thought that the change was a good idea.

From that day on, Bob loved checking his new postbox every day. He was glad he made the change.

Once upon a time, there was a small boy named Timmy. Timmy had long hair that covered his eyes, so his mom said it was time to go to the barber. Timmy was scared to go, but his mom said the barber was nice and would make him look handsome.

When they got to the barber, Timmy saw a small chair and the barber said, "Come and sit here, little one." Timmy sat in the chair and the barber started to cut his hair. Timmy was nervous at first, but the barber was kind and talked to him about his favorite toys.

After the haircut was done, Timmy looked in the mirror and saw that he looked very handsome. He thanked the small barber and said he would come back again. From that day on, Timmy loved going to the small barber and getting his hair cut.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved to collect junk. She would pick up anything she found on the ground and keep it in her room. Her parents would always tell her to stop, but she didn't listen.

One day, Lily found an adorable little toy on the street and brought it home. She was so happy to add it to her collection of junk. But what she didn't know was that the toy was broken and had sharp edges.

Later that night, Lily was playing with her junk when she accidentally cut herself on the broken toy. She cried out for her parents, but it was too late. She had to go to the hospital and get stitches.

The moral of the story is that sometimes, things that seem cute or fun can be dangerous. It's important to listen to our parents when they tell us to stop doing something, even if we don't want to.

Once upon a time, there was a hero. He had a special job - he had to store all the smooth rocks, so no one could take them away. He was a very special hero!

Every day, the hero would climb up a big hill and store the smooth rocks. He knew it was very important work and he was proud of himself!

At the end of the day, the hero would head back down the hill with bags full of smooth rocks. He was exhausted but happy. He knew he'd done a great job, and he'd help to keep the rocks safe.

And that's what the hero did every single day. On and on, he'd gather and store smooth rocks - and he was the bravest hero ever.

Once upon a time, there was a big, unusual bird. This bird had a very long neck. One day, the bird went to play with his friends. They played a game called "hold the neck." The bird was very good at this game because of his long neck.

As they played, a little boy came to watch. The little boy wanted to play too. The bird's friends said yes, but the unusual bird did not want the boy to play. He was scared that the boy might hurt his long neck.

The little boy did not listen to the bird. He wanted to play "hold the neck" too. The boy held the bird's neck too tight. The bird tried to get away, but the boy would not let go. The bird's neck got hurt, and the bird could not play with his friends anymore. The unusual bird was very sad, and the little boy was sorry for what he did.

Once upon a time there was a powerful castle. Inside, an underground room was hidden away. A brave prince wanted to explore the secret room. He shut the door behind him and entered.

He looked all around. He saw tall towers and lovely trees but no sign of life. The prince was so brave, he ventured further down. As he went lower, the walls around him rumbled. He was amazed by the powerful noise and he kept walking.

At last, he reached the bottom. He found a special surprise - it was a shining crown! The prince made his way back up, holding the crown in his hands. He opened the door to the castle and his family cheered. The prince was proud of his powerful discovery!

Once upon a time, there was a little boy. He had a very special hat and he loved it very much. He always put it on before running out to play.

One day, he put on his hat and ran outside. He wanted to see how fast he could go. He ran and ran and ran, getting faster and faster. He ran so fast that he was a blur.

When he stopped, he was out of breath. He had run so fast that he was exhausted. He was also very quiet, too quiet. His mom was worried and asked him what happened.

He told her about his aim to go very fast, and his mom smiled. She said she was proud of him for trying something new.

The little boy was happy and went back outside to play, but he promised to not go so fast again. He still kept his hat on, reminded of the adventure he had that day.

Once upon a time, there was a brother and sister. They both liked to write. But the brother was weird. He wrote funny words on the walls and the floor. The sister didn't like it. She thought her brother was being silly.

So, one day she grabbed some paper and a pencil and told her brother, "Let's write something different and have fun!" The brother was excited. He thought of lots of weird things to write. He wrote funny words and funny stories.

The sister laughed. She thought it was funny and fun. They spent all day writing weird things and having fun. In the end, the brother and sister were both very happy.

One day, a mom and her 3-year-old daughter decided to take a jog. They went to the park, put on their running shoes and started to run. Suddenly, the little girl noticed a large printing machine in the distance.

“Mommy, can I go print?” asked the little girl.

“I’m sorry, honey, you can’t go print today. Mommy and you need to finish the jog,” the mom said.

The little girl was very frustrated. She wanted to go print so badly. Frustrated tears were welling up in her eyes. Meanwhile, the mom was feeling sad. She wanted her daughter to be happy.

So the mom thought of an idea. “Let’s do a deal, sweetie - if you finish the jog, you can go print afterwards. Is that okay?”

The little girl smiled and they both finished their jog. Afterwards, they spent some time printing and left the park with smiles on their faces.

One day, Bobby was playing in his room when his mama called him. She was standing in the living room, holding his new bright red shirt. She said, "Bobby, it's time to dress up."

But Bobby didn't want to put on his shirt. He wanted to play some more. He shouted, "No! I don't want to dress!"

Mama frowned. She said, "You must dress. Mama's very enthusiastic about this outfit."

Bobby was still mad. He didn't want to dress. He said, "No! I want to play more!"

Just then, his papa came out of the kitchen, carrying a big cake from the refrigerator. His papa said, "Come on, Bobby. Don't make mama angry. Put your shirt on and mama will give you a slice of cake."

Bobby smiled. He quickly said, "Okay, papa!" He took the shirt and dressed himself quickly. He was happy to be wearing his new shirt and he was even more excited about the yummy cake.

Once there was a girl who loved to polish things. She would take all sorts of things and make them sparkle. One day, the girl heard about an event in her town. She wanted to go and show off the things she had polished.

The girl was so excited when she arrived. She ran around showing everyone the things she had polished, but they all just laughed at her. They didn't understand how something as simple as polishing things could be so special.

The girl was very upset by the reaction she had gotten. She didn't know what to do. Then, she turned and saw a gentle look on someone's face. He looked like he was watching her with understanding and admiration.

The girl smiled for the first time that day. The man then said to her, “Maybe you can’t show them how important polishing is. But you can show how beautiful and gentle it can be.”

With new hope and determination, the girl started to polish things again. Everyone quickly noticed how special it was this time and showed the girl respect. From that day, the girl focused on being gentle when it came to polishing, and her work always stood out.

Tom and Sue were friends who liked to play outside. One day, they saw a big snowman in the park. It had a hat, a scarf, a carrot nose and two buttons for eyes.

"Wow, look at the snowman!" Tom said. "He is so big and nice!"

"Let's go and say hello to him," Sue said. "Maybe he wants to play with us."

They ran to the snowman and hugged him. The snowman was cold and hard, but they did not mind. They smiled and talked to him.

"Hello, Mr. Snowman," Tom said. "We are Tom and Sue. What is your name?"

The snowman did not answer. He just stared at them with his button eyes.

"Maybe he is shy," Sue said. "Or maybe he is too old to talk. He looks very old, don't you think?"

"Yes, he does," Tom said. "But he is also very generous. Look, he has a hat and a scarf. Maybe he will share them with us. It is very cold today."

Tom reached for the hat and Sue reached for the scarf. But as soon as they touched them, something bad happened. The snowman came to life and grabbed them with his stick arms. He was not a nice snowman. He was a mean and angry snowman.

"Let go of us!" Tom and Sue cried. "Help! Help!"

But no one heard them. The snowman was too strong and too fast. He dragged them into his big mouth and ate them. He did not like children. He only liked snow.

The snowman smiled and burped. He felt warm and full. He put his hat and scarf back on and froze again. He looked like a normal snowman, but he was not. He was a monster. And he waited for more children to come and play with him.

There was once a family who had a theater in their backyard. Every day they would raise the curtains and let the sun in. Everyone was grateful for the theater and they would use it to have a good time together.

One day, a storm came and blew away all the curtains. The family was so upset, they didn't know what to do. Their theater lay in ruins.

The family worked together to try and fix their theater. They all spent long hours raising the curtains, patching up the walls and putting the chairs back in order. Everyone worked hard and eventually, their theater was back to how it was before.

The family was so grateful for all their hard work. The theater brought their family pleasure and they were all very happy to see it brought back to life.

Once upon a time there was a little boy who loved to go outside and play. One Sunday, the little boy was in his garden when his aunt came to visit. She had a big, green present in her hands.

The little boy's eyes lit up and asked his aunt what it was for him. His aunt replied and said, "It's for you, sweetheart!"

The little boy was so excited to receive his special present. He opened it and inside was a big, green teddy bear. The little boy hugged his aunt and thanked her for his new friend.

His aunt smiled and said, "You're very welcome, my darling. Now you two can have lots of fun in the garden."

The little boy and his new green teddy bear started playing together in the garden. They had a wonderful time with their aunt.

The end.

Tom and Sam are friends. They like to play with toys. They have a big tank that can move and make noise. They take turns to drive the tank and shoot balls at each other.

One day, Tom wants to drive the tank more. He does not let Sam have a turn. He says, "This is my tank. You can play with something else." Sam is upset. He wants to play with the tank too. He says, "That is not fair. We should share the tank. It is our tank."

Tom does not listen. He drives the tank faster and faster. He shoots more and more balls at Sam. Sam tries to dodge the balls, but he gets hit. He cries. He says, "Stop it, Tom. You are hurting me. You are not a good friend."

Tom does not care. He thinks he is having fun. He drives the tank to the edge of the table. He wants to see how far he can go. He does not see that the table is not flat. It is tilted. He does not balance the tank well. The tank falls off the table and breaks. Tom is shocked. He says, "Oh no, what have I done? I broke the tank. It is not working anymore."

Sam stops crying. He sees the broken tank. He is angry. He says, "You are a bad boy, Tom. You broke our tank. You did not share. You did not listen. You did not care. I do not want to play with you anymore. Go away."

Tom is sad. He wants to fix the tank. He wants to play with Sam. He says, "I am sorry, Sam. I made a mistake. I was selfish. I was mean. I want to be your friend. Please forgive me."

Sam does not forgive him. He says, "No, I do not forgive you. You ruined our game. You ruined our toy. You ruined our friendship. You are not my friend. You are nothing to me."

Tom cries. He has no tank. He has no friend. He has nothing. He is alone. He is unhappy. He is sorry. But it is too late. The end.

Once upon a time there was a big yellow boat that lived in the lake. The boat was old and needed to be fixed. So Papa and Maple, the little three-year-old girl, set out to restore the boat.

Maple asked, "What are we doing, Papa?"

Papa looked up from the boat and said, "We are restoring the boat, Maple. We need to make it look new again."

Maple nodded and said, "Yes! It will look so pretty!"

Papa warned Maple to be careful, for the lake was dangerous. Maple said, "Okay Papa, I will be careful."

So Papa and Maple worked together to restore the boat. They cleaned it, painted it and even placed a rainbow flag at the top! When they were finished, they looked at the little yellow boat with pride.

"It looks so pretty now, Papa!" Maple said.

"Yes, it does," Papa replied with a smile.

And from that day on, the little yellow boat in the lake was safe and restored.

Lily and Ben are playing in the garden. They see a furry rat under a bush. Lily is scared of the rat. She runs away and cries.

"Come back, Lily!" Ben says. "The rat is not bad. He is just looking for food."

Ben tries to be brave. He goes near the bush and talks to the rat. "Hello, rat. What is your name? Do you want to be my friend?"

The rat is shy. He does not answer. He hides under the leaves.

"Please, rat. Don't be afraid. I have some cheese for you. Do you like cheese?" Ben says. He puts a piece of cheese on the ground.

The rat smells the cheese. He is hungry. He comes out of the bush and takes the cheese. He nibbles it and makes a happy sound.

"See, Lily? The rat is nice. He likes cheese. Can we play with him?" Ben says.

Lily comes back. She is still scared, but she is curious. She sees the rat eating the cheese. She sees his furry tail and his whiskers.

"Maybe he is not so bad," Lily says. "But he is very small. We have to be gentle with him."

Ben and Lily try to be gentle. They give the rat more cheese. They stroke his fur. They make him a bed of grass. The rat likes them. He snuggles with them and falls asleep.

They have a new friend. They call him Cheese. They are happy.

Ben loves rockets. He has many rockets in his room. He plays with them every day. He makes them fly and zoom and blast off. He does not like to share his rockets with anyone.

One day, his friend Sam comes to his house. Sam likes rockets too. He sees Ben's rockets and wants to play with them. He asks Ben, "Can I play with your rockets, please?"

Ben says, "No, they are mine. You cannot play with them. Go away." He is very mean to Sam. Sam feels sad and hurt. He says, "Okay, I will go away. But you are not a good friend."

Sam leaves Ben's house. He goes to his own house. He has a big surprise in his house. His mom and dad give him a new rocket. It is bigger and better than Ben's rockets. It has lights and sounds and stickers. It is a very cool rocket.

Sam is very happy. He thanks his mom and dad. He says, "I love you and I love my new rocket. Can I show it to Ben?"

His mom and dad say, "Yes, you can. But be careful. Ben may not be nice to you. He may not like your rocket. He may be sour."

Sam says, "I know. But I want to be a good friend. I want to share my rocket with him. Maybe he will change his mind and be nice to me."

Sam takes his new rocket and goes to Ben's house. He knocks on the door. Ben opens the door. He sees Sam's new rocket. He is very surprised and jealous. He says, "Wow, what a cool rocket. Where did you get it?"

Sam says, "My mom and dad gave it to me. It is my new rocket. Do you want to play with it?"

Ben says, "Yes, I do. Can I play with it, please?"

Sam says, "Yes, you can. But you have to share it with me. And you have to be nice to me. And you have to let me play with your rockets too."

Ben thinks for a moment. He remembers how he was mean to Sam. He feels sorry and ashamed. He says, "Okay, I will. I am sorry for being mean to you. You are a good friend. Can we be friends again?"

Sam says, "Yes, we can. I forgive you. Come on, let's play with our rockets together."

They hug and smile. They play with their rockets. They have fun. They learn to share and be kind. They are happy.

The moral of the story is: Sharing is caring. Be nice to your friends. Don't be sour.

Lily and Ben were playing with their blocks in the living room. They wanted to make a big building with many rooms and windows. They were having fun until they heard a loud noise outside.

They ran to the window and saw that it was raining hard. The sky was dark and the wind was blowing. They saw some people running with umbrellas and some cars splashing water.

"Wow, look at the rain!" Ben said. "It is so wet and noisy!"

"I don't like the rain," Lily said. "It makes everything wet and cold. And it ruins our plans. We wanted to go to the park today."

"Maybe the rain will stop soon," Ben said. "Then we can go outside and play."

They waited for a while, but the rain did not stop. It got even harder and louder. They heard a thunder and saw a lightning. They got scared and hugged each other.

"Ben, I'm afraid of the thunder and the lightning," Lily said. "They are so angry and scary!"

"Don't be afraid, Lily," Ben said. "They are just noises and lights. They can't hurt us. We are safe inside our house. And we have each other."

He gave her a kiss on the cheek and smiled. "And we still have our blocks. We can make our building here. We can make it as big and as beautiful as we want. And we can pretend that it is our park."

Lily smiled back and nodded. "You are right, Ben. We can still have fun. And maybe the rain will be nice and stop soon. And then we can see a rainbow."

They went back to their blocks and started to build their building. They forgot about the rain and the thunder and the lightning. They were happy and busy. They used their imagination and their creativity. They made their building and their park. And they had fun.

Once there was a little squirrel named Johnny. He was always very happy and loved to play in the woods. One day, he heard something strange coming from an old tree. He went over and saw that a small nut was stuck in the tree. He tried to get it out but it was too hard for him.

Suddenly, he heard someone else in the woods. A kind old lady was walking by and noticed the little squirrel. She felt compassionate and carefully climbed up the tree. She took the nut out and gave it to Johnny.

Johnny was so thankful and thanked the kind lady. The old lady smiled and left, but Johnny never forgot how compassionate she was. Every time he looked at the nut, he remembered the kindness of the old lady.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Sarah. Every day, Sarah wanted to make something special. So she went to the store and bought some shiny gems. She decided to prepare a perfect gift for her mom.

Sarah began to make the gift. She used the shiny gems to create a beautiful necklace. She worked for hours to make the necklace look perfect.

When the necklace was done, Sarah ran to her mom. Her mom was very happy to see the perfect gift. Sarah was so proud that she had made such a beautiful necklace.

Sarah and her mom put the necklace on, and they twirled around the house. Mom said she had never seen a gift as perfect as the one her daughter had prepared. And they lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time there was a mighty monster. The monster was so big that its feet touched the sky. It had a really long tail and huge claws. Every day, the monster would hop around the forest looking for food.

As the monster hopped around the forest, it noticed something very special. A tiny bunny playing in the grass. The monster was very curious so it hopped a little closer to the bunny. When the monster got close enough, it saw that the bunny was very scared.

The monster realized that it needed to be gentle, so it tried to hop away slowly. But as soon as it hopped away, the bunny began to smile. For the first time, the mighty monster and the tiny bunny were friends. They hopped through the forest together, playing and laughing all day.

By the time the sun went down, the monster and bunny were the best of friends. They said goodbye to each other and promised to meet again the next day. And so the monster hopped away, happy to have such a new and mighty friend.

Once upon a time, there was a cute little duck named Ducky. Ducky loved to wander around the pond all day long. One day, Ducky decided to go to a new pond and see what was on the menu there.

Ducky waddled and wandered until she found a new pond. She looked at the menu and saw lots of yummy things to eat like bugs and worms. Suddenly, Ducky saw an adorable little frog hopping around.

Ducky thought the frog was so cute and wanted to be friends. She waddled over to the frog and said hello. The frog was happy to have a new friend and they hopped and played together all day long. From that day on, Ducky and the adorable frog were best friends and they wandered and explored together every day.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a black cat named Midnight. One day, Lily and Midnight went for a jog in the park.

As they were jogging, they saw a big dog with a collar around its neck. The dog barked at them and Lily got scared. "Don't worry," said Midnight, "I'll protect you."

Midnight bravely walked up to the dog and meowed at it. The dog stopped barking and wagged its tail. "Good job, Midnight!" said Lily, giving her cat a hug. They continued their jog in the park, feeling happy and safe.

Once upon a time, there was a little bunny named Fluffy. Fluffy loved to play outside in the sun and eat carrots. One day, Fluffy's friend, a little bird named Tweet, flew down to say hello.

"Hi Fluffy! What are you doing?" asked Tweet.

"I'm just soaking up the sun and munching on some carrots," said Fluffy.

Tweet looked up at the sky and noticed the light was getting dimmer. "Uh oh, it looks like it's going to rain soon. You better go inside before you get wet and your fur gets all soft."

Fluffy hopped into his burrow just in time before the rain started pouring down. But the rain was too strong and the burrow started to fill with water. Fluffy tried to swim to safety, but he couldn't escape. Sadly, Fluffy drowned in the flood and his friend Tweet never saw him again. The end.

Lily liked to rub her doll's hair. She loved her doll very much. Her doll was a gift from her grandma. Grandma said the doll was expensive, but Lily did not know what that meant. She only knew that the doll was pretty and soft and smelled nice.

One day, Lily took her doll to the park. She wanted to show her doll to her friend Ben. Ben liked to play with cars and trucks. He did not like dolls. He said dolls were silly and boring. He grabbed Lily's doll and threw it in the mud. Lily was very sad and angry. She ran to get her doll and shouted at Ben.

"Give me back my doll! You are mean and rude! You don't know how to be a good friend!"

Ben laughed and said, "Your doll is ugly and dirty now. You can have it. I don't want it. It's not fun to play with."

Lily picked up her doll and hugged it. She tried to rub the mud off her doll's hair, but it was hard. She felt tears in her eyes. She wished grandma was here. Grandma would know how to clean her doll and make it pretty again.

She looked around and saw a lady sitting on a bench. The lady had a kind face and a big bag. Lily walked to the lady and said, "Excuse me, can you help me? My doll is dirty and I don't know how to clean it."

The lady smiled and said, "Of course, I can help you. I have some wipes and a towel in my bag. Let me see your doll."

The lady took Lily's doll and gently wiped the mud off her hair and face. She dried her with a towel and combed her hair. She said, "There, your doll is clean and beautiful again. What's her name?"

Lily said, "Her name is Rose. She is my favorite doll. Thank you for helping me. You are very nice."

The lady said, "You're welcome, Lily. I'm glad I could help. Rose is a lovely doll. She looks very special. Where did you get her?"

Lily said, "My grandma gave her to me. She said she was expensive, but I don't know what that means."

The lady said, "It means that your grandma paid a lot of money for your doll. She must love you very much. You should take good care of your doll and cherish her. She is a rare and valuable doll."

Lily said, "I do love her very much. And I love my grandma too. She is the best grandma in the world."

The lady said, "I'm sure she is. And I'm sure she would be proud of you for being brave and polite. You are a good girl, Lily. And you have a good friend in Rose."

Lily smiled and said, "Thank you, lady. You are a good friend too. Can I give you a hug?"

The lady said, "Of course, you can. I would love a hug."

Lily hugged the lady and said, "Thank you for everything. You made me happy."

The lady hugged Lily back and said, "You're welcome, Lily. You made me happy too."

Sara likes to play in the attic. She finds many old things there. She finds books, toys, hats and boxes. One day, she finds a big box with photos. She opens the box and looks at the photos.

She sees photos of her mom and dad when they were young. She sees photos of her grandma and grandpa when they were young. She sees photos of her aunt and uncle when they were babies. She likes the photos. They are original. They are not like the photos on her mom's phone.

She takes one photo out of the box. It is a photo of her mom and dad on their wedding day. They look happy and pretty. She likes their clothes and their flowers. She wants to show the photo to her mom and dad.

She runs down the stairs with the photo in her hand. She finds her mom and dad in the kitchen. They are making lunch. She shows them the photo and says, "Look, mom and dad, I found an original photo of you in the attic. You look happy and pretty. I like your clothes and your flowers."

Her mom and dad smile and hug her. They thank her for finding the photo. They tell her it is a special photo. They tell her they love her. They ask her if she wants to see more photos in the attic. She says yes. She runs back to the attic with her mom and dad. They look at more photos together. They have fun.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. He loved to take pictures with his camera. One day, he went to the park to take some pictures of the birds. But when he got there, he saw a big dog that made him frightened. He wanted to take a picture of the dog, but he was too scared to get close.

Just then, a little girl named Sarah came by. She saw the dog too, but she wasn't frightened. Timmy asked her if he could take a picture of the dog, but Sarah disagreed. She said it wasn't safe to take pictures of dogs you don't know. Timmy was sad, but he knew Sarah was right. He put his camera away and they both went to play on the swings instead.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys and sing songs. One day, she found a beautiful flute in her toy box. It was shiny and sparkly and made a pretty sound when she blew into it.

Lily's mommy came into her room and saw her playing the flute. "Oh, Lily, that's an adorable flute! Can you play a song for me?" she asked.

Lily tried to play a song, but she wasn't very good at it yet. "I don't know how to play," she told her mommy.

"That's okay, sweetie," her mommy said. "I can teach you. Just keep practicing and you'll get better."

Lily was happy that her mommy could tell her how to play the flute. She practiced every day and soon became very good at it. She would play for her mommy and daddy, and they would always tell her how proud they were of her. And that's how Lily learned to play the adorable flute. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to dance to jazz music with her parents. One day, Lily's mom gave her a useful tip. "Lily, when you dance, try to kneel down and spin around. It will make your dancing even more fun!" Lily was excited to try this new move.

At the next jazz dance party, Lily showed off her new move. Her friend, Timmy, saw her and said, "Wow, Lily! That move was so cool! Can you teach me how to do it?" Lily was happy to teach him and they both danced together, kneeling and spinning around.

After the party, Lily's dad said, "Lily, you were amazing! You are such a great dancer!" Lily smiled and felt proud of herself. She replied, "Thanks, Dad! I learned a new move today, and it was very useful!"

Once upon a time, there was a kind mouse named Mickey. Mickey loved to go on adventures, so one day he decided to explore a maze. When he got to the maze, he saw a big, scary cat.

"Hello, little mouse," said the cat. "Do you want to play a game with me?"

Mickey was scared, but he didn't want to be rude. "Sure, I'll play a game with you," he said.

The cat led Mickey into the maze and they started to play. But soon, Mickey realized that the cat was trying to trick him. Mickey remembered his mom telling him to never trust strangers. So, he used his cleverness to find his way out of the maze and go back home safely.

Mickey learned that it's important to be kind to others, but also to be careful and smart. From that day on, he only went on adventures with his friends and family.

Lila and Ben were playing with blocks in the living room. They liked to build towers and bridges and castles. Lila had a big red block that was heavy and strong. She put it on top of her tower to make it taller.

"Look, Ben, my tower is the highest!" she said, proud of her work.

Ben looked at Lila's tower and felt a little jealous. He wanted a big red block too, but he only had small blue blocks that were light and weak. He tried to make his tower higher, but it kept falling down.

"Your tower is too high, Lila. It will fall and break!" he said, hoping to make her scared.

Lila shook her head. "No, it won't. My tower is strong. Your tower is too low, Ben. It is boring!" she said, sticking out her tongue.

Ben felt angry and sad. He wanted to make Lila's tower fall and break. He picked up a small blue block and threw it at Lila's tower. The block hit the big red block and made a loud noise. The big red block wobbled and slid off the tower. It fell on the floor and cracked in half.

"Ben, why did you do that?" Lila cried, seeing her big red block broken. "You are mean and bad!"

Ben felt sorry and ashamed. He didn't mean to break Lila's big red block. He just wanted to have one too. He looked at Lila's sad face and felt a big lump in his throat.

"I'm sorry, Lila. I didn't mean to break your block. I was jealous of your tower. Can you forgive me?" he said, picking up the two pieces of the block.

Lila looked at Ben and saw that he was sorry. She felt a little better. She knew that Ben was her friend and that he made a mistake.

"It's okay, Ben. I forgive you. You are my friend and I love you. But you have to be careful with my blocks. They are mine and I like them." she said, taking the two pieces of the block from him.

"Thank you, Lila. You are my friend and I love you too. I will be careful with your blocks. They are yours and you like them. Can we share them and play together?" he said, giving her a hug.

"Yes, we can share them and play together. We can make a new tower with both red and blue blocks. It will be the best tower ever!" she said, smiling.

They hugged and kissed and went back to playing with the blocks. They made a new tower that was high and strong and colorful. They were happy and had fun. They learned to say thank you and to share. They were good friends. The end.

One day, a little girl called Alice decided to explore her garden. As she hugged the big tree, she discovered a big and shiny button! She got so excited and ran to her mom. She shouted: "Mommy! I found a button!"

Her mom was very happy and bent down to hug her. She asked Alice: "What are you going to do with the button?"

Alice thought for a while and exclaimed: "I want to push it!"

Her mom smiled and said: "That's a good idea. But first, you need to be obedient and help me take in the clothes from the line."

Alice said yes, and was very obedient. She helped her mom hang the clothes and soon, she was done. Her mom said: "Now, you can go and push the button!"

Alice ran to the tree and pushed the button with all her might. Suddenly, the button lit up and a dozen of beautiful butterflies filled the sky! She was so happy! She looked up and smiled at her mom. Her mom was very proud of her daughter. Alice had discovered something magical.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a unique mop that she loved very much. One day, Lily's friend came over to play. Lily showed her friend her mop and her friend wanted to play with it too. Lily didn't want to share her mop, but her mom told her she should accept her friend's request.

Lily's friend accidentally broke the mop while playing with it. Lily was very sad and upset. She didn't want to be friends with her anymore. Her mom told her that accidents happen and that she should forgive her friend. But Lily didn't want to forgive her friend.

The next day, Lily's friend came over to apologize and try to make things right. But Lily still didn't want to be friends with her. Her friend felt very sad and left. Lily realized that she made a mistake and wanted to apologize, but it was too late. She lost her friend and her unique mop. She learned that forgiveness is important and that it's okay to share things with others.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a bean plant in her garden that she loved very much. One day, she noticed that the bean plant was starting to stretch higher and higher towards the sky.

Lily was amazed by how tall the bean plant was getting. She had never seen anything like it before. It was so unique and special to her.

Every day, Lily would water the bean plant and watch it grow taller and taller. She was so proud of her little bean plant and couldn't wait to see how much it would stretch in the future.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside and look at the big trees. One day, she saw her friend Timmy walking by.

"Hi, Timmy!" said Lily. "Do you want to play with me?"

"Sure!" said Timmy.

Lily and Timmy decided to make a big sandcastle. They worked together to build it up, and it looked so pretty. They were proud of what they had made.

"Wow, that looks so big!" said Timmy.

"Yeah, it does!" said Lily. "Let's add some more shells to make it look even better."

They added more shells and made the sandcastle look even bigger. They were both very happy with what they had made. They sat down and looked at it for a while.

"It looks so pretty," said Timmy.

"I know," said Lily. "I'm glad we made it together."

Ben and Lily are twins. They like to joke with each other. Sometimes they joke with their dad too. He is in the navy. He wears a blue suit and a hat. He works on a big boat.

One day, Ben and Lily find a can of paint in the garage. It is navy blue. They have a crazy idea. They sneak into their dad's room and paint his hat blue. They think it is very funny.

When their dad comes home, he sees his hat. He is very surprised. He says, "Who did this to my hat?" Ben and Lily giggle. They say, "We did, dad. We joke with you. Do you like your new hat?"

Their dad smiles. He says, "You are very silly, Ben and Lily. But I love you. And I love my new hat. It matches my suit. But don't do it again, okay?" Ben and Lily nod. They hug their dad. They are happy. They like to joke, but they also like to make their dad happy.

Once upon a time, a boy named Timmy went to the park with his colorful bucket. He wanted to play with it in the sandpit. But when he got there, he saw that another boy was already playing there. The other boy had a big shovel and was making a big castle.

Timmy asked if he could play too, but the other boy said no. Timmy felt sad and didn't know what to do. Then he remembered that his mom had taught him how to cook. So he went home and asked his mom if they could make cookies together.

They made yummy cookies and put them in Timmy's colorful bucket. When he went back to the park, he offered the other boy a cookie. The other boy smiled and said they could play together. They had fun making a big castle with the shovel and the bucket. Timmy learned that sometimes being kind can make conflicts go away.

Once upon a time, there was a very troubled little bear. His fur was all matted and he had no one to play with. He was so sad and lonely. One day he decided to go for a walk.

As he was walking through the woods, he spotted something. It was a big, fluffy towel! He was so excited and he ran to get it. He picked it up and hugged it tightly, squeezing with all his might.
