The bear enjoyed his new toy so much that he brought it everywhere with him. Whenever he felt troubled, he would hug the towel and squeeze it tightly. He even slept with it under his head.

The bear was very happy and content with his new friend. It made life so much brighter. He never went anywhere without his towel and he never felt troubled again.

Once upon a time, there was a little bug named Billy. Billy liked to crawl around and explore the world. One day, he met a big ant named Andy.

"Hi there, little bug! What are you doing?" asked Andy.

"I'm just crawling around, looking for food," replied Billy.

Andy looked at Billy's tiny brain and felt upset. "You know, little bug, you should be careful. You have a small brain and you might get hurt."

Billy felt sad and upset. "But I want to explore and have fun," he said.

Andy thought for a moment and then said, "Well, I can help you. I have a big brain and I can show you how to crawl safely."

Billy was happy and excited. "Thank you, Andy!" he said.

And so, Andy taught Billy how to crawl safely and they became good friends. From that day on, Billy was careful and always remembered to use his brain.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved going to the beach and swimming in the ocean. One day, she saw a dolphin jumping out of the water. Lily thought it was so cool!

Later that day, Lily's mom gave her a box of chocolates. Lily opened the box and tried one. It was bitter! She didn't like it very much.

The next day, Lily went back to the beach. She saw the dolphin again and remembered the bitter chocolate. She wondered if the dolphin liked bitter things too. Suddenly, the dolphin swam up to her and opened its mouth. Inside, Lily saw something shiny. It was a treasure! The dolphin had found it and wanted to share it with her. From that day on, Lily and the dolphin were the best of friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She lived in a small house in the countryside with her mommy and daddy. One day, her mommy asked her to help mail a letter to her grandma who lived in another country.

Lily was very excited to help her mommy. She ran to the mailbox and put the letter inside. She watched as the mailman came and took the letter away.

After a few days, Lily and her family received a letter from her grandma. She was so happy to read it! But she noticed that her grandma's handwriting was very pale and hard to read. So, Lily's mommy helped her read the letter and they talked about how much they missed her grandma who lived so far away in another country.

Once upon a time, there was a big red barn in a small town. In the barn, there lived a kind cow named Molly. Molly had a smooth, shiny coat that was soft to touch. She loved to play with her friends in the green grass.

One day, Molly saw a little bird with a broken wing. The bird was sad and could not fly. Molly wanted to help the bird. She thought of something she could do. Molly decided to lend her barn to the little bird.

The little bird was very happy to have a safe place to stay. Molly and the bird became best friends. They played together every day. The bird's wing got better, and it could fly again. Molly was happy that she could help her friend. And they all lived happily ever after.

Once there was a little girl who admired her dad. Every day he worked hard to take care of his family. He was reliable and never gave up even when things seemed hard.

One night the girl woke up and heard her dad crying. She got out of bed and saw that he was in pain. She didn't understand why her dad was so sad but she knew he needed help.

The little girl carefully touched her dad's arm and softly said "I will take care of you." Tears rolled down his face as he looked at her and said "Thank you". From that day on, the dad knew he could always depend on the little girl. He was so proud of how reliable and caring she was.

The little girl will always admire her dad, no matter how old she gets.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, she got sick and her mommy took her to the doctor. The doctor put a thermometer in Lily's mouth to check her temperature. Lily was curious about what the thermometer was doing in her mouth.

After the doctor checked her, Lily's mommy asked, "Is everything okay, doctor?" The doctor said, "Lily has a fever. She needs to rest and drink lots of water." Lily started to cry because she didn't want to be sick.

Her mommy hugged her and said, "It's okay to cry, sweetie. We'll take care of you and make you feel better." Lily felt better knowing that her mommy was there to take care of her.

Lily and Ben were at the beach with their mom and dad. They liked to play in the sand and make castles and tunnels. They also liked to swim in the water, but only when it was not too cold or too deep.

One day, they saw a big bucket near the shore. It was blue and shiny and had a handle. Lily and Ben ran to the bucket and looked inside. There were some shells and stones and a little crab.

"Wow, look at this!" Lily said. "Can we keep it?"

"I don't know," Ben said. "Maybe it belongs to someone else."

They looked around and saw a distant man sitting on a towel. He had a hat and a book and a cooler. He did not seem to notice them.

"Maybe he is the owner of the bucket," Lily said. "Let's ask him."

They picked up the bucket and walked towards the man. They were careful not to spill the water or hurt the crab.

"Excuse me, sir," Ben said. "Is this your bucket?"

The man looked up and smiled. He saw the bucket and the crab and the shells and the stones.

"No, it's not mine," he said. "I found it here this morning. You can have it if you want."

"Really?" Lily and Ben said. "Thank you!"

They were very happy. They thanked the man again and ran back to the water. They put the bucket down and decided to swim with the crab. They named him Bob and made him a friend. They had a lot of fun. They also shared some of their shells and stones with the man. He was very nice. They had a great day at the beach.

Lily and Ben were playing in the park with their toy jets. They made zooming noises and pretended to fly around the trees and swings. They had a lot of fun, but their jets got dirty from the grass and the sand.

"Look, my jet is all brown and green," Lily said, showing her jet to Ben.

"Mine too," Ben said, "Let's wash them in the fountain."

They ran to the fountain, where the water was sparkling and splashing. They dipped their jets in the water and rubbed them with their hands. They watched the dirt wash away and their jets shine again.

"Wow, they look like new," Lily said, smiling.

"Hey, kids, what are you doing?" a voice said behind them. They turned around and saw a bald man wearing a blue uniform. He had a badge that said "Park Ranger".

"We are washing our jets, sir," Ben said, politely.

"Your jets?" the man said, confused. He looked at their toys and saw that they were plastic models of airplanes. He smiled and said, "Oh, I see. Those are very nice jets. But you know, this fountain is not for washing toys. It is for people to enjoy and for the birds to drink. You should use a bucket or a hose at home to wash your toys."

Lily and Ben felt sorry and said, "We didn't know, sir. We are sorry. We won't do it again."

"That's OK, kids. I'm glad you like the park and your jets. But please, be careful and respectful of the fountain and the animals. Here, let me help you dry your jets with this towel," the man said, kindly.

He took a towel from his bag and gently wiped their jets. He handed them back to Lily and Ben and said, "There you go. Now they are clean and dry. Have a nice day, kids. And remember, always fly safe and high."

"Thank you, sir. You are very nice. Have a nice day, too," Lily and Ben said, gratefully.

They waved goodbye to the man and ran back to their spot. They resumed their play, but this time, they kept their jets away from the fountain and the dirt. They learned a lesson and made a new friend.

One day, a little girl named Daisy went to play outside. She loved to play with her ball. She would throw it up in the air and catch it. Daisy was having so much fun.

But then, Daisy threw the ball too high. She tried to catch it, but she missed. The ball went far away and she could not see it. Daisy felt hurt and sad because she lost her ball.

Daisy looked and looked for her ball. She found it under a big tree. She was so happy! Daisy played with her ball again and did not miss. She had a great day playing outside.

Once upon a time, there was a cheap old house. It had a cobweb in one corner and the walls were starting to rot. One day, a little mouse came to the house. It crept into the cobweb and fell asleep.

The next day, the mouse came out of the cobweb. It was covered in sticky cobwebs and had to clean up. It scratched and scratched until it was all clean again.

The mouse wanted to find a better place to sleep. So it went from house to house, looking for a better place. But every house was either too expensive, or was starting to rot too.

Finally, it came to the same old cheap house. It knew this was the best place for it. So it hopped into the cobweb, said goodnight and fell asleep. The mouse lived happily ever after, in the cheap old house with the cobweb.

Once upon a time there was a brilliant factory. All the machines were bright and shiny, and all the workers were very happy. One day, one of the workers, called John, decided to quit.

"Why are you quitting?" asked another worker.

John replied, "I'm not happy here anymore."

A supervisor heard this and said, “But this is the best factory around. You'll never find a more brilliant factory. Don't quit!"

John thought it over and decided he had made a mistake. He changed his mind and said, "I'm staying. This is an amazing factory."

And so John stayed and everyone was happy. The factory continued being brilliant and the workers enjoyed their jobs.

Ben and Lily were playing with a big puzzle. It had many pieces with different colors and shapes. They wanted to make a picture of a farm with animals and trees.

"Look, I found the cow!" Lily said, holding a piece with black and white spots. "Where does it go?"

Ben looked at the puzzle board. He saw a green piece with grass and a red piece with a barn. He pointed to a spot next to the barn. "It goes here, Lily. See, the cow lives near the barn."

Lily nodded and put the piece in the right place. She smiled and said, "Thank you, Ben. You are a good brother. You support me."

Ben smiled back and said, "You are welcome, Lily. You are a good sister. You help me too."

They continued to work on the puzzle, finding more pieces and matching them. They found the horse, the pig, the sheep, the chicken, the dog, the cat, the tractor, the fence, and the farmer. They filled the puzzle board with the farm picture.

When they finished, they clapped their hands and cheered. They were very proud of their puzzle. They showed it to their mom, who was watching them from the couch.

"Wow, Ben and Lily, you did a great job!" Mom said. "You made a beautiful puzzle. I am proud of you too."

She hugged them and gave them a kiss. They hugged her back and said, "We love you, Mom."

They were happy and proud. They had fun playing with the puzzle. They had fun supporting each other.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved to play in her room. One day, her big brother Jack came in and started to tease her. "Your room is terrible," he said. "It's so messy and boring."

Lily felt sad and didn't know what to do. She didn't want her room to be terrible. So, she asked Jack for help. "Can you help me clean it up?" she asked.

Jack thought about it for a moment and then said, "Sure, I'll help you." Together, they cleaned up the room and made it look nice and tidy. Lily was so happy and thanked Jack for his help.

From that day on, Lily and Jack played together in her room and had lots of fun. And whenever Jack felt like teasing her again, he remembered how happy they were when they worked together.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to color and had a big box of crayons. One day, she wanted to color a picture for her mommy's birthday. She asked her daddy to help her find the perfect colors.

But her daddy was busy and said, "I can't help you right now, Lily. I'm sorry, but I have to delay helping you until later."

Lily was sad, but she didn't give up. She looked through her box of crayons and found some attractive colors. She started coloring the picture all by herself. When her daddy saw what she had done, he was so proud of her. "Wow, Lily! You did a great job! Your mommy will love this picture!" he said.

Lily was happy and proud of herself too. She learned that even if things are delayed, she can still do them on her own and make something beautiful.

Once there was a little girl who was always up to something. One day she was playing in her garden when she saw something peek out of the ground. She quickly ran over and saw something sparkly. It was so fine and she knew it was special so she quickly dug it up. When she gave it a closer look, she was so excited to find it was a box of salt! She had never seen something so fine and shiny before. She was so proud of the find that she quickly ran inside to show her family. It was so exciting! They all said it was very special and talked about how proud she was for finding such a special thing. She took the box of salt and kept it safe for the special days to come.

One day, a little boy named Tim found a big bin. The bin was green and had a funny face on it. Tim thought it was a very silly bin. He wanted to show his friend, Sue.

Tim marched to Sue's house with the silly bin. He was so excited to show her. When he got to Sue's house, he knocked on the door. Sue came out and saw the bin.

"Look, Sue!" Tim said. "I found this silly bin! It has a funny face on it."

Sue laughed and said, "That is a very silly bin, Tim! Let's play with it!"

They played with the silly bin all day. They marched around the yard, pretending the bin was a big, funny monster. They had so much fun with their new silly friend, the bin.

Once upon a time there lived a queen. She was known for her kindness and generosity. Every day, she would take creations from the people of her kingdom and make them even better.

One day, the queen heard a knock on the door. She opened the door to find a mysterious box. Inside the box was something unknown. Before the queen had the chance to find out what it was, the box began to shake. Suddenly, it tore open and out flew a beautiful bird.

The queen was delighted and she quickly named the bird Fred. Everyone in the kingdom loved Fred and all the people cheered. As time went on, the unknown bird became a part of the royal family.

It was then that the queen knew that the unknown bird was no ordinary creature. It was a magical bird that the queen had heard stories about from her ancestors. She realized that the bird was sent to her from the heavens above! From then on, the queen and the bird were best friends.

Once upon a time, there was a big, hairy dog named Max. Max loved to chew on things, especially his owner's sweater. Max's owner would scold him, but Max couldn't help it. One day, Max got very sick because he had swallowed a piece of the sweater.

Max's owner rushed him to the vet, but it was too late. Max had to have surgery, but it didn't work. Max passed away because he had eaten something he shouldn't have. Max's owner was very sad and missed him very much. She learned to be more careful with her things and to keep them away from Max. The end.

Tom and Ann are friends. They like to play with their toys. But today they have a quarrel. They both want the same toy. It is a sheep with soft wool.

"Give me the sheep!" Tom says. "It is mine!"

"No, it is mine!" Ann says. "I saw it first!"

They pull the sheep from each other. The sheep makes a sad sound. Baa!

Aunt Sue hears the quarrel. She comes to see what is wrong. She sees Tom and Ann with the sheep.

"What are you doing, children?" she asks. "Why are you fighting over the sheep?"

Tom and Ann stop pulling. They look at Aunt Sue.

"We both want the sheep," Tom says.

"It is so soft and nice," Ann says.

Aunt Sue smiles. She has an idea.

"I have something for you," she says. "Come with me to the kitchen."

She takes Tom and Ann to the kitchen. She shows them a big cake. It has icing and sprinkles. It smells yummy.

"This is a cake for you," she says. "You can share it and be happy."

Tom and Ann forget the sheep. They see the cake. Their eyes grow big.

"Wow!" Tom says.

"Yummy!" Ann says.

They hug Aunt Sue. They say thank you. They cut the cake and eat it. They are happy.

The sheep is happy too. It sits on the sofa. It has its wool. It does not quarrel. Baa!

Once upon a time, there was a big party. Everyone was happy and having fun. They were there to celebrate a special day. It was a day when the sun shone bright and the birds sang sweetly.

The party was held outside in a huge park. There were lots of people and lots of food. Kids were playing games and laughing. Suddenly, it started to get dark. But then, someone turned on a light. It was a huge light that shone brightly on everyone.

The light made everyone happy again. They danced and sang under the light. It was a special moment that they would never forget. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Mint who was very troubled. Everywhere she went, she carried buckets and bags to collect things.

One day, Mint was walking in the park. She saw a beautiful feather and put it in her bucket. She noticed a pretty stone on the ground and added it to her collection. She even found a tiny shell and added it too!

Mint kept searching the park and came across a big apple tree. Its branches were full of apples. Mint reached up and picked one and put it in her bag. She ate the apple and felt so happy!

Mint kept looking around and finally found the most special item of all - a shiny silver coin! She put it in her collection and went home with a happy heart.

Mint now had a wonderful collection that she could look at and enjoy, and she was no longer troubled.

Once upon a time, there was a big, soft armchair. It lived in a house with a little girl named Amy. Amy loved to sit in the armchair and read books with her mom. The armchair was very flexible, so Amy could sit in many ways and still be comfy.

One day, Amy and her mom read a story about a race. The race was very long and had a big end. Amy wanted to have a race too. She asked her mom, "Can we race to the armchair and back?" Her mom said, "Yes, let's do it!"

Amy and her mom got ready to run. They raced as fast as they could. Amy was so quick, she got to the armchair first. But her mom was not far behind. They both laughed and sat in the armchair. They were happy and tired. The race had a fun end, and they enjoyed their time in the flexible armchair.

Bob was walking through the park one day and stumbled upon a pond. He saw a little boy swimming in it, but he appeared to be in trouble. Bob became very serious, he knew he had to help him.

"Hello, do you need help?", asked Bob.

The little boy was too shocked to reply.

Bob ran to the edge of the pond and scrambled in, not even thinking of his own safety. He swam to the little boy and grabbed his arm, holding him up above the water.

"It's okay, you're safe now!", said Bob with a big smile on his face.

The little boy, calmer now, smiled back. "Thank you! You are very brave".

Bob smiled, feeling very proud. He carried the boy out of the pond and they looked at each other, both with serious faces.

Bob knew that the little boy was safe now, but he was also aware of the importance of being careful when in water. He patted the boy's arm and promised him he wouldn't forget.

They both went on their way, with a newfound respect for each other.

Once upon a time, there was a tasty squirrel. He was a very small squirrel, but he was full of energy and brave.

One day, he decided to explore the world around him. He jumped from tree to tree and ran across the grass. Suddenly he heard a noise. He looked around, but he couldn't find out what it was.

Curious, he decided to investigate and see what he could find. He kept running until he arrived at a giant tree. It was so big that he had never seen anything like it before. Suddenly, he heard the noise again. He looked up and saw a big bird flying above him. He was so excited to see something new.

The squirrel watched the bird fly away, until he was too far away to be seen. The squirrel was happy and full of joy after his adventure and he ran back to his family. From then on, he always enjoyed exploring the world around him.

The end.

Bob, a 3 year old boy, wanted to play with his blocks. He started building a tower, but his sister Sarah came and knocked it down. Bob instantly felt bitter and shouted at her. Then, his mum stepped in, saying "Bob, Sarah is your sister and you should not be angry. Go kneel in the corner for a few minutes to think about what you did wrong".

Bob obediently kneeled in the corner, but he was still feeling bitter. Suddenly, he heard a loud sound from outside and noticed that his blocks had been blown away by a strong wind.

Bob quickly ran to the garden and found his blocks scattered everywhere. The wind was too strong and they had already been damaged. Bob realised his tower would never be built again.

Moral: Be kind to your siblings and cherish things before it is too late.

One day, a little cat was walking along the beach, when it saw something very strange in the distance. It looked like a big ship in the water! Pointing to the ship the cat ran towards it, hoping to get a closer look.

When the cat reached the ship, she noticed it looked pretty ordinary. It wasn't very big and there were no special features about it. But then, the cat heard a noise coming from inside the ship and was very curious to find out what it was!

Suddenly, the noise got louder and someone opened the door. It was a very grumpy looking pirate! The pirate yelled at the cat and started chasing after it. The little cat was terrified and started running away.

In the distance, the cat saw a tall tree and quickly ran up it. From the branches, the cat watched as the pirate circled the ship, looking for her. After some time, the pirate got tired and stopped searching, and the cat was able to climb down the tree and scamper away.

The cat went back home, having escaped the pirate and his ship safely. She had an adventure she would never forget!

Once upon a time, there was a small girl who liked to pretend. She hoped and wished for lots of fun.

One day, when she wanted to play dress up, she couldn't find her tie. She screamed, scrunched up her face, and jumped up and down. But no matter how loudly she yelled, her tie did not appear.

Suddenly, her mom came running in. She had a very compassionate look on her face. She wrapped her arms around the little girl, and asked her what was wrong. Carefully, she explained about how she needed her tie.

The mom smiled, and said "I'll help you look for it!" She rummaged through the dresser, and finally found the missing tie. She put it around the little girl's neck, and the girl smiled.

The mom thanked her for being brave and not giving up. Then, the two went to play dress up - even more fun than before!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Amy. She was very hungry. Her tummy felt funny and all she wanted was something yummy. So she went outside to look for something to eat.

As she walked, the sky grew dark and a storm began. Big rain drops started to fall and thunder clapped in the sky. Amy was scared and started to cry.

But then, she heard a voice from behind, saying "Amy, don't worry". When she looked back, she saw her Mommy. Her Mommy opened her umbrella and said, "Come here, I will squeeze you tight".

Amy felt much better when her Mommy held her. She knew she felt safe and loved in her Mommy's arms.

From that day on, Amy learned that when times were tough and the storm was scary, all she had to do was squeeze her Mommy and she would feel safe. This taught her that love was one of the most important things in life.

Lisa and Tom were moving to a new house with their mom and dad. They had many boxes to unpack and put in their rooms. Lisa liked to be organized and put her things in the right places. Tom liked to play and make messes.

"Can I help you unpack, Lisa?" Tom asked.

"Sure, but you have to be careful and not break anything," Lisa said.

Lisa gave Tom a box of books and showed him where to put them on the shelf. Tom tried to be helpful, but he was bored. He saw a roll of tape on the floor and had an idea. He took the tape and started to stick it on the books, the shelf, the wall, and even Lisa's hair.

"Tom, what are you doing?" Lisa shouted. "You are ruining my books and my room!"

Tom laughed and ran away with the tape. Lisa was angry and sad. She tried to pull the tape off, but it was hard and sticky. She cried and called for mom and dad.

Mom and dad came and saw the mess. They were not happy. They scolded Tom and made him apologize to Lisa. They also made him help Lisa clean up and unpack the rest of the boxes.

Tom learned his lesson. He realized that playing with tape was not fun, but mean and wasteful. He also learned that being organized was important and respectful. He said sorry to Lisa and hugged her. Lisa forgave him and thanked him for his help. They finished unpacking and made their rooms cozy and neat. They were happy and ready to enjoy their new house.

Once upon a time, there were two friends named Pete and Paul. Pete loved to race and always wanted to be the fastest. Paul thought Pete was too competitive and always wanted him to slow down.

One day, Pete saw a light shining in the distance. He told Paul about it, and they decided to go and explore. As they got closer, they saw it was a trophy of the biggest race in the world! Pete was overjoyed and told Paul he would enter the race and win the trophy.

Paul was worried and said it was too dangerous. He begged Pete to stay and said he didn't want him to get hurt. But Pete was determined and promised Paul he wouldn't get hurt.

Finally, the day of the race arrived. Pete was feeling nervous, but was determined to win the trophy. The race started and Pete ran as fast as he could as he heard Paul cheer him on. As Pete rounded the last corner, he could see the trophy waiting for him. He raced to the finish and won the trophy! Pete celebrated with Paul and they both agreed that Pete had done an amazing job.

Once upon a time, there were two friends named Joe and John. Joe was brave and always loved to dare to try new things.

One day, Joe saw a beehive in a tree near his house. He told John that he was daring enough to get some of the honey from the hive. John was scared, but Joe was determined.

Joe got some sticks and used them to climb the tree. It was hard, but with some help from John, Joe climbed to the top of the tree where the beehive was.

When Joe got to the beehive, the bees started to buzz angrily and some of them even tried to sting him. Joe was frustrated, but he kept trying to get some of the honey from the beehive.

Finally, after lots of hard work, Joe got some honey from the beehive. He was so proud of himself for being brave and daring enough to do it.

Joe and John enjoyed the honey and were happy to have been able to get it. From then on, Joe was always daring enough to try new things.

Once upon a time, there was a little mole who lived underground. He loved to dig tunnels and find yummy worms to eat. One day, he found a big stick and decided to play with it. He ran around with the stick in his mouth and accidentally dropped it near a big fire. The stick caught on fire and started to burn!

The little mole was scared and didn't know what to do. He ran back to his underground home and told his family about the fire. They all quickly ran outside to see what was happening. The fire was getting bigger and bigger, and the little mole knew they had to do something.

Luckily, the little mole's dad was very fit and strong. He grabbed a bucket of water and poured it on the fire. The fire started to sizzle and eventually went out. The little mole and his family were safe and sound. From that day on, the little mole learned to be careful with fire and never played with sticks near it again.

Once upon a time, there was a delicate stick. The stick felt bad because it was very plain.

One day, the stick decided to try and improve. So, it began to wiggle and twist. Slowly, it became more pretty and strong.

The stick kept practising until it was very strong and sturdy. People began to admire the delicate stick. It was so pleased with itself!

Soon, the stick was part of interesting stories and events. Whenever someone needed help, they would come to the stick for advice.

The stick was so pleased with itself for making such an improvement. It had gone from being plain to a star. It was happy and will always remember to keep practising and improving.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to dance around her room and twirl in her pretty dress. One day, her mommy told her she had an exam at school. Lily didn't know what an exam was, but she knew it sounded scary.

On the day of the exam, Lily was feeling very clumsy. She tripped on her shoelaces and dropped her pencil. She felt like she couldn't do anything right. But then, her teacher told her to take a deep breath and try her best.

Lily remembered how she loved to dance and decided to dance in her head while she took the exam. She felt happy and confident. When the exam was over, she got a good grade! Her mommy was proud of her and told her that even when things are tough, it's important to keep trying and believe in yourself.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who loved chocolate. Every day after school she'd go to the shop and buy some.

One day she was so excited to buy some chocolate that she forgot her money. She stood at the shop door and started to cry.

"What's wrong, honey?" asked the shopkeeper.

"I forget my money," she said.

The shopkeeper was kind and gave the little girl a weak smile. He said, "Don't worry. I'll give you a bar of chocolate, but next time remember to bring your money!"

The little girl was so excited, she thank the shopkeeper and ran off with her chocolate. From that day on, she always remembered to bring her money to the shop.

Ben and Lily love to play at the park. They like to swing, climb and run. But their favorite thing is to slide. They slide down the big slide, the small slide and the twisty slide. They laugh and shout as they go fast.

One day, they find a peanut on the ground near the slide. They wonder who left it there. Maybe a squirrel or a bird. They decide to share it. Ben breaks it in half and gives one part to Lily. They both eat it and say yum.

But then, they feel itchy in their mouths. Their tongues feel big and their throats feel tight. They are scared and sad. They run to their mom and dad, who are sitting on a bench. They show them the peanut shell and cry.

Mom and dad see the peanut and know what is wrong. They are quick and smart. They give Ben and Lily some medicine from their bag. They call for help and wait for the ambulance. They hug Ben and Lily and tell them it will be okay.

Ben and Lily go to the hospital with mom and dad. The doctor and nurse check them and give them more medicine. They say they are allergic to peanuts. That means peanuts make them sick. They tell them to never eat peanuts again. They give them a bracelet that says "no peanuts".

Ben and Lily feel better after a while. They are glad they are safe and loved. They are also very tired. They fall asleep in their beds, holding hands. They dream of playing at the park again. But they do not dream of peanuts. They dream of slides.

One great year, two friends were out for a walk. As they walked, they began to talk. One of them mentioned how the sky was so blue and the birds were singing so sweetly. The other one mentioned how the trees were so green and the sun was so warm.

The two friends kept walking and began to talk about the things they wanted to do. One of them mentioned how they wanted to go to the park and play with their friends. The other one mentioned how they wanted to get lots of ice cream and go to the zoo.

They both thought it would be a great year and the plans they had would certainly make it special. So they kept walking and talked about all the great things they wanted to do together.

Tom and Lily were at the beach with their mom and dad. They liked to play in the sand and splash in the water. They saw a big boat with a funny name: Ancient Shark. They asked their dad what it meant.

"It's a boat that looks for old things under the sea. Things that were there a long time ago, before we were born. Like pots and coins and bones. They are called ancient things," dad explained.

"Can we go on the boat, dad? Please?" Tom and Lily begged.

"Sorry, kids. The boat is not for visitors. It's only for people who work there. They have special tools and machines to find the ancient things. Like this one," dad pointed to a hose that was attached to the boat. "It can spray water very hard and make the sand move away."

Tom and Lily were curious. They wanted to see how the hose worked. They waited until dad was busy talking to mom and sneaked to the boat. They climbed on the deck and found the hose. Tom turned the knob and the hose started to spray water everywhere.

"Wow, this is fun!" Tom shouted.

"Be careful, Tom! You might break something!" Lily warned.

But Tom did not listen. He sprayed the water at the boat, at the sand, at the sky. He sprayed the water at a big metal box that was on the boat. The box had a lock on it, but the water was so strong that it broke the lock and opened the box.

Inside the box, there was something that made Tom and Lily scream. It was a big, gray, scary shark. It had sharp teeth and a fin. It was not alive, but it looked very real. It was an ancient shark that the boat people had found under the sea.

"Help! Help!" Tom and Lily cried.

The boat people heard them and ran to the deck. They saw the hose, the box, and the shark. They were very angry.

"What are you doing here? How did you get on the boat? Do you know how much this shark is worth? It's a rare fossil! You could have damaged it!" one of them yelled.

Tom and Lily were very sorry. They did not mean to cause trouble. They just wanted to see the hose. They apologized to the boat people and ran back to their dad and mom. They told them what happened and promised to never go on the boat again.

Dad and mom were not happy. They scolded Tom and Lily for being naughty and dangerous. They said they had to respect other people's work and property. They said they had to be more careful and listen to them.

Tom and Lily felt bad. They learned their lesson. They said they were sorry and hugged their dad and mom. They decided to play in the sand and splash in the water instead. They did not want to see the ancient shark ever again.

John went to the market one day with his mom. He saw a beautiful blue kite that he really wanted. His mom told him he couldn't have it, but he wouldn't listen. He was too excited and ran to the kite to grab it.

Suddenly, a tough foot stepped on the kite. John was scared and turned around. There was a big man with a mean look on his face. “Mommy,” John said, scared.

The man said, “I run the market and I won’t provide for any children running around and taking things that don’t belong to them.” John was still scared and backed away slowly.

His mom told the man she was sorry and would pay for the kite. But the man said it was too late and he wanted John to learn a lesson. He told John to never take things that don't belong to him again, and he made John leave the market.

John and his mom had a bad ending that day. He never got the kite and he was reminded to never take things that weren't his.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved going to the theater with her mommy and daddy. They would watch plays and musicals together. One day, they went to see a play about a little mouse who wanted to be a chef. The mouse cooked yummy food and everyone in the theater loved it.

After the play, Lily's mommy asked her, "Did you like the play, Lily?" Lily nodded her head and said, "Yes, mommy! I want to cook yummy food like the little mouse." Her daddy smiled and said, "That's a great idea, Lily. You can be anything you want to be if you work hard enough."

As they were leaving the theater, Lily saw the actors coming out. She clapped her hands and said, "Good job! Good job!" Her mommy explained to her that clapping is a way to applaud and show appreciation for someone's hard work.

The moral of the story is that if you work hard and follow your dreams, you can be anything you want to be. And it's always important to show appreciation for others' hard work by applauding them.

Once upon a time, there was a ship in the sea. It was a beautiful ship, with tall masts and lots of colored sails.

One day, three small children with their dog climbed on board the ship. They were so happy and excited!

“Look at all the birds flying above us!” one of them said.

“Let's explore the ship!” said another one.

The children and their dog explored the ship, but they had to be careful. “It's not safe for us here,” said one of the children.

Then suddenly, the ship began to move quickly. The children were scared, so they quickly looked for a safe place to hide.

The dog found the safest place - a big box in the middle of the room. “Let’s hide in here,” he said.

So they all climbed inside the big box and stayed there until the ship stopped moving.

When the ship stopped, the children and the dog came out of their hiding place. They were so relieved that they were safe!

The children thanked their dog for being so careful and taking them to a safe place.

They all looked back at the ship and smiled. “That was an adventure we will never forget!” one of them said.

Lily and Ben were playing in the snow. They made a big snowman with a hat and a scarf. They had fun throwing snowballs at each other. But then they saw a big dog coming towards them. The dog had sharp teeth and a loud bark. It looked fierce.

"Run, Lily, run!" Ben shouted. He was scared of the dog. He thought the dog wanted to bite them.

But Lily did not run. She stayed calm and smiled at the dog. She said, "Hello, doggy. Do you want to play with us? You look cold and hungry. We have some cocoa and cookies at home. Do you want to come with us?"

The dog stopped barking. It wagged its tail and licked Lily's hand. It was not fierce. It was lonely and cold. It wanted to be friends.

Lily and Ben took the dog home. They gave it some cocoa and cookies. They named it Snowy. They played with it and cuddled it. They asked their mom if they could keep it. Their mom said yes, as long as they took good care of it.

Lily and Ben were happy. They learned that sometimes, the best way to deal with a scary situation is to be kind and suggest a solution. They also learned that you can't judge a book by its cover, or a dog by its bark. They made a new friend and had a warm and cozy winter.

Emily was a three year old girl who loved to swim. Her parents took her to the pool to practice her swimming every week.

"Are you ready to go swimming?" asked her mother. Emily was so excited. She jumped up and down and smiled.

At the pool, Emily put on her swimsuit. It was pink and comfortable. Her mother helped her into the water. Emily liked feeling the cool water on her skin.

She asked her mother to play a game. "Let's pretend I can swim to the other side of the pool," Emily said. Her mother smiled and said, "Sure, why not".

Emily took a deep breath and jumped into the water. She was a strong swimmer and she was soon at the other side of the pool. She was so proud of herself.

Her mother said, "Great job, Emily. You swam so fast!" Emily smiled and said, "Can I swim back now?" Her mother said, "Of course, you can!"

Emily jumped back in the water. She felt so comfortable swimming and made it back to her mother easily.

When she was done, Emily said, "Let's go swimming again tomorrow!" Her mother smiled and said, "Of course, we will!"

And so, Emily and her mother kept swimming every week, and had lots of fun in the water.

Once upon a time, there was a cute little squirrel who loved to swing from the branches of trees. His name was Spike. Every day, Spike would swing from tree to tree in the park and look for something yummy to eat.

One day, he spotted a big delicious nut on a branch. He quickly ran over and began to swing to get closer to it. Suddenly, he heard someone call out, "Stop! Don't take that nut!"

Spike looked around and saw a little boy standing nearby. The boy said, "That nut belongs to me. I planted it here. Please don't take it!"

Spike thought for a moment and then smiled. He said to the boy, "OK! I won't take your nut if you will swing with me. What do you say?" The little boy smiled and replied, "Yes, I'd love to swing with you!"

So the two of them swung together for the rest of the day, having lots of fun in the park.

One day, Jenny looked into her closet. She couldn't believe it! Everything was a different color. Her clothes were colorful! What a change from the boring hangers she usually saw.

Jenny smiled. She grabbed red hangers and hung up all her bright clothes. Before she knew it, her closet was even more colorful than before.

After that, Jenny went over to her mom's closet. She found some plain hangers there. She put them in her mom's closet and filled them up with colorful clothes. Now the closet was even more magical!

Jenny was so happy with her new colorful closet that she danced around in circles. When she was done, she looked at her closet one last time and said, "What a change!"

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved playing with clay. He would make all sorts of things like animals and cars. Timmy's friends would come over to play, but they would always break his clay creations. Timmy would get upset and cry.

One day, a wise old man saw Timmy crying. The old man asked Timmy what was wrong. Timmy told the old man about his friends breaking his clay creations. The old man said, "Timmy, you should not be angry at your friends. They are ignorant of how much time and effort you put into your clay creations. Instead, you should teach them how to make their own clay creations. That way, they will admire your work and appreciate it more."

Timmy listened to the old man and taught his friends how to make clay creations. They all had fun and admired each other's work. Timmy learned that it's better to teach others than to get angry at them. The end.

Once upon a time, there was an old man. He lived in a house near a busy road with lots of traffic. The old man liked to sit on his porch and watch the cars and trucks go by. One day, a little boy came to visit him. The boy asked the old man what he liked to do. The old man said he liked to study things. The little boy asked what he was studying, and the old man said he was studying the traffic. The little boy thought that was very interesting and sat with the old man to watch the traffic too. They sat there for a long time, watching the cars and trucks go by. The little boy had fun spending time with the old man and learning about traffic.

Once upon a time, there was a human who was very bad. He was so bad, that no one wanted to be around him. One day, he wanted to get back at everyone so he decided to throw something. He threw a rock at a window and the glass broke, making a terrible noise. The noise scared everyone and they all ran away. The human realized that he had made a terrible mistake and felt bad. He apologized to everyone and said he would never throw something again. Everyone forgave him and they all started getting along again. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Max. He was very lucky. One day, Max was walking in the park and he saw a rainbow in the sky. He was so excited. He screamed in delight.

Max ran over to the rainbow and he saw a magical pot of gold beneath it. He was so happy. He picked up the pot of gold and started shouting with joy. He was very lucky! Suddenly, it started to rain. Max screamed again, this time from surprise. He grabbed the pot of gold and ran home. Back at home, Max kept the pot of gold safely under his bed. Every day he dreamed of rainbows, and of being lucky enough to find another one.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She wanted to sit on a comfortable chair, but all the chairs in her house were hard and not cozy. So, she asked her mommy if they could order a new chair that is soft and comfortable.

Lily's mommy went online and found a chair that was just perfect for her little girl. It was pink and fluffy, and Lily was so excited when it arrived. She sat on it and it was so comfortable that she didn't want to get up.

From that day on, Lily sat on her new chair every day, and it made her so happy. She was grateful that her mommy ordered it for her because she finally had a chair that was cozy and soft. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved ice cream very much. One day, she went to the ice cream shop with her mom. She saw many flavors of ice cream on the menu. She wanted to try them all!

Lily said to the lady at the ice cream shop, "Can I have a scoop of strawberry ice cream, please?" The lady said, "Sure, I will print it for you." Lily was confused but then she saw the lady put a scoop of strawberry ice cream on a cone.

Lily took a lick of the ice cream and said, "Wow, this is great!" Her mom smiled and said, "I'm glad you like it, Lily." They sat down and enjoyed their ice cream together. It was a very happy day!

Lily and Tom were playing in the park. They liked to pretend they were famous people. Lily was a singer and Tom was a king. They had a lot of fun.

"Look at me, I am the king of the world!" Tom said. He wore a paper crown and a cape. He sat on a bench and waved to the birds and the flowers.

"You are a great king, Tom. I admire you very much," Lily said. She wore a dress and a necklace. She sang a song for Tom and the park.

"Thank you, Lily. You are a wonderful singer. I admire you too," Tom said. He clapped his hands and smiled.

They were happy and proud of each other. They played until it was time to go home. They hugged and said goodbye.

"See you tomorrow, Tom. You are my best friend," Lily said.

"See you tomorrow, Lily. You are my best friend too," Tom said.

They went home with their moms. They had a good day. They dreamed of being famous.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lily. She loved to play outside and skip around. One day, Lily went to the ocean with her family. She loved the sound of the waves and the feeling of the wet sand on her feet.

Lily wanted to skip across the ocean, but her parents told her it was too dangerous. She didn't listen and ran into the water. Suddenly, a big wave knocked her down and she couldn't get back up.

Her parents tried to save her, but it was too late. Lily had drowned in the ocean. Her family was very sad and missed her very much. They wished she had listened to them and stayed safe on the shore.

Jamie was a cheerful 3 year old girl who liked to bake with her mom. Every morning, they would go to the kitchen and get the ingredients they needed. Jamie would mix the flour, sugar and eggs while mom prepared the pans and preheated the oven. Then they would pour the mix into the pans and bake the port together.

When the port was done, mom and Jamie took it out of the oven. The sweet smell of freshly baked port filled the house and made Jamie's tummy rumble. She couldn't wait to try it!

Jamie and her mom put the port on a plate and added some butter, jam and cream. Then they sat down for breakfast with dad. Jamie took one bite and smiled. The port was delicious! Then she took another big bite and kept smiling.

Jamie was so excited to have made the port with her mom that day. She was so cheerful and proud – she could barely believe it!

Billy was walking in the park with his mom. He saw something that made him stop and smile. It was a zipper! He asked his mom what it was and she said it was a toy. He liked it, so he reached out to touch it.

Suddenly, he heard something. It was a loud noise! He looked around and saw a Deaf man who was tapping the zipper with his fingers. The noise was coming from the zipper.

Billy's mom smiled and told him that the Deaf man was using the zipper as an instrument. Billy watched as the man continued to touch the zipper, creating a beautiful sound. Billy thought it was awesome.

Billy decided he wanted to try touching the zipper like the Deaf man. He asked his mom if he could and she said yes. Billy stepped closer and started tapping the zipper with his fingers. He was amazed at how he could make the same noise as the Deaf man.

He touched the zipper over and over again, creating a wonderful sound with every touch.

Once there was a bear called Bob. He loved to shake furniture. He would shake chairs, tables and couches. He loved making them wobble.

One day, Bob had a great idea. He decided to ask his friend, Sammy, to help him make the furniture more reliable. Sammy was a very clever rabbit.

Bob asked Sammy: "Can you help me make the furniture more reliable?". Sammy thought for a while and then said: "Yes, I can try!"

So, Bob and Sammy worked together. They put all the furniture pieces in different positions and then they tightened up all the screws. Finally, Bob and Sammy stepped back and admired their work. It looked much more reliable.

They were both very happy with their achievement. From then on, Bob’s furniture was always reliable, no matter how much he shook it.

Once there was a beetle who wanted to create something special. He flew around the garden looking for something he could use.

Suddenly he saw a peaceful pond and he decided this was the perfect place to make something special. He gathered the stones, the leaves and sticks and made himself a lovely home.

But then a mean spider came along. It did not like the idea that the beetle had created something so beautiful. It wanted to stop him and make him leave.

The beetle was scared, but he bravely stood his ground. He waved his antennae and made some special noises that the spider did not like. The spider ran away and the beetle was left in peace.

The beetle was very happy that he had been brave and was now able to live peacefully in his new home.

Once upon a time there was a small boy called Tom. Each day he went to school and each day he was very happy. In the morning he would have breakfast, and in the afternoon he always had a yummy lunch.

One day, Tom was so excited for lunch. He ran out of the classroom and headed for the lunch room. But when he got there, something strange was happening. Lots of other children were applauding!

Tom looked around and saw that the lunch room was very messy. The floor was dirty and there were half-eaten sandwiches everywhere. Tom had never seen it like this before.

Tears started to form in Tom’s eyes. He realised that the children were applauding because they had made a huge mess, and were happy that the lunch room was so dirty.

Tom didn’t want to be like them. He wanted to be the type of person who always respects their surroundings.

The moral of the story is that it’s important to stay respectful, tidy up your mess and never applaud dirtiness.

Once upon a time there was a poor boy. He lived in a small house and had very few toys. But he was happy, until one day he was told he had to move away.

He went to the wild and he was scared but he went anyways. He arrived at a big and tall mountain and he heard the birds singing. He took a deep breath, but then he heard something else.

It was a voice - it was an old man. The old man told him that he was looking for help. He said he was looking for someone strong and brave. The poor boy said he was brave and he wanted to help.

The old man was happy and he told the poor boy about a quest. He said the boy had to find a magical dragon and that the dragon would be able to help him.

The poor boy was scared but he believed the old man. He set off on his journey, determined to find the dragon.

And that's the end of the story!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily loved to travel with her family. One day, they went to a restaurant and Lily got a menu. She looked at all the pictures and pointed to what she wanted to eat.

Lily's mom said, "Let's make sure to keep our table tidy." Lily nodded and used her napkin to wipe her mouth. Suddenly, Lily's dad got a call from work and had to leave.

Lily asked her mom, "Where did daddy go?" Her mom replied, "Daddy had to go to work. But don't worry, we can still have fun and enjoy our meal together." Lily smiled and continued to look at the menu. She was excited to try something new and travel to different countries through the food she was going to eat.

Once there was a boy who wanted to move. He wanted to explore outside and see what he could find. He moved towards the backyard and found a big, open space. He excitedly moved around the space, feeling the grass and the sunshine on his skin.

Then the boy found the pitch. It was wide and long and he couldn't wait to move around it. He moved around the pitch, running and turning and laughing. Soon he was too tired to move anymore.

He felt safe as he sat down in the middle of the pitch. No one was around and he felt very special, like a king sitting in the middle of his palace. All around him was the sound of nature, the birds and the trees. It was so peaceful that he fell asleep.

When they boy woke up, he felt so safe and content. He had moved and explored until he felt ready to rest, and now he was ready to move onto the next adventure.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy who loved to ride his bike. He had a special gear on his bike that helped him go very fast. One day, Timmy was riding his bike down a big hill when he saw a big rock in the middle of the road. Timmy tried to turn, but he lost control and fell off his bike.

Timmy was very scared and his bike was broken. But he remained strong and didn't cry. His mom came to help him and they fixed his bike together. Timmy was happy to have his bike back and he promised to be more careful when riding it. From that day on, Timmy always checked his gear before riding his bike and he never had another accident again. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a big jungle with many animals. One day, a kind man came to the jungle and gave all the animals some food. He provided them with bananas, apples, and carrots. The animals were very happy and thanked the man.

In the jungle, there was a parrot who loved to sing and talk. He was very loud and could be heard from far away. One day, the man heard the parrot singing and he thought it was very beautiful. He decided to take the parrot with him and bring him to his home.

The parrot was very happy to go with the man, but he missed his friends in the jungle. So, the man decided to bring the parrot back to the jungle and let him live with his friends. The parrot was grateful to the man for providing him with a home and for bringing him back to his friends. From that day on, the parrot sang even louder and all the animals in the jungle were happy to hear him.

Lily and Ben were playing in the garden. They liked to dig in the dirt and find bugs and stones. They had a big bucket to put their treasures in. They were very happy.

But then they saw a big, shiny box near the fence. It had a lock on it and a sign that said "Do not open". Lily and Ben were curious. They wanted to see what was inside the box. Maybe it was a toy or a cake or a surprise.

"Let's open it!" said Lily. She ran to the box and tried to pull the lock. But it was too hard. She could not open it.

"No, Lily, we can't!" said Ben. He was scared. He remembered that Mommy and Daddy told them to never open things that were not theirs. And the sign said "Do not open". Maybe there was something bad or dangerous inside the box. "We have to resist, Lily. We have to listen to Mommy and Daddy."

But Lily did not listen to Ben. She was stubborn. She wanted to open the box. She found a stick and tried to break the lock. She hit the lock with the stick. But the stick broke. She found another stick and tried again. She hit the lock harder and harder.

Suddenly, the lock snapped. The box opened. Lily and Ben looked inside. They gasped. There was nothing but filthy garbage inside the box. Rotten food, dirty diapers, old cans, and smelly socks. It was disgusting. It made them feel sick.

"Yuck!" said Lily. She dropped the stick and ran away from the box. She wished she had not opened it.

"See, Lily, I told you we shouldn't open it!" said Ben. He followed Lily and hugged her. He was glad they were not hurt. He hoped Mommy and Daddy would not be angry.

They ran back to their bucket and played with their bugs and stones. They forgot about the box and the garbage. They were happy again.

Once upon a time there lived a small boy who loved to play outside. One day, he and his mom were playing in the park, when suddenly, the sky turned dark.

"Mommy," the little boy said, pointing to the sky, "What's that?"

"That's thunder," his mother replied. "It's a strong sound that comes from the sky."

The little boy looked up in awe, as his mom held his hand. Then, a loud burst of thunder filled the air, and the little boy held on to his mom even tighter.

He was scared, but his mother reassured him by saying "It's ok. Everything will be clean again soon."

The little boy struggled to hold back his tears, as his mom hugged him tight and said "I'm here to help you. You can do it!"

The thunder continued to crash and rumble in the sky, but the little boy stayed brave and calm with the help of his mom's love. Soon, the storm passed, and the sky became clean again.

The little boy smiled and hugged his mom. "Thank you for helping me, mommy," he said.

His mother smiled and ruffled his hair. "You're so brave," she said. "I'm proud of you."

Once upon a time, there was a chubby bird named Bob. Bob liked to dive and fly in the sky. He had a lot of friends who liked to play with him.

One day, while Bob was diving, he saw a big bin. The bin was full of yummy food. Bob wanted to eat the food, so he went to the bin and looked inside.

Bob ate and ate until he was very full. His friends came and they all ate from the bin too. They were so happy and they played together all day. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a bedroom with a big bed and a window. One day, it rained a lot and her bedroom floor got wet. Lily did not like wet floors, so she went to her mom and said, "Mommy, my bedroom is wet. Can you make it dry?" Her mom said, "Of course, Lily. I will put a towel on the floor to make it dry." Lily smiled and said, "Thank you, Mommy. You always accept my requests."

Once upon a time, there lived a family with two children, a boy and a girl. The boy's name was Sam and the girl's name was Jane.

One day, the family decided to make pancakes. Sam ran to the kitchen and grabbed the butter. In one hand he had the butter, and in the other hand was a bottle of syrup. Sam was excited to pour the syrup on the pancakes.

Jane asked, "What did you get, Sam?" Sam smiled and said, "I got butter and syrup."

Mom smiled and said, "That's great, Sam. Now let me give you a spoon so you can help me make the pancakes." She gave him a spoon and Sam helped to spread the butter on the pancakes.

They all worked together and made the best pancakes. They were fit for a king.

After having their delicious pancakes, the family was very happy and full.

Once upon a time, there was a dad and his son. The dad's name was Adam and the son's name was Jack. Each day, Adam and Jack would go to the park.

One day, after playing at the park, Adam said to Jack, "It's time to go home now, Jack. We must go and bathe".

Jack was excited! He loved having a bath. He ran up to his dad, smiled and said, "Yay! Bath time!"

Adam and Jack went home and took a bath together. Adam got out of the bath first and Jack continued to play in the water.

Adam looked at Jack and laughed. "Look at your face," he said. It's all soapy and wide!

Jack touched his face and laughed too. A wide face was funny!

Adam and Jack got dressed, dried their hair and cuddled up together on the sofa. They were happy and clean now.

Once upon a time, there was a little bird. The bird loved to sing all day long. One day, the bird flew to a garden and saw a big pepper. The pepper was so red and shiny that the bird wanted to sing a song for it. So the bird started to sing a happy song.

Suddenly, a bee came and hurt the bird. The bird felt sad and scared. But then, the bird remembered the pepper and started to sing again. The singing made the bird feel better and forget about the hurt. From that day on, the bird went to the garden every day to sing for the pepper and feel happy again.

Once upon a time, there was a small bird with soft feathers. He dreamed of flying high up where the wind was very mild. He flapped his wings every day, but he couldn't seem to get very far.

One day, he decided to try something new. Gently, he grabbed a feather from his soft wings. Then he held it tightly in his beak and closed his eyes.

He dreamed of soaring through the clouds and flapping his wings with ease. Suddenly, he felt himself rising high into the sky. The wind was mild and he felt the sun on his wings.

He flew around until the sun began to set. When he finally reached the ground, he tucked the feather back between his wings and smiled. Now, he knew he could trust his dreams.

Once there was a foolish man who loved to raise animals in his backyard. He wanted to have a big farm with lots of animals. The man had an oak tree in his backyard. He decided to raise pigs under the tree.

The man made a fence around the tree and filled it with pigs. The pigs were so happy in their new home that they started making a lot of noise. Every morning, the neighbors heard the animals squealing and grumbling.

The neighbors were so mad that they asked the man to find a new home for the pigs. But the foolish man refused.

One day, the neighbors got so angry that they decided to cut down the oak tree. The tree fell and all the animals were killed. The foolish man was very sad and never raised animals again.

Tom and Lily were playing with their toy cars in the living room. They liked to make noises and pretend they were driving fast. Tom had a red car and Lily had a blue car. They had a lot of fun.

But then, Tom saw a shiny yellow car on the shelf. He wanted to play with it too. He asked his mom if he could have it. "Please, mom, can I have the yellow car?" he requested. His mom looked at him and said, "No, Tom, you can't have the yellow car. It is broken. It doesn't move. It was your dad's car when he was little. He likes it very much. You have to be careful with it."

Tom was sad. He really wanted the yellow car. He thought it was the best car ever. He didn't care if it was broken. He tried to reach for it, but it was too high. He looked at Lily and had an idea. He said, "Lily, can you help me get the yellow car? You are taller than me. You can stand on the chair and grab it. Please, Lily, help me."

Lily looked at Tom and then at the yellow car. She liked the yellow car too. It was shiny and pretty. She wanted to play with it as well. She said, "OK, Tom, I will help you. But you have to share it with me. We can take turns." Tom agreed. He said, "OK, Lily, we can share it. But you have to be quick. Mom might see us."

Lily nodded. She climbed on the chair and reached for the yellow car. She was careful not to drop it. She gave it to Tom and got down. Tom was happy. He held the yellow car in his hands and smiled. He said, "Thank you, Lily. You are a good sister. Here, you can have it first." He gave the yellow car to Lily and watched her play with it. He waited for his turn.

But then, mom came back. She saw Tom and Lily with the yellow car. She was angry. She said, "Tom, Lily, what are you doing with the yellow car? I told you it was broken. I told you it was dad's car. You are not supposed to touch it. You could have hurt yourself or damaged it. Give it back to me right now."

Tom and Lily were scared. They knew they were in trouble. They gave the yellow car back to mom and said, "Sorry, mom. We just wanted to play with it. We didn't mean to be bad." Mom took the yellow car and put it back on the shelf. She said, "I know you like the yellow car, but you have to respect dad's things. He loves the yellow car very much. It reminds him of his childhood. It is not a toy. It is a memory. You have to ask before you take something that is not yours. Do you understand?"

Tom and Lily nodded. They said, "Yes, mom, we understand. We are sorry. We won't do it again." Mom hugged them and said, "I love you, Tom and Lily. But you have to be more careful and listen to me. Now, go back to your toy cars and play nicely. And don't forget to share." Tom and Lily said, "We love you too, mom. And we will share." They went back to their toy cars and played together. They forgot about the yellow car. They had fun with their red car and blue car. They were happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who loved being outdoors. She loved learning about all of the different plants and animals and especially playing in the summer sunshine.

One day, she went out for a walk and spotted a peach tree. She was so excited to see all of the peaches growing on it.

Without hesitation, she ran up to the tree and looked around. She spotted a little peach at the very top, so she decided to see if she could reach it.

She stretched her arms up, but she just couldn't get it. Feeling discouraged, she walked away.

Just then, an kind old voice spoke to the girl. "Why don't you ask the peach if you can have it?"

The little girl was surprised. She turned around to see an old lady smiling at her.

The girl thought for a minute and then asked the peach if it was ok for her to take it.

To her surprise, the peach said yes!

The little girl was so excited. She quickly plucked the peach off the tree, thanked the kind old lady, and ran home with her little peach.

Once upon a time there was a little girl. She was curious and always wanted to discover new things. She loved to crawl around the garden. Everywhere she went, she wanted to know more. One day, she came to a dull wall. What was behind it? She had to find out. So she crawled closer and closer, until she found a big hole in the wall. Peeking through it, the little girl's eyes glowed with wonder. On the other side of the wall, there was an amazing garden. The little girl smiled with delight. She crawled through the hole and spent the whole day playing in the gorgeous garden. She was so happy!

Once there was a gray beetle. She wanted to go on an adventure. So, she got up and started walking. She walked and walked until she came to a big green hill. It was so big she couldn't see the top. The beetle was excited and started to climb the hill. She climbed and climbed until she got to the top. From the top she could see for miles and miles. But the most exciting thing she saw was a big lake. The beetle jumped off the hill and ran to the lake. When she got there she could see all kinds of different beetles in the water. She said hello to them, and then she jumped in.

The beetle had so much fun swimming and playing with the other beetles. When it started to get dark, she got out of the lake and began to walk home. As she walked she thought of all the wonderful things she had seen and done.

The beetle was so happy she had been brave enough to get up and go on an adventure.

Once upon a time, there were five friends who were playing in the garden. They decided to have a contest to see who could find the most interesting thing.

Bob found a weird herb and showed it to his friends. They all thought it was so cool and couldn't believe what he had found.

Then Joe said, "Let's have a number contest. I bet I can find the most things." So they started counting things around the garden. Joe saw five birds, four trees, and seven flowers.

Then Lucy said, "I think I can find more. Let me try." She found nine bugs and twelve leaves. Joe and Lucy had the most things, so they were the winners!

The five friends had used their numbers to have a fun contest and were all very happy.

Once upon a time, a little girl named Lily went to her grandma's house. She saw a big red knob on the door and turned it to go inside. Her grandma was cooking something that smelled spicy.

Lily asked, "What are you making, grandma?"

"I'm making chili, it's a spicy soup that will excite your taste buds," her grandma replied.

Lily tasted the chili and said, "Wow, it's so spicy! Can I have some more?"

"Of course, my dear," her grandma said with a smile. "I'm glad you like it."

Lily ate the chili happily and they spent the rest of the day playing games and telling stories. When it was time to go home, Lily hugged her grandma and said, "Thank you for the yummy food and fun day. I'm excited to come back soon!"

Once upon a time there was a little boy called Timmy. He was three years old. Every day he would go out and ride his bike. One day he was out riding when he saw a newsboy. He had a big box with lots of papers in it. Timmy stopped his bike and asked the newsboy, "What are you carrying?" The newsboy replied, "I'm carrying newspapers. I'm taking them around to people's houses." Timmy said, "That looks like an uncomfortable job." The newsboy agreed and said, "It can be. But sometimes I get a free ride in a big van, so it's not so bad." Timmy smiled and said, "That sounds nice. I'm glad you get a comfortable ride too!" The moral of the story is that it is important to be thankful for the good things we have. Everyone should take the time to appreciate the small comforts in life!

Lily and Tom are poor. They live in a small house with their mom and dad. They do not have many toys or clothes. But they have a radio. The radio plays music and stories. Lily and Tom love to listen to the radio.

One day, the radio stops working. It makes a loud noise and then it is quiet. Lily and Tom are sad. They try to turn it on and off, but nothing happens. They ask their mom and dad to fix it, but they say they have no money to buy a new one.

Lily and Tom go to their neighbor, Mr. Lee. Mr. Lee is old and kind. He has many things in his garage. He likes to fix things. Lily and Tom knock on his door and ask him to help them.

"Hello, Lily and Tom. What can I do for you?" Mr. Lee says.

"Mr. Lee, our radio is broken. Can you fix it for us, please?" Lily says.

"Let me see. Where is your radio?" Mr. Lee says.

Lily and Tom bring their radio to Mr. Lee. He looks at it and shakes his head.

"I'm sorry, Lily and Tom. This radio is very old and damaged. I can't fix it. You need a new one." Mr. Lee says.

"But we have no money to buy a new one. We love our radio. It makes us happy." Tom says.

Mr. Lee thinks for a moment. He smiles and says, "I have an idea. Why don't you take this radio instead? It is newer and works well. I don't use it much. You can have it for free."

Lily and Tom look at the radio. It is bigger and nicer than their old one. It has many buttons and colors. They are happy and excited.

"Thank you, Mr. Lee. You are very nice. Can we take this radio?" Lily says.

"Of course, you can. It is yours now. Enjoy it." Mr. Lee says.

Lily and Tom hug Mr. Lee and thank him again. They take the radio and run back to their house. They plug it in and turn it on. It plays music and stories. Lily and Tom dance and laugh. They are happy. They have a new radio.

One day John went to visit his grandpa. Grandpa showed John something wide and modern. It was a big grey room with sparkling lights. Grandpa showed John a cool machine that made music. It moved and twirled and sang high and low. John clapped and smiled. Grandpa showed John a big far away screen. It showed videos of dogs playing and cars driving. John shouted with joy. Grandpa and John both laughed a lot. When it was time to go, Grandpa said goodbye and gave John a hug. John waved goodbye and promised to come back soon to show Grandpa something wide and modern.

Once there was a small child named Alex. Alex was only three years old. One day, Alex was walking through the forest with his Mom. Suddenly, Alex found himself in trouble! He had stepped on a twig and it had snapped, causing him to fall to the ground. He couldn't get up on his own.

Alex called for help. Fortunately, his Mom heard him and came running. She stopped and bent down beside him. She asked if he was OK and gave him a big hug. Alex felt safe and secure in his Mom's arms.

His Mom then reached out her hand and lent Alex a helping hand. She gently helped him get up again. Alex was so very thankful to his Mom for coming to his aid. He picked up the twig and showed it to his Mom. Alex was alright again and he was not helpless any more!

Molly went to see her friend. She was very excited! When she arrived she saw a big basket. It was full of cakes and biscuits. They looked very yummy and Molly wanted to eat one.

She asked her friend, "Can I have some?" Her friend said, "Yes, help yourself." Molly took a biscuit and she bit it. It was so tasty she wanted another one. She ate two more and a cup of tea.

Molly said, "The tea is very good and the biscuits were delicious!" Her friend smiled and said, "I'm glad you liked them."

Molly was full up and very happy. She went home and thought about her friend and the good tea and biscuits.

Lily and Ben are twins. They like to go on trips with Mom and Dad. Today, they are going to the zoo. They have to take the subway to get there.

The subway is a big train that goes under the ground. It makes a loud noise and goes very fast. Lily and Ben sit on the seats and look out the window. They see a lot of gray walls and tunnels.

"Where are the animals?" Lily asks.

"They are at the zoo, silly," Ben says. "We have to get off the subway first."

The subway stops at a station. Mom and Dad take Lily and Ben by the hand and lead them to the exit. They walk up the stairs and see the sun and the sky.

"Wow, look at that!" Ben points to a big sign that says "ZOO".

Lily and Ben are very excited. They run to the gate and show their tickets. Mom and Dad follow them.

Inside the zoo, there are many animals. Lily and Ben see lions, monkeys, elephants, and more. They hear them roar, chatter, and trumpet.

But their favorite place is the aquarium. There, they see fish of all colors and shapes. They swim in the water and make bubbles. Some fish are big and some are small. Some have stripes and some have spots.

Lily and Ben press their noses to the glass and watch the fish. They wish they could swim with them.

"Look, a starfish!" Lily says.

"Look, a shark!" Ben says.

They giggle and clap their hands. They have so much fun at the zoo. They love to see the animals, especially the ones that swim.

Once upon a time, there was a furry cat named Mittens. Mittens loved to play all day long with his toys, but sometimes he got tired. When he felt tired, he would go to his bed and rest.

One day, Mittens saw a big tank of water in the backyard. Mittens was curious and went to check it out. He saw some fish swimming inside the tank. Mittens thought the fish looked funny and he wanted to play with them.

But Mittens was tired from playing all day, so he decided to rest first. He curled up in a ball next to the tank and closed his eyes. As he rested, he dreamed of playing with the fish in the tank. When he woke up, he felt refreshed and ready to play again.

Lily was a big girl now. She was going to school for the first time. She was very happy and excited. She put on her new dress and shoes and packed her bag with her books and crayons.

"Are you ready, Lily?" her mom asked. "Let's go to the car and pick up your friend Anna. She is going to the same school as you."

"Yes, mom, I'm ready!" Lily said. She hugged her mom and ran to the car. She could not wait to see Anna and play with her.

They drove to Anna's house and saw her waiting outside with her dad. She was wearing a pink skirt and a yellow shirt. She had a big smile on her face.

"Hi, Lily! Hi, Lily's mom!" Anna said. She waved and ran to the car. She hugged Lily and sat next to her. "I'm so happy we are going to school together. We are going to have so much fun and learn many things."

"Hi, Anna! Hi, Anna's dad!" Lily said. She smiled and held Anna's hand. "Me too. I hope we have a nice teacher and make new friends."

They arrived at the school and saw many other kids and parents. They got out of the car and followed their moms to the classroom. They saw a sign that said "Welcome to Kindergarten!"

They entered the classroom and saw a lady with long brown hair and glasses. She was wearing a blue dress and a necklace. She had a friendly voice and a warm smile.

"Hello, everyone! I'm Miss Lee, your teacher. I'm so happy to see you all. You are going to have a successful year in kindergarten. You are going to learn how to read and write and count and draw and sing and play. You are going to make wonderful memories and have lots of fun. Come on, let's find your seats and get to know each other." Miss Lee said.

Lily and Anna looked at each other and smiled. They felt nervous and curious and excited. They walked to the table where their names were written and sat down. They saw some other kids sitting nearby and said hello. They felt happy and proud. They were big girls now. They were going to school.

Once upon a time, there was a little bird. The bird had a bright yellow wing. He loved to fly around and play with his friends. One day, he met a friendly rabbit who asked, "Do you want to play with me?"

The little bird replied, "Yes, I do! But my wing hurts."

The rabbit replied, "Don't worry, I know how to fix it. I have a special plant that can help you feel better."

The little bird was happy and followed the rabbit to a nearby field. The rabbit showed him a plant with bright green leaves. "This is the plant that can help you. It includes a special juice that can heal your wing."

The little bird drank the juice and felt better. He thanked the rabbit and flew away happily with his bright yellow wing. From that day on, the little bird and the rabbit became good friends and played together every day.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys all day long. One day, her mom asked her to clean up her toys, but Lily forgot. Her mom got mad and told her that forgetting is not good.

Later that day, Lily saw her friend Sarah playing with a perfect toy. She wanted it so badly that she asked Sarah if she could have it. Sarah said no, and Lily got upset. She told Sarah that she didn't like her anymore, but that wasn't the truth. Lily realized that it's not nice to lie and that the truth is always better.

Lily learned that forgetting and lying are not good things to do. She promised to always remember to clean up her toys and to tell the truth. From that day on, Lily became a better person and a better friend.
