Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved winter because he could play in the snow. One day, Timmy went outside to build a snowman. It was very cold outside and Timmy's fingers started to freeze.

When Timmy went inside, he saw his mom looking at the calendar. She was planning a party for Timmy's birthday. Timmy was so excited! He loved birthdays.

The next day, the weather was mild. Timmy went outside to play again. He saw his snowman had melted a little bit. Timmy was sad, but he knew he could build another one next winter.

Anna and Ben were playing in the park. They liked to run, swing and slide. But it was very hot and sunny. They felt thirsty and tired.

"Let's go to the big tree," Ben said. "It has shade. We can rest there."

"OK," Anna said. They ran to the big tree and sat under it. They felt cooler and happier.

They saw a bird's nest on a branch. It had three eggs inside. They were blue and speckled.

"Wow, look at the eggs!" Anna said. "They are so pretty."

"Yes, they are," Ben said. "But we should not touch them. They are delicate. The bird will be sad if we break them."

"I know," Anna said. "But I want to see them better. Can I remove this leaf? It is in the way."

"No, don't do that!" Ben said. "The leaf gives them shade. They need shade to stay cool and safe. If you remove the leaf, the sun will hurt them."

Anna listened to Ben. She did not remove the leaf. She smiled and said, "You are right, Ben. The leaf is good for them. Let's leave them alone. They are happy in their nest."

They got up and went to play some more. They were happy too. They had seen something beautiful and learned something new.

Once upon a time, there was a fish who wanted to go on an adventure. Her name was Spot. She swam to the edge of a big lake and looked around. It was very quiet. Suddenly, she heard a splash!

Spot swam closer. She was curious to see what was happening. As she got closer and closer, she spotted a little frog. He was making huge splashes in the water! Spot was so amused that she joined him, making big splashes too.

The frog said, "Hi, Spot! Let's have more fun!" They splashed and laughed together. Spot had the best time of her life!

When the sun started setting, Spot said goodbye to the frog. She swam away with a happy heart. Spot had made a new friend.

Mum and Dad were in the living room. Dad was holding a brown cup. Mum smiled and said, "Look, Dad has a cup of coffee". Dad smiled and started to explain. He said, "Coffee is a drink that tastes nice".

Mum and Dad then looked at the bald man on the TV. Dad said, "That man is bald - he doesn't have any hair". Mum nodded and said, "Yes, he is bald, but he still looks nice".

Mum and Dad finished their coffee and then went outside to play. The sun was shining and the birds were singing. It was a nice day and everyone was happy.

Once there was a girl called Jane. She was very polite and kind. One day, she wanted to help her Mom in the kitchen.

She went to the cupboard and found a plate. She was so excited and carried it to the kitchen table.

Suddenly, Jane heard her Mom calling her, "Jane honey, could you be a polite girl and carry the plate to the dining room?"

Jane smiled and said, "Yes Mommy, I can do that". She neatly carried the plate to the dining room, and put it on the table.

Jane's Mom hugged her and said, "Thank you sweetheart, you are such a good girl!" Jane was so pleased and could not stop smiling.

Once upon a time, there was a star that was very hungry. One day, it saw a crazy bug. The star decided to bite the bug. The bug jumped and tried to get away from the star, but the star chased it. The star was faster and eventually bit the bug hard. The bug flew away and the star had a full tummy. The end.

Once, there was a little girl named Emma. She was three years old and loved to play hide and seek.

One day she went to hide, but couldn't remember her number. She tried counting to 10 but then she got stuck. She sat on the stairs and started to miss her number.

Then grandma came over and heard Emma's story. She saw that Emma was sad, so she told her to look very carefully. Grandma said, "Look around and be clear. What number do you see?"

Emma looked around and there it was! Her number! She was so happy and she went out to play with her friends.

Grandma was very proud of Emma for looking so clearly and she smiled. Emma never forgot her number again!

Once there was a smart dog. His name was Zoom. He was very fast. Every day he ran and ran.

One day he was running in the yard when he hurt his paw. It was very painful. He cried and he hopped on three legs.

His mom was very worried. She picked him up and carried him inside. She kissed his hurt paw and made it feel better.

The next day Zoom was all better. He zoomed around the yard again. He didn't get hurt this time. He was happy and smart.

One day, Jack and his mom were walking together. Jack saw a big stair and wanted to try it out. As soon as he reached the top, he was so happy! But then he fell and broke it.

Jack started to cry. His mom was so sad too. Then she hugged him and said, "It's ok, Jack".

Then they both went to the store and bought some glue. Jack was so happy when he saw it! He quickly grabbed the glue and ran to the stair. He put the glue all over the stair, and fixed it.

Now the stair was as good as new. Jack and his mom were happy too!

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to count everything he saw. He counted the flowers in the garden, the birds in the sky, and even the cars on the road. He was very good at counting.

One day, Timmy went for a walk with his mommy. They walked past a big billboard with a picture of a happy family on it. Timmy pointed to the billboard and said, "Mommy, I want to count the people on the billboard."

Mommy smiled and said, "Okay, Timmy. Let's count together." They counted one, two, three, four, five people on the billboard.

Later that day, Timmy felt proud of himself for counting the people on the billboard. He knew he was good at counting and he couldn't wait to count more things in the future.

Once upon a time there was a little girl who was only three years old and she loved to explore. Every day she would venture out, looking for new things to discover.

One day she decided to try opening a door she had never opened before. She pushed it open and entered a room filled with all kinds of amazing items and objects. In the corner was something that looked like a soft bag; it had a belt around the middle and was something she had never seen before.

The little girl approached the bag and suddenly it opened. It was a bathrobe! The 3-year-old was so excited, she couldn't believe her eyes. She started trying it on, but she was so careless that the belt came undone and the bathrobe fell off her shoulders.

The girl noticed something written on the inside of the bathrobe. It said, “Remember to be careful.” The 3-year-old smiled and started to take more care with how she was putting the bathrobe on—just like the message said. The little girl was so proud of herself for being so careful. And that was the end of her adventure, and the start of a lovely friendship with her new bathrobe.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a blue dress that she loved to wear every day. One morning, Lily's mom asked her to help set the table for breakfast. Lily got a teaspoon and put it on the table.

As they ate their breakfast, Lily's mom said, "Lily, we are going to have a special guest today. Can you guess who it is?" Lily thought for a moment and said, "Is it my friend Emma?" Her mom smiled and said, "No, it's someone who loves to tie things up."

Lily didn't know who it could be, but she was excited to find out. After breakfast, there was a knock on the door. When they opened it, they saw Lily's grandpa standing there with a big bag of presents. He loved to tie ribbons around the presents to make them look pretty. Lily was so happy to see him and they spent the whole day playing together.

At the end of the day, Lily's grandpa gave her a present with a blue ribbon tied around it. Lily was so excited to open it and inside was a new dress that was even more beautiful than her old one. She hugged her grandpa and said, "Thank you for the present and for coming to visit me. I love you!"

Once upon a time, there was a big dog named Bobo. Bobo was very compassionate. He loved to help his friends. One day, his friend Sally the cat was in panic. Sally was going to a marriage party but she lost her pretty hat.

Bobo said, "Don't worry, Sally! I will help you find your hat." So, they looked everywhere for the hat. They looked in the house, in the yard, and even in the trees.

Finally, they found the hat under a big rock. Sally was so happy! She said, "Thank you, Bobo! You are a great friend!" Then, they went to the marriage party together and had lots of fun.

Once upon a time, there was a little white boat floating on the lake. The sun sparkled on the water, and the boat glided along.

Suddenly, the boat stopped and the little engine sputtered out some steam. The steam was so white, it seemed like clouds were flowing from the boat.

Out of the steam came a tall man. He waved his hands, and asked the boat, "What are you doing resting here?"

The boat said nothing. The man smiled and said, "Come on, let's keep going. I'm sure it will be a nice trip".

The boat hummed, and the engine started again. The man waved goodbye and the boat sailed away, leaving a white cloud of steam behind it.

The man had been glad to help the little white boat and show it the way. Now the boat was off to explore the world!

Once upon a time, there was a big and furry panda named Pandy. Pandy lived in a big zoo with lots of other animals. One day, a little girl named Lily came to visit the zoo with her mom.

Lily saw Pandy and said, "Wow! Look at that big furry panda!" Pandy heard Lily and turned to stare at her. Lily smiled and said, "Hi, Pandy! You're so cute!"

Pandy was happy to hear Lily's kind words. He said, "Thank you, Lily! Would you like to come closer and pet me?" Lily nodded her head and walked over to Pandy's enclosure. She reached out her hand and petted Pandy's soft and furry fur.

From that day on, Lily visited Pandy every time she came to the zoo. They became good friends and Pandy always looked forward to seeing Lily's smiling face.

Once upon a time, there was a little puppy who was very tired. He was feeling really sick, so his owner took him to the veterinarian.

When they entered the office, the puppy was scared. His owner tried to calm him, but he was still very confused. The veterinarian had all sorts of tools that she wanted to use - like a stethoscope and a thermometer. The puppy barked and cowered away.

The veterinarian was very nice, though. She talked to the pup in a gentle voice, and showed him all of the tools she was going to use. Then she patted him on the back and said 'It's okay. I just want to help you.'

The puppy calmed down and the veterinarian was able to check him out. After a few minutes, the veterinarian said that the puppy was going to be okay. The puppy's owner was so happy and thanked the veterinarian!

The veterinarian smiled and said 'He's a brave little pup. I'm sure he'll be fine.' Then they all went home to take a nap.

Once there was a thin rabbit. He wanted to find a place to put his new hat. He walked to the park and looked around. He could not find a good place to put it. Then he spotted a big tree with a big hole in the trunk. He thought it would be the perfect place, so he put his hat in the hole. It was just the right size.

The rabbit was happy with his decision. He danced around the tree singing and hopping. All of a sudden, he noticed something moving near his hat in the hole. He peered into the hole and saw a little mouse. The mouse was very thin too!

The rabbit said hello and the mouse said hello back. The rabbit asked the mouse if he wanted to be his friend. The mouse said yes! The rabbit asked the mouse if he wanted to put his hat too. The mouse thought for a few moments then said yes.

The two friends put their hats into the hole together and smiled. They were both so happy that they had found each other. They stayed there for many more days, playing together and putting little things in their hole. They were the best of friends!

The evening was regular and dark. But then, something magical happened. The sky started to glow. The glow was bright and beautiful. The whole sky was glowing in pinks and blues and yellows. Everyone stepped outside to look up and smile. The little girl couldn't take her eyes off the sky. She felt so happy and excited.

The glow was everywhere. It lit up the darkness and made the night look special. Birds flew up and sang with joy. Everyone was happy and smiling. The little girl hugged her mom and dad. They were laughing and singing and clapping.

The glow stayed in the sky all evening. Even after the sun set, the sky kept glowing until it was bedtime. Then, the glowing stars twinkled until everyone was safe in bed. What an amazing evening!

Once there was a lady who wanted to crawl. Every day she would go to the park and crawl around. She would crawl around the trees, and then to the playground. She was a regular crawler.

One day, while the lady was crawling, she saw a little boy. He was only 3 years old and playing in the sand. The lady smiled and crawled over to him. She offered to help him build a sandcastle and asked him what his name was.

The little boy said his name was Jack. He and the lady played together for a long time. Jack was so happy to have a friend to play with.

The lady and Jack crawled around the park together. They crawled around the pond and played hide-and-seek. They had so much fun. After a while, the lady said goodbye to Jack and crawled off into the sunset.

Once upon a time, there was a wide tree. The tree had many big branches. Birds loved to sit on the branches. One day, a little bird found a wire. The little bird wanted to play with the wire.

The little bird took the wire to the wide tree. It wanted to put the wire on the branches. But, the wind blew the wire away. The little bird was sad. It wanted to find the wire again.

The little bird looked for the wire. It found the wire in the grass. The little bird was happy. It took the wire back to the wide tree. The wind did not delay the little bird this time. The little bird played with the wire on the branches. The little bird was very happy.

Once upon a time, there was a happy goat named Billy. Billy lived on a farm with lots of other animals. One day, something strange happened. Billy's pen got too small for him, and he wasn't comfortable anymore.

Billy tried to tell the farmer, but the farmer didn't understand goat language. So, Billy decided to take matters into his own hooves. He climbed over the fence and went for a walk.

As he walked, Billy found a big open field. It was so comfortable! Billy decided to stay there and make it his new home. And that's how Billy the goat found a new place to live.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the rain. One day, her mom asked her to come inside because it was wet outside.

Lily said, "But mommy, I love the rain! Can't I stay outside and play?"

Her mom replied, "I know you love the rain, but you need to behave and come inside. You don't want to get sick."

Lily sighed but knew her mom was right. As she walked inside, she looked up at the sky and saw the earth getting wetter and wetter. She couldn't wait for the rain to stop so she could go back outside and play again.

Mommy opened the box. Inside was something soft. She took it out. It was velvet. She laid it on the floor and started to unpack it. Mommy took something out of the velvet. It was empty. She looked sad.

Mommy put the empty thing back into the velvet. Then she put the velvet back into the box and closed the lid. She took the box and put it under the bed.

Mommy smiled and said, "It's time to go to the park!" She grabbed her coat and took me by the hand. We walked to the park and played on the swings.

We had so much fun. Before we knew it, it was time to go home. Mommy looked at me and said, "Let's go unpack the velvet box again." We went back home. Mommy opened the box and we both looked inside.

This time, inside the velvet was something wonderful. It was a teddy bear! Mommy and I hugged the teddy bear and she said, "Now it doesn't feel so empty anymore."

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to paint with her white paint. One day, Lily was painting a picture of a flower when she accidentally got a spot of paint on her dress.

"Oh no!" Lily cried. "I got paint on my dress!"

"Don't worry, Lily," her mom said. "We can wash it off."

But Lily didn't want to wait for her mom to wash it off. She wanted to do it herself. So, she tried to wash it off with water, but it didn't work. The spot of white paint stayed on her dress.

Lily was sad because she loved her dress. She didn't want to wear it with a spot on it. From that day on, Lily learned to be more careful when she painted.

Lily and Ben were going to visit their grandma. They had to pack their bags with clothes and toys. Lily was curious about what grandma had in her house. She wanted to see her books, her dolls, and her garden. Ben was more interested in playing with grandma's dog, Rex.

"Are you ready, Lily?" Ben asked. He had already packed his bag and was waiting by the door.

"Not yet, Ben. I have to pack my favorite teddy bear. He likes to travel with me," Lily said. She looked for her teddy bear in her room, but she could not find him. She felt sad and worried.

"Where is teddy?" she asked herself. She looked under the bed, in the closet, and in the drawers. She did not see teddy anywhere.

"Maybe he is hiding," Ben said. He came to help Lily look for teddy. He was a good brother. He liked to make Lily happy.

They searched all over the room, but they still could not find teddy. Lily was about to cry. She loved teddy very much. She did not want to leave him behind.

"Maybe he is in the living room," Ben said. He had an idea. He took Lily's hand and led her to the living room. There, on the sofa, they saw teddy. He was sitting next to a big suitcase.

"Teddy!" Lily exclaimed. She ran to the sofa and hugged teddy. She was so happy to see him. She kissed his nose and whispered in his ear. "I missed you, teddy. I'm glad you're here."

Teddy smiled. He had a surprise for Lily. He opened the suitcase and showed her what was inside. It was full of books, dolls, and flowers. They were all gifts from grandma. She had sent them ahead of time for Lily and Ben.

"Wow!" Lily said. She was amazed by the gifts. She thanked grandma in her heart. She was very excited to see her.

"Look, Ben. Grandma sent us these. Aren't they wonderful?" Lily said. She showed Ben the gifts. Ben was also happy. He saw a ball, a car, and a bone. They were for him and Rex.

"Awesome!" Ben said. He thanked grandma too. He was eager to play with Rex.

Lily and Ben packed their bags with their clothes, toys, and gifts. They were ready to go. They said goodbye to their mom and dad. They got in the car with teddy and drove to grandma's house. They felt a victory. They had found teddy and received gifts. They were curious about what else grandma had for them. They could not wait to see her. They knew they would have a lot of fun.

Jack and his mom were out for a walk and Jack was looking for things to find. Suddenly he exclaimed, "Mom! Look at this page I found!" His mom picked it up and was amazed. "This is incredible," she said. "What do you think this page will grow?"

"I think it will grow a flower!" Jack responded, excited by the possibilities.

His mom chuckled and said, "Maybe it will. Let's take the page home, put it in the soil and see what will happen."

Jack was filled with hope and anticipation as they walked home and got their gardening supplies. Together the two of them put the page in the soil and watched it carefully. Before long, a small green sprout began to grow. Slowly the sprout grew and a few days later, a colorful flower blossomed.

Jack smiled proudly. "Incredible!" he exclaimed. His mom smiled back and said, "Yes, it is incredible. We are so lucky!"

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to collect shiny rocks. Every time he went outside, he would search for new rocks to add to his collection. He was very proud of his collection and would show it to anyone who came to visit.

One day, Timmy went to the park with his mom and dad. He saw some other kids playing a game with a ball. They were trying to score points by throwing the ball into a net. Timmy wanted to play too, but he didn't know how. The other kids were very kind and taught him how to play. Timmy was very happy when he scored his first point.

After playing for a while, Timmy went back to collecting rocks. He found a very shiny one that he had never seen before. He was so excited that he showed it to the other kids. They were impressed by his humble attitude and how proud he was of his rock collection. From that day on, Timmy had new friends to play with and show his collection to.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to ride his bike with his red helmet on his head. One day, Timmy's mom asked him to mail a letter at the post office. Timmy was happy to help his mom and put the letter in the mailbox.

On his way back home, Timmy saw a sad puppy on the street. The puppy didn't have a home and was upset. Timmy asked the puppy if he wanted to come home with him. The puppy was happy and followed Timmy home.

When Timmy got home, his mom was upset. She had received a letter that said Timmy's dad was not coming home from the war. Timmy's mom hugged him and told him the sad news. Timmy was sad too, but he was happy to have the puppy to keep him company. They cuddled together with Timmy's red helmet by their side.

Today was a sunny day. The sky was blue and the sun was out. I went to the park with my flexible ball. I threw it in the air and caught it. It was so much fun!

As the day went on, the sun started to go down. The sky started to glow orange and pink. It was so pretty! I watched the sky until it got dark.

When it was time to go home, I was sad to leave the park. But I was happy because I had a fun day with my flexible ball and got to see the sky glow.

Once there was a girl named Sue. She was very regular - she always followed her daily routine. Today, it was time for Sue to take a test. She was very excited!

She put on her outfit and ran out the door to catch the bus. The bus was almost full when she arrived but she caught the last seat. On the way to school, Sue thought of a plan.

When the bus arrived at school, Sue turned to the other passengers and said, "I'm going to catch the test. Who's going to join me?" Everyone said no, but Sue didn't give up.

Finally, one little girl said she would join Sue. Together, the two of them ran for the test. They were so happy when they caught it!

Jack was walking through the hallway. He saw an enormous mess! Everywhere he looked there was something spilled on the floor. Jack knew he couldn't leave the mess there, he needed to clean it.

He went to the closet and grabbed a mop. The mop was too big for Jack but he needed it to clean the mess. He tried to lift it but it was so heavy he couldn't carry it.

Then his big brother came by and saw the mess. He said he would help and grabbed the enormous mop. He started to mop the floor and it didn't take long before the hallway was clean! Both Jack and his brother were very happy.

Once there was a little girl named Abigail who loved to play dress up. One day she put on a rare dress that her mom let her borrow.

Abigail twirled around in the flowy dress and asked, "Mommy, how do I look?"

Mommy smiled and said, "Oh sweetie, you look beautiful. Just like a princess!"

Abigail smiled and said, "Can I go outside and show Daddy?"

Mommy said, "Yes, be sure to take your shoes and don't forget your hat. I don't want you to get too hot out there."

Abigail skipped outside and showed Daddy her new dress.

Daddy said, "Wow, Abigail, you look stunning! Let's go pick some fruit in the garden, so we can make a tasty treat!"

So, they went out to the garden, picked up some apples and oranges, and brought them back inside.

Abigail helped Daddy mix the fruit together and she tasted a small spoonful.

Abigail smiled and said, "It tastes so yummy, Daddy! Can I have some more?"

Daddy made up a big bowl of the rare fruit salad and said, "It's all yours, little one. Enjoy it!"

Abigail happily ate the fruit salad and even offered some to Mommy and Daddy.

Lily and Max were playing with pastels. They liked to draw on the big paper with the soft colors. Lily made a flower and Max made a car. They were happy and proud of their pictures.

"Look, Lily, I made a fast car!" Max said, showing his picture to Lily.

"Wow, Max, your car is very nice!" Lily said, smiling. "Look, I made a flower for you!"

"Thank you, Lily, your flower is very pretty!" Max said, taking the flower picture. He gave Lily a hug.

They decided to hang their pictures on the wall. They got some tape and a chair. Lily climbed on the chair and taped her flower. Max climbed on the chair and taped his car. But the chair was not very stable. It wobbled and Max lost his balance. He stumbled and fell off the chair. He landed on the floor with a thud.

"Ow, ow, ow!" Max cried, holding his knee. It was red and sore.

Lily ran to Max and helped him up. She saw his knee and felt sorry for him.

"Are you okay, Max?" Lily asked, worried.

"It hurts, Lily, it hurts!" Max said, tears in his eyes.

Lily hugged Max and kissed his knee. She got a band-aid and put it on his knee. She rubbed his back and sang a song.

"It's okay, Max, it's okay. You are brave and strong. The band-aid will make it better. I love you, Max, I love you."

Max felt better. He smiled and hugged Lily back. He thanked her for the band-aid and the song. He told her he loved her too.

They looked at their pictures on the wall. They were still smooth and bright. They were happy and proud of their pictures. They were happy and proud of each other.

Once upon a time, there were two friends named Bob and Sam. They were playing in the park when it started to rain.

Suddenly, a nosy crow came and said, "What are you fight about?" Sam and Bob looked at each other and said, "We're not fighting!" But the crow wasn't convinced and kept asking until they got mad and started to fight.

It was a big fight and the two friends were not talking to each other. Then, suddenly, the sun came out and a rainbow appeared in the sky! Sam and Bob looked at each other and started to laugh. They remembered that they were friends, and they stopped fighting.

The nosy crow flew away and Bob and Sam went back to playing in the park. They laughed, danced and smiled under the beautiful rainbow.

One day, a boy named Tim went to play at the park. The sun was bright, and Tim was happy. He saw his friend, Sam, and ran to him. Sam was kicking a ball. Tim knew it was a fun sport.

"Can I play too?" asked Tim. Sam did not answer. He looked sad. Tim thought something was wrong. He felt that he would find out soon.

They played the sport for a while. But Sam was not having fun. The game felt dull. Tim stopped and asked, "Why are you sad, Sam?"

Sam looked at Tim and said, "I lost my toy car. It was my favorite." Tim wanted to help his friend. They looked all around the park.

Finally, they found the toy car under a big tree. Sam was happy again. The sport was fun now. Tim and Sam played and laughed together.

Once upon a time there was a game. The game was modern, with a lot of beeps and bells. It was the perfect game for a 3 year old, who was eager to learn how to play. In the game, the 3 year old had to use her finger and tap the different scores on the screen. She had to accept that different scores led to different outcomes. She had to tap each of the scores in the right order to complete the game. With patience and practice, the 3 year old started getting better and better at the game. She learned to accept and understand the scores, until eventually she was able to complete the game all on her own!

Once upon a time, a little girl named Lily was playing with her wagon in the park. She loved to pull it around and collect pretty flowers. Suddenly, she saw a little boy crying nearby.

"What's wrong?" asked Lily.

"I lost my toy truck," said the boy.

Lily had an idea. She looked in her wagon and saw a toy truck that looked just like the one the boy had lost. "Does this match your toy truck?" she asked.

The boy's face lit up with joy. "Yes, it does!" he said.

Lily was happy to help the boy find his lost toy truck. She felt proud that she could make someone else happy. As they played together, they found a dead butterfly on the ground. Lily said, "Oh no, the butterfly is dead. Let's say a little prayer for it."

The boy nodded his head and they both closed their eyes and said a prayer for the butterfly. They continued to play together and had a fun afternoon.

Once upon a time, there was a little mouse named Timmy. Timmy loved to eat cheese, but he was very clumsy. One day, Timmy went to the market to trade some cheese for some bread.

At the market, Timmy met a cat named Mittens. Mittens was planning to catch Timmy and eat him for dinner. "Hello, little mouse," said Mittens. "What brings you to the market today?"

"I'm here to trade some cheese for some bread," replied Timmy.

Mittens smiled slyly. "I have a better plan," she said. "Why don't you come back to my house and we can share the cheese and bread together?"

Timmy thought this was a good idea, but he was also a little scared of Mittens. "Okay," he said, "but can we eat the cheese and bread outside?"

Mittens agreed and they went to her house. They ate the cheese and bread and had a nice time. Timmy was happy that he made a new friend, but he also knew he had to be careful around Mittens.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved lollipops and always carried one with her wherever she went. One day, while playing in the park, she accidentally dropped her lollipop and it got stuck in a tree.

Lily was very sad and didn't know what to do. Just then, her friend Timmy came along and saw her crying. "What happened, Lily?" he asked.

"I lost my lollipop and it's stuck in the tree. I don't know how to get it down," Lily replied.

"Don't worry, Lily. I can solve this problem for you," Timmy said. He climbed up the tree and retrieved the lollipop for Lily.

"Thank you, Timmy! You're so kind and beautiful," Lily said with a big smile on her face.

From that day on, Lily and Timmy were the best of friends and always helped each other out when they had a problem. And Lily never forgot how Timmy had solved her lollipop problem and made her so happy.

Once upon a time, there was a shy little crab named Blue. Blue lived in the sea and loved to play with his fish friends. One day, Blue saw a pretty shell near the shore. He wanted to take it home to show his friends.

Blue went to the shell and tried to pick it up. But it was too big for him. He tried to pinch it with his claw, but it didn't work. Blue's friend, Fish, saw him having trouble and asked, "Blue, do you need help?"

Blue was too shy to ask for help, so he said, "No, I can do it." He tried again and again to pinch the shell, but it just wouldn't move. Blue didn't want to give up, so he kept trying.

As Blue was trying to pinch the shell, a big wave came and washed him onto the shore. Blue was sad and scared. He couldn't get back to the sea. His fish friends tried to help him, but they couldn't. Blue was stuck on the shore, all because he was too shy to ask for help.

Once there was a small frog. He was happy and hopped around all day. One day he found a card on the ground. He picked it up and it said "Frogs can disappear".

The frog was very excited and wanted to try it out. So he hopped onto the card and started to disappear. Suddenly, the frog was gone! The card was dead and it had taken the frog with it.

The frog was so sad. He couldn't find his way home. He missed his friends and family. But he kept looking, hoping one day he'd find a way back.

So he hopped and he hopped, never giving up. Finally, one day, the frog found a way back home. Everyone was so happy to see him again and the frog had an adventure to tell. He never forgot the card but he never tried to disappear again!

Lily and Ben were twins who liked to play outside. One morning, they woke up very early and saw the sunrise. The sky was pink and orange and the sun was bright and warm.

"Look, Lily, the sunrise is so fair!" Ben said.

"Yes, Ben, it is fair and pretty. Let's go outside and march to the park!" Lily said.

They put on their shoes and coats and ran to the door. They asked their mom if they could go outside.

"Can we go outside, mom? Please, please, please?" they said.

Mom smiled and said, "Yes, you can go outside, but only for a little while. And stay close to the house, okay?"

"Okay, mom, thank you!" they said.

They opened the door and went outside. They saw some birds and flowers and trees. They held hands and started to march.

"March, march, march, we are going to the park!" they sang.

They marched and sang and had fun. They saw the sunrise and felt happy. They were fair and kind to each other. They loved to play outside.

Lily and Ben were playing in the garden. They liked to look at the flowers and the bugs. They saw a big red flower that was very pretty. Lily wanted to smell it.

"Wait, Lily!" Ben said. "I see something on the flower. It is black and small and has many legs. It is an ant!"

Lily did not care. She wanted to smell the pretty flower. She moved closer to it.

"Stop, Lily!" Ben said. "The ant might bite you. It might hurt. I warn you, Lily, do not touch the flower!"

But Lily did not listen. She touched the flower with her nose. The ant saw her and got angry. It bit her nose. Lily cried out loud. It hurt a lot.

Ben ran to her and hugged her. He was sorry for her. He said, "I told you, Lily, the ant might bite you. You should have listened to me. I warned you, Lily, do not touch the flower!"

Lily nodded. She was sorry too. She said, "You were right, Ben, the ant did bite me. It hurt a lot. I should have listened to you. You warned me, Ben, do not touch the flower!"

They went to their mom and told her what happened. She gave Lily a kiss and a band-aid. She said, "Next time, listen to your brother. He was trying to help you. He warned you, Lily, do not touch the flower!"

Lily and Ben said, "Yes, mom, we will. We love you, mom!"

They hugged their mom and went back to the garden. They played with other flowers and bugs. They were careful and happy.

Jim had a huge dog. His dog was always very helpful and kind. One day, he wanted to go and visit his friend, but he didn't have a way to get there. Jim's dog offered to lend him a ride. Jim got onto the dog's back and the dog carried him to his friend's house. It was a very long journey but Jim's dog was strong and carried him all the way. When Jim arrived safely at his friend's house, he was very happy and grateful for the dog's kindness. He thanked his dog for lending him a ride and promised to bring him something special to show how much he appreciated his help.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She was very hungry and wanted to eat something yummy. She looked in the kitchen, but there was nothing to eat. So she went outside to play.

While she was playing, she saw a ladder leaning against a tree. She climbed up the ladder and saw a big juicy apple. She was so happy to find something to eat!

But then, a boy came by and said, "That's my apple! You can't have it!" Lily didn't want to give up the apple, but she didn't want to be mean either. So she said, "I'm sorry, I didn't know it was yours. Here, you can have half." The boy was happy and they shared the apple together.

Lily and Ben were playing in the park. They liked to go on the swings and the slide. Lily saw a big red button on a pole. She wondered what it was.

"What is that?" she asked Ben.

"I don't know," he said. "Maybe it makes a sound or a light."

Lily wanted to find out. She ran to the button and pushed it. Nothing happened. She pushed it again and again. Still nothing.

"Maybe it's broken," she said.

Suddenly, they heard a loud siren. They saw a fire truck coming to the park. The firemen jumped out and ran to the button.

"Who pushed this?" one of them asked.

Lily and Ben were scared. They hid behind a tree.

"We did," Lily said in a small voice.

The fireman looked at them. He was not angry. He smiled.

"Don't worry, kids. This is a test button. We use it to practice for real events. It's safe. But you shouldn't push it unless there is a fire. It makes a lot of noise and it can confuse people."

Lily and Ben felt sorry. They said they were sorry.

"It's okay," the fireman said. "You didn't know. But now you do. Next time, ask an adult before you push a button you don't know. Okay?"

Lily and Ben nodded. They thanked the fireman. He gave them stickers and a hat. They were happy.

They learned a new word: event. They also learned to be careful with buttons. They went back to the swings and the slide. They had fun.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy lived in a house with his mom and dad. Timmy loved to play outside and run around in the grass.

One day, Timmy fell down and hurt his knee. It hurt a lot and he couldn't run or play anymore. His mom and dad took him to the doctor. The doctor said Timmy's knee would heal soon and be fine.

A few days later, Timmy and his family went on a trip to the west. Timmy saw lots of big mountains and beautiful sunsets. He felt happy and his knee was fine. Timmy knew his knee would heal and he could run and play again soon.

Once upon a time, three adventurers set off to explore an ancient cave. As they approached, they noticed a long cable stretching farther and farther into the darkness.

The brave explorers decided to follow the cable and see where it went. They soon discovered a huge room filled with treasures from long ago!

The adventurers noticed a tall stone chest in the corner of the room. They opened it up and to their surprise, it was stuffed with precious diamonds and jewels!

They collected all the treasure and stored it in sacks to take back with them. The explorers felt so proud!

When they reached the entrance of the cave, they carefully strung a new cable to help others find the secret room.

The adventurers went home with happy hearts and many stories to tell.

Once upon a time, there was a princess. She loved to ride on a horse. Her horse was white, and very beautiful.

One day, the princess went to the opera. She was so impressed by the show that she had to go back a second time. The music was magical and the singing was very impressive.

On the way home, the princess stopped for a ride on a carousel. There were many different animals, and the lights were so pretty. The princess sang along and enjoyed the ride.

The princess had a wonderful day and rode back home with a smile on her face.

Once upon a time there was a little boy named David. He was only three years old and loved to watch the birds flying in the sky. One day, his mommy showed him a jar with a brown sauce inside.

David asked her “What is that?"

“It's a spicy tomato sauce!” mommy said.

“It looks yummy!” David said as he smiled. His mommy laughed and said “Yes, it is yummy but it is also a bit bitter. You need to be careful.”

David watched as his mommy opened the jar. She took a spoonful of the sauce and tasted it. She made a yucky face and said “It's too bitter!”

David smiled and said “Can I try it? I want to see how bitter it is!”

Mommy looked surprised and said “Are you sure? You don't have to do it if you don't want to. It might not taste good.”

David nodded and took the spoonful of sauce. He tasted it and made a funny face. “It's a bit bitter,” he said.

His mommy smiled and said, “Yes it is. Let's not eat the sauce. We can find something else to eat.”

David nodded and watched

Once upon a time there was a small boy called Tim. He wanted to gain a tent of his own. He had seen his friends with tents and wanted one too.

One day, when Tim was out playing, he saw something shiny in the grass. It was a tent! But when he looked closer, he realised it was a fake tent. It was made from plastic and couldn't keep rain out!

Tim was very disappointed. He went back home and told his mum what had happened. His mum said that she would help him to get a real tent.

The following weekend, his mum and dad took him to the shops. There were so many tents to choose from! After looking at lots of different tents, Tim found one he liked.

His mum and dad bought it for him and they set it up in their back yard. Tim was so happy! He had finally gained a tent of his own.

Tom and Lily were playing in the garden. They liked to dig in the dirt and look for bugs. Sometimes they found worms, beetles, or spiders. They put them in a jar and watched them.

One day, they saw a big bug flying near a flower. It had a long nose and thin wings. It made a loud buzzing sound.

"Look, Lily, a mosquito!" Tom said. "Let's catch it!"

"No, Tom, don't!" Lily said. "Mosquitoes are bad. They can bite you and make you itch. Mommy warned us about them."

But Tom did not listen. He ran after the mosquito with his jar. He tried to trap it inside. The mosquito was fast and smart. It dodged Tom's jar and flew towards his arm. It landed on his skin and bit him.

"Ow!" Tom cried. "It hurts!"

Lily ran to him and saw a red bump on his arm. She felt sorry for him. She took him to the house and gave him a band-aid. She also gave him a hug.

"Next time, listen to me, Tom," she said. "And listen to Mommy. She knows a lot of things. She is ancient."

Tom nodded. He learned his lesson. He did not like mosquitoes. He liked Lily. She was his sister and his friend. He hugged her back.

Once there was a mouse. The mouse liked to lean against the wall. It was all alone, until one day, it found a fake friend. The fake friend was a toy mouse. It was so clever that it leaned against the wall just like the real mouse.

The two mice became friends, leaning against the wall together. They chatted away happily, enjoying their new found friendship.

One day, a little girl saw the two mice leaning together. She was so excited! She picked them up and put them into her pocket, then took them home.

The little girl loved when the mice leaned against each other, so she put them back in the same position and they continued to be best friends. The little girl was very happy. The real mouse and the fake mouse were very happy too, leaning together side by side.

Once upon a time, there was a peaceful town. In the town, there was a big steel car. This car was very special. It could drive very fast. Everyone in the town loved the car.

One day, a little boy named Tim wanted to drive the car. He asked his mom, "Can I drive the car, please?" His mom said, "You are too little, but you can watch me drive it."

Tim and his mom went to the car. His mom drove the car. Tim watched and smiled. The car went fast. Tim was very happy. The peaceful town had a fun day with the steel car.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play in the park and pick apples from the trees. One day, she saw a big, blue apple on the ground. She picked it up and showed it to her mom.

"Look, Mommy! A blue apple!" Lily said.

"That's very strange, Lily. Apples aren't usually blue," her mom replied.

Suddenly, Lily stumbled and almost dropped the blue apple. "Be careful, Lily!" her mom said.

"I'm okay, Mommy. I just tripped on a rock," Lily said as she continued to admire her blue apple.

Once upon a time, there was a dog named Max. Max was very popular in the neighborhood. Everyone loved to play with him and give him treats. Max's owner, a kind lady named Mrs. Smith, always made sure Max was clean and well-fed.

One day, Max went to play in the park with his friends. While playing, Max accidentally knocked over a trash can and made a big mess. The park owner saw what happened and got very angry. "Who is the owner of this dog? They need to clean up this mess!" he shouted.

Max's owner heard the commotion and came running over. "I'm sorry, sir. I'll clean up the mess right away," she said. The park owner was still angry, but Mrs. Smith apologized again and promised to be more careful in the future.

Max was happy to be back playing with his friends, and Mrs. Smith made sure to keep him on a tight leash so he wouldn't cause any more trouble. From then on, Max and his owner made sure to always be respectful and clean up after themselves.

Once upon a time there was a little girl who wanted to go on an adventure. She wanted to explore a lively village. So one Saturday morning, the little girl decided to jump into her red car and drive on a long journey. She drove for hours until she spotted the lively village.

When she arrived, the village was filled with people who were talking, laughing and singing. She was so excited to explore the village and see all the lovely things! She jumped from one spot to the next, looking at all there was to see.

The little girl saw a beautiful playground with swings and slides. She jumped onto the swing and swung all day, until it was time to leave.

The little girl said goodbye to the lively village and jumped into her car. She knew that she couldn't wait to come back and explore more.

Once upon a time, there was a mommy and her little girl. The little girl loved to play in the garden. One day, the mommy told the little girl to put a pot of dirt in the garden. The little girl was very excited, so she ran to grab the pot.

The mommy noticed that the pot was very tight and needed help to open it. She knelt down and said to the little girl, "Honey, can you help me? Can you put the pot on the ground so I can open it?"

The little girl proudly knelt down and placed the pot on the ground next to the mommy. Then, the mommy thanked the little girl and opened the pot to put the dirt in the garden. The little girl helped the mommy sprinkle the dirt in the garden.

The little girl and the mommy smiled, as they had planted seeds together and were now waiting for them to grow.

Timmy was so excited - he was going to ride his bike up the hill. He hopped onto his bike and peddled up the hill with excitement.

But halfway up the hill, he started to worry. "I'm so alone! What if I can't get to the top?", he thought. He stopped peddling and just sat there.

Suddenly he heard a voice. "Hey, don't worry! I'm right here." It was his mom. She had run up the hill after him "I'm not going to let you go alone," she smiled.

Timmy felt so relieved and happy. His mom had come to make sure he was safe! He hopped back on his bike and, with his mom walking next to him, finished going up the hill.

At the top of the hill, Timmy and his mom both cheered. His mom threw her arms around him and said "Nobody has to feel lonely when I'm around".

Then, with a smile, Timmy started to peddle back down the hill. Now he was not worried - he was with his mom.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Lucy. Lucy was 3 years old and she lived in a big house in the middle of a field. One day, Lucy decided to go outside and explore the field.

As she did, she discovered something special - silence. She had never heard something so quiet before. It was so special that she sat down and just enjoyed being with the silence.

For a few moments, she thought about the world around her. Lucy felt peaceful and happy. But after a while, she started to feel helpless and alone.

Just then she heard the sound of birds and realised she was not alone - she was surrounded by nature. Lucy smiled and carried on exploring the field. She felt less helpless. The silence and nature reminded Lucy that she was brave and could explore many more things in the world.

Lila and Ben were bored. They had no toys to play with. All their toys were in a big box. But the box had a lock. And they did not have the key.

"Where is the key?" Lila asked.

"I don't know," Ben said. "Maybe Mom has it."

They looked for Mom. But Mom was busy. She was making dough. She was going to bake a cake.

"Mom, can we have the key?" Lila asked.

"Not now, sweetie," Mom said. "I'm busy. Go play with something else."

But there was nothing else to play with. Lila and Ben were sad. They went back to the box. They tried to open it. But it was too hard.

"Maybe we can use something to unlock it," Ben said.

"Like what?" Lila asked.

Ben looked around. He saw a dull knife. It was on the table. Mom had used it to cut the dough.

"Maybe this will work," Ben said. He took the knife. He went to the box. He tried to put the knife in the lock. But it did not fit.

"Be careful, Ben," Lila said. "You might hurt yourself."

Ben did not listen. He pushed harder. He twisted the knife. He heard a click. He smiled.

"I did it!" he said. "I unlocked the box!"

He opened the box. He saw all their toys. He was happy. He took out his favorite car. He gave Lila her favorite doll.

"Look, Lila," he said. "We can play now!"

Lila was happy too. She hugged her doll. She thanked Ben.

"You're smart, Ben," she said. "You unlocked the box!"

They played with their toys. They had fun. They forgot about Mom and the dough. They did not hear Mom calling them.

"Kids, come here!" Mom said. "The cake is ready!"

But Lila and Ben did not hear. They were too busy playing. They were not bored anymore. They were happy.

Once upon a time, there was rot in the air. Two humans and their pet pig, Piggles, were walking in the forest. Suddenly, they found a large, pretty tree.

“What a pretty tree,” said the first human.

“Let’s make something special!” exclaimed the other human.

They gathered lots of sticks, climbing high up in the tree, and made a big, cozy nest.

“Don’t worry, Piggles!” said the first human. “We’ll come back on the weekend and give you something special.”

The humans left. When they returned, the tree was rotten and their special nest was gone!

Piggles was sad, but he didn't understand why the tree had rotted from the time they had left it. The humans hugged Piggles, knowing that rot began in their hearts a while ago - they just couldn't feel it in their pretty tree until now.

Once upon a time, there was a boy who had a balloon. He loved his balloon very much and wanted to deliver it.

The boy took his balloon and went to the park. On the way, he met some kids who wanted to play with the balloon. The boy was excited and let them have a turn. But then one of the kids grabbed the balloon and ran away with it!

The boy didn't know what to do. He was very uncomfortable and it made him sad. He chased after the kid, but the kid was too fast.

Suddenly, a big bird flew down from the sky and picked up the balloon with its beak. The bird flew away with the balloon, but then came back and delivered it to the boy!

The boy was so happy to get his balloon back. He thanked the bird for helping him. Now he can delivery his balloon himself whenever he wants.

One day, a little boy named Tim was very enthusiastic about going to the park with his mom. They wanted to have a fun day outside. Tim's mom brought a big bag of popcorn for them to share. Tim loved popcorn very much.

At the park, they saw a big tree. Tim's mom said, "Let's sit under the tree and eat our popcorn." Tim was excited and said, "Yes, yes, yes!" They sat down and opened the bag of popcorn. Tim started to eat the popcorn very fast.

Suddenly, a squirrel came and took some popcorn from the bag. Tim was not happy. He said, "No, squirrel! That's my popcorn!" The squirrel ran away with the popcorn. Tim's mom laughed and said, "Don't be embarrassed, Tim. It's just a squirrel." Tim smiled and they continued to eat their popcorn and enjoy their day at the park.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Sam. He loved to explore. Today, he wanted to go for a walk in the woods to find a creek. So he said goodbye to his parents and started walking.

On his way, Sam heard a noise coming from the trees. When he looked between the branches he saw an amazing sight. A group of frogs were jumping from stone to stone in the creek.

Sam wanted to stay and watch but he didn't want to delay his adventure, so he said goodbye to the frogs and continued his walk.

Later, he came across a tall mountain and said, "Wow, that's amazing!" He was quite happy and excited.

He followed the creek until he reached his parents house. When he walked inside he said, "Mummy, look I found a creek! It was amazing!"

His Mummy smiled and said, "I'm glad you had a great adventure, Sam."

Lily was a big girl who liked to dance. She had a pretty dress and a veil that her mom made for her. She was going to dance in front of many people at the school show.

She was not scared, but excited. She wanted to show everyone how well she could dance. She practiced a lot with her mom and her teacher. She knew all the steps and the music.

When it was her turn, she went on the stage with a big smile. She saw her mom and dad in the crowd. They waved at her and gave her a thumbs up. She heard the music start and began to dance. She twirled, jumped, and spun with grace. She felt happy and proud.

The music ended and she bowed. She heard a loud noise. It was the people clapping. They were applauding for her. They liked her dance. She saw her mom and dad stand up and cheer. They were so proud of her. She felt a warm feeling in her heart.

She ran to them and hugged them. They told her she was amazing and brave. She thanked them and told them she loved them. She felt very lucky. She had a tough day, but a wonderful night. She was a big girl who liked to dance.

Sara and Ben are twins. They like to play and have fun. Today is their birthday. Mom and Dad have a surprise for them.

"Come on, Sara and Ben. We are going to a special place," Mom says.

"Where are we going, Mom?" Sara asks.

"You will see. It is a surprise," Mom says.

They get in the car and drive for a while. Sara and Ben look out the window and try to guess where they are going. They see trees, houses, and shops. They do not see the surprise.

"Are we there yet, Dad?" Ben asks.

"Almost, Ben. Just a few more minutes," Dad says.

They turn into a big parking lot. Sara and Ben see a sign with colorful letters. It says "Zoo".

"Wow! We are going to the zoo!" Sara and Ben shout.

They are very happy. They love animals. They have never been to the zoo before.

Mom and Dad park the car and take them to the entrance. They buy tickets and enter the zoo. They see lions, monkeys, elephants, and many other animals. They hear them roar, chatter, trumpet, and make other noises. They feed some of the animals and pet some of them. They learn their names and what they eat and where they live.

They have a lot of fun. They take pictures and laugh and run. They are hungry and thirsty. Mom and Dad take them to a cafe in the zoo. They order pizza and juice. The pizza is delicious. They eat and drink and talk about the animals.

"Did you like the surprise, Sara and Ben?" Mom asks.

"Yes, Mom. We loved it. Thank you, Mom and Dad. This is the best birthday ever," Sara and Ben say.

They hug Mom and Dad and smile. They are very happy. They have a surprise and a special place and a delicious pizza. They have a wonderful day.

Anna and Ben are friends. They like to play with toys. One day, Anna has a new toy. It is a blue box. She can open it and find a surprise inside.

Ben wants to see the surprise too. He asks Anna, "Can I open your blue box, please?" Anna says, "No, it is mine. You have your own toys." Ben feels sad. He thinks Anna is not kind.

Anna opens her blue box. She sees a shiny ring. She puts it on her finger. She says, "Look, it is so pretty!" Ben says, "Wow, it is. Can I try it, please?" Anna says, "No, it is mine. You have your own toys." Ben feels angry. He thinks Anna is mean.

Anna plays with her ring. She does not share with Ben. Ben does not play with her. He goes to his toys. He finds a red car. He likes it. He says, "Look, it is so fast!" Anna says, "Wow, it is. Can I play with it, please?" Ben says, "No, it is mine. You have your own toys." Anna feels sorry. She thinks Ben is right.

Anna goes to Ben. She says, "I am sorry, Ben. I was not kind. I want to share with you. You can open my blue box and try my ring. I can play with your red car. We can have fun together." Ben says, "Thank you, Anna. I am sorry, too. I want to share with you. You can play with my red car and I can open your blue box and try your ring. We can be friends again." Anna and Ben hug. They share their toys. They are happy.

The moral of the story is: Sharing is caring. It is good to be kind to your friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Sue. Sue was very sleepy one night. She put on her soft bathrobe and got ready for bed. But Sue could not find her favorite toy, Mr. Bear. She felt sad and began to weep.

Sue's mommy heard her weep and came into the room. She saw Sue in her bathrobe, with tears in her eyes. "What's wrong, Sue?" asked her mommy. Sue said, "I can't find Mr. Bear, and I can't sleep without him." Her mommy gave her a hug and said, "Don't worry, we will find Mr. Bear."

Together, they looked all around the house for Mr. Bear. They looked in the living room, the kitchen, and even the bathroom. Then, they saw something behind the couch. It was Mr. Bear, hiding behind a pillow! Sue was so happy to see her toy. She hugged Mr. Bear, put on her bathrobe, and went to bed. That night, Sue and Mr. Bear slept very well, and Sue did not weep anymore.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her guitar and sing songs. One day, Lily went on an adventurous walk in the forest. She saw many trees and animals.

Suddenly, she heard a loud noise. It was a group of ants marching towards her. She asked, "Why are you marching?" The ants replied, "We are going to a party." Lily said, "Can I come too?"

The ants said, "Sure, but only if you bring your guitar and sing us a song." Lily was happy and played her guitar while the ants marched. They arrived at the party and danced all night long. From that day on, Lily and the ants were friends forever.

Once upon a time, there were two children; one was named Alex and the other one was named Maria. Alex was jealous of Maria because Maria had a special cone that made her look taller. Alex wanted to have a cone like his friend Maria.

So, one day Alex and Maria went to a special places that sold cones. Alex looked at all of the cones to find the perfect one. He wanted one that was heavy enough to make him as tall as Maria. He chose a cone that was very heavy, but he was still shorter than Maria. Disappointed, Alex took the cone home.

That night, Alex was playing with his new cone when he heard a noise from outside. It was Maria, who had come to see him. She had brought a secret for Alex; it was a sack full of stones. Since Alex's cone was so heavy, it was the perfect size for stones. She had weighed the stones to make sure that Alex's cone was heavy enough.

Alex was so happy to have found a special friend like Maria. He learned that when we can't get what we want, it can sometimes turn out to be something much better if we trust our friends. He learned that it's not wise to be jealous of other people's stuff. Alex and Maria remained good friends after that day. The End.

Once there was a bear who wanted to shine. He thought it would make him comfortable. So every day he worked very hard. He polished and shined until nothing else was brighter.

One day, he met a little child. At first, the bear was scared, but the child seemed friendly. They talked and laughed together.

"Do you want to shine too?" Asked the bear.

"Yes!" Said the child happily.

So together they continued working and shining until the sun set. But they were so busy they forgot something important.

The next morning, when the sun was just starting to rise, the bear looked around and noticed the child was gone. He had forgotten to take his home!

The bear was sad. He had forgotten to take care of his new friend. The moral of the story is that it's important to be safe and take care of others, even if you're focused on something else.

Anna was a good girl who liked to help her mom and dad. She always did what they told her and never told a lie. One day, she saw a shiny necklace in her mom's drawer. She wanted to wear it and pretend she was an angel. She took the necklace and put it in her pocket.

Later, her mom asked her if she had seen the necklace. Anna felt anxious. She knew she should tell the truth, but she was afraid of getting in trouble. She shook her head and said, "No, mom, I don't know where it is." Her mom looked sad and said, "That's strange. I was going to wear it for your dad's birthday. He gave it to me when you were born. It's very special to me."

Anna felt very bad. She wanted to make her mom happy, not sad. She decided to give the necklace back and say sorry. She ran to her room and took the necklace out of her pocket. But as she did, she dropped it and it broke into pieces. She cried and cried. She had ruined the necklace and lied to her mom.

She went to her mom and showed her the broken necklace. She said, "Mom, I'm sorry. I took the necklace and lied to you. I wanted to be an angel, but I was very bad. Please forgive me." Her mom hugged her and said, "Anna, I'm glad you told me the truth. Lying is wrong and it hurts people. But I love you and I forgive you. You are still my angel, but you have to learn from your mistake. Next time, ask me before you take something that is not yours. And always be honest, even if it's hard."

Anna nodded and said, "I'm sorry, mom. I love you too. I will never lie again." She gave her mom a kiss and helped her fix the necklace. They smiled and hugged. Anna learned a lesson that day. She realized that lying is not worth it, and that telling the truth is always the best. She also learned that her mom's love was more precious than any necklace. She was happy and grateful. She was a good girl again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to talk to her friends and family. One day, her mommy and daddy went to the store to buy some wine for a party. They found a cheap bottle of wine and decided to buy it.

When they got home, Lily saw the bottle of wine and asked her parents what it was. They told her it was a drink for grown-ups and that she couldn't have any. But Lily wanted to talk about the bottle of wine with her friends at school the next day.

The next morning, Lily went to school and showed her friends a picture of the bottle of wine. They talked about how it looked and how it was a grown-up drink. Lily was happy she could talk about it with her friends, even though she couldn't have any.

Lily and Ben were playing with their toy guns in the backyard. They liked to pretend they were cowboys and robbers. Lily was the cowboy and Ben was the robber. Lily chased Ben around the trees and the swing.

"Stop, robber, or I will shoot you!" Lily shouted.

"No, you can't catch me, cowboy!" Ben said. He ran faster and faster.

Lily was impatient. She wanted to catch Ben and put him in jail. She aimed her toy gun at Ben's leg and pulled the trigger. The toy gun made a loud noise and a plastic bullet flew out.

"Ow, ow, ow!" Ben cried. He fell to the ground and held his leg. "You shot me, Lily! That hurts!"

Lily ran to Ben and saw a red mark on his leg. She felt sorry for Ben. She did not mean to hurt him. She threw her toy gun away and hugged Ben.

"I'm sorry, Ben, I'm sorry. I did not want to hurt you. Are you okay?" Lily said.

Ben looked at Lily and saw her sad face. He felt better. He knew Lily was his friend. He hugged Lily back.

"It's okay, Lily, it's okay. I'm okay. It was just a game. You are a good cowboy. I am a bad robber." Ben said.

They smiled at each other and got up. They decided to play a different game. They did not want to shoot each other anymore. They wanted to have fun.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved dinosaurs. One day, Timmy went to the museum with his mommy. At the museum, Timmy saw an ancient dinosaur skeleton. It was very big and scary-looking.

Timmy tried to speak to the dinosaur skeleton, but it didn't answer back. His mommy told him that the dinosaur was very old and didn't talk anymore. Timmy was sad that the dinosaur couldn't speak, but he still thought it was really cool to see an ancient dinosaur.

After they left the museum, Timmy went home and drew a picture of the dinosaur. He showed it to his mommy and said, "Look, mommy! This is the dinosaur I saw today. It was really big and ancient." His mommy smiled and said, "Wow, Timmy! That's a great picture of a dinosaur." Timmy was happy that he could share his love of dinosaurs with his mommy.

Once upon a time, there was a big yard with green grass and a tall tree. A little girl named Lily loved to play in the yard with her toys. One day, she found a shiny rock and wanted to keep it safe. She decided to store it in her toy box so she wouldn't lose it.

But Lily's big brother, Jack, thought it was foolish to keep a rock. He laughed and said, "Why would you store a silly rock? It's not even a toy!" But Lily didn't listen and kept the rock in her toy box.

Later that day, Lily and Jack's mom asked them to clean up the yard. Jack grumbled and complained, but Lily happily picked up her toys and put them away. When she opened her toy box, she saw the shiny rock and smiled. She was glad she had stored it away safely.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a big thumb that she loved to suck on. Her mommy always told her not to suck her thumb, but Lily didn't listen.

One day, Lily's mommy took her to the park. Lily saw a big, shiny red apple on the ground. She picked it up and took a big bite. But the apple was spoiled! Lily didn't feel so good.

Later that day, Lily's mommy put her in a big, comfy chair to rest. Lily sat and sucked her thumb, feeling much better. She learned her lesson and never picked up a spoiled apple again.

Once upon a time, there were two children that were best friends. They played together all the time and did everything together, even going shopping at the store.

The two children liked to look at all the things that were in the store, and they loved the clothes that they saw. One day, one of them found an especially nice hanger and wanted to buy it. But the other one was envious and wanted it too.

The two of them started to argue, and neither would back down. Before too long, they were screaming and crying and making a big fuss. Other customers in the store started to get angry, so the store manager had to come over and tell them to leave because they included too much noise.

The two unhappy friends had to walk away from the store, without the hanger or each other. They never made up or became friends again, and so the story ended horribly.

Once upon a time there was a kitten who was feeling very anxious. She was stuck up a tree and had no way to get down. She was starting to worry she was going to have to stay there forever, when suddenly, a brave dog came to her rescue.

The dog barked up at the kitten and she meowed down. He barked again and again and soon enough, a kind man appeared to help. He grabbed a big piece of cloth and threw it up to the kitten. The kitten grabbed onto it and the man pulled her down safely and carefully.

The kind man patted the dog and gave him a treat as a thank you. The kitten was so happy to be safe and she gave the brave dog lots of cuddles. After that, the kitten never left the dog's side because she was so thankful for his help. She knew she could always count on him to rescue her if she was ever in trouble again.

Once upon a time there was a green frog. The frog wanted to get away, so he looked for a way to escape. He saw a tall tree and decided to climb to the top. The tree was very high, but the frog was determined. He pointed his little feet and inched his way up, higher and higher until he reached the top. From the highest branch, he could see the whole world. Everywhere the frog looked, he could see the sun shining, the trees swaying and the birds flying - it was so beautiful! The frog had escaped to a place of peace, he would never forget it.

Tom and Mia were going to the lake with their dad. They wanted to ride on a big boat that had a loud horn and a long rope. Dad said they could help him steer the boat and wave to the other boats.

Tom was very excited. He liked boats and horns and ropes. He ran to the boat and climbed on. He put on a life jacket and sat next to dad. He looked at the water and the sky and smiled.

Mia was very nervous. She did not like boats and horns and ropes. She thought the water was too deep and the boat was too fast. She walked slowly to the boat and held dad's hand. She put on a life jacket and sat on the other side of dad. She looked at the water and the sky and frowned.

Dad started the boat and made the horn go beep. Tom laughed and shouted, "This is fun!" Mia cried and said, "This is scary!" Dad hugged them both and said, "Don't worry, we are safe. Look, there is a duck on the water. Do you see it?"

Tom looked and saw the duck. He pointed and said, "Yes, I see it. It has a green head and a yellow beak. Can we feed it?" Mia looked and saw the duck. She squeezed dad's hand and said, "No, I don't see it. It has a big mouth and sharp teeth. Can we go back?"

Dad smiled and said, "The duck is friendly. It does not have teeth. It has a tongue. It likes bread and seeds. Do you want to try to feed it?" He took out some bread from his bag and tore it into pieces. He gave some to Tom and some to Mia.

Tom threw the bread to the duck and said, "Here you go, duck. Eat and be happy." The duck swam to the bread and ate it. It quacked and wagged its tail. Tom clapped and said, "The duck likes me. Can I pet it?"

Mia held the bread in her hand and said, "No, thank you, duck. I don't want to feed you. You are too big and too close." The duck swam to Mia and tried to get the bread. It nibbled her fingers and made her drop the bread. Mia screamed and said, "The duck bites me. Can we leave?"

Dad said, "The duck does not bite. It tickles. It just wants the bread. It is not mean. It is hungry." He took Mia's hand and said, "Let's go to the other side of the boat. There is a fish on the water. Do you want to see it?"

Tom said, "Yes, I want to see the fish. Maybe it has a red fin and a blue eye. Can we catch it?" Mia said, "No, I don't want to see the fish. Maybe it has a long tail and a sharp spine. Can we stay here?"

Dad said, "The fish is pretty. It does not have a spine. It has a scale. It likes worms and bugs. Do you want to try to catch it?" He took out a fishing rod from his bag and put a worm on the hook. He gave it to Tom and said, "Hold this and wait. Maybe the fish will bite."

Tom held the fishing rod and said, "OK, I will wait. Maybe the fish will bite. Then I can pull it out and show it to you." Mia held dad's hand and said, "No, I will not wait. Maybe the fish will bite. Then it can pull me in and eat me."

Dad said, "The fish does not eat people. It eats worms. It is not strong. It is small. You are bigger and stronger. You can hold on." He gave Mia a hug and said, "You are brave. You can do it. Do you want to try to catch the fish?"

Tom said, "Yes, I want to try to catch the fish. Maybe I can catch a big one and a small one. Then we can have a fish party." Mia said, "No, I don't want to try to catch the fish. Maybe I can catch a cold and a sneeze. Then we can have a sick day."

Dad said, "The fish will not make you sick. It will make you happy. It is fun to catch a fish. It is a surprise. You never know what you will get." He gave Mia a kiss and said, "You are smart. You can do it. Do you want to try to catch the fish?"

Tom said, "Yes, yes, yes. I want to try to catch the fish. Maybe I can catch a yellow one and a purple one. Then we can have a rainbow

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to whistle, and he would whistle all day long. One day, Timmy found a stamp on the ground. He was so lucky!

Timmy decided to show the stamp to his friend, Sally. As he walked to Sally's house, he continued to whistle. But then, a big dog appeared and scared Timmy. He stopped whistling and dropped the stamp.

The stamp fell into a puddle and got all wet. Timmy was sad because he couldn't show Sally the lucky stamp. He went home feeling sad and disappointed.

Timmy learned that sometimes lucky things can turn unlucky, but he knew he could always find something else to make him happy, like whistling.

Once upon a time, there were two best friends named Max and Molly. Max was a little boy and Molly was a little girl. Max and Molly were always playing together. One day, Max fell and hurt his knee. Molly wanted to help him, so she went to her house to borrow a bandage for Max.

Molly knocked on the door and said, "Mommy, can I borrow a bandage for Max?"

Mommy said, "Yes, sweetheart, you can borrow one. Here, take this one."

Molly took the little bandage and ran back to Max. She put the bandage on Max's knee.

Max smiled and said, "Thank you Molly, it feels much better now!"

Molly smiled and said, "You're welcome, Max!"

The two best friends hugged and went back to playing together. They never stopped having fun!

Once upon a time there was a piece. It was very original. One day Sam decided to stretch the piece. But when he did, the piece broke into two pieces. Sam was very sad. He tried his best to put the two pieces back together but they wouldn't fit. So in the end, Sam had nothing left but two small pieces. The original piece was gone forever and he was very sad.

Once there was a large building with a dark sky above it and a bright moon. Anna was walking around the building with her big brother, Jack, who was smiling a lot.

Suddenly, they heard a growling sound coming from the large, dark forest. "What's that sound?" asked Anna. Jack just smiled and said, "Let's find out!"

The two walked cautiously, Anna holding tightly onto Jack's hand into the darkness of the forest. As they got closer, Anna could see a large, fierce bear standing before them. The bear was growling angrily and blocking their way.

Jack looked very scared but he still managed to smile and said, "We should turn around and go back". Anna smiled and nodded, and they both ran quickly out of the forest.

The two were very relieved to be out of the dark forest and away from the large bear. They gave each other a big hug and smiled, happy that they were safe.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to ride her bike through the park. One sunny day, Lily saw a big pile of wood. She wanted to ride over it, but it was too high. So, she got off her bike and climbed up the wood. When she got to the top, she looked around and saw that the park was very quiet. It was nice to be up high and see everything. After a while, Lily climbed back down and rode her bike home. The end.

One day, a young boy was near a lake. He looked around the lake and wondered what he could find. As he walked along, he saw a fisherman in the distance. The fisherman was casting his net into the lake. The boy wondered what kind of creature the fisherman would catch.

The young boy decided to speak to the fisherman. He approached and asked the fisherman what he had caught. But the fisherman shook his head and said he had not caught anything yet. The boy asked again and the fisherman smiled but still said he had not caught anything yet.

The boy continued to walk along beside the lake and he saw many beautiful creatures. The lake was full of life. The boy watched the lake and soon the sky grew dark. He quickly said goodbye to the fisherman and ran home.

The next day, the young boy was a bit sad as he walked down to the lake. He had wanted to stay and see if the fisherman would catch something. But when he reached the lake, he saw the fisherman and he could tell the fisherman had been quite successful.

The fisherman had caught a big, golden fish. The young boy was so grateful to the fisherman for letting him stay around and watch. The fisherman grinned, happy that the young boy enjoyed his day at the lake.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lucy. She loved to dance. Every day, she would put on her pretty dress and dance around her room. She would jump, spin, and wiggle like a crazy dancer. Lucy always had a big smile on her face when she danced.

One sunny day, Lucy went to the park with her mom. She saw a group of kids playing and dancing to music. She wanted to join them, so she asked her mom if she could. Her mom said yes, and Lucy ran over to the kids. They were all dancing and having lots of fun.

Lucy started to dance with the kids. They played a game called "Follow the Leader." One kid would do a dance move, and the others would follow. They all took turns being the leader. Lucy did her crazy dance moves, and everyone laughed and had a great time. The day was full of fun, and Lucy was so happy to make new friends who loved to dance just like her.

Once upon a time there was a young girl called Lily. Lily loved to explore outdoors. One day she saw a big boat sailing in the lake nearby. She wanted to sail too!

So Lily asked her mommy to take her to the lake. When they got there, mommy showed Lily how to sail the boat. Lily was so excited and laughed with joy as she learned how to move the boat.

After sailing for a while, Lily spotted a trail in the forest nearby. She wanted to follow the trail and explore! Mommy told her to be careful and with that Lily set off on her adventure.

Lily followed the trail into the forest, full of excitement. She saw many animals and trees, and some big rocks that she could climb on. She felt so happy and free as she went along the trail.

When it was time to go home, Lily had many stories to tell Mommy about her adventure. She said goodbye to the trail, feeling happy and content.

Tom is a dog. He likes to run and play and bark. He lives with Sam, who is a boy. Sam loves Tom and gives him food and water and hugs.

One day, Sam and Tom go for a walk in the park. They see many things: trees, flowers, birds, squirrels. Tom is eager to chase them, but Sam holds his leash. He says, "No, Tom, stay with me."

But then, Sam sees a big truck. It is loud and fast and scary. Sam wants to see it closer, so he lets go of Tom's leash. He runs to the road, but he does not look both ways. Tom sees a car coming. It is going to hit Sam. Tom is scared, but he is brave. He runs after Sam and barks. He jumps and pushes Sam out of the way. The car misses them, but it honks. Sam and Tom fall on the grass. They are safe, but they are shaken.

Sam hugs Tom and says, "Thank you, Tom, you rescued me. You are a good dog. I am sorry I let go of your leash. I was silly and careless. I will never do that again."
