Once, there was a little girl named Sarah. She was three years old, and loved to roll around in the grass. It made her stomach flutter when she rolled.

Sarah had a gloomy day one day. It was raining, and everything outside was wet. She decided to stay inside and rolled around on the rug.

She rolled and rolled, but she wasn't happy. Then, something magical started to happen! The rain started to stop, and the sun was out again.

Sarah jumped off the rug and ran outside. She rolled around in the grass and the sun warmed her back. She continued rolling and giggling and it filled her stomach with joy.

The rain had gone, and Sarah had a great day. She kept on rolling, until her mom called her in for dinner.

Lily loved ponies. She had a toy pony that she played with every day. She named her pony Star, because she had a white star on her forehead. Lily wanted to see a real pony, but she did not know where to find one.

One day, Lily and her mom went to the park. Lily saw a big field with some animals. She saw cows, sheep, and chickens. She also saw a fence with a sign that said "Farm". Lily wondered if there were any ponies inside.

"Mom, can we go to the farm?" Lily asked.

"Sure, honey. Maybe we can see some ponies there," her mom said.

They walked to the farm and asked the farmer if they could look around. The farmer was very nice and said yes. He showed them his animals and told them their names. Lily liked the animals, but she did not see any ponies.

"Excuse me, sir. Do you have any ponies?" Lily asked.

"Well, I do have one old pony, but she is very shy. She likes to hide in the barn. You can try to search for her, but be gentle and quiet. Her name is Daisy," the farmer said.

Lily and her mom thanked the farmer and went to the barn. Lily searched for Daisy, but she did not see her. She looked behind the hay, under the blankets, and in the corners. She was about to give up, when she heard a soft neigh.

Lily followed the sound and found Daisy in a dark corner. She was a brown pony with a white star on her forehead, just like Lily's toy. Lily smiled and whispered, "Hello, Daisy. I'm Lily. I'm your friend."

Daisy looked at Lily and slowly came out of her hiding place. She sniffed Lily's hand and licked it. Lily giggled and petted Daisy's mane. Daisy nuzzled Lily's cheek and neighed again.

Lily and Daisy became friends. Lily's mom took a picture of them and said, "You found her, Lily. You found your pony." Lily hugged Daisy and said, "I love you, Daisy. You are my star."

Once there was a three year old boy. He liked to jog in the park. One day he saw something glimmering in the grass. He went to take a closer look and saw it was a magnet! He picked it up and put it in his pocket.

The boy went home and asked his mum what the magnet could do. His mum said it could stick things together. So the boy and his mum went to the kitchen and tried the magnet on the fridge. It worked! The magnet stuck pictures of their family to the fridge.

The boy decided to take the magnet with him when he went to the park again. He liked to jog in the park and the magnet was nice and comfortable in his pocket. He ran around the park, holding the magnet and feeling very pleased with himself.

Back at home, the boy's mum asked him what he wanted to do with the magnet. He said he wanted to keep it forever! So, the boy put the magnet away in his bedroom and always kept it safe. Every day he liked to take it out and remember his adventure in the park.

Mum read a story to Tom. Tom watched with wide eyes. He liked when Mum told stories. When the story was done, Mum gave Tom a wipe. She wiped his face until it was clean. Then Tom had his milk. Mum helped him hold the cup. Tom smiled, he liked the way the warm milk felt in his mouth.

Next, Mum had an idea. She said, "Let's play a game!" Tom jumped out of bed and said, "Yes!" Mum clapped her hands and said, "Let's fit the pieces into the box!"

Tom and Mum worked together, fitting the pieces into the box. It was a fun game. They laughed and smiled until all of the pieces were fit in the box. Then they had a hug and said goodbye. Tom felt happy and fit.

Once upon a time, there was a big war between two kingdoms. The land was not dry anymore because of all the rain from the sky. One day, a little bird was flying over the battlefield and saw all the fighting. It started to panic and flew away as fast as it could.

The bird flew to a nearby forest where it saw a family of rabbits. The rabbits asked the bird why it was panicking. The bird explained about the war and how it was making the land wet. The rabbits were scared too and decided to leave their home and find a safer place to live.

As they were leaving, they saw a wise old owl perched on a tree. The owl asked them what was wrong and the bird explained about the war and the wet land. The owl told them not to panic and that they should work together to find a solution. They all agreed and decided to search for a dry place to live until the war was over. And so, they set off on their journey, hoping to find a new home soon.

Once upon a time, there lived a little girl named Sophie. Sophie was three years old and she loved to dream. Every night, she would close her eyes and dream of special things.

One night, Sophie dreamed of a beautiful laser that shimmered and sparkled in every color of the rainbow. As she looked at the laser, she wished she could have one for herself.

The next morning, Sophie woke up feeling very worried. She had not seen her laser anywhere. She searched around the house and asked everyone in her family, but no one had seen it.

Sophie was very sad, but then she realized something. She had been dreaming about the laser! Suddenly she was happy again and she thanked the stars for letting her dream such wonderful things.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl and her mom. The girl was named Cherry. One day, Cherry's mom asked her if she wanted to go for a ride. But Cherry refused.

"Let's go for a ride, Cherry," said mom. "No, I refuse," said Cherry.

Mom was feeling sad because Cherry didn't want to go on a ride. But then an idea came to her. "I know! Let's get a comfortable car seat for our ride," said Mom.

Cherry smiled and said, "Yes! I like that." So mom got a comfortable car seat and put it in their car.

Finally, Cherry and mom went for the ride. They both had a lot of fun. At the end of the ride they got an ice cream cone with a cherry on top. Cherry was so happy!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to cook with her mommy. One day, they decided to prepare dinner together. Mommy asked Lily to wash the mushrooms. Lily loved to play with water, so she was happy to help.

While they were cooking, the pots and pans made a lot of noisy sounds. Lily covered her ears and giggled. Mommy said, "Don't worry, Lily. The noisy sounds mean that the food is cooking well."

Finally, dinner was ready. Mommy served the mushrooms and Lily was so happy to have helped prepare them. She took a bite and said, "Yum, these mushrooms are delicious!"

Once upon a time, there was a little house in the deep woods. In the house lived a kind bunny named Bobo and his best friend, a tiny bird named Chirpy. They were always happy and played together every day.

One day, Bobo and Chirpy were playing hide and seek. Chirpy hid in a tree, but Bobo could not find her. He looked and looked, but Chirpy was too good at hiding. Bobo became sad and went back to the little house. Chirpy saw Bobo was sad and felt bad.

Chirpy flew back to the house and said, "I am sorry, Bobo. I did not mean to make you sad." Bobo looked at Chirpy and said, "I forgive you, Chirpy. We are still friends." They hugged and played happily together again. From that day on, they always remembered to take care of each other's feelings.

Once upon a time, there was a boy called Jack. He was three years old and he liked to ride.

One day Jack saw an enormous peach. It was the biggest peach he had ever seen! He wanted to go on an adventure so he decided to climb onto the peach and ride.

Jack rode the peach all around. He rode up high mountains and down low valleys. He flew through the clouds and across the sea. He even rode over the rainbow!

Jack had the best adventure ever! He was so happy and excited when he got off the peach and back home.

He could not wait to go riding on the enormous peach again!

Once upon a time, there was a small boat. On the boat, there were two friends, Tara and Pete.

Tara and Pete were sailing in the sea on their boat, when they saw something strange in the water. As they looked closer, they saw that it was a whale.

The whale looked very sad and was unable to move. Tara and Pete knew that the whale was in danger, so they bravely decided to save it.

Tara and Pete were very persistent. They worked together, using nets and ropes to try to save the whale. They worked for hours and hours until finally, the whale was saved.

The whale thanked Tara and Pete and swam away, free and happy again. Tara and Pete had saved the whale and they were proud, and they vowed to always help animals in need.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She was very curious and loved to explore. One day, she went to the park with her mommy and saw a big fountain. It was so pretty and Lily wanted to touch it. She asked her mommy if she could go closer and her mommy said yes.

Lily walked closer to the fountain and saw a shiny coin at the bottom. She wanted to get it, but it was too far down. Then, she had an idea! She pulled on her mommy's hand and asked for help. Her mommy understood and pulled her up onto her shoulders.

Lily was so happy! She could see everything from up high and her mommy helped her get the shiny coin from the fountain. She felt proud and excited to have found it. From that day on, Lily loved going to the park and seeing all the beautiful things there.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a hairy cat named Fluffy and loved to play with her spoon. One day, Lily's grandma came to visit her. They played together and ate cookies. Lily was happy to have her grandma around.

But then, something bad happened. Fluffy got sick and passed away. Lily was very sad and cried a lot. She missed Fluffy and her spoon didn't bring her any joy anymore. Even grandma couldn't make her feel better.

Lily learned that sometimes things don't end well, but she will always remember the fun times she had with Fluffy and her grandma's visit.

Ben and Mia were playing with their toy rockets in the garden. They liked to pretend they were flying to different planets and having adventures. Ben said, "I want to go to the red planet. It has big rocks and fire." Mia said, "No, I want to go to the green planet. It has pretty flowers and animals."

They argued for a while, until they heard a loud noise from the shed. They looked and saw a big, smelly monster coming out. It had fur, horns, and sharp teeth. It roared and stomped towards them. Ben and Mia were very scared. They dropped their toy rockets and ran to the house.

They knocked on the door and shouted, "Mom, Dad, help! There's a monster in the garden!" Their parents opened the door and saw the monster. They laughed and said, "That's not a monster, that's Uncle Bob. He's wearing a costume for Halloween. He wanted to scare you as a joke."

Ben and Mia were confused and angry. They said, "That's not funny, that's mean. You scared us a lot. We don't like Uncle Bob's costume. It's too smelly and scary." Uncle Bob took off his mask and said, "I'm sorry, kids. I didn't mean to scare you so much. I thought you would like a surprise. Do you want to see my costume? It's from a movie about space."

Ben and Mia shook their heads and said, "No, thank you. We don't want to see your costume. We want to play with our toy rockets. We like our own planets better. They are not smelly and scary. They are fun and nice." They picked up their toy rockets and went back to the garden. They decided to take turns flying to the red planet and the green planet. They had fun and forgot about the monster. Uncle Bob felt bad and went to the shed. He hoped they would forgive him later.

One day, there was a mouse walking around outside in the garden. The mouse saw a pretty trap. She decided to have a closer look and stepped right into it.

The mouse bleated, "Help me! Help me!"

An old farmer was walking by and heard the mouse crying. He came over to see what was the matter and saw the mouse trapped. He knew the mouse wanted to get out so he said, "I will release you."

The farmer grabbed the trap, opened the door and released the mouse. The mouse was so happy and thanked the farmer for letting her go. She scurried away quickly.

But when the farmer released the mouse, a lot of other animals that were living in the garden came out of their hiding places. The animals were scuttling about and making a lot of noise. The old farmer freaked out. He quickly reached for his gun and fired at the animals to get them to go away. The animals ran away and the old farmer felt a bit better.

But in the end, the animals never returned to the garden and the farmer was very sad.

Jack was walking to the park when he noticed a woman's bracelet lying on the ground. It shone in the sunlight like a million diamonds. Jack had never seen something so pretty before. He picked it up and thought he would surprise his mum later.

At the park, Jack met his friend Daisy. Daisy asked him what he had in his hand. Jack proudly showed her the bracelet and said he was going to give it to his mum.

All of a sudden, a woman came up to them. She said, "That's my bracelet! You stole it!" Jack was so scared and he quickly handed the bracelet back to the woman. She thanked Jack for returning it and scurried away.

Jack and Daisy sat down on a regular bench, full of shame. Daisy said, "We should always ask before we take something that doesn't belong to us." Jack nodded and said "I promise I won't do something like this again."

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to make things with her hands. One day, she decided to make a candle. She got some wax and a wick and put them together. She lit the wick and the candle started to burn.

Lily loved the candle's soft light, but her mom said it was too harsh for her eyes. So, Lily put the candle in a jar to make it softer. She was happy with her creation and showed it to her friends. They all thought it was amazing.

From that day on, Lily loved to make candles. She made them in different colors and shapes. She even made some for her mom and dad. And they all loved them too!

Anna and Ben like to jog with their dad. They put on their shoes and hats and go outside. The sun is bright and the air is fresh. It is a perfect day for jogging.

They jog on the path that goes around the park. They see birds and flowers and other people. They say hello to them. Anna and Ben like to jog fast, but their dad tells them to slow down sometimes.

"Look, there is a big hill ahead," their dad says. "Do you want to jog up the hill?"

"Yes, yes, yes!" Anna and Ben say. They love hills. They think hills are fun and exciting.

They jog up the hill, but it is hard. Their legs get tired and their breath gets short. They have to stop and rest a few times. Their dad cheers them on.

"You can do it, Anna and Ben! You are strong and brave!"

They finally reach the top of the hill. They feel proud and happy. They look at the view. They see the park, the trees, the sky, and the clouds. They see their house in the distance.

"Wow, this is beautiful," Anna says.

"I like it here," Ben says.

"Me too," their dad says. "You did a great job, Anna and Ben. You are amazing joggers."

They hug and smile. They jog down the hill and go back home. They have a snack and a drink. They tell their mom about their adventure. They have a perfect day.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. He loved to read his favorite novel about a brave knight who saved a princess. One day, Timmy stumbled while walking in the park and fell on the ground.

"Are you okay?" asked a kind lady who saw him fall.

"Yes, I'm okay," replied Timmy, holding his novel tightly. "I just stumbled."

The kind lady smiled and helped Timmy stand up. "Be careful next time," she said.

Timmy nodded and continued to read his novel as he walked home. When he got home, he told his mom about his adventure in the park. "I stumbled, but I didn't drop my novel," he said proudly.

"That's great, Timmy," said his mom. "You're such a brave boy."

Timmy smiled and went to bed, happy and content with his exciting day.

Sam was miserable. He did not like the rain. He wanted to play outside with his ball and his bike, but the sky was grey and the water was falling. He looked out the window and saw a big puddle. He wished he could jump in it and splash.

"Sam, come here," his mom called. "I have something for you."

Sam walked to his mom. She was holding a yellow coat and a pair of boots. "Look, these are your rain clothes. You can wear them and go outside. But you have to be careful and stay close to the house, okay?"

Sam smiled. He liked his rain clothes. They were bright and warm. He put them on and ran to the door. His mom opened it and gave him a hug. "Have fun, but don't get too wet," she said.

Sam nodded and went outside. He saw the big puddle and ran towards it. He jumped in it and splashed. He laughed and felt happy. He saw a stick and picked it up. He used it to make waves and bubbles. He saw a frog and said hello. The frog croaked and jumped away.

Sam saw something shiny under the water. He was curious. He bent down and tried to reach it. He felt something hard and round. He pulled it out and looked at it. It was a coin. It was silver and had a picture of a man on it. Sam wondered who the man was and why he was on the coin. He decided to keep it. He put it in his pocket and looked for more shiny things.

He did not see his mom watching him from the window. She smiled and felt proud. She was glad that Sam was having fun and finding treasures. She thought he was a brave and clever boy. She hoped he would always be happy, even when it rained.

A boy was outside in his yard, playing with a toy car. He saw something off in the distance and ran toward it. As he got closer, he saw that it was a truck and that it was full of sand. The boy was so excited! He got right up to it and started to load the toy car with sand.

The boy thought this was great fun and he kept loading until the car was full. Suddenly he realized that the truck was moving, and it was moving away from him! He had been so foolish to not notice that the truck was going down the street.

The boy ran and ran but he was too late. The truck was gone and all the sand was gone too. The boy was very sad that he had made the foolish mistake of not paying attention to where the truck was going. He should have known it would leave him.

He learned an important lesson that day; never be foolish and always pay attention to where things are going.

Once upon a time, a little boy named Timmy went to the park with his mom. Timmy loved playing on the swings, but he was too small to reach the handle. His mom helped him get on the swing and held onto the handle to keep him safe.

Suddenly, Timmy's friend Billy came over and wanted to play too. Billy was bigger than Timmy and wanted to swing higher. He pushed Timmy off the swing, and Timmy fell down.

Timmy started to cry, and his mom came over to see what happened. Timmy told her what happened, and his mom talked to Billy. Billy said sorry and promised to be more careful next time. Timmy's mom helped him back onto the swing and held onto the handle to make sure he was safe. Timmy smiled and started swinging again, feeling happy and safe.

Carly and Jeff were two friends who were very organized. They planned to take a trip on a yacht. On the morning of their trip, Carly and Jeff got ready. They grabbed their bags and hats. Then they shut their door and ran to the boat. They stepped onto the yacht and waved goodbye to their friends. The boat was so big! They looked around and saw the 'captain' steering. Carly and Jeff were so excited. The boat sailed across the water. The sun shined and birds sang. After a while, Carly and Jeff took turns steering. They had a wonderful time. When it was time to go back, Carly and Jeff shut the doors to the boat and headed home. They were so glad they got to take a ride on a yacht!

Once upon a time, there was a big boat that went on a long trip. The boat had many people on it, and they were all happy. They saw many fish in the water and birds in the sky. One day, they saw a big seal that was swimming in the water. The seal was fierce and had big teeth, but it didn't hurt anyone.

After many days, the boat arrived at a new place. It was a big island with many trees and animals. The people on the boat were happy to be there. They went to explore the island and see all the new things. But then, they saw the fierce seal again. This time, the seal was angry and attacked the people. They tried to run away, but the seal was too fast.

In the end, the people were hurt and scared. They had to leave the island and go back on the boat. They were sad because they wanted to stay on the island, but the fierce seal made it too dangerous. They hoped that one day they could come back and see the island again, but they knew they had to be careful of the fierce seal.

Once upon a time, there lived a dinosaur. It was so big and strong, yet gentle and kind. The dinosaur loved to soar in the big blue sky. It would flap its wings and be up high in no time.

The dinosaur started to think up a new way to fly. He thought it would be so much fun to try something creative. He came up with a plan and flew up high. He twirled around, flapped his wings, and zoomed through the sky.

As he soared through the sky, the dinosaur was amazed at all the beauty and fun. He was so high up and felt so free. All the animals below cheered and waved as he flew past. They were glad to see the dinosaur so happy.

Finally, the dinosaur landed in a meadow. He was super tired and snuggled up for a nap. What a fun and creative way to soar in the sky!

One day, there was a clown in the park. He was smiling and making faces. The 3 year old child wanted to go over and talk to him. His mom said it was ok, as long as he felt safe. So, he walked over to the clown and said hello. The clown was very friendly and asked for the child's name. He was happy to understand what was said.

The clown then had a big surprise. He showed the child a magic wand that could make bubbles fly in the air! The 3 year old was so excited and jumped up and down. The clown helped him to make the bubble fly, which made him even more excited.

The child thanked the clown and said goodbye. He understood that he was very lucky to have met the clown in the park. He even thought it might be a good idea to come back again and play with the magic wand.

Once upon a time, there was a monkey who loved bananas. One day, he got very hungry and wanted a banana to eat. But he didn't have any bananas left. So, he decided to ask his friend, the bird, to deliver a banana to him. The bird was very fast and flew to the banana tree to get a banana for the monkey. Soon, the bird came back with a big, yellow banana for the monkey to eat. The monkey was very happy and thanked the bird for delivering the banana so fast. From that day on, the monkey and the bird were good friends and shared bananas together.

One day, a little boy named Tim found a wallet on the floor. It was big and brown. Tim wanted to see what was inside, but he needed to balance on his toes to reach the table.

Tim put the wallet on the table and opened it. Inside, he found a picture of an angry cat. The cat had a big frown on its face. Tim thought the cat looked funny, so he laughed.

Tim's mom saw the wallet and asked, "Whose wallet is this?" Tim said, "I found it." They looked inside and saw the angry cat. They both laughed at the funny cat. Then, they went to find the wallet's owner, so they could give it back.

Once upon a time, there was a bald man who loved to dance. He would dance all day long and he was very happy. One day, he went outside to dance in the park. While he was dancing, he tripped and fell down. He hurt his head and started to cry.

Some children saw him and ran to help. They tried to make him feel better, but he was still sad. He didn't want to dance anymore because he was afraid he would fall again. He went home feeling very sad.

The next day, the man didn't come out of his house. His neighbors were worried and went to check on him. They found him lying on the floor. He had fallen again and hurt himself badly. Sadly, the man never danced again.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. He lived in a modern house with his mom and dad. Tim loved to play with his toys and eat yummy food. One day, his mom was making dinner. Tim was very hungry and could not wait to eat.

Tim went to the kitchen and asked his mom, "What's for dinner, Mom?" His mom smiled and said, "You have to guess, Tim!" Tim thought for a moment and said, "Is it pizza?" His mom shook her head and said, "No, try again!" Tim guessed, "Is it spaghetti?" His mom nodded and said, "Yes, you guessed right!"

But, there was a problem. Tim did not like spaghetti. He wanted to eat pizza for dinner. Tim felt sad and did not want to eat. His mom saw that Tim was not happy. She wanted to make him happy again.

So, Tim's mom thought of a fun idea. She said, "Let's make the spaghetti look like a pizza!" They put cheese and tomato sauce on the spaghetti. Tim was excited to try the spaghetti pizza. He took a bite and said, "Yummy! This is the best dinner ever!" Tim and his mom smiled and enjoyed their dinner together.

Lily and Tom are at the park with their mom. They like to play on the swings and the slide. They also like to look at the birds and the flowers. Sometimes they gaze at the sky and see the clouds and the sun.

Mom says it is time to go home. She tells Lily and Tom to come to the bench. She has a surprise for them. Lily and Tom run to the bench. They are curious and excited.

Mom opens her bag and takes out two ice creams. One is chocolate and one is vanilla. She gives one to Lily and one to Tom. She says they can choose which one they want. Lily and Tom are happy. They thank mom and lick their ice creams.

Mom says they have to eat quickly because the ice creams will melt. She also says they have to be careful not to drop them or make a mess. Lily and Tom nod and eat their ice creams. They enjoy the cold and sweet taste.

A big truck passes by the park. It is very noisy. It makes a loud honk and a rumble. Lily and Tom are scared. They drop their ice creams on the ground. They cry and hug mom. Mom says it is okay. She says the truck is just doing its job. She says she will buy them new ice creams later. She says they have to follow her order and go home now. Lily and Tom wipe their tears and hold mom's hand. They walk home with mom. They hope the truck will not come back.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play outside with his kite. He would run and run until the kite would fly high up in the sky.

One day, Timmy's kite got stuck in a big tree. Timmy was frightened and didn't know what to do. He asked his friend, "Can you help me climb up the tree to get my kite?"

His friend said, "Sure, I can climb up the tree and get your kite for you." So, Timmy's friend climbed up the tree and got the kite down. Timmy was so happy and thanked his friend for helping him.

Once upon a time there was a beautiful forest filled with flowers and trees. In the forest there were lots of animals, like deer and birds. Each day one of the animals, a fox, went out to search for food.

One day the fox found a hidden rice field. The fox was very happy and it was hungry so it started to fill its belly with rice.

But soon, the rice field started to empty, and the fox could not find enough food. The fox was sad because it had to go home with an empty stomach.

The fox learned the important lesson that it was better to find food that would not be hidden so it could always be found. That way, the fox and the other animals would always have enough to eat.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl. She liked to go for walks in the park.

One day, the little girl went for a walk and she saw some trouble. She tried to step away from it but couldn't. She started to fall down the hill.

The little girl started to cry. She was scared and didn't know what to do. Suddenly, a bird came and scooped her up in his wings. He flew so high in the sky, until they reached the top.

The little girl smiled. The bird told her that sometimes trouble can make you sour, but that you can still find things to be happy about.

The little girl thanked the bird and they went back down the hill. From that day on, the little girl was a lot braver and never forgot what the bird had said.

Once upon a time there was a panda. The panda was very different from the other animals. He was red and he wore funny clothes.

One day, the panda saw a bunny. He shouted, "Hi Bunny!"

The bunny was so scared that he ran away. The panda felt sad and shouted, "Come back!" but the bunny did not hear him.

Then the panda saw a lion. The lion was very angry. He shouted at the panda "How dare you shout at my friend!"

The panda was so scared that he ran away. Suddenly, he fell into a deep hole and could not get out. He shouted for help but no one heard him.

And that's how the panda was never seen again. He was stuck in the deep hole and never came out.

The sun was shining and children were playing together outside the church. Emily was playing with them, but she was feeling very miserable. She watched as the others laughed and danced around.

Suddenly, a voice called out to Emily. "Come here, Emily," said the voice. Emily looked around, but she didn't see anyone. The voice said again, "Come here Emily. I have something for you."

Emily was scared, but she slowly made her way towards the church. She stopped at the entrance, and she was amazed by what she saw. Inside the church were people dancing happily. Emily wanted to be like them, but she was too scared.

The voice said, "Come on in, Emily. We'll teach you how to dance." Emily hesitantly stepped into the church. She watched as the others danced, and soon she was joining in too. She found it so much fun! She was no longer feeling miserable at all.

A year later, everyone gathered at the church again, but this time they were not dancing. They were celebrating Emily and her new talent for dancing. She had been learning more steps and movements, and she was so proud of herself. Everyone was amazed and happy for Emily.

The voice from the past year watched Emily in the church and smiled. She thought to herself, I knew this day would come.

Once there were two friends, Jane and Ross. Ross was always very honest, and Jane loved him for that. One day, Ross invited Jane to join him on an adventure.

"Will you come?" Ross asked.

"Yes!" Jane said excitedly.

The two friends went off to explore. On their way, they saw a big number, written in sparkly silver. Jane asked Ross what it was.

"That is a magical number," Ross said. "It includes lots of fun things."

Ross then opened the door next to the number. Inside, they saw a room filled with wonderful surprises! There were toys, games and trinkets, all just for them! Ross was so happy to share this wonderful place with Jane.

They had lots of fun. Ross was thankful for an honest friend like Jane. Without her, he would never have found the magical number.

Lily and Max are best friends. They like to play together in the park. One day, they find a big camera on a bench. It has a red button and a screen.

"Look, a camera!" Lily says. "Let's record us playing!"

"Okay!" Max says. "How do we do it?"

Lily picks up the camera and points it at Max. She presses the red button. The screen shows Max's face.

"Say something, Max!" Lily says.

"Hello, camera!" Max says. He makes a funny face and sticks out his tongue. Lily laughs.

"Your turn, Lily!" Max says. He takes the camera and points it at Lily. He presses the red button. The screen shows Lily's face.

"Hello, camera!" Lily says. She smiles and winks. Max giggles.

"You are adorable, Lily!" Max says.

"Thank you, Max!" Lily says. "You are adorable, too!"

They hug and laugh. They record more of their fun in the park. They are very happy.

Once upon a time, there was a pale girl who liked to play with her friends. One day she received an invitation to a special event. She was excited and couldn't wait to go!

When she arrived she saw all of her friends there. But something felt wrong. Suddenly, the bad guy appeared. He was angry and said that nobody was allowed to leave. He took away the invitation from the pale girl.

Everyone was scared, but the pale girl was brave. She tried to fight back against the bad guy. In the end, the bad guy won. He shouted at everyone to never come back.

The pale girl was sad. She wanted to be with her friends, but it was too dangerous. The bad thing had happened and everyone had to go home.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Millie. She was three years old and loved to play. Every day she went to her room to find something new and interesting to do.

Today, Millie found her mom's scissors. She liked how smooth and shiny they were! Millie picked them up and started playing. She heard a voice that said “Stop!” Millie stopped and looked around. It was her mom!

Her mom said “The scissors are very sharp. You need to be gentle with them.” Millie nodded her head and carefully placed the scissors down. She smiled and said “Okay! I'll be gentle.”

Millie picked up some paper and used the scissors gently to cut shapes and animals. She was so proud of her creations!

When it was time for dinner, Millie put the scissors away to save for another day. She went to the dinner table and smiled, knowing that she had used the scissors safely and kept them nice.

Once upon a time, there was a fat crane who lived by a big lake. The fat crane had many friends who played with him every day. They liked to splash in the water and have fun.

One day, a new bird came to the lake. She was shy and didn't know anyone. The fat crane saw her and said, "Hi, I am Fat Crane. Do you want to play with us?" The new bird smiled and said, "Yes, I would like that."

After they played, Fat Crane gave the new bird a big hug. The new bird was happy to have a new friend. From that day on, they all played together and had lots of fun.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved playing with balloons, especially the big, colorful ones. One day, she went to the park with her friends and they all had balloons. Lily's balloon was the biggest and most beautiful of them all.

But then, a boy named Max came along. He didn't have a balloon and he looked envious of Lily's. He asked if he could have it, but Lily said no. Max got angry and tried to take the balloon from her. Suddenly, the balloon snapped and popped loudly.

Lily was sad that her balloon was gone, but she realized that sharing is important. She gave Max one of her other balloons and they became friends. They played together and had fun, and Lily learned that being kind is better than being selfish.

It was spring and the sun was shining brightly in the sky. Little Lucy wanted to prepare something special. She grabbed a bag and filled it with some yummy treats and a special present.

As she walked to the park, she met her friend Tim. He was also getting ready to go.

"What are you preparing, Lucy?" Tim asked.

"I'm making a special surprise for the park. I brought lots of treats," Lucy said, showing the bag.

"That is so nice of you! What a great way to enjoy spring," Tim said.

Unfortunately, it started to rain and soon it became a terrible storm. The sky turned a dark grey and it was too dangerous to continue walking.

Tim and Lucy had to return home and unfortunately their plans for the park had to be cancelled.

But, because of their kind gestures, the people of the park remembered their friendship and the sweet surprise Lucy was preparing.

Lily and Tom were twins who liked to play together. One day, they found a candle in a drawer and decided to light it. They thought it was fun to watch the flame flicker and make shadows on the wall.

"Look, Lily, the candle is so pretty!" Tom said.

"Yes, Tom, it is. But we have to be careful. Mommy said candles can be hot and dangerous," Lily said.

They played with the candle for a while, but then they heard Mommy calling them for dinner. They ran to the kitchen, forgetting to blow out the candle.

The candle burned slowly on the table, until it reached a paper napkin. The napkin caught fire and soon the whole table was on fire. Smoke filled the room and the fire alarm went off.

Mommy smelled the smoke and ran to the living room. She saw the fire and grabbed a blanket to put it out. She was very scared and angry.

"Lily! Tom! What have you done? You could have burned the house down! How could you play with a candle?" Mommy shouted.

Lily and Tom came back to the living room and saw the mess. They felt very sorry and ashamed. They hugged Mommy and cried.

"We're sorry, Mommy. We didn't mean to. We just wanted to see the candle. We forgot to blow it out. We love you, Mommy. Please don't be mad at us," they said.

Mommy hugged them back and calmed down. She was glad they were not hurt, but she was still upset.

"I love you too, Lily and Tom. But you have to listen to me. Candles are not toys. They are for grown-ups only. They can cause fire and hurt people. You have to be more careful and responsible. Do you understand?" Mommy said.

"Yes, Mommy. We understand. We're sorry. We won't play with candles again. We learned our lesson. We don't want to miss you or our home," they said.

Mommy kissed them and took them to dinner. She hoped they would remember their mistake and never do it again. She also hoped they would always appreciate what they have and not take it for granted. She knew they were good kids who made a bad choice. She loved them very much.

One day, Margaret was getting ready for dinner. She was wearing her furry coat and picking up her hat. She was almost ready to go, but she decided to resist. She wanted to stay home and play.

Her mother came into the room. "Margaret, what are you doing? You must come to dinner."

"But I don't want to go. I want to stay home and play!"

"You need to come to dinner. It will be fun," said her mother.

Margaret thought for a moment. "Okay," she said. "I'll come."

So they both went out to dinner. It was a fun evening. Everything was furry, warm, and delicious. Margaret had a great time and was glad that she resisted staying at home.

Tom and Ben were best friends. They liked to play with trucks in the sandbox. They had many trucks of different colors and sizes. But Tom's favorite truck was the enormous red one. It was bigger than all the other trucks and could carry a lot of sand.

One day, Tom and Ben were playing with their trucks in the sandbox. Tom was using the enormous red truck to make a big hill of sand. Ben was using a small blue truck to make a tunnel under the hill. They were having fun.

But then, Ben saw the enormous red truck and wanted to try it. He said to Tom, "Can I use your red truck for a little bit? It looks so cool."

Tom did not want to share his red truck. He said to Ben, "No, you can't. It is my truck. You have your own truck. Go away."

Ben felt sad and angry. He said to Tom, "That is not nice. You are a bad friend. You should share your trucks. I will take your red truck anyway."

Ben tried to grab the red truck from Tom, but Tom held on tight. They both pulled and pushed the red truck, making a lot of noise. The red truck lay between them, but neither of them could have it.

Their teacher heard the noise and came to the sandbox. She saw Tom and Ben fighting over the red truck. She said to them, "What is going on here? Why are you fighting? You should play nicely and share your toys."

Tom and Ben stopped fighting and looked at their teacher. They felt ashamed and sorry. They said to their teacher, "We are sorry, teacher. We both wanted the red truck and we did not share. We were not good friends."

The teacher said to them, "I am glad you are sorry, but you need to apologize to each other and make up. The red truck is not more important than your friendship. You can take turns using it or play with it together. There are enough trucks for everyone."

Tom and Ben nodded and said to each other, "I am sorry, friend. I was selfish and mean. Can we share the red truck and play together?"

They hugged and smiled. They picked up the red truck and decided to use it to make a bigger hill and a longer tunnel. They thanked their teacher and went back to the sandbox. They played with their trucks happily and peacefully. They were best friends again.

Sara and Tom were friends who liked to play soccer. They had a goal made of sticks and a ball made of rags. They took turns to kick the ball and try to score in the goal.

One day, a fat boy named Ben came to their field. He saw their goal and their ball and he wanted them. He said, "Give me your goal and your ball. They are mine now."

Sara and Tom were scared and angry. They said, "No, they are not yours. They are ours. We made them. Go away."

But Ben did not go away. He ran to their goal and kicked it down. He grabbed their ball and ran away. He laughed and said, "Ha ha, I have your goal and your ball. You have nothing."

Sara and Tom were very sad. They had no goal and no ball. They could not play soccer. They cried and hugged each other.

Then, they had an idea. They said, "We can make a new goal and a new ball. We can use stones and leaves and mud. We can change our game. We can still have fun."

They worked hard and made a new goal and a new ball. They were proud and happy. They played soccer again and had fun.

Ben saw them and came back. He said, "Give me your new goal and your new ball. They are mine now."

Sara and Tom were not scared and angry. They said, "No, they are not yours. They are ours. We made them. You can't have them."

Ben tried to take them, but Sara and Tom kicked the ball at him. The ball was hard and wet and dirty. It hit Ben in the face and made him fall. He cried and ran away.

Sara and Tom laughed and said, "Ha ha, we have our goal and our ball. You have nothing."

They hugged each other and played soccer. They were happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to touch everything she saw. One day, she saw a thin butterfly and wanted to touch it. But her mom said, "No, Lily. You might hurt it."

Lily was sad but then her mom showed her a fashion magazine with beautiful dresses. Lily loved the colors and patterns. She said, "Mommy, I want to wear a pretty dress like that."

Her mom replied, "Sure, we can go shopping for a dress tomorrow."

Lily was happy and went to bed dreaming of all the pretty dresses she would get to touch and wear.

Once upon a time, there was a kind and compassionate girl named Lily. She loved to collect shiny things, especially crystals. One day, she found a beautiful crystal that she loved very much.

One day, Lily met a boy named Jack who was sad because he lost his favorite toy. Lily wanted to help Jack find his toy, so she looked everywhere for it. Finally, she found the toy and gave it back to Jack. Jack was very happy and grateful.

Lily learned that being kind and helping others can make them happy. She realized that helping others is like matching puzzle pieces together, and it makes everyone feel good. From that day on, Lily made it her mission to help others whenever she could.

Once upon a time, there was a brave girl named Sandy. Sandy was always searching for adventures. One night, Sandy wanted to explore the dark woods.

So, she picked up her flashlight and went outside. She shone the flashlight in all directions and saw something shiny. Sandy got excited and ran over to the shiny thing and it was a special kind of toy. She looked closely and saw it was a flexible toy train.

"I'm going to grab it," Sandy said.

Just then, her mom called out to her from the window. "Sandy, come back home. It's too dark and it's dangerous!"

But Sandy was determined. She turned on the flashlight and grabbed the flexible toy train.

Sandy smiled and waved at her mom before running back to her house. She had a great new toy for her adventures.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy who liked to eat. One day, he went to the kitchen to get something to eat. His mom was working on a file, but it was a dirty file.

The little boy said, "Mommy, what are you doing?"

His mom replied, "I'm trying to clean this file. It's very dirty!"

The little boy asked, "Can I help you?"

His mom said, "Yes! You can help me! Can you get me a wet cloth?"

The little boy ran and got his mom a wet cloth. His mom used the cloth to wipe the file. She also washed it to make it clean.

When the file was clean, his mom said, "Thanks for your help! Now let's go get something to eat!"

The little boy was so happy that he had helped his mom. And he got to eat too! He ate his favorite food and was filled with joy.

Once upon a time there was a girl who loved candy. Every day she would go out and buy a new kind of candy to try.

One day she was walking down the street and she heard a lot of noise coming from a nearby house. She looked up at the house and saw it was full of people talking and laughing. The girl was curious and she wanted to see what was inside the house.

So she went up to the house and knocked on the door. All the people inside quickly got quiet and opened the door. They saw the girl and invited her inside. The girl was so excited!

Inside the house there was candy everywhere. Everyone talked and laughed while they shared the candy. The girl loved it! She was filled with joy and ate as much candy as she could.

The girl stayed in the house until it was time to go. But before the girl left she was given a big bag of candy to bring home. She said thank you, and was filled with happiness.

The girl went on her way with a big smile on her face. She had so much candy and was so glad to have made some new friends. She knew she would come back soon and she couldn't wait.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a new dress that was purple and very pretty. She loved to twirl around in it and feel the soft fabric on her skin.

One day, Lily went to the park and saw a butterfly with purple wings. She wanted to catch it, but she didn't want to scare it away. So, she whispered to the butterfly, "Don't be afraid, I just want to see your pretty wings."

The butterfly stayed still and let Lily admire its wings. Lily was very happy and felt like she had made a new friend. She twirled around in her purple dress and watched the butterfly fly away. From that day on, Lily loved the color purple even more because it reminded her of her new friend.

Once there was an unlucky bug who was very scared. He did not know where to go or what to do. Suddenly he heard the sound of a grill and he was scared. He saw that it was coming closer, so he quickly ran away.

The bug was afraid, but he kept running until he saw a field of glowing yellow flowers. He was so relieved when he saw them and he stopped running. He felt so lucky to have found the field of flowers.

The bug decided to stay near the flowers and be happy. He was sure he was safe near them and he never felt scared again. From then on, the bug was so lucky to have found the flowers - and he was never scared again.

Once upon a time, there was a cat called Pat. Pat lived in a big house with lots of stairs. One day, Pat was happily running up the stairs to his favourite room when suddenly he tripped and fell. He couldn't move! He had twisted his paw and was very sore.

Pat lay at the bottom of the stairs, feeling sad and helpless. He wanted to make sure that everyone could see that he was injured, so Pat made a loud meow to make sure everyone knew he needed help.

When Pat's family heard his meow, they came running. They saw Pat at the bottom of the stairs, with his paw displayed in a way that showed it was dead. Pat's family was sad, but they knew he would have to go to the vet.

So they called the vet, and the vet visited Pat at his home. The vet made Pat feel much better, and after a few visits, Pat was back up and running - even harder than before! Everyone was happy, and Pat's hurt paw was healed.

The end.

Lily was a little girl who liked to play dress-up. She had many clothes and hats and shoes in her big sack. She liked to pretend she was a princess or a fairy or a doctor. One day, she found a veil in her sack. It was white and shiny and had flowers on it. Lily put it on her head and felt very pretty.

She wanted to show her veil to her friends. She ran outside with her sack and her veil. She saw Anna and Ben playing with a ball. She called them and said, "Look at my veil! Isn't it lovely?" Anna and Ben looked at her and smiled. They said, "Yes, it is very lovely. Can we try it on?" Lily said, "No, it is mine. You can't have it." She hugged her sack and her veil and ran away.

She saw Tom and Mia playing with a doll. She called them and said, "Look at my veil! Isn't it wonderful?" Tom and Mia looked at her and nodded. They said, "Yes, it is very wonderful. Can we see it?" Lily said, "No, it is mine. You can't touch it." She hugged her sack and her veil and ran away.

She saw Sam and Zoe playing with a puzzle. She called them and said, "Look at my veil! Isn't it amazing?" Sam and Zoe looked at her and frowned. They said, "Yes, it is very amazing. But why are you so mean? You don't want to share with anyone. You are not a good friend." Lily said, "No, you are not good friends. You want to take my veil. It is mine. You can't have it." She hugged her sack and her veil and ran away.

She ran and ran until she reached a big tree. She sat under the tree and looked at her veil. She felt very lonely and sad. She wished she had someone to play with. She wished she had someone to tell her how pretty she was. She wished she had someone to hug her and make her happy. She realized she had been very selfish and rude. She had hurt her friends' feelings. She had been fearful of losing her veil, but she had lost something more important: her friends.

She decided to go back and say sorry to her friends. She hoped they would forgive her and play with her again. She put her veil back in her sack and ran back to where she had seen them. She saw them playing together and having fun. She felt very sorry and ashamed. She went to them and said, "I am sorry, friends. I was very mean and silly. I don't want to keep my veil to myself. I want to share it with you. You can try it on and see how lovely you are. You can play with it and have fun. You are more precious to me than my veil. Will you be my friends again?" Her friends looked at her and smiled. They said, "We are happy you are sorry, Lily. We forgive you and we love you. You are a good friend. We are glad you want to share your veil with us. It is very kind of you. You are very lovely, too. Come and play with us." They hugged her and took turns wearing the veil. They played and laughed and had a good time. Lily felt very happy and grateful. She learned that sharing is caring and that friends are more valuable than things.

Once upon a time, there was a kid named Timmy. Timmy loved to play outside, but one day it got very cold. Timmy's mom said, "Timmy, you need to wear a warm coat." Timmy said, "Okay, Mommy."

Timmy went outside to play, but he got lost in the woods. He was very scared and cold. He saw a man and said, "Please save me, I'm lost."

The man said, "Don't worry, I'll help you." The man took Timmy to his mom. Timmy's mom said, "Thank you for saving my kid." Timmy was very happy to be warm and safe with his mom.

Once upon a time, there was a cat and a dog. The cat liked to joke a lot. The dog liked to read the newspaper. One day, the cat found an interesting newspaper. The cat wanted to joke with the dog about the newspaper.

The cat said, "Look, dog! This newspaper says cats can fly!" The dog looked at the cat and said, "You are joking, cat. Cats cannot fly." The cat laughed and said, "You are right, dog. I was joking."

The dog smiled and said, "It is good to joke, but we must tell the truth too." The cat and the dog learned that it is fun to joke, but it is important to be honest. They both read the interesting newspaper and had a fun day together.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Tim. Tim loved to read books. He also liked to play with his football. One day, Tim went to the park with his mom.

In the park, Tim saw a pretty girl named Sue. Sue was very attractive. She had a big smile and wore a nice dress. Tim wanted to be friends with Sue. So, he asked if she wanted to play football with him.

Sue said yes, and they played football together. They had so much fun. After playing, they sat down and Tim read a book to Sue. They became good friends and played together every day.

Once upon a time there was a little boy who was three years old. He was very lively and he loved to play games. Every day he would go outside to play in the sand or run around with his best friends.

One day he decided to be naughty and he started throwing sand at his friends. His parents saw him and got very angry. They shouted at him and told him that this was not OK and it was not nice to do this to his friends.

So his parents punished him. They said that he would not be allowed to go outside and play for the rest of the day. The little boy was very sad but he knew he had to listen to his parents.

He stayed inside and was, not very lively any more. He read stories, watched TV and played some computer games. But he knew that he could not play outside for now.

The little boy soon realised he had done something wrong and he told his parents he was sorry and he would never do this again. His parents were very happy and they said he could go outside and play his games again.

The little boy was very happy and he ran outside to play with his friends. He had learnt his lesson and he vowed to always obey his parents and never do anything naughty again.

Once upon a time there were two friends, Lily and Max. Lily loved hide and seek and one day she found a hidden box. Inside the box, she found a pair of scissors. She was so excited, but then something strange happened - the scissors started to melt!

Max could not believe it. He tried to pick up the scissors, but they had melted into a puddle. Lily was disappointed, but then she had an idea. She wanted to hide the scissors so nobody else could find them.

The two friends worked together and hid the melted scissors in the ground. They laughed and ran away, happy that their secret was safe.

The end!

Once upon a time, three sheep lived on a farm. They had soft and fluffy wool. Every day, they would make a promise to each other to have fun.

One day, they heard something new. A spicy aroma! They followed their noses, and they saw something they'd never seen before. It was a big pot, full of spice.

The spice looked so yummy, and they couldn't wait to try it. The three sheep all shared their wool, and they made something special out of it. They rolled their wool into a ball and added a bit of the spicy to it.

The first sheep tasted it, and it was delicious! The other two sheep followed, and they both also loved the taste. From then on, the three sheep made their yummy spicey wool every day and shared it with each other. They even made a promise to share their new treat with their friends on the farm.

Once upon a time there was a little boy who loved to wander. He would take his toy car and explore the world around him. Everywhere he went he heard new and exciting language. The boy couldn't understand any of it but he thought it sounded so pretty.

One day, the boy came across a soft kitten. He picked it up and it nuzzled in his arms. He was so excited and talked to it in his own special language. He wandered around with the kitten, showing it all of the new places he had discovered.

The kitten followed him around, making sure to stay close. Everywhere they went it was like the boy was speaking a magical language - one that only the two of them understood. It was so soft, kind and wonderful.

The boy and his little friend were always together and they wandered through the world side by side. Everywhere they went, they shared their special language, leaving a little sparkle behind them.

Once there was a little boy named Ben. He loved music and wanted to make his own. One day, his Mommy asked him if he wanted to play her drum. Ben was so excited! He said yes and asked if he could have a party to show off his new drum.

Mommy said yes! She invited all of Ben's friends. When they arrived, they were all amazed by Ben's drumming. He made wonderful music and everyone clapped and cheered.

But then something terrible happened. Ben's drum broke in the middle of his show! Everyone gasped and Ben started to cry.

Mommy knew just what to do. She took Ben's hand and said, "Don't worry little one. We'll get you a new drum, I promise." Ben smiled and everyone hugged him. He was so happy that he was able to play the drum and invite his friends over for a party.

Once upon a time, in a small town, there lived a shy girl named Lily. She had a favorite glove that she would always wear. One day, she lost her glove while playing outside.

Lily looked everywhere for her glove, but she couldn't find it. She saw her friend, Tim, and asked him, "Tim, have you seen my glove?" Tim said, "No, but I will help you look for it." They looked and looked, but they still couldn't find it.

Then, they saw a big dog with something in its mouth. Lily said, "Look, the dog has my glove!" They went to the dog and asked, "Dog, can we have the glove back?" The dog refused to give it back. But when they gave the dog a treat, it finally let go of the glove. Lily was so happy to have her glove back, and she thanked Tim for helping her.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, Lily was playing with her toys when she saw a ghost. She was scared and started to cry.

Her mom asked her what was wrong and Lily told her about the ghost. Her mom hugged her and said, "Don't worry, I'll provide you with a nightlight to make you feel safe."

Lily felt better and went to bed with her nightlight. The next day, Lily saw her friend Sarah who was sad because her dress didn't fit her anymore.

Lily said, "Don't be sad, I have a dress that will fit you perfectly!" Sarah was happy and thanked Lily.

The moral of the story is that it's important to help others and provide them with what they need. And sometimes, we can make others happy by giving them something that fits just right.

Once upon a time there was a bite-sized puppy. It was fast, brown and strong. One day it decided to go for a walk. It wandered for a while until it came to a house. It was a big house with a tall fence. The puppy wagged its tail. It wanted to explore.

The puppy started to climb the fence. It was strong and determined to get inside. When the puppy made it to the top, it jumped into the garden. The puppy could feel the soft grass beneath its paws. It started to sniff around.

Suddenly the owner of the house appeared. He clapped his hands and shouted "Good puppy!". The puppy was scared but the owner was kind. He give the puppy a rub on the head and gave it a treat.

The puppy soon learned that this was his new home. The owner smiled and petted the puppy gently. The puppy was so thankful and happy. It knew that it had a strong and kind owner who would take care of it.

Anna and Ben are friends who like to play in the park. One day, they see a new person in the park. He is wearing a blue shirt, a black hat, and a shiny badge. He is a cop.

"Who is he?" Anna asks Ben.

"I don't know. Let's go say hello," Ben says.

They run to the cop and smile.

"Hello, we are Anna and Ben. We like to play here. Who are you?" Ben says.

"Hello, Anna and Ben. I'm Officer Mike. I'm a cop. I help people and keep them safe. Do you want to see my badge?" Officer Mike says.

"Yes, please!" Anna and Ben say.

Officer Mike shows them his badge and tells them what it means. He also lets them touch his hat and his radio. He is very nice and friendly.

"Wow, you have a cool job, Officer Mike. Thank you for helping people and keeping them safe," Anna says.

"You're welcome, Anna. And thank you for being polite and kind. You are good kids," Officer Mike says.

Anna and Ben learn that the cop is not scary, but helpful and fun. They also learn to introduce themselves to new people and be respectful. They make a new friend in the park. They are happy.

Once upon a time, there was a dull radio. It had no sound and it just sat there, alone. One day a little girl came along and saw the radio. She wanted to make it sound better so she picked it up.

The girl found a big box of buttons and she started to sort them. She put all the round ones together, the square ones together and all the other shapes together.

When she was done sorting the buttons, the girl went back to the radio. She started pressing the buttons and soon music and laughter filled the air! Everyone was so happy and the girl was proud of her work.

The girl had found a way to make the dull radio sound amazing! From then on, the radio always had music and laughter which made everyone smile.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the sunshine with her toys. But one day, she was feeling very bored. Her toys were dull and she didn't know what to do.

Suddenly, she saw her shadow on the ground. It was big and dark, just like a monster! Lily got scared and ran away. But then she remembered her mommy telling her that shadows can't hurt her.

Feeling brave, Lily went back to her shadow and started to play with it. She made funny shapes with her hands and her shadow copied her. It was so much fun! But then, Lily's mommy came outside and saw her playing with her shadow instead of doing her chores. She had to punish Lily by sending her inside to clean her room. But Lily didn't mind, because she knew she could always play with her shadow again tomorrow.

Once there was a lion who lived in a big forest. He liked to roar every day so all his friends could hear him. Every afternoon he liked to go to the river to have a drink of water.

One day, the lion saw something in the sky. It looked like a big white bird! He watched it fly over and then land. When he went closer he saw it was the news.

The news had a letter for the lion. It said there was going to be a fair soon! The lion was so excited! He started to roar with joy!

The lion got ready for the fair. He put on his best mane and practised roaring out loud so he could show everyone.

The fair was so much fun! The lion met lots of new friends who also liked to roar. They roared so loud they could be heard all around the forest!

At the end of the day, the lion waved goodbye to all his new friends. He was so happy and he couldn't wait to come back to the fair next year.

Tim and Tom are brothers. They like to play with cars. They have many cars of different colors and sizes. Sometimes they share their cars, but sometimes they fight over them.

One day, they both want to play with the same car. It is a big red car that makes loud noises. It is a powerful car. Tim says, "It is my car. I saw it first." Tom says, "No, it is my car. I like it more." They pull the car from each other. They are angry.

Mom hears them and comes to see what is wrong. She says, "Boys, stop fighting. You have to learn to yield. Yield means to let someone else have something. It is nice to yield. If you yield, you can take turns and play together. If you don't yield, you will be unhappy and lonely."

Tim and Tom think about what Mom says. They don't want to be unhappy and lonely. They want to play together. They decide to yield. Tim says, "OK, Tom, you can have the car first. But then I can have it later." Tom says, "OK, Tim, thank you for yielding. You can have the car after me." They hug and smile.

Mom is happy to see them yield. She says, "Good boys. I am proud of you. Now you can play on the same side. Side means to be together and help each other. It is fun to be on the same side. If you are on the same side, you will have more friends and more joy."

Tim and Tom nod and agree. They say, "We want to be on the same side. We love each other. We love you, Mom." They take their cars and go to play on the same side. They make loud noises and have fun. They are happy.

Tom likes to read books. He has many books in his room. He reads about cars, animals, and space. He reads every day before he sleeps.

One day, Tom finds a new book in his room. It is a big book with a picture of a fish on the cover. Tom likes fish. He opens the book and sees many words and pictures. He wants to read the book.

He asks his mom, "Mom, can you read this book to me?"

Mom smiles and says, "Sure, Tom. This is a book about fishing. Do you know what fishing is?"

Tom shakes his head. He does not know what fishing is.

Mom says, "Fishing is when you catch fish from the water. You need a rod, a line, and a hook. You put a worm on the hook and throw the line in the water. Then you wait for a fish to bite the hook. When you feel a tug, you pull the rod and catch the fish."

Tom listens and looks at the pictures. He sees a man with a rod and a fish. He thinks fishing looks fun.

He says, "Mom, can we go fishing?"

Mom says, "Maybe someday, Tom. But fishing is not easy. You need to be patient and quiet. And sometimes it is cold and wet. You need to wear warm clothes and boots."

Tom nods. He understands. He says, "Thank you, Mom, for reading to me. I like this book. I want to learn more about fishing."

Mom hugs him and says, "You're welcome, Tom. I'm glad you like this book. Maybe we can go to the library and find more books about fishing. Would you like that?"

Tom smiles and says, "Yes, Mom. I would like that very much."

Ben and Lily went to the park with Mom. They saw a huge pond with many ducks. Ben and Lily liked ducks. They wanted to feed them.

"Mom, can we give them some bread?" Lily asked.

"Sorry, sweetie, we don't have any bread. But we have some olives. Do you think they will like olives?" Mom said.

"Let's try!" Ben said. He took an olive from Mom's bag and threw it into the pond. A duck saw the olive and swam to get it. It picked up the olive with its beak and ate it.

"Yay! The duck likes olives!" Ben cheered.

"Me too! Me too!" Lily said. She took another olive and threw it into the pond. Another duck swam to get it. It also ate the olive.

"Wow! The ducks love olives!" Lily said.

"Can we swim with the ducks, Mom?" Ben asked.

"No, honey, the pond is too deep and cold for you. And the ducks might not like it. They need their space. But you can watch them swim and quack. They are very happy." Mom said.

"Okay, Mom. We will watch them. They are very cute." Ben said.

"Yes, they are. And you are very kind to share your olives with them." Mom said.

Ben and Lily smiled. They sat on the grass and watched the ducks swim and eat olives. They had a lot of fun at the park.

Once upon a time there was a girl called Ruby. One day, Ruby met a very nice dog. She was very excited and gave him a pat on the head. As she did this, a tray of food fell from the table. The dog was so hungry that he ate all the food in the tray. Ruby felt sad that the dog was so hungry, so she decided to try to help him.

As she was thinking, she realized that she didn't know how to care for the dog. She felt quite ignorant but she was determined to take care of the dog. She went inside and searched the drawers until she found a food tray. She filled it up with delicious food and a bowl full of water. She gave it to the dog, and he was so happy he ate it all.

Ruby felt very happy that the dog was now happy and well-fed. From then on, Ruby and the dog were great friends. Every day the dog would meet Ruby at the door, excited for the tray of food. She never forgot how ignorant she felt when she first met the dog, but she learned that it is always worth trying to help others in need.

One day, a little girl named Lucy went to the park with her mom. Lucy saw an enormous slide. She was scared to go down. Her mom said, "Lucy, I encourage you to try. You can do it!"

Lucy was still scared, but she wanted to be brave. She climbed up the slide step by step. When she got to the top, she took a deep breath and slid down. Whee! She laughed and felt happy.

At the bottom of the slide, Lucy's mom gave her a big hug. She said, "Good job, Lucy! I am proud of you!" Then, Lucy's mom gave her a yummy lollipop as a treat. Lucy smiled and licked her lollipop. She knew she could do anything with a little encouragement.

Once upon a time there was a chubby silver rabbit. He loved hopping around in his garden and eating carrots. One day, however, he noticed something strange. His tail was missing!

He searched high and low, but still couldn’t find it. Then one day, a friendly fairy appeared and said she could replace the rabbit’s tail. She waved her magic wand and suddenly a nice big, fluffy, white tail appeared on the rabbit’s bottom.

The rabbit was very pleased with his new tail and thanked the fairy. He hopped around happily and even flicked his new tail as he did so. He had a wonderful time showing it off to his friends and spent the rest of the day picking flowers and singing in his garden.

Sam and Lily were twins who liked to play outside. One day, they found a big cooler in the garage. They opened it and saw many yummy things inside. There were juice boxes, cheese sticks, crackers, and cookies.

"Wow, look at all the snacks!" Sam said. "Let's take them to the park and share with our friends."

"OK, but we have to ask Mom first," Lily said. She was a good girl who always followed the rules.

Sam and Lily ran to the house and asked Mom if they could take the cooler to the park. Mom said yes, but they had to be careful and come back soon. She also told them to split the snacks evenly with their friends.

Sam and Lily nodded and thanked Mom. They took the cooler and went to the park. They saw their friends playing on the swings, the slide, and the sandbox. They called them over and showed them the cooler.

"Wow, look at all the snacks!" their friends said. "Can we have some?"

"Sure, you can have some," Sam said. "But you have to give me something in return."

"Like what?" their friends asked.

"Like your toys, your stickers, your hats, anything you have," Sam said. He was a greedy boy who wanted more things.

Lily did not like what Sam was doing. She thought it was not fair to their friends. She said to Sam, "No, Sam, that's not nice. We have to split the snacks evenly with our friends. That's what Mom said. We don't need their things. We have enough."

Sam did not listen to Lily. He said to her, "No, Lily, you are silly. We can get more things from our friends. They want the snacks. They will give us anything we want. You can split your snacks, but I will keep mine."

Sam and Lily started to argue. They pulled the cooler from each other. Their friends watched them and felt sad. They did not want to trade their things for the snacks. They just wanted to play and share with Sam and Lily.

The cooler was too heavy for Sam and Lily to hold. It slipped from their hands and fell to the ground. It opened and all the snacks spilled out. Some of the juice boxes burst and made a mess. Some of the cheese sticks and crackers broke and got dirty. Some of the cookies were eaten by a dog that ran by.

Sam and Lily looked at the cooler and the snacks. They felt sorry for what they had done. They had wasted the snacks and hurt their friends. They wished they had listened to Mom and split the snacks evenly.

They looked at each other and said, "We're sorry."

They looked at their friends and said, "We're sorry."

Their friends came closer and said, "It's OK. We're still friends."

They hugged and made up. They decided to play together and have fun. They did not need the snacks or the things. They had each other. They were happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim was very hungry. He went to his mom and said, "Mom, I am hungry. Can I have some food?"

His mom smiled and said, "Yes, Tim. Let's go to the kitchen and find something to eat." They went to the kitchen and Tim's mom asked him to kneel down by the cupboard. Tim kneeled down and opened the cupboard.

Inside the cupboard, there were many snacks. Tim saw cookies, chips, and fruits. He looked at his mom and asked, "What is the truth, Mom? Can I eat all of these snacks?"

His mom laughed and said, "No, Tim. You can only pick one snack. Eating too many will make your tummy hurt." Tim thought for a moment and picked an apple. He was happy with his choice and ate the apple with a big smile on his face.

Ben and Sam were friends. They liked to play with cars and balls. One day, they saw a big truck on the street. It had many boxes and bags inside.

"Wow, look at that truck!" Ben said. "I wonder what is in there."

"Let's go and see!" Sam said. "Maybe we can find something fun."

They ran to the truck and climbed inside. They opened some boxes and bags. They found toys and candy and clothes.

"Look, I found a robot!" Ben said. "And I found a bike!" Sam said. "This is awesome!"

They did not see the man who owned the truck. He was angry. He came back and saw Ben and Sam in his truck. He shouted at them.

"Hey, you little thieves! Get out of my truck! You are in big trouble!"

He grabbed Ben and Sam and took them to his car. He drove them to the jail. The jail was a big building with bars and locks. It was gloomy and scary.

Ben and Sam were very sad and scared. They cried and said sorry.

"Please, let us go!" Ben said. "We did not mean to steal anything!"

"Too bad!" the man said. "You have to stay here until the police come. You will learn your lesson!"

He locked them in a small room with a bed and a toilet. He left them alone.

Ben and Sam hugged each other. They wished they had never gone to the truck. They hoped someone would come and help them. They missed their moms and dads. They learned a hard lesson. They never wanted to steal anything again.

Once upon a time there was a very intelligent mouse. He lived in a tall chimney, with many nooks and crannies to explore. Every day, the mouse would wander around his chimney, curious about the world and thinking about what lay beyond.

One day, the mouse saw an even taller chimney in the distance. He wanted to explore the new and mysterious chimney, but he was scared of the unknown. The mouse wanted to turn away, but he was determined to be brave. Taking a deep breath, he decided to surrender to his curiosity.

The mouse entered the new chimney, and he was amazed. Everything was so new and exciting! He explored the twists and turns of the chimney, learning and discovering so much. The mouse eventually made his way back to his home chimney, full of stories to tell his friends.

From then on, the mouse trusted his curiosity and never surrendered to fear. He was as brave and intelligent as ever, and was always excited for his new discoveries!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to draw pictures, but she didn't know where to keep them safe. Her mommy gave her a folder that was flexible and could hold all her drawings.

One day, Lily's friend came over and saw her folder. She wanted one too, but her mommy said they didn't have enough money to buy one. Lily explained that her mommy got it on sale and maybe her friend's mommy could find one too.

Lily learned that being helpful and sharing is important. She shared her folder with her friend so she could keep her drawings safe too. And her friend was happy because she learned that sometimes you don't need to buy new things, you can find them on sale or share with your friends.

Once upon a time there was a rich garden. It was full of colourful flowers and the juiciest fruits. The people who owned the garden were very happy.

One day, it rained and rain kept coming. The garden was getting wet. The owners worried that the plants would perhaps drown or get too much water.

So they decided to take action. They put up a large umbrella to prevent the rain from coming into the garden.

And it worked! The rain stopped and the garden was saved. Everyone was very happy.

And from then on, the garden stayed dry and the people stayed rich. The end.

Lily was a humble girl who liked to help her mom and dad. She did not ask for many things or make a fuss. She was happy with her toys, her books and her friends.

One day, Lily was very tired after playing in the park. She wanted to nap, but she could not find her pillow. She looked in her room, in the living room, in the kitchen, but she could not see it anywhere. She felt sad and sleepy.

She asked her mom, "Mom, where is my pillow? I need it to nap."

Her mom smiled and said, "Lily, your pillow is in the laundry. It was dirty and I washed it. It is still wet and needs to dry. Why don't you use this soft blanket instead?"

Lily nodded and took the blanket. She wrapped it around her and lay down on the couch. She closed her eyes and thought of her pillow. She hoped it would be dry soon. She missed it, but she did not complain. She was a humble girl who liked to nap.

Once upon a time, there was a big blueberry. It was in a pond and wanted to swim. But it couldn't swim without help.

Lucky for the blueberry, there was a very helpful fish living in the pond. He saw the blueberry and wanted to help it. The fish used its fins to push the blueberry through the water.

The fish and the blueberry swam around the pond together. They had lots of fun. After a while, the blueberry grew a bit too tired to keep swimming. The fish said goodbye and swam away.

The blueberry found a sunny rock to rest on. It felt warm and peaceful and the blueberry was happy. The end.

Once upon a time there was a lively shop. People would come to the shop and buy things they needed or wanted. The shopkeeper was always very friendly.

One day, a little 3 year old boy named Jack came to the shop. He wanted to buy an ice cream cone but he didn't have any money. He started to complain to the shopkeeper.

The shopkeeper was very kind. He said, "I'm sorry Jack, I can't sell you the cone if you don't have money." Jack was very unhappy. He started to cry and complain again.

But the shopkeeper had an idea. He asked Jack if he was a good helper. Jack nodded yes. So, the shopkeeper told Jack he could help him with some jobs around the shop. If he worked hard and helped with all the jobs, he could have an ice cream cone for free!

Jack was so excited! He worked hard all morning, helping the shopkeeper. When the jobs were done, the shopkeeper said, "Thank you for all your help Jack! You can have your ice cream cone now."

Jack was so happy! He waved goodbye to the shopkeeper, licking his delicious ice cream cone, and he ran happily back home.
