Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She lived on a ranch with her parents and many animals. One day, Lily's dad asked her to come with him to feed the cows. Lily was so excited and said, "I want to follow you, Daddy!"

As they walked to the cow pen, Lily noticed a little calf that was lost. She said, "Daddy, look! The calf is lost. We have to help him." Her dad smiled and said, "You're so kind, Lily. Let's bring him back to the ranch."

When they got back to the ranch, Lily's mom was proud of her for helping the lost calf. She said, "Lily, you did a great job. Always remember to help others when they need it." From that day on, Lily always made sure to follow her parents and help any animals that were lost.

Once there was a soft bear named Brownie. Brownie wanted to win something so he could be special. He went outside to try and find something to win.

He saw a race and decided to join. He was nervous but he wanted to try his best. He ran and ran and ran as fast as he could. In the end, he won!

Brownie was so happy he won. He got a pot of cream as his prize. He licked it and it tasted so sweet and creamy. He loved it! He was so glad he won something.

Brownie was so proud to have won the race. He carried the cream around all the time so he could show everyone he had won something. He wanted to win something again someday.

The End

Once upon a time, a little girl named Lily went for a walk in the park with her mommy. They saw a long path and decided to follow it. Suddenly, Lily saw a shiny stone on the ground. She picked it up and showed it to her mommy, saying "Look, mommy! A pretty stone!"

Her mommy replied, "Wow, Lily! That's a beautiful stone. It's so shiny and smooth."

As they continued walking, they came across a surprise. They saw a big fountain in the middle of the park with water shooting up into the sky. Lily exclaimed, "Mommy, look! A surprise! A big fountain!"

Her mommy smiled and said, "Yes, Lily. It's a beautiful surprise. Let's sit here and watch the water for a while." They sat down on a nearby bench and enjoyed the surprise together.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy was very excited because his mommy told him they were going to spend the day at the park. Timmy loved the park because he could play on the swings and slide.

As they were walking to the park, Timmy saw some police officers. He asked his mommy, "Mommy, why are the police here?" His mommy explained that the police were there to keep everyone safe.

Later, while Timmy was playing, he saw a little girl crying. He went up to her and asked, "Why are you crying?" The little girl said she lost her teddy bear. Timmy was very brave and decided to help her find it. They looked all over the park and finally found it under a tree.

The little girl was very happy and thanked Timmy for helping her. Timmy felt proud of himself for being brave and helping someone. He told his mommy, "I spent the day being brave and helping someone find their teddy bear." His mommy smiled and gave him a big hug.

Once upon a time, there was a little spider named Spidey. He lived in a big tree in the forest. One day, Spidey was playing hide and seek with his friends. He was very good at hiding because he was smart.

But when he came out of his hiding spot, he saw a big cobweb in front of him. He tried to get rid of it, but he couldn't. He was sad because he thought he would get in trouble with his mom.

Just then, his mom came and saw the cobweb. She said, "Don't worry, Spidey. I will help you get rid of it." Spidey was happy that his mom came to help him. They worked together and finally got rid of the cobweb. Spidey learned that it's always good to ask for help when you need it.

One day, a little girl named Mia went to the park with her mom. She saw a big slide and wanted to try it. But she was scared of going too fast and falling down.

"Mom, can you support me?" she asked, holding her mom's hand.

"Of course, sweetie. I will be right behind you. You can do it!" her mom said, smiling.

Mia climbed up the stairs and reached the top of the slide. She looked down and saw other kids sliding and laughing. She felt a little brave and let go of her mom's hand.

"Whee!" she shouted, as she slid down the slide. She felt the wind in her hair and the sun on her face. She landed on the soft grass and rolled over.

"That was fun!" she said, jumping up.

"I'm proud of you, Mia. You were very brave," her mom said, hugging her.

"Thanks, mom. You have a lot of wisdom. You always help me when I'm scared," Mia said, looking at her mom with love.

They walked to the swings and saw a wild bird on a branch. It had bright feathers and a long tail. It sang a beautiful song.

"Look, mom. A wild bird. It's so pretty," Mia said, pointing at the bird.

"Yes, it is. Do you know what kind of bird it is?" her mom asked.

"No, I don't. Do you?" Mia asked.

"I think it's a parrot. They can talk and copy sounds. Do you want to try to talk to it?" her mom asked.

"Okay. Hello, parrot. How are you?" Mia said, waving at the bird.

The bird looked at Mia and tilted its head. Then it opened its beak and said, "Hello, parrot. How are you?"

Mia and her mom laughed. The bird repeated what they said and added some funny noises.

"Wow, mom. The parrot can talk. It's so smart," Mia said, clapping her hands.

"Yes, it is. But you know what? You are smarter and braver and more beautiful than any parrot in the world," her mom said, kissing her cheek.

"I love you, mom. You are the best mom in the world," Mia said, hugging her mom.

They swung on the swings and listened to the parrot's song. They had a wonderful day at the park.

Once upon a time, there was a clean picnic in the park. Two kids, one called Ben and the other called Lucy, were excited to eat their lunch.

Ben said, "Let's close the picnic basket so no bugs come in". He shut the lid and the two kids sat on a blanket. They started to munch on their food, but soon heard a loud buzzing noise.

Lucy said, "That's strange! What is that noise?" She looked around and saw a bee flying above them. Ben said, "We should have kept the picnic basket closed!" They started to run away, but Ben quickly realized he left the blanket on the ground.

Ben felt that they must go back, but Lucy refused. She thought the bee would still be around. Ben said, "We have to go back, otherwise the blanket will get dirty!" Finally, they ran back and quickly grabbed the blanket.

The two kids laughed as they ran away with the blanket. They learned an important lesson that day - to always keep their picnic basket closed!

Once upon a time, there was a lady named Kate. She had a very special buckle. Every day, she wore the buckle on her coat. She loved the buckle because it was a very good one.

One day, Kate had a very special idea. She decided to display her buckle for all her friends to see. She put the buckle on the wall and everyone admired it. They all said it was a very good buckle.

Kate was so proud that she showed off her buckle every day. Now whenever Kate goes out, she gets lots of compliments about her buckle. Everyone loves how good it looks.

The end.

Once upon a time there was a special video. Every boy and girl wanted to watch it, but it was too noisy! It made all the children cover their ears.

One day a special man came to help the children. He said he would find a way to restore the video so the children could watch it without covering their ears.

The man worked very hard and after many hours, he finally made the video quiet. The children were so excited and watched the video with big smiles on their faces.

The man was so proud of himself for helping the children. He had restored the video, and now it was not too noisy! Everyone was so happy.

The end.

Once there was a baby elephant. His name was Tim. Tim loved adventures! One day, he wanted to escape from the zoo. So, he started squeezing through the bars of his cage.

Suddenly, the zookeeper noticed. He shouted loudly, "Stop, Tim!" But Tim continued running until he came to the zoo’s door. He squeezed through the door too. But he was still inside the zoo!

He needed a plan. He looked around and noticed a bottle of shampoo. He grabbed it and started squirting the shampoo onto the ground. Soon, he had drawn a fine, slippery path. He walked onto it and he slipped out of the zoo!

In the end, Tim escaped the zoo! He was so excited! He ran away and never looked back. And he found a place full of adventures.

Sara liked to collect makeup. She had many colors of lipstick, eye shadow, and nail polish. She kept them in a big box under her bed. Sometimes, she played with them and made herself look pretty.

One day, her brother Tom found her box of makeup. He thought it was stupid. He did not like makeup. He liked cars and trucks and dinosaurs. He took some of Sara's makeup and drew on the walls and the floor. He made a big mess.

Sara saw what Tom did and was very angry. She yelled at him and told him to stop. She said he was a bad brother and he ruined her makeup. She ran to her mom and told her what happened.

Mom came and saw the mess. She was not happy. She scolded Tom and made him clean up. She said he had to say sorry to Sara and give her some of his toys. She said he had to learn to respect Sara's things and not touch them without asking.

Tom felt sorry. He did not mean to make Sara and mom angry. He said sorry to Sara and gave her some of his cars and trucks and dinosaurs. He said he would not touch her makeup again. Sara forgave him and hugged him. She said she would share some of her makeup with him if he wanted to play with her. They both smiled and went to play together.

Once upon a time, there was a mom and a daughter. They were going on a trip. The mom told the daughter to pack her bag. The daughter was happy and packed her toys and clothes.

They went to a high hill to have a picnic. The daughter played with her toys and the mom watched her. The sky was blue and the sun was warm. They ate their food and had a lot of fun.

But then, the sky got dark and it started to rain. The mom and the daughter tried to pack their things fast. The wind blew their things away. They ran to their car, but the car was stuck in the mud. They were sad and wet. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a pretty kitten named Mittens. Mittens was very soft and cute. One day, Lily was holding Mittens too tight and Mittens wanted to go play. So Mittens meowed and Lily knew she had to release her.

Lily let go of Mittens and Mittens ran away to play. Lily felt sad for a moment, but then she saw how happy Mittens was playing. Mittens was chasing a butterfly and it was very pretty. Lily smiled and felt happy too.

After a while, Mittens got tired and came back to Lily. Lily picked up Mittens and gave her a hug. Mittens purred and Lily knew that she loved her pretty kitten. From that day on, Lily made sure to not hold Mittens too tight and to always release her when she wanted to play.

One day, a girl named Lucy and a boy named Tom were playing. They were very good friends. Lucy said, "Let's play marry!" Tom said, "Yes, let's do it!" So they pretended to marry each other.

While they were playing, they saw a big hole. It was very deep. Lucy said, "Be careful, Tom!" But Tom fell in the hole. Lucy was scared. She knew this was an emergency. She ran to get help.

Lucy found her mom and told her about the emergency. Her mom ran to the hole and helped Tom get out. Tom was okay. They were all happy. Lucy and Tom said thank you to Lucy's mom and continued to play.

Tim and Kim were twins who loved dinosaurs. They had many dinosaur toys and books in their room. They liked to pretend they were dinosaur explorers and find new kinds of dinosaurs.

One day, their mom told them she had a surprise for them. She said she ordered something special online and it would be delivered soon. Tim and Kim were very excited and wondered what it could be.

They waited by the window and watched for the delivery truck. After a while, they saw a big brown truck stop in front of their house. A man came out of the truck and carried a big box to their door. He rang the bell and mom opened the door.

"Hello, I have a delivery for Tim and Kim," the man said.

"Thank you, that's very kind of you," mom said. She took the box and gave the man some money. She closed the door and brought the box to the living room.

"Tim and Kim, come here and see what you got!" mom called.

Tim and Kim ran to the living room and saw the big box. They were very curious and eager to open it. Mom helped them cut the tape and lift the lid. Inside the box, they saw something amazing.

It was a giant dinosaur! It was green and scaly and had a long neck and tail. It had a button on its chest that made it roar and move. It was the coolest dinosaur toy they had ever seen.

"Wow, mom, thank you so much!" Tim and Kim exclaimed.

"You're welcome, my loves. I know how much you love dinosaurs, so I thought you would like this one. It's a brontosaurus, one of the biggest and gentlest dinosaurs ever," mom explained.

Tim and Kim hugged mom and thanked her again. They took the dinosaur out of the box and played with it. They named it Bob and made it their new friend. They had so much fun with Bob, they forgot about their other toys.

But Bob was not very happy. He felt weak and lonely in the new house. He missed his home and his family. He wished he could go back to the truck and find them. He did not like the loud noises and the bright lights. He did not like the small space and the hard floor. He did not like the twins who pulled his tail and pushed his button.

He wanted to escape. He waited for a chance to sneak out of the door. He hoped the man would come back and take him away. He dreamed of a place where he could be free and happy. He dreamed of a place where he could find other dinosaurs like him. He dreamed of a place where he could be a real dinosaur.

Once upon a time, there was a very powerful lion. He had a special suit that allowed him to roar very loudly. He was so loud that the whole jungle could hear him. Everyone was scared of him, because he was so powerful.

The lion decided to take a walk in the forest one day. As he was walking, he roared and roared. All of the animals in the jungle began to flee. Even the brave tigers ran away scared. The lion had never felt so powerful before.

He kept walking and roaring until he had enough. He stopped, took off his suit and went home. Everyone in the jungle felt safe again.

The lion never forgot how powerful he felt that day. He kept his special suit and always remembered how much fun it was to roar.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved coloring with her long crayons. One day, Lily's friend, Max, came over to play. They started coloring together, but Max accidentally broke one of Lily's long crayons.

"Oh no, my crayon!" Lily cried.

"Don't worry, I have an idea," Max said.

Max went to his bag and took out a surprise. It was a new box of long crayons for Lily.

"Wow, thank you Max!" Lily said happily.

From that day on, Lily and Max colored together with their long crayons and had lots of fun. They both learned that accidents can happen, but good friends are always there to help.

Once upon a time, there was an elderly man who loved to drive his car. He had a license that said he could drive. One day, he decided to go for a drive in his car.

As he drove, he saw a big sign that said "Turn left". He turned his car to the left and drove down a bumpy road. Suddenly, his car started to make a strange noise. The man was worried and didn't know what to do.

Just then, he saw a helpful boy walking by. The boy asked the man if he needed help. The man explained the problem with his car. The boy knew just what to do and fixed the car. The man was so happy and grateful to the boy for helping him. From then on, he always made sure to turn left at the sign and remember the boy who helped him.

Anna and Ben are playing with their toys in the living room. They have a lot of fun making noises with their cars, dolls and blocks. They zoom, beep, bang and chatter as they pretend to be drivers, doctors and builders.

But their mom is working in the kitchen. She has a big headache and needs some quiet. She comes to the living room and says, "Anna, Ben, please stop making so much noise. You are hurting my head. Can you play something else?"

Anna and Ben look at their mom. They see that she is not happy. They love their mom and do not want to make her sad. They say, "Sorry, mom. We did not know you had a headache. We will play something else."

They put away their noisy toys and pick up some books. They sit on the couch and read quietly. They look at the pictures and say the words softly. They learn about animals, colors and shapes.

Their mom comes back to the living room. She sees that Anna and Ben are reading. She smiles and says, "Thank you, Anna, Ben. You are very good and kind. I feel better now. Do you want to read with me?"

Anna and Ben nod and hug their mom. They say, "Yes, mom. We love you. We love reading with you." They snuggle on the couch and read together. They are happy and quiet.

Once there was a little girl named Lily. She was very lucky, and she knew it. She saw all the things she could do and all the places she could go with her luck.

One summer day, Lily walked into the kitchen and saw something that made her smile. Sitting in the corner was a big freezer - filled with ice cream! Too excited to contain her joy, she jumped up and down, clapping her hands.

"Oh, look at all the ice cream I can have!" she said. "Who's that lucky?"

Then Lily saw her mom standing in the room. "Where did you get this freezer, Mommy?" she asked.

Her mom smiled. "I found it at the store. It's a new model and it was on sale, so I decided to buy it!"

Lily admired her mom for her clever idea. "Wow, you are so lucky, Mommy! I'm glad you got it."

Lily's mom leaned down, placing her hand on Lily's shoulder. "Yes," she said, "I'm very lucky. But you are lucky too, Lily. You have me as your mom and that is even luckier than this freezer."

Lily laughed, knowing that her mom was right. She hugged her mom tightly and they both admired the new freezer in their kitchen.

Once upon a time, there was a creative little girl named Lucy. She had a box full of shapes. She liked to play with the shapes and make them into fun things. One day, Lucy found a big door with a lock on it. She thought, "I want to open the lock."

Lucy went to her box of shapes and found a key shape. She thought, "Maybe this shape will open the lock." She took the shape to the big door and put it in the lock. It fit just right! Lucy turned the key shape and the lock clicked open.

When the door opened, Lucy saw a room full of more shapes! She was so happy. She played with the new shapes and made even more fun things. The key shape helped her unlock a world of fun.

Sara and Ben like to play in the snow. They make a big snowman with a hat and a scarf. They give him a carrot nose and two black stones for eyes. They are very happy with their snowman.

But then, a mean boy comes. He has a stick with fire on it. He wants to burn the snowman. He laughs and runs to the snowman. Sara and Ben are scared. They shout, "No, no, stop!"

The mean boy does not stop. He puts the fire stick on the snowman's hat. The hat starts to burn. The snowman's head starts to melt. Sara and Ben cry. They love their snowman.

Then, a big dog comes. He is white and fluffy. He sees the mean boy and the fire stick. He does not like the mean boy. He barks and runs to him. He bites the fire stick and pulls it away. The mean boy drops the fire stick and runs away. He is afraid of the dog.

The dog is a good dog. He wags his tail and licks Sara and Ben's faces. He is sorry for the snowman. He helps them to fix the snowman. He gives him a new hat and a new scarf. He also gives him a hug. Sara and Ben hug the dog too. They are very happy with the dog. They name him Snowy. They are friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little bear. He was shy and liked to play on his own. One day, he was in the forest looking for acorns to snack on. When he came across a big acorn, he got excited!

He tried to twist it open, but couldn't. Frustrated, he started to cry. Suddenly, he heard a friendly voice.

"Oh, what's wrong?" asked the voice.

The little bear looked up and saw a friendly squirrel.

"I can't twist the acorn open," sobbed the bear.

"Don't worry", said the squirrel. I can help you. Ready? On the count of three, we'll both twist the acorn open!

The bear and the squirrel worked together and on the count of three, they both twisted the acorn open and suddenly, the acorn split in half! The little bear was so happy.

The bear and the squirrel were now friends and they played and snacked together until it was time to go home.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Lucy. She was only 3 years old and she loved exploring.

One day, she discovered a vine growing up the side of a tree. She spotted a big basket hanging from the vine and decided to take a closer look. As soon as she touched the basket, the vine broke.

The basket crashed to the ground and Lucy was so scared that she began to cry.

The crying soon caught the attention of a friendly fairy who was nearby. He said, "Don't worry little one, I will help you fill the basket back up".

He waved his wand and suddenly the vine was no longer broken. Then he filled the basket with some of the prettiest flowers and sparkly gems Lucy had ever seen.

Lucy smiled with delight and thanked the fairy for his help. "You're welcome", he said, "Now go on, explore and have fun!"

Tom was a boy who liked to learn new things. He liked to learn about animals, colors, shapes, and numbers. He also liked to learn how to do things by himself, like tying his shoes, brushing his teeth, and riding his bike.

One day, Tom went with his dad to the barber shop. The barber was a kind man who cut people's hair. He had a big chair, a sharp scissors, and a funny mirror. Tom wanted to learn how to cut hair like the barber. He asked his dad if he could try.

"Can I cut your hair, dad?" Tom said.

"No, Tom, you can't," his dad said. "Cutting hair is not easy. You need to learn a lot before you can do it. You need to be careful, patient, and humble. You need to listen to what people want and make them happy. You need to practice a lot and get better. The barber is very good at his job because he learned all these things."

Tom looked at the barber and saw that he was smiling. He saw that he was careful, patient, and humble. He saw that he listened to his dad and made him happy. He saw that he practiced a lot and got better.

Tom decided that he wanted to be like the barber when he grew up. He said to the barber, "Can you teach me how to cut hair?"

The barber was surprised and pleased. He said, "Sure, Tom, I can teach you. But you have to promise me that you will learn well and work hard. And you have to wait until you are older and your hands are bigger. Do you promise?"

Tom nodded and said, "I promise. Thank you, barber. You are very nice."

The barber gave Tom a hug and said, "You are very welcome, Tom. You are very smart."

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to look at the big blue sea. He would go to the beach every day and watch the sail boats go by. One day, Timmy saw a sail boat that looked so tasty. It was covered in candy and had a big chocolate sail.

Timmy wanted to taste the sail boat, so he swam out to it. But when he got there, he realized that the candy was not real. It was just a picture on the sail. Timmy was very sad and started to cry. Suddenly, a big wave came and knocked Timmy over. He couldn't swim back to shore and he drowned in the sea.

The end.

Once there was a bird named Sue. She was a mess! She lived in a tree and kept forgetting to clean up her nest.

One day Sue was feeling energetic. She opened up her wings and began to speed around the sky. She was so happy to feel the wind whizzing through her feathers.

Down on the ground, Sue spotted a friend. It was Gail, a small green bird. Sue flew down to greet her. “Let’s have a race!” shouted Sue.

Gail said, “OK! Ready, set, go!”

The two birds sped up and dodged through the clouds. They flew around buildings and darted low towards the ground. They cheered and whooped as they raced around the sky.

When they both finished, they were breathless. Gail smiled at Sue. “Well done! You’re the fastest messy bird I know.”

One hot day, two children were playing in the park. One was a 3 year old and the other was a bit older. They were having so much fun.

The 3 year old saw a triangle in the sand and they decided to make a game out of it. They took turns skipping around the triangle and laughed with glee. As the game went on, their skipping got faster and faster.

Soon, it got too hot so they stopped and sat in the shade. They were so happy that they decided to have a water fight, splashing each other with the cool water.

The two children had a wonderful time, and when it was time to go home, the 3 year old happily skipped happily all the way back.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to travel on airplanes. He would go to the airport with his family and watch the planes take off and land.

One day, Timmy's mom told him they couldn't go on their trip because there was a rough storm. Timmy was sad because he wanted to go on the airplane. But his mom explained that they had to prevent any danger and stay safe.

Timmy understood and waited until the storm passed. Finally, they were able to go to the airport and board their plane. Timmy was so happy he could hardly contain his excitement. He looked out the window as the plane soared through the sky, feeling grateful that they prevented any danger and made it safely to their destination. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved Sundays because he got to go to the park with his mommy and daddy. On this particular Sunday, Timmy was feeling mighty excited because he was going to ride his bike for the first time without training wheels.

As they were getting ready to leave, Timmy's little sister, Sally, wanted to come too. But Timmy didn't want her to because he wanted to be a big boy and ride his bike alone. Sally started to cry and Timmy felt bad. "Okay, you can come with us," he said.

At the park, Timmy tried to ride his bike by himself but he kept falling. Sally tried to help him but he didn't want her to. Just then, a kind man came over and said, "I can help you zip around on your bike." Timmy was happy and the man helped him ride his bike without falling.

Afterwards, Timmy said, "Thank you for helping me. I'm sorry I didn't want Sally to come with us." The man said, "It's okay. You were mighty brave to try riding your bike without training wheels. And it's always nice to share your fun with others." Timmy smiled and felt happy he made a new friend.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to walk on the path in the park with her mommy. One day, they went on a long walk and Lily got very hungry. Her mommy gave her a yummy apple to eat.

As they walked, Lily saw a butterfly and asked her mommy what it was. Her mommy told her it was a butterfly and Lily was happy to learn something new. They kept walking and saw a squirrel running up a tree. Lily asked her mommy what the squirrel was doing and her mommy told her it was looking for nuts to eat.

Lily was happy to learn about the butterfly and the squirrel. She ate her apple and they continued on their walk. When they got home, Lily told her daddy about what she learned on their walk. He was proud of her and gave her a big hug.

Ben and Mia are twins who like to play with their toys. One day, they find a big box in the attic. Inside the box, there are many shiny things. They see rings, necklaces, bracelets, and coins. All of them are made of gold.

"Wow, look at these!" Ben says. He picks up a ring and puts it on his finger. "I am a king!"

"I want to be a queen!" Mia says. She grabs a necklace and puts it around her neck. "This is mine!"

They start to polish the gold with their clothes. They want to make them more brilliant. They pretend they are in a castle and have a lot of money.

But soon, they begin to fight. Ben wants the bracelet that Mia has. Mia wants the coin that Ben has. They pull and tug at each other's gold.

"Give me that!" Ben shouts.

"No, it's mine!" Mia shouts back.

They are so loud that their mom hears them. She comes up to the attic and sees the mess. She is not happy.

"What are you doing?" she asks. "These are not your toys. These are grandma's treasures. You have to be careful with them. And you have to share. You can't be greedy."

She makes them put the gold back in the box. She tells them to say sorry to each other and to grandma. She also tells them to find something else to play with.

Ben and Mia feel bad. They hug each other and say sorry. They also say sorry to grandma. They promise to be nice and not fight over gold.

They decide to play with their stuffed animals instead. They have more fun and don't argue. They learn that gold is not the most important thing.

Once upon a time, there were two friends, a boy and a girl. The girl had a spade, and she liked using it to dig in the ground.

One day, the boy said to the girl, “Let’s make a hole together!” He had a spade too, and he held it in his hands. Together, they used their spades to dig into the ground.

But soon the ground became very dirty, so filthy that the friends couldn’t see. So the girl said, “Let’s join our hands to make a big circle.” And when they did that, the dirt moved away and the ground was clean.

The friends were so happy that they had been able to unite and make the ground clean again. They hugged each other and laughed. And from then on, whenever they had a problem, they would unite to solve it.

Once upon a time, there was a young girl named Abbie. Abbie had a lot of dreams and wanted to become a scientist one day. So every day, she would go to the library and learn all about science.

One day, when she was visiting the library, she saw something shiny and magical in the corner. Abbie ran over and saw that it was a microscope! Abbie was so excited to use the microscope, she couldn't wait to start dreaming about all the amazing things she could do with it.

“Can you help me use this microscope?” Abbie asked the librarian.

“Of course I can!” said the librarian. “You can use the microscope to look at tiny things, like ants and leaves. You can even make them look bigger!”

Abbie was so excited. She couldn't believe that she could use this microscope to make her dreams come true! She thanked the librarian and ran off to start exploring.

Every day, Abbie would use her microscope to explore the tiny things around her. It was a magical way to make her dreams come true. Whenever she felt discouraged, she would remember the words of the librarian and keep dreaming.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved summer because he could play outside all day. One day, Timmy's mom said they were going to travel to the beach. Timmy was very enthusiastic and couldn't wait to see the ocean.

They packed their bags and drove for a long time. Finally, they arrived at the beach. Timmy ran to the water and splashed around. He built sandcastles and collected seashells. He was having so much fun!

As the sun began to set, Timmy's mom said it was time to go back to their hotel. Timmy was sad that the day was over, but he was already looking forward to the next day's adventures. He went to sleep with a smile on his face, dreaming about all the fun he would have on his travels.

Once upon a time, there was a jolly girl named Joy. She liked to guess what would happen next.

One day, Joy was playing with her doll when her mom came in the room.

"Let's go for a walk!" said mom.

Joy smiled and said, "I guess so!"

So the two of them went outside. Joy saw the birds flying in the sky and asked her mom, "Will you get me some bird food?"

Mom smiled and said, "Let's guess what we will find when we get to the park!"

Joy squealed with joy! She couldn't wait to see what they would find.

They soon arrived at the park and Joy saw some squirrels eating nuts. She giggled and asked her mom, "Will they like the bird food too?"

Mom smiled and said, "Let's guess!"

Sure enough, when they put the bird food out, the squirrels came to eat it too. Joy was so happy!

They stayed at the park until it was time to go home. Joy had had so much fun. She said to her mom, "I guess this was a jolly good day!"

Lily was a healthy girl who liked to observe everything. She liked to watch the birds, the flowers, the clouds and the stars. She also liked to observe her friends and learn from them.

One day, it was Lily's birthday. She was very happy and excited. She invited her friends to her house for a party. She had a big cake, balloons, games and presents. She wanted to share her joy with everyone.

But some of her friends were not very nice. They did not observe the rules of the party. They ate too much cake, popped the balloons, cheated in the games and took the presents. They did not say thank you or happy birthday to Lily. They made a big mess and left.

Lily was very sad and angry. She felt like her friends did not care about her. She cried and told her mom what happened. Her mom hugged her and said, "I'm sorry, Lily. Some people are not very kind or grateful. But you are a good and generous girl. You observe how to be a friend and how to be happy. You have a healthy heart and a healthy mind. And you have other friends who love you and appreciate you. Don't let the bad ones spoil your birthday. You are special and you deserve to be happy."

Lily smiled and wiped her tears. She said, "Thank you, mom. You are right. I have other friends who are nice and fun. I will observe who they are and invite them next time. And I will observe how to be a good friend to them too. I love you, mom. And I love my birthday."

Once upon a time, there was a white dog with a long tail. The dog liked to wake up very early every morning. He would jump and run around the house, wagging his tail.

One day, the white dog went outside to play. He saw a big tree with a bird on it. The bird had a pretty tail too. The dog wanted to play with the bird. He tried to jump and catch the bird, but the bird flew away.

The white dog was sad. He wanted to find the bird. He looked and looked, but could not find the bird. The dog went back home, still sad. He did not wake up early the next day. The white dog never saw the pretty bird again.

Lily and Max were twins who liked to play pretend. One day, they found a big box in the basement. They decided to make it into an elevator. They cut out a door and some buttons. They drew a sign that said "Elevator to the Moon".

They took turns pushing the buttons and making noises. "We are going to the moon!" Lily said. "We will see stars and aliens!" Max said. They had a lot of fun.

But then, their mom came down to the basement. She saw the box and the sign. She was not happy. "What are you doing?" she asked. "You are making a mess and wasting paper. This is not an elevator. This is a fake."

Lily and Max felt sad. They did not want to make their mom angry. They tried to explain. "We are playing pretend, mom. We are using our imagination. We are not hurting anyone."

Their mom listened. She understood. She smiled. "I'm sorry, kids. I was too harsh. Playing pretend is good. It helps you learn and have fun. But you also need to be careful and respectful. You can't use things without asking. You can't leave a mess. You can't lie. Do you understand?"

Lily and Max nodded. They said sorry. They hugged their mom. They cleaned up the box and the paper. They learned a lesson. Playing pretend is good, but being honest and responsible is better.

Lila and Ben liked to play in the park. They liked to swing and slide and run. One day, they saw a big stone with funny marks on it. It was near a tree. Lila and Ben ran to the stone. They wanted to see what it was.

The stone was very old and hard. It had ancient words on it. Lila and Ben did not know what they said. They tried to touch the words. They felt bumpy and cold. Lila and Ben wondered what they meant. They wanted to know more.

They saw a hole in the stone. It was round and dark. Lila and Ben looked inside. They saw something shiny. It was a metal ring. It was attached to a chain. Lila and Ben wanted to have it. They thought it was pretty and fun.

Lila reached her hand into the hole. She grabbed the ring. She tried to pull it out. But it was stuck. She pulled harder. She felt something move. She heard a click. She was scared. She wanted to let go. But she could not.

Ben saw Lila's face. She looked sad and hurt. He wanted to help her. He pulled her arm. He tried to free her. But he could not. He heard a rumble. He saw the stone shake. He saw cracks appear. He was scared. He wanted to run. But he could not.

The stone broke. It fell apart. It crushed Lila and Ben. They screamed. They cried. They died. The ring was still in the hole. It was a trap. It was a curse. It was the end.

Anna and Ben were twins who liked to play in the pool. They had a big calendar on the wall that showed them when it was summer. They were very happy when they saw the sun and the flowers on the calendar, because that meant they could splash in the water.

One day, they put on their swimsuits and ran to the pool. They jumped in and started to splash each other. They laughed and shouted and had fun. They also played with their toys, a ball and a duck. They threw the ball and caught it, and they made the duck float and quack.

"Look, Anna, I can spin in the water!" Ben said. He twirled around and around until he felt dizzy. He stopped and held his head. "Wow, that was fun, but now I feel funny."

Anna giggled and tried to spin too. She also felt dizzy and stopped. "Me too, Ben, me too. Let's do it again!"

They spun and spun until they were very dizzy. They fell on their backs and looked at the sky. They saw the clouds and the birds and the sun. They smiled and closed their eyes. They felt the water and the breeze and the warmth. They were very happy. They loved to splash in the pool.

Once there was a gentle bear. He liked to sleep and eat. One day, he walked to the west. He was looking for a new home and adventures. Suddenly, he heard a scary noise. The noise made the bear scared. He tried to hide, but he couldn't find a place. Then, he decided to run away. He ran as fast as he could until he reached a quiet place. He was safe there and he felt calmer. Even though he was scared, he was brave enough to never give up. He knew he could find a way to stay safe.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved listening to the radio. His favorite songs made him dance and sing. One day, Timmy's radio stopped working. He was sad and didn't know what to do.

Timmy's mom saw how poor he felt and decided to buy him a new radio. Timmy was so happy and hugged his mom. He turned on the new radio and listened to his favorite songs again.

But then, the music suddenly stopped. Timmy was confused and thought his new radio was broken too. His mom explained that the song had just ended. Timmy learned that all songs and things come to an end, but he could always listen to more music on his new radio.

Today was Mabel's birthday! Her mommy and daddy were so excited. They wanted to make it special for Mabel. Mommy ordered a big, tasty cake for her. Dad ordered lots of balloons for the walls.

When Mabel woke up, her room was full of balloons! She was so excited she jumped up and down. But then she saw a big, messy mess on the floor. She couldn't believe it.

Mommy and Daddy then told her that it was all a part of their plan to make today special. They told her to go outside and find all the presents that her friends left for her.

Mabel had such a great time playing with her friends. Her birthday was perfect! The cake was yummy and everything turned out just right. And Mabel was so happy that everything was so orderly!

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. He liked to play with his toys and go to the park. One day, Tim found a shiny, light rock. It was a special rock called copper.

Tim wanted to introduce the copper rock to his best friend, Sam. He took the rock to Sam's house. When Sam saw the rock, he was very happy. Tim and Sam played with the copper rock all day.

At the end of the day, Tim and Sam were tired. They said goodbye to each other and went to bed. The copper rock was now a special part of their friendship. They knew they would play with it again soon.

Once upon a time, there was a little train. The train was very sad because it was terrible at going fast. One day, a big train came by and saw the little train.

"Hi, little train! Why are you so slow?" asked the big train. The little train replied, "I am terrible at going fast. I wish I could be like you."

The big train thought for a moment and said, "I have an idea! Let's shut all the doors and windows. Maybe that will help you go faster." So, the little train shut all the doors and windows.

The little train tried to go fast, but it still could not. It felt even more terrible. The big train left, and the little train was all alone, feeling sad and slow.

Maddie was a 3 year old girl who had a lot of trouble sleeping. She tossed and turned throughout the night and barely got any rest. So her parents decided to take her to the doctor.

When she arrived at the doctor's office, she was feeling a bit troubled. She had never been to the doctor's before.

The doctor said, "Let's get you feeling better. I'm going to include a special pillow in your treatment plan."

Maddie was a bit confused and asked, "What's a pillow?"

The doctor smiled. "It is something you can use to help you sleep better. When you lay down at night, it can make you feel more comfortable."

Maddie perked up when she heard this. "Okay! I'd like one of those pillows, please!"

The doctor was happy to help and gave Maddie a special pillow. That night, Maddie slept like a baby, and she never again had trouble sleeping.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, she was walking in the forest when she saw a little bird. The bird was hurt and couldn't fly. Lily felt sad for the bird and wanted to help. She found a twig and gently picked up the bird.

"I'll hug you and make you feel better," said Lily to the bird. The bird chirped happily and snuggled into Lily's arms.

As they walked, they met a friendly fox. "What do you have there?" asked the fox.

"It's a hurt bird," said Lily. "I'm taking care of it."

"That's very kind of you," said the fox. "Let me show you the way out of the forest."

Lily and the bird hugged each other tightly, feeling grateful for the fox's help. They all walked together, happy and safe.

Tom and Lily are friends who like to play together. One day, they see a big van on the street. The van has many colors and pictures on it. Tom and Lily think the van is fun and want to look inside.

They run to the van and open the door. But when they get in, they hear a loud noise. The van starts to move! Tom and Lily are scared and cry for help. They do not know how to stop the van.

A man sees the van and runs after it. He is the owner of the van. He is angry and worried. He catches up with the van and jumps in. He stops the van and turns to Tom and Lily.

"What are you doing in my van?" he asks. "You could have been hurt or caused an accident. You should not go into other people's things without asking."

Tom and Lily are sorry and ashamed. They say sorry to the man and promise to never do it again. The man is kind and forgives them. He tells them that his van is a puzzle van. He travels around and helps people solve puzzles and have fun. He shows them some of the puzzles in his van and lets them try.

Tom and Lily enjoy the puzzles and learn something new. They thank the man and say goodbye. They go back to their parents and tell them what happened. Their parents are glad that they are safe and that they learned a lesson. They hug them and tell them to always be careful and respectful. Tom and Lily agree and remember the puzzle van and the man who helped them.

Joe was an eager boy. He was always ready to learn something new. His favorite teacher was Ms. Smith. She was always so kind and gentle.

One day, Joe's teacher had an exciting new lesson to teach him. She held a stick in her hand and said, "Joe, I want to show you something special. Can you hold your hand out?" Joe was eager to learn and he held up his hand.

Ms. Smith smiled and said, "This is called striking. Watch what I do". She moved the stick back and forth, tapping it on Joe's hand. It felt funny, but Joe liked it.

Ms. Smith smiled and said, "Now it's your turn. Can you strike your hand like I did?" Joe was very eager to learn. He moved the stick back and forth and soon he was striking his hand just like his teacher.

Ms. Smith was very proud of Joe. She said, "You did great! You are so eager to learn. Keep practicing and you'll get it just right!"

Joe smiled and said, "Thank you, Ms. Smith!" He was so proud of himself and he couldn't wait to practice striking again.

Once upon a time, there was a little bear named Teddy. Teddy was very furry and loved to play in the forest. One day, Teddy was walking in the forest when he saw a shiny object on the ground. He picked it up and saw that it was a gold coin. Teddy was very happy and decided to keep it.

As Teddy was walking home, he felt something cold on his paw. He looked down and saw that he had stepped in a puddle. His paw was very cold and wet. Teddy realized that he had been so focused on the shiny coin that he had forgotten to watch where he was going.

Teddy learned an important lesson that day. He realized that sometimes things that shine are not as important as they seem. It's important to pay attention to what's around you and not get distracted by shiny things. And always remember to watch out for cold puddles!

Johnny was a very persistent boy. Every day he looked forward to playing with his favorite toy, a bouncy ball. Johnny loved to bounce it around his house, up and down the stairs, and even outside with the other kids.

One day, Johnny's mom noticed how happy he was when bouncing the ball. She suggested that he go outside to the park with his ball and see what he could do. Johnny was excited and ran out the door with his ball, but soon found out that the park was closed.

Johnny was disappointed, but he was persistent. He looked around and noticed that there was a building nearby. He went inside and saw that it was the local library. Johnny became excited, because this meant he could browse the books for fun. However, library rules said that he needed a license.

Johnny didn't give up though. He asked a librarian for help, and the staff were so impressed with his persistence. They soon gave him a special bouncy ball library license. From then on, Johnny could come in and out of the library whenever he wanted, so he could bounce his ball among the book shelves and have lots of fun.

Ben loves his scooter. He rides it every day in the park. He likes to go fast and make noise. He does not like to share his scooter with anyone.

One day, he sees a girl with a pink scooter. He wants to try it. He rides to her and says, "Give me your scooter!" The girl says, "No, this is mine. You have your own scooter." Ben gets angry. He raises his hand and hits the girl. The girl cries and falls down.

A man sees what Ben did. He is the girl's dad. He runs to Ben and grabs his scooter. He says, "You are a bad boy. You hurt my daughter. You cannot have your scooter anymore." He throws Ben's scooter in the trash. Ben cries and screams. He wants his scooter back. But it is too late. The man and the girl leave the park.

The park is peaceful now. But Ben is not happy. He is sad and sorry. He wishes he was nice to the girl. He wishes he still had his scooter. He learns a hard lesson. He will never hit anyone again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to wear her favorite silver dress that sparkled in the sun. One day, while playing in the park, she met a wise old owl. The owl had big, round eyes and a soft, fluffy coat.

Lily was scared at first, but the owl spoke softly and kindly. He asked her why she loved her silver dress so much. Lily explained that it made her feel pretty and special. The owl nodded his head and said that it was important to wear things that made us feel good.

From that day on, Lily visited the wise old owl every week. They would sit together and talk about all sorts of things. Lily loved listening to the owl's stories and advice. And every time she wore her silver dress, she felt a little bit wiser and a lot happier.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy had a tutor named Mrs. Smith. Mrs. Smith was a nice lady, but sometimes she did weird things.

One day, Timmy was playing with his toys when Mrs. Smith came in. She told Timmy that they were going to do some reading. Timmy didn't feel like reading, but he didn't want to be rude, so he said okay.

As they were reading, Timmy noticed that Mrs. Smith kept looking at the window. He thought it was weird, but he didn't say anything. Suddenly, Mrs. Smith said it was time to close the book. Timmy was happy because he wanted to play again. But then, Mrs. Smith closed the curtains and turned off the lights. Timmy was scared! He didn't know what was happening. But then, Mrs. Smith turned on a flashlight and they read a spooky story together. Timmy realized that Mrs. Smith was just trying to make reading fun! From then on, he looked forward to his tutoring sessions with Mrs. Smith.

Harry and his sister Sally were walking near the lake. Harry saw something long and wriggly under a log. He squealed with joy, "Look, it's a snake!" Sally was scared and ran away. She hoped that it would go away. Harry wanted to catch the snake and pet it. He bravely stepped closer, but it slithered away. He followed it for a long time. Eventually, the snake went far away and Harry was sad. But he still hoped that one day he could pet a snake. Later, Harry and Sally went to the park. They saw a long snake in a cage and they both shouted in surprise. Sally felt safe and excited to see the snake. They both got close to the cage and watched it with curiosity. They both hoped to see it again soon.

Jimmy was going for a walk with his mom, when suddenly, he saw something very brilliant in the sky.

Jimmy: Mom, look up! Jimmy's Mom: What is it? Jimmy: I think it's mist!

Jimmy's Mom smiled and remembered a time when she, too, was a child running in the mist. She reached out, and the mist responded with brilliant colors.

Jimmy giggled and noticed the different colors too. The colors of the mist were so beautiful!

Jimmy remembered how his mom told him that the mist was magical. He smiled at his mom, and they happily watched the colors together.

Once upon a time there were two friends, Bob and Amy. Bob was always insisting that winter was the best season of all. He was so excited for the snow to come and for all the fun activities he could do in winter.

Amy kept telling him that summer was better. She wanted to go to the beach and find seashells and make sandcastles. But Bob kept insisting that winter was the best!

Their argument kept going until finally, their parents told them to come in. They both stopped talking, but Amy kept feeling like Bob was right. She just couldn’t get excited for summer anymore.

When winter came, Amy was surprised to find out that Bob was totally right. She had so much fun playing in the snow and exploring the cold season. She was so excited!

And she kept insisting to her friends that winter was the best season of all.

Sadie the mommy was going on a trip. She was packing up her suitcase. She put in lots of clothes and towels. She added her special flower too. It was her favourite.

When it came time to leave, Sadie felt a bit guilty. She didn't want to leave her little girl alone. But she knew it was important to go away. The mommy hugged her girl and kissed her goodbye.

Then Sadie went away. The little girl was sad and she missed her mommy. But she had her special flower to make her happy. She snuggled it close to her heart every night until she saw her mommy again.

Sadie came back after a few days and the little girl was so happy. She hugged her mommy tight and never wanted to let her go!

The mommy was glad she was back too. She saw the flower in her little girl's hands and smiled. They hugged again and the mommy said she would never leave her again.

Once upon a time, there was a pretty little girl named Ella. On her fourth birthday, Ella’s parents gave her a special present. It was a rod that glowed in the dark!

Ella was so amazed. She jumped up and down and shouted: “Look! It’s glowing!”

Ella’s parents laughed, and said, “Yes, isn’t it wonderful? You can wave it around and it will light up the room.”

So, Ella waved her rod around in circles, and the whole room glowed a beautiful pink and purple.

“Wow, it’s so pretty!” said Ella, clapping her hands in delight.

And from that day on, Ella was never without her glowing rod. Everywhere she went, it lit up the world with its pretty glow.

Once upon a time, there was a lovely princess who loved to play with her board. She would play with it every day and have so much fun. One day, as she was playing with her board, it disappeared! She looked everywhere for it but couldn't find it.

The princess was very sad and didn't know what to do. She asked her friends if they had seen her board, but no one had. She started to cry and thought she would never find her board again.

But then, her fairy godmother appeared and asked her what was wrong. The princess told her about her missing board. The fairy godmother waved her wand and suddenly the board appeared right in front of the princess! The princess was so happy and hugged her fairy godmother. From then on, she made sure to keep her board safe and never let it disappear again.

Once upon a time there was a small girl who loved to play in the garden. She had a special spade that she liked to use so she could dig in the dirt. One day she decided to use her spade to make a hole. She worked hard until she had a nice clean hole.

Suddenly she heard a voice speaking from inside the hole! She was very surprised and asked, "Who is there?" A friendly voice spoke back, "I'm a little boy. Can you help me get out of here?"

The girl was so excited. She put down her spade, reached in and pulled the little boy out. He was so happy to be out of the hole. He thanked the girl for helping him.

The girl gave the little boy a big hug and asked him, "What was your name?" He smiled and said, "My name is Tom." The girl was so happy that Tom was free and she was sure they would be friends forever. They giggled and ran around the garden together, making memories that they would never forget.

Once upon a time, there was a prince who was very gifted. But one day the prince realised he had a problem - he had broken his favorite toy sailboat and was sad.

He went to a wise old wizard and asked him to fix it. The wizard smiled and said, “I can certainly fix it for you.”

The prince said, “Thank you, I really want to play with my sailboat again. Can you fix it soon?”

The wizard replied, “Yes, I will fix it in no time.”

The wizard worked hard and soon he had fixed the sailboat. The prince was happy and thanked the wizard. He said, “You are so gifted at fixing things!”

The prince was now able to play with his sailboat again and he was very happy.

Lila was a big girl who liked to drive her toy car. She had a pink car with four wheels and a horn. She liked to go fast and make noise. She also had a license that her dad made for her. It had her name and picture on it. She was very proud of her license.

One day, Lila wanted to drive her car to the park. She asked her mom if she could go. Her mom said yes, but she had to be careful and follow the rules. Lila said okay and put on her helmet. She took her license and her car and went outside.

On the way to the park, Lila saw a big, shiny car. It was a modern car with many buttons and lights. It looked very cool and fun. Lila wanted to see it closer. She drove her car next to the modern car and stopped. She looked at the driver. He was a man with a beard and glasses. He smiled at Lila and said hello.

"Hi," Lila said. "I like your car. It is very modern."

"Thank you," the man said. "I like your car too. It is very cute."

"Can I see your car?" Lila asked. "Can I touch the buttons?"

"Sure," the man said. "But you have to be careful. Some buttons are not for kids."

Lila nodded and got out of her car. She walked to the modern car and climbed inside. She saw many buttons and lights. She touched some of them. They made sounds and changed colors. She liked them a lot. She felt like a real driver.

The man watched Lila and laughed. He said she was a smart and curious girl. He asked her if she had a license. Lila said yes and showed him her license. He said it was very nice and asked her if she made it herself. Lila said no, her dad made it for her. He said her dad was very clever and kind.

Lila and the man talked for a while. They became friends. They shared stories and jokes. They had fun. Lila forgot about the park. She was happy in the modern car.

After some time, Lila felt tired. She yawned and rubbed her eyes. She said she wanted to sleep. The man said he was tired too. He said they should go back to their cars and sleep. Lila agreed. She said goodbye to the man and thanked him for letting her see his car. He said goodbye to Lila and thanked her for being his friend. He gave her a hug and a kiss.

Lila got out of the modern car and walked to her car. She got in and put on her helmet. She drove her car back to her house. She parked her car in the garage and took her license. She went inside and found her mom. She told her mom about her adventure and showed her her license. Her mom said she was very brave and adventurous. She said she was proud of her. She gave her a hug and a kiss.

Lila said she was hungry and sleepy. Her mom said she would make her some food and then tuck her in bed. Lila said okay and smiled. She ate her food and drank her milk. She brushed her teeth and put on her pajamas. She went to her room and climbed into her bed. She put her license under her pillow and hugged her teddy bear. She closed her eyes and fell asleep. She dreamed of driving the modern car with her new friend. She was happy.

Lily and Ben went to the zoo with Mom and Dad. They saw many animals, like lions, monkeys, and elephants. But Lily's favorite animal was the penguin. She liked how they waddled and splashed in the water.

She asked Mom if she could go closer to the penguin house. Mom said yes, but to be careful and stay with Ben. Lily and Ben walked to the fence and looked at the penguins. There were many of them, black and white and gray. They were very organized. They stood in lines and groups, and followed a leader. They made funny noises, like honks and squawks.

Lily stared at the penguins. She wanted to touch them and play with them. She wondered if they were soft or cold. She wondered if they liked fish or ice cream. She wondered if they had names and families. She stared so hard that she did not hear Mom calling her.

"Come on, Lily, it's time to go," Mom said. "We have to see the other animals and have lunch."

But Lily did not want to go. She wanted to stay with the penguins. She did not answer Mom. She kept staring at the penguins.

Mom came closer and saw Lily's face. She smiled and said, "You really like the penguins, don't you?"

Lily nodded and said, "Yes, Mom, I do. They are so cute and organized. Can we take one home?"

Mom laughed and said, "No, Lily, we can't take a penguin home. They belong to the zoo. They need their friends and their water and their fish. But we can come back another day and see them again. How about that?"

Lily thought for a moment. She was sad to leave the penguins, but she was also hungry and curious. She said, "OK, Mom, let's go. But can we come back soon?"

Mom hugged Lily and said, "Of course, we can. Now, let's go find Dad and Ben and have some lunch. Maybe we can have some fish, like the penguins."

Lily smiled and said, "Yes, Mom, let's do that. But I want ice cream too."

Mom said, "OK, Lily, you can have ice cream too. But only after you eat your fish."

Lily agreed and followed Mom. She waved goodbye to the penguins and said, "Bye, penguins. See you soon. I love you."

Once upon a time, there was a clumsy mole who lived in a big field. He was a very clumsy mole, and he was always tripping over his feet.

One day, the mole's best friend, a squirrel, came over for a visit. The mole was excited and asked his friend, "What should we do?"

The squirrel answered, "Let's cover things with leaves!"

The mole thought it was a great idea, so they spent the day covering things like rocks, trees, and even a hole in the ground with colorful leaves.

When they were done, the mole was tired and said, "This is fun! Let's do it again!"

The squirrel laughed and said, "Sure, let's do it tomorrow!"

The End.

Once upon a time, there was a hunter who went to the forest. He had a big hat and a long gun. He walked for a long time and saw many animals. He was very happy. But then he forgot the way back home. He felt uncomfortable and scared. He looked around but did not recognize anything. Suddenly, he saw a little bird. The bird showed him the way back home. The hunter was very grateful and promised to never forget the way again.

Once upon a time, there was a naughty little boy. He had a special mask of his own. He liked to put it on and pretend he was an animal. He would dash around, pretending to be a lion. His mom would smile and tell him to be careful.

One day, the naughty little boy decided to do something naughty. He put on his mask and ran away! He thought it was fun to play hide and seek. He ran really fast and found a nice hiding place. But then his mom saw him and called him home.

The naughty little boy was not happy. He had wanted to play longer. But he knew it was wrong to run away. He picked up his mask and brought it back home.

When the naughty little boy's mom saw him, she hugged him and said, "Always remember, masks are fun but it's important to follow the rules too." The naughty little boy promised to be a good boy from now on.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to help her mommy in the kitchen. One day, her mommy asked her to take the useful spoon from the drawer. Lily was happy to help and quickly found the spoon.

While they were cooking, Lily accidentally dropped the spoon on the floor. She felt very sad and thought her mommy would be angry. But her mommy just smiled and said, "It's okay, accidents happen. Let's clean it up together."

From that day on, Lily learned that it's okay to make mistakes as long as you try to fix them. And she continued to be a helpful little girl in the kitchen, always eager to take the useful tools and lend a hand.

Once upon a time there was an elderly man. He was walking in the park one day and saw a cooler. He went over to look inside the cooler and he saw something strange! It was a bee! The bee buzzed angrily and then it bit the man! The man was not happy about this. He quickly closed the cooler and stepped away. He didn't want to get hurt again!

The man walked away from the cooler and soon he saw some other people in the park. They had a young child with them. The child noticed the cooler and ran over to take a look. The child opened it up, but nothing happened. The bee was already gone.

The child was excited and went to show their parents the cooler. They hugged the little one and smiled, but they were also a bit worried. They told the elderly man to always be careful around bees, because they can hurt you!

The elderly man thanked them and vowed to remember their wise words. From then on he was always extra cautious when coming across a bee or a cooler.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl. She was walking through the jungle and saw a big, ugly spider. She was scared and started to cry.

Suddenly a monkey came down from a tree. The monkey said, “It’s okay! Don’t be scared! I’ll put it in a jar for you.”

The little girl was very thankful. She said, “Thank you!”

Then the monkey carefully put the ugly spider in a jar. The little girl thanked him again and continued on her way through the jungle.

The monkey watched as she walked away and smiled. He was very happy to help.

Once upon a time there was a poor family, who lived deep in the jungle. They were very kind, but did not get to do many of the fun things that other families did.

One day, a big surprise came to the family's door. It was a new friend, and they all wanted to introduce him to the family. He was a monkey, and he had a special way of introducing himself.

The monkey jumped around and chattered as he showed everyone things in the jungle. He showed them all his favorite places to eat and sleep, and he really liked playing games with them. They all had so much fun with their new friend, and the family felt so happy to meet him.

The family and the monkey were best friends ever after. They would play together and explore the jungle every day. The family was no longer so poor and lonely; they were happy and filled with joy.

The end.

Mum and Dad took Lucy to the store. They all wanted to buy a new perfume. Lucy went to the store with them and she was so excited.

They looked at the different perfumes and Mum asked Lucy, “Which one do you like the best?”

Lucy pointed to the sweetest perfume she saw. She said, “This one, I like it!”

Mum examined it and sniffed it but then said, “No, that one is too weak. We will get another one that is stronger.” So they picked another perfume and brought it home.

But when they opened the new perfume at home it didn't smell as good, it was much weaker than the one at the store. Mum was very disappointed and angry.

She turned to Lucy and said sternly, “You made a bad choice!”

Lucy was scared and started to cry. She had not expected such a bad ending.

Once upon a time there was a fish. He was helpless and alone in the deep, dark sea. One day, he saw a mermaid wiping her eyes. He swam closer and asked why she was so sad. She told him that she had no one to help her clean the ocean. The fish told her that he could help. He swam around and wiped away all the dirt and grime. The mermaid was so pleased. She thanked the little fish and gave him a big hug. From that day on, the fish and mermaid were the best of friends. They cleaned the ocean together and everyone was happy. The end.

Once upon a time, there were two friends, Jack and Joe. Jack was very hungry, and he could not find anything to eat. Joe suggested that he should try some tuna.

Jack said, "Tuna? What is that?"

Joe took out a large can from his bag, and opened it. "This is tuna!" He showed Jack the tuna inside the can.

Jack was happy, and he said, "Thank you. How am I supposed to eat it?"

Joe said, "Look at the back of the can. It will tell you how to read."

So, Jack read the instructions on the back of the can and learned how to eat the tuna. He opened the can and ate the large chunks of tuna. It tasted delicious.

He thanked Joe and said, "This tuna was so good! Thank you so much!"

Once upon a time, there was a rich man. He had lots of nice things.

One day, he wanted a new hedge in his garden. He asked for everyone to come and help build it.

But the day was sunny, and everyone was enjoying the weather. They all delayed helping the rich man.

So the man decided to do it on his own. He worked very hard, and he managed to build a big and beautiful hedge.

The rich man was very happy with his hedge. All his friends admired it, and they were sorry they had delayed helping him.

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play her flute and make beautiful music. One day, she met a cute puppy who was so adorable.

"Hello, little puppy! Do you want to hear me play my flute?" Lily asked.

The puppy wagged his tail and nodded his head. Lily played her flute and the puppy barked happily.

Suddenly, a big scary bear appeared and started to chase them. Lily and the puppy ran as fast as they could, but the bear was too fast.

Lily bowed her head and whispered to the puppy, "I'm sorry, we can't outrun the bear." The bear caught up to them and they were never seen again.

It was the night of the big storm. The rain was pouring and the wind was blowing. Very suddenly, a little rabbit was in trouble. He had gotten stuck in the mud. He was scared and alone.

But then, help was on its way. His parent arrived, looking very brave. He had a big umbrella in his arm to keep him clean. He watched as his parent carefully tried to rescue the little rabbit from the mud.

But the mud was very deep and slippery. His parent tried for a long time, but the little rabbit was stuck. At last, his parent carefully pulled the little rabbit from the mud.

The little rabbit was happy and relieved. His parent had come to his rescue and finally, after some hard work, was able to get him safely out of the slippery mud.

The little rabbit thanked his parent for his rescue and crawled off to his warm and cozy home, thankful for his parent's help.

One day, a little boy named Tim went to play outside. He saw a big box near the tree. Tim was very curious. He wanted to know what was inside. So, he went closer to the box and took a peek.

Inside the box, Tim found a toy gun. He was so happy! He picked up the gun and started to play with it. He pretended to be a superhero, saving the world from bad guys. Tim ran around the yard, laughing and having fun.

After playing for a while, Tim started to feel hungry. He went back to his house and saw his mom in the kitchen. She had made some yummy cookies for him. Tim ate the cookies and told his mom about the toy gun and his adventures. His mom smiled and gave him a big hug.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She was very nervous because she was going to start school soon. Her mom told her that everything would be okay and that she would make lots of friends.

One day, Lily and her mom went to a restaurant to order some food. The waiter was very nice and said, "Welcome to our restaurant. What would you like to order?" Lily's mom ordered some pasta and Lily ordered some chicken nuggets.

While they were waiting for their food, Lily saw a little boy at another table. He looked nervous too. Lily went over to him and said, "Hi, my name is Lily. What's your name?" The boy smiled and said, "My name is Jack. I'm starting school soon and I'm nervous."

Lily remembered what her mom said and told Jack that everything would be okay. They became friends and played together while their moms finished their meal. When Lily went to school, she saw Jack again and they were happy to see each other. They were no longer nervous because they had each other.

Once there was a little boy. He was a very hungry boy. He looked for food, but all he could find was an eraser. He picked it up and held it tight. He didn't like it.

He hated it. He stomped on it and threw it away. He scrunched up his face, he was angry. His tummy was still rumbling, he was so hungry.

He went to the kitchen and opened the fridge. Inside he saw a big apple. He smiled, he liked apples. He grabbed it and ate quickly. The apple was sweet and juicy - it tasted so good!

He ate it all up and he was very full. He was so happy. He loved the apple. He took the eraser and threw it away. He never wanted to see it again. He was glad that he didn't have to hate it anymore.

There was an event at the park. Jack and Julie were excited to go but their mom told them it had to be a modest event. So Jack and Julie left the house and went to the park.

When they got to the park, they looked around but all they could see was a pile of dirt. Jack said, "Mom said it was an event! Where is it?!" Julie said, "Maybe there's something buried here?"

So Jack and Julie started to dig. Sure enough, after a short time, they found a box buried in the dirt. Jack said, "We found something! Open it up, Julie!" Julie said, "Ok!"

When Julie opened the box, she found a strange creature inside. Jack and Julie screamed in terror. "Run!" Jack shouted, and they both ran away as fast as they could.

As they left, the creature was still screaming, and it sounded like it was angry. Mom was waiting back at the house and when they ran in, she said, "what happened? Why are you so scared?!" But Jack and Julie just wouldn't talk about it.

They had left the event with a bad ending, and they wanted to forget it ever happened.

Once upon a time, there was a painter. He was very lucky because he had many friends who liked his paintings. One day, he wanted to peek at his friend's painting. But he accidentally knocked the painting over and it got ruined. His friend was very angry and sad. The painter felt bad and tried to fix it, but it was too late. His friend never talked to him again. The painter learned a lesson to never peek at someone's painting again.

Once upon a time, there was a sweet little boy named John. He loved to explore the town and the people who lived there.

One day, John was wandering around town and he came across a nice old lady. She said, "Good morning, little boy! Would you like to come with me?".

John looked around and smiled. He said, "Yes please, I would love to follow you!".

So John and the old lady walked around town together. They stopped to buy some sweet treats and watched the sun set together.

The old lady said, "That was a wonderful day! I'm so glad you followed me around the town!".

John nodded and smiled. "Me too!" he said, happy to have spent a sweet day with the old lady.

Tom and Anna are friends. They like to play in the farm. They see many animals and plants. They see cows, pigs, chickens, and corn.

One day, they want to pick some corn. They ask the farmer if they can. The farmer says yes, but they have to be careful. He says the corn is very big this year. He says the corn increased a lot because of the rain and the sun.

Tom and Anna are happy. They run to the corn field. They see many yellow ears of corn. They pull some of them and put them in a basket. They want to eat the corn later.

But they pull too many. The basket is full. They cannot carry it. They try to lift it, but it is too heavy. They fall down. The corn falls out of the basket. The basket is empty.

The farmer sees them. He laughs. He says they are silly. He says they do not need so much corn. He says he will help them. He takes some of the corn and puts it in his truck. He says he will give some to the other animals. He says they can keep some for themselves.

Tom and Anna are sorry. They say they are sorry. They say they were greedy. They say they will not pull so much corn next time. They say they will share the corn with the farmer and the animals.

The farmer smiles. He says it is okay. He says he is glad they like the corn. He says the corn is good for them. He says they can eat some now. He says he will cook some for them. He says he will add some butter and salt.

Tom and Anna are excited. They say thank you. They say they love the corn. They say they love the farmer. They follow him to his house. They smell the corn. They taste the corn. They say the corn is yummy. They are happy.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the snow. One day, she went out to play and forgot to wear her glove. Her hand was cold, but she didn't want to go back inside to get her glove.

Lily started to build a snowman. She was proud of her snowman because it was bigger than any snowman she had ever made before. But then she realized that her hand was getting even colder. She remembered that she forgot her glove.

Lily went back inside to get her glove. When she put it on, her hand felt warm again. She went back outside to play with her snowman. She was proud of herself for remembering her glove.

Riley was a curious three year old. She loved exploring, dancing and having fun with her friends. One day, while wandering around the park, she heard a strange noise coming from a nearby bush. She tiptoed closer and peered into the bush. There she saw a bright yellow bird with a red beak, chirping away and hopping from branch to branch.

Riley was so enchanted that she forgot to be scared. She reached out her hand, and the bird perked up. She said, "Hello, birdie!" The bird chirped gently in response.

Riley smiled, and encouraged the bird to come closer. The bird hopped from branch to branch and eventually perched on her finger. She was so delighted that she started giggling.

The bird started chirping words in an unusual language, which Riley could not understand. She looked confused and the bird encouraged her to keep trying. So Riley made bird-like sounds, and soon she caught on to the strange language.

Riley and the bird kept talking, asking questions and learning about each other. By the end of the day, Riley had learned something new, and she was so proud. She had stumbled upon something unusual, but it made her smile, and that was all that mattered.

Once upon a time, a little girl named Lucy went to the park with her mom. Lucy saw a little boy playing with a ball and she felt curious. She went to the boy and said, "Hi, can I play with you?"

The boy said, "Sure, let's play together!" They played for a while and then the boy said, "I'm hungry, do you want some jelly?" Lucy said, "Yes please!" and the boy gave her some jelly.

After they finished eating, Lucy's mom came to pick her up. The boy said, "Thanks for playing with me, it was fun!" Lucy smiled and said, "Thank you too! You're a nice friend." The moral of the story is that it's always good to make new friends and share with others.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lily. She was very wealthy and had many toys to play with. One day, while playing with her toys, she saw a bird that was hurt. The bird couldn't fly and needed help.

Lily wanted to help the bird, but she didn't know what to do. She asked her mom for help, but her mom was busy. So, Lily decided to lay a blanket for the bird to rest on. She also gave the bird some food and water.

But then, Lily's cat came and tried to attack the bird. Lily tried to stop the cat, but it was too fast. The bird flew away, and Lily felt sad. She realized that sometimes, even when we try to help, things don't always go as planned. But she was happy that she tried to help the bird.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to run fast and play with her friends. One day, she was playing with her friends when she saw a bird with a hurt eye.

Lily: "Look, friends! That bird has a hurt eye. We should help it."

Friend 1: "I don't want to help. Let's play instead."

Friend 2: "Yeah, let's ignore the bird."

Lily: "But we should help. It's not nice to ignore someone who needs help."
