The friends didn't listen to Lily and continued to play. But Lily remembered the bird and went back to help it. She brought some seeds and water for the bird and stayed with it until it felt better.

From that day on, Lily's friends learned that it's important to help others and not ignore them, even if it means taking a break from playing.

Lily is a daughter. She is deaf. She cannot hear words or sounds. She can see and feel and smell and taste. She likes to play with her toys and her dog.

One day, Lily and her mom go to the park. Lily sees a big slide. She wants to go on it. She runs to the slide and climbs up the ladder. She sits on the top and smiles.

Mom watches Lily. She is happy. She wants to tell Lily something. She waves her hands. She signs "I love you". Lily looks at mom. She sees her hands. She knows what mom is saying. She signs back "I love you too". She slides down the slide.

Lily and mom hug. They start to play more. They have fun. They are a happy daughter and mom.

Once there was a girl called June. She was three years old and loved to explore and have adventures. One day, she decided to explore a meadow near her home. She entered the meadow, looking around at all the tall and mild grass.

She looked down and saw something shiny. It was a rock with a purple sparkle inside. June bent down and carefully picked it up. She put the shiny rock in her pocket and continued exploring the meadow.

She soon noticed a large pond and wanted to explore. She carefully took off her shoes and entered the pond. The water was cool and mild, and it felt really nice against her legs. She stepped deeper into the pond and soon, the water was up to her waist. She moved her legs, splashing around and having so much fun.

After a while, June stopped playing and exited the pond. She put her shoes back on and continued to explore the meadow until it was time to go back home. The meadow had been such an exciting place to explore.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Jack. Jack loved to play outside. One day, Jack went to the park to play on the swings. He loved to swing high up in the sky and feel the wind in his hair.

Suddenly, Jack heard a voice. It was his friend, Lily. "Hi Jack, do you want to play with me?" asked Lily. Jack replied, "Yes, let's play together!"

Lily had a new helmet on. Jack thought it looked very cool and brave. "Wow, Lily! Your helmet looks so cool and brave!" said Jack. Lily smiled and said, "Thanks, Jack! Do you want to try it on?"

Jack put on the helmet and felt very brave. They played together on the swings and had so much fun. Jack felt happy to have such a brave friend like Lily.

Once upon a time, there was a playful kitten. She loved to explore and have fun. She often went to a pond to play. Her favorite thing to do was to catch bugs with her net.

One day, the kitten saw a fish swimming around the pond. She wanted to catch it, so she took her net and quietly crept up to it. She was so excited! But, when she tried to catch it, the fish swam away. She chased it around the pond, but it was too fast!

Suddenly, a frog hopped up to the kitten. It gave her an idea. She set her net in the water and then waited. After a few minutes, the fish came by and the kitten quickly turned the net over. The fish was caught! The playful kitten was so happy. She will remember this adventure forever.

Once upon a time, there was a little otter who lived by a river. He was very proud and always wanted to go and explore as far around the river as he could.

One day, the little otter decided to go a long way from home. He swam further than he'd ever been before, and soon it started to get cold. He shivered as the water grew cooler.

The little otter noticed a cave by the riverbank and he decided to go inside and get warm. When he was inside, he heard a voice saying, "Who do we have here?" He was scared but he looked up, and he saw a friendly old bear.

The bear asked him why he was shivering, and the little otter said he had ventured too far away from home and was cold. The bear asked him why he had gone so far, and the little otter proudly said he wanted to explore the new and exciting world around him.

The bear smiled and said, "Well, that's very brave. Now, let's get you warm!" The bear gave him a big big hug, and the little otter felt warm and safe again. He thanked the bear and they said goodbye.

The little otter made his way back home, and thanked the bear in his heart for being so kind. From then on, he was always proud of himself for exploring, no matter how cold it got or

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Jane. She was very persistent and wanted to take a vacation. So with a big smile, she asked her mom if they could go. Mom said, "Sure, we can go. But only if you help clean your room!"

Jane's room was a mess. She had lots of toys scattered everywhere, and clothes laying around. But Jane was determined. She worked hard to clean up her room, picking up toys, putting away books, and folding her laundry.

Finally, all the cleaning was done. Jane was proud of her work and went to show her mom. Mom looked at the room and smiled. She said, "You did a great job, Jane! Let's go on vacation."

Jane was excited and happily hugged her mom. From this story, we learn that if we are persistent and work hard, we can achieve great things!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to wear pretty clothes, but her mom always made her wear tight clothes that made her feel uncomfortable.

One day, Lily went to the park to play with her friends. She saw a little boy who was suffering because he had fallen down and hurt his knee. Lily went to him and asked if he was okay.

The little boy said, "My knee hurts a lot. I need a band-aid, but I can't reach it because my clothes are too tight."

Lily felt sorry for the little boy and said, "I have a band-aid in my pocket. Let me help you." She took out the band-aid and helped the little boy put it on his knee. The little boy felt much better and thanked Lily for her help. From that day on, Lily learned that helping others is more important than wearing pretty clothes.

Once upon a time, there was a plane who was very small and light. She was very eager to fly and was determined to manage.

One day, she couldn't wait any longer and decided to go for it. First, she flew up into the clouds and felt so free! But she worried that she would get lost.

So, the plane decided to ask a friendly bird for help. The bird told her to just keep going up and soon enough, she would find her way back down.

The plane was so excited; she flew up and up with the bird close behind. Finally, after a long time she managed to find the way back down to the ground and it had been the best adventure of her life!

Once upon a time there was a mighty dragon. He wanted to travel, so he packed his things and zoomed off. The dragon flew faster than the clouds and whizzed past the trees and buildings.

After a while, the dragon arrived at a very magical place. In front of him was a big, shiny fridge. The dragon was very excited and he ran over to it. The fridge had a very big door and inside it were all sorts of yummy things.

The dragon grabbed a few treats and stuffed them in his bag. He thanked the fridge and took one last look at the magical place before flying away. He was delighted with his mighty adventure and he was looking forward to his next one.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily had a sister named Lucy. Lucy was very graceful when she danced. One day, Lily and Lucy were playing hide and seek. Lily found Lucy hiding behind a tree.

"I found you!" Lily exclaimed.

Lucy smiled and said, "You're getting better at this game."

Lily was happy to hear that. She loved playing with her sister.

As the sun started to set, Lucy said, "It's time to close our eyes and go to sleep."

Lily agreed and they both closed their eyes, ready for a good night's rest.

Once there was a boy. He loved speed. So, one day he decided to ride his bike really fast. He was pedaling so quickly that he had to be careful not to go too fast.

Soon he arrived at his destination, the toilet! He went inside and saw it was very regular. He liked it that way.

All of a sudden the boy heard a noise. It was his dad, running towards him! He was scared so he quickly hopped back on his bike and began to speed away.

He laughed as he rode away and enjoyed the wind in his hair. He was so happy he had gone to the regular toilet!

Once upon a time, there was a girl who was very fearful. One night, there was a big fire in her house. The girl was very scared, but her mommy came to comfort her. Her mommy held her close and told her it would be alright. She said no matter what happens, she would be there to take care of her.

The mommy then took the girl out of the house to safety. The girl felt so much better when she was in her mommy’s arms. She could feel her mommy’s love and care for her. Together, the girl and her mommy watched the fire from a safe distance until it was put out.

The girl was still a bit scared but her mommy was there to comfort her. Her mommy hugged her tightly and said everything was going to be alright. With her mommy’s love, the girl no longer felt so fearful and they went home together.

It was raining outside. The wind blew around the house and it was a bit cold. The little girl was watching everything from the window and thought it was very interesting. She had never seen so much rain before.

Her parents were very serious. They were talking about the weather and how it might affect them. The little girl noticed the seriousness and wanted to help in some way.

So, she went to the kitchen, opened the fridge and took out an umbrella for her parents. She put the umbrella next to her mom and said, "You don't have to worry, the umbrella will keep you dry from the rain".

Her mother smiled and thanked the girl. She said, "You're so thoughtful. It looks like you understand the seriousness of this weather."

The little girl smiled and nodded. Then they all went outside, opened the umbrella and walked in the rain together. They laughed and played in the rain until it stopped.

Jack and Lucy were best friends. Every night, they'd play together and make up stories about their adventures. One night, Jack and Lucy heard a loud noise above and went outside to look. They saw a dark jet flying in the sky and both recognized it right away.

"That's an airplane!" said Jack. "Oh, I want to fly in one of those!" said Lucy.

Just then, the jet made a big circle and flew back around.

"It's coming this way!" said Jack.

The jet got closer and closer, and then landed on a nearby field. Jack and Lucy were so excited and ran up to it to take a look.

A man stepped out of the jet and said to them, "Do you two want to go for a ride in the airplane?"

Jack and Lucy looked at each other and then yelled, "Yes!"

Once upon a time there was a lonely boat. It was a small boat and had no other boats around it. Every day, the little boat bobbed up and down in the sea.

One day, a big whale swam up to the little boat. The whale bowed its head and said, "Hello, little boat. Would you like to go on an adventure with me?" The little boat was very excited.

So, the whale and the boat began to swim away. They swam past dolphins, who danced and smiled at them. They saw other boats, but none of them joined them on their adventure.

They swam all day and when the sun went down, they were still swimming. They finally reached a beautiful beach. The boat was so happy and proud to have made it to the beach with the whale. They bowed to each other, said goodbye and the boat sailed back to the sea, where it was no longer lonely.

Once upon a time there was a sailor who sailed his boat from island to island. He was a very reliable sailor, never missing a trip. But one day, he ran into big waves. The waves kept splashing the boat and he had to resist the waves to stay afloat.

The sailor thought to himself, “I have to be strong and resist the waves!” He was determined to reach the other island. Suddenly he heard a voice.

“Sailor, don’t worry. I will help you resist the waves.”

The sailor looked around and saw a little fish.

“Thank you!” said the sailor.

The fish swam around the boat and used its fin to create a shield of bubbles. The bubble shield helped the sailor resist the waves.

The sailor was so relieved to have such a reliable friend. Finally, they reached the other island safely. They celebrated with a big hug and kept sailing together to more islands.

Once upon a time there was a very clean opera house. Inside the opera house was a woman who liked to mention opera music. Every day she would talk to her friends and mention her love of opera.

One day, a 3-year-old child was walking past the opera house. She heard the woman talking about her favorite opera music and stopped to listen. She started to learn the beautiful songs and words that the woman was mentioning.

The woman noticed the 3-year-old and smiled. She asked the child if she wanted to come inside the opera house and learn more about opera music. The 3-year-old happily agreed and the woman showed her all around the opera house.

The woman taught the 3-year-old new words and songs about opera and the 3-year-old learned them all very quickly. Before the 3-year-old left the opera house she thanked the woman for teaching her about opera and for showing her around the very clean opera house.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his toys, especially his toy car. He would zoom it around the house all day long. One day, Timmy's car stopped moving. He looked at it and saw that the battery was dead. Timmy was sad because he couldn't play with his car anymore.

Timmy's mommy saw him looking sad and asked him what was wrong. Timmy told her about his car and the dead battery. His mommy said not to worry and went to get a new battery. Timmy watched as his mommy put the new battery in his car. He was so happy to see his car move again, he couldn't stop gazing at it.

But then, Timmy's little sister came and took his car away. Timmy got angry and started crying. His mommy came over and asked what happened. Timmy told her about his sister taking his car. His mommy talked to his sister and gave Timmy his car back. Timmy was happy again and continued to play with his car all day long.

Sara and Ben are twins. They like to play in the park. They see a big slide. Sara wants to go first. She runs to the slide and climbs up. Ben waits for his turn.

"Look at me, Ben!" Sara says. "I am so fast and brave!"

She slides down very quickly. But she does not hold on to the sides. She falls off the slide and lands on the ground. She makes a loud noise. She hurts her knee. It bleeds. She cries.

Ben runs to Sara. He sees her knee. He feels sorry for her.

"Are you okay, Sara?" he asks. "Do you need help?"

Sara stops crying. She looks at Ben. She sees his kind face. She feels ashamed.

"I am sorry, Ben," she says. "I was not fast and brave. I was silly and rude. I should have waited for you. I should have held on to the slide. I was not careful."

Ben hugs Sara. He helps her stand up. He takes her to their mom. Their mom has a purple band-aid. She puts it on Sara's knee. She kisses it.

"It will be better soon, Sara," she says. "But you have to be more careful next time. And you have to share with your brother. He loves you and he wants to play with you."

Sara nods. She smiles at Ben. She says thank you to her mom. She learns her lesson. She and Ben go back to the park. They play together. They have fun. They are happy.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Sue. Sue had a big staff. She used the staff to help her dress. She had a hard time dressing herself. One day, Sue saw a boy named Tim. Tim was sad. He could not dress himself too. Sue wanted to help Tim.

Sue went to Tim with her staff. She said, "I can help you dress. My staff can help us." Tim was happy. They worked together to dress. It was hard, but they did not give up. They tried and tried until they could dress.

After they dressed, Sue and Tim were proud. They learned that helping each other made hard things easier. They became good friends. They always helped each other. The moral of the story is to help others when they need it.

Once upon a time, there was a little animal. The animal was very frightened. It was lost in the big woods.

One day, it found a small house. Inside the house, there was a man who liked to fix things. The frightened animal went to the man for help.

The man saw the frightened animal and wanted to help. He gave the animal food and a warm place to sleep. The man also fixed a map to help the animal find its way home. The animal was no longer frightened and was very happy. They both became good friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys, especially her blocks. One day, she decided to build a big tower with her blocks. She picked up the red block and put it on top of the blue block. Then she picked up the yellow block and put it on top of the red block. She kept picking up blocks and stacking them until she made a long tower that reached all the way up to the ceiling.

Lily was so proud of her tower, but then she noticed that one of the blocks was a triangle shape. She thought it looked funny, but she decided to keep it in the tower anyway. She showed her tower to her mom and dad, and they thought it was amazing. They were especially impressed with the triangle block because it made the tower look even more interesting.

From that day on, Lily loved to build towers with her blocks, and she always made sure to include the triangle block in every tower she built. She loved to pick up the blocks and stack them up high, making long towers that reached all the way up to the sky.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Jane. She was three years old, and she loved to go on vacation.

One day, her mom asked her if she wanted to go away together for a week. Jane was so very excited!

Suddenly, Jane felt a bit scared. She thought that a trip by herself with her mom seemed a little bit scary. She told her mom this and her mom smiled.

"Don't be fearful," her mom said, "We can have lots of fun and I'll take good care of you."

Jane thought about it for a few moments and then smiled. She nodded and said, "Yes! I'm ready to go on vacation."

And so Jane and her mom packed their bags and went on their vacation. They had a wonderful time!

One day, a little boy named Tim went to play outside. He saw a small door with a big knob. Tim wanted to see what was behind the door. He turned the knob and opened the door. Inside, he found a room full of toys. Tim was very happy and thought it was a good place to play.

While Tim was playing, a little girl named Sue came into the room. Sue saw Tim playing with her toys and said, "Hey, those are my toys! You can't play with them!" Tim felt sad and didn't know what to do. He didn't want to make Sue mad, but he also wanted to play with the toys.

Tim had an idea. He kneeled down and said, "I'm sorry, Sue. I didn't know they were your toys. Can we play together and share the toys?" Sue thought about it and then smiled. "Okay, Tim. We can play together and share the toys." They both played and had lots of fun. From that day on, Tim and Sue became good friends and always shared their toys.

Sue was a little girl who loved honey. Her parents were always very helpful, and would often give her honey to enjoy.

"Mommy," Sue said one day, "Can I please have some honey?"

"Of course, honey," her mom replied. She took Sue by the hand and led her to the kitchen.

Sue smiled as she saw the honey jars that were sitting on the kitchen table.

"Yay!" Sue exclaimed. She grabbed the biggest jar of honey and opened it. She spooned some honey out of the jar with her little spoon and ate it happily.

"Mmm, it's so yummy," Sue said. "Thank you, mommy, for being so helpful!"

Her mom smiled and replied, "You're welcome! Enjoy!"

Once upon a time, there was a small boy named Peter. Peter was only 3 years old, but he was already very brave. One day, he decided that he wanted to learn how to swim. So he went to his friends house and asked to learn.

His friend's parents said that he could learn, but they told him to be careful and not get too close to the pool, because it was very filthy. Peter was a little scared because he had never seen a pool so dirty.

But then something amazing happened. His friend took him to the pool, and started teaching Peter some easy swimming moves. Peter was a fast learner, and after a few tries, he was able to swim on his own!

He was happy and excited because he had learned something new. From then on, Peter was confident and happy when he went to the pool, and he enjoyed swimming with his friends.

Once upon a time, there was a kind girl named Lily. She had a big box with a lock on it. She wanted to see what was inside, but she couldn't open it. So, she asked her mom to help her unlock the box. Her mom found the key and unlocked the box.

Inside the box, Lily found a file. It was a thin, flat tool with a sharp edge. She didn't know what it was for, but she thought it was pretty. She showed it to her mom and her mom explained that it was used to make things smooth.

One day, Lily met a new friend named Timmy. Timmy was deaf, which meant he couldn't hear. Lily didn't know what to do, but she wanted to be friends with him. She remembered the file and thought it might be fun to use it to draw pictures in the sand that Timmy could feel with his hands. They spent the whole day drawing and laughing together, and Lily was happy to have made a new friend.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved playing outside, especially in the rain. But one day, her mommy told her it was too dry outside to play. Lily didn't understand what "dry" meant, so she asked her mommy lots of questions.

"Mommy, what does 'dry' mean?" Lily asked.

"It means there hasn't been any rain in a long time, and the ground is very thirsty," her mommy explained.

Lily was sad she couldn't play outside, but she had an idea. She filled up a bucket of water and poured it on the ground. The result was amazing - the grass turned green and the flowers started to bloom.

From that day on, whenever it was too dry outside, Lily would water the plants and make everything beautiful again. And every time she did, she would smile and remember the day she questioned what "dry" meant, and the wonderful result that came from it.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy was very clumsy. He would always trip and fall when he played outside. One day, Timmy decided to make some cookies with his mom. They mixed the flour, sugar, and butter together in a big bowl. Timmy loved mixing the ingredients with a big spoon. He made a wish that the cookies would turn out yummy. After they mixed everything, they put the cookies in the oven to bake. When they were done, Timmy's wish came true! The cookies were delicious and Timmy was very happy.

Once there was a clever baby bird called Twig. He lived in a tree and loved to fly up high and sing his beautiful songs.

One day Twig went to the forest and saw a huge pile of lumber. He wanted to play fun games but all the lumber was in his way. Twig hated it.

Twig said to the nearby fox, "This is no fun! I want to jump, fly and sing but I can't with all this lumber here."

The fox replied, "No need to hate it Twig, there is a clever way to clear it."

Twig thought and thought, then he had an idea. He flew up and called for all the birds in the sky. With their help, Twig soon had all the lumber cleared away.

Twig was so happy and could now jump, fly and sing around the forest with all his friends.

Once upon a time there was a lively little dog. The dog loved running around and playing in the park with the other animals.

But the little dog’s owner was often too busy to take him for walks. Day after day the dog watched sadly out of the window as the other animals played.

One day the owner said to little dog, “I'm sorry, I'm so busy. I will take you out later.”

The little dog waited, but his owner kept delaying the promise to take him out. The little dog was sad and lonely.

Finally, the owner felt guilty for not spending time with the little dog. He apologized for the delays, and the two went off to the park together. From then on, the owner made sure to take the little dog out every day.

The moral of the story is that it’s important to spend time with the things that you love and care about. If you delay, you might miss out on some of the most precious moments.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Lily. She was very happy, and she smiled all the time. Every time Lily smiled, her lips would turn up in a colorful way.

Lily’s favorite time of day was when her mommy came home from work. Then she would give Lily a big hug and a smile. The smile on Lily’s mommy’s face was the most colorful of all.

One day, Lily decided to make her own smile. She puckered her lips and stretched them up until they made a funny shape. It didn’t look like her mommy’s or even hers, but it made Lily giggle.

Lily kept practicing until she could make her smile look just like her mommy’s. She was so happy, and smiled brightly each time she made it.

Lily’s mommy was so proud of her. She gave Lily a big hug and said, “You have the most wonderful smile!” Lily was so happy, and her colorful lips were the prettiest they had ever been.

Once upon a time there was a curious little girl called Daisy. She loved to explore and one day, while out walking around her garden, she noticed a rainbow in the sky.

Daisy was so excited to see such a beautiful sight that she ran to get a closer look. She was so happy and amazed! She stayed in one spot and watched the rainbow for what seemed like forever.

Then, all of a sudden, it started to rain. Daisy was about to go and hide, but then she realized that the rain was creating even more rainbows. She was so excited that she decided to stay and watch the rain and all the rainbows it made.

Soon, the sky was filled with rainbows of every size and color. Daisy was so curious that she stayed there until all the rainbows disappeared.

And, with all the rainbows safely in her memory, Daisy happily ran back home.

Anna and Ben are friends. They like to play near the river. The river is big and blue and makes a nice sound. Sometimes they see fish and ducks in the river.

One day, Anna and Ben find a big stick. They want to use it as a bridge. They put the stick across the river. They think they can walk on the stick and go to the other side.

"Let's try it!" Anna says. She holds Ben's hand and steps on the stick. The stick is not very strong. It starts to bend and shake. Anna and Ben are scared.

"Help!" Ben shouts. He tries to go back, but the stick breaks. The stick separates into two pieces. Anna and Ben fall into the river. The water is cold and wet. They splash and cry.

"Anna! Ben!" They hear a voice. It is their mom. She sees them in the river. She runs to them and pulls them out. She hugs them and wraps them in a light blanket. She is angry and worried.

"What were you doing?" She asks. "The river is dangerous. You could have been hurt. You should never play on the stick. You should stay away from the river."

Anna and Ben are sorry. They say they are sorry. They promise they will not do it again. They are glad their mom is there. They are glad they are safe. They are still friends.

Once upon a time there was a humble pool. It was crystal clear and shimmered in the summer sun.

Every day, some children would come and splash in the pool. They happily swam and giggled all afternoon.

One day, a little duck came to the pool. He wanted to take a dip, but he wasn't sure if he was going to fit. He asked all the kids to get out of the pool and help him.

The children put their hands together and started to weigh the little duck. They counted the duck's feathers and said that he weighed just enough.

So the duck jumped right in and everyone cheered! He had a big smile on his face and swam around the pool with the kids.

The pool was the happiest place in town, and the duck was glad to be a part of it.

Tommy and his mom went for a walk in the park. Mom was talking and Tommy was looking at the ducks. Suddenly, Tommy saw a big doggy. The doggy barked and Tommy got scared. Mom said, "It's OK, Tommy. That doggy won't hurt you. It's just a pet." Tommy was still scared and he held his mom's hand tight.

Then, they saw a kitty. The kitty meowed and Tommy smiled. He liked the kitty. He reached out and tried to pet the kitty, but it ran away. Tommy started to cry. Mom said, “It’s ok, Tommy. The kitty didn’t mean to hurt your feelings.”

Tommy felt better, so they kept walking around the park. They saw birds, butterflies and bunnies. Tommy was happy and he wasn’t scared anymore.

Once upon a time, there was a yellow duck. One day, she decided to join the other ducks in the swamp.

The yellow duck was excited! She flew over to the swamp and saw all the other ducks swimming happily. They were so excited to see a new friend.

The yellow duck quickly joined the other ducks in the swamp. They swam around together, laughing and playing.

The yellow duck was so happy to have found new friends in the swamp. She stayed with the other ducks for many days, until one day she decided it was time to go back home.

The yellow duck said goodbye to all the other ducks, and she flew off to her home. She was so happy to know that she now had friends in the swamp.

Mommy and Rachel were walking hand in hand down the street. Rachel was so excited because this was her first time to ever visit the park. She had heard about it from one of her friends, who said the park was really fun!

"Welcome to the park, Rachel!" Mommy said, hugging her tightly.

Rachel smiled and said, "Oh wow! It's so colorful!" She ran around, looking at all of the different sights.

Mommy came over to Rachel and said, "What would you like to do first? Would you like to go on the swings or the slide?"

Rachel thought for a moment before saying excitedly, "Let's go on the slide! I love sliding!"

Mommy nodded and said, "Okay, let's do it. But don't forget to take off your shoes because it's slippery!"

Rachel laughed and took off her shoes. She and Mommy ran up the stairs of the slide. Rachel was so excited that she couldn't stop smiling. They went down the slide over and over again.

When it was time to leave, Rachel was sad. She missed the slide and the fun she had had. So Mommy took her to get a spicy ice cream cone to make her feel better.

Rachel smiled and said, "This is the best welcome ever!" Mommy smiled, happy that Rachel was feeling better.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside and explore the world around her. One day, she found a small bird with a broken wing. Lily felt sad for the bird and wanted to help it feel better.

She asked her mom if she could take care of the bird and her mom said yes. Lily took the bird home and made a cozy nest for it to rest in. She fed it and gave it water every day. The bird began to feel better and soon it was able to fly again.

Lily was happy that she was able to help the bird feel well. She felt proud and independent that she was able to take care of the bird all by herself. From that day on, Lily knew that she could do anything she set her mind to.

Once upon a time there were two friends, Bill and Jane. Bill loved playing with cars and Jane loved playing with dolls.

One day Bill and Jane wanted to have a fair race. So they set up two rows of cars and dolls and then they each got in one of the rows. They both were excited because they could race and find out who was the fastest!

The friends said 'ready, set, go!' and both of them started racing. Bill was running so fast with his cars and Jane was running with her dolls too.

At the finish line, the friends both stopped. They looked at each other and laughed, it was so much fun! Then they looked at the race and saw that it was fair, they both raced their best and neither one was faster than the other.

The friends thought that was the best race ever and they knew they would do it again soon.

Lila was a big sister. She had a new infant brother, Max. He was very small and slept a lot. Lila wanted to play with him, but Mama said he was too little.

One day, Lila saw Max in his crib. He was awake and making noises. Lila ran to him and said, "Hi, Max! Do you want to play with me? I have a ball and a doll and a book. Come, come, come!"

But Max did not come. He just looked at Lila with his big eyes and waved his arms. Lila tried to pick him up, but he was heavy and wiggly. Lila dropped him on the bed and he started to cry.

Mama heard the cry and came to the room. She saw Lila and Max and said, "Oh, Lila, what did you do? You can't lift Max by yourself. He is too small and fragile. You could hurt him or yourself. You have to be gentle and careful with him."

Lila felt sorry and sad. She said, "I'm sorry, Mama. I just wanted to play with him. He is my brother and I love him. But he never plays with me. He is always distant and quiet."

Mama hugged Lila and said, "I know, Lila. You are a good sister and you love Max very much. But he is still a baby and he can't do many things yet. He needs time to grow and learn. He is not distant, he is just different. He loves you too, in his own way. He likes to hear your voice and see your face. He likes to touch your hand and feel your hug. He likes to smile and laugh with you. He will play with you more when he is bigger. But for now, you have to be patient and gentle with him. Can you do that, Lila?"

Lila nodded and said, "Yes, Mama. I can do that. I will be patient and gentle with Max. I will wait for him to come and play with me. I will be his best sister ever."

Mama smiled and said, "That's my girl. Now, let's go and make Max happy. Let's sing him a song and read him a book and give him a kiss. Come, come, come!"

Ben and Lily liked to play in the park. They liked to swing, slide and run. One day, they saw a big metal box near the trees. It was dark and shiny. They were curious.

"Let's go see what's inside," Ben said.

"OK, but be careful," Lily said.

They walked to the metal box and opened the door. It was dark inside. They saw some buttons and wires. They heard a strange noise.

"What is this?" Ben asked.

"I don't know. Maybe it's a spaceship," Lily said.

"Wow, a spaceship! Let's pretend we are astronauts," Ben said.

He pushed a button. The metal box started to shake. The noise got louder. The door closed.

"Ben, what did you do?" Lily cried.

"I don't know. I just pushed a button," Ben said.

They felt the metal box lift off the ground. They looked out the window. They saw the park get smaller and smaller. They saw the sky change from blue to black. They saw stars and planets.

"Ben, we are in space!" Lily said.

"Wow, we are in space! This is amazing," Ben said.

They smiled at each other. They forgot to be scared. They were happy. They had changed their game. They had changed their world. They had changed their lives.

Once upon a time, there were two best friends, Ally and Daisy. Ally was an elephant and Daisy was a bird. They were both very patient, and so they enjoyed taking long walks together in the huge, green field.

One day, Ally was worried about something and she said to Daisy, "I am so worried. Can you help me?" Daisy replied, "Of course, I can try." But Ally wasn't sure how to tell Daisy what was bothering her.

Finally Daisy said, "It's okay, Ally. You don't have to tell me. I am here for you." Ally looked so relieved when she heard this, and so the two friends continued their walk in the field and eventually Ally felt a lot better.

The end.

Sara was playing with her doll in the garden. She liked to pretend that her doll was a doctor and she was a patient. She put a bandage on her doll's arm and said, "There, you are all better now."

But then, she heard a loud meow from the fence. It was a black cat with a white spot on its nose. The cat looked hungry and scared. Sara liked cats, so she ran to the fence and said, "Hello, kitty. Do you want to play with me and my doll?"

The cat meowed again and jumped over the fence. It ran to Sara and rubbed its head on her leg. Sara smiled and picked up the cat. She said, "You are so soft and cute. What is your name?"

The cat did not answer, but it licked Sara's face. Sara giggled and said, "I will call you Spot. Do you want some milk and cookies?"

The cat nodded and purred. Sara said, "OK, let's go to the kitchen. But first, we have to ask Mommy."

Sara carried the cat to the house and knocked on the door. Mommy opened the door and saw Sara and the cat. She said, "Sara, who is this?"

Sara said, "This is Spot, Mommy. He is a hungry cat. Can we give him some milk and cookies, please?"

Mommy looked at the cat and said, "He is a very pretty cat, Sara. But he is not our cat. He belongs to someone else. We can't keep him."

Sara felt sad and said, "But Mommy, he likes me and my doll. He needs a bandage, too. He has a scratch on his ear. Can we keep him for a little while, please?"

Mommy shook her head and said, "No, Sara. We can't keep him. He might have a family who is looking for him. We have to find his owner and return him. That is the right thing to do."

Sara did not want to let go of the cat. She said, "No, Mommy. He is my cat. I want to keep him. He is my friend."

Sara started to cry and demand, "Please, Mommy. Please, please, please."

Mommy sighed and said, "Sara, stop crying and demanding. You have to be a good girl and share. We can give the cat some milk and cookies, but then we have to look for his owner. Maybe we can find another cat for you later. OK?"

Sara sniffed and said, "OK, Mommy. But can I play with him for a little while?"

Mommy nodded and said, "Yes, you can play with him for a little while. But then you have to say goodbye."

Sara hugged the cat and said, "Thank you, Mommy. You are the best Mommy ever."

Mommy smiled and said, "You are welcome, Sara. You are the best Sara ever."

Sam and Bill were friends. Bill always wanted to play but Sam would ignore him. One day Sam used a marker to draw on one of Bill's favourite toys. Bill was so angry. He confronted Sam and shouted "Why did you do that?!" But Sam just ignored him. Bill shouted again, this time louder. But even then Sam just continued to ignore him.

Furious, Bill ran to fetch his mum. When she came, he pointed at Sam and told her what had happened. Sam's face went red. His mum scolded him and asked him to apologise to Bill for ignoring him.

Sam was very sorry and apologised to Bill. He made a promise to always listen to him in future. Bill accepted Sam's apology and they became friends again. Bill even forgave Sam for the mark he made on his toy.

Tom and Lily were friends who liked to play in the garden. They liked to smell the herbs that grew there, like mint and rosemary. They liked to see the sun shine on the flowers and the bees. They liked to hear the birds sing and the wind blow.

One day, Tom and Lily saw a new herb in the garden. It was tall and green, with purple flowers. It smelled sweet and spicy. They wanted to touch it and taste it, but they did not know what it was.

"Let's ask Mom," Tom said.

"No, let's try it ourselves," Lily said. "It looks yummy."

Lily picked a leaf and put it in her mouth. She made a face and spat it out. "Yuck! It's bitter and hot!"

Tom laughed. "You're silly, Lily. You should not eat things you don't know."

Lily felt angry and sad. She wanted to make Tom feel bad too. She saw a shiny red berry on the herb. She picked it and gave it to Tom. "Here, try this. It's sweet and juicy."

Tom trusted Lily. He took the berry and bit it. He felt a pain in his mouth and his throat. He dropped the berry and cried. "Ow! Ow! It hurts! It burns!"

Lily saw Tom cry and felt scared. She did not mean to hurt him. She wanted to help him, but she did not know how. She ran to the house and called Mom.

Mom came and saw Tom. She saw the herb and the berry. She knew what they were. They were poison. She was very angry and very worried. She took Tom to the car and drove to the hospital.

Lily stayed in the garden. She felt lonely and sorry. She wished she had not given Tom the berry. She wished she had listened to him. She wished they were still friends. She cried and cried. The sun did not shine for her anymore.

Once upon a time there was a girl. She had a stomach which was always grumbling. She was feeling very bored. Every day she would look for something exciting to do, but she couldn't find anything.

One day she had an idea. She left her house and went to the park. There she saw lots of interesting things. She played games with the other children and listened to the birds singing. Her stomach felt much better. The girl was no longer bored. She stayed in the park for many hours and had lots of fun. She spent all her time playing different games and her stomach was happy again.

When it was time to go back home, the girl was very happy. She said goodbye to the other children and went home smiling. Now she had lots of new things to do, so she was never bored again!

Once upon a time, there were two friends called Mandy and Joe. They both wanted to win the same prize, but it was only for one of them.

Mandy and Joe both tried very hard to win the prize. They worked and worked, strugglin gto be the cleverest. But in the end, nobody could win because it was too hard.

But then they realised that they could work together and they were very clever. Together, they worked out a way to get the prize.

At the end, Mandy and Joe both got the prize and they were very happy. They had worked very hard and had been clever, so it was worth it!

Sally was walking through the woods when she noticed a fierce net on the ground. She was curious and decided to shake it. As she shook the net, she heard a low growling noise. Suddenly, a big, fierce animal appeared and Sally got very scared.

The animal was growling and pacing around the net. Sally tried to get away but she was too scared. She tried to scream but nothing came out. The animal suddenly stopped and grabbed the net with its teeth. It shook it one more time, and something flew out of the net into the air!

Sally couldn't believe her eyes - it was a flurry of small, colourful birds! They were so beautiful and they flew around the forest, making all sorts of happy noises. Sally had saved the birds from the fierce animal!

From then on, Sally visited the forest often to shake the net and release more birds. She was happy to have helped so many of them find their way to freedom.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy who loved going for a walk every day. He liked looking for little flags that were along the path. One day he found a lovely, pink flag that was blowing in the wind. He was so excited and took it home.

When the little boy got home, he showed the flag to his mom and dad. His mom was very worried. She warned the little boy not to take any flags he would find on his walks. She said that the flag could belong to somebody else. The little boy was sad at first, but he respected his mom's warning.

The little boy decided to make his own flag. He picked out a lovely yellow piece of cloth and decorated it with sparkly stars. Then he found a stick and attached the flag to it. From then on, the little boy carried his flag with him whenever he went for a walk.

He showed it proudly to his mom and dad, who were so pleased with his lovely flag. From that day on, the little boy was always careful to respect the warnings from his parents and to make sure not to take anybody else's flag.

Once upon a time, there was a mild little cat named Dare. Dare loved to eat oats. One day, Dare went to the big tree to find more oats.

Under the tree, Dare met a big dog. The big dog said, "I dare you to climb the tree and get the oats." Dare was scared but wanted the oats so much.

Dare climbed the tree and got the oats. The big dog was happy and said, "Good job!" Dare and the big dog shared the oats and became friends. They played together every day.

Sam and Mia are twins. They like to play with their toys and run in the park. But today, they have to go to the doctor. They do not like the doctor. He has a big needle and a cold stethoscope.

"Can we delay going to the doctor, Mom?" Sam asks. He holds his teddy bear tight.

"No, sweetie, we have to go now. The doctor needs to check your lungs. You know, the parts that help you breathe." Mom says. She puts on their coats and hats.

"Why does he need to check our lungs?" Mia asks. She grabs her doll.

"Because you both had a bad cough last week. The doctor wants to make sure your lungs are regular and healthy." Mom says. She takes their hands and leads them to the car.

Sam and Mia are scared. They do not want the doctor to poke them or listen to their lungs. They hope it will not hurt. They hug their toys and each other. Mom smiles and tries to calm them down.

"Don't worry, my loves. The doctor is very nice and gentle. He will only do what he needs to do. And then we can go home and have some ice cream. How does that sound?" Mom says.

Sam and Mia nod. They still do not like the doctor, but they like ice cream. They decide to be brave and let the doctor check their lungs. They hope their lungs are regular and healthy. They hope they can go home soon and play with their toys and run in the park.

Once upon a time there was a gifted girl called Daisy. Daisy loved playing with her toys and wanted to record them every day. She had a special chain that she used to tie all of her toys together at the end of each day.

One day, Daisy was playing with her dolls when she had a wonderful idea. She wanted to record all of her dolls on video and save them forever! She got her dad's camera and started to make a movie of her dolls dancing and singing. Daisy was so excited to record her dolls - it was like she was making her own movie!

When Daisy had finished recording, she put all of her dolls back in a line and used her special chain to tie them together. The video was saved forever, and Daisy could watch it any time she liked. Everyone was so happy with Daisy's movie, and they all said she was so gifted!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, she went to school and her teacher gave her a folder to keep her papers in. Lily was happy to have a new folder because it was pink and had sparkles on it.

During class, Lily noticed her friend Timmy looked troubled. She asked him what was wrong, and he said he lost his pencil. Lily smiled and said, "Don't worry, I have an extra one you can use." Timmy was happy and said thank you.

After class, Lily showed Timmy how to put his papers in his folder. Timmy smiled and said, "Thank you for helping me, Lily." Lily smiled back and said, "You're welcome, Timmy. Friends help each other."

Once upon a time, there was a clown named Bobo. Bobo was always grumpy because he had lost his red nose. One day, Bobo met a little girl named Lily.

"Hi, Bobo!" Lily said. "Why are you so grumpy?"

"I lost my red nose," Bobo replied sadly. "I can't find it anywhere."

Lily thought for a moment and then said, "I can help you find it! Let's look together."

Bobo was so happy that he started to speak again. "Thank you, Lily! You are a kind friend." Together, they searched high and low until they found Bobo's red nose. Bobo was so happy and grateful that he gave Lily a big hug. From that day on, Bobo wasn't grumpy anymore.

Once upon a time, in a small village, there lived a little boy named Tom. Tom loved to whistle all day long. He would whistle while he played, while he walked, and even while he ate. Everyone in the village knew Tom because of his whistling.

One day, Tom found a shiny mineral near the river. It was so pretty that he wanted to show it to his friends. But when he got to his friends, a bad dog came and took the mineral away. Tom was very sad and didn't know what to do.

Tom had an idea. He started to whistle very loud. The bad dog didn't like the loud sound and dropped the mineral. Tom's friends came to help him chase the bad dog away. They all laughed and played together with the shiny mineral. And from that day on, Tom's whistling became the hero of the village.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the sun. One day, she went outside to play and her hair got wet in the rain. She didn't like her hair to be wet, she wanted it to be dry.

Lily's mom said, "Lily, let me show you how to dry your hair. You can use a towel to dry it." Lily listened and used the towel to dry her hair. She was happy because her hair was dry again.

Lily learned that it's important to take care of her hair and to listen to her mom. The moral of the story is that we should always listen to our parents because they know what's best for us.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a little cube toy that she loved to play with. One day, her grandma came to visit her. Lily was very happy to see her grandma. They played with the little cube toy together and had lots of fun.

After they played with the cube toy, grandma gave Lily a little present. It was a book with lots of pictures. Lily loved the book and asked her grandma to read it to her. They sat down and grandma read the book to Lily.

When it was time for grandma to leave, Lily felt sad. She hugged her grandma and said goodbye. She couldn't wait for her grandma to visit again and play with her little cube toy.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy liked to play outside on his porch. He would sit on his porch and watch the cars go by. One day, Timmy's mom took him to the park. Timmy was so happy! He ran around and played on the swings. But then, Timmy saw a boy who looked angry. The angry boy was kicking a ball really hard. Timmy felt scared and wanted to go back to his porch. But then, Timmy's mom gave him a hug and told him everything was okay. Timmy felt better and went back to playing at the park.

Once upon a time, there was a big bridge. It was so long that it went over a river. One day, a little girl was walking on the bridge. She saw something incredible! It was a big bird with feathers of many colors. The bird set on a tree near the bridge. The little girl was so happy to see the incredible bird. She wanted to take a picture, but she didn't have a camera. She decided to draw a picture of the bird when she got home. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim was a reliable helper in his house. Every day, he helped his mom with the dishwasher. He liked to twist the knob to turn it on. It was fun to watch the water clean the dishes.

One day, Tim wanted to play with his toy car. He put the car inside the dishwasher. He thought it would be fun to see the car twist and turn with the water. Tim twisted the knob and watched the car go round and round.

But, oh no! The dishwasher broke. The water came out and made a big mess on the floor. Tim's mom was not happy. The toy car was wet and broken too. Tim was sad that his car was gone and the dishwasher was broken. He learned not to put toys in the dishwasher again.

Once upon a time, there was a messy room. There were toys everywhere and clothes on the floor. It was very filthy.

One day, a little girl came to the room. She wanted to play but she couldn't find her toys. She looked around and saw the messy room. She decided to clean it.

First, she put the toys in a box. Then, she picked up the clothes and put them in the closet. She worked hard to make the room clean and in order. When she was finished, she felt happy. Now, she could play in a clean room with her toys.

Ben loved dinosaurs. He had many dinosaur toys in his room. He liked to play with them and make them roar and stomp. He knew their names and what they ate. He wished he could see a real dinosaur.

One day, he went to the park with his mom. He saw a big sign that said "Dinosaur Show". He was very excited. He pulled his mom's hand and said "Mom, mom, can we go? Please, please, please?" His mom smiled and said "OK, Ben, let's go see the dinosaurs."

They walked to a big tent. Inside, there were many people and many noises. Ben saw some big shapes moving behind a curtain. He wondered what they were. He heard a loud roar. He felt scared and happy at the same time.

The curtain opened. Ben saw many dinosaurs on the stage. They were not real dinosaurs, but they looked very real. They had scales and teeth and tails. They moved and roared and snarled. Some were big and some were small. Some were green and some were brown. Some had horns and some had spikes. Ben clapped his hands and shouted "Wow, wow, wow!"

The show was very fun. Ben saw the dinosaurs do many things. They ran and jumped and fought and played. They ate leaves and meat and bones. They made friends and enemies. They included Ben in their games. They asked him to join them and help them. Ben felt like he was part of their world. He felt like he was not an ordinary boy, but a dinosaur boy. He had the best time ever.

Once upon a time, there was a little beetle named Ben. Ben lived in a tidy home under a big tree. The tree had many leaves that made a nice roof for Ben's home.

One day, Ben saw a small bug trying to climb the tree. The bug was having a hard time. Ben wanted to help, so he went to the bug and said, "You can do it! I encourage you!" The bug smiled and tried harder to climb the tree.

With Ben's help, the bug finally made it up the tree. They became good friends and played together every day. And from that day on, Ben always encouraged his friends whenever they needed help.

Once upon a time, there was a little puppy named Spot. Spot had a big, fluffy tail that he wagged whenever he was happy. One day, Spot was playing in the park when he saw a rich-looking dog walking by.

"Hello there!" said Spot. "What's your name?"

"My name is Max," replied the rich dog. "I come from a very wealthy family."

Spot was impressed. He had never met a dog that was rich before. He wanted to be friends with Max, but he didn't know how to approach him. That's when Spot had an idea.

"I know!" said Spot. "Let's unite our tails together and become friends forever!"

Max thought this was a great idea and the two dogs wagged their tails together happily. But then, a mean cat came along and started teasing Spot and Max.

"You two don't belong together," said the cat. "Spot is just a scruffy little mutt and Max is a fancy, rich dog. You'll never be friends!"

Spot and Max were upset by the cat's mean words, but they didn't let it get to them. Instead, they stood up for each other and barked at the cat until it ran away.

From that day on, Spot and Max were the best of friends. They would wag their tails together and play in the park every day. And whenever they faced a bully or a mean cat, they would unite and stand up for each other.

Lily and Ben are twins who like to play in the kitchen. They pretend to cook and wash dishes in the sink. One day, they find a big problem. The sink is full of water and it does not go away. They try to push the water with their hands, but it splashes everywhere. They try to pull the plug, but it is stuck. They start to worry. The water might spill on the floor and make a mess.

They call their mom for help, but she is busy on the phone. She tells them to wait a minute. Lily and Ben do not want to wait. They want to solve the problem by themselves. They look around the kitchen for something to help them. They see a big spoon, a cup, a bowl, and a sponge. They have an idea.

They use the spoon to scoop some water from the sink and pour it into the cup. Then they use the cup to pour the water into the bowl. They do this over and over until the sink is almost empty. They use the sponge to soak up the last drops of water and squeeze them into the bowl. They are very careful not to spill any water on the floor. They are very proud of themselves. They solved the problem!

They show their mom what they did. She is very happy and proud of them too. She tells them they are very smart and clever. She also tells them they are very serious about solving problems. She gives them a hug and a kiss. She helps them to empty the bowl in the garden. She also helps them to unstick the plug in the sink. She tells them they can play in the kitchen again, but they have to be careful with the water. Lily and Ben agree. They love to play in the kitchen and solve problems. They are happy.

Once upon a time there was a little boy named Joe. Joe really liked playing with his toys. One day Joe was in the garden when he saw something sparkly in the grass. He got closer and saw that it was a jewelry box.

Joe carefully opened the box and inside, he saw something amazing. Inside was a little jewelry with a shiny diamond at the center. Joe was so happy and he wanted to show it off to his friends.

He took the box and ran to the playground where his friends were playing. He poked the jewelry with his finger and everyone looked at it in awe. All the kids were so amazed and started asking Joe where he got the little jewelry.

Joe smiled and said that he found it in the garden and he was so lucky to find it. All the kids were really excited and congratulated Joe on his great discovery.

Joe smiled and was really happy to have found his treasure. He kept the jewelry safe and it became his most treasured possession.

Once upon a time, there was a little bunny named Benny. Benny loved to play in the forest with his friends. One day, Benny's friend, a little bird named Billy, said, "Let's go underground and explore!"

Benny was scared, but he didn't want to ignore his friend's idea. So, they went underground and saw many beautiful things. They saw glowing rocks and colorful flowers. They even saw a tiny mouse who was happy to see them.

As they were exploring, they heard a loud noise. Benny was scared again and wanted to go back up to the forest. But Billy said, "Don't worry, it's just a mole digging his home."

Finally, they reached the end of the underground tunnel and saw a big surprise. There was a treasure chest filled with shiny gold coins! Benny and Billy were so happy and excited. They took some coins and went back up to the forest. From that day on, they always remembered their beautiful adventure underground.

Once upon a time, there was a mommy and her baby girl. Mommy had a special key that she kept safe and gave to her baby girl.

One day, the mommy said to her baby girl: "I want to give you this key. It will open the door to a special place."

The little girl smiled, and she asked her mommy: "Where does this key go?"

Mommy told her: "This key goes to a light place, a place full of happiness and joy."

The little girl looked up at her mommy. She took the key and said: "Thank you, Mommy. I can't wait to see the light place!"

The mommy smiled and hugged her baby girl. "You're welcome, sweetheart," she said. "Now, go explore the light place!"

The little girl hugged her mommy and skipped away with the key to the light place. And they all lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lily. She had a pretty comb with sparkles on it. She loved to comb her hair every day. One day, Lily went to a party. She wore a fancy dress with lots of colors. At the party, she met a boy named Jack. Jack was sad because he missed his mom. Lily wanted to help Jack, so she gave him a big hug. Jack felt better because Lily was so kind. From that day on, Lily and Jack were friends forever.

Once upon a time, a little boy named John woke up early one morning. He was excited because he knew what was for breakfast - hot, delicious toast! He ran to the kitchen where his mom was busy cooking.

John's mom smiled and said, "Good morning, John! Here is your toast." She gave him a dry piece of gray toast. "Mommy, why is my toast gray?" John asked.

John's mom laughed. "It's a special toast!" she said. She showed him how to twist the toast around to make a spiral shape.

John smiled. Even though his toast was gray, it was so special and tasty. And it was so much fun to twist it around! He had a great breakfast.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to act and pretend she was different characters. One day, Lily's mommy spilled some wine on the carpet. Lily's mommy got very upset and started to yell. Lily felt sad because she didn't like it when her mommy was angry.

Lily wanted to make her mommy happy again, so she decided to act like a silly clown. She put on a big red nose and started to make funny faces. Her mommy couldn't help but laugh and forget about the spilled wine. Lily felt grateful that she could make her mommy happy again.

From that day on, whenever there was a problem, Lily would act like a different character and make everyone laugh. It made her feel good to see everyone happy and grateful that she could bring joy to their lives.

John was an excited 3 year old eager to carry his very own light. He wasn't sure if he could trust the light as it came from a place he didn't know. He asked his mom if the light was reliable. His mom said yes, that the light was reliable and he could trust it.

John was so happy, he started running all around the house with the light. He showed his mom and dad the light and they smiled and laughed. He was so proud of himself for carrying this reliable light.

John took the light with him everywhere he went, in the morning and in the evening. He showed all of his friends the light and showed them how strong it was. Everyone kept telling him it was a very reliable light.

John was so happy that he could carry this light and it was so reliable. He promised himself he would always take good care of the light. Everywhere he goes, he takes the light with him and tells everyone how reliable it is.

Lily and Ben are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big man talking to many people. He has a book and a stick. He points at the book and says many words.

"What is he doing?" Lily asks Ben.

"He is giving a lecture," Ben says. "He is telling the people about something he knows."

"What does he know?" Lily asks.

"I don't know," Ben says. "Maybe he knows about animals or plants or stars."

Lily and Ben are curious. They go closer to the big man and the people. They sit on the grass and listen. The big man talks about birds. He shows pictures of different birds in the book. He says their names and their sounds.

Lily and Ben like birds. They see some birds in the trees. They point at them and make their sounds. They have fun.

The big man sees Lily and Ben. He smiles. He is kind. He asks them if they like birds. Lily and Ben nod. They say yes.

"Would you like to see my book?" the big man asks.

Lily and Ben nod again. They say yes.

The big man gives them his book. He lets them look at the pictures. He tells them more about the birds. He teaches them some new words.

Lily and Ben are happy. They learn a lot. They thank the big man. They wave to him and the people. They go back to the park. They play with the birds. They are friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She liked to play outside in the garden. One day, she saw a pretty red flower called a poppy. She wanted to touch it, but she was afraid it might hurt her.

Her mommy said, "Don't worry, Lily. Poppies are soft and gentle. You can touch it." So, Lily touched the poppy and it felt soft and silky. She smiled and said, "It's so pretty!"

From that day on, Lily loved to touch poppies whenever she saw them. She liked the way they felt and how they looked so red and beautiful. Whenever she saw a poppy, she would say, "Look mommy, a pretty red flower! Can I touch it?" And her mommy would always say yes.

Once there was a dad who was very selfish. He wanted to go out in his motor and go really fast. But his little son wanted to come with him. The dad said no, he was too little and it was too dangerous.

The little boy was very sad, but he was also very brave. He wanted to go with his dad. Then he had an idea. He asked his dad to take him in the motor. The dad said no again.

The little boy got angry. He went up to his dad and he slapped him. Dad was surprised. He saw the look in his son's eyes and he knew he was brave and hopeful. Dad changed his mind and said 'yes, lets go!'

The dad and the little boy got in the motor and they drove off, faster and faster. Dad was so happy and proud, but also a bit scared. They had so much fun together. Dad learned that being selfish doesn't always have to be a bad thing.

Once upon a time, there was a happy little animal that lived in a big forest. It always sang very loudly, so all the other animals could hear. One day, the animal accidently made a mess on the ground and felt very guilty.

The animal knew that it had made a mistake, so it decided to sing a song as an apology. All the other animals in the forest sang along with the happy little animal. They all enjoyed the song, and soon the animal felt better.

After everyone had finished singing, the animal said goodbye to all its friends and started to look for a new place to sing. The other animals all waved goodbye and wished the animal luck as it went along its way.

One day, Tom and his family went for a drive in their car. They drove west for a very long time until they arrived in a new place. Tom was very excited.

Suddenly, Tom saw a strange building. It had a big sign that said "Stir It Yourself". Tom jumped out of the car and ran over to take a closer look.

Tom's mother saw him and shouted, "Tom, come back over here!" She looked very uncomfortable.

Tom turned back around and asked his mother, "Why are you so uncomfortable, Mommy?"

"Well," she said, "I'm not sure what they do inside this building, but it doesn't seem like something a 3 year old child should be getting into!"

Tom wasn't sure why his mom was so worried, but he decided not to stir anything up and stayed close to her.

Once upon a time, there was a big, wide house and it was dark inside. But then something special happened - a bulb lit up the room! It was so bright and cheery. But then, it started to scare the little boy who lived in the house.

He was so scared, that he hid under the bed and closed his eyes tight. The bulb kept shining and he could hear it buzzing. He was too scared to come out, so he stayed under the bed for a long time.

But then he heard a voice coming from outside the house. It was his mom calling him. He quickly ran outside to her and she gave him a big hug. He felt safe again and was no longer scared.

The bulb kept shining brightly in the house, but the little boy now felt brave enough to look at it. He saw it was beautiful and he was no longer scared. He knew the bulb would always keep the house nice and bright.

Once upon a time, there was a monkey who lived in the jungle. He loved to swing from tree to tree and eat bananas. One day, he saw a big, brown sack lying on the ground. He wondered what was inside and decided to investigate.

As he approached the sack, he noticed a mild smell coming from it. He cautiously opened the sack and was surprised to find a bunch of bananas inside! The monkey was so happy and started to eat them all.

But little did the monkey know, the sack belonged to a group of hunters who were looking for their lost bananas. They saw the monkey with their bananas and chased him through the jungle. The monkey had to use all his swinging skills to escape from the hunters.

From that day on, the monkey learned to be more careful and not take things that didn't belong to him. He also made sure to always keep an eye out for any sacks that might belong to someone else.

Tom and Amy were twins who liked to play outside. One day, it rained a lot and the water came up high. Mommy told them to stay inside and not go near the flood. But Tom and Amy were naughty and did not listen. They put on their boots and coats and sneaked out of the house.

They ran to the park where they saw a big puddle. They jumped and splashed and laughed. They did not see the water getting higher and higher. They did not hear Mommy calling them. They did not notice the big wave coming.

"Look, Amy, a boat!" Tom said, pointing to a wooden box floating in the water. "Let's get on it and pretend we are pirates!"

"Okay, Tom, that sounds fun!" Amy said, following her brother. They climbed on the box and waved their sticks like swords. They did not see the hole in the box. They did not feel the water seeping in. They did not know they were in danger.

The box sank quickly and dragged them down. Tom and Amy were scared and cold. They tried to swim and shout, but the water was too strong and loud. They shivered and cried and wished they had listened to Mommy. But it was too late. The flood took them away. They never saw Mommy again.

Lily was a helpful girl. She liked to help her mom and dad with things. One day, she wanted to help her mom make lunch. She saw a big plate on the table. It had a lid on it. Lily wanted to see what was inside.

She climbed on a chair and reached for the plate. She opened the lid. But she did not see food. She saw a big snake. The snake was angry. It hissed and bit Lily on the hand. Lily screamed and dropped the plate. The snake slithered away.

Mom and dad heard Lily scream. They ran to the kitchen. They saw Lily crying and bleeding. They saw the broken plate and the snake. They were scared and angry. They called the doctor and the animal catcher. They asked Lily why she opened the plate. Lily said she wanted to help. Mom and dad said she should not open things without asking. They said the plate was a gift for uncle Bob. He liked snakes. Lily said she was sorry. She learned a lesson. She did not feel helpful anymore. She felt bad.

Once upon a time, there were two friends named Sarah and Tony, who loved to go for walks in their town. One day, they wanted to explore a part of town they hadn't seen before. They had to choose which way to go. There was a beautiful creek with a bridge that crossed over it or a dark, mysterious forest.

Tony chose the creek and they headed towards the bridge. It was a beautiful walk and they found a lot of new things to explore. But when they reached the bridge, they stopped. It looked old and dangerous, and they weren't sure if it was safe to cross.

Sarah stopped and thought for a moment. She said to Tony, "Let's not cross it, Tony. It looks too dangerous. Let's find another way."

Tony realized Sarah was right, and they chose the safe option. They found a nicer, safer bridge to cross, and they safely made it to the other side of the creek and found some wonderful things to explore.

The moral of the story is that it is important to choose the safe option, even if it is not the most exciting. Taking chances can be dangerous and it is better to make wise choices.

Once upon a time there was a brave man. He had interesting pants and his friends called him Super Sam. One day Super Sam heard a loud noise. He went to see what it was and he saw a little kitten stuck in a tree! The little kitten meowed and Super Sam knew he must save it. He looked for a ladder and found one in the garden shed. He put on the interesting pants and climbed high up the ladder. He reached out and held the kitten gently in his hands. He carefully got back down the ladder and placed the little kitten on the ground. The little kitty thanked Super Sam and ran off. Super Sam was so happy he'd been able to save the little kitten. He was proud of his interesting pants and happy he was able to help!

Once there was a dependable jellyfish called Jimmy. He was blue and had long, wiggly tentacles. Every day, Jimmy would swim around, looking for new spots to explore.

One day, Jimmy came across a fish called Timmy. Timmy was eager to have a new friend and asked Jimmy to join him on an adventure. Jimmy agreed, but was a bit scared. He wasn't sure if he should trust Timmy.

Timmy noticed Jimmy's hesitation and said, "Don't worry, Jimmy. I'm very dependable. I will never quit on you!" Jimmy thought about it and decided that he could trust Timmy, so they set off on an adventure.

On their journey, they found many exciting things, like an old shipwreck and a beautiful coral garden. They played games together and laughed until the sun went down. When it was time to go home, Timmy said goodbye to Jimmy with a hug and a smile. He said, "I'll never quit on you, Jimmy. We'll always be friends." From that day on, Jimmy knew he could always trust Timmy.

Once upon a time, there were two best friends named Sarah and Jack. They were always playing together in the park. One day, Sarah said to Jack, "Let's go to my house and collect some dishes". Jack was very excited, so they went.

When they arrived at Sarah's house, they saw a lot of dishes. Sarah said, "Wow, let's collect them all". They ran around, collecting dishes. Every time they got one they would be very excited, and give each other a high-five.

Once they had collected all the dishes, they put them all in Sarah's toy box, which was really big. Sarah and Jack wanted to play with the dishes, so they ran back outside to the park.

They had such a great time playing with the dishes, that when it was time to go home, neither Sarah or Jack wanted to stop. They knew it was getting late, so they put all their dishes back into the box and said goodbye. They agreed to play with the dishes again soon.

One day, Timmy went to the store. He saw something he wanted, so he asked his mom if he could please have it. His mom said yes, and they went home with the special thing. It was a big roll of colorful tape!

Timmy was so lucky! Tape was so much fun! He wrapped presents for his friends, and he even taped pictures to his wall.

But then, Timmy wanted to use all his tape. He started to get sad. He wanted more colored tape! So he asked his mom if he could please have some more tape.

Mom smiled and said yes. She took Timmy back to the store, and they bought lots of colorful tape. Now Timmy can have fun and make things with tape for years and years to come. He is so lucky!

Ben and Lily were playing in the park with their ball. They liked to kick the ball to each other and run after it. Sometimes the ball would go near the road, where the big cars and buses went fast. Ben and Lily knew they had to be careful and look both ways before they crossed the road.

One day, a wild dog came into the park. It saw the ball and wanted to play with it too. It ran after the ball and barked loudly. Ben and Lily were scared of the dog. They wanted their ball back, but they did not want to go near the dog.

"Go away, dog!" Ben shouted. "That is our ball!"

The dog did not listen. It picked up the ball in its mouth and ran away. Ben and Lily chased the dog, hoping to get their ball back. They did not see the red light or the big truck that was coming.

The truck driver saw the children and the dog running into the road. He tried to stop, but he could not. He honked his horn and yelled, "Stop! Yield!"

But it was too late. The truck hit the dog and the ball. The ball popped and the dog yelped. Ben and Lily stopped and saw what happened. They were very sad and scared. They cried and hugged each other.

A nurse who was walking by saw the accident. She ran to help the dog and the children. She called for an ambulance and a police officer. She tried to comfort Ben and Lily and tell them it was not their fault.

But the dog was badly hurt. It did not move or bark anymore. The nurse said it was dead. Ben and Lily felt very sorry for the dog. They wished they had not chased it. They wished they had stayed away from the road. They wished they had listened to their mom and dad. They learned a hard lesson that day.

Once upon a time, there was an elderly man who loved festivals. He enjoyed seeing all of the celebration and cheer that they brought to the community. Everyone knew the elderly man and they thought of him as a kind and helpful friend.

One day, the elderly man decided to create a festival of his own. He asked the townspeople to help him by supplying the things he needed. Everyone was excited and spent the days preparing for the festival.

On the day of the festival, there were decorations, music, and delicious food. The whole town came to enjoy the festivities and they celebrated all day long. When it was time to go home, they thanked the elderly man for supplying all of the fun food, decorations and games.

The festival was a huge success and the elderly man was happy. Although he was old, everyone said that he was still young at heart. The town had a great time and it was all thanks to the elderly man and his kind heart.

John was a friendly 3 year old. Every morning he liked to pray. He knelt down and closed his eyes and said a prayer for the day.

One morning, his mom walked into the room and saw him. She smiled and said, "John, why don't we have some toast for breakfast?"

John opened his eyes and said, "Yes! I love toast!"

He stood up and ran to the kitchen. His mom put two slices of bread into the toaster and they waited together.

When the toast popped up, John smiled. He watched as his mom spread butter on it and then he said, "Let's pray again before we eat!"

His mom smiled and they both bowed their heads. When they finished, they said "Amen" and enjoyed their friendly toast breakfast.

Once upon a time, there was a pink bunny. The bunny liked to hop and step all day. One day, the bunny went for a hop near a big cliff.

As the pink bunny hopped near the cliff, it saw a big bird. The bird was blue and liked to fly high in the sky. The bird saw the bunny and flew down to say hi.

The pink bunny and the big bird became friends. They played near the cliff every day. They were happy and had lots of fun together. And they lived happily ever after.

Anna and Ben are friends. They like to play soccer. One day, they have a big game. They play very hard. They score many goals. They win the game. They are very happy.

They get a trophy. It is shiny and big. They want to show it to their families. They run to the car. Anna sees her mom. She waves and smiles. She holds the trophy high.

"Mom, look! We won! We have a trophy!" Anna shouts.

But her mom does not look. She does not smile. She does not hear. She is deaf. She can only talk with her hands. Anna knows that. She feels sad.

She tries to show her mom the trophy with her hands. She points and signs. But her mom is busy. She is talking with another mom. She does not see Anna. She does not pay attention.

Anna feels angry. She wants her mom to be proud. She wants her mom to see her trophy. She wants her mom to hear her voice. She throws the trophy on the ground. It breaks. It makes a loud noise.

The other mom hears the noise. She looks at Anna. She looks at the trophy. She looks at Anna's mom. She is shocked. She is mad.

"Anna, what did you do? That was a very bad thing! You should not break your trophy! You should be sorry!" She scolds.

Anna's mom hears the scolding. She looks at Anna. She looks at the trophy. She looks at the other mom. She is confused. She is sad.

She does not know what happened. She does not know why Anna is angry. She does not know how to fix it. She hugs Anna. She signs.

"Anna, I love you. I am proud of you. I am sorry I did not see your trophy. Please tell me what happened. Please do not be mad." She pleads.
