When he got home, he realized that he should have listened to the signs of the storm and stayed on land. From that day on, he always checked the weather before going on his boat.

Ben liked to play mailman. He had a big bag of letters and cards that he made with paper and crayons. He went around the house and put them in different places for his family to find. He thought it was fun to surprise them.

One day, he saw a big chair in the living room. It was his dad's chair. It was brown and soft and had a pillow on it. Ben thought it would be a good place to put a letter. He climbed on the chair and reached for the pillow. But when he lifted it, he saw something disgusting.

It was a spider. A big, hairy, black spider. It had eight legs and eight eyes and it looked angry. Ben screamed and dropped the pillow. The spider ran out from under the pillow and onto the chair. Ben jumped off the chair and ran away. He was scared and he dropped his bag of letters.

His dad heard him scream and came to see what was wrong. He saw the spider on the chair and the letters on the floor. He understood what happened. He picked up the spider and put it outside. He picked up the letters and put them in the bag. He hugged Ben and said, "It's okay, buddy. The spider was just as scared as you. It won't hurt you. You're a brave mailman."

Ben felt better. He said, "Thank you, dad. I'm sorry I messed up your chair." His dad said, "Don't worry, son. I like your letters. They make me happy. You're a good mailman." He gave Ben a kiss and helped him finish his game. Ben smiled and said, "I love you, dad. You're the best."

Once upon a time, there was a small bunny that lived in a forest. Every day, he would go outside and pick yummy treats. One day, he was feeling extra adventurous and started to explore the forest. He was careful not to go too far, but he didn't listen to what his mommy had said.

As he ventured further and further away, he noticed it was getting darker and he became fearful. He thought he heard something, and started to run. He stumbled and fell into a deep hole. He couldn't get out!

The bunny started to cry and he heard a voice. He looked around and it was a fox. The fox said, “Don't worry, I can save you!” The bunny was relieved and smiled at the fox.

The fox used his sharp claws to help the bunny out of the deep hole. The fox was very kind and the bunny was so happy that he was safe and sound. From then on, the bunny never ventured too far away from the forest and remembered to listen to his mommy.

Once there was a little boy called Max. He liked to go on adventures. One day he had a grand plan. He wanted to go deep into the woods to find something special.

Max ventured deep into the forest and eventually he found a cave. He stepped inside and saw a big pile of treasure! He smiled and quickly grabbed some for himself. But then he heard a voice. It was an old man.

The old man said he would let Max keep the treasure if he promised one thing. He asked Max to offer some of his treasure to the forest. Max felt a little sad. He wanted to keep it all for himself. But finally he agreed.

The old man pointed Max in the direction of a big tree. Underneath, he said, was a mine of magical crystals. Max put some of his treasure in front of the tree and waited. Suddenly, sparkly stones began to appear. Max touched one cautiously, and was surprised to find it was bitter!

Max smiled, happy that he had offered the right thing. The forest had rewarded him with lots of magical crystals as a thank you.

Max ran home with his treasure and the bitter crystals, feeling very pleased with himself.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Maddy who lived in a big, beautiful house. Maddy had a special toy – a purple statue. Whenever she held it, Maddy felt happy and safe.

One day, a gust of wind blew Maddy's special purple statue out of her hands and it flew away! Maddy started to worry that she had lost it forever.

Maddy started to search for her special statue everywhere. She looked in the garden, the shed and even under the bed. But, no matter how hard she tried, Maddy could not find her statue.

Maddy was so worried. She did not want to lose her special purple statue.

Luckly, her mother had an idea. She remembered seeing Maddy's purple statue in the garden a few days ago.

Maddy and her mother went outside, and there it was! Maddy's special purple statue! She was so happy and hugged it tight.

Maddy never worried about losing her special purple statue again.

Once upon a time, there was a shy rabbit named Benny. Benny liked to hop on the path in the forest. One day, Benny found a shiny rock and wanted to polish it. He hopped to his home and got some water to clean the rock. Then, he rubbed the rock with a leaf to make it shiny.

As he was polishing the rock, a big, mean fox appeared. The fox wanted the shiny rock and chased Benny. Benny was too shy to run away, so the fox took the rock and ran off. Benny was sad and scared. He didn't want to hop on the path anymore. From that day on, Benny stayed in his burrow and never went out again. The end.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Sally. She was full of energy and loved to explore. One day Sally was playing near her house and saw something shiny on the ground. She went to take a closer look and it was a big piece of gum! She was so excited and quickly put it in her pocket.

Sally's mom saw her and said, "Sally, you know you shouldn't keep the gum. You can eat it now but then you must throw it away."

Sally whispered, "Yes, Mommy." But when her Mommy left, Sally stayed with the gum in her pocket.

A few days later, the gum was still in Sally's pocket and it had started to stretch! It was so long that it dragged behind her when she was walking.

Sally's mom noticed this one day and she asked Sally, "What's that behind you?" Sally told the truth and said, "It's the gum". Her Mom didn't look happy, she said, "Sally, why did you not throw it away when I said so? Now you must remain in your room until it disappears!"

Sally knew she had been naughty and she now had to stay in her room all day. The gum remained in her pocket and slowly stretched back to normal. And that's the end of Sally's story.

Once upon a time, in a small garden, there was a little herb. The herb was green and smelled nice. One day, a big bird came to the garden. The bird was hungry and impatient. The bird saw the herb and wanted to eat it.

The herb said, "Please don't eat me, big bird! I am just a small herb and I won't fill your tummy." But the bird was so impatient, it did not listen. It tried to pick up the herb with its beak to eat it.

Just then, a strong wind blew and made the bird drop the herb. The herb fell back into the garden, safe and sound. The bird was sad and flew away, still hungry.

The herb was happy to be back in the garden. It thanked the wind for saving it. From that day on, the herb and the wind became good friends. They played together in the garden every day, and the herb grew big and strong. And the bird learned to be more patient and find other food to eat.

Once upon a time, there was an animal. He was a large, brown bear. But he was broken. One day, he was walking and carrying a big stick, but he was too heavy. The stick dropped to the ground and made a loud noise. The animal was sad and he started to cry.

But then out of the corner of his eye, he saw a bright, yellow butterfly. He watched as it fluttered around and lit up the sky. Seeing the butterfly made him feel better and he stopped crying. He bent down and picked up the stick. Then, he went on his way.

As the animal went on his way, he saw a broken bird in a tree. He reached up and carefully dropped the stick. Then, he used the stick to help the bird and carefully carried her away until she felt safe.

The animal was happy that he was able to help the bird, but he felt a little sad about his broken stick. He put the stick back where he had found it and smiled as he saw the bright, yellow butterfly flying around again.

The animal was still broken, but he was content knowing that he had made the world a brighter, and safer, place for one small animal.

Molly was a very fashionable little girl. She loved to dress up in all the latest styles. One day, she decided to go to work with her mom. When Molly arrived, everyone was wearing great clothes. She was so excited to be there.

Molly and her mom worked hard all day. They put together lots of new outfits and shoes. Molly's mom was so proud of her for helping.

At the end of the day, Molly put on a new dress that she had made. Everyone thought it looked so great. They all said how fashionable Molly was!

Molly was so proud of herself. She had worked hard that day and it paid off. She was learning so much about fashion, and she loved it. She was sure to have a great time exploring fashion more and more.

Once upon a time, there was a man named John. John had a big belt that he wore every day. One day, John's belt broke and he needed to fix it. He went to his garage and got his tools. He worked and worked to fix his belt, but it was very hard.

As John worked, his tools made a loud noise. The noise was so loud that it scared John's cat, Mittens. Mittens ran away and hid under the bed. John felt bad that the noise scared his cat, so he worked quietly.

Finally, after a lot of work, John fixed his belt. He was so happy that he did a little dance. Mittens came out from under the bed and meowed at John. John picked up Mittens and gave her a big hug. From that day on, John made sure to work quietly so that he wouldn't scare Mittens again. The end.

Once there was a humble little girl called Daisy. She loved to run and explore. One day, while running in the sun she saw the mist. It was the prettiest thing she had ever seen! She wanted to make the mist her special place.

But the sun was so hot. Daisy was getting very dry. The mist seemed so far away and she wanted to run to it, but she was too dry. Suddenly, an idea came to her!

Daisy got a very big bucket and filled it with water. She then ran and poured the water on the ground between her and the mist. Suddenly, there was a beautiful path of water. Daisy splashed and ran through the water.

Very soon Daisy reached the mist. She felt the refreshing coolness very near. The mist was so peaceful and Daisy felt so happy. From that day onward, the mist was Daisy’s very special place. She returned to the mist whenever she wanted to feel happy and humble.

Once upon a time, there was a big bird. The bird lived in a tree by a path. Every day, the bird would sing a song. The song was so pretty that all the animals on the path would stop and listen.

One day, a little mouse was walking on the path. The mouse heard the bird's song and wanted to sing too. The bird saw the mouse and invited it to sing along. The mouse was shy at first, but soon it was singing with the bird.

From that day on, the bird and the mouse would sing together every day. They became the best of friends and would always meet on the path to sing their songs. And all the animals on the path would stop and listen to their beautiful music. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to sing songs all day long. One day, she found a cherry tree in her backyard. She loved to eat cherries, but she couldn't reach them.

Lily saw a friendly bird sitting on the tree. She asked the bird to help her get some cherries. The bird agreed and plucked some cherries for her.

Lily was very happy and thanked the friendly bird. She learned that it's good to be kind and friendly to others. And that's why she sang a happy song for the bird. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his toy cars and trucks. One day, he saw a big truck with expensive tires driving down the street. He wanted to play with it, but he knew it wasn't his.

Timmy decided to march over to the truck and ask the driver if he could play with it. But when he got closer, he saw that the driver was very angry. The driver had a flat tire and didn't have a spare. He didn't know what to do.

Timmy thought for a moment and remembered that his dad had a spare tire in the garage. He offered to help the driver and they went to get the spare tire. Timmy felt proud that he could help someone in need. From that day on, the driver always waved to Timmy when he drove by.

Once upon a time, there was a caterpillar. The caterpillar wanted to go on an adventure. But it was difficult for the caterpillar to move around because it was so small.

So, the caterpillar asked its friends for help. They decided to pack some food and go on an adventure together. They went through the grass and over some rocks.

It was a difficult journey, but the caterpillar was happy to have friends to help. When they reached the end of their adventure, they all sat down and ate the food they packed. The caterpillar was very happy and grateful to have such good friends.

Mum took Sally to the shop. There was a big bookcase. "That's silly!" laughed Sally. Mum smiled too. She took Sally's hand and they walked over to the bookcase. It was so big Sally could hardly see to the top. She couldn't take it home as it was so big. Mum took some books off the shelf and gave them to Sally. She was very excited. "Can I keep them?" she asked. Mum said, "Yes, but we have to take them home so you can read them". Sally put the books in her pocket and gave Mum a big hug. She was so happy. Mum and Sally went home with the books to read. Sally loved her new books and took care of them. She looked at the funny bookcase every time she went to the shop.

One day, Mommy and Daddy were very glad. They were going to a store to pay for a special magnet. The magnet was small, shiny and pretty. They paid the cashier and put the magnet in their pocket. When they got home, they gave it to their little three year old. The little three year old was so glad! He hugged the magnet and ran around the house, showing it to everybody he could find. He kept it next to him the whole day and everywhere he went. Now the little three year old has a new magnet that he loves. It's so shiny and pretty, and he is so proud and happy!

Once upon a time, there was an ugly mineral. This mineral was very special, it was the only kind of its kind. It sparkled brightly in the sunshine and everyone who saw it loved it.

One day, a little girl saw the mineral and decided she wanted to take it home. She asked her mom if she could keep it, but her mom said no. The little girl got sad, but she asked her mom if she could at least polish it. Her mom agreed and the little girl got to work.

For weeks, the little girl polished and polished until the mineral shone brightly. Everyone was amazed at how beautiful it had become. But then one day she accidentally dropped the mineral and it broke into two pieces.

The little girl started to cry and her mom quickly came over to help. She told the little girl that it was ok and that she still had made the mineral look beautiful. She hugged the little girl and told her that she was still very proud.

The little girl learned an important lesson that day, that things can still look beautiful even if they become broken.

Once upon a time there was a happy boy named Owen. He was very excited when he went to the park and saw lots of clay. He wanted to build something with it.

He found a spot on the grass to sit and he started to shape the clay into different sizes. He made a little square which fit perfectly into a piece of the clay he had just shaped into a big box.

He kept on building until his mom said it was time to leave. Owen was so excited about all his creations he had made out of clay.

On their way home, Owen told his mom about all the wonderful things he had built and how he wanted to take them home. His mom thought that it would be better to leave the clay where it was, but Owen was insistent.

When they got home, Owen went straight to his room to put the clay in his toy box. But when he got there, his mom was already waiting. She had found the clay in his pocket and was not happy. She told him that he should not have taken it from the park. Owen was sad, but he realized he had done something wrong.

The next day, Owen was excited when his mom took him back to the park. He wanted to put the clay back exactly where he had found it, but when he got there, there was nothing left. He had made a mistake, and now the clay was gone. It was a very bad

Once there was a boy named Joe. He liked to discover new things. One day he wanted to go for a walk in the forest. As he walked, he looked up and discovered the sky. It was bright blue and very beautiful. Joe felt so comfortable.

He decided to keep walking and discover more. After walking for a while, he saw a big lake. The water looked so clean and blue. Joe came closer and looked into the lake. He saw fishes swimming and birds flying in the sky. It was so spectacular!

Joe kept walking until he reached the top of a hill. From there he could see the whole forest below and the sky above. He sat down on the grass and felt so relaxed. Suddenly, he heard the sound of nature and he noticed how big and wonderful the sky was. Joe smiled and was happy to discover new things.

Once upon a time there were two friends - a slow turtle and a small flea. They were very close and would spend time together everyday.

The flea was so tiny that he could jump very high and very far. The turtle was too slow to do any of these things, but he was so patient and kind.

One day, the flea said to the turtle, "Let's have a race!" The turtle was a bit embarrassed but he agreed. The flea excitedly hopped away and the turtle followed behind slowly.

The flea was so fast that he crossed the finish line first. When the turtle finally made it, he was embarrassed and a bit sad.

The flea could see this, and he said to the turtle, "It's ok that you're slow, that's the way you are! Let's still stay friends and keep helping each other out." The turtle smiled and was glad he had such a good friend.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy had a tall toy tower that he loved to play with. He would build it up high and then knock it down with a big smile on his face.

One day, Timmy's mom told him it was time to finish playing and clean up his toys. Timmy was sad because he didn't want to stop playing with his tall tower. But he knew he had to listen to his mom.

So, Timmy carefully took apart his tower and put all the toy blocks back in their box. He felt proud that he finished cleaning up his toys like a big boy. And he knew he could always build his tall tower again tomorrow. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her dolls and her favorite color was pink. One day, Lily's mommy took her to a big park where they saw lots of people playing and having fun.

Suddenly, they heard a loud noise. It was a group of people arguing and fighting. Lily felt scared and sad. Her mommy told her to close her eyes and pray for peace. Lily closed her eyes tight and said a little prayer for everyone to be happy and peaceful.

After a few minutes, Lily opened her eyes and saw that the people had stopped fighting. They were all smiling and talking to each other. Lily felt happy and proud that her prayer had worked. From that day on, she always remembered to pray for peace whenever she felt scared or sad.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys all day long. One day, she saw a big machine in her backyard. It was orange and looked very strange.

Lily asked her mom, "What is that big orange machine?"

Her mom replied, "It's a lawnmower. It performs the task of cutting the grass."

Lily was curious and wanted to try it out. She climbed up onto the machine and started it up. But she didn't know how to control it and ended up crashing into a tree. She was scared and started to cry.

Her mom came running and asked, "What happened?"

Lily replied, "I tried to perform the task of cutting the grass, but the machine was too hard to control."

Her mom comforted her and said, "It's okay, we can try again another day. Let's go inside and have some orange juice." And they went inside and enjoyed a glass of orange juice together.

Once upon a time, there were two friends named Jack and Lisa. It was winter outside, so they decided to have some fun indoors.

Jack found some paint and paper. He spread out the paper and gave Lisa a brush. Together, they dipped the brush in the paint and began to paint. They painted a beautiful picture of colorful winter trees!

Jack and Lisa liked their painting very much. They were very proud of their work and felt very independent.

After they finished painting, they hung the picture up on their wall where they could admire it all winter long.

Jack and Lisa had a lot of fun painting together and enjoyed feeling independent. They thought that it was the best way to spend a winter day!

Tom and Lily were twins who liked to play and have fun. But sometimes they did not listen to their mom and dad. They made a mess in their room, they spilled their juice on the sofa, and they broke their toys. Mom and dad were not happy. They said, "Tom and Lily, you have been very bad. You need to learn to be good. We will punish you. You have to do a hard task."

Tom and Lily were scared. They did not want to be punished. They did not want to do a hard task. They said, "We are sorry, mom and dad. Please do not punish us. Please do not give us a hard task. We will be good from now on."

Mom and dad looked at Tom and Lily. They saw that they were sorry. But they also wanted them to learn a lesson. They said, "We love you, Tom and Lily. But you have to be responsible for your actions. You have to clean your room, wash the sofa, and fix your toys. That is your hard task. You have to do it by yourself. We will help you only if you ask nicely."

Tom and Lily nodded. They knew they had to do their hard task. They went to their room and started to clean. They picked up their clothes, their books, and their toys. They put them in their drawers, their shelves, and their boxes. They found some glue and tape and tried to fix their broken toys. They worked hard and did not complain.

When they finished, they went to the living room and washed the sofa. They used a sponge, some soap, and some water. They rubbed the stain until it was gone. They dried the sofa with a towel. They worked hard and did not complain.

They went to mom and dad and said, "We did our hard task, mom and dad. We cleaned our room, we washed the sofa, and we fixed our toys. We are sorry for being bad. We will be good from now on."

Mom and dad smiled and hugged Tom and Lily. They said, "We are proud of you, Tom and Lily. You did your hard task very well. You showed us that you are sorry and that you can be good. We forgive you. You can play and have fun now. But remember to listen to us and to take care of your things."

Tom and Lily said, "Thank you, mom and dad. We love you. We will listen to you and take care of our things." They went to play and have fun. They were happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his toy cars and trucks. One day, Timmy was playing with his toy truck when he accidentally twisted the wheels too hard and they fell off!

Timmy's mommy came into the room and saw the wheels on the floor. She told Timmy not to twist his toys too hard or they might break. Timmy nodded his head and promised to be more careful.

Later that day, Timmy and his mommy went to a barbecue with their friends. There was a big grill with lots of hot coals and smoke coming out of it. Timmy thought it was noisy and covered his ears. But he loved the smell of the meat cooking on the grill.

After dinner, Timmy and his friends played tag in the backyard. They ran around and made lots of noise. Timmy had so much fun that he forgot all about his toy truck and the wheels that fell off earlier.

Lily and Anna were sisters who liked to play dress-up. They had many dresses of different colors and shapes. They also had hats, shoes, and jewels to match. They liked to decorate their dresses with stickers, ribbons, and buttons.

One day, they found a new dress in their closet. It was very wide and long, with many flowers on it. It looked like a dress for a princess. Lily and Anna wanted to try it on.

"Let me wear it first!" Lily said. She was the older sister and liked to be in charge.

"No, I want to wear it first!" Anna said. She was the younger sister and liked to be fair.

They both pulled on the dress, but it was too wide for both of them. They could not fit in it together.

"Stop pulling!" Lily said. "You are going to rip the dress!"

"Stop pushing!" Anna said. "You are going to make the dress dirty!"

They both let go of the dress and looked at it. It was wrinkled and torn, and some of the flowers had fallen off. They felt sad and sorry.

"We ruined the dress!" Lily said.

"We can't play dress-up anymore!" Anna said.

They started to cry. Their mom heard them and came to see what was wrong. She saw the dress and understood what had happened.

"Don't cry, girls," she said. "It's okay. The dress is not ruined. It's just different. We can fix it and decorate it again."

She took the dress and gave them some scissors, glue, and paper. She helped them cut out new flowers and glue them on the dress. She also gave them some sparkly stickers and ribbons to add some shine.

"Look, girls," she said. "The dress is beautiful again. And it's unique. No one else has a dress like this. You can both wear it and share it."

Lily and Anna smiled and hugged their mom. They thanked her for helping them. They put on the dress, one after the other, and admired themselves in the mirror. They felt happy and proud.

They decided to play dress-up with their other dresses and decorate them too. They had fun and played nicely. They learned to share and be creative. They loved their dresses and each other.

Once there was an adorable little girl named Claire. She had a scooter that she loved. She would ride around the park and laugh and play. One day she noticed something strange. The scooter was starting to rot! It was getting rusty and the paint was chipping off. She didn’t want it to rot anymore so she told her parents.

Her parents went to the store and bought some special paint to fix the scooter. They sanded the rusty parts and applied the paint. Then they let the scooter dry outside in the sun.

When the scooter was all done, Claire ran outside with a big smile on her face. The scooter was as good as new! Claire was so happy that she hugged it and gave it kisses. She gleefully hopped on and began riding around the park again, laughing and singing as she went.

Once upon a time, there was a cheerful little insect. He lived in a big tree in the forest. Every day, he enjoyed playing and singing in the sunshine. Then one day, he saw something to his surprise. It was a giant snapping something in the air!

He flew closer and saw it was a tiny snapping turtle. He was so excited to see him.

The insect said, “Hello there! What are you doing?”

The snapping turtle smiled and said, “I’m having so much fun snapping in the air. Would you like to join me?”

The insect was so delighted. He started snapping in the air. They laughed and played together for hours.

At the end of the day, the insect was so happy and cheerful. He had a wonderful time with his new friend, the snapping turtle.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Lucy. She was very stubborn. Her mom and dad tried to tell her things, but she always had to do things her own way.

One day, Lucy wanted to speed down the hill in her village. She knew it was dangerous, but she was too stubborn to listen. She put her hands on the handle of her bike and zoomed off!

At the same time, Lucy's mom saw and shouted, “Don’t speed!" But it was too late - Lucy was already riding down the hill in full speed.

Lucy got to the bottom of the hill faster than she expected. She nearly fell off her bike, but was brave enough to handle it.

When she got home, she realized the truth - it hadn’t been worth it to speed. Lucy learned her lesson, and from that day on she always listened to her mom and dads’ advice.

Lily was a little lamb who loved to play with her friends in the meadow. She had soft white wool that kept her warm and cozy. She liked to jump and run and chase butterflies with her friends.

One day, a man came to the meadow with a big pair of scissors. He wanted to cut the wool from the sheep and the lambs. He said he would make sweaters and hats and scarves from the wool. Lily was scared of the scissors. She did not want to lose her wool.

She ran away from the man and hid behind a bush. She saw the man cut the wool from her friends. They looked sad and cold. She heard them cry and bleat.

"Lily, where are you?" her mother called. "Don't be afraid. The man will not hurt you. He only wants your wool. It will grow back soon. Come out and let him cut your wool. It will make you famous. People will wear your wool and admire it. You will be a famous lamb."

Lily did not want to be famous. She wanted to keep her wool. She liked her wool. It was part of her. She did not care what people thought of her wool. She shook her head and stayed behind the bush.

The man looked for Lily. He could not find her. He gave up and left with his bag of wool. He did not manage to cut Lily's wool. Lily was happy. She came out of the bush and ran to her mother. She hugged her and said, "I love you, Mommy. I love my wool. I don't want to be famous. I want to be me."

Her mother smiled and licked her face. She said, "I love you too, Lily. You are my brave and smart lamb. You can keep your wool if you want. You are famous to me. You are my precious Lily."

Anna likes to print. She likes to print pictures of flowers and animals and people. She likes to print with many colors. She likes to show her prints to her mom and dad.

One day, Anna goes to the office with her mom. Her mom has to work on the computer. Anna sees a big printer in the office. She thinks it is beautiful. She wants to print with it.

She waits until her mom is busy. Then she sneaks to the printer. She finds some paper and some buttons. She pushes the buttons. She hears the printer make noises. She sees the paper come out. She is happy.

But then she sees the paper. It is not beautiful. It is black and white. It has words and numbers and lines. It is not what she wanted to print. She is sad.

She hears her mom shout. She turns around. Her mom is angry. She sees the paper. She sees the printer. She sees Anna. She says, "Anna, what did you do? You wasted the paper. You messed up the printer. You ruined my work. You are in big trouble."

Anna starts to cry. She is sorry. She did not mean to do it. She just wanted to print. She says, "Mom, I'm sorry. I love you. Please don't be mad."

But her mom is still mad. She takes Anna by the hand. She says, "We have to go home. Now. You are not allowed to print anymore. You are not allowed to come to the office anymore. You are grounded."

Anna cries more. She feels bad. She wishes she did not print. She wishes she did not go to the office. She wishes her mom was not mad. She wishes she could make it better. But she can't. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved playing outside with his friends. One day, Timmy and his friends found a bow and arrow. They were eager to try it out.

Timmy's friend, Billy, said, "I want to try shooting the arrow!" Timmy replied, "Okay, let's take turns." Billy shot the arrow and it flew far away. Timmy and his friends laughed and cheered.

Then it was Timmy's turn. He pulled back the bow and shot the arrow. It went straight up into the sky and they all watched it disappear. They laughed again and ran off to play some more.

Once upon a time, a man had a wife who loved fancy things. She always wanted new dresses and jewelry. But the man didn't have much money, so he couldn't buy her all the fancy things she wanted.

One day, the wife saw a beautiful necklace in a store. She begged her husband to buy it for her, but he couldn't afford it. The wife got very angry and accused her husband of lying about how much money he had.

The husband felt very sad and didn't know what to do. He loved his wife very much, but he couldn't make her happy with all the fancy things she wanted. Finally, the husband had an idea. He went home and made a necklace out of flowers for his wife. When she saw it, she was so happy and realized that her husband's love was more important than any fancy thing. From that day on, they lived happily ever after.

Tom and Sue like to play with their toy boat. They sail it in the pond near their house. They take turns to hold the boat and make it go fast or slow.

One day, a big wind comes and blows their boat away. They run after it, but it is too fast. The boat sails to the other side of the pond, where there is a big tree.

Tom and Sue are sad. They want their boat back. They see a boy near the tree. He has their boat in his hands. He is laughing.

"Hey, that is our boat!" Tom shouts. "Give it back!"

The boy shakes his head. He says, "No, this is my boat now. It is a nice boat. Your boat is ugly."

Sue gets angry. She says, "That is not true. Our boat is pretty. You are ugly."

The boy gets angry too. He says, "No, you are ugly. And your boat is ugly. Watch this." He throws the boat at the tree. The boat hits the tree and breaks.

Tom and Sue cry. They see their boat in pieces. They are very sad. They wish the boy was nice. They wish the wind was calm. They wish they had their boat.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy who had many nuts in his bucket. Every day he would take a few nuts and put them in his pocket. One day, the little boy was investigating his nuts when a squirrel came up to him and said "Hello, can I take a nut?"

The little boy was very surprised and said "Yes, You can have a mild nut." The squirrel jumped with joy and said, "Thank you! I was so hungry."

The squirrel took the nut and said goodbye. The little boy watched as the squirrel ate the nut and then ran off into the woods. The little boy was very happy he could help the squirrel and continued to take his nuts with him each day.

Once there was a girl called Emma. She loved to look out of the window. One day she saw something in the field. It was a big bull! Emma was scared, so she didn't go outside. She watched the bull and he was looking around.

Emma's dad saw what was happening. He said to Emma, "Don't worry, he won't hurt you. Let's go get a closer look". So they went outside. When they got close, Emma saw that the bull was hurt.

Emma's dad said to her, "Don't worry, I'm sure he will be okay. Let's get help for him". So he called the vet. The vet came and looked at the bull. The vet told them the bull was OK.

Emma was so happy. She smiled and said, "Thank you for helping the bull". Emma learned a valuable lesson that day: you should always help someone who is hurt.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her dolls and teddy bears on the table in her room. One day, her mommy came in and said, "Lily, let's go to the park!"

Lily was so excited to go to the park and play on the swings. When they got there, Lily saw a charming puppy running around. She said to her mommy, "Look at the cute puppy! Can we pet him?"

Her mommy said, "Yes, but be gentle and let him come to you." The puppy came over and Lily petted him gently. She was so happy and said, "This is the best day ever!"

After a while, it was time to go home. Lily said goodbye to the puppy and they went back to their house. When they got inside, Lily's mommy said, "Let's have some snacks at the table." They sat down and ate some yummy cookies together. Lily smiled and said, "I love spending time with you, mommy."

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to build towers with blocks and make them into a big stack. One day, she was building a tower when her little brother came and knocked it over. Lily got angry and started to cry.

Her mom came and asked what was wrong. Lily said, "My tower fell down and I worry that I can't build it again." Her mom said, "Don't worry, you can build it again. Let's do it together."

Lily's mom helped her build the tower again and they made it even taller than before. When they finished, Lily's mom said, "You were very polite to let me help you. It's always good to ask for help when we need it." Lily smiled and was happy that her tower was even better than before.

One day, a little boy named Tim was excited to play with his blocks. He had many blocks in different colors: red, blue, yellow, and green. Tim loved to build tall towers with his blocks.

Tim's friend, Lily, came over to play. "Can I play with your blocks too?" she asked. Tim said, "Yes, let's build a big tower together!" They started to build the tower with the colorful blocks, and it got taller and taller.

But then, Tim's dog, Max, ran into the room. He bumped into the tower, and the blocks fell down. Tim and Lily were sad. "Max, quit knocking down our tower!" said Tim. Lily agreed, "Yes, Max, quit it!"

Tim and Lily decided to try again. They picked up the blocks and started to build another tower. This time, they built it even taller than before. They were excited and proud of their new tower.

Max saw the tower too and wanted to play. But he remembered what Tim and Lily said. So, Max quit bumping into the tower and sat down to watch them play. Tim and Lily were happy, and they all had a fun day playing with the blocks.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Rosie who really wanted a lollipop. Every time she saw one in a store, she asked her mom if she could have it. Her mom always said no.

One day, something exciting happened: a modern lollipop machine came to their town! It was so big and shiny and colorful. Rosie had never seen anything like it before.

Rosie begged her mom, but her mom still said no. That's when Rosie realized that she needed to find a way to get money to buy the lollipop.

So she went outside and looked for something she could do to make some money. She saw a few neighbors who needed help with their gardens, so she asked them if she could help them.

The neighbors said yes, and soon Rosie had earned enough money to buy her lollipop! She was so proud of herself!

Then, at last, Rosie was able to buy her very own modern lollipop. She took a big lick and smiled. From then on, she never stopped dreaming of lollipops.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Daisy. She loved to go to the market. One day, Daisy went to the market with her mom. That day, it was pouring rain. Daisy didn't care – she grabbed her umbrella and ran inside the market.

She quickly found her favourite spot in the market, the fruit and vegetable stand. Daisy was about to pick an orange when she heard a voice.

"Daisy! It's too hard to pour in the rain. I need your help to carry the oranges."

It was her mom, asking her to help. Daisy got to work, picking oranges and picking them up one by one into a basket. Her mom smiled proudly.

Together, Daisy and her mom took the oranges home. Daisy was very proud of herself for helping to carry the oranges in the pouring rain!

Once upon a time, there was a little bunny named Benny. Benny was a good bunny who always listened to his mommy. One day, Benny and his mommy went for a walk to the east. Benny saw a big, scary dog and started to panic.

Mommy said, "Don't panic, Benny. Just be obedient and stay close to me." Benny listened to his mommy and stayed close. The big, scary dog didn't come near them because Benny was being obedient.

After they passed the big, scary dog, Benny asked his mommy, "Why did you say 'obedient'?"

Mommy replied, "Being obedient means doing what you're told and staying safe. You were obedient by staying close to me and not running away from the big, scary dog."

Benny felt proud of himself for being obedient and staying safe. From that day on, Benny always remembered to be obedient and listen to his mommy.

Mikey was very worried about his exam. He had been studying all week, but he was still worried he wouldn't do well.

His teacher had been so gentle with him while he practiced. She showed him the answers and gave him a big hug when he was feeling anxious.

His dad took him to the exam hall. He worried less when he sat down at his desk. He knew his dad was in the room so he felt safe.

When the exam started Mikey was a bit scared again. But he tried to remember his teacher's gentle advice and tried his best.

At the end, he felt so relieved to know he had done his best. He hadn't needed to worry so much after all.

George was so happy. He wanted to go outside and skip. He ran to his door, but it was hard. He kept pushing and pushing, but it wouldn't open.

Then he heard a voice. It was his mom.

"George, why don't you skip on the carpet instead?" said Mom.

He ran to his carpet and started skipping. He liked the way it felt under his feet. It was soft, but not too soft. He could skip on it all day long.

George smiled and he skipped and skipped. He even sang a little song as he went.

Finally, he was tired. He curled up on the carpet and fell asleep. He had had such a fun day.

The End.

Tommy did not like vegetables. He liked candy and cake and ice cream. But his mom said he had to eat his vegetables if he wanted dessert. She put a big plate of green beans and carrots in front of him.

"Mom, I don't want this. It looks yucky and dry," Tommy said, making a face.

"You have to eat your vegetables, Tommy. They are good for you. They make you strong and healthy," his mom said, urging him to take a bite.

"But I don't like them. They taste bad. Can I have some juice instead?" Tommy asked, pushing his plate away.

"No, you can't have juice. You can have water or milk. And you can't have dessert until you finish your vegetables. Come on, Tommy, it's not that hard. Just try one bite and see if you like it," his mom said, picking up a fork and a green bean.

She held it near his mouth and smiled. Tommy looked at the green bean and felt scared. He did not want to eat it. He wanted to run away and play with his toys. He shook his head and closed his mouth.

"Please, Tommy, just one bite. For me. I promise you will like it. It's crunchy and sweet. And if you eat it, you can have a cookie later," his mom said, trying to be nice.

Tommy looked at his mom and saw that she was sad. He did not want to make her sad. He loved his mom. He opened his mouth and let her put the green bean in. He chewed it and swallowed it. It was not as bad as he thought. It was a little dry, but it was also crunchy and sweet.

"See, Tommy, that wasn't so bad, was it? Do you want another one?" his mom asked, holding another green bean.

Tommy nodded and took another one. He ate it and smiled. He liked green beans. He ate some more and then some carrots. He finished his plate and felt proud.

"Good job, Tommy! I'm so proud of you. You ate all your vegetables. You are a big boy. Now you can have your dessert. What do you want?" his mom asked, hugging him.

"I want a cookie, please. And some milk. And some more green beans," Tommy said, surprising his mom.

"More green beans? Really? You like them that much?" his mom asked, laughing.

"Yes, mom. I like them. They are good for me. They make me strong and healthy. And they are crunchy and sweet," Tommy said, repeating his mom's words.

"Okay, then. You can have some more green beans. And a cookie. And some milk. You are a very good boy, Tommy. I love you," his mom said, kissing him.

"I love you too, mom. Thank you for the vegetables," Tommy said, happy.

Once upon a time, there was a big, heavy box. Inside the box, there was a yummy waffle. The waffle was very special because it could talk. It was a cold day, and the waffle was feeling very cold. It wanted to find a warm place, so it would not freeze.

The waffle jumped out of the heavy box and started to look for a warm place. It found a big, warm house. The waffle went inside the house and saw a nice, warm fire. The waffle was very happy because it would not freeze now. It sat close to the fire and started to feel warm and cozy.

But then, a big, hungry dog came into the room. The dog saw the waffle and thought it looked very yummy. The waffle was scared and tried to run away, but it was too late. The dog ate the waffle, and the waffle was gone forever. The waffle could not find a warm place to stay, and it had a bad ending.

Once there was a boy. He was walking along a smooth path when he saw a mountain. He wondered what it would be like to climb the mountain. He started to feel excited and wanted to try. He started to climb the mountain slowly. As he went up, he got a little bit scared, but kept going because he was so curious. Little by little, the boy increased his speed and he made it all the way to the top of the mountain. He looked down and felt proud of himself. He was happy that he conquered the mountain.

Lily liked to pick flowers in the garden. She saw many colors and shapes. She smelled the sweet and fresh air. She felt happy and free.

One day, she saw a little light in the grass. It was shiny and sparkly. It moved like a butterfly. Lily was curious and followed it. She wanted to say hello.

The light was a spirit. It was a kind and friendly spirit. It liked to play and make friends. It saw Lily and smiled. It flew closer to her and said, "Hi, I'm Star. You are adorable. Do you want to play with me?"

Lily nodded and smiled back. She said, "Hi, I'm Lily. You are pretty. I want to play with you." She reached out her hand and touched Star. Star felt warm and soft. They giggled and hugged.

They played together in the garden. They picked flowers and made crowns. They chased each other and hid behind trees. They sang songs and told stories. They had fun and became best friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little dog named Spot. Spot had a regular routine every day. He would wake up, eat his breakfast, and then go outside to play. Spot loved to run and chase his ball.

One day, Spot's owner took him to the park. There were lots of other dogs there, and Spot was very excited. His owner threw the ball for him, and Spot ran to get it. But when he came back, there were too many dogs around. Spot didn't know which one was his owner!

Spot started to bark and run around, trying to find his owner. Just then, his owner called out his name. Spot saw her and ran over to her. His owner gave him a big hug and told him he was a good boy. Spot was so happy to be back with his owner, and he knew the number one thing was to never leave her side.

Sam and Mia are friends. They like to play with their toys in the park. One day, they find a big box. They open the box and see many shiny things inside. They see a cell, a watch, a necklace, and a ring.

"Wow, look at these!" Sam says. He picks up the cell and presses some buttons. "This is fun!"

"I want the cell too!" Mia says. She tries to grab the cell from Sam. "Give it to me!"

"No, it's mine!" Sam says. He holds the cell tight. "You can have the watch!"

"I don't want the watch, I want the cell!" Mia says. She pulls the cell hard. "Let go!"

They both pull the cell and fight. The cell breaks in half. They hear a loud beep. They see a red light on the cell.

"Oh no, what did we do?" Sam says. He drops the cell. "Is it broken?"

"I don't know, maybe it's a bomb!" Mia says. She runs away. "Help, help!"

A man comes to the park. He sees the box and the cell. He is angry. He is a spy. The cell is his. It is a dependable cell. He needs the cell to talk to his boss. He sees Sam and Mia.

"Hey, you kids, what did you do to my cell?" he says. He runs after them. "Give it back to me!"

Sam and Mia are scared. They run to their moms. They tell them what happened. Their moms hug them and take them home. They say they are sorry. They learn not to touch things that are not theirs. They hope the spy will not find them. They hope the cell will not explode.

One day, there was a bear living in the woods. He had not seen his friends in a very long time, so he decided to go on a walk. When he arrived at the edge of the woods, he saw something very unusual - an enormous cherry tree! As the bear was about to reach out for the biggest cherry of them all, a rabbit hopped out from underneath the tree and warned him.

"Don't eat that cherry!", the rabbit said. "It's enormous, so it must be very old. You don't want to get sick."

But the bear didn't listen. He was so excited to find the cherry tree, he couldn't resist tasting the enormous fruit. Much to his surprise, it didn't make him sick at all - it was the sweetest and juiciest cherry he had ever tasted!

From that day on, the bear always invited his friends to share the enormous cherry with him whenever they came to visit. He was able to warn his friends about the cherry and make sure that none of them ever got sick.

Once upon a time, there was a little bird named Tweety. Tweety wanted to fly high in the sky but was too scared. Tweety's friend, a wise old owl, noticed Tweety's fear and said, "Don't be fearful, Tweety. Just try to fly a little bit every day, and soon you'll be soaring through the clouds."

Tweety listened to the owl's advice and tried to fly a little bit each day. At first, Tweety could only fly a short distance before landing on the ground. But with each try, Tweety got better and better.

One day, Tweety decided to try to fly higher than ever before. Tweety flapped their wings with all their might and suddenly, they were flying high in the sky! Tweety felt so proud and happy.

As Tweety was flying, they saw a butterfly struggling to fly. Tweety said, "Don't worry, little butterfly. Just try to fly and soon you'll be flying like a pro!" The butterfly listened to Tweety's advice and soon, it was flying gracefully through the air. From that day on, Tweety and the butterfly were the best of friends, flying high together in the sky.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved to wear necklaces. One day, she saw a beautiful necklace in a store. It was very shiny and had many pretty colors. Lily wanted it very much.

When she asked her mommy to buy it for her, her mommy said, "No, it's too expensive. We can find a cheap necklace that's just as pretty."

Lily didn't want a cheap necklace. She wanted the shiny one she saw in the store. She started to frown and cry. But then her mommy explained that it's important to be grateful for what we have and not always want more. Lily understood and decided to be happy with the necklaces she already had. From that day on, she never asked for expensive things again.

Once upon a time, there was a little fish named Nemo. Nemo loved to swim in the big blue sea with his friends. One day, Nemo saw a shiny hook and thought it looked like fun to play with. But when he tried to bite it, he got caught!

Nemo was scared and didn't know what to do. Luckily, a kind dolphin saw what happened and swam over to help. The dolphin used her nose to push the hook out of Nemo's mouth. Nemo was so grateful and thanked the dolphin for being so kind.

But Nemo was still scared and didn't want to swim anymore. The dolphin knew how Nemo felt and told him that he needed to forgive himself for making a mistake. Nemo didn't understand what "forgive" meant, but the dolphin explained that it meant to be kind to yourself and not be mad anymore. Nemo thought about it and decided to forgive himself. He felt much better and swam happily with his friends again. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Steve. He was three years old and was very excited for the day.

Steve was going to the park to play a game. He wanted to win, so he tried his very best. When it was his turn, he ran as fast as he could.

At the park, there was a tall tower. It was very high! Even though Steve was scared, he still wanted to win.

He tried and he tried, but he was very slow. He started to feel embarrassed.

But then, just when he thought he wouldn’t win, he made it to the top of the tower! Everyone cheered, and Steve was so happy to have won!

Once upon a time, there was a princess who lived in a big castle. She had a pretty dress and a shiny crown. One day, a monster came to the castle with a big weapon. The princess was scared, but she knew she had to be brave. She grabbed a stick and tried to fight the monster. Suddenly, the sun started to rise and the light shone on the monster's face. The monster got scared and ran away. The princess was happy and felt proud of herself for being brave.

Once upon a time, there was a small crab who found a shiny shell on the beach. The crab thought it was real and was very happy to find it. He tried to pick it up but it wouldn’t move. He realized it was fake.

The crab wasn’t sure what to do. Then he heard a voice, saying “You don’t need fake things, you need the real things in life.” It was the voice of the ocean.

The crab followed the voice and found a real shell, but it was empty. He took the shell and sat in it, pushing it around the shore. As he was pushing it, he saw other crabs and thought about how nice it would be if he had friends to push his shell with.

So he asked the ocean, “How can I make friends?” The ocean said, “Do something kind. Offer a seat in your shell and always be kind.”

The crab offered a seat in his shell to the other crabs and soon he made lots of friends.

The moral of the story is that real things can bring lasting happiness, and to make friends, offer a seat and be kind.

Once upon a time, there was a pretty princess who loved to play with her dolls. One day, she saw her mommy ironing clothes. "Mommy, what are you doing?" she asked. "I am ironing clothes to make them pretty and smooth," her mommy replied.

The princess wanted to help her mommy, so she asked, "Can I help you iron?" But her mommy said, "No, it's not safe for you to use the iron." The princess felt sad, so she went to her room and sat on her bed.

Suddenly, she heard a knock on her door. It was her daddy. "Why are you sad, my princess?" he asked. "Mommy won't let me help her iron," she replied. "Well, how about you help me sack some potatoes instead?" her daddy suggested. The princess smiled and said, "Okay, let's do it!" And they went to the kitchen to sack some potatoes together.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, Lily lost her favorite teddy bear. She looked everywhere but couldn't find it. She asked her mom and dad to help her search for it.

Lily's mom said, "Let's search in the living room." Lily's dad said, "Let's search in the bedroom." But they still couldn't find it. Lily started to cry and shout, "Where is my teddy bear?"

Just then, Lily's little brother came into the room with the teddy bear in his hands. Lily was so happy to see her teddy bear, but also a little embarrassed that she couldn't find it herself. Her mom and dad told her it's okay to ask for help and that they were happy to help her search. From that day on, Lily made sure to keep her teddy bear close so she wouldn't lose it again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play in the forest and look for mushrooms. One day, she met a sad rabbit named Benny.

"Why are you so gloomy?" asked Lily.

"I lost my favorite carrot," replied Benny.

Lily wanted to help Benny, so she searched for the carrot with him. After a while, they found the carrot under a big mushroom.

"I found your carrot!" exclaimed Lily.

Benny was so happy and grateful. He realized that sometimes, when things seem gloomy, there is always hope and someone who can reveal a solution. From that day on, Benny and Lily became the best of friends and always looked out for each other.

Jimmy was a very intelligent 3-year-old. He knew lots of things and was always finding new ways to have fun.

One day, Jimmy was walking through the park with his parents. He saw a big bird flying up in the sky, and he thought it was so cool. He wanted to follow it, so he started running.

But then, he heard a loud voice shouting at him! He stopped and looked around, his heart beating quickly. It was a park ranger.

"What are you doing?" the ranger asked. "You must stay on the path!"

Jimmy was scared, but he tried to be brave. "I was just trying to find the bird," he said.

The ranger smiled. "It's nice to be curious and adventurous," he said. But then he added, "But you must be careful - there are dangers in the park. Always stay on the path and don't forget to carry a threat in case you get lost."

Jimmy nodded. He thanked the ranger and promised to be careful. Then he and his parents continued walking through the park, with Jimmy remembering the advice he was given. He felt happy knowing that he was intelligent enough to understand things like this.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Emily. Emily was a very independent girl and she loved to go outside and do things by herself. One day she was feeling happy and decided to go skipping. She skipped through the long grass and sang a song. Soon she came to a big garden full of different plants and flowers.

But what caught Emily's eye was the strange little trees growing in the garden. She couldn't believe her eyes! They were broccoli trees! She skipped over to the trees and looked closely at the broccoli. It was so delicious and juicy.

Emily started picking the broccoli and putting it in the basket she was carrying. Then she skipped off happily to deliver the broccoli to her family. From that day on, Emily was so proud of herself for being so independent and she never forgot her broccoli picking adventures.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Emma. She was three years old. One day, Emma decided to go on an adventure. She went exploring in the garden.

Emma was running around and she soon realized that her dress had a hole in it. She was so sad. She wanted to fix the hole, so she went and found a patch.

Emma slowly and gently put the patch over the hole. She took time to stick it down, making sure it was nice and tidy.

Emma smiled when she saw the patch. She was so proud of herself. She had realized that she could fix her dress, and now it was good as new!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a favorite toy that she loved to play with every day. One day, her toy broke and she was very sad.

Lily's mom said, "Don't worry, we can go to the store and buy a new one."

Lily asked, "Is it expensive?"

Mom said, "Yes, but we can manage. We'll just have to save up for a minute."

Lily was happy to hear that they could get a new toy soon. She hugged her mom and said, "Thank you for helping me."

Lily and Max love to play with cars. They have many cars of different colors and sizes. They like to make them go fast on the floor or on the ramp. They say "vroom, vroom" and "beep, beep" as they race their cars.

One day, they decide to play with their cars outside. They find a big hill with a smooth path. They think it is perfect for their cars. They put their cars on the top of the hill and let them go. The cars zoom down the hill with great speed. Lily and Max cheer and clap as they watch their cars.

"Wow, look at my red car!" Lily says. "It is the fastest of all!"

"No, my blue car is faster!" Max says. "It will beat your car!"

They decide to have a race. They put their cars on the hill again and count to three. Then they let them go. The cars roll down the hill, side by side. They are very close. Lily and Max run after them, shouting and laughing.

But then, they see something on the path. It is a big dog. The dog is busy sniffing a flower. He does not see the cars coming. Lily and Max stop and gasp. They are afraid that their cars will hit the dog.

"Look out, dog!" Lily yells.

"Move, move, move!" Max yells.

The dog hears them and looks up. He sees the cars and jumps out of the way. The cars pass by him and reach the end of the path. They stop and spin around. Lily and Max catch up with them and pick them up. They are relieved that their cars and the dog are okay.

"Good dog!" Lily says. "You are very smart!"

"Sorry, dog!" Max says. "We did not mean to scare you!"

The dog wags his tail and licks their faces. He is not angry. He is friendly. Lily and Max pet him and smile. They are happy that they made a new friend. They decide to share their cars with the dog. They take turns rolling them on the hill and letting the dog chase them. They have fun together. They love their cars, their speed, and their dog.

Once upon a time, there was a chubby little mouse. His name was Bill. He loved to explore and everyday he would go out to search for new things. One day, he came across a strange case. It was so shiny and pretty. Bill wanted to open it and see what was inside.

He asked kindly for someone to open it for him, but no one was around. So Bill decided to open it himself. He pushed and pulled, but the case wouldn't budge. He demanded it to open and finally it opened.

He was so excited! Inside the case he found some cheese and he ate it all up. Now he could go and explore some more. From then on, wherever he went, he always took the chubby little case with him.

Jimmy woke up in the morning. He was so excited because he wanted to see the friendly zebra. He had seen pictures of zebras and heard stories about them. He couldn't wait to meet one.

He asked his parents if he could go for a walk outside, and they said yes. So he put on his hat and coat, and he ran all the way to the farm. When he got there, he saw the big gate.

Jimmy peeked through the gate and he saw the friendly zebra. He waved to the zebra and said, "Hi there!" The zebra didn't say anything, but it waved too.

Jimmy was so happy. He couldn't believe he was finally meeting a friendly zebra. He thanked his parents and said, "Can I come back later?" And they said yes.

Jimmy waved goodbye to the zebra and ran back home with a huge smile on his face. He had the best morning at the farm!

Once upon a time, there was a boy. His name was Bob and he was three years old. One day, Bob wanted to drive. His parents said he was too young to drive, but Bob said he wanted to try it. So his dad got him some toy wheels and put them on Bob's feet.

As Dad held onto him, Bob started to drive around the house. It was so fun. He was driving faster and faster. He laughed and he was so excited.

Suddenly, Bob heard a whistle. He looked up and saw a bright sun in the sky. he kept driving and the sun shone brighter and brighter. It was so beautiful and it made him smile. He kept driving around and the sun kept shining, following him wherever he went.

Bob stopped and looked up at the sun. Then he said to his dad, "Thank you for helping me drive, Daddy! This is the best day ever!"

Once upon a time, in a hot, sandy land, there was a pretty oasis. The oasis had cool water, green grass, and tall trees. Many animals liked to play there. It was a happy place.

One day, a little boy named Tim came to the oasis. Tim saw a toy bow and arrow on the ground. He picked it up and started to shoot the arrows at the trees. The animals watched and thought it was fun. They clapped and cheered for Tim.

Tim played fair with the animals. He shared his toy bow and arrow, and they all took turns shooting at the trees. They had a great day at the oasis, playing together and being friends.

Tom and Lily liked to play with their toys in the garden. They had a big box of toys, with cars, dolls, animals, and a boat. One day, they found a new toy in the box. It was a small fisherman, with a hat, a coat, and a fishing rod. He looked very serious.

"Let's play with him!" said Lily. "He can catch fish in the pond!"

"OK!" said Tom. "But be careful. He is very small. We don't want to lose him."

They took the fisherman and the boat to the pond. They put him in the boat and pushed it into the water. The fisherman held his fishing rod and waited for a fish.

"Look, he is fishing!" said Lily. "He is so cute!"

But then, something strange happened. The fisherman started to shrink. He became smaller and smaller, until he was as tiny as a bug. The boat was too big for him. He fell into the water and disappeared.

"Where did he go?" said Tom. "He shrank!"

"Oh no!" said Lily. "He is gone! Maybe a fish ate him!"

They ran to the pond and looked for the fisherman. But they could not see him. He was too small.

They were very sad. They had lost their new toy.

They did not know that the fisherman was a magic toy. He had a secret. He could shrink and grow. He did not like to be played with. He wanted to be free. He shrank on purpose, to escape from the children. He swam to the other side of the pond, where he found a small hole. He crawled into the hole and grew back to his normal size. He was happy. He had found a new home. He decided to stay there and fish in peace. He never saw Tom and Lily again.

Once there was a little boy named Tony. He was a very special boy because he had a magic trophy. Whenever Tony felt happy, the trophy would grow bigger and bigger. Tony was very proud of his trophy, and he showed it off to everyone.

One day, the weather was very warm. Tony wanted to play outside and enjoy the sunshine. When he was playing, Tony forgot about his trophy. When he went back to his room, the trophy had shrunk!

Tony was sad because he wanted his trophy to be big again. Then he had an idea. He ran outside and played under the warm sun. In a few minutes, the trophy was back to its normal size. Tony was very happy and gave the trophy a big hug.

The little boy was now very careful with his trophy. He kept it close to him and enjoyed the warm weather. His trophy was always growing and shrinking, and it reminded Tony to have fun and enjoy life.

Tom and Lily were best friends. They liked to play in the park every day. They had a lot of fun on the swings, the slide and the seesaw. But one day, they saw something new in the park. It was a big, red, shiny bike. It had two wheels, a bell and a basket. It looked very fun.

"Wow, look at that bike!" Tom said. "I want to ride it!"

"Me too!" Lily said. "But who does it belong to?"

They looked around, but they did not see anyone. The bike was just standing by a tree. Tom and Lily decided to go closer and have a look.

"Maybe we can take turns," Tom said. "You can go first, and then I can go."

"OK," Lily said. She was very excited. She ran to the bike and tried to get on. But it was too big for her. She could not reach the pedals or the handlebars. She felt sad.

"It's too hard," she said. "I can't ride it."

Tom saw her struggle. He felt sorry for her, but he also wanted to try the bike. He thought he could do better. He walked to the bike and pushed Lily aside.

"Let me try," he said. "I can ride it. I'm bigger than you."

He got on the bike and tried to pedal. But he also found it hard. The bike was too heavy for him. He could not balance or steer. He felt scared.

"It's too hard," he said. "I can't ride it."

Just then, they heard a loud voice.

"Hey, what are you doing with my bike?" It was a big boy, who looked angry. He had been playing soccer with his friends, and he had left his bike by the tree. He saw Tom and Lily on his bike, and he did not like it.

He ran to them and grabbed his bike. He pushed Tom off and shouted at him.

"Get off my bike, you little thief! That's mine!"

Tom fell to the ground and hurt his knee. He started to cry. Lily ran to him and hugged him.

"I'm sorry, Tom," she said. "Are you OK?"

Tom nodded, but he felt bad. He wished they had not touched the bike. He wished they had played with their own toys.

The big boy rode away on his bike, ringing his bell. He did not care about Tom and Lily. He did not say sorry.

Tom and Lily learned a lesson. They decided to never touch things that did not belong to them. They decided to be happy with what they had. They decided to stay best friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy had a big question in his head. He wanted to know why the sky was blue. He asked his mommy, but she didn't know the answer. So, they went to the grocery store to ask the man who worked there.

The man was very gifted and knew a lot about the sky. He explained to Timmy that the sky looks blue because of the way the sun's light shines on the Earth. Timmy was very happy to learn something new.

As a thank you, Timmy's mommy bought the man a gift. It was a big bag of candy. The man was very happy and thanked them for the sweet gift. Timmy felt proud that he had asked a good question and learned something new.

Once upon a time, there was a boy who had a bicycle. He loved to ride it all around his town. One day, he left his bicycle outside and it got hidden behind some bushes. He looked and looked but he couldn't find it.

The boy was sad because he missed his bicycle. His mom told him to keep looking and not give up. So, he went back outside and kept looking. Suddenly, he saw his bicycle! It was chewed up by a dog, but he was so happy to have found it.

The boy took his bicycle to his dad, who fixed it up good as new. From that day on, the boy made sure to always keep his bicycle safe and not hidden.

Mum was walking with her daughter in the park. The little girl wanted a ride on the swing, but Mum said no. "You must wear your helmet!" She insisted.

The little girl started to cry. "No helmet," she said with a big frown on her face. Mum knew she was hungry, so to make her happy, she bought her some ice cream.

When they got to the swings, the little girl was feeling much better. She asked if she could go on the swing. She had forgotten about the helmet. Mum said "Yes, but only if you wear your helmet".

Again, the little girl started to cry. She refused to listen and said "No helmet. I don't want it."

Mum left the park with the little girl in her arms. She had to insist that she wears the helmet for the next time, or else there will be no swing rides.

It was a bad ending for the day, and a lesson for the little girl to remember.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved animals and wanted to go on a safari. One day, she asked her mommy if she could go on a safari. Her mommy said, "Yes, I permit you to go on a safari with me."

Lily was so excited! They went on a big adventure and saw lots of animals like lions, zebras, and giraffes. They even saw a monkey swinging from tree to tree! Lily felt dizzy from all the excitement.

After their safari, they sat down to rest. Lily said to her mommy, "That was the best adventure ever! Thank you for permitting me to go with you." Her mommy smiled and said, "I'm glad you had fun, my little safari explorer."

One day, a curious dog named Spot went for a walk. He saw a big tree and thought it would be fun to play near it. As he got closer, he heard a strange sound coming from the tree.

Suddenly, a bird appeared from the tree and said, "Hello, dog! My name is Chirpy. Do you want to play with me?" Spot wagged his tail and barked, "Yes, I want to play!"

They played together all day long, running around the tree and chasing each other. Spot and Chirpy became best friends. At the end of the day, they were both very tired but very happy. They promised to meet again near the big tree and play together every day.

Once upon a time, there was a fish who loved to swim. He swam each day in the cool, blue water. One day, he swam to the bottom of the sea and found a jar of jam. It was weird jam- it was green, pink and yellow. The fish was so excited! He loved jam.

He opened the jar and tried some. But the jam didn't taste normal. He swam away, feeling a little bit sad. He wanted to eat the jam, but it was weird.

Suddenly, a big green eel appeared. He said that the jam was special. He told the fish to follow him, and the fish did. The eel took the fish to a party of sea creatures.

The creatures ate the jam and told the fish it was magic. When they ate it, they could swim faster and stronger. The fish was so happy! He brought the magic jam with him whenever he went swimming, so he could swim as fast as the wind.

He never got bored of swimming, because the magic jam made it even more fun. And the fish and the eel became good friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play in the rain. One day, it started to rain really hard, and Lily's mom told her to come inside. But Lily didn't want to stop playing.

"I don't want to come inside, Mommy. I want to play in the rain!" Lily said.

"But you'll get all wet and catch a cold," Mommy replied.

Lily thought for a moment and then said, "I know! I'll cover myself with my black umbrella so I don't get wet!"

Mommy smiled and said, "That's a great idea, Lily. But be careful not to slip on the drain."

Lily nodded and ran outside with her umbrella. She covered herself and danced in the rain, making sure to avoid the drain. When she came back inside, she was a little wet, but she had so much fun playing in the rain with her black umbrella.

Once upon a time, there was a bald man. He went to an old, abandoned building and saw a brick on the ground. He wanted to surprise himself, so he picked up the brick and threw it through a window.

The man heard a loud crash and soon he was surrounded by policemen. They shouted, "Sir, what have you done?".

The man was embarrassed and he said, "I was just trying to surprise myself!". But the policemen did not believe him and they arrested him and took him away. The man was never able to surprise himself with the brick again.

Tom and Lily like to play with balloons. They have many balloons of different colors. They blow air into the balloons and tie them with strings. Then they attach the balloons to their chairs, their toys, and their hats. They pretend they can fly with the balloons.

One day, they find a big blue balloon in the closet. It is very shiny and round. They want to play with it, but they cannot blow air into it. It has a metal thing on the bottom. Tom says it is a gas balloon. He says gas is like air, but lighter. He says the gas balloon can fly higher than the other balloons.

Tom and Lily are curious. They want to see how high the gas balloon can fly. They untie the metal thing and attach the balloon to a long string. They go outside and let go of the string. The gas balloon goes up, up, up in the sky. It is so high that it looks like a small dot. Tom and Lily are happy. They clap and cheer.

But then, a strong wind comes. It blows the gas balloon away. Tom and Lily are sad. They cannot see the gas balloon anymore. They run after it, but it is too fast. They lose the string. They cry and hug each other.

Mom and Dad see them crying. They ask them what is wrong. Tom and Lily tell them about the gas balloon. Mom and Dad hug them and say they are sorry. They say they will buy them a new balloon. They say they love them. Tom and Lily feel better. They say they love Mom and Dad too. They go inside and play with their other balloons. They are still curious, but they are also careful. They do not attach the balloons to anything that can fly away.

Once upon a time, there was a little birdie. The birdie was very busy building a nest in a tree. It flew east to find some twigs and leaves to make the nest strong.

One day, a wise owl came to visit the birdie. The owl wanted to teach the birdie how to fly higher and faster. The birdie was excited to learn and listened carefully to the owl's lesson.

After the lesson, the birdie flew east to show off its new flying skills to its birdie friends. They were amazed and happy for the birdie. From then on, the birdie was known as the best flyer in the east.

Anna and Ben are friends. They like to play at the park. One day, they see a big slide. It is colorful and shiny. Anna and Ben want to try it.

"Can I go first?" Anna asks.

"OK, you can go first," Ben says. He is nice.

Anna climbs up the stairs. She sits on the seat. She slides down fast. She laughs and says, "Whee!"

Ben claps his hands. He climbs up the stairs. He sits on the seat. He slides down fast. He laughs and says, "Whee!"

Anna and Ben slide again and again. They have fun.

Then, they see a girl. She is sad. She has no friends. She wants to slide, but she is shy.

Anna and Ben see her. They want to help her.

"Hi, what is your name?" Anna asks.

"I am Lily," the girl says.

"Do you want to slide with us?" Ben offers.

"Really? Can I?" Lily asks.

"Of course, you can. Come on, we will show you," Anna says.

Anna and Ben take Lily's hand. They climb up the stairs. They sit on the seat. They slide down fast. They laugh and say, "Whee!"

Lily smiles. She is happy. She has new friends.

Anna, Ben, and Lily slide again and again. They have fun. They like the colorful slide. They like each other.

Tom and Lily are friends. They like to play in the park. They see a bench near the slide. They run to the bench and sit down.

"Let's joke with each other," Tom says. "I will say something funny and you will laugh."

"OK," Lily says. "You go first."

Tom thinks for a moment. Then he says, "Why did the chicken cross the road?"

Lily waits for the answer. She knows this joke.

"To get to the other side," Tom says.

Lily laughs. She thinks Tom is funny.

"Your turn," Tom says.

Lily thinks for a moment. Then she says, "What do you call a fish that wears a bow?"

Tom waits for the answer. He does not know this joke.

"A rainbow fish," Lily says.

Tom laughs. He thinks Lily is funny.

They joke with each other for a while. They have fun.

Then they see a lady with a big bag. The lady looks tired. She walks to the bench and puts the bag down.

"Hello," the lady says. "Can you be helpful and watch my bag for a minute? I need to go to the bathroom."

"Sure," Tom and Lily say. They are kind.

The lady smiles and says, "Thank you. I will be back soon."

She leaves the bag on the bench and walks away.

Tom and Lily look at the bag. They wonder what is inside.

"Maybe it is a surprise," Tom says.

"Maybe it is a toy," Lily says.

They are curious.

They decide to open the bag and see. They unzip the bag and peek inside.

They see a lot of books. They are disappointed.

"Books are boring," Tom says.

"Books are not fun," Lily says.

They close the bag and sit back on the bench.

They wait for the lady to come back.

They do not joke anymore.

Lily and Ben were playing in the park with their dog, Spot. They liked to run, slide, and swing. Spot liked to chase, bark, and chew. He chewed on sticks, balls, and shoes. Sometimes he chewed too much and made Lily and Ben mad.

One day, the sky became dark and loud. Lily and Ben heard a big boom. It was thunder. They were scared. Spot was scared too. He ran to Lily and Ben and hid under their legs. He whimpered and shook.

"It's okay, Spot. We are here," Lily said. She hugged Spot and rubbed his ears. Ben did the same. They were compassionate. They knew how Spot felt.

"Let's go home," Ben said. "Mom will make us hot cocoa and read us a story."

They got up and walked to their house. Spot followed them. He did not chew anything on the way. He was happy to be with Lily and Ben. They were his best friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She lived in a house with her family. One day, Lily's mom told her not to hang on the door because it was very old and could break.
