But Lily was a curious girl, and she wanted to see what was behind the door. So, when her mom wasn't looking, she hung on the door to see if it would open. Suddenly, the door broke and fell on top of her.

Lily was very miserable and cried a lot. Her mom came running to see what had happened and saw that Lily was hurt. From that day on, Lily learned to listen to her mom and never hung on the door again.

Lily and Tom were playing in their room. They had a big carpet with many colors and shapes. They liked to pretend it was a map of a faraway land. They made up stories about the animals and people who lived there.

One day, they heard a knock on the door. It was their nosy neighbor, Ben. He always wanted to see what they were doing. He pushed the door open and walked in.

"Hi, Lily and Tom. What are you playing?" he asked.

"We are playing map," Lily said. "This is our carpet. It is very special. It can take us to different places."

"Really? Can I play too?" Ben said.

"OK, but you have to follow the rules," Tom said. "You can only go where the carpet fits. If the carpet does not fit, you cannot go there. It is too dangerous."

Ben nodded. He looked at the carpet. He saw a small corner that was not covered by anything. He thought it looked like a fun place to go.

"I want to go there," he said. He pointed at the corner.

"No, Ben. You cannot go there," Lily said. "The carpet does not fit there. It is too small. There is nothing there."

"But I want to see what is there," Ben said. He did not listen to Lily. He ran to the corner and tried to fit the carpet under the bed. He pushed and pulled, but the carpet was too big. He made a big mess. He knocked over a lamp and a toy box. He tore the carpet.

Lily and Tom were very angry. They shouted at Ben.

"Ben, you are very bad. You broke our carpet. You ruined our game. You are not our friend. Go away!"

Ben felt sorry. He did not mean to break the carpet. He just wanted to play. He said sorry to Lily and Tom. He helped them clean up the mess. He gave them a hug.

"Can we still be friends?" he asked.

Lily and Tom looked at each other. They saw that Ben was sad. They forgave him.

"OK, Ben. We can still be friends. But next time, you have to listen to us. And you have to be careful with our things."

Ben nodded. He learned his lesson. He was not nosy anymore. He played nicely with Lily and Tom. They had fun on the carpet. They went to many places. They were happy.

The girl was standing outside. She waved at everyone who walked by. They all waved back with a twinkle in their eyes and a wink.

The girl watched the people go by. She was nosy and wanted to know what they were doing.

Suddenly, she saw a dog. The dog had a big, fluffy tail that waved at the girl. She waved back, excited to see her new friend. The dog barked and then ran away.

The girl was sad, but she kept waving at everyone. Some of them even waved back.

Then she saw an airplane flying high in the sky. It had a trail of smoke behind it. She waved at it and it seemed to wave back!

The girl was so happy and couldn't stop smiling. She kept waving until everyone was gone.

One day, a wide tornado came to a small town. It was very big and scary. The people in the town were afraid. They did not know what to do.

A brave girl named Lily said, "We need to complete our safe place before the tornado comes." The people listened to Lily and they all worked together. They built a strong and safe place for everyone to hide.

When the tornado came, all the people were safe inside. The tornado went away and the town was okay. The people said, "Thank you, Lily, for helping us complete our safe place!" And they all lived happily and safely.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Mary who had lost her green dress. She looked everywhere, but she couldn't find it.

Mary was sad. She started to cry.

Her Mama saw her and asked, "What's wrong, my sweet?"

"I lost my green dress," Mary said, tears streaming down her face.

Mama hugged her and said, "It's ok, we will find it. Don't be so bitter."

So together, Mama and Mary went in search of the dress. They looked through the cupboard, under the bed and behind the door.

Suddenly, Mary cried, "I found it!"

She grabbed the dress from under the sofa and showed it to her Mama.

Mama said with a smile, "Well done, Mary! The dress is a bit wrinkled, but it is still green!"

Mary felt happy again. She hugged her Mama and said, "Thank you, Mama, for helping me find my green dress!"

Mama smiled and hugged her daughter, feeling relieved that Mary was no longer so bitter. And they all lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his toy cars and watch cartoons on the TV. One day, Timmy's mom took him to the store to buy some groceries. While they were there, Timmy saw a shiny wallet on the shelf. He asked his mom if he could have it, but she said it wasn't available for him to buy.

Later that day, Timmy's mom was cooking dinner in the kitchen. Timmy was playing with his toy cars on the floor. Suddenly, he saw a pair of scissors on the counter. Timmy remembered how he wanted the shiny wallet from the store. He thought if he cut some money from his mom's wallet, he could buy the shiny one. So, he took the scissors and cut the wallet open.

When Timmy's mom found out what he did, she was very upset. She explained to Timmy that cutting someone's wallet is not okay and that he should never do it again. Timmy felt bad for what he did and promised to never cut anything without permission. From that day on, Timmy learned that it's important to ask before taking something that isn't available to him.

Tom and Mia are playing in the park. They see a big, furry dog. The dog is friendly and wags its tail. Tom and Mia want to pet the dog, but they are afraid.

"Who is the dog's owner?" Tom asks.

"I don't know. Maybe he is lost," Mia says.

They look around, but they do not see anyone who looks like the dog's owner. The dog comes closer and sniffs them. He licks Tom's hand and Mia's cheek. They giggle and stroke his fur.

"Maybe we can keep him," Tom says.

"No, we can't. He belongs to someone. We have to find his owner," Mia says.

They see a tag on the dog's collar. It has a name and a phone number. The name is Max.

"Let's call the number and tell them we found Max," Mia says.

They run to the nearest phone booth. They dial the number and wait. A voice answers.

"Hello?"

"Hello, we found your dog. His name is Max. He is a big, furry dog. He is very nice. We are in the park. Can you come and get him?" Mia says.

"Thank you so much! I have been looking for him all day. He ran away when I opened the door. I am so glad he is safe. I will be there in ten minutes. Where are you in the park?" the voice says.

"We are near the big slide. We will wait for you here. Bye," Mia says.

They hang up and go back to Max. They play with him until they see a car pull up. A man gets out and runs to them. He hugs Max and thanks Tom and Mia.

"You are very kind and brave. You saved my dog. How can I thank you?" he says.

Tom and Mia smile. They are happy they helped Max and his owner.

"Can we pet him one more time?" Tom asks.

"Of course. He likes you very much. You are his new friends," the man says.

He lets them pet Max and gives them a big chocolate bar each.

"Thank you for the chocolate. And thank you for letting us play with Max. He is a great dog," Mia says.

"You are very welcome. Maybe we can meet again in the park. Max would love that. Bye for now," the man says.

He puts Max in the car and waves goodbye. Tom and Mia wave back and share their chocolate. They are proud of what they did. They sent Max back to his owner. They made a new furry friend.

Sam and Mia are friends. They like to play outside. But today, it is raining. The sky is gray and the water falls on the ground.

"Let's go inside," Sam says. "We can play with our toys."

"No, I want to stay outside," Mia says. "I like the rain. It is fun."

Sam shakes his head. "The rain is not fun. It is wet and cold. And we have to follow the law."

"What is the law?" Mia asks.

"The law is what Mom and Dad say. They say we have to wear our coats and boots when it rains. And we have to stay away from the high places."

"Why?" Mia wonders.

"Because the high places are dangerous. They can be slippery and we can fall. And we can get sick if we get too wet. The law is to keep us safe and happy."

Mia thinks for a moment. She does not want to fall or get sick. She wants to be safe and happy. She looks at Sam and smiles.

"Okay, let's go inside," she says. "But can we play with the rain later?"

Sam nods. "Yes, we can play with the rain later. When it stops raining, we can make puddles and splash. That is fun too."

They hold hands and run inside. They take off their coats and boots and play with their toys. They are good friends. They follow the law. And they wait for the rain to stop.

Sara and Ben like to play in the park. They like to swing, slide and run. One day, they see a new lady in the park. She has a big hat, a long dress and a black cat. She looks at Sara and Ben with her eyes. She stares at them.

Sara and Ben feel scared. They think the lady is a witch. They run to their mom and dad. They tell them about the witch. Mom and dad smile. They say the lady is not a witch. She is just a nice lady who likes hats and cats.

Sara and Ben are not sure. They go back to the park with mom and dad. They see the lady again. She smiles at them. She says hello. She gives them some cookies. They are mild and sweet. Sara and Ben like the cookies. They say thank you.

The lady tells them her name is Lily. She says she is new in town. She says she likes to make hats and play with her cat. She says she is not a witch. She is just a lady who likes to stare at the sky and the birds.

Sara and Ben feel silly. They think Lily is nice. They say sorry for thinking she is a witch. They ask her if they can play with her cat. She says yes. They pet the cat. The cat purrs. Sara and Ben are happy. They make a new friend.

Once upon a time, there was a cute bunny named Benny. Benny liked to jump and play with his friends. One day, Benny went to his classroom and saw that someone had taken his favorite carrot pencil. Benny was sad and didn't know what to do.

Benny asked his friends if they had seen his pencil, but nobody knew where it was. Benny felt frustrated and didn't want to do his work without his special pencil. Suddenly, Benny saw a little mouse with his pencil in the corner of the classroom. Benny didn't want to be mean, but he needed his pencil back.

Benny decided to jump over to the mouse and kindly ask for his pencil back. The mouse was surprised but gave the pencil back to Benny. Benny was happy again and could finish his work. Benny learned that it's always better to ask nicely instead of being mean.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Sally. She loved to play outside, even when it was dark. One night, Sally went outside to play with her flashlight. She was happy to have her flashlight because it made her feel safe.

As she was playing, she saw her friend Billy walking towards her. Sally was glad to see Billy. However, Billy didn't have a flashlight and he was scared of the dark. Sally offered to share her flashlight with Billy, and they played together until it was time to go inside.

The moral of the story is that it's always good to share with others, especially when they need help. Sally was happy to share her flashlight with Billy and it made their playtime even more fun.

Mia was a 3 year old who loved to learn and always behaved very well. One day, she asked her mom if she could use the computer. Her mom said she could, as long as she promised to behave. Mia promised that she would, so her mom let her sit in front of the computer. She thought it was so cool that it could do so many things!

But then, something terrible happened... the computer started to make strange noises and wouldn't work anymore. Mia had no idea what to do, so she asked her mom for help. Her mom was very angry and said, "You promised to behave! I told you not to break the computer!"

Mia was sad and didn't mean to break the computer. She promised to be very careful in the future and offered to help fix the computer. She was happy when her mom showed her how to do it, and soon the computer was working again.

Mia had learned her lesson: no matter how much fun it is to use the computer, she must always remember to behave and be careful.

Once upon a time there lived a brilliant tiger. It ate lots of fruit and vegetables and was very strong.

One day, the tiger decided to go for a swim. It was having so much fun. But then it noticed a cut in the water. It was a scary cut and it made the tiger worried.

The tiger wanted to fix the cut to make the waters safe again. So it started to work. The tiger worked hard and valued the work it was doing.

But even after all the hard work the cut was still there. The tiger had only made it bigger and deeper!

The tiger was very sad. It had worked so hard, but the cut was still there. The bad ending had happened after all.

Once upon a time, there was a mysterious girl who lived in a forest. Every day she would go for long walks and discover amazing things.

One day when she was out walking, she saw something sparkly and colourful. It was a spirit! It was dancing and singing, like nothing she had ever seen before.

The spirit asked the girl what she wanted most of all, and the girl replied that she wanted to explore the world. The spirit said it would grant her wish and then it melted away.

The girl found a magical wand and she used it to explore every corner of the world. Everywhere she went, she felt the spirit's presence, like it was guiding her.

One day, she felt the spirit's presence more than ever before. Suddenly, out of nowhere, the spirit appeared in front of her and said: "You have explored the world with my help - now it's time for you to go back home!"

The girl was sad that she had to leave, but she thanked the spirit for his mysterious help. With a sparkle and a twinkle, the spirit melted away.

Once upon a time, there was a very special ancient castle. It was a luxury place and the King and Queen lived there. One day, the King of the castle decided he wanted to give all of his special treasures away.

The King called his daughter, the Princess, into the throne room. The Princess walked in and the King said, "My daughter, I want you to complete a special task. For my birthday, I want you to find me the most ancient and luxurious treasure you can find!"

The Princess was so excited because she wanted to make her father happy. She said, "I will complete it! I will go out and find the most luxurious ancient treasure!"

The sky started to turn pink as the Princess left the castle in search of the perfect treasure. After days of searching, she found a box with a beautiful diamond necklace inside! She couldn't believe her luck and quickly took the necklace back to the castle.

When the Princess arrived, the King was overjoyed. He put on the necklace with a huge smile. The King said, "Thank you for completing this special task. I am the luckiest King in the world!" And the Princess and King lived happily ever after.

Anna likes to be creative. She likes to draw, and sing, and make things with her hands. She has a big box of crayons, and a lot of paper, and some scissors and glue. She can make anything she wants with them.

One day, she decides to make a card for her mom. She takes a big piece of paper, and folds it in half. She draws a heart on the front, and writes "I love you" with her best letters. She colors the heart with red and pink crayons. She thinks it looks very pretty.

She opens the card, and thinks of what to write inside. She wants to say something nice, something that will make her mom happy. She thinks hard, and then she has an idea. She writes "You have a nice stomach". She smiles, and draws a picture of her mom's stomach, with a flower on it. She thinks it looks very nice.

She closes the card, and puts it in an envelope. She writes her mom's name on it, and sticks a sticker on it. She is very proud of her card. She runs to the living room, where her mom is sitting on the couch. She gives her the card, and says "This is for you, mom. I made it myself".

Her mom smiles, and hugs her. She opens the card, and reads it. She sees the heart, and the words, and the picture. She laughs, and says "Thank you, Anna. This is a very creative card. I love it, and I love you. You have a nice stomach, too". She kisses her on the cheek, and puts the card on the table. Anna is very happy. She sits next to her mom, and cuddles with her. She feels her mom's stomach, and thinks it is very warm and soft. She loves her mom, and her mom loves her. They are very happy.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Susie. She was three years old and loved to play with her friends. One day Susie was playing in the park near her house. She saw a telephone on the ground. She nodded and decided to pick it up and play with it. It was very hot to the touch so Susie put it down.

A wise old man saw what Susie had done. He came up to her and said, “Susie, I know it was tempting to play with that telephone, but it can be dangerous. You should always be careful and not touch things you don't know.”

Susie nodded. She understood the old man's words and from then on was always careful.

The moral of this story is that it is important to be careful when you are exploring and to not touch things that could be dangerous.

Tommy and his grandpa were outside in the garden one day. Grandpa was proud because he had just built a brand new statue for the garden. It was shiny and tall, and it sparkled in the sun.

Tommy was so excited! He ran around the statue, looking up and down at it. Then he stopped. There was some damage on the statue. Grandpa said, "Never mind, it's ok. I can easily fix it."

So Grandpa got out all his tools, and kept working on the statue while Tommy watched. Grandpa explained different things he was doing, as he was fixing.

Finally, the statue was finished! Tommy was so proud of it. Now it looked perfect and reliable. Grandpa said, "There it is! I'm so happy it's fixed. You can go and play now."

Tommy was so thankful that Grandpa was able to fix the statue. He was relieved, and ran off to go and play while Grandpa just smiled.

Once there was a girl called Jane who lived in a big city. She loved to play outside and explore the city. One day, she spotted a funny looking tube on the ground. It was thick and looked interesting. She picked it up and took it home with her.

When she got home, Jane showed her mom the big tube. Her mom thought it was a great find, and had an idea. She told Jane she could sell the tube and make some money. Jane thought that was a great idea, so she got to work.

First, she spread the word about the tube in her neighbourhood. Soon she had lots of people coming to buy it. Jane was so happy and excited to see how much money she could make. People used the tube for different things, like carrying things around with them or even using it as a toy.

At the end of the day, Jane had sold all the tubes. She had made a lot of money and was so proud of her achievement. She had a big smile on her face and ran off to go and buy herself a special treat.

Little Sam had a very special treasure. It was a tiny necklace made of shiny stones. The necklace never left him, he always wore it around his neck.

Every day, he put on his shiny treasure and went on an adventure. He played with his friends in the park and ran around the school grounds. He was never lonely.

But one day, Little Sam had no one to play with. His friends were all busy, so he was all alone. He felt so lonely and sad. He looked at his necklace, and it suddenly seemed to twinkle brighter. It suddenly reminded him of good times with his friends, and it made him feel not so lonely anymore.

Little Sam never went anywhere without his treasure again. He wore it everyday and felt safe and happy.

Once upon a time, there was a big, heavy cat named Fluffy. Fluffy loved to eat and sleep all day. One day, Fluffy saw a little stand with food. The stand had lots of food for cats to eat. Fluffy was very happy.

Fluffy walked to the stand to feed. She ate and ate until her belly was full. After eating, Fluffy felt very heavy. She wanted to take a nap, but she was too far from her cozy bed.

Fluffy walked very slowly back to her bed. She was so heavy, but she finally made it. Fluffy took a long nap and had happy dreams about the stand with food. When she woke up, Fluffy was ready to eat again.

Once upon a time there was a wide room. It was dark, so the people inside decided to get a lamp. They found a big, yellow lamp and put it in the room. It made the room much brighter!

The people were very happy and they started to play. They ran around the room, laughing and smiling. They had so much fun! They played until the day began to end.

When the day ended, the lamp got tired. It stopped glowing and the room got dark again. The people started to get sad, but then someone remembered a secret. They opened a window, and the bright moonlight filled the room.

The room lit up with the moonlight and everyone was happy again. They all hugged the lamp, thanked it for its help, and said goodnight. The lamp was happy and it sent them off with its last wide smile.

Once upon a time, there was a dish in the kitchen. It was a very tough dish. The dish was old and hadn't been used in a while.

One day, a little 3 year old boy called Mark saw the dish. He wanted to use the dish, but he couldn't lift it because it was so tough.

Mark asked his daddy to help him with the dish. His daddy picked up the dish and put it on the counter. Then he showed Mark how to use the dish.

Mark was so happy that he could use the dish. He ran to his bedroom to get some toys. He put all of his toys on the dish and played games with them.

Mark was very excited to have the dish. He plays with it every day and it'll always be special to him.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She went to the park with her mom and saw a lost puppy.

"Mommy, can we help the puppy?" asked Lily.

"Yes, we can help the puppy. Let's take it to the safe place," replied her mom.

They took the puppy to the animal shelter where it would be available for someone to adopt. Lily was happy because she cared about the puppy and wanted it to be safe.

"Mommy, can we come back and visit the puppy?" asked Lily.

"Of course, we can come back and visit the puppy anytime," replied her mom.

Lily and her mom left the animal shelter feeling good about helping the puppy. They knew it would be safe and available for someone to give it a loving home.

Sara and Ben were playing in the kitchen. They wanted to make a cake for Mom. They found some flour, sugar, eggs and milk. They put them in a big bowl and started to stir.

"Stir, stir, stir!" Sara said. "We are good cooks!"

"Yes, we are!" Ben agreed. "But we need something else. Something yummy and colorful."

He looked around and saw a jar of sprinkles on the shelf. He reached for it, but it was too high. He climbed on a chair and stretched his arm.

"Be careful, Ben!" Sara warned. "You might fall!"

But Ben did not listen. He grabbed the jar and jumped down. But he was not careful. He dropped the jar and it broke. Sprinkles went everywhere. On the floor, on the table, on the bowl, on Sara and Ben.

"Oh no!" Sara cried. "Look what you did!"

"I'm sorry, Sara!" Ben said. "It was an accident!"

But Sara was very mad. She picked up the bowl and threw it at Ben. The cake mix splashed on his face and clothes.

"That was rude, Sara!" Ben shouted. "Why did you do that?"

They heard Mom coming. They were scared. They ran to the closet and hid.

Mom came in and saw the mess. She was shocked. She called their names.

"Sara? Ben? Where are you?"

They did not answer. They stayed in the closet. They hoped Mom would not find them. They felt bad. They wished they had not fought. They wished they had made a nice cake for Mom. They wished they had used simple words.

Lily and Tom were hungry. They went to a big place with many people and food. They sat on chairs and looked at pictures of food. A nice lady came and asked them what they wanted.

"I want a big burger and fries and ketchup," Tom said.

"I want a salad and water and salt," Lily said.

The nice lady nodded and went away. She came back with their food. Tom was happy. He ate his burger and fries and ketchup very fast. He drank his soda and burped. Lily was not happy. She looked at her salad and water and salt. She did not like it. She wanted Tom's food.

"Can I have some of your fries?" Lily asked Tom.

"No, they are mine. You ordered salad. You have to eat it," Tom said.

"But I don't like salad. It is boring and green. I want fries. They are yummy and crispy," Lily said.

"Too bad. You should have ordered fries. Salad is healthy. You need to eat healthy," Tom said.

Lily was sad. She tried to eat her salad, but she did not like it. She put a lot of salt on it, hoping it would taste better. It did not. It tasted salty and bitter. She drank her water, but it did not help. She felt sick. She wanted to cry.

Tom finished his fries and smiled. He was full and happy. He saw Lily's face and laughed. He said, "See, I told you. You should have ordered fries. Salad is bad for you. Fries are good for you."

Lily did not say anything. She felt worse and worse. She got up and ran to the bathroom. She threw up. She felt very bad. She wished she had ordered fries.

The moral of the story is: Don't order food you don't like. Don't put too much salt on your food. Don't be mean to your friends. Don't laugh at their problems.

Once upon a time, there was a big mountain high in the sky. It seemed to stand forever and its peak touched the clouds. On the mountain, there lived a wise old man who saw the world's troubles. Each day he looked out on the horizon and prayed for peace.

One day, the man's prayers were answered. A messenger descended from the sky and asked the man what he wanted most. The old man said, “I want peace for everyone on the earth.”

The messenger nodded and said, “I promise to bring peace to the world.”

The old man thanked the messenger and said “May your promise come true!”

The messenger smiled and flew away to other places. Everywhere he went, he spread peace and joy. People’s lives were full of happiness and contentment. The wise old man watched and smiled.

The promise was kept!

Once upon a time, there was a big bear who lived in the forest. The bear was very peaceful and loved to take long naps in the sunshine. One day, a little girl came to visit the forest and saw the bear sleeping. She was scared and didn't know what to do.

Then, a kind man came to her and explained that the bear was just sleeping and wouldn't hurt her. He said that the bear was a friendly animal who liked to be left alone. The little girl felt better and watched the bear sleep for a while.

After a few minutes, the bear woke up and saw the little girl. The bear was curious and walked over to say hello. The little girl was scared again, but the man explained that the bear was just being friendly. The little girl petted the bear and they became friends. From that day on, the little girl visited the bear in the forest and they played together happily.

Lily was a pale girl who liked to play with dolls. She had many dolls in her cabinet, but her favorite one was Anna. Anna had long hair and a blue dress. Lily liked to take Anna everywhere she went.

One day, Lily wanted to take Anna to the park. She opened the cabinet and looked for Anna, but she could not find her. She saw other dolls, but not Anna. She felt sad and angry. Where was Anna?

She ran to her brother Tom, who was reading a book on the sofa. She asked him, "Tom, did you take Anna? She is my doll, not yours!"

Tom looked at Lily and shook his head. He said, "No, Lily, I did not take Anna. I don't like dolls. I like books. Maybe you left Anna somewhere else."

Lily thought hard. Where could she have left Anna? She remembered that yesterday she went to the grocery store with Mom. She took Anna with her and put her in the cart. Maybe she forgot to take her back.

She ran to Mom, who was in the kitchen. She asked her, "Mom, did we leave Anna at the store? She is my doll, not theirs!"

Mom hugged Lily and smiled. She said, "No, Lily, we did not leave Anna at the store. I saw you take her back and put her in the cabinet. Maybe she is hiding behind the other dolls. Why don't you look again?"

Lily ran back to the cabinet and looked again. She moved the other dolls and saw a blue dress. She pulled it and found Anna. She was so happy. She hugged Anna and said, "Anna, I found you! You are my doll, not theirs!"

She took Anna to the park and played with her. She was not pale anymore. She was pink and cheerful. She loved Anna and Anna loved her. They were best friends.

Once upon a time, there was a group of animals who lived in the forest. There were rabbits, birds, and squirrels. They all played together and had fun. One day, a big storm came and destroyed their homes. The rabbits' burrows were gone, the birds' nests were blown away, and the squirrels' trees fell down. They were all sad and scared.

But then, they saw a big, friendly bear who came to help them. The bear knew how to build new homes for them. He helped the rabbits dig new burrows, the birds build new nests, and the squirrels find new trees. The group of animals was so happy and grateful to the bear. They played together again and had fun. They knew they were lucky to have a friend like the bear who saved them from being dead.

Sara and Tom were playing with their balloons in the park. They liked to see how high they could make them go in the sky. The sky was very blue and sunny, and the balloons were colorful and shiny.

"Look, Sara, my balloon is red like a fire truck!" Tom said.

"Wow, Tom, that's cool! My balloon is yellow like a sunflower!" Sara said.

They laughed and ran with their balloons, but then a strong wind came and blew them away. Sara and Tom watched as their balloons flew higher and higher, until they could not see them anymore.

"Where did they go?" Tom asked.

"I don't know, Tom. Maybe they went to the moon." Sara said.

They felt very sad and started to weep. They wanted their balloons back. They hugged each other and cried.

A nice lady saw them and came over. She had a big basket full of balloons.

"Hello, little ones. Why are you weeping?" she asked.

"We lost our balloons. The wind took them away." Sara said.

"That's too bad. But don't worry, I have some more balloons for you. You can choose any color you like." the lady said.

She gave them each a new balloon. Sara picked a pink one and Tom picked a green one.

"Thank you, lady. You are very kind." Tom said.

"Yes, thank you. You made us happy again." Sara said.

They smiled and thanked the lady again. Then they went back to playing with their balloons in the park. They looked at the sky and hoped their old balloons were having fun too. The sky was still very blue and sunny, and the balloons were still colorful and shiny.

Anna and Ben like to play with tubes. They have many tubes of different colors and sizes. They like to put the tubes together and make shapes and tunnels.

One day, they find a big tube in the garage. It is green and shiny. Anna wants to play with it. She says, "This is my tube. I can fit inside it. It is fun."

Ben wants to play with it too. He says, "No, this is my tube. I can fit inside it too. It is mine."

They both try to fit inside the tube at the same time. They push and pull and squeeze. But the tube is too small for both of them. They get stuck in the tube. They cannot move. They feel sad and angry.

They start to cry and shout. They make a lot of noise. They say, "Help! Help! Get us out of here!"

Mom hears the noise. She comes to the garage. She sees Anna and Ben in the tube. She says, "Oh, no! What have you done? You are both in trouble. You have to share the tube. You cannot be selfish."

She pulls the tube and frees Anna and Ben. They come out of the tube. They are red and sweaty. They say, "Sorry, Mom. Sorry, Anna. Sorry, Ben."

Mom says, "It's okay. I'm glad you are safe. But next time, you have to ask before you take something. And you have to take turns and play nicely. Do you understand?"

Anna and Ben nod. They say, "Yes, Mom. We understand. We will share the tube. We will be friends."

Mom smiles. She says, "Good. Now, go and wash your faces. Then you can play with the tube again. But be careful and have fun."

Anna and Ben hug Mom. They say, "Thank you, Mom. We love you."

They go and wash their faces. Then they go back to the garage. They play with the tube again. But this time, they take turns and fit inside it one by one. They make shapes and tunnels. They laugh and have fun. They are happy.

Once there was an ostrich. He was very proud. One day he went for a walk and saw something sparkly in the grass! He was so excited and went over to look at it.

But then he saw something he wasn't expecting. There was an evil fox trying to steal the sparkly thing. The ostrich didn't like it. He got angry and decided he had to do something.

He ran over to the fox and shouted at him. This made the fox so embarrassed that he ran away! The ostriches was so happy to have saved the sparkly thing. He was very proud of himself.

The bird picked up the sparkly thing, and he took it home with him. From then on he looked after it and kept it safe. He never let any fox try to steal it again!

Once there was a woman. She was very popular. Everywhere she went, people waved and said "hi".

Every day, she repeated the same things. She got up early and made breakfast. Then she would work in her garden and play with her puppy.

At the end of each day, she would sit in the garden and watch the sun go down. Then she would start to repeat her day all over again.

The woman was very happy with her life. Every day was the same, but she enjoyed seeing all the little things that changed each time. That's why she was so popular.

Once upon a time there was a girl named Lucy. She was so excited to go on a special trip. She was going to meet a deep statue.

The next morning Lucy’s mom drove her to the park. When they arrived, the statue was so tall. It was so deep, Lucy was scared. But then she said to herself, “It’s okay, I can do this!”

She slowly and carefully walked up to the statue. She was so close! She reached out and touched the statue. It felt so cold and wet.

Lucy was so proud that she had met the deep statue. She shouted and jumped for joy. She looked up to the sky and whispered a thank you to the statue.

Lucy felt so brave, she knew she could do anything! She hugged her mom and skipped off home with a big smile on her face.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved going to the park with her mommy and daddy. They would go on the swings and slide down the big slide.

One day, Lily saw an empty seat on the see-saw. She ran to it and sat down. She asked her mommy and daddy to come and weigh the other side. They did and they all went up and down on the see-saw.

After playing, they went home and had a yummy dinner. Lily was so tired that she fell asleep right away. She dreamt about the see-saw and how much fun it was to weigh the sides.

One day, Mikey was allowed to walk outside his house alone. He was so excited and he couldn't believe it. He looked up at the sky and saw a giant, golden sun. It made him feel safe and happy.

As he walked further, he came across a beautiful lily. It was white and had yellow dots on it. Mikey came closer and touched it ever so gently. He felt it's soft petals.

Suddenly, he noticed something amazing happen. The sun's warmth was making the lily melt into the ground. Mikey smiled because he knew he was safe and he could be a part of something magical. He sat and watched until the lily was gone.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Molly. She wanted to understand how steel feels. So, one day she found a piece of steel and touched it with her fingers. It felt really rough. Molly was so surprised. She couldn't understand why it felt so rough. She asked her mom for help.

Her mom explained that steel is a very strong material and that's why it feels so rough. Molly liked to learn about different things and she was so happy to understand why steel felt that way. She felt like she had discovered a new secret.

From then on, every time Molly saw steel, she remembered the way it felt. Whenever she felt uncertain, she remembered that if steel can be strong, so can she. Even when something was tough and seemed hard to do, Molly knew that if she was strong like steel, that she could do it!

Once there was a little girl and she liked shining things very much. One day, her dad gave her a sack and said, "Polish this for me."

The little girl was frightened because she didn't know how to polish, but she wanted to help her dad. She got some cloth and started to clean the sack.

She kept shining and rubbing until the sack was gleaming. Then she showed it to her dad and he said, "Oh, well done! You worked so hard. This sack looks beautiful!"

The little girl was happy and proud. Then her dad said, "Always try your best even if you're scared. Doing your best is what's important."

The little girl understood and hugged her dad. From then on, she was not afraid to try her best even when she was frightened.

Once there was a naughty comet. One day, while flying through the sky, it decided it would be fun to splash its tail in the sea. The comet barged into the ocean and spun around, causing a huge splash.

The sea creatures were not pleased. The little fishes and crabs scurried away, to shelter from the comet's splash.

An old wise whale watched the comet. He said, "That was very naughty of you. You should not splash in the sea like this – think of others before yourself!" The comet listened and felt ashamed, and swam away quietly.

The whale was happy, as he knew this experience would help the comet become more thoughtful and kind. He said, "Now, go and be careful, no more naughty splashing!"

Once upon a time, there was a little crab named Tim. He lived near the wide sea. Every day, he would play with his friends in the water. They liked to splash and have fun in the tide.

One day, a big fish came to the sea. He was not nice. He splashed water at Tim and his friends. They could not play and relax. They were sad.

Tim had an idea. He talked to his friends. They all worked together. They made a big sand wall. The big fish could not splash them now. Tim and his friends were happy. They could play and relax again. The tide was safe and fun for everyone.

Once upon a time there was a little girl. She was only three years old and loved being with her mama. Every night they would have a special meal together. The girl would help set the table and pick out which dinner she wanted.

One day, the little girl had a hurt tummy. She felt sad and didn't want to eat dinner. But her mama knew how important dinner was for her. She was able to value how important it was for the little girl to eat every night.

So mama made her favourite meal for dinner. It was macaroni and cheese with a side of carrots. As the little girl ate her dinner, she felt better. Soon she was smiling and laughing with her mama. They finished dinner and the little girl was happy. Mama had valued the special meal they shared together.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, she was playing outside when she noticed something in the sky. It was a big, bright light that flashed really quickly. She asked her mommy what it was and her mommy said it was lightning.

Lily thought the lightning was really cool, but it was very far away. She couldn't hear any thunder, so she knew it was very distant. She wished the lightning would come closer so she could see it better.

As she watched the distant lightning, Lily felt happy and excited. She loved being outside and seeing all the amazing things in the world. She knew there was so much to discover and explore, and she couldn't wait to see what else she would notice.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved to play outside. She would run and jump and play with her toys. But one day, it started to rain and Lily had to stay inside. She was sad because she didn't have any toys to play with inside.

But then her mom came in with a big basket. "Lily, I have a surprise for you!" her mom said. Lily was curious and opened the basket. Inside, she found lots of colorful balls! She was so happy and started to play with them.

At first, Lily thought playing with the balls was boring. But then she had an idea. She started to throw the balls into the basket from far away. It was like playing a game! Lily had so much fun and played with the balls all day long. From that day on, Lily knew that even something that seemed boring could be fun if you use your imagination.

Once upon a time there was a leopard who lived in the forest. He was very brave and strong, but never could decide what to do.

One day, he noticed something on the path ahead. It was something small and crazy that he had never seen before. He decided that he should try to figure it out.

As he got closer, he realized that it was a very small spider. The spider was scuttling around in circles, not noticing the leopard at all.

The leopard decided it was a good idea to let the spider be. After watching it for a while, he noticed that the spider was making something that was getting bigger and bigger.

The leopard was so amazed! He realized that the spider had been spinning a web. He watched for hours as the spider made its web. The leopard was so happy.

The leopard had decided to let the spider be free, and now he saw that it had worked out for the best. He soon realised that he should make more decisions like this, so he decided to do just that.

Anna and Ben love to travel with their mom and dad. They go on a big train that runs on steel tracks. The train is very fast and loud. It makes Anna and Ben excited and happy.

One day, they travel to a big city. They see many tall buildings and bright lights. They also see a fancy park with flowers and swings. Mom and dad take them to the park and let them play. Anna and Ben have fun on the swings and slides. They make new friends with other kids.

But soon, it is time to go back to the train. Mom and dad pack their bags and hold their hands. They walk to the train station and find their seats. The train starts to move and leaves the city. Anna and Ben look out the window and wave goodbye to the park and the buildings and the lights. They are tired but happy. They cuddle with mom and dad and fall asleep. They dream of their next travel.

Lily and Tom were best friends. They liked to play in the park every day. They had a lot of fun on the swings, the slide and the seesaw. They also liked to make up stories and pretend to be different animals.

One day, it was very cold and windy. Lily and Tom wore their warm coats and hats. Lily also wore a scarf that her grandma had made for her. It was red and blue and had little stars on it. Lily loved her scarf. It was very soft and cozy. She thought it was the most original scarf in the world.

"Look at my scarf, Tom!" Lily said. "It is so pretty and special. Do you like it?"

"Yes, I do, Lily," Tom said. "It is very nice. Your grandma is very good at making things. My scarf is just plain green. It is boring."

"No, it is not, Tom," Lily said. "Your scarf is also nice. It is very warm and bright. And it matches your eyes. Green is my favorite color."

"Really?" Tom said. "Thank you, Lily. You are very kind. Green is my favorite color too."

They smiled at each other and hugged. Then they ran to the park to play.

They had a lot of fun in the park. They pretended to be lions and tigers and bears. They roared and growled and chased each other. They also made a snowman and gave him a carrot nose and a hat. They were very happy.

But then, it was time to go home. Lily and Tom said goodbye to each other and to the snowman. They put on their coats and hats. But Lily forgot something. She forgot her scarf. She left it on the bench where they had sat before. She did not notice.

She walked home with her mom. She was still smiling and thinking about the park. She did not feel cold. She did not remember her scarf.

But Tom did. He saw the scarf on the bench. He knew it was Lily's. He picked it up and ran after her. He wanted to give it back to her. He did not want her to lose it. He knew how much she loved it.

"Lily, Lily, wait!" Tom shouted. "You forgot your scarf!"

Lily heard him and turned around. She saw him holding her scarf. She was surprised. She had forgotten her scarf. She felt silly.

"Oh, Tom, thank you!" Lily said. "You are very smart and nice. You saved my scarf. I would have been very sad if I had lost it. It is my favorite scarf. It is very original."

"You are welcome, Lily," Tom said. "I am glad I saw it. It is a very original scarf. And it is very pretty. Just like you."

They smiled at each other and hugged again. They exchanged their scarves. They wanted to share. They thought it was fun. They felt warm and happy.

They waved goodbye and went home. They wore their new scarves. They looked very original. They were very original. They were best friends.

Tom and Jen are dogs. They like to play and run in the park. One day, they find a big bone. It is cool and hard and smells good.

"Wow, look at this bone!" Tom says. "It is so big and yummy!"

"I want it too!" Jen says. "Let's share it!"

But Tom does not want to share. He growls and shows his teeth. He thinks the bone is his.

"No, it is mine!" Tom says. "Go away!"

He slaps Jen with his paw. Jen yelps and runs away. Tom is happy. He has the bone all to himself.

But he does not see the big cat. The cat is hiding behind a bush. He sees the bone and wants it too. He is hungry and sneaky.

He waits until Tom is busy chewing the bone. Then he jumps out and pounces on Tom. He scratches and bites him. Tom is scared and hurt. He drops the bone and runs away.

The cat is happy. He has the bone all to himself.

He does not see the big man. The man is walking in the park. He sees the bone and the cat. He is angry and loud.

"Hey, that's my bone!" the man says. "I threw it away because it was old and bad!"

He kicks the cat away. He picks up the bone and throws it in the trash. He walks away.

The cat is sad and sore. He has no bone.

Tom and Jen see the cat. They feel sorry for him. They go to him and lick his wounds. They become friends.

They decide to play and run in the park. They do not need a bone. They have each other. They are happy.

Once upon a time, there was a fair board. It had bright colors and nice shapes on it. Every day something exciting would happen on the board.

One day, a bear came to the board. He had a fair hat and a fair scarf on. The bear started tapping his hat on the board, making sounds and music. The bear made the board very happy.

Suddenly, a rabbit hopped onto the board! The rabbit started hopping around, and the board was even happier. The bear and the rabbit played all day. They chased each other and hopped around together.

At the end of the day, the bear and the rabbit said goodbye to the board. The board was sad to see them go, but happy to have had such a fair day!

Anna and Ben were twins who liked to play outside. They liked to dig in the sand, splash in the water, and chase the birds. But they did not like to wash their hands and faces when they came home. They said it was boring and itchy.

One day, their mom told them they had a lovely surprise. She said they could go to the park and have a picnic with their friends. Anna and Ben were very happy and ran to get their hats and shoes. But mom stopped them and said, "Wait, you have to wash your hands and faces first. You are very dirty and you don't want to make your friends sick."

Anna and Ben did not want to wash. They said, "No, mom, we don't need to wash. We are not dirty and we are not sick. We have our own opinion and we think washing is silly."

Mom was not happy. She said, "I'm sorry, but you have to respect my opinion too. I am your mom and I know what is best for you. Washing is not silly, it is important and healthy. If you don't wash, you can't go to the park and have the picnic."

Anna and Ben did not like this. They wanted to go to the park and have the picnic. They looked at each other and decided to listen to mom. They said, "Okay, mom, we will wash. We are sorry for being rude. We love you and we want to make you happy."

Mom smiled and hugged them. She said, "Thank you, Anna and Ben. I love you too and I want to make you happy. I'm glad you understand that washing is good for you and for others. Now you can go to the park and have the picnic. And I have another lovely surprise for you. I made your favorite cookies for dessert."

Anna and Ben were very happy and thanked mom. They washed their hands and faces and went to the park. They had a lot of fun with their friends and enjoyed the picnic. They also shared their cookies with their friends and said they were delicious. They learned that washing was not so bad after all and that listening to mom was a good thing. They also learned that having an opinion was okay, but respecting other people's opinions was also important. They had a lovely day and went to bed with a smile.

Once upon a time, there were two best friends, Jack and Jill. They always agreed on things and spent lots of time together playing.

But then one day, they started to disagree. Jack wanted to go outside and play in the park, but Jill wanted to stay in and read a book.

Jack and Jill argued for a long time about what to do. Finally, they decided to ask their tutor for help. The tutor was very wise and had a wide knowledge.

The tutor told Jack and Jill that it wasn't good to always disagree. He said that if they took turns doing what each was most interested in, they could still be friends and have lots of fun.

Jack and Jill agreed with the tutor and decided to share their time together, so they could be friends forever.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Maggie. Every morning, Maggie liked to dress herself. She would pick out clothes from her special drawer and put them on. She would wear skirts and pretty dresses and felt very happy.

One day Maggie was worried because it was almost the end of the week. She looked through her special drawer, but she couldn't find a nice dress. She looked everywhere, but it was nowhere to be found.

Maggie felt very worried. She asked her mom for help. Her mom looked in the drawer too, but still no dress. Then she had an idea. She took some pretty fabric from the closet and made a new dress for Maggie.

Maggie was so happy when she put on the dress. She twirled around and danced. She looked and felt beautiful and she was no longer worried.

Once upon a time, there was a bird named Tweety. Tweety loved to soar high in the sky and sing happy songs. One day, Tweety saw a shiny object on top of a tall stair. Tweety wanted to see what it was, so she flew up to the top of the stair. But when Tweety got there, she saw a noisy cat waiting for her!

Tweety tried to fly away, but the cat was too fast. The cat chased Tweety around and around, trying to catch her. Tweety was scared and didn't know what to do. Suddenly, Tweety had an idea. She flew up high into the sky and then dove down fast, right past the cat. The cat was so surprised that he fell down the stair and ran away.

Tweety was safe and happy once again. She flew back up into the sky and sang a happy song, grateful to be free from the noisy cat. From that day on, Tweety knew to be careful when exploring new places.

John had a regular melon and it was his favorite fruit. He wanted to enjoy it, so he asked Mom for help. Mom took a knife and cut the melon. The melon was juicy and sweet. He loved it so much. He picked up the pieces with his hands and put them in his mouth. It was the best snack ever! He smiled and thanked Mom for helping him eat the melon. They shared the melon together and it was a happy time.

Once upon a time, there was a big lion. He liked to roar very loud. One day, he saw a car zoom by. It was very fast! The lion thought it was nice. He wanted to ride in the car too.

So, the lion went to the driver and asked if he could go for a ride. The driver was scared at first, but then he saw that the lion was nice. The lion got in the car and they zoomed away. The lion roared with joy as they drove on the road.

After a while, they stopped at a park. The lion got out of the car and saw some kids playing. He wanted to play too. So, he ran over and played with them. The kids thought it was nice to have a lion friend. They played together until it was time for the lion to go back home. The lion said goodbye and roared one last time before he left.

Once there was a little bunny named Benny. Benny was very shy and didn't like to talk to other animals. One day, Benny's mom gave him a task to go to the store and buy some carrots. Benny was scared to go alone, but he knew he had to be brave.

On his way to the store, Benny saw a friendly squirrel. The squirrel warned Benny about a big dog that was roaming around the corner. Benny was scared, but he knew he had to keep going to finish his task.

As he got closer to the store, Benny saw the big dog. He was so scared that he froze in his tracks. But then he remembered what the squirrel had said and he knew he had to be brave. He slowly walked past the dog and made it to the store.

Benny was so proud of himself for finishing his task, even though he was scared. When he got home, his mom praised him for being so brave. From that day on, Benny wasn't so shy anymore and he knew he could do anything if he tried.

Once upon a time, there was a brilliant girl named Susie. One day, Susie requested to go outside to play at noon. Her parents were very busy and so they said no to her request. Susie was disappointed but she knew that her parents had other important things to do.

Later in the day, Susie's parents got very busy with work and they forgot all about Susie. Noon came and went and it was very late at night by the time Susie's parents noticed her.

Susie was so sad that her request was not granted, she cried and said she wanted to go outside. Her parents felt awful but they did not have enough time to take her outside.

The next day, Susie still felt sad. She felt like her parents would never grant her request and that her request would always be ignored.

Things like this kept happening and Susie felt very lonely. No matter how brilliant and brave she was, things always seemed to end badly for her.

Tom and Mia are friends. They like to play in Tom's garage. There are many toys and tools in the garage. Tom's dad lets them use some of them, but not all of them.

One day, Tom and Mia are playing with a big red car. They pretend to drive it around the garage. They make noises like vroom and beep. They have fun.

"Are you thirsty?" Tom asks Mia.

"Yes, I am," Mia says.

"Me too. Let's go drink some water," Tom says.

They get out of the car and walk to the door. Tom opens the door and sees his mom. She is holding a tray with two cups and a pitcher.

"Hi, kids. I made you some lemonade. Do you want some?" she asks.

"Yes, please. Thank you, mom," Tom says.

"Thank you, Tom's mom. You are very nice," Mia says.

They take the cups and drink the lemonade. It is cold and sweet. They smile and say, "Ahh."

They go back to the garage and play some more. They are happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys and her favorite was a big orange ball. One day, she went to the park to play with her ball. She was having so much fun kicking it back and forth with her friend, Timmy.

Suddenly, they heard a loud noise and saw steam coming out of the ground. They both got scared and ran away. As they were running, they saw a big rock fall from the sky and land on the park. They were so scared and didn't know what to do.

They went to tell their parents what happened, but it was too late. The rock had destroyed the park and all their toys were gone. Lily and Timmy were sad and didn't know what to do without their toys. They learned that sometimes bad things happen and it's important to stay safe.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the park. One day, she saw a bird flying in the sky. She wanted to grab it, but she couldn't reach it.

Suddenly, she saw a piece of bread on the ground. She picked it up and threw it in the air. The bird came down to grab the bread. But then, a big cat appeared and grabbed the bird.

Lily felt helpless and sad. She said to the cat, "Please let the bird go." But the cat didn't listen and ran away with the bird in its mouth. Lily cried and went back home. She learned that sometimes, we can't always help others, but we can always try.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who loved to unpack things. One day, she went on an adventure with her mom and dad. After a long drive, they arrived at a valley. It was a very special place. The girl saw a big box. She was thrilled and ran over to it.

The girl started to unpack it. It was full of gross and disgusting things. Worms, bugs, and slimy goo were everywhere. The girl screamed and ran away. She was so scared. Mom and Dad saw her and laughed.

The girl soon realized that there was nothing to worry about. Mom and Dad had brought the box of gross stuff to the valley to help the animals who lived there. They wanted to make sure the animals had enough to eat. The girl was so happy that she ran back to the box to help unpack it!

Once there was a girl named Jane and she loved motors. She had one motor at home and on her birthday her mom bought her a new motor.

Jane was very happy with her new motor and she asked her mom, "Can I go outside and play with my motor?"

Her mom said, "Yes, but you must be careful. Do not go too far from home and do not let your motor run by itself".

So Jane went outside and she was very persistent trying to find the perfect spot for her motor. She asked everyone she met for the perfect spot for her motor.

Finally, she found the perfect spot - a big empty field with lots of open space. Jane was very excited and started playing with her motor.

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to swim in the big blue pool at her house. One day, Lily saw a beautiful angel in the sky. The angel had big, white wings and a golden halo on her head.

Lily wanted to meet the angel, so she decided to swim up to the sky. But her mommy told her it was foolish to try to swim in the sky. Lily was sad, but she knew her mommy was right.

Instead, Lily made a drawing of the angel and hung it in her room. Every time she saw the drawing, she remembered the beautiful angel in the sky and smiled. From then on, Lily knew that sometimes it's okay to dream big, but it's also important to listen to those who love and care for us.

Tommy loved to watch cartoons on TV. He liked the ones with wild animals that talked and did funny things. He wished he could be friends with them and go on adventures.

One day, he found a big cardboard box in the garage. He decided to make it his own cartoon machine. He cut out a window and drew some buttons and dials on the side. He got some crayons and paper and made his own cartoon characters. He had a lion, a monkey, a zebra and a giraffe.

He put his cartoons inside the box and turned a dial. He looked through the window and imagined that his cartoons came to life. He saw the lion roar and the monkey swing from a vine. He saw the zebra run and the giraffe stretch his neck. He heard them talk to him and invite him to join them.

He crawled inside the box and imagined that he was in the cartoon world. He played with his new friends and had a lot of fun. He pretended that they went to the jungle, the savanna, the desert and the mountains. He learned about different animals and places.

He was so happy in his cartoon machine that he did not hear his mom call him for lunch. She came to the garage and saw him in the box. She smiled and asked him what he was doing. He told her he was watching cartoons. She laughed and said he had a great imagination. She helped him out of the box and took him to the kitchen. He said he would come back to his cartoon machine later. He hugged his mom and thanked her for the box. He was glad he had his cartoons and his mom.

One day, Timmy was playing with his friends in the park. They were running and dancing and having a great time.

Suddenly, they saw a small rabbit through the bushes. It was fragile and timid.

The children squealed in delight and ran towards the rabbit, wanting to play with it.

"Let's celebrate," Timmy said. "Let's give the rabbit a party!"

His friends cheered and clapped their hands.

The children slowly approached the rabbit and made it a special party. They decorated the area with paper streamers, and provided the rabbit with yummy fruit snacks.

The rabbit stayed to enjoy the delicious treats and the children showed their love and respect for the small creature.

At the end of the day, the rabbit hopped away into the bush, feeling happy and safe.

The children hugged each other and celebrated the wonderful moment they had shared.

Once upon a time there was a small oyster who lived in the river. She was very brave and always wanted to explore the world.

One day she decided to journey away from home. She swam up and down the river, looking for adventure.

As she was swimming, she came across a dangerous place. The water was rough and rocky. But the little oyster did not get scared. She decided to take a risk and swim through.

She made it to the other side and the water was much calmer. She saw a big, beautiful ocean and lots of different sea creatures. She decided to stay and explore the new place.

But after a few days, she missed her home. So the brave oyster decided to go back home. And she never tried to explore the dangerous part of the river again.

Once upon a time, there were two friends, Tom and Jerry. They both loved to eat grapes. They always went to the same grape tree to eat grapes. One day, Tom said to Jerry, "Let's go to a different grape tree. Maybe the grapes there will taste better."

Jerry thought it was a good idea and they went to a different grape tree. But when they got there, they saw a sign that said, "Do not eat the grapes. They are not ready yet." Tom didn't care and he ate a grape anyway. Suddenly, a man came out and slapped Tom's hand. Tom felt bad and realized that he should have listened to the sign.

The moral of the story is to always listen to the rules and not do things that could get you in trouble. And also, it's not good to be different just for the sake of being different. Sometimes, it's better to stick with what you know is good and right.

Mummy and Daddy were picking flowers in the garden. Mummy picked a red daisy, Daddy picked a purple thistle and the little girl picked a beautiful lily. The lily was her favorite because it was so fluffy and white and the aroma was heavenly.

Daddy said, "Let's bring this lily inside and put it on the windowsill."

Mummy said, "How about we make it a surprise?"

So the family all went inside and the little girl put the lily on the windowsill.

When she stepped back to admire her work, she noticed a bright yellow butterfly that had landed on the lily. The little girl smiled.

Mummy said, "Oh my, that lily looks so warm and cozy with the butterfly on top."

The little girl nodded, delighted with her surprise. And, from that day on, the warm lily became a happy reminder of the special family day.

Once upon a time, there was a friendly cat named Tom. He lived with a little girl named Sue. Tom and Sue liked to play all day. They laughed and had fun together.

One day, Tom and Sue heard a loud noise coming from the big room. They went to see what it was. They saw a big box. Sue shut the box, and there was silence. Tom and Sue looked at each other and smiled.

Tom and Sue opened the box again. Inside, they found a big, friendly bear. The bear wanted to play with Tom and Sue. They all played together and had a lot of fun. Tom, Sue, and the friendly bear became best friends forever.

Tim and Lily were twins who liked to play outside. One day, they found a camera in the grass. It was big and shiny and had a button. Tim wanted to press the button, but Lily said no. She said they should ask Mom first.

They ran to the house with the camera. Mom was in the kitchen, making juice. She saw the camera and smiled. She said it was Dad's camera, and he used it to take pictures of animals. She said they could play with it, but they had to be careful and not break it.

Tim and Lily thanked Mom and drank some juice. Then they went back outside with the camera. They pretended to be animal explorers, and took pictures of birds, bugs, and flowers. They had a lot of fun, until they saw a big, furry thing in the bushes. It looked like a bear, but it had a long tail and stripes. It was a tiger!

Tim and Lily were scared, but they also wanted to take a picture of the tiger. They thought it would be a great surprise for Dad. They crept closer to the bushes, holding the camera. They hoped the tiger would not see them or hear them. They were very quiet and brave.

But the tiger was not a real tiger. It was a toy tiger that someone had left in the bushes. It had a battery inside, and a switch. When Tim and Lily got close enough, the switch turned on, and the toy tiger made a loud roar. It also moved its head and paws, and opened its mouth.

Tim and Lily screamed and dropped the camera. They ran away as fast as they could, thinking the tiger was chasing them. They did not see that the camera had taken a picture of the toy tiger, with its crazy eyes and teeth.

When they got to the house, they told Mom what happened. Mom hugged them and said they were safe. She said there were no real tigers in the park, only toy ones. She said someone must have played a trick on them. She said they should go back and get the camera, and see if it was okay.

Tim and Lily agreed, but they were still a little scared. They held Mom's hand and walked back to the bushes. They saw the camera on the ground, and the toy tiger next to it. They realized it was not a real tiger, and felt silly. They picked up the camera and looked at the screen. They saw the picture of the toy tiger, and laughed. It was a funny picture, and they were glad they had taken it. They decided to show it to Dad when he came home, and tell him their crazy story.

It was a quiet day and Tommy was at home with his mom. He was very excited because it was his birthday. As they watched, his dad pulled out a big box from the basement and put it in front of him. Inside the box was a new bicycle!

Tommy was so happy that he started clapping his hands. He couldn't wait to go outside and ride his bike. His mom and dad told him to put on his helmet and ride safely.

Tommy got on his bike and slowly pulled on the handlebars. He slowly rolled down the driveway and around the neighbourhood. He stopped at the park to show his friends his new bike. He had so much fun and couldn't believe it was his birthday.

When he came home, the sun was setting and it was getting dark and quiet. Tommy thanked his mom and dad for the wonderful birthday gift and went off to bed. It had been the best birthday ever!

Once upon a time, there was a man named Joe. Joe liked to work at the ice-cream shop. He made yummy ice-cream for all the kids. One day, Joe made a big batch of chocolate ice-cream. It was so yummy that all the kids came to the shop to buy some. Joe worked hard to scoop the ice-cream and put it in cones for the kids. They all smiled and said "thank you" to Joe. Joe felt happy that his hard work made the kids happy.

Once upon a time, there was a chubby little girl called Jane. She loved her rug because it was very soft and fluffy. Every day, she would drag it outside into the garden and enjoy sitting and playing on it with her toys. She liked to pretend that her rug was a boat, or that it was a magical carpet, or even a secret cave. She felt very brave and adventurous when she was playing on it. Jane's favourite game was to pretend that she was an explorer, searching for hidden treasure. She would sit on the rug, close her eyes and imagine herself finding different kinds of treasure. Every day Jane would enjoy her little adventures and discover something new. She was always excited to find out what the rug had in store for her. The end.

Ben and Jen were twins who liked to play on the farm. They had many animals to see and feed, like cows, pigs, chickens and horses. But their favorite animal was Molly, the mule. Molly was very friendly and smart, and she liked to carry things for them.

One day, Ben and Jen decided to have a tea party with Molly. They put a hat and a scarf on her, and gave her some carrots and apples. They also brought some cups and plates and pretended to drink and eat.

"Molly, you are our best guest," said Jen. "You are so nice and pretty."

"Yes, Molly, you are very special," said Ben. "Can you do a trick for us?"

Molly nodded and bowed her head. She lifted one of her front legs and waved it in the air. Then she made a funny sound with her mouth.

Ben and Jen clapped and laughed. They hugged Molly and gave her more treats.

"Molly, you are not boring at all," said Jen. "You are very fun and clever."

"Yes, Molly, you are not like the other animals," said Ben. "You are our friend."

Molly smiled and nuzzled them. She was happy to play with Ben and Jen. She liked their tea party. She liked being their friend.

Jimmy loved to follow his Mommy. He always looked forward to the fun adventures they went on together. One day, his Mommy had a special surprise for him. She showed him a calendar and explained that they would be visiting an elderly lady.

Jimmy was a bit concerned, he had never been to an elderly person's home before. But his Mommy reassured him it would be fine, so they packed up and headed out.

When they arrived, Jimmy was immediately drawn to a special music box in the elderly lady's living room. He started to reach for it to take a closer look, but the elderly lady screamed and told him to stop.

Embarrassed, Jimmy stopped and looked down at the ground. His Mommy apologized and quickly began to leave. As they were about to go, the elderly lady warned them not to ever come back.

Jimmy was sad as he and his Mommy drove away. He never got to play with the music box and he wondered if he would ever be able to come back. Sadly, the answer was no.

Once there was a little girl called Daisy. Daisy was very brave and loved to explore. One day she saw a tall tower that sparkled in the sun. Daisy thought the tower was very important and wanted to explore it. She took one step forward, but she slipped! Daisy started to cry.

But then, something wonderful happened. A lovely fairy flew down from the sky and landed beside Daisy. She said, "Don't be scared, Daisy! I'm here to help you explore the tower!" Daisy was so happy and smiled.

The fairy waved her wand and a special ladder appeared. Daisy climbed the ladder carefully and when she reached the top, she saw the most beautiful sights! She waved goodbye to the fairy and thanked her for her help. Daisy had a wonderful time exploring the tower and she never forgot how important it was.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Emma. Emma was very alert and always listened carefully.

One day, Emma heard a voice coming from the door. It was someone calling her. She said, “Emma! Open the door!” Emma was a bit scared and she didn't want to open the door.

But the voice kept calling. This time it said, “Emma! You must open the door! Please don't be scared!”

Emma thought for a few moments, then she took a deep breath and opened the door. She saw an old man standing outside. He looked at Emma and smiled. Then he said to her, “Hello Emma! I urged you to open the door because I have an important message for you. Can you please come with me?”

Emma nodded her head. She followed the old man and he told her some important news. Emma was so happy to hear it! From that day onward, Emma was always very alert and she always listened carefully.

Once upon a time, there was a stubborn cow. The cow lived on a farm with many other animals. The cow liked to be alone and did not play with the other animals.

One cold day, the cow felt a shiver. It was very cold outside. The other animals went into the warm barn to stay warm. But the stubborn cow did not want to go inside with them.

As the night came, the cold got worse. The stubborn cow still did not go into the warm barn. The cow shivered all night long. In the morning, the farmer found the stubborn cow outside, very cold and sick. The cow did not get better, and it was a sad day on the farm.

Sara liked to play dress-up with her old clothes. She had a big wardrobe full of dresses, hats, shoes and scarves. She liked to pretend she was a princess, a teacher, a doctor or a spy. She had a lot of fun with her wardrobe.

One day, her mom told her they had to move to a new house. She said they had to sell some of their things, because they did not have enough space. She said they had to sell Sara's wardrobe, too. Sara was very sad. She did not want to sell her wardrobe. She loved her wardrobe.

She begged her mom to let her keep it. She said she would miss it too much. She said it was her favorite thing. Her mom said she was sorry, but they had to sell it. She said she would buy her a new wardrobe in the new house. She said it would be bigger and better. She said it would be impressive.

Sara did not believe her. She thought her mom was lying. She thought her mom did not care about her wardrobe. She thought her mom did not care about her. She was very angry. She did not want to talk to her mom. She did not want to move. She did not want to sell her wardrobe.

The next day, a man came to their house. He said he wanted to buy Sara's wardrobe. He said he liked it very much. He said he had a daughter who liked to play dress-up, too. He said he wanted to give it to her as a surprise. He said he would pay a lot of money for it.

Sara's mom said yes. She said she was happy to sell it. She said she needed the money for the new house. She said she would help Sara pack her clothes. She said they would find a new wardrobe soon. She said it would be impressive.

Sara did not say anything. She watched the man take her wardrobe away. She felt a big hole in her heart. She felt like she had lost her best friend. She felt like she had nothing left. She felt like she did not want to live in the new house. She felt like she did not want to see the impressive wardrobe. She felt like she did not want to play dress-up ever again.

One day, a little girl named Jill wanted to take a bath. She took off all of her clothes and jumped in the tub.

The water was warm and she had lots of fun playing in it. She grabbed a sponge and some soap, and she splashed around.

After she was done playing, she reached for a diamond. It was white and shiny, and it sparkled in the sun. She put it in her pocket and smiled.

Finally, she got out of the tub. She dried herself off with a towel and got dressed. The bathroom was now empty and she wished she could take another bath right away.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Jane. She loved to play outside with her friends. One day, while playing, she found a big stone. It was round and smooth. Jane thought it was very special.

Jane wanted to fix the stone to make it even more special. She found some tasty fruit and decided to make a necklace with the stone and the fruit. She asked her mom for help. Her mom helped her put a hole in the stone and tie it with a string.

Now, Jane had a beautiful necklace with the stone and the tasty fruit. She wore it every day and showed it to all her friends. They all loved it and wanted one too. Jane felt very happy that she could fix the stone and make something so pretty.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She lived in a big house with a high ceiling. One day, Lily was playing with her favorite toy when she accidentally threw it too high and it hit the ceiling. The ceiling made a loud noise and Lily started to cry because she thought she was in trouble.

Her mommy came running to see what had happened and saw that the toy had not damaged the ceiling too bad. She hugged Lily and told her it was okay, accidents happen. Lily stopped crying and felt better. From that day on, she learned to be more careful when playing with her toys near the ceiling. The end.

Lila and Sam are playing in the living room. They have a big carpet that they like to fold and make into different things. Sometimes they fold it into a tent, sometimes into a boat, sometimes into a castle.

Today, Lila wants to fold the carpet into a tent and pretend they are camping. But Sam wants to fold the carpet into a boat and pretend they are sailing. They both pull on the carpet and try to fold it their way.

The carpet is rough and scratchy. It hurts their hands and makes them angry. They start to yell at each other and tug harder on the carpet. The carpet rips and makes a loud noise.

Mom hears the noise and comes to the living room. She sees the ripped carpet and the angry children. She is not happy. She tells them to stop fighting and to share the carpet. She says they can take turns folding it into different things, or they can fold it together and make something new.

Lila and Sam feel sorry for ripping the carpet and for yelling at each other. They say sorry to Mom and to each other. They decide to fold the carpet together and make a big pillow. They hug and lie down on the pillow. They are happy again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to help her mom make cookies. One day, her mom let her help make the dough. Lily was so happy and grateful to help. She mixed the flour, sugar, and butter together with her hands.

Then her mom said, "We need to let the dough soak in the fridge for a little bit before we can bake the cookies." Lily didn't know what soak meant, but her mom explained that it meant the dough needed to rest in the fridge to get cold.

After a while, they took the dough out of the fridge and rolled it into little balls. They put the balls on a baking tray and put them in the oven. Soon, the cookies were ready and they smelled so good! Lily was so proud of herself for helping make the cookies. She couldn't wait to share them with her friends.

Emma was so excited! Today was the day she would join her first tooth club. She had been counting the days until she got to join the club and now the moment had arrived.

The tooth club was in a nearby park and was filled with other children. As soon as Emma got there, they all began talking. They all loved talking about their teeth!

Emma was talking to one of the other children when she noticed something was wrong. Her tooth felt dull and wobbly. She quickly put her hands up to her mouth to check. Sure enough, her tooth was almost ready to come out!
