Emma was so sad. She had been so excited to join the tooth club, but now her membership would be over just as it had begun. Everyone was so disappointed for her, but there was nothing more to be done.

Sadly, Emma said goodbye and went home. From then on, she wouldn't be able to join the tooth club anymore.

Once upon a time, there was a bunny. He was hopping around in the forest when he heard a noise coming from the nearby pond. Curious, he hopped over to the pond and to his surprise, he saw a small island. He hopped onto it and as soon as he stepped onto the island he saw it was dirty.

Afraid, he started to hop away but he noticed something else on the island. It was a kitty, and it was meowing for help. He hopped closer and realized the kitty was stuck in the dirt on the island. The bunny hopped around, looking for something to help him but it was all too dirty.

Suddenly, the bunny had an idea. He hopped around and found a stick, and started to dig the kitty out of the dirt. After a few minutes of hopping and digging, he freed the kitty from the dirt and was able to hop away from the island.

The bunny and the kitty were both happy to be safe and return to the forest. From then on, they would always remember the dirty island and how they helped each other when they were in trouble.

Once upon a time, there was a sleepy cat named Tom. Tom lived in a big maze with many paths. One day, Tom woke up and wanted to find his friend, a little mouse named Jerry.

"Jerry, where are you?" Tom called. He looked left and right, up and down, but he could not find Jerry. Tom felt sad and worried. He knew he had to find Jerry to make sure he was safe.

As Tom walked through the maze, he met a wise owl. "Mr. Owl, have you seen Jerry?" Tom asked. The owl nodded and said, "I saw him go down that path." Tom thanked the owl and went to look for Jerry.

Finally, Tom found Jerry stuck in a corner of the maze. "I am here to help you, Jerry!" Tom said. Together, they found their way out of the maze and went home. They were so happy to be safe and together again.

One day, a little rabbit named Bob was playing in the yard. He liked to jump and spring high in the air. He was a very happy rabbit. In the yard, he found a tool. It was a small shovel. Bob wanted to dig a hole with the tool.

Bob started to dig, but he found a big, sour lemon in the hole. The lemon was so sour that it made Bob's face scrunch up. He didn't like the sour lemon. He wanted to keep digging, but the lemon was in the way.

Bob thought hard about what to do. He decided to push the sour lemon out of the hole with the tool. He used the shovel to move the lemon away. Now, he could dig his hole and play. The little rabbit was happy again, and he kept springing and playing in the yard.

One day, Anna and Ben went to the park with their mom. They saw a big train with a lot of smoke coming out of it. The smoke was hot and wet. It was called steam.

"Can we ride the train, mom?" Anna asked.

"Sure, but you have to be careful and listen to the conductor. He will tell you when to get on and off the train. He is very nice and compassionate. He likes children and he knows a lot about trains. Do you trust him?" mom said.

"Yes, mom, we trust him. He has a funny hat and a whistle. He smiles a lot." Ben said.

They waited in line and then got on the train. The conductor checked their tickets and gave them a sticker. He said, "Welcome to the park train. I hope you enjoy the ride. Please stay in your seats and do not lean out of the windows. The train will go around the park and show you some animals and flowers. If you have any questions, you can ask me. I am here to help you."

The train started to move and the steam made a loud sound. Anna and Ben looked out of the windows and saw ducks, rabbits, roses, and sunflowers. They waved to the people and the animals. They felt happy and excited.

"Wow, this is so fun. I love the train. Thank you, mom. Thank you, conductor." Anna said.

"You're welcome, Anna. I'm glad you like it. The train is my favorite too. It is very old and special. It needs a lot of care and love. That's why I always check the steam and the wheels and the brakes. I want to make sure the train is safe and happy." the conductor said.

The train stopped at the station and the conductor said, "This is the end of the ride. I hope you had a good time. Please get off the train and have a nice day. Come back soon."

Anna and Ben got off the train and hugged the conductor. They said, "Thank you, conductor. You are very compassionate. We trust you. We will come back soon."

They walked back to their mom and told her everything they saw and heard on the train. They said they wanted to ride the train again. Mom smiled and said, "Maybe next time. Now let's go home and have some lunch. You must be hungry after such a big adventure."

Once upon a time, there was a furry octopus named Ollie. Ollie lived in the sea with his friends, the fish and the crabs. One day, Ollie saw a little fish with a hurt fin. The little fish was sad because it could not swim.

Ollie swam to the little fish and said, "Don't worry, little fish! I can help you heal your fin." The little fish looked at Ollie and said, "Thank you, furry octopus! I want to swim with my friends again."

Ollie used his soft, furry arms to wrap around the little fish's fin. He held it gently and sang a special song. After a while, the little fish's fin began to heal. Soon, it was all better!

The little fish was so happy that it could swim again. It said to Ollie, "Thank you, furry octopus! You are a good friend." Ollie smiled and said, "You're welcome, little fish! Have fun swimming with your friends!"

From that day on, Ollie and the little fish became best friends. They swam together and played in the sea. And if any of their friends got hurt, Ollie would always be there to help them heal.

Once upon a time, there lived a family of four. They were very happy together, until one day when the little girl got very angry. She shouted and screamed as loud as she could. Everyone around her was very shocked and asked her why she was so mad. The little girl said it was because of the selfishness of her brother. She said he had been hiding the truth and not telling them something important.

The little girl was so sad and the family was in shock. But after a while they realised that it was important to tell the truth even if it was hard. They shouldn't be selfish and keep secrets, because it only made things worse.

The family hugged each other and said that from know on, they would always tell the truth, no matter what.

The moral of the story is that being truthful is always the best way and that being selfish only causes misery.

Lily and Tom were enthusiastic to help Mom cook dinner. They liked to stir the rice in the pot and smell the yummy sauce. Mom said they were good helpers and gave them each a spoon.

"Can we taste the rice, Mom?" Lily asked.

"Not yet, sweetie. It's still too hot. You have to wait a little bit," Mom said.

Lily and Tom nodded and went to the table. They saw a big bowl of salad and a plate of bread. They were hungry and wanted to eat.

Suddenly, they heard a loud noise from the kitchen. It sounded like a bang and a hiss. They turned around and saw Mom running out of the kitchen with a wet towel. She looked scared and angry.

"What happened, Mom?" Tom asked.

"The rice pot exploded! It was too full and the lid flew off. The rice and the water went everywhere. It was a big mess and it burned my hand," Mom said.

Lily and Tom gasped. They felt sorry for Mom and the rice. They ran to hug her and asked if she was okay.

"I'm okay, honey. It's just a little red. But we can't eat the rice now. It's ruined," Mom said.

Lily and Tom frowned. They liked rice and they wanted to eat it. They wondered what they would have for dinner now.

"Can we have pizza, Mom?" Lily asked.

Mom smiled and wiped her face. She hugged them back and said, "Sure, why not? Pizza sounds good. Let's order some and have a fun night. Maybe we can watch a movie too."

Lily and Tom cheered. They were happy again. They liked pizza and movies. They forgot about the rice and the scare. They helped Mom clean the kitchen and waited for the pizza to arrive. They had a good dinner and a good night.

Tommy did not like to go to bed. He was afraid of the dark and the bad dreams. He wanted to stay up and play with his toys. But his mom said he had to sleep.

"Tommy, it's time for bed. You need to rest and grow. Don't worry, I'll read you a story and tuck you in," his mom said.

"No, mom, please. I don't want to sleep. I want to play. I don't like the dark. I have nightmares. They are scary and mean. They make me cry," Tommy said.

"Tommy, I know you are scared, but nightmares are not real. They are just pictures in your head. They can't hurt you. And I'm here to protect you. I'll leave the light on and give you your teddy bear. He will keep you company. And I'll check on you later. OK?" his mom said.

"OK, mom. But can you read me a happy story? Not a scary one. And can you hug me and kiss me goodnight?" Tommy said.

"Of course, my sweet boy. I'll read you a happy story. And I'll hug you and kiss you goodnight. I love you very much. Now, let's go to bed," his mom said.

They went to Tommy's room. His room was filthy. He had toys and clothes and books everywhere. His mom sighed and picked up some of the mess. She made his bed and put his teddy bear on his pillow. She read him a story about a brave knight and a friendly dragon. She hugged him and kissed him goodnight. She turned on the light and left the door open.

Tommy felt a little better. He cuddled with his teddy bear and closed his eyes. He tried to think of the happy story. He hoped he would not have nightmares. He fell asleep. He did not have nightmares. He had nice dreams. He dreamed of playing with his toys and his mom and his teddy bear. He smiled in his sleep. He was happy.

Once upon a time, there was a boy who went for a walk. He saw a smooth circle on the ground. He was very excited to walk around it! He stepped into the middle of the circle, and then he started walking around it. He felt so happy and giggled as he walked around and around. When he finished, he stepped out of the circle and went for another walk. He was so happy that he had found such a fun thing to do. He was sure that he would go back every day to play in the smooth circle. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. He loved to play with his toy cars and trucks. One day, he found a shiny coin on the ground. He picked it up and showed it to his mom. She told him that it was a special coin and he should keep it safe.

The next day, Timmy went to the park to play with his friends. He brought his special coin with him. When it was time to go home, he couldn't find his coin. He looked everywhere, but it was gone. Timmy felt sad and sighed.

But then, his friend Johnny found the coin on the ground. He gave it back to Timmy and said, "I found your coin. You can always rely on me to help you." Timmy was happy and thanked his reliable friend. They went home together, playing with their toy cars and trucks along the way.

Once upon a time, there was a loyal dog called Patch. He lived with his family in a small house. One day, Patch noticed something strange - the family's trash bin was open. He knew that he had to stop whatever was happening. He ran to the bin and barked loudly to prevent it from being tipped over.

Patch's family came out of the house to see what was happening. They saw Patch and smiled. His mom said, “Good boy, Patch! You are so loyal. You were trying to prevent the bin from getting knocked over.” She rubbed his head and thanked him.

After that, Patch and his family made sure to close the bin properly every day. They were thankful for Patch's loyal barking. Patch was proud of himself for keeping the bin safe. He looked up his family with a big smile.

Once upon a time, there was a cowboy named Jack. Jack had a big pistol that he liked to show to his friends. One day, Jack went to the rodeo to watch the horses and bulls. While he was there, he saw a clown who made him feel dizzy.

After the rodeo, Jack went to a shooting contest. He wanted to see if he could match the other cowboys. Jack took out his pistol and aimed at the targets. He was very good at shooting and he hit all the targets.

When Jack went home, he felt very proud of himself. He couldn't wait to tell his friends about the shooting contest. He also told them about the clown who made him feel dizzy. Jack had a great day at the rodeo and he was happy he could match the other cowboys in the shooting contest.

Sara and Ben are twins. They like to play together, but sometimes they fight. One day, they find a big mirror in the attic. They think it is fun to make faces and dress up in front of the mirror.

"Look at me, I am a princess!" Sara says, putting on a tiara and a necklace. "You are a frog, Ben!"

"No, I am not a frog, I am a knight!" Ben says, holding a sword and a shield. "You are a witch, Sara!"

They start to argue and push each other. The mirror shakes and falls to the floor. It breaks into many pieces. Sara and Ben are scared. They hear their mom coming up the stairs.

"What happened here?" Mom asks, seeing the mess. "Who broke the mirror?"

Sara and Ben look at each other. They don't want to get in trouble. They don't know what to say.

Mom looks at them with a serious face. "I want you to be honest with me. Tell me the truth. How do you feel?"

Sara and Ben feel sorry and ashamed. They know they did something bad. They don't want to lie to Mom.

"We broke the mirror, Mom," Sara says, with a small voice. "We were playing and fighting and we made it fall. We are sorry, Mom."

"We are very sorry, Mom," Ben says, with a small voice too. "We didn't mean to break it. We were just having fun."

Mom sighs and hugs them. "Thank you for being honest with me. I am not happy that you broke the mirror, but I am glad that you told me the truth. You know that lying is wrong, right?"

Sara and Ben nod. They know that lying is wrong. They feel a little better.

"Next time, be more careful and respectful with the things you find in the attic. And don't fight with each other. You are twins, you should love and help each other. Do you understand?"

Sara and Ben nod again. They understand. They say sorry to each other and hug. They love each other.

Mom smiles and kisses them. "I love you both. Now, let's clean up this mess and go downstairs for a snack. How does that sound?"

Sara and Ben smile too. They say yes and help Mom pick up the pieces of the mirror. They feel happy and hungry. They go downstairs for a snack.

Once upon a time, there was a farmer who had a big red barn. It was his own barn and he loved it very much. He had many animals like cows, pigs, and horses that lived in the barn. The farmer would go to the barn every morning to feed and take care of his animals.

One day, a little girl came to the farm. She saw the big red barn and thought it was sweet. She asked the farmer if she could see inside the barn. The farmer said yes and showed her all the animals. The little girl was so happy and said that she wished she could own a barn like this one someday.

The farmer smiled and said that maybe one day she could. He was happy to share his barn with the little girl and show her how much he loved it. From that day on, the little girl always remembered the sweet barn and the kind farmer who let her see inside.

Once upon a time, there was a little mouse. The mouse was not a normal mouse. It had a long tail that could attach to things. One day, the mouse went to the park to play.

At the park, the mouse saw a big ball. The mouse wanted to play with the ball. So, it used its long tail to attach to the ball. Then, the mouse and the ball rolled around the park. They had lots of fun.

A little boy saw the mouse and the ball. The boy said, "Wow! You are not a normal mouse! Can I play with you?" The mouse nodded its head. The boy, the mouse, and the ball played all day. They were very happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a cat named Mittens who had soft fur that she loved to pet. One day, Mittens got very dirty and Lily knew she had to give her a bath. She was a little scared because Mittens didn't like water, but she managed to get her in the bathtub.

After the bath, Mittens was wet and looked very different. Her fur was all flat and not as soft as before. Lily was worried that Mittens wasn't going to be as pretty as she was before, but her mom told her that Mittens was still cute, just in an ordinary way. Lily realized that even though Mittens didn't look the same, she still loved her just as much.

Dave and his daughter had a happy life. Every day, they would go to the park and play together. Dave would load his daughter into the stroller while they went on walks. Together they were very healthy and strong.

One day, Dave and his daughter were out for a walk, but this time something was wrong. Suddenly, Dave started to feel weak. He asked his daughter to wait for him at the park, and he went home.

When he got there, he saw a man. The man said he was a doctor and that Dave was very sick. Dave was scared. He asked the doctor what was wrong and the doctor said he had a bad illness.

Dave was sad. He said goodbye to his daughter, not knowing if he would ever see her again. The doctor tried to do his best to make Dave feel healthy, but eventually Dave passed away.

His daughter was devastated. She cried and cried until her tears ran out. Dave was gone and her life was never the same again.

Katie woke up one morning and noticed her cereal was missing. She asked her mom where it had gone, but Mom didn't know. Katie was so hungry, she started to look everywhere for it. Soon, she saw something clumsy moving under the couch. It was her cereal! It was trying to hide! She jumped up and grabbed the box. Yay, now she could eat. She enjoyed her delicious cereal before going to play with her friends.

Once upon a time, there was a hairy cow named Bessie. Bessie lived on a big farm with her friends. She liked to play in the sun and eat green grass.

One day, Bessie met a new friend named Tim. Tim was a boy who liked to design things. He said to Bessie, "Let's make a fun game to play together!" Bessie was happy to have a new friend and a fun game.

Tim and Bessie worked together to design the game. They used big rocks and sticks to make it. When they were done, they played the game all day long. Bessie and Tim laughed and had a great time. They became best friends, and they loved to play their game on the farm.

Once, there was a little boy named Tim who had big dreams. He wanted to be the fastest runner in the world and he set out to make his dreams a reality. He started running on the track every day. He worked hard and got faster and faster.

One day, Tim's mom saw him running and said, "Timmy, why are you running so hard?". Tim looked up and smiled brightly. He said, "Mom, I'm working hard and running every day so I can be the fastest runner in the world!".

Tim's mom smiled and said, "That's very nice, Timmy. I believe you can do anything you set your mind to!"

Months passed and Tim kept practicing. One day, he was looking for a place to race. His mom noticed and asked him why he needed a race. Staring straight ahead and focused, he told her that he wanted to prove to everyone that he could succeed.

His mom, proud of her son, took him to the biggest race he could join, and Tim raced against all of the fastest runners in the world! Even though he was nervous, he worked hard and in the end, he won the race! Everyone was cheering him on and clapping.

Tim was so happy that he had succeeded, and he had made his dream come true. He ran back to his mom, hugged her tightly and said, "Mommy, I

Once upon a time, there was a small squirrel. The squirrel lived in a big oak tree. The oak tree was in a pretty park. The squirrel had a lot of friends in the park.

One sunny day, the squirrel and his friends played a fun game. They would shoot acorns with their tails. The acorns flew high into the sky. All the animals laughed and clapped.

At the end of the day, the small squirrel went back to his oak tree. He was happy and tired. He curled up in his cozy nest and went to sleep. The squirrel had a good day with his friends.

Once upon a time there was a little bear who loved to sit and admire the world around him. One day while sitting, he noticed a zip on the ground. He had never seen one before and he was very curious. He asked his mother what it was.

“That’s a zip,” she said. “It’s like a string that can open and close special pockets.”

The little bear started to get excited. He asked his mother if there were any zips available for him to use.

His mother smiled and said, “Yes, here you go!” She handed him a blue zip that he could use to open and close pockets on his own.

The little bear was so excited to have his own zip! He hugged his mother and ran off to play with his new toy. From that day forward, he loved to sit and open and close his pocket with his zip.

Once upon a time, there was a kind little girl who wanted to explore the sea. She put on her red swimming costume and headed to the beach. The sun was shining and the water was calm.

As she got closer to the sea, she noticed a dolphin in the distance. She was so happy to see it! But before she could get in the water, she remembered what her mum had told her: "Behave, little one".

"I promise to behave," she said aloud. She slowly stepped into the warm water and started swimming towards the dolphin. She wanted to get closer, so she came up with a plan.

She decided to stay quiet and get as close as she could. The dolphin became curious and came right up to her. The little girl was so excited she wanted to swim with the dolphin, but she remembered what her mum had said. She stayed quiet and calmly watched the dolphin.

The dolphin looked at her and then swam away. The little girl was so happy, she had managed to behave. She learned a valuable lesson that day - if we want something, we must stay quiet and be patient.

Once upon a time, there was a puppy called Terry. Terry was a very anxious pup, but he loved his owner very much. One day, Terry's owner came to him and said, "Terry, let's go out for a walk". His owner showed him a leash and said, "put this on and then let's go!". Terry was so excited that he began to jump around!

When Terry and his owner went outside, Terry saw lots of trees and a sidewalk. He was so excited to explore them! His owner said, "Let's read the signs along the sidewalk". Terry didn't know what that meant, but he trusted his owner and followed him along. They read signs about friendly dogs and leashes, and Terry learned that he had to stay close to his owner while they were walking.

After a while, they came back home. Terry was a bit anxious, but he learned a lot. He never forgot the lesson and always followed the leash while out on walks with his owner.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Anna. She liked to explore new places. One day, she wanted to go to the harbor. Her mom said yes, so they went together.

The harbor was big and busy. They watched boats come and go. Anna saw a big ship with thick ropes. It was so cool!

A friendly harbor worker saw Anna. He asked her, "Do you like the boats?" Anna smiled and nodded. She loved the boats.

The harbor worker asked Anna another question. He wanted to know, "Where do the boats go?" Anna didn't know the answer. But her mom helped her out. She said, "The boats go to many places around the world".

Anna was very happy. She had a great time at the harbor. She learned something new and even got to answer a question!

Once there was a goat. She was very helpful and looked after the farm where she lived. She used to always shut the farmer's gate after she went into the field to eat.

One day, a little boy came to visit the farm. He was only 3 years old and loved animals. He wanted to meet the goat. The goat was so nice and helpful and she helped the little boy open the farm gate.

The little boy said hello and the goat was so happy. They played together in the field. When they were finished, the goat helped the boy shut the gate. The goat was so helpful and the boy waved goodbye and thanked her.

The goat was happy to have made a new friend. She waved goodbye and smiled. The little boy walked away with a smile on his face, knowing that he had made a new friend.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a purple dress that she loved to wear. One day, Lily and her grandma went for a walk. Her grandma used a cane to help her walk.

As they walked, they saw a pretty butterfly. Lily wanted to catch it, but it flew away too fast. Her grandma said, "Remember, butterflies are very fast!"

Lily and her grandma continued their walk and saw a big tree. They sat down under the tree and rested for a bit. Lily looked up at the leaves and saw a bird's nest. She pointed to it and said, "Look, Grandma! A bird's house!"

After their rest, Lily and her grandma continued their walk with the purple dress swishing and the cane tapping along. They had a lovely time together.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who was very excited to play outside. She asked her mommy if she could go outside and play. Her mommy said yes, but only if she wore her coat.

Lily didn't want to wear her coat because she was too excited to play. She refused to put it on and ran outside without it. She played for a while, but then it started to get cold. She wanted to go back inside, but the door was locked.

Lily was stuck outside in the cold and she started to shiver. She looked up and saw the curtain in her bedroom window. She knew her mommy was inside, but she couldn't get her attention. Lily was sad and cold, and wished she had listened to her mommy and worn her coat.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy had to take an exam at school. He was very nervous because he had never taken an exam before.

On the day of the exam, Timmy's teacher gave him a piece of paper and told him to open it. Timmy was surprised to see that there were pictures on the paper. He thought exams were only for writing!

Timmy looked at the pictures and answered the questions. He felt happy when he was done because he did his best. Timmy's teacher was proud of him for taking the exam and trying his hardest.

Once there was a girl. Every day, she would feed the birds. One day, there was an uncomfortable earthquake. The girl jumped in fear. She ran away and hid, but when the earthquake was over, she felt brave. She went out and started to feed the birds again. It felt good to help the birds in spite of feeling uncomfortable. The girl went home happy.

It was time to celebrate! The family was so excited as they got on the subway. It felt like they were going to a distant place. As they went on the subway, everyone laughed and talked about all the fun they would have.

When they arrived at their destination, their eyes lit up. They saw a big park full of tall trees and colorful flowers. There were swings and slides everywhere and the kids were so excited.

The family spent the day playing and laughing. They went on rides, ate cotton candy and built sandcastles. Everyone had a lot of fun and was so happy to spend quality time with each other.

Towards the end of the day, the family gathered around for a group hug. They were so thankful for the special day and for the time they got to celebrate together. They smiled, hugged and laughed as the sun began to set in the distant sky.

The family made so many memories that they would never forget. They said goodbye to the park and happily got back on the subway back home.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the park with her friends. One day, Lily found a shiny coin on the ground. She picked it up and showed it to her friend, Timmy.

"Look what I got, Timmy! It's a coin!" said Lily.

"Wow, that's so cool! You're so strong for finding it," replied Timmy.

Lily felt proud of herself for being strong and finding the coin. She decided to save it in her piggy bank at home. From that day on, Lily always looked for coins when she played outside with her friends. She wanted to get more coins and become even stronger.

One day, it began to rain. The rain was soft and gentle, and it felt nice against the grass. The lawn was a beautiful, lush green, and stretched on for a long way. In the distant sky, there was a brilliant rainbow.

The rain kept coming, and it was so much fun to play in. The children jumped and splashed, and soon they were so wet and muddy! The grass was so soft beneath their feet, and the entire lawn was full of laughter and joy.

The rain eventually slowed to a stop, but the children were still happy. They had enjoyed the rain, and the distant rainbow in the sky. They waved goodbye to each other, and then went back to their homes.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to draw and color with her crayons. One day, Lily wanted to make a special picture for her mommy. She got out her paper and crayons and started to draw.

Lily was very creative and drew a big flower with lots of petals. She wanted to make the flower even more special, so she decided to spread some honey on the petals. She took a spoon and carefully spread the honey on the petals of the flower. The honey made the flower look shiny and sticky.

When Lily's mommy saw the picture, she was so happy and proud of her creative little girl. She could see the honey on the petals and smiled. Lily was so happy that her mommy loved her picture. From that day on, Lily loved to spread honey on all of her pictures to make them extra special.

Once upon a time, there was a girl called Anna. She had a room that was full of toys and games. One day, Anna had a brilliant idea. She decided to set up a pretend shop in her room.

Her mum found some old boxes and crates in the garage and Anna set them up around her room. She filled her boxes with small toys and things to make a shop. She was very excited!

Anna ran around the house to find all the things she wanted. She used soft toys, blocks and things from the kitchen. Once everything was ready, Anna stepped back and saw her brilliant room. It was full of fun things to pretend.

Anna's mum was so proud of her! She spent the whole afternoon playing shop. It was great fun.

Anna had created a wonderful world using her imagination. She had made something really special in her room.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Bryan. He was only three years old and very anxious about his first day of school. His Mum was at his side, and she wanted to encourage him.

“You can do it,” she said. She held his ears, so he could feel her warmth.

“I’m scared,” said Bryan.

Mum smiled brightly. “It’s okay, I’m here. I’ll be right here when you come out.”

Bryan nodded and took a deep breath. He couldn’t believe he was really going to do it. With a final look at Mum, Bryan walked into school.

Mum stayed outside and waited. After an hour or so, Bryan came out with a smile on his face.

“How was it?” Mum asked.

“Good!” said Bryan.

Mum was very happy to see that she had encouraged him. She hugged Bryan and told him the same thing: “You can do it!”

And from then on, Bryan knew he could do anything if he just believed in himself.

Once there was a boy named Steve who always liked to keep very clean. He washed his hands carefully, brushed his teeth every day and made sure his clothes were neat and tidy.

One day, Steve was sitting in the garden, daydreaming about all the things he could do to stay clean. He thought about a pleasant image he'd seen, an image of himself being very clean.

Just then, he heard his mom calling. She asked him to help with chores, to help clean the garden. Steve smiled and said "Yes, mom!"

Steve began cleaning the garden. He dug deep into the dirt and pulled out vegetable scraps and weeds. He planted beautiful flowers and watered them carefully. Finally, he felt satisfied seeing the lovely, clean garden.

Steve had done a great job. His mom praised him, saying, "Your hard work has created a deep and beautiful image in the garden."

That made Steve smile. He was happy that his hard work had created such a pleasant image. He had created something wonderful.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Rachel. Rachel loved to ride her bike. She asked her mom if she could ride outside. Her mom said yes and told her to be careful.

Rachel got on her bike and rode around in circles. She was having so much fun! Then she noticed something huge on the other side of the street. Rachel thought it was a table.

Rachel was curious, so she decided to take a closer look. She got off her bike and walked over to the table. When she got closer, she couldn't believe her eyes. It was an enormous table!

Rachel said to herself, "I wish I could ride this table!" Then she heard a voice say, "You can ride it if you want!"

Rachel looked around and she saw a fairy. The fairy said, "I can make your wish come true. Just hop on the table and the magic will begin!"

Rachel was so excited! She hopped onto the huge table and closed her eyes. Suddenly, the table started to move. Rachel was riding the table! She was amazed and shouted out in joy, "This is so much fun!"

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lucy. She had a rag doll named Daisy. Lucy loved Daisy very much. She would hug Daisy every day and night. They were the best of friends.

One sunny day, Lucy and Daisy went to the fair. There were many fun rides and games. Lucy and Daisy went on the merry-go-round. They laughed and smiled as they went round and round. After that, they played a game where they had to throw a ball to win a prize. Lucy threw the ball and won a big blue teddy bear.

"Wow, I won a new friend for us!" Lucy said to Daisy. "Let's all hug!" So, Lucy hugged Daisy and the blue teddy bear. They were all very happy.

At the end of the day, Lucy, Daisy, and the blue teddy bear were tired. They went back home and got ready for bed. Lucy put Daisy and the blue teddy bear next to her on the bed. She hugged them both and said, "Good night, Daisy. Good night, blue teddy bear. I love you both."

And with that, Lucy, Daisy, and the blue teddy bear closed their eyes and went to sleep, dreaming of more fun days at the fair.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved playing with sand at the beach. One day, she went to the beach with her mom and dad. She was very excited to play with the sand.

Lily's mom and dad were setting up their beach chairs when Lily saw a boy playing with a sandcastle. She ran over to him and asked if she could play too. The boy said, "No, I don't want to share my sand." Lily felt sad and impatient.

Lily's mom saw her daughter's face and asked her what was wrong. Lily said, "The boy won't let me play with his sand. I want to display my sandcastle too." Lily's mom told her not to worry and they went to find their own spot to play with the sand. They built a beautiful sandcastle and had lots of fun together.

Lily and Ben were eager to play outside. They saw a big barrel in the yard. They wondered what was inside.

"Let's open it!" Lily said.

"Maybe it has toys or candy!" Ben said.

They ran to the barrel and lifted the lid. They saw nothing but water. They felt sad.

"Aw, it's just water," Lily said.

"Wait, look!" Ben said. He pointed to something shiny in the water. It was a necklace with a star pendant.

"Wow, it's so pretty!" Lily said.

"Maybe it's magic!" Ben said.

He took the necklace and put it around his neck. He closed his eyes and made a wish.

"I wish I could fly!" he said.

He opened his eyes and jumped. He felt a breeze under his feet. He was flying!

"Lily, look! I can fly!" he said.

Lily couldn't believe it. She saw Ben flying in the air. She clapped her hands and laughed.

"Ben, that's amazing!" she said.

"Come on, Lily! You can fly too!" Ben said.

He flew down and gave Lily the necklace. She put it around her neck and made a wish.

"I wish I could fly with Ben!" she said.

She opened her eyes and jumped. She felt a breeze under her feet. She was flying too!

"Yay, we can fly!" she said.

They flew together in the sky. They felt happy and free. They believed the necklace was magic. They didn't know it was just their imagination.

Tom and Jen are friends. They like to play with toys. One day, they find a big box. They want to make a house with the box. They need to cut the box with scissors.

"Can I cut the box?" Tom asks Jen.

"No, I want to cut the box," Jen says.

They both grab the scissors. They pull and pull. The scissors break. Tom and Jen are sad.

A cop sees them. He is walking his dog. He stops and asks, "What are you doing, kids?"

"We want to make a house with the box, but the scissors broke," Tom says.

The cop smiles. He says, "I have a knife. I can help you cut the box. But you have to be careful. Knives are sharp and can hurt you."

"Thank you, cop," Jen says.

The cop cuts the box for them. He makes a door and a window. He gives them the knife. He says, "You can cut some more, but only with my help. And don't cut yourself or the dog."

Tom and Jen are happy. They say, "You are a good cop. You are not weak. You are strong and kind."

They play with the box house and the dog. The cop watches them. He is happy too. He likes to help kids. He likes to play with toys.

Once upon a time there was a little girl. Her name was Sammy and she just turned three years old.

Sammy was feeling brave one day, so she wanted to go to a restaurant. Her mommy wanted Sammy to stay at home, but she urged her to come. Sammy got scared.

But her mommy said that it would be fun, so Sammy agreed to go. Mommy and Sammy went to a restaurant. Sammy was surprised. The restaurant was big and loud and a little bit scary. Mommy said it was ok and urged Sammy to sit down.

At the end, Sammy had a lot of fun!

Once upon a time, there was a princess who lived far away. She was so far that no one knew where she was.

One day, a brave boy wanted to find the princess. He looked and looked, up high and down low. Finally, he saw something far away. Could it be the princess?

The boy ran as fast as he could until he caught up to her. He was so happy!

They ran around, playing and laughing together. They even sang a song. Eventually, it was time for the boy to go home. But before he left, the princess gave him a big hug and said goodbye.

The boy had caught the princess! He was so excited. He held on to the hug from the princess, and walked back home with a smile on his face.

Once there was a mom and a dad. They had a little girl. Her name was Cathy.

One day, the mom said, "Cathy, let's go for a walk!" So Cathy said, "Good!"

They went to the park. Cathy's dad said, "Cathy, wait here. I'll be back soon." So Cathy said, "Good!"

Cathy waited and waited and waited. Finally, her dad came back. He said, "Cathy, let's go home now." So Cathy said, "Good!"

They all went home together. The mom and dad said, "Cathy, it was fun! We had a good time."

And Cathy said, "Good!"

Lila liked to read books. She had many books in her room. She read them every day. She learned new things from the books. She was happy.

One day, Lila saw a big trunk in the attic. She was curious. She opened the trunk. She found more books inside. She was excited. She wanted to read them all.

She took some books from the trunk and went to her room. She read them one by one. She liked the stories. She did not hear her mom calling her for dinner. She did not hear her dad coming home. She did not hear the fire alarm.

The trunk had a secret. It was a magic trunk. It made the books come alive. But it also made the books burn. The books caught fire in Lila's room. The fire spread to the attic. The fire reached the trunk. The trunk exploded.

Lila did not see the fire. She did not smell the smoke. She did not feel the heat. She was too busy reading. She did not notice anything until it was too late. She screamed. But no one heard her. She was trapped. She was scared. She was sorry.

The firemen came. They tried to save Lila. But they could not. The fire was too big. The house was too damaged. Lila was gone. The books were gone. The trunk was gone.

Lila's mom and dad were sad. They cried. They wished they had been more generous with Lila. They wished they had spent more time with her. They wished they had told her they loved her. They wished they had never found the trunk.

Once upon a time there was a gentle giant. He was so gentle that no one ever heard him speak a loud word.

The giant was walking through a forest one day when he heard a small voice calling out. He wondered who it could be and followed the sound until he saw a 3 year old child.

The child had been playing and accidentally destroyed his toy car. He was sitting there crying and the giant felt so sad for him. The giant wanted to help so he crouched down and softly said, "Don't worry, there's an easier way to fix this".

The child was surprised and looked up to see the giant. He asked, "How?"

The giant smiled and replied, "We can use our gentle words to put it back together". The child thought and then tried to say the words, eventually piecing the car back together. He was so happy and thanked the giant.

The giant grinned and said, "See, sometimes gentle words can do more than destroy".

Once there was a boy named Jack. He was only three years old and loved to bounce!

One day, Jack went to the park. He was so excited to bounce around! He ran all around the park, bouncing whenever he could.

But then something sad happened. Jack tripped and hurt his leg. He started to cry because it really hurt.

Luckily, his mom saw him, ran over, and picked him up. She hugged him tight and said, "It's ok. Let's find a bench to sit down and rest."

Jack and his mom sat down and Jack stopped crying. He looked out at the park and smiled. Even though he was sad, he still loved to bounce!

Lily and Ben were best friends. They liked to play in the park with their dog Spot. Spot was a loyal dog. He always followed them and helped them.

One day, Lily and Ben found a basket in the park. It had some bread and cheese and fruit in it. Lily and Ben were hungry. They decided to eat the food in the basket.

But the basket was not for them. It was for an old lady who lived near the park. She was sick and had no food. A kind man had brought the basket for her. He had left it on a bench while he went to get some water.

When the man came back, he saw Lily and Ben eating the food. He was angry. He shouted at them and took the basket away. He said they were bad and selfish.

Lily and Ben felt sorry. They did not know the basket was for the old lady. They wanted to say sorry, but the man did not listen. He walked away with the basket.

Spot saw the man walking away. He thought the man was bad. He wanted to serve Lily and Ben. He ran after the man and bit his leg.

The man screamed and dropped the basket. He kicked Spot and ran away.

Spot was hurt. He whimpered and limped back to Lily and Ben. They hugged him and cried. They loved Spot. He was a loyal dog.

But the old lady had no food. She was hungry and sad. She waited for the man to come back, but he did not. She felt sick and cold. She had no one to help her.

The end.

One day, there was a little girl named Lily who loved listening to jazz music. She had a cute teddy bear named Teddy who always danced with her. One day, Lily's mom asked her, "Lily, do you want to learn how to play jazz music?"

Lily's eyes lit up with excitement and she replied, "Yes, please!" Her mom smiled and said, "Okay, let's go to the music store and buy you a cute little saxophone."

At the music store, Lily picked out a shiny red saxophone and started to learn how to play jazz. She practiced every day and soon she was able to play a beautiful jazz tune. Teddy was so proud of her and danced along to the music.

One day, Lily's dad came home from work and heard her playing jazz on her saxophone. He was so impressed that he said, "Lily, you are amazing! I didn't know you could play jazz so well." Lily smiled and replied, "Thanks, Dad! I learned how to play from my mom."

Once upon a time there was a girl who loved pretty jewelry. She always wanted to have many shiny necklaces and sparkly earrings, so one day she went to a store to buy them. But in the store, all of the jewelry was very expensive and the girl didn't have enough money.

She walked away sadly, feeling very disappointed. On her way home, she saw her friend with a shiny new car. The girl asked him where he got it from, and he said that he had worked hard and saved up his money until he could buy it.

The girl was inspired by her friend's story, so she decided to start putting some money away every day so that one day she could buy the pretty jewelry she had wanted. In time, she saved enough money and went back to the store to buy her jewelry.

This story teaches us that if we work hard and aim for something, we can achieve it. Rather than try and take shortcuts, it's better to save up and drive towards our dreams.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Sue. She had a big exam at school. Sue was scared. She wanted to do well on her exam.

Sue's mom said, "Don't worry, Sue. I will make you a delicious snack. It will help you think better." Sue's mom made her a yummy sandwich. Sue ate it and felt happy.

Before the exam, Sue rubbed her hands together. She said, "I can do it!" Sue took the exam and did great. She was very proud of herself. Sue and her mom celebrated with more delicious snacks.

Anna and Ben like to play with trains. They have a big box of trains and tracks. They make long and short trains. They make loops and bridges. They have fun.

One day, they see a real train outside. It is big and loud. It has smoke and steam. They run to the window and watch. They want to ride the train.

"Can we go on the train, Mom?" Anna asks.

"Maybe another day, dear. The train is not for us. It is for people who go far away," Mom says.

"But I want to see the steam. It is white and thin. It goes up and up," Ben says.

"I know, Ben. The steam is very pretty. But the train is very fast. It is not safe for little kids. You have to mind the train," Mom says.

Anna and Ben are sad. They want to go on the train. They look at their box of trains. They have an idea.

They take out their trains and tracks. They make a big train. They put a kettle on the stove. They wait for the water to boil.

When the water boils, the kettle makes a whistle. It makes steam. Anna and Ben take the kettle and put it behind their train. They pretend it is the engine. They make train noises.

"Choo choo! Look, Mom, we have steam!" Anna says.

"Wow, you do! That is very clever. You made your own train with steam," Mom says.

Anna and Ben smile. They are happy. They play with their train with steam. They mind the kettle. They have fun.

Once upon a time, there was a pirate named Tom. Tom loved to kick a big, heavy ball. One day, he saw a little boy named Tim. Tim was sad because he lost his ball.

"Hi, Tim! Why are you sad?" asked Tom the pirate.

"I lost my ball," said Tim. "Can you help me find it?"

Tom and Tim looked for the ball. They looked under a tree and behind a rock. At last, they found the ball near a big, heavy box.

"Thank you, Tom!" said Tim. "Let's play together!"

Tom and Tim kicked the ball and had lots of fun. They played until the sun went down. Tim was happy, and Tom the pirate made a new friend.

Tommy loves hockey. He has a hockey stick and a ball. He plays hockey in the yard with his dad. Sometimes, his dad lets him wear a helmet and gloves. Tommy feels like a big hockey star.

One day, Tommy sees an enormous bird in the sky. It is black and white and has a long neck. Tommy thinks it is a hockey bird. He wants to play hockey with it. He runs inside and gets some bread. He breaks the bread into small pieces and puts them in his pocket.

He goes back outside and calls the bird. "Hey, hockey bird! Come here! I have something for you!" Tommy waves his hockey stick and throws some bread on the ground. The bird sees the bread and flies down. It lands near Tommy and eats the bread. Tommy is happy. He thinks the bird likes him.

"Can you play hockey with me, hockey bird?" Tommy asks. He gives the bird his ball and taps it with his stick. The bird looks at the ball and pecks it. It makes a loud honk. Tommy laughs. He thinks the bird is funny.

The bird honks again and flaps its wings. It picks up the ball in its beak and flies away. Tommy is sad. He wants his ball back. He runs after the bird and shouts. "Hey, hockey bird! Give me my ball! That's not fair!"

But the bird does not listen. It flies higher and higher until Tommy cannot see it anymore. Tommy stops and cries. He lost his ball and his hockey friend. He wishes the bird would come back.

His dad sees him and comes over. He hugs Tommy and wipes his tears. He says, "Don't worry, Tommy. That was not a hockey bird. That was a goose. Geese are not good at playing hockey. They are good at flying and swimming. Maybe it will bring your ball back someday. But for now, I have a surprise for you."

He takes Tommy inside and shows him a new hockey ball. It is red and shiny and has a star on it. Tommy smiles. He likes his new ball. He says, "Thank you, dad. You are the best. Can we play hockey now?"

His dad nods and smiles. He says, "Of course, Tommy. Let's go. But first, let's feed the cat. She is hungry too." He gives Tommy some cat food and a bowl. Tommy feeds the cat and pets her. She purrs and rubs against him. Tommy thinks she is nice.

He grabs his hockey stick and his new ball and runs outside with his dad. They play hockey in the yard until it gets dark. Tommy has fun. He forgets about the goose and the old ball. He thinks hockey is the best game ever.

Once upon a time, there was a kind boy named Jimmy. He was very honest and always tried to do the right thing. One day, he was feeling very curious and decided to take a look inside the big wardrobe in his bedroom. He opened the door, and peeked inside. He was surprised to see a tiny creature!

"Hello!" said Jimmy.

The creature smiled and said, "Hello! My name is Benny. I like to play hide and seek."

Jimmy was excited. He and Benny played together for a while, until suddenly, Benny bit Jimmy! Jimmy was confused and asked, "Why did you do that?"

Benny replied, "I just wanted to make sure you were honest. See, I can only stay with someone who is honest."

Jimmy was sad and said, "I am honest. I promise!"

Benny nodded his head and said, "Then I won't bite again. Let's go back to playing hide and seek!" From that day forward, Jimmy and Benny were the best of friends. They played together all the time, and Jimmy never stopped being honest!

Once upon a time, there was a little cowgirl named Jenny. She lived in a big ranch with her parents and animals.

One day, Jenny was walking outside and saw a big horse standing far away. She stopped and stared at it for a long time. Jenny was so amazed, she felt so calm watching the horse.

She walked closer and closer, until she was right in front of the horse. But the horse seemed very scared and backed away.

Jenny was sad, she wanted to be friends with the horse. So she said something very softly.

"Hello there, don't be scared. I won't hurt you, I promise."

The horse seemed to understand her, and slowly came closer. It looked Jenny in the eyes and stayed very still and calm. Even though Jenny was still scared, she was very happy.

So they both continued to stare at each other. The horse and the little cowgirl from the ranch. And from that day on, they were best friends forever.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys all day long. One day, her mom gave her a task to clean up her room. Lily didn't want to do it because she wanted to play more. But her mom told her that it was an important task to do.

Lily started to clean up her room slowly. She didn't know how to add all her toys together in one place. She was getting frustrated and wanted to give up. But then, she remembered her mom's words and decided to be intelligent. She started to group her toys by color and put them in their right place.

After she finished, she felt proud of herself for completing the task. Her mom came in and saw how clean her room was. She hugged Lily and told her how proud she was of her. From that day on, Lily learned that completing tasks is important and it feels good to be intelligent and do your best.

Once upon a time there was a compassionate lady. She wanted to help everyone and make them smile.

One day she decided to enter the park early in the morning. She noticed a small group of children in the corner. She crept closer to say hello and saw they were very sad.

"What's the matter?" she asked.

"We are sad because we don't know how to start the game," one of the children explained.

The compassionate lady knew just what to do. She helped them decide what game to play.

"Let's play tag!" she said.

The children were so excited they started jumping up and down.

"Let's play!" they shouted and soon they were running around the park together.

The compassionate lady smiled and watched them enjoy the game. She left the park happy to know that she had helped the children have fun.

Once upon a time, there was a little mouse. He loved to play hide and seek with his friends. One day, he was playing in the garden when he heard a loud noise. He got scared and ran to hide under a leaf.

After a while, the noise stopped and he came out of his hiding spot. But then he saw that his cheese was gone! He looked around and saw his friend, the cat, with a full tummy. The mouse got upset and asked the cat why he ate his cheese. The cat apologized and promised to never do it again.

From that day on, the mouse was careful to hide his cheese in a safe place where the cat couldn't find it. And they continued to play hide and seek together, but the mouse always made sure to keep an eye on his cheese. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play outside. He would run and jump and have so much fun. One day, Timmy decided to use a long stick to draw in the sand. He drew a picture of a big castle on the land.

As he was drawing, he saw a little bird with a long tail. The bird was hopping around and chirping happily. Timmy smiled and waved at the bird. The bird flew away, but Timmy continued to draw in the sand.

When he was finished, Timmy stood back and looked at his picture. He was proud of what he had created. He decided to show his picture to his mom and dad. They were so impressed by Timmy's drawing that they hung it up on the fridge for everyone to see. Timmy was so happy and proud.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She was very excited because her family was going on a trip to the beach. She packed her bags with all her favorite toys and clothes, but she forgot one thing - her favorite book.

When they arrived at the beach house, Lily's mom asked her to unpack her bags. Lily was happy to help and started taking out all her things. Suddenly, she found a note from her grandma. It said, "Dear Lily, I hope you have a powerful imagination to make new memories at the beach."

Lily didn't understand what "powerful" meant, so she asked her mom. "Mommy, what does 'powerful' mean?" she asked. Her mom explained that it meant strong and full of energy.

Lily smiled and said, "I will use my powerful imagination to have fun at the beach!" And with that, she ran outside to play in the sand and waves.

Molly was very creative. She loved to make things. One day, she asked her older sister for help.

"Sister, can you help me make something?" Molly asked.

"Sure," her sister smiled.

Molly told her sister what she wanted to make. They collected sticks, rocks, and bright leaves they found on the ground.

Molly and her sister made a beautiful garden with the things they found. They mixed the rocks and sticks and the bright leaves to make it colorful.

Molly was so happy. She showed off her creative garden to her mom, who was so proud of her.

The end.

Tom and Sue like to play with their toy boat. They take it to the pond and sail it on the water. They have fun watching it go fast and slow, left and right.

One day, they see a big fat duck on the pond. The duck is hungry and looks at their boat. It thinks it is food. It swims towards it and opens its mouth.

"Look out, Tom!" Sue shouts. "The duck wants our boat!"

Tom tries to pull the boat back, but it is too late. The duck bites the boat and breaks it. It makes a loud quack and swims away.

Tom and Sue are sad. They cry and hug each other. They have no boat to play with anymore.

They go home and tell their mom what happened. She is sorry for them, but she is also angry. She says they should not have taken the boat to the pond. She says it was her laundry basket and she needs it to wash their clothes.

Tom and Sue feel bad. They say they are sorry and they will not do it again. They help their mom with the laundry, but they still miss their boat. They wish they had a real boat that the duck could not eat.

Lily and Ben are friends. They like to play and joke with each other. One day, they go to the park with their moms. They see a big slide and run to it.

Lily goes first. She slides down fast and laughs. Ben waits for his turn. He wants to joke with Lily. He thinks of a funny thing to do. He slides down with his foot up in the air. He hopes Lily will see his foot and laugh too.

But Lily does not see his foot. She only sees his face. She thinks he is making a funny face at her. She laughs and says, "You look silly, Ben!" Ben is confused. He looks at his foot and says, "No, look at my foot, Lily! It is a joke!"

Lily looks at his foot and sees it in the air. She does not think it is funny. She thinks it is rude. She says, "That is not a joke, Ben! That is mean! You should not put your foot up like that. It is not fair to the other kids. They might get hurt by your foot."

Ben feels bad. He did not mean to be mean. He only wanted to make Lily laugh. He says, "I am sorry, Lily. I did not know it was mean. I will not do it again. Can we still be friends?"

Lily thinks for a moment. She sees that Ben is sorry. She says, "OK, Ben. I forgive you. But you have to be careful with your foot. And you have to find better jokes. Can you do that?"

Ben nods. He says, "Yes, Lily. I can do that. Thank you for being my friend. You are very fair."

They hug and smile. They go to play some more. They have fun and joke with each other. But they do not use their feet. They use their words.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved to play in the park. She had a favorite toy, a stuffed bear named Ted. One day, Lily accidentally left Ted on a bench and went home without him.

The next day, Lily went back to the park to look for Ted, but he was gone. She asked everyone she saw if they had seen her bear, but no one had. Lily was very sad and cried a lot.

But then, a kind lady came up to Lily and said she had found Ted and brought him to the police station. Lily was so happy to be reunited with her beloved bear. She learned that it's important to follow the law and not leave things behind, but also that there are good people who will help you when you need it. She felt peaceful knowing that Ted was back where he belonged, with her.

Tom and Sue were twins who liked to play outside. One day, they saw a big chimney on a house near their yard. They wondered what was inside the chimney and how it worked.

"Let's go look at the chimney," Tom said. "Maybe we can see smoke or fire or something."

"OK, but be careful," Sue said. "Mom said chimneys can be hot and dirty and dangerous."

They ran to the house and climbed on a pile of wood next to the chimney. They looked up and saw a round hole at the top of the chimney. They could not see anything inside.

"Maybe we can hear something," Tom said. He put his ear to the chimney and listened. He heard a soft rumbling sound.

"What is that?" Sue asked.

"I don't know," Tom said. "Maybe it's a monster or a dragon or something."

They got scared and jumped off the wood. They ran back to their yard.

They did not know that the chimney belonged to Mr. Brown, who was baking a cake in his oven. The rumbling sound was the fan that blew the hot air in the oven. Mr. Brown was not a monster or a dragon, but a nice old man who liked to share his cakes with the children.

Later that day, Mr. Brown came to their yard with a plate of cake. He smiled and said, "Hello, Tom and Sue. I made a cake for you. Do you want some?"

Tom and Sue looked at each other and felt silly. They realized that they had been stupid to think that there was something scary in the chimney. They thanked Mr. Brown and took a piece of cake.

They learned that chimneys were not for monsters or dragons, but for baking cakes. They also learned that they should not judge things by their looks, but by their tastes.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Daisy. Daisy was curious to explore the world. One day, she found herself standing in front of a palm tree. She thought it was a very beautiful tree.

Daisy asked her mum what was so special about the trees, her mum replied, “Well, palm trees have long leaves, and this one probably used to belong to someone.”

Daisy was even more curious and asked her mum, “Where did the person go?” Her mum replied, “The person moved away.” Daisy looked sad as she didn’t want the tree to be alone.

Suddenly, Daisy had a great idea. She said to her mum, “Let’s play a game. We can pretend to be the arms of the tree and hug the tree. That way, the palm tree won’t feel alone.”

Daisy and her mum hugged the palm tree like two loving arms. Daisy was filled with joy and the joy made the tree even more beautiful.

The End.

Anna and Ben are twins. They like to play in the park with their dog, Max. Max is a big dog, but he is very cute and friendly. He likes to run and chase balls and sticks. Anna and Ben love Max very much.

One day, they go to the park with their mom. They see a new boy there. He has a small cat in his arms. The cat is black and white and has a pink bow on her head. The boy sees Anna and Ben and says, "Hi, I'm Tom. This is my cat, Lily. Do you want to play with us?"

Anna and Ben smile and say, "Yes, we do. We're Anna and Ben. This is our dog, Max. He is very cute and friendly, too."

They go to a bench and sit down. Tom puts Lily on his lap and pets her. Anna and Ben pet Max and talk to Tom. They tell him about their favorite games and toys and books. Tom tells them about his cat and his school and his family. They have a lot of fun.

But then, something bad happens. A big, mean dog comes to the park. He is not on a leash. He sees Lily and barks loudly. He runs towards them. He wants to hurt Lily.

Tom is scared. He hugs Lily and says, "Go away, bad dog! Leave us alone!"

Anna and Ben are scared, too. They don't know what to do. They look at their mom, but she is far away. She doesn't see the bad dog.

But Max sees the bad dog. He knows his job. He has to protect his friends. He jumps off the bench and runs to the bad dog. He growls and shows his teeth. He says, "Stop, bad dog! You can't hurt Lily! She is my friend! Go away, or I will bite you!"

The bad dog is surprised. He sees Max and stops. He is afraid of Max. He thinks Max is bigger and stronger than him. He doesn't want to fight. He turns around and runs away.

Max chases him until he is out of the park. Then he comes back to the bench. He wags his tail and licks Anna and Ben and Tom and Lily. He is happy. He did his job. He protected his friends.

Anna and Ben and Tom and Lily hug Max and say, "Thank you, Max! You are a hero! You are the best dog ever!"

Max barks and smiles. He is proud. He is a hero. He is the best dog ever.

Lily and Ben were playing in the park with their ball. They liked to kick the ball to each other and run after it. They were having fun and laughing.

But then, the sun started to go down and the sky became dark. Lily and Ben saw their shadows on the ground. They looked big and scary. Lily and Ben felt afraid.

They heard a loud noise behind a tree. It sounded like a growl. Lily and Ben thought it was an unknown animal that wanted to hurt them. They dropped their ball and ran to their mom.

"Mom, mom, help!" they shouted. "There is a monster in the park!"

Mom hugged them and said, "Don't worry, my loves. There is no monster. It was just a dog. He was barking because he wanted to play with your ball. He is a friendly dog. See, he is wagging his tail."

Lily and Ben looked at the dog. He was not big and scary. He was small and cute. He had brown fur and black spots. He was holding their ball in his mouth.

Lily and Ben smiled. They were not afraid anymore. They went to the dog and petted him. He licked their faces and gave them their ball back.

"Can we play with him, mom?" they asked.

"Sure, if his owner says yes. Look, there he is. He is waving at us. He is sorry for scaring you. He says his dog's name is Spot."

Lily and Ben said hello to the owner and Spot. They played with them until it was time to go home. They had fun and made new friends. They learned that shadows and unknown noises are not always monsters. Sometimes, they are just dogs.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lily. She wanted to go on a trip to the park with her mommy. They packed some snacks and a ball to play with.

Lily asked her mommy, "Are we there yet?" Her mommy said, "Not yet, but we will complete our trip soon."

They walked and walked until they reached the park. Lily saw a big slide and ran towards it. But her mommy said, "Wait, let's find a dependable spot to sit and eat our snacks first."

After they ate, they played with the ball and went on the slide. Lily had so much fun on her trip with her mommy. She said, "This was the best trip ever!"

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a garden with lots of pretty flowers and herbs. One day, her friend Timmy came over to play.

"Wow, Lily! Your garden is so pretty! Can we pick some flowers?" asked Timmy.

"No, Timmy. We can't pick the flowers. They are not available for picking," replied Lily.

Timmy looked sad, but then he saw the herbs. "What are these?" he asked.

"They are herbs. We can discuss what they are used for," said Lily.

As they were discussing, a big storm came and destroyed all of Lily's flowers and herbs. Lily and Timmy were very sad. "Now we can't play in the garden anymore," said Timmy.

"I know. It's very sad," said Lily. They hugged each other and went inside to play indoors.

Lila and Ben are friends who like to play in the park. One day, they see a big truck with a picture of a rhinoceros on it. They run to the truck and ask the man who is driving it, "What is that?"

The man smiles and says, "That is a rhinoceros. It is a big animal with a horn on its nose. It lives in Africa, where it is very hot and dry. I work for a zoo, and I am taking the rhinoceros to a new home where it will be happy and safe."

Lila and Ben are curious and want to see the rhinoceros. The man says, "You can see it, but you have to be very quiet and gentle. The rhinoceros is scared of new things and noises. Follow me, and I will show you."

The man leads them to the back of the truck, where there is a big cage with a door. He opens the door and says, "Look, there he is. His name is Rocco. He is very strong and brave, but he also likes to eat and sleep a lot. He likes to eat leaves and grass, and he likes to drink water. The zoo will provide him with all the food and water he needs, and also a big space to run and play."

Lila and Ben look inside the cage and see Rocco. He is very big and gray, with a long horn on his nose and two small ears. He looks at them with his black eyes and snorts. He is lying on a pile of hay, and he has a bucket of water and a bunch of leaves next to him.

Lila and Ben are amazed and excited. They say, "Wow, he is so big and cool! Can we touch him?"

The man says, "You can touch him, but only very gently and on his back. Do not touch his horn or his face, because he might think you are trying to hurt him. And do not make any loud sounds, because he might get scared and angry. Be very careful and respectful, and he will be friendly to you."

Lila and Ben nod and say, "Okay, we will be very careful and respectful. Thank you for letting us see him."

The man says, "You are welcome. I am glad you like him. He is a very special animal, and he needs a lot of love and care. The zoo will take good care of him, and you can visit him anytime you want."

Lila and Ben smile and say, "We will visit him soon. We want to be his friends. Bye, Rocco. Bye, man."

They wave to the man and to Rocco, and then they run back to the park. They are very happy and proud that they saw a rhinoceros. They tell their other friends about their adventure, and they all agree that it was a very clear and fun day.

Once upon a time there was a girl named Lorraine. She was very brave and loved to explore. One day she decided to climb a mountain. She ran up the smooth, green slopes, laughing with joy.

But when Lorraine got to the top, she found something scary. A big, mean dragon was on the mountain! It roared and Lorraine tried to run away.

But then the dragon spoke to her. It said, "Lorraine, if you kiss me, I will let you go". Lorraine was scared, but she bravely stepped closer. She closed her eyes, ready for the kiss.

But then Lorraine felt a hot breath on her face. The dragon had burnt her with its fiery breath! Lorraine ran away from the mountain, crying with pain. It was a bad ending for poor Lorraine.

Once upon a time there was a black infant. He rested in his crib all day and watched the world outside his window. Every day he saw old birds flying in the sky and young children playing in the grass. Every night he heard the night creatures stirring in the darkness.

One day the infant decided he wanted to explore outside his window. He pushed his way out of the crib and flopped into the grass below. He was amazed by the world around him. Everything seemed so big and he was so small.

He rested near a tree and looked up in the sky. He saw a blackbird flying above him and then he noticed a yellow butterfly fluttering near his face. He reached out to touch it, but it flew away.

The infant watched until the sun began to set. When it was too dark to see he tucked himself back into his crib and closed his eyes. He felt tired and content after his exploration. The night was peaceful and he soon fell asleep, happy to rest after a full day of adventure.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Wendy. She was happy and kind and loved to play in the park.

One day, Wendy decided to take a snack to the park to share with her friends. She was so excited and full of joy!

When she got to the park, she found all of her friends. She shared her snack and everyone was happy. But then, one of her friends was rude and started shouting and hitting people. Wendy was very sad.

Wendy decided to hug her friend in order to make them feel better. She hugged her friend tight, and the rude behavior stopped.

Everyone was happy again, and Wendy and her friends played in the park for the rest of the day. They all decided that being kind was way more fun than being rude.

Once upon a time, there lived a powerful seal. It lived on the beach and it loved singing to the ocean. Every day the seal would stand up on its back fins and sing loudly for everyone to hear.

One day, a three year old girl walked over to the beach. As soon as she heard the powerful seal singing, she got very excited. She ran straight over to it and asked "Can I sing with you?"

The seal smiled and said "Of course! Let's sing together!" So, the little girl and the seal began to sing and play in the ocean. They sang so loudly that it echoed across the beach.

The little girl was so happy. She was so excited to sing and play with the powerful seal. She said goodbye to the seal and skipped off into the sunset, laughing and singing the rest of the way home.

Once there was a brother and sister. They were playing in the light, when suddenly they started to fight. They both wanted the same toy. The brother didn't want to ask a question, so they kept fighting. Suddenly, their mom yelled at them. Her words were loud and sharp, like a thunder cloud. She was so mad that she took away their toy. Neither brother nor sister could make her change her mind. The brother and sister stayed mad at each other. They both sat in the light, not talking, with a sad look in their eyes. No more playing, no more fighting. They went to bed feeling sad and lonely.

One day, a brave goose named Gaby wanted to polish her feathers. She found a shiny pond and dipped her head in the water. She rubbed her beak on her wings and tail, making them sparkle.

"Look at me, I am so pretty!" she said to her friends. "Do you want to polish your feathers too?"

But her friends were scared. They saw a big fox hiding behind a bush. The fox was hungry and wanted to eat the geese.

"No, thank you, Gaby. We want to stay away from the pond. The fox might catch us!" they said.

Gaby was not afraid of the fox. She was brave and smart. She had a plan.

"Come on, don't be silly. The fox is too far away. He can't see us. And if he comes closer, I will honk loudly and scare him away. Trust me, it will be fun!" she said.

She smiled and winked at her friends. They did not know that she had seen the fox too. She wanted to trick him and save her friends.

She pretended to polish her feathers more and more. She made a lot of noise and splashed the water. She hoped the fox would hear her and come closer.

The fox did hear her. He thought she was an easy meal. He crept out of the bush and ran towards the pond.

But Gaby was ready. As soon as she saw him, she honked as loud as she could. She flapped her wings and flew away. She also honked to warn her friends. They followed her and flew away too.

The fox was surprised and angry. He missed his chance to eat the geese. He growled and went back to the bush.

Gaby and her friends were safe and happy. They praised Gaby for her bravery and cleverness.

"Gaby, you are the best! You polished your feathers and fooled the fox. You saved us all!" they said.

Gaby blushed and thanked them. She was glad they were all okay.

She said, "You are welcome, my friends. But remember, polishing your feathers is not as important as sticking together. We are stronger as a flock. And we are always brave!"

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Jamie. He was so excited because he was going to the track to play. He took off running, rushing to the track.

When Jamie got there, he was amazed. He saw a red track that went around and around. He couldn't wait to get started. He put on a helmet and hopped in a car.

Jamie started to rush around and around the track. He went faster and faster. He went so fast that his tummy felt funny with all the rushing. But he kept going because he was having so much fun.

When the race was over, Jamie was so proud. He had gone faster than ever before and he was the winner. He couldn't wait to tell his friends and family what a great time he had.

Once there was a little girl named Sarah. She was very excited because today was her birthday. She was wearing a pretty dress with bubbles all over it. She couldn't wait to play outdoors and have fun with her friends.

So Sarah and her friends ran outside. They started blowing bubbles and watched them float away. Sarah was so excited that she started jumping up and down. Soon all of the other children joined in.

They played and played until all of the bubbles were gone. When the bubbles were gone, the kids went inside for some cake and ice cream. Sarah was so excited that she could hardly eat.

The day was so much fun! Sarah went to bed that night with a smile on her face, dreaming about her wonderful birthday.

Lily and Ben are playing with their toys. They have many things to play with: cars, dolls, blocks, and puzzles. Lily likes puzzles. She likes to match the pieces that have the same shape and color. Ben likes cars. He likes to make them go fast and make noises.

"Look, Lily, I have a red car and a blue car. They are very fast and loud. Vroom, vroom!" Ben says.

"Look, Ben, I have a puzzle with animals. They are very cute and quiet. See, this is a cat and this is a dog. They match!" Lily says.

They show each other their toys and smile. They are happy to play together.

But then, the wind blows and the door opens. A cold air comes in. Lily and Ben shiver. They feel cold.

"Brrr, it is cold. I don't like cold. Do you, Lily?" Ben asks.

"No, I don't like cold either. Let's close the door and get a blanket. Then we can play more." Lily says.

They run to the door and close it. They find a big blanket and wrap it around them. They feel warm and cozy. They go back to their toys and play more. They match their puzzles and race their cars. They have fun. They are happy.

Once upon a time, a little girl called Jane was looking for something special. She looked and looked but could not find it. Then one day, she looked under her bed and found a beautiful doll! She was very happy because she had been looking for it for so long. The doll was wearing a pretty dress with lots of lovely colours. She hugged and hugged the doll and never wanted to let go of it. Jane and the doll became very good friends and did lots of fun things together. She took the doll with her everywhere! Jane and the doll were the best of friends.

Once upon a time, there was a mighty jeep named Max. Max loved to drive around and explore the world. One day, Max met a little girl named Lily. Lily said, "Hi Max, can I ride with you?" Max replied, "Sure, hop in!"

As they drove, they saw a big tree in the middle of the road. Max tried to go around it, but the road was too narrow. So, Max had to twist and turn to get past the tree.

Suddenly, they heard a loud noise and Max stopped moving. Lily asked, "What happened, Max?" Max replied sadly, "I think I broke down, Lily. We can't go anywhere now."

Lily was sad too, but she said, "Don't worry, Max. We can call for help." They waited for a long time, but nobody came to help them. It started to get dark and cold. Lily and Max were very scared. They wished they were home safe and warm. The end.

Once upon a time there was a bad fox. He was always looking for trouble and didn't like to following the rules. One Wednesday, he was feeling particularly rebellious and decided to break the biggest rule in the forest by entering an Unknown part of the woods. The fox explored the Unknown, looking around at all the strange things. After a while, the Fox got lost and he couldn't remember the way home. The bad fox eventually made it back to the forest, but had learned a valuable lesson. He remembered that it is very important to only go where you know. The moral of the story is to always remember to stay where you are familiar with, as exploration can be dangerous.

Once upon a time there was a brave little girl called Lizzy. She loved to explore and follow the adventures she could find in nature. One day she came across a wide lake with a lot of ducks. She wanted to see them up close, so she followed them down to the lake.
