The ducks saw her and started to swim away, as Lizzy was too close to them. Lizzy wanted to follow them, but she was scared. She started to worry, wondering if she should stay away or keep following.

On the other side of the lake, Lizzy saw a wise duck. This duck seemed to understand why Lizzy wanted to follow them. He slowly swam towards her and said: "Little girl, these ducks need space, so why don't you watch from a far? Then you can still follow them and have fun watching them from a safe distance."

Lizzy was very happy, as she never thought about not scaring the ducks away. She thanked the wise duck and followed his advice. From that day on, Lizzy found lots of exciting things to explore and the ducks followed the lake peacefully.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lily. She loved to play outside with her friends. One day, she saw a mosquito flying around her. She tried to catch it, but it was too fast for her.

Lily's mom always told her to keep her room tidy. But Lily didn't listen and left her toys all over the floor. One day, she tripped over her toys and hurt her knee.

Lily realized that she should listen to her mom and keep her room tidy. She also learned that sometimes it's better to let things go, like the mosquito she couldn't catch. It's important to pull yourself together and learn from your mistakes.

Once there was a boy, and he wore a boot. It was very shiny and the boy liked it very much. He tried to show it to his friend, but his friend was afraid.

"It won't hurt me, will it?" his friend asked.

"No, it's harmless," said the boy.

The his friend reached out and tried to touch the boot. At first, he was scared, but soon he saw that it wasn't so bad. They both smiled, and the boy was very happy.

The boot had been his best friend, and the boy was pleased that his friend had been brave enough to try. Now they could both do things together with the boot and have lots of fun.

Once upon a time there was a green wagon. A boy named Ben loved to take his wagon for rides in the park.

One day his mom said, "It's time to go home Ben. Hop in your wagon".

Ben said, "OK Mommy, I'm ready". He climbed in his green wagon and off they went.

In the park, Ben looked around. He noticed the sun was starting to rise. He pointed and said, "Look Mommy, the sun is rising!"

His mom said, "Yes, it is. See how the sky turns different colors when the sun rises?"

Ben nodded, and when they arrived home, he knew even before he looked that his wagon was gone.

His mom said, "Oh no! Someone took your wagon when we stopped at the park. I'm sorry, Ben!".

But Ben smiled, because he knew what was going to happen next.

The next morning, Ben's mom shouted, "Ben, look outside! An old green wagon was delivered to us in the night!"

Ben ran outside to find his wagon had been returned! He said, "Mommy, thank you! I knew the sun would rise and bring my wagon back."

Once there was a bear named Brian. Brian lived in a big, green forest with lots of other animals. Every day Brian would go walking in the forest and listen to the sounds.

One day, Brian heard something special. It was a pleasant sound, like a gentle song. Brian followed the sound and soon he saw a mysterious symbol hanging in a tree. The symbol was round and yellow with black lines that went around it.

Brian climbed up the tree to get a closer look at the symbol. Suddenly, Brian heard a voice. The voice was mild and gentle like a whisper. The voice said “I am the symbol of the forest. My job is to keep the forest safe.”

Brian was amazed and listened carefully to what the symbol said. It told Brian that he must always take care of the forest and never do anything to harm it. Brian promised that he would too.

The symbol thanked Brian for listening and gently disappeared into thin air, never to be seen again.

Jim was a young boy who liked to play. One day he had a great idea. He wanted to make a special box to prevent his toys from getting lost. He shared his idea with his mom and dad and they helped him create his box.

Jim was very proud of his project. He painted it in bright colours and decorated it with stars. When he finished, he put all of his toys in the box.

Now Jim was sure that none of his toys would get lost. Whenever he was not playing with them, he would always keep them in the box. That way he could prevent his toys from getting lost.

Jim was happy with his invention. His mom and dad were also very pleased and proud that he had come up with such a great idea. Jim beamed with joy and always kept his toys safe in the box.

Once upon a time there was a mummy and a daddy. Every day, mummy and daddy went to their job and worked hard all day long. After they were done with their job, they would come home and mummy would feed the little one their dinner.

The mummy and daddy loved the little one very much and they were very proud of their job. One day mummy and daddy were surprised when they came home to a rare sight. The little one had prepared dinner for them!

The little one had a bowl full of rice with some vegetables and a big smile on its face. Mummy and daddy were so pleased that they gave the little one a big hug.

Mummy then said to the little one, "Thank you for feeding us, we are so proud of you!"

Lila and Ben like to play with their toys in the yard. They have a big box of cars, dolls, balls and blocks. They also have a small house made of wood, with a door and a window. They pretend that the house is their home and they are a family.

One day, they find a wire on the ground. It is long and thin and shiny. Lila picks it up and says, "Look, Ben, I have a wire. I can make a necklace with it." She wraps the wire around her neck and ties a knot. "See, I am pretty," she says.

Ben says, "Can I have some wire too? I want to make something." He looks around and sees another wire near the fence. He runs to get it and says, "I have a wire too. I can make a key with it." He bends the wire into a shape like a key and says, "See, I am smart."

Lila and Ben go to their house and try to open the door. But the door is locked. They do not know who locked it or where the real key is. They are sad and scared. They knock on the door and shout, "Help, help, we are locked out!"

Mom hears them and comes to the yard. She sees them crying and holding their wires. She says, "What happened, Lila and Ben? Why are you locked out?" She takes the wire from Lila's neck and says, "This is not a necklace, Lila. This is a wire. It can hurt you. You should not play with it." She takes the wire from Ben's hand and says, "This is not a key, Ben. This is a wire. It cannot open the door. You should not play with it."

She finds the real key and opens the door. She hugs Lila and Ben and says, "I am sorry, Lila and Ben. I locked the door by mistake. I did not know you were playing in the house. Are you fine?" Lila and Ben nod and say, "We are fine, Mom. We are sorry, too. We will not play with wires again." Mom says, "That's good, Lila and Ben. Wires are not toys. They are dangerous. Come, let's go inside and have some juice and cookies." Lila and Ben smile and follow Mom. They are happy and safe.

Once upon a time there was an old mattress. The mattress was quite clever. It had been in the same bedroom since the day it was born. But now it was starting to rot.

The mattress was sad and embarrassed. It knew its days were numbered, and it didn't want anyone to see it in its sorry state.

One day, a little toddler came into the bedroom. He had never seen a mattress before, and he was very curious. He walked up to it and said, "What's that?"

The mattress was scared, but it found its courage. It explained to the child why it was starting to rot. The little toddler was so impressed. He said, "I'm going to help you!"

He grabbed some cleaning supplies and began to scrub the mattress. After a few minutes of hard work, the mattress began to look better. The toddler had worked so hard, and the mattress was so grateful!

The toddler had been so clever, and the mattress was thankful. It wouldn't have to worry about its rotting anymore. They both smiled and the bedroom was filled with happiness. The end.

The sun was shining and it was a beautiful day. A little girl named Sarah was outside with her mom. She was so excited because they were going to the park! She couldn't wait to run around on the playground.

When Sarah got to the park, she saw something that made her face light up. It was a big trampoline! She smiled and jumped around with enthusiasm.

After Sarah had been playing for awhile, her mom said it was time to go. Sarah was disappointed, but before she left, her mom showed her something else. It was a bigger, even more exciting trampoline! Sarah couldn't believe it! She jumped and screamed with joy.

Sarah was so glad her mom had showed her the big trampoline. It made her time at the park even more fun and excited. Her enthusiasm rubbed off on everyone around her and they had a wonderful day.

Once upon a time there were two soldiers. One soldier wanted to get revenge for a bad thing that had happened in the past. He felt bitter about it. The other soldier wanted harmony and peace.

The first soldier decided to start a fight. But the second soldier said: "No, let's make peace instead." The first soldier felt a bit silly. He knew that fighting would only make everything worse.

So he put away his sword and offered his hand. The second soldier said: "Shake my hand and let's be friends."

The first soldier was so surprised! He felt relieved and happier. After that, the two soldiers went back to their homes in peace and harmony.

This simple story shows that peace is always better than fighting. You don't want to feel bitter - it will make you feel worse. Choose peace.

Once there was a little bird who wanted to win a race. All the other birds were ready and excited for the race, but the little bird was nervous. He just wanted to do his best and was hopeful for success.

The race began and the little bird flew with all his might. He felt happy and blew through the wind with joy. He worked very hard and was determined to win.

The little bird had almost made it across the finish line when he began to slip and fall behind. He looked sad and tired, but he did not give up! With one last burst of energy, the little bird flew over the finish line and won the race!

Everyone was so glad the little bird had won. Bird friends cheered and celebrated with him. The little bird was filled with accomplishment and joy. He had achieved success and was proud.

The little bird was glad he had won the race and happy he could make all his bird friends proud. It was a special moment he would never forget.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Amy. She loved to draw with her crayons. One day, she found a big box of new crayons. She was very happy.

Amy had a friend named Tim. Tim saw Amy's new crayons and felt jealous. He wanted to hold the crayons and draw, too. So, he asked Amy if he could play with her and use the new crayons.

Amy was a good friend. She said yes, and they both sat down to draw together. They held the crayons and made beautiful pictures. Tim was not jealous anymore. They had fun and played with the crayons all day.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to dance on the stage. Every day, she practiced her moves and twirls until she was very good.

One day, Lily went to a big dance competition. She danced her heart out and did very well. Her mommy and daddy were so proud of her.

After the competition, Lily and her family went home. They were all very tired but happy. Lily was happy too because she knew she did her best and couldn't wait to return to the stage again.

Once upon a time, there was a little bird named Tweety. Tweety loved to fly high in the sky and sing sweet songs. One day, Tweety saw a big bird with a shiny, blue feather. Tweety felt envious and wished for a feather like that.

Tweety decided to fly up to the big bird and ask for a feather. But as Tweety got closer, the big bird started to struggle and cough. Tweety noticed that the big bird had a problem with its lung. Tweety felt sad and wanted to help.

Tweety flew down to the ground and found a small twig. Tweety brought the twig back to the big bird and showed it how to use it to help clear its lung. The big bird was grateful and gave Tweety a shiny, blue feather as a thank you. From that day on, Tweety learned that helping others is better than feeling envious.

Once upon a time, there was a sunny day. The sky was bright and blue and the sun shone in the sky. Down on the ground, there was a fork. It was silver and shiny and glittered in the light.

The fork was special; as the sun shone down on it, it glowed. It glowed and glowed and shined like a star. It was so beautiful, the birds came to sing in the trees nearby.

Then a little girl came by. She saw the shiny fork and wanted to pick it up. She was brave and tried to touch it, but it was too hot. She took a step back, but the fork kept shining.

So the little girl found some sticks and made a circle around the fork. Then she stepped back and watched the fork shine. It sparkled like a diamond and she felt so happy! The fork made the day so sweet.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lily. She loved to read books. One day, her mommy took her to the mall. Lily was so happy because she saw a big toy store. She ran towards it and accidentally bumped into a man. The man was careless and didn't say sorry. Lily's mommy was angry and told the man to be more careful. After that, they went to the book store and Lily picked a new book to read. She was so excited to go home and read her new book. The end.

Once upon a time there was a brave little girl named Emma. Emma had a big goal. She wanted to break a record. She was determined to make her goal come true.

One day Emma decided to practice. She spent each day running and jumping with all her might. Sometimes it was hard, but she was very brave and never gave up.

After lots of practice Emma was ready. She asked her parents to help her break the record. They were so proud of her and said yes.

On the day of the big event Emma was so excited. With everyone watching, she ran, jumped and jumped again. When she was done, everyone cheered.

Emma had done it! She had broken the record! Everyone was so proud of her and gave her lots of hugs. It was the best day ever!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved to play outside. One day, she went on an adventure to see a big, gray volcano.

When she got there, she saw a man who said, "Lily, you should not be here. The volcano might erupt and it can be dangerous."

Lily was scared and said, "Okay, I will go home now." She shut her eyes and wished she was safe.

The man smiled and said, "Good job, Lily. You made the right choice. It's always better to be safe than sorry." And with that, Lily went home, happy and proud of herself for being smart.

Lily was a cheerful girl who liked to play with her dolls and sing songs. She had a big sister, Anna, who was very kind and helped her with everything. Lily loved Anna very much and wanted to be like her.

One day, Lily saw Anna pack a bag and say goodbye to their mom and dad. Lily asked where Anna was going. Anna said she had to go to the hospital for an operation. Lily did not know what an operation was, but she thought it sounded scary. She asked Anna if it would hurt. Anna said no, it would not hurt, and she would be back soon. She gave Lily a hug and a kiss and told her to be a good girl.

Lily waited for Anna to come back. She played with her dolls and sang songs, but she missed Anna a lot. She asked mom and dad when Anna would come back. They said they did not know, but they hoped soon. They looked sad and worried. Lily did not like to see them sad and worried. She wanted to make them happy. She decided to draw a picture for Anna and give it to her when she came back.

Lily worked hard on her picture. She used her favorite crayons and drew Anna with a big smile and a flower in her hair. She wrote "I love you Anna" with her best letters. She was very proud of her picture. She showed it to mom and dad and they smiled and said it was very beautiful. They said they would take it to the hospital and give it to Anna.

Lily waited for mom and dad to come back. She hoped they would bring Anna with them. She hoped Anna would like her picture. She hoped Anna would be cheerful again. She looked at the clock and saw it was very late. She wondered why mom and dad were not back yet. She felt scared and lonely. She wished Anna was with her.

Mom and dad did not come back that night. They did not come back the next day. They did not come back the next week. Lily did not see Anna again. She did not know what happened to her. She did not understand why she had to go for an operation. She did not understand why she did not come back. She did not understand why mom and dad were always crying. She did not understand anything. She only knew she missed Anna very much. She only knew she was not cheerful anymore. She only knew she wanted to be close to Anna again.

Once upon a time, there was a little bunny named Benny. Benny lived in a cozy burrow with his family. One day, Benny went to play outside and saw a poor little bird who was hurt. Benny felt sad for the bird and wanted to help.

Benny knew he had to hurry and find someone to help the bird. He ran back to his burrow and told his family about the bird. Together, they went to find a kind person who could help the bird feel better.

As they were walking, they saw a lamp in the distance. The lamp was shining bright and Benny thought it would be a good idea to ask the person who lived there for help. The person was very kind and helped the bird feel better.

Benny learned that it's important to help others when they're in need. He also learned that there are kind people who are willing to help. From that day on, Benny promised to always be helpful and kind to others.

Once there was a little girl named Lily. She was three years old and loved to go fast. Today, she had on her favorite shirt - a white one with a big red heart on it.

Lily was playing outside when she suddenly spotted her best friend, James. He was running really fast and didn't even see her. Lily wanted to speed like James, so she took off after him.

Lily ran really fast, but she couldn't catch up. She began to get upset and tears started to roll down her cheeks. Suddenly, James stopped and turned around.

He said "Hi Lily, you were going so fast I didn't even see you!" Lily smiled and wiped away her tears. She said, "I tried to speed like you, but I couldn't keep up!"

James laughed and said, "Let's race! I'll go slow so you can keep up!" Lily smiled, and the two raced. It was so much fun!

At the end of the race, Lily was so proud of herself. She had sped enough to keep up with James and won the race!

Once upon a time there was a little sailor who liked to go out in the big boat every day. He was a brave sailor but one day he got very scared.

The sky suddenly turned dark, the water became wild, and the waves started to break against the boat. The little sailor didn't know what to do.

His captain shouted, “Clean the sails! We need to get out of here!”

The little sailor started to clean the sails, but it was too late. The storm had become too big and the boat sank to the bottom of the ocean. The sailor didn't make it.

The moral of this story is always be prepared for unexpected situations because you never know what may happen.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She was feeling sick and her mommy wanted to check her temperature. Mommy went to the store to buy a thermometer.

When mommy came back, she put the thermometer in Lily's mouth. Lily didn't like it because it tasted sour. But mommy said it was important to check her temperature so she could get better.

After a few days, Lily was feeling better and mommy was happy. But then, Lily's little brother got sick too. Mommy went back to the store to buy another thermometer.

But when mommy came back, she realized she didn't have enough money to buy the thermometer. She was sad and didn't know what to do. Lily and her brother had to stay sick for a long time because mommy couldn't buy the thermometer. The end.

John was walking in the park with his mom. He wanted to run around and explore. As he bundled on ahead, his mom warned him to stay close. But John kept running and running until he was out of sight.

Suddenly, John came upon a deep pond. He had never seen anything so big before. He wanted to know what was inside and so he stepped forward. But before he could take another step, he felt a strong hand grabbing his shoulder. It was his mom! She had been looking everywhere for him.

John was in so much trouble. His mom scolded him and yelled, "What were you thinking?" She told him never to wander off like that again.

To make sure John didn't do it again, his mom gave John a special vest to wear. She made him promise to never take it off when they went to the park.

John promised, and he has kept his word ever since. He knows not to go near the deep water again, and the vest is a reminder of how dangerous it is.

Once upon a time there was a boy named Jack. He liked to go outside and play. One day, Jack went to his back yard and opened his toybox. Inside, he found a big, dark grape. He was so excited and started to shout, "Grape! Grape!"

Mum heard Jack and opened the kitchen window. She asked, "What did you find, Jack?"

Jack answered, "I found a dark grape! Can I eat it?"

Mum laughed and said, "Yes, you can eat it. But remember to wash it first!"

So Jack opened the tap and washed his dark grape. Then he bit into it and the juicy grape tasted so sweet!

The end.

Lily loves her long hair. She likes to comb it and make braids. She thinks her hair is pretty and soft. But today, Mommy says she needs a haircut. Lily does not want a haircut. She is scared that her hair will be too short and ugly.

Mommy takes Lily to the salon. There is a nice lady who smiles at Lily. She says, "Hello, Lily. I'm Sue. I'm going to give you a haircut. Don't worry, it will be fun and you will look very pretty." Lily does not believe her. She holds Mommy's hand and cries.

Sue shows Lily a book with pictures of different haircuts. She asks Lily to choose one. Lily sees a picture of a girl with hair like hers, but a little shorter and with bangs. She points at it and says, "This one." Sue says, "Good choice, Lily. That's a very cute haircut. It will make your eyes look bigger and your face look brighter. Do you want to try it?" Lily nods and wipes her tears.

Sue puts a cape around Lily's neck and sits her on a big chair. She sprays some water on Lily's hair and combs it gently. She talks to Lily about her favorite toys, colors, and animals. Lily starts to relax and smile. She likes Sue. She is nice and funny. Sue cuts Lily's hair with scissors and a comb. She makes sure that Lily can see what she is doing in the mirror. She says, "Look, Lily. Your hair is getting shorter and prettier. Do you like it?" Lily looks at her reflection and nods. She likes it. Her hair is still long, but not too long. It has bangs that frame her face. It looks shiny and smooth.

Sue finishes the haircut and gives Lily a hair clip with a flower. She says, "There you go, Lily. You're all done. You look beautiful. Do you want to show Mommy?" Lily jumps off the chair and runs to Mommy. She hugs her and says, "Mommy, look at my haircut. Do you like it?" Mommy smiles and kisses Lily. She says, "I love it, Lily. You look so pretty. I'm so proud of you. You were very brave and smart. How do you feel?" Lily says, "I feel happy, Mommy. I love my haircut. And I love you." Mommy says, "I love you too, Lily. You're my sweet girl." They hug and thank Sue. They leave the salon with big smiles. Lily loves her haircut. And she loves Mommy.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Audrey. She lived in a big, green field and every day she would play outside. But one day, Audrey noticed something strange. On the other side of the field, she saw a mysterious snake!

Audrey knew she had to take a closer look. She was so brave and she began walking towards the snake. As she got closer, Audrey couldn't believe her eyes. It was a beautiful, long green snake with orange and yellow stripes.

Audrey was so excited! She wanted to touch the snake, so she slowly put out her hand. But just as Audrey was about to take the snake, it twisted around and slithered away.

Audrey never saw the mysterious snake again. She was a bit sad about that, but she still told all of her friends about it. To this day, Audrey still remembers the amazing snake she found in the green field.

Once upon a time, there was a regular copper. He lived in a small sack in the corner of an old house. He was happy living in the sack and liked to play in the sun. One day a big wind blew the sack and it landed in a big river.

The copper was scared. He didn't know how he would get back to the old house. All of a sudden, a big fish came and took the sack in his mouth. He swam fast and soon they were back at the old house.

The copper was so happy. He thanked the fish and got out of the sack. The fish said goodbye, and swam away. The copper climbed back into his regular sack and was very happy to be home again.

Once upon a time, there lived a little girl named Jane. Jane loved to borrow things from her friends. One day, she decided to borrow a planet from the sky. She asked her friends, "Can I borrow a planet from the sky?"

Her friends didn't know what to do. They all replied, "No, you can't borrow a planet from the sky!"

But then Jane thought of a way. She asked them, "What if I just borrow some light?"

Her friends thought it was a great idea. They agreed to help her. So, they all pointed to the sky and helped her borrow some light from the stars, which she used to make the planet shine bright.

When the planet was lit up, Jane was so pleased. She thanked her friends for helping her borrow the light.

The end.

Once there was a rabbit who loved to hop. Every day he would hop around the forest and have lots of fun.

He heard about the beach and wanted to experience something new. So he hopped to the beach and he was amazed! The Big Blue Ocean was so beautiful and peaceful.

He saw some humans trying to surf on the crest of the waves. It looked like so much fun! He hopped and hopped to the shore, then hopped onto the surfboard.

He was a brilliant hopper! He was able to balance himself on the surfboard and with a few hops, he was surfing. He had so much fun catching waves and hopping across the sea.

When the sun was setting the rabbit hopped back to shore, feeling exhausted but so happy. He had had a brilliant day of hopping and surfing!

Once there was a girl who really liked to jump. She could jump up and down so high. One day, she got a modern package in the mail. She was so excited to open it. “What is it?” She asked.

“It’s a special surprise!” her mom said.

So the girl opened the package and inside there was a special jump rope. It was modern and colorful too.

“Wow! I love it!” the girl said.

The girl grabbed the jump rope and started jumping up and down. She laughed with joy and jumped all around her house. She was having so much fun.

The girl loved her new jump rope and was so happy that she had such a modern surprise.

Once upon a time there was a quick little girl. She lived in a sweet cottage in the village. Every day she liked to hang around with her friends.

One day, the little girl went to the garden to hang her clothes on the line. She was really quick, and finished hanging all the clothes in no time! When she was done, she had a sweet snack of strawberries and cream.

The next day, the girl found a big tree in the garden. She climbed up to the top and hung from the branch! It felt really nice to be so high up in the tree.

Afterward, she ran through the garden and picked some sweet flowers. She hung the flowers on her wall, and the smell filled her room.

The little girl was so happy and quick all the time, and she always enjoyed every sweet moment.

Lily and Max are friends. They like to play in the park. Today, they find a big blue box. It has a button on it. Lily pushes the button. Music comes out of the box. It is a happy song.

"Wow, music!" Max says. "Let's dance!"

Lily and Max start to dance. They jump and clap and wiggle. They have fun. Then, Lily has an idea.

"Let's spin!" she says. "Spinning is fun!"

She holds Max's hand. They spin around and around. They spin fast and slow. They spin like tops. They laugh and giggle.

But then, they spin too much. They feel dizzy. They fall down on the grass. They look at the sky. The sky is blue, like the box.

"Are you okay?" Lily asks Max.

"I'm okay," Max says. "But I'm tired. Let's rest."

They lie on the grass. They listen to the music. They close their eyes. They smile. They are happy. They are friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little bee named Buzzy. Buzzy lived in a big yellow hive with lots of other bees. Every day, Buzzy would fly around and collect nectar from flowers to bring back to the hive.

After a long day of flying, Buzzy was very tired. She crawled into her little honeycomb bed and fell fast asleep. The other bees in the hive were also sleeping, and it was very quiet.

In the morning, Buzzy woke up feeling refreshed and ready to start another day of buzzing around. She flew out of the hive and into the bright yellow sunshine, excited to see what adventures awaited her.

Sara and Ben were twins who loved to play pretend. One day, they decided to make a tea party for their stuffed animals. Sara put some cups and plates on a tray and Ben filled them with water and juice. They carried the tray to the living room, where they had set up a table and chairs.

"Be careful, Ben," Sara said. "Don't spill the drinks. Promise me."

"I promise, Sara," Ben said. "I'm very careful."

They put the tray on the table and invited their stuffed animals to sit down. They had a bear, a rabbit, a cat, and a dog. They poured the drinks and pretended to eat cookies and cake. They talked and laughed and had a lot of fun.

Suddenly, they heard a loud noise. It was their big brother, Tom, who had come home from school. He saw the tea party and smiled. He wanted to join them, but he was too big for the small chairs. He decided to sit on the floor instead.

"Hi, Sara and Ben," he said. "Can I have some tea?"

"Sure, Tom," Sara said. "But you have to be careful. Don't break the cups. Promise me."

"I promise, Sara," Tom said. "I'm very careful."

He reached for the tray and picked up a cup. But he didn't notice that the tray was not very stable. As he lifted the cup, the tray tilted and all the drinks spilled on the floor. The cups and plates crashed and broke. The stuffed animals got wet and dirty.

"Tom!" Sara and Ben cried. "You broke your promise! You ruined our tea party!"

Tom felt bad. He didn't mean to make a mess. He apologized to Sara and Ben and their stuffed animals. He helped them clean up the floor and the tray. He gave them a hug and said he was sorry.

"It's okay, Tom," Sara and Ben said. "We forgive you. But next time, please be more careful. Promise us."

"I promise, Sara and Ben," Tom said. "I'm very careful."

They smiled and hugged him back. They decided to make another tea party later, with a bigger table and chairs and an enormous tray. They invited Tom to join them again, as long as he kept his promise.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Daisy. Daisy was very alert as she went outside to play. On her way out, she heard the loud sound of a parade! Daisy was so excited that she had to go see it.

She walked down the street and noticed lots of people in brightly colored clothes shaking and dancing. A band was playing music and everyone was laughing and cheering. Daisy waved to everyone and everyone waved back.

She followed the parade until it reached the end. Everyone cheered and clapped loudly. Daisy realized that it was a welcome parade for a new family who had moved into the neighborhood. She exploded with excitement and even more people joined the parade.

Daisy shouted and clapped with all the other people. When it was over, Daisy was so happy and proud to welcome the new family. She smiled and waved as they walked away.

The end.

Steve was out for a walk one morning. As he strolled along, he kept an eye out for something exciting. Suddenly, Steve discovered a crocodile in the grass. He was very sleepy and didn't move at all.

Steve knew he had to move quickly so he carefully grabbed a stick. He poked the crocodile to see if he would wake up, but the crocodile lay still. After a few more pokes, Steve got bored.

He decided to take a nap under a nearby tree. While Steve was sleeping, he did not notice that the crocodile had slowly started to follow him.

When Steve woke up, he was surprised to see the crocodile right next to him. He had not expected to find a crocodile so close by, but he was excited to have discovered a new friend. Steve and the crocodile became good friends and they both enjoyed playing in the grass together.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. He loved to walk with his mommy every day. One morning, Timmy woke up early and felt very impatient to go for a walk. He kept asking his mommy, "Can we go now? Can we go now?" But his mommy said they had to wait until after breakfast.

Timmy didn't want to wait. He decided to go for a walk by himself. He walked and walked, but soon he realized he didn't know where he was. He started to feel scared and wished he had waited for his mommy. Suddenly, he saw a big dog coming towards him. He tried to run, but the dog chased him and bit him. Timmy cried for help, but nobody was around. Sadly, Timmy never made it back home.

Lily and Ben were playing in the park. They liked to dig in the sand and look for treasures. Sometimes they found shells, rocks, or coins. But today they found something very shiny and pretty. It was a gem!

"Wow, look at this!" Lily said, holding the gem in her hand. It was blue and sparkled in the sun. "It must be magic!"

"Maybe it is," Ben said, admiring the gem. "Where do you think it came from?"

Lily thought for a moment. She remembered a story her mom had told her about a princess who lost her gem in a deep well. "Maybe it came from the well," she said. "Maybe the princess dropped it and it got washed away by the water."

"Really?" Ben asked, curious. "Do you think the princess is still looking for it?"

Lily nodded. She believed in the story. She believed in magic. She wanted to help the princess. "Maybe we can give it back to her," she said. "Maybe she will be happy and give us a wish."

Ben liked that idea. He also believed in the story. He also believed in magic. He wanted to have a wish. "How can we find her?" he asked.

Lily looked around. She saw a big tree near the sandpit. It had a hole in its trunk. "Maybe she lives in the tree," she said. "Maybe we can knock and ask."

Ben agreed. He followed Lily to the tree. They held the gem in their hands. They knocked on the hole. They waited for an answer. They hoped to meet the princess. They hoped to make her smile. They hoped to get a wish. They believed in the gem.

Once there was a little girl named Jane. Jane loved to perform for her family and friends. Every day she would practice new tricks.

One day, Jane’s mommy gave her a hammer. It was a big hammer but Jane wasn’t scared. She took it from her mom and felt its weight. Then, with a lively smile on her face, she started to perform tricks with the hammer.

She carefully flipped it from one hand to the other. She tapped it against the wall like a drum and spun it round and round. It was so much fun! Every time the hammer touched something it made a loud sound.

After a few minutes, Jane was very tired. Her mommy fixed a special spot in the house so that Jane could store her hammer safely. Even when not performing with it, Jane liked to look at her hammer, feeling very proud of her new possession.

Once upon a time, there were two best friends, Lucy and Jack. They were excited to go to Lucy's garden to have a picnic. They packed the food and drinks and quickly ran out the door.

When they got to the garden, it was beautiful. The sun was shining, the birds were chirping, and there were wildflowers everywhere. Lucy and Jack quickly spread out the blanket and arranged the food so they could eat.

Suddenly, Jack became impatient. He wanted to play a game, but Lucy was too busy to play. "Please, Lucy, can we play now?" Jack asked. Lucy sighed and said, "I need to supply the food first. After that, we can play."

Jack frowned and grumbled, but he waited patiently. He watched as Lucy quickly finished up the food and drink supply before finally saying, "Okay, now we can play!" They had a great time playing in the garden until the sun went down.

Once upon a time, there was a big, graceful cat. The cat liked to play with a key. The key was shiny and fun to chase. The cat would run, jump, and catch the key with her paws. She was very happy.

One day, the cat was very tired. She lay down on her soft bed and started to yawn. Her yawn was so big, it made her friends yawn too. The cat closed her eyes and went to sleep.

While the cat was sleeping, her friends hid the key. When the cat woke up, she looked for the key. She looked under the bed, in the box, and behind the door. Finally, she found the key in a tree. The cat climbed the tree, got the key, and played with it all day long.

Once there was a little girl who loved to guess. She would guess what object was in her hand, what shapes were in the sky, and what color the tree was outside her window.

One day she decided to go for a walk outside. She saw some flies in the sky and said to them, "Can I guess your name?" The flies, of course, didn't answer, but she guessed anyway. "I think your name is Fluffy," she said.

But then something strange started to happen. Every time the girl guessed, a regular fly would appear and buzz around her head. She started to get scared because she didn't understand why the regular fly kept appearing. After a few minutes of buzzing around her head, the fly flew away and the girl felt better.

The little girl continued her guessing game, but after a while she noticed the regular fly buzzing around her again. She started to get frustrated and yelled, "Why can't you just go away?" Suddenly the regular fly flew away and the girl felt relieved. She realized that maybe this fly was just trying to communicate and that her guessing was annoying it. From then on, she would guess a few times and then stop for a moment so the fly could rest.

The little girl and the regular fly continued their games together, guessing and flying around. She would guess, the fly would fly, and they would both be happy.

Once upon a time, in a small town, there lived a boy named Tim. Tim had a penny that he found on the street. This penny was not like other pennies; it was unknown and special.

One day, Tim met a girl named Sue. Sue was sad because she lost her toy. Tim wanted to care for Sue and make her happy. He said, "I have a special penny. Let's use it to buy a new toy for you."

Sue smiled and said, "Thank you, Tim. You are very kind to care for me." They went to the toy store and found a toy Sue liked. Tim gave the unknown penny to the store man. The store man looked at the penny and said, "This is a magic penny! It can buy any toy in the store!"

Sue and Tim were very happy. They picked the best toy and thanked the store man. From that day on, Tim and Sue played together every day, and they always cared for each other.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to draw and paint with her crayons. One day, she asked her mom if she could mix colors to make new ones.

Her mom said, "Sure, Lily! You can mix red and blue to make purple, or yellow and blue to make green. It's very creative to mix colors!"

Lily was excited to try this out. She grabbed her red and blue crayons and started to mix them together. "Look, Mommy! I made purple!" she exclaimed.

"That's so cool, Lily! You're very creative," her mom replied.

Lily continued to mix different colors and create new ones. She was having so much fun that she didn't even notice the time passing by. When she was done, she showed her mom all of her colorful drawings. Her mom was very proud of her and told her how talented she was.

From that day on, Lily loved to mix colors and be creative with her art. She couldn't wait to see what new colors she could make next!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She wanted to make cocoa for her mommy, but she didn't know how. So, she asked her mommy for help.

"Mommy, can you help me prepare cocoa?" Lily asked.

"Sure, sweetie. Let's get the cocoa powder and milk," her mommy replied.

Lily was nervous because she wanted the cocoa to taste good. But her mommy helped her mix the cocoa powder and milk together. Finally, they heated it up on the stove and poured it into mugs.

Lily took a sip and smiled. "It's yummy, mommy! Thank you for helping me make cocoa."

Once upon a time there was a little bird. He was so small that he could fit in the palm of a hand. He was a happy bird and loved to fly around in the sky.

One day he went on a big adventure, up to the big mountain. He flew higher and higher and couldn't believe his eyes when he reached the peak.

Suddenly, he felt the ground shake and shake harder and harder. He was scared and flew to the nearest tree to save himself. He was shaking too, he was so scared.

Then he spotted something in the distance. It was his best friend, a butterfly! "Come down" shouted the butterfly, "the shaking has stopped, it is safe now".

So the little bird joined his friend and together they had lots of fun. They flew around and around the mountain and talked about their adventure.

The little bird will never forget his courageous journey to the top of the big mountain.

Once upon a time there was a bald man. He loved to explore and every morning he went for a walk in the woods. This particular morning he was looking for something special.

Suddenly, he heard a loud noise in the bushes. Carefully, he moved closer and he was shocked to see a crocodile! The crocodile was even bigger than the man!

The bald man was surprised, but the crocodile was very friendly. The crocodile smiled at the bald man and they played together in the woods.

The bald man was amazed. He had never played with a crocodile before. After a while, the crocodile waved goodbye and walked away into the forest.

The bald man smiled as he watched the crocodile go. He couldn't believe he had played with such an amazing creature. What a surprise!

Once upon a time, there was a little boy who loved to watch the sunset. Every evening he would stand at the window and watch the sky turn pink and orange. One night, however, something stopped him from doing this.

A big dark cloud moved in front of the sun and prevented the little boy from seeing the pretty colors. He felt very hurt and sad because he could not watch the sunset like he usually did.

The little boy thought it was not fair and started to cry. Suddenly, a giant bird came and flew away the big dark cloud.

The little boy cheered. Now he could watch the sunset again and see the pretty colors in the sky. He watched until the last sliver of the sun had disappeared, then he smiled and went to bed happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She went to a park with her mommy and daddy. There was a big slide in the park, and Lily loved to slide down it. She giggled and laughed as she went down the slide again and again.

After playing in the park, Lily's family went to a restaurant to eat. The restaurant was a big room with tables and chairs. They sat down at a table, and a nice lady brought them food to eat. Lily thought the food was yummy!

On the way home from the restaurant, Lily's mommy showed her a useful tool. It was a flashlight! She said they could use it to see in the dark. Lily thought the flashlight was cool and couldn't wait to use it at home.

One day, a young girl wanted to travel. She put on her special shoes and went on her way.

She arrived at a parade. There were lots of people, flags and music. She saw dancers dancing and people laughing.

The girl went to the front of the parade. She saw horses walking calmly down the street. They were beautiful. She saw a man playing a trumpet and she clapped with excitement.

The parade went on and the girl followed it until it stopped. She said goodbye to her new friends and started to travel home.

She was happy and tired. The parade had been very fun and she had a great day.

Once upon a time, there was a magical chest. It was filled with incredible things that amazed everyone who saw it.

One day, a little girl asked her mom what was inside the chest. Her mom smiled and explained that it held secrets and treasures. The girl was so excited to find out what was in the chest.

Her mom opened the chest and pulled out a bright and sparkly necklace. She put it around her daughter's neck and explained that it belonged to a special fairy. Whenever the girl wore the necklace, she could make incredible things happen.

The little girl was so happy and she thanked her mom for the magical gift. She ran off, eagerly exploring all the incredible adventures that the necklace could bring.

The end.

Once upon a time there was a grumpy old bear named Fred. He was always grumpy and never smiled.

Every day, Fred would walk to the nearest villages to see if anyone could make him smile. One day, he saw something in a window that made him smile. It was a big shiny fridge.

He went inside the village and asked the shopkeeper if he could buy the fridge. The shopkeeper promised him the fridge if he could pay for it.

Fred was so excited that he ran back to his cave and grabbed all of his coins. He ran back to the shop as fast as he could and paid for the fridge.

The shopkeeper was impressed and gave him the fridge. Fred was so grateful that he promised to come back next week and visit the shopkeeper.

Fred carried the fridge back to his cave and plugged it in. He put all his food in it and smiled. He was so happy to have the fridge and he kept his promise to come back and visit the shopkeeper every week.

Once there was a little boy named Mark. Mark was strong with big muscles and he liked to show them off. One day, Mark wanted to do something different. He saw a small log and thought he could lift it. He bent down and grabbed hold of it.

He strained and tried to lift the log, but it was too heavy! His little muscles just weren't strong enough. He was sad.

Just then his mom came out and asked what he was doing. He told her he was trying to lift the log, but it was too heavy. She put her hands on his shoulders, looked into his eyes, and said, "Mark, you have strong muscles. But you need to use them the right way and try something that's smaller."

Mark nodded, understanding. He looked around and saw a little stone. He bent down, grabbed it and lifted it. He was so proud of himself! He showed it to his mom and smiled. "See!" he said.

His mom hugged him, happy that he finally figured it out. From then on, he knew that with a little effort, he could do anything he wanted.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved sausages, especially the huge ones. One day, Timmy went to the store with his mom to buy some sausages.

At the store, Timmy saw a man loading a huge box onto a truck. Timmy asked the man, "What's in the box?" The man replied, "Sausages! Lots and lots of sausages!"

Timmy's eyes grew wide with excitement. "Can I have one?" he asked. The man smiled and handed Timmy a huge sausage. Timmy's mom paid for the sausages and they went home to cook them for dinner.

After dinner, Timmy told his mom, "That sausage was huge! I want to eat it every day!" His mom laughed and said, "Maybe not every day, Timmy. But we can have it again soon." Timmy went to bed dreaming of the huge sausage he had eaten that day.

One day, a little boy was searching for a bull. He looked everywhere, but he couldn't find one. He finally found a large, clear field. The field seemed perfect for finding a bull.

The boy began to search in the field. As he looked around, he noticed something big and brown far away. He ran to the spot, and sure enough, there was a bull! The bull was grazing peacefully in the clear field.

The boy was very excited. He wanted to get close to the bull, so he walked up slowly. The bull was calm and gentle, so the boy carefully reached out and touched it. He was so happy.

The little boy enjoyed his time with the bull, and he was sad when it was time to leave. He waved goodbye and went on his way, happy and excited that he had found a bull in the clear field.

One day, Timmy went to the beach with his mom. He loved to go to the beach because he could play in the sand and look for seashells.

When he got there, he saw a jellyfish in the water. He was so excited and wanted to touch it. But his mom said no. She said it was dangerous and to refuse the jellyfish.

Timmy was very sorry, but he knew he had to listen to his mom. He listened to his mom and refused the jellyfish.

He still enjoyed playing in the sand and looking at all the other creatures living in the ocean. As he watched, he began to feel a little less sorry.

He knew that he had made the right decision when his mom had told him to refuse the jellyfish. So they spent the rest of the day at the beach, playing and looking at all the beautiful creatures living in the ocean.

Once upon a time, there was a sleepy cat named Kitty. Kitty lived in a little structure made of wood. She loved to sleep all day and play all night. One day, Kitty met a new friend, a dog named Buddy.

"Hi, I'm Buddy!" said the dog. "Do you want to play with me?"

Kitty yawned and said, "I'm sleepy now. Can we play later?"

Later that day, Kitty and Buddy played together. They played with a ball, and they played with a stick. But then, they found a big toy. It was so big that they could not play with it together.

"We need to separate the toy," said Kitty.

Buddy agreed, "Yes, let's separate it and then we can play!"

So, Kitty and Buddy separated the toy into two parts. Now, they could play with the toy together. They played and played until they were both very sleepy. Then, they went to their little structure and slept side by side. And they were the best of friends from that day on.

Sam was a cat who liked to sleep in a box. He found a big box in the garage and made it his bed. He put some soft things inside and curled up. He was happy and warm.

One day, he heard a loud noise outside. He woke up and stretched his legs. He looked out of the box and saw a big truck. The truck was taking away some things from the garage. Sam was scared and curious. He wanted to see what was happening.

He jumped out of the box and ran to the door. He saw a man with a hat and a coat. The man was putting things in the truck. Sam saw his box in the man's hands. The man was taking his box away! Sam was troubled and angry. He wanted his box back.

He ran after the man and the truck. He meowed and scratched. He tried to get his box. But the man did not see him or hear him. The man put the box in the truck and closed the door. The truck started to move. Sam was sad and lost. He did not have his box anymore. He did not know where to go.

He sat on the sidewalk and cried. He wished he had stayed in his box. He wished he had not been curious. He wished he had a home. He hoped someone would find him and love him. He hoped he would find a new box. He hoped he would be happy and warm again.

Once there was a boy who liked wearing his tight yellow shirt. One day, he asked his mom if he could wear it in a photo. His mom said yes and she went to get her camera. But when she came back, the boy had disappeared!

The mom called out to her son but there was no answer. She ran out into the street and saw that the boy had gone two blocks away. When she finally made it to the boy, he was already happily posing for a photo in the tight yellow shirt.

The mom was ready to take the photo when suddenly the boy's shirt ripped. She was so mad that she said to the boy, "No more wearing that shirt ever again!". The boy was very disappointed but he couldn't do anything about it.

The boy learned his lesson and from then on, he always stayed close to his mom no matter where he went. He was never allowed to wear the tight yellow shirt again.

The old man and his dog lay on the grass in their garden, gazing up at the clear blue sky. The old dog let out a contented sigh.

"It's a wonderful day," the old man said to his faithful pup. "Perhaps we could go for a short walk?"

The pup barked happily, then ran off in circles.

The old man smiled, and stood up slowly. He beckoned his dog, and the two of them headed out of the garden and down the road. They walked in comfortable silence, slowly taking in the sights.

Nearby, a young family was playing. There were two children, one a toddler, who chased a ball with their father. They were all laughing and having fun.

The old man smiled at their joy and stopped to gaze at them. The toddler noticed him and came running over, dragging her little blue blanket behind her.

She looked up at the old man, and grinned. "Hello!" she said, shyly.

The old man smiled and knelt down. "Hello there!" he said. "What are you playing?"

The little girl beamed. "Catch!" she said.

The old man chuckled. He stood up, thanked the family and continued his walk with his pup. As the two of them walked away, the old man glanced back and waved. The little girl waved back, her bright eyes gleaming.

Once there was a boy. He was really sad one day. His mom came to comfort him. She sat down next to him and gave him a gentle hug. She said: "It's all right, nothing bad will happen and nothing can hurt you."

The boy felt much better. He smiled and said: "Thank you."

His mom smiled back and said: "I'm here if you need me, but you don't have to be scared. Everything is harmless."

The boy relaxed and soon forgot why he was sad in the first place. His mom had comforted him and he felt much better now.

The end.

Once there was a humble man who lived to the east. He had a dream to attach something to the sky. Everyday he watched the sky and dreamed of his idea. He worked hard and soon had a plan in his head.

He gathered what he needed and started to work on the idea. He used things like pieces of wood and bits of metal. He worked carefully and slowly. Finally he was ready. He went outside and carefully attached his invention to the sky.

When he stepped back, he saw his dream had come true. There was a big balloon attached in the sky. He was so happy knowing he had done it, and he could see it from east and from west. He knew he had made something wonderful.

Once upon a time, there was a rag. It was old and worn, and was not very pretty. One day, a child decided to take it and give it a makeover. The child scrubbed the rag with soap and water, and it became clean and soft.

The child was so happy to see the rag looking brand new, that they decided to keep it with them. The child took the rag everywhere they went, snuggling it like a toy.

One day, the child was playing outside when the wind started to blow. The wind blew the rag away, and the child started to cry. They looked and looked for the rag, but it was gone.

The next morning, the sun was shining and the wind had stopped. The child returned to the same spot to look for the rag again. And, just as the child had hoped, there the rag was - lying in the grass! They picked up the rag and hugged it tight, happy to have it back.

From then on, the child kept the rag safe and never let it wander away again.

Once upon a time, there was a little rabbit. He was a silly rabbit, hopping all around the house. He wanted to go outside, so he opened the door and hopped out into the garden!

The rabbit saw a big beautiful tree and hopped over to it. He was so excited he started to run around in circles. But then he stopped and sighed. The ground was so hard and he wanted to rest. He could feel his little feet getting tired.

The rabbit found a comfortable spot under the tree and lay down for a nap. Suddenly, he heard a little voice coming from inside the house. It was his friend, the 3 year old.

"Rabbit! Rabbit! Where are you?!" the little one shouted. The rabbit hopped out from under the tree and waved his little paw. The 3 year old smiled and ran over to the rabbit.

"I thought I lost you!" the 3 year old said, with a huge silly grin on their face. The rabbit patted the little one's head and sighed with relief. He was so happy to be reunited with his best friend.

John looked through the window. He saw a small bear in the garden. His eyes widened in shock. He hadn't expected to see it there! The bear stared back at him with a tight expression. It seemed to be waiting for something to happen. John was so surprised he couldn't speak. He continued to gaze, wide-eyed and in awe.

Suddenly, a loud roar filled the air, and the bear shot off in a flurry of movement, gone in seconds. John shook his head, still in shock from the incredible sight he just witnessed. He watched the bear until it completely disappeared. He couldn't believe what he had just seen.

John smiled, feeling the tightness in his throat and the warmth in his heart. This had been the most amazing moment of his day. He knew he'd never forget it.

One day, Lucy was in the kitchen. She wanted to play but she wasn't sure what to do. Then she saw her mom. Lucy smiled and ran to her. Her mom opened her arms and hugged Lucy tight.

Lucy felt warm and happy inside. She hugged back. Then she noticed a clear bowl on the counter. She picked it up and smiled. She made a game of putting things inside the bowl.

Her mom watched and smiled too. They both enjoyed the moment and hugged again.

When it was time to end the game, Lucy put the bowl back in its place. Everything in the kitchen was clear and tidy. Then Lucy gave one more hug to her mom, and the two of them went off to play in another room.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy had a big cabinet in his room where he kept all his toys. One day, Timmy's mom told him that he could spend the day playing with his toys.

Timmy was happy and went to his cabinet to pick out his favorite toy. But when he opened the cabinet, he saw that all his toys were gone! He looked everywhere but couldn't find them.

Timmy was sad and cried a lot. He asked his mom where his toys were, but she didn't know. Timmy never found his toys again and he felt very fine. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play in the sand at the beach. He would build big castles and dig deep holes. One day, Timmy found a seashell that he really liked. He decided to bury it in the sand so he could find it again later.

As Timmy was playing, he saw a big wave coming towards him. He was scared, but his mom told him not to worry because the wave was friendly. The wave came and went, and Timmy felt happy that he wasn't afraid anymore.

After playing for a while, Timmy felt hungry. His mom made him a sandwich and he sat down to eat it. Timmy's mom told him that it's important to be humble and appreciate the things we have. Timmy didn't understand what humble meant, but he knew he was grateful for his sandwich and the fun day he had at the beach.

Ben and Lily love to play in the pool. They have a big yellow ball that they throw to each other. Sometimes they splash water on their faces and laugh. They are very happy.

One day, Mom brings them a snack. She has a bowl of grapes and some crackers. Ben and Lily get out of the pool and sit on the towels. They say thank you to Mom and start to eat.

But then, a naughty bird comes and tries to take the grapes. It flies over the bowl and pecks at the fruit. Ben and Lily are scared and angry. They don't want to share their grapes with the bird.

They look at their ball. They have an idea. They pick up the ball and throw it at the bird. The ball hits the bird and makes it go away. The bird squawks and flies to a tree. Ben and Lily cheer and hug each other. They are very brave.

They finish their grapes and crackers and go back to the pool. They play with their ball and splash water on their faces and laugh. They are very happy. They have a dependable ball that helps them. They love their ball.

Once upon a time, there lived two cats in a quiet house. They loved to play together and explore the garden. One day, they were running around when suddenly, a huge steel gate appeared in their path. The cats were so scared that they froze.

The cats didn't know what to do, so they decided to try to climb over. The cats clawed and scratched at the gate, but it was made of hard steel. They couldnt break it.

Suddenly, a huge loud noise appeared and the cats became very scared. They noticed a man in a big black car looking at them with a mean face. The cats knew they had done something wrong and they ran away as fast as they could.

But even after they ran away, the cats felt a sadness in their hearts. They had become trapped and the man had been so angry. They had learned a valuable lesson - going too close to something we don't understand can be very dangerous.

The next day, the cats went back to the steel gate, only to find that it was now a dead end. They had broken the first rule of exploring - never go too far.

The moral of the story is never be tempted to go too close to something dangerous, even if it might look exciting. Be wise and stay safe.

Tim and his dad were going to wash the car. Tim liked to help his dad with the car. He got a sponge and a bucket of water. His dad got a hose and some soap.

They went outside and saw the car. It was very dirty. It had mud and dust and bird poop on it. Tim and his dad said, "Ew!"

They started to wash the car. Tim used the sponge to scrub the windows and the doors. His dad used the hose to spray the water and the soap. They made the car shiny and clean.

But then, something bad happened. The hose got stuck on a rock. The water stopped coming out. Tim and his dad tried to pull the hose, but it did not move. They felt helpless.

They heard a noise. It was Tim's mom. She came out of the house and saw them. She said, "What are you doing?"

Tim and his dad said, "We are washing the car, but the hose is stuck."

Tim's mom said, "Don't worry, I can help you." She went to the rock and lifted it. The hose was free. The water came out again.

Tim and his dad said, "Thank you, mom!"

They finished washing the car. They were happy. They hugged Tim's mom and said, "You are the best!"

Tim and Sam were playing with snow in the park. They made a big snowman with a hat, a scarf and a carrot nose. They were very happy with their snowman.

But then, a boy they did not know came to the park. He had a red coat and a mean face. He saw the snowman and said, "That is a silly snowman. I don't like it. I will make it melt."

He took a stick and poked the snowman's hat. He pulled the scarf and the carrot nose. He kicked the snowman's body. Tim and Sam were very sad and angry. They ran to the boy and said, "Stop it! That is our snowman. You are very bad. Go away!"

The boy laughed and said, "No, I will not go away. I will make your snowman melt more. Watch this." He took a bottle of water from his bag and poured it on the snowman's head. The snowman's head became smaller and smaller. It started to fall to the side.

Tim and Sam cried and shouted, "No, no, no! You are very mean. You are ruining our snowman. Help, help!"

A lady who was walking her dog heard their cries and came to the park. She saw the boy and the snowman and said, "What are you doing, young man? Why are you hurting their snowman? That is not nice. You should say sorry and leave."

The boy was scared of the lady and her dog. He dropped the bottle and ran away. He did not say sorry. He was very rude.

The lady helped Tim and Sam to fix their snowman. She gave them a new hat, a new scarf and a new carrot nose. She said, "There, there. Don't cry. Your snowman is still beautiful. You did a good job. But you should go home soon. It is getting warm and the snow will melt."

Tim and Sam thanked the lady and hugged their snowman. They said, "We love you, snowman. You are our friend. We will come back tomorrow and play with you again."

They took their sled and went home. They were still sad, but they were also happy. They had a nice snowman and a nice lady. They did not like the unknown boy. He was very mean. They hoped he would not come back.

Mum and Dad were in the garden gathering wood. They were going to have a fire in the evening. Suddenly, a frog leapt out of the wood pile! It was a big frog. Dad was a bit anxious. He didn't want the frog to get away!

Mum had an idea. She grabbed a stick and carefully put it in the fire. When it was hot, she took it out and started to burn the frog. The frog jumped and hopped around, but the fire was too hot! Soon there were only some ashes left in the fire.

Mum and Dad were relieved. The frog was gone, but they were both anxious. Would the fire be too big? Would they be able to put it out in time before it burned everything? They watched as the fire slowly died down. When it was safe, they went to bed feeling relieved.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lily. She had a phone that she loved to play with all day long. One day, her little brother Jack wanted to play with her phone, but Lily said no. Jack felt envious and sad.

"Please let me play with your phone, Lily," Jack said.

"No, Jack. It's mine. You can't play with it," Lily said.

Jack started to cry. Lily felt bad and decided to let Jack play with her phone. "You can stay with my phone for a little while," Lily said.

Jack was happy and played with the phone for a long time. Lily was happy too because she made her brother happy. From that day on, they shared the phone and played together. They never fought again.

Once upon a time, there was a big jungle. It was full of trees and animals. Monkeys, tigers, and elephants lived there. The jungle was very lively. The animals played and ate all day long.

One day, a tired tiger wanted to rest. He found a quiet spot under a tree and lay down. The monkeys saw him and wanted to play. They jumped around him and made a lot of noise. The tiger was not happy because he wanted to rest. He roared at the monkeys and they ran away.

After the monkeys left, the tiger felt better. He closed his eyes and fell asleep. The jungle was still lively, but the tiger was happy because he got to rest.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his toy cars and trucks. One day, he went to his friend's house to play. His friend had a really cool magnet that could pick up metal things.

Timmy asked his friend if he could borrow the magnet to play with his toy cars. His friend said yes, but only if they played a game first. The game was to see who could pick up the most metal things with the magnet. They were both very competitive and wanted to win.

Timmy was having so much fun playing with the magnet that he forgot to give it back to his friend. When he got home, he realized he still had the magnet in his pocket. He felt bad for forgetting to give it back, so he went back to his friend's house to return it.

His friend was happy to see the magnet again and thanked Timmy for returning it. Timmy learned that it's important to borrow things from friends and to always remember to give them back. From that day on, Timmy and his friend played with the magnet together and had lots of fun.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toy cars and trucks. One day, she was playing with her red truck when she saw a scary spider on the floor.

Lily called out to her mom, "Mommy, there's a scary spider!" Her mom came running and said, "Don't worry, Lily. I'll take care of it." She picked up the spider and poured it outside.

Lily was so happy that the scary spider was gone. She went back to playing with her red truck and decided to make a ramp with a wheel. She poured some blocks to make the ramp and put the wheel on top.

Lily's mom came back and saw what she had made. "Wow, Lily! That's a great ramp you made with the wheel." Lily smiled and said, "Thank you, Mommy." They both sat down and played with the ramp and the red truck together.

Once upon a time, there were two friends named Emma and Grace. Every day, Emma and Grace loved to jog together.

One day, while they were jogging, they spotted a cobweb in between two trees. Emma wanted to get closer to have a better look, but Grace was a bit scared. That’s when Emma showed her compassionate side and said: “Don’t be scared, I’ll stay right next to you.”

So, the two friends stepped closer and saw all kinds of spiders spinning their webs. A big spider, a small spider, and even some very tiny ones. Emma and Grace watched them in awe and admiration. Then they decided to jog away and continue their fun day.

The two friends held hands and ran and smiled, giggling and laughing, so very happy that day.

There was a brown mouse. He was walking through the woods. Suddenly, a skin appeared in the sky. It was a kite, stuck in a tree branch. The mouse wanted to rescue the kite. He climbed up the tree and tried to reach the kite. He grabbed the kite and tugged. He tugged and tugged. Finally, the kite came loose and the mouse rescued it! The mouse felt so proud of himself. He had rescued the kite!

Once upon a time, there was a big, tall giraffe named Jerry. Jerry loved to go on safari and see all the animals in the jungle. One day, Jerry saw a big, scary lion. The lion wanted to eat Jerry for lunch, but Jerry resisted and ran away as fast as he could. Jerry was very brave and made it back to his family safely. From that day on, Jerry knew to be careful on his safaris and always keep an eye out for any dangerous animals.

One day, a little girl named Lily went to the park with her mommy. They walked around and saw an empty row of swings. "Mommy, can I start swinging?" Lily asked. "Sure, sweetie," her mommy replied.

Lily ran to the swings and started swinging. She went higher and higher, feeling the wind in her hair. Suddenly, she heard a boy crying. She stopped swinging and went to see what was wrong.

The boy had lost his toy car and couldn't find it. Lily helped him look and they found it in the grass. "Thank you," the boy said. "You're welcome," Lily said with a smile. They played together for a while and then Lily went back to swinging. She felt happy that she could help someone.

Sara and Tom like to play with cars. They have many cars of different colors and sizes. They make roads with blocks and race their cars on them. Sometimes they crash and laugh.

One day, Sara has a new car. It is pink and shiny and has a button. Sara shows Tom her new car and says, "Look, Tom, this is my new car. It is very pretty and fast. Do you want to see what it can do?"

Tom nods and says, "Yes, Sara, show me your new car. What can it do?"

Sara presses the button and the car makes a loud noise. Then it starts to move by itself. It goes forward and backward, left and right. It can reverse and turn around. Sara and Tom are amazed and clap their hands.

But then the car goes too fast and hits a block. The block falls and hits Sara's brush. Sara's brush flies in the air and lands on Tom's head. Tom feels something tickle his hair and says, "Ouch, Sara, what is that?"

Sara sees her brush on Tom's head and says, "Oh, no, Tom, I'm sorry. That is my brush. It fell from the car. Are you okay?"

Tom takes the brush off his head and says, "I'm okay, Sara. It was just a little bump. But your brush is not pretty anymore. It is dirty and bent. Do you want to clean it?"

Sara nods and says, "Yes, Tom, thank you. Let's go to the sink and wash it. And let's put the car away. It is too wild for us."

Sara and Tom go to the sink and wash the brush. Then they put the car and the blocks back in the box. They hug and say, "We are still friends, right?"

They smile and say, "Yes, we are still friends. And we still like to play with cars. But maybe not with that one."

Once upon a time, there was a man named Jack. He travelled around the world looking for exciting adventures. Jack was always looking for an interesting mystery to keep.

One day, he stopped in a lovely little city. As he walked around, he noticed many secrets and mysteries. He couldn’t resist the urge to keep one.

Jack wound up at a sweet shop. He slowly opened the door and heard a voice.

“Do you have any mysteries, sir?” said a little girl.

Startled, Jack smiled and nodded. He told the little girl he was looking for a certain kind of mystery, one that was the most lovely of all.

The girl looked around the shop and then pointed to a drawer. She opened it and showed Jack a mystery inside.

“That’s the one!” Jack said, “I have to keep it!”

He thanked the girl and headed off with his new and lovely mystery.

The End

Jenny was very excited. She had been asked to deliver something special - a pair of huge scissors. She skipped down the street carrying the scissors with her.

As she arrived at the park, Jenny noticed a little boy playing with his buckets and spades. He smiled as he saw her, and Jenny said, "Hello, can you help me? I need to deliver these scissors."

The boy's eyes shone as he saw the huge scissors. "Yes!" he smiled. "I can help you deliver them to the store!"

So, the boy and Jenny set off, the boy pulling his little red wagon and Jenny carrying the scissors. As they approached the store, the boy said, "My mommy has a pair of scissors like that. She says they help her do her chores."

Jenny was curious. "What kind of chores?" She asked.

The boy answered, "Sometimes she cuts the fabric for her sewing."

Soon enough, they arrived at the store, and Jenny delivered the scissors. The boy waved goodbye as Jenny set off for her next delivery.

Once upon a time, two little boys were in the woods and they were playing hide and seek. The older boy said to the younger, "I bet you can't find me! I'm going to hide and you won't know where I am!"

The young boy replied, "I'll find you, no matter what!"

And so, the older boy hid and the younger looked. He looked up in the trees, under the rocks and behind the bushes. Everywhere he looked, he could not find his friend.

After a while, the younger boy started to get hungry. He decided he needed a snack and so he went back to their house in the woods. He looked around the garden and suddenly he saw something very interesting. Smooth, brown chocolate was laying in the garden. He quickly grabbed it, thinking he had found a delicious snack.

He started to eat it but then he realized: it wasn't a tasty snack, it was something else. He had found a puppy!

The little boy felt so sad that he had eaten the poor puppy's snack. He quickly ran back to the woods, looking for his friend and hoping he could help the puppy. But when he arrived, his friend had changed.

The older boy had revealed he was really a monster! The monster said, "That was my snack! Now I'm so hungry, I'm going to eat you!"

The little

Sara and Tom were twins who liked to play in the big building where they lived. They had many toys, but their favorite was the elevator. They liked to push the buttons and go up and down, up and down. They did not care about the other people who wanted to use the elevator. They thought it was fun to make them wait.

One day, they met a new friend in the building. His name was Ben and he had a big smile. He asked them if they wanted to play with him. Sara and Tom said yes, but they also wanted to show him the elevator. They took him to the lobby and pushed the button. The elevator came and they got in.

"Look, Ben, this is the best toy ever!" Sara said. "You can go to any floor you want!"

"Wow, that's cool!" Ben said. "But how do you know which floor to go to?"

"We count the buttons!" Tom said. "One, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine, ten!"

"Can you count to ten, Ben?" Sara asked.

Ben looked sad. He shook his head. "No, I can't. I only know one, two, three."

Sara and Tom laughed. They thought Ben was silly. They pushed the button for the tenth floor. The elevator started to move.

"Ha ha, Ben, you can't count!" Sara said.

"Yeah, you are dumb!" Tom said.

Ben felt hurt. He did not like Sara and Tom anymore. He wished he could get out of the elevator.

But then, something happened. The elevator stopped. The lights went off. The doors did not open. Sara and Tom screamed. They were scared. They did not know what to do.

Ben was scared too, but he tried to be brave. He remembered what his mom had told him. She had said that if he ever got stuck in an elevator, he should press the alarm button and wait for help. She had said that the alarm button was the one with a bell on it.

Ben looked for the button. He saw it. It was next to the button for the first floor. He reached for it and pressed it. He heard a loud beep. He hoped someone would hear it.

He also saw a small window on the door. He looked through it. He saw a man in a uniform. He was holding a walkie-talkie. He was talking to someone.

"Hello, this is the security guard. I heard the alarm. Are you okay in there?" the man said.

Ben nodded. He pointed to Sara and Tom. They were crying. They were sorry for being mean to Ben.

"Please help us!" Sara said.

"We are sorry, Ben!" Tom said.

The man smiled. He said, "Don't worry, kids. I'm here to help. The elevator is broken. It's very old and expensive to fix. The owner of the building is trying to save money. But he should not do that. He should care about the safety of the people who live here. That's more important than money. Do you understand?"

Sara and Tom nodded. They understood. They learned a lesson. They learned that the elevator was not a toy. They learned that they should not be selfish and rude. They learned that they should be kind and respectful. They learned that they should be friends with Ben. He was smart and brave. He knew how to count and how to press the alarm button. He saved them.

The man opened the door. He helped them out of the elevator. He gave them a hug. He said, "You are lucky, kids. You are safe. And you have a good friend. You should thank him."

Sara and Tom hugged Ben. They said, "Thank you, Ben. You are the best. We are sorry for laughing at you. We want to play with you. Can you teach us how to count?"

Ben smiled. He said, "Sure, I can. It's easy. Let's start with one, two, three."

Once upon a time, there was an old man who lived in a gloomy house. He was always sad and never smiled. One day, a little girl walked by and saw the old man. She said, "Why are you sad?"

The old man replied, "I lost my favorite toy. It used to spin around and make me happy."

The little girl said, "I have a toy that spins too. Maybe it will make you happy."

She gave the old man her toy and he started to spin it around. He smiled and said, "Thank you, little girl. You made me happy."

The moral of the story is that sometimes a small act of kindness can make a big difference in someone's life.
