Billy thought for a moment. Then he said, "I want to fix you an avocado". His mom smiled. She nodded and said, "Ok, that would be nice. Let me show you how it's done." She took Billy's hand and together they went to the kitchen.

Billy was a very patient learner and soon he was cutting the avocado, just like his mom did.

When he was done, his mom looked at the avocado and said, "You did a great job, Billy! I'm very proud of you!"

Billy grinned and said, "That was fun! Can I fix something else tomorrow?"

His mom laughed and said, "Of course you can!"

Once upon a time, there were two good friends. One was a bird, and the other a squirrel. One day, the two friends decided to take a walk in the park. As they were walking, they came across something shiny on the ground. It was a silver coin.

The squirrel reached forward to grab the coin and said, "I'm going to spend it on something cool!" The bird quickly said, "No, no! That is wrong. We should rest it in the bank and save it for a rainy day."

The squirrel thought for a moment, and then decided the bird was right. He couldn't resist, however, adding that the coin was too beautiful not to look at every once in a while.

The bird agreed and so the two friends decided to save the coin and look at it from time to time.

The moral of the story is: It's important to save for a rainy day. Don't rush to spend what you have, otherwise you will regret it later.

Once upon a time, in a charming little town, there lived a boy named Tim. Tim had a red wagon that he loved very much. Every day, he would play with his wagon in his yard.

One day, while Tim was playing with his wagon, a big dog came running by. The dog saw Tim's red wagon and thought it was a toy. The dog grabbed the wagon in its mouth and started to run away.

Tim was very sad and started to scream, "No, my wagon!" He ran after the dog, trying to get his wagon back. Tim's mom heard him scream and came outside. She saw the dog with the red wagon and helped Tim get it back.

In the end, the big dog let go of the wagon and Tim was very happy. He thanked his mom for helping him. From that day on, Tim made sure to keep his charming red wagon safe inside when he was not playing with it.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lily. She loved to eat olives, they were her favorite food. One day, Lily's mom brought her a jar of olives. Lily was so happy and ate all the olives.

After a while, Lily noticed that the jar was empty. She asked her mom, "Where did the olives go?" Her mom replied, "They disappeared because you ate them all." Lily was sad that the olives were gone, but she was happy that she got to eat them all.

Suddenly, Lily's dad came in and said, "I have a powerful surprise for you!" He showed her a magic trick where he made a coin disappear and reappear. Lily was amazed and asked, "Can you make the olives reappear too?" Her dad laughed and said, "No, but we can buy more olives and make them disappear again!"

John was a small boy who liked to explore every day. One day, he decided to explore behind his house. He was excited to see a big, shiny automobile. He smiled and ran towards the car.

Suddenly, he realized it was dangerous. He saw a big sign that said "do not touch". John frowned and stepped back. He was a little sad but knew it was the right thing to do.

The next day, his mom took him to the park. She wanted him to have fun in a safe place. He smiled and had a lot of fun.

At the end of the day, John was happy that he was able to explore and to still be safe. He realized that it was important to know when something was dangerous.

Once upon a time, there was a deaf man named Mike. He had a big problem with his hair, so he went to a barber to get a haircut.

The barber looked at Mike's hair and said, "We will need to fix this. It needs a repair". Mike didn't understand what that meant but he nodded his head.

So the barber started to fix Mike's hair. He trimmed it, cut it and combed it. The whole time the barber was very gentle and Mike liked the feeling.

When it was finished, Mike's hair looked so good! He was very glad he got a haircut.

The barber smiled and said, "There you go! Now you look great!" Mike felt so happy and left the shop with a big smile on his face.

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim loved to eat pepper on his food. One day, he wanted to improve his pepper eating skills. So, he asked his mom for help.

"Mom, can you help me improve my pepper eating?" Tim asked. His mom was excited to help her son. She said, "Yes, Tim, let's start by putting a little pepper on your food."

Tim and his mom went to the kitchen. Tim's mom put a little pepper on his food. But Tim was rude and said, "No, I want more pepper!" His mom was sad but she gave him more pepper.

Tim ate his food with lots of pepper. It was too spicy for him. He cried and his mouth hurt. His mom said, "I told you not to be rude and ask for more pepper." Tim learned his lesson and never asked for too much pepper again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who loved to whistle. Every day, the little girl would go outside and whistle songs she knew. One day, while walking in the park, the girl noticed a cobweb against the side of a tree. "What's that?" asked the girl. Just then, a butterfly flew by and said, "That is a cobweb. It's harmless, so don't worry about it". The girl smiled and said, "Thank you".

The butterfly said, "I'm so glad you understand. Some people would have been scared and tried to break it down, but that would be very wrong. Cobwebs are actually important for all kinds of animals to use in their homes, so it's best to leave them alone."

The little girl thanked the butterfly again and went back to whistling her favorite songs while walking in the park. She learned a very important lesson that day - to be kind to all living things, even to something so small and harmless like a cobweb.

Jill walked into her room and saw the bookshelf. It was brown and tall. She liked it. She excitedly walked to it and started to poke it. She poked it softly and then poked it a bit harder. She was having fun.

Then she heard a noise! She looked around and saw something behind the bookshelf. She wondered what it was. She walked closer and saw a big box. Inside the box was a big, stuffed bear. She clutched it tightly and hugged it. She was so happy!

Jill hugged the bear and started to poke the bookshelf again. She had so much fun playing with the bear and the bookshelf. She stayed in her room all day, playing with her new toy and poking the bookshelf. She was having the best day ever!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to count and always wanted to know the number of everything. One day, she went to the park with her mom and saw a little boy crying. She asked him why he was sad, and he said he lost his toy.

Lily wanted to help the boy feel better, so she asked him what toy he lost. The boy said it was a red ball. Lily told him not to worry and that she would help him find it. They started looking together, and after a few minutes, they found the red ball under a bush.

The boy was so happy and thanked Lily for helping him. Lily felt happy too and said, "I'm glad we could get the ball back. It's not nice to be sad." The boy nodded and smiled. From that day on, Lily learned that helping others can make them happy and make you happy too.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lilly. Lilly had a pink hammer and she used it for building things. On one particular day, Lilly was playing with her hammer in the garden.

Suddenly, she saw a small animal. It was black with a fluffy tail and big ears. Lilly smiled and said, "Hello!"

The animal looked at Lilly and asked, "What is that?" Lilly held up her hammer and explained, "It's a hammer. I use it for building things."

The animal seemed a bit confused. It continued to question Lilly, "What can you make with a hammer?"

"Oh," Lilly said, "I can make lots of things. I make chairs, tables, and houses. The hammer is soooooo useful!"

The animal seemed pleased. Lilly smiled and went back to playing with her pink hammer.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys and her friends. One day, Lily and her friends went to the beach. They saw a big boat called a port. The port was very white and clean.

Lily and her friends walked closer to the port. They saw a man on the boat. He was talking to someone on the phone. Lily wanted to talk to the man too. She said, "Hello! How are you?" The man smiled and said hello back.

Lily and her friends had so much fun at the beach that day. They played in the sand and swam in the water. When they were leaving, they saw the white port again. Lily said goodbye to the man on the boat and waved. She couldn't wait to come back and visit the port again.

Anna and Ben like to play sport. They have a ball and a net. They throw the ball to each other and try to catch it. Sometimes they miss and the ball falls on the grass.

One day, they play sport in the park. They have fun and laugh. But then a big cloud comes. It is dark and cold. Anna and Ben hear a loud noise. It is thunder. They see a flash. It is lightning. They are scared.

"Let's go home!" Anna says. "It will rain soon!"

But Ben is stubborn. He likes to play sport. He does not want to stop.

"No!" Ben says. "I want to play more!"

He throws the ball to Anna. But Anna does not catch it. She runs to the bench. She sees a blanket. She covers herself with the blanket. She feels warm and safe.

"Ben, come here!" Anna says. "It is not good to play in the storm!"

But Ben does not listen. He runs after the ball. He does not see the rain. He does not feel the wind. He is wet and cold.

"Ben, please!" Anna says. "You will get sick!"

But Ben is still stubborn. He throws the ball to the net. He misses. The ball rolls away. He chases the ball. He does not hear Anna. He does not see the car. He is in danger.

"Ben, watch out!" Anna screams.

The car stops. The driver gets out. He is angry. He yells at Ben. He takes the ball. He drives away.

Ben is sad. He lost his ball. He lost his sport. He runs to the bench. He sees Anna. She is still covered with the blanket. She is still warm and safe.

"Anna, I'm sorry!" Ben says. "You were right. I was wrong. I was stubborn."

Anna hugs Ben. She shares the blanket. She forgives Ben.

"It's okay, Ben." Anna says. "We can play sport another day. But now we have to go home. Mom and Dad will be worried."

They hold hands. They walk home. They are friends. They are happy.

Once upon a time, there was a big human named Bob. He liked to play with his dog, Max. Max was very happy when Bob played with him. They would run and jump in the park together.

One day, Bob met a large elephant named Ellie. Ellie was bigger than any human Bob had ever seen. Bob was scared at first, but then he saw that Ellie was friendly. They started to play together too. Bob threw a ball and Ellie caught it with her trunk.

Bob was happy that he had made a new friend. He learned that even though Ellie was large, she was still a nice and playful animal. From that day on, Bob and Max would go to the park to play with Ellie. They had lots of fun together.

Once upon a time there was a little bear, and his name was Brownie. He was a very calm bear and he liked to take slow walks in the forest.

One day, as Brownie was walking, he saw a muffin sitting on a log. It looked yummy and he wanted to try it. So he leaned down and took a big bite!

Mmm... it was delicious! Brownie was so pleased, he licked the crumbs from his paw and smiled. He was so happy with his find!

He finished eating his muffin and snuggled back into the log. Then he leaned up against the log and closed his eyes, feeling very calm and content.

The end.

Once upon a time, in a big forest, there was a little mushroom. The mushroom was very fast. It could run faster than any other mushroom in the forest. It loved to play with its friends, the bugs and the birds.

One day, the fast mushroom found a store in the forest. The store had many things like toys, food, and clothes. The mushroom wanted to buy something special for its friends. So, it picked a big toy ball for the bugs and a soft nest for the birds.

The fast mushroom took the gifts back to its friends. The bugs and the birds were so happy when they saw the presents. They all played together with the ball and rested in the soft nest. The fast mushroom was happy too, because it made its friends smile.

One day, Tom had a string. He was very excited; he wanted to play with it. He asked his mom, "What can I do with the string?"

Mom smiled. "You can make something special with it," she said.

Tom thought and thought. Suddenly, he shouted, "I know! I will make a kite!"

Mom said, "That sounds like a serious idea. Let's do it!"

So they got some other things they needed to make the kite. They used some paper and tape and soon it was ready.

Tom and his mom went to the park. Tom was so excited wanting to fly it. He ran around and said, "Look at my kite! Let's make it fly!"

They ran and ran until the kite flew high in the sky. Tom had done it! He felt so proud and kept saying, "I made a kite with my string!"

Jill was out walking with her grandma. She loved holding on to Grandma's hand as they walked together. She spotted a cane lying on the ground and ran to pick it up. Grandma said it was bad to take things that weren't hers, so Jill put it back down. She was sad and looked away. Suddenly, Grandma said to her, "Let's take it". They bent down and pushed the cane to the end of the road. It felt nice to help.

At the end of the road, they saw an old man struggling to walk. Grandma said, "That's why we picked up the cane. We brought it for him." The old man was very happy. He thanked Jill and Grandma and started walking with the cane. Grandma said, "Now, you see why it was bad to take things that weren't yours." Jill nodded and held on tight to Grandma's hand.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy liked to play with his toys all day long. One day, Timmy wanted to make a tower with his blocks. He stacked them up one by one until the tower was very tall and thick.

Timmy's mommy saw the tower and said, "Wow, Timmy, you did a great job! You made a very tall tower." Timmy was very happy and proud of himself. He wanted to show his tower to his friends.

The next day, Timmy had a race with his friends. They all ran very fast, but Timmy was the fastest. He won the race! Timmy was so happy that he jumped up and down. His friends clapped and said, "Good job, Timmy! You are the winner!" Timmy felt very proud of himself and his thick tower.

Ben and Lily were playing with their blocks. They liked to build towers and houses and cars. They used tape to attach some blocks together. They made a big car with four wheels and a roof.

"Look at our car!" Ben said. "It is so cool!"

"Yes, it is!" Lily said. "Let's go for a ride!"

They pushed the car to the door. They wanted to go outside and play. But then they heard a loud noise. It was thunder. The sky was dark and angry. It started to rain.

"Oh no!" Ben said. "We can't go outside! The rain will ruin our car!"

"Maybe we can wait until it stops," Lily said. "Let's put our car in the corner."

They moved their car to the corner of the room. They hoped the rain would stop soon. They sat on the floor and waited.

But the rain did not stop. It got louder and louder. The thunder got closer and closer. The lights went off. The room was dark and scary.

Ben and Lily were afraid. They hugged each other. They wished their mom and dad were home.

Suddenly, they heard a big boom. It was the thunder. It was so loud that it shook the house. It made the tape come off the blocks. The car fell apart. The blocks flew everywhere.

Ben and Lily screamed. They were hurt by the blocks. They cried and cried. They felt very sad. They lost their car. They lost their fun. They had a bad day.

Anna and Ben were playing in the yard. They saw a big box by the fence. It had a sticker that said "mail". They were curious.

"Let's open it!" Ben said.

"Maybe it has a toy or a book inside!" Anna said.

They ran to the box and tore the tape. They lifted the lid and saw a lot of bottles and cans. They had strange words and pictures on them.

"What are these?" Ben asked.

"I don't know. Maybe they are drinks or snacks," Anna said.

She picked up a bottle and shook it. It made a fizzing sound. She opened the cap and smelled it. It was disgusting. It made her nose hurt and her eyes water.

"Yuck! This is not a drink. This is poison!" she said.

She threw the bottle away and wiped her nose. Ben saw the bottle and read the label. It said "bleach".

"Anna, you are right. This is poison. It can make you sick or die. We should not touch these. They are dangerous," he said.

He closed the box and put the tape back. He saw a note on the side. It said "To Mr. Smith, from the pest control company. Do not open. Contains hazardous chemicals."

"Who is Mr. Smith?" Anna asked.

"I don't know. Maybe he lives in the house next to ours. Maybe he has bugs or rats in his house. That's why he needs the poison," Ben said.

They decided to leave the box alone and go back to their yard. They told their mom what they saw. She was glad they did not drink or eat the poison. She called Mr. Smith and told him to get his mail. She also told him to be careful with the poison and keep it away from children and pets. She hugged Anna and Ben and gave them some juice and cookies. They were happy and safe.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily loved to help her mommy cook in the kitchen. One day, Lily's mommy asked her to design an apron for her to wear while cooking.

Lily thought hard about what color to use for the apron. She decided to make it green because it was her favorite color. She got some paper and crayons and started to draw the apron.

Her mommy was so happy with the apron Lily designed. "Wow, Lily! This is the prettiest apron I have ever seen!" exclaimed her mommy. "Thank you, mommy!" replied Lily with a big smile on her face.

From that day on, Lily's mommy wore the green apron every time they cooked together. And Lily was so proud of herself for designing such a beautiful apron for her mommy.

Once upon a time, there was a big tree with lots of apples. The tree was very happy because it was wealthy in fruits. One day, a little girl came by and asked for an apple. The tree was happy to share and split an apple in half for the girl.

The little girl was so happy with the apple that she wanted to give something back to the tree. She made a loop out of a piece of string and put it on one of the branches. The tree was very grateful and felt even more wealthy now that it had a new decoration.

The moral of the story is that sharing makes us all feel wealthy in our hearts. Even if we split what we have, we can still be happy and make others happy too.

Once upon a time there was a brave knight. He wore armour, a shield, and a shining helmet. He was always ready to help others, especially children.

One day he noticed a small girl, who looked very anxious. He approached her and said, "What is wrong?"

The girl shook her head sadly. "My friends don't want to play with me," she replied.

The knight smiled and said, "Maybe I can help. I'll give you a special shield to protect you when you're feeling scared."

The knight gently placed the shield in the girl's hands. He encouraged her to be brave and told her that she was special.

The girl smiled and thanked the knight. From then on she was never anxious when she went out to play. She bravely wore her shield as a reminder that she was safe.

The knight was very proud of her. He said, "See, you can do anything you put your mind to!" The girl beamed with happiness and ran off to join her friends.

Once there was a little girl named Emily. She was very impatient and wanted to play chess with her brother. She went to the toy shop and was very happy when she saw the chess set. She showed it to her brother and they started to play.

Emily was winning the game but then something strange happened. All of a sudden, the pieces on the board started to disappear! Emily was so surprised. She looked around the room but the pieces were nowhere to be seen.

Emily got very upset. She wanted to finish playing the game but the pieces had all disappeared. She started to cry, but then her brother had a great idea. He told her that if they both closed their eyes and said a magic spell, the pieces would come back.

So they both closed their eyes and said the magic words. When they opened their eyes the pieces had reappeared! Emily was so happy that she hugged her brother and continued to play her game.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Maria. She had long, blonde hair and she was very brave. One day, she found a dead bird in her backyard. She was very sad, so she put a scarf around it.

The next day, Maria went out to her backyard. To her surprise, she heard the bird speaking to her. It said, "Thank you, Maria, for the lovely scarf."

Maria was so happy that the bird was alive. She smiled and asked the bird, "How did you get better?"

The bird said, "The scarf gave me life".

Maria was so amazed! She hugged the bird and said, "I'm so happy you're alive." They spent the day playing in the backyard and telling each other stories.

And they lived happily ever after. The end.

Once there was a twin boy and girl who did many amazing things. One day they went to the beach and wanted to keep something special. They saw a bright, shiny shell in the sand and they kept it together.

Next it was time to explore the ocean. Their amazing twin powers allowed them to swim deeper and further than any other children! They were so excited by the beautiful fish and other creatures that they kept swimming and didn’t want to come out.

Then the sun began to go down, and the twins had to return home. But before they went, they hid the shell on the beach so that no one would take it, and kept the location a secret.

The twins couldn’t wait to come back someday and find the shell they had kept. They knew it was amazing and they would have many more amazing adventures together!

One day, Mommy and Daddy were playing with their little girl. The little girl was having lots of fun. She was laughing and jumping around.

Mommy said, “It’s time to rest now. Let’s sit on the floor and be quiet.”

The little girl sat on Daddy’s knee. Then Daddy said, “Let’s be extra quiet and listen. What do you hear?”

The little girl listened. She heard the birds singing and the wind blowing. Then the little girl smiled and said, “I hear lots of things.”

Mommy said, “That’s wonderful! You have very good hearing. Now, let’s be quiet and enjoy being together.”

And so, the family spent some time in the quiet, listening to the birds and the wind. It was a beautiful moment they all shared.

Anna and Ben are twins. They like to play with their toys and books. But sometimes they get tired and need a nap. Mommy tells them to go to their room and sleep for a little while.

"Can we keep playing, Mommy?" Anna asks. She holds her doll and makes it talk.

"No, sweetie, you need a nap. You can play more later. Naps are good for you. They make you grow and learn," Mommy says. She gives Anna a kiss and tucks her in.

"But I'm not sleepy, Mommy," Ben says. He holds his truck and makes it zoom. "I want to play with my truck. It's impressive. It can go fast and make noises."

"I know, honey, your truck is impressive. But you need a nap too. You can play with your truck more later. Naps are good for you. They make you strong and happy," Mommy says. She gives Ben a kiss and tucks him in.

Mommy leaves the room and closes the door. Anna and Ben look at each other. They are not sleepy. They want to keep playing.

"Let's pretend we are asleep," Anna whispers. "Then Mommy won't know."

"OK," Ben whispers. "But don't make any noise."

They close their eyes and lie still. They think they are very clever. But soon they feel very cozy and warm. They forget about their toys and books. They fall asleep and have nice dreams. They have a good nap after all.

Lily liked to spend time with her grandma. Grandma had a big house with many toys and books. Lily also liked to help grandma in the kitchen. Grandma taught Lily how to make cookies and cakes.

One day, Lily and grandma decided to make ice cream. They mixed milk, sugar, and vanilla in a bowl. Then they poured the mixture into a metal pan. Grandma said they had to put the pan in the freezer for a long time. The freezer was a big box that made things very cold.

Lily was very excited to try the ice cream. She asked grandma how long they had to wait. Grandma said they had to wait for two hours. Lily thought that was too long. She wanted to eat the ice cream now. She had an idea. She sneaked into the kitchen when grandma was not looking. She opened the freezer and took out the pan. The ice cream was not ready yet. It was still liquid and cold. Lily did not care. She grabbed a spoon and started to eat.

Grandma heard a noise in the kitchen. She went to see what was going on. She saw Lily with the pan and the spoon. Lily had ice cream all over her face and hands. Grandma was not happy. She said, "Lily, what are you doing? You can't eat the ice cream yet. It's not good for you. It will make you sick and fat. You have to put it back in the freezer and wait until it's ready."

Lily felt sorry. She did not mean to make grandma angry. She said, "I'm sorry, grandma. I was too hungry. I wanted to taste the ice cream. It was yummy." Grandma sighed. She said, "I know, Lily. But you have to be patient. Good things take time. Come on, let's clean up this mess and then we can read a story together. Maybe later we can have some ice cream, if there's any left." Lily nodded. She hugged grandma and said, "I love you, grandma. You make the best ice cream." Grandma smiled and said, "I love you too, Lily. You make me happy." They put the pan back in the freezer and went to the living room. They read a story about a fat cat and a thin mouse. They laughed and had fun. They forgot about the ice cream for a while.

Once upon a time, there was a car. The car had a driver, who drove the car all day long. Suddenly, the driver had to stop. He said, "Oh dear, my car has run out of gas! Now I must go and find some more."

The driver started walking towards a gas station. He said, "I sure hope they have gas when I get there."

When the driver arrived, he was so happy! The station had lots of gas. The driver yelled, "Hooray! I have gas!" He put the gas in his car, then he drove off.

The next day, the driver was driving the car again. He had to yield to a loud truck. The driver was scared of the loud sound the truck made, so he stopped and watched until it passed.

When the truck was gone, the driver started driving again. He drove all day, with no big surprises. He got home safe and sound, thankful that he had yielded. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, Lily wanted to get a snack from the fridge. She opened the door and saw that there was no more juice left. She felt sorry because she really wanted some juice.

Lily decided to ask her mom to get more juice from the store. Her mom said she was sorry too, but they would have to wait until tomorrow to get more juice. Instead, they had some yummy fruit from the fridge. Lily was happy because she got a tasty snack and her mom was happy because they didn't have to go to the store. The end.

Once upon a time, there were two friends named Paul and Sam. They both lived near a big hedge. One day, the two friends decided to separate and play on different sides of the hedge.

Paul was confused and didn't understand why they had to separate. He was sad and wanted to play with Sam again.

So Paul called out to Sam on the other side of the hedge and said, "Come back so we can play together again."

Sam shouted back, "I will come back after I explore the other side of the hedge!"

Paul was excited and waited by the hedge. After a while, Sam came back with a big smile on his face. Paul was happy and they played together under the big hedge again.

Once upon a time two friends, Jenny and Betsy, were playing together. Jenny wanted to draw a purple picture, but Betsy wanted to draw a black one. They both wanted to do something different and they disagreed.

The two friends argued back and forth and did not know what to do. All of a sudden, a prune fell from a nearby tree and landed on the ground between them. Jenny thought the prune was so beautiful and suggested that she and Betsy each draw a picture of the prune. Betsy liked this idea and agreed! They both used some black crayons to draw the prune and were very proud of their work.

In the end, the two friends were happy and had learned a valuable lesson. Even when they disagreed, they found a way to be friends and make each other happy.

Lily liked to play with frogs. She liked to catch them in the pond and put them in a bucket. She liked to look at their green skin and big eyes. She liked to hear them croak and jump.

But her mom did not like frogs. She said they were dirty and slimy. She said they could make Lily sick. She said Lily had to leave the frogs alone and play with her dolls.

One day, Lily found a big frog in the pond. It was the biggest frog she had ever seen. It had spots and stripes on its back. It had a loud croak and a long tongue. Lily wanted to keep it as a pet. She put it in her bucket and ran to her room.

She hid the bucket under her bed and gave the frog some water and flies. She talked to the frog and named it Spot. She said Spot was her best friend.

But mom smelled something bad in Lily's room. She looked under the bed and saw the bucket. She opened it and saw the frog. She screamed and dropped the bucket. The frog jumped out and hopped away.

Mom was very angry. She said Lily was naughty and lied to her. She said Lily had to punish the frog and let it go. She said Lily had to clean her room and say sorry.

Lily was very sad. She did not want to punish Spot. She did not want to lose her friend. She cried and begged mom to let her keep the frog.

But mom did not listen. She took Lily and the frog to the pond. She made Lily say goodbye to the frog and throw it in the water. She said frogs belonged in the pond, not in the house.

The frog was scared and confused. It did not understand why Lily hurt it. It did not understand why Lily left it. It was a modest frog. It did not ask for much. It just wanted to be with Lily.

The frog croaked sadly and swam away. Lily watched it go and cried. She wished she could play with Spot again. She wished mom would understand. She wished frogs and people could be friends.

Lily and Tom were playing with bubbles in the park. They had a big bottle of soap and a wand to make the bubbles. They were very jolly and laughed as they chased the bubbles in the air.

"Look, Lily, I can make a big bubble!" Tom said, as he blew hard on the wand. A huge bubble came out and floated in the wind.

"Wow, Tom, that's amazing!" Lily said, clapping her hands. "Can I try?"

"Sure, Lily, here you go." Tom handed her the wand and the bottle. "But be careful, don't spill the soap."

Lily took the wand and dipped it in the bottle. She tried to blow a big bubble, but she blew too hard and the soap splashed on her face. She felt a sting in her eyes and started to cry.

"Ow, ow, ow, it hurts!" Lily wailed, rubbing her eyes.

Tom felt sorry for Lily and ran to help her. He grabbed a tissue from his pocket and tried to wipe her face. But he was not gentle and he pushed the tissue too hard on her eyes. Lily felt more pain and cried louder.

"Stop, stop, stop, you're hurting me!" Lily screamed, pushing Tom away.

Tom was shocked and hurt by Lily's push. He dropped the tissue and the bottle and the wand. He felt angry and sad. He picked up a rock and threw it at Lily. The rock hit Lily on the head and made a big bump. Lily fell to the ground and fainted.

Tom realized what he had done and felt scared and sorry. He ran to Lily and tried to wake her up. But Lily did not move or talk. Tom cried and cried and cried.

The end.

Once there was a 3 year old boy named Riley. He felt like an ordinary kid and he had never really stood out before. Everyday, he would go to a big park with some of his friends.

One day, they decided to play a game. His friends all cheered him on, and tried to encourage him to play. Riley felt a little shy, but eventually he mustered up the courage to give it a try. His friends cheered louder and louder.

Every day he got a little braver and played more games. He felt encouraged by his friends who were so supportive. One day, everyone was so sweaty and hot from all the games so they decided to cool off with some water from the cooler. They all had fun that day.

Riley was very happy and felt so encouraged by his friends. In the end, he wasn’t an ordinary kid anymore. He realized that with the support of his friends, he was capable of doing anything he set his mind to!

Tina and her mom were walking down the street one day when suddenly the ground started to shake. Tina was scared and her mom was scared too. They both knew what it was: an earthquake!

Tina's mom held tightly onto her hand and said, "Let's hurry home, honey. Don't be scared." But it was hard to walk because the ground was shaking so much. Shoulders hunched, they struggled to make their way home.

When they got there, Tina's mom tightly hugged her, saying, "We made it, sweetie! Now let's sit here and wait until it's over."

Tina was impatient and asked, "When will it end, mommy?"

Her mom replied, "I'm not sure, honey. We just have to wait and see."

So they sat quietly and held each other until the trembling stopped. Then they smiled and hugged each other, feeling glad that the struggle was over.

Once upon a time, there was a boy called Toni. He was very happy all the time because he had a nice watch. He liked to play with it and he always looked after it.

One day, Toni was playing with his watch outside with his friends. Suddenly, another boy, who was a bully, came over to them. He grabbed Toni's watch and ran away with it. Toni was so sad. He didn't know what to do.

His friends were very angry with the bully and decided to go and get Toni's watch back. They ran after the bully and were able to finish him by the park. Then they grabbed Toni's watch back and gave it back to him.

Toni was so happy. He said thank you to his friends for getting his watch back. Then, they all went back to play together and have fun.

It was a nice day and everyone was happy. Toni was happy to have his watch back and he finished playing with it until it was time to go home.

Tom and Jen are twins. They like to play games. One day, they find a big box in the attic. It has a label that says "Prize".

"What is in the box?" Tom asks.

"I don't know. Let's open it and see," Jen says.

They open the box and see many toys. There are cars, dolls, books, puzzles, and more. They are very happy.

"Wow, look at all these toys! They are so fun!" Jen says.

"Yes, they are. But we have to be careful. Mom and Dad don't know we are here. They will be mad if they find out," Tom says.

They decide to take some toys and hide them in their room. They think they can keep the prize a secret. They are very busy moving the toys.

But they don't see that the box has a hole. Some toys fall out of the hole and make a trail on the floor. Mom and Dad come home and see the trail.

"What is this?" Mom asks.

"Let's follow it and find out," Dad says.

They follow the trail and find Tom and Jen in their room. They see the toys everywhere.

"Tom and Jen, what are you doing?" Mom asks.

"We found a prize in the attic. We wanted to play with it," Tom says.

"Did you ask us first?" Dad asks.

"No, we didn't. We are sorry," Jen says.

Mom and Dad are not happy. They tell Tom and Jen that the prize is not theirs. It belongs to their uncle. He left it for them when he moved away. He wanted them to have it when they are older.

"You can't keep the prize. You have to put it back in the box and in the attic. And you have to clean up your room," Mom says.

Tom and Jen are sad. They like the toys. But they know they did something wrong. They say sorry to Mom and Dad. They put the toys back in the box and in the attic. They clean up their room.

They learn a lesson. They have to ask before they take something. And they have to be honest. They hope their uncle will give them the prize when they are older. They hug Mom and Dad and say they love them.

Sara and Ben are twins. They like to play in the backyard. They have a big tent that their dad made for them. They pretend it is a castle or a spaceship or a cave.

One day, they see a new family move in next door. They have a little girl named Lily. She is shy and does not talk much. Sara and Ben want to be her friends.

They go to the fence and say hello. Lily looks at them and smiles. She sees their tent and says, "Wow, that is a nice tent. I wish I had one."

Sara and Ben are happy. They say, "Thank you. We like our tent. Do you want to play with us? You can come inside and see our toys."

Lily nods and follows them. They show her their dolls, cars, books and puzzles. They play together and have fun. Lily is playful and laughs a lot. She likes Sara and Ben.

Sara and Ben admire Lily. They think she is smart and kind. They ask her, "Do you want to be our friend?"

Lily says, "Yes, I do. You are very nice. Can I come back tomorrow?"

Sara and Ben say, "Of course. We are glad you are our neighbor. We can play every day."

They hug and say goodbye. They go back to their houses. They are happy. They have a new friend.

Once upon a time, there was a bad man. He wanted to hide away from everyone. So he found a big, dark carpet in the corner of the room. He was calm and quiet, and he didn't move for a very long time. Everyone wondered where he was.

But then one day, the bad man found that the carpet was too itchy and uncomfortable to hide in. He decided to go somewhere else. He started looking for somewhere new to hide in.

The bad man started to get angry. He started banging and smashing his fists on the walls. Then he got into the cupboard where he thought no one would be able to find him. But he didn't know that there was someone already in the cupboard – the 3 year old child!

The child was scared and he started to cry. He didn't know why the bad man was so angry. The bad man was so angry that he threw the child out of the cupboard. The poor child was hurt and frightened, and the bad man ran away.

The child was very sad and he was never able to find the bad man again. The bad man had gone and the carpet in the corner of the room was still calm, but it was never used to hide in again.

Once upon a time, there was a poor boy who really wanted a scarf. So, one day he ventured out in search of one.

He walked and walked for what seemed like forever, until he reached a meadow in the middle of the woods. Suddenly, he spotted a scarf lying in the grass.

The boy ran towards it, speeding as fast as his little legs could take him.

When he finally got there, he bent down and picked it up. He couldn't believe his luck! He carefully inspected the scarf, looking for flaws, and couldn't find a single one.

He shouted, "Hurray! This scarf is perfect!"

At that moment, a kind old fairy appeared from behind a tree and said with a smile, "Yes, it sure is!"

The boy smiled back and thankfully said, "Thank you for the scarf!"

The old fairy nodded and said, "You're welcome, little one."

And with that, the boy was on his way - scarf in hand.

One day, Spot the dog was running very fast. He ran faster than ever before. Spot was running so fast, it felt like he was flying! As he flew along, he saw a balloon in the sky. He reached out for it, and it came down to him.

Spot was so happy. He held the balloon tight and it lifted him off the ground. Spot was so amazed. He had never been in the sky before. He flew higher and higher, faster than ever before. It was like he was running in the sky.

Then, Spot saw something amazing. It was a powerful wind coming directly towards him. He closed his eyes and felt the powerful wind scoop him up, whizzing faster through the sky. The wind was more powerful than Spot had ever felt.

He stayed in the wind for a long time, until it finally dropped him off, gently placing him back on the ground. Spot opened his eyes, and he was back where he started. He looked up and saw the balloon was still there, high in the sky. He smiled, knowing that he had travelled the sky with the balloon and the powerful wind, faster than ever before.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with cars and trucks, so his parents bought him a big garage to play with. Timmy was very happy and played with his garage every day.

One day, Timmy's friend Billy came over to play. Billy also loved cars and trucks and wanted to play with Timmy's garage. But Timmy didn't want to share. He said, "No, it's mine!"

Billy felt sad and left. Timmy continued to play with his garage, but he wasn't as happy as before. He realized that it wasn't nice to be selfish and not share with his friend.

The next day, Timmy went to Billy's house to apologize and bring his own truck to play with. But when he got there, he saw that Billy had a bigger and better garage than his own. Timmy felt jealous and didn't want to play anymore.

Timmy's humble garage didn't match up to Billy's fancy one, and he felt sad. He went back home, feeling bad about not sharing with his friend. The bad ending was that Timmy lost his friend because of his selfishness.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to read books. She had a big bookshelf in her room. One day, Lily wanted to read a book about a princess, but she couldn't reach it. She asked her mommy, "Please can you help me get the book?" Her mommy smiled and got the book for her.

Later that day, Lily went outside to play. It was very cold outside. The ground was icy and slippery. Lily's mommy told her to be careful. Lily was having fun, but then she slipped and fell down. She said, "Ouch! That was icy!" Her mommy helped her up and they went back inside to read more books from the bookshelf. The end.

John was a big boy for three. He liked to do what his Dad did, so every day he would stare at his Dad’s job. She did things with a computer and wrote things down. John thought it looked like fun.

One day, his Dad told him he should think about getting a job when he was older. He said it could be anything but that some jobs could be very competitive.

John didn't really know what ‘competitive’ meant, so he asked lots of questions. His Dad said it meant that lots of people wanted the same job and so you had to be better than them to get it.

John thought about this a lot. He wanted to have a job one day that was fun and that lots of people wanted. He wanted it to be a special job.

So, every day, he would stare at his Dad’s job and try to think of his own special job. Then he could be the best and get it!

Once upon a time, there was a driver named Tom. He drove a big car with four wheels. One day, Tom saw a little girl trying to cross the road. He stopped his car and waited patiently for her to cross safely.

The little girl was happy and grateful. She smiled and bowed to Tom. Tom smiled back and drove away.

Later that day, Tom saw another driver who was not patient. He honked his horn and drove recklessly. Tom thought to himself, "I am glad I was patient and helped the little girl cross the road safely."

From that day on, Tom always tried to be patient and kind to others on the road.

Once upon a time, there were two friends who were very important to each other. One was a little boy, and one was a little girl. They liked to play together, running and having fun.

One day, the two friends found something special - two matches. They were so excited to find something that united both of them. The little girl said, "we can use this to keep our friendship together".

The little boy was so happy, he wanted to do something special with the matches. So they each made a special wish on their own match. Then they put the two matches together and created a spark.

The little girl said "This is how we stay united." And so, the two friends stayed together forever, forever linked by their special matches. They both knew that their friendship was very important!

Once upon a time, there was a foolish boy who wanted to sell the earth. He thought he could make a lot of money from it. So, he set out to find people who would buy the earth.

One day, the boy came across an old man. He asked the man if he would buy the earth. The old man laughed and said, "No, I could never pay for the whole earth!"

The foolish boy didn't give up. He asked another person, then another, but nobody wanted to buy the earth. Finally, a wise old lady smiled and said, "I can't buy the earth either, but I do have an idea."

The wise old lady said, "There can be peace and happiness on this earth if we all share it. If we share the earth, everyone can live together in harmony. That's much better than trying to sell something that can't be sold!"

The foolish boy was surprised to hear this and learned an important lesson about sharing. From then on, he shared the earth with everyone.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who enjoyed creating things. One day, the little girl saw a file on the floor. She was curious and wanted to explore it. She picked up the file and opened it. Inside, she found a blank piece of paper.

The little girl got excited and decided to get creative. She grabbed some crayons and set to work. She drew a picture of a big sun, a beautiful tree and some friendly animals. Eventually, she created a magical scene.

The little girl felt very calm. She knew that she had made something special. She put the crayons back and took the file with her.

The little girl admired her creation and smiled. From that day on, every time she looked at her file, she felt calm. The little girl had created a magical masterpiece!

Once there was a figure, and it was weird. The figure was round, like a ball. It had two arms and two legs and eyes for seeing and a mouth for smiling. One day the figure wanted to be wrapped up, so it did something weird. It wiggled and jiggled and wrapped itself up, just like the mummy. It was so funny the other figures laughed and clapped. The weird figure smiled and stayed wrapped up. It was a happy figure!

Molly had a fan. She liked it because it made the air cooler in her bedroom. She plugged it in and turned it on. The fan made a quiet whirring sound.

Molly said, "Hello, fan!"

The fan replied loudly, "HI, MOLLY!"

Molly was surprised and asked, "Did you just talk?"

The fan said, "Yes, I did!"

Molly was even more surprised and said, "What else can you do?"

The fan replied in a soft, gentle voice, "I can make you feel cooler. Would you like that?"

Molly said, "Yes, please!"

The fan started to blow gently and soon Molly felt nice and cool. She smiled and thanked her fan.

The fan replied in its quiet voice, "You're welcome, Molly!"

Once upon a time, there was a girl called Emmi. She was really excited one day to find that her family had a secret history. She set off on a journey to find it.

First, Emmi visited the library. She searched for books about her family and asked the librarian for help. The librarian was super kind and showed Emmi some cool history books. But Emmi couldn't find any information about her family there.

Next, she asked her mum and dad. They had some stories to tell and showed Emmi some old photos. Emmi was so happy that she finally found out about her family's secret history.

After that, Emmi went with her family to the museum. The guide showed them around the museum and explained all the interesting things about the past. Emmi was so excited. Seeing history for real was so cool!

Emmi had such a great day finding out about her family's secret history. She couldn't wait to tell all her friends about it.

Tim was suffering. He had been all alone for days, so he went to the store to buy a magazine. He was so happy to see the colorful pages full of stories that he didn't realize how late it had become.

The sun was beginning to set, and the streets started to become quiet. But Tim didn't have time to worry about the fading light. He was too busy looking through the magazine.

Suddenly, a sharp noise startled Tim. He looked up to see a tall figure behind him. It was a robber, and he was not happy to see Tim. The robber grabbed the magazine and ran away.

Tim was left alone in the quiet street with nothing. He had been enjoying his magazine, but now all he had was the suffering of being robbed. He wished he had left the store earlier, but now it was too late.

Ben and Lily liked to play with their toy cars. They had many cars of different colors and sizes. They made a road with their blocks and drove their cars on it. They made sounds like vroom and beep.

One day, Ben found a big round thing in the garage. It looked like a wheel, but it was fake. It was made of plastic and had holes in it. Ben thought it would be fun to use it as a car. He took it to his room and showed it to Lily.

"Look, Lily, I have a new car!" he said. "It is big and round and fast. Do you want to drive it with me?"

Lily looked at the fake wheel. She did not think it was a car. She thought it was silly. She liked her toy cars better. They had doors and windows and lights. She shook her head.

"No, thank you, Ben," she said. "That is not a car. That is a fake wheel. It cannot drive. It can only roll."

Ben did not listen to Lily. He was sure his fake wheel was a car. He put it on the floor and sat on it. He pushed with his feet and made it roll. He felt happy and proud.

"See, Lily, I can drive!" he said. "This is the best car ever. It is so fun and smooth. You are missing out."

Lily watched Ben roll on his fake wheel. She felt bored and annoyed. She wanted to play with her toy cars, but Ben did not want to. She wished he would stop rolling and come back to the road.

Suddenly, Ben hit a bump on the floor. His fake wheel bounced and wobbled. Ben lost his balance and fell off. He hit his head on the wall and started to cry.

Lily ran to Ben and helped him up. She saw a bump on his head. She felt sorry for him and hugged him.

"Are you okay, Ben?" she asked. "That was a big fall. Does your head hurt?"

Ben nodded and sniffed. He felt sad and scared. He looked at his fake wheel. He did not like it anymore. He wished he had listened to Lily.

"I'm sorry, Lily," he said. "You were right. That was not a car. That was a fake wheel. It was not fun and smooth. It was bad and dangerous. Can we play with your toy cars instead?"

Lily smiled and nodded. She took Ben's hand and led him to the road. She gave him a toy car and drove it with him. They made sounds like vroom and beep. They felt happy and safe.

Once upon a time, there were two mugs. They were very different, one was big and round, the other was small and square. The big one was really interesting, with lots of lines and spots on it.

Then, one day, something magic happened! The mugs split. They opened up and became two new mugs. The interesting one still had the same lines and spots, but now it was two mugs.

The mugs were so happy to be two. They were so excited to explore separately. They could go to different places and meet new people. They had so much fun.

Eventually, the two mugs came back together as one. Now they were back together, but they remembered all their interesting adventures separately.

Anna and Ben were twins who liked to perform. They could sing, dance, and act. They always made their parents and friends happy with their shows. One day, they went to camp with their class. They were very excited to sleep in tents, roast marshmallows, and see the stars.

At camp, they met a boy named Max. Max was not nice. He said mean things to Anna and Ben. He said they were silly and boring. He said their shows were bad. He made them feel sad and angry. Anna and Ben wanted to teach Max a lesson.

They had an idea. They decided to perform a scary story for the campfire. They practiced in their tent. They made masks, costumes, and props. They used a flashlight, a whistle, and a rope. They were ready to scare Max.

That night, they gathered around the fire. Anna and Ben said they had a special story to tell. They asked Max to sit in front of them. They said he would like it. Max was curious. He agreed.

Anna and Ben began their story. They told about a monster that lived in the woods. They said the monster was hungry and angry. They said the monster liked to eat children. They made scary noises and faces. They used their flashlight, whistle, and rope to make the story more real. They moved closer and closer to Max.

Max was scared. He did not like the story. He did not like the noises and faces. He did not like the flashlight, whistle, and rope. He thought the monster was real. He screamed and ran away. He tripped and fell. He hurt his knee.

Anna and Ben stopped their story. They saw Max on the ground. They saw his knee bleeding. They felt sorry for Max. They realized they had gone too far. They ran to help him. They said they were sorry. They said it was only a story. They said they wanted to be friends.

Max was still scared. He was also hurt and angry. He did not want to be friends. He said they were mean and cruel. He said he hated them. He said he wanted to go home.

Anna and Ben were very sorry. They had not meant to hurt Max. They had only wanted to make him stop being mean. They had only wanted to have fun. They had made a mistake. They wished they could take it back. They wished they could make Max happy. They wished they could perform a nice story instead.

Once upon a time, there was a small girl named Leah. She was not feeling very happy that day because the sky was gloomy.

Leah's mommy asked her, "What is wrong sweetheart?"

Leah replied, "I have a dream, but I don't know how to bring it to life."

Her mommy said, "You can always bring your dream to life. Just never give up and find the courage to make it happen."

So Leah smiled, and said, "Thanks mommy!" She went outside, looking for the courage to bring her dream to life. She gathered enough courage, and soon enough, her dream started to become true.

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a happy bird. She loved to sing all day long in the trees. One day, she found a message in a bottle. The message said, "You have a perfect voice. Keep singing!" The bird was so happy and sang even louder. She flew all around the forest, singing to all her friends. They loved her singing too! The bird knew that her voice was special and she would always sing her heart out.

Once upon a time there was a small boy who was very scared. He was frightened by the big police car that drove by his house. He saw the bright lights and heard the loud siren buzzing.

One day, while the boy was playing in his garden, the police car came back. Two police officers got out of the car and waved at the boy.

The boy was too frightened to speak, but his mommy came to help. She said to the police officers, "He's just a little boy, he can't talk to you right now."

The police officers were nice, so they smiled at the boy and offered a gift. It was a special police uniform they had brought, complete with a hat and badge.

The boy was delighted and put on the special uniform right away. He was so proud that he even made the police officers salute him! They laughed and said, "You look so cute in your police dress!"

From then on, the boy stopped being so scared of the police car. Instead, he looked forward to seeing it drive by each time, and would proudly wave at the police officers with a big smile!

Once upon a time there was a little girl who loved to go outside and explore her neighborhood. One day she wandered into a big park and noticed a friendly old man. He smiled and asked her if she wanted to hear a story.

The girl said yes, excitedly. He smiled and whispered: “Once upon a time there was a brave knight who carried a bow. He was gentle, kind and compassionate. He used his bow to protect the people in his kingdom and they were very grateful.

The man then asked the little girl, “Do you know what the most important thing was to the brave knight?”

The little girl shook her head. “It’s his compassion. He was able to show kindness to everyone and help make the kingdom a better place.”

The man smiled warmly and the little girl thanked him for the story. She went home feeling inspired and determined to be kind like the brave knight, who never stopped using his bow and showing compassion to everyone.

Davey was walking along the street when he saw something furry. He wanted to catch it and make it his pet. He got closer and closer because he was so persistent. He was determined to catch it, but every time he got near, it would scurry away.

At last he got his hands on it and held it tight. It was a little grey rabbit.

Davey knew that if he kept it, he would need a place to keep it. So he went to a nearby garage and opened the door. He was about to put his furry friend inside when suddenly a voice called out.

The voice shouted, "What do you think you're doing?" Davey screamed and ran away. The voice had belonged to the garage owner and he shut the door quickly. Davey's furry friend was gone and Davey was left with a bad ending.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in her garden. One day, she found a rare flower. It was very pretty and had many colors. She wanted to pick the flower, but her mom told her to please leave it in the garden so that everyone could enjoy its beauty.

Lily was sad at first, but then she realized that it was better to leave the flower where it was. She knew that the flower was special and she didn't want to take it away from the garden. So, she left the flower and went to play with her friends.

Later that day, Lily's mom showed her a book about rare flowers. They looked at all the pretty pictures and Lily was happy that she got to see a picture of the flower she found in her garden. She was proud that she helped keep the rare flower safe in the garden for everyone to see.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Susie. She was three years old and loved to spend time in her garden.

One day, Susie was in the garden,when she heard a surprising sound coming from the woods. She was curious, so she decided to take a look.

She walked deep into the forest and saw a cabin. The cabin was incredible, and Susie was excited. Then, she heard a loud noise. It was the sound of somebody shooting!

Susie was scared, and shouted out to whoever was shooting. A voice shouted back, "Don't worry, little one. I'm just shooting cans for fun!".

Susie was relieved and smiled. The voice belonged to her neighbour, Joe. She thanked Joe before running back home.

Grace woke up in the morning feeling happy. She put on her favourite dress and went straight to the living room. On the floor, she found a puzzle! She was so excited! She immediately started putting the pieces together. Suddenly, she was distracted by a loud noise outside.

She peeked out the window and saw her neighbour in the garden. He looked guilty and was trying to hide something. Grace opened the window to watch. After a few minutes, she saw the neighbour sprint away. Grace ran outside to see what he had left; it was a brand new puzzle!

Grace was so excited, she dragged the puzzle back inside and had the whole thing done by lunch. She was so proud of herself!

When her mum came home from work, Grace proudly showed her the puzzle. Her mum was surprised and gave Grace a big hug. Grace knew then that she had done something special!

Lily and Ben are friends. They like to play in the park. They have a ball and a kite. They run and laugh and have fun.

But then, Lily feels hungry. She looks at her watch. It is time for lunch. She says to Ben, "Ben, I am hungry. Let's go home and have lunch."

Ben nods. He is hungry too. He picks up the ball and the kite. He says to Lily, "Lily, what do you want for lunch?"

Lily thinks. She likes many things. She likes cheese and bread and fruit and juice. She says to Ben, "I don't know. What do you have at home?"

Ben thinks. He has cheese and bread and fruit and juice too. He also has soup and crackers and milk. He says to Lily, "I have soup and crackers and milk. Do you like that?"

Lily smiles. She likes soup and crackers and milk. She says to Ben, "Yes, I like that. That sounds good."

They hold hands and walk to Ben's house. They are patient and polite. They say hello to Ben's mom. She is happy to see them. She says, "Hello, Lily and Ben. You are welcome to have lunch with us. What are your names?"

Lily and Ben say their names. They say thank you to Ben's mom. They sit at the table and eat their lunch. They share their cheese and bread and fruit and juice. They enjoy their soup and crackers and milk. They are full and happy.

They say thank you again to Ben's mom. They say goodbye to each other. They hug and promise to play again soon. They are good friends.

Once upon a time, there was an old man. He had a bike with lots of special gear. It was a special bike because the old man used it to make things.

One day, the old man was riding his special bike, when something went wrong. Suddenly, all of his gear was broken! The old man was very sad.

The old man had to take his bike to the mechanic. The mechanic tried, but he couldn't fix the broken gear. So, the old man decided to take a break and rest. He left the bike with the mechanic and went to the park.

At the park, the old man was very happy. He took a long rest and forgot about his broken gear. After a few days, the mechanic had fixed the bike. The old man was very happy and he rode his bike home.

The old man was happy that he had taken the time to rest, because it allowed the mechanic to fix his bike. From then on, the old man made sure to take a rest when something went wrong!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her dolls on the table in her room. One day, her mom came in and said, "Lily, we need to remove this table from your room. It's too big and taking up too much space."

Lily didn't want her table to go away. She said, "Mommy, why do we have to remove my table? I like it here."

Her mom explained, "We need to make room for your new bed. The table can go in the living room."

Lily thought this was crazy, but she knew her mom was right. She helped her mom remove the table from her room and put it in the living room. Now, Lily had more space to play and a new bed to sleep in. She was happy.

Once there was a little girl named Lucy. She decided to go to a very special event. It was going to be a fake event, but she didn't know that.

When she got there, the event was decorated with streamers and balloons. But everything seemed too good to be true. Then Lucy looked a little closer and she noticed the decorations were made of paper and not real.

Lucy was disappointed, so she decided to go home. On the way, she found a real event full of real decorations. Lucy was so happy and excited! She wanted to stay forever.

The end.

Sara and Tom are playing with their toy dinosaurs. Sara has a big green one with sharp teeth and spikes. Tom has a small brown one with a long neck and a tail. They make noises and pretend to fight.

"Rawr! My dinosaur is stronger than yours!" Sara says.

"No, mine is faster and smarter!" Tom says.

They bump their dinosaurs together and knock over a block tower. They laugh and build it again.

Then Sara sees something shiny on the floor. It is a scale from a real fish. It is silver and smooth and sparkles in the light.

"Wow, look at this!" Sara says. She picks up the scale and holds it to her dinosaur's back. "Now my dinosaur has a shiny scale! It is so pretty!"

Tom looks at the scale and wants it too. He thinks his dinosaur is dull and boring.

"Give me that scale!" Tom says. He tries to grab it from Sara.

"No, it is mine! I found it!" Sara says. She pulls it away from Tom.

They tug and pull and shout. The scale slips from their hands and flies across the room. It lands on the window sill and sticks there.

They stop and stare at the scale. They feel sad and sorry.

They look at each other and say, "I'm sorry."

They hug and make up. They decide to share the scale and take turns putting it on their dinosaurs.

They go back to playing and having fun. They forget about the block tower and knock it over again. They laugh and build it again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to wander in the forest near her house. One day, she saw a band of animals walking by. There were rabbits, squirrels, and even a deer. They looked lost and confused.

Lily asked, "What's wrong? Why are you all wandering around?"

The rabbit replied, "We lost our way home. We can't find our burrow."

Lily thought for a moment and said, "Don't worry, I can help you find your way. Follow me."

Lily led the band of animals through the forest, and soon they found their burrow. The animals were so happy and grateful to Lily. They thanked her and gave her a clear crystal as a gift.

Lily smiled and said, "I'm glad I could help. Now, I have to go home for dinner. Bye!"

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One night, she had a bad dream and woke up crying. Her mommy came to her room and asked what was wrong. Lily said she had a nightmare about a big, scary monster.

To make her feel better, mommy told Lily they could act out a funny story together. They pretended to be silly animals and made funny noises. Lily laughed and forgot all about her bad dream.

From that night on, whenever Lily had a bad dream, she knew her mommy would be there to act out a funny story and make her feel better. And she never had to be scared of the monsters in her nightmares again. The end.

Lily was a lazy cat. She liked to sleep on the sofa all day and night. She did not like to play with toys or run around the house. She only woke up when she was hungry or thirsty.

One day, Lily was sleeping on the sofa as usual. She did not hear the door open and close. She did not see her owner, Sam, come in with a big bottle of shampoo. She did not smell the soap and water in the bathroom.

Sam wanted to give Lily a bath. He thought Lily was dirty and smelly. He picked up Lily from the sofa and carried her to the bathroom. He put her in the tub and turned on the faucet.

Lily was very scared and angry. She did not like water or shampoo. She did not like to be disturbed from her sleep. She meowed loudly and scratched Sam's arm. She tried to jump out of the tub, but Sam held her firmly.

"Stop it, Lily!" Sam said. "You need a bath. You will feel better and look nicer. It will be over soon. I promise."

Lily did not listen to Sam. She kept meowing and scratching. She hated the bath. She hated the shampoo. She hated Sam for disturbing her. She wished she was back on the sofa, sleeping.

One day, there was a little boy who had to pass a gloomy forest. The forest was filled with steel trees. He had to be careful because the trees were very sharp! He slowly passed between the trees, making sure to stay away from them. As he made his way through, he heard some curious noises coming from deep in the forest.

He nervously took a few steps closer and realized the noises were coming from a scary, steel monster! He was scared but bravely moved closer anyway. The monster inched closer and closer but then suddenly stopped. After a long pause, it unexpectedly passed him by.

He was so relieved and continued to pass through the gloomy forest. Soon he made it out of the forest and smiled with relief. He looked back at the steel monsters, realizing how brave he had been.

Once upon a time, there was a strong kitten. The kitten was so strong that no one could prevent it from jumping around and having fun. One day, the kitten hat a wonderful idea: to climb the tallest tree in the forest. It began to climb and soon was at the top. But then, something very bad happened: the strong wind started to blow and the kitten started to fall. The kitten tried to grab onto branches but the wind was just too strong. Luckily, a kind angel was watching from above and came to the kitten's rescue. She grabbed the kitten and held it tight in her arms. She prevented the kitten from falling and saved its life. The kitten was so thankful and decided to be a good friend to the angel. From that day on, they were the best of friends. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to help his mom in the kitchen. One day, his mom asked him to put some wheat into a bowl. Timmy was so excited to help! He took a little scoop of wheat and put it into the bowl. His mom was so happy and gave him a big hug. Timmy felt so proud of himself for being such a good helper. From that day on, Timmy loved to help his mom in the kitchen and put things into bowls.

Molly was a healthy three year old girl. She was full of energy and adventure. One morning, Molly was so excited to go to the classroom. She ran and pulled her mom's hand down the hallway. The classroom was full of fun and energy. When Molly entered the room she saw lots of crayons, books and toys. Molly was so happy she started to spin around and pull the toys off the shelf. She then ran around the classroom and pulled her friends hands to join her in the fun. Even though the day was over, Molly was still full of energy. She pulled her mom's hand and ran off to have a healthy snack.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his toy bricks. One day, Timmy's friend Billy came over to play. Billy was being naughty and broke one of Timmy's favorite bricks.

Timmy's mommy saw what happened and offered to help fix the broken brick. She used some glue and put it back together like a puzzle. Timmy was so happy that his mommy could fix his broken brick. From that day on, Timmy and Billy played nicely with the bricks and had lots of fun together.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys and her friends. One day, Lily lost her favorite toy, a little teddy bear. She searched everywhere for it, but she couldn't find it.

Lily asked her mom for help. Her mom said, "Let's search together!" They looked under the bed, in the closet, and even outside. Finally, they found the teddy bear in the toy box.

Lily was so excited and happy to have her teddy bear back. She hugged it tightly and smiled. Her mom said, "Remember, Lily, if you lose something, don't give up. Keep searching and you will find it." From that day on, Lily always searched for things she lost and never gave up.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl. She was very excited. She had a special cloth in her hands. It was blue, and sparkly. She looked at it and said "thank you!

She ran to her mom and said "thank you for the cloth!" Her mom was very happy and smiled. She said "you're welcome. I'm glad you like it."

Then the little girl ran to the store to show everyone her cloth. Her friends were very excited to see it. They all said "thanks for sharing! It's beautiful!"

The little girl smiled and said "you're welcome!" She was so excited to show everyone her special cloth. And they were all so excited to see it.

Tim has a pet cat. He likes to play with his cat and give her food. His cat is soft and nice. She purrs when Tim pets her.

One day, Tim hears a loud noise outside. He goes to the window and sees a big dog. The dog is fierce and angry. He barks and growls at the cat. The cat is scared and runs away.

Tim is sad and worried. He wants to find his cat and make her safe. He puts on his shoes and coat and goes outside. He listens for his cat. He hears a meow from under a car. He sees his cat hiding there.

Tim calls his cat and reaches for her. The cat comes out and jumps into his arms. Tim hugs his cat and takes her inside. He gives her some milk and a toy. The cat is happy and calm. She purrs again when Tim pets her.

Tim is glad he found his cat. He loves his pet and wants to protect her. He tells his cat not to go outside when there is a fierce dog. He tells his cat he will always listen to her. The cat and Tim are good friends.

Tim and Kim are twins. They like to play with their toys and books. But they do not like to clean their room. They are lazy.

One day, Mom comes to their room. She sees a big mess. She is angry. She says, "Tim and Kim, you need to clean your room now. It is not nice to leave your toys and books everywhere. You will lose them or break them. And you will have no space to play. You are big enough to help me. Do not be lazy."

Tim and Kim do not want to clean their room. They want to play. They say, "Mom, we are tired. We do not want to clean. Can we do it later?"

Mom says, "No, you cannot do it later. You need to do it now. If you do not clean your room, you will not get any dessert. And you will have to listen to a lecture from me. Do you want that?"

Tim and Kim do not want to miss dessert. And they do not want to listen to a lecture. They know Mom is serious. They say, "OK, Mom, we will clean our room. But can you help us?"

Mom says, "I will help you a little bit. But you have to do most of the work. It is your room. And you have to learn to be responsible. Now, let's start. First, we will weigh your toys and books. We will put the heavy ones in the big box. And we will put the light ones in the small box. Then, we will put the boxes on the shelf. Do you understand?"

Tim and Kim nod. They say, "Yes, Mom, we understand. We will weigh our toys and books. And we will put them in the boxes. And we will put the boxes on the shelf. We will make our room clean and nice. And we will not be lazy anymore."

Mom smiles. She says, "That's good. I am proud of you. Now, let's get to work. And when we are done, we will have some dessert. And we will read a story. How does that sound?"

Tim and Kim smile. They say, "That sounds great. Thank you, Mom. We love you."

Mom says, "I love you too. Now, let's go."

Once upon a time, there were two friends named Jill and John. They were playing together in the park.

Jill found a board and grabbed it. She was so excited because it was the perfect size for a game that she wanted to play. John was a bit jealous and said, "Can I grab it too?"

Jill said, "No, John. This board is for me." She was starting to feel embarrassed because she didn't want to make John sad.

John felt a bit sad, but he understood. He said, "That's okay. We can play together."

Jill smiled. She said, "Yes, let's play together! We can both grab this board and have lots of fun!"

They grabbed the board and ran around the park together. They had a great time and weren't embarrassed anymore.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily loved to play all day long and never wanted to go to bed. Her mom always told her that she would become tired if she didn't sleep, but Lily didn't listen.

One night, Lily's mom tucked her into bed and said, "Goodnight, Lily. Sleep well." Lily replied, "I don't want to sleep. I want to play." Her mom said, "But if you don't sleep, you'll become tired." Lily said, "I don't care. I want to play."

Lily stayed up all night playing and didn't go to sleep. The next day, she became so tired that she couldn't even get out of bed. Her mom said, "I told you that you would become tired if you didn't sleep." Lily said, "I'm sorry, Mom. I'll go to sleep early tonight." But it was too late. Lily had become sick from not sleeping and had to stay in bed for a whole week.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved playing with cardboard boxes. He would build huge forts and castles out of them.

One day, Timmy's mom came in and said, "Timmy, it's time to clean up your room." But Timmy didn't want to stop playing. He resisted and said, "No, Mommy! I want to keep playing with my cardboard castle."

His mom replied, "I understand that you love playing with cardboard, but we need to clean up so we can find your toys." Timmy thought about it for a moment and then said, "Okay, Mommy. I'll help clean up."

Together, they cleaned up the room and put away all of Timmy's toys. Timmy felt proud of himself for helping his mom. And later, he built an even bigger cardboard castle to play in.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to gaze at the stars every night before she went to bed. One night, she saw a shooting star and made a wish.

The next day, Lily went to the park to play with her friends. They decided to play hide and seek. Lily found a good hiding spot behind a big tree. But when she tried to come out, she couldn't. The lock on the tree was stuck!

Lily's friends saw her and asked her what was wrong. "I'm stuck!" Lily said. "The lock won't open." Her friends tried to help, but they couldn't get the lock to budge. Just when they thought they were stuck for good, a rich man came by and saw what was happening. He had a big key that fit the lock perfectly. He opened it and Lily was free. "Thank you, kind sir!" Lily said.

Ben and Lily went to the beach with Mom and Dad. They liked to play in the sand and look for shells. They also liked to splash in the water, but not too deep.

One day, the water was very high and fast. It was a tide. Mom and Dad told Ben and Lily to stay close and be careful. But Ben wanted to see how far he could go. He walked into the water until it reached his waist.

"Ben, come back!" Lily called. "The tide is too strong!"

Ben did not listen. He wanted to be brave and have fun. He tried to walk more, but the water pushed him back. He tried to resist, but the water was stronger. He started to feel scared.

"Help!" Ben shouted. "I can't go back!"

Mom and Dad heard Ben and ran to him. Dad reached out his hand and pulled Ben out of the water. Mom hugged Ben and Lily and checked if they were okay.

"Ben, you were very silly," Mom said. "You could have been hurt by the tide. You have to listen to us and be safe."

"I'm sorry, Mom," Ben said. "I won't do it again."

Mom and Dad gave Ben and Lily a sweet kiss and a sweet treat. They told them they loved them very much. Ben and Lily said they loved them too. They learned to be careful and obey at the beach.

Once upon a time, there was a little penguin named Pippin. Pippin lived in a cold place with lots of snow and ice. He had many friends, but his best friend was a big, white bear named Benny.

One day, Pippin was playing with Benny when he fell down and hurt his wing. Pippin was sad because it was hard for him to play with his friends. Benny wanted to help Pippin feel better, so they went to search for something to make his wing stop hurting.

They looked all over the snowy ground and found a soft, warm cloth. Benny put the cloth on Pippin's hurt wing, and it made him feel much better. Pippin and Benny were very happy, and they played together in the snow for the rest of the day.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to visit her grandma's house. One day, Lily saw something different in the sky. It was a big, bright, yellow sun! Lily was so happy to see it.
