She asked her grandma why the sky was different today. Her grandma explained that sometimes the sky looks different because of the weather. Lily thought that was very interesting.

After they talked about the sky, Lily and her grandma played games and had snacks. Lily loved visiting her grandma's house because they always had fun together. She couldn't wait to come back and see what other things they could do.

Mama and Papa had a party for their little girl. It was her third birthday. Everyone had come over to celebrate. There was cake, games, and balloons. The little girl was so excited.

The guests all cheered as Mama and Papa gave the little girl a shiny new toy. "Thank you," she said with a smile.

Mama and Papa then revealed to the guests that the toy was actually a surprise. They said it was a trap. The little girl was curious and asked what it was. Papa explained it was like a game. He said if she did something the trap would make a noise and they would all applaud.

The little girl was embarrassed, but she was excited too. She stepped up to the trap and tried her best. When the trap finally made a sound, everyone clapped and cheered. She was so proud of herself.

"See," Papa said, "you were brave and you did it!" The little girl smiled and hugged Papa. She was so happy to have accomplished something and everyone else was proud of her. It was her best birthday yet.

Once upon a time there was a little dog who lived in a house with his family. He was very happy. One day, the little dog got lost in the woods and he couldn't find his way back home. He was very scared, but then he heard his family calling for him.

The family came to rescue the little dog and brought him back home. But the little dog was sick, so the family brought him to a veterinarian. The veterinarian examined the little dog and said he was not feeling well.

The veterinarian gave the little dog medicine and talked to the family about how to take care of him. The veterinarian was very kind, but his medicine was very expensive. The family had to pay a lot of money to the veterinarian to help the little dog get better.

But luckily, the little dog was rescued and soon he was feeling much better. He was very thankful to his family, the veterinarian, and to all the people who helped save him. And they all lived happily ever after!

Suddenly there was a loud noise. All the children rushed to see what was happening.

They saw an old bald man running. He was running very fast and his body was shaking.

Suddenly the man stopped and he clapped his hands. He looked very happy. He said, "Come and join me. Let's have a race!"

The children started to race around. They were laughing and rushing around. After a few minutes, the old man said, "That's enough, come have a rest."

The children sat down in a circle around the old man. He said, "Great job everyone. That was lots of fun!" Everyone smiled and laughed.

The old man said he had to go. The children said goodbye and waved as he walked away. They had a lot of fun racing with the old bald man.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, she went to the park with her mom. Lily saw a big swing and wanted to play on it. "Mommy, can I reach the swing?" she asked. Her mom said yes and helped her get on the swing.

Lily was having so much fun swinging back and forth. But then, she accidentally fell into a pile of mud. Her clothes were filthy! "Oh no, Mommy! Look at me, I'm so dirty," Lily said.

"It's okay, sweetie. We can go home and change," her mom replied. They went back home and Lily took a nice warm bath. She felt much better and clean again. "Thank you, Mommy," Lily said. "I love you." "I love you too, Lily," her mom replied with a smile.

Once upon a time, there were two boys, Peter and Jack. Peter was a very tidy boy and he kept his room neat and clean. Jack, on the other hand, was very messy. Jack didn’t like to clean his room and every day his room got messier and messier.

One day, Jack was feeling hungry and went to his cupboard to get some jam. Unfortunately, he couldn’t find it because his room was so messy. He started to look everywhere but the jam was nowhere to be found.

At the same time, Peter was tidying up his room and found the jam. Peter smiled and ate it happily.

From this experience, Jack learned an important lesson. He realized that if he had been tidy and kept his room clean, he would have found the jam easily.

So from that day forward, Jack tidied his room every day and kept it nice and neat. And whenever he felt tired he would take a nap in his tidy room so he felt happy and comfortable.

Once upon a time there was a chubby little girl called Sally. She had never seen a cupboard before and was very excited to meet one. She was playing in her garden when she heard a creak. Looking up, she saw a big wooden cupboard standing tall in the distance.

Sally couldn't believe her eyes. She didn't know cupboards could be so tall. She just had to meet it. She ran to the cupboard and began running her hands up and down its wooden sides. As she did so, she heard a voice behind her. "Hello there," the voice said. It was the cupboard! "My name is Cupboard. It's so nice to meet you!"

Sally was so happy. She had never met a cupboard before, and it was even chubbier than her! She smiled brightly and said, "My name's Sally. It's nice to meet you too!"

They talked and played together for the rest of the day. When it was time to leave, Sally gave the cupboard a big hug and said goodbye.

From that day, Sally and her new friend Cupboard were best friends. They would often meet up in Sally's garden to play and have fun. What a wonderful friendship!

Once upon a time there was a little boy named Tom. Tom loved looking up into the night sky. One night he saw a star that was twinkling just for him. As it shone, Tom wished that he could pick the star right off the sky. Suddenly, he heard a 'plop' and the star dropped onto the ground in front of him. Tom bent down to pick up the star. He was surprised by its shape and how sparkly it was. When he looked closer he saw that the star was really a delicious cookie. He ate it and it tasted so yummy. Tom was so pleased. What a special night it had been- he had seen a twinkling star and got a delicious cookie! Tom promised to go outside late at night and wish on the stars, because you never know- one of your wishes might drop right in front of you!

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved playing with his toys, but he had a hard time keeping them organized. His mom told him that it's important to keep things tidy and clean, so Timmy decided to unpack all of his toys and put them away neatly.

Timmy's favorite toy was a big blue ball. He loved playing with it, but it was hard to put away because it was so big. However, Timmy knew that it was important to keep his room clean and he didn't want his mom to get upset with him.

So, Timmy took a deep breath and began to put away his toys. It wasn't easy, but he felt proud of himself when he was finished. His room looked neat and tidy, and he knew his mom would be happy.

The moral of the story is that sometimes things might seem hard, but if you try your best and keep at it, it can become easy. And when you keep things organized, it makes everyone happy!

Ben and Lily were playing in the kitchen. They wanted to make a cake for Mom. They found some dough in the fridge and put it on the table. They rolled it and cut it with cookie cutters. They made stars and hearts and circles.

"Look, Lily, I made a big star!" Ben said. He showed his cookie to his sister.

"That's nice, Ben. I made a heart for Mom. She will love it!" Lily said. She smiled and put her cookie on a tray.

They had some dough left. They decided to make funny shapes with it. They twisted it and squeezed it and stretched it. They made snakes and worms and balls.

"Look, Lily, I made a crazy snake!" Ben said. He waved his dough snake in the air.

"That's funny, Ben. I made a crazy worm!" Lily said. She wiggled her dough worm on the table.

They laughed and played with their dough. They did not see that Mom was watching them from the door. She smiled and took a picture of them.

"Hi, kids. What are you doing?" Mom asked.

"We are making a cake for you, Mom!" Ben and Lily said together.

"That's very sweet of you, but you know what? You need to bake the cookies in the oven, not play with the dough. And you need to clean up the mess. Look, you have dough on your hands and faces and clothes. And on the floor and the walls and the chairs. You made a big splash of dough everywhere!" Mom said.

"Oops, sorry, Mom. We did not mean to make a mess. We just wanted to have fun." Ben and Lily said.

"I know, I know. You are very creative and playful. But you also need to be careful and tidy. Come on, let's wash your hands and faces and put the cookies in the oven. Then we can clean up the kitchen together. And then we can eat the cake and enjoy your wonderful shapes. How does that sound?" Mom said.

"Okay, Mom. That sounds good. We love you, Mom." Ben and Lily said.

They hugged Mom and followed her to the sink. They washed their hands and faces and helped Mom put the cookies in the oven. Then they cleaned up the kitchen and waited for the cake to be ready. They were happy and proud of their work. They had a lot of fun with the dough. And they learned a lesson about splashing and cleaning.

Sara loves to play with her tea set. She has a pink pot, four cups, and a big cake. She invites her teddy bear, her doll, and her cat to have tea with her. She pours water from the pot into the cups and pretends it is hot tea. She gives each of her friends a slice of cake and says, "Here you go, enjoy your tea and cake!"

But her cat does not like tea and cake. He likes milk and fish. He looks at the water and the cake and feels sad. He does not want to hurt Sara's feelings, but he does not want to eat or drink what she offers. He says, "Meow, meow, thank you, Sara, but I do not like tea and cake. Can I have some milk and fish instead?"

Sara hears her cat and feels sad too. She wants her cat to be happy and have fun with her. She says, "Oh, I am sorry, cat. I did not know you do not like tea and cake. I only have water and cake. I do not have any milk and fish. What can I do?"

Her teddy bear and her doll see Sara and her cat feeling sad. They want to help them. They say, "Sara, cat, do not be sad. We have an idea. Why don't you pretend that the water is milk and the cake is fish? Then you can both enjoy your tea and cake and have fun together."

Sara and her cat think about the idea. They decide to try it. They use their imagination and pretend that the water is milk and the cake is fish. They say, "Cheers, let's have some milk and fish!" They sip and nibble and smile. They feel happy and have fun with their friends. They thank their teddy bear and their doll for their idea. They say, "You are very smart and kind. You made our dream come true!"

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his toys, but he always had trouble keeping them on his shelf. One day, he asked his mommy for help.

"Mommy, can you help me keep my toys on my shelf? They keep falling off," Timmy said.

"Yes, Timmy. I can prevent your toys from falling off your shelf by putting up a rough piece of paper to hold them in place," Mommy replied.

"Thank you, Mommy!" Timmy said with a big smile.

Mommy grabbed a rough piece of paper and put it on the shelf. Timmy's toys stayed in place and he was very happy. From then on, Timmy made sure to put his toys back on the shelf to keep them safe. The end.

Once upon a time, there lived a clever squirrel. The squirrel loved to explore the forest, looking for acorns and other tasty treats. One morning, the squirrel had to decide where to go. Suddenly, he spotted a delicious looking nut in a nearby tree. He decided to quickly climb the tree to get the nut. Climbing the tree was tricky because he had to be very careful not to miss his footing. Eventually, the squirrel reached the nut and grabbed it with his claws. He scurried back down the tree and happily enjoyed his tasty snack. The squirrel was very happy with his decision and enjoyed his delicious nut. The End.

One day, a little girl named Lucy went to the park. She saw a good spot to lay her blanket. She put her blanket down and lay on it. Lucy wanted to have a fun day at the park.

Soon, Lucy's friend Tom came to the park. He saw Lucy's blanket and said, "Lucy, I want to lay on your blanket too!" Lucy said, "Okay, Tom. But first, we have to pass a test. We have to find five rocks."

Tom and Lucy looked all around the park for rocks. They found one, two, three, four, but they could not find the fifth rock. Tom was sad. He said, "I don't think we can pass the test, Lucy."

Lucy did not want Tom to be sad. She said, "I have an idea! Let's look for the last rock together!" They looked and looked, and finally they found the fifth rock. They passed the test and were both happy. Tom and Lucy lay on the blanket together, and they had a great day at the park.

Billy was feeling sad because he was alone in the big city. He had never been so far away from home. Suddenly, he saw an elevator nearby and he decided to take it.

The elevator was big and shiny. Billy watched it move up and down. Suddenly the doors opened and he saw a lady inside. She looked very kind and compassionate.

The lady smiled at Billy and said, "don't be scared. I'm here to help you find your way." The lady asked Billy where he wanted to go.

Billy told the lady he wanted to get back home. She said that she knew the way and asked if he wanted to watch the elevator while they travelled. He nodded and they stepped into the elevator.

Billy watched the numbers change as the elevator moved up and down. It felt like a long time but eventually Billy was home. The lady gave him a hug and said goodbye.

Billy knew he had made a friend and thanked the lady for being so compassionate.

Lily and Tom were playing with their crayons and paper. They liked to draw and color different things. Lily drew a big flower with many petals. Tom drew a car with four wheels. They were proud of their work.

"Look at my flower, Tom. It is very pretty and colorful," Lily said.

"Look at my car, Lily. It is very fast and shiny," Tom said.

They showed each other their drawings and smiled. They decided to give their drawings to their mom as a gift. They wanted to surprise her and make her happy.

They ran to the kitchen where their mom was making cookies. They hid their drawings behind their backs and said, "Mom, we have something for you."

"What is it, my sweeties?" Mom asked.

They showed their drawings to Mom and said, "We made these for you. They are prints of our art. Do you like them?"

Mom was very surprised and happy. She hugged them and said, "I love them. They are very attractive and creative. You are both very talented and thoughtful. Thank you so much."

She put their prints on the fridge with magnets. She gave them each a cookie and a kiss. Lily and Tom felt very proud and happy. They had surprised their mom with their prints. They had made her smile.

Once upon a time, there was a big brown cow named Betsy. Betsy lived on a farm with lots of other animals like chickens and pigs. One day, the farmer came to Betsy and said "I need your help, Betsy. I need some meat for dinner tonight." Betsy said "Moo, I can supply the meat for you!"

The farmer was very happy and said "Thank you, Betsy! But the meat needs to be ready soon." Betsy didn't know what "ready" meant, so the farmer explained "It means the meat needs to be cooked and delicious to eat." Betsy said "Moo, I understand now. I will make sure the meat is ready for you!"

Betsy went to the other cows and asked if they wanted to help supply the meat. They all said "Moo, yes!" So, Betsy and her cow friends went to the farmer and gave him the meat. The farmer cooked it and it was very tasty. Betsy was happy that she could help supply the meat and make it ready for the farmer. The end.

Ben and Mia liked to play in the park. They had a small boat that they could sail on the pond. They also liked to pick berries from the bushes and eat them.

One day, they saw a big boat on the pond. It was red and white and had a flag. It looked impressive. Ben and Mia wanted to see it closer.

"Whoa, look at that boat!" Ben said. "It is so big and pretty!"

"Can we sail to it?" Mia asked.

"Sure, let's go!" Ben said. They got on their boat and started to paddle.

As they got closer, they saw a man on the big boat. He was wearing a hat and a coat. He smiled and waved at them.

"Hello, little sailors!" he said. "Do you like my boat?"

"Yes, we do!" Ben and Mia said. "It is very impressive!"

"Thank you!" the man said. "It is my hobby. I like to make boats and sail them. What is your hobby?"

"We like to pick berries and eat them!" Ben and Mia said.

"That sounds fun!" the man said. "Do you have any berries with you?"

"Yes, we do!" Ben and Mia said. They showed him their basket of berries.

"Wow, those look delicious!" the man said. "Can I have some?"

"Sure, you can!" Ben and Mia said. They shared their berries with the man.

The man thanked them and gave them some cookies. They ate and talked and laughed. They had a good time.

Ben and Mia liked the man and his boat. They made a new friend. They were happy.

Anna and Ben are twins. They like to play with their toy cars. But they do not like to share. One day, they have a big fight over a red car.

"I want the red car!" Anna says. "It is mine!"

"No, it is mine!" Ben says. "You have the blue car!"

They pull and tug at the red car. They make a lot of noise. They do not listen to their mom.

"Stop fighting, Anna and Ben!" their mom says. "You have many cars. You can play with different cars."

But Anna and Ben do not want different cars. They only want the red car. They complain and cry.

Their mom has an idea. She takes the red car and puts it in a box. She shakes the box. She makes a funny motion with her hands.

"What is in the box?" she asks. "Do you want to see?"

Anna and Ben are curious. They stop crying. They nod their heads.

Their mom opens the box. She shows them the red car. But the red car is not the same. It has stickers and glitter on it. It looks different.

"Wow!" Anna says. "It is so pretty!"

"Yuck!" Ben says. "It is so ugly!"

Anna smiles. She takes the red car. She says thank you to her mom.

Ben frowns. He does not want the red car anymore. He looks at the blue car. He says sorry to Anna.

They hug and make up. They play with their cars. They share and have fun.

Once upon a time, there was a little duck named Ducky. Ducky loved to play in the pond and eat yummy bugs. One day, Ducky saw a fire burning in the forest. The fire was big and scary. Ducky knew he had to do something to help.

Ducky ran to all his friends and asked them to help put out the fire. They all said no because they were scared. But Ducky was brave and went to get some water to put out the fire. He flew back and forth, carrying water in his beak, until the fire was out.

Everyone was so proud of Ducky for being brave and helping to put out the fire. They all gave him a big hug and told him how rare it was to find someone as brave as him. From that day on, Ducky knew that even though he was small, he could still make a big difference in the world.

One day, a little bear named Tim went for a walk in the woods. He saw a cave that looked different from the other caves he had seen before. Tim was curious and wanted to see what was inside.

As he moved closer to the cave, he saw a big bird sitting near the entrance. The bird said, "Hi, I'm Bobby! This is my cave. It's different because it's my home." Tim smiled and said, "Hi Bobby, I'm Tim. Can I see your cave?"

Bobby nodded and they both moved inside the cave. The cave was warm and cozy. Tim and Bobby became good friends and played together every day. They were happy to have found each other and their different cave.

Once upon a time, there were two friends, Tom and Jerry. They decided to go to the train station to have some fun. They were excited to ride the big, cool train!

When they arrived at the train station, they saw a really cool train with its doors open. They hopped on and found a seat. Soon, the train started to move.

Tom and Jerry were enjoying their ride on the train, looking out of the window and waving to people they could see. Then they heard an announcement, "This stop is the Cool Station. Please mind your step as you get off."

Tom and Jerry got off the train and looked around the station. It was very cool! They saw lots of shops, benches and a big yard. They decided to play there for a while.

They ran around and laughed and had lots of fun. Before they knew it, it was time to leave. They said goodbye to the cool station and hopped back on the train for the journey home. They had a lovely time at the train station and were ready for their next adventure!

Once there was a naughty boy. He was always getting into trouble. One day, the boy was playing outside and he heard a ringing. He followed the sound and it led him to a bell in the garden. The boy thought it looked fun, so he decided to ring it.

He rang it over and over again, until his mom heard it. His mom ran outside and shouted at the boy. She said, “Why are you ringing that bell?” The boy looked down and said “I’m sorry mommy, I didn’t mean to.” His mom told him that he should never do it again.

The naughty boy was sad and he promised he would never ring the bell again. He knew that he had to be careful and always obey his mother’s rules. He went back to playing and never touched the bell again.

Tom and Mia are playing in the park. They see a big balloon in the sky. It is red and shiny. They want to catch it.

"Look, look!" Tom says. "A big balloon!"

"Let's get it!" Mia says. They run after the balloon.

The balloon is tied to a fat man. He is sitting on a bench. He has a blanket on his lap. He is reading a book.

"Hello, mister," Tom says. "Can we have your balloon?"

The fat man looks at them. He smiles.

"Sure, you can have it," he says. "But you have to do something for me first."

"What do we have to do?" Mia asks.

"You have to release my blanket," he says. "It is too hot for me."

Tom and Mia nod. They pull the blanket off the fat man. He sighs.

"Thank you, children," he says. "You are very kind. Here is your balloon."

He gives them the balloon. They are very happy.

"Thank you, mister," they say. "Bye-bye!"

They wave at the fat man. They run away with the balloon. They play with it in the park. They have a lot of fun.

The boy had many questions. He wondered what an airport was. He asked his mum what the strange place was and why they were heading there. His mum smiled and explained that an airport was a special place where people fly around the world in big colourful planes. She said that they were going to the airport to go on a holiday.

The boy was excited! He liked flying on planes, and he liked discovering new places so he couldn't wait to get to the airport.

At the airport, he was amazed. It was big, bright and busy. He turned to his mum and wondered out loud. He asked if they were allowed to fly. His mum laughed and said yes of course! He was going to fly to the beach!

The boy was so happy. He couldn't believe that he was going to fly in the sky. The boy stayed close to his mum and watched in awe. He watched people check in their bags and thought of creative ways to use their luggage.

When the plane took off, the boy felt so excited. He waved goodbye to the airport and looked forward to all of the new adventures that his holiday would bring!

One day, a little boy named Tim went to the park with his mom. They saw a big slide there. Tim was very happy and ran to the slide. He climbed up the steps and sat at the top.

"Ready, set, go!" Tim whispered to himself. He slid down the slide very fast. "Wee!" he shouted as he reached the bottom. Tim's mom clapped her hands and smiled at him.

Tim met a girl named Sue at the park. She had a rich, red ball. "Can I play with your ball?" Tim asked Sue. "Yes, you can!" Sue said with a big smile. They played with the ball and had lots of fun. After playing, they went back to the slide and took turns sliding down. Tim and Sue became good friends and played together at the park every day.

It was a sunny day and Sally was outside on the porch. She was young, only three years old. She looked around, feeling curious. She saw a ladybug on a flower and watched as it flew away. Suddenly, she heard a sound and spun around. There was a dog on the porch! Its tail was wagging and it was looking at Sally. She was a bit scared, but shrugged her shoulders. She remembered what her mom had said, to be friendly. So she smiled and said hello to the dog. The dog's tail wagged even faster and Sally knew it was happy. She started to giggle and then petted the dog's head. The dog licked her hand, and they became friends.

The sun was starting to go down, so Sally said bye to her new friend. She watched as the dog went back down the porch and waved as it disappeared from her sight. She smiled and walked back inside her house, feeling a bit braver for having made a new friend.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved his uncle very much. His uncle was always happy and made Timmy laugh. One day, Timmy's uncle got very sick. Timmy was very sad and worried. He wanted his uncle to feel better.

Timmy's mom took his uncle to the hospital. Timmy waited and waited for his uncle to come back home. Finally, his uncle came home and he was all better. Timmy was so excited! His uncle hugged him and said, "I feel much better now, thanks to the doctors who helped heal me."

Timmy learned that it's important to take care of the people we love when they are sick. He was happy that his uncle was healthy again and they could play and laugh together like before.

Once upon a time, in a small town, there was a famous sunflower. The sunflower was very big and tall. All the people in the town loved the sunflower. They would come to see it every day.

One day, a little boy named Tim went to see the famous sunflower. He saw that the sunflower was sad. Tim asked the sunflower, "Why are you sad?" The sunflower said, "I am sad because I am all alone." Tim wanted to help the sunflower. He had an idea.

Tim went home and got some seeds. He came back to the sunflower and planted the seeds all around it. Soon, many new sunflowers grew. The famous sunflower was not alone anymore. It was very happy. The people in the town were happy too. They learned that it is important to help others when they are sad or alone. And that is the story of the famous sunflower and the little boy named Tim.

Once upon a time, there was a dark little girl. Her name was Daisy and she loved to play. One day, Daisy was playing in the park when she spotted something strange. It was a big box and it looked very heavy! Daisy was curious, so she asked her aunt what it was.

Her aunt laughed and explained that it was a scale. It was used to weigh things. Daisy thought this was fascinating and asked her aunt to show her how it worked.

So Daisy and her aunt went over to the big box. Daisy's aunt put a big rock on the scale and it showed that the rock was very heavy. Daisy was amazed. She could not believe how the scale could tell her how heavy something was.

Next, Daisy's aunt asked her to get on the scale. Daisy was scared at first, but she got on the scale to see how heavy she was. She was delighted when she saw the numbers go up on the scale!

At the end of the day, Daisy was happy that she learned a new way to measure how heavy something was. She thanked her aunt for showing her a new way to learn.

Daisy ran back to the park to show her friends the amazing new thing she had learned. They were equally amazed and excited by the scale. From that day forward, Daisy and her friends would always use the scale to weigh things. Together, they would have lots of fun!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Louise. Louise lived in a big house all by herself, and it made her feel very lonely. So, one day Louise decided to go for a walk. She walked and walked until she found a big and dark exit.

At the exit, Louise stopped and looked all around. Then, suddenly, she felt a twist in her stomach. She heard two strange voices coming from behind her. Startled, Louise turned around and saw two scary looking men facing her!

"We are lost and looking for the exit, can you help us?" they asked her. Louise was so scared she could barely speak. "I-I-I d-d-don't k-k-know," she said.

The men turned to each other and said "Let's look for it somewhere else". Then, they quickly walked away. Louise felt so relieved! She quickly ran out of the exit and back to her house. She was glad to be safe in her home again and never wanted to twist back to the lonely exit ever again.

Anna likes to play with her toy animals. She has a big lion, a small mouse, a long snake and a round turtle. She also has a scale that can tell how heavy things are. She wants to see how heavy her animals are.

She puts the lion on the scale and looks at the number. "Wow, the lion is very heavy!" she says. "He is ten." She takes the lion off and puts the mouse on. The number is very small. "The mouse is very light," she says. "He is only one."

She tries to put the snake on the scale, but it is too long. It does not fit. The snake slides off the scale and falls on the floor. "Oops, the snake is too long for the scale," she says. "He does not fit."

She picks up the turtle and puts it on the scale. The number is five. "The turtle is not too heavy and not too light," she says. "He is five." She looks at the turtle's shell. It is clear. She can see the turtle's head and legs inside. "The turtle has a clear shell," she says. "He is cool."

She hears her mom calling her for lunch. She puts her animals back in the box and takes the scale with her. She wants to show her mom how heavy her animals are. She hopes her mom will like her clear turtle.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lily. She had a pretty thumb, which she liked to suck on. One day, Lily went to the park and saw a boy with an attractive toy. She wanted to play with it, but the boy said no. Lily started to weep and her thumb didn't taste good anymore.

Suddenly, a kind dog appeared and licked Lily's face. She stopped weeping and played with the dog instead. The boy saw how happy Lily was and decided to share his toy with her. Lily was so happy that she forgot about her thumb and played all day long. From that day on, she knew that sharing was better than weeping.

There was a girl named Alicia. She loved to write. Every day she would find a quiet spot and write. One day Alicia was walking in the park when she saw something great. There were many blueberries. Alicia smiled and ran over. She started picking some of the blueberries and put them in her pocket to take home.

When she got home, Alicia put the blueberries in a bowl and got some paper and a pencil. She started to write. She wrote about the great blueberries she had found and how much fun it was picking them. It took her a while to write, but the final results were worth it.

Alicia smiled while she looked at her writing. She was proud of the great story she had written. She finished eating her blueberries and knew that she would cherish her writing forever.

Once there was a bear named Red. He was very brave, even though he was small for his age. Red really wanted to go on some very big adventures. One day, Red set out and walked for miles, looking for these adventures.

Finally, he saw something in the distance. It was a spike sticking out of the ground! Red was so excited to see it - he wanted to know what it could lead him to. So Red moved closer and closer.

He soon realized that the spike was one of many that lined a winding path through the forest. Red smiled, knowing that this spike was leading him to something special. He carefully followed the spikes and soon found himself in a beautiful glade with a rushing river. Red was so excited to explore.

As he looked around, Red saw something amazing - a red dragon! It was huge, and Red could tell it was a very special creature. Red waved at the dragon, and it waved back. It was magical!

Red explored the glade until the sun set, and then he followed the spikes back home. He was so glad that the spike had lead him to such a wonderful place. He was afraid, but he was also very brave to find this adventure using only the red spike!

Anna and Ben are twins. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big rock near the slide. They want to climb on it.

"Look, Ben, a big rock!" Anna says. "Let's go up!"

"OK, Anna, but be careful!" Ben says. They run to the rock and try to climb.

But the rock is too high and slippery. Anna slips and falls. She hurts her knee. She cries.

"Anna, are you OK?" Ben asks. He jumps down and hugs her.

"No, Ben, it hurts!" Anna says. "I want Mommy!"

Ben looks around. He sees a man sitting on a bench. He has a lot of money in his hand. He looks mean.

"Maybe he can help us," Ben thinks. He walks to the man and says, "Excuse me, sir, can you help us? My sister is hurt. We need to go home."

The man looks at Ben. He sees his dirty clothes and shoes. He sees his sad face. He does not care.

"Go away, kid, I don't have time for you," the man says. He puts his money in his pocket and walks away.

Ben feels angry and sad. He feels helpless. He does not know what to do.

He goes back to Anna. He sees her still crying. He tries to make her feel better.

"Don't worry, Anna, we will be OK," he says. "Maybe someone else will help us. Or maybe Mommy will come soon. I love you, Anna."

He rocks her gently in his arms. He hopes for a miracle.

Once upon a time, there was a very small needle. It was harmless and very tiny. One day the needle needed to be replaced. But where could it find something to replace it?

The needle looked up and saw a beautiful big kite in the sky. The kite had special strings that were thin and strong, just like the needle. The needle called out to the kite and asked if it could replace it.

The kite said "Of course. I can help you." The kite flew down from the sky and gently wrapped its strings around the needle. The needle had been replaced. Now the needle could continue on its way, without any worries at all.

Once upon a time, there was a monkey who lived in the jungle. His name was Tony. Every day, Tony would go out and get fruit from the jungle and keep it all to himself. One day, Tony was feeling really hungry and so he decided to get all the fruit he could find in the jungle. He took all the fruit from the other animals, too.

The other animals were getting angry with Tony so they asked him why he was taking all their fruit. Tony said he was too hungry to care. The animals told Tony that taking other people's food was wrong and he should share. Tony nodded and put all the fruit back where it came from.

The animals were happy that Tony had listened but they also felt guilty that they had yelled at Tony. So they thought of a plan. They decided to all get together and work to create more food for Tony. Every day they all worked together to get fruit and then they shared the food with Tony.

From then on Tony was happy, full and never went hungry.

The moral of the story is that we should always share and help each other. If we all work together we can make sure that no one goes without.

One day, Tom was walking in the park. He saw a small store and decided to go inside. He looked around to find something nice. Suddenly, he saw a big toy that he liked. He wanted to store it with him, so he took it.

Tom excitedly went outside of the store and went on his way. On his way, he suddenly slipped and the toy fell to the ground. Tom was very sad. He started to cry and asked himself why this bad day had to happen. He tried to look for the toy but it was gone.

Tom went home with a heavy heart. He tried to tell his mom what had happened but he couldn't stop crying. His mom hugged him tightly and said, "It's okay, Tom. Don't worry. We will buy you a new toy tomorrow."

But Tom was still sad because he knew he wouldn't be able to get that same toy ever again. All he could do was hope for a better day tomorrow.

Once upon a time there was a little girl who was playing in the mud. She was so happy when she rolled around in the mud and made a big mess.

Suddenly her mommy arrived and saw what she was doing. Her mommy was very angry and told the little girl to stop playing around in the mud. The little girl was very embarrassed and she started to cry.

After that, her mommy told her that it was time for her to go to sleep. But the little girl was feeling sleepy and tired. So she brushed all the mud off her clothes and went to bed.

The little girl was so embarrassed and tired that she couldn't stop thinking about her muddy adventure. But she soon fell into a deep sleep and she started dreaming.

Once upon a time, in a small house, there lived a kind lady named Sue. Sue loved to welcome friends to her home. One day, she invited her friends, Tom and Lily, to come for lunch.

When Tom and Lily arrived, they saw that Sue had made a big lunch with many yummy foods. They all sat down to eat, but Lily felt uncomfortable in her chair. Sue saw this and quickly found a soft cushion for Lily to sit on. Now, Lily was happy and comfortable.

They all enjoyed their lunch and had a great time together. The friends learned that it is important to help others feel comfortable and welcome. This made their friendship even stronger. And they all lived happily ever after.

Sara and Tom are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big flower. It is red and yellow and smells good.

"Wow, look at the flower!" Sara says. "It is so pretty!"

"I want to touch it!" Tom says. He runs to the flower. But he does not see the bee. The bee is on the flower. It is angry.

"Buzz, buzz, buzz!" The bee says. It flies to Tom. It stings him on the nose. "Ow, ow, ow!" Tom says. He cries.

Sara runs to Tom. She hugs him. She says, "I'm sorry, Tom. The bee is silly. It does not like to share the flower."

Tom stops crying. He says, "It's okay, Sara. You are a good friend. The flower is still pretty. But I don't want to touch it anymore."

They go to the bench. They sit and eat their snacks. They look at the flower. They smile. They are happy.

Once upon a time, there was a big, strong truck. The truck could drive really fast on the road. One day, the truck went on a bumpy, rough road. It was not an easy drive for the truck.

Suddenly, the truck got stuck in a trap! It was a big hole in the ground. The truck tried to move, but it couldn't. It was trapped!

The driver of the truck was very sad. But then, a kind farmer came to help. He used his tractor to pull the truck out of the trap. The truck was free again! The driver was so happy and thanked the farmer. From then on, the truck always drove carefully, so it wouldn't get trapped again.

Once there was an old man. He wanted to lend something to the humans. One day, he saw a 3 year old girl. He thought she was special and asked her if he could lend her something. The little girl was so excited. She said yes and took whatever the old man gave her: a beautiful new doll.

The old man smiled and said, "Remember, you can always lend this doll to someone else, too!" The little girl promised she would take care of it and lend it out.

So the old man went away feeling happy. The little girl was still excited and spent the rest of the day playing with her new doll. She even let her friends borrow it when they came over.

The little girl was so happy that the old man had lent her the doll. And she was thankful that she was able to lend it out to her friends, too. She learned a valuable lesson that day: always lend and be kind to others.

Once upon a time, there was a lovely little girl called Mary. Mary was very enthusiastic, and loved doing fun things.

One day, Mary wanted to make jam. She got out a pot and some fruit, and began to have a lot of fun.

She watched as the fruit slowly turned into yummy jam. After a bit of stirring, the jam started to disappear.

Mary was so excited! She put the jam into a jar and it tasted so good. She laughed out loud.

The jam was so tasty that it disappeared very quickly. Everyone was so happy to have tasted the jam that had been made with love by Mary.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play outside. One day, Timmy went to the park with his mom. At the park, Timmy saw a big puddle of mud. The mud looked hard, but Timmy wanted to jump in it.

Timmy's mom told him not to jump in the mud because it was too hard and he might get dirty. Timmy listened to his mom and decided to play on the swings instead. While he was swinging, he saw a group of kids playing in the mud.

Timmy wanted to play too, but he remembered what his mom said. Instead, Timmy asked his mom if they could go home and play in the mud there. When they got home, Timmy put on his old clothes and jumped in the mud. It was so much fun! Timmy's mom watched him play and smiled. She was happy that Timmy listened to her and didn't get dirty at the park.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved playing chess with her grandpa. One day, Lily's grandpa bought her an expensive chess set. Lily was so happy and thanked her grandpa.

Later that day, Lily's friend came to play with her. They decided to have a tea party and pour some tea for their dolls. Lily's friend saw the chess set and asked, "What is that?" Lily replied, "It's a chess set. My grandpa gave it to me today. It's very expensive."

Lily's friend asked, "Can we play chess?" Lily said, "Yes, but I don't know how to play very well. Can you teach me?" They played chess and had a lot of fun. Lily's grandpa was very proud of her for learning how to play. From that day on, Lily and her friend played chess every time they had a tea party.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who loved to listen. Everywhere she went, she listened intensely. One day, she wanted to find something new to listen to, so she went for a walk in the park.

When she arrived, it was very quiet. She saw a big tree and thought it was so neat. She sat under the tree, closed her eyes and started to listen. Suddenly, she heard a voice saying, "Cake!"

The little girl opened her eyes and saw an old man with a plate of delicious-looking cake. "Would you like some cake?" he asked.

The little girl was very excited. She said, "Yes, please!" She sat down next to the old man and enjoyed the cake while they talked. The old man told her stories that were not boring at all.

The little girl thanked him and said goodbye. As she started to leave, she waved goodbye and said, "Thank you for listening."

Once upon a time, there were two friends, Sam and Jill. Sam and Jill liked to play together.

One day they were walking on the beach and they saw something strange. It was an igloo made of sand.

"Wow!" said Sam. "What is it?"

"It's an igloo. Let's wave to the people inside it," said Jill.

The two friends waved to the people inside the igloo. The people inside were very independent. They waved back, smiling.

Sam and Jill were so happy that they waved and waved until their hands got tired.

Eventually, Sam and Jill had to leave. Goodbye was said, and then Sam and Jill had to go.

But every time they went to the beach, they remembered their special wave hello to the people in the igloo.

Jill and Jack came to the vegetable patch. Jill saw a brilliant cauliflower. She wanted to pick it. But Jack warned her not to.

"We can't pick it" said Jack. "It will make the farmer very sad."

Jill was sad too but she listened to Jack. Then they saw more cauliflowers in the vegetable patch. They were the same size, and just as brilliant.

Jack told Jill, "Let's pick one of these cauliflowers and take it home."

Jill was so happy. She said "Yes, let's do that. But let's leave the other cauliflowers so the farmer can have them too."

Jack smiled. "That's very kind of you Jill. You are so brilliant!"

Sam and Lily were playing in the park. They liked to run and jump and slide on the grass. But today, the grass was wet and dirty. It had rained a lot last night, and there was mud everywhere.

"Look, Sam, mud!" Lily said, pointing to a big puddle. She ran towards it and splashed in it with her boots. She laughed and made mud bubbles with her feet.

Sam followed her and joined the fun. He liked the sound and the feel of the mud. He kicked it with his foot and watched it fly in the air. He tried to hit a tree with his mud ball.

But then, he heard a voice behind him. It was Tom, the big boy from the next street. He was always mean and bossy. He did not like to share or play nice.

"Hey, you two, get out of my mud!" Tom shouted. He ran towards Sam and Lily and pushed them away. He glared at them with his angry eyes.

"But we were here first!" Sam said, standing up. He did not like Tom. He was not afraid of him.

"I don't care. This is my park, and this is my mud. You can't play here. Go away, or I'll kick you!" Tom said, raising his foot.

Lily was scared. She did not want to fight. She grabbed Sam's hand and pulled him away. She wanted to go home.

"Come on, Sam, let's go. He's not nice. He's impatient. He can have his mud. We can play somewhere else." Lily said, trying to sound brave.

Sam nodded. He did not want to play with Tom either. He was rude and selfish. He did not know how to have fun.

"Okay, Lily, let's go. We don't need his mud. We have each other. We can play with our toys or read a book or draw a picture. We can do anything we want." Sam said, smiling at Lily.

They walked away, holding hands. They left Tom alone in his mud. He looked around and saw no one to play with. He felt lonely and bored. He kicked his mud again, but it did not make him happy. He wished he had friends like Sam and Lily.

Once upon a time there was a small boy called James. He was very excited because he was going to get a new bicycle. It was big and red and shiny. James couldn't wait to ride it!

On the morning that James got his bicycle, a larger boy took it away. James was sad and he began to cry.

Then a pale lady saw the boy. She had a pen and paper and she said 'write your name on the paper and no one can take it away from you'.

So James wrote his name on the paper and he was happy. He knew that no one could take his bicycle away.

The moral of the story is, when you’re faced with a problem, writing your name is a way to stay in control no matter what happens.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved to play outside. One day, she was riding her bike when she fell and hurt her knee. She cried and cried until her mommy came running outside.

Mommy saw that Lily's knee was bleeding and promised to make it all better. She picked Lily up and carried her inside the house. Then, mommy called the ambulance to come and help.

The ambulance was big and red and it came quickly to Lily's house. The ambulance driver was very nice and helped mommy and Lily get into the ambulance. They went to the hospital where the doctor fixed Lily's knee. After that, mommy and Lily went home and had some ice cream to make them feel better. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a big round number named Zero. Zero was very sad because he felt like he had no friends. All the other numbers were always busy, and there was no one available to play with him.

One day, Zero saw a little girl named Lily playing by herself in the park. She was trying to turn a big wheel on the playground, but it was too heavy for her. Zero wanted to help her, so he rolled over and pushed the wheel with all his might. Together, they made the wheel turn, and Lily was so happy.

From that day on, Lily and Zero became best friends. They played together every day, and Zero was no longer sad. He was glad that he could help Lily and that he finally had a friend who was always available to play with him. And they all lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was an adorable little farm full of animals. Every day, the farmer and his children would feed the animals. One day, they noticed a flag twirling in the wind near the farm.

The children didn't know what it meant, but the farmer knew. He said the flag was special and that he had been expecting it for a long time. They all wondered what the flag meant.

Finally, the farmer explained that it meant a new animal was coming to the farm! The children were so excited and decided to name the animal before it even arrived.

When the new animal did arrive, the children were so happy to see that it was a fluffy little lamb, just like they had imagined! They fed it and played with it, and it was so adorable that they all agreed that it deserved its special name - Flag.

Lily and Ben were friends who liked to gaze at the stars. They had a big book with pictures of stars and planets. They wanted to visit the space museum, where they could see real rockets and learn more about space.

One day, their teacher said they could go to the museum with the class. Lily and Ben were very happy. They packed their lunch and their book and got on the bus. The museum was very popular. There were many other children and adults there.

Lily and Ben followed their teacher and saw many things. They saw a big rocket that could fly to the moon. They saw a suit that astronauts wore. They saw a model of the earth and the sun. They learned many new words and facts.

But then, they saw a big telescope. It was shiny and had a long tube. Lily and Ben wanted to look through it and see the stars. They ran to the telescope and pushed each other.

"Let me see first!" Lily said.

"No, me!" Ben said.

They both grabbed the telescope and pulled. They did not see that a sign said "Do not touch". They did not hear their teacher calling them. They did not notice that the telescope was wobbly.

Suddenly, the telescope fell over and broke. It made a loud noise. Everyone looked at Lily and Ben. They were scared and sorry. Their teacher came and was angry.

"What did you do?" she asked. "You broke the telescope! You did not listen to me or the sign! You were rude and selfish!"

Lily and Ben felt ashamed. They said they were sorry. They said they only wanted to see the stars. They said they were friends.

The teacher sighed. She said they had to pay for the telescope. She said they had to apologize to the museum staff. She said they had to learn to share and be careful.

Lily and Ben nodded. They realized they had made a mistake. They said they would do better. They hugged each other and said they were still friends.

They learned that gazing at the stars was fun, but not more important than being kind and respectful. They learned that visiting the museum was a privilege, not a right. They learned that being popular was not worth losing a friend.

Lily was a little girl who liked to help her mom. She liked to serve tea and cookies to her mom and her dolls. She had a tea set with cups and plates and a pot. She also had a tray to carry them.

One day, she was playing with her tea set in her room. She wanted to make a new dress for her doll, so she looked for some cloth and a needle. She found an old cloth in a drawer and a needle in a box. She was very careful with the needle, because she knew it was sharp and could hurt.

She cut a piece of cloth and wrapped it around her doll. Then she tried to sew it with the needle. But the needle was too big and the cloth was too thick. She could not make a stitch. She tried harder and harder, but the needle only made holes in the cloth.

She was frustrated and sad. She wanted to make a pretty dress for her doll, but she could not. She started to cry. Her mom heard her cry and came to her room. She saw Lily with the cloth and the needle.

"What's wrong, Lily?" her mom asked.

"I want to make a dress for my doll, but I can't. The needle is too big and the cloth is too old. It's not working," Lily sobbed.

Her mom hugged her and said, "Don't cry, Lily. I can help you. We can find a smaller needle and a softer cloth. Then we can make a dress together. How does that sound?"

Lily smiled and said, "That sounds good, mom. Thank you. Can we still have tea and cookies after?"

"Of course, we can. You are such a good helper, Lily. You always serve me tea and cookies. I love you," her mom said.

"I love you too, mom," Lily said. They put away the old cloth and the big needle. Then they went to find a new cloth and a small needle. They made a beautiful dress for Lily's doll. Then they had tea and cookies and played with the dolls. Lily was happy.

Once upon a time there was a man who worked very hard on his farm. One day he decided to make something special to make his family happy. He decided to make a fruit feast for them!

The man went out and picked all sorts of tasty fruit from his farm. He picked delicious apples and sweet watermelons. He also grabbed some bright oranges and a big bunch of bananas.

The man made a nice big platter of fruit and brought it to the family. But when his family tried to take a bite of the fruit, it wasn't sweet at all. It was too harsh. They were so surprised and confused.

The man had forgotten to add sugar to the fruit. He knew he had made a mistake and apologised to his family. He promised that next time he would make sure to add a generous amount of sugar to sweeten the fruit.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Kate. Kate was only three years old, but she loved to jog. Every weekend, she and her mom would go to a big, enormous park.

When Kate and her mom got to the park, Kate was so excited! She started to jog around the park, running past the trees and birds. She felt so happy and free!

Next, Kate and her mom went to a special place. It was a place just for little kids like Kate, with enormous slides and swings. Kate jogged around and around the playground, having the best time.

Finally, it was time to go home. Kate was tired from jogging, but she was so happy that she said goodbye to the enormous park with a smile.

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a clever and smart dog called Max. Max was very intelligent and always knew what to do. One day, Max heard some music playing in the park. He went to see where the music was coming from and saw a man playing guitar. Max loved the music and wagged his tail happily.

Suddenly, Max saw a little girl who was crying. She had lost her balloon and was feeling sad. Max knew what to do. He lifted the little girl up and carried her to the man playing music. The man saw the little girl and started playing a happy song. The little girl stopped crying and started dancing. Max was happy to see the little girl happy.

Once upon a time, there lived a family. One day, they decided to celebrate. They began to make plans for a fun and adventurous day.

The father said, "Let's start in the morning. We'll go to the mailbox and see what surprises await us."

The mother replied, "That sounds like a great idea! I'm sure there are some surprises that we can enjoy."

The children asked, "Can we join too?"

The father smiled and said, "Of course you can join us. It'll be a fun and adventurous surprise."

The children jumped up and down with excitement. The next morning, the family got ready to explore the mailbox. They opened it and found some amazing surprises! It was even better than they expected. They celebrated the whole day together and had an amazing time.

Once there was a little bird named Baby. She lived in a tree with her family in a big forest. She was glad to live in the tree, but she wanted to explore the forest. One day, Baby flew over the forest and saw a tall branch. She was so excited and asked her mom, "Can I go climb the branch?" Her mom said, "Yes, but be careful."

Baby was feeling brave and flew up as high as she could. It was a bit scary, but she was glad to get to the top. As she hopped from branch to branch, she could see everything in the forest. Then, something extraordinary happened. Baby heard a gentle voice tell her, "Believe in yourself, little bird!" She was surprised, but remembered her mom always telling her that.

Baby was so inspired and felt glad. She thought, "Maybe if I believe in myself, I can do anything!" She spread her wings and flew back to her tree, ready to keep exploring the world.

Olive was a great monkey. She was very brave and always really happy. One day, Olive wanted to see what the world was like outside of her home. She asked her mom if she could go and explore. Mom knew it would be dangerous, so she asked Olive to trust her. She said it was important to stay safe and to come back home soon.

Olive knew she could trust her mom, so she jumped out into the world. She found lots of wonderful things! She saw big hills and small rivers. On the way back, Olive remembered to stay close to home so she wouldn't get lost.

When she arrived, she and her mom were so happy. They celebrated with a big hug and lots of cuddles. Olive learned that when she trusted her mom, lots of great things could happen.

One day, little Sally took a walk by the lake. She wanted to explore and find exciting new things. When she heard a loud noise, she stopped and looked around. She noticed a large, gray truck coming from around the bend. She eagerly stepped closer to get a better look.

Sally waved to the driver of the truck and was surprised when the truck replied with a single honk of its horn. Sally giggled at the sound; it was so loud and exciting. She waved her arms and smiled, excited to talk to the truck.

The truck drove away, but Sally was eager to see if it would reply again. She kept walking and a few minutes later, the truck drove by. Sally waved her arms and the truck honked its horn in response. She couldn't believe it; the truck was talking back to her. She waved again as the truck drove around the bend.

Sally was amazed and decided she would come back to the same spot tomorrow. Perhaps the truck would honk at her again.

Once upon a time, there was a big red truck. The truck liked to go far away to distant places. One day, the truck met a small blue car.

"Hi, car! Do you want to settle and play with me?" asked the truck.

The car said, "Yes, I want to play with you!"

They played all day long. They played in the mud and raced each other. They had so much fun. But then, the sky got dark, and it started to rain.

The truck and the car got very wet. They tried to find a place to hide from the rain, but they could not. The rain made the truck and the car very sad. They wished they had stayed home.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. He loved to play in his room with his toys. One day, he noticed that his room was very messy. He decided to tidy it up all by himself.

As he was cleaning, he saw something appear in the corner of his room. It was a monster! Timmy was scared, but he remembered his parents telling him that monsters weren't real. He tried to ignore it and continued cleaning.

But the monster kept appearing and scaring Timmy. He tried to tell his parents, but they didn't believe him. One night, the monster came out from under his bed and took Timmy away.

The moral of the story is that sometimes, it's okay to ask for help when we're scared. It's important to tell someone if we think there's a monster in our room, and not to be afraid to ask for help tidying up.

Molly was very cold. She was wearing her favourite blouse, but it was not enough. She shivered and rubbed her hands together.

Her mum said to her, "Come and sort your things, Molly. It will help you warm up!"

Molly smiled and went to sort her room. She began to arrange her toys in size order. Big toys on one side, small ones on the other. Then she sorted her clothes. She put her blouse beside her dress.

By the time Molly had finished sorting, she was warm and ready for some hot chocolate!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved presents more than anything in the world. One day, her mom told her that they were going to visit her grandma. Lily was so happy because she knew that her grandma always gave her the best presents.

On the way to her grandma's house, Lily saw a poor boy sitting on the sidewalk. He looked sad and hungry. Lily's mom gave him some food and money. Lily asked her mom why they did that. Her mom said that it's important to help others because it makes us happy.

When they arrived at her grandma's house, Lily was excited to see her present. But when her grandma gave her a small box, Lily was disappointed. It wasn't the big toy she was hoping for. However, when she opened the box, she saw a beautiful necklace inside. Her grandma told her that the necklace was very special and valuable. Lily realized that even though the present wasn't what she expected, it still made her happy.

Once upon a time, there was a kid named Zac. Zac was very smart and he loved to do cool things.

One day, Zac was walking through the park when he saw a giant squash. It was huge! He decided it would be fun to zip around on the squash. Zac hopped on top and he started zipping around.

Zac really liked zipping on the squash, and he got very good at it. He could zip around corners and even jump off the squash to do flips in the air. Zac was so proud of how smart and zippy he was!

The fun didn't last long though. All the zipping around on the squash made it really squishy and it slowly started to fall apart. Zac was very sad to see it go, but he was happy with all the fun he had.

Zac learned that zipping on the squash was fun, but it was also important to be careful. He was glad that he was so smart and chose to play in a safe way.

Anna was a happy three-year-old. She liked to play outside and ride her scooter. She loved the bright colors on her scooter, such as red and blue.

Today, Anna was alert. She knew it was time to take her scooter and go around the block. She wanted to show her scooter to everyone! As she went along, she was looking carefully and making sure everything belonged.

When Anna arrived back at her house, she was so proud of herself. “I know my scooter belongs here,” she said. She put her scooter away, and she felt very safe and secure.

Anna was glad that she could be alert and own a scooter. She always knew where everything belonged!

Lily wanted to mail a picture to her grandma. She drew a big heart and wrote "I love you" with her crayons. She asked her mom for an envelope and a stamp. Her mom helped her put the picture inside and write the address.

"Can we go to the mailbox now?" Lily asked.

"Yes, let's go," her mom said. They put on their coats and shoes and walked to the mailbox. Lily was very happy.

But on the way, Lily saw a juice stand. She loved juice. She wanted to buy some. She asked her mom for some money.

"Sorry, honey, I don't have any money with me. We can have some juice when we get home," her mom said.

Lily was very sad. She wanted juice now. She saw a coin on the ground. She picked it up. She thought maybe she could use it to buy juice. She ran to the juice stand and gave the coin to the man.

"Thank you," the man said. He gave her a cup of juice.

Lily drank the juice. It was very good. She felt better.

But then she remembered her picture. She looked at her hand. She had dropped the envelope. She didn't have it anymore. She felt very bad. She had lost her picture for grandma.

She ran back to her mom. She was crying.

"Mom, I'm sorry, I'm sorry, I lost the picture, I lost the envelope, I found a coin and I bought juice and I dropped it and I'm sorry, I'm sorry," she sobbed.

Her mom hugged her. She was not angry. She was sad too.

"It's okay, Lily, it's okay. I know you didn't mean to. You made a mistake. You were tempted by the juice. But you shouldn't have taken the coin. That was not yours. You should have asked the man if he lost it. You should have been honest. Do you understand?" her mom said.

Lily nodded. She understood. She felt ashamed. She had done something wrong.

"I'm sorry, mom. I'm sorry, grandma. I love you. Can I make another picture?" she asked.

"Of course, you can, Lily. And we can mail it tomorrow. And we can also return the coin to the man. And we can say sorry to him too. And we can learn from this. And we can still have some juice at home. Okay?" her mom said.

"Okay, mom. Thank you, mom. You are the best mom," Lily said.

They hugged again. They walked home. They made another picture. They returned the coin. They said sorry. They had some juice. They mailed the picture. They felt better. They loved each other. The end.

Once there was a little girl named Daisy. She was only 3 years old and loved to play outside. One day she was out playing in her garden when she saw a bee. She was so excited! She wanted more than anything to catch the bee.

“Come here, bee!” Daisy said. She wanted to catch the bee, but it did not listen. So she tried again and again and again.

“Maybe if I kick this ball,” Daisy thought to herself. She kicked the ball. The bee was startled and flew away. Daisy was disappointed but then noticed something on the ground.

It was a pot of honey. Daisy was so happy! She couldn’t believe her luck. She quickly opened the pot and took a taste. It was delicious!

As Daisy enjoyed the honey, she noticed the pot was dirty. She got an idea and started to dig around the pot. After a few minutes, she saw something glimmering in the dirt.

It was a beautiful diamond necklace! Daisy was so excited. She knew the pot of honey was meant to lead her to the necklace.

Daisy smiled as she put the necklace around her neck. All thanks to the little bee and her kick!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Jenna. Jenna loved to explore her small town and whenever she had the chance, she enjoyed going to the market.

One day, Jenna's mom told her she could go to the market on her own to get some apples. Jenna was so excited! She put on her pink shoes and headed down the street.

Once she reached the market, Jenna saw lots of vendors. She had never seen so many people in one place before. She went up to one of the vendors and politely said, "Hello, could I please have some apples?"

The vendor replied in a rude voice, "No! You can't." This upset Jenna and she began to walk away when she heard someone calling her.

It was the same vendor. He said, "Come back and I'll give you the apples. I apologize if I was rude before." Jenna was still a bit shy, but she did gather up the courage to go back and get the apples.

The vendor smiled and said, "Enjoy those apples!" Jenna thanked him and happily skipped back home with the apples.

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim loved to study about boats. His favorite boat was a kayak. He liked to read about them and look at pictures of them.

One day, Tim was sad and miserable. He wanted to see a real kayak, but he didn't know where to find one. His mom saw that he was sad and had an idea. She took Tim to a big lake where people could ride in boats.

When they got to the lake, Tim saw a kayak. His face lit up with a big smile. He got to sit in the kayak and ride on the water. Tim was not miserable anymore. He had a great day at the lake with his mom.

Mira was a wealthy girl who had many toys and clothes. She liked to go to the zoo with her parents and see the animals. Her favorite animal was the otter, who was playful and cute. She wanted to have an otter as a pet, but her parents said no. They said otters belong in the water, not in a house.

One day, Mira decided to sneak out of her house and go to the zoo by herself. She took some money from her piggy bank and bought a ticket. She ran to the otter exhibit and climbed over the fence. She saw a baby otter sleeping on a rock and reached out to grab it. She thought it would be fun to take it home and play with it.

But the baby otter was not happy to be woken up by a stranger. It bit Mira's hand and made a loud noise. The other otters heard the noise and came to help. They splashed water at Mira and chased her away. Mira was scared and hurt. She dropped the baby otter and ran back to the fence. She cried and wished she had listened to her parents.

The zookeeper saw what happened and called Mira's parents. They came to the zoo and were very angry. They punished Mira by taking away her toys and clothes for a month. They also made her apologize to the zookeeper and the otters. Mira learned her lesson and never tried to take an animal from the zoo again. She realized that otters are better off in the water, not in a house.

Once upon a time there was a gloomy arrow. It was so sad and did not have anyone to play with. One day, a little boy saw the arrow and thought it was so pretty. He wanted to be friends with it. He asked the arrow if it wanted to play.

The arrow said yes! So the little boy and the arrow played together in a field. They ran and laughed. The little boy even tickled the arrow.

But then, a big, mean bird swooped down from the sky. It was angry and wanted the arrow for itself. The little boy shouted at the bird to go away. But the bird didn't listen. It kept trying to grab the arrow.

The little boy got so mad! He ran up to the bird and slapped it. It flew away, yelping in surprise. The arrow was so happy and thanked the little boy.

The little boy smiled. The only thing that can make a gloomy arrow happy again is a brave friend!

Cherie had a special bond with her daddy. Whenever Cherie was feeling lonely, she would urge her daddy to play with her. The two of them would have the best time with laughter, games and cuddles - until one day, daddy was no longer available.

"Where is daddy?", Cherie asked her mommy.

"He has gone away for a little while", mummy replied.

Cherie felt an urge to be with her daddy, but felt resigned that it was not possible. She knew that her daddy was special and always made her feel loved but she just wished he would come back to her. Days passed, until one day, mummy told Cherie the exciting news - Daddy was back home! Cherie was so happy that he was once again available to her. She rushed to daddy and hugged him tight.

"Welcome home, Daddy!", Cherie said happily.

Once upon a time there was a hanger that belonged to a nosy little three year old. She loved to use her hanger to hang her clothes up in the closet. But one day, when she went to hang up her dress, she noticed something strange about the hanger. It seemed like something else was using her hanger too!

Over the next few days, she noticed more and more strange things. Every time she looked in her closet, her hanger was moved. She decided that she needed to investigate more to figure out what was going on.

So she waited. Then one day, when she went to hang up her favorite shirt, she noticed something clinging to the hanger. It was a tiny monkey! Apparently, the monkey had taken a liking to the little girl's hanger and thought it belonged to them.

The little girl laughed and smiled, and then she decided to let the monkey keep her hanger. From then on, they were inseparable and the hanger belonged to both of them!

Once upon a time there was a strong man. He loved demanding things from others. One day, he saw a little bird perched in a tree. He demanded that the bird obey his command. The little bird didn't know what to do, so she just chirped sadly. The strong man demanded again, and the little bird still didn't understand. He asked one more time, and this time the bird flew away. The strong man was angry! He decided to demand something from the wind. He asked the wind to carry him away from the bird. The result was unbelievable! The wind took him far away, and the bird was safe. The man smiled, happy with the result of his demand.

Once upon a time, there was a beautiful girl named Grace, who loved fashion. Every day she would go to the store and try on lots of pretty clothes. She wanted to be the most graceful girl in town.

At the store, Grace would twirl around in the different outfits and check herself out in the mirror. She would look elegant in a pink dress, and fun in colorful shorts.

One day, Grace found a special outfit that was perfect for her. She was filled with joy when she put it on and saw how graceful she looked. From then on, she chose her clothes carefully, striving for perfection and gracefulness.

Whenever she was at the store, Grace was filled with happiness. She enjoyed the chance to mix and match new fashion items. She was proud of herself, feeling graceful and confident in the clothes she chose.

The end!

Once upon a time, a brave little girl named Lizzie went on a walk in the woods. She was mesmerized by the sunshine and happy birds, and the beauty of nature around her.

As she walked deeper into the trees, she stopped in front of a large hole in the ground and gazed. Suddenly, there was a loud roar from the depths of the dark tunnel. Lizzie was scared and peered down, and noticed a huge lion! She was absolutely terrified, but her curiosity got the best of her so she decided to stay and watch it.

The lion paced around the edge of the dark and deep cave, making frightening noises. The animal seemed to be very angry, and it's fur was unruly and matted. Its yellow eyes were tinged with a dark and disgusting fire.

Lizzie thought she should leave the cave before the lion noticed her, so she started to edge backwards, keeping her eye on the lion at all times. Without thinking, she stepped on a branch, which made a loud crack!

The lion looked up and snarled. It started to run towards Lizzie and soon she was surrounded by the intimidating creature. There was no where to go! She tried to run but it was too late.

The lion pounced and she screamed. All that echoed through the forest was her dreadful scream and then...silence.

Once upon a time there was a little girl. She was walking down a sunny path. All of a sudden, she saw a long shadow. It was very dark and long. She stopped walking to look at the shadow. She waited and watched it carefully. She was very patient. She waited so long until some of the dark parts of the shadow changed to a light color. She smiled at the light shadow. She knew she had seen something special. Then she started walking again, now with a happy feeling in her heart.

Alma was tired and wanted a hug. She looked around for her mom and dad but couldn't find them. She thought of something else though. She went to the tv and turned it on.

When it came on, she saw a cartoon! It was colorful and she smiled. The cartoon was about a family of animals. They were all giving each other hugs. Alma wanted a hug too.

She looked in the room, but still couldn't find her mom and dad. She sat down and watched the cartoon. After a while, she felt better.

When the cartoon finished, her mom and dad walked in. Alma was so happy, she jumped up and ran to them. They hugged her tight and she felt better. She was glad that she had a hug, even if it was just from a cartoon.

One day, a little girl named Lucy asked her mom, "What day is today?" Her mom replied, "Today is Sunday, my dear." Lucy was happy because Sunday is her favorite day. She loves to play with her friends on Sunday.

Lucy went to the park to play with her friends. She saw her friend Tom playing with a ball. She asked Tom, "Can I play with you?" Tom replied, "Yes, you can play with me, Lucy." They played together and had lots of fun.

While playing, Lucy fell down and her face turned red. She was embarrassed. But her friend Tom helped her up and said, "It's okay, Lucy. We all fall down sometimes." Lucy smiled and they continued to play together on the sunny Sunday.

Lily and Tom were twins who liked to play in the park. They had a favorite tree, a big old oak, that they climbed and swung from. One day, they saw a new boy in the park. He had a red bike and a mean face. He rode his bike to the oak and got off.

"Hey, this is my tree now," he said. "You can't play here. Go away."

Lily and Tom were angry and scared. They loved their tree and did not want to leave. They said, "No, this is our tree. We were here first. You go away."

The new boy did not listen. He pushed Lily and Tom and tried to climb the tree. Lily and Tom pushed him back and tried to stop him. They shouted and cried and fought.

But the new boy was bigger and stronger. He kicked Lily and Tom and made them fall. He climbed the tree and laughed. He said, "Ha ha, I win. This is my tree now. You are losers."

Lily and Tom were hurt and sad. They ran to their mom and told her what happened. Their mom hugged them and said, "I'm sorry, my loves. That boy was very rude and mean. He should not have done that. He should have shared the tree with you."

But Lily and Tom did not feel better. They looked at the oak and saw the new boy sitting on a branch. He looked smug and happy. He had their tree and they had nothing. They wished they could have their tree back. They wished the new boy would go away. They wished they could make him pay. But they could not. They had lost. The end.

Once upon a time, in a small town, there lived a nosy cat named Tom. Tom loved to watch what everyone was doing. One day, Tom saw two little birds having a fight over a toy.

"Stop!" Tom said to the birds. "Why are you fighting?"

The first bird said, "I found the toy first, but he insists on taking it away from me!"

The second bird said, "No, I found it first! You are trying to take it away from me!"

Tom thought for a moment and said, "I have an idea. Let's share the toy. You can play with it in the morning, and you can play with it in the afternoon."

The two little birds agreed to share the toy, and they stopped fighting. Tom was happy that he could help his friends. From that day on, the birds and Tom played together and shared all their toys. And Tom learned that being nosy can sometimes be helpful.

Anna and Ben were very happy. They were going to visit their grandma and grandpa. They packed their bags and got in the car with mom and dad.

"Are we there yet?" Ben asked.

"Not yet, sweetie. It's a long drive," mom answered.

Anna and Ben played with their toys and sang songs. They looked out the window and saw trees and cows and birds.

"Look, there's a big red barn!" Anna said.

"I see it! I wonder what animals live there," Ben said.

They kept driving until they saw a sign that said "Welcome to Grandma and Grandpa's Farm".

"Yay, we're here!" Anna and Ben shouted.

They got out of the car and ran to hug their grandma and grandpa. They were very happy to see them.

"Hello, my darlings! We're so glad you came to visit us," grandma said.

"We have a surprise for you," grandpa said.

"What is it?" Anna and Ben asked.

"Follow me," grandpa said.

He led them to the back of the house, where there was a big fence. He opened the gate and said, "Meet our new friends."

Anna and Ben gasped. Inside the fence, there were two goats, a pig, a duck, and a chicken.

"Wow, they're so cute!" Anna said.

"Can we pet them?" Ben asked.

"Of course, but be careful. They can be a bit naughty sometimes," grandpa said.

He gave them some corn and bread to feed the animals. Anna and Ben had fun feeding and petting them. They laughed when the goat nibbled on Ben's shirt and when the duck quacked loudly.

But then, they saw something that made them stop. There was a big hole in the fence, and the pig was trying to squeeze through it.

"Grandpa, look! The pig is escaping!" Anna said.
