"Oh no, you're right! We have to stop him!" grandpa said.

He ran to the hole and tried to pull the pig back. But the pig was too strong and stubborn. He pushed and pushed until he got out of the fence.

"Come back here, you foolish pig!" grandpa shouted.

He chased after the pig, who ran towards the road. Anna and Ben followed him, worried and scared.

"Mom, dad, help!" they cried.

Mom and dad heard them and came out of the house. They saw what was happening and ran to help.

"Be careful, there's a car coming!" mom said.

She waved her arms and shouted at the driver to stop. The driver saw them and slowed down. The pig stopped too, confused and scared.

Grandpa caught up with the pig and grabbed him by the ears. He lifted him up and carried him back to the fence.

"Sorry, mister. Thank you for stopping," grandpa said to the driver.

"It's okay, no harm done. But you should fix that fence, or you'll lose your pig again," the driver said.

He drove away, shaking his head.

Grandpa put the pig back in the fence and closed the gate. He checked the hole and said, "I'll have to get some nails and boards to fix this. That pig is too clever for his own good."

He looked at the pig, who was snorting and grunting. He said, "You're lucky you didn't get hurt, you foolish pig. You could have caused an accident. Don't you ever do that again, do you hear me?"

The pig looked at him and nodded. He seemed to understand.

Anna and Ben hugged grandpa and said, "We're sorry, grandpa. We didn't mean to let the pig out."

"It's not your fault, my darlings. You didn't know. It's the pig's fault. He's always looking for trouble," grandpa said.

He hugged them back and said, "But I'm glad you're safe and sound. You're very brave and smart. I love you very much."

"We love you too, grandpa," Anna and Ben said.

They went back to the house, where grandma was waiting for them. She had made some cookies and milk for them.

"Come on, let's have a snack. You must be hungry after your adventure," grandma said.

They sat at the table and ate the cookies and drank the milk. They told grandma what happened and how they helped grandpa catch the pig.

"Wow, that was quite a story. You're very lucky nothing bad happened. That pig is very foolish indeed," grandma said.

She smiled and said, "But I'm very proud of you. You're very good and kind. You're the best visitors ever."

Anna and Ben smiled and said, "Thank you, grandma. You're the best grandma ever."

They hugged

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who had a sweet brother named Max. They loved to play together in the park and eat candy.

One day, they went to the park and saw a puzzle on the ground. Lily said, "Let's solve this puzzle, Max!" Max said, "Okay, Lily. I love puzzles."

They worked on the puzzle for a long time, but they couldn't solve it. Suddenly, a big dog came and ate the puzzle. Lily and Max were sad because they couldn't finish the puzzle.

Lily said, "I wish we could solve the puzzle, Max." Max said, "Me too, Lily. But we can't now because the dog ate it." They went home feeling sad that they couldn't finish the puzzle.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to paint and would often paint on everything she could find. One day, Lily's mom asked her to clean up her mess. Lily didn't want to stop painting, so she ignored her mom's request.

The next day, Lily woke up and couldn't find her favorite towel. She asked her mom where it was, and her mom said it was in the laundry because it was smelly from all the paint. Lily felt bad for not cleaning up her mess and promised her mom she would clean up from now on.

The moral of the story is that it's important to listen to your parents and clean up after yourself.

Once upon a time, there was a big car named Dependable. He had a very important job. Dependable would take a family to the park every day. The family had a mom, dad, and a little girl named Lily. They all had a lot of love for each other.

One day, when they got to the park, they saw a big sign that said, "Fun Race Today!" The family was very excited. They knew that Dependable was very fast and could win the race. So, they decided to join the race.

The race started, and Dependable went very fast. The other cars tried to catch up, but Dependable was too quick. In the end, Dependable won the race! The family was so happy and proud of their car. They knew that their love for each other and their trust in Dependable made them win the race. And from that day on, they had even more fun at the park, knowing that they had the fastest and most dependable car around.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy lived in a small house with his mommy and daddy. One day, a big tornado came and took Timmy's house away. Timmy was scared and didn't know what to do.

But then, a brave firefighter came to rescue Timmy and his family. The firefighter was strong and quickly pulled them out of the rubble. Timmy was happy to be safe and hugged the firefighter tightly.

After the tornado, Timmy learned that it's important to always listen to the grown-ups and have a plan in case of an emergency. He also learned that even though things may seem dull and boring sometimes, they can be very important to keep us safe.

Once upon a time, there was a jolly little girl named Sophie. Sophie loved to keep her things very neat. Each morning, she would tidy her room and keep her toys all in a row.

One morning, Sophie found a surprise. She had forgotten all about the big box of pasta that she had asked for last week. She opened it up, and the pasta came out in all sorts of shapes and sizes. She was so happy!

Sophie quickly set out to make her lunch. She boiled a pot of water, dropped in the pasta and stirred it around. When it was nice and cooked, she served it in a bowl with some cheese and butter.

After lunch, Sophie felt very full and content. She curled up in her bed and smiled. She had been jolly all day, and the food she had made was the best! Sophie had certainly kept very busy, but it had all been worth it.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Sue. Sue was only three years old, but she was very smart.

One day, Sue's mom said to her, "Sue, why don't you tell me a story? I love listening to your stories!" Sue smiled.

So she began to tell her mom a story. She said, "Once there was a smooth road. Everyone who drove on that road had a good time. They worked together to make it better."

Sue's mom smiled and said, "That's a wonderful story, Sue. I love listening to your stories!"

Sue was very proud of herself. "I worked hard on that story!" she said. She knew that her story was smooth and she was glad to share it with her mom.

Molly walked into the bathroom and looked at herself in the mirror. She wanted to dress up in something nice. She went to her dresser and opened the drawer. Inside was a lovely dress covered in lace. Molly was so excited to put it on! She took off her ordinary clothing and put the dress on. She felt so pretty.

Suddenly, her brother Jonathan ran into the room. He said in a selfish voice, "Give me the dress!" Molly refused. She said, "No, this is my dress!" Jonathan was mad and started to cry. Molly felt bad but she knew she had to be firm.

Molly's mom came running into the bathroom. She asked Jonathan what was wrong. He pointed angrily at Molly and said, "She won't let me wear her dress!" Molly shook her head and said, "This is my dress and I want to keep it." Mom said, "It's ok Jonathan, you can dress up too in something else."

Molly was relieved. She smiled at her brother and they both hugged each other. She said, "Let's go show Mom our outfits!" Jonathan happily agreed and they both went off together to show Mom the dresses they both had chosen.

Once upon a time, there was a small boy who was walking in the woods. Suddenly, he came to a cliff. The cliff was very tall and fierce. It scared the little boy and made him panic. All he wanted to do was get away. He started to run as fast as he could. His tiny legs carried him spritely through the woods and away from the cliff.

When he was far away, he stopped to catch his breath. He was so happy that he had made it away from the cliff. He decided he would never come to the woods again. He never wanted to see the fierce cliff again.

The boy went home and told his parents all about his adventure. They were so happy he was safe, and they told him that it was wise to stay away from the cliff.

They all lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time there were two humans. One was very alert, and the other was sleepy. The alert human said, "Let's go for a walk." But the sleepy human just stayed in the same spot.

The alert human said, "Come on! Let's walk into the forest." But the sleepy one just shrugged and said, "No."

"Oh, come on!" said the alert human. "It'll be fun!"

Finally, the sleepy human agreed and they started walking into the forest. But when they got there, they got separated. The alert human kept walking and calling out the sleepy one's name, but he couldn't find him. He was all alone.

Finally, he heard someone call out his name. He looked up and there was the sleepy human! He had found him!

The alert human breathed a sigh of relief and said, "Let's go home together!"

And so that's what they did. They always stayed together from then on!

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play outside and explore. One day, he went on an adventurous walk in the woods. He saw lots of trees and animals. Suddenly, it started to rain. Timmy got very wet and cold.

When he got home, his mommy told him to take a warm bath. Timmy loved to bathe in the tub. He splashed and played with his toys. While he was in the tub, he thought about the universe. He learned about it in school. He wondered what it would be like to travel in space and see all the stars.

After his bath, Timmy felt warm and clean. He put on his pajamas and went to bed. He dreamed about exploring the universe and having more adventures. He was very happy.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Chloe. She was all alone in a dark forest. She felt scared and alone. Then, she saw a bottle. It was shiny and the label said it would remind her of magic. She was curious, so she decided to open it.

When she opened it, something amazing happened. She was surrounded by a bright light and then she realised it was her mummy and daddy. They had come to remind her that she was not alone, even in the dark.

Chloe was amazed and hugged her parents tightly. From that day, Chloe never felt alone and scared when walking through the dark woods. The bottle had reminded her that her parents were always there for her.

Once upon a time, there was a kind dog named Max. Max had a loyal friend named Lily. One day, Max and Lily went to the park to play. When they got there, they saw a little girl who looked tired. Max offered her a seat on his blanket.

The little girl was happy and sat down on the blanket. Max and Lily played with the little girl and they all had fun together. After a while, the little girl said she had to go home. Max and Lily said goodbye and the little girl thanked them for being so nice.

Max and Lily felt happy that they could help the little girl. They knew it was important to be loyal friends and offer help to others. From that day on, Max and Lily always brought an extra blanket to the park, just in case someone needed a seat.

Once there was a rabbit who was very hungry. He was looking for something to eat. Suddenly, he saw some grapes. He was so happy! He quickly hopped over to them and started to eat them. The grapes were so yummy and good! The rabbit ate the grapes until he was full. He was so happy that he had something to eat. It was the best thing ever!

Once there was a little girl. She was chubby and had beautiful blond hair and big brown eyes.

One day the little girl was walking in the park when she found an old newspaper. It was crumpled up and looked like it had been outside for a long time.

The little girl wanted to take the newspaper home with her. She carefully folded it up and tucked it under her arm.

On the way home she stopped at the store. She bought herself a new newspaper. She wanted to compare the old one to the new one.

When she arrived home, she spread out the old newspaper and the new one on the table. She carefully examined them side by side.

At last she closed the old newspaper and put it away. She kept the new one to read.

She was so happy with her discovery. It was like she found a treasure!

Once upon a time, there was a happy girl called Happy. Happy was very proud of herself because she was so clever.

One day, she found something strange in the garden. It was glowing very brightly. Happy was so excited!

She stood on her tippy toes to see what it was. She realised it was some special food. She was so proud of finding it!

Happy took the food inside to show her mum and dad. They were very proud of her too.

The family decided to have a special dinner to celebrate. Happy was so excited to eat the glowing food.

When they bit into it, it tasted delicious! They had the most special dinner ever.

Happy was so proud of herself and so were her parents. She had the best night ever!

Once upon a time, there was a little fish named Blue. Blue lived in a stream with many other fish. One day, Blue wanted to explore a different part of the stream. So, Blue swam away from the other fish.

As Blue swam, the stream became narrower and the water moved faster. Suddenly, Blue saw a big rock in the middle of the stream. Blue tried to swim around the rock, but the current was too strong. Blue got stuck behind the rock and couldn't move.

Blue called out for help, but no other fish were around. Blue remained stuck for a long time, feeling scared and alone. Finally, another fish named Red came by and saw Blue in trouble. Red swam over and helped Blue get free from behind the rock.

From that day on, Blue and Red became friends and explored the different parts of the stream together. They knew that even though they were different, they could still help each other when they needed it.

Anna and Ben like to pretend. They have a stage in their room. It is a big box with a curtain. They can be anything they want on the stage.

One day, they pretend to be animals. Anna is a lion and Ben is a monkey. They make loud noises and jump around. They have fun.

"Roar! I am a big lion. I am the king of the stage," Anna says.

"Ooh-ooh-ah-ah! I am a silly monkey. I can swing from the curtain," Ben says.

They laugh and play until they hear their mom call them.

"Anna, Ben, time for lunch. Come downstairs, please."

They stop pretending and get off the stage. They are hungry and thirsty. They run to the kitchen.

"Mom, we were pretending to be animals. It was fun," Anna says.

"Mom, we have a stage in our room. It is a big box with a curtain," Ben says.

"That sounds wonderful. I'm glad you have such a good imagination. Now, wash your hands and sit down. I made you some soup and sandwiches. They are warm and yummy," Mom says.

Anna and Ben wash their hands and sit down. They eat their soup and sandwiches. They are warm and yummy. They thank their mom and give her a hug.

They love to pretend. They love their stage. They love their mom. They are happy.

One day, a little boy named Tim went to the park. He saw a girl with a net. The girl was trying to catch a butterfly. Tim thought it was fun, so he went to help her.

"Hi, I am Tim. I think your net is important to catch the butterfly. Can I help you?" Tim asked the girl. The girl smiled and said, "Yes, you can help me. My name is Lily."

Tim and Lily ran around the park with the net. They tried to catch the butterfly, but it was too fast. They did not give up. They kept trying. After some time, they finally caught the butterfly in the net.

"Look, we caught the butterfly!" Tim said, very happy. Lily was happy too. They let the butterfly go and watched it fly away. Tim and Lily became good friends and played with the net every day at the park.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play at the park every day. She always went with her mommy and daddy. They would play on the swings, slide down the slide, and climb on the jungle gym.

One day, Lily saw a little boy crying by the exit of the park. She asked him what was wrong. He said he lost his regular toy car. Lily said she would help him find it. They looked all around the park, but they couldn't find it.

Suddenly, Lily remembered that she saw a toy car on the ground by the swings earlier. They went back to the swings and found the toy car. The little boy was so happy and thanked Lily for helping him.

Lily's mommy and daddy were proud of her for being kind and helpful. They told her that it's important to help others when they need it. Lily felt happy that she made a new friend and helped him find his toy car.

Sam was a poor boy who lived in a small house with his mom and dad. He had only one sock that he wore on his left foot. His right foot was always cold and dirty. He wished he had another sock, but his mom and dad had no money to buy him one.

One day, he saw a big truck outside his house. It had many boxes and bags on it. Sam was curious and wanted to see what was inside. He crawled under the fence and ran to the truck. He climbed on it and opened a box. He saw many things that he had never seen before: toys, books, clothes, and shoes. He was so happy and excited. He wanted to take something for himself.

He saw a pair of socks that looked soft and warm. They were blue and had stars on them. He thought they would fit his feet perfectly. He grabbed them and put them in his pocket. He was about to climb down from the truck when he heard a voice.

"Hey, kid, what are you doing there?" It was the driver of the truck. He was a big man with a beard and a hat. He looked angry and scary.

Sam was afraid and tried to run away. But the driver caught him by his shirt and pulled him down. He took the socks from his pocket and threw them on the ground.

"These are not yours, kid. These are for the orphanage. You are a thief and a liar. Go away and don't come back!" He shouted at Sam.

Sam felt ashamed and sad. He crawled away from the truck and ran back to his house. He cried and hugged his mom. He told her what happened and said he was sorry.

His mom was kind and gentle. She kissed his head and said, "It's okay, Sam. I know you were just curious and wanted something nice. But you can't take things that don't belong to you. That's wrong and hurtful. You have to be honest and respectful. Maybe someday, someone will give you a pair of socks as a gift. But until then, you have to be happy with what you have. You have me and dad, and we love you very much. That's more than many kids have."

Sam nodded and smiled. He felt better and hugged his mom back. He said, "I love you too, mom. You are the best mom in the world. And I don't need socks. I have you."

One day, a big bad wolf came to the farm. He saw three pigs who lived in three houses. One house was made of straw, one of wood, and one of bricks. The wolf wanted to eat the pigs, so he went to the straw house first.

"Little pig, little pig, let me in!" he said.

"No, no, no, by the hair of my chinny chin chin!" said the pig.

"Then I'll huff and I'll puff and I'll blow your house down!" said the wolf. And he did. The straw house fell down and the pig ran to the wood house.

The wolf followed him and said, "Little pig, little pig, let me in!"

"No, no, no, by the hair of my chinny chin chin!" said the second pig.

"Then I'll huff and I'll puff and I'll blow your house down!" said the wolf. And he did. The wood house fell down and the pigs ran to the brick house.

The wolf followed them and said, "Little pig, little pig, let me in!"

"No, no, no, by the hair of my chinny chin chin!" said the third pig.

"Then I'll huff and I'll puff and I'll blow your house down!" said the wolf. But he could not. The brick house was too strong. He tried to climb the roof and go down the chimney, but the pigs had a fire ready. The wolf burned his tail and ran away.

The pigs were happy and safe. They thanked the third pig for providing them a strong house. They learned that it is better to work hard and be smart than to be lazy and helpless. They lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved the holiday because she got to play with her friends all day long. One day, Lily's friend Sarah was feeling sad because she missed her mom.

Lily said, "Don't be sad, Sarah. Let's play together and have fun!"

Sarah said, "I don't feel like playing today, Lily. I miss my mom too much."

Lily thought for a moment and said, "I know! Let's draw a picture for your mom and send it to her. That way, she'll know we're thinking of her and we can still have fun together."

Sarah smiled and said, "That's a great idea, Lily. You always encourage me to feel better."

Lily and Sarah spent the rest of the day drawing pictures and having fun together. Even though Sarah missed her mom, she was happy to have such a good friend like Lily.

Once upon a time, there was a queen. She had long, shiny hair and wore a very pretty crown. The queen was very tough. She could lift heavy things and she never cried.

One day, the queen went to the field. She wanted to pick some fruit to eat. But when she got there the fruit had all rotted. It was very brown and smelled bad. The queen was very sad.

Suddenly, a big bird flew by. He carried a basket full of fresh, juicy apples. The queen was so happy! She thanked the bird and took the apples. She ate them all and they tasted so good.

The queen was very happy. She was tough and the bird had helped her. The queen smiled and thanked the bird for being so kind. The bird smiled back and flew away.

Once upon a time, there was a big library. In the library, there were many books. One day, a little boy named Tim went to the library with his mom. Tim was hungry, so he brought an apple with him.

In the library, Tim saw a little girl named Amy. Amy was sad because she could not find a book to read. Tim wanted to help Amy. He said, "Don't be sad, Amy. I will help you find a book." Tim and Amy looked at the books together.

Tim encouraged Amy to pick a book about animals. They found a book with a big lion on the cover. Amy was happy and said, "Thank you, Tim!" Tim and Amy sat down and read the book together. After they finished reading, Tim shared his apple with Amy. They both smiled and had a great day at the library.

Once there was a little white rabbit named Ted. He was very small and liked to play with his friends in the meadow. One day he wanted to explore, so he hopped away from the meadow.

He came to a big tree that was shaking and making a loud noise. Ted was so scared that his whole body trembled. Suddenly an x-ray came out of the tree and said it was a monster. Ted felt guilty because he had wandered away from the meadow.

The x-ray told Ted it was alright and that he could go back home. Ted was so relieved, then he hopped back to the meadow. He never felt so happy, and he learned his lesson to never go too far away.

Once upon a time there were two friends who liked to play together. They were best friends and liked to play games.

One day, their favorite game was chess. The game was interesting and fun. The two friends liked to see who could win the game.

Suddenly, something strange happened. The pieces on the chess board started to disappear! The two friends were surprised and looked everywhere for the pieces. But the pieces had gone!

The two friends looked and searched, but they couldn't find the chess pieces. They searched and searched, but the chess pieces had disappeared!

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to watch TV all day long. His mommy said, "Timmy, you need to let the TV rest for a while." But Timmy didn't want to stop watching his favorite show.

One day, the TV started to go slow. Timmy became sad because he couldn't watch his show. He said, "Mommy, why is the TV so slow?" His mommy said, "Maybe it needs a break. Let's turn it off for a bit."

Timmy agreed and turned off the TV. After a while, he turned it back on and it worked perfectly fine. Timmy learned that sometimes it's good to let things rest so they can work better.

Lily and Sam like to pretend. They pretend to be animals, or pirates, or superheroes. They have a lot of fun with their toys and their imagination.

One day, they find some paint in the garage. They ask their mom if they can use it. Mom says yes, but only outside and with old clothes. She gives them some paper and brushes and tells them to be careful.

Lily and Sam go outside and start to paint. They paint the sky, the grass, the sun, and the flowers. They paint their faces and their hands. They paint their dog, who is very patient and does not mind.

They see a long fence by the road. They think it is boring and white. They want to make it more colorful. They paint the fence with stripes, dots, stars, and hearts. They paint their names and a big smiley face.

They are very proud of their work. They think it is beautiful and happy. They show their mom, who is surprised and amused. She says they are very creative and talented. She takes a picture of them and the fence. She says they have to clean up, but they can keep the picture. Lily and Sam hug their mom and their dog. They are happy and tired. They go inside and wash up. They have a snack and a nap. They dream of more things to paint.

Once upon a time, there was a three-year-old boy called Tommy. Tommy was worried because he had a lot of things to do. Every day he looked at the calendar to try and remember his activities.

One day, Tommy's mom saw him looking at the calendar. She said, "Tommy, why are you so worried?"

Tommy replied, "Mom, I'm trying to remember what I have to do today!" His mom smiled and said, "Don't worry! I'll help you. Come and have some lunch first, okay?"

Tommy went to the kitchen and sat at the table. On the table was a sandwich. He picked it up and started to chew. Tommy enjoyed the sandwich so much that he wanted to have another one. His mom said, "Maybe later Tommy. Now you have to go outside and play!"

So Tommy happily finished his sandwich and went outside to play. He smiled, no longer worried.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a pretty dress with pink spots on it. One day, she went to visit her friend, Timmy. Timmy was playing with his toy cars.

Lily said, "Can I play with you, Timmy?"

Timmy replied, "Sure, but first let's measure who has the fastest car."

Lily didn't know what "measure" meant, so Timmy explained, "It means to see who has the longest car. We can use this ruler to measure them."

Lily thought it was a good idea and they measured their cars. Timmy won, but Lily didn't mind because she was having too much fun playing with her pretty dress and Timmy's cool cars.

Tom is a boy who likes to play with his toys. He has a big horn that makes a loud noise. He thinks it is fun to blow the horn and scare his cat and his sister. He does not care if they cry or run away. He thinks he is funny and smart.

One day, Tom sees a big truck outside his house. It has a horn like his, but bigger and louder. He wants to try it. He runs to the truck and climbs inside. He sees a button that says "horn". He thinks it will be fun to press it and make a big noise.

But he does not know that the truck belongs to a mean man. The mean man is inside the house, talking to Tom's mom. He hears the horn and gets very angry. He runs outside and sees Tom in his truck. He yells at Tom and grabs him. He says he will call the police and take away his horn. He does not care if Tom cries or begs. He thinks Tom is naughty and stupid.

Tom is very scared and sad. He wishes he did not play with the horn. He wishes he was nice to his cat and his sister. He thinks he is in big trouble and he will lose his horn and his toys. He thinks he is not funny or smart. He thinks he is a bad boy.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the garden. One day, she saw a little ant walking on the ground. The ant was very small and Lily thought it was cute.

She picked up the ant and held it in her hand. The ant was very graceful and walked around on her hand. Lily liked the ant and wanted to keep it as a pet. But then she heard a voice in her head that said, "It's not nice to keep animals as pets without their permission."

So, Lily put the ant back on the ground and said, "I'm sorry, little ant. I didn't mean to take you without your request." The ant walked away and Lily felt happy that she did the right thing. The moral of the story is to always be kind to animals and respect their wishes.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to eat spicy food, but her mommy always told her that it was too hot for her little tummy. One day, Lily went to a restaurant with her family. She saw a dish on the menu that looked very yummy, but it said it was spicy.

Lily's mommy warned her that it might be too hot, but Lily wanted to try it anyway. When the food arrived, Lily took a big bite. It was very spicy and her mouth felt like it was on fire! She drank lots of water, but it didn't help.

Suddenly, Lily's daddy had an idea. He ordered a cold glass of milk for her. Lily was hesitant at first, but she decided to accept the milk. As soon as she took a sip, the cold milk soothed her mouth and made the spicy feeling go away. From that day on, Lily always remembered to ask for a cold drink when she ate spicy food.

Once upon a time there were two friends, Sarah and Mark. Mark had a special thing that was small. It was so special to him, he carried it with him everywhere he went.

One day Sarah and Mark were playing when the special thing fell out of his pocket and broke. Mark was so sad and he didn't know how to fix it.

Sarah had a good idea. She told Mark they should visit Bob. Bob was a magical person who had special powers to restore things. Mark was excited to go and see if Bob would be able to help.

When they arrived, Bob looked carefully at the broken thing. He used some of his special powers to restore it. Soon the special thing was just like new! Mark was very happy and so was Sarah. They thanked Bob and took the thing home.

They had all learned a valuable lesson: never give up hope, because even broken things can be restored.

Once there was a happy little boy called Jack. He loved playing with his marbles. He had lots of different marbles and he loved collecting them.

One day Jack went out to the park and he saw something shiny on the ground. He picked it up and it was a marble! He was so excited.

Jack decided to show the marble to his Grandma. So he ran inside and said, "Look, Grandma! I found a marble!" His Grandma smiled and said, "That's wonderful, Jack! What a lucky thing to happen!"

Jack was so happy and he said, "Can I keep it, Grandma? Please!" Grandma said, "Of course, you can keep it. I'm so glad something happy happened for you today!"

Jack smiled and he put his new marble in his pocket. He was so proud of his new marble and he knew he would treasure it forever.

Sara liked to dream. She dreamed of big things, like flying in a plane, or seeing a lion, or having a lot of toys. She did not have many things, because her family was modest. They lived in a small house, and did not have much money. But Sara was happy, because she had her case.

Her case was a gift from her grandma. It was a red case, with a lock and a key. Inside, Sara kept her treasures: a doll, a book, a necklace, and a picture of her grandma. She loved her case, and took it everywhere. She would open it and play with her treasures, and make up stories about them.

One day, Sara went to the park with her mom. She brought her case, of course, and put it on a bench while she played on the swings. She saw a boy, who was bigger than her, and had a bike. He looked at her case, and smiled.

"Hi, what's in your case?" he asked.

Sara was shy, but she wanted to be friendly. She said, "It's my treasures. Do you want to see?"

The boy nodded, and followed her to the bench. Sara opened her case, and showed him her treasures. He looked at them, and said, "These are not treasures. These are old and boring. You should have something better, like a bike, or a game, or a candy."

Sara felt sad. She said, "But I like my treasures. They are special to me. They make me happy."

The boy laughed. He said, "You are silly. These are not special. They are trash. Watch this." He grabbed her case, and ran away. He threw it in a trash can, and rode away on his bike.

Sara cried. She ran to the trash can, but it was too late. The trash truck came, and took her case away. She lost her treasures, and her grandma's gift. She felt very bad. She wished she never met the boy, and never showed him her case. She wished she could dream again.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Anna. She loved to swim! Whilst swimming one day, she noticed something strange. Suddenly, a thick fog started to appear. Anna stopped swimming and stared at the fog with excitement. She couldn’t see very far and the fog was so thick that she could only see a few meters away!

The fog made everything look so mysterious, like a special adventure was just around the corner. Anna took a deep breath and started swimming into the fog. She was a very enthusiastic swimmer and she didn’t want to miss out on the fun!

She swam through the fog for what felt like an eternity. Finally, Anna could see an open space up ahead. As she swam closer, she saw that the fog was surrounding a beautiful lake. Anna was overjoyed and she swam around the lake for the rest of the day. The fog eventually melted away and Anna left with a happy heart.

Tom was a clumsy frog. He liked to hop, but he often fell into the mud or bumped into trees. His friends laughed at him and called him silly. Tom felt sad and wished he could hop better.

One day, he met a wise owl in the forest. The owl said, "I can help you, Tom. I know a magic spell that can make you hop very high and fast. But you have to do something for me first. You have to find a shiny stone and bring it to me."

Tom was curious and excited. He wanted to try the magic spell. He said, "OK, owl. I will find a shiny stone for you. Where can I look?"

The owl said, "You can look in the pond. There are many shiny stones at the bottom. But be careful, Tom. The pond is deep and cold. And there is a big fish that likes to eat frogs. Do not let him see you."

Tom nodded and hopped to the pond. He saw the shiny stones glittering in the water. He wanted to get one, but he was afraid of the big fish. He waited until the fish was far away, then he jumped into the pond. He grabbed a shiny stone and tried to hop out. But he was too clumsy. He slipped and splashed and made a lot of noise. The big fish heard him and turned around. He saw Tom and opened his mouth.

Tom was scared and screamed, "Help! Help! The fish is going to eat me!"

The owl heard Tom and flew to the pond. He saw the fish and said, "Stop! Do not eat Tom. He is my friend. He has a shiny stone for me. If you let him go, I will give you a magic spell too. A spell that can make you swim very fast and far."

The fish was curious and greedy. He wanted to try the magic spell. He said, "OK, owl. I will let Tom go. But you have to give me the spell first."

The owl said, "OK, fish. The spell is this: Swim, swim, swim, as fast as you can. Swim, swim, swim, to the other end of the pond. Then swim back and say, 'I am the fastest fish in the world.'"

The fish liked the sound of the spell. He said, "Swim, swim, swim, as fast as I can. Swim, swim, swim, to the other end of the pond." He let Tom go and swam away.

Tom was happy and relieved. He thanked the owl and gave him the shiny stone. The owl said, "Thank you, Tom. Now I will give you the magic spell. The spell is this: Hop, hop, hop, as high as you can. Hop, hop, hop, to the top of the hill. Then hop back and say, 'I am the best hopper in the world.'"

Tom liked the sound of the spell. He said, "Hop, hop, hop, as high as I can. Hop, hop, hop, to the top of the hill." He hopped away.

The owl smiled and watched Tom and the fish. He knew that the spells were not real. He had tricked them. He had made them practice and exercise. He had made them more confident and happy. He had helped them in his own way. He was a wise owl. He flew away with his shiny stone.

Once upon a time, there was a little bird named Tweety. Tweety lived in a cozy nest on top of a big house with a tall chimney. One day, Tweety was flying around when she saw a cat staring at her with big eyes. Tweety got scared and quickly flew back to her nest on top of the safe house with the big chimney.

Tweety felt relieved when she was back in her nest. She looked around and saw other birds flying and chirping happily. She felt safe and happy in her home. Tweety decided to take a nap in her nest and dreamt about flying high in the sky. When she woke up, she saw the sun setting behind the chimney. She stared at the beautiful colors in the sky and felt grateful for her safe and cozy home.

Once upon a time there was a clumsy staff. Its name was Clumsy. Tom and Jill had never seen a staff like Clumsy before. They fed Clumsy some nice treats and wanted to play with it.

Jill wanted to hold Clumsy, so Tom gave it to her. But Clumsy was so clumsy that it slipped out of Jill's hands and fell on the ground.

Tom and Jill were sad when the clumsy staff was broken. So the two friends decided to make a new staff for Clumsy.

They took some sticks and tied them together. Tom and Jill painted it beautiful colors and called it "New Clumsy". Then they gave it back to the clumsy staff.

From that day forward, Clumsy was never clumsy anymore. Tom and Jill were happy and enjoyed playing with New Clumsy!

Once upon a time there was a little boy named Max. Max wanted permission to do something special. He asked his mom for a license. Max’s mom said “A license? What do you need a license for?” Max said “So I can take a bath outside in the garden.” Max’s mom said “Oh, that might be fun! But I'm sorry, I don't have a license for you.” Max was sad but then he thought of a clever idea. He asked if he could make a fake license. Max’s mom thought for a moment and then said “Alright, you can make a fake license. As long as you don’t get into any trouble.” Max was very excited. He ran outside to the garden and set up his fake license. Then he grabbed a big bucket and filled it with water. He sprinkled soap over himself and splashed around. Max was so happy he was finally taking a bath outside!

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play outside and run around. One day, he was playing and he hurt his foot. He was sad and worried that he wouldn't be able to play anymore.

Timmy's mom saw him and asked what was wrong. Timmy pointed to his foot and said it hurt. His mom looked confused for a moment, but then she knew what to do. She helped Timmy clean his foot and put a bandage on it.

Timmy learned that even when he was worried and confused, he could always ask for help. He also learned to be careful when he played, so he wouldn't hurt his foot again. The moral of the story is that it's okay to ask for help when you're worried or confused, and it's important to take care of yourself.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a cozy armchair in her room where she loved to sit and read her books. One day, her mom came in and said, "Lily, it's time to go to the park!"

Lily jumped up from her armchair and ran to get her shoes. "I want to swing really fast!" she said.

At the park, Lily saw a big tree and wanted to climb it. "Mommy, can you help me stretch my arms so I can reach the branches?" she asked.

Together, they stretched their arms and Lily was able to climb up high into the tree. She felt so happy and proud of herself. "This is fun!" she shouted down to her mom.

Once upon a time there was a sunny day at noon. The sky was dry and the air was warm.

Two curious little children, called Max and Jenny, played together in the garden. Max found a box full of interesting things and he said to Jenny, “I’ll open it and see what’s inside!”

Max opened the box, and to the children’s surprise, he found a colourful kite! They both shouted in excitement, “Wowwie!”

Max and Jenny took the kite and ran quickly into the open field.

Max took a breath and said, “Let’s see if it will fly!” He let the string loose, and the kite started flying in the sky.

Max and Jenny were so happy and shouted, “Yay, the kite is flying!” They watched the kite until it disappeared in the dry sky.

Max and Jenny hugged each other and went back home, full of joy and surprise!

Once upon a time there was a big package that wanted to travel. So the package started to move very slow. It was such a slow pace that it took a long time for the package to get anywhere.

But the package didn't give up, it kept on travelling, taking one step at a time. Finally after a long journey, the package arrived at its destination. Everyone was so excited that the package had arrived.

They opened it up to find lots of toys, candy and books! Everyone was so happy with the package and everyone thanked the package for taking such a slow journey to get there. The End.

Jimmy liked to watch things. He liked to watch the birds in the sky, the bugs in the garden and the cars along the road. One day his mom took him to the bathroom. It was a regular bathroom. She said, “Jimmy, watch what you do in here.” Jimmy watched as his mom washed her hands. He wanted to wash his hands too, so he watched as his mom showed him how. He said, “I did it right, mommy!” His mom smiled and said, “Yes, you did it just like a regular person. Now let’s go!” Jimmy smiled and they left the bathroom. He was happy he watched and he thought that bathrooms were pretty cool.

Tom and Anna are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big tent. It is for a fair. They want to go inside.

"Can we go, please?" Tom asks his mom.

"Sure, but stay close to me," his mom says.

They go inside the tent. There are many things to see and do. There are games, toys, books, and food. Tom and Anna are happy.

They see a man who can cook. He has a big pot. He puts things in the pot. He stirs and stirs. He makes soup. It smells good.

"Can we have some soup?" Anna asks her mom.

"OK, but first you have to untie this knot," her mom says. She gives Anna a rope with a knot. "If you can untie it, you can have some soup."

Anna tries to untie the knot. She pulls and twists. But the knot is too hard. She cannot untie it.

Tom sees Anna. He wants to help her. He knows how to untie knots. He learned from his dad. He goes to Anna.

"Can I help you?" he asks.

"No, I can do it myself," Anna says. She is jealous. She does not want Tom to untie the knot. She wants to do it herself.

But Tom does not listen. He takes the rope from Anna. He unties the knot. He gives it back to Anna.

"Here you go," he says. "Now you can have some soup."

Anna is angry. She does not say thank you. She does not want the soup. She wants the knot. She snatches the rope from Tom. She ties the knot again. She runs away.

Tom is sad. He does not understand. He only wanted to help. He goes to his mom.

"Why is Anna mad at me?" he asks.

"Sometimes people get jealous when they think someone else is better than them," his mom says. "But you did nothing wrong. You were kind and generous. Maybe Anna will say sorry later."

Tom nods. He hopes Anna will be his friend again. He goes to the man who can cook. He asks for some soup. He shares it with his mom. It is warm and tasty. He smiles.

One day there was a hill near a lake. The lake shone in the sun, and it was the most beautiful lake in the world.

But one day a big, tall fence appeared around the lake, and all the animals were locked inside. They were so sad.

One animal - a rabbit - decided to try and get out. He hopped as high and as far as he could, but he couldn't get over the fence. Then he saw a hill and he knew he could try to get over the fence if he could get over the hill.

The rabbit was very polite and he said please to the hill. "Please, Hill, can you help me get over the fence so I can be free?"

The Hill thought for a moment and then said, "I can help you. I can make a ramp for you, but you have to promise to be careful and not hurt yourself."

So, the Hill made a ramp and the rabbit hopped up and over the fence. As he hopped away, the Rabbit said thank you to the Hill. "Thank you, Hill, for being so polite and helping me get out of the fence!"

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. He lived in a normal house with his mom and dad. Tim loved to play with his toys and have fun every day.

One day, Tim's mom gave him a task. She asked him to put away his toys before bedtime. Tim was not happy about this task, but he knew he had to do it. As he started to put away his toys, he saw his favorite toy, Mr. Bear, peek from under the bed. Tim was excited to find Mr. Bear and quickly put away the rest of his toys.

After Tim finished his task, his mom gave him a big hug and said, "Well done, Tim! You did a great job putting away your toys." Tim felt proud and happy. He learned that doing tasks, even if they seem hard or not fun, can make him and others happy. And that was the moral of the story: always try to do your tasks with a happy heart, and you will feel good in the end.

Lily was a compassionate girl who loved animals. She had a pet rabbit named Fluffy who was white and soft. She liked to hug Fluffy and feed him carrots and lettuce. Fluffy liked Lily too and would hop around her room and lick her face.

One day, Lily's mom said they had to go to the store and buy some things. She told Lily to put Fluffy in his cage and lock the door. Lily did as she was told, but she felt sad to leave Fluffy alone. She gave him a kiss and said, "I'll be back soon, Fluffy. Don't be scared."

But Fluffy was curious and wanted to explore. He saw a small hole in the cage and pushed his nose through it. He realized he could squeeze his body out of the hole and escape. He was happy and jumped out of the cage. He saw a bag on the floor that smelled good. He went inside the bag and found some bread and cheese. He nibbled on them and felt full.

But then he heard a loud noise. It was Lily's mom who picked up the bag and put it in the car. She didn't see Fluffy inside the bag. She drove to the store and parked the car. She left the bag in the back seat and locked the doors. Fluffy was scared and wanted to go back to Lily. He tried to get out of the bag, but it was too dark and tight. He started to cry and make noises.

Lily and her mom came back from the store and opened the car. Lily heard Fluffy's cries and looked in the back seat. She saw the bag moving and opened it. She was surprised and happy to see Fluffy. She hugged him and said, "Fluffy, you escaped from your cage! How did you get in the bag? You must have been so scared. I'm sorry, Fluffy. I love you."

Lily's mom was shocked and angry. She said, "Lily, how could you let Fluffy out of his cage? He could have been hurt or lost. You have to be more careful and responsible. You're lucky we found him."

Lily felt sorry and said, "I'm sorry, mom. I didn't let Fluffy out. He escaped by himself. He was curious and hungry. He didn't mean to cause trouble. He's a good rabbit. Please don't be mad at him. He's my friend."

Lily's mom sighed and said, "I'm not mad at Fluffy. I'm glad he's safe. But you have to watch him more closely and make sure he stays in his cage when we're not home. He's a smart rabbit, but he doesn't know the dangers of the outside world. He needs your protection and care."

Lily nodded and said, "I understand, mom. I'll be more careful and responsible. I'll make sure Fluffy stays in his cage and has enough food and water. I'll also play with him and keep him company. He's a compassionate rabbit, and I'm a compassionate girl. We love each other."

Lily's mom smiled and said, "That's good, Lily. You're a compassionate girl, and I'm proud of you. Now let's go home and give Fluffy a treat. He deserves it after his big adventure."

Lily and Fluffy were happy and went home with Lily's mom. They learned a lesson and became closer friends. They never escaped again.

John was walking in a deep dark forest. Suddenly, he stumbled on a big pile of leaves.

John was scared, but he decided to keep going. Eventually, he saw an owl perched atop a tall tree, its eyes glimmering in the moonlight. It was so quiet and still, so John thought that it must be wise.

John whispered to the owl, “Why are you so thoughtful?”

To his surprise, the owl replied, “I’m waiting. Something big is coming soon.”

John was curious, but he was so tired he stumbled all the way home. The owl remained perched in the same spot.

The next morning, when John returned, he saw a huge king cobra coiled up in front of the tree. It raised its hood and hissed, ready to strike. But the owl flew away before the snake could attack.

John was so amazed that he clapped his hands. He was grateful for the owl's thoughtful warning that saved him from the cobra.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy who loved to play in the sun. He was very happy and had lots of friends. One day, he was playing in the sunshine when he realized something was different. It felt like a spirit was watching him.

The boy kept playing, but the spirit didn't leave him alone. He started to feel uncomfortable, so he slowly walked back home. When he got back, he kept looking around in case the spirit was still there. He did this every day, but he still couldn't shake the feeling that something was following him.

Finally, he realized the spirit had been there all along. His home was no longer a comfortable place to be. He was scared and lonely, and the bad feeling of the spirit followed him wherever he went. He was never able to be happy and free again.

Lily loved her colorful wardrobe. She had many dresses, skirts, and shirts in different colors. She liked to mix and match them and make new outfits. She also had a big mirror where she could see how pretty she looked.

One day, Lily was playing dress-up with her wardrobe. She put on a pink dress, a yellow hat, and a green scarf. She looked at herself in the mirror and smiled. She felt like a princess. She wanted to show her mom how beautiful she was.

She ran out of her room and down the stairs. She called out, "Mom, mom, look at me!" But when she reached the living room, she saw that her mom was not there. Instead, she saw a big suitcase and a coat on the couch. She felt a pang in her chest. She remembered that her mom had told her that she had to go away for a few days for work. She had said that Lily would stay with her grandma, who would take good care of her. She had said that she loved Lily very much and that she would call her every night.

Lily felt tears in her eyes. She did not want her mom to go. She wanted her to stay and play with her. She wanted her to see her colorful wardrobe. She wanted her to hug her and comfort her. She ran back to her room and threw herself on her bed. She buried her face in her pillow and sobbed.

She did not hear the door open or the footsteps on the carpet. She did not notice the gentle hand on her back or the soft voice in her ear. She only felt a warm embrace and a kiss on her cheek. She looked up and saw her mom smiling at her.

"Hey, sweetie, what's wrong?" her mom asked.

Lily sniffled and pointed at her wardrobe. "I wanted to show you my dress. I wanted you to stay with me. I don't want you to go."

Her mom hugged her tighter and wiped her tears. "I know, honey, I know. I'm sorry I have to go. But I'll be back soon, I promise. And I'll always be with you in your heart. And you know what? I have a surprise for you."

She reached into her pocket and pulled out a small box. She opened it and showed Lily a shiny necklace with a heart pendant. "This is for you, my princess. It's a special necklace that will remind you of me. Whenever you miss me, you can look at it and feel my love. And you can wear it with any of your colorful outfits. Do you like it?"

Lily gasped and smiled. She loved it. She loved her mom. She nodded and hugged her mom again. "Thank you, mom. I love you. And I love my necklace. It's so pretty."

Her mom smiled back and put the necklace around Lily's neck. She kissed her forehead and said, "You're welcome, my love. I love you too. And you're the prettiest princess I've ever seen. Now, let's go downstairs and have some cookies. Grandma is waiting for us. And then we'll pack your things and go to her house. And I'll call you tonight, okay?"

Lily nodded and took her mom's hand. She felt better. She still did not want her mom to go, but she knew that she would come back. And she knew that she had her necklace, her grandma, and her colorful wardrobe to comfort her. She looked at herself in the mirror and smiled. She felt like a princess.

Sara and Ben were best friends. They liked to play in the park, eat ice cream and read books. One day, they found a big chair in the park. It was red and soft and had flowers on it.

"Wow, what a nice chair!" Sara said. "Can we sit on it?"

"Sure, let's sit on it," Ben said. They climbed on the chair and made themselves comfortable.

They pretended they were a king and a queen. They wore crowns made of leaves and flowers. They waved to the birds and the squirrels.

"Ben, do you want to marry me?" Sara asked. She had seen grown-ups get married on TV. They wore pretty clothes and kissed and danced.

"OK, Sara, I want to marry you," Ben said. He liked Sara very much. She was kind and funny and smart.

They held hands and kissed on the cheek. They were very happy.

But then, a chubby man came to the park. He saw the chair and got angry.

"Hey, you kids, get off my chair!" he shouted. "That's my chair! I left it here for a while. How dare you sit on it and mess it up?"

Sara and Ben were scared. They jumped off the chair and ran away. They did not want to make the man more angry.

They ran to Sara's house and hugged each other.

"Don't worry, Sara, we are still married," Ben said.

"Yes, Ben, we are still married," Sara said.

They smiled and played with Sara's toys. They forgot about the chair and the man. They were still happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little fish named Nemo. Nemo lived in a big ocean with lots of other fish. One day, Nemo's mommy told him to be careful because there was a bad shark swimming around. Nemo didn't know what a shark was, but he knew it sounded scary.

Nemo swam around, looking for some food to eat. Suddenly, he saw a big shadow coming towards him. It was the bad shark! Nemo was so scared and didn't know what to do. But then he remembered what his mommy told him. He had to protect himself.

Nemo swam as fast as he could, trying to get away from the bad shark. But he was running out of oxygen and couldn't swim anymore. Just when he thought he was going to be eaten by the bad shark, he saw a big rock. Nemo swam towards the rock and hid behind it. The bad shark couldn't find him and swam away.

From that day on, Nemo always remembered to protect himself and stay safe from the bad shark. He also made sure to always have enough oxygen so he could swim away if he needed to.

Once upon a time there was a little boy who loved to play in the sunshine. He would run around in the grass and make a big, messy mess. One day he was out playing under the blue sky and heard a noise from far away.

He couldn't see what was making the sound so he stopped to listen. The noise got louder and then it stopped. Then he heard it again, louder than before. He looked around and saw a big, yellow sun coming up from beyond the trees.

The little boy was filled with joy. The sun was so bright and warm and the sunshine made him feel happy. He jumped for joy and ran around in the sunshine, making a bigger and messier mess than before.

The sun kept shining and the little boy kept running and playing in the sunshine until he was too tired to play anymore. He lay down in the grass and watched the sun go down. He was happy and content as he watched the sun's glow slowly fade away.

Mum was teaching Emma how to fly a plane. The plane was big and expensive. Emma was so excited! She loved planes and wanted to learn how to fly one.

Mum showed her how to press all the buttons. She also taught her to make sure the plane was going just right. Emma was a quick learner! She practiced and soon could fly the plane all by herself.

Mum and Emma took the plane up very high. From up there they could see lots of things. Emma was giggling and laughing the whole time. She was having a wonderful time.

When it was time to come down, Mum showed Emma how to slow the plane down and land back safely. They said goodbye to the plane and went home. Emma was so happy she had learnt how to fly a plane. It was an expensive but amazing day!

Once upon a time there was a girl named Sue who wanted to get some apples from the top of the tree. She asked her Mom for a ladder so she could climb up to get the apples. Mom gave her a ladder and Sue got very excited.

Sue nervously put the ladder against the tree, and began to climb up. She was a bit scared of the height, but she was determined to reach the apples. She was almost at the top of the tree when suddenly her Mom called her.

Mom reminded her to be careful, because climbing a ladder can be dangerous. Sue listened to her Mom and carefully climbed down the ladder. When she was back on the ground, she gave the ladder a big hug, feeling grateful for her Mom's reminder to be careful.

And so Sue got her apples and enjoyed them with a big smile. The end.

Steve and Jill were getting married. They were so excited. Jill was wearing a beautiful white dress with lots of lace and Steve was wearing a suit and a tie.

On their way to the wedding, they drove past a big factory. Steve looked scared as he stared out of the window. Jill asked, “What’s wrong, Steve?” Steve replied, “That’s my old factory. When I was a child, I worked there. It made me sad.”

Jill understood why Steve was scared and said to him, “Let’s not think about the factory. We have each other and we’re getting married, so let’s be happy.” Steve smiled, and they arrived at the wedding.

Steve and Jill got married, and they were both very happy. They had finally escaped the sadness at Steve’s old factory and started a life of their own.

Once upon a time, there was a small girl named Emma. She was very excited because today was her birthday. In her hand, she held a piece of gum.

Suddenly she heard a familiar sound. It was the sound of something ringing! Emma looked up and there was a telephone on the wall!

Emma dropped her gum and ran to answer the phone. She was so excited as she picked up the receiver. On the other line, Emma could hear her Mom singing the "Happy Birthday" song. Emma was so happy to hear her Mom.

After Emma said goodbye to her Mom, she picked her gum up from the floor and ran back to play with her new toys. Emma was the happiest girl in the world.

Once upon a time, there was a little sheep named Baa. Baa was worried because she couldn't find her friends. She looked and looked but couldn't see any of her sheep friends. Suddenly, she saw her friends far away on a hill. Baa was happy to see them, but she was worried because she didn't know if she could fit through the fence to get to them. She tried and tried, and finally, she fit through the fence and was reunited with her friends. They all played together and had a great time. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her dolls and wear pretty dresses. One day, she wanted to wear her favorite dress, but it was on a hanger high up in the closet. She tried to reach it, but she couldn't.

Lily asked her mom to help her, but her mom was busy cooking dinner. Lily got upset and started to cry. She wished she could wear her dress and regretted not asking for help earlier. Suddenly, her little brother came in and asked what was wrong.

Lily told him about her dress and her brother climbed up to get it for her. Lily was so grateful and hugged her brother tightly. She learned that it's okay to ask for help and that she should always be grateful for the people who love and help her.

Once upon a time there was a generous olive tree. The tree wanted to give to the world in any way it could. Then one day, a little girl came up to the tree and said, "I'm very hungry. Would you mind giving me some of your olives?" The generous olive tree was very kind and mindfully shared some of its olives with the little girl.

The little girl took the olives and thanked the tree. "I'm so grateful that you are being so generous," she said. The olive tree felt great joy in being able to help and said, "It is always my pleasure to share."

The little girl ate the olives and felt full and happy. The olive tree was glad to have done something generous and kind, and the little girl was thankful for the olives. They both went on their way with big smiles on their faces.

The End.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his toy boats in the bathtub. One day, Timmy's mom reminded him to clean up his toys before getting out of the tub. Timmy said, "Okay, Mommy!" and quickly put his boats away.

The next day, Timmy went to the beach with his family. He saw a big sailboat in the distant ocean. Timmy asked his dad, "What's that?" pointing to the sailboat. His dad replied, "That's a sailboat, Timmy. It uses the wind to move." Timmy thought it was really cool.

Later that day, Timmy and his sister built a sandcastle on the beach. His sister said, "Timmy, can you remind me to bring our bucket back to the car?" Timmy said, "Sure!" and made sure to remind her before they left. They had a fun day at the beach and Timmy was happy to help his sister.

Once upon a time, there was a little ball named Rollie. Rollie was a delicate ball, made of soft yarn. He lived in a small town with a big church. Rollie loved to roll around the town and visit his friends.

One day, Rollie was rolling near the church when he saw his friend, Birdie. Birdie was up in a tree. Rollie called out, "Birdie, come down and play!" Birdie flew down and they played together. They rolled and flew all around the church, laughing and having fun.

As they played, Rollie didn't see a big hole in the ground. He rolled right into it! Birdie cried, "Rollie, be careful!" But it was too late. Rollie was stuck in the hole. Birdie flew to get help from their friends.

Soon, all their friends came to help Rollie. They worked together and gently lifted the delicate ball out of the hole. Rollie was so happy to be free. He thanked his friends and said, "I will be more careful when I roll near the church from now on."

From that day on, Rollie always looked where he was going when he rolled around the town. He played with his friends and visited the big church, but he never forgot to be careful. And they all lived happily ever after.

Anna and Ben like to pretend. They pretend to be animals, or pirates, or superheroes. Sometimes they pretend to be chefs and make food out of play-doh. One day, they pretend to make a cake for their mom. They use blue play-doh for the batter, and red play-doh for the frosting. They also find some prunes in the kitchen and put them on top of the cake as decorations.

They are very proud of their cake and want to show it to their mom. They carry it carefully to the living room, where their mom is reading a book. They say, "Surprise, mom! We made you a cake!" They put the cake on the table and smile.

Their mom looks at the cake and tries not to laugh. She sees the blue and red play-doh and the prunes on top. She says, "Wow, what a beautiful cake! Thank you, Anna and Ben! You are very sweet and creative. But you know, this cake is not real, right? It is only pretend. We cannot eat play-doh or prunes. They are not good for us."

Anna and Ben feel embarrassed. They did not know that play-doh and prunes are not good for cakes. They thought they were making a yummy and pretty cake for their mom. They say, "Sorry, mom. We did not know. We just wanted to make you happy."

Their mom hugs them and says, "It's okay, my loves. I am very happy that you made me a cake. It is a very nice thought. But next time, let's use real ingredients, okay? And maybe not prunes. They are too wrinkly and sour for cakes. How about some strawberries or chocolate chips instead?"

Anna and Ben nod and say, "Okay, mom. We will use strawberries or chocolate chips next time. Can we still play with the play-doh and the prunes?"

Their mom says, "Sure, you can still play with them. But only as toys, not as food. And please wash your hands after, okay?"

Anna and Ben say, "Okay, mom. Thank you. We love you."

They kiss their mom and go back to their room. They still pretend to be chefs, but they make different kinds of food with the play-doh and the prunes. They have fun and learn new words. They are not embarrassed anymore. They are happy.

Once upon a time, there was a small girl who was three years old. She loved going to explore in her wardrobe.

The wardrobe was very big and she had to stand on her tip-toes to reach the top. She would explore in it for hours. One day she was exploring and decided to take a peek into the back corner.

Just as she was about to take a look, her foot slipped on the wooden floor. She felt herself falling backwards, but nothing happened. It was as if time was going very slow.

After a few moments, she stopped falling and opened her eyes. She couldn't believe what she saw! All the way at the back of the wardrobe was a secret doorway leading to a little magical garden. She had found a secret place!

The girl smiled and ran outside into the garden, happy to have made such a special discovery.

Once there was a little girl named Lucy. She loved growing things. One day she planted a little seed in the ground. Then she waited and watched it every day.

After some time, a little plant grew up from the ground! It had big green leaves and a little white flower. Lucy was so excited.

One day, when Lucy was checking on her plant, she saw something different. It was a tiny, green pear growing. Lucy was so happy. She took the pear and hugged it.

One day, Lucy was playing in the garden and she dropped the pear on the ground. Lucy felt sad and she was ashamed. She knew she was not supposed to drop her pear.

But then something wonderful happened. Lucy looked down, and more pears had started to grow from the ground! Now Lucy could pick a new, fresh pear every day. She was so happy.

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who was very eager to go on an adventure. She put on her coat and hat, and set off into the woods.

As she traveled through the forest, she felt chilly and soon came across a shelter with a door made from logs. She opened the door, and saw a little furry creature inside with two big eyes. She knew immediately that this was the adventure she was looking for.

The little animal looked so happy to see her. She couldn't help but give it a big kiss! The little creature was so pleased that it stayed with her for the rest of her journey.

The two of them eventually came to the edge of the woods, and the little girl said goodbye to her furry friend with one last kiss. She waved goodbye and began her journey home— content and happy with her day.

Lily was a little girl who liked to poke things. She poked her toys, her books, her cat, and sometimes her brother. She wanted to see what would happen when she poked them. Sometimes they made noises, sometimes they moved, and sometimes they got angry.

One day, Lily saw something new in the bathroom. It was a green bottle with a spray on top. She wondered what was inside. She picked up the bottle and poked the spray. A mist came out and smelled funny. Lily coughed and sneezed. She did not like the smell.

She put the bottle down and ran out of the bathroom. She saw her mom in the kitchen. She told her mom what she did. Her mom was not happy. She told Lily that the bottle was for cleaning the bathroom, not for poking. She said that the mist was bad for Lily's nose and eyes. She took Lily to the sink and washed her face with water.

Lily felt sorry for poking the bottle. She said sorry to her mom. Her mom hugged her and said it was okay. She told Lily to be careful and not poke things that she did not know. She said that some things were not for playing, but for grown-ups. Lily nodded and said she understood. She asked her mom if she could poke her cat instead. Her mom smiled and said yes, but gently. Lily ran to find her cat and poked him softly. He purred and licked her hand. Lily was happy. She liked to poke things, but only the right things.

Once upon a time, there was a big lion who lived in a jungle. One day, he saw a little rabbit eating some carrots. The lion wanted to eat the rabbit, so he chased after him.

The rabbit was very scared and ran as fast as he could. Suddenly, he saw a friendly monkey in a tree. "Please, Mr. Monkey! Help me!" cried the rabbit.

The monkey was very helpful and threw a spear at the lion to protect the rabbit. The lion was scared and ran away. "Thank you so much, Mr. Monkey! You saved my life!" said the rabbit.

The monkey replied, "Don't worry, little friend. I will always be here to help you. And if that lion comes back, I will punish him!" The rabbit felt very safe and happy with his new friend.

Once upon a time there lived a little girl called Lucy. She wanted a bottle very much.

One day, Lucy asked her daddy for a bottle. She said, "Daddy, can I have a bottle and fill it with water?"

Her daddy smiled and said, "Yes, you can have a bottle. We will go to the shop and pick out a pretty one."

So, they got dressed and drove to the shop. Lucy saw so many bottles and couldn't pick just one. She asked, "Can I have the blue bottle, please Daddy?"

Her daddy smiled and said, "Yes, you can have the blue bottle." Lucy was so excited and ran to the counter to pay for it.

When they got back home, Lucy put water in her bottle and played with it. Every time she drank from it she thanked her daddy for giving her a pretty bottle.

Once upon a time, there lived a strong princess. She lived in a big castle and every day she tried to find something special. One day, she tried to find a diamond. She searched the castle high and low, but she could not find one.

The princess was very sad and she decided to go outside and look for a diamond. She went to the forest and looked everywhere. She climbed trees and looked in bushes, but she still could not find a diamond.

The princess wasn't very happy, so she decided to try one more time. She went to the river and tried to find a diamond there. The river was very deep and the princess was scared, but she had to keep looking. Suddenly, she saw a sparkle at the bottom of the river. She dived into the water and found the biggest diamond she had ever seen!

The princess was so happy and she took the diamond back to her castle. She kept it safe in the castle forever and told everyone about her special diamond.

One day, a little girl named Sally went to the park with her mom. Sally's mom had a big purse. Inside the purse, Sally found a small, dull rock. She picked it up and showed it to her mom.

"Look, Mommy! I found a rock!" said Sally. Her mom smiled and said, "That's a nice rock, Sally. But be careful not to pinch your fingers with it."

Sally played with the rock all day. She held it tight in her hand so she wouldn't lose it. But when it was time to go home, Sally felt a pinch on her fingers. "Ouch!" she cried.

Her mom looked at her hand and saw the pinch. "I'm sorry, Sally," she said. "Let's put the rock back in the purse so it doesn't hurt you again."

Sally agreed and put the rock back in the purse. She felt better now that the rock was safe and her fingers didn't hurt anymore. Sally and her mom walked home, holding hands and talking about their fun day at the park.

Once upon a time, there lived a very honest boy named Ben. Ben spent his days playing in the park near the harbor. He would bring his toy boat and pretend to sail in the harbor. Ben included his friends in his fun and they all had a great time. On sunny days, they liked to have a picnic in the park.

One day, Ben decided to take his friends on an adventure. He took them to the harbor to explore the boats. Ben showed them all the different boats, including the sailboats and their bright sails. They also saw a tugboat which was towing a barge. Ben told them all about the things the boats carry, like oil and fruit.

They all had a marvelous time at the harbor and Ben was very honest with them to explain all the boat facts. Even though the adventure was over, Ben's friends knew they could always count on him for an honest and fun adventure!

Once upon a time, there was a dependable dog named Spot. Spot loved to nap and play with his sock. He was a very good dog and always listened to his owner, Sam.

One sunny day, Spot and Sam went to the park. Spot was very happy. He played with his sock and then took a little nap under a big tree. Sam watched Spot and smiled.

When it was time to go home, Spot woke up from his nap. He picked up his sock and went home with Sam. They had a great day together. Spot was a dependable friend and Sam loved him very much.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to draw and color. One day, she went for a walk with her mommy and daddy. They climbed up a big hill, and when they got to the top, they saw a beautiful sunset.

Lily said, "Mommy, daddy, look at the pretty colors in the sky!"

Her mommy replied, "Yes, Lily. The sky looks very creative today."

Suddenly, Lily's little brother woke up from his nap in his stroller. He looked up at the sky and said, "Wow!"

Lily smiled and said, "See, even baby likes the pretty colors!"

They all sat on the hill and watched the sunset until it was time to go home. Lily was happy because she got to see something so beautiful and share it with her family.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to help her mom in the kitchen. One day, her mom was making a cake and asked Lily to polish the silverware.

Lily found it difficult to hold the silverware, but she tried her best. While she was polishing, her mom asked her, "Lily, do you know what season it is outside?"

Lily looked out the window and said, "It's summer!"

"That's right," said her mom. "And in the summer, we like to eat cake with fresh fruit on top. Can you go pick some strawberries from the garden?"

Lily was excited to help and quickly ran outside to pick some strawberries. When she came back inside, her mom had finished the cake and they sat down to eat it together.

"This cake is delicious!" said Lily.

"I'm glad you like it," said her mom. "And thank you for helping me polish the silverware and pick the strawberries. You're such a good helper."

Lily smiled and felt proud of herself for being such a good helper in the kitchen.

Ben and Lily liked to play in the park. They liked to slide, swing, and run. But their favorite thing was the tunnel. The tunnel was big and dark and had a hole at each end. They liked to crawl through the tunnel and pretend they were in a cave or a spaceship.

One day, they saw a new boy in the park. He was bigger than them and had a mean face. He came to the tunnel and said, "This is my tunnel. You can't play here." Ben and Lily were scared and sad. They did not want to fight. They wanted to play.

They asked the boy, "Why is this your tunnel? Can't we share?" The boy did not answer. He was ignorant. He did not know how to share or be nice. He just pushed them away and went inside the tunnel.

Ben and Lily did not give up. They had a plan. They waited until the boy was in the middle of the tunnel. Then they ran to the holes and blocked them with their bodies. They shouted, "Now you are trapped in the tunnel. How do you like it?"

The boy was angry and scared. He could not see or get out. He banged on the walls and cried for help. He wished he had not been so mean and ignorant. He learned a lesson.

Ben and Lily felt sorry for the boy. They did not want to be mean either. They moved away from the holes and let the boy out. They said, "We are sorry we trapped you. But you were not nice to us. Can we be friends and play together?"

The boy was ashamed and sorry. He said, "I am sorry too. I was not nice to you. I was lonely and bored. I did not have any friends. Can you forgive me and be my friends?"

Ben and Lily smiled and nodded. They said, "Yes, we can forgive you and be your friends. But you have to share and be nice. Do you want to play with us in the tunnel?"

The boy smiled and nodded. He said, "Yes, I want to play with you in the tunnel. Thank you for being kind and giving me a chance."

They all hugged and went to the tunnel. They crawled through the tunnel and pretended they were in a cave or a spaceship. They had fun and laughed. They became good friends. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to run and play in the fields near her house. One day, as she was walking, she saw a beautiful red flower. It was a poppy, and it looked so pretty!

Lily decided to pick the poppy and take it home. She held it gently in her hand and walked quietly so she wouldn't hurt it. As she walked, she saw a man in the distance. He was waving at her, but Lily didn't know him, so she was scared.

But then, the man came closer and Lily saw that he was a friendly farmer who lived nearby. He smiled and said hello. Lily felt relieved and waved back. She showed him the poppy she had picked, and the farmer told her that poppies were his favorite flower too. He said he had a whole field of them nearby, and he invited Lily to come see them.

Lily was excited and followed the farmer to the field. When they arrived, she saw a sea of red poppies waving in the wind. It was so beautiful! Lily felt happy and grateful that she had found the poppy earlier. She knew it was a special flower, and she would always remember that day.

Jim was keen to join a team. He wanted to find a fit team as he wanted to be the strongest. So, every day he would wake up early, yawn and go running. Then, he would go to the park and practice his skills.

There was a soccer team with lots of fit men playing. Jim watched them for a few days. He knew he wanted to join. So one day, he approached them and asked if he could join.

The coach noticed how fit Jim was and how keen he was to be part of the team. So he said yes! Jim was so happy, he yawned and smiled.

Jim joined the team and they practised together every day. Soon they were fit and ready to play in their first tournament. It was a great success! Jim was so proud to be a part of the team.

One day, Mommy opened a bottle of wine and put it on the table. She smiled and said to the little girl, "Let's have a picnic!"

But the little girl said, "Where's Daddy?"

Mommy said, "Oh dear. Daddy is at his office."

The little girl looked around the room, and she saw the bottle of wine. She asked, "What's in the bottle?"

Mommy answered, "It's wine. It's a special drink that adults like to have sometimes. It's not normal for children to have it."
