Later that day, Ben felt very sleepy. He decided to take a nap under a tree. As he closed his eyes, he heard the birds singing and the leaves rustling in the wind. He felt very peaceful and happy. When he woke up, he felt refreshed and ready to play again. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a young bear called Beartie. Beartie had been invited to a party, but he was feeling very sad and he forgot to get ready. Suddenly, his grandmother came in. She was so wise and she had a plan to make Beartie feel better.

Grandma smiled and said: "Let’s get you all clean and ready for the party. You look very nice in your clean clothes.”

Beartie smiled and hugged his grandma. He felt much better now that they had a plan. Together they got Beartie dressed in a brand new outfit.

Beartie felt so excited, but then he remembered something else. He felt sad again.

Grandma smiled and said: “Don’t worry. I will remind you to bring a special gift for the party. I know you will find the perfect one.”

Beartie smiled and hugged his grandma again. He felt much better now and went off to the party with a happy heart.

Lily liked to hug her parrot, Coco. Coco was green and red and had a yellow beak. He could talk and say "hello" and "I love you". Lily and Coco were best friends.

One day, Lily and Coco went to the park with Mommy. They saw a big dog that was barking and running. Lily was scared of the dog. She held Coco tight and said, "Don't worry, Coco, I will keep you safe."

But the dog saw Coco and wanted to play. He ran towards Lily and Coco and jumped on them. Lily screamed and Coco flew away. The dog chased Coco and tried to catch him. Lily cried and Mommy ran to help.

Mommy shouted at the dog and made him go away. She hugged Lily and said, "It's okay, Lily, you are safe now. Where is Coco?" Lily looked around and saw Coco on a tree. He was scared and said, "Help, help, I love you."

Mommy and Lily called Coco and asked him to come down. Coco was afraid of the dog, but he saw Lily and Mommy and trusted them. He flew down and landed on Lily's shoulder. Lily hugged Coco and said, "I'm sorry, Coco, I'm glad you are safe. I love you." Coco hugged Lily and said, "I love you too." Mommy smiled and said, "Let's go home, Lily and Coco. You are both brave and good." Lily and Coco nodded and went home with Mommy. They were happy and safe.

Once upon a time, there was a big oak tree in the middle of the forest. It was very tough and strong. Many animals lived in the forest and loved the oak tree.

One day, a squirrel and a bird were talking near the oak tree. The squirrel said, "I found a big nut, but it's too tough to open." The bird replied, "Let's ask the oak tree for help!"

The squirrel and the bird went to the oak tree and asked, "Can you help us separate the nut?" The oak tree agreed and used its strong branches to separate the nut into two pieces. The squirrel and the bird were very happy and thanked the oak tree.

From that day on, the squirrel and the bird became good friends. They played together every day and always remembered how the tough oak tree helped them. The oak tree continued to help other animals in the forest, and they all lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time there was a clever fish, swimming in the salty ocean. He saw a big rock, and decided to hide underneath it, to keep safe from bigger fish. As he was swimming, he saw a tiny little fish, who was calling out for help.

The clever fish smiled and said, "Don't worry, little one. What's wrong?"

The tiny fish said, "I'm so scared, I can't find my way home. I'm lost in the salty sea and my family is far away. Can you please help me?"

The clever fish said, "Of course, I can help you! Follow me." The clever fish swam in a particular direction, and soon enough they came to the tiny fish's home.

The tiny fish was so happy and thanked the clever fish. "You saved me and helped me find my home!"

The clever fish smiled and said, "You're very welcome, little one. Be careful and swim home safely."

And so the tiny fish swam home, safe and happy once again.

Once upon a time there was a little girl. She was very wild and loved to play. One day, while she was playing, she found something interesting. It was the refrigerator! She had never seen one before. She opened the door, and saw all the different things inside. She said to herself, “This looks like so much fun!”

So she started to play. She took out the apples, the bananas, and the oranges, and she made a big pile of them on the floor. Then she grabbed the milk and the juice, and she put them in her pockets.

Just then, her mom came in. She was surprised to see the little girl playing with the refrigerator! She said, “What are you doing, sweetheart?”

The little girl smiled, and said, “I'm playing with the fridge! It's so much fun, Mommy!”

Her mom just smiled and said, “Well, that's good, honey. Just make sure you put everything back before you go outside to play.”

So the little girl put everything back in the refrigerator and then went outside to continue her wild playing.

Once there was a clever radish. He lived in the mud. Every day he watched the sun come up and go down. He saw other things living in the mud too, like worms and slugs.

One day, he noticed something different in the mud. It was a beautiful butterfly! The radish thought it was so pretty. He watched as the butterfly moved around the mud. It was very quick and clever.

The radish wanted to try and touch the butterfly, so he used his leaves to wiggle closer. He was very careful! He was almost close enough, when suddenly the butterfly flew away. The radish was sad.

But the butterfly soon came back. This time, the radish was able to touch one of the butterfly's wings! He was so happy. They were friends until the sun went down.

The radish was a clever one. He had made a new friend that day!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She liked to play in her backyard with her toys. One day, she saw a cactus in the corner of her yard. The cactus had sharp needles and looked very prickly. Lily didn't like it and wanted it to go away.

But the cactus didn't move. It stayed in the corner, looking dead and dry. Lily tried to push it, but it was too heavy. She felt sad and didn't know what to do. Then, she had an idea. She decided to play a game with the cactus. She would try to win by throwing a ball and hitting the cactus.

Lily threw the ball as hard as she could, but it bounced off the cactus and hit her foot. She cried and felt angry. She tried again and again, but the cactus didn't move. She realized that it was okay to have a cactus in her yard, even if she didn't like it. She learned to accept it and play around it. From that day on, Lily and the cactus were friends.

Once upon a time, there were two friends, Timmy and Tommy. They loved to play games together. One day, they decided to play a game of thumb wrestling.

Tommy said, "I will win this game, Timmy!"

Timmy replied, "No way, I will win because I have a cool trick up my sleeve."

They both placed their thumbs in the middle and started to wrestle. Timmy used his cool trick and won the game. Tommy was upset and said, "I don't want to play with you anymore, Timmy."

Timmy felt bad and said, "I'm sorry, Tommy. Let's play another game and have fun."

Tommy smiled and said, "Okay, let's play hide and seek."

They both had fun playing hide and seek and forgot about their thumb wrestling game. From that day on, they learned that winning isn't everything and having fun with your friends is the coolest thing of all.

Once upon a time there was a young boy called Jack. He lived in a small village and loved to play all day. One day he found a magical sword in the woods. He had heard stories about magical swords and was very excited. He wanted to find out what the sword could do. Jack took the sword home and was about to use it, when a fairy appeared and spoke to him. She said, “Young Jack, this sword is special. It has magical powers and can be used to settle any disagreement.” Jack was excited and said, “I will use it for good!” The fairy smiled and said, “Excellent. I will give you a task. Use the sword to settle any disagreements and show people the path of kindness and understanding.” Jack said, “I promise!” The fairy was pleased and waved her wand. The sword glowed brightly and the fairy disappeared. From that day forward, Jack used the magical sword to help settle disagreements and spread kindness through the village.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to collect things like rocks, sticks, and shells. One day, he saw an aeroplane flying in the sky. Timmy had never seen an aeroplane before, so he wanted to collect it.

Timmy asked his mom if he could catch the aeroplane. His mom said, "No, Timmy. The aeroplane is too high up in the sky. It's unknown where it's going." But Timmy didn't listen. He went outside and tried to catch the aeroplane anyway.

Timmy ran and ran, but he couldn't catch the aeroplane. Suddenly, he tripped and fell. He hurt his knee and started to cry. His mom came outside and saw what happened. She told Timmy, "I told you not to try and catch the unknown aeroplane. Now you're hurt."

Timmy learned his lesson and never tried to catch an aeroplane again.

Tom and Lily were twins who loved to watch movies at the theater. They always went with their mom and dad and shared a big bag of popcorn. But one day, they had a big fight. Tom wanted to watch a movie about cars and Lily wanted to watch a movie about fairies. They yelled and cried and pulled the popcorn bag until it split and the popcorn fell on the floor.

Mom and dad were very sad and angry. They said, "If you can't agree on a movie, you can't go to the theater. You have to stay home and play by yourselves." They took Tom and Lily back to the car and drove home.

Tom and Lily were very sorry and wished they had not fought. They missed the theater and the popcorn and their mom and dad. They felt very lonely in their rooms. They did not have anyone to talk to or play with.

After a while, Tom knocked on Lily's door. He said, "Lily, I'm sorry I was mean to you. I don't care what movie we watch. I just want to be with you and have fun." Lily opened the door and hugged Tom. She said, "I'm sorry too, Tom. I love you and I don't want to fight with you. Let's go and say sorry to mom and dad and ask them if we can go to the theater another day."

Tom and Lily ran to their mom and dad and said sorry and hugged them. Mom and dad smiled and said, "We're glad you made up. We love you both very much. Maybe we can go to the theater next week and watch a movie that you both like." Tom and Lily nodded and said, "Yes, please. And can we have a new bag of popcorn?" Mom and dad laughed and said, "Of course. But don't split it again."

The moral of the story is: Don't fight with your siblings over small things. You will miss out on fun and happiness. Be kind and share and enjoy your time together.

Tommy loved to visit his elderly grandma every week. She always had something nice for him to receive. Sometimes it was a cookie, sometimes a book, sometimes a toy. Tommy always said thank you and gave her a big hug.

One day, Tommy went to see his grandma and saw a big box in the living room. He wondered what was inside. He asked his grandma, "What is that, grandma?"

Grandma smiled and said, "That is a present for you, Tommy. Do you want to open it?"

Tommy nodded eagerly and ran to the box. He tore off the wrapping paper and saw a beautiful carpet. It had many colors and shapes and animals on it. Tommy liked it very much. He said, "Wow, grandma, this is a wonderful carpet! Thank you so much!"

Grandma said, "You're welcome, Tommy. I made it for you. You can use it to play on, or to read on, or to nap on. It is very soft and warm."

Tommy hugged his grandma again and said, "I love you, grandma. You are the best grandma ever!"

Grandma said, "I love you too, Tommy. You are the best grandson ever!"

They both smiled and sat on the carpet. They played with Tommy's toys, read some books, and sang some songs. They had a very happy time together.

Molly was walking in the park. As she walked, she saw a bubble. It was a big, round bubble and it was hidden in the tall grass. Molly wanted to stay and play with it, but it started to float away. Molly smiled and raced to catch it. She tried to grab it, but it popped and disappeared into thin air.

She felt disappointed. Then she saw a bee buzzing around and suddenly she got an idea. She grabbed some flowers from the ground and blew into them. She formed a giant bubble and it stayed in the air. She was so excited.

Molly ran around the park. She chased after the bubble, trying to keep it from popping. She laughed as the bubble stayed with her, until it eventually made its way back to the tall grass and softly settled there. Molly smiled and hid the bubble in the grass so nobody else could find it. The bubble was hidden away and she was sure that it was staying safe.

Tom loved to help his mom in the kitchen. He liked to watch her chop and stir and bake. Sometimes, she let him do some things too, like wash the fruits or pour the milk. Today, she said he could help her prepare a salad for lunch. Tom was very happy.

She gave him a big bowl and a small knife. She showed him how to cut the lettuce and the cucumber. She said he had to be careful with the knife and not cut his fingers. Tom nodded and did as she said. He felt very proud. Then, she gave him a tomato. Tom looked at the red fruit. He did not like tomatoes. He thought they were yucky and slimy. He did not want to cut it.

He tried to give it back to his mom, but she was busy with something else. She said he had to cut the tomato too, or the salad would not be good. Tom felt scared. He did not want to touch the tomato. He did not want to eat it. He wished he could throw it away. But he did not want to make his mom sad or angry. He decided to be brave and cut the tomato.

He held the tomato in his hand and brought the knife to it. He tried to cut it, but it was too hard. He pushed harder, but the knife slipped. He heard a loud pop and felt something wet and sticky on his face. He dropped the tomato and the knife and screamed. He opened his eyes and saw red everywhere. He thought he was bleeding. He thought he had cut himself.

His mom heard him and ran to him. She saw him crying and covered in tomato juice and seeds. She realized what had happened and hugged him. She said he was not hurt, he was just messy. She said the tomato was too ripe and it burst when he tried to cut it. She said it was not his fault and he did not have to eat it. She said she was sorry and she loved him. She took him to the sink and washed his face. She gave him a towel and a kiss. She said they could finish the salad together. Tom felt better. He smiled and said he loved her too. He said he still did not like tomatoes, but he liked to help her in the kitchen. She laughed and said that was okay. They went back to the bowl and prepared the salad. They had a nice lunch. Tom ate everything, except the tomatoes.

Once upon a time there lived a brave girl called Lily. Lily lived in a tiny village, where the days were long and hot. One day, Lily noticed something wasn’t quite right. She could see angry people everywhere, shouting and being mean to each other.

Lily asked her mum what was happening, and her mum said sadly that a very harsh rule was being enforced in the village. Everyone had to obey it, but Lily wanted to resist.

She thought hard about what to do, and eventually she decided to go and talk to the people in charge. Everyone thought she was silly, but Lily was brave.

When she arrived, the people all laughed. They said that no one so small could change the way things were done. But Lily just smiled and asked them politely if they could change the rule.

They looked shocked, no one had ever asked them before. Finally, they agreed, and the rule was changed. Lily was very proud of what she had done, and the people of the village were forever grateful.

Once upon a time, in a hot desert, there lived a little cactus. The cactus was good and loved to make friends. Every day, the sun would rise, and the cactus would say "hello" to all the animals that passed by.

One day, a small bird came to the cactus. The bird said, "Hello, cactus! Can I sit on you?" The cactus was happy and said, "Yes, bird, you can sit on me. But be careful of my prickles." The bird was careful and sat on the cactus. They became good friends.

As the sun rose each day, the bird would come and sit on the cactus. They would talk and laugh together. The cactus and the bird were very happy. And they lived happily ever after.

"What's in the sack, Mama?" asked Billy, a three-year-old boy. "It's a tie," she smiled and replied. "What's a tie, Mama?" "It's something special I wear around my neck. You can wear ties too when you grow up," she said. Billy smiled and touched the sack, feeling the soft fabric. He opened the sack and took out the tie. It was gray with a yellow stripe. "It looks bitter," he said. Mama laughed and said, "No, it's not bitter. It's called a pattern. It's cool, isn't it?" Billy nodded and put the tie back in the sack. He was excited to wear a tie when he was older.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, she went to the park with her mommy. It was a cold day and Lily was wearing her warm coat. She saw many things to play with, but she couldn't choose which one to play with first.

After a while, Lily saw some kids playing with a ball. She wanted to play with the ball too, but the kids were bigger than her. Then, one of the kids came up to her and asked if she wanted to play. Lily was happy and chose to play with the ball. They had so much fun playing together.

When it was time to go home, Lily felt normal again. She was happy to have made a new friend and to have had fun in the park. She couldn't wait to come back and play again. The end.

Once upon a time there were two friends, one named Sam and the other named Pam. They both wanted to play catch and pitch a ball together. So Sam had an idea. He hoped that if he pitched the ball then Pam could catch it and then he shouted, "Let's play!"

Pam was very happy when Sam pitched the ball and was excited to try to catch it. But when Pam tried to catch the ball, it was too silly. She laughed and tried again and again, but it kept looking silly.

Watching Pam, Sam could tell she was struggling. He thought and thought of a way to help and then he had an idea. He said, "Hey, why don't you stand a little closer so it's easier to catch the ball?"

Pam was excited with Sam's idea and tried it. She began to catch the ball with ease and Sam cheered for her. They played catch for a long time and had lots of fun, and they even hugged each other when they both went home.

The end.

Sara was a painter. She liked to design new things with her paints. She made flowers, animals, and stars on paper. She was very good at painting.

One day, she wanted to design a big picture on the wall. She asked her mom if she could do it. Her mom said yes, but she had to be careful and patient. She gave Sara some paints and brushes and a big sheet of paper to cover the floor.

Sara was very happy. She started to design her picture on the wall. She painted a big sun, a blue sky, and some green trees. She was having fun.

But then, she saw a fly on the wall. She did not like the fly. She wanted to make it go away. She took her brush and tried to hit the fly. But she missed. She hit the wall instead. She made a big red spot on the wall. She was not careful.

She tried to fix it. She painted over the red spot with white paint. But the white paint was not the same as the wall. She made a big white spot on the wall. She was not patient.

She started to cry. She made a mess. She did not know what to do.

Her mom heard her cry. She came to see what was wrong. She saw the wall. She saw the big red spot and the big white spot. She saw Sara's picture. She was not angry. She was sad.

She hugged Sara. She said, "Sara, I know you wanted to design a beautiful picture on the wall. But you were not careful and patient. You made a mistake. You should have left the fly alone. You should have waited for the paint to dry. You should have asked me for help. Now, the wall is ruined. We have to fix it."

Sara felt sorry. She said, "Mom, I'm sorry. I did not mean to ruin the wall. I was not careful and patient. I made a mistake. Can we fix it?"

Her mom said, "Yes, we can fix it. But it will take time and money. We have to buy new paint and hire someone to paint the wall. We have to clean the floor and the brushes. We have to be careful and patient. Do you understand?"

Sara said, "Yes, mom, I understand. I will help you. I will be careful and patient. I will not paint on the wall again. I will paint on paper. I will design new things with my paints. But I will ask you first. I love you, mom."

Her mom said, "I love you, too, Sara. You are a good painter. You can design beautiful things with your paints. But you have to learn from your mistakes. You have to be careful and patient. That is how you become a better painter. And a better person."

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her dolls and make them pretty clothes. One day, she wanted to add some pretty beads to her doll's dress. She asked her mommy for some thread to sew the beads on. Her mommy gave her some smooth thread that was easy to sew with.

Lily carefully threaded the needle and began to add the beads to the dress. She was very happy with how it turned out. Her doll looked so pretty with the new beads on her dress. Lily was proud of herself for doing such a good job. She hugged her doll and went to show her mommy. Her mommy was very proud of her too.

Sara and Ben were going to the beach with Mom and Dad. They were very happy. They had to pack their bags with toys, clothes, and snacks. Sara packed her doll, her hat, and her book. Ben packed his ball, his shovel, and his crab.

Crab was Ben's best friend. He was a toy crab that could pinch and snap. Ben liked to make crab talk and play with him. He put crab in his bag and zipped it up. He was ready to go.

They got in the car and drove to the beach. It was a long drive. Sara and Ben were sleepy. They closed their eyes and dreamed of the sand and the sea. Mom and Dad were sleepy too. They did not see the big truck that came from the other side.

The truck hit the car. There was a loud noise and a lot of smoke. The car flipped over and rolled. Sara and Ben's bags flew out of the window. Crab flew out too. He landed on the road.

Sara and Ben woke up. They were scared and hurt. They cried for Mom and Dad. But Mom and Dad did not answer. They were very still and quiet. Sara and Ben were alone.

Crab saw Sara and Ben. He wanted to help them. He crawled to them. But he was too slow. Another truck came. It did not see crab. It ran over him. Crab was smashed. He could not pinch or snap anymore. He was broken.

Sara and Ben saw crab. They cried more. They lost their best friend. They were very sad. They wished they never went to the beach. They wished they stayed home. They wished they were safe.

Tom and Lily were playing in the park. They liked to swing, slide and run. But then the sky became dark and the wind became cold. They heard a loud noise. It was thunder.

"Let's go home!" Lily said. She was scared of the thunder.

"But I want to play more!" Tom said. He was not scared. He was strong.

"You are not strong, you are silly!" Lily said. She grabbed her coat and ran to the gate. Tom frowned. He did not like what Lily said.

He followed her, but he was angry. He did not want to wear his coat. He threw it on the ground. He wanted to show Lily that he was strong.

But then he felt something wet on his head. It was rain. It was raining hard. He looked at his coat. It was wet too. He felt cold and wet. He wished he had his coat.

He ran to the gate, but Lily was not there. She had gone home with their mom. He was alone. He was not strong. He was sad.

He cried. He wanted his mom. He wanted his coat. He wanted Lily. He was sorry for what he did.

He saw a man coming. It was the park keeper. He had a big hat and a big umbrella.

"Hey, little boy, what are you doing here?" the park keeper asked. He saw Tom's coat on the ground. He picked it up and gave it to Tom.

"Thank you," Tom said. He put on his coat. He felt warm and dry.

"Where is your mom?" the park keeper asked.

"She went home with Lily," Tom said.

"Who is Lily?" the park keeper asked.

"She is my sister. She is scared of thunder. I am not scared. I am strong," Tom said.

"Is that so?" the park keeper said. He smiled. "Well, being strong is good, but being kind is better. Sometimes you have to think of others, not just yourself. Do you understand?"

Tom nodded. He understood. He was not kind to Lily. He was mean.

"I am sorry," Tom said.

"That's okay. Everyone makes mistakes. The important thing is to learn from them and say sorry. Do you want me to take you home?" the park keeper asked.

"Yes, please," Tom said.

The park keeper took Tom's hand and walked with him to his house. Tom saw his mom and Lily waiting for him. They were happy to see him.

"Tom, where were you? We were worried!" his mom said. She hugged him.

"I was in the park. I was playing. I was strong. But I was also silly. I threw my coat. I made Lily sad. I am sorry," Tom said.

Lily hugged him too. "It's okay, Tom. I forgive you. You are my brother. I love you," she said.

Tom smiled. He felt happy. He loved his mom. He loved his sister. He loved his coat. He was strong. But he was also kind.

Anna and Ben were playing on the porch. They had many toys to play with. They had cars, dolls, balls, and blocks. Anna liked to put the blocks on top of each other and make towers. Ben liked to put the cars on the floor and make them go fast.

"Look at my tower, Ben!" Anna said. "It is very tall and strong."

"I like your tower, Anna," Ben said. "But look at my car. It is very fast and shiny."

They played happily for a while. Then they heard a sound. It was a distant sound. It was a sound of a train.

"Wow, a train!" Ben said. "Do you hear it, Anna?"

"Yes, I hear it, Ben," Anna said. "It sounds very loud and big."

They ran to the edge of the porch. They looked at the distant hills. They saw a small dot of smoke. It was the train.

"Can we go see the train, Anna?" Ben asked. "Can we go closer?"

"I don't know, Ben," Anna said. "We have to ask Mommy first. She is inside the house."

They ran to the door of the house. They knocked on the door. They waited for Mommy to come.

"Mommy, Mommy!" they shouted. "Can we go see the train?"

Ben and Mia are twins. They like to watch films on the big TV. Today, they want to watch a film about dinosaurs. But they have to wait for Mom and Dad to come home from work.

They play with their toys and look at the clock. It is almost time. They hear a car in the driveway. They rush to the door and hug Mom and Dad. "Can we watch the film now?" they ask.

"Sure, sweeties. Let's go to the living room," Mom says. She puts her bag on the couch and turns on the TV. Dad gets the film from the shelf and puts it in the player.

Ben and Mia sit on the floor in front of the TV. They are excited to see the dinosaurs. The film starts. They see big and small dinosaurs. They hear them roar and run. They see them eat and fight.

But then, something bad happens. A big dinosaur with sharp teeth and claws comes out of the woods. It chases a small dinosaur that looks like Ben and Mia's toy. It catches it and bites it. The small dinosaur cries and bleeds.

Ben and Mia are scared. They feel uncomfortable. They don't like to see the small dinosaur hurt. They cover their eyes and ears. They want the film to stop.

"Mom, Dad, can we turn it off?" they say.

Mom and Dad look at them and see their faces. They realize the film is too scary for them. They feel sorry.

"Of course, honey. We're sorry. We didn't know it was so scary. Let's watch something else," Mom says. She gets the remote and stops the film. She hugs Ben and Mia and kisses their heads.

Dad takes out the film and puts it back on the shelf. He finds another film that is fun and funny. He puts it in the player and turns it on.

Ben and Mia smile. They feel better. They watch the new film and laugh. They forget about the scary dinosaur. They are happy.

Ben and Mia like to play with tubes. They have many tubes of different colors and sizes. They can make tunnels, bridges, and towers with them. Sometimes they share, and sometimes they fight.

One day, Ben and Mia find a big tube in the garage. It is blue and shiny. They both want to play with it. Ben grabs one end, and Mia grabs the other. They pull and pull, but the tube does not break.

"Let go, it's mine!" Ben complains.

"No, it's mine!" Mia complains.

They pull harder and harder, and make a lot of noise. They do not see the cat sneaking up behind them. The cat is alert and curious. It wants to see what the tube is.

The cat jumps on the tube and bites it. The tube makes a loud hiss and pops. Air comes out of the tube. Ben and Mia let go of the tube and fall down. They are surprised and scared.

The cat runs away, happy and proud. It thinks it has won the game.

Ben and Mia look at the tube. It is flat and sad. They feel sorry for the tube. They also feel sorry for themselves. They have no more tube to play with.

They hug each other and say sorry. They decide to play with something else. They go to the garage and look for another toy. They hope the cat will not find it.

Once upon a time, there was a big cat named Fluffy. Fluffy was very envious of his friend, the little birdie, because the birdie could fly and Fluffy couldn't. One day, Fluffy saw the birdie wink at him and he got very happy. Fluffy asked the birdie how he could fly and the birdie said he had to stay light and eat lots of seeds. Fluffy listened carefully and decided to eat seeds too. He ate and ate until he felt very light. Then he tried to fly, but he couldn't. Fluffy realized he couldn't fly because he was a cat and cats can't fly. But he was still happy because he had learned something new from his friend. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a troubled sack. It was sad and didn't know what to do. Suddenly, something special happened. It started to freeze. The sack was so excited! It knew it was time to go on an adventure.

The sack slowly drifted away as it rode on the cold wind. It soared through the sky and saw many exciting places. Mountains, forests and rivers flew by. Soon, the sack arrived at its destination.

It landed in a meadow full of wildflowers. The sack was in awe. Then, something unexpected happened. The flowers, grass and trees all started to freeze. The sack was so scared.

But then, it realized that all the plants were just on a journey like the sack. The plants were taking a magical nap and would soon wake up in a new, beautiful place. The sack was not troubled anymore. It smiled and joined the plants in their deep freeze.

Once upon a time, there was a big party at the park. Lots of people were there, and they were all having fun. There were balloons and cake and games to play.

One lady had a big box with her. She said it was a surprise. Everyone was excited to see what was inside. The lady said she needed to put a label on the box first, so no one would open it by mistake.

The lady put the label on the box and everyone gathered around to see what was inside. When she opened the box, it was full of musical instruments! Everyone started playing and it was very noisy. But the lady said, "Welcome to the music party!" and everyone had a great time playing together.

One day the sun was shining and it was very warm. Mama and Ben were outside playing in the garden. Suddenly, dark clouds appeared in the sky and it started to rain.

Mama said, "Oh, it's raining! Quick, let's run inside."

They both ran inside the house, laughing. Ben said, "I like the rain! It's fun!"

Mama smiled. "I like the rain too, especially because it makes the flowers grow. But we will have to stay inside until the rain stops."

Mama then turned on the news. They learned that the rain was going to be very heavy. Mama said, "Well, that's too bad! We won't be able to go outside for a while."

Ben said, "Oh, I hope the rain stops soon!"

Mama smiled and said, "It will, Ben. Let's get some fat snacks for when the rain stops. What do you think?"

Ben smiled and said, "Yes! That's a great idea!"

Once upon a time, there was a little kangaroo. He wanted to help people and animals around him, so he hopped around looking for someone to lend a hand. One day, he encountered a grumpy bear. The bear said 'I need help to find food.'

The little kangaroo nodded eagerly and followed the bear. He hopped around looking for food, but his efforts were in vain. The bear became angrier and began to yell.

The kangaroo suggested they take a break and the bear agreed. However, as they stopped to rest, the bear had an idea. He said, 'Let’s play a game. If you win, I will help you find food.'

The little kangaroo was not so sure, but he agreed to play. Suddenly, the bear lunged forward and grabbed the kangaroo with his claws. The kangaroo cried for help, but no one came to his rescue. The grumpy bear ate the poor kangaroo and hop away. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a big palace. In the palace, there lived a king and queen. They had a little girl named Lily. She had a toy bear named Mr. Bear. Lily and Mr. Bear were best friends.

One day, Lily and Mr. Bear were playing in the palace. They heard a loud noise. It made them feel frightened. They did not know what it was. Lily asked Mr. Bear, "What was that?" Mr. Bear said, "I don't know, but we should hide." So, they hid under a table.

The loud noise came again, and the palace started to shake. Lily and Mr. Bear held each other tight. The king and queen came running in. They were not frightened. They told Lily and Mr. Bear, "It's just a big truck outside. It's okay." Lily and Mr. Bear felt safe again, and they went back to playing in the palace.

Once upon a time, there was a big, big dinosaur who lived in a forest. He was very friendly and liked to talk to all the animals he met. One day, he met a small bird who was sad. The bird said, "I have a big, big opinion to share, but I am too small to deliver it to everyone."

The dinosaur replied, "Don't worry, little bird. I can help you deliver your opinion to all the animals in the forest." So the bird shared her opinion with the dinosaur, and he went around the forest telling everyone about it.

All the animals listened to the dinosaur because he was so large and had a loud voice. They all agreed with the bird's opinion and thanked the dinosaur for delivering it to them. From that day on, the little bird was no longer sad and felt happy that her opinion was heard by everyone in the forest.

Once upon a time, there was a little red motor. The motor was very strong and always wanted to help others. It lived in a small town where everyone was kind and grateful for each other.

One day, a big truck was stuck in the mud. The driver of the truck said, "Oh no! I need help!" The little red motor heard the driver and came to help. The motor said, "Don't worry! I will pull you out."

The little red motor pulled and pulled with all its strength. Slowly, the big truck came out of the mud. The driver of the truck was so grateful. He said, "Thank you, little red motor! You are very strong and helpful."

From that day on, the little red motor continued to help everyone in the town. The people in the town were always grateful for the little red motor's help. And the little red motor was happy to be a helpful friend to everyone.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lucy. She was 3 years old and liked playing with her toys.

One day, Lucy found a white box in her garden. She was curious and opened it. Inside was a beautiful, peaceful bird. It was so calm and gentle. Lucy got to understand that the bird wanted her to take care of it.

Lucy said, "Hello, Birdy! Can I play with you?"

The bird nodded and said, "Yes, you can play with me. I will be your friend."

Lucy was so happy and excited. She took the bird inside her house and fed it. From that day on, Lucy and Birdy were best friends. They would play together in the garden and always have fun.

Lucy understood that Birdy was the best friend she could ever have.

One day, Amy was feeling very sick. She had a big fever and felt very weak. Her Mommy gave her some medicine to make her feel better. After taking it, Amy felt much better.

Her Mommy said, "Let's go outside to get some fresh air." Together, they went to the park. There was an enormous tree in the park, and Amy was so excited. She ran over to it and jumped.

Mommy said, "We can't jump today. Let's go for a jog around the park instead!" Amy was surprise, but liked the idea. Together, they jogged around the park. It was so much fun!

Amy was so happy that she felt better and that they had jogged around the park. Soon it was time to go home, but Amy had a lot of energy still.

Mommy said, "Let's stay here a while longer and jog some more!" So they jogged around the park one more time, and then they went home.

That was the best day ever!

Lily liked to cook with her mom. They made cakes and pies and soup. Lily had a pink apron and a wooden spoon. She helped mom stir and pour and taste.

One day, mom said they would cook something new. It was called lemon curd. It was yellow and sweet and sour. Lily was curious. She wanted to try it.

Mom said they needed eggs and butter and sugar and lemons. She cracked the eggs and melted the butter. She added the sugar and squeezed the lemons. She put the pot on the stove and turned on the heat.

Lily watched as the pot bubbled and steamed. She smelled the lemon and the butter. She asked mom if she could taste it. Mom said yes, but be careful. It was very hot.

Mom gave Lily a small spoon and a helmet. She said the helmet was to protect her head from the steam. Lily put on the helmet and took the spoon. She dipped it in the pot and brought it to her mouth.

She tasted the lemon curd. It was very sweet and very sour. It was also very bitter. Lily made a face and spat it out. She did not like it at all. She said it was yucky.

Mom laughed and hugged her. She said it was okay. Not everyone liked lemon curd. She said they could make something else. Something that Lily liked.

Lily smiled and nodded. She took off the helmet and gave it to mom. She said she wanted to make chocolate cake. Mom said that sounded good. They washed the pot and the spoon and started to cook again.

Once upon a time there lived a little girl named Sarah. She was very excited one day because her mommy gave her a new purse. Sarah loved her purse and it was brightly coloured and had lots of pretty ribbons on it.

Every day when Sarah went to school, she put her purse in her cubby and played happily with her friends. But one day, her friends saw that she had a new purse and got very envious. They started to ask her where she had gotten her purse and became very jealous.

Sarah's mommy had taught her to behave nicely, so she smiled and explained where she had gotten her purse. All her friends smiled when they heard the story and said they were happy that Sarah had a new purse.

Ever since that day, Sarah and her friends have been very kind to each other and shared their things. Sarah still loves her purse and takes it everywhere she goes!

Anna looked out the window. She wanted to see the clear sky and the shiny stars. She wished she could reach them. All of the sudden, a glowing envelope appeared. Anna was so excited. She opened it. Inside the envelope were stars that were glowing too. Anna reached her hand to take one of the stars. She could feel its magic. She put it in her pocket and went back to bed. The star kept on glowing in her pocket. This made Anna feel very happy and special.

Once upon a time, there was a big boat with a powerful engine. It could go very fast on the water. One day, some kids went on the boat to sail. They had so much fun! They saw lots of fish and birds. But then, the engine stopped working. The boat couldn't move anymore. The kids were sad because they thought their fun was spoiled. But then, they saw a big whale swimming next to the boat. The whale pushed the boat with its big powerful tail and saved the day. The kids were so happy they could sail again.

Mama and her daughter were walking near their house. The daughter saw a tall tree and wanted to measure how high it was. Mama looked at the tree, too. It was so tall the top was lost in the gloomy sky. She smiled, grabbed a ruler and said: "let's measure its power".

They put the ruler up to the first branch. Mama was amazed to find the ruler was much too short to reach the top! Her daughter just laughed, excited to find out how tall the tree really was.

Mama measured with her long arms instead, stretching them up as high as she could. It turned out the tree was even taller than she thought — twice as tall as Mama! Her daughter was so excited, she laughed and clapped her hands.

Mama couldn't believe it. She'd never seen a tree so tall before. Even though it was so gloomy outside, watching the way her daughter was so happy filled mama's heart with joy.

Lily and Tom were best friends. They liked to play in the park, share their toys and hug each other. They always said "I love you" before they went home.

One day, Lily saw a big, shiny bike in the park. She wanted to ride it, but it was not hers. She looked around and saw no one. She thought no one would mind if she took it for a little while. She got on the bike and started to pedal.

Tom saw Lily on the bike. He knew it was not hers. He ran after her and shouted "Lily, stop! That is not your bike! You are taking someone else's bike! That is wrong!"

Lily heard Tom, but she did not stop. She liked the bike too much. She rode faster and faster, until she crashed into a tree. She fell off the bike and hurt her knee. She started to cry.

Tom reached Lily and helped her up. He saw the bike was broken. He also saw a man running towards them. He was angry. He said "That is my bike! How dare you take it and break it! You are very naughty and rude!"

Lily felt ashamed. She knew she did a bad thing. She said "I'm sorry, I'm sorry, I'm sorry. I just wanted to ride the bike. I did not mean to break it. Please forgive me."

The man looked at Lily and saw her tears. He saw her knee was bleeding. He felt sorry for her. He said "It's okay, I forgive you. But you should not take things that are not yours. That is stealing. You should ask first. And you should listen to your friend. He was trying to help you."

Lily nodded. She said "I know, I know, I know. I was wrong. I will not do it again. And I will listen to Tom. He is my best friend. I love him."

Tom smiled. He said "I love you too, Lily. And I'm glad you are okay. But next time, let's play with our own toys, okay?"

Lily hugged Tom. She said "Okay, okay, okay. Let's go home now. And let's say sorry to the man again."

They said sorry to the man again. He gave them a band-aid for Lily's knee. He said "Be careful next time. And be good to each other."

They said thank you to the man. They walked home, holding hands. They remembered their mistake, but they also remembered their love. They were still best friends.

There was a boy named Tim. He had a modern toy car. One day, Tim went to the store with his mom. He saw a candy he wanted. But Tim did not have a penny to buy it.

Tim started to complain. He wanted the candy so much. His mom said, "No candy today, Tim." Tim was sad. He went back home with his mom.

At home, Tim played with his modern toy car. He smiled and forgot about the candy. Tim's mom was happy. She knew Tim didn't need the candy to be happy.

Anna and Ben are twins. They like to play in the park with their mom and dad. One day, they see a big fountain in the park. The fountain has water that goes up and down. It makes a nice sound.

Anna and Ben run to the fountain. They want to touch the water. Mom and dad say, "Be careful, don't get wet." Anna and Ben say, "OK, mom and dad." They put their hands in the water. It feels cold and soft. They laugh and splash.

After a while, Anna and Ben get tired. They say, "Mom, dad, we are sleepy." Mom and dad say, "Let's go home, then." They take Anna and Ben to the car. Anna and Ben fall asleep in the car. They dream of the fountain and the water. They are happy.

Once there was a man who was deaf. He struggled to hear most things, but he loved the sound of birds singing. One day he decided to save the birds by buying them special thread. He wrapped it around the trees so the birds could make their nests and feel safe. The man worked all day long, making sure that each tree was safe and secure with the thread.

When he was done, he sat back and watched the birds come to the trees, singing a sweet song. He smiled as he watched the birds make their nests, safe from the wind and the rain. He could not hear the birds singing, but he knew they were singing for him.

The man was happy to have saved the birds and to have given them a safe, secure place to live. He will never forget the sound of birds singing, even though he is deaf.

Once upon a time, there was a green piano in the park. It was a very pretty piano. Many kids loved to play with it.

One day, a little girl named Lily went to the park with her mom. She saw the green piano and said, "Mom, look! A green piano! Can I play with it?" Her mom said, "Yes, you can play with it, but be careful."

Lily played with the green piano and made nice music. Other kids came to look and listen. They clapped their hands and danced to the music. Lily was very happy.

Then, a little boy named Tim joined Lily. He said, "Can I play the green piano too?" Lily said, "Yes, let's play together!" They played the green piano and made even more nice music.

In the end, all the kids in the park had fun playing with the green piano. They loved the music it made and they all had a great day.

Once upon a time there was a little green frog. He was sitting in the pond and enjoying the sun. Suddenly he felt the earth shaking beneath him. It was an earthquake! He was scared and he began to hop around the pond.

"Help me!" he shouted. "I need someone to help me!"

Just then he saw a big green bird. "Can you help me?" he asked.

The bird looked around and shook his head. "I'm sorry, little frog," he said. "But I can't help you. I need to find a safe place before the earthquake gets worse."

The frog felt very sad and afraid. He jumped around the pond, looking for something or someone to help him. But the earthquake was very strong and he couldn't find anyone. Suddenly it stopped and the frog was safe. But he was sad. He'd needed help and he had been all alone.

Once there was a mommy, a daddy, and a little toddler. The toddler loved to scatter things throughout the house.

One day, the toddler saw an empty stove. He thought it was fun and started to scatter things around it. Mommy and Daddy watched as the toddler took his toys and spread them around the stove.

Mommy and Daddy laughed and smiled at the fun the little toddler was having. They told him to stay away from the stove so he wouldn't get hurt. But the little toddler scattered his toys until he was all done playing.

Then Daddy scooped up the toddler, holding him in his big strong arms. Mommy and Daddy shared a smile as the little toddler wrapped his arms around Daddy and fell asleep. That was the end of an afternoon of fun and a stove scattered with toys.

Lily and Ben were twins who liked to play with their toys. They had a big tree in their living room with many shiny things on it. They were called ornaments and they were very pretty. Lily and Ben wanted to touch them, but Mommy said no. She said they were breakable and not for playing.

One night, Lily and Ben woke up when it was dark. They heard a noise from the living room. They got out of their beds and tiptoed to the door. They opened it and saw a big man in a red suit. He had a big bag on his back and he was putting things under the tree. He was Santa!

Lily and Ben were very excited. They wanted to say hello to Santa and see what he brought them. They ran to the living room and shouted, "Santa, Santa, we are here!"

Santa turned around and smiled. He said, "Ho ho ho, hello Lily and Ben. You are very brave and tough to wake up and see me. But you should be sleeping, it is not time to open your gifts yet."

Lily and Ben looked at the tree and saw many boxes with ribbons and bows. They also saw some new ornaments that Santa had hung on the tree. They were very curious and wanted to touch them.

Santa said, "Be careful, these ornaments are very special. They are from different places in the world. They tell stories and make wishes. But they are also very fragile and can break easily. You have to be gentle and respectful with them."

Lily and Ben nodded. They reached for the ornaments and touched them softly. They felt warm and sparkly. They heard some sounds and saw some pictures in their minds. They saw snow and mountains and animals and people. They felt happy and amazed.

Santa said, "Do you like them? They are my gift to you. They will help you learn and dream and grow. But you have to promise me something. You have to promise to take good care of them and share them with each other. Can you do that?"

Lily and Ben said, "Yes, Santa, we promise. Thank you, thank you, thank you!"

Santa said, "You are very welcome, Lily and Ben. You are very good and sweet children. Now, you have to go back to your beds and sleep. I have to go to other houses and deliver more gifts. I will see you next year. Merry Christmas!"

Lily and Ben hugged Santa and said, "Merry Christmas, Santa! We love you!"

Santa hugged them back and said, "I love you too, Lily and Ben. Good night!"

Lily and Ben ran back to their beds and snuggled under their blankets. They closed their eyes and smiled. They had the best night ever. They had met Santa and he had given them the most wonderful ornaments. They could not wait to wake up and see them again.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. He was very hungry and wanted to eat dinner. His mommy asked him what he wanted to eat, and Timmy said he wanted pizza. Mommy said, "Okay, let's go buy pizza!" Timmy was very happy because he loved pizza.

They went to the pizza place and mommy bought a big pizza with lots of cheese and pepperoni. Timmy was so happy and couldn't wait to eat it. They went back home and sat down to eat their dinner. Timmy took a big bite of pizza and smiled. He was very happy because it was so yummy.

After they finished eating, Timmy said, "Thank you mommy for buying me pizza. I'm so happy!" Mommy was happy too because Timmy was happy. They hugged and went to bed, dreaming of more happy dinners together.

Ben and Mia were friends who liked to play together. They had a big pool in their backyard where they could swim and splash. One day, they decided to have a race in the water.

"Ready, set, go!" Ben shouted and started to swim as fast as he could. Mia followed him, but she was slower. Ben reached the other side of the pool and turned around. He saw Mia still swimming and smiled.

"I win, I win!" he said. "I am the best swimmer!"

Mia did not like that. She felt envious of Ben. She wanted to be the best swimmer too. She reached the other side of the pool and got out. She looked at Ben and said, "No, you are not the best swimmer. You cheated. You started before me."

Ben was surprised. He did not cheat. He started when he said go. He looked at Mia and said, "No, I did not cheat. You are just slow. You are a bad swimmer."

Mia and Ben started to argue. They did not agree. They said mean things to each other. They made each other sad and angry.

Their mom heard them and came outside. She saw them fighting and said, "Stop, stop! What is going on? Why are you not playing nicely?"

Mia and Ben told their mom what happened. They blamed each other for the race. Their mom listened and said, "I see. You both wanted to win, but you did not have fun. You let your envy and pride hurt your friendship. That is not good. You should be happy for each other and share your skills. You should say sorry and hug."

Mia and Ben thought about what their mom said. They realized they were wrong. They did not want to lose their friend. They felt sorry and hugged.

"I am sorry, Ben. You are a good swimmer. You did not cheat. Can we be friends again?" Mia said.

"I am sorry, Mia. You are a good swimmer too. You are not slow. Can we be friends again?" Ben said.

Their mom smiled and said, "That is better. Now, why don't you swim together and have fun? You can take turns to be the leader and the follower. You can teach each other new tricks. You can enjoy the pool and the sun."

Mia and Ben agreed. They jumped back into the pool and swam together. They had fun and laughed. They were friends again.

Yesterday was a dependable day for Dan. He woke up and there was mommy and daddy with a big smile. Then Dan and his family went outside to play. Dan was excited to see all the flowers and the bugs. He ran around and had lots of fun.

But then it started to rain and it was getting harder and harder. Dan tried to keep playing but it was a struggle. He was getting wet and he was starting to get scared.

Mommy and Daddy knew how to help. They got out their coats and umbrellas and they held Dan's hands. With their help, he made it through the rainy day. Dan was so happy to feel safe and warm with his family. He learned that why it is important to have dependable people to help.

Lily and Ben were at the zoo with their mom. They saw many animals, like monkeys, lions, and giraffes. They were happy and excited. But when they came to the rhinoceros, they saw that he was gloomy. He was sitting in a corner of his pen, not moving or making any noise.

"Why is he so gloomy, mom?" Lily asked.

"Maybe he is lonely, or bored, or misses his home," mom said. "Rhinoceroses are very big and strong, but they also have feelings."

"Can we make him happy, mom?" Ben asked.

Mom thought for a moment. Then she said, "Maybe we can. Why don't we try to talk to him and cheer him up?"

Lily and Ben nodded. They walked closer to the rhinoceros and said, "Hello, Mr. Rhinoceros. We are Lily and Ben. We came to see you and your friends at the zoo. You are very big and strong and cool. We like you a lot."

The rhinoceros lifted his head and looked at them. He saw their smiling faces and heard their kind words. He felt a little bit of warmth in his heart. He snorted softly and moved closer to them.

"Hello, Lily and Ben. I am Rocco. Thank you for talking to me and liking me. You are very sweet and brave and nice. I like you too."

Lily and Ben giggled. They reached out their hands and touched his rough skin gently. He lowered his horn and let them stroke it. He felt a little bit of joy in his soul.

Mom smiled and took a picture of them. She was proud of her children and happy for the rhinoceros. She said, "See, you made him happy. You are very good and kind and smart. I love you very much."

Lily and Ben hugged their mom and said, "We love you too, mom. And we love Rocco. He is our new friend."

Rocco nodded and said, "Me too. You are my new friends. You made me less gloomy. Thank you very much."

Once upon a time, there was a handsome prince. He wanted to get married, so he threw a party for all his friends and family. He invited a beautiful princess, and she said yes.

They had a deep love for each other, so they decided to get married. It was a wonderful day with all their friends and family around them. Everyone was so happy.

The prince and the princess walked down the aisle, and they said special words to each other. They were so in love. They threw the bouquet of flowers and the garter, and everyone cheered.

Finally, the prince and princess were married. They hugged and kissed, so all their friends and family cheered again. They lived happily ever after.

Lily and Tom were hungry. They wanted to eat pizza for lunch. Mom said she would make pizza for them. She put cheese and sauce and ham on the bread. She put the pizza in the oven.

"Can we help you, Mom?" Lily and Tom asked.

"Sure, you can help me set the table. But be careful, the plates are breakable," Mom said.

Lily and Tom took two plates from the cupboard. They walked to the table. But Tom was not careful. He ran too fast. He tripped on the rug. He fell down. The plate fell down too. It broke into pieces.

"Oh no, Tom! Are you okay?" Lily asked.

"I'm okay, but the plate is broken. Mom will be mad at us," Tom said.

Mom heard the noise. She came to the table. She saw Tom and Lily and the broken plate.

"What happened here?" Mom asked.

"I'm sorry, Mom. I fell down and broke the plate. I was not careful," Tom said.

Mom hugged Tom. She was not mad. She was glad that Tom was not hurt.

"It's okay, Tom. Accidents happen. I'm happy that you are honest and sorry. But next time, you have to be more careful. Broken plates can hurt you and make a mess," Mom said.

"I will, Mom. I'm sorry," Tom said.

Mom smiled. She took another plate from the cupboard. She gave it to Lily. She took the pizza out of the oven. It smelled good. She cut it into slices. She put it on the plates.

"Here you go, kids. Enjoy your pizza. And remember, be careful and honest," Mom said.

Lily and Tom thanked Mom. They ate their pizza. It was yummy. They learned their lesson. They were careful and honest. They were happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She lived in a small town with her mommy and daddy. One day, Lily and her mommy went to the park to play. It was a messy day because it rained a lot.

Lily saw her friend Tommy at the park. "Hi Tommy!" said Lily. "Do you want to play with me?"

Tommy nodded his head and said, "Yes, I do!"

Lily and Tommy played on the swings and the slide. They had so much fun together. After they finished playing, Lily's mommy said, "It's time to go home now."

Lily said goodbye to Tommy and they both nodded their heads. They walked home and talked about their fun day at the park. When they got home, Lily's mommy gave her a bath to wash away the mess from the rainy day. Lily was tired and went to bed with a smile on her face, dreaming about her next playdate with Tommy.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to explore the world and look at maps. She had a map of the whole world in her room and she would admire it every day.

One day, Lily went on an adventure to find a treasure. She followed the map and found a big cave. Inside the cave, she saw a shiny treasure chest. She was so excited and opened it quickly. But when she looked inside, she saw that the treasure was fake! She felt sad and disappointed.

But then, Lily remembered something her mom had told her. Sometimes, things are not what they seem. She looked closer at the fake treasure and saw that it was actually a puzzle. She put the puzzle together and it revealed a secret message. The message led her to a real treasure! Lily was so happy and proud of herself for not giving up.

David was a happy boy. He was very excited when he got to go to his friend's house to play. His friend had a big cupboard in his bedroom. David started to hide inside it. He thought the cupboard was a good place to hide but his friend wouldn't found him. Suddenly the door shut! David was stuck inside! He started to panic but he was determined to escape. He pushed and pushed and eventually the door opened! He crawled out of the cupboard and ran to find his friend. He was relieved to be free and he was so happy to see his friend again.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim loved to play with his toy train on the track. One day, he wanted to make his train go faster. So, he thought of a plan.

Tim went to the kitchen and found spicy sauce. He put the sauce on the track, thinking it would make the train go fast. He said to his train, "Now you will be super fast!" But when the train went over the sauce, it got stuck!

Tim's sister, Sue, came into the room and saw the spicy mess. She said, "Oh no, Tim! The sauce made the train stop, not go fast!" Tim realized that the spicy sauce was not a good idea. Together, they cleaned the track and put the train back on. Tim learned that sometimes, his ideas might not work, but trying new things is always fun.

Once upon a time there was a little girl who loved to play. She especially loved to play with her plastic toys and dolls. One day, she was having so much fun playing with her doll when it accidentally fell out of her hand and onto the ground. It made a loud noise which hurt her ears and she started to cry.

Just then, her mummy came into the room and heard the noise. She quickly ran to her daughter, hugged her and asked what had happened. The little girl told her about the toy falling and her mummy gave her a big kiss on her forehead.

"No worries, sweetheart" said mummy, "I'll get another toy for you". She went to the living room and called her dad. She asked him to bring some new plastic toys from the shop.

The next day, daddy arrived home with many colorful plastic toys for the little girl. She was so happy and quickly started to play with them. And from that day onwards, she made sure to be extra careful with her toys so it wouldn't hurt her ears again.

Once upon a time, there was a clumsy little bear. He had lots of fun trying all sorts of things. One day, he saw a bee fly near a pretty flower. The bee wanted to gather the sweet honey, so it urged the bear to help it. The little bear hesitated; he was afraid he'd ruin the flower. But the bee kept urging him and finally the bear got up the courage to help.

The bear carefully touched the flower and it was still ok. Then, the bee thanked the bear and showed him what it looked like inside the flower. The bear felt really happy to have had fun while helping out the bee.

The moral of this story is that some things may be a bit tricky to do, but with help and patience, something good can come out of it.

Once upon a time there was a little boy called Joe. Joe was very creative and was always thinking of new ideas. Joe decided to make a house. He started to hammer nails into the wall and was getting excited as he built his house.

Joe's brother Benny was watching Joe and he was very jealous. He wanted to make a house too but he couldn't help but feel frustrated about not having the same toys and tools as Joe.

Benny said to Joe "Why do you get to build a house? That's not fair!" Joe stopped hammering and looked at Benny. He wanted Benny to be happy so he said "You can build a house too!"

Benny was so excited he started to yell with joy. Joe smiled and handed some tools to Benny. Together, they both built beautiful houses.

This story teaches us that when we share with others, everyone can be creative and have fun.

Once upon a time there was an enormous mountain. It was the highest mountain in the world and it was very special. On the peak of the mountain lived two friends called Jack and Jill.

One day, Jack said to Jill "What shall we do today?" Jill replied "Let's go on a walk around the mountain!"

So Jack and Jill set off on a walk. They explored the different paths and enjoyed the bright weather. They stopped to pick some delicious berries and looked out at the beautiful landscape.

Suddenly, a huge gust of wind pushed them both away! They realised that the enormous mountain included some very strong wind.

Jack and Jill clung to each other as they flew into the distance. They screamed with delight as they enjoyed the ride!

Eventually the wind stopped and they landed safely in a different place. They looked up at the enormous mountain and smiled. They knew they would never forget their magical adventure.

Once upon a time, a little girl had a puppy. The puppy was very cute and fluffy. One day, the little girl and her puppy went for a walk in the park. They saw a man sitting on a bench. The man looked sad and he sighed.

The little girl asked, "Why are you sad?" The man replied, "I lost my puppy. I don't know where he went." The little girl felt sorry for the man and said, "Don't worry. We will help you find your puppy."

So, they searched for the man's puppy. They looked everywhere, but the puppy was unknown. The little girl didn't give up and she kept looking. Finally, they found the puppy hiding behind a tree. The man was very happy and he thanked the little girl and her puppy. They all went home with big smiles on their faces.

Once upon a time there was a wise rabbit.He lived on a hill and liked all sorts of yummy food.

One day he wanted to try a radish. He hopped up to the garden to find one. He found the biggest, brightest radish and he hopped back home with it.

He took a big bite and tasted it. He liked the taste of the radish. It was sweet and crunchy! He ate it all up and smiled.

The wise rabbit thought to himself 'I am glad I tried this radish! It was so delicious!' He hopped away happy and full. The End.

Once upon a time, a little girl lived in a big house. One day it was her birthday and her mummy and daddy had a surprise for her! They brought out a big box - inside was a beautiful red cushion! The little girl was so excited she jumped up and down.

She quickly ran to get her toys, ready to act out stories on the cushion. She opened her dolly's house, got all the dolls out and then put them around the cushion. She made up lots of stories that her dolls could 'act' out on the cushion.

Every day the little girl would find different toys and act out stories on the cushion. She acted out stories with fire engines and dragons, with little animals and even with her teddies! She had so much fun and the red cushion was the centre of her imagination.

The little girl would take the red cushion with her everywhere she went - it was such a beautiful and comfy cushion! Even when she was all grown up and moved away, she would take the cushion with her and act out stories. She was never too old for a red cushion with special magical powers!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to eat peaches because they were so soft and sweet. One day, her mom gave her a basket of peaches and told her to share them with her friends.

Lily went to her friends' house and offered them the peaches, but they didn't believe that they were as soft and sweet as she said. So, Lily took a peach and showed them how soft it was by squeezing it gently. Her friends were amazed and believed her.

The moral of the story is that sometimes we need to show others what we believe in for them to understand. Just like how Lily showed her friends how soft the peach was, we need to demonstrate our beliefs to others.

Once upon a time, there was a boy who had a special hat. He always had a big smile when he wore it. One day, the hat started to itch and started to disappear. The boy was sad, he thought he had lost it forever.

He asked his mom if she could help him find his hat. His mom said she would try her best. She went everywhere looking for it but sadly she came back empty handed.

The boy remembered his grandpa. He was always very reliable when he needed help. So grandpa went out and searched everywhere he could think of until he found it! The boy was overjoyed to have his hat back. From then on, the boy was always sure to be extra careful with his hat, so it wouldn’t disappear again.

Once upon a time, there was a family. The family had a big house with a garden. The family loved to play in the garden and have picnics together.

One day, the family decided to have a big party. They invited all their friends and family to come and celebrate. The family wanted to make the party special, so they decided to make an original cake.

The family worked hard all day to make the cake. They used special ingredients and decorated it with colorful frosting. When the guests arrived, they were amazed by the original cake. They all had a great time at the party and everyone loved the cake.

Years later, when the family looked back on that day, they remembered how much fun they had and how special the original cake was. They were happy to have such a loving family and to have made such great memories together.

Once upon a time, there was a ranch full of animals. It was a big ranch, with lots of grass, trees and mud. One day, a big truck arrived. It parked in front of the ranch. Out stepped a family, looking around like they had never seen a ranch before.

The family was ignorant of the ranch. They didn't know how to take care of the animals, and they didn't know how to tend to the land.

Luckily, the ranch's owner was patient. He showed the family how to look after their new home. He helped them learn how to feed the animals, clean the mud and take care of the grass and trees.

Pretty soon, the family was no longer ignorant. They could care for the ranch by themselves. And they all lived happily ever after!

Jimmy was getting ready for bed. He brushed his teeth at the sink and said goodnight to Mom and Dad. He was about to go to bed when he heard a voice near the sink. He was very surprised!

He crept closer and saw a tiny fairy. She was asking for help. Jimmy was worried, but he wanted to be helpful.

The fairy said she was looking for her wand. Jimmy looked around and soon found it behind the sink. He answered the fairy and said, "I found it!"

The fairy thanked Jimmy and said, "You're so helpful! I'll grant you one wish." Jimmy thought for a moment and said, "I wish for a puppy!"

The fairy smiled and waved her wand. Suddenly, a puppy appeared! Jimmy was so excited. The fairy said goodbye and flew away.

Jimmy said thanks before snuggling up with his new puppy. He quickly fell asleep, dreaming of all the adventures they would have.

One day, Jack saw something special in the sky. It included a big, white dove. It was flying in circles and it looked so smooth. Jack liked the dove so much and decided he wanted to be like it. He jumped up and tried his best to flap his arms like wings. But he just couldn't fly.

The dove watched Jack with interest as he jumped and flapped his arms. Suddenly, it flew down to the ground in front of Jack and they both laughed together! Jack gave the dove a friendly pat and it flew away.

From then on, Jack and the dove were special friends. Whenever the dove arrived, Jack waved and said a great big hello. It was a smooth friendship and they both enjoyed spending time together.

The end.

Once upon a time there was a young girl called Jane. Jane was an adventurous girl and she was always looking for something new to explore. One day, Jane decided to go for a walk and find something exciting.

On her walk, Jane came across an orange opera house. She was amazed by it and couldn't wait to get inside! Jane found a way in through a side door and started exploring.

As Jane wandered around, she heard a loud noise coming from a nearby room. She opened the door to find a big man with a deep voice. He was very angry and said to Jane, "You shouldn't be here!"

Jane did not know what to do and felt very scared. She tried to explain that she was just exploring and wanted to find out more about the opera house, but the man did not listen. He grabbed Jane, threw her out and locked the door.

Jane was very upset and ran home crying. Even though she had found something interesting, in the end it had not been worth it as she had been thrown out.

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play hide and seek with his friends. One day, Timmy found a hidden exit in the park. He thought it would be fun to hide there and surprise his friends.

Timmy's friends looked and looked for him, but they couldn't find him anywhere. They were worried and asked the grown-ups to help them look. But nobody could find Timmy.

Days went by and still no sign of Timmy. Everyone was very sad. Then, one day, they found the hidden exit where Timmy had gone to hide. But it was too late. Timmy had gone away and nobody could bring him back.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl and a big elephant. The little girl was so excited to meet the elephant, but she was a bit scared too. She had heard that they could be really strong, so she didn't want to get too close.

The elephant saw the little girl and smiled. He was gentle and friendly. He reached out with his trunk and touched her arm. It tickled!

The elephant took out a test and asked the girl if she wanted to have a game. It looked like a lot of fun! She said yes, so the elephant showed her how to play. She was very good at it and they played together for a long time.

At the end of the game, the elephant gave the girl a tasty treat. She smiled and thanked him. The elephant was so kind and happy. He gave her a hug and then released her. The little girl waved goodbye as she skipped away.

Once upon a time, there was a little goat. The goat liked to play in the grass. One day, the goat saw a big rock. The goat thought the rock was harmless. But the goat did not know that the rock was very slippery.

The next day, the goat went to play near the big rock again. The sun was shining, and the grass was wet. The goat tried to jump on the rock. But the rock was too slippery, and the goat slipped.

The goat was sad and scared. It did not want to slip again. So, the goat asked its friends for help. The friends told the goat to be careful near the big rock. The goat listened to its friends and never slipped on the rock again. The goat was happy and safe.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Amy. She was three and loved to travel. One day, she packed her bag and was ready to go. Her parents said goodbye, then she set off.

Amy travelled on and on until she arrived at a special place, with loads of people and lots of noise. She could see bright lights and she could hear bangs in the sky. She had arrived at a firework show!

Amy watched the show, spellbound. Fireworks of all colours whizzed through the sky, and she smiled and laughed. After the last firework, she said goodbye to the show, then she began her journey home.

When she got back, Amy's parents were so happy. She had a great time and was all ready for bed. Goodnight Amy!

Once upon a time, in a fine little town, there lived a girl named Amy. Amy liked to play with her friends and have fun. One day, they decided to build a big tower with their toy blocks. They all worked together to make the tower very tall.

As they were about to finish the tower, a little dog came running into the room. The dog was so happy to see Amy and her friends, that he wagged his tail and knocked the tower down. The blocks went everywhere, and the tower was gone.

Amy and her friends were sad at first, but then they decided to build the tower again. This time, they made it even taller and stronger. When they finished, they were very proud of their fine tower. The little dog sat and watched, making sure not to knock it down again. In the end, everyone in the town was happy and had a great time.

Anna and Ben were playing in the garden. They liked to dig in the dirt and look for bugs. They had a jar with some ants and worms inside.

"Look, Ben, I found a big beetle!" Anna said, holding up a shiny black bug.

"Wow, let me see!" Ben said, reaching for the beetle.

But as he touched it, the beetle opened its wings and flew away. Anna and Ben screamed and ran away from the beetle.

They bumped into a rock and fell down. They looked up and saw something on the rock. It was a lizard. It had green scales and a long tail. It stared at them with its small black eyes.

"Ah, a lizard!" Anna said, panicking. She did not like lizards. She thought they were disgusting and scary.

"Shh, don't move. Maybe it will go away," Ben said, trying to be brave.

But the lizard did not go away. It opened its mouth and showed its sharp teeth. It hissed and flicked its tongue.

"Help, help!" Anna and Ben shouted, crying. They wanted their mom and dad to come and save them from the lizard.

They heard footsteps and saw their mom and dad running towards them. They picked them up and hugged them.

"What's wrong, sweeties? What scared you?" their mom asked, worried.

"The lizard, the lizard!" Anna and Ben said, pointing at the rock.

Their mom and dad looked at the rock and laughed. They saw the lizard, but it was not a real lizard. It was a toy lizard. Someone had left it on the rock as a joke.

"It's okay, it's not a real lizard. It's just a toy. See?" their dad said, picking up the toy lizard and showing it to them.

Anna and Ben looked at the toy lizard and felt silly. They realized they had been afraid of nothing. They laughed too and hugged their mom and dad.

"Sorry, we were silly. We thought it was a real lizard," Anna said.

"It's okay, we all get scared sometimes. But you don't have to be afraid of lizards. They are not disgusting. They are just animals. They won't hurt you if you leave them alone," their mom said.

"Really? Can we see a real lizard?" Ben asked, curious.

"Sure, maybe we can find one in the garden. But don't touch them, just look at them. They are very interesting and beautiful," their dad said.

"Okay, let's go find a real lizard!" Anna and Ben said, excited.

They put the toy lizard back on the rock and went with their mom and dad to look for a real lizard in the garden. They learned that lizards were not so bad after all. They had fun and forgot about the beetle.

Once upon a time, there was a little rabbit called Fuzzy. Fuzzy loved hopping around and feeling the light sun on his ears.

One day, Fuzzy woke up and it was raining outside. "Oh no!" Fuzzy said, "I wanted to hop and enjoy the weather today". He was so disappointed that the weather was not light.

Suddenly, Fuzzy heard a voice say: "Never fear Fuzzy, the sun is here". Fuzzy looked up and saw a big bright rainbow above him. "I can hop in the sun now", Fuzzy said happily, and he began to hop around in the light weather.

He hopped around all day, and soon the sun was setting and it was time to go to sleep. Fuzzy was so happy that he experienced the light weather and he said, "I love to hop in the sun".

Once upon a time, there were two friends, Jack and Lucy. They were both very happy and liked to play together. One day, Jack said to Lucy, "I want to marry you." Lucy was very happy and said yes.

They both ran off to the nearest fire. Jack put his hands in the fire and said, "We are now married!" Everyone was very happy and cheered.

But there was one person who was not happy. His name was Bob and he was very envious of Jack and Lucy's love. He wished he could be married too but he just didn't have anyone to marry.

So Jack and Lucy had a special surprise for Bob. Without telling him, they had made plans to have a special wedding ceremony just for him! Bob was so happy when he saw it and thanked Jack and Lucy for their kindness.

From then on, Jack, Lucy and Bob were all like one big family and always had each other's backs. They were all very happy and never stopped smiling.

Lily was very happy today. She was going to see her uncle Tom. Uncle Tom was very nice and funny. He always brought her a gift when he visited. Lily wondered what it would be this time.

She ran to the door when she heard the bell. She opened it and saw uncle Tom smiling. He had a big bag in his hand.
