"Hello, Lily! How are you?" he said.

"Hello, uncle Tom! I'm good. What do you have for me?" she asked.

Uncle Tom knelt down and opened the bag. He took out a big, fluffy teddy bear. It had brown fur and a red bow.

"This is for you, Lily. I hope you like it. It's very soft and cuddly," he said.

Lily's eyes widened. She loved teddy bears. She reached out and hugged the bear.

"Thank you, uncle Tom! I love it. It's the best gift ever," she said.

She accepted the bear and gave uncle Tom a kiss on the cheek. He hugged her back and laughed.

"You're very welcome, Lily. I'm glad you're happy. Do you want to play with the bear?" he asked.

"Yes, please. Let's go to my room. I have more toys there," she said.

She took uncle Tom's hand and led him to her room. She was very alert and excited. She wanted to show him all her toys and stories. She knew they would have a lot of fun. She was very lucky to have uncle Tom. He was her favorite uncle.

Once upon a time, a little girl named Lily went to the park to play. She saw her friends playing in a circle and ran towards them. They were playing a game called "Duck, Duck, Goose". Lily was excited to join in and play with her friends.

But when it was her turn to be the goose, she accidentally tripped and fell. Everyone laughed and Lily felt embarrassed. She wanted to go home and cried, "I am embarrassed!" Her friends felt bad and said, "Don't be embarrassed, Lily. We all fall sometimes."

Lily felt better and decided to keep playing. She joined the circle again and this time, she was careful not to fall. She even became the goose and tagged her friends. They all cheered and Lily felt happy. From that day on, Lily learned that it's okay to make mistakes and feel embarrassed sometimes.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside and explore the world around her. One day, while she was walking in the park, she saw a big sign that said "Stop". She knew that it meant she should pause and wait before crossing the street.

Lily was very persistent in following the sign's instructions. She waited patiently until the cars stopped and the pedestrian light turned green. Then, she crossed the street safely and continued her adventure in the park.

As she played, Lily noticed a butterfly flying around her. She tried to catch it, but it was too fast. So, she decided to pause and watch it fly away. She was amazed by its beautiful colors and how gracefully it moved. Lily realized that sometimes, it's important to pause and appreciate the little things in life.

Tom and Jen are friends. They like to play with blocks and cars. One day, they have a big fight. Tom wants to build a tower with all the blocks. Jen wants to share the blocks and make a bridge. Tom says, "No, they are mine! Go away!" Jen says, "That is not nice! You are mean!" They push and pull the blocks and make a mess.

Mom sees them and is sad. She says, "Why are you fighting? You are friends. You should help each other and have fun. Fighting is bad. It makes you and others unhappy. Do you want to be unhappy?" Tom and Jen shake their heads. They do not want to be unhappy. They want to be happy.

Mom says, "Then you should say sorry and share. Sharing is good. It makes you and others happy. Do you want to be happy?" Tom and Jen nod. They want to be happy. They say sorry and hug. They share the blocks and make a tower and a bridge. They play together and have fun.

Mom smiles and says, "Good job! You are good friends. You succeed in life when you are kind and generous. Kindness and generosity make you and others happy. Happiness is the best thing in life. Do you agree?" Tom and Jen agree. They are happy. They thank Mom and continue to play.

The moral value of the story is: Sharing is good. Kindness and generosity make you and others happy. Happiness is the best thing in life.

Once upon a time, there was a little dog named Spot. Spot loved to go for walks with his owner, Timmy. Timmy always put Spot on a leash so he wouldn't run away.

One day, Timmy said to Spot, "Let's go for a drive in the car!" Spot was so excited, he wagged his tail and barked happily.

Timmy put Spot in the back seat and they drove to a pretty park. Spot was so happy to be out of the car and running around in the grass.

After playing for a while, Timmy said, "It's time to go home, Spot." Spot was sad to leave the park, but he knew he would be back soon. Timmy put Spot back in the car and drove home.

When they got home, Timmy took off Spot's leash and gave him a big hug. Spot was so happy to be home and he knew he had the best owner in the world.

Anna and Ben like to play with their toy cars. They have a big rug with roads and buildings on it. They make sounds like vroom and beep as they drive their cars around. Sometimes they have races or pretend to go to the shop or the park.

One day, Anna and Ben have a problem. They both want to play with the same car. It is a red car with a shiny sticker on it. They think it is the coolest car ever. They both reach for it at the same time and pull on it.

"Let go, it's mine!" Anna says.

"No, it's mine!" Ben says.

They tug and tug until the car breaks in half. They both gasp and drop the pieces. They feel sad and angry.

"Look what you did!" Anna says.

"You did it!" Ben says.

They start to cry and yell at each other. Their mom hears them and comes to see what is wrong. She sees the broken car and the upset children.

"What happened here?" she asks.

They both point at each other and say, "He/she did it!"

Mom sighs and picks up the pieces of the car. She looks at them and says, "I think I can fix this. But first, you two need to calm down and say sorry to each other. How about you do some exercise to get rid of your bad feelings?"

Anna and Ben nod. They don't like to fight. Mom shows them how to do some jumping jacks, some squats, and some stretches. They follow her and start to feel better. They breathe deeply and smile.

"Are you ready to say sorry now?" Mom asks.

Anna and Ben look at each other and say, "Sorry."

They hug and say, "I love you."

Mom smiles and says, "I love you too. And I have good news. I fixed your car. See, it can still drive and reverse. And the sticker is still cool. But you have to share it and be gentle with it, okay?"

Anna and Ben nod and say, "Okay."

They take the car and thank Mom. They go back to their rug and play nicely. They take turns driving and reversing the car. They make sounds like vroom and beep. They are happy again.

Once upon a time there was a bear. He was very sad. He wanted to be happy. But he didn't know what he needed to do.

He walked for a long time until he saw a line. It was a long line. Everyone was waiting in it. He wanted to know why they were waiting.

He asked a man why they were in the line. The man said they were waiting to get what they need. So the bear joined the line.

The line took the bear a long time to get to the end. But when he got there he found what he needed. It was not hard to get. It was easy.

So the bear was happy. He got what he needed and he felt better.

Tim and Liz are playing pirates in the backyard. They have a big box that is their ship and a stick that is their sword. They also have a hook that Tim's dad made for them from a coat hanger and some tape. It is a fake hook, but they pretend it is real.

"Arrr, matey, I am the captain of this ship!" Tim says, putting the hook on his hand. "You are my first mate, Liz. We are looking for treasure!"

"Okay, captain, where is the treasure?" Liz asks, holding the stick.

Tim looks at the map he drew on a piece of paper. It has a big X on it. "The treasure is in the sandbox, of course! Come on, let's go!"

They jump out of the box and run to the sandbox. They dig with their hands and their stick, looking for shiny things. They find some coins, a necklace, and a ring that belong to Tim's mom. They are very happy.

"Wow, look at all this treasure!" Liz says, putting the necklace around her neck. "We are rich, captain!"

"Yes, we are, first mate!" Tim says, putting the ring on his finger. "But we have to be careful. There might be other pirates who want to take our treasure!"

Just then, they hear a loud bark. It is Tim's dog, Rex, who has come to see what they are doing. Rex sees the hook on Tim's hand and thinks it is a toy. He jumps on Tim and tries to grab the hook.

"Hey, stop it, Rex!" Tim shouts, trying to push him away. "This is not a toy, this is my hook!"

"Rex, no!" Liz says, helping Tim. "Bad dog, bad dog!"

Rex does not listen. He pulls the hook with his teeth and runs away with it. Tim and Liz chase him, but he is too fast. He runs into the house with the hook.

"Oh no, he took my hook!" Tim cries. "What are we going to do?"

"Maybe we can order a new one?" Liz suggests. "Or we can ask your dad to make another one?"

Tim thinks for a moment. He is sad, but he still has his treasure. And he still has his friend.

"Okay, let's do that," he says. "But first, let's hide our treasure. We don't want Rex to take that too!"

They put their treasure in the box and cover it with a blanket. Then they go inside to find Rex and the hook. They hope they can get it back. They still want to play pirates.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved to wear her pink cap everywhere she went. One day, Lily's mom took her to a store to buy a new cap because her old one was too small. Lily saw a beautiful red cap with a shiny gold star on it that she really wanted, but it was too expensive.

Lily's mom said they couldn't buy the expensive cap, so they left the store with a plain blue one instead. Lily was sad and didn't want to wear her new cap. Later that day, Lily and her mom went to the park where they saw a boy crying because he lost his red cap with a shiny gold star on it.

Lily's mom asked the boy if he had seen another red cap with a shiny gold star on it, and the boy replied that he hadn't. But then, Lily took off her blue cap and gave it to the boy. The boy was happy and thanked Lily for her kindness. Lily felt happy too, knowing she had helped someone in need.

Once upon a time, there was a dog named Max. Max loved to stand in the sun and feel the warm rays on his fur. One day, Max's owner gave him a treat. It was a bone that Max loved to chew. Max was so happy and he felt fine.

Max went outside to play with his friends. They ran and played together, but Max wanted to show off his new treat. He stood up on his hind legs and held the bone in his mouth. His friends were impressed and wanted to play with Max's bone. Max was happy to share his treat and they all had a fine time together.

Ella was a happy three-year-old. She loved to play in the park, go to the beach and pretend to be a princess. One day, Ella's parents took her to the university. She stood by the big entrance, amazed and full of curiosity.

Everywhere she looked, she saw bigger people walking around. She noticed big statues, trees and lots of buildings. Ella's parents took her on a tour around the university. They showed her the classrooms, the library and the gym.

Ella was very excited. She saw people from different countries who were talking and smiling. Ella felt very happy to be there. She said goodbye to the university and promised to return soon.

Ella's parents were proud of her for being so brave and adventurous. They were sure that one day she would stand in the same place but as a student.

Once upon a time there was a clumsy crab. The crab was in a rush because he wanted to get to the beach by lunchtime. He tried going faster but added too much speed and ended up bumping into things. He was so clumsy that he fell over several times.

The crab was determined to make it to the beach in time. He knew if he added more speed he could get there faster, but he didn't want to be clumsy again. He decided to take it slow and moved at a careful pace.

Finally, the crab made it to the beach and was so happy. He had managed to add just the right amount of speed to not be clumsy and to make it to the beach on time.

Once upon a time, there was a lonely guard. His job was to add things. He would add lots of different things together, like special stones and coins.

One day the guard was feeling lonely. He was tired of always adding things and wanted a friend. So he went walking around, looking for a new friend.

He walked for a long time until he came to a big hill. He started to go up the hill and slowly he saw a person walking down. He waved to the person and they waved back. It was a nice surprise!

The guard smiled and he went down the hill with his new friend. The guard was happy to have a new friend so he added his new friend to his list of best friends. Now he was even happier because he didn't have to feel so lonely anymore.

The guard and his new friend had lots of fun together! They added rocks and sticks on the hill to make a special game. They would add up the numbers on their fingers and try to guess the answers. It was so much fun!

The guard and his new friend spent many days together, adding rocks and coins, and playing lots of games. From that day on, the guard was not so lonely anymore. He had a friend he could add things with and he was happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who had the most wonderful dream. She dreamed she was a rocket flying through the sky! She flew so high, she could see the entire world. The sun was so bright and the sky was pale blue and clear.

The rocket was so strong! It flew so fast that the wind blew her hair back and she laughed and smiled. She flew through the clouds and then around the moon. The stars twinkled and the planets shone in the night sky.

It felt so nice to be back on the ground. She looked up one last time and waved goodbye to the sky and said, "I will come back soon, I dream of flying through the sky again!"

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy had an ancient toy car that he loved to play with. One day, Timmy's dad told him that they needed to sell some old things to make room in the house. Timmy was sad because he didn't want to sell his toy car.

But then, Timmy had an idea. He decided to sell his dad's old thumbtacks instead. His dad was happy because he didn't need them anymore and Timmy was happy because he got to keep his toy car.

From then on, Timmy learned that it's okay to sell things you don't need anymore, but it's important to keep the things you love. And his toy car was definitely something he loved!

Tom and Lily were going to the park with Mom. They had a big bag with snacks and toys. Mom said they could unpack the bag when they found a nice spot.

They walked and walked until they saw a big tree with a swing. "Can we play here, Mom?" Tom asked. Mom nodded and smiled. She put the bag under the tree and helped Tom and Lily on the swing.

They had fun swinging high and low, laughing and singing. Then they saw a chubby squirrel on the tree. It had a big nut in its mouth. It looked at them with curious eyes.

"Hello, squirrel!" Lily said. "Do you want to play with us?"

The squirrel twitched its nose and tail. It ran up and down the tree, then jumped to another one. It was too shy to play with them.

"Maybe it wants some snacks," Tom said. He got off the swing and ran to the bag. He started to unpack it. He found some crackers, some cheese, and some grapes.

He took a cracker and broke it in half. He put one half on the ground and held the other half in his hand. He called the squirrel softly.

"Come here, squirrel. I have something for you. It's yummy and crunchy. Don't be afraid."

The squirrel watched him from a branch. It smelled the cracker. It was hungry and curious. It slowly came down the tree and approached the cracker. It sniffed it and took a bite. It liked it. It took another bite and then ran back to the tree with the rest of the cracker.

"Good job, Tom!" Mom said. "You made a new friend."

Tom smiled and unpacked more snacks. He shared them with Lily and Mom. They also gave some to the squirrel, who came back for more. They had a picnic under the tree and enjoyed the sunny day. They were happy.

Once upon a time, there was a black bow. It was so shiny and all alone. One day, the bow decided to bloom. Out of the ground, many colorful petals grew. The bow had become a flower!

The flower was so happy. Its petals were so soft and pretty. All the animals came out to look. The birds flew around, singing a beautiful song. The flower was so pleased with its new look.

But then one day, the flower got a surprise. It was a big, black bow. The bow wrapped around the flower and made it look even prettier! The flower couldn't believe it. It felt like it had a special hug.

And that's how the black bow and the flower bloomed together. From then on, they were always best friends.

Once upon a time there was a little red mouse. It lived in a big attic all by itself. One day as it was running around, it started to sneeze.

The mouse stopped and said, “Ah-choo! What was that?”

It looked up and saw a big red box with a special key inside.

The mouse grabbed the key and said, “I wonder what this opens!”

The mouse put the key in the lock, and sure enough, it opened the box. Inside the box was a big red surprise!

The mouse squeaked in delight! It had found a big red hat just its size. It put on the hat and said, “Now I look different!”

With a content smile on its face, the little red mouse ran out of its attic and never had to sneeze again.

Mommy and little Tommy went to a store. Tommy saw a beautiful blouse and wanted it.

Mommy: "That blouse doesn't look fit, Tommy."

But Tommy wanted the blouse more than anything. He saw the beautiful pink color and it sparkled in the light.

Mommy: "Take it off the rack, Tommy. Let me see if it fits." Mommy tried to fit the blouse onto Tommy. It was too big!

Tommy: "Mommmyyyy, pleeease!"

Mommy sighed and said: "No, Tommy. We need to find one that fits better."

But Tommy was sad. He wanted the pretty pink blouse.

Mommy: "Let's try another store, Tommy. We can find one that fits you."

They searched and searched, until finally, they found one! It was the same pretty pink blouse, but it fit Tommy perfectly!

Tommy smiled and Mommy said: "See, Tommy! Now it looks fit!"

And they both went home happy.

Once there was a little girl called Ellie. She was always very independent. She wanted to do everything by herself.

One day she went to the park with her mom. They stood watching the birds in the trees. Ellie was excited and she wanted to look closer.

Her mom tried to explain that she should not go too close. But Ellie insisted and tried to walk towards the birds. Her mom told her to stay on the grass so she wouldn't get hurt.

But Ellie was determined. She wanted to stand near the birds and prove she could do it by herself.

Eventually her mom agreed and let her stand at a cool spot near the birds. Ellie was so proud of herself! She smiled at Mom and they watched the birds until it was time to go home.

Ben was a furry dog who liked to drive. He had a red car that he drove around the park. He liked to honk his horn and wave at the other animals. But some animals did not like Ben's driving. They thought he was too loud and too fast.

One day, Ben saw a big hill in the park. He wanted to drive up the hill and see what was on the other side. He drove very fast and tried to climb the hill. But the hill was too steep and his car slid back down. Ben tried again and again, but he could not reach the top. He was sad and angry.

Then he saw a bird flying over the hill. The bird was blue and had a long tail. The bird saw Ben and his car and flew down to him. The bird said, "Hello, furry driver. Why are you trying to drive up the hill?"

Ben said, "I want to see what is on the other side. But the hill is too hard. I can't do it."

The bird said, "Maybe you can't do it alone. But you can do it with a friend. I can help you. I can fly over the hill and tell you what is there. Then you can decide if you want to go or not."

Ben liked the bird's idea. He said, "Thank you, bird. You are very kind. Can you be my friend?"

The bird said, "Of course, furry driver. I can be your friend. Friends help each other. Come on, let's go."

The bird flew over the hill and came back. He told Ben what he saw. He said, "There is a lake on the other side. The lake is blue and shiny. There are fish and frogs and ducks in the lake. There is a bridge over the lake. You can drive over the bridge and see the lake."

Ben was happy. He said, "That sounds wonderful. I want to see the lake. Can you show me the way?"

The bird said, "Sure, furry driver. Follow me. I will fly ahead and guide you. But you have to be careful. The hill is still steep and the bridge is narrow. You have to drive slowly and safely."

Ben said, "OK, bird. I will listen to you. You are a good friend."

Ben followed the bird and drove up the hill. He drove slowly and safely. He reached the top and saw the lake. It was beautiful. He drove over the bridge and saw the fish and frogs and ducks. He honked his horn and waved at them. They waved back and smiled. Ben was happy. He had a new friend and a new place to explore.

The moral of the story is: Sometimes you need a friend to help you achieve your goals. Friends can offer support, advice, and encouragement. Friends can also show you new things and make you happy. It is good to be friendly and make friends.

Once upon a time there was a brave kid named Jack. He entered a strange new room. In the room was a big thermometer. He wondered what it was and decided to take a closer look.

He cautiously walked towards it and soon he was touching it. He realized it was a special thermometer. The thermometer changed colors and was super fun to play with.

Jack played with the thermometer for hours. Before he knew it, night time had arrived. He said goodbye to the thermometer and went home to bed.

The next morning, Jack couldn't wait to visit the thermometer again. He was so brave to try something new and he was very proud.

Once upon a time, there was a big boat. This boat was in the navy. The boat had many friends. They all worked together.

One day, the boat saw a problem. It wanted to solve the problem. The boat asked its friends for help. But the friends were busy. They had no time. So, the boat asked the available birds for help.

The birds helped the boat. They solved the problem together. The boat was happy. The birds were happy too. They all learned that when we help each other, we can solve problems. And that is the moral value of this story.

One day, a little boy named Tim went to a fun event with his mom. There were lots of games, food, and friends to play with. Tim was very happy.

At the event, Tim saw a small box with unknown things inside. He asked his mom, "What is in the box?" His mom said, "I don't know, Tim. Why don't you search and find out?" Tim was excited to search the box.

He opened the box and found many colorful toys. Tim played with the toys and shared them with his new friends. They all had a great time at the event.

Once upon a time, there was a little daisy. The daisy was sad. It did not like the rain. The rain made the daisy wet.

One day, the sun came out. The daisy was happy. The sun made the daisy warm and dry. The sun and the daisy were friends.

But the rain did not like the sun. The rain and the sun disagree. They both wanted the daisy to be their friend. The daisy wanted to be friends with both the sun and the rain. The sun and the rain became friends too. Now they all play together and the daisy is not sad anymore.

Once upon a time there was a wide bug. He liked to mix things up. So he decided to go on an adventure. He went to many different places and saw lots of interesting things.

At the park he mixed stones and twigs in the sandbox. Then it rained and he mixed the mud with some leaves. He also went to the ocean and mixed sand and water.

The bug had so much fun mixing things. One day he even mixed some food from the kitchen and made a delicious snack.

Mixing things was the bug's favorite thing to do. Everywhere he went he found something new to mix. He even mixed things with his best friends.

He was so happy to be able to mix so many different things. He could mix for hours each day and he never got tired of it!

Once upon a time there lived a little boy. He was only three-years-old and he loved adventures!

Every week, he would go exploring in the dark woods near his home. Late one week, his mom said he couldn’t go because it was getting too dark outside. The little boy asked her why he couldn’t go and she replied, “It’s too dangerous in the dark, my love – we don’t want you to get lost!”

The little boy was sad but he listened to his mom's words and stayed at home. He looked out the window and imagined what the dark woods might be like. Then, the little boy had an idea. He asked his mom if he could go exploring, but during the day!

His mom was very happy that her little boy was so brave. She agreed to let him go and they went exploring together the following week. The little boy felt so brave, and he was so proud that he had gone exploring during the day instead of the dark!

Lily and Tom were twins who liked to play in their big garden. They had many toys and games, but their favorite thing was to dig in the dirt and look for bugs. They thought bugs were very interesting and funny.

One day, they found a big, shiny beetle under a rock. It had green and blue spots on its back and long, thin legs. Lily and Tom were very happy and decided to keep it as a pet. They put it in a glass jar with some leaves and water and gave it a name: Sparky.

They took Sparky to their room and put him on their table. They wanted to show him to their mom and dad later. They felt very lucky to have such a special bug.

But they did not know that their cat, Fluffy, was very nosy. Fluffy liked to explore the house and sniff everything. She saw the jar on the table and jumped on it. She wanted to see what was inside. She pushed the jar with her paw and made it roll off the table. It fell on the floor and broke. Sparky crawled out of the jar and ran away.

Lily and Tom heard the noise and ran to their room. They saw the broken jar and the empty spot where Sparky was. They felt very sad and worried. They looked for Sparky everywhere, but they could not find him.

"Where is Sparky?" Lily asked, crying.

"I don't know. Maybe he went outside." Tom said, sniffing.

They went to their mom and dad and told them what happened. Their mom and dad hugged them and said they were sorry. They said they would help them look for Sparky, but they also said that bugs like to be free and not in jars.

Lily and Tom understood, but they still missed Sparky. They hoped he was happy and safe. They learned that having a bug as a pet was not a luxury, but a responsibility. They also learned that Fluffy was too nosy for her own good. They decided to play with Fluffy more and give her some toys, so she would not bother their things. They also decided to look for more bugs in the garden, but not to keep them, just to watch them and let them go. They thought that was more fun and kind.

The wealthy dad had a daughter and she was invited to a party. When she got there, she saw a lot of people and they were all having fun. The daughter had lots of friends to play with. But then something happened; another child did not like the daughter and they started to fight.

The daughter was sad because her friends were mad at her. Dad was there and he saw what was happening. He put his arm around his daughter and smiled. He asked the other child why they were fighting and the other child said their not friends.

Dad said to both the children, “It’s time to stop fighting and have some fun.” The daughter smiled and then all the children enjoyed the party. Dad was proud that his daughter had accepted the invitation and made new friends. Everyone was happy and the daughter learned that fighting isn't the answer.

Once upon a time there was a brave little girl who lived in an ordinary chamber. She loved to dress up! Every day she would put on a different outfit. She would put on a dress and shoes, a hat and gloves and a necklace too. She always felt so special when she was dressed up!

One day she decided to go for a walk. She put on her fanciest dress and her brightest shoes and set off. In the park, she got lots of compliments from everyone who saw her. She felt like a princess and smiled ear to ear!

When she got back to her chamber, she took off her dress and put on her ordinary clothes. She knew it was important to always feel special, and that's why she liked to dress up.

The end

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved going to the park with her mom and dad. One day, when they were at the park, Lily saw a butterfly. She ran after it, but it flew away.

Lily's mom said, "Don't worry, Lily. Maybe you'll see another butterfly soon."

Lily said, "I hope so. I want to catch it!"

As they were leaving the park, Lily's dad said, "That was a perfect day at the park."

Lily said, "Yes, it was. But I don't want to exit the park. I want to stay here forever!"

Her mom said, "Don't worry, Lily. We'll come back soon. But for now, we have to go home and eat dinner."

Lily said, "Okay, I'll mind leaving the park if we can come back tomorrow!"

Tom and Mia are in school. They sit at their desks and draw with crayons. Tom likes to draw cars and trucks. Mia likes to draw flowers and butterflies.

"Look at my car, Mia!" Tom says. He holds up his paper. "It has big wheels and a loud horn."

Mia does not look at Tom's car. She ignores him. She keeps drawing her flower. She thinks Tom's car is boring.

"Look at my flower, Tom!" Mia says. She holds up her paper. "It has pretty colors and a sweet smell."

Tom does not look at Mia's flower. He ignores her. He keeps drawing his truck. He thinks Mia's flower is silly.

The teacher comes to their desks. She smiles at their drawings. She gives them each a sticker. She says, "Good job, Tom and Mia! You are very creative."

Tom and Mia look at their stickers. They are yummy stickers. They smell like fruits and candies. Tom has a banana sticker. Mia has a strawberry sticker.

"Wow, yummy stickers!" Tom says. He peels off his sticker and puts it on his nose.

"Wow, yummy stickers!" Mia says. She peels off her sticker and puts it on her cheek.

Tom and Mia look at each other. They laugh. They do not ignore each other anymore. They share their stickers and their drawings. They are friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her dolls and teddy bears. One day, Lily went to the park to play with her friends. She saw a boy who had a skull on his shirt. Lily thought it was cool, so she asked him where he got it.

The boy told Lily that his dad gave it to him. Lily felt envious because she wanted a skull shirt too. But then, the boy said he loved Lily's pink dress. Lily felt happy and forgot about the skull shirt. They played together and had fun.

After playing, Lily went home and told her mom about her day at the park. She said she loved playing with her friends and meeting the boy with the skull shirt. Her mom smiled and gave her a big hug.

One day, a little girl named Lily found a furry cat. The cat was soft and nice. Lily wanted to play with the cat. She took the cat to her house.

Lily said to the cat, "Let's play on the stairs!" They went to the stairs. Lily sat down and the cat sat next to her. They started to slide down the stairs together. It was fun and they laughed.

After they had slid down the stairs many times, the cat said, "Thank you, Lily, for playing with me." Lily hugged the furry cat and said, "You are my new friend." They played together every day and were very happy.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Jack who loved to play on the beach. He would build sandcastles and collect shells. One day, he saw a big wave coming towards him. The wave was so high that it scared Jack. He ran away from the water and waited for the tide to go back.

As Jack was waiting, he saw a little girl crying. She had lost her favorite toy in the water. Jack felt sad for her and wanted to help. He went back to the water and searched for the toy. After a while, he found it and gave it to the little girl. She was so happy to receive her toy back.

But then, Jack realized that the water had come back up and his sandcastle was gone. He felt sad and angry. He didn't know what to do. But then, he remembered that he helped the little girl and that made him feel better. He realized that sometimes you have to give up something to help someone else.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Jane who loved to dress up fancy. One day, Jane's mom told her she was going to get a special treat. She was going to be served some ice cream! Jane was very excited, and she decided to put on her fanciest sunglasses.

Upon arrival to the ice-cream parlour, Jane was really impressed. There were lots of different flavors of ice cream, and she couldn't decide what to pick. She asked her mom, "Which one should I serve?"

"You can pick whichever flavor you like!" said her mom.

So, after much deliberation, Jane chose the chocolate ice cream. She was delighted when it arrived in front of her. She couldn't wait to take a bite. Jane said to her mom, "It looks fabulous in my fancy sunglasses!"

And that was the end of Jane's exciting ice cream adventure!

Once upon a time, there was a little boy called John. John was three years old and he really loved to skip. Every day, he would skip around the garden with his friends.

One day, John's dad asked him for help. He wanted John to go and talk to the mechanic about his car. John was a bit troubled, but he agreed to help his dad. The mechanic looked at the car and said he could fix it.

John listened carefully while the mechanic talked and later he skipped happily back home. He couldn't wait to tell his dad the news. When John got home, his dad was sad. He said the mechanic had fixed the car, but it cost too much money. He didn't have enough money to pay the mechanic's bill.

John was very sad and troubled. He sat in the garden and watched as his dad's car drove away. He never skipped again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to eat cauliflower, but her mommy didn't like it. One day, Lily went to the store with her mommy and saw a big, beautiful cauliflower. She asked her mommy if they could buy it and her mommy said no.

Lily was sad and started to cry. A kind old lady saw her crying and asked what was wrong. Lily told her about the cauliflower and the old lady said she had some at her house. She gave Lily a piece of cauliflower and Lily felt so happy. She said "thank you" to the old lady and ran back to her mommy.

When they got home, Lily's mommy was dizzy and felt sick. They had to go to the hospital and it turned out the cauliflower was bad. Lily felt so sad and wished she had listened to her mommy. From then on, Lily always listened to her mommy's advice.

Once upon a time, there were two friends, a rabbit and a squirrel. Every day, they would jump and play together. One day though, the rabbit said to the squirrel, “let’s make a sail! Then we can go on a big adventure!”

The squirrel was so excited, she started to jump up and down! They found some big leaves, and things from their garden. They put them together and started to make their sail.

When they had finished their sail, the rabbit said to the squirrel “now it is time to be brave and humble! We must be brave to go on an adventure, and humble to remember that not everything will be perfect.”

The squirrel felt strong and determined. They hopped onto the big sail, and began to float away. They explored wonderful places, and saw amazing things. The rabbit and squirrel were so happy, they even took a selfie together!

In the end, the rabbit and squirrel said goodbye to their sail, and came home to play. But they knew they would never forget the amazing adventure they had together!

Once upon a time, there was a hungry clay. He was all alone in the world and wanted to make some friends. One day, he had an urge to go exploring so he hopped up and began walking.

As he go further and further away from his home, he saw other clays. Still feeling hungry, he called out to the new clays. The clays heard him and waved him over to join them.

They all went to a nearby river and found a big pile of clay in the mud. They decided to have a clay party!

The hungry clay joined in and felt much better after being around all of the other clays. He had a lot of fun and hugged his new friends goodbye before he went back home.

The hungry clay felt much happier now that he had made friends. He would often urge his friends to come visit him at his home. Together they would play happily until the sun went down. The End.

Once there was a little girl. She was three years old and her name was Lily. One day, Lily was playing outside. She saw an interesting thing on the ground.

It was very dry and it felt strange. She picked it up and looked at it. It was so interesting that she wanted to keep it.

So, Lily took the thing and ran home. She put the thing in her pocket and went inside.

But when she took the thing out of her pocket later, it had gotten wet! She was very sad and started to cry.

Lily's mom tried to make her feel better, but she couldn't. It was too late. The thing was ruined.

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved going on adventures with her family. One day, they went on a trip to the countryside. They stayed in a small cabin and had a lot of fun.

When it was time to go home, Lily's dad asked her to help unpack their bags. She was happy to help and quickly started to put things away. But then she realized that she had lost her favorite teddy bear. She looked everywhere but couldn't find it.

Feeling sad and embarrassed, Lily decided to go outside and look for her bear. She wandered around the woods and eventually came across an underground tunnel. Curious, she went inside. But it was dark and scary and she couldn't find her way back out. Her family searched for her but they never found her. Poor Lily was lost forever.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She was very hungry and wanted a sandwich to eat. Her mom made her a yummy peanut butter and jelly sandwich.

Lily took a big bite of the sandwich, but it hurt her teeth because she had a loose tooth. She whispered to her mom and showed her the tooth. Her mom said it was okay and that the tooth would fall out soon.

Lily finished her sandwich and went to play outside. She saw her friend and whispered to her about her loose tooth. They played together and had lots of fun in the sand. They made a big sandcastle and pretended to be princesses. Lily forgot all about her hurt tooth and was happy to be with her friend.

Sam was a curious boy who liked to examine everything he saw. One day, he found a big onion in the kitchen. He wondered what it was and how it smelled. He picked up the onion and peeled off the brown skin. He saw many white layers inside.

He wanted to know more, so he brought the onion to his nose and sniffed it. It smelled very strong and made his eyes water. He sneezed and rubbed his eyes. He felt a burning pain in his eyes and nose. He dropped the onion and cried.

His mom heard him and ran to the kitchen. She saw him holding his face and the onion on the floor. She knew what happened and felt sorry for him. She hugged him and took him to the sink. She washed his eyes and nose with water. She told him the onion was a food that made people cry. She said he should not examine it with his nose. She gave him a cookie and a kiss.

Sam learned his lesson and never examined an onion again. He still liked to be curious, but he was more careful. He asked his mom before he touched anything new. He did not want to cry or hurt himself again. He was a smart boy.

Once upon a time, there were two beds in a bedroom. One was a big, soft mattress and the other was a small hard one. The mattress was for the big brother and the small one for the little sister.

One day, the big brother was playing on his bed when the little sister came in. She was jealous and wanted to play too.

“Can I play too?” she asked hopefully.

“No!” shouted the big brother. “This is my mattress. You can’t play on it.”

The little sister got really angry and so she struck the mattress with her hand. The mattress was too big and soft and only moved a little bit. The brother laughed and the sister got crosser.

“It’s not fair!” she yelled.

The big brother realised he had made his sister jealous and apologied.

“Sorry,” he said. “You can play too.”

The little sister smiled and hopped onto the big mattress. She had lots of fun playing as the brother watched and smiled.

Once upon a time there was a mighty lion. He lived happily in the jungle, but one day an elephant started to tease him. The elephant was so big that the lion knew he didn't stand a chance against him.

So the lion ran away. He ran for days and days until he came to a big house. He curled up beneath it to rest.

Suddenly, he heard a voice. It said: "Hey, lion! I'm scared of you. Is there anything I can do to make you leave?"

The lion was so surprised that he didn't say anything. But then he saw a pill lying on the floor.

The lion told the voice that if he ate the pill, it would make him as strong and mighty as any other animal. The voice agreed and the lion ate it.

The lion felt a new power inside him! He was so mighty and brave that the elephant and all the other animals stopped teasing him. The lion lived happily ever after and was never bothered again.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Jenny. Jenny was three, she had long blonde hair and loved to wear pretty dresses. She was very loyal to her family and friends, always helping them when they needed her.

One day, Jenny went to the park with her family. As they walked, she started to sing a happy tune. Her mum smiled, giving her a hug and they kept walking.

At the park, they found a wide open space in the middle of the grass. Jenny's dad quickly put down a blanket and they all sat down. Jenny asked to play on the seesaw, so they got out and Jenny put her waist in the middle of the seat.

Then, her dad started to sing to her. His voice was deep and beautiful making Jenny smile. She sang along, clapping her hands and swaying back and forth on the seesaw. They kept singing and playing together until it was time to go home.

Jenny was very lucky to have such a loyal family. She hugged them tight and promised she would always love them.

The end.

Lily and Tom were playing in the kitchen. They liked to pretend they were chefs and make food with pots and pans. Lily found a big spoon and said, "Look, Tom, I can stir the soup with this spoon." She put the spoon in a pot and moved it around.

Tom saw a shiny tap on the sink. He wanted to see what it did. He climbed on a chair and reached for the tap. He turned it and water came out. He said, "Wow, Lily, look, I can make water with this tap." He turned it more and more and water splashed everywhere.

Lily heard the water and looked at Tom. She saw the water on the floor and on the walls. She said, "Tom, stop, stop, you are making a mess. Turn off the tap, turn off the tap." She ran to the sink and tried to turn the tap. But the tap was too tight and she could not move it.

Tom got nervous. He said, "Lily, I can't turn it off, I can't turn it off. What do we do?" He jumped off the chair and ran to the door. He said, "Let's go and get mom, let's go and get mom."

Lily was scared. She said, "No, Tom, we can't go. Mom will be angry. We have to fix the tap, we have to fix the tap." She grabbed the spoon and hit the tap with it. She hoped the tap would stop. But the tap did not stop. The tap broke. Water sprayed out of the tap like a fountain. Lily and Tom screamed. They heard mom coming. They were in big trouble.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, Lily's mom made her a yummy lunch with a sandwich and some fruit. Lily was so excited to eat it! But when she went outside to play, she didn't notice that the ground was icy. She slipped and fell down, hurting herself.

Lily's mom came outside and saw what happened. She warned Lily to be careful when the ground is icy because it can be very slippery. Lily learned that she needs to pay attention to her surroundings and be careful.

The moral of the story is that we need to listen to our parents when they warn us about something. They want to keep us safe and healthy. And we need to be careful when the ground is icy so we don't get hurt.

Bubba the bear was so excited to wake up in the morning. He couldn't wait to explore the forest. He was very hairy and loved the feel of the sun's warmth on his fur.

As he started walking, he saw something on the ground. He got closer and saw it was a piece of gum. He knew he wasn't allowed to eat it, so he bent down and grabbed it carefully.

"What are you going to do with that?" asked a nearby squirrel.

Bubba smiled. "I'm going to rub it on that big tree up ahead. I heard the gum can make it nice and shiny!"

The squirrel thought this sounded like fun and wanted to help. So the two friends took turns rubbing the gum on the tree, until it was nice and shiny. The tree looked so happy!

Bubba and his squirrel friend enjoyed the sunny day and went on to play the rest of the day.

Once upon a time, there was a clumsy bunny named Benny. Benny loved to hop and play, but he always tripped over his big feet. One day, Benny went on an adventure to find his friends. He hopped and hopped until he saw a big mist in the air.

Benny was scared, but he knew he had to complete his mission to find his friends. He hopped through the mist and finally found his friends playing in a field. They were happy to see Benny and they played together all day.

As the sun began to set, Benny realized he had completed his adventure and found his friends. He felt proud of himself for being brave and not giving up. Benny and his friends hopped back home, through the mist and into their cozy burrows. The end.

Once there was a little boy called Jack. Jack wanted to prove he was brave, so he decided to climb the tall tree. Jack climbed to the top and he could feel the wind in his hair. He shouted to his parents down on the ground, "Look at me, I'm so brave!"

But then Jack's foot slipped, and he started to fall. He screamed and shouted for help, but it was too late. He crashed to the ground onto a pile of leaves, and felt so embarrassed.

His mom and dad ran over to him, looking worried and scared. Jack was a bit shaken, but he said he was okay.

"Well," said his dad, "you certainly have passed the test of bravery, but you also have a filthy face and clothes. I think it's time for a bath for you, my lad!"

Jack sighed. He knew his dad was right. He had wanted to prove he was brave, and he had - but at what cost?

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a red coat with a zip. One day, Lily was walking in the park with her mom. Suddenly, she saw a butterfly and got very excited. She tried to catch it, but accidentally dropped her toy.

Lily's mom was alert and quickly picked up the toy for her. Lily was happy and thanked her mom. They continued to walk in the park and saw many beautiful flowers. Lily loved the colors and smelled them one by one.

As they were leaving the park, Lily remembered her dropped toy and looked for it. Luckily, her mom had it safe in her pocket. They went home happily and Lily hugged her mom tightly.

Ben and Lily are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big sign. The sign has a picture of a jar. The jar is full of candy. The sign says: "Guess how many candy in the jar. Win a prize!"

Ben and Lily want to win the prize. They go to the table where the jar is. A nice lady is there. She says: "Hello, kids. Do you want to play the game?"

"Yes, please!" Ben and Lily say.

"OK, then. Write your name and your guess on this paper. Put it in this box. The one who is closest to the right number wins the prize. Good luck!"

Ben and Lily take the paper and the pen. They write their names. They look at the jar. It is very big. It has many candy. How many? Ben thinks hard. He writes: "50". Lily thinks harder. She writes: "100".

They put their papers in the box. They say thank you to the lady. They wait for the winner to be announced.

The lady looks at the papers. She counts the candy in the jar. She smiles. She says: "We have a winner! The right number is 97. The closest guess is 100. Lily, you win the prize!"

Lily is very happy. She jumps up and down. She hugs Ben. She says: "Yay! I win! I win!"

Ben is happy for Lily. He claps his hands. He says: "Good job, Lily! You are very smart!"

The lady gives Lily the prize. It is a long, soft, colorful scarf. Lily loves it. She wraps it around her neck. She says: "Thank you, lady! Thank you, Ben! This is the best day ever!"

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved watching films with her mommy and daddy. One day, Lily's friend Sophie came over to play. Sophie saw that Lily had a new film and she felt jealous.

Sophie asked Lily if they could watch the film together. Lily was happy to share and she requested that they watch it in her bedroom. They snuggled up with some popcorn and enjoyed the film together.

After the film, Sophie thanked Lily for sharing and they played some more. Lily was happy that she could make her friend feel better and they had a great time together.

Once upon a time, there was a little rabbit named Benny. Benny loved to play hide and seek with his friends. One day, Benny thought of a great hiding spot behind a big tree. His friends searched and searched, but they couldn't find him. Benny felt very happy and proud of himself for being so clever.

But then, a judge came along and saw Benny hiding. The judge thought Benny was being sneaky and not playing fair. Benny didn't understand why the judge was angry at him. Benny was just having fun.

The judge took Benny away from his friends and scolded him. Benny felt sad and scared. He didn't know what he did wrong. From that day on, Benny became very thoughtful and always made sure to play fair and not hide in sneaky spots. But he never forgot the day he was judged and taken away from his friends. The moral of the story is to always play fair and be kind to others.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Lucy. She loved to play and explore around her house. Today, she decided to venture outside. She stepped out into her garden and saw a neat, tidy bush. She headed straight for it and twisted it around. Suddenly, Lucy heard a tinkling sound and she saw something glittering in the bush. She reached in and found a beautiful, shiny gem. She squealed in excitement and quickly put the gem in her pocket.

Lucy's mom was close by and heard her laugh. She said, "What did you find, Lucy?". Lucy smiled brightly and pulled the gem out of her pocket. She showed it to her mom and said, "Look, a gem!"

Her mom smiled and said, "Wow! What a bright gem. Where did you find it?". Lucy pointed to the bush and said, "Twist it around and out came the gem". Her mom replied, "That's amazing! Let's keep the gem safe and show it to everyone later".

Lucy happily agreed and she couldn't wait to show off her special, tidy gem.

Once upon a time there was a little boy. He wanted to find something special. Each week he looked and looked but he couldn't find it anywhere.

The boy was starting to feel helpless. He didn't know what to do. So he asked his mom and his dad for help.

His mom looked around and she soon found something special. It was a big box of toys! The little boy was so happy and he hugged his mom.

Each week the little boy would open the box of toys and find something new and fun to play with. He was so happy that his mom had found it for him and he never felt helpless again.

Tom is a pilot. He likes to fly planes in the sky. He is very dependable. He always does his job well and helps people go to different places.

One day, Tom has to fly a big plane with many people inside. He is happy and ready to go. But when he gets to the plane, he sees a problem. The wing of the plane is broken. It has a big hole in it. Tom is worried. He cannot fly the plane like this. It is not safe.

Tom tells the people in the plane that they have to wait. He calls his boss and asks for help. He says they need a new plane or a way to fix the wing. His boss says he will try to find a solution. But he says it might take a long time.

The people in the plane are not happy. They are angry and bored. They want to fly now. They do not want to wait. They start to complain and shout at Tom. They say he is a bad pilot and he should fix the plane himself.

Tom feels sad and stressed. He wants to make the people happy and fly the plane. But he knows he cannot do it alone. He needs help. He hopes his boss will find a way to help him soon. He tries to be calm and patient. He tells the people in the plane that he is sorry and he is doing his best. He says he is a dependable pilot and he will not let them down. He asks them to be calm and patient too. He says they will fly soon. He hopes they will believe him.

Jill and Tom were playing with crayons in their room. They liked to draw on paper, but sometimes they also drew on the wall. They knew it was bad, but it was fun.

One day, it was very hot outside. The sun was shining on the window and made the room warm. Jill and Tom felt sweaty and thirsty. They wanted to drink some water, but they did not want to stop playing.

"Look, Tom," Jill said, pointing to the ceiling. "The crayons are melting. They are dripping down like rain."

Tom looked up and saw the colorful drops falling from the ceiling. He was amazed and curious. He wanted to touch them.

"Wow, they are so pretty," he said. "Can we catch them?"

He reached out his hand and tried to grab a red drop. But it was hot and sticky. It burned his finger and made him cry.

"Ow, ow, ow!" he shouted. "It hurts!"

Jill heard him and ran to him. She saw his finger and felt sorry for him.

"I'm sorry, Tom," she said. "The crayons are too hot. They are not good to play with. Let me get you some ice."

She ran to the kitchen and got some ice from the freezer. She wrapped it in a cloth and gave it to Tom. She held his hand and kissed his finger.

"Does it feel better?" she asked.

Tom nodded and smiled. He felt the ice cool his finger and ease his pain. He looked at Jill and thought she was very kind and attractive.

"Thank you, Jill," he said. "You are the best sister ever."

Jill hugged him and smiled. She was happy to help him and make him feel better.

They decided to stop playing with crayons and draw on paper instead. They also drank some water and ate some cookies. They learned their lesson and never drew on the ceiling again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play in the sea and collect shells. One day, she found a smelly fish on the beach.

"Eww, this fish is smelly!" exclaimed Lily.

Just then, a kind man walked by and said, "That fish may be smelly, but it's still a living thing. We should respect all living things."

Lily thought about what the man said and decided to throw the fish back into the sea. As she did, the man applauded her for doing the right thing.

From then on, Lily always remembered to respect all living things, even if they were smelly.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to explore the world around her. One day, she went for a walk in the countryside. She saw a beautiful landscape with green trees and colorful flowers. It was so pretty that she wanted to spread her arms and hug it.

As she walked, she found a little bird with a broken wing. She felt sad for the little bird, so she picked it up and took it home. She spread a soft blanket on the floor and put the little bird on it. She gave it some water and seeds to eat.

Days passed, and the little bird got better. It could fly again. Lily was happy to see the little bird healthy and free. She took it outside and let it go. The little bird flew away, and Lily watched it until it was just a little dot in the sky. She felt happy to have helped the little bird and to have seen the beautiful landscape.

Sara liked to play with her toy bunny. She called him Hoppy and he was very dependable. He always stayed with her when she was sad or scared. He was soft and white and had long ears.

One day, Sara and her mom went to the farm. Sara wanted to see the animals and the corn. She brought Hoppy with her and held him tight. Mom said they could walk in the corn field, but they had to stay close. Sara nodded and followed mom.

The corn was tall and green and made a rustling sound. Sara thought it was fun to run between the rows. She saw a butterfly and chased it. She forgot about mom and Hoppy. She reached out to catch the butterfly, but it flew away. Sara looked around and realized she was lost. She couldn't see mom or the farm. She felt scared and alone.

She remembered Hoppy and reached for him. But he was not there. She had dropped him somewhere in the corn. She started to cry. She wanted Hoppy and mom. She wanted to go home.

She heard a voice calling her name. It was mom. She ran towards the voice and saw mom's face. Mom hugged her and said she was sorry. She said she had been looking for her and was worried. Sara said she was sorry too. She said she had lost Hoppy in the corn. She said he was dependable and she missed him.

Mom said they would find Hoppy. She said he was dependable too and he would not disappear. She said they would look in the corn together. Sara smiled and held mom's hand. They walked back to the corn field and searched for Hoppy. After a while, they saw a flash of white. It was Hoppy. He was lying on the ground, near a scarecrow. Sara ran to him and picked him up. She hugged him and said she was happy. He was soft and white and had long ears.

Mom smiled and said they had found Hoppy. She said he was a good bunny and a good friend. She said they should go back to the farm and have some lunch. Sara nodded and followed mom. She held Hoppy tight and said he was dependable. He always stayed with her when she was sad or scared. He was her toy bunny and she loved him.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Abby. Abby loved playing outside in the garden.

Today, Abby decided to pick some dandelions. She spotted one, and as quickly as a bee she bent down to pick it.

While she was picking the dandelion, she saw something sparkly in the grass. It was a match. She was so excited!

Abby quickly picked up the match and showed it to her mom. Mom said it was very special so Abby had to be careful with it.

The days went by, and Abby had a lot of fun with her match. But quickly she found out that playing with the match was a bit boring.

Mom then suggested a fun game, and Abby and mom played together in the garden. It was much more fun than playing with the match!

One day little Grace wanted to watch a movie but her mom said no. Grace got very upset and spoiled. She started screaming and crying until her mom had to give in. Mom couldn't manage them both and said Grace could watch one movie.

Grace was so excited. She picked out her favorite movie and settled down in front of the TV. She was so busy watching she didn't even realise when her mom came to take her to bed.

The next day, Grace asked for another movie, but her mom said no again. But this time, with a little bit of bargaining, Grace managed to watch yet another movie. Grace was a bit spoiled, but it was okay because she had so much fun.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy had a toy car that he loved to play with. One day, Timmy's mom asked him to help her with the iron. Timmy didn't understand what an iron was, so his mom showed him. The iron was hot and it made Timmy a little scared.

Timmy's mom left the room and Timmy went back to playing with his toy car. Suddenly, his older sister came in and accidentally stepped on his toy car. Timmy got very angry and started crying. His mom came back in and saw that Timmy was upset. She asked him what was wrong and Timmy told her about his toy car.

His mom hugged him and said she was sorry. Then, she helped Timmy fix his toy car. Timmy was happy again and he understood that sometimes accidents happen.

Once there was a little boy named Jack. He was three years old and he liked to explore the world around him. One day while playing in the backyard, Jack found a strange object. It was a vest. He was very curious so he carefully put it on.

That's when something amazing happened. He noticed he could fly! With his new vest, Jack flew higher and higher in the sky. He flew so high that he met the clouds. They were excited to meet a new flying friend.

Jack had so much fun with the clouds, but eventually he knew it was time to go home. He carefully flew back to the ground and took off his vest. He smiled, delighted to have found such an amazing thing.

Jack knew this vest was special, so he decided to keep it safe in a secret hiding spot. He tucked it away and promised to remain careful with it. Jack was so excited to fly some more in the future!

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to explore and go on adventures. One day, he found a big box with a mystery inside. He was so curious that he couldn't wait to see what was inside.

But Timmy was also anxious because he didn't know what to expect. He decided to hold the box tightly and take it home to open it with his family.

When he got home, Timmy's family gathered around the box and opened it together. Inside, they found a beautiful treasure that they all shared. Timmy learned that sometimes it's better to share the mystery with others instead of keeping it to himself.

The moral of the story is that sharing can bring joy and happiness to everyone.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy who loved to go to the beach. One day, he saw a big shrimp in the water and he was very excited. He tried to catch it, but it was too fast.

Timmy's grandma was with him and she was very old. She couldn't hear very well, so Timmy had to shout to talk to her. She sighed and said, "I wish I could hear you better."

Timmy didn't catch the shrimp, but he had a fun day at the beach with his grandma. They built sandcastles and played in the water. Timmy was happy and he went to bed dreaming about the big shrimp he saw.

Once there was a little boy. He was three years old and he really loved to measure things. One day, he saw a big card on the floor. He picked it up and looked at it.

"What is this?", he asked his mom. Mom smiled and said, "This is a measuring card."

The little boy was so excited. He had heard that measuring cards were popular and he wanted one. He asked if he could keep the card.

His mom said, "Yes, you can keep it. But there is a lesson to learn first. We should not measure things only by their popularity. Instead, we should measure it by what it can teach us. That is the true value of things."

The little boy nodded. From that day on, he used his measuring card to learn important lessons and he was very happy.

Once upon a time there was a mighty bed. Every night, it was used to count sheep. A three-year-old child loved to count with the bed. They would jump on the bed and count to ten. After counting the sheep, the child would snuggle deep in the sheets and go to sleep. The mighty bed was so cozy, it made the child happy and sleepy. Every night, the bed and the child would count sheep together until the child fell asleep.

Once upon a time in a land far away, there lived a young girl. Her name was Sarah and everyday she would wake up in her beautiful bedroom. She would look out the window and see bright birds, green trees and blue sky. One morning, Sarah woke up and decided she wanted to explore the world.

So, she put on her shoes and went outside. As she walked, she saw different things like tall buildings, little animals and nice people. She said hi to them all and waved.

She came to a big field with a river through the middle of it. Sarah lay down and looked up. The sky was so blue and the clouds so white. She saw them move and change shapes.

Suddenly she noticed a little baby rabbit near her. Sarah smiled and the rabbit hopped away. She followed the baby rabbit and saw something even more beautiful. A big garden of many colours - green, pink, yellow, orange and purple.

The young girl was in awe and said, "This place is so beautiful". She spent the rest of the day playing and discovering the world around her. At night, she went back home, dreaming of all the beautiful things she'd seen.

Once there was a boy called Jack. He was only three years old. One day Jack went for a walk with his mom. They walked and walked until they came to a tall tree. Jack was happy because the tall tree was his favorite.

Suddenly, Jack realized he couldn't hear anything. He looked around and saw that everything was silent and still. He felt strong and happy in the silence.

"Mommy," he said, "it's so quiet here." His mom smiled and said, "That's why it's so special." Jack understood and enjoyed the silence for many minutes.

When it was time to go, Jack was sad. But he knew he'd come back one day and realize the silence again.

One day, a little girl named Suzy went to a parade with her mom. Suzy saw pale blue balloons and big red drums. She heard loud music and saw people dancing. Suzy was so happy.

At the parade, Suzy saw her friend Tom. Tom said, "Hi Suzy! Do you want to find more fun things at the parade with me?" Suzy said, "Yes, let's go find them!"

Suzy and Tom walked together and found a man making funny faces. They laughed and clapped their hands. Then they found a big ice cream truck. Suzy got a pink ice cream and Tom got a green one. They both smiled and enjoyed their ice cream. The parade was so much fun!

Timmy was playing in the park one day when he saw a modern toilet. His eyes lit up with excitement and he ran towards it. But when he went to open the door he found it was locked. Timmy started to cry. Then he heard a voice from inside the toilet. It was an old grumpy man.

The man said, "What are you doing here? I'm trying to get some peace and quiet and you're making a racket. Go away and play elsewhere."

Timmy looked up at the man with sad eyes and said, "Please, can I just have a look? It looks so modern and exciting."

The old grumpy man sighed and said, "All right. Come in but just have a quick look."

Timmy looked around the toilet in awe and he was very excited to have seen such a modern place. Then he went to the park to play some more with a smile on his face.

Once upon a time there was a green car. The car was getting ready to go on a trip. It said to itself, "I'm ready for my trip!" The car had lots of things to prepare for. It filled up with gas, and added a spare tire. The car also made sure to get plenty of air in its tires. Then it opened its windows and doors, and polished its paint.

The car was now ready to go. It revved up its engine and drove down the road. It rolled through the countryside, enjoying the view. The car was so excited to reach its destination. Finally, it drove up to a house, and the car's driver hopped out.

The car had finished preparing for its trip. Now, it was ready to take its driver wherever they wanted to go!

Once upon a time there was a wise old lady. She lived in a tall, green tree and liked to look out over the countryside.

One day, a gentle breeze blew through the sky and scattered the lady's coins all over the ground. The old lady was very surprised and, using her wisdom, she quickly jumped out of her tree.

The lady dashed around trying to collect all her coins, but she was too slow. With all the coins scattered, it was hard for the old lady to find them all.

But then something amazing happened - the lady heard a chirping noise and, turning around, she saw a group of happy birds. The birds had found all the scattered coins and were gathering them back together in a pile.

The lady was very pleased and thanked the birds for their help. She quickly collected all her coins and started to head back to her tree.

The wise lady was glad to have her coins back and thanked the birds for their kindness. She knew she had been very lucky, and from then on the old lady was always generous to the birds who had helped her.

Once upon a time, there was a little fishy named Blue. Blue loved to swim and play with his fishy friends. One day, Blue felt very tired and could not breathe well. His mommy fishy told him he needed oxygen, which is like the air we breathe.

Blue swam up to the top of the water and took a big gulp of air. He felt better and could swim and play again. Blue saw a big, friendly dolphin swimming by and smiled at him. The dolphin smiled back and Blue felt happy.

From that day on, Blue made sure to always take big gulps of oxygen so he could keep swimming and playing with his fishy friends. And whenever he saw the friendly dolphin, he would smile and the dolphin would smile back. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Jane. Jane was helping her mom clean the garden that day. As they worked, they saw something strange - a very hot trap.

“What’s that, Mommy?” Jane asked.

Her mom sighed and said, “That’s a trap, honey. It’s supposed to help keep the animals away from the garden.”

Jane was curious and wanted to get a closer look. Before her mom could stop her, Jane reached out to touch the trap. As soon as she did, it snapped shut and she was stuck!

“Help, Mommy!” Jane shouted.

Her mom ran over and examined the trap. She reached out and tried to pull it open, but it wouldn’t budge. With a quick thought, her mom ran back into the house and grabbed a big rock. She came back and smashed the rock against the trap until it opened.

At last, Jane was free! She hugged her mom and thanked her for helping. They both agreed never to touch the trap again, and they continued working in the garden.

Tommy wanted a dream. So, he went to the dark room. He closed his eyes, and made a wish. He wished for a toy train with lots of tracks.

He opened his eyes and he saw a very big box. He was excited! He opened the box and there was the toy train! He started to play with it, making it go round and round the tracks.

Then, he heard a noise. It was coming from outside. It was the postman with a letter. He opened the letter and it said his dream had come true!

Tommy was so happy. He smiled and said, "My dream came true!" He hugged the toy train tight and thanked his lucky stars. His dream was real!

Anna and Ben are friends. They like to play outside. They enjoy exercise. They run, jump, and kick a ball. They are clever. They know how to share and take turns.

One day, they see a big dog. The dog is black and white. It has a long tail. It looks friendly. Anna and Ben want to pet the dog. They run to the dog. They say, "Hello, dog! Can we play with you?"

The dog does not like Anna and Ben. The dog is angry. It barks and growls. It shows its teeth. It bites Anna and Ben. They cry and scream. They are hurt. They are scared.

A man comes. He is the dog's owner. He says, "Sorry, sorry! My dog is not nice. He does not like children. He is a guard dog. You should not go near him."

Anna and Ben are sad and mad. They say, "You are a bad man! You should not have a bad dog! You should keep him away from us!"

The man takes the dog and leaves. Anna and Ben go home. They tell their moms what happened. Their moms hug them and take them to the doctor. The doctor gives them medicine and bandages. He says, "You are brave. You will be okay. But you should be careful. Not all dogs are friendly. Some dogs are dangerous. You should always ask before you pet a dog."

Anna and Ben learn a lesson. They do not enjoy exercise today. They do not feel clever. They feel sorry and silly. They wish they had not met the bad dog.

Once upon a time there were two friends, Jojo and Tim. Jojo was always making new things and Tim was jealous of all the fun things Jojo made.

One day Jojo said to Tim, "I have an amazing surprise for you!" Tim was very curious and asked excitedly, "What is it??" Jojo said, "Wait and see!" and shrugged.

The next day, when they met, Jojo asked if Tim wanted to help him with his new surprise. Tim was so happy he clapped his hands. Jojo said, "We have to do the laundry first before I can show you my surprise." Tim was a little confused but he agreed to help.

When they were done doing the laundry, Jojo smiled and took out a very special toy. It was a toy car made out of soap bubbles and it glowed brightly in the sun! Tim was amazed and forgot all his jealous feelings. He said to Jojo, "Thank you so much! I love it!" Jojo smiled and said, "I knew you would!"

Once upon a time there was a famous princess. She was so famous that everybody wanted to be like her. One day she was walking and thinking when she noticed something shiny on the ground. It was a magical key!

The princess was so excited and she picked up the key and put it in her pocket. She followed the path the key seemed to lead her on. The princess looked around as she walked and suddenly saw a big castle in the distance.

She began to run, feeling so happy and excited. When she reached the castle she used the magic key to open the door. Inside the castle was a big room filled with treasure. She had found the treasure from her dreams!

The princess was so happy. She and her friends celebrated with lots of singing and dancing. From that day forward, the princess was even more famous than before. Everyone wanted to be like her and follow her lead.

Tom and Lily are friends. They like to play pretend. Today, they pretend to be singers. They have a big show in the garden. They wear cool hats and scarves. They sing songs they know.

"Are you ready, Lily?" Tom asks.

"Yes, Tom. Let's perform!" Lily says.

They go to the stage. The stage is a big box. They have a microphone. The microphone is a banana. They sing loud and happy. They dance and clap. They have fun.

But then, Lily trips. She falls off the stage. She hurts her knee. She cries.

"Oh no, Lily! Are you okay?" Tom says. He runs to help her.

He gives her a hug. He says sorry. He gets a band-aid. He puts it on her knee.

"Thank you, Tom. You are a good friend," Lily says.

She smiles. She feels better.

"Can we perform again?" she asks.

"Of course, Lily. We can perform again. You are a great singer," Tom says.

They go back to the stage. They sing more songs. They are careful not to trip. They have more fun. They are happy.

Once upon a time, there was a ducky who lived in a wild pond. One day, it hopped onto a rock and noticed a vegetable nearby. The vegetable was very tasty and the duck wanted to try it. But there was a problem - it was too big for the duck to eat!

"Help! I need to save this vegetable," the duck said.

The duck asked a frog nearby if it could help. The frog hopped away, and soon another frog appeared with a stick. The first frog used the stick to slice the vegetable into small pieces. Now the duck could eat the vegetable.

"Thank you!" said the duck.

The duck ate the small pieces of vegetable and enjoyed every bite! It was a wild and wonderful snack!

Sara was a girl who liked to play with her toys. She had a doll, a ball, a car and a bear. She played with them every day in her room. She made them talk to each other and have fun.

One day, Sara was playing with her bear. She pretended that he was her friend and they went to the park. She said, "Hello, bear. Do you want to go on the slide?" The bear nodded and said, "Yes, Sara. I like the slide. It is fast and fun." Sara smiled and took the bear to the slide. She put him on the top and pushed him down. The bear laughed and said, "Whee! That was fun. Thank you, Sara."

Sara and the bear played on the slide for a long time. They also played on the swings, the seesaw and the sandbox. They had a lot of fun. But soon, Sara felt tired. She yawned and said, "I am sleepy, bear. Let's go home." The bear yawned too and said, "Me too, Sara. Let's go home and take a nap."

Sara and the bear walked back to her room. They saw that Sara's mom was waiting for them. She said, "Hello, Sara. Hello, bear. Did you have fun at the park?" Sara nodded and said, "Yes, mom. We had fun. But we are sleepy now. Can we take a nap?" Sara's mom smiled and said, "Of course, Sara. You can take a nap. But first, you need to wash your hands and face. You are dirty and smelly from playing." Sara said, "Okay, mom. I will wash my hands and face. But what about the bear? He is dirty and smelly too." Sara's mom said, "Don't worry, Sara. I will wash the bear for you. He needs a bath too. Then he will be clean and soft again."

Sara and the bear washed their hands and face. Then Sara's mom took the bear and put him in the sink. She used soap and water to wash him. She rinsed him and dried him with a towel. She gave him back to Sara and said, "Here you go, Sara. Your bear is clean and soft now. He smells good too." Sara hugged the bear and said, "Thank you, mom. You are the best. I love you and I love the bear." Sara's mom said, "I love you too, Sara. And I love the bear too. Now, let's go to your bed and take a nap. You need to rest after playing so much." Sara and the bear said, "Okay, mom. Let's go to bed and take a nap." They followed Sara's mom to the bed. They snuggled under the blanket and closed their eyes. They fell asleep and dreamed of the park. They were happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who liked to go for walks. She had never seen such a big, old tree in her life. Its roots seemed to go on forever, and its branches stretched high into the sky. Each time she walked by it, the little girl couldn't help but stare and wonder what was hidden inside.

One day, the little girl decided to take a closer look. As she got closer, she noticed something strange about the tree. Its bark was brown and chunky, and it was filled with a bunch of small holes. As she went to touch it, something flew out of one of the holes and flew away.

The little girl was curious and decided to investigate so she climbed up the trunk of the tree. When she reached the top, there was a humble little wooden house built around the trunk of the tree!

The girl had never seen anything like this before, so she stared in awe at the tiny house. She couldn't believe that something so small could be so special.

The little girl soon returned home, but the memory of the tiny house stayed in her heart forever.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved toys and he always wondered where they came from. One day, he asked his mommy, "Where do toys come from?"

His mommy smiled and said, "Toys come from a special place called a factory. That's where they make all the toys you love to play with."

Timmy's eyes widened with excitement. "Can we go there?" he asked.

His mommy nodded and they went on a trip to the toy factory. When they arrived, Timmy was so proud to see all the toys being made. He saw machines moving and workers busy making toys.

Suddenly, the workers revealed a new toy they had just made. It was a shiny red car and Timmy couldn't wait to play with it. He was so happy to have learned where toys come from and he couldn't wait to tell his friends all about it.
