Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy was very hungry, but he didn't know how to cook. So, he went to the kitchen to find something to eat.

When he got to the kitchen, he saw a cookie jar on the counter. He reached up to grab a cookie, but his mom saw him and said, "Timmy, you can't have a cookie before dinner. If you do, I will have to punish you."

Timmy felt sad, but he knew his mom was right. He decided to wait for dinner and eat his vegetables so he could have a cookie for dessert. And he never tried to sneak a cookie again!

Anna likes to sew with her mom. She has a box of thread in many colors. She can make dolls and clothes for them. She knows how to use a needle and a knot.

One day, Anna wants to sew a dress for her doll. She picks a pink thread and a blue fabric. She cuts a piece of fabric and starts to sew. She is happy and sings a song.

But then, she sees a problem. The thread is too short. She cannot finish the dress. She is sad and stops singing.

She runs to her mom and says, "Mom, I need more thread. The thread is too short. The dress is not done."

Her mom looks at her and smiles. She says, "Don't worry, Anna. I have more thread for you. You can use this one. It is the same color as the one you have. Here you go."

She gives Anna a new thread. Anna says, "Thank you, mom. You are so nice. The thread is important for the dress. The dress is important for the doll. The doll is important for me."

She hugs her mom and runs back to her sewing. She finishes the dress and puts it on her doll. She is happy and sings again. She shows her mom and says, "Look, mom. The dress is done. It is pretty. Do you like it?"

Her mom says, "Yes, Anna. I like it very much. You did a great job. You are a good sewer. I am proud of you."

She hugs Anna and says, "I love you, Anna. You are important for me."

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to collect shiny rocks and put them in his pocket. He would go on walks with his mommy and daddy and look for rocks to add to his collection.

One day, Timmy's mommy told him that when he grows up, he will need to find a job. Timmy didn't know what a job was, but he knew it was important. He wanted to make his mommy and daddy proud.

As Timmy continued to collect rocks, he noticed that some of them were not shiny anymore. They were dull and grey. Timmy didn't like the dead rocks, so he threw them away.

Years later, when Timmy was all grown up and had a job, he realized that his job was like collecting rocks. He had to find the shiny ones that were important and throw away the dead ones that were not. Timmy was happy that he had learned this lesson from his rock collection.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy who loved to play with his toys. One day, he was playing with his favorite toy car when suddenly he noticed that one of the wheels was missing. He looked everywhere but couldn't find it. He went to his mother and said, "Mommy, my car is broken. Can you help me solve it?"

His mother looked at the car and said, "Don't worry Timmy, we will find the missing wheel." They searched the whole house but still couldn't find it. Timmy got upset and said, "This is stupid. I can't play with my car anymore."

His mother hugged him and said, "Don't worry Timmy, we will buy a new wheel tomorrow." Timmy smiled and hugged his mother back. He was happy that his mother solved the problem and he could play with his car again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved to play outside in nature. She liked to look at the flowers and listen to the birds sing. One day, she decided to have a picnic with her teddy bear, Mr. Snuggles.

Lily's mom made her a yummy sandwich with peanut butter and jelly. Lily also had some grapes and a glass of lemonade. She poured the lemonade into a cup and sat down to eat her lunch with Mr. Snuggles.

Suddenly, a gust of wind blew and knocked over the cup of lemonade. It spilled all over the blanket and Lily's sandwich. She was upset and started to cry. But then, Mr. Snuggles said, "Don't worry, Lily. Let's clean up the mess and have some fun!"

Lily and Mr. Snuggles cleaned up the spilled lemonade and decided to have a tea party instead. They poured pretend tea into cups and had a great time. Lily learned that even when things go wrong, you can still have fun and enjoy nature with your friends.

Once upon a time, there was a furry cat named Tom. He loved to play outside with his friends. They would run, jump, and have lots of fun together.

One day, while playing, Tom saw a big fall. He wanted to show his friends how brave he was. So, he decided to jump over the fall. He ran fast and jumped high. But, he did not make it to the other side.

Tom's friend, a little bird, saw him fall. She flew down to help him. She used her wing to slap the water away from his face. Tom felt better and thanked the little bird. They became best friends and played together every day.

Ben and Mia were playing with their toys in the garden. They had a big ship that they pretended was sailing on the sea. They made noises like waves and wind and seagulls.

"Look, there is an island!" Mia said, pointing to a pile of sand. "Let's go and explore it!"

"OK, but be careful, there might be pirates or monsters!" Ben said, following her. They jumped off the ship and ran to the sand. They found some sticks and stones and shells that they used as tools and treasures.

They dug a hole in the sand and put some shells inside. "This is our secret stash!" Mia said. "We have to hide it from the bad guys!"

They covered the hole with more sand and a big leaf. Then they heard a loud noise. It was their mom, calling them for lunch.

"Come on, kids, it's time to eat!" she said. "You can play more later!"

Ben and Mia ran back to the ship. They grabbed their toys and put them inside. They wanted to keep them safe.

"Let's open the ship and see what we have!" Ben said. He lifted the lid of the ship and looked inside. He saw their toys, but also something else. It was a lemon that had fallen from the tree.

"Yuck, what is this?" he said, picking it up. He smelled it and made a face. It was bitter and sour.

"It's a lemon, silly!" Mia said, laughing. "It's good for making lemonade!"

She took the lemon from him and squeezed it into a cup. She added some water and sugar and stirred it.

"Here, try this!" she said, handing him the cup. "It's sweet and refreshing!"

Ben took a sip and smiled. It was delicious. He liked lemonade.

"Thank you, Mia!" he said. "You are a good cook!"

They drank their lemonade and went to have lunch with their mom. They were happy and hungry. They had a lot of fun playing with their ship.

Once there was a boy named Tom. Tom loved trophies. Every morning he looked in his trophy cabinet in his bedroom and he felt so proud. Today was a different day. When Tom opened the trophy cabinet, he saw that it was empty. He started to cry.

Tom's mother saw how sad he was and came into his bedroom. She asked Tom why he was crying. Tom said: "My trophy cabinet is empty."

His mum said: "That's okay. Do you want to come with me to buy a trophy?". Tom was so happy that he quickly said yes.

Tom and his mum went to the store and they saw lots of trophies. Tom chose the best trophy. The trophy had a star on it and it was so sparkly. He gave it a big hug.

Tom's mum said: "That's a really beautiful trophy! Now let's go home and show everyone".

At home, Tom showed his family his new trophy. Everyone was so happy for him. His dad said: "This calls for a celebration. Let's all go out for pizza."

Tom was so happy that he was talking a lot about his trophy. He told everyone about how he got it, and how he chose it.

Tom loves his trophy and he keeps it in his trophy cabinet so he can look at it every day.

Once there was an ostrich. It was very clean. Every morning it took a bath in the river and then it would run around in the sun.

One day it decided to quit. It quit running and it quit taking baths in the river. It quit looking for food and it quit sleeping in its nest.

The ostrich was tired. So it took a nap in the shade of a tree. After its nap the ostrich felt better so it started to do all the things it loved again. It took baths in the river, it ran around in the sun and it ate all the food it could find.

From then on, the ostrich was happy and clean and it never quit again!

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Clara. She was three years old and she loved to explore the world around her.

One day, Clara was playing in a park near her house when she saw a big white bird. It had a long neck and a beak. She was very curious and asked the bird, “What are you?”

The bird replied, “I am a crane.”

Clara was so excited. She asked the crane, “Can I take you flying?” The crane smiled and replied, “Yes, let’s go!”

So, Clara and the crane flew into the sky. It was very chilly and there were icy clouds everywhere. Clara was so happy she couldn’t stop laughing.

After a while the crane said, “It’s getting too cold for me, so I need to go now.” “Okay,” replied Clara sadly. “Fly safely."

The crane smiled and flew away. Clara waved goodbye and went home. She felt very happy and cozy inside.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy. He loved to whistle! He would whistle all day long and hum when he was happy. One day, he asked his mom to buy some jelly. His mom told him that jelly was not very cheap, but he begged and begged until she said yes.

The little boy was so excited! He ran to the store to pick out his favourite jelly. He picked up the biggest jar of jelly he could find. It was so yummy! The little boy hopped all the way home, whistling a happy tune.

When he got home, the little boy was eager to eat his jelly. He spread some on his toast and it was delicious. He ate so much, he whistled with joy!

The little boy was so happy with his cheap jelly. He knew he had made the right choice and would continue to enjoy it for many days to come!

One morning, little Caroline woke up early. She looked out her window and saw a museum across the street. It was very attractive, so she decided to go inside.

Caroline knocked on the door and waited. A kind old lady opened it.

"Good morning," she said. "Good morning," Caroline replied.

The old lady asked, "Would you like to come inside?"

"Yes, please!" said Caroline.

The old lady smiled and said, "Why not? You're very welcome here!"

Caroline stepped inside and looked around. She saw lots of fascinating things. She wanted to explore every corner of the museum.

The old lady told Caroline, "My museum is very special. I'm sure you'll have lots of fun here!"

Caroline smiled and thanked the old lady for the amazing museum. She couldn't wait to explore it!

Once upon a time there was a mum and her daughter. The daughter was very small and soft. One day the mum said to her daughter, "Let's try making a cake together." The daughter was very excited and said, "Yes, let's try!" The mum and her daughter went to the kitchen and gathered all the ingredients they needed. The daughter was very eager to help. She watched very carefully as the mum poured the flour, sugar and milk into a bowl. Then they stirred it together and added some butter. The daughter was allowed to crack an egg and mix it with the other ingredients. Once everything was mixed together, the mum and daughter put the mixture in the oven and waited for it to bake. The daughter jumped up and down with excitement. Finally, the cake was done. The mum and daughter took it out of the oven, it was warm and soft. The mum said happily, "We did it! Look at our lovely cake!" The daughter smiled and hugged her mum. She said, "We tried hard and it was worth it!" The mum and her daughter enjoyed the cake together. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a favorite rug in her room. It was soft and pink. Lily loved to play on it every day.

One night, Lily's mom came into her room and said, "Lily, it's time to sleep." Lily didn't want to go to sleep. She wanted to play some more. But her mom said, "You need to sleep so you can grow big and strong."

Lily crawled into bed and closed her eyes. She felt the soft rug under her feet. It made her feel cozy and safe. As she drifted off to sleep, she dreamed of all the fun things she would do when she woke up.

The next morning, Lily woke up feeling rested and happy. She remembered her dream and couldn't wait to start her day. She jumped out of bed and ran to her rug. But when she got there, she saw that it was gone! In its place was a bigger, more modest rug. Lily was sad at first, but then she realized that it was still soft and cozy. She knew she would love it just as much as her old rug.

Once upon a time, there was a gray mouse who lived in a old house. He was a very busy mouse, always running and playing. One day, his tummy was grumbling and he knew he was hungry.

So he went in search of a snack. He ran around and around, but in the end all he could find were old, yucky crumbs. But the mouse did not give up. He kept searching until he finally found a nice, tasty morsel.

He was so happy that his hard work was rewarded. The mouse had learnt a valuable lesson - never give up and always keep trying!

Once upon a time there was a girl named Lucy. She was a very naughty girl who didn't listen to her parents. Every day she would do things she wasn't supposed to do.

One day her mom caught her doing something bad in the kitchen. She was very angry and told Lucy that she had to be punished. Lucy was so scared she started to cry.

Her mom decided to punish her by taking away her favorite book, a novel. Lucy was so sad, she couldn't stop crying.

But then her dad came up with a plan. He said that if Lucy can be a good girl and stop doing naughty things, he will get her a new novel! Lucy was so excited and promised to be better.

Two weeks later, Lucy had become a very good girl. She was so happy when her dad came to visit with a new novel. The novel was so exciting, it even had a sour candy tucked inside when Lucy opened it!

Lily and Ben were very excited. They were going on vacation with Mom and Dad. They packed their bags and toys. They put on their hats and shoes. They were ready to go.

But Mom and Dad were not ready. They had to do many things. They had to lock the door, check the mail, turn off the lights, and call Grandma. They were very busy. They told Lily and Ben to wait in the car.

Lily and Ben did not want to wait. They wanted to go now. They were bored and restless. They started to whine and fuss. They said, "Hurry up, Mom and Dad! We want to go! We want to go!"

Mom and Dad heard them. They felt sad and angry. They said, "Lily and Ben, stop whining and fussing. We are doing our best. We have to do these things. They are important. You have to be patient and respectful. You have to be grateful. We are going on vacation. That is a special thing. Not everyone can go on vacation. You should be happy and thankful."

Lily and Ben thought about what Mom and Dad said. They realized they were being rude and ungrateful. They felt sorry and ashamed. They said, "We are sorry, Mom and Dad. We love you. We are grateful. We are happy and thankful. We will be patient and respectful. We will wait in the car."

Mom and Dad smiled and hugged them. They said, "We love you too, Lily and Ben. We are grateful for you. We are happy and thankful. We are almost ready. We will go soon."

They finished their things. They got in the car. They drove away. They had a wonderful vacation. They had fun and learned new things. They were grateful for each other and for their vacation. They never forgot to be patient and respectful. They never forgot to be happy and thankful.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play outside with his friends. One day, Timmy's mom warned him to be careful when playing because the ground was rough and he might fall and hurt himself.

Timmy listened to his mom and was careful when playing. But when his friend Joey wanted to play a game of math, Timmy became very excited and forgot about his mom's warning. He ran to get his math book and tripped on the rough ground, hurting his knee.

Timmy's mom came to his rescue and took care of his knee. She reminded Timmy that it's important to listen to warnings and be careful, even when doing something fun like playing math games with friends. Timmy learned his lesson and promised to be more careful next time.

Once there was a parrot who loved to slide. He would stand on top of the highest hill and slide down over and over again. One day, he saw something disgusting at the bottom of the hill. It was slimy and smelly. He didn't know what it was, but it made him want to slide even more! So he did. He went up the hill and slid down quickly and then back up, over and over again. It was so much fun! Every time he went down the hill, he zoomed past the disgusting thing and would laugh. Eventually, he got tired, but he had a great time!

Mum and Dad had a plan. They wanted to find some peace. So, they decided to take their polite three year old on a picnic.

On the way to the park, Dad pointed up at the sky and wanted the three year old to see the beautiful white clouds. She looked up, smiled and chirped happily.

At the park, they spread a blanket on the grass and opened their picnic basket. The three year old was happy to see some of her favourite foods inside.

After their picnic, they went for a walk. The three year old skipped through the grass laughing and playing while Mum and Dad watched with a smile.

When the sun began to set, it was time to go home. As they drove back, the three year old fell asleep in the car. When she woke up, she was happy to be home again, surrounded by peace and politeness.

Tom and Anna were playing in the park. They saw a big kangaroo with a baby in her pouch. They wanted to pet the baby kangaroo, but the mother kangaroo did not like that.

"Can we touch the baby, please?" Tom asked the mother kangaroo.

"No, you can't. The baby is mine. Go away!" the mother kangaroo said. She hopped away with her baby.

Tom and Anna were sad. They followed the mother kangaroo. They wanted to see the baby. They tried to be quiet, but the mother kangaroo heard them.

"Stop following me! You are bad children!" the mother kangaroo said. She kicked Tom and Anna with her strong legs. Tom and Anna fell down and cried.

A man who worked in the park saw what happened. He ran to help Tom and Anna. He gave them a band-aid and a hug.

"I'm sorry, kids. The mother kangaroo is very protective of her baby. She doesn't like strangers. You should not bother her," the man said.

Tom and Anna nodded. They learned their lesson. They said sorry to the mother kangaroo. They decided to play with something else.

The mother kangaroo was happy. She opened her pouch and kissed her baby. She was a successful mother. She kept her baby safe.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Peter. He was three years old and liked to play with toys. One day, he saw a nice hat. He wanted the hat for himself and picked it up.

Just then, a big man came over to Peter. The man said, "That's my hat! You must give it back," The man was very angry.

Peter felt sorry. He wanted to keep the hat and said, "Please, let me keep it."

The man became even more angry. "No! Give it back now!" he shouted.

Peter started to cry, but reluctantly gave the hat back to the man. He felt so sad. He knew he had done something wrong and said, "I'm sorry!"

The man grabbed the hat and said, "That's what you get for trying to take something that does not include you!" He then walked away with the hat.

Peter was left feeling very sad. He learned a lesson that day about including himself in something before taking it.

Once upon a time, there were two friends named Timmy and Tommy. They loved to play outside in the park every day. One day, they decided to fly a kite. The wind was different that day, and it made the kite fly higher than ever before.

Timmy said to Tommy, "Wow, this is amazing! We should record this moment!"

Tommy replied, "Yes, let's do that so we can remember how much fun we had."

They took out their phone and recorded the kite flying in the wind. They were so happy that they could watch it again and again. From that day on, they always tried to do something different every time they played in the park.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved to play outside. One day, she found a big maze made out of green bushes. She wanted to explore it but didn't know how to get through it.

Suddenly, a modern robot appeared and said, "Hello, little girl. Do you need help getting through the maze?" Lily was surprised but happy to have found a friend. "Yes, please," she said.

The robot led the way and showed Lily how to yield to the right path. They talked and laughed as they made their way through the maze. Finally, they reached the end and Lily said, "Thank you so much, Mr. Robot. You're the best!" The robot replied, "It was my pleasure, Lily. I'm glad I could help." And with that, they said goodbye and went their separate ways.

Johnny was an intelligent three year old. He wanted to climb a big tree in the park. He was so excited to get to the top. He put his first foot on the trunk and began to climb.

But as Johnny climbed higher, he started to tremble. He looked down, and the ground was so far away. He was scared to keep going.

Johnny's mum saw that Johnny was afraid. She asked him to come down. She hugged him and said, "You can try again, when you're brave enough".

Johnny felt sad, but he knew his mum was right. He tried to be brave, but he couldn't help but tremble. He decided to wait until he felt ready.

The next day, Johnny tried again. He was so determined to reach the top. This time, he didn't tremble. With lots of hard work and courage, he made it to the top!

Johnny was so proud of himself. He waved down to his mum and said, "I'm so intelligent! I made it to the top without falling!"

Once upon a time, there was a jolly cat named Tom. Tom loved to eat spaghetti. One day, Tom went to the store to buy food. He wanted to make a big meal for his friends. He made a list that included spaghetti, sauce, and cheese.

Tom cooked the spaghetti in a big pot. He added sauce and cheese. He stirred the pot with a big spoon. The smell of the spaghetti made Tom's tummy rumble. His friends would be so happy to eat this tasty meal!

When the spaghetti was ready, Tom's friends came to visit. They all sat around the table and ate the yummy spaghetti. Everyone was jolly and laughed. They all thanked Tom for the delicious meal. Tom was happy that he could make his friends smile.

Anna and Ben are friends. They live in a big city with many cars and buildings. They like to play in the park with their toys. One day, they bring their bikes to the park and ride around.

"Look at me, Anna!" Ben says. "I can go very fast!"

"I can go faster!" Anna says. She pedals hard and tries to catch up with Ben.

But then, Anna's bike makes a loud noise. She stops and looks at her bike. Her tire is flat. She feels sad.

"Ben, my bike is broken!" she cries. "I can't ride anymore!"

Ben comes back and sees Anna's bike. He feels sorry for her.

"Don't cry, Anna," he says. "I have an idea. You can replace your bike with mine. I can share with you."

"Really?" Anna says. "You are very nice, Ben. Thank you!"

They switch bikes and ride together. Anna smiles. She thinks Ben is an incredible friend. They have fun in the park. They forget about the flat tire. They are happy.

Lily and Ben are playing with their toys in the living room. Lily has a big box of crayons and Ben has a small pencil. They are drawing pictures on some paper.

"Look, Lily, I made a house!" Ben says, showing his picture to his sister.

"That's nice, Ben. But your house is very small. You need a bigger pencil," Lily says.

"No, I like my pencil. It is comfortable in my hand. And I can make fine lines with it," Ben says.

"But you can make more colors with crayons. And they are softer and brighter. Here, try one," Lily says, offering a red crayon to Ben.

Ben looks at the crayon and then at his pencil. He has an idea. He takes the crayon from Lily and attaches it to the end of his pencil with some tape. Now he has a long pencil with a crayon tip.

"Look, Lily, now I have the best of both. I can make fine lines and colors with my pencil-crayon," Ben says, smiling.

Lily is surprised and impressed. She thinks Ben is very clever. She wants to make a pencil-crayon too. She asks Ben for some tape and a crayon. Soon they both have pencil-crayons and they draw more pictures together. They are happy and proud of their creations.

Once upon a time there was a great big bear. He wanted to borrow some snow for a playdate with his friends. He asked the little fox, who was close by, if he could borrow some snow.

The fox said, “No, I can’t lend you any snow. I don't have enough for myself!”

The bear felt sad and tried to explain that he and his friends wanted to have a great snow day. But the fox still wouldn't lend him any snow.

The bear got angry and shouted, “This isn't fair!” He then decided to take some of the fox's snow without asking.

The fox was scared and started to cry. The bear ran away. Even though the bear had taken the snow he had not had a great day after all.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to go fishing with his grandpa. One day, Timmy and his grandpa went to the lake to catch some fish.

Timmy's grandpa gave him a hook and some bait. Timmy put the bait on the hook and threw it in the water. He waited and waited, but no fish came.

Timmy's grandpa said, "Imagine you caught a big fish, Timmy. What would you do?"

Timmy smiled and said, "I would clean it and cook it for dinner!"

Suddenly, Timmy felt a tug on his line. He pulled and pulled until he finally caught a big fish! Timmy was so happy. He cleaned the fish and his grandpa cooked it for dinner. It was the best meal Timmy ever had.

Tom and Lily were twins who liked to play in the woods. One day, they found a big tree with a hole in it. They wanted to see what was inside.

"Maybe there is a treasure," Tom said.

"Or a fairy," Lily said.

They took turns to peek into the hole. But they saw nothing but darkness.

"Let's go inside," Tom said. He was brave and curious.

"No, it's scary," Lily said. She was afraid and careful.

But Tom did not listen. He crawled into the hole. Lily waited outside. She heard a loud noise.

"Tom, are you okay?" she called.

Tom did not answer. Lily was worried. She crawled into the hole too. She saw Tom lying on the ground. He was not moving. He was dead.

Lily screamed. She saw what killed Tom. It was an owl. A big, angry owl. It had sharp claws and a big beak. It was hiding in the hole. It did not like visitors. It was waiting for Lily too.

The owl flew at Lily. It wanted to eat her. Lily was scared. She had no way to escape. She closed her eyes. She waited for the end.

But then, she heard another noise. A loud, happy noise. It was a surprise. It was their dog, Spot. Spot had followed them into the woods. He heard Lily scream. He ran to the tree. He saw the owl. He barked and bit the owl. He chased the owl away. He saved Lily.

Lily hugged Spot. She was glad he came. She was sad about Tom. She wished he had listened to her. She wished they had never found the hole. She wished they had played somewhere else. She wished they had stayed home.

Once upon a time, in a small house, there lived a little boy named Tim. Tim had a big nose. One day, he went outside to play in the park.

While playing, Tim met a new friend named Sam. They both loved to run and jump. As they played, Tim started to feel dizzy. He sat down on the grass and said, "Sam, I feel dizzy."

Sam looked at Tim's big nose and said, "Maybe you need to breathe through your nose more." Tim tried to breathe through his nose, and he started to feel better.

As they played more, they discovered a big tree. They climbed the tree and saw many birds. Tim and Sam laughed and played until the sun went down. They were very happy to have found each other and the big tree.

Once upon a time there was a baby squirrel called Tizzy. She was very small, but very brave. One day she decided to go and explore the forest. As she hopped along, she spotted a delicious acorn on the ground. She said to herself, "I wonder what this is?". She picked it up and took a bite. It was so yummy! She knew she had to eat it all.

Tizzy enjoyed her snack so much that she didn't notice the large fox watching her from the distance. The fox was hungry and so he decided to try some of his own delicious acorn. He crept nearer, getting closer and closer to Tizzy. When he was only a few steps away, his presence startled Tizzy and she ran away as fast as she could.

The fox chased her, but Tizzy was too fast and she managed to escape. But what had happened there left a bitter taste in her mouth. From that moment, Tizzy knew she had to be more careful when she went out exploring the forest.

Tom and Sue like to play with trains. They have a big box of trains and a long track. They make the track go around the room and under the table. They take turns to push the trains and make noises.

One day, Tom has a bad idea. He sees a big train outside the window. It is on a real track. It is very fast and loud. Tom wants to see it up close. He urges Sue to go with him.

"Come on, Sue, let's go to the big train. It will be fun. We can touch it and ride it."

Sue is scared. She knows they are not allowed to go outside alone. She knows the big train is dangerous. She shakes her head.

"No, Tom, we can't go. Mommy said to stay inside. The big train can hurt us. It is too big and too fast."

Tom does not listen. He grabs Sue's hand and pulls her. He runs to the door and opens it. He drags Sue to the street. He sees the big train coming. He runs to the track.

Sue tries to stop him. She cries and screams. She pulls his hand. She sees the big train getting closer. She sees the thick smoke and the bright light. She hears the horn and the brakes.

"Tom, stop, stop, stop! The big train will hit us! We have to go back!"

But it is too late. Tom and Sue are on the track. The big train cannot stop. It hits them with a loud crash. They fly in the air and fall on the ground. They do not move. They do not make noises. They are gone.

The end.

Once there was a girl named Mary. She was three years old and loved to explore. One day she decided to go on an adventure and explore the forest.

When Mary started her adventure, she came across a crystal lake. As she was walking, she stepped too close to the lake and slipped in! She started to sink to the bottom, until suddenly something got her hand. It was a new, shiny fork! She saved herself with it and climbed back onto the shore.

The next day, Mary was exploring the forest with her new fork. She was so happy to have found such a nifty new toy. Suddenly, she heard a loud noise from deep in the forest. It sounded like a dragon!

Frightened, Mary started running, but she slipped and fell. Her fork flew out of her hand and landed in the bushes nearby. The dragon was getting closer and closer. Finally, the fork saved her! It was so strong that it managed to keep the dragon away and help Mary get back to the safety of home.

The next day, Mary showed off her new fork to all of her friends. From that day forward, the fork was her constant companion and saved her from danger many times.

Once upon a time there was a little girl who wanted to discover something. She wanted something to be a mystery.

One day while playing in her room, she looked around her and saw her toys all organized. She thought it would be so cool if she could find a secret hiding place.

So she got to work. She opened the closet door and started searching for a place. Then, she discovered a secret panel at the back. It was the perfect place for a mystery.

The little girl was so excited - she couldn't wait to explore! She opened the panel and peeked inside.

"Oh, wow!" she said. On the shelves were lots of small boxes with decorations. This was the perfect place for a treasure.

The little girl explored the boxes and found lots of wonderful things. She was so excited to discover this amazing mystery.

"I am the best explorer ever!" she shouted. And she knew she had found a very special hiding place.

Once there was a boy who loved to play outside. He liked to pick flowers and swing in his swing. One day he was playing and he forgot to come inside for dinner. His mom got worried and called out to him. He remembered that he had forgotten to come inside and he ran to the house.

When he got there he saw something funny - his mom was wearing only one sock! His dad had to take a shower and his mom couldn't find the other sock. She asked the little boy if he knew where it was, but he had forgotten all about it.

The little boy looked around and he found the little sock right outside the door. It was filled with crumbs and the little boy looked inside. He saw some tasty-looking cookies - the sock was full of delicious cookies!

The boy was so happy that he had found the sock because now his mom could have her two socks back. He gave the sock to his mom and they all enjoyed the tasty cookies!

Once upon a time, there was a playful cat named Kitty. Kitty loved to play with her toy mouse and jump around the house. One day, Kitty found a big thing called a piano. The piano had many black and white keys that made fun sounds when Kitty pressed them with her paws.

Kitty's friend, Doggy, came over to see what the noise was. "What are you doing, Kitty?" Doggy asked. "I am playing the piano," Kitty said with a big smile. "It is so much fun! Do you want to try?" Doggy wagged his tail and said, "Yes, please!"

Kitty and Doggy played the piano together, making loud and soft sounds. They laughed and danced to the music they made. They played until they were tired and then lay down near the piano, happy with their new game. From that day on, Kitty and Doggy loved to play the piano and make music for everyone to hear.

Once, there was a lovely ladybug called Lily. She loved to explore the woods. One day, Lily wanted to make a new trail. She went out with her shovel and started to dig.

Suddenly, Lily felt a sharp pinch on her back. She felt a bit sad as she turned around to see what happened. She saw a small frog! Lily smiled.

"What are you doing?" Lily asked the frog.

The frog replied, "I'm making a trail too! I said 'hello' but you didn't hear me. So, I pinched you."

Lily said, "Let's make a trail together! We can explore the woods together. Then, we can be friends!"

The frog smiled and hopped along. Lily smiled too and together, they made a beautiful trail in the woods.

Once upon a time, there lived a big bear named True. True was always very happy, but one day he got into trouble. He was walking through the woods and he slipped on a rock. His foot mind broken. He started to feel very sad and he didn't want to move.

Suddenly, True heard a voice coming from nearby. It was a small mouse, who said the only way he could be fixed was if he believed in the power of True. True was a bit scared, but then he remembered how happy he was before and he decided to believe in the power of True.

He tried to take a step with his foot, but nothing happened. Then suddenly, his foot started to feel better. True was so happy that he started to jump around and dance. His foot was all healed and better than before.

From then on, True always believed in the power of True. Whenever he felt sad, he remembered that True would always help him. He knew that was the True way.

Ben had a parrot named Polly. Polly was a good parrot. She could talk and sing and make funny noises. Ben loved Polly very much.

One day, Ben and Polly were playing in the backyard. Ben threw a ball and Polly flew after it. But Polly flew too fast and hit a tree. Polly fell to the ground and cried. Ben ran to Polly and picked her up.

"Polly, are you okay?" Ben asked. He saw that Polly had a cut on her wing. It was red and hurt. Ben felt sad and scared.

"Polly hurt, Polly hurt!" Polly said. She was in pain and scared too.

Ben hugged Polly and said, "Don't worry, Polly. I will help you. We will go to the vet. The vet will make you better. You are my best friend, Polly. I love you."

Ben took Polly inside and told his mom what happened. His mom said, "Oh, poor Polly. Let's go to the vet right away. He will fix Polly's wing. You are a good boy, Ben. You care for Polly."

Ben and his mom got in the car and drove to the vet. The vet was a nice man. He looked at Polly's wing and said, "Polly has a small cut. It is not bad. I will clean it and put a bandage on it. Polly will be fine. She just needs some rest and love."

The vet cleaned Polly's wing and put a bandage on it. He gave Polly a treat and said, "You are a brave parrot, Polly. You will heal soon. You have a good friend, Ben. He loves you."

Polly smiled and said, "Thank you, vet. Thank you, Ben. I love you too."

Ben and his mom took Polly home. Ben put Polly in her cage and gave her some water and food. He said, "Polly, you are my best friend. I am sorry you got hurt. I will never quit playing with you. I will always be with you."

Polly said, "Ben, you are my best friend too. I am happy you helped me. I will never quit talking to you. I will always love you."

Mandy was a three year old girl who loved to explore her garden. One day, when she was running around, she saw an old and attractive structure. She felt curious and stepped closer for a better look.

Mandy asked her dad, "What is it, daddy?"

Her dad smiled and told her, "It is an old wishing well, Mandy. It needs some repairs to be restored to its former glory."

Mandy clapped her hands and said, "Let's restore it, daddy! I am sure it will be very attractive when it's finished".

Her dad nodded and agreed. Over the following weeks, they repaired the old structure with love and care. Soon they were done and Mandy ran around the garden with excitement. Sure enough, the wishing well was restored, and looked more attractive than ever.

Once upon a time there was Bob. Bob was a boy and he loved to drive. Every day he would drive around the neighbourhood in his vehicle. He would drive up hills and down roads — it was so much fun!

Bob had a unique vehicle. It was shaped like a square and it was bright yellow! It had big red wheels and it was very special.

Bob drove his vehicle all around town, every day. He drove it to the park and the beach, and even to the ice cream shop. Everyone loved his unique vehicle!

One day, all the children in Bob's neighbourhood gathered to give his vehicle a nice surprise. They decorated it all over with balloons and streamers, and Bob loved it. He drove his vehicle proudly around town with a giant smile on his face.

And that's why Bob liked to drive his vehicle all around town every day — it was always so much fun.

One day, a girl named Lily saw a big pumpkin in the garden. She wanted to make a pie with it. She asked her mom if she could take it. Her mom said yes, but she had to share it with her brother Max.

Lily was happy. She ran to the garden and picked up the pumpkin. It was heavy and round. She started to go back to the house. But on the way, she saw a rabbit. The rabbit was white and fluffy. It looked at Lily with big eyes.

Lily liked the rabbit. She wanted to play with it. She put the pumpkin down and ran after the rabbit. The rabbit ran away. Lily chased it for a long time. She forgot about the pumpkin and the pie.

Max saw the pumpkin in the garden. He wondered who left it there. He knew it was rare to find such a big pumpkin. He decided to take it and make a pie with it. He picked up the pumpkin and went to the house. He asked his mom if he could use it. His mom said yes, but he had to share it with Lily.

Max was happy. He cut the pumpkin and scooped out the seeds. He mixed the pumpkin with sugar and spice. He rolled out the dough and put the pumpkin on it. He made a nice pie and put it in the oven. He waited for it to bake.

Lily came back to the garden. She was tired and hungry. She looked for the pumpkin. But she could not find it. She saw a hole where the pumpkin was. She was sad. She wondered what happened to the pumpkin. She went to the house and asked her mom.

Her mom told her that Max took the pumpkin and made a pie with it. She said that Lily should have been more careful with the pumpkin. She said that pumpkins are rare and valuable. She said that Lily should have shared it with Max.

Lily felt sorry. She realized that she was selfish and greedy. She wished she had not chased the rabbit. She wished she had made the pie with Max. She went to Max and said sorry. She asked him if he would share the pie with her.

Max was surprised. He saw that Lily was sincere and humble. He felt sorry for her. He remembered that she was his sister and he loved her. He said sorry too. He said that he would share the pie with her. He said that they should have worked together.

Lily and Max hugged each other. They thanked their mom for the pumpkin. They cut the pie and ate it. It was delicious and sweet. They learned a lesson. They learned that pumpkins are rare and precious. They learned that sharing is caring. They learned that love is more important than pie.

Once upon a time, there was a little bird who loved to fly. One day, the bird flew too high and hit a tree. The bird fell down and hurt its wing. The bird could not fly anymore.

The bird's friend, a little girl, found the bird and took it home. She put the bird in a birdcage and gave it food and water. The bird was happy to have a new home, but it missed flying.

The little girl had an idea. She put a stick in the birdcage and the bird balanced on the stick. The bird felt like it was flying again. The bird was no longer dead inside. It was alive again. The little girl was happy to see her friend happy.

Once upon a time, there lived a little girl. Her name was Lily. One day, she went to the market. It seemed very big. Lily looked at all of the vegetables. She saw a big vegetable she liked. She wanted to buy it, but her mom said no.

Lily was sad. She said, "Momma, please let me buy the big vegetable!"

But her mom said, "No, Lily. You don't need it. It's too big for you!"

Lily felt upset. She asked, "What am I supposed to do? It looks so yummy!"

Her mom thought for a moment and then said, "Alright, I suppose you can have a small piece."

Lily was so excited, she hugged her mom and said, "Thank you!" With a big smile on her face, she took the big vegetable home.

The end.

Once upon a time there was a Mommy and Daddy who loved each other very much. But one day they had an argument and they said mean things to each other. They felt so sad and sorry.

Then Daddy had a great idea. He went to the store and bought Mommy her favorite pink pastry. He said, “I’m sorry” and gave it to Mommy.

Mommy smiled and said, “I forgive you” and they hugged. Suddenly, they were happy again! The pink pastry was a symbol of their love and showed them that they could forgive each other and be happy again.

Once upon a time, there were two friends called Tim and Tom. Tom wanted to get a powerful point. He asked Tim for help. Tim agreed and the two of them set off on a journey together.

They looked all over the countryside, but could not find a powerful point.

When they got tired, Tom said to Tim, "Let's take a break" But Tim was determined to get what his friend wanted, so he kept searching.

Finally, Tim found a powerful point but when he picked it up, the powerful point was too heavy for him. He asked Tom to help him but Tom refused--he was too scared!

The powerful point was too heavy and it dropped on Tim's foot, hurting him really bad. Tim lay there, crying. Tom had to leave him there, all alone.

The end.

Pete was excited. It was a bright, sunny day and he was allowed to play outside. He ran around and laughed as the sun shone brightly. But, eventually he started to get very hot and decided to go inside to cool off.

When he got inside, he saw his mom cooking something on the stove. Pete wanted to help, but his mom said it was too hot and he had to stay away. So, he sadly stayed back.

Soon, his mom started to yell out in surprise. Pete knew he shouldn't have, but he stepped closer to take a look. His mom cried out, "No Pete, the stove is too hot!"

Pete regretted not listening to his mom when she told him not to come close. He knew it was dangerous and he should have stayed away. He promised himself never to do it again and to always listen to warnings about the hot stove. He shone brightly with the lesson he learnt that day.

Once upon a time there was a girl who went on a wild adventure. She had a weird rag with her and it was her best friend. One day, she went deep into the forest and came across a strange creature. The creature was so weird that the girl was scared. The creature said, "Will you feed me?"

The girl was unsure what to do. She thought about the rag she had with her. She slowly took the rag out of her pocket and offered it to the creature. To her surprise, the creature was so happy! It said, "Thank you for feeding me", before it disappeared back into the forest.

The girl was glad she had her rag with her. From then on, she always kept it with her on all of her adventures. She learned that it's better to be kind to creatures, no matter how weird they may look!

Mia and her Mama had decided it was a perfect day for a beach trip. So Mia quickly put on her swimming suit and grabbed her bucket and shovel. As they opened the car door, Mia hopped out and ran towards the beach.

"Wait, Mia!", Mama said. "We still need to put on our suntan lotion!"

Mia smiled and ran back to take the bottle. She hopped over the sand until they arrived at the beach. It was full of people and Mia was so excited that she started to skip and hop around.

Mia wanted to build a sand castle, so she and Mama started to collect shells and rocks while they dug out the sand. But it wasn't as easy as Mia thought, so after a while she started to get frustrated.

Mama must have noticed because she said, "Let's take a break. Hop into the water, Mia!"

Mia was so happy! She quickly hopped into the water and the splashing was so much fun that she forgot about the sand castle. Mama and Mia stayed at the beach until the sun began to set. Mia felt so happy and content, she couldn't remember ever being this content.

One day, Sally was feeling sad. She was having a difficult time trying to find something to make her smile. She looked around and saw a sparkly angel on the floor. Immediately, Sally decided to put it back up on the shelf. She grabbed the angel and placed it carefully back up on the shelf.

Just then, she heard a small voice. It was the angel! "Thank you for putting me back," it said.

Sally was surprised. She had never heard an angel talk before. "Why did you come down from the shelf?" she asked.

The angel smiled. "I wanted to help you find something to make you happy and smile," it replied.

Sally was touched. She gave the angel a big hug and said, "Thank you. I will always remember how difficult it can be to find happiness." And with that, Sally and the angel smiled together.

Once upon a time there was a police officer. He was a very patient man. He loved his job and he would spend hours sorting things out. He was like a big detective!

Every day he would go out and sort things that were wrong. He protected people and made sure that everyone was safe. He was so patient and didn't get angry when things were hard to fix.

One time he had to help an old lady cross the road. He was so patient and sort of guided her to safety. Everyone was thankful for him.

The police officer worked so hard to keep the world safe and sort out any problems. Everyone was so grateful for his hard work, and everyone thanked him for being so patient.

Once upon a time, there was a big, fat cat named Whiskers. Whiskers loved to eat and sleep all day. One day, Whiskers' owner, a little girl named Lily, said to him, "Whiskers, you need to study how to catch mice. It will make you happy and healthy."

Whiskers didn't want to study. He just wanted to eat and sleep. But Lily was persistent. She said, "If you study, you will become a great mouse catcher and you will be able to catch all the mice you want to eat."

Finally, Whiskers agreed to study. He practiced catching mice every day. He became very good at it. Lily was proud of him and gave him lots of treats. Whiskers was happy and healthy, and he realized that studying was not so bad after all.

Once there was a car. Inside sat a girl and her mom. They drove along the road.

The girl pointed out the window at a cow. "Moooo!" said the cow. The girl laughed.

Mom looked at the cow too. "That cow looks sad," she said.

"Why sad?" asked the girl.

"The cow's leather is too weak," said Mom. "She can't work in the fields."

The girl felt sorry for the cow. "Can we help her?" she asked.

Mom smiled. "Yes, we can buy her some strong leather. But first, let's keep driving."

So, the girl and her mom drove off down the road, looking for the right kind of leather for the cow.

Tom and Jen liked to roll down the hill in the park. They had big wheels that they could sit on and go fast. They laughed and shouted as they rolled down and up again. They liked to play this game every day.

One day, they saw a big parade on the street. They saw many people and cars and flags and balloons. They wanted to see the parade better, so they rolled their wheels to the edge of the park. They saw a big truck with a loud horn and a big cake on it. They thought the cake looked yummy.

They did not see the red light or the sign that said stop. They did not hear their mom and dad calling them to come back. They only saw the big cake and wanted to get closer. They rolled their wheels onto the street, right in front of the big truck.

The big truck could not stop in time. It hit Tom and Jen and their wheels. There was a big crash and a big boom. The cake flew off the truck and landed on the ground. Tom and Jen and their wheels were broken and hurt. The people in the parade and the park were shocked and sad. The mom and dad ran to Tom and Jen and cried.

Tom and Jen did not roll down the hill anymore. They did not laugh and shout anymore. They did not play anymore. They were gone. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved to play outside. One day, she went for a walk in the woods and saw an empty house. She decided to go in and explore. As she walked around, she felt a little scared because it was very quiet and dark.

Suddenly, she heard a voice say, "Who are you?" She turned around and saw a ghost! The ghost was friendly and asked Lily why she was there. Lily said she was just exploring. The ghost said, "I like to gaze out the window and watch the animals in the woods. Do you want to join me?"

Lily was happy to have a new friend and they spent the afternoon gazing out the window together. When it was time to go home, Lily said goodbye to the ghost and promised to come back and visit. From that day on, Lily and the ghost were the best of friends and they always had fun adventures together in the woods.

Lily and Tom were twins, but they were very unique. Lily liked to play with dolls and draw with crayons. Tom liked to play with cars and build with blocks. They had different toys, different clothes, and different dreams.

One day, their mom said, "It is time to go to the park. Put on your shoes and coats and march to the door." Lily and Tom did as they were told, but they were not happy. They wanted to stay home and play with their own things.

At the park, there were many other kids. Some of them had dolls and crayons, some of them had cars and blocks. Lily and Tom wanted to join them, but they were shy. They did not know how to share or make friends.

"Hello, what are your names?" a girl asked them. She had a doll and a crayon in her hands.

"I am Lily and this is Tom. We are twins," Lily said.

"Wow, you are twins? You look very unique. Do you want to play with me?" the girl asked.

Lily nodded, but Tom shook his head. He did not like dolls or crayons. He wanted to play with cars and blocks.

"Come on, Tom, don't be rude. Let's play with the girl. Maybe she has a brother who has cars and blocks," Lily said.

"No, I don't want to. I want to go home. You are a bad sister. You always do what you want. You never do what I want," Tom said.

He ran away from Lily and the girl. He did not see where he was going. He ran into the street. He did not hear the car. He did not feel the pain. He did not see the blood.

Lily and the girl screamed. Their mom and the driver ran to Tom. They tried to help him, but it was too late. Tom was gone.

Lily cried and cried. She wished she had played with Tom. She wished she had shared her toys. She wished she had been a good sister. She wished Tom was still alive. But he was not. He was unique, and he was gone.

Once there was a little plant. It was small and looked very sad. Every day it seemed to get a little bit weaker.

But then one day something changed. The little plant started to get a bit stronger. Everyday it would grow a little bit bigger.

Soon the person looking after the plant gave the plant a test. The test was harsh and the little plant wasn't sure if it could do it. But the little plant was determined and it worked hard.

With this determination the little plant grew even bigger. Every day it got a bit bigger and bigger until it could survive on it's own. The little plant was so happy and strong.

One day, Jack saw a telephone on the table. He was very curious and he asked his mom, "Mom, what is this?" His mom explained, "It is a telephone, and you can talk to your friends and family through it." Jack thought for a moment and his eyes went wide. "Can I call my grandma now?" he asked. His mom smiled and said, "Of course! Let me show you how to use the telephone."

Jack was so excited that he could call his grandma. He listened carefully as his mom explained how to dial the number and push the buttons. After a few tries, he got it just right! When his grandma answered the phone, Jack's face beamed with joy!

Jack learned an important lesson that day: It's important to ask questions and listen carefully to understand how things work. Asking questions not only helps us learn, but it also helps us build strong relationships with our family and friends.

Lila and Ben were playing with snow in the park. They made a big snowman with a hat and a scarf. Lila wanted to be the bossy player. She told Ben what to do and how to make the snowman. Ben did not like that. He wanted to have fun and make his own snowman.

Ben said, "Stop being bossy, Lila. I want to play too. Let me make the snowman's eyes and nose." Lila said, "No, I will do it. You can make the snowman's arms and buttons." Ben was sad and angry. He did not want to play with Lila anymore.

Ben saw a big pile of snow near a tree. He ran to it and started to make his own snowman. He used rocks and sticks and leaves to make the eyes, nose, mouth, arms and buttons. He was happy and proud of his snowman. He said, "Look, Lila. I made my own snowman. He is better than yours."

Lila was jealous and mad. She did not like Ben's snowman. She said, "Your snowman is ugly and silly. Mine is bigger and prettier. Watch this." She picked up a big ball of snow and threw it at Ben's snowman. The ball of snow hit the snowman's head and made it fall off. Ben's snowman was broken.

Ben was very sad and cried. He said, "Why did you do that, Lila? You are mean and rude. You broke my snowman. I don't want to play with you anymore." Lila felt sorry and bad. She said, "I'm sorry, Ben. I was wrong and bossy. I should not have thrown the snow at your snowman. Can we be friends again?"

Ben looked at Lila and saw that she was sorry. He said, "OK, Lila. I forgive you. But you have to be nice and share. Can we make a new snowman together?" Lila said, "Yes, Ben. Let's make a new snowman together. But we have to hurry. The sun is shining and the snow will melt soon." They hugged and smiled and went to make a new snowman. They were friends again.

Once upon a time there was a yellow ghost. She was very silly and loved to play.

One day she wanted to surprise her friend so she decided to send him a present. She found some balloons and sent them to his house. When he opened his door, the balloons flew out!

He was so surprised! He asked the ghost where the balloons came from. The ghost laughed and said she had sent them.

The friend loved the surprise so much he asked the ghost to send more presents. The ghost was happy to do this and sent the friend lots of other presents.

Each time the friend opened the door, he laughed and cheered because of the surprise the yellow ghost had sent him.

Once upon a time there was a girl and a boy. The girl was very kind, and she loved to give the boy lots of kisses.

The boy was old enough to talk, but he was still very cute. He liked it when the girl kissed his face, and so he asked for more.

The girl was so happy that the boy wanted her to kiss his face, but one day the boy said something mean and stupid.

The girl felt very sad, and she didn't know what to do. Then she thought it would be nice to give the boy one more kiss on his face, to show he was sorry.

So the girl leaned in close and gave the boy a big kiss on his face. The boy was so happy, he smiled and hugged her.

The girl was glad she kissed him and everything was good again.

Once upon a time there was a big jug. It was cool and looked fun to play with. Little John wanted to keep it. So he grabbed the jug and ran home.

When he got home he put the jug in the corner of his room. He wanted to play with it, but he knew his mum would not like it. So he decided to keep it a secret.

Every day Little John got his jug out and played with it. He filled it with water and would pretend to be a pirate with it. Then he would carefully put it back and keep it hidden.

One night, Little John was playin with his jug, when suddenly his mum stormed in! Little John was so scared! But then his mum started to smile. She said she was happy that Little John was using his imagination and being creative! She said she was glad he wanted to keep the jug.

Since that day, Little John always plays with his cool jug happily.

Once upon a time, there was a silly little frog named Freddy. Freddy loved to jump around in the pond all day long. One day, he met a beautiful frog named Lily. They started to talk and Freddy asked Lily if she wanted to marry him.

Lily was surprised and asked, "Why do you want to marry me, Freddy?"

Freddy replied, "Because you are the prettiest frog in the pond and I want to be with you forever."

Lily blushed and said, "Yes, I will marry you, Freddy."

After they got married, they went to the post office to buy stamps for their wedding invitations. Freddy thought it was silly that they had to lick the stamps before putting them on the envelopes. But Lily explained that the stamps needed to stick to the envelopes so they could be delivered to their friends and family.

From that day on, Freddy and Lily were the happiest couple in the pond and they always made sure to use plenty of stamps when sending letters to their loved ones.

Johnny was a happy little boy. He loved playing with his toys and playing outside.

One day in the park, he saw a big avocado on the ground. He had never seen one before and he was so excited to try it.

He carefully picked it up and settled down on the grass with it. He delicately peeled it open and took a big bite. It was delicious! Johnny was so grateful that he had found this avocado.

The avocado made him so full that he decided to take a nap. He lay down on the grass and settled in. He was so content, knowing he had found such a special treat.

Johnny smiled as he went off to sleep, content and grateful for his avocado.

Once upon a time there was an ugly blue creature. He was very unhappy and it showed on his face. He wanted to be happy. So, he looked for something blue to make him happy. He looked and looked for something blue but he could not find anything.

Then one day, he saw a beautiful blue butterfly. He asked if he could be friends with the butterfly and the butterfly said yes! The ugly blue creature was so happy! He smiled and laughed and even did a little dance.

From that day on, the ugly blue creature was never lonely again. He and the blue butterfly were the best of friends. They were always together, playing and laughing. The ugly blue creature was so much happier.

The end.

Lily was a naughty girl. She did not like to eat her dinner. She only liked to eat cake and candy. She hid her dinner under her bed and told her mom she was full.

"Good girl, Lily. You ate all your dinner. Now you can have some cake," her mom said.

Lily was happy. She ran to the kitchen and took a big piece of cake. She ate it very fast. It was sweet and yummy. She wanted more.

She went back to the kitchen and saw another cake on the table. It was a big cake with pink frosting and sprinkles. It looked very pretty. Lily thought it was for her. She did not know it was for her mom's birthday.

She took a big bite of the cake. But it did not taste good. It tasted bad. It tasted like soap and dirt. Lily spat it out. She felt sick.

She heard her mom coming. She was scared. She ran to her bed and hid under the blanket.

Her mom came into her room. She saw the cake on the table. She saw the bite mark. She saw the dinner under the bed. She was angry.

"Lily, what did you do? You were very naughty. You did not eat your dinner. You ate my birthday cake. And you made a big mess. Why did you do that?" her mom asked.

Lily did not answer. She was sorry. She cried.

Her mom sighed. She was sad. She loved Lily, but she did not like her behavior.

She hugged Lily and said, "Lily, I love you, but you have to be a good girl. You have to eat your dinner. You have to ask before you take something. You have to say sorry when you do something wrong. Do you understand?"

Lily nodded. She said, "I'm sorry, mom. I love you too. I won't be naughty again. Can I have some water? The cake tasted bad."

Her mom smiled. She said, "Yes, you can have some water. And maybe a little piece of cake later. But first, you have to clean up your mess. And then you have to go to bed. It's late."

Lily agreed. She helped her mom clean up. She drank some water. She gave her mom a kiss. She went to bed. She dreamed of nice things. She hoped her mom would have a happy birthday.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a flexible toy snake that she loved to play with. One day, she went to the park to play with her snake. While she was playing, she saw a boy named Max. Max had a notebook in his hand.

Lily went to Max and said, "Hi! What's in your notebook?" Max replied, "It's my drawing notebook. I like to draw pictures." Lily was interested and said, "Can I see?" Max showed her his notebook and Lily was amazed. She said, "Wow! You're so good at drawing."

Max smiled and said, "Thank you! Do you want to draw with me?" Lily happily replied, "Yes, please!" They spent the rest of the afternoon drawing together and having fun. When it was time to go home, Lily said, "Thank you for letting me draw with you. I had so much fun." Max replied, "Me too! Let's do it again soon." And they both went home with big smiles on their faces.

Little Wes was walking through the garden looking for something fun. Suddenly, he spotted a big muffin sitting on the grass. His eyes lit up. He quickly ran over to it and took a big bite. It was delicious!

Little Wes was so happy that he started running around the garden, even faster than before. He was having so much fun, he didn't even notice that he had been running away from something.

Suddenly, he heard a loud laugh coming from behind him. He stopped running and slowly turned around.

There, standing in front of him, was an evil witch. She had a loud, funny laugh, and she was looking very mischievous.

Little Wes knew he was in trouble. He was about to escape when the witch pointed her finger at him. Suddenly, he felt a powerful force pull him towards the witch.

However, Little Wes was brave and determined. He closed his eyes tightly, and with a big burst of energy he was gone—escaping the clutches of the evil witch.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to draw and color with his markers. One day, Timmy's mom bought him a new tool to draw with, a tough pencil.

Timmy was so excited to use his new tool, but when he tried to draw with it, he found it difficult. He couldn't make the same marks he could with his markers. Timmy's mom saw he was struggling and said, "Timmy, just keep practicing and soon you'll be able to make great marks with your new tool."

Timmy listened to his mom and kept practicing. Soon, he was able to make amazing drawings with his tough pencil. Timmy learned that sometimes things are tough at first, but with practice and patience, you can do anything you want.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily had a favorite cup that she used every day to drink her milk. One day, Lily accidentally dropped her cup and it broke into many little pieces. Lily was very sad and anxious because she loved her cup so much.

But then, Lily's mom came up with an idea. She said, "Don't worry Lily, we can replace your cup with a new one!" So, they went to the store and picked out a new cup that looked just like the old one. Lily was so happy and hugged her new cup tightly.

From that day on, Lily learned that even when things break, there is always a way to replace them and make them new again. And she learned that it's okay to feel anxious sometimes, but there is always someone who can help make things better.

Ben and Lily were going to the park with Mom. They got in the car and put on their seat belts. Mom said, "Close your buckles, please. It is safe and normal to wear them." Ben and Lily closed their buckles and heard a click. They smiled at Mom.

On the way to the park, they saw a big truck. It was red and loud. It had a lot of boxes on the back. Ben and Lily wondered what was inside the boxes. Maybe toys, or books, or candy. They asked Mom, "What is in the boxes, Mom?"

Mom said, "I don't know, sweeties. Maybe the truck is taking them to a store, or a school, or a home. Maybe someone will open them and find a surprise." Ben and Lily liked surprises. They imagined what they would like to find in a box.

They reached the park and got out of the car. They opened their buckles and heard a click. They ran to the swings and the slide. They had fun playing and laughing. They forgot about the truck and the boxes. They were happy to be at the park with Mom.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a cat named Mittens who loved to play with yarn. One day, Lily saw a big red mailbox on the corner of her street. She asked her mommy what it was for and her mommy said, "It's where you can mail letters to your friends and family."

Lily was so happy to hear this because she wanted to mail a letter to her grandma who lived far away. She wrote a letter to her grandma and put it in the mailbox. She waited and waited for a response from her grandma.

One day, Mittens disappeared and Lily was very sad. She looked everywhere for him but couldn't find him. Then, one day, she heard a meowing sound coming from the mailbox. She opened it and there was Mittens, happy and safe inside! It turned out that he had climbed into the mailbox and gotten stuck, but someone had heard him meowing and rescued him.

From then on, Lily was always careful to check the mailbox before she mailed anything, just in case Mittens was inside again.

One day, a little girl named Joanna was walking through a field when she noticed something strange. She saw a vine growing up the side of a nearby tree trunk. She decided to take her chances and requested the vine to move so she could get back home. The vine stirred and replied in a grouchy voice: "Why should I do that for you?"

Joanna was so surprised that the vine was talking that she was speechless. Sensing her surprise the vine went on to explain that it has angrier than usual because no one ever requested its help before.

Joanna felt sorry for the vine and offered to help it in any way she could. The vine asked her to find some friends so that it could have some company. Joanna happily agreed and promised to come back with some friends.

The vine settled down once Joanna left, looking forward to her return. Joanna kept her promise and that weekend she brought her friends to meet the vine. They all had a great time playing and talking with the vine. It was so happy that it promised to move every time Joanna requested. Joanna smiled, feeling like she had made a new friend.

Once upon a time, there was a little fish named Bubbles. Bubbles lived in a big ocean with lots of other fish. One day, Bubbles saw a big hook in the water. He knew it was dangerous, so he swam away quickly.

Bubbles wanted to perform a trick to impress his fish friends. He practiced jumping out of the water and doing flips. He felt very proud of himself when he finally got it right.

Later that day, Bubbles found a comfortable spot to rest. He snuggled up in some seaweed and felt very cozy. He was happy to have a safe place to relax after his exciting day.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play soccer with her friends. One day, they had a big game against another team. Lily was very nervous because she wanted her team to win.

During the game, Lily's team was losing. But Lily didn't give up. She kept playing and trying her best. Her friend, Max, saw how brave she was being and said, "Lily, you're doing great! I hope we can still score a goal."

Lily smiled and felt better. She kept playing and finally, with only a few minutes left, her team scored a goal! They won the game and Lily was so happy. She knew that even though they were losing, she had hope and kept trying.

Once upon a time there lived a mighty hunter. He lived in a small house in the middle of a great forest. Every day he would wander through the forest, looking for animals to hunt.

One morning, the hunter was on his way to hunt for his dinner, but he stopped in his tracks. He heard a high-pitched noise coming from a nearby creek. He looked around and found a small baby squirrel in peril. Its tiny legs were stuck in the mud and it couldn't escape.

The hunter thought for a moment and then decided to delay his hunt. Instead, he gently moved the small animal from the mud and placed it on a nearby tree branch. The squirrel happily chattered at the hunter before scurrying away.

The hunter smiled and continued on his way, safe in the knowledge that his kindness had saved the small animal. From then on, he was known as the mighty hunter who always helped anything in need.

Once there was a little girl named Jane who wanted to be a Superhero. One day in her backyard, she found a box of steel. It was very heavy, so she needed help from her Parents. With their help, she was able to turn the steel into a cape and it fit perfectly!

Jane was so excited and put on her cape. She twirled and twirled again, so happy to be a superhero. She imagined she could fly, run super fast and help people.

Jane decided to make some shoes too so she could fly. She got a big hammer and tried to turn the steel into shoes but they were too heavy. Jane and her Parents kept trying, but in the end, Jane decided it was better to just keep it simple and she used the steel to make a helmet.

Jane was so proud of the helmet. With it on, she felt like a real superhero. Jane ran around the yard pretending to rescue people in need and with her heavy steel helmet, she knew she was ready for anything!

Once upon a time, there was a tall duck who liked to swim in the pond. He was happy and quacked loudly. One day, a hunter came to the pond with a gun. He wanted to shoot the duck. The poor duck didn't know what was happening and continued to swim. Suddenly, the hunter shot the duck and he fell to the ground. The other ducks were sad and they quacked quietly. The hunter took the duck away and the pond was never the same again.

John and Grace were discussing a package. They wanted to find the perfect present for their friend. After looking around, they eventually decided to buy a cute little puppy.

The puppy was so adorable. John and Grace knew their friend would love him. So they went ahead and bought him.

John and Grace took the puppy home. They started playing with him, but the puppy ended up hurting himself. They took him to the vet, but it was too late. The puppy had died.

John and Grace were so sad. They knew their friend had wanted the puppy so much. They realized they made a mistake, and that the package was not a good present at all.

Lily and Tom were twins who liked to play outside. One day, they found a big ladder near their house. They wanted to see what was on the roof, so they climbed up the ladder. They saw many things on the roof: leaves, sticks, stones, and a bird's nest.

"Look, Tom, a bird's nest!" Lily said. "Let's take it and play with it."

"No, Lily, that's not nice. The bird needs its nest. We should leave it alone." Tom said.

But Lily did not listen. She grabbed the nest and ran down the ladder. Tom followed her. The bird saw what Lily did and was very angry. It flew after Lily and pecked her hair.

"Ow, ow, ow!" Lily cried. "Tom, help me!"

Tom ran to Lily and tried to shoo the bird away. He said, "Lily, you should not have taken the nest. That was the bird's home. How would you feel if someone took your home?"

Lily felt sorry. She said, "You're right, Tom. I was wrong. I'm sorry, bird. Here, take your nest back." She put the nest on the ground and the bird flew to it. It stopped pecking Lily and made a happy sound.

Lily and Tom learned a lesson. They learned to respect other living things and their homes. They also learned to clean the roof and put the ladder back where they found it. They never climbed the roof again.

Once upon a time, there was a daddy who was going on a long trip. He was very worried, so he wanted to give his daughter a special gift before he left. He gave her a bubble.

The daughter thanked her dad and carefully put the bubble on her shelf. She loved to watch it shine! Every night, she said to it: "Hello Bubble, you and me will be friends forever."

One day, the daughter waved her hand and noticed the bubble was waiting for her. She was so excited and stretched her hand to grab it. Suddenly, the bubble popped! She was very sad.

After that, the daddy took his daughter on the trip. He showed her many wonderful things. But the daughter still felt down about the bubble.

The daddy said to his daughter: "Sometimes, when things are too special we can get too worried. We should just be happy and enjoy the present. Then happy moments will last forever."

The daughter hugged her dad and knew he was right. She smiled and the two of them enjoyed the rest of the trip together.

Tom and Sam are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a man with a stick in his mouth. The stick makes smoke. Tom and Sam are curious.

"Hello, man. What is that?" Tom asks.

"This is a cigarette. It helps me relax. Do you want to try?" the man says.

Tom and Sam shake their heads. They know cigarettes are bad. They make people sick and smell bad.

"No, thank you. Cigarettes are stupid. They hurt your lungs and teeth. We don't want to smoke," Sam says.

The man laughs. He thinks Tom and Sam are silly. He blows smoke in their faces. Tom and Sam cough and run away.

"Hey, come back. Don't be afraid. Smoking is cool. You are missing out," the man says.

Tom and Sam ignore him. They find a bench and sit down. They see a dog. The dog is friendly. He wags his tail and licks their hands. Tom and Sam pet the dog. They like the dog.

"Hello, dog. What is your name?" Tom asks.

The dog barks. He does not have a name. He is a stray. He is hungry and lonely.

"Can we be your friends?" Sam asks.

The dog nods. He is happy. He likes Tom and Sam. They share their snacks with him. They play fetch with him. They hug him.

"You are a good dog. We love you," Tom and Sam say.

The dog loves them too. He bites the man's cigarette and spits it out. The man is angry. He yells at the dog. He tries to kick the dog. Tom and Sam protect the dog. They bite the man's leg. The man screams and runs away.

"Good job, dog. You are brave. You saved us from the smoke," Tom and Sam say.

The dog barks. He is proud. He thanks Tom and Sam. They thank him too. They decide to adopt him. They name him Spot. They take him home. They give him a bath, a bed, and a collar. They are a family.

The moral of the story is: Smoking is bad for you and others. It is not cool or relaxing. It is stupid and harmful. Friends are good for you and others. They are not silly or afraid. They are kind and helpful. Friends are the best.

Lily was a little girl who liked to play with her toys. She had a big teddy bear, a yellow ball, a red car and a blue doll. She put them all on her bed and made them talk to each other. She had fun with her toys until it was time to sleep.

She said good night to her toys and hugged her teddy bear. She closed her eyes and dreamed of happy things. She dreamed of going to the park, eating ice cream, and riding a bike. She smiled in her sleep.

But in the middle of the night, she heard a loud noise. It was a thunder. It made a boom sound and flashed a bright light. Lily was scared. She opened her eyes and saw the dark room. She wanted to turn on the lamp, but it was too far. She tried to reach it, but she could not. She felt alone and sad.

She looked at her toys. They were still on her bed, but they did not talk to her. They were quiet and still. She wished they could help her. She reached for her blue doll, but it was rough. It had a button eye that poked her hand. She did not like it. She reached for her red car, but it was hard. It had a sharp edge that scratched her arm. She did not like it. She reached for her yellow ball, but it was cold. It had a wet spot that made her shiver. She did not like it.

She reached for her teddy bear, but it was gone. She looked around and saw it on the floor. It had fallen off the bed. She felt sorry for her teddy bear. It was soft and warm and cuddly. She liked it. She wanted to get it, but she was afraid of the dark. She did not know what was under the bed. She did not know what was in the closet. She did not know what was outside the window.

She cried for her teddy bear. She cried for her mom. She cried for the light. She wished the thunder would stop. She wished the morning would come. She wished she could wake up from the bad dream.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who loved to swim in the lake. She had a big yellow board that she would hold onto. One day, the little girl got in the water with her board. She wanted to swim really far.

She paddled and paddled, but she couldn't get to the other side of the lake. She was getting tired and frustrated.

The little girl stayed in the water for a while, feeling discouraged. Suddenly, she felt a gentle current start to pull her across the lake. She paddled and the current kept taking her farther and farther. She ended up on the other side!
