They started again and this time, they made the biggest tower they had ever made. Her brother was so happy and they both laughed and played together for hours. From that day on, they always played together and built the biggest and strongest towers.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily loved Tuesdays because that was the day she got to go to the park with her mommy. They would swing and slide and have so much fun.

One Tuesday, Lily brought her new toy to the park. It was a useful toy that could spin and light up. But when Lily went to play on the slide, another little boy took her toy and wouldn't give it back. Lily was sad and didn't know what to do.

Her mommy noticed she was upset and asked what was wrong. Lily told her what happened and her mommy said, "Let's go talk to the little boy and ask him to give your toy back." So they walked over to the little boy and Lily's mommy said, "Excuse me, can you please give Lily's toy back? It's very important to her." The little boy said sorry and gave the toy back. Lily was happy and they all sat down to play together.

Once upon a time, there was a cute little bunny. The bunny loved to play in the park and eat carrots. One day, the bunny's mommy wanted to have some tea, so she asked the bunny to come inside. The bunny followed his mommy inside and watched her make the tea.

After they had their tea, the bunny's daddy came home and asked if they wanted to go for a drive. The bunny got very excited and jumped up and down. They all got in the car and drove to the beach. The bunny loved feeling the wind in his fur and seeing all the pretty colors of the sky.

When they got back home, the bunny was very tired from all the fun. He snuggled up with his mommy and daddy and fell asleep. From that day on, the bunny loved going for drives and having tea with his family.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy had a big alarm clock in his room that would ring really loud in the morning to wake him up. But one day, the alarm clock was broken and it didn't ring anymore.

Timmy's mom told him that they needed to go to the store to buy a new alarm clock. They got into the car and drove to the store. At the store, Timmy saw a red alarm clock that he really liked. His mom bought it for him and they went back home.

The next morning, Timmy woke up to the sound of his new alarm clock. It had a mild sound that was much nicer than the old one. Timmy was happy that he could wake up on time for school. He passed his mom in the hallway and said, "Thanks for buying me the new alarm clock, Mom!"

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his toys and run around outside. One day, Timmy fell down and hurt his knee. He cried and cried because it hurt so much.

His mommy came over and picked him up. She hugged him and said, "Don't worry, Timmy. It's okay. I'm here to comfort you." She gave him a snack, a yummy apple, to make him feel better.

After a little while, Timmy's knee started to feel normal again. He smiled and went back to playing with his toys. He was happy because his mommy was there to make him feel better.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to eat cereal in the morning. One day, she got a surprise when she saw her mom had put her cereal in a big bowl with her favorite cartoon character on it. Lily was so happy!

She sat down at the table and ate her cereal. The bowl was so big that she could have eaten all day! It made her feel peaceful and happy. After she finished her cereal, she gave her mom a big hug and said thank you for the surprise bowl. From that day on, every morning Lily would eat her cereal in her special bowl and it always made her feel peaceful and happy.

Sara and Ben are friends. They like to go to the zoo with their moms. The zoo has many animals. Sara and Ben want to see the monkeys. They run to the monkey house.

"Look, Ben, the monkeys are hanging from the trees!" Sara says. She points to the brown and black monkeys. They swing and jump and make funny noises.

"Wow, they are so cool!" Ben says. He tries to hang from a branch like a monkey. He falls down and laughs.

The moms come to the monkey house. They smile at Sara and Ben.

"Are you having fun, kids?" Sara's mom asks.

"Yes, mom, we love the monkeys!" Sara says.

"Do you want to see more animals?" Ben's mom asks.

"Yes, mom, we want to see more!" Ben says.

"OK, then, let's go on a tour of the zoo. Follow me, kids!" Sara's mom says. She holds Sara's hand and Ben's mom holds Ben's hand. They walk to the next animal house.

Sara and Ben see many animals on the tour. They see lions and tigers and bears. They see elephants and giraffes and zebras. They see penguins and seals and flamingos. They see snakes and frogs and turtles.

Sara and Ben like all the animals. But they like the monkeys the best. They think the monkeys are the most fun.

"Look, Sara, that monkey is taller than you!" Ben says. He points to a big monkey with a long tail.

"Wow, he is taller than me!" Sara says. She stands next to the monkey and compares their heights.

The monkey looks at Sara and Ben. He smiles and waves his tail. Sara and Ben wave back. They laugh and clap their hands.

The moms take pictures of Sara and Ben and the monkey. They are happy to see their kids enjoy the zoo. They hug and thank the monkey for being friendly.

Sara and Ben say goodbye to the monkey. They say goodbye to the other animals. They say thank you to the zoo. They have a great day. They are happy.

Once upon a time there was a yacht. It floated in the deep blue sea. The yacht was big and white and shiny. The people who lived in the yacht were happy.

One day, the people on the yacht wanted to add something special. They asked a friendly fish. The fish gave them a disgusting old shell. The people laughed but they decided to add it to the yacht.

The people decorated the shell with shiny pain and blue ribbons. It looked lovely. The people added it to the yacht and the yacht looked even better! Everyone on the yacht was so happy.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his toys, but his favorite toy was a noisy robot. One day, Timmy's robot broke and he needed to fix it.

Timmy went to his dad and said, "Daddy, please help me fix my robot."

Dad said, "Sure, Timmy. Let's go to the garage and find a screw to fix it."

In the garage, Timmy and his dad looked for a screw. They found one and dad used a tool to fix the robot.

Timmy was so happy that his robot was fixed. He hugged his dad and said, "Thank you, daddy. You are the best!"

Once upon a time, in a small house, there lived a girl named Lily. She had a great big smile and loved to draw. One sunny day, she decided to make a picture for her friend, Sam.

Lily took her crayons and drew a big, happy sun. She also drew some pretty flowers and a cute little dog. When she finished, she looked at her picture and was very happy with it.

Lily went to Sam's house to give him the picture. When she arrived, Sam's mom opened the door and said, "Welcome, Lily! Sam is in his room." Lily went to Sam's room and showed him the picture. Sam loved it so much and gave Lily a big hug. They both felt great and spent the rest of the day playing together.

Once upon a time, there were two brave friends: Tom and Sue. Tom and Sue were best friends and were always looking for new adventures.

One day, Tom said, “Let’s go on a tour!” So the two brave friends went out for a fun tour. They saw lots of exciting things like mountains, trees, and lakes.

They got to the top of a very tall hill and Tom said, “Let’s roll down!” Sue said, “That sounds fun!” So they both rolled down the hill together, laughing the whole time.

At the bottom of the hill, they stopped and hugged each other. It was the best tour they ever went on!

Once upon a time there was a boy named Tom. He was three years old and he loved chocolate.

Every Friday night Tom's parents would let him pick his favorite chocolate from the store. Tom always picked the same one: it was smooth, shiny and yummy.

One day, Tom was eating his yummy chocolate when his mommy came in.

Tom's Mommy said, "Hey Tommy, I wanted to tell you something special. You know how Daddy and I love each other?"

Tom nodded and said, "Yeah, yeah!"

His Mommy said, "Well, Daddy and I are going to get married!"

Tom smiled and said, "Yay! Yummy chocolate!"

So the next day Tom and his parents went to a big party to celebrate the happy day when Mommy and Daddy would marry. Everyone was happy and Tom ate lots of delicious smooth chocolate and had lots of fun.

And they all lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Ruby. She was only three years old and she loved to play. One day, Ruby's parents introduced her to TV. It was a big, white box with lots of colors and noises. Ruby was so excited when she saw the TV!

Ruby's parents explained to her that TV was good as it could teach her lots of things. They told her that it could teach her how to count, how to color and how to tell stories. Ruby was so excited that she started playing with the TV.

She watched it for hours until her parents had to turn it off and tell her it was time for dinner. Ruby was very upset and started to cry. She was so sad to turn off the TV.

Her parents hugged her and told her that there was a lesson in all of this. They said that TV was great, but that it also had to be used in moderation. They said that she could watch it everyday, but not all day. She would have to play different games, go out and make use of her imagination.

Ruby understood and was now happy. She was glad that her parents had introduced her to TV but made sure that it was only used in moderation.

Once there was a boy named Steve. He was very competitive and always wanted to be the best.

One day, Steve saw a big ball and he ran over to grab it. But a big girl also wanted the ball. She yelled out "Stop!"

Steve was scared. He let go of the ball and ran away. The girl shouted, "Come back here!"

The girl was a police officer. She put Steve in jail because she thought he'd taken her ball. But Steve hadn't taken it. So he had to stay in jail for a while.

After a few days, the police officer found out that Steve hadn't taken the ball. So she let Steve go. He was very happy to be free.

From then on, Steve was very careful about grabbing things he didn't own. He wanted to make sure he never went to jail again!

Once upon a time, there were two friends called Jack and Jill. Jack liked to carry things around, but Jill was a bit bossy.

Today, Jack found a special handle in the park. He wanted to show Jill, so he picked it up and carried it with him. "Hey, look what I found!" he said to Jill.

Jill was very bossy and said, "That's mine! Give it back to me!" Jack knew that Jill was always bossy, so he gave it back to her.

Jill said, "Thank you Jack. This handle is really special." She gave him a hug and said, "You are a really good friend."

Jack was happy that he helped his friend and they went off to play together.

Once upon a time, there was a barber. He was very serious and worked hard all day. Every day, people passed by his shop and he would call out to them inviting them to get their hair cut.

One day, a little 3-year-old boy named Timmy passed by. The barber smiled and called out, but Timmy was too shy and stayed away.

So, the barber got an idea. He took out a simple brush and said to Timmy, "Would you like me to brush your hair?" Timmy was so excited and nodded his head.

The barber carefully brushed his hair, making it neat and tidy. Timmy loved it! He waved goodbye to the barber and ran off.

The barber smiled as he watched Timmy go. He knew his kindness had made the serious barber happy!

Once there was a little dog named Bob. Bob was a small, hairy pup. He loved running around outside, chasing after all the other animals.

One day, Bob wanted to get the best view of everything in the park. He saw a tall stand and decided to climb it. But Bob didn't have any paws to help him grip, so he started to slip.

Just then, he heard a loud SNAP, and a shining white hand appeared near the top of the stand. Bob looked up to see a kind stranger smiling down at him.

The stranger said, "Hi there, little pup. Don't worry, I'll help you. Just grab my hand and you can make it up here!"

Bob grabbed the stranger's hand and she pulled him up to the top of the stand. From there, Bob could see everything. He wagged his tail with delight.

The stranger smiled and said, "You were quite brave for a little pup. Now, let's get you back down safe." And with another SNAP, the stranger was gone.

And Bob? Well, he was just as happy as could be. He sauntered off, happily exploring the park with a new view from above.

Once upon a time, there was a bald man. He was feeling really hungry and he looked around the kitchen to find something to eat. He saw a big bunch of celery and thought that he could eat it. He leaned down and picked it up. He liked the taste of the celery and ate it all.

The man then went outside to take a walk in the sunshine. He leaned against a big tree and felt himself relaxing. He closed his eyes and let the sunshine warm his face. It felt really good.

He decided he should go back inside and get something else to eat. When he got to the kitchen, he saw another bunch of celery. He leaned down to pick it up and realized that it was even bigger than the one he had eaten earlier. He was so happy and quickly started eating it.

He enjoyed his snack and decided that he should always keep some celery in the kitchen. That way, he'd never have to go hungry again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play in her garden. Her garden was very pretty and had lots of flowers. One day, Lily's mom told her that she would receive a surprise package in the mail. Lily was so excited! She waited and waited for the package to arrive. Finally, the mailman came and gave her the package. Lily opened it and found a new toy to play with in her clean garden. She was so happy! She played with her new toy in the garden all day long. The end.

Once upon a time, there lived a little bunny who loved to explore. One day, the little bunny hopped to the edge of a cliff. He looked over the edge, and it was really high! He asked himself, "What should I do?"

Suddenly, he heard a voice. Looking up, he saw a large, grey bird above him. The bird asked, "Do you want to come with me?"

The bunny was scared, so he was quiet. "Come on, let's go!" said the bird.

The bunny thought for a moment and then he replied, "Yes!" He hopped onto the bird and they flew off. The wind was cold and the sky was very far away. When they reached the other side of the cliff, it was very rough and rocky.

The bunny was very brave and he hopped off the bird. He looked around and saw a big, open meadow. He thanked the bird for taking him there.

"You're welcome," replied the bird. The bunny hopped away and the bird flew off in the direction of the cliff.

The bunny hopped around the meadow and explored for the rest of the day. He liked the rough ground, and he was happy that he had trusted the bird.

The End.

Susie was playing at the beach. She picked up a shell and held it in her hand. She could feel how smooth and hard it was and it looked so pretty. She thought it would be a great toy to play with.

Susie carried the shell around the beach and stopped to look at all the other shells. She put her shell down and paused to look around. She saw a healthy looking seagull flying around in the bright blue sky.

Susie decided to take her shell and explore the other parts of the beach. She wanted to find more shells like the one she was holding. She looked and looked and eventually found another shell, but this one was bigger than the one she already had!

Susie smiled as she looked around the beach. She had a lot of healthy shells to play with now. She was so happy that she decided to stay a bit longer and enjoy her new shells.

Mommy was getting ready to cook dinner. She explained to her 3 year old daughter what they were going to have. The daughter smiled and got excited when Mommy said they were having "fancy shrimp." Mommy explained that fancy shrimp was different than the normal kind because it was bigger, better and tastier. The daughter watched as Mommy cooked the shrimp with special spices. When dinner was ready, the daughter eagerly ate the shrimp. It was delicious! Mommy smiled and explained that the fancy shrimp made dinner extra special. They both had a wonderful dinner time together.

Once upon a time, there was a boy called Bob. Bob was very creative, so he loved to make things. One day, he wanted to make something different. He had an idea - what if he mixed some lotion with some other things?

So, he grabbed some lotion, and mixed it with some crayons and paint. Then, he carefully mixed it all together. He was so excited to see what would happen!

He took the mixture outside and threw it up in the air. It created a beautiful rainbow in the sky! Bob was so happy with his creation, and he thanked the lotion for helping him make it.

Bob was very proud of himself for being so creative with the lotion!

Lily and Ben were playing with their toys in the living room. Lily had a big doll and Ben had a small car. Lily liked her doll very much, but she wished she had a car too. She asked Ben if she could play with his car for a while.

"No, this is my car. You have your doll. Go away!" Ben said. He was not very friendly.

Lily felt sad and angry. She wanted to have a car too. She thought of a plan. She saw a bottle on the table. It had a label that said "shrink". She did not know what that word meant, but she thought it might make things smaller. She took the bottle and sprayed some of it on Ben's car.

Ben saw what Lily did and shouted. "Hey, what are you doing? Stop it! You are making my car shrink!"

Lily laughed. She thought it was funny to see Ben's car get smaller and smaller. She picked up the tiny car and put it in her pocket. She said, "Now I have a car too. And you have nothing. Ha ha!"

Ben was very upset. He cried and ran to his mom. He told her what Lily did. Mom was not happy. She scolded Lily and made her give back the car. She said, "Lily, that was not nice. You should not take things that are not yours. And you should not use things that you do not understand. You could have hurt Ben or yourself. You need to say sorry to Ben and share your toys."

Lily felt sorry. She realized she was wrong. She gave back the car to Ben and said, "I'm sorry, Ben. I was mean. I should not have sprayed your car. Can we be friends again?"

Ben was still sad, but he forgave Lily. He said, "It's okay, Lily. I'm sorry too. I should have been more friendly. Can we play together?"

Lily and Ben hugged and smiled. They decided to play together and share their toys. They learned a lesson. They wished they would never fight again.

Tom and Mia are friends. They like to play outside. One day, they see a big puddle of water. It is brown and muddy.

"Let's splash in the puddle!" Tom says. He runs to the puddle and jumps in. He makes a big splash. Water goes everywhere.

"Me too!" Mia says. She follows Tom and jumps in the puddle. She makes a bigger splash. Water goes on Tom's face.

"Hey, that's not fair!" Tom says. He splashes water back at Mia. Mia laughs and splashes water at Tom. They have fun.

But then, they hear a voice. It is Tom's mom. She is angry.

"Tom! Mia! What are you doing? You are so dirty! Look at your clothes! Look at your body! Come here right now!" she says.

Tom and Mia stop splashing. They look at each other. They are wet and muddy. They feel bad.

"Sorry, mom," Tom says.

"Sorry, mom," Mia says.

They walk to Tom's mom. She takes them inside. She gives them a bath. She washes their body and their clothes. She makes them clean.

"Next time, don't splash in the puddle," she says.

"Okay, mom," Tom says.

"Okay, mom," Mia says.

They hug their mom. They are still friends. They still like to play outside. But they don't splash in the puddle anymore.

One day, there was a small boy, and he was walking in the woods all on his own. He had a small sack in his hand. Suddenly, the day grew very cold and the boy began to shiver. He looked up and saw that the sky had gone grey and everything was very still. The boy was miserable.

He did not know what to do, so he looked around for shelter. He saw a cave and decided to go inside. It was very dark and he could see his breath in the air.

He curled up into a ball and hugged his sack, trying to keep warm. Suddenly, the temperature dropped even further and the boy felt like his skin was starting to freeze. Everything around him had gone silent, and the boy was scared.

Outside the cave, he could hear the wind starting to blow and he knew that it was winter. Soon the ground was covered in a thick layer of snow. The boy was very happy because now he was warm and safe.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who liked to pick things up. She was picking things up everywhere she went – in the garden, in the park and even by the side of the road. One day, she spotted something special - a shiny pick. She jeaped over and grabbed it, proud that she could pick it up.

The girl skipped away with her prize, wanting to show her mum. Suddenly, she heard a noise. It was a car coming around the corner. It was coming very fast and the little girl had to move quickly. She ran as fast as she could, with tears in her eyes, and made it back home safely.

She showed her mum what she had picked up. "Wow!" said her mum. "That's a very special pick. You must have been very brave to pick it up with a car coming so tight!" The little girl smiled with pride. She had learned a lesson -Don't speed too close to a pick!

Max was a little kid who loved to speed around his backyard. He would run as fast as his little legs could go. One day, his parents saw the way he was running around the yard and they both laughed. They thought it was so funny watching him speed around.

Max's parents had an idea. They built him a go-kart and filled it with gas. Then, they took Max out to the road. Max was so excited! His parents told him to go as fast as he could. He pressed the gas and went really fast. He sped down the road in his go-kart. He was so happy!

Max was feeling a bit brave so he decided to race his parents. He flew down the road and his parents followed behind. He was going so fast he felt like he might fly away. Suddenly, his parent's car flew past him and won the race.

Max's parents were so proud. They laughed and said that Max was a really good racer. Max smiled and thought that his parents were so crazy for racing him. He had never felt so excited in his life!

Jill and Tom were bored. They had no toys to play with and no books to read. They looked out the window and saw a big orange truck. It was making loud noises and digging a hole in the street.

"Let's go see the truck!" Tom said. He grabbed Jill's hand and ran to the door.

"No, we can't!" Jill said. "Mom said we have to stay inside. It's not safe outside."

"But I want to see the truck!" Tom said. He pulled Jill's hand harder.

Jill sighed. She did not want to make Tom sad, but she did not want to make Mom mad. She had an idea. She let go of Tom's hand and ran to the kitchen. She opened a drawer and took out a small green box. It had a picture of a mint leaf on it.

"Look, Tom!" Jill said. "I have a surprise for you. It's a mint candy. It's sweet and fresh. Do you want to try it?"

Tom's eyes lit up. He liked candy. He ran to Jill and took the green box. He opened it and saw a shiny white candy. He put it in his mouth and smiled.

"Mmm, this is good!" Tom said. "Thank you, Jill!"

Jill smiled too. She was happy that Tom was happy. She took another candy and put it in her mouth. They sat on the couch and ate the mint candies. They forgot about the orange truck and the hole in the street. They were not bored anymore. They were just happy.

Once upon a time there were two friends, Sam and Joe. Sam was a bunny and Joe was a bear. Every day, Sam would insist that Joe play with him. But Joe was lazy and never wanted to play.

On day Sam had an idea. He went to Joe's house with a journal. Sam opened the journal and said to Joe, "Let’s make stories together! I will draw pictures and you can tell me stories about them."

Joe wasn't so sure. He said, "It sounds like a lot of work."

But Sam insisted. He said, "Come on! It won’t be boring, I promise!"

Finally, Joe agreed. They made funny stories and drew pictures in the journal all day. In the end, Joe was glad he listened to Sam and had so much fun.

One sunny day Amy went out for a walk. She saw a rose in the grass. She bent down and looked at it. It was red and so pretty. Amy reached out and touched it. The petals were wet. She looked up and saw the sky was full of sunshine. Amy smiled and continued her walk.

Later, Amy saw a park. She went inside and saw many children playing. She asked a girl for a turn and the girl handed her a rose. Amy looked at it and saw it was red. She held it close to her and felt its wet petals.

Amy looked at the girl and smiled. The girl smiled too. Amy thanked her and went on her way. She still had the rose in her hand and could feel the wet petals against her skin. She smiled again and went back home.

Lily and Max were going to Grandma's house for the weekend. They packed their bags with clothes, toys and books. They were very excited to see Grandma and play in her big garden.

When they got to Grandma's house, they ran to hug her and say hello. Grandma smiled and said, "Welcome, my sweeties! Come, let me show you your room." She took them upstairs to a cozy room with two beds and a window. "You can unpack your bags and make yourselves comfortable," she said.

Lily and Max opened their bags and started to unpack. Lily took out her clothes and put them in a drawer. She took out her toys and put them on a shelf. She took out her books and put them on a nightstand. She was very neat and organized.

Max took out his clothes and threw them on the floor. He took out his toys and scattered them on the bed. He took out his books and tossed them on the chair. He was very messy and careless.

Lily looked at Max's side of the room and felt frustrated. She said, "Max, you have to unpack properly. You can't leave your things everywhere. Grandma will be upset if she sees this."

Max shrugged and said, "I don't care. I want to go outside and play. Come on, let's go." He grabbed Lily's hand and pulled her to the door.

Lily said, "Wait, Max. We have to finish unpacking. And we have to say thank you to Grandma for letting us stay here."

Max said, "Fine, fine. Let's go say thank you and then go outside." He dragged Lily downstairs to find Grandma.

Grandma was in the kitchen, making cookies. She smiled when she saw Lily and Max. She said, "Did you unpack your bags? Do you like your room?"

Lily said, "Yes, Grandma. Thank you for the room. It's very nice. But Max didn't unpack properly. He made a big mess."

Grandma said, "Oh, dear. Max, you have to unpack properly. You can't leave your things everywhere. It's not polite or respectful."

Max said, "Sorry, Grandma. I was in a hurry to go outside and play. Can we go now?"

Grandma said, "Yes, you can go now. But you have to promise me that you will unpack properly when you come back. And you have to help me clean up the kitchen later."

Max said, "OK, OK. I promise. Come on, Lily. Let's go." He ran to the door and opened it.

Lily said, "Bye, Grandma. We love you." She followed Max outside.

Grandma said, "Bye, my sweeties. I love you too. Have fun and be careful."

Lily and Max went outside and saw a big garden with flowers, trees and a pond. They saw a lot of things to explore and play with. They saw a swing, a slide, a sandbox and a bike. They also saw a big mushroom growing under a tree. They ran to the mushroom and touched it. It was soft and round and had white spots on it.

Lily said, "Wow, look at this mushroom. It's so big and pretty. I wonder if it's magic."

Max said, "Maybe it is. Maybe if we eat it, we will grow bigger or smaller or fly or turn invisible."

Lily said, "That sounds fun. But maybe we shouldn't eat it. Maybe it's poisonous or yucky or makes us sick."

Max said, "You're right. We shouldn't eat it. But we can play with it. We can pretend it's a house or a hat or a cake."

Lily said, "OK, let's play with it. But we have to be gentle and not break it. It's part of nature and we have to respect it."

Max said, "OK, OK. Let's be gentle and not break it. But let's have fun and use our imagination."

Lily and Max played with the mushroom for a long time. They pretended it was a house for fairies and elves. They pretended it was a hat for a giant or a princess. They pretended it was a cake for a birthday or a tea party. They had a lot of fun and used their imagination.

They forgot about their bags and their room and their promise. They only remembered the mushroom and their play. They were happy and curious and creative.

Once there was a little boy who loved to please. He did what his mommy and daddy asked him to do and always said "please" when he wanted something.

His favorite thing was motion. He loved to swing on the swing and run around with his friends at the park. Whenever he had a free moment he wanted to move!

One day, a very popular motion came to town. It was called a seesaw and everyone wanted to try it. The little boy loved it and asked his mommy and daddy to please buy him one for his backyard.

They said yes and gave him the best seesaw ever! He stayed outside playing on it for hours, swinging up and down, asking his friends to please join him every chance he got.

The little boy was so happy and pleased that his special motion was now in his backyard.

One day a shy zigzag moved to a new home. He was a bit nervous but he was excited to settle into his new home.

The zigzag liked exploring the new area, but he was too shy to meet any of the other animals who were living nearby. Every day he would watch the animals from afar and even tried to copy the different ways they moved.

But one day he noticed a friendly looking bird sitting nearby. He was too scared to say hello, but the bird seemed to understand and flew closer. The zigzag was still very shy and didn't know what to say, but the bird kept coming closer until it was right next to him.

The two of them stayed there for the rest of the day and the zigzag finally felt comfortable enough to settle. He soon became friends with the birds nearby and the other animals in the area. The zigzag was so happy to have finally found a place where he could settle for good.

Once upon a time, there was a fake rabbit. It liked to lead its friends on adventures. One day, it wanted to explore a big castle. But, the big castle was locked. The fake rabbit thought and thought until it had an idea. It asked its friends to help it make fake soap key. Together they mixed together some water, soap and magic. Then, when they had the fake soap key, they all lit up. The fake rabbit used the key and it lead them into the castle. They all ran around the castle, looking at all the wonderful things, until night fell and it was time to go home. The fake rabbit and its friends left, but the castle holds many secrets until this day.

Once upon a time, there was a brave clown named Bobo. Bobo loved to make kids laugh and play. He had a big red nose and funny shoes.

One day, Bobo went to the park. He saw a big puddle. He thought it would be fun to splash in the puddle. Bobo ran to the puddle and jumped in. "Splash!" went the water. The kids at the park laughed and clapped.

A little girl named Lily came up to Bobo. She said, "I want to splash too, but I'm scared." Bobo smiled and said, "You can be brave like me. Let's splash together!" Lily took Bobo's hand and they splashed in the puddle. Everyone had a fun day at the park.

One day Tommy was walking in the park when he saw a very noisy dog chasing something. Tommy followed the dog to a tunnel, and saw it was trying to catch a bunny. The little bunny tried to escape by running inside the tunnel, but he was too slow.

Tommy had an idea; he ran to the nearby pond and filled his bucket with water. He quickly ran back to the tunnel and threw the water at the dog. Suddenly, the noisy dog stopped chasing the bunny and ran away!

The bunny looked up at Tommy. He was so thankful for being rescued and filled Tommy's heart with joy. He thanked Tommy with a big hug and then scampered away into the distance.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tom. Tom loved to read books. Every day, he would read about big ships that sail on the sea. He wished he could sail on a ship one day.

One sunny day, Tom met a girl named Sally. Sally saw Tom reading a book. "What are you reading?" she asked. Tom felt ashamed because he thought Sally would not like his book. "I am reading about ships that sail," he said in a small voice.

Sally smiled and said, "I like to read about ships too! Let's read together." Tom and Sally became good friends. They would read about ships and dream of the day they could sail on one. And they were never ashamed to share their dreams with each other.

Once there was a little girl who really liked cards. She had a stack of colourful cards that she liked to look at and play games with. One day, she was feeling very eager and decided to show her cards to a friend. She raced to her friend's house and knocked on the door, holding her cards in her hands.

Her friend's mom answered the door and said, "Why, hello there. What do you have in your hands?" The little girl showed her cards and said, "I have cards to show my friend."

The mom smiled and said, "That's wonderful, but you need to remember to be polite. You can't just come in and scream." The little girl looked ashamed and apologised.

The mom smiled again and said, "That's better! It's important to remember to use politeness when interacting with others. Always use your kind words instead of screaming."

The little girl thanked the mom and then went in to show her friend the cards. She was happy to have learned an important lesson - always think before you act!

Once upon a time, there were two friends named Penny and Henry. They lived in a small, modest house next to a big field.

One day, Henry had an idea. He wanted to explore the big field, so he asked Penny if she wanted to come join him.

Penny said, “Yes! That sounds like fun. But be sure to bring a match. It might get dark soon.”

So the two friends went out to the field and started to explore. Suddenly, they heard a phone ringing. They looked around and couldn’t find anyone.

Henry said, “Maybe it’s coming from over there. Let’s go take a look.”

When they got closer, they noticed that the phone was inside a big hollow tree. Henry wanted to find out who owned the phone, but Penny was scared.

Penny said, “I think we should go back. It might be dangerous.”

But Henry said, “Don’t worry. We’ll use the match to look inside the tree. Maybe we can find who the phone belongs to.”

So the two friends took the match and lit it. when they looked inside the tree, they saw a small pack of puppies.

Penny said, “Awww! They’re so cute! I think they must have

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a sister named Rose who was very little too. One day, Lily's mom asked her to deliver a cake to their neighbor's house. Lily thought it was easy and said yes.

Lily took Rose with her and they started walking. But then, they saw a big dog on the way. Rose got scared and started crying. Lily tried to calm her down but it didn't work. Then, Lily remembered what her mom always said, "When you have a problem, talk to someone about it." So, Lily asked the dog's owner to help them cross the street.

The dog's owner was very nice and helped them cross the street. Lily delivered the cake to the neighbor's house and they thanked her. Lily felt proud of herself for being brave and helping her sister. The moral of the story is that it's always good to ask for help when you need it.

Lily and Ben like to play with clay. They have many colors of clay. They can make animals, cars, flowers and more. Lily wants to make a round ball. She rolls the clay in her hands. She tries to make it perfect. But the clay is sticky and lumpy. She struggles to make it smooth.

Ben sees Lily's ball. He thinks it is funny. He laughs and says, "That is not a round ball. That is a silly blob. Look at my ball. It is round and perfect." He shows Lily his ball. It is blue and shiny. He rolls it on the table. It does not stick or lump.

Lily feels sad. She does not like Ben's laugh. She does not like his ball. She says, "Your ball is not perfect. It is boring. It has no color. It has no shape. It has no fun. My ball is better. It is colorful. It is lumpy. It is fun." She picks up her ball and throws it at Ben.

Ben is surprised. He dodges the ball. But the ball is sticky. It sticks to his hair. He feels the clay in his hair. He screams and says, "Get it off! Get it off! Your ball is awful. It is sticky. It is lumpy. It is messy." He tries to pull the clay out of his hair. He struggles to get it off.

Lily sees Ben's hair. She thinks it is funny. She laughs and says, "That is not hair. That is a silly wig. Look at my hair. It is round and perfect." She shows Ben her hair. It is red and curly. She shakes it on her head. It does not stick or lump.

Once upon a time, there was a clumsy bear named Bobo. Bobo loved to play with his stuff. He had lots of toys and soft things. One day, Bobo found a big, red ball in the forest.

Bobo was so happy. He said, "Wow, a big ball! I want to play with it!" He tried to squeeze the ball, but it was too big. Bobo was sad. He wanted to play with the ball, but he didn't know how.

Then, Bobo's friend, a little bird named Chirpy, flew by. Chirpy saw Bobo looking sad. "Why are you sad, Bobo?" asked Chirpy. Bobo said, "I found this big ball, but I can't squeeze it." Chirpy smiled and said, "You don't need to squeeze it. You can roll it and play with it that way!"

Bobo and Chirpy played with the big, red ball all day. They rolled it, kicked it, and had so much fun. Bobo learned that even if he was clumsy, he could still play and have fun with his friends.

Once upon a time there was a poor little girl. Her name was Lucy. Every morning Lucy would wake up early and start her day.

One morning, Lucy woke up feeling really hungry. She couldn't wait to try out the yummy food in the kitchen. She shuffled out of bed and started walking towards the kitchen.

When she arrived, Lucy was excited to find a plate of food on the table. It had the best smell! She quickly grabbed a spoon and took a big bite. But OH NO! It tasted so bad! Lucy quickly decided the food was too poor for her to eat.

That's when Lucy's mom walked into the kitchen. She saw what was wrong and smiled. "Don't worry, sweetheart," she said. "I promise I'll make you something better for breakfast." And she did. Lucy and her mom enjoyed a yummy breakfast together and Lucy smiled all morning long.

Sam was walking around the park one day. He stopped to watch some people jogging. He thought it looked fun so he decided to try it.

He asked his mom, "Mom can I jog too?"

His mom replied, "Yes you can, but you must wash first."

So Sam went to wash up and when he was done he was ready to jog. He found it was easy to jog around the park. He had so much fun and he jogged all day.

At the end of the day, Sam was very tired but he felt great! He knew he had made the right decision to jog around the park.

Mommy was enthusiastic about Jake's jacket. It was bright blue with a happy smiley face on it. She said it was perfect for him and she recommended it to him.

Jake was excited to show his dad. He spun around and around, shouting that he wanted to wear his new jacket. His dad was very proud and Jake wore it to school the next day.

At school that day, Jake showed off his new jacket to his friends. Everyone was so excited to see it, they asked him where he got it. Jake said "My mommy recommended it to me -- it's so special!"

The next day, Jake's teacher asked where he had gotten his new jacket. All the kids said it was from his Mommy and that she had recommended it to him. Everyone was impressed and even more enthusiastic about Jake's new jacket.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Jane. Jane was three years old and loved to go outside and see things.

One day, Jane's mommy took her to a very pretty place: a school! Jane was so excited to see it.

There was a big playground with slides and swings. Jane jumped and ran around until she was tired. Then she saw all the classrooms with books and desks.

Before she knew it, it was time to go home. Jane hugged her mommy, gave a big wave to the school, and off they went. Jane couldn't wait to come back and see the pretty school again!

Once upon a time, there was a noisy jungle. The birds chirped loudly and the monkeys hollered from the trees. One day, a leopard came to the jungle. He was very big and had lots of spots. He roared loudly and scared all the animals.

The leopard was very hungry and wanted to eat something. He saw a little rabbit and chased it. The rabbit ran and ran, but the leopard was too fast. The leopard caught the rabbit and ate it all up.

The other animals wept and wept. They were sad that the leopard had eaten their friend. They wished the leopard had never come to their jungle. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her dolls and dress up like a princess. One day, she found a shiny crown in her toy box. It was so pretty and sparkly, she put it on her head and pretended to be a queen.

Suddenly, she heard a whisper coming from the corner of her room. "Psst, Lily, I have a secret to tell you," the voice said. Lily looked around but didn't see anyone. "Who's there?" she asked.

"It's me, your fairy godmother," the voice whispered again. "I gave you that powerful crown so you can be a real princess. But you must be kind and brave to wear it."

Lily was so happy, she hugged her fairy godmother. From that day on, she wore her crown with pride and always remembered to be kind and brave, just like a real princess.

The big Lion roared loud and harsh. He was the King of the jungle and wanted everyone to know it. Everyone in the jungle was scared of the loud roar, except for the little fox. He had a saw in his hand, and thought he could cut down the lion with it!

The little fox ran towards the lion and began to saw, but the lion just roared even louder. The saw was no match for the King of the Jungle. He blasted out a roar that was so loud and so harsh, it made the fox drop his saw and run away.

The lion was victorious. He knew that he was powerful and no one could stand up against him! He roared with joy, and the animals of the jungle knew he was the king once again.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy who loved to play with cars. One day, he was playing with his favourite car, a red engine. He pushed it as fast as he could and pretended to race it around the room. After a while, he got a bit sleepy and put the engine down, his eyelids beginning to get heavy.

Just as he was about to sleep, the little boy heard a noise. He looked up and saw a fairy, hovering in the air right in front of him. She said, "My name is Flora. I heard you playing with your engine and I wanted to tell you something special. I wanted to tell you that if you dream hard enough, you can make amazing things happen. So never give up on your dreams."

The little boy was amazed. He thanked the fairy and promised that he would always remember what she said. He put the engine down and drifted off to sleep, feeling very happy.

The next morning, the little boy woke up and remembered what the fairy said. He promised himself that he would never stop dreaming, no matter what the dreams were about. He smiled and hugged his engine tight, feeling excited about what could happen next.

Once upon a time, there was a frog named Fred. Fred lived in a pond with his friends. One day, Fred saw a butterfly and he hopped after it. He hopped and hopped until he found himself far away from the pond.

Fred was having so much fun chasing the butterfly that he didn't notice the sun was setting. Suddenly, he realized he was lost. He tried to hop back to the pond, but he didn't know which way to go.

Just then, he heard a voice. "Hello, little frog. Are you lost?" It was a wise old owl. "Yes," said Fred, "I can't find my way back to the pond." The owl looked serious and said, "Let's pause for a moment and think. Which way did you come from?" Together, they figured out the way back to the pond and Fred was so happy to be back with his friends.

Lila and Ben were friends who liked to play outside. One day, they found a big red sweater on a bench. It was cold, so they decided to share it.

"Let's take turns wearing the sweater," Lila said. "You can wear it first, then I will wear it."

"Okay," Ben said. He put on the sweater and felt warm and cozy. He liked the sweater so much that he did not want to give it to Lila.

Lila waited and waited, but Ben did not return the sweater. She felt cold and sad. She asked Ben, "Can I have the sweater now? It is my turn."

"No," Ben said. "I like the sweater. It is mine now. Go away."

Lila was angry and hurt. She ran away and cried. She saw a lady walking by with a basket of cookies. The lady saw Lila and said, "What is wrong, little girl? Why are you crying?"

Lila told the lady what happened. The lady said, "That is not nice of Ben. He should share the sweater with you. Here, have a cookie. It will make you feel better."

Lila took a cookie and thanked the lady. She bit into the cookie and felt a burning sensation in her mouth. The cookie was spicy. Lila spit out the cookie and said, "Yuck! This cookie is spicy. I don't like it."

The lady said, "I'm sorry. I like spicy cookies. They are good for me. But they are not good for everyone. You see, different people have different tastes and preferences. Just like you like the red sweater, but Ben likes it more. Maybe you can find another sweater that you both like, or trade something else with him."

Lila thought about what the lady said. She realized that she and Ben were different, and that was okay. She also realized that she should not take things that were not hers, and that she should be kind and respectful to others. She decided to return the sweater to Ben and say sorry. She hoped that Ben would say sorry too, and that they could be friends again. She learned that sharing is caring, and that spicy is not always nice.

Lila and Tom were twins who liked to organize their toys. They had many toys because their parents were wealthy and bought them new ones often. But they did not like to share their toys with each other or with their friends.

One day, they decided to make a mountain of toys in their room. They piled up all their dolls, cars, blocks, books, and stuffed animals. They wanted to have the biggest and best mountain of toys in the world.

"Look at our mountain, Tom!" Lila said. "It is so high and colorful. No one has a mountain like ours."

"Yes, Lila, it is amazing. We are the kings and queens of toys. No one can touch our mountain or play with our toys." Tom said.

But then, they heard a knock on the door. It was their friend Sam, who came to visit them. Sam was not wealthy and did not have many toys. He liked to play with Lila and Tom, but they did not like to share their toys with him.

"Hi, Lila and Tom. Can I come in and play with you?" Sam asked.

"No, Sam. You cannot come in. This is our room and our mountain of toys. You cannot play with our toys. Go away." Lila and Tom said.

Sam felt sad and hurt. He did not understand why Lila and Tom were so mean to him. He liked them and wanted to be their friend. He walked away from their door and went to the backyard.

There, he saw a pile of leaves that had fallen from the trees. He thought they looked like fun. He started to rake the leaves and make a big pile. He jumped into the pile and laughed. He felt happy and free.

He saw a stick and a pine cone and pretended they were a sword and a crown. He imagined he was a brave knight who lived in a castle. He had many adventures and made friends with the animals and the plants.

He heard a voice behind him. It was Lila and Tom. They had seen him from their window and were curious. They came down to the backyard and saw his pile of leaves.

"Hi, Sam. What are you doing?" Lila asked.

"I'm playing with the leaves. They are fun and soft. Do you want to join me?" Sam asked.

Lila and Tom looked at each other. They felt ashamed and sorry. They realized they had been selfish and rude. They saw that Sam was having more fun with the leaves than they had with their toys. They saw that he was generous and friendly. They wanted to be his friend.

"Yes, Sam. We want to join you. We are sorry we were mean to you. Can you forgive us?" Tom asked.

"Of course, I can. You are my friends. Come on, let's play together." Sam said.

Lila and Tom smiled and ran to the pile of leaves. They threw the leaves in the air and caught them. They made leaf angels and leaf hats. They laughed and hugged. They felt happy and free.

They learned that playing with the leaves was more fun than playing with the toys. They learned that sharing and caring was more important than having and hoarding. They learned that friendship was more valuable than wealth. They learned to organize their hearts.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. He was very curious and loved to explore. Timmy went on a walk and found a big tree. He climbed the tree and discovered a bird's nest with little eggs inside.

As Timmy continued his walk, he saw a sign that said "Exit". He didn't know what it meant, but he followed the arrow and found himself outside of the park.

Timmy was happy he discovered something new, but he knew it was time to go home. He followed the path back to his house and told his mom all about his adventure. She was so proud of him for being so brave and curious.

One day, a little girl named Amy was feeling troubled. She wanted to make cocoa for her friends, but she didn't know how. So, she asked her mom for help. Her mom showed her how to make the cocoa. Amy was very happy.

Amy took the cocoa to her friends. They all loved it. They played and drank cocoa all day. But then, a big dog came. The dog was hungry and wanted to eat their cocoa. The kids got scared and ran away. The dog started to bite their cups.

The dog ate all the cocoa and the cups. The kids were sad because they had no more cocoa to drink. They learned that they should be careful with their things and not leave them alone. The moral of the story is to always be careful and protect your things from danger.

Once upon a time, there was a great pupil at school. She was the best at learning and always happy to help her friends. One day, the pupil got angry and said bad words to her friend. Her friend was sad and hurt by the words. The pupil felt so sorry for what she had done and wanted to make it up.

So she went to her friend with a big hug. She said sorry and asked for forgiveness. Her friend was so happy to see the show of love and hugged her back. Her friend said that she forgave her and that everyone makes mistakes. The pupil was so relieved and grateful. She thanked her friend for being so kind and understanding. From that day onward, the pupil learned to always be kind and to forgive others. She realized that it is better to forgive than to hold grudges.

The end.

Once upon a time, there was an elephant named Ted. Ted lived in the jungle and often played with the other animals. One day, Ted was feeling very dizzy. He wanted to do something fun, but he was not sure what. He asked his friend, the monkey, "What can I do?"

The monkey thought for a moment and then he said, "I know! Let's play tag! It is lots of fun."

So Ted and the monkey began to play tag. Ted ran around, chased by the monkey, and soon he no longer felt dizzy! He was having a great time.

At the end of the game, Ted was so happy and full of energy. He said to the monkey, "That was so much fun! Let's do it every day!"

And so Ted and his monkey friend played tag every day. They were always dizzy with laughter and smiles.

Once upon a time, in a small village, there was a little girl named Lucy. Lucy loved to pick apples from the trees in her backyard. One sunny day, she took her basket and went outside to pick some apples. She was very happy.

As Lucy was picking the apples, she saw a tiny bird on a tree branch. The bird looked confused and sad. "What's wrong, little bird?" asked Lucy. The tiny bird replied, "I tried to fly, but I fell down and now I can't find my mom." Lucy felt sad for the bird and decided to help.

Lucy put the tiny bird in her basket and walked around the village, asking other birds if they knew the tiny bird's mom. Finally, they found the mom, who was so happy to see her baby. The tiny bird thanked Lucy and said, "You are a good friend. I will never forget your help."

Lucy felt very proud and happy that she could help the tiny bird. From that day on, Lucy learned that helping others is a good thing to do. The village people also heard about Lucy's kindness and they all loved her even more. And everyone lived happily ever after.

The moral of the story is: always be kind and help others when they need it.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who was very lonely. She didn't have any friends to play with. One day, she decided to bake some cookies to make herself feel better. She mixed the ingredients together and put them in the oven to bake.

While the cookies were baking, the little girl went outside to play. She saw another little girl who was also alone. The little girl went up to her and said hello. The other girl was happy to have a new friend.

When the cookies were done, the little girl brought some over to her new friend. They both enjoyed the cookies together and became good pupils in school. They played together every day and were no longer lonely.

There was a little girl called Lucy. She was a very cheerful person who loved exploring nature. One day she was near the sea. She saw the tides flowing in and out. It was so interesting.

"Look, it's a tide," Lucy said cheerfully.

She started to explore the beach and soon the tide was rising. She was concerned but then she saw the beach start to dry.

"Look, it's drying," Lucy said happily.

Soon, the tide was completely gone and Lucy jumped with joy. She was so glad to see the beach back in its usual state.

She gathered some shells that were on the beach and took them home.

"Mum, I found shells on the beach," Lucy said cheerfully.

Her mum was so glad to see her daughter so happy. They had a wonderful day full of cheerfulness.

Once there was a little boy named Jack. He had green eyes and was three years old. Each day, Jack played in the garden with his friends. But today, something unknown was about to happen.

Jack found a pair of scissors in the garden. He remembered that he had seen his mom use them before. He wanted to try them out and see what would happen.

So, Jack held the scissors in his hands and started to cut. He cut some leaves, some grass and a few flowers. Finally, he started to feel sleepy.

He went back inside and lay down for a nap. When he woke up, he took out the scissors and went back to the garden. But nothing felt the same, it felt unknown to him now. He decided not to cut anything anymore, and just enjoy the garden with his friends instead.

Once upon a time, there was a wide path in the woods. Many animals lived near the path. One day, a little rabbit named Remy was hopping along the path. The sun was shining, and Remy was very happy.

Suddenly, a big frog named Fred appeared on the path. Fred was green and had big eyes. Remy and Fred looked at each other, and they both smiled. They wanted to be friends and play together.

Remy and Fred played on the wide path all day. They ran, they hopped, and they laughed. As the sun went down, they said goodbye and went back to their homes. They knew they would see each other again on the wide path, and they couldn't wait to play together again.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Adam. He wanted to be lucky. So one day, he found a rope and started to play with it. Adam wanted to use it to deliver good luck.

He went outside and started to deliver the rope to the people in his neighborhood. He thought this would make him lucky. Adam was happy until the rope started to tear apart.

The rope broke and Adam became scared. He started to run but the rope was still stuck to him. He ran and ran until he reached the edge of a cliff.

The rope got stuck in the rocks, so Adam couldn't get away. He looked around and noticed he had reached the edge of a mountain. He shouted for help, but no one came.

Adam felt sad and scared. He slipped and the unlucky rope dragged him off the cliff. He never made it back home.

Once upon a time, there was a little mouse named Max. Max liked to walk around and explore. One day, he found a big maze. The maze was gray and looked very confusing. Max wanted to explore the maze, so he started to walk through it.

As he walked, Max found many twists and turns. He had to be careful not to get lost! But he kept walking and eventually, he found his way out of the maze. Max was very happy that he had explored the maze and found his way out. From then on, he continued to walk and explore new places every day.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her dolls and stuffed animals. One day, she went outside to play with her friends. They decided to have a picnic in the park.

Lily's mom packed a basket full of yummy treats like sandwiches, fruit, and cookies. When they got to the park, they found a nice spot to sit in the grass. Lily's friend, Timmy, asked if anyone had brought napkins.

Lily's mom said, "Oh no, I forgot to pack napkins. But don't worry, I can fold up some paper towels for us to use." She took out an empty plastic bag and pulled out some paper towels. She folded them neatly and handed them to the kids.

After they finished eating, Lily and her friends played games and had fun. When it was time to go home, Lily's mom said, "Let's make sure we pick up all of our trash and throw it away in the trash can over there." The kids helped pick up the empty wrappers and put them in the bag.

As they walked home, Lily's mom said, "Remember how I folded up those paper towels for our napkins? That's called being prepared. It's always good to plan ahead and think about what we might need." Lily smiled and said, "I'm going to remember that for next time!"

Sara liked to act. She liked to pretend she was a princess, a fairy, a doctor, or anything she wanted. She had many toys and costumes to help her act. But her favorite toy was her flute. She loved to play her flute and make music. She felt happy and free when she played her flute.

One day, Sara went to the park with her mom and her flute. She saw some other kids playing on the swings, the slide, and the sandbox. She wanted to join them and make friends. She thought they would like her flute and her acting. She walked up to them and said hello. She showed them her flute and asked if they wanted to hear her play.

But the other kids did not want to hear her play. They laughed at her flute and said it was silly and boring. They said they did not like acting and that she was weird. They told her to go away and leave them alone. Sara felt sad and hurt. She did not understand why they were so mean to her. She ran back to her mom and cried.

Her mom hugged her and wiped her tears. She told her that some kids can be mean and rude, but that does not mean she should stop playing her flute and acting. She told her that her flute and her acting were special and beautiful, and that she should be proud of them. She told her that she was a humble and kind girl, and that those are the best qualities to have. She told her that she would always love her and support her.

Sara felt better and smiled. She thanked her mom and gave her a kiss. She decided to ignore the mean kids and keep playing her flute and acting. She knew that her mom was right, and that she was humble and kind. She also knew that someday, she would find other kids who would appreciate her flute and her acting, and who would be her true friends. She played her flute and acted happily, and felt happy and free again.

Carla picked up her cuddly toy bear. It was adorable. She loved to squeeze it tight and feel its soft fur against her skin. She was never without it!

One day, Carla put the bear near the window. Then clouds appeared in the sky, and rain started to fall. Carla watched as steam rose up from the warm rain.

Suddenly, a gust of wind blew the window open. The bear flew away! Carla tried to catch it, but it was lost. Carla was very sad. She had lost her most beloved and adorable friend.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lily. She had a pretty bracelet that she wore every day. One day, she found another bracelet that was different from hers. She wanted to wear the new bracelet, but it was locked.

Lily tried to open it, but she couldn't. She asked her mommy to help her unlock it. Her mommy used a key to unlock the bracelet and gave it to Lily.

Lily was so happy to wear her new bracelet. She showed it to her friends and they thought it was beautiful. Now, Lily had two bracelets, but they were different from each other. She loved them both the same.

Once upon a time there was a delicate flower. The flower was happy living in its special garden until one day it wanted to see the world. So the flower said goodbye to its friends in the garden and set off for the market.

At the market there were lots of things for the flower to see. It saw bright colors, fascinating sounds and lots of people walking around. The flower stayed at the market all day, but eventually it got tired and decided to return home.

The flower was very happy to see its garden friends again. All the other flowers welcomed it back with a big cheer. Together they watched the sun go down and the stars come out. The delicate flower felt content and knew it was safe at home.

One day, Timmy went to the park with his mom. He saw a big puddle and wanted to splash in it. "Mommy, can I splash in the puddle?" he asked. "Sure, just be careful not to get too wet," she replied.

As Timmy splashed in the puddle, he saw a rat running by. "Look, Mommy! A rat!" he shouted. His mom quickly picked him up and said, "Rats are not our friends. They can be dangerous."

After a while, Timmy got tired and they sat on a bench. His mom showed him a fragile flower and said, "This flower is delicate and needs to be taken care of." Timmy looked at the flower and said, "It's pretty, but it could break easily."

As they walked home, Timmy thought about the rat and the flower. He realized that some things are not meant to be played with, and some things need to be treated gently.

Once upon a time, there was a big school with a huge blackboard. The blackboard was very big and it was black like the night sky. One day, the teacher came to the school and she had a spray bottle with her. She wanted to clean the blackboard because it was very dirty.

The teacher sprayed the blackboard with water and wiped it clean with a cloth. The children watched her and thought it was very impressive how she made the blackboard look new again. They were happy because they could now see the words and numbers clearly.

After the teacher finished cleaning the blackboard, she wrote some words on it with chalk. The children were excited to learn and they listened carefully to the teacher. From that day on, the blackboard was always clean and the children loved to learn new things on it.

Tom and Lily were twins. They liked to do everything together. They played with the same toys, ate the same food, and wore the same clothes. They were happy and ordinary.

One day, their mom said, "Tom and Lily, you are going to school tomorrow. You will learn new things and make new friends. But you will not be in the same class. You will be split."

Tom and Lily did not like this. They did not want to be split. They wanted to stay together. They cried and hugged each other.

"Why do we have to be split, mom?" Tom asked.

"Because you are big now, and you need to try new things and meet new people. You will still see each other at recess and lunch. And you will still come home together. You will always be twins, and you will always love each other. But you will also have your own space and your own adventures. It will be fun, I promise." Mom said.

Tom and Lily were not sure. They were scared and sad. But they trusted their mom. They decided to give school a try. They packed their backpacks and went to bed.

The next day, they woke up and got ready. They held hands as they walked to the bus. They said goodbye and kissed each other. They went to their different classes.

At first, they felt lonely and missed each other. But soon, they found out that school was not so bad. They learned new things and made new friends. They had fun and did well. They still saw each other at recess and lunch. They told each other what they did and what they learned. They were proud and happy.

They realized that being split was not so bad. They could still stay together in their hearts. And they could still be ordinary and happy.

Once upon a time there was a sad bear. The bear felt down so he decided to sit in the sun and read a book. The sun was so warm that it melted the book. The bear became very upset and started to cry. He wished he had been more careful to keep his book safe.

At that moment a wise owl flew by and said to him, "Nothing lasts forever, so take care of the things that you love." The bear thought about what the owl said and realised that he should cherish the things he holds dear.

From that day forward, the bear was mindful of how he treats his possessions and always looks after them with care.

The moral of the story is that we must be careful with the things we own, because nothing lasts forever.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy lived in a house with his mommy and daddy. One day, Timmy and his family went for a picnic in the park. They brought a big thermos filled with thick juice to drink.

While they were having fun, Timmy saw a bird flying towards the east. "Look, mommy! A bird going to the east!" Timmy said. "Yes, Timmy. Birds like to fly to different places," mommy said.

After playing for a while, Timmy got thirsty. He went to the thermos and drank all the juice. "Mmm, that was yummy!" Timmy said. But then, Timmy started feeling sick. He drank too much juice and got a tummy ache.

The moral of the story is that we should always drink in moderation and not overdo it. Too much of a good thing can be bad for us.

John was in the park, happy and playing with his toy truck. Suddenly, he saw a bug and was excited to catch it. He picked it up and threw it, but he missed. He was sorry, but he wanted to try again. He bent down, holding out his hand and said "Come here, bug!"

But the bug was smarter than John and ran away. John chased the bug, but it was too fast. He tried to pick it up again, but it always ran away.

John was very frustrated and said to the bug, "You are so silly!" But the bug kept running away.

Unfortunately, John never did catch the bug. He was very sorry and had to go home without it.

Lily and Ben are playing with their toy cars in the garden. They make noises like motors and zoom around the grass. Lily has a red car and Ben has a blue car. They pretend to race each other and have fun.

"Look, Lily, I can go faster than you!" Ben says, pushing his car hard.

"No, you can't, Ben, I can catch you!" Lily says, chasing him with her car.

They run and laugh until they reach the fence. There, they see a big dog on the other side. The dog is brown and furry and has a long tongue. He barks at them and wags his tail.

"Hi, doggy!" Lily says, waving at him.

"Can we pet him, Lily?" Ben asks, looking at her.

"I don't know, Ben, he might bite us," Lily says, feeling scared.

The dog jumps up and puts his paws on the fence. He licks Lily's face and makes her giggle.

"He likes you, Lily, he's giving you a kiss!" Ben says, smiling.

Lily wipes her face and laughs. She gives the dog a kiss back and strokes his fur.

"He's soft, Ben, and warm," Lily says, feeling happy.

Ben comes closer and gives the dog a kiss too. The dog licks him and makes him dizzy.

"Wow, he's strong, Lily, he's making me dizzy!" Ben says, holding his head.

They both hug the dog and thank him for the kisses. The dog barks and wags his tail. He likes Lily and Ben. They are his new friends.

Once upon a time there was a gentle girl named Millie. She loved to wear a skirt everywhere she went. Millie's mom told her that she had to be careful not to get it too dirty.

One day Millie went outside to play. She was so happy running around with her little skirt. Suddenly, a large sack attacked Millie. She screamed and ran away. She was so scared that she forgot to take her skirt off.

Millie's mom found her and saw that she was holding onto her skirt with all her might. Millie's mom asked her, "Millie, why are you still wearing your skirt?" Millie told her mom, "The sack came out of nowhere and tried to attack me! I was so scared that I couldn't take it off!"

Millie's mom hugged Millie close and said, "Sweetheart, don't worry. The sack won't attack you anymore. Now let's get you out of that dirty skirt and go back home."

Then Millie and her mom went back home, and Millie was never attacked by the sack again.

John was feeling so excited. Today, he was going to the restaurant with his family. He kept bouncing around the house in anticipation.

Finally the time came, and John's family made their way to the restaurant. When they arrived, John ran inside to explore. He saw bright colors everywhere. He noticed a long table with a candle in the center. He wanted to bounce on it, but his parents warned him against it.

"John, don't bounce on that long table," his mother said.

John nodded, but he still felt disappointed. He looked around for something else he could bounce on. Suddenly he noticed an empty corner.

"Can I bounce there mommy?" John asked happily.

His mother nodded with a smile. John happily ran to the corner and started bouncing. He bounced and laughed for a long time. After a while, his parents joined him and they all enjoyed bouncing together.

Molly and her dad went for a walk. They went down a busy trail. It was a lot of fun! They saw lots of birds and flowers.

Molly and her dad saw a big tree and Molly thought it was special. She ran up to it and said, "This tree looks like a seat! Can I sit there?"

Molly's dad smiled and said, "Sure!" Molly started to climb the tree and when she was way up high, she looked down and laughed. It felt like she was flying!

When Molly was done sitting and enjoying the view, she and her dad walked back home. They had a lot of fun walking down the busy trail.

Once upon a time, there was a little fish named Nemo. Nemo loved to swim in the big blue sea. One day, Nemo met a crab named Mr. Crabby.

Mr. Crabby said to Nemo, "Hello little fish, do you want to come to the restaurant with me?" Nemo was excited to go to a restaurant.

When they got to the restaurant, Nemo saw a crazy octopus dancing on the table. Nemo said to Mr. Crabby, "Look at that crazy octopus!" Mr. Crabby laughed and said, "Yes, he is very silly."

After they ate their food, Nemo said goodbye to Mr. Crabby and went back to swimming in the big blue sea. Nemo couldn't wait to tell his fish friends about the crazy octopus at the restaurant.

Once upon a time, there was a happy mine. Inside the mine were lots of treasure. Every day, the mine held something special.

One day, a little girl found the mine. She was so happy. She held out her hands and started to fill them with the treasure. The girl felt so lucky! She ran back home and showed her mom what she had found.

Her mom was so pleased. She smiled and said, "This is your special mine. You can keep all the treasure for yourself." The little girl was so excited!

From that day, the mine was the little girl's special place. Whenever she wanted, she went back to the mine. She held the treasure close and was happy.

One day, a charming little mosquito named Momo was flying around. Momo loved to play with his friends. He saw a big tree and many friends were there. Momo wanted to join them, so he rushed to the tree.

"Hi, friends!" Momo said. "Can I play with you?" His friends were happy to see him. They all played fun games like hide and seek. Momo was very fast and good at hiding.

As they played, a big wind came. All the friends held onto the tree. Momo was scared, but his friends helped him. They all stayed safe and the wind went away. Momo was happy to have such good friends. They all laughed and played until the sun went down.

Once upon a time, there was a gray cat named Spike. Spike loved to run and play with his friends. One sunny day, Spike went outside to play with his best friend, a little dog named Max.

As they were playing, they saw a big ball rolling towards them. They wanted to play with the ball, but they could not agree on who would get it first. Spike said, "I want it!" Max said, "No, I want it!" They both wanted the ball so much that they began to fight over it.

Spike and Max stopped fighting and decided to run and chase the ball together. They had so much fun playing with the ball, and they learned that sharing was better than fighting. From that day on, Spike and Max always shared their toys and had lots of fun playing together.

Once there was a little fish named Tim who liked to play in the big blue sea. He loved to swim around the colourful reef and explore the undersea world. Tim was usually very careful and stayed safe by the reef but today he was feeling adventurous. He swam away from the reef, further and further into the deep blue.

Tim was so excited that he forgot to be careful. He didn’t realise that a big, scary shark was swimming towards him until it was too late. The shark opened its big mouth to eat Tim when suddenly a huge wave hit the shark and pushed it away.

The wave was caused by a group of dolphins who had seen the shark and wanted to help Tim. They swam around him protectively, making sure the shark stayed far away. Tim was so relieved and grateful. He thanked the dolphins for saving him and they happily swam away, back to their normal swimming spot.

From that day on, Tim was always careful when swimming near the reef and never swam too far away. He remembered how lucky he was that the dolphins had cared enough to help him and made sure that he was safe.

Once upon a time, there lived a boy named Jake. Jake was a mischievous boy who liked to have fun. One day, Jake was playing in the park when he found a book. He was curious and wanted to learn more about it.

He opened the book and read about the law. Jake thought it would be great to break the law and have some fun. He decided to do something risky.

He ran through the park, knocking over trash cans and making a loud noise. He felt scared but he kept going. Soon, two police officers arrived and saw Jake. They immediately started to sort him out.

The police asked Jake several questions but he couldn't answer them. He was scared and started crying. In the end, the police had to take him away.

That was the last time Jake ever played in the park. He learned his lesson and never made the same mistake again.

Once there was a silly little girl named Lucy. Every day, Lucy would feed her pet frog some soup. The soup was Lucy's favourite because it was nice and warm. Lucy would fill a bowl with the soup and sit on the floor with her froggy.

One day, Lucy dropped the bowl and it smashed on the floor. Some of the soup spilled onto the floor. Lucy was surprised, but she wasn't worried.

Lucy quickly ran to the kitchen and grabbed a new bowl. She filled it with fresh soup and put a new spoon inside. Lucy fed her pet frog the soup again and was so happy to see him eating it up.

He was so funny when he ate, making Lucy laugh. She felt silly for being so clumsy with the bowl, but she was relieved that her froggy was still eating his soup.

The End.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Penny. She had a bright smile and a love for adventure. One morning, Penny decided to wander around her neighbourhood. She grabbed her little cart and wandered through the street.

As Penny wandered, she noticed a lazy cat. It was snuggled up in the middle of the road. "Hi kitty," Penny said. But the kitty was sound asleep. So she left it be and continued on her wandering.

Finally, Penny reached a park. She pushed her cart up to a park bench and looked around. She saw a lazy dog lying in the sun and an old man lazily reading a book.

Penny grinned. She hopped onto the cart and continued wandering. She rode through the park, feeling the warm sun on her face. She smiled and laughed, enjoying the sights and sounds of a perfect, lazy summer day.

Ben and Lily were friends who liked to play outside. They had a big slide in their yard that they could zip down very fast. They also had a sandbox where they could make castles and shapes with their toys.

One day, they decided to have a race to see who could zip down the slide the fastest. They climbed up the ladder and got ready to go. Ben said, "On your mark, get set, go!" and they both pushed off.

But Ben wanted to win so much that he pushed Lily with his hand. Lily lost her balance and fell off the slide. She landed on the grass and started to cry. Ben zipped down the slide and shouted, "I win, I win!"

He looked back and saw Lily crying. He felt bad for what he did. He ran to her and said, "I'm sorry, Lily. I didn't mean to hurt you. Are you okay?"

Lily was hurt and angry. She said, "You cheated, Ben. You pushed me. That's not fair. You're not a good friend."

Ben felt even worse. He said, "You're right, Lily. I cheated. That's not fair. I'm not a good friend. I'm sorry. Can you forgive me?"

Lily looked at Ben and saw that he was sorry. She said, "I forgive you, Ben. But you have to promise me that you won't cheat again. Cheating is bad. It hurts people and makes them sad. Friends should be nice and honest and share."

Ben nodded and said, "I promise, Lily. I won't cheat again. Cheating is bad. It hurts people and makes them sad. Friends should be nice and honest and share. Can we still be friends?"

Lily smiled and said, "Yes, Ben. We can still be friends. Come on, let's play in the sandbox. Look, the sun is shining and the sky is colorful. It's a beautiful day."

They hugged and went to the sandbox. They made castles and shapes with their toys. They had fun and laughed. They learned their lesson. They were happy and good friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her mom's makeup. One day, Lily found her mom's makeup bag and started to put makeup on her face. She felt so happy and pretty.
