Tim and Sam were best friends. They liked to play in the yard with their toys. One day, they saw a big hole in the fence. They wanted to see what was on the other side.

"Let's go, Tim!" Sam said. "Maybe we can find something fun!"

"I don't know, Sam," Tim said. "Mom said we should not go out of the yard. And I am scared of the hole. What if there is a big dog or a mean man?"

"Don't be scared, Tim. We can be fast and quiet. And we can replace the fence when we come back. No one will know. Come on, it will be an adventure!"

Sam grabbed Tim's hand and pulled him to the hole. They crawled through and found themselves in a different yard. There were many flowers and trees and a small pond. They also saw a big red ball.

"Wow, look at that ball!" Sam said. "It is so big and shiny! Let's play with it!"

Sam ran to the ball and kicked it hard. It flew in the air and landed in the pond with a splash. Tim followed him and laughed.

They had fun playing with the ball in the pond. They did not notice that someone was watching them from the window of the house. It was an old lady with a stern face. She did not like children in her yard. She opened the door and shouted at them.

"Hey, you! Get out of my yard! That is my ball! How dare you take it and make a mess!"

Tim and Sam were scared. They dropped the ball and ran to the hole. They crawled back to their yard and replaced the fence. They hoped the old lady would not tell their mom.

They decided to never go through the hole again. They learned that it was not nice to take things that did not belong to them. And they learned that some adventures were not worth the trouble.

Once there was a dog called Ginger. She was very obedient. Every day, her master would feed her some food. He would always give her delicious treats.

One day, Ginger's master raised the bowl of food and put it underground. Ginger didn't understand why he was doing this, but she was obedient, so she waited until her master came back.

When her master returned, he lifted the bowl out of the ground, and a surprise was inside. There were lots of juicy bones! Ginger was so happy that she jumped up and down with joy.

Ginger was so grateful that she showed her master how obedient she was. She licked his face with her tongue and thanked him for the delicious bones. From that day onward, every day she got a surprise when her master put the bowl underground.

One day, two friends went to the park. They had fun playing together and made lots of noise. Suddenly, they decided to race each other!

The two friends ran back and forth, and the first one to the fence at the end of the park won. One friend stood with his arms around the fence, while the other was a few steps away.

The first friend started to laugh as he won, but the other friend felt very bitter. He had wanted to win the race and felt upset.

When the friends hugged each other goodbye, they weren't mad at each other anymore. They had a fun time racing and they wanted to do it again soon!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved stars. She would watch them twinkle in the sky every night. One day, she found a star on the ground that looked very attractive. She picked it up and showed it to her mom.

"Mommy, look at this pretty star! Can we keep it?" Lily asked.

Her mom replied, "Oh, that's a lovely star, but it's not clean. We need to polish it first."

Lily was sad because she didn't know how to polish the star. But then, her mom showed her how to use a cloth to make it shine. After they polished it, the star looked even more attractive. Lily was so happy that she hugged her mom and said, "Thank you for helping me make the star pretty!"

Suddenly, a bird flew by and tried to take the star away. Lily and her mom had to chase the bird to get the star back. After a short chase, they caught the bird and got the star back. Lily hugged her star tightly and said, "I will never let anyone take you away from me again!"

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved cakes and always wondered what kind of cake she would have for her birthday. Her mom promised to make her a special cake, but Lily had no idea what it would be.

One day, Lily's mom went to the store and bought all the ingredients to make the cake. Lily was so excited and wondered what kind of cake her mom would make. She even helped her mom mix the ingredients and put the cake in the oven.

The next day was Lily's birthday, and when she woke up, she smelled something sweet. She ran to the kitchen and saw the most beautiful cake she had ever seen. It was covered in pink frosting and had sprinkles on top. Lily felt so lucky to have such a wonderful mom who made her a special cake.

Lily and her family enjoyed the cake all day long, and Lily felt so happy and loved. She knew she was lucky to have such a wonderful family who cared for her. From that day on, Lily always wondered what kind of cake her mom would make for her next birthday.

Once upon a time, there was a unique flower named Poppy. Poppy lived in a big, green field with other flowers. Poppy was very happy and loved to play with her friends.

One sunny day, Poppy and her friends saw a big truck. The truck was there to deliver water to the field. Poppy said to her friends, "Look, the truck is here to help us! Let's say thank you!" The other flowers agreed and they all shouted together, "Thank you, truck!"

After the truck delivered the water, Poppy and her friends drank it up. They grew bigger and more beautiful. Poppy felt very special and loved being unique. She knew that being different was a good thing.

Once upon a time, there was a big, mean dragon. He liked to destroy things like castles and trees. One day, he saw a little girl eating a tasty pastry. The dragon wanted the pastry, but the little girl said no. The dragon got very angry and tried to take the pastry from her.

The little girl was very brave and said, "No, that's my pastry. You can't have it." The dragon realized that he was being selfish and apologized. He said, "I'm sorry. I shouldn't have tried to take your pastry. Can we share it?"

The little girl smiled and said, "Yes, we can share it." The dragon and the little girl sat down together and enjoyed the pastry. From that day on, the dragon didn't destroy things anymore. He learned to be kind and share with others. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a busy girl. She named her toy bear Panda. One day Panda asked her to play with him. The girl said yes, and the two started playing games together. They laughed and had lots of fun.

Suddenly the girl stopped. Panda asked why, so the girl explained that she was very busy. She said she had to turn her attention to other things.

Panda was sad that they could not play anymore, so he asked if they could play again soon. The girl smiled and said yes. They hugged and said goodbye.

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a dry ant who wanted to mail something special to his friends. He didn't have enough money to buy any envelopes, so he decided to walk to the post office. On the way, he met a wicked fox. The fox wanted to steal the ant's special package, so the ant decided to run away.

The ant was much faster than the fox, but he got tired and had to stop for a break. He looked around and saw a huge rock. He quickly crawled under the rock and hid the package.

The fox looked around but couldn't find the ant or the package. Soon, the ant was able to mail the package safely. He was very happy and thanked the rock for helping him. He made it back home, safe and sound. The end.

Lily was a black sheep who lived on a farm with many other sheep. She liked to play and run and jump, but the other sheep did not want to be her friends. They said she was too different and too strange. They ignored her and made fun of her.

One day, a man came to the farm. He had a big bag and a big pair of scissors. He wanted to cut the wool from the sheep and take it away. The other sheep were happy. They thought their wool was very nice and soft and white. They wanted the man to see how good they were.

But the man did not care about the other sheep. He only saw Lily. He liked her wool because it was very black and rare and shiny. He said, "What a beautiful sheep! I want her wool for my special coat." He went to Lily and cut her wool very gently. He put it in his bag and smiled.

Lily felt cold and scared. She did not like the man or his scissors. She wanted her wool back. She cried, "Help me! Help me!" But the other sheep did not hear her. They ignored her and looked at their own wool. They thought they were better than Lily.

The man left the farm with his bag. He was very happy. He said, "Thank you, black sheep. You gave me the best wool in the world." He did not thank the other sheep. He did not care about them.

Lily was alone and sad. She had no wool and no friends. She wished the other sheep would be nice to her. She wished they would not ignore her. She wished they would see that she was just like them.

Today was cold. Johnny was walking home from school. He looked sad. His friend asked him why he was frowning. Johnny said, "I don't want to go home". His friend asked why. Johnny said, "My mom is mad at me".

Johnny's friend said he should try to make his mom happy. Johnny thought he would do something nice. He skipped home and when his mom saw him she smiled.

Later that day, Johnny's mom got mad again. This time she was really angry. She scolded Johnny and told him not to do what he did earlier. Johnny was very sad. He started to cry and frowned.

His mom felt bad, but she said nothing. Johnny knew he had done something wrong and that made him even more sad. He went to his room, feeling very cold and alone.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Susie. She was only 3 years old. Susie felt very alone and felt like she didn't belong. One day her mommy asked her, "Susie, why do you feel so miserable?"

Susie looked up at her mommy and said, "Because nobody wants me. I can't do things like the big kids do and no one let's me play."

Her mommy smiled kindly and said, "Oh Susie, you can do lots of things. Yes, maybe you can't do some things like the big kids but that doesn't mean you don't belong. Come here. I want to show you something."

Susie followed her mother into the kitchen. Mommy opened the cupboard and took out a big jar. It was full of colorful candy.

"Do you see this jar Susie? Every candy has a different taste and it is all special. Just like those candies, everyone is different but everyone still belongs. Just like you. You are special and you belong."

Susie smiled. She realized that even though she was different, she was still special and she did belong.

Once there was a boy who loved to compete with his friends. He was very competitive, and he always wanted to win in all the games they played.

One day, he thought of a new game. He wanted to see if he could change the measure of something. He grabbed a ruler and measured his arm. Then he asked his friends to try and measure something bigger or smaller than him.

At first, no one could succeed in changing the measure. But then his friend Jerry tried and measured his foot. It was bigger than the boy's arm! Everyone cheered for Jerry and the boy was impressed.

From then on, the boy was always excited to play games with his friends. He was even more competitive, trying to change the measures of different things and see who could win!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who was very troubled. She had been having a lot of bad dreams lately, and she was feeling very scared.

One day, her mommy said, "Come on darling, let's go for a nap so you can get some rest."

The little girl replied, "But what if I have a bad dream again?"

Her mommy smiled and said, "Don't worry, I'll make sure all the bad dreams vanish."

So the little girl lay down on her bed and soon enough, she felt all her troubles vanish as she fell fast asleep. When she woke up, the bad dreams were all gone and the little girl felt very happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Alice. She was three years old and loved to wander. Every single day she would wander in the forest, exploring and finding new places to discover.

One day, while wandering, Alice spotted a pole in the distance. She ran closer with excitement and tried to grab it, only to find that it was far too high! She was disappointed, but she didn't give up.

Suddenly, an old woman came up to Alice, with a look of compassion on her face. She told Alice that she knew a way of getting the pole down - if Alice wanted to learn how. Alice quickly agreed and the old woman showed her how to use her feet and hands to climb up the pole.

Alice was so excited, she cheered with joy! She reached the top of the pole and grabbed the treat she had been eyeing.

The old woman smiled at Alice, her compassionate heart glad that she had helped the wandering little girl achieve her goal. Alice thanked the old woman and wandered on her way, feeling happy that she had made a new friend.

Once upon a time, there was a little hurricane named Harry. Harry was always restless. He liked to spin and spin all day long. He would dance in the sky, and the clouds would laugh with him. But sometimes, Harry would spin too fast and make a big mess.

One day, Harry met a bird named Betty. Betty was very good at managing things. She knew how to keep her nest clean and her eggs safe. She saw Harry spinning and making a mess, so she decided to help him.

Betty taught Harry how to spin just the right amount, so he didn't make a big mess anymore. Harry was so happy that he could still spin and dance without causing trouble. Now, Harry and Betty are the best of friends, and they dance in the sky together every day.

Once upon a time, there was an old barber who loved to stir his soup every day. One day, a little boy came to the barber's shop and asked for a haircut. The old barber was happy to help and started cutting the boy's hair.

But then, the old barber accidentally cut the boy's ear. The boy started crying and the old barber felt very bad. He tried to make it better by giving the boy some candy, but the boy was still upset.

The boy's parents came to pick him up and they were very angry at the old barber. They told him that he could never cut hair again. The old barber was very sad and went home to stir his soup alone. From that day on, he never cut hair again and always felt guilty for what he had done.

Once upon a time, there was a big black rhinoceros. He lived in a jungle. One day, he met a little bird. The bird asked, "What are you doing?" The rhinoceros replied, "I am spreading my wings." The little bird said, "But you don't have wings!" The rhinoceros laughed and said, "I know, I was just joking." The little bird and the rhinoceros became friends and played together every day.

Once upon a time, there was a red cup. It was a special cup because it could sail on the water. One day, a little girl took the red cup to the lake. She put it in the water and watched it sail away. The red cup sailed and sailed until it was too far away for the little girl to see. She was sad that her special cup was gone, but she knew it was having a fun adventure on the water. The end.

Once upon a time there were two birds. They lived together in a big tree. One day, they decided to sing a song. They looked around the tree and spied a long line of apples. So they hopped along the line and sang their song.

The bird on the left started with a fancy tune. The other bird followed and added her own notes. They chirped and sang until all the apples in the line were full of music.

The birds sang with such joy that the apples began to dance. They twisted and twirled and even jumped up high. The birds smiled and laughed and sang even louder.

When the song was finished, the apples thanked the birds for their wonderful singing. Then, with one final chirp the birds flew away, leaving the trees full of happiness.

Once upon a time there was a wealthy garage owner called John. John had lots of money and was very proud of it.

One day, a young boy and his father knocked on John's door. They asked if they could have shelter in the garage and John said no. He was not willing to accept them, even though they were poor.

The boy's father spoke up and said, "Please, my son is only three years old and it's getting late. We just need a place to sleep for the night, just until the morning."

But John refused to accept them and said, "I am wealthy and have a nice garage. Not just anyone can stay here!"

The father and son left feeling sad and scared. They walked on into the night not knowing where they could go.

The bad ending is that John never accepted the father and son, and they were out in the cold until the morning.

Once upon a time, there was a strong boy named Tim. He liked to play in the park. One day, he saw a tap near the big tree. The tap was old and rusty.

Tim said, "I want to turn the tap and see what happens." He tried to turn the tap, but it was very hard. He tried again and again. Finally, the tap turned, and water came out.

Tim's friend, Sam, came to see what was happening. "Wow!" said Sam. "You are so strong, Tim!" Tim smiled and said, "Yes, I am strong. Let's play with the water from the tap!" So Tim and Sam played in the water and had lots of fun.

One day, Joe and his mom went for a walk. They found some very pretty flowers growing in the ground. Joe wanted to pick one to bring home. His mom said it was not okay to steal from the ground. Joe said he would find an original flower to pick.

He found a unique yellow flower like none that he had seen before. But, it was growing in the ground. His mom repeated that it was not okay to steal from the ground. Joe said, “But, I want this flower for my room!” His mom said if he was very careful, he could pick it and take it home. Joe carefully picked the flower and brought it home.

Joe put the flower in a vase in his room. His mom smiled and told him he made a good decision by not stealing the flower. Joe was happy that the yellow flower was now in his room.

Once upon a time, there was a big, tough bear. He liked to march through the forest and scare all the little animals. One day, he got very tired and decided to take a nap. While he was sleeping, a tiny mouse tiptoed by and saw the big bear snoring. The mouse was brave and decided to tickle the bear's nose. The bear woke up with a start and saw the little mouse. But instead of scaring the mouse, the bear smiled and they became friends. From that day on, the bear would nap with the mouse and they would march through the forest together, but this time, the bear wasn't so tough anymore.

Once there was a very enthusiastic youth. He loved to go places and explore. One day, he decided to stay and explore the woods near his home. He stayed in the woods for a long time, observing all the different trees and animals.

He was so excited to explore the unknown and was filled with energy and enthusiasm. He would listen to the birds chirping and watch the squirrels running around while he stayed and admired the beauty of nature.

He continued to stay in the woods, exploring and admiring, until it started to get dark. He started to worry so he began to walk home. As he said goodbye to the woods, he promised himself to come back soon as he enjoyed his stay so much.

He skipped home, feeling full of energy and enthusiasm for life. His stay in the woods was one he would never forget.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to have fun and play with her toys. One day, she had a great idea. She wanted to have a party with her friends. She felt very happy about it.

Lily and her mommy made a big cake for the party. It was a yummy cake with pink and blue icing. Lily was excited to share the cake with her friends. They also had juice to drink. All the kids loved the cake and the juice.

At the party, everyone played games and laughed a lot. They were all happy. After they ate the cake and drank the juice, they played some more. Lily's party was so much fun. At the end of the day, all her friends went home with big smiles on their faces.

The sun was in the sky and the birds sang in the trees. Mary was walking in the park. She saw a frame on the ground. It was a picture of a distant house. But suddenly, the frame fell to the ground. Mary was surprised and bent down to pick it up. As she did, she saw a note stuck to the back of the frame. It said "Meet me at the distant house". Mary was excited. She thought it was a secret adventure! Mary ran through the park, she was so excited. Finally, she reached the distant house. Inside the house, she met her best friend who had left the note. They had a wonderful day together.

Once upon a time, there was a big dog. He loved to play catch with his friends in the park. He had four furry feet and a soft, pink nose.

One day, the dog was playing catch with his friend. He ran so fast that he tripped and fell on his knee. It hurt! He started to cry and his friend came to help.

His friend gave the dog a big hug and said, "It's okay. I'll help you," and put him on his soft lap. He put some cold water on the dog's knee and it felt better.

Then, his friend helped him up and said, "Let's play catch again!" The dog was so happy, and he barked and wagged his tail. They played for hours and everyone had lots of fun. It was the best day ever!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to receive cards from her friends. One day, Lily's friend sent her a card in the mail. Lily was so happy and excited to receive it. She opened the envelope and read the card. It said, "Happy Birthday Lily!"

Lily was so happy, but then she became frustrated. She realized that her birthday was not for another three months. She asked her mom, "Why did my friend send me a birthday card now?" Her mom explained that sometimes people send cards early because they might forget later.

Lily was still frustrated, but she decided to write a thank you card back to her friend. She thanked her friend for the card and told her that she was excited for her birthday in three months.

Unfortunately, a few days later, Lily's friend got very sick and had to go to the hospital. Lily was sad and worried about her friend. She wanted to visit her in the hospital, but her mom said they couldn't go because of the germs.

A few weeks later, Lily received another card in the mail. This time, it was from her friend's mom. The card said that Lily's friend had passed away. Lily was very sad and cried a lot. She was frustrated that she couldn't visit her friend in the hospital and say goodbye.

From that day on, Lily kept the card from her friend close to her heart, and she always remembered the happy times they had together.

Once upon a time, there was a little mouse who loved to explore. One day, he went on an adventure to find some yummy food. He followed a secret path and soon he came across a wine cellar. He was delighted!

He snuck into the cellar and he began to explore. On the shelves were many bottles of yummy red wine. He couldn't resist, so he quickly tried one of the bottles. But he had taken a little bit too much and he lost his balance and fell off the shelf!

He quickly scrambled back on the shelves, but he had dropped some of the wine. He was so embarrassed. He quickly gathered all the tiny drops of wine, but no matter how hard he tried, he couldn't find them all. He sighed. He had lost some of the wine!

But that was ok, he thought. He was happy just to have had the chance to explore and try the wine. He wished it hadn't been lost, but at least he had a little bit of fun. He was determined to be a little more careful the next time!

Once upon a time, there was a cute little dog named Spot. Spot loved to play with his friends in the park. One day, Spot saw a big iron gate. He wanted to go through the gate to find new friends.

Spot met a big dog named Max on the other side of the gate. Max liked to tease Spot because he was so small. Max said, "You are so tiny, you can't catch me!" Spot did not like being teased, but he wanted to be friends with Max.

Spot and Max played chase in the park. Spot ran as fast as he could, and he caught Max! Max was surprised and said, "Wow, you are fast for a little dog!" Spot and Max became best friends, and they played together every day. They learned that it is better to be kind than to tease each other.

Once upon a time, there was a little black cat named Mittens. Mittens liked to play all day, but today was a special day. It was bath day! Mittens didn't like baths, but she knew it was important to stay clean.

"Mittens, it's time to bathe," said her owner.

"I don't want to," replied Mittens.

"It's okay, Mittens. You'll feel much better after your bath," said her owner.

Mittens reluctantly got into the bath and her owner gently washed her with soap and water. When they were done, Mittens felt soft and clean. She was happy she had taken her bath and could now enjoy the rest of her day.

Once upon a time there was an elderly man who loved to watch the sunset every night. One night a small child asked the elderly gentleman why he watched the sunset every day. The elderly man replied, “I love to watch the sunset because it is a beautiful sight and it reminds me that every day is a new beginning.” The small child thought about the man's answer and asked him one more question “What if I miss the sunset? Will I miss out on the new beginning?” The elderly man smiled and replied, “No, my child, even if you miss the sunset, you can still make a new beginning every day. The sunset is just a reminder of how each day offers a fresh start.” The small child thanked the elderly man and said good-bye. After the child walked away, the elderly man smiled, happy that he had been able to teach the small child a valuable lesson. Whenever the elderly man watched the sunset from that day on, he would always remember the moral value he shared with the small child.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play in the park with her friends. One day, after playing on the swings and slide, Lily's mom gave her a towel to wipe her face. The towel was soft and fluffy, just like her favorite stuffed animal.

Lily's mom told her to examine the towel to make sure it was clean before using it. Lily looked at the towel closely and saw that it was safe to use. She wiped her face and hands and felt clean and refreshed.

After playing some more, Lily and her friends went home. Lily's mom was happy to see that she used the towel and kept herself clean. Lily was proud of herself for examining the towel and making sure it was safe to use.

Once upon a time, there was a soft sheep. The sheep had a lot of wool that kept her warm. One day, the sheep saw a butterfly and she wanted to play with it. She ran and jumped and sprang up into the air. The butterfly flew away, but the sheep was happy because she had fun. The end.

Tom and Lily were playing with their toy cars in the garden. They liked to make them zoom and crash on the grass. But then, Tom's car broke. One of its wheels came off and rolled away.

"Oh no!" Tom cried. "My car is broken! I need to repair it!"

Lily saw Tom's sad face and wanted to help. She looked around and found the wheel under a flower. She picked it up and ran to Tom.

"Here, Tom, I found your wheel!" she said. "Let me help you repair your car!"

But Tom was grumpy. He did not want Lily to touch his car. He snatched the wheel from her hand and said, "No, Lily, this is my car! You can't repair it! You don't know how!"

Lily felt hurt and angry. She crossed her arms and said, "Fine, Tom, be grumpy! I don't want to play with you anymore!"

She took her car and walked away. Tom tried to repair his car by himself, but he could not. He needed Lily's help. He realized he was mean to her and felt sorry.

"Lily, wait!" he called. "I'm sorry, Lily! Please come back and play with me! Please help me repair my car!"

Lily heard Tom's voice and turned around. She saw his sorry face and felt sorry too. She smiled and said, "OK, Tom, I forgive you. Let's repair your car together!"

She walked back to Tom and they fixed his car. They hugged and said, "We are friends again!"

They played with their cars happily and shared them with each other. They learned to be kind and helpful and not grumpy.

Once upon a time there was a lemon tree. It grew big and strong. Every day the sun shone on the lemon tree and it became more and more perfect.

One day, a small girl came to the lemon tree. She said, "I want to pick a lemon for my mommy." She reached for one of the lemons and pulled. But the lemon wouldn't come off.

The girl tried again. She pulled and pulled until finally the lemon came off the tree.

But when the lemon fell to the ground, it split in two. Juice sprayed all over the girl's clothes.

The girl was so sad. She had wanted a perfect lemon for her mommy. But now it was ruined.

She looked up at the tree sadly and said, "I'm sorry, lemon tree. I didn't mean to break your lemon."

But the lemon tree said nothing. Its perfect lemons were gone.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved to ride her bicycle. She had a pink bicycle with a basket in the front where she would put her toys.

One day, Lily's mom told her they were going on a picnic. Lily was very excited and got her bicycle ready. She put her favorite teddy bear in the basket and made sure her helmet was on tight.

As they rode their bicycles to the park, Lily's mom said, "I have a surprise for you, Lily. I planned a special treat for our picnic." Lily was curious and wondered what the surprise could be.

When they arrived at the park, Lily's mom took out a big red balloon from her bag. Lily was so happy and excited to play with the balloon. She thanked her mom for the surprise and happily rode her bicycle around the park with her balloon in the basket.

Once upon a time, there was a clever dog named Spot. Spot loved to run and play. One day, Spot heard about a big race in a stadium. Spot wanted to go and try to win.

Before the race, Spot saw a big hole near the stadium. He thought, "Hmm, maybe this hole will help me later." So, Spot put a big stick by the hole and went to enter the race.

During the race, Spot and the other dogs ran very fast. They were all trying to be first. Then, Spot remembered the hole. He ran to the hole, picked up the stick, and jumped over it. The other dogs fell into the hole, but Spot kept running. Spot won the race and everyone cheered. Spot was very clever and happy.

Ben and Lily liked to play in the garden. They had a big box of toys and they could build anything they wanted. One day, they decided to build a castle with blocks and a sword with sticks and tape.

"Look at my sword!" Ben said, holding up his stick. "It is long and sharp. I can fight the bad guys with it."

"Wow, that is a good sword!" Lily said, admiring his work. "Can I try it?"

Ben thought for a moment. He liked his sword very much, but he also liked Lily. She was his friend and she always shared her toys with him. He decided to be generous and let her use his sword.

"Okay, you can try it," he said, handing her the stick. "But be careful, it is very strong."

"Thank you, Ben, you are very generous," Lily said, smiling. She took the stick and pretended to swing it around. "I am a brave knight, too. I can help you protect the castle."

They played together for a long time, having fun and making noises. They built a big castle with blocks and put a flag on top. They used their sword to fight the bad guys and save the princess. They were happy and proud of their work. They were good friends and good builders.

Once upon a time, in a small town, there lived a girl named Amy. Amy loved to bake yummy cakes. One day, she had to bake a cake for her friend's birthday. She was a little anxious because she wanted the cake to be perfect.

Amy started to part the sugar into the cake mix. She added more and more sugar because she wanted the cake to be very sweet. When the cake was done, she put it in the oven to bake. She waited and waited for the cake to be ready.

Finally, the cake was done. Amy took it out of the oven and let it cool down. She tasted a small piece and realized it was too sweet! She felt sad because she added too much sugar. Amy learned that sometimes, adding too much of something can make it not good. From that day on, she always followed the recipe and her cakes turned out just right.

Once there was a little boy who loved spicy food. He always asked his mom to make him the spiciest food she could think of. One day, his mom reminded him that quiet was an important part of being at home. So the boy decided to try some quiet time.

He went outside and sat in the garden. He closed his eyes and tried to be still. Suddenly, he smelled something spicy. It was his mom cooking something delicious in the kitchen. He couldn't help but smile.

He tried to stay quiet, but he couldn't hold it in. He started to laugh, and soon his mom came outside to see what was funny. When she saw him sitting there enjoying the aroma, she smiled and hugged him. She reminded him that it's okay to laugh and be happy, but it's also important to take some time for quiet.

Tom and Anna are friends. They like to play in the field near their house. The field has many flowers and trees and birds. Sometimes they see a rabbit or a squirrel.

One day, Tom and Anna find a big bell in the field. It is shiny and has a rope. Tom and Anna wonder what it is for. They pull the rope and the bell makes a loud sound. Ring, ring, ring!

"Wow, that is fun!" Tom says. "Let's do it again!"

"No, Tom, stop!" Anna says. "That bell is important. It is for the farmer. He uses it to call his cows and sheep. If we ring it too much, he will be angry. And the animals will be confused."

"But I like the sound. It is pretty." Tom says. He pulls the rope again. Ring, ring, ring!

Anna is scared. She sees the farmer coming. He looks mad. He has a big hat and a stick. He shouts at Tom and Anna.

"Hey, you kids! What are you doing with my bell? Get away from there! You are making a mess!"

Tom and Anna run away. They are sorry. They did not know the bell was important. They say sorry to the farmer and to the animals. They promise to not touch the bell again. They go back to their house and play with their toys. They learn to be careful with things that are not theirs.

Once upon a time, a little girl named Lily loved to study. She had a big piano in her room. Lily played the piano every day. She wanted to play long songs on the piano.

One day, Lily's friend Tim came over to play. Tim wanted to play with toys, but Lily wanted to study the piano. They did not know what to do. Lily and Tim were sad.

Lily had an idea. She said, "Let's play a game. We can study the piano and play with toys." Tim liked the idea. They took turns playing the piano and playing with toys. They had a fun day and learned new songs.

Once upon a time, there was a fish named Nemo. Nemo loved to swim in the sea with his friends. One day, Nemo saw a shiny thing in the water. He thought it might be a treasure. Nemo asked his friend, "What is that shiny thing?" His friend said, "It's a pearl. It has a great price!"

Nemo wanted the pearl so badly that he swam to get it. But the pearl was tied to a fishing line. Suddenly, Nemo felt a tug and he was pulled out of the water. A man on a boat caught him with a fishing rod. Nemo cried, "Help! Help!" But it was too late. The man took Nemo away and sold him for a great price. Nemo's friends never saw him again.

Sam was a boy who liked to play with his toys. He had a big truck, a red car, a yellow ball and a hairy bear. He liked to make noises with his toys and pretend they were alive.

One day, Sam was playing with his hairy bear on the sofa. He made the bear say "Hello, I am a bear. I like honey and fish. Do you want to be my friend?" Sam said "Yes, I do. You are a nice bear. Can I hug you?" He hugged the bear and smiled.

But then, his mom came into the room. She said "Sam, it is time to go to the doctor. You have a sore arm and we need to see what is wrong." Sam did not like the doctor. He said "No, I don't want to go. I want to stay with my bear. He is my friend." He held the bear tight and frowned.

His mom said "I know, Sam, but the doctor will help you feel better. He will not hurt you. He will just look at your arm with a special machine. It is called an x-ray. It can see inside your arm and show us if there is a boo-boo." Sam was curious. He said "An x-ray? What does it look like? Can I see it?"

His mom said "Yes, you can. Come on, let's go. You can bring your bear with you. He can see the x-ray too. Maybe he will like it." She took Sam's hand and led him to the car. Sam said "Okay, mom. I will go with you. But only if you let me hold my bear. He is my friend." His mom said "Of course, Sam. You can hold your bear. He is your friend. And so am I." She kissed him on the cheek and drove to the doctor. Sam hugged his bear and hoped the x-ray would be fun.

Sara liked to play in the park with her friends. They ran, jumped, and slid on the grass and the swings. One day, Sara saw a big tree with many red and yellow leaves. She wanted to climb the tree and see the sky.

She asked her friends to help her, but they said no. They said the tree was too high and too hard. They said Sara could fall and hurt herself. They said they wanted to play with the ball instead. Sara was mad. She said she did not need their help. She said she was brave and strong. She said she would climb the tree by herself.

She left her friends and went to the tree. She grabbed a branch and pulled herself up. She felt happy and proud. She climbed higher and higher, until she reached the top. She looked around and saw the park, the road, and the hills. She saw the sun and the clouds. She smiled and waved at her friends. They looked very small and scared.

But then, Sara heard a loud crack. The branch she was on broke and she fell. She screamed and closed her eyes. She felt a deep pain in her arm and her leg. She cried and cried. She wished she had listened to her friends. She wished she had not climbed the tree. She regretted being mad and proud. She regretted leaving nature alone. She wanted her friends to help her. She wanted to go home.

Once upon a time, a little boy named Timmy went on a long walk. He was very thirsty and tired. Suddenly, he saw a beautiful oasis in the distance. He ran towards it as fast as he could.

When he arrived at the oasis, he felt very grateful. He drank some water and rested under a big tree. He observed the oasis and saw many animals drinking from the water. He saw birds flying in the sky and felt very happy.

After a while, Timmy continued his walk. He was no longer thirsty or tired. He felt happy and grateful for the oasis and all the wonderful things he observed there.

Lila and Ben liked to play in the park. They had a secret spot under a big tree, where they made a tunnel with sticks and leaves. They crawled inside and pretended they were on an adventure.

One day, they saw a new boy in the park. He had a red hat and a big smile. He came over to their tree and said, "Hi, I'm Sam. Can I play with you?"

Lila and Ben looked at each other. They liked their tunnel, but they also liked to make new friends. They said, "Sure, you can play with us. This is our tunnel. We made it ourselves. It's original."

Sam nodded and said, "Wow, that's cool. Can I see inside?"

Lila and Ben nodded and said, "Yes, but be careful. It's dark and narrow. You have to crawl on your hands and knees."

Sam followed them into the tunnel. He liked the feeling of being in a secret place. He said, "This is fun. Where does it lead?"

Lila and Ben smiled and said, "It leads to a magic land. We can go there if we say the magic word."

Sam asked, "What's the magic word?"

Lila and Ben said, "Part."

Sam said, "Part?"

Lila and Ben said, "Yes, part. Watch this."

They pushed on the wall of the tunnel and it opened up. They crawled out and saw a bright and colorful garden. There were flowers and butterflies and birds and a fountain. They said, "Welcome to our magic land. We can play here as long as we want."

Sam gasped and said, "Wow, this is amazing. How did you do that?"

Lila and Ben said, "We don't know. We just found it one day. It's our secret. Do you want to join us?"

Sam said, "Yes, please. This is the best game ever. Thank you for sharing it with me."

Lila and Ben said, "You're welcome. We're happy to have you as our friend."

They ran and played and laughed in the magic land. They forgot about the park and the time. They only remembered the tunnel and the word. Part.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy. He went into the park and he found an empty box. Inside the box was a key. He was so excited. He asked his mom what the key was for.

His mom said, "It looks like it might be the key to a door."

The little boy said, "What kind of door?"

His mom said, "We'll have to raise the box to find out."

So, the little boy and his mom raised the box. They saw that it was the door to a secret garden. They put the key in the lock and the door opened. Inside, there were so many fun things to explore!

The little boy said, "Mommy, can we explore it?"

His mom said, "Of course, let's go!"

And so, they explored the secret garden. It was an empty adventure, but it was full of wonder!

Sara was very sick. She had a bad cough and a hot head. She did not want to play or eat. She only wanted to rest in her bed.

Her mom was worried. She called the doctor and asked him to come. The doctor was a kind man with a big bag. He knocked on the door and said hello.

"Hello, Sara. I'm here to help you. Can I check your head and your chest?" he asked.

Sara nodded. She did not like the doctor's hand. It was rough and cold. It made her shiver. The doctor looked at his watch and said, "Hmm, you have a fever. You need some medicine and some water. And you need to rest a lot."

He gave Sara a spoon of medicine. It was bitter and yucky. Sara made a face and said, "Blech! I don't like it!"

"I know, Sara. But it will make you feel better. Trust me. And you can have some juice after. Do you like juice?" he said.

Sara nodded. She liked juice. It was sweet and yummy. She drank some juice and said, "Thank you, doctor."

"You're welcome, Sara. You're a brave girl. Now, you rest and sleep. I'll come back tomorrow and see how you are. OK?" he said.

Sara nodded. She was tired and sleepy. She closed her eyes and rested. She hoped she would feel better soon.

Once upon a time, there was an energetic little girl who had a special copper dress. Every morning she would dress in the copper dress and go outside to play with the other kids who lived in her town. Everyone enjoyed playing with her because she was so lively and full of energy, and always so cheerful and happy.

One day, the lively girl was late getting dressed and she didn't have time to put on her copper dress. She quickly ran outside, without her dress on. All the other kids started to giggle, and she felt embarrassed.

Seeing how upset and embarrassed the little girl was, the other kids understood that it was wrong to laugh and tease her. From then on, they chose to be kind and to not mock her. To remind everyone of the lesson learned, the lively girl made a plan and asked her mum for the copper dress. The next day, she put on the dress and went outside to play with her friends and neighbors - them all cheering her and celebrating her strong spirit!

The moral of this story is to remember not to make fun of other people, no matter how they look or what they’re wearing. We should always be kind, generous, and lively to each other.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to dance and sing, but sometimes she felt shy. Her mom would always encourage her to be brave and show her style.

One day, Lily's family went to a restaurant. Her dad ordered some spicy food, but Lily was scared to try it. Her mom said, "Don't worry, Lily. You can try a little bit. It's okay if you don't like it."

Lily took a small bite and her mouth felt hot. She drank some water and said, "It's too spicy for me." Her mom smiled and said, "That's okay. Everyone has different tastes. You can try something else next time."

Lily felt happy that her mom encouraged her to try something new, even if it was too spicy for her. She knew that her mom loved her and wanted her to be brave and confident in everything she did.

Lily was a little girl who liked to test things. She liked to test how high she could jump, how fast she could run, and how loud she could scream. She also liked to test her family, to see how they would react to her tests. Sometimes they would laugh, sometimes they would scold, and sometimes they would ignore her.

One day, Lily decided to test her family in a new way. She found a big bottle of paint in the garage, and thought it would be fun to test how it looked on the walls, the furniture, and the clothes. She opened the bottle and started to splash the paint everywhere, making a big mess. She giggled as she saw the bright colors on the gloomy things.

But her family did not giggle when they saw what she had done. They were very angry and sad. They yelled at her and told her she was naughty and mean. They said she had ruined their home and their things. They said they did not want to play with her or hug her anymore. They sent her to her room and locked the door.

Lily felt very sorry and scared. She did not mean to make her family mad. She just wanted to test them and have some fun. She wished she could take back the paint and the mess. She wished she could say sorry and make them happy again. But she could not. She was alone in her room, with no one to love her. She cried and cried, until she fell asleep. She had a bad dream. She dreamed that her family left her and never came back. She woke up and found that it was true.

Once upon a time, there was a tiny little bug that lived in a huge forest. One sunny day, he set out on an adventure to find a new home. The bug walked on the road and saw a beautiful butterfly. The butterfly had huge wings with lots of colors.

The bug asked the butterfly, "Where can I go home?" The butterfly said, "Come with me and I'll show you."

The bug and the butterfly flew over the road until they reached a large lake. The bug was so excited that he pinched the butterfly's wing. Ouch! The butterfly said, "That's not nice. Look over there. There's a huge tree with lots of leaves. That could be your new home!"

The bug thanked the butterfly and flew to the tree. He started making a home in the leaves and was very happy. He didn't want to leave this huge tree ever again.

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little bunny named Benny. Benny was very curious and loved to explore the forest. One day, he saw a big, scary wolf with sharp teeth. Benny was scared and ran away as fast as he could.

As he was running, he saw a squirrel with a soft, fluffy fur. Benny thought it was so pretty and wanted to touch it. But when he got close, the squirrel disappeared. Benny was confused and didn't understand where it went.

He kept running until he found a big rock that was very hard. Benny tried to move it, but it was too heavy. He thought about giving up, but then he remembered the squirrel that disappeared. He realized that sometimes things can appear or disappear, and that's okay. He learned that it's important to keep trying, even if things seem hard at first. From that day on, Benny was brave and never gave up.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to look at the stars at night. One night, he saw a bright planet in the sky. He was so happy to see it that he jumped up and down.

The next day, Timmy went to school. He was worried because he forgot to do his homework. When he got home, he regretted not doing his homework. He realized that he should have done it so he could learn more.

Later that night, Timmy went outside and looked up at the stars again. He saw the same planet from the night before. He smiled and felt happy again. Timmy learned that it's okay to make mistakes, but it's important to try your best and not regret things later.

Once upon a time there was a chubby rat. He was called Tiny. He wanted to find a job but couldn't find anyone who would hire him. He walked around town all day, hoping to find someone who needed his help.

One day, he stumbled across a cafe. The sign said "Help Wanted!" Tiny decided to give it a shot. He walked in and asked if they needed help.

The owner smiled and said, "Yes! We need someone to serve the customers. Can you do that?"

Tiny smiled and nodded. "Yes, I can serve the customers."

The owner hired Tiny on the spot and from then on, Tiny was a loyal and hardworking employee. He served happy customers with a smile on his face. Everyone was amazed by Tiny the chubby rat!

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim was going on a trip with his family. He was very excited and couldn't wait to go. Tim's mom asked him to pack his bag for the trip. Tim put his toys, clothes, and a book in his bag. He was very happy to help.

Tim's dad said they needed money for the trip. Tim went to his room and found his piggy bank. He shook it and heard the coins inside. Tim gave the piggy bank to his dad, who smiled and thanked him.

The day of the trip came, and Tim was impatient. He wanted to leave right away. His mom and dad told him they had to wait for his sister. When his sister was ready, they all got in the car and went on their fun trip. Tim was very happy, and they all had a great time.

Once upon a time, there was a nation. It was very comfortable and everyone was happy. One day, a curious kid pulled on the flagpole near the center of town. He tugged and tugged, but it was too heavy for him. Suddenly, the flagpole began to move! The ground started to shake, and the kid could feel a big change coming. With one final pull, the nation was lifted up into the sky! Everyone in the nation cheered and smiled as they looked down on their cozy home from up above. Even though the kid had never seen anything so amazing, he felt comfortable and safe. With a tug, the nation had been transformed into something new and wonderful. The people all lived happily ever after in the sky.

Jake and his mom were walking through the town. Everything was so bright and colourful. As they walked they saw a fake bus. It was so shiny and yellow. It had fake windows and seats inside.

Suddenly his mom stopped and pointed. “Look Jake,” she said. “That man is trying to separate the bus!”

Jake saw the man. He was pulling the bus apart with a big machine. It was making loud noises and the man had to cover his ears. The two of them watched as the man separated the bus into two pieces.

When the man was finished he smiled at Jake and his mom. He waved and said, “It’s all done now!”.

Jake and his mom said goodbye to the man then continued walking through the town. Jake smiled, he had never seen a fake bus separate before!

Once upon a time, there was an alert cat who was looking for something special. He wanted to win a prize. He had heard that he just needed to find a steel box. He searched high and low, but he just couldn't find the steel box anywhere.

Finally, he got to a big wide lake. He saw a steel box hidden in the water. He was so excited! He carefully swam close to it and reached out his paw. He opened the box and there was a big surprise inside! It was a shiny toy car. He had won a prize!

The cat was so happy, he ran back home with his new toy car to show his family. From that day on, he was proud of his win!

Lily and Tom were playing in the park. They liked to slide, swing and run. They saw a big puddle. They wanted to jump in it.

"Let's jump in the puddle!" Lily said.

"OK!" Tom said.

They ran to the puddle and jumped in. Splash! They got very wet. They laughed and jumped again.

A lady was walking by. She had a big hat and a long dress. She did not see the puddle. She stepped in it. Splash! She got very wet too. She was not happy.

"Hey!" she said. "What are you doing? You made me wet!"

Lily and Tom stopped jumping. They looked at the lady. They were sorry.

"We are sorry, lady," Lily said. "We did not see you. We were playing."

The lady looked at them. She saw their wet clothes and their wet faces. She saw their big eyes and their small mouths. She guessed they did not mean to make her wet. She guessed they were just having fun.

She sighed. She smiled. She said, "It's OK. I guess it was an accident. But next time, be careful. You might make someone else wet."

Lily and Tom nodded. They said, "OK, lady. We will be careful. Thank you for being nice."

The lady nodded. She said, "You're welcome. Have a good day."

She walked away. She was still wet. But she was not angry.

Lily and Tom looked at each other. They smiled. They said, "Let's play some more!"

They ran to the slide. They slid down. They had fun. They were wet. But they were happy.

Once upon a time, two friends went for a walk outside. It was a sunny day and the birds were singing.

The two friends spotted an underground entrance in the ground.

"Let's go in," said one of them.

"No, it looks bad," said the other. “We should not care.”

But his friend didn't listen. He went inside and a strange noise came out.

The other friend called out to him, "Come out! You should not care if it's bad!"

His friend listened and came out, safe and sound.

The two friends hugged and laughed, happy that they had taken care. They promised each other never to go into the underground again.

The End.

Once upon a time, there was a boat with an anchor. The boat was very lively and sailed on the big blue sea. The anchor helped the boat to remain in one place when the sea got rough.

One day, a big storm came and the boat was not able to remain in one place. The anchor was not strong enough to hold the boat and the boat was thrown around by the big waves.

The boat was not able to make it through the storm and it sank to the bottom of the sea. The moral of the story is that sometimes things that seem strong are not strong enough to withstand the power of nature.

Tim and Kim were twins who liked to play in the garden. They had a big sandbox, a slide, and a swing. They also had a dog named Spot who liked to dig holes and chase birds.

One day, Mom told them to come inside for lunch. "Tim, Kim, Spot, it's time to eat. Come on, hurry up!" she called from the kitchen.

But Tim and Kim did not want to stop playing. They wanted to build a castle in the sand. "Just a little more, Mom. We are almost done," they said.

Mom sighed. She knew they loved to play, but they also needed to eat. She decided to give them a few more minutes. She went back to the kitchen and finished making sandwiches and juice.

Meanwhile, Spot saw a big black bird on the fence. He barked and ran towards it. The bird flew away, but Spot did not stop. He jumped over the fence and followed the bird into the street.

Tim and Kim heard Spot's barking and looked up. They saw him running away from the garden. They were scared. They knew the street was dangerous. There were cars and trucks and bikes. They dropped their shovels and ran after Spot. "Spot, come back! Spot, stop!" they shouted.

Mom heard their shouting and looked out the window. She saw them running after Spot. She was very worried. She grabbed her keys and ran outside. She saw a mop leaning against the wall. She took it with her. She thought she might need it to catch Spot or to scare away the cars.

She ran after Tim and Kim and Spot. She saw them crossing the street. She saw a car coming fast. She yelled, "Tim, Kim, Spot, watch out!"

The car saw them and stopped. The driver honked his horn. He was angry. He got out of his car and said, "What are you doing? You could have been hurt. You should not run in the street. It's very serious."

Mom reached Tim and Kim and Spot. She hugged them and said, "I'm so glad you are okay. But you should not have run after Spot. You should have listened to me. It's very serious. You could have been hurt. You made me very scared."

Tim and Kim and Spot looked at Mom. They saw her face. They saw her mop. They knew they were in trouble. They said, "We are sorry, Mom. We were playing and we did not hear you. We wanted to save Spot. We did not mean to delay lunch. We did not mean to make you scared."

Mom said, "I know you love Spot, but you have to be careful. The street is not a place to play. You have to obey me when I call you. You have to come inside for lunch. You have to eat and rest. Then you can play again. But only in the garden. Do you understand?"

Tim and Kim and Spot nodded. They said, "We understand, Mom. We will obey you. We will come inside for lunch. We will eat and rest. Then we will play again. But only in the garden."

Mom smiled. She said, "That's good. Now let's go inside. Your sandwiches and juice are waiting for you. And your mop too. You have to help me clean the floor. You made it dirty with your shoes and paws. It's not serious, but it's fair."

Tim and Kim and Spot said, "Okay, Mom. We will help you clean the floor. We will use the mop. We will make it shiny. It's not serious, but it's fair."

They all went inside. They ate their lunch. They helped Mom clean the floor. They used the mop. They made it shiny. Then they played again. But only in the garden. They were happy. And Mom was happy too.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, she found a pretty jewel on the ground. She picked it up and held it in her hand. It sparkled and shone in the sunlight.

Lily loved her jewel so much that she didn't want to let it go. She held onto it tightly all day long. But, when it was time for bed, her mommy told her she couldn't sleep with the jewel because it was too precious. Lily felt foolish for not knowing that.

The next day, Lily went outside to play and found a little boy who had lost his toy car. She saw how sad he was and decided to help him. She held his hand and they searched everywhere until they found the toy car. The little boy was so happy and grateful that he gave Lily a hug. Lily felt happy too, and realized that holding onto something precious is not as important as helping others.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She lived in a small house near a big mill. The mill was very noisy and Lily didn't like it.

One day, Lily's mom asked her to mail a letter at the post office. Lily was very excited to do this because she had never done it before. She put on her modest dress and ran to the post office.

When she got there, she gave the letter to the nice lady behind the counter. The lady smiled and said, "Thank you, Lily!" Lily felt very proud of herself for mailing her first letter. She ran back home, past the noisy mill, and told her mom all about it. From that day on, Lily loved to mail letters and always wore her modest dress when she did.

Lily liked to play with her dolls. She had many dolls, but her favorite was Anna. Anna had a pink dress, blue eyes and long hair. Lily thought Anna was charming.

One day, Lily's aunt came to visit. She brought a big box for Lily. Lily was happy and curious. She opened the box and saw a new doll. The doll had a yellow dress, green eyes and curly hair. She also had a buckle on her belt. Lily's aunt said, "This is Belle. She is from France. I bought her for you when I was there. Do you like her?"

Lily looked at Belle and smiled. She liked her too. She said, "Thank you, auntie. She is very pretty. I like her buckle. It is shiny." She hugged Belle and kissed her cheek.

Lily's aunt said, "You're welcome, sweetie. I'm glad you like her. I have to go now, but I will see you soon. I love you." She hugged Lily and kissed her forehead.

Lily said, "I love you too, auntie. Bye bye." She waved at her aunt as she left.

Lily took Belle and Anna to her room. She said, "Anna, this is Belle. She is your new friend. Belle, this is Anna. She is my best friend. You can play with us." She put them on her bed and gave them each a toy. She said, "Let's pretend we are princesses. We can send letters to each other with our toys. It will be fun." She smiled and started to play.

Tim and Sam are friends. They like to play in the farm. They see many animals. They see cows, sheep, chickens and pigs.

One day, they hear a loud noise. They run to see what it is. They see a big truck. The truck has a cage. The cage has many pigs. The pigs are scared. They squeal and cry.

Tim and Sam are worried. They love the pigs. They do not want the pigs to go away. They talk to the pigs.

"Hello, pigs. Why are you sad?" Tim asks.

"We are sad because we have to leave. The truck will take us to a bad place. We do not want to go. We want to stay here with you." A pig says.

Tim and Sam are sad too. They hug the pigs. They want to help the pigs.

"Can we stop the truck? Can we free the pigs?" Sam asks.

"I do not know. The truck is big and fast. The driver is mean. He will not listen to us." Tim says.

They think hard. They have an idea. They run to the barn. They find a rope. They tie the rope to the fence. They stretch the rope across the road. They hide behind the bushes.

They wait for the truck. The truck comes. The truck does not see the rope. The truck hits the rope. The truck stops. The cage opens. The pigs run out. The pigs are happy. They thank Tim and Sam.

"Thank you, Tim and Sam. You are our heroes. You saved us. You are our friends." A pig says.

Tim and Sam are happy too. They smile and wave. They watch the pigs run to the field. They play with the pigs. They are the best friends.

Once there was a thin tooth. She wanted to act in a play, but she was scared. She was too scared to try. But then one day, she thought she should take a chance. She took a deep breath, plucked up her courage, and began to act in the play. At first she was very scared and kept messing up her lines. But then she felt more comfortable and started to do better. Soon enough, she was talking with confidence and the audience clapped and cheered. Now the tooth felt so happy and brave, and she knew she could do anything she put her mind to!

Ben loved his scooter. He rode it every day in the park with his mom and dad. He liked to go fast and make loud noises with his mouth. He felt happy and free on his scooter.

One day, he saw an elderly lady sitting on a bench. She had white hair and a kind face. She smiled at Ben as he zoomed by. Ben stopped and said hello. The lady said hello back and asked him his name. Ben told her his name and showed her his scooter. The lady said it was a nice scooter and asked if she could try it.

Ben was surprised. He had never seen an elderly lady ride a scooter before. He wondered if she could do it. He was curious and generous, so he said yes. He helped the lady get on his scooter and held her hand. The lady thanked him and started to move slowly. She looked happy and excited. She said it was fun and reminded her of when she was young.

Ben watched her and felt proud. He thought she was brave and cool. He clapped and cheered for her. The lady rode for a while and then came back to Ben. She gave him his scooter and hugged him. She said he was a very nice boy and that he had made her day. She told him to always enjoy his scooter and his life. She said goodbye and left.

Ben waved goodbye and felt warm and fuzzy. He had made a new friend and learned something new. He got on his scooter and rode away with a big smile. He felt happy and free on his scooter.

Once upon a time, there was a small little girl called Lucy. She was three years old and really liked to dance. Every day she would put on her favourite pink dress and dance to the music.

Today was especially exciting because there was a jazz band coming to Lucy's house. As they started to play, Lucy began to dance. She was so happy!

Suddenly there was a really loud crash and the music stopped. Lucy looked around, confused. One of the musicians had broken their instrument! Everyone was so disappointed.

The Jazz Band leader said, "This is terrible! We need to mail this instrument to the shop to get it fixed. We won't be able to finish our performance."

The band packed up their things and left. Lucy looked very sad, until she remembered that she could keep on dancing. She smiled and put on her favourite pink dress. She danced for the rest of the day and had lots of fun.

Once upon a time there was a girl named Mary. Mary loved to relax. She would go to the park and sit on a big green blanket. Under the sun she would lay down and look up at the sky.

One day Mary found something special in the park – a red herb. She knew it was a special type of plant because it was so bright and smelled so nice.

Mary carefully picked the red herb and took it home to put in a pot of soil. She watered it every day and it soon grew bigger and bigger. Every time she looked at it, it made her feel happy because it brought back memories of the park.

The red herb helped Mary relax. She read books and smelled the sweet aroma of the herb. It made her feel so calm and peaceful.

Mary was so happy with her red herb. She kept taking care of it and relaxing in its presence. It became one of Mary's favorite things in the whole world.

Once there was a girl named Joy. She was three years old and liked to explore. There was one thing she liked to do more than anything, and that was to reach for the stars.

The other day, Joy looked around her room and saw something she had never seen before. It was a funny looking notebook with an open cover. It was so colourful and fun! She grabbed it quickly and opened it up.

Suddenly, a voice said, "What do you want?" It was coming from inside the notebook. Joy was so surprised!

"I want to reach the star!", said Joy.

The voice answered, "Well, Joy, this notebook can help you reach your dream. Turn the page and you'll see how."

Joy turned the page and there was a map with a star right in the middle. Joy was so excited! She followed the map, and sure enough, soon she was standing right beneath a star. Joy had reached her dream!

Once upon a time there was a boy called Tim. Tim really wanted to play but his mum said he had to stay inside. Tim felt anxious but he tried to let it go.

Tim asked his mum if he could go outside and play. His mum said no. Tim felt very sad and angry. He started making a fuss and begging his mum to let him go out.

Mum said no, again. Tim was getting anxious. He started to cry. Then his mum said he could go out in the garden - but he had to stay there and take care.

Tim was so happy. He put his shoes on and ran outside. He started playing with his toys and laughed and smiled. He popped in from time to time to check with his mum. He was relieved and happy.

Tim played for hours and hours and ended up with a smile on his face.

Tom and Lily are friends. They like to play in the school. One day, they enter the class and see a new desk. It is big and shiny. Tom and Lily want to sit on the new desk.

"Let's sit on the new desk!" Tom says.

"Yes, let's!" Lily says.

But then, Sam comes. Sam is big and mean. He pushes Tom and Lily away.

"This is my desk!" Sam says. "Go away!"

Tom and Lily are sad and scared. They do not know what to do.

Then, Miss Lee comes. Miss Lee is the teacher. She is kind and smart. She sees what Sam is doing.

"Sam, what are you doing?" Miss Lee says. "Why are you pushing Tom and Lily?"

Sam does not answer. He looks angry.

"Sam, this is not your desk. This is the new desk for the class. Everyone can use it. You have to share and be nice." Miss Lee says.

Sam does not like to share. He does not like to be nice. He makes a face.

"Fine!" Sam says. He gets off the new desk. He goes to his old desk.

Miss Lee smiles. She helps Tom and Lily to sit on the new desk.

"Tom and Lily, you can use the new desk today. Tomorrow, you can take turns with the other kids. Okay?" Miss Lee says.

Tom and Lily nod. They are happy. They thank Miss Lee.

"Thank you, Miss Lee!" Tom and Lily say.

They play on the new desk. They draw and write and read. They have fun.

They are glad that Miss Lee is kind and smart. They are glad that they are friends.

Molly and her mommy went to the store. Molly wanted to get a new toy, so mommy said yes.

At the store, there was a big sign that said "No Toys Allowed!" Molly was very sad and decided to refuse the sign.

Mommy was very thoughtful. She said, "I know you want the toy, but we can come back another day. Let's look for something else instead."

So, Molly picked out a pretty necklace and mommy bought it for her. Molly was so happy, she forgot all about the toy!

Molly and her mommy smiled as they left the store. Molly was glad that mommy was so thoughtful!

Once upon a time, there was a big bear. The bear liked to go to the shop to buy honey. But one day, the shop was closed. The bear didn't like that. He got mad and started to fight with the door. The door didn't move, but the bear kept trying. After a while, the bear got tired and went back to his cave. But on the way, he smelled something smelly. It was a skunk! The bear didn't like the smell, so he ran away as fast as he could. From that day on, the bear made sure to check if the shop was open before going there.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy had a big dog named Spot. Spot was very friendly and loved to play with Timmy. One day, Timmy and Spot went on a walk and found an open book on the ground. Timmy picked up the book and saw that it was about animals. He decided to study the book and learn all about the different animals in it. Spot sat next to him and listened as Timmy read the book out loud. Timmy was very happy to learn new things and Spot was happy to be with his best friend. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a quiet little girl who went outside to play. She played all day and had a lot of fun.

Around dinner time, the little girl wanted to catch something for dinner. She looked all around and then she saw a big butterfly. She chased it until she caught it.

Then the little girl took her butterfly home to show her mom. The mom was very proud of her daughter and they made a delicious dinner with the butterfly.

They ate dinner together and the little girl was so happy. She enjoyed her delicious dinner and had a good night's sleep afterwards. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a poor boy called Benny. He was very sad, as he had no friends to play with.

One day, Benny got an idea. He took out his big box of masks and held them up to his face.

“Maybe if I dress up, my friends will come to find me," he thought.

He picked out his favourite mask and put it on. All of a sudden, he heard someone giggling behind him.

When he turned around, he saw a girl wearing a mask too. She smiled at him and said, “Hi Benny, do you want to play?”

Benny was so happy. He said, “Yes, let’s guess what our masks are!”

So they took turns guessing what their masks were. Benny guessed that his mask was a rabbit and the girl's mask was a cat. He was right and the girl was very impressed.

By the time it was dark, Benny and the girl's masks had become the best of friends. Benny was no longer poor, he had a new friend.

Jax was always an adventurous three-year-old. He had an unusual scooter that he loved to play on. One day Jax had the urge to explore the world around him. He decided to take his scooter out into the backyard and see what he could find.

Jax pedaled around the yard, looking at the plants and bugs that he came across. He even saw a bird and waved to it! Eventually, he stopped at the pond in the backyard and looked in. Jax had the urge to jump in the water, but he remembered what he had been told by his parents. So he stayed on his scooter, content with just looking.

Soon Jax heard his mom call for lunch. He quickly pedaled back to the house, feeling happy and excited about the unusual adventure he had just gone on. He was also excited for what adventures he would go on the next day!

Sam was so excited! Every day he got to go to the park and slide down the really big slide. It was so much fun. Today was even more special for Sam. He got to take his fish with him! Of course, it wasn't a real fish – it was his toy shark.

The slide was so big and so fast! As he went down, Sam's shark was tumbling around in his hands. He was so grateful that he had it to share this moment with him.

At the bottom of the slide Sam and his shark looked up with big smiles. Slide again? Yes, please! This time Sam put his shark in front of him and put his arms around it as they zoomed down the slide.

When they reached the bottom Sam and his shark were so happy. What a great day filled with slides and fun! Sam was so grateful he got to share it with his special shark.

One day, a big storm came to the village. The sky was dark and loud. The wind was strong and cold. The people were scared and ran to their houses.

But one boy, Tom, was not scared. He liked storms. He wanted to see the lightning. He ran out of his house and climbed a hill. He saw the bright flashes in the sky. He heard the big booms. He felt the rain on his face. He was happy.

"Tom, come back!" his mother shouted. "It is not safe! The lightning can strike you!"

But Tom did not listen. He wanted to see more. He ran to a big tree. He touched the tree. He felt the bark. He felt something else. He felt a shock. He saw a flash. He heard a boom. He fell down.

The lightning had struck the tree. And Tom. He was hurt. He was not happy. He was sorry.

His mother ran to him. She saw him on the ground. She saw the tree on fire. She was scared and sad. She hugged him. She cried.

"Tom, Tom, are you okay?" she asked.

Tom opened his eyes. He saw his mother. He saw the smoke. He felt the pain. He was sorry.

"Mom, I am sorry," he said. "I was bad. I did not listen. I wanted to see the storm. But it was not fun. It was rare. And dangerous."

His mother kissed him. She was glad he was alive. She was not angry. She was sorry too.

"Tom, I am sorry too," she said. "I love you. You are not bad. You are curious. But you have to be careful. The storm is rare. And dangerous. You have to stay with me. And be safe."

She carried him to their house. She put him in his bed. She gave him some water. She sang him a song. He felt better. He felt sleepy.

He closed his eyes. He dreamed of the storm. But he did not like it anymore. He liked his mother. And his house. And his bed. He was safe. He was happy.

Anna and Ben are twins. They like to play with their toys and their dog, Spot. Spot is a cute dog. He has brown fur and a black nose. He likes to run and jump and lick Anna and Ben.

One day, Anna and Ben are playing in the living room. They hear Spot barking in the kitchen. They run to see what is wrong. They see Spot standing on his hind legs, trying to reach the cupboard. The cupboard has the dog food inside.

"Spot, what are you doing?" Anna asks. "You are not supposed to open the cupboard. That is naughty."

"Maybe he is hungry," Ben says. "Let's feed him some dog food."

Anna and Ben get a bowl and a scoop. They open the cupboard and take out some dog food. They pour some dog food into the bowl and put it on the floor. Spot wags his tail and runs to the bowl. He starts to eat the dog food.

"Good boy, Spot," Anna says. "You are a good dog. We love you."

"Yes, we love you, Spot," Ben says. "But next time, wait for us to feed you. Don't try to open the cupboard by yourself. You could hurt yourself or make a mess."

Spot looks up at Anna and Ben. He licks his lips and barks. He is happy and full. He thanks Anna and Ben for feeding him. He cuddles with them on the couch. They play and laugh together. They are a happy family.

One day, a 3-year-old boy named Jimmy went to the store with his mom. He saw a big can of tuna and asked his mom if he could have it. She said yes, and they took the tuna home.

At home, Jimmy tried to open the can of tuna, but he couldn't. His mom said: "Let me help you." She showed Jimmy how to open the can, and he learned quickly.

Jimmy was so excited to try the tuna. But when he opened the can, he saw that the tuna was a little bit upset. He didn't know what this meant, but he was very curious. So, he asked his mom, "What does 'upset' mean?". His mom said, "It means the tuna isn't very fresh, Jimmy".

Jimmy was a little disappointed, but he still tried the tuna. He thought it was delicious. So he said to his mom: "I learned something today: tuna can be upset, but it still tastes good!"

Lily and Ben were twins who liked to play with their toys. They had many toys, but they always wanted more. They asked their mom and dad for new toys every day. Mom and dad said no, because they had enough toys and they should be happy with what they had. But Lily and Ben did not listen. They cried and whined and threw tantrums. They said they were not happy and they wanted more toys.

One day, mom and dad had to go to work and they left Lily and Ben with their grandma. Grandma was very kind and gentle. She made them pancakes for breakfast and read them stories. She also gave them a big box of toys that she had saved from when mom and dad were little. Lily and Ben were very excited. They opened the box and saw many toys that they had never seen before. There were cars and dolls and puzzles and books and blocks and animals. Lily and Ben grabbed the toys and ran to their room. They did not say thank you to grandma. They did not share the toys with each other. They fought and snatched and broke the toys. They made a big mess in their room.

Grandma heard the noise and came to their room. She saw the toys scattered and torn and ruined. She saw Lily and Ben crying and yelling. She was very sad and angry. She said, "Lily and Ben, you have spoiled the toys that I gave you. You have spoiled the fun that you could have had. You have spoiled the day that we could have spent together. You have been very selfish and ungrateful. You do not deserve these toys. You need to learn to be happy with what you have and to share and care for others. Now you have to clean up this mess and put the toys back in the box. And you have to say sorry to me and to each other. And you have to sit in the corner and think about what you have done. No more toys for you today."

Lily and Ben felt very ashamed and sorry. They did what grandma said. They cleaned up the mess and put the toys back in the box. They said sorry to grandma and to each other. They sat in the corner and thought about what they had done. They realized that they had been very bad and that they had hurt grandma and themselves. They wished they had been more kind and thankful and happy. They wished they had played nicely with the toys and with each other. They wished they had spent more time with grandma and listened to her stories.

The rest of the day was very quiet and boring. There was no more noise and fun and laughter. There was only silence and sadness and regret. Lily and Ben learned a hard lesson that day. They learned that being greedy and spoiled can make you lose what you have and what you love. They learned that being happy and grateful and sharing can make you gain more than you expect. They learned that being good and respectful and loving can make you and others happy. They learned that sometimes, less is more.
