Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved to play with her toys. One day, she accidentally knocked over a jar of perfume and it scattered all over the floor.

"Oh no!" cried Lily. "My mommy's perfume is all over the place!"

Lily's mommy came into the room and smelled the sour scent of the perfume. "Lily, what happened?" she asked.

"I'm sorry, mommy," said Lily. "I knocked over the jar and it scattered everywhere."

"Don't worry, sweetie," said her mommy. "Let's clean it up together."

Lily and her mommy cleaned up the perfume and the room smelled much better. From that day on, Lily learned to be more careful with her toys and her mommy's things.

Once upon a time, there was a woman named Jane. Jane had a cat named Fluffy. One day, Jane was nervous because Fluffy was missing. She looked everywhere for him.

Jane saw a little boy named Timmy. Timmy had Fluffy. Jane was upset that Timmy took Fluffy. Timmy said he was sorry. He did not know that Fluffy was Jane's cat.

Jane was nice and decided to forgive Timmy. She knew Timmy did not mean to take Fluffy away. Jane and Timmy became friends. They played with Fluffy together. They all lived happily ever after.

Tom and Lily were playing in the sandbox. They liked to make castles and bridges with the sand and water. But it was very hot and sunny, and they were thirsty and tired.

"Let's go find some shade and juice," Lily said.

"OK," Tom agreed. They got up and looked around. They saw a big tree with green leaves and red fruits. It looked like an oasis in the desert.

"Wow, look at that tree!" Tom exclaimed. "It has apples!"

"Let's go get some!" Lily said. They ran towards the tree, hoping to find some cool and sweet snacks.

But when they reached the tree, they saw a grumpy old man sitting under it. He had a long beard and a hat. He was holding a stick and a basket.

"Hey, you kids, get away from my tree!" he shouted. "These are my apples, and you can't have any!"

Tom and Lily were scared and sad. They wanted some apples, but they didn't want to make the old man angry.

"Please, sir, can we have just one apple?" Lily asked politely. "We are very thirsty and hungry."

"No, you can't!" the old man snapped. "These are my apples, and I worked hard to grow them. You can't just come and take them. Go find your own tree!"

Tom and Lily felt like crying. They turned around and walked away. They looked for another tree, but they couldn't find any. They only saw sand and rocks and cacti.

They were about to give up, when they saw something shiny and colorful. It was a kite, hanging from a cactus. It had a long tail and a smiling face.

"Look, Lily, a kite!" Tom said. "Maybe someone left it here. Maybe we can play with it."

"Maybe," Lily said. "But how can we get it? It's too high."

Tom had an idea. He found a big rock and climbed on it. He reached for the kite, but it was still too far. He stretched his arm and his fingers, but he couldn't touch it.

"Come on, Tom, you can do it!" Lily cheered.

Tom tried harder. He jumped and grabbed the kite. He pulled it down and freed it from the cactus. He was happy and proud.

"Yay, I got it!" he said. "Let's fly it!"

He gave the kite to Lily and took the string. They ran with the kite, making it soar in the sky. They laughed and smiled, forgetting about the heat and the thirst and the grumpy old man.

They found a new oasis, and they had fun.

Lily liked to make things with her hands. She had a box of buttons of different colors and shapes. She liked to sew them on her clothes, or glue them on paper, or string them on a thread. She was very proud of her button crafts.

One day, she wanted to show her friend Ben what she had made. She took her box of buttons and went to his house. She knocked on the door and Ben opened it.

"Hi, Lily! What do you have there?" Ben asked.

"I have my buttons. I made some things with them. Do you want to see?" Lily said.

"Sure, I like buttons too. Come in, come in!" Ben said.

Lily followed Ben to his room. She opened her box and showed him her button crafts. She had a button necklace, a button bracelet, a button flower, and a button star.

"Wow, Lily, these are amazing! You are very good at making things with buttons. How did you do it?" Ben said.

Lily smiled. She was happy that Ben liked her button crafts. She told him how she sewed, glued, and strung the buttons. She also gave him some tips on how to choose the right buttons for each craft.

"Thank you, Lily. You are very kind and helpful. Can I try to make something with your buttons too?" Ben said.

"Of course, Ben. You can use any buttons you want. I have plenty. I will help you if you need. We can make something together." Lily said.

They decided to make a button picture of their favorite animal. Ben chose a dog and Lily chose a cat. They looked for buttons that matched the colors and shapes of their animals. They glued them on a piece of paper. They also added some details like eyes, nose, mouth, and ears with a marker.

They finished their button picture and showed it to each other. They were very happy with their work. They complimented each other on their creativity and skill.

"Lily, you are very modest. You don't brag about your button crafts, but you share them with me and encourage me to try. You are a good friend." Ben said.

"Ben, you are very nice. You don't laugh at my button crafts, but you admire them and ask me to teach you. You are a good friend too." Lily said.

They hugged and agreed to make more button crafts together. They put their button picture on the wall and admired it. They had fun with their buttons.

One day Lucy went for a walk. She was carrying an ordinary bucket. The sun was shining and she wanted to have some fun.

She came to a park and she saw swings. She ran over and had a go. Then she saw a slide. She went over and tried it.

After that, Lucy looked around and saw sand. She smiled and put her bucket down. She started to fill it with sand. She made a big pile.

Suddenly, a big shadow covered the sand. Lucy turned around and saw a big airplane flying above her head. She waved at it and it flew away.

Lucy picked up her bucket and went home. She had had a great day.

Once upon a time, there was a little dog named Max. Max loved to move and play all day. One day, Max saw a dish with yummy food on the table. Max knew he should not touch the dish, but he could not help himself.

Max jumped up and knocked the dish down. The food went everywhere! Max felt guilty for making the mess. He knew it was wrong to take the dish.

Max's owner found the mess and asked Max if he did it. Max nodded his head and said sorry. Max's owner told Max that it is important to be honest and not take things that are not his. Max learned his lesson and never took a dish again.

Lily and Tom are twins. They have long, curly hair. They like to play with their hair and make funny shapes. But today, they have to go to the salon. They have to get a haircut.

Lily is scared of the scissors. She does not want to cut her hair. She thinks it will hurt. She cries and hides behind Mom. Tom is brave. He wants to cut his hair. He thinks it will make him look cool. He smiles and sits on the chair.

The lady with the scissors is nice. She talks to Tom and shows him pictures. She asks him how he wants his hair. Tom points to a picture of a boy with short, spiky hair. He says he wants that. The lady nods and starts to cut his hair.

Lily watches from behind Mom. She sees Tom's hair fall to the floor. She sees his new hair. It is short and spiky. It looks cool. Lily feels something in her chest. She feels envious. She wants to have cool hair too. She stops crying and comes out from behind Mom. She says she wants a haircut too.

The lady with the scissors is happy. She says she can give Lily a haircut too. She asks her how she wants her hair. Lily looks at the pictures. She sees a girl with long, straight hair. She says she wants that. The lady nods and starts to cut her hair.

Tom watches from the chair. He sees Lily's hair fall to the floor. He sees her new hair. It is long and straight. It looks pretty. Tom feels something in his chest. He feels envious. He wants to have pretty hair too. He says he wants his hair back.

Mom and the lady with the scissors laugh. They say hair grows back. They say Lily and Tom are both beautiful. They say they can play with their hair and make funny shapes again. Lily and Tom hug each other. They say they love each other. They say they love their hair. They are happy.

Once upon a time, there was a humble doctor. Every day he questions people to make them feel better. One day, he met a 3 year old child with a big smile.

The doctor asked the child: "How are you?". The little child replied with a giggle "I am happy!". The doctor smiled and asked the child other questions to help him understand him better. The child enjoyed talking to the doctor and sharing his thoughts with him.

The doctor asked the child many questions, but the child only ever had one answer. He told the doctor that he was always happy. After much questioning, the doctor began to understand why the child was so happy. He explained to the child that sometimes life gets hard, but having a positive outlook could help him find better solutions to life's problems.

The little child smiled at the doctor. He thanked him for teaching him the importance of being happy and humble. From then on the little child kept his happy smile and spread happiness to those around him.

Tim and Jen are twins. They like to play in the snow. They put on their coats, hats, boots and gloves. They go outside with their mom.

"Look, mom, snowman!" Tim says. He points to a big snowman in the park. The snowman has a carrot nose, a scarf and a hat.

"Can we play with the snowman, mom?" Jen asks. She likes the snowman's smile.

"Sure, but be careful. Don't break the snowman," mom says. She sits on a bench and watches them.

Tim and Jen run to the snowman. They say hello to him. They touch his nose, his scarf and his hat. They hug him. They are happy.

But then, Tim sees something. He sees a glove on the ground. It is red and open. It looks like the snowman's glove.

"Hey, Jen, look! The snowman lost his glove!" Tim says. He picks up the glove.

"Oh no, poor snowman! He must be cold!" Jen says. She feels sorry for the snowman.

"Let's give him back his glove, Jen. Come on, march with me!" Tim says. He holds the glove in his hand. He starts to march to the snowman.

"Okay, Tim, I'm coming. March, march, march!" Jen says. She follows Tim. They march to the snowman.

They reach the snowman. They see his hand. It is white and bare. They put the glove on his hand. They smile.

"There, snowman, now you have your glove. You are warm and cozy," Tim says. He pats the snowman's hand.

"Thank you, Tim and Jen. You are very kind and helpful," the snowman says. He winks at them.

Tim and Jen are surprised. They hear the snowman talk. They look at each other. They look at mom. Mom smiles and nods.

"Wow, the snowman can talk! How cool!" Tim says.

"Yes, he can. He is a magic snowman. He likes to make friends," mom says.

"Can we be your friends, snowman?" Jen asks.

"Of course, you can. You are my friends. You made me happy," the snowman says.

Tim and Jen are happy too. They hug the snowman again. They laugh and play with him. They have fun in the snow.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside, and one day she saw a purple building in the distance. She wanted to go see it, but her mom said it was too far away.

But Lily was determined, so she went on her own. When she got there, she saw a little puppy stuck in a window. She knew she had to rescue him. She climbed up the building and got the puppy out.

As she was walking home with the puppy, her mom asked where she got him. Lily said, "I rescued him from the purple building." Her mom was so proud of her bravery and kindness. From that day on, Lily and her new puppy were best friends.

Lily and Ben were playing with their dolls in the living room. They liked to pretend that they were the dolls' parents and take care of them. Lily had a pink doll with long hair and a dress. Ben had a blue doll with short hair and a hat.

"Look, my doll is so pretty," Lily said, brushing her doll's hair. "She has a lot of lotion on her skin. She smells good."

"My doll is so cool," Ben said, putting his doll's hat on and off. "He has a lot of lotion on his hair. He looks smart."

Lily and Ben started to argue about whose doll was better. They raised their voices and said mean things to each other.

"Your doll is stupid," Lily said. "She has no hat. She will get cold."

"Your doll is stupid," Ben said. "He has no dress. He will get dirty."

They got so angry that they grabbed each other's dolls and tried to pull them away. They pulled so hard that they tore the dolls' clothes and hair. The dolls looked sad and hurt.

Lily and Ben stopped pulling and looked at what they had done. They felt sorry and ashamed. They started to cry.

"Mommy, Daddy, we are sorry," they said. "We tore our dolls. We were bad."

Mommy and Daddy came to the living room and saw the mess. They were not happy, but they were also kind. They hugged Lily and Ben and told them to calm down.

"It's okay, sweeties," Mommy said. "We know you love your dolls. But you have to be gentle and respectful with them. And with each other. You are brother and sister. You should share and play nicely."

"Yes, Mommy," Lily and Ben said. "We are sorry. We love each other. And we love our dolls."

Mommy and Daddy helped them fix their dolls' clothes and hair. They put some more lotion on them to make them smell good again. They gave them back to Lily and Ben and told them to hug and kiss their dolls.

Lily and Ben hugged and kissed their dolls. They also hugged and kissed each other. They said sorry again and promised to be good. They smiled and played with their dolls happily. They learned their lesson.

One day, Mommy found a big bin in the yard. She was very pleased and asked the children to help tidy it up. They happily agreed.

First they shoveled the dirt and put it in the bin. Then they carried it away to the end of the garden and made a special space. Mommy said they were going to bury something special in the bin.

So the children collected lots of stones and leaves and covered the bin. They then carefully covered it with shovels full of dirt. By the time they were finished, the bin was all tucked away, safe and sound and very tidy!

The children were excited to come back the next day and find out what was inside the bin. But until then, the bin was buried with a secret.

Once upon a time, there was a little car named Red. Red liked to go fast and speed around the world. One day, Red was driving really fast and he saw a little bunny in the road. Red knew that bunnies were harmless, so he slowed down and let the bunny hop away. Red realized that it was important to be careful when speeding around the world. From that day on, Red always watched out for harmless animals when he was driving fast.

Once there was a brilliant little boy who was walking around his parents' ranch. He was looking for something fun to do when he saw a large pile of snow. He thought it was brilliant and wanted to play.

The boy walked over to the snow and started to jump and laugh. He was having so much fun that he didn't notice how cold it was getting. Suddenly his feet got stuck in the snow and he was unable to move. He had frozen to the ground!

The boy's parents were so worried when they couldn't find him. They ran around their ranch calling for him, but there was no answer. They were relieved when they finally saw him and ran to him. Unfortunately it was too late - the little boy was frozen and could no longer move.

The boy's family was so very sad. They had hoped for a brilliant ending, but it didn't turn out that way. Sadly, they had to say goodbye to their little boy.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Joe. One day, Joe decided he wanted to find an oyster. He jumped in the ocean and swam around until he saw something in the sand. He got excited as it was an oyster! Joe tried to open it but it was very hard. He used his hands to try and open it but he got hurt. Joe was feeling sad. Suddenly, he heard a noise. When he looked closer, he saw the oyster had opened! Inside, Joe found a shiny pearl. It made him so excited! He showed the pearl to all his friends and brought it home to show his family. Joe was so happy he found an oyster and the pearl made his day special.

Once upon a time, in a small garden, there was a scary tree. The scary tree would shake when the wind blew. All the little animals were scared of the tree.

One day, a small bird came to the garden. The bird saw the scary tree and wanted to be friends. The bird flew to the tree and said, "Hi, tree! I want to be your friend." The tree did not shake.

The scary tree was happy to have a friend. The bird and the tree played in the garden. Soon, all the little animals came to play too. The scary tree did not shake anymore, and the garden was a happy place.

Jack was tall. He liked to watch TV, but his mom said no. Jack complained. His mom said it wasn't good for him to watch too much TV. Jack asked why.

Mom said it made people lazy. Jack asked what lazy meant. Mom said lazy means no energy. Jack was sad. He didn't want to be lazy.

Mom said to play outside instead. Jack smiled. He liked playing outside! Jack went to the park to play tag with his friends. He laughed and smiled and was full of energy!

In the end, Jack was happy because he didn't complain anymore. He had fun playing outside and he wasn't lazy.

Once upon a time, there was a chamber. It was a colorful place and there was fun to be had.

Two friends, Charlie and Anne, were playing in the chamber. Charlie wanted to play one game, and Anne wanted to play another. Charlie tried to persuade Anne to play his game.

"Please, Anne, let's play my game," said Charlie.

"No way!", said Anne. "I want to play my game now."

But Charlie was insistent. He wanted to win and was not ready to give in. Anne, however, was not willing to change her mind.

"Okay," said Charlie. "Let's try to reverse the rules. We'll both play my game the first time, and when we're done, we'll play your game."

Anne thought about it and agreed. They played Charlie's game and when it was finished, they played Anne's game. They had a lot of fun and it was a colorful time.

Lily and Tom were playing in the park. They liked to slide on the big slide. It was fun and fast. They took turns to go down the slide and then ran back to the top.

One day, they saw something new near the slide. It was a big ball of sticks and mud. It had a hole in it and made a loud buzzing sound. Lily and Tom were curious. They wanted to see what was inside.

They went closer to the ball and peeked inside. They saw many yellow and black bugs flying around. They were bees. They lived in the ball, which was their hive. They made honey in the hive.

"Wow, look at the bees!" Lily said. "They are so busy and noisy!"

"Can we touch them?" Tom asked. "Maybe they are friendly."

Lily shook her head. "No, we can't touch them. They might sting us. That would hurt a lot. Bees are fierce when they protect their hive."

Tom nodded. He did not want to get stung. He backed away from the hive. But he was not careful. He stepped on a twig and made a loud snap. The bees heard the noise and got angry. They thought Tom was trying to hurt their hive. They flew out of the hole and chased Tom.

"Help! Help!" Tom cried. He ran away from the bees. He ran to the slide and climbed up. He hoped the bees would not follow him.

Lily saw Tom in trouble. She wanted to help him. She ran to the slide and shouted at the bees. "Go away! Go away! Leave Tom alone! He is my friend!"

The bees did not listen to Lily. They wanted to sting Tom. They flew up to the slide and tried to catch him. Tom was scared. He slid down the slide as fast as he could. He hoped the bees would not catch him.

Lily slid down the slide after Tom. She wanted to be with him. She hoped the bees would leave them alone. They slid down the slide and ran to the other side of the park. They did not stop until they were far away from the hive.

The bees saw that Tom and Lily were gone. They did not chase them anymore. They flew back to their hive. They were calm again. They did not want to hurt anyone. They just wanted to make honey and live in peace.

Tom and Lily were safe. They were out of breath and had red faces. They hugged each other. They were glad they were not stung. They learned a lesson. They would not go near the hive again. They would respect the bees and their home. They would play on the slide and have fun. They were happy.

Once upon a time, there was a young boy named Timmy who loved to play with his toys. One day, he found a puzzle with many pieces. He tried to put the pieces together, but it was very hard. He needed help.

Timmy's mom came to help him. She showed him how to match the pieces. They worked together and finally finished the puzzle. Timmy was very happy.

But then, they heard a strange noise. It was a ghost! Timmy was scared. His mom told him not to be afraid because ghosts are not real. She said it was just the wind.

Timmy felt better, but he was still a little scared. His mom hugged him and told him that she would always be there to protect him. Timmy felt safe and went to bed with a smile on his face.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, she went outside to play with her friends. They were having so much fun, but then Lily saw a drain. She wanted to study it, so she went closer to look. Suddenly, her ball fell into the drain!

Lily was very sad because she thought her ball was dead. She asked her friends what to do, but they didn't know. Just then, a kind man walked by and asked what happened. Lily told him about her ball, and he said he could help. He got a long stick and fished the ball out of the drain.

Lily was so happy and thanked the man. She learned that she should be careful around drains and that there are always kind people who can help. She went home and told her mom all about her adventure. Her mom was proud of her for being brave and for learning something new.

Fred was walking outside when he saw a big bird flying in the sky. He watched as the bird dropped something from its beak. He ran over and saw that it was mail. He was so excited that he picked it up. He opened it and saw a deep, blue lake inside. He was so excited to explore the lake, so he went to the corner store and bought himself a boat.

He set sail on the deep blue lake. He was wowed by the beauty of the lake and the animals living there. After a while, he was getting tired, so he sat down and dropped his mail in the boat. Then he lay down and started to drift off to sleep.

The boat had gone too far, so it started to drift away from the shore. Fred was asleep and didn't notice. But luckily, he was spotted by a fisherman who saw the boat and brought it back in.

When Fred woke up, he was so happy to be back on shore. He was also happy because he'd remembered to drop his mail in the boat so he wouldn't forget about it. He thanked the fisherman for bringing him back, and then ran off with a smile on his face.

Once upon a time there was a little boy called Jack. He was a very flexible boy and could skip everywhere. Every day, Jack would go outside and skip around his garden.

One day, in the sky, Jack saw a beautiful star. It was twinkling and shimmering and Jack wanted to touch it. He skipped around his garden and jumped really high, but he just couldn’t reach the star.

But Jack was a very flexible boy and he didn’t give up. He started to use all his body and move it in different ways. Finally, after lots of stretching, Jack was able to touch his twinkly star!

Jack was so excited and he knew he could always use his flexible body to catch a star.

Once upon a time there was a bunny named Binky. Binky wanted to build something special. He hopped to the store and saw a nice microphone. He wanted it for his house.

Binky asked the shopkeeper, "Can I build this with my hands?"

The shopkeeper smiled, "Of course you can. You need blocks and tools."

Binky hopped home and started to build. He put the blocks together and was really proud. He was finished!

The microphone was shiny and perfect. Binky was so excited, he wanted to get something tasty to celebrate. He hopped to the bakery and bought some cookies. They were so yummy and sweet!

Binky decided to take a break and try out the microphone. He talked into it and heard his own voice, loud and clear! He was so happy.

Binky was so proud of his microphone. He had a tasty snack and was pleased with his work. Binky hopped home, ready for his next adventure.

One day, a boy named Tim found a broken rod. He wanted to fix it. He asked his mom, "Can I fix this rod?" His mom said, "Yes, but be careful."

Tim tried to fix the broken rod. He put tape on it, but it did not work. He felt sad. He asked his dad for help. His dad said, "Let's cook a yummy meal and think about it."

They cooked a big meal together. While they cooked, Tim's dad had an idea. He said, "We can use glue to fix the rod!" Tim felt happy.

They ate the yummy meal and then fixed the rod with glue. The broken rod was now strong again. Tim said, "Thank you, Dad!" They went outside to play with the fixed rod.

Once upon a time there was a man who had a modern pistol. He was very proud of the pistol and held it carefully. One day, a thief came to the man's house. The man took the modern pistol and bravely held it up. He pointed it at the thief and said, "Go away!" The thief was so scared that he quickly ran away. The man was happy that he was able to use his modern pistol to make the thief go away. He held it tightly, safe in the knowledge that his modern pistol had kept his house safe.

Once upon a time a family lived in a small house near an old oak tree. The oak gave them shade and the family treated it kindly. Every week they would raise money to help people in need nearby.

One day the family decided to raise more money to help more people. They found a generous old man who offered them a lot of money for the tree. The family had a hard decision to make.

The father said "We need the money, but this tree has been so good to us. We can't take it away".

But the mother said "Let's do it! We can buy two trees and still help those in need. It will be a generous gift from our family".

The family agreed, and soon the old man bought the tree. With the money, they planted two new oak trees and sent generous donations to those in need. The family was happy with their decision, and the old oak tree saw a new generation grow.

Sara and Ben went to the mall with Mom. They liked to see the big shops and the colorful toys. Mom said they could have a treat if they were good.

They saw a big stand with many balloons. Sara wanted a pink one and Ben wanted a blue one. Mom bought them each a balloon and tied them to their wrists. They were very happy.

They walked to the food court and saw a man selling lemonade. Mom said they could have a cup of lemonade too. Sara and Ben liked lemonade. It was sweet and cold.

But when they drank the lemonade, they made a funny face. It was not sweet and cold. It was sour and warm. They did not like it at all.

"Yuck!" Sara said. "This lemonade is bad!"

"Me too!" Ben said. "It hurts my tongue!"

Mom tasted the lemonade and agreed. It was bad. She went to the man and told him. The man was sorry. He said he forgot to put sugar and ice in the lemonade. He gave Mom a new cup of lemonade. It was sweet and cold.

Mom gave the new lemonade to Sara and Ben. They drank it and smiled. It was good.

"Thank you, Mom!" Sara said. "You saved us from the sour lemonade!"

"You're welcome, Sara!" Mom said. "You're a good girl!"

"Thank you, Mom!" Ben said. "You're the best!"

"You're welcome, Ben!" Mom said. "You're a good boy!"

They hugged Mom and finished their lemonade. They were happy. They liked the mall.

Once upon a time, there was a young girl named Sarah. Sarah was walking near her house when she noticed her elderly neighbor. He was sitting on a bench in his garden.

Sarah walked up to him and said, "Hi, neighbor!"

The neighbor smiled and replied, "Hello, Sarah! How are you this day?"

Sarah laughed and said, "I'm great! Can I sit here with you?"

The elderly neighbor nodded and said, "Of course! It's nice to have some company on such a beautiful day."

So Sarah and the Neighbor sat there, watching the birds fly around in the sky and talking about the new flowers in the garden. They talked until it started to get dark.

Then the elderly neighbor gave Sarah a hug, and said, "It was nice to talk to you today. You make an old man feel young again."

Sarah smiled and said, "It was nice to talk to you too! See you soon, neighbor!"

And with that, Sarah waved goodbye to the elderly neighbor and skipped home with a smile on her face.

Once there was a little girl. She was happy and brave. One day, she was running to catch a butterfly when she tripped and fell. She split her tooth. It was unknown what was going to happen.

The little girl was very scared. The tooth felt very cold and hurt a lot. She didn’t know what to do. So, she called her mom.

Her mom came quickly and was very kind. She hugged her daughter and told her that it would be alright. Then, she quickly took the girl to the dentist.

The dentist looked at the tooth with a big smile and said, "Don't worry! I will make your tooth strong and new! So, the little girl stayed brave and still, as the dentist mended her tooth.

When she was finished, the little girl looked in the mirror. She was surprised and happy to see her tooth looking new and strong again. She never had to worry again!

Once upon a time there was a small pink doll. It was very special and very loved by all. One day, the little girl who owned the pink doll decided to attach it to her shirt with a ribbon. She thought it would be a great way to keep her special doll close to her at all times.

But, tragedy struck! The ribbon broke, and the pink doll fell to the ground. The little girl started to cry, for she knew this was not a good sign. She looked everywhere for her pink doll, but could not find it. Sadly, the poor little girl had lost her pink doll forever!

Once, there was a little girl called Emily. She was three years old. Every night, Emily's mum would close her door and say good night. Emily didn't like it. Every time, she wanted mum to stay in her room with her.

One night, Emily cried until her mum promised to stay with her. So, mum closed the bedroom door and sat on her bed. They both looked out of the window at the night sky.

Suddenly, the darkness was filled with a deep, sad silence. Emily was confused and a bit scared. She asked her mum, "What's wrong? Why is silences so sad?"

Mum explained that sometimes, even adults need a bit of a hug when it's quiet. Mum hugged Emily and spoke softly, "The silence will pass soon, and there will be happy noises again. It's OK."

Emily felt better and smiled. She closed her eyes and soon fell asleep in her mum's warm arms.

Anna and Tom were going on a big trip with Mom and Dad. They were very happy and excited. They had to pack their bags with clothes and toys and books. Mom and Dad helped them pack. They also gave them a passport each. A passport is a book with your name and picture that you need to go on a plane.

"Look at your passport, Anna. It is very pretty. You are a big girl now. I am very proud of you," Mom said.

"Thank you, Mom. I like my passport. Can I hold it?" Anna asked.

"Sure, but be careful. Don't lose it or drop it. You need it to go on the plane," Mom said.

Anna nodded and held her passport tight. She wanted to show it to Tom. She ran to his room, where he was packing his bag. She opened the door and said, "Look, Tom. I have a passport. Do you have one too?"

Tom looked up and saw Anna holding her passport. He was jealous. He wanted to have a passport too. He did not have one yet. Mom and Dad said he was too little. He was angry and sad. He said, "No, I don't have a passport. You are lucky. You get to go on the plane. I have to stay home with Grandma. It is not fair. Give me your passport. I want it."

He grabbed Anna's passport and tried to take it from her. Anna did not want to give it to him. She said, "No, Tom. It is mine. You can't have it. Let go."

They pulled and tugged and fought over the passport. They did not hear Mom and Dad coming. They did not see the scissors on the floor. They did not notice the passport tearing in half.

Mom and Dad saw what happened. They were very angry and sad. They said, "Oh no. What have you done? You ruined Anna's passport. Now she can't go on the plane. Now we have to cancel the trip. Now we have to stay home. You are very naughty and mean. We are very disappointed in you."

Anna and Tom started to cry. They were very sorry and sad. They wished they had not fought over the passport. They wished they had been nice and kind. They wished they could go on the big trip. But it was too late. The passport was broken. The trip was over. The end.

John and his family were on vacation. They wanted to explore the sea, so they requested a dependable yacht. They were so excited! The yacht was big and brightly coloured. It was ready to sail on the waves.

John's dad was a captain, so he knew how to sail the yacht. He took everyone on a journey around the island. John and his siblings all had turns steering the yacht. Everyone was having fun!

At the end of the day, John's dad asked if everyone knew how to sail the yacht. Everyone nodded yes. They said good-bye to the dependable yacht and made plans for their next adventure.

Once upon a time, there was a huge twig in the woods. It was so tall that it reached up to the clouds.

One day, a bird flew by and saw the huge twig. He flapped his wings and waved at it. But the twig did not move.

So the bird flew off to find some friends. He found a fox and a squirrel. He told them about the huge twig.

The fox, the squirrel and the bird flew back to the twig. They waved their tails and hopped up and down. But the twig still did not budge.

Suddenly, the wind began to blow. It picked up the twig and sent it flying! All of the animals waved goodbye as the twig disappeared over the horizon.

Tom and Sam love to play baseball. They have a big field near their house where they can run and hit the ball. They have a red bat, a white ball and two gloves. They are very happy when they play baseball.

One day, they wake up and see dark clouds in the sky. They hear a loud noise. It is thunder. They see flashes of light. It is lightning. They are scared. They run to their mom and dad.

"Mom, dad, can we play baseball today?" they ask.

"No, my boys, you can't. It is going to rain soon. Rain is water that falls from the sky. It can make you wet and cold. It can also make the field muddy and slippery. You have to stay inside today." their mom says.

"But we want to play baseball!" they cry.

"I know, I know. But you can play something else inside. How about you draw a picture of baseball? Or you read a book about baseball? Or you make a puzzle of baseball?" their dad suggests.

Tom and Sam think for a moment. They like to draw and read and make puzzles. They decide to try them all. They go to their room and find their crayons, their books and their puzzles. They start to have fun.

They look out the window and see the rain. It is enormous. It covers the whole field. They can't see the bat, the ball or the gloves. They are glad they are inside. They are warm and dry.

They say to each other: "We love baseball. But we also love to draw and read and make puzzles. And we love mom and dad. They are very nice. Maybe tomorrow the sun will come out and we can play baseball again. But today we are happy inside."

Once upon a time, there was a dry queen. She was very wise and kind to everybody she met. One day, she heard a loud call coming from far away.

The queen found out that the call was coming from a little bird. She wanted to help the little bird, so she went to find it.

When she arrived at the bird's nest, she saw that the nest was dry. It was too dry for the little bird to live in. The queen called out to some of her animals and asked for their help.

One of the animals brought some water, another brought some soft grass, and the third brought some leaves. The queen and the animals worked together to build a new, nice, wet nest for the bird.

The little bird thanked the queen and flew away. Everyone rejoiced, and all the animals were happy that their kind queen helped the bird. And they all lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a queen. She liked to walk around her kingdom. But she was very selfish. She didn't think of anyone else, only herself.

One day, a little girl was walking in the forest. She saw the queen walking as well and ran over to her. The little girl looked excited to meet the queen. But the queen kept walking, not even looking at the little girl.

The little girl was sad. She wanted the queen to stop and talk with her. But no matter how much she tried, the queen just kept walking.

So the little girl made a wish. She wished that the queen would be more kind and generous. Then the queen stopped and finally said hello to the little girl. They talked and laughed together all afternoon.

The little girl was so happy. From that day on, the queen was no longer selfish. She treat everyone with kindness and made sure everyone in her kingdom was happy.

Once upon a time, there was a big foot. It belonged to a giant who lived in a nearby castle. He rarely ever stepped outside of his fortress.

One day, the giant decided to take a walk in the forest. He was so big and his foot was so big that it left a giant footprint wherever he went.

A small girl was playing in the forest when she saw a big footprint. She was very curious and followed the giant footprint until she arrived at the giant's castle.

The girl was very scared. She was about to turn around and run away when suddenly the door opened. The giant smiled at her and said, "Come in and see the surprise I have waiting for you!"

The girl was still scared, but the giant was so kind and friendly. She decided to take a chance and go inside.

When she entered, she found the biggest surprise of all. The giant had filled the entire castle with colorful toys and sweets. The girl was so excited that she couldn't believe her eyes.

The girl and the giant played together all day, and she was never scared of him again. They stayed friends long after, and the girl remembered that surprise forever.

Tom likes to wear his frog hat. It is green and soft and has big eyes. He thinks it makes him powerful, like a frog that can jump high and swim fast. He wears it every day, even when it is hot or cold.

One day, he goes to the park with his mom and his frog hat. He sees a pond with real frogs. He wants to play with them. He runs to the pond and says hello to the frogs. He thinks they are his friends.

But the frogs are scared of Tom and his frog hat. They think he is a big frog that wants to eat them. They croak and hop away. Tom is sad. He does not understand why the frogs do not like him.

His mom sees him and comes to him. She hugs him and tells him that the frogs are shy and do not know him. She says he can watch them from a distance, but not touch them. She says he can still be powerful with his frog hat, but he has to be gentle and kind to the frogs.

Tom nods and smiles. He still likes his frog hat, but he also likes the real frogs. He decides to be a good friend to them. He sits on a bench with his mom and his frog hat and watches the frogs. He says thank you to them for letting him see them. He thinks they are powerful too, in their own way.

Once upon a time, there was a little bird. The bird was very hungry and wanted to find some food. It flew around all morning looking for something to eat, but it couldn't find anything.

Finally, at noon, the bird saw a thin worm crawling in the grass. It was so excited to find food that it quickly swooped down to catch the worm. But just as the bird was about to eat the worm, something surprising happened.

The worm suddenly revealed that it was not just a worm, but a magical creature that could grant wishes. The bird was amazed and asked for a big feast. The magical creature granted the wish, and the bird had a delicious meal. From then on, the little bird knew that even when things seemed hopeless, something wonderful could still happen.

Once upon a time, there was a little kitten. The kitten was troubled. It could not find its mom. The kitten looked everywhere. It looked under a big tree. It looked by a small pond. But it could not find its mom.

One day, the kitten met a friendly frog. The frog liked to dance. The frog saw the troubled kitten and asked, "Why are you sad?" The kitten said, "I can't find my mom." The frog wanted to help the kitten. So, they went on a search together.

They looked and looked. Then, they heard a soft "meow." The kitten's mom was behind a bush! The kitten was so happy. The frog danced with joy. The kitten and its mom thanked the frog. They all became good friends and danced together in the sun.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, her mommy gave her a peach to eat. The peach was very big and thick. Lily tried to bite it, but she couldn't. She asked her mommy to help her open the peach.

Mommy tried to open the peach, but it was too hard. She told Lily to wait until it gets softer. But Lily was very impatient. She wanted to eat the peach right away. She started to cry and said, "I want my peach now!"

Mommy told Lily that she needs to be patient and wait for the peach to get soft. She said, "Good things come to those who wait." Eventually, the peach got soft, and mommy was able to open it. Lily was very happy and learned that it's important to be patient and wait for good things to come.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, Lily went to the fridge to get some juice. But when she opened the fridge, she saw that there was no juice left. She felt sad and said, "Oh no! No juice!"

Her mom heard her and asked, "What's wrong, Lily?"

Lily said, "No juice in fridge. I want juice."

Her mom said, "Don't worry, we can spring to the store and buy more juice. Everything will be calm."

Lily smiled and said, "Yay! Juice!"

One day, a creative little girl named Lily went to the park with her mom. They brought a big, red napkin to sit on. They put the napkin on the grass and sat down to eat lunch. Lily had a yummy sandwich and her mom had a salad.

After they ate, Lily saw her friend, Tim, across the park. She wanted to say hi, so she picked up the red napkin and started to wave it. Tim saw the napkin and waved back with his hand. He ran over to Lily and her mom.

Lily and Tim played together in the park. They ran, jumped, and laughed. They had so much fun. When it was time to go home, Lily and her mom waved goodbye to Tim. They took the red napkin and went home, happy after a fun day at the park.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Amy. She was very comfy when she sat down in her special chair. One day when she was sitting there, she felt a shock. It frightened her and she cried out for her mommy.

Mommy came over, picked her up and said, "Everything is okay, Amy." She hugged Amy, who soon felt safe and comfortable again.

Then, her mommy asked her a question. She said, "Amy, can you please tell me what happened?" Amy told her mommy all about the shock.

Mommy hugged Amy again, and said "Let's not worry about the shock. Let's focus on feeling comfortable. Let's play a game and have some fun!"

And with that, Amy and her mommy played a game together and soon Amy was feeling comfy and very happy.

The End.

Once upon a time, there was a unique boy named Jack. He had a pet dog called Fluffy. Every morning, Jack would take Fluffy for a walk.

One day, Jack and Fluffy went to the beach. They saw a lot of waste on the beach and Jack was very sad. Jack said to Fluffy, "It's not nice to leave waste around. Let's clean it up!" Fluffy barked in agreement.

So they both started to collect the waste. They filled up a big bag and waved goodbye to the beach. Jack was very proud of himself.

As they walked back home, they came across some friends. Jack waved at them and said, "We were just cleaning the beach! It is important to keep the environment clean!" His friends were very impressed and smiled at Jack.

Jack and Fluffy went back home feeling happy and unique.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim had a toy raft that he loved to play with. One day, Tim's raft broke and he was very upset.

Tim's mom saw him crying and said, "Why are you so upset, Tim?" Tim showed her the broken raft and said, "My raft is broken, and I am sad."

Tim's mom had an idea. She said, "Let's create a new raft together!" Tim smiled and they went to find things to make a new raft. They found sticks and string, and they worked together to make a strong, new raft.

Tim was so happy with the new raft he and his mom created. He played with it all day long and said, "Thank you, Mom, for helping me create a new raft!"

From that day on, Tim was never upset about his broken raft again. He learned that with a little help and creativity, he could create something even better.

Once upon a time, there was a dog named Max. Max was a good dog who loved to play and eat treats. One day, Max got very sick and his owner took him to see the veterinarian. The veterinarian was a nice person who helped animals feel better. Max was scared, but the veterinarian was honest and told Max that he would receive some medicine to help him feel better.

Max went home with his owner and took his medicine. He felt much better and was back to playing and eating treats in no time. Max was happy that he got to see the veterinarian and receive the medicine he needed to feel better. From then on, Max made sure to eat healthy and play safely so he wouldn't get sick again. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play outside and explore the world around him. One day, while he was playing in the park, he fell down and hurt his knee.

"Ouch!" cried Timmy. "My knee hurts!"

His mom came over to him and said, "Don't worry, Timmy. We'll put a band-aid on it and it will heal soon."

Timmy smiled and felt better knowing that his mom would take care of him. As they walked home, Timmy saw a shiny rock on the ground.

"Look, Mommy! Gold!" he exclaimed.

His mom picked up the rock and smiled. "It's not real gold, Timmy. But it's still pretty."

They continued walking until they reached their house. Timmy's mom gave him a flexible toy to play with while he rested his knee.

"Thank you, Mommy. This toy is so bendy!" said Timmy.

His mom smiled and said, "I'm glad you like it, Timmy. Now let's get that knee healed up!"

One day, a 3 year old boy named Max was really confused. He chewed his fingernails and wondered why his mom and dad didn't understand him. They always looked so sad.

So he went to his grandpa for advice. Grandpa smiled and held out a shiny red apple.

"Do you like apple, Max?" Grandpa asked.

Max nodded eagerly. Grandpa smiled and said, "Max, you know your value. You must always remember how special and important you are. That should help you feel less confused".

Max smiled, took the apple and started to chew. He felt good and excited to remember his value and learn new things.

The End!

Once upon a time, there was a loyal dog named Max. Max loved to play with his best friend, a little boy named Tim. They would run and jump all day long.

One day, Tim got a new toy. It was a model car that could turn in many ways. Max and Tim played with the car, making it turn left and right. They had lots of fun together.

But then, Max saw a big cat in the yard. He wanted to chase the cat, but he also wanted to stay with Tim and the car. Max thought about it and decided to be loyal to Tim. He stayed and played with the car, and the cat ran away.

The moral of the story is that being loyal to your friends is more important than chasing after something new.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside with her friends. One day, Lily was running and she fell down. Her knee hurt a lot, and she started to cry.

Her mom heard her crying and came outside. "What happened, sweetie?" her mom asked. "I fell down and hurt my knee," Lily said, still crying.

Her mom picked her up and took her inside to get a Band-Aid from the fridge. She put the Band-Aid on Lily's knee and gave her a hug. "Don't worry, I am here to take care of you," her mom said. Lily felt better and hugged her mom back. Her mom was so compassionate.

From that day on, Lily knew that whenever she fell down or got hurt, her mom would be there to take care of her.

Lily liked to collect things. She had a box full of shiny things, soft things, and pretty things. She liked to look at them and play with them. Sometimes she shared them with her friends.

One day, she saw a new thing on the door of her room. It was a knob. It was round and smooth and had a hole in the middle. Lily wanted to collect it. She tried to pull it off the door, but it was stuck. She asked her mom for help.

"Mom, can I have this knob?" she said.

"No, Lily, you can't have the knob. It belongs to the door. If you take it off, the door won't close and it will be dark and cold in your room," her mom said.

"But I like the knob. It is shiny and smooth and has a hole. I want to put it in my box," Lily said.

"I know, Lily, but the knob is not for collecting. It is for opening and closing the door. You have many other things in your box that you can play with. Why don't you find something else to collect?" her mom said.

Lily thought for a moment. She looked around her room and saw a book on her shelf. It had a picture of a cat on the cover. Lily liked cats. She decided to collect the book instead. She took it off the shelf and put it in her box.

"Look, mom, I found a new thing to collect. It is a book. It has a cat. I like cats," she said.

"That's great, Lily. I'm glad you found a new thing to collect. Books are good for collecting. They have stories and pictures and words. You can read them and learn from them. Maybe you can read the book with the cat to me later," her mom said.

"Okay, mom. I will read the book with the cat to you later. Thank you for helping me," Lily said.

"You're welcome, Lily. I love you," her mom said.

"I love you too, mom," Lily said.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Rachel. Rachel lived in a small house by herself. She was very lonely. Each day Rachel would go outside and find a quiet spot in the park. She would sit there alone and watch the world around her. She loved to try and spot the different kinds of birds in the sky.

One particular day she noticed an old man sat nearby. The old man was talking to himself in a different language. Rachel was curious and she asked him what language he was speaking. The old man smiled at her and said he was speaking Spanish!

Rachel was so excited. She enjoyed learning words in the different language, so she asked the old man to teach her some Spanish. The old man was so happy to help Rachel. He spent some time teaching her different words and phrases. Rachel was so excited and soon she had learned lots of Spanish!

At the end of the day, Rachel was not lonely anymore. She was grateful for the old man's help, and for the wonderful time that she had enjoyed.

One day, a pale bunny named Bob hopped in the grass. He saw a big carrot stuck in the ground. Bob wanted to eat the carrot, but he could not pull it out by himself. He looked around and saw a friendly bird named Lily.

"Hi, Lily! Can you help me pull this carrot?" asked Bob.

"Sure, Bob! Let's pull it together," said Lily.

They both pulled the carrot. With a little help, the carrot came out of the ground. Bob and Lily were very happy. They shared the big carrot and ate it together. From that day on, they became best friends who helped each other.

Once upon a time, there was a kind girl named Lily. She loved to play outside and pick fruits from the trees. One day, she found a lime tree and picked a lime. She wanted to print her name on the lime, so she used a marker to write "Lily" on it.

But then, a big storm came and destroyed all the trees in the garden, including the lime tree. Lily was very sad because she loved the lime tree and the lime she picked. She searched for it everywhere, but she couldn't find it.

Days passed and Lily realized that the lime was gone forever. She felt very sad and missed the lime tree. She wished she could have printed her name on something else, so she could remember the lime tree forever. But she knew that nothing could replace it. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside with her friends. One day, she was running around the park when she felt tired. She sat down on a spot of grass and rested.

Her friend, Tommy, came over and asked, "Lily, are you okay? You look tired."

Lily replied, "Yes, I feel tired. I ran a lot today."

Tommy said, "Let's take a break and sit here for a bit."

Lily agreed and they sat together on the spot of grass. They talked about their favorite toys and what they wanted to be when they grew up. After a while, they felt refreshed and got up to play again.

From that day on, Lily learned that it was okay to take a break when she felt tired. She also learned that good friends like Tommy will always be there to help her feel better.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy had a lamp in his room that he loved very much. It was his favorite thing in the whole wide world. One day, when Timmy was playing with his toys, he accidentally knocked over the lamp and it broke into a million pieces. Timmy was very sad.

Suddenly, Timmy's mom came into the room and noticed that Timmy was upset. She was very alert and asked him what was wrong. Timmy told her about the lamp and how it vanished into tiny pieces. His mom hugged him and said that it was okay and that they would get a new lamp. Timmy felt better and smiled. He knew that his mom loved him very much. The end.

Once there was a young girl named Lily. Lily was very curious and loved playing wild games. One day, Lily was exploring when she found a big, metal door. She tried to open it, but it was locked.

Lily didn't want to give up just yet. She found a long stair behind the door. She wondered what was behind the door and what was at the top of the stair. Could it be even wilder than before? Lily was determined to unlock the door.

Finally, she found the key. She put it in the keyhole and the door was unlocked! Lily was so excited at the possibilities that lay ahead. She climbed the long, wild stair to the top. When she got to the top of the stair, she found a magical world full of wild adventures!

Lily never forgot the magic that was discovered behind the big, metal door. She was so thankful she was brave enough to unlock it and go explore the wild stair.

Once upon a time there was a girl named Jane. Jane loved to write! She wrote stories and poems every day.

One day Jane wore her new shoes to go for a walk. They had big thick heels. After a while Jane felt very tired, so she sat down to rest.

But when she looked down she noticed that the heel of her shoe was stuck in an icy crack in the sidewalk. Jane tried to pull it out, but it was stuck!

Suddenly Jane remembered a story her grandfather had told her - if you write on icy things with your finger, the ice will melt and you can pull it out.

So Jane took out a pencil and wrote on the icy crack. Sure enough, it started melting! Jane was able to twist and pull the heel of her shoe free.

Jane was so pleased she skipped the rest of the way home.

Once upon a time, there was a big castle where a king lived. He was very important and everyone liked him because he was charming. One day, a little girl went to the castle to see the king. She saw him walking in the garden and she wanted to talk to him. But the king was too tall, so the little girl asked him to kneel down. The king was surprised, but he did it anyway. The little girl told him that she liked his castle and that he was a very nice king. The king was happy to hear that and he gave her a candy. The little girl was very happy and she went back home with a big smile on her face.

Once upon a time, there was a happy little girl named Lily. She loved to play at the park with her friends. One sunny day, Lily and her friends went to the park to play on the swings and slide. They had so much fun!

After playing for a while, Lily's mom called her to come home for lunch. Lily said goodbye to her friends and walked home with her mom. For lunch, they had oatmeal with raisins and milk. Lily loved oatmeal because it was yummy and healthy.

Later that day, Lily went back to the park to play. But when she got there, she saw that someone had broken the swing and slide. Lily was sad and asked her friend, "Who did this? Why would they do this?" Her friend replied, "I don't know, but it's not cheerful anymore."

Lily went home feeling upset and disappointed that someone had ruined her favorite place to play. She wished that the park would be fixed soon so she could have fun there again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside and catch bugs. One day, she found a bug she had never seen before. It was small and green with unknown spots on its back.

Lily picked up the bug and showed it to her mom. "Mommy, can we buy a bug house so I can keep this bug?" she asked. Her mom smiled and said, "Sure, let's go to the store and buy one."

At the store, Lily and her mom found a bug house with little doors and windows. "This is perfect!" Lily said. They bought the bug house and brought it home. Lily put the unknown bug in the bug house and watched it crawl around. "Thank you, mommy, for buying me this bug house," Lily said with a big smile on her face.

Once upon a time there were two friends, Charlie and Daisy. Charlie and Daisy were three years old and were best friends.

One day, they were playing in Daisy's backyard when they noticed a delicious place up in a tree. Charlie said to Daisy, "Let's go and get it!" Daisy agreed and they started to climb.

When they reached the place, they saw that it was full of delicious wrapped sweets. Charlie said they should each take one. Daisy said, "No, we should share them!"

Charlie said, "No, I want them all for myself!" Charlie started to wrap the sweets in his shirt. He was about to climb down when Daisy said, "Stop! Don't be so greedy! We should share them all."

Charlie thought for a moment and said, "OK, let's share them." Daisy and Charlie shared the delicious sweets and agreed to always take turns and share with each other.

Tim and Sam were best friends. They liked to play with cars and balls and blocks. They also liked to celebrate their birthdays. Tim's birthday was in spring, when the flowers were pretty and the grass was green. Sam's birthday was in winter, when the snow was white and the trees were bare.

One day, Tim had an idea. He wanted to make Sam's birthday amazing. He asked his mom to help him. She said yes and smiled. She gave him some green paper, some scissors, some glue and some glitter. Tim worked hard to make a surprise for Sam.

The next day, Tim went to Sam's house with his mom. He hid his surprise behind his back. He knocked on the door. Sam opened it and said, "Hi, Tim! Come in, it's my birthday!" Tim said, "Happy birthday, Sam! I have something for you." He showed him his surprise. It was a big green tree made of paper and glitter. It looked like a Christmas tree.

Sam was so happy. He hugged Tim and said, "Wow, Tim, this is amazing! How did you make it?" Tim said, "I used green paper and scissors and glue and glitter. I wanted to make your birthday special. I know you like green and trees." Sam said, "Thank you, Tim. You are the best friend ever. Come on, let's celebrate!"

They went inside and had cake and ice cream and played with their toys. They had a lot of fun. They learned that celebrating is not about the season or the weather, but about the friendship and the love. They also learned that making someone happy is a wonderful gift. They were very grateful for each other.

One day, a girl named Lily was very excited. She wanted to design a big mall. Lily loved to draw and make things look nice. So, she started to draw a mall on a big paper.

In her mall, there were many fun shops. There was a toy shop, a candy shop, and a dress shop. Lily drew a big play area where kids could play and have fun. She also drew a food place where people could eat yummy food.

When Lily finished her mall design, she showed it to her mom and dad. They were so happy and proud of her. They put her mall design on the fridge for everyone to see. Lily felt very happy and couldn't wait to design more things.

Once upon a time there was a lady named Kate. She was walking in a meadow one day when she saw something weird. Kate squinted her eyes and realised that it was cereal!

She picked up the cereal, which was covered in green and yellow pieces, and put it in her shopping bag. When she got home, Kate opened the cereal. Inside, she found something even weirder! There were little plastic eggs!

Kate was so excited! She wanted to know what was inside these eggs, so she ran outside and put the plastic eggs on the ground. Then she waited. Suddenly, out of each egg came a little animal who jumped up and down! They were baby rabbits and they had been hidden inside the plastic eggs.

The rabbits hopped around in the meadow and Kate watched in happy surprise. She knew that it must be spring! The birds were singing, the flowers were blooming and the baby rabbits had been born. Kate smiled to herself and she was glad that she had found the weird cereal.

Once upon a time, there was a kind girl named Lily. She was very compassionate and loved to help others. One day, she saw a small cat stuck in a tree. Lily dared to climb the tree to save the cat.

As Lily climbed, she saw a big shadow on the ground. It was a tall man who came to help her. He held out his long arms to catch the cat. Lily gently pushed the cat, and it fell into the man's arms.

Lily and the man were happy to save the cat. They became good friends and helped other animals together. They were brave and kind, and everyone loved them. The end.

Lila did not like to brush her hair. She said it hurt and it was boring. She had long, curly hair that got tangled and messy. Every morning, her mom tried to make her sit still and let her brush her hair. But Lila was stubborn. She ran away, hid under the bed, or threw her brush on the floor.

One day, her mom had a new idea. She showed Lila a book with pictures of different animals. She asked Lila, "Do you want to look like a lion, a zebra, or a peacock today?" Lila was curious. She liked animals. She looked at the book and pointed to the peacock. She said, "I want to look like a peacock. They have pretty feathers."

Her mom smiled. She said, "Okay, then we need to brush your hair and make it shiny and smooth. Then we can turn your hair into a peacock tail with clips and ribbons. Do you want to try?" Lila nodded. She liked the idea of having a peacock tail. She let her mom brush her hair gently and carefully. She watched in the mirror as her mom turned her hair into a colorful fan. She was happy. She said, "Look, mom, I'm a peacock!"

Her mom hugged her. She said, "You are a beautiful peacock, Lila. And you have been a very good girl today. Thank you for letting me brush your hair." Lila smiled. She said, "You're welcome, mom. Can we do this again tomorrow?" Her mom said, "Sure, we can. What animal do you want to be tomorrow?" Lila thought for a moment. She said, "Maybe a lion. Or a zebra. Or a unicorn." Her mom laughed. She said, "We'll see, Lila. We'll see."

Once upon a time there was a brave bear. He wanted to explore the world. He looked around, but all he saw was a cold landscape.

The bear was feeling a bit sad he didn't have anywhere to go. So he decided to make a request. He asked the wind to take him somewhere new.

The wind heard his request and became very excited. It picked up the bear and blew him all around the world.

The bear got to see so many exciting places. He saw mountains and canyons, sandy beachs and icy glaciers. Every place he went was so different and exciting.

Finally, the wind brought him back home. The bear thanked the wind for his adventure and ran off into the cold landscape. He was so happy to be home.

Bobby was playing outside when it started to rain. He ran inside and saw his mother listening to music. She was dancing and having so much fun.

Bobby asked, "Mommy, can I dance too?"

His mother said, "Yes! Music is creative. It helps us resist the rain."

Bobby smiled and enjoyed the music. He took his mom's hand and started spinning in circles. He loved the way the music made him feel.

When the song was over, Bobby said, "Mommy, that was so much fun! Can we do it again?"

Mommy said, "Of course. We can always go back to dancing and music when we need to resist the rain."

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a pale face and loved to play with her toys. One day, Lily went to the park with her mom. She saw a beautiful butterfly and tried to catch it, but it flew away.

Lily's mom told her to stay close, but Lily forgot and ran after the butterfly. She got lost and couldn't find her way back to her mom. She started to cry and feel scared.

A kind lady found Lily and asked her name. Lily told her the true name and the lady took her to the police station. They found Lily's mom, but she was very worried and sad. She hugged Lily tightly and told her to never forget to stay close.

Even though Lily was safe, she learned a lesson and felt sad for making her mom worry.

Once upon a time, there lived a little girl named Emily. She loved to listen to stories and look at pictures. Every day her mommy would read her a book and they would look at the pictures together. Emily loved this time with her mommy.

One day, Emily wanted to find a new book to listen to. She went to her bedroom and looked on the shelf. All of the books were organized in a row. They were all pretty and colorful! Emily picked one that was her favorite.

She went back to the livingroom and showed her mommy the book. Then they both snuggled up on the couch together and Emily listened as her mommy read the book. Emily was so happy!

Emily loved to listen to stories and she enjoyed spending time with her mommy. This made her feel special and really organized her thoughts. Every time her mommy read her stories, Emily felt like she was living a fairytale.

Once there was a little girl named Daisy. Daisy was playing with her eraser when something exciting happened. She noticed a number on the eraser.

Daisy was very curious and wanted to try and figure out what the number was. She asked her mom what it meant, but her mom didn't know.

Daisy asked her little brother and he told her that it was a secret number that nobody could guess. Daisy didn't like this answer, so she started to get upset.

Daisy's mom was patient with her and helped her figure out what the number was. With Mom's help, Daisy tried counting from one to ten again and again.

Finally, Daisy was able to successfully find the number. She was very proud of herself for being so patient and for figuring out such a tricky secret.

Once upon a time, there was a sad little boy. He had no one to play with and he always felt alone. He wanted to own something so he could have something of his own. But he had nothing.

One day, the boy saw a small puppy in the park. The puppy was all alone and it looked sad too. The boy wanted to own the puppy so he could have somebody to be with. He asked his mom if he could have the puppy and his mom said yes.

The boy and the puppy became friends. They would play in the park together and have lots of fun. The boy was no longer sad because he had a friend to be with every day.

The weather also changed for the better. It was no longer cold and grey, but sunny and warm outside. The boy and his puppy would take long walks and explore the neighborhood. The boy was happy to own the puppy because he finally had someone to be with, no matter what the weather was.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his toy jeep. He would push it around and make vroom vroom noises. One day, Timmy went to the park with his mommy. They were having so much fun playing on the swings and the slide.

Suddenly, Timmy's mommy saw a big dog running towards them. She shouted, "Timmy, be alert! Pick up your jeep and let's go!" Timmy quickly picked up his toy jeep and followed his mommy.

But the dog was too fast and it caught up to them. It started barking and growling at them. Timmy's mommy tried to protect him, but the dog was too strong. Timmy was very scared and he started to cry.

In the end, the dog hurt Timmy and his mommy very badly. They had to go to the hospital and Timmy's toy jeep was left behind. Timmy was very sad that he lost his favorite toy, but he was grateful that his mommy was okay.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Amy. She loved sports, and wanted to fold her own sport. She asked her elderly grandma for help. Grandma smiled and said: "Of course, I can help you. What kind of sport do you want to fold?"

"A boat," said Amy.

Grandma had never folded a boat before, but she showed Amy how to do it. She showed her how to fold the paper until it looked like a little boat. When she was done, Amy was so happy.

The next day, Amy showed her friends her new boat. They all cheered and praised her for making such a cool boat.

Amy thanked her elder grandmother for teaching her how to fold the boat. From that day on, she loved spending time with her elder grandma, learning more and more fun things.

Once upon a time there was a girl called Lisa. She was very creative and loved to go on adventures. She had a good idea one day. She decided to take a bin, hold it carefully and let it lead the way.

Lisa took her bin down the street, through the park, into the woods and all the way to a special pond. Along the way she noticed all kinds of things, like birds singing and trees growing. When she finally arrived at the pond, she could see the sparkle of the sun on the water.

Lisa looked around and noticed a beautiful, jiggly butterfly. She asked the bin to lead her to it so she could get a better look. She followed the bin and the butterfly soon flew away, but it left a trail of glitter behind it.

The glitter lead Lisa back to her bin and that's when she realized she had gone on an amazing journey. She took her bin back home where she put it away and made a plan for her next adventure.

Lily liked to play with her toy camera. She liked to record things that she saw and heard. She liked to record her cat, Max, who had soft fur and green eyes. She liked to record her mom, who sang songs and read books to her. She liked to record her dad, who made jokes and built things with her.

One night, Lily had a big idea. She wanted to record the stars and the moon. She asked her mom if she could go outside and look at the sky. Her mom said yes, but she had to wear her coat and hat. It was cold and dark outside. Lily put on her coat and hat and took her toy camera. She went outside with her mom.

Lily looked up at the sky. She saw many stars and a big moon. They were bright and shiny. She pointed her toy camera at them and pressed the button. She said, "I am recording the stars and the moon. They are so pretty. I want to show them to dad and Max."

Her mom smiled and said, "That's a great idea, Lily. You are very smart and creative. I'm sure dad and Max will love your video. But we should go back inside soon. It's getting late and you need to sleep."

Lily nodded and said, "Okay, mom. Can I record one more thing?"

Her mom said, "Sure, what do you want to record?"

Lily looked around and saw a big tree. It had many leaves and branches. She said, "I want to record the tree. It is so tall and strong. Maybe it has a bird or a squirrel in it."

Her mom said, "Okay, let's go to the tree. But be careful, don't go too close. The tree might have thorns or bugs."

Lily and her mom walked to the tree. Lily pointed her toy camera at the tree and pressed the button. She said, "I am recording the tree. It is so green and brown. I wonder what lives in it."

Suddenly, they heard a loud noise. It was a hoot. It came from the tree. Lily and her mom looked up and saw a big owl. It had yellow eyes and dark fur. It looked at them and hooted again.

Lily was surprised and excited. She said, "Wow, mom, look! It's an owl! It lives in the tree! Can I record it?"

Her mom said, "Yes, you can, but be quiet. Don't scare it. It might fly away."

Lily whispered, "Okay, mom. I will be quiet." She pointed her toy camera at the owl and pressed the button. She said, "I am recording the owl. It is so dark and fluffy. It makes a funny sound. I like it."

The owl looked at them and hooted one more time. Then it spread its wings and flew away. Lily and her mom watched it go. They smiled and hugged. They said, "That was amazing. We saw an owl. We recorded it. We will remember it forever."

They went back inside and showed their video to dad and Max. They were happy and proud. They had a good night. They slept well and dreamed of stars and moons and trees and owls.

One day, the naughty yellow bird was hopping around and having lots of fun. He hopped to a big lake and he saw a bunch of fish swimming. He wanted to join in on the fun, so he took a deep breath and dove into the water. He swam around and around and had a great time. He even found a big green turtle and said hello.

The bird then went back up to the surface of the water and hopped around on the banks. He then noticed a big, yellow sun setting in the sky. He smiled and thought about how much fun he had diving into the lake and swimming around.

He then hopped back to his nest, tired from all his adventures of the day. He happily cuddled up in his bed and fell asleep. He dreamed of diving in the lake again and having more fun!

Once upon a time, there was a friendly dog named Spot. Spot loved to play with his ball and run in the park. One day, Spot saw a big camera on the grass. Spot was curious and wanted to see what the camera was for.

Spot's friend, a little girl named Sue, came over and said, "Spot, I want to take a picture of you with this camera. But you need to improve your pose. Can you sit and smile for me?" Spot nodded and tried his best to sit still and smile for Sue.

But as Sue was about to take the picture, a naughty cat named Whiskers jumped in front of the camera. Whiskers wanted to be in the picture too! Spot and Whiskers started to argue about who should be in the picture. Sue said, "Stop! We can all be in the picture together. Let's be friends and share." Spot and Whiskers agreed, and they all posed for a friendly picture together.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved animals. One day, she went on a safari with her mommy and daddy. They saw lots of big animals like elephants and giraffes.

As they were walking, Lily felt very cold. "Mommy, I'm cold," she said. "Can we go back to the car?"

Her mommy replied, "Sure, but first let's examine these footprints. They belong to a lion!"

Lily's eyes widened in amazement. "Wow, a lion! Let's go see if we can find him!"

But her mommy said, "No, it's not safe. We need to go back to the car and warm up."

So they went back to the car and drank hot chocolate to warm up. Lily was happy to have gone on a safari and couldn't wait to go on another one.

Once upon a time, there was a lucky dog. His name was Spot. Spot was very friendly and made lots of new friends. His mommy and daddy brought him a leash so he could go for walks with them. Spot was so excited to take walks with his mommy and daddy.

One day, Spot found a yucky old bone in the park. It had dirt and mud on it. So Spot's mommy cleaned it for him so he wouldn't get sick. She used water and soap and scrubbed it until it was shiny clean. Spot was so happy!

After that, Spot and his mommy and daddy went for a walk. Spot was so happy to feel the leash and to be out with his family. Spot knew that being lucky was more than just fun - it was being clean, too!

Once upon a time there was a brilliant battery. The battery was very special and could mix things. One day, the battery wanted to mix some glue and water to make something special.

So the battery mixed the glue and water together in a bowl. As they mixed, they started to make a wonderful bubble mixture. The battery was very excited! The bubble mixture was very strong and the bubbles were bigger and brighter than ever.

The battery was so proud of its bubble mixture, that it shared it with all its friends. Everyone loved the bubble mixture, and the battery was so proud to be the one that mixed it. The battery was very proud of its brilliant bubble mixture.

The battery was so happy that it mixed the glue and the water and made something so special. From then on, the battery was known as the brilliant battery!

Anna and her mom went to the station to catch a train. Anna liked the station. She saw many people and things. She saw big trains and small trains. She saw red trains and blue trains. She saw a man with a hat and a whistle. He was the train man.

"Mom, can I talk to the train man?" Anna asked.

"Okay, but be quick. Our train is coming soon," mom said.

Anna ran to the train man. She smiled at him. He smiled back. He was kind.

"Hello, little girl. Do you like trains?" he asked.

"Yes, I love trains. They are fast and loud and fun," Anna said.

"I love trains too. I work with trains. Do you want to see my whistle?" he asked.

"Yes, please," Anna said.

The train man showed Anna his whistle. It was shiny and silver. He blew it softly. It made a sound.

"Wow, that's cool. Can I try?" Anna asked.

"Sure, but be careful. Don't blow it too hard. It might scare the trains," he said.

He gave Anna his whistle. Anna put it in her mouth. She blew it hard. It made a loud sound.

Blink, blink, blink. The lights at the station changed. The trains heard the whistle. They thought it was a signal. They started to move.

"Anna, what are you doing? Stop that!" mom shouted.

She ran to Anna. She grabbed her hand. She pulled her away from the train man.

"Sorry, sorry, sorry," Anna said.

But it was too late. The trains were confused. They bumped into each other. They crashed. They made a big mess. There was smoke and fire and noise. People screamed and ran. The station was broken.

Anna and her mom were scared. They hid behind a wall. They hugged each other. They cried.

The train man was sad. He lost his whistle. He lost his job. He lost his smile. He cried too.

The end.

Lily was a dog who liked to lead. She always ran in front of her family when they went for walks. She liked to sniff new things and bark at other dogs. She was a happy dog.
