Lily liked to make poems. She would think of words that sound nice together and say them out loud. Sometimes she would write them down with her crayons. She had a book of poems that her mom gave her. She liked to read them and look at the pictures.

One day, she wanted to show her poems to her friend Max. She took her book and went to his house. She knocked on the door and Max opened it. He was happy to see her. He invited her in and they went to his room. He had a lot of toys and books.

Lily said, "I have something to show you. It is my book of poems. Do you want to hear them?" Max said, "Yes, I like poems. Can I see your book?" Lily gave him her book and he opened it. He looked at the pages and frowned. He said, "These are not poems. These are just words. And these are not pictures. These are just scribbles. This is a fake book."

Lily felt sad and angry. She said, "No, these are my poems. I made them. They are not fake. They are real. You are mean. You don't understand poems." She grabbed her book and ran out of his room. She went to the door and opened it. She wanted to go home.

But then she heard Max call her name. He followed her and said, "Wait, Lily. I'm sorry. I didn't mean to hurt your feelings. I was just joking. I like your poems. They are very creative. Can you read them to me? Please?"

Lily paused. She looked at him and saw that he looked sorry. She thought for a moment. She liked Max. He was her friend. Maybe he was just teasing. Maybe he did like her poems. She said, "Okay, I will read them to you. But you have to listen carefully. And you have to say something nice after each one. Deal?"

Max nodded. He said, "Deal. I promise. Let's go back to my room. We can sit on the floor and read your book together. And maybe I can show you some of my books too. Do you like dinosaurs?"

Lily smiled. She said, "Yes, I like dinosaurs. They are big and scary and cool. Come on, let's go." She took his hand and they went back to his room. They sat on the floor and opened her book. She read him her poems and he listened. He said something nice after each one. They had fun. They learned to appreciate each other's words and pictures. They became better friends.

Lila likes to have fun with her toys. She has many toys, but her favorite is a big bulb. The bulb is shiny and colorful. It can make different sounds and lights when Lila presses a button.

One day, Lila wants to show her bulb to her friend Max. She takes her bulb to his house and knocks on the door. Max opens the door and smiles. He likes Lila and her bulb. He invites her to come in and play.

Lila and Max have a lot of fun with the bulb. They press the button and watch the lights and hear the sounds. They laugh and clap their hands. They pretend the bulb is a spaceship, a robot, or a monster. They are very happy.

But then, Max's mom calls them for lunch. She tells them to put away their toys and wash their hands. Lila and Max do what she says. They put the bulb on the table and go to the bathroom.

When they come back, they see that Max's little brother Sam has taken the bulb. He is playing with it and making a mess. He has broken the button and ripped the colors. He has ruined the bulb.

Lila and Max are very sad and angry. They yell at Sam and try to get the bulb back. But Sam does not listen. He cries and holds the bulb tight. He does not want to give it back.

Max's mom hears the noise and comes to see what is wrong. She sees the broken bulb and the upset kids. She scolds Sam and takes the bulb from him. She gives it back to Lila and says she is sorry. She tells Sam to say sorry too and to share his toys.

Lila is glad to have her bulb back, but she is still sad. The bulb is not the same as before. It is not shiny and colorful. It does not make sounds and lights. It is not original. She does not want to play with it anymore.

Max sees that Lila is sad and tries to cheer her up. He says he is sorry too and that he likes her and her bulb. He says they can still have fun with the bulb. They can fix it and make it new. They can use glue and tape and paper and crayons. They can make it original again.

Lila smiles and hugs Max. She likes him and his idea. She says they can do that and have fun. They go to get the things they need and start to work on the bulb. They are very creative and happy. They make the bulb original again.

Once upon a time, there was a little squirrel named Sammy. Sammy lived in a big oak tree with his family. One day, Sammy's mom told him they were going on a trip. "Sammy, we need to pack our things for our trip," said his mom.

Sammy was very excited and asked, "Where are we going?" His mom replied, "We are going to visit our cousins who live in a fancy tree. They have lots of acorns to share with us."

Sammy and his family packed their acorns and set off on their trip. When they arrived at their cousins' tree, Sammy was amazed. The tree was very fancy, with twinkling lights and colorful leaves. Sammy and his cousins played and shared their acorns together.

As the sun began to set, Sammy's mom said it was time to go back to their own tree. Sammy was sad to leave his cousins, but he knew he would see them again soon. He packed his things and said goodbye to his new friends. Sammy and his family returned home, happy and tired from their adventure.

Once there was a grumpy bear who lived in a big cave.

One day the bear was so grumpy that he went to find something to cheer him up. He found a long chain.

The bear decided to perform with the chain because he knew it would make him happy. He laughed and cheered as he twisted and turned the chain around his body.

The bear smiled and laughed and made the chain fly over his head and behind his back. He performed with the chain until he was too tired to continue.

The bear had so much fun that day; he was not grumpy anymore! He went to sleep with a huge smile on his face.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved going to the park with his mommy. They would swing and slide and play together.

One day, on their way to the park, Timmy's mommy realized they were low on fuel. She said, "Oh no! We need to stop and get some gas before we go to the park." Timmy asked, "What's gas?" His mommy explained that it's what makes the car go.

They finally found a gas station and filled up the car. Timmy was excited to go to the park and play, but his mommy said they had to go home because she was feeling persistent pain in her back. Timmy asked, "What's persistent?" His mommy said it means the pain won't go away. They went home and Timmy helped his mommy by bringing her a blanket and some water.

Once upon a time, there lived a mommy and a daddy and a little girl named Lucy.

One day, Lucy's mommy was mail-ing a letter to her friend. But when Lucy saw the mail, she wanted to mail something too. So she asked her mommy if she could mail her toy truck. Her mommy said yes and helped Lucy put the toy in the mailbox.

After a while, Mommy and Daddy had to go to the store. But before they left, Mommy put dinner in the dishwasher.

When they got back home, Mommy and Daddy noticed that the dishwasher was hurt. They opened the dishwasher and saw that Lucy's toy truck was inside.

Dad asked Lucy why the toy truck was in the dishwasher. Lucy said she wanted to mail it by mistake.

Mommy and Daddy hugged Lucy and said it was an honest mistake. They were very happy that the toy truck wasn't hurt.

Then, they all ate dinner and went to bed. Lucy was so glad she still had her toy truck.

Anna and Ben were playing in the park with their toy cars. They liked to make them zoom and crash and honk. Sometimes they pretended they were drivers and talked to each other.

"Look out, Ben, there is a big bird!" Anna said, pointing to a crow that landed on a bench.

Ben saw the bird and felt fearful. He did not like big birds. They had sharp beaks and loud cries. He thought the bird might peck his car or his head.

"Let's go away, Anna, the bird is scary!" Ben said, grabbing his car and running.

Anna did not think the bird was scary. She thought it was funny. She wanted to see it closer. She left her car on the ground and walked to the bench.

"Hello, bird, what are you doing?" Anna said, smiling.

The bird looked at Anna and tilted its head. It saw her car on the ground and hopped to it. It picked it up with its beak and flew away.

"Hey, that's my car, give it back!" Anna shouted, jumping and waving her arms.

The bird did not listen. It flew higher and higher, holding the car. Anna felt angry and sad. She wanted her car back.

"Ben, help me, the bird took my car!" Anna cried, running to Ben.

Ben heard Anna and turned around. He saw the bird and the car in the sky. He felt sorry for Anna. He wanted to help her.

"Maybe we can make the bird drop the car," Ben said, thinking.

"How?" Anna asked, wiping her tears.

"Maybe we can make a loud noise and scare the bird," Ben said, looking around.

He saw a big trash can and had an idea. He ran to the trash can and kicked it hard. It made a loud bang.

The bird heard the bang and got startled. It dropped the car from its beak. The car fell down and landed on the ground.

Anna and Ben saw the car and cheered. They ran to the car and picked it up. It was not broken. It still worked.

"Thank you, Ben, you are smart and brave!" Anna said, hugging Ben.

"You're welcome, Anna, you are kind and fun!" Ben said, hugging Anna.

They smiled and played with their cars again. They made them reverse and go forward and turn. They forgot about the bird and had a good time.

Once upon a time, there was a zebra. It was running in a big field. It ran and ran and ran, enjoying the day. But then it stopped. It was trying to find a hidden place to rest.

The zebra found a tree with some big, green leaves. It was hidden, so the zebra thought it was a perfect place to rest. It stepped into the leaves and fell asleep.

When the zebra woke up, it saw a little boy. He was looking at it, but he didn't move. The zebra wanted to play, so it stopped in front of the little boy.

The little boy smiled and ran away. The zebra followed the boy. They played together for a long time. The zebra was having lots of fun!

Finally, it was time for the zebra to go back to its hidden place. It stopped to say goodbye to the little boy. Then it ran back to its secret spot and had a nice, long rest.

Once upon a time there was a little creature who wanted to go on a hop. His name was Figure and he was very original. He wanted to explore the world so he hopped out of his home and started down the path.

He hopped and hopped until he saw something exciting! It was a big tree with lots of fruit. He hopped up in the tree and started to eat the delicious fruit.

Just then he heard a voice coming from behind him. "Hello Figure, who are you?" Figure looked around to see a fluffy bunny standing there. Figure hopped down the tree and said hi back to the bunny.

The bunny said, "My name is Jumpy and I would like to be your friend. Would you like to come and play with me?"

Figure was so happy to have a new friend and he said, "Yes, I would love to play with you!" And that's just what they did; They hopped and hopped, exploring new places and having lots of fun.

And they have been friends ever since!

Once upon a time there was a little kid who wanted to pretend. So, she ran over to the big, fluffy pillow and hopped on it. She started pretending to ride a horse around the world.

The silly little kid rode through the jungle, through the desert, and over the ocean. Everywhere she went she saw something new and exciting.

Then, she came across a foolish lion. He was so silly that he kept roaring instead of eating his dinner. The little girl pretended that she was brave and bravely yelled back at the lion. She was so brave that the lion ran away and never came back!

The little girl finished her pretend journey and hopped down off the pillow. She had had so much fun pretending and was so proud of herself for being brave.

Once upon a time, there was a lucky little boy. His name was Tim, and he loved to go outside and play. One day Tim was playing in his backyard when he saw a big jeep! He was so excited and he wanted to explore it.

Tim jumped in and let out a big squeak! He was having so much fun, he decided to kick the seat. But just as he was about to get out of the jeep, he heard an engine starting. It was a surprise adventure!

The jeep drove fast and Tim was so happy. He waved to all the cows he passed and saw so many beautiful flowers. After a while, the jeep stopped and Tim got out. He realized he was in the most beautiful park he had ever seen! Everywhere he looked he could see more friendly animals and beautiful plants. He was so lucky to have such a fun day on his surprise adventure!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Jill. She was an attractive three-year-old who loved reading books. One day, she decided to take her book outside so she could read it in the sunshine.

As she was walking, Jill found a beautiful shell in the grass. She was amazed at its beauty and wondered if there might be something fascinating inside.

Suddenly, a voice called out to her, “Do you want to read the story inside the shell?”

Jill looked around, but saw nobody. She looked back at the shell and asked, “Who said that?”

The voice replied, “I’m the shell. I tell stories. Do you want to hear mine?”

Jill was surprised, but also very excited. She nodded her head and carefully opened the shell. Inside, there was a beautiful tale about a brave prince. Jill read it with delight and thanked the shell for the amazing story when she finished.

Jill collected more shells from then on, always looking for that same exciting and attractive story.

Lila and Ben were playing with paper. They liked to cut, fold and draw on it. They made paper hats, paper planes and paper animals. They had a lot of fun.

But they also made a lot of mess. They left paper scraps and bits everywhere. They did not care about cleaning up. They did not think about how paper came from trees and how trees were important for the air and the animals.

One day, their mom came to their room and saw the paper mess. She was not happy. She said, "Lila and Ben, you are wasting paper. Do you know how paper is made? Do you know how many trees are cut down to make paper? Do you know how far away some of the trees are? They are in distant lands, where there are different people and animals. They need the trees to live and be happy. You should not waste paper. You should save paper. You should use it wisely and recycle it when you are done. That way, you can help save the trees and the planet."

Lila and Ben felt sorry. They did not know that paper was so precious. They did not want to hurt the trees and the planet. They said, "We are sorry, mom. We did not know. We will save paper from now on. We will use it carefully and recycle it. We will also clean up our mess. Can you teach us more about the trees and the distant lands?"

Their mom smiled. She was glad that they learned their lesson. She said, "Of course, I will. I am proud of you for wanting to save paper and the planet. Come, let's go to the library and find some books about the trees and the distant lands. You can also make some paper crafts with the paper you have left. But remember, only use what you need and recycle what you don't."

Lila and Ben nodded. They hugged their mom and thanked her. They went to the library and learned more about the trees and the distant lands. They also made some paper crafts with the paper they had left. They used paper clips, glue and scissors to make them. They made paper flowers, paper stars and paper birds. They gave some of them to their mom and some of them to their friends. They told them about the importance of saving paper and the planet. They felt happy and proud. They had a lot of fun.

Tom and Mia are busy. They have to clean their room. Mom said so. They put their toys in the box. They make their bed. They throw away the trash.

But Tom has a problem. He has an itch on his nose. He rubs it with his hand. But it does not help. The itch is still there.

"Ow, ow, ow!" Tom says. "My nose is itchy!"

Mia looks at him. She sees a red spot on his nose. She knows what it is. It is a mosquito bite.

"Tom, you have a bite!" Mia says. "A mosquito bit you!"

Tom does not like mosquitoes. They are mean. They make him itch.

"How can I make it stop?" Tom asks.

Mia thinks. She remembers what Mom does when she has a bite. She gets a wet cloth. She puts it on the bite. She says it makes it cool and better.

"Mia, can you help me?" Tom says.

Mia nods. She goes to the bathroom. She gets a wet cloth. She comes back to the room. She puts the cloth on Tom's nose.

"Does it feel better?" Mia asks.

Tom nods. He feels the cloth on his nose. It is cool and nice. The itch is gone.

"Thank you, Mia!" Tom says.

"You're welcome, Tom!" Mia says.

They hug. They are happy. They finish cleaning their room. They are good. Mom is proud.

Tim and Lily liked to ride their bikes in the park. They had big bikes with two wheels and pedals. They wore helmets and gloves to be safe. One day, they saw a new sign in the park. It had a picture of a bike and an arrow. It said "Bike Trail".

"Let's follow the sign!" Tim said. "Maybe we can find a new place to ride."

"OK!" Lily said. "But be careful. We don't know what's ahead."

They followed the sign and the arrow. They rode on a dirt path that went up and down and around. They saw trees and flowers and birds. They had fun.

But then, they came to a big hill. The sign said "Caution". It had a picture of a bike and a line. It said "No Bikes".

"What does that mean?" Tim asked.

"It means we can't ride our bikes here," Lily said. "We have to stop and walk."

"Why?" Tim asked.

"Maybe because it's too steep or too rocky or too dangerous," Lily said.

But Tim did not listen. He wanted to ride his bike down the hill. He thought it would be fun. He did not stop. He did not walk. He pedaled faster and faster.

"Tim, wait!" Lily shouted. "Stop! It's not safe!"

But Tim did not hear her. He zoomed down the hill. He did not see the big hole in the ground. He did not see the ancient bones that were buried there. He did not see the skull that looked like a dinosaur.

He only saw them when it was too late. He crashed into the hole. He fell off his bike. He landed on the bones. He hurt his arm and his leg and his head. He cried.

Lily ran down the hill. She saw Tim and his bike and the bones and the skull. She was scared. She called for help.

Soon, a man came. He was a park ranger. He had a radio and a first aid kit. He helped Tim. He bandaged his wounds. He called an ambulance.

He also looked at the bones and the skull. He was amazed. He said they were very old and very rare. He said they were fossils. He said they were from a time when dinosaurs lived.

He said Tim and Lily had made a big discovery. He said they were very lucky.

But Tim and Lily did not feel lucky. They felt sorry. They wished they had followed the sign. They wished they had stopped and walked. They learned their lesson. They never rode their bikes where they were not supposed to again.

Anna was very happy. Today was her birthday. She had a big cake with four candles. She had many presents from her family and friends. She had a new doll, a book, a ball, and a hat.

She wanted to thank everyone for her birthday. She hugged her mom and dad and said, "Thank you for my cake and my presents. I love you very much." She smiled at her grandma and grandpa and said, "Thank you for my doll and my book. They are very pretty and fun." She waved at her friends and said, "Thank you for my ball and my hat. They are very cool and nice."

But there was one more present that she did not see. It was hidden behind the sofa. It was a big box with a bow. Her dad said, "Anna, there is one more present for you. Do you want to see what it is?" Anna nodded and ran to the sofa. She pulled the box and opened it.

Inside the box, there was a puppy. It was brown and white and had a red collar. It wagged its tail and licked Anna's face. Anna was very surprised and happy. She said, "Wow, a puppy! Is it for me?" Her mom said, "Yes, it is for you. We know you love animals and you are very kind and responsible. We think you are ready to have a pet. But you have to take good care of it. You have to feed it, walk it, play with it, and keep it healthy."

Anna hugged the puppy and said, "Thank you, thank you, thank you! This is the best present ever! I will take good care of it. I will name it Spot. I love you, Spot." Spot barked and cuddled with Anna. Everyone clapped and cheered. Anna had a very happy birthday.

Mommy was happy. She was pouring warm water into a building. She said it was for the people who lived there. She said they needed it to stay warm.

When they finished pouring, they went home and had dinner. Mommy said it was time for bed. Daddy said they'd done a good job.

The next morning Mommy was happy again. She took us back to the building and we saw the people. They were smiling and hugging her. They thanked her for the warm water.

Everyone was happy. They said goodbye and we went home. Mommy and Daddy said they were proud of us. We had done a nice thing!

Once upon a time, there was a little fish named Bubbles. Bubbles loved to travel around the sea and see all the pretty things. One day, Bubbles met a sweet little crab named Sally. Sally was very kind and offered to show Bubbles around the sea.

Bubbles was very excited and they swam all around. They saw big rocks and little fish, and even a big whale! Bubbles loved traveling with Sally and they became good friends.

After a long day of swimming, Sally showed Bubbles a secret spot where they could rest. They found a sweet little cave and settled in for the night. Bubbles was so happy to have a new friend and to have traveled to so many new places in the sea.

Once there was a lazy bear. He used to sleep all day and eat honey. One day he ate too much honey and he started to shrink! He was so small that he fit in the ash. He stayed there all day, feeling very silly. But the lazy bear never learned his lesson. Every day he keeps eating more honey, so he still hasn't grown back to normal size.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Mike. Mike was 3 years old and loved to explore new things.

One day, Mike went to the park with his dad. In the park, there was a big maze. Mike was excited! He wanted to explore the maze and see what was inside.

Mike's dad said, "Mike, don't go too far." But Mike didn't listen. He kept going into the maze.

It was quiet in the maze, but soon Mike heard some voices. He saw two people arguing. Mike was scared and he wanted to go back.

Mike shouted, "Please stop fighting!"

The two people stopped arguing and saw Mike. They said sorry to him and they made friends.

Mike went back home with a big smile. He had an amazing adventure in the quiet maze!

Sara was sick. She had a sore throat and a cough. She did not want to play or eat. She only wanted to sleep and drink water.

Mom gave Sara some mint tea. Mint tea was good for sore throats. It was hot and sweet and smelled nice. Sara liked mint tea. She drank some and felt a little better.

Tom was Sara's brother. He was not sick. He wanted to play and eat. He did not like mint tea. He thought it was bitter and smelled bad. He was jealous of Sara. He wanted Mom to give him something too.

He said to Mom, "Mom, I want some juice. Juice is better than mint tea. Can I have some juice?"

Mom said, "No, Tom. Juice is not good for you right now. It has too much sugar. Sugar can make you sick too. You can have some water or some milk. And you can have some mint tea if you want."

Tom did not want water or milk or mint tea. He wanted juice. He was angry and sad. He said, "That's not fair. Sara gets mint tea and I get nothing. I don't like mint tea. I don't like Sara. She is always sick and gets everything."

Mom said, "Tom, that's not nice. You should not be jealous of Sara. She is sick and needs mint tea to heal. You are healthy and strong and can play and eat. You should be happy and kind. You should help Sara and share with her. Maybe you can read her a story or draw her a picture. That will make her happy and help her heal faster."

Tom thought about what Mom said. He felt sorry for Sara. He did not want her to be sick. He wanted her to be happy and play with him. He decided to be nice and help her. He said, "OK, Mom. I will read Sara a story and draw her a picture. I will share with her and be kind. I love Sara. I hope she heals soon."

Mom smiled and hugged Tom. She said, "That's very good, Tom. I'm proud of you. I love you too. And I'm sure Sara will love your story and your picture. And she will heal soon. Mint tea and love are good for healing."

Once upon a time, in a small village, there was a helpful man named Tom. Tom liked to create things with his hands. One day, he decided to make a big chest to store toys for the children in the village.

Tom worked hard to make the chest. He used wood, nails, and paint. When he was done, the chest was very big and colorful. He put the chest in the middle of the village and filled it with toys.

One day, a little girl named Lily saw the chest and said, "Wow! Look at all the toys!" Tom smiled and said, "Take one, and share with your friends." Lily took a toy and shared it with her friends. They all played together and had a lot of fun.

Soon, all the children in the village learned to share the toys from the chest. They learned that sharing was good and made everyone happy. The helpful man, Tom, was happy to see the children playing together.

The moral of the story is that sharing is a good thing, and being helpful can make everyone happy.

Tom and Lily went to the shop with Mom. They wanted to buy some food for dinner. Mom gave them a list of things to find. Tom and Lily liked to help Mom.

But the shop was very big and had many things. Tom and Lily got tired of looking for the things on the list. They wanted to play with the toys and the books. They did not want to buy food. They thought the shop was boring.

"Mom, can we go now?" Tom asked. "We have been here for a long time."

"Not yet, Tom. We still need some eggs and some cheese," Mom said. "Please stay with me and help me."

"But Mom, we want to play!" Lily said. "The shop is boring. There is nothing fun here."

Mom sighed. She knew Tom and Lily were bored. But she also needed to buy the food. She had an idea.

"OK, Tom and Lily. How about this? If you help me find the eggs and the cheese, I will let you choose one thing each from the shop. Anything you want. But you have to be quick and good. Deal?"

Tom and Lily nodded. They liked Mom's idea. They wanted to choose something from the shop. Maybe a toy or a book or a candy. They followed Mom and helped her find the eggs and the cheese.

Soon, they had everything on the list. Mom checked out and paid. Then she let Tom and Lily choose one thing each from the shop. Tom chose a car and Lily chose a doll. They were happy.

"Thank you, Mom!" Tom and Lily said. "You are the best!"

"You're welcome, Tom and Lily. You are very good helpers. Now let's go home and make dinner. And maybe we can play with your new things later. How does that sound?"

Tom and Lily smiled. They liked that sound. They hugged Mom and left the shop. The shop was not so boring after all. The end.

Molly was a curious little girl. She often liked to explore her backyard and it was her favorite place to be.

One day, she noticed something special in the sky. It was a bright, colourful birdcage! She thought it was so beautiful and she wanted to get closer to get a better look.

Molly went to the birdcage and she tried to open it. But it wouldn't open! Then, she heard a loud noise. It was coming from a strange and naughty animal. It was trying to spoil the birdcage and stop Molly from opening it!

Molly was scared and ran away. She was so sad that she couldn't explore the birdcage. She never got a chance to find out what was inside.

Once there was a boy named Tom. Tom lived on a farm with his mom and dad. They had a big field of wheat. Tom loved to play in the wheat. One day, Tom saw a filthy dog. The dog was very dirty and sad.

Tom said, "Hi, dog! You are so dirty. I will help you." Tom took a cloth and began to wipe the dog. The dog wagged its tail and was happy. Tom's mom called him, "Tom, come inside! It's time to eat!" Tom said goodbye to the dog and went inside.

The next day, Tom went to play in the wheat field again. But the wheat was gone! The filthy dog had eaten all the wheat. Tom's mom and dad were very sad. The farm had no more wheat, and they had no food. Tom was sad too. He wished he had not wiped the filthy dog.

One day, there was a girl called Lucy. She was three years old. Lucy was playing in the garden when she saw an ugly ice cube. She decided that she wanted to sign her name on it.

Lucy took a black marker pen and wrote her name on the ice cube. Mom saw her and shouted, "No Lucy! You mustn't sign it!"

But Lucy was very stubborn. She ignored Mom and kept signing.

Mom was very angry. She said, "If you keep signing the ice, it will melt and your name will be gone!"

Lucy didn't understand and kept signing.

Mom took away the marker pen and said, "We must respect nature, Lucy. We must not make it look ugly."

Lucy was sad and said, "I'm sorry Mom."

Mom hugged her and said, "It's ok my darling. Let's go inside and have a nice cold ice cream."

Lucy smiled and ran inside with Mom. From that day on, she always respected nature.

Once upon a time, there was a frog named Freddy. Freddy lived in a pond with his friends. One day, Freddy saw a beautiful frog named Lily. He asked her, "Will you marry me?" Lily said, "Yes!"

Freddy was so happy, but his friends were miserable. They didn't like Lily because she was different from them. They said, "We don't want you to marry her, Freddy." But Freddy loved Lily and didn't listen to his friends.

Finally, Freddy and Lily got married by the pond. All of their friends came to the wedding and saw how happy Freddy was with Lily. They realized that being different was okay and they all became friends again. Freddy and Lily lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to travel with her family. One day, they went on a trip to the beach. Lily was so excited to play in the sand and swim in the ocean!

But before they left, Lily's mom told her to pack a bag with all her things. Lily put in her swimsuit, towel, and sunscreen. She also packed some snacks and a book to read.

When they arrived at the beach, Lily ran straight to the water. She played and splashed for hours. But when it was time to go home, she realized her bag was wet and all her things were now wet too! She was sad because she couldn't use any of her things anymore.

Lily's mom told her that next time, she should make sure her bag is dry before they travel home. Lily learned her lesson and always made sure her bag was dry after that day. The end.

Once upon a time there was a big rabbit named Bob. Bob had a big, shiny, red nose. Every day he would go into the woods with his friends and they would jump and run around. On one particular day, they heard a loud, strange noise. The friends were scared and stopped what they were doing to investigate.

Bob bravely stepped up towards the noise. He went closer and closer until he could see what was causing the noise. It was a dead bird! Bob felt sad and started to cry.

His friends noticed Bob, and went over to check on him. "What's wrong Bob?" they asked. Bob pointed to the dead bird and said, "The noise disturbed me".

His friends were sad, too. "Let's plant a beautiful sign near the dead bird to remember it," said Bob's friends. They all agreed and when they were finished, they left the woods. Bob's friends were happy that Bob wasn't scared anymore and decided to always remember his big, shiny, red nose.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the sunshine. One day, she found a new rock in her backyard. It was shiny and sparkly, and she loved it very much.

Lily's mommy said, "Remember to be careful with your new rock, Lily. It's very special."

Lily nodded her head and put the rock in her pocket. She went to play with her friends at the park. When she got there, she showed her new rock to her friends. They all thought it was very pretty.

Suddenly, Lily realized that her new rock was gone! She looked everywhere, but she couldn't find it. She started to cry.

Her friend asked, "What's wrong, Lily?"

"I lost my new rock," Lily said sadly.

"Don't worry," her friend said. "We'll help you find it."

They looked and looked, and finally, they found the new rock. Lily was so happy! She hugged her friend and said, "Thank you for helping me remember where I put my new rock."

Once upon a time there was a little girl. Her name was Daisy. She had two arms that were orange. She liked to use her arms to join with other people.

One day, Daisy went to the beach with her family. When they arrived at the beach, she saw a lot of people swimming and playing. She wanted to join in the fun.

So Daisy waved her orange arms in the air to get their attention. Everyone at the beach stopped and smiled at Daisy. Then, they all joined hands and formed a big circle around Daisy and laughed together.

Daisy loved joining with all of the people at the beach and having fun with her orange arms. After that day, she always wanted to join in with others.

Anna loved ponies. She had many pony toys in her room. She played with them every day. She wished she had a real pony to ride and hug.

One day, Anna's mom said, "I have a surprise for you, Anna. Come with me to the car." Anna was excited. She wondered what the surprise was. She hoped it was a pony.

They drove to a big farm. Anna saw many animals. She saw cows, sheep, pigs, and chickens. She also saw some horses. They were big and beautiful. Anna liked them, but they were not ponies.

Anna's mom parked the car and said, "Follow me, Anna. I have something to show you." She led Anna to a small barn. She opened the door and said, "Look, Anna. This is your surprise."

Anna looked inside the barn. She saw a brown pony. It was small and cute. It had a long mane and a fluffy tail. It looked at Anna with friendly eyes. Anna gasped. She could not believe it. She had a real pony.

"Mom, is this my pony?" Anna asked.

"Yes, Anna. This is your pony. His name is Coco. He is very gentle and sweet. He likes carrots and apples. Do you want to pet him?" Mom said.

Anna nodded. She ran to the pony and hugged him. He nuzzled her hair and snorted. Anna felt happy. She thanked her mom and said, "I love you, Coco. You are the best surprise ever."

One day, Lily and Tom went to the park with their mom. They saw a big pond with many ducks and doves. Lily liked the doves because they were light and pretty. Tom liked the ducks because they made funny noises.

"Look, mom, a dove!" Lily said, pointing to a bird on a branch. "Can I feed it?"

"Sure, honey, here are some seeds," mom said, giving Lily a handful. Lily walked slowly to the dove and held out her hand. The dove looked at her and flew down to eat the seeds.

"Wow, it likes you!" Tom said, watching from a distance. He wanted to feed a duck, so he ran to the edge of the pond and threw some bread. A big duck saw the bread and swam to get it.

"Quack, quack!" the duck said, nibbling the bread. Tom laughed and threw more bread. The duck was happy and followed him.

"Look, mom, a duck!" Tom said, waving to his mom. "Can I pet it?"

"Be careful, sweetie, ducks can bite," mom said, walking to Tom. She helped him stroke the duck's feathers gently. The duck seemed to like it and wagged its tail.

"Wow, it likes you too!" Lily said, joining them. She wanted to pet the duck too, so she reached out her hand. The duck saw her and quacked loudly.

"Quack, quack!" the duck said, snapping at Lily's hand. Lily was scared and pulled back her hand. She cried and ran to her mom.

"Ow, ow, ow!" Lily said, sobbing. "The duck bit me!"

"I'm sorry, honey, are you okay?" mom said, hugging Lily. She looked at her hand and saw a small red mark. "It's just a scratch, don't worry. The duck didn't mean to hurt you, it was just protecting its food."

"Sorry, Lily, I didn't know the duck was mean," Tom said, feeling sorry for his sister. He gave her a hug and a kiss. "Do you want to play with the doves again?"

"Okay, Tom, thank you," Lily said, wiping her tears. She smiled and took Tom's hand. They walked back to the branch where the doves were. They fed them some more seeds and watched them fly and jump. The doves were nice and gentle. They made Lily and Tom happy. Mom smiled and took a picture of them. They had a fun day at the park.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy had a new toy train that he loved to play with. One day, Timmy's friend Billy came over to play. Billy saw Timmy's new toy train and wanted to play with it too. Timmy said, "No, it's mine. You can't play with it."

Billy got angry and said, "If you don't let me play with it, I'll take it from you." Timmy was scared and didn't want Billy to pull his train away. He thought of a plan to keep his toy train safe.

Timmy said, "Let's play hide and seek instead. I'll hide first and you can find me." Billy agreed and started counting while Timmy ran to hide his toy train. Billy couldn't find Timmy, but he also couldn't find the toy train. Timmy had hidden it well.

When Billy gave up, Timmy showed him where he had hidden the train. Billy apologized for threatening to take it and they played with the train together. Timmy learned that sharing can be fun and Billy learned that threatening others is not nice.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys, but she had so many that they cluttered up her room. Her mom told her to put them away in a box, but Lily didn't want to.

"I don't want to put my toys away," Lily said.

But her mom was persistent. "You need to put them away so you can find them later," she said.

Lily sighed and started putting her toys in the box. She found it was actually fun to organize them. When she was done, she looked at her tidy room and smiled.

"Wow, this looks great!" she said.

From then on, Lily made sure to put her toys away in the box every day.

Once there was a young girl named Jessica. She wanted to gain something special so one day she ventured out into the world. Along her journey, she stumbled upon a huge pile of grey dust. She was curious so she scooped it up in her hands and was surprised by what happened next.

When Jessica opened her hands, the grey dust turned into a beautiful golden coin. Jessica was so excited and couldn't believe her luck! She tucked the coin into her pocket and thanked the pile of ash for her special gain.

Jessica quickly made her way back home and showed her family the coin. Her parents praised her for her luck and they all decided to use the coin to buy some special treats.

Jessica was so happy with her gain and it was a special moment she would never forget. It was amazing what she had found in the pile of ash. It showed her that even when she was young, she could achieve something special.

Jason was walking in the park one day with his mum when he saw a deaf chicken. He asked his mum, "What is that?" His mum replied, "That's a deaf chicken".

Jason was fascinated by this chicken and so he decided to gain its attention. He carefully approached the chicken and started to clap his hands slowly. The chicken noticed and started to cluck at Jason.

Jason smiled as he watched the chicken. He said to his mum, "I'm glad I have gained the chicken's attention". She smiled and replied, "Me too".

The two of them watched the chicken for a while before it wandered off into the bushes. Jason and his mum then started walking home, talking about the deaf chicken they had just seen.

Anna and Ben like to play with their cart. It is a big cart with four wheels and a handle. They can put toys and books and snacks in the cart and pull it around the yard. They have a lot of fun with their cart.

One day, they are playing with their cart when they hear a loud snap. One of the wheels breaks off the cart and rolls away. The cart falls to the ground and spills everything. Anna and Ben are sad and scared. They do not know what to do.

They run to their mom and show her the broken cart. Mom looks at the cart and says, "Don't worry, we can repair it. We just need some glue and a new wheel. Do you want to help me?"

Anna and Ben nod and follow mom to the garage. Mom finds some glue and a wheel that looks like the original one. She puts some glue on the wheel and sticks it to the cart. She holds it for a while until it is dry. Then she turns the cart over and says, "There, it is fixed. Good as new."

Anna and Ben are happy and hug mom. They thank her for repairing their cart. They take their cart back to the yard and put their toys and books and snacks in it. They pull it around and laugh and smile. They love their cart. It is their favorite toy.

Once there was a little girl named Emma. She was three years old and was so excited to go to the pool. She put on her bathing suit and floated around in the pool with her friends.

Emma began to splash around in the pool and soon she was very wet. But then suddenly, she heard a noise. She looked over and saw that one of the tiles in the pool had broken.

Emma’s friends started to cry. Emma tried to comfort them and said, “Don’t worry, let’s just smile and go and play somewhere else.” Her friends smiled, and soon the sadness was gone.

The children went outside and played together. They laughed and smiled and the broken pool was soon forgotten. Emma was so happy to be able to still have fun with her friends, despite the broken pool. She was glad that all her friends could still smile.

Once upon a time, there were two friends, Jack and Jane. They were playing together in the park with their wagon. Jack wanted to pull the wagon and was so excited to play. Jane was happy too, but she said "Wait a minute! Let's delay, we should get a sparkly toy first!"

So, they went to the popular store. When they arrived, the store was full of different kinds of toys. It was so hard for them to choose just one - all the toys looked exciting! But finally, Jack chose a fire truck with red and blue colors. Jane was so excited and said "Can I play with it too?" Jack said "Yes!"

After they bought the toy, they went back to the park with the wagon. They had so much fun playing together. They even got to give their wagon a ride too.

The end!

Once upon a time, there was a dog named Spot. Spot was an ordinary dog with brown fur and a wagging tail. One day, Spot decided to travel to the park. He wanted to play fetch with his bone.

Spot walked and walked until he finally arrived at the park. He dug a hole and buried his bone. Then he ran around and played with his friends.

After a while, Spot got tired and decided to go back home. He dug up his bone and carried it in his mouth as he walked back home. Spot was happy because he had a fun day and found his bone.

Sara and Tom were playing in the park. They liked to run and slide and swing. They saw a big hill with many rocks. They wanted to climb the hill and see what was on the other side.

"Let's go, Sara!" Tom said. "Maybe we can find something fun!"

"OK, Tom!" Sara said. "But be careful. The rocks are hard and sharp."

They started to climb the hill. They used their hands and feet to hold on to the rocks. They went higher and higher. They felt the wind in their hair and the sun on their skin.

They reached the top of the hill. They looked around. They saw trees and flowers and birds. They also saw something shiny and bright. It was a thin silver chain with a small heart pendant. It was lying on the ground, next to a rock.

"Wow, look, Sara!" Tom said. "It's a pretty necklace! Can I have it?"

"No, Tom!" Sara said. "It's not yours. Maybe someone lost it. We should give it back."

"But I like it, Sara!" Tom said. "It's so shiny and nice. Please, can I have it?"

"No, Tom!" Sara said. "It's not fair. You have to share. You have to yield."

Tom frowned. He did not want to share. He did not want to yield. He wanted the silver necklace. He reached for it with his hand.

But then, he heard a loud noise. It was a roar. It came from behind the rock. It was a big, angry bear. It had seen the silver necklace. It wanted it too.

"Run, Sara, run!" Tom shouted. He was scared. He forgot about the silver necklace. He only wanted to be safe.

Sara and Tom ran down the hill. They ran as fast as they could. They did not look back. They reached the park. They saw their mom and dad. They hugged them. They were glad.

They learned a lesson. They learned that some things are not worth fighting for. They learned that sometimes, it is better to yield.

Mummy was taking Mary to the park to play. When they arrived at the bus stop, a big, empty bus was waiting. Mary was so excited she jumped up and down!

When Mummy paid for the tickets, she told Mary to get on. As she stepped onto the bus, something strange happened. Suddenly, it started to shrink! Mary gasped as the bus got smaller and smaller.

The shrinking bus was soon the size of a toy! Mary was so surprised she had to laugh!

Mummy picked up the tiny bus and said, "Look, Mary, we can take it with us to the park. Isn't that great?"

Mary smiled and nodded her head. She was so happy to have a mini bus of her own!

Once upon a time, there lived a little boy called Jack. He loved exploring outside in the garden. One day, Jack found a nut on the ground and thought it looked delicious.

Jack shouted out to his dad, "Dad! Look what I found!" His dad came over and said, "That looks filthy! I wouldn't recommend you eat it!"

Jack was a little bit sad, but he still wanted to try it. He asked his dad, "Can I please have a try?" His dad thought for a moment and then said, "Okay, but just a try."

Jack carefully picked up the nut and took a bite. He immediately spat it out and said, "It's yucky!" His dad laughed and said, "See, I told you. I wouldn't recommend it!"

The End.

Jimmy was playing with his truck in the backyard. He was having a lot of fun, pushing it around and making engine noises. But then he started to feel tired and he yawned. His careless behavior had made him tired and he was ready for a nap. He carefully put his truck away and headed inside. He went to his room and lay on his bed and quickly fell asleep.

Jimmy's truck stayed outside in the backyard, waiting for him to play with it again. The sun was going down, so the truck waited until the morning when Jimmy woke up. He yawned as he stepped out of his room and stretched. Excited to play with his truck, he quickly ran to the backyard. With a huge smile on his face, he ran out into the sunshine and began playing with his truck for the day.

Lily and Tom are friends. They like to play with dolls and cars. One day, Lily has a new doll. It is pink and shiny. It can talk and sing. Lily loves her new doll.

Tom sees Lily's new doll. He wants to play with it too. He is jealous of Lily. He says, "Can I use your doll, Lily? It looks fun."

Lily says, "No, Tom. This is my doll. You have your own toys. Go away."

Tom is angry. He thinks of a plan. He waits until Lily is not looking. He grabs her doll and runs away. He hides behind a tree. He thinks he is smart.

But Lily sees Tom. She knows he took her doll. She is sad and mad. She runs after Tom. She says, "Tom, give me back my doll. That is not nice. That is my secret doll. My grandma gave it to me. She said it is special."

Tom hears Lily. He feels sorry. He knows he did a bad thing. He comes out from behind the tree. He says, "I'm sorry, Lily. I was jealous of your doll. It is very pretty. But I should not have taken it. Here, you can have it back."

Lily takes her doll. She hugs it. She says, "Thank you, Tom. I forgive you. You can play with my doll sometimes. But you have to ask me first. And you have to be gentle."

Tom nods. He says, "OK, Lily. I will ask you first. And I will be gentle. Can we still be friends?"

Lily smiles. She says, "Yes, Tom. We can still be friends. Do you want to play with me and my doll?"

Tom says, "Yes, Lily. I do. Let's play together."

Lily and Tom play with the doll and the cars. They are happy. They are friends.

Once there was a father who had a daughter. The daughter was very sick and he wanted to heal her. So he went to the market to buy some tasty food.

He bought some apples, oranges and some sweet honey. He mixed them together to make a special drink. He took this back to his daughter and gave it to her.

The daughter sipped the drink and smiled. She said it was tasty! And very soon she started to feel better.

The drink had healed her and the dad was very happy. He hugged her and smiled. From then on, the dad always made sure his daughter had lots of tasty food to keep her healthy!

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Today was a nice day, and he wanted to go outside and play. He asked his mom if he could go to the park, but she said he had to clean his room first. Timmy didn't want to clean his room, so he started to cry.

His mom came to him and said, "Timmy, if you clean your room, we can go to the park and rock on the swings. It will be a fun day!" Timmy thought about it and decided to clean his room. He worked hard and did a good job.

When they got to the park, Timmy was so happy that he cleaned his room. He ran to the swings and started to rock back and forth. His mom watched him and smiled. She was proud of him for doing the right thing. Timmy learned that sometimes you have to do things you don't want to do, but it can lead to fun and happiness in the end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who lived with her family. Every day after school, she would stumble up the porch and open the door. As soon as she did, the whole house lit up with amazing colors and sounds.

The little girl always felt so excited as she stumbled around. She would explore every room in her home, finding something new and exciting every time.

One day, as the girl stumbled out of the house onto the porch, she heard the most amazing noise. It was the sound of birds chirping and singing. She was so amazed and searched the sky for the birds. She followed the sound until she stumbled upon a beautiful bird perched on the edge of the porch.

The little girl could hardly believe her eyes. She was so amazed that something so small and beautiful had come to visit her. She wanted to stay outside and watch the bird, but it was getting late so she stumbled back inside for bed.

From then on, the girl stumbled up and down the porch every night, hoping to see the bird again and experience the amazing sight and sound.

Once upon a time, there lived a bug. The bug was fiercely brave. Everywhere it flew, it made its mark. Everyone knew and respected the bug. Friends called it brave bug.

One day the brave bug went out on an adventure. It flew around high and low, near and far. Suddenly, it noticed something strange. Its friends were disappearing!

The bug asked, “Where did you go?” But there was no answer. The bug was afraid and wanted to help. So it looked everywhere and finally found a secret hiding place. It was quiet and dark but the brave bug didn’t back away.

Suddenly he heard his friends’ voice, “Brave bug! We were taken by the fierce monster. Please help us!” The bug knew it had to help. So it flew bravely and tried to find the monster.

The brave bug found the fierce monster, but it was too strong. The bug fought bravely, but it could not win. In the end, the bug disappeared too! But its friends were safe, and forever thankful for brave bug’s courage.

Once upon a time there was a large tree. The tree wanted to help, but it was too big. The tree needed an axe.

One day a kind bear came along. He was very large. He saw the big tree and said he could help. He went to get his axe.

He chopped down the tree. Then he used the wood and branches to help the animals who lived nearby. They all thanked the large bear for his help.

The tree was so glad they found the axe. Now all the animals had homes, food, and shelter. The tree was very proud of the bear and his large axe!

Once there was a poor spot. It was a small, round spot on the ground. The spot was so poor that it had nothing.

One day, the spot decided it wanted to have something. So it looked around to find things. But it couldn't find anything. The spot was so sad.

But then the spot saw a toy. It was a shiny, red toy! The spot reached for the toy, but it was so far away. The spot tried to reach it, but it couldn't. The spot was so sad.

Then, the spot had a plan. It rolled and rolled and rolled until it reached the toy. The spot was so happy! But then it lost its grip on the toy and it rolled away!

The poor spot was so sad. But it was happy that it tried.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lisa. She was a very glad girl and loved spring time. Every day she would go out in the garden and pick flowers.

One day, she decided to make a special surprise for her family. She went around gathering colorful petals and leaves and really made a beautiful piece of art. When she was done, she decided to mail it.

She went to the post office, got the envelope and stamps, and mailed her surprise! She was so happy and couldn't wait to find out the reaction of her family.

Days passed by and one morning, the mailman arrived with a big surprise for Lisa. It was a card from her family. They loved the surprise, thanked her for her hard work and told her that she was the best. Lisa was so glad and filled with joy.

This was the best spring ever for her she thought, filled with surprises and love. She was happy to have shared this joyful moment with the people she love most.

Once upon a time, there was a tiny mouse. It was trying to get to its shelter before the rain started. But it was too late! As soon as the mouse stepped outside, it began to pour. The small mouse was stuck outside in the rain.

Suddenly, it noticed a tree nearby. The tree was big and strong. The mouse had an idea. It quickly ran to the tree and climbed up inside. The tree was its shelter from the rain.

But soon, the mouse began to worry. What if the rain delayed its journey home? The mouse knew it was very important for it to get back home safely as soon as possible.

Luckily, the rain stopped soon enough and the mouse was able to make its way home. It was relieved and very happy. The shelter of the tree had kept it safe and allowed it to return home quickly.

Tom and Sam are friends. They like to play with trucks in the park. Tom has a big red truck. Sam has a small blue truck. They make noises and drive their trucks on the grass.

One day, they see a new boy in the park. He has a yellow truck. But his truck is not like Tom's or Sam's. His truck can spin. He pushes a button and his truck spins around and around. It makes a funny sound. Tom and Sam stop playing and watch the yellow truck.

"Wow, that truck is cool!" Tom says. "I want to try it."

"Me too!" Sam says. They run to the new boy and ask him if they can play with his truck.

The new boy shakes his head. "No, this is my truck. You can't touch it. Go away."

Tom and Sam feel sad and angry. They are jealous of the yellow truck. They want to have a truck that can spin too.

They go back to their trucks and try to make them spin. But they can't. Their trucks only go forward and backward. They don't have a button to make them spin.

They look at the new boy again. He is still spinning his truck and laughing. He doesn't want to share or make friends.

Tom and Sam decide to ignore him. They say to each other, "We don't need his truck. We have our own trucks. And we have each other. We are still friends."

They smile and hug. Then they go back to playing with their trucks. They make noises and drive their trucks on the grass. They have fun. They are happy.

Once there was a mountain and upon it a billboard. Each day the sun shined brightly and the trees sang. But one day, the sun became very harsh, and the billboard got bigger and bigger.

The animals were scared and ran away from it. They gathered around to figure out what to do.

The peacock spoke first. "Let us ask the mountain," said the peacock.

The animals shouted to the mountain. They asked, "Why does the billboard increase? It's too harsh for us."

The mountain replied, "I cannot stop it. It is beyond my control."

The animals then looked around at each other, but no one had any idea how to make the billboard reduce. So the animals kept running away from the bright and harsh billboard.

All the animals lived in fear, until one day the sun went away and the billboard reduced back to its original size. The animals rejoiced and ran home, happy to be back in the peaceful mountain.

Once there was a little girl named Mia. She was feeling very anxious because she saw something strange in her backyard - a tunnel! Mia wanted to fix it and make it better.

She walked up to the tunnel and said "Let's fix it together!"

Mia started to fill up the tunnel with dirt, using her hands and a shovel. She worked really hard and was very careful not to cover up any creatures that were living there.

After she filled the tunnel up all the way, Mia stepped back and looked at her work. The tunnel was fixed! She was so proud of herself and smiled with joy.

Mia had made a big difference and was very happy. From then on, she always tried to fix things that needed help.

George loved to get mail. Every week his grandma would send him something in the mail. Today, he opened a package to find a big ball of yarn. It was so colorful and soft. He couldn't wait to play with it.

He used the yarn to make a lovely scarf. He wrapped the spicy colored yarn around and around until it was long and cozy. He was so proud of his creation.

When his grandma came by, he ran to her, holding the scarf. He excitedly told her about the colorful yarn sent to him in the mail. His grandma was delighted. She showed him how to tie the scarf around his neck.

The spicy colored scarf kept George warm every day until it was too worn out to wear. He proudly hung it on the wall to show his friends all the special things he had made. He loved when his grandma would send him new yarn in the mail.

Once upon a time, there was a happy little pig named Pinky. Pinky lived in a barn with all of her animal friends. One day, Pinky saw an unusual slide outside the barn. She wanted to try it out, but her friends warned her it might not be safe.

Pinky didn't listen and went down the slide anyway. But the slide was too slippery and she went too fast. She couldn't stop and crashed into a tree. Pinky was hurt badly and her friends had to take her to the animal hospital.

Sadly, Pinky never fully recovered from her injuries and couldn't play with her friends anymore. They all felt very sad and missed her very much. They wished Pinky had listened to them and not gone down the unusual slide.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys in the bathtub. One day, she accidentally dropped her favorite toy boat in the sink. She tried to reach it, but it was too far down.

Lily asked her mommy for help. "Mommy, can you please get my boat out of the sink?" she said. Her mommy said, "Sure, I'll get it for you." She reached down and grabbed the boat. "Here you go, Lily. Is everything okay?" she asked.

Lily smiled and said, "Yes, thank you mommy. I'm sorry I dropped my boat in the sink." Her mommy replied, "It's okay, accidents happen. Just be careful next time." Lily nodded and hugged her mommy. She was happy to have her toy boat back in her hands.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Holly. Holly was three years old and she liked to explore new places. One day, Holly decided to go on a big adventure. She packed her things and set off.

Holly walked and walked until she found a big house. She thought this was very exciting! Holly went inside the house to explore. She opened the doors and looked inside the rooms.

Suddenly, she found something. It was a human! Holly was very happy. She talked to the human and asked them questions. But the human said that it was too expensive for her to take home. Holly was sad, but she was still happy she found the human.

Holly said goodbye to the human and continued on her adventure. She travelled for a long time and found lots of interesting things. Holly was very happy that she had gone on the adventure!

Once upon a time there was a rat who went on an adventure. He wanted to see the world, so he decided to visit many different places.

His first stop was a colorful farm. He saw cows and horses, they were all so big and beautiful. He couldn't believe that the animals were so colorful! He continued to explore and saw many different birds and animals.

Next, he decided to visit a river. The water was cool and refreshing. He watched the fish swim and listened to the birds sing. He felt so relaxed and peaceful.

He then visited a park with many tall trees and monuments. He loved the tall buildings and all the green grass. He was amazed by the colorful flowers and enjoyed looking at them.

Finally, the rat found his way home again. He had so much fun visiting different places and was happy to be home safe and sound.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Susie who loved to go to the park. Every day, Susie would go to park and admire all the beautiful things around her.

One day, Susie saw a huge bird in the sky. It was a big, tall crane. Susie was so excited and she ran over to her mom.

Susie said, “Mommy, look at the big bird in the sky!”

Her mom replied, “It’s a crane, Susie. It’s so beautiful!”

Susie was so happy, she ran around trying to get a better look at the crane. Suddenly, Susie saw that the crane was flying away. She looked worriedly at her mom and asked, “Mommy, why is the crane leaving?”

Her mom smiled and said, “The crane has a family it needs to take care of, so it’s going to find them.”

Susie smiled and waved goodbye to the crane as it flew away. She admired the way it flew gracefully in the sky and she knew that the crane was happy to be with its family.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved helicopters. He would always point at them and say "wow!" One day, Timmy saw a helicopter that was troubled. It was making a loud noise and smoke was coming out of it. Timmy was scared.

Timmy saw a man who was trying to fix the helicopter. The man looked worried. Timmy wanted to help, so he went to talk to the man. "Can I help you?" Timmy said. The man smiled and said "sure!" Timmy helped the man fix the helicopter.

Finally, the helicopter was fixed. The man thanked Timmy and took off. Timmy was happy that he could help. But then, something bad happened. The helicopter crashed and the man died. Timmy was sad. He wished he could have done more to help.

Alice was in her car with her dad. She looked out the window and saw a bright blue sky. Everything was calm and peaceful.

Suddenly, Alice noticed something. “Dad!” she said in a cheerful voice, “Look at that car! It’s so cool!”

Alice’s dad smiled. “I know, Alice,” he said. “That’s a great car.”

Alice was so excited she started to bounce up and down in her seat. But then something caught her eye. “Dad, can I drive the car?”

Alice’s dad shook his head. “Not yet, Alice,” he said. “But you can miss the car until you’re big enough to drive it.”

Alice smiled and looked out the window. She felt calm and content knowing that she could drive the car someday.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Jasmine. She loved exploring the forest near her house. She was so brave!

One day, Jasmine decided to go on a big search. She grabbed her coat and put on her boots. She was ready!

Jasmine walked into the forest and soon found a big tree. "Look!" said Jasmine. "I'm gonna climb that tree!"

Jasmine quickly climbed up the tree and sat at the top. From there she could see everything! She saw a sparkly stream and lots of tiny animals. It was so fun!

Suddenly she heard a sound coming from the bushes. It was a dangerous sound - a growling sound. Jasmine was scared!

"Who's there?" she called out.

"It's me," a voice said. It was a fierce looking bear! "What are you doing in my forest?" the bear asked.

"I'm on a search," Jasmine said bravely.

The bear smiled. "That's a good idea," she said. "But it can be dangerous here. So be careful."

Jasmine thanked the bear and then climbed down the tree. She continued her search and had many more adventures!

Susan was playing in the garden. She was swinging on her swing. Suddenly, she saw a mosquito. She shouted loudly and pointed at it. The mosquito flew away quickly.

Susan kept playing. She tried hard to climb up a tree. But it was too difficult. She kept trying, but it was too hard.

Suddenly, her mom shouted from the window. She said, "Come inside now, Susan!" So Susan quickly ran back into the house. She had lots of fun in the garden, but now it was time to go inside.

Mama was in the kitchen getting dinner ready. Baby wanted to help, but Mama said no. "Mama, can I do something?" asked Baby. "No, Baby. You need to stay out," Mama said. Baby saw a big black box sitting in the corner. It had a fierce look. "Mama, what's in the box?" Baby asked. Mama sighed. "It's just some old things, Baby. You can't touch it," she said. But Baby was curious. He wanted to see what was inside. He moved closer. "No, Baby!" Mama said. "You mustn't remove things from the box!" Baby stepped back. He didn't want to make Mama mad. Mama smiled at him. "Now stay out of trouble, okay?" Baby nodded. He stayed far away from the black box.

Lila and Max were best friends. They liked to play in the park with their toys. One day, they saw a new girl with a big doll. The doll had long hair, a pretty dress and shiny shoes. Lila and Max looked at the doll and felt envious.

"Wow, look at her doll!" Lila said. "It is so big and nice. I wish I had a doll like that."

"Me too," Max said. "Maybe we can ask her to play with us and share her doll."

They walked over to the new girl and said hello. The new girl smiled and said her name was Mia. She held her doll close to her waist.

"Hi, Mia. We are Lila and Max. Can we play with you and your doll?" Lila asked.

"Sure, you can play with me. But you can't touch my doll. She is mine and I love her very much. She is the best doll in the world," Mia said.

Lila and Max felt sad. They wanted to play with the doll, but Mia did not want to share. They thought Mia was not very nice. They looked at each other and had an idea.

"Okay, Mia. We will play with you. But we have a game for you. It is called 'seem'. Do you know how to play?" Max asked.

"No, I don't. How do you play?" Mia asked.

"It is easy. You just have to say what things seem like. For example, I can say 'the sky seems blue' or 'the grass seems green'. Do you understand?" Max explained.

"I think so. It sounds fun. Let's play," Mia said.

"Okay, you go first. What does your doll seem like?" Lila asked.

Mia looked at her doll and smiled. She said, "My doll seems like a princess. She has beautiful hair, a lovely dress and sparkly shoes. She is the most wonderful doll ever."

Lila and Max nodded. They waited for Mia to look away. Then they quickly grabbed the doll and ran away. They laughed and said, "Your doll seems like ours now. Bye, Mia!"

Mia was shocked and angry. She shouted and cried. She wanted her doll back. She did not like the game of 'seem'. She thought Lila and Max were very mean. She wished she had shared her doll with them.

Mum and Dad were getting ready to go out on their bikes. They put on their helmets and Dad checked the tires to make sure they were working. Then they were ready to go.

They cycled through the park, going up and down the big hills. It was very rough but they held on tight. Dad was careful to avoid all the bumps in the road.

After a while, they stopped in the clearing. Dad took off his helmet and looked around. He was so happy to be in nature.

They explored for a while, climbing the hills and looking for special things. Then it was time to go home again. Mum and Dad prepared for the journey back. They put on their helmets and started cycling. They were back in no time and were very happy to be home.

Once upon a time there was a foolish black cat who loved to sleep. He would sleep all day long, from morning to night. One day the cat was sleeping in a patch of sun when he was startled by a noise. Something was rustling in the bushes! The cat crept closer and saw a mouse!

The mouse was so small and he had the biggest eyes. The cat was so curious that he wanted to chase it. But he was so sleepy, so he decided to take a nap instead. He curled up near the mouse and started to snooze.

The mouse was soon sound asleep, too. The sun made them both feel so warm and fuzzy inside. When they woke up, they were both still safe and happy. Since then, they have been good friends and always take naps together when they are feeling foolish.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his toys and run around the house. One day, Timmy's mom told him they were going to the park. Timmy was eager to go and play on the swings.

At the park, Timmy ran to the swings and started to swing back and forth. He tried to balance himself and go higher and higher. Suddenly, he felt a rumble in his tummy. He had to go to the toilet!

Timmy's mom took him to the toilet and he felt much better. As they were leaving the toilet, Timmy saw a sign that said "Please wash your hands". Timmy remembered his mom always telling him to wash his hands after going to the toilet. So, he washed his hands and left the toilet feeling happy and clean.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved ice cream and always got a cone when she went to the ice cream shop. One day, she was walking in the park and saw a cone on the ground. She picked it up and saw that it was not smooth, but instead it was bumpy and dirty.

Lily wanted to bury the cone so nobody would see it and step on it. She found a spot under a tree and dug a little hole with her hands. She put the cone in the hole and covered it with dirt.

As she walked away, she felt happy that she did something good for the park. She learned that even small actions, like burying a cone, can make a big difference. It's important to take care of our environment and keep it clean for everyone to enjoy.

Lily liked to play with water. She had a big tub of water in the garden. She had many toys to put in the water. She had a duck, a boat, a fish and a frog. She liked to make them splash in the water. She liked to hear the sound of the water.

One day, Lily wanted to play with water inside the house. She went to the kitchen. She saw a cabinet under the sink. She opened the cabinet. She saw many bottles and boxes. She did not know what they were. She took them out of the cabinet. She put them on the floor.

She saw a big bottle with a blue cap. She liked the color. She opened the bottle. She smelled something funny. She poured some of the liquid in the tub of water. She saw bubbles and foam. She thought it was original. She put the duck, the boat, the fish and the frog in the tub. She made them splash in the water. She liked to see the bubbles and foam.

But the liquid was not water. It was soap. It was not good for the toys. It was not good for the floor. It was not good for Lily. The soap made the toys slippery. The soap made the floor slippery. The soap made Lily's eyes sting.

Lily started to cry. She wanted to stop playing with water. She wanted to put the toys back in the garden. She wanted to put the bottles and boxes back in the cabinet. She wanted to clean the floor. She wanted to wash her eyes. But she could not do it by herself.

She heard her mom coming. She heard her mom saying, "Lily, what have you done?" She saw her mom looking at the mess. She saw her mom looking at her. She felt sorry. She said, "I'm sorry, mom. I wanted to play with water. I wanted to be original. I did not know it was soap." She hoped her mom would not be angry. She hoped her mom would help her. She hoped her mom would hug her.

Lily wanted to go to the park with her mom, but her mom said no. She said they had to go to the store first. Lily did not like the store. It was boring and loud. She wanted to play on the swings and the slide.

"Please, mom, can we go to the park?" Lily asked.

"Not now, Lily. We need to buy some things for dinner. Maybe later, if we have time," her mom said.

Lily was sad and angry. She did not want to wait. She wanted to go to the park now. She saw her mom's purse on the couch. She had an idea. She ran to the purse and grabbed it. She ran to the door.

"Hey, Lily, what are you doing?" her mom said. She saw Lily with her purse. She ran after her.

"Give me back my purse, Lily. That's not nice. You can't take my purse," her mom said.

Lily did not listen. She tried to open the door. She wanted to go outside. She wanted to go to the park. She did not want to give back the purse. She tried to resist her mom.

"No, mom, I want to go to the park. I don't want to go to the store. The park is fun. The store is not," Lily said.

Her mom reached her and took the purse from her. She was not happy. She was upset. She said to Lily:

"Lily, that was very naughty. You can't take my purse without asking. You can't run away from me. You have to listen to me. I'm your mom. I know what's best for you. We have to go to the store. The park is not available right now. Maybe later, if you behave, we can go to the park. But you have to say sorry first."

Lily did not want to say sorry. She did not think she was naughty. She thought her mom was mean. She crossed her arms and pouted. She did not say anything.

Her mom sighed. She said to Lily:

"Lily, I love you, but you have to learn to follow the rules. You have to respect me and my things. You have to be patient and polite. You have to say sorry when you do something wrong. Do you understand?"

Lily looked at her mom. She saw her mom's face. She saw her mom's eyes. She saw her mom's purse. She felt sorry. She did not want to make her mom sad. She wanted to make her mom happy. She wanted to go to the park with her mom. She said to her mom:

"I'm sorry, mom. I love you. I won't take your purse again. I will listen to you. I will go to the store with you. Can we go to the park later?"

Her mom smiled. She hugged Lily. She said to Lily:

"Thank you, Lily. I love you too. I'm glad you said sorry. I forgive you. Yes, we can go to the park later, if we have time. But first, let's go to the store. Maybe we can find something fun there too."

Lily nodded. She took her mom's hand. She went to the store with her mom. She hoped they would have time to go to the park later. She hoped the park would be available. She hoped her mom would be happy. She learned to resist her bad impulses. She learned to respect her mom's purse. She learned to say sorry.

Once upon a time there was a well. This well was very special because it was full of exciting surprises. Every day people from far and wide would come to the well to take a peek inside.

One day, a little girl named Lisa was visiting the well. She was so excited to see what the well had in store for her. She put her hand carefully into the well and pulled out a cheap shiny toy. She was so happy to find the surprise!

The little girl ran to show her parents what she had found. They were so excited to see the toy and gave her lots of hugs and kisses.

From then on, Lisa visited the well every day. She never knew what she would find next, but it always made her very excited.

Lily and Max were playing in the garden. They liked to dig and find bugs and flowers. They had a big box where they kept their treasures. The box had a lock and a key.

One day, Lily wanted to show Max a shiny stone she had found. She ran to the box and tried to unlock it. But the key was not there. She looked around and saw the key on the grass. A bird had taken it and dropped it.

"Max, Max, come here!" she shouted. "The bird took our key!"

Max came running and saw the key. He picked it up and gave it to Lily. "Here you go, Lily. Now you can unlock the box."

Lily smiled and thanked Max. She put the key in the lock and turned it. The box opened and they saw their treasures. Lily took out the shiny stone and showed it to Max.

"Wow, Lily, that's a pretty stone. Where did you find it?" Max asked.

"I found it under a big tree. It was shining in the sun. Do you like it?" Lily asked.

Max nodded. "I like it very much. It's a nice treasure. Can I hold it?"

Lily nodded. "Sure, Max. You can hold it. But be careful. Don't drop it."

Max took the stone and held it in his hand. He felt its smoothness and weight. He looked at its colors and sparkles. He liked it a lot.

"Lily, this is a very good stone. I think it's the best treasure in the box. What do you think?" Max asked.

Lily thought for a moment. She looked at the other treasures in the box. She saw shells, feathers, buttons, and coins. She liked them all. But she liked the stone the most.

"I think you're right, Max. This is the best treasure in the box. It's my favorite. But I'm happy to share it with you. You're my best friend." Lily said.

Max smiled. "You're my best friend too, Lily. Thank you for sharing your stone with me. It's very kind of you."

They hugged and put the stone back in the box. They locked the box and hid the key under a flower pot. They went back to playing in the garden. They were happy and had the same opinion. The stone was the best treasure in the box.

Lily and Ben were playing in the park. They liked to swing, slide and run. But today, it was very hot and sunny. They felt weak and thirsty.

"Can we go home, mom?" Lily asked. "I want some water and a nap."

"Not yet, sweetie," mom said. "We have to wait for dad. He is coming soon."

Lily and Ben sat on a bench under a big tree. They saw a man selling ice cream. They wanted some, but mom said no. She said ice cream was not good for them when they were weak.

"Look, mom, look!" Ben said. He pointed to a palm tree near the ice cream man. "What is that? It has big green leaves and a long brown trunk."

"That is a palm tree, Ben," mom said. "It grows in warm places. It has fruits called dates. They are sweet and chewy."

"Can we have some dates, mom?" Lily asked. "Maybe they will make us strong."

Mom smiled. She walked to the palm tree and picked some dates. She gave one to Lily and one to Ben. They bit into them and felt the juice in their mouths.

"Mmm, these are good, mom," Lily said. "Thank you."

"You're welcome, my loves," mom said. "Now, let's remain here and eat our dates. Dad will be here soon. Then we can go home and have some water and a nap."

Once there was a very intelligent girl. She loved to fold things. Her mum and dad took her on a visit to the park one day.

At the park she found lots of things to fold. She folded leaves, flowers and even big pieces of paper. She folded them very carefully.

Everyone was amazed by her intelligence. Even her mum and dad were surprised by how clever their daughter was.
