Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to ride his bike around the park. One day, Timmy put on his helmet, which was tight on his head, and rushed outside to ride his bike.

As he rode around the park, he saw his friend Billy. Billy didn't have a helmet on his head, so Timmy told him to go home and get his helmet. Billy rushed home to get his helmet, and when he came back, he put it on his head.

Now, Timmy and Billy could ride their bikes together safely with their helmets on. They had so much fun riding around the park together, and they both knew they were being safe with their helmets on. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Tim. Tim loved to go fishing with his dad. They would go to the lake and sit in a boat. Tim would hold a net and wait for the fish to swim by. He loved to catch the fish and put them in a bucket.

One day, Tim and his dad went fishing very early in the morning. The sun was just starting to come up and the light was very pretty. Tim looked out at the water and gazed at the beautiful colors in the sky. He felt happy and peaceful.

After a while, Tim caught a big fish! He was so excited that he jumped up and down. His dad helped him take the fish off the hook and put it in the bucket. Tim was proud of himself and couldn't wait to show his mom the fish when they got home.

Once upon a time, there was a big orange cat. The cat had a tie. The tie was pretty. The cat liked to play with the tie.

One day, the cat went outside to play. The cat found a box. The box was open. The cat put the tie in the box. Then, the cat closed the box.

The cat went home. The cat was happy. The cat had a fun day with the tie and the box. The cat liked the orange tie and the closed box.

Once upon a time, there was an incredible farmer. He loved the land more than anything.

One day, he was walking around his farm when he heard a strange noise. It was a voice which said: "I urge you, please help me!"

The farmer was very curious, so he followed the voice. Suddenly, he saw a tiny mouse.

The mouse said: "I'm stuck under this big rock and I can't get out. Please help me!"

The farmer was very kind, so he got down and carefully lifted the rock. As soon as the mouse was free, he thanked the farmer and ran away.

The farmer smiled and said: "That was an incredible act of kindness."

One day, a little girl named Lily went to the kitchen. She saw her mom making a hot drink. "Mom, what is that?" Lily asked. "It's coffee, dear," her mom said. Lily wanted to try it, but her mom did not permit her. "No, Lily. Coffee is not for little kids."

Lily felt miserable. She wanted to taste the coffee. She thought it would be fun. So, she made a plan. When her mom went to the living room, Lily took a little sip of the coffee. But it was not good at all. It was bitter and yucky. Lily made a face and said, "Yuck!"

Her mom came back and saw Lily's face. She knew Lily had tried the coffee. "Now you know why I didn't permit you to drink coffee," her mom said. "It's not for little kids like you." Lily nodded and said, "I understand now, Mom. I won't try it again." They both smiled and hugged each other.

Sara liked to roll her stuff on the floor. She had a ball, a car, a doll and a bear. She made them go fast and slow, and made noises for them. She was happy.

But her brother Tom did not like her stuff. He said they were baby things. He wanted to play with his big toys, like his bike and his robot. He was angry.

One day, Sara was rolling her stuff on the floor, when Tom came in. He saw her stuff and kicked them away. He said they were stupid and boring. He took his bike and his robot and left. Sara was sad.

She cried and picked up her stuff. She hugged them and said sorry. She wished Tom would be nice to her and her stuff. She was lonely.

But then, she heard a loud noise outside. She looked out the window and saw Tom. He had fallen off his bike and his robot was broken. He was hurt and scared. He cried and called for Sara.

Sara ran outside and saw Tom. She felt sorry for him and his stuff. She helped him up and hugged him. She said it was okay and she loved him. She gave him her ball and her bear. He smiled and said thank you. He said he was sorry and he loved her. He gave her his bike and his robot. They were happy.

They went inside and played with their stuff. They rolled them on the floor and made noises for them. They were quiet and nice. They were friends.

Tom was very excited. He was playing with his new toy - a yellow string! He poked it, pulled it and twisted it in between his fingers. He couldn't wait to show his sister.

When she came home, he showed her the string and she was so excited too! She giggled and poked the string too. She twisted it around her wrists like bracelets.

Then Tom and his sister went outside and took the string with them. They held the two ends of the string and tried to stretch it as far as they could. Tom got so excited when he saw how long the string had become!

They laughed and giggled while they were playing with the string. It was so much fun! But soon enough it was time to go home, so Tom put the string back into his toy box.

He couldn't wait to play with it again the next day!

One day, a restless girl wanted to explore. She asked to go to the forest, and her parents said yes. The girl was so excited. She quickly put on her best shoes and ran out the door.

When she arrived, the forest was full of trees, bushes, and animals. The girl was amazed. She giggled with delight as she chased a squirrel up the nearest tree.

As she continued exploring, she saw something in the distance. It looked like a cage, but she couldn't tell what was inside. She bravely poked at the bars with a stick, and suddenly, the door opened. Out flew a beautiful butterfly!

The butterfly quickly fluttered around the girl's head. She was filled with joy! She then released the butterfly back out into the forest. Off it went as she watched with a smile.

The girl had an amazing adventure that day. She went back home feeling more peaceful than ever.

Sam liked to study golf. He watched his dad play golf on TV and learned the names of the clubs and the holes. He also had a toy golf set that he played with in the yard. He wanted to be a good golfer like his dad.

One day, his dad said, "Sam, do you want to come with me to the golf course? I have a lesson with the coach and you can watch and learn."

Sam was very happy and said, "Yes, dad, I want to go!"

They got in the car and drove to the golf course. Sam saw many people playing golf and hitting the ball with different clubs. He also saw the coach, who was a tall and friendly man. He said hello to Sam and his dad and gave them some tips.

"Sam, do you want to try hitting the ball?" the coach asked.

Sam nodded and took a small club from his toy set. He put the ball on the ground and swung the club. But he missed the ball and fell down. He felt embarrassed and sad.

The coach and his dad helped him up and said, "Don't worry, Sam, it's okay. Golf is hard and you need to practice a lot. You are doing great for your age. Just keep studying and trying and you will get better."

Sam felt better and said, "Thank you, coach, thank you, dad. I will keep studying and trying. I want to be a dependable golfer like you."

The coach and his dad smiled and said, "You are welcome, Sam. We are proud of you. You are a dependable son and a good learner. You have a bright future in golf."

Sam hugged them and said, "I love you, coach, I love you, dad. You are the best teachers."

The moral of the story is: study hard, try your best, and don't give up. You will learn from your mistakes and improve your skills. You will also earn the respect and love of your teachers and parents.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Ella. Every morning, Ella's mommy would make her a special breakfast with a pan. Ella was so happy and thankful for the yummy breakfast! But one morning when Ella's mommy was making breakfast, something happened. The kitchen was spinning around and around and Ella felt very dizzy. She tried to stay on her feet but quickly fell to the ground. Ella's mommy was concerned, so she took Ella to the doctor to get checked out. After the doctor examined Ella, she was given the all-clear and felt much better. Ella's mommy was so relieved and thanked the doctor. Ella was thankful too. From that day on, Ella was extra careful in the kitchen and made sure to stay away from the pan.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play in the mud and dig for worms. One day, Timmy found a big, juicy worm and he was so excited. He picked it up carefully and held it in his hand.

But then, Timmy's little sister came over and wanted to play too. She accidentally knocked the worm out of Timmy's hand and it fell onto the wet ground. Timmy was sad because he thought the worm might get hurt.

He quickly picked up the worm and wiped it dry with his shirt. The worm was okay! Timmy was so happy that he was able to be careful and help the worm. From that day on, Timmy and his sister played together and were always careful with the worms they found in the mud. The end.

Ben likes to play basketball with his dad. They have a big orange ball that bounces and a hoop on the wall. Ben tries to throw the ball in the hoop, but it is too high for him. His dad helps him and says, "Good job, Ben!"

One day, Ben sees a shiny new ball in the store. It is red and blue and has stars on it. Ben wants the ball very much. He asks his dad, "Can we buy this ball, please?" His dad looks at the price tag and shakes his head. He says, "No, Ben, this ball is too expensive. We already have a good ball at home."

Ben feels sad and angry. He does not want the old ball. He wants the new ball. He starts to cry and kick his feet. His dad picks him up and carries him out of the store. He says, "Ben, you need to calm down. Throwing a tantrum is not nice. You should be happy with what you have."

Ben stops crying and looks at his dad. He sees that his dad is not happy either. He says, "I'm sorry, dad. I love you and I love our ball." His dad smiles and hugs him. He says, "I love you too, Ben. And I'm proud of you for saying sorry. How about we go home and play some basketball?"

Ben nods and smiles. He and his dad go home and play with their big orange ball. Ben has fun and forgets about the new ball. He learns that expensive things are not always better than simple things. He also learns to sit and listen to his dad when he says no.

Once upon a time, there was a beautiful olive tree. It had green leaves and big olives that were so juicy they looked like they had been freshly plucked. Every day the olive tree spoke to the sun, the animals, and the birds that visited.

One day, a little bird came close to the olive tree and spoke to it. "Please, I am so hungry!", begged the bird. The olive tree felt sorry for the little bird and offered some olives as a snack.

The little bird happily took the olives and thanked the olive tree for being so kind. The olive tree replied, "Whenever you are hungry, you can come here and olives will always be available for you."

The little bird felt so lucky to find such a generous olive tree. He went back to the olive tree whenever he was hungry, and the tree was always ready to provide him with plenty of olives. It was like the tree had known that the bird would need it, and was waiting for him.

Ben and Lily wanted to mail a card to their grandma. They drew pictures of flowers and hearts on the card. They wrote "We love you, Grandma" with big letters. They put the card in an envelope and asked their mom for a stamp.

"Can we go to the mailbox now, Mom?" Ben asked.

"Not yet, sweeties. We have to go to the store first. We need to buy some squash for dinner. Do you want to help me pick one?" Mom said.

"Yes, Mom!" Lily said. She liked squash. It was orange and soft and sweet.

They got in the car and drove to the store. Mom gave them a basket and told them to look for the squash. They saw many different kinds of squash. Some were green, some were yellow, some were round, some were long.

"Which one should we get, Ben?" Lily asked.

"Let's get this one!" Ben said. He pointed to a big, orange squash. It looked like a pumpkin, but smaller.

"OK, Ben. That's a good one. It's called a butternut squash. It's very tasty and healthy. Let's see if it's available." Lily said. She looked at the price tag. It said $1.99 per pound.

"Is that a lot, Lily?" Ben asked.

"I don't know, Ben. Let's ask Mom." Lily said. They took the squash to Mom, who was buying some apples.

"Mom, can we get this squash?" Lily asked.

"Sure, honey. That's a nice squash. Let me weigh it for you." Mom said. She put the squash on the scale. It said 2.5 pounds.

"That's $4.98, kids. Do you have enough money?" Mom asked.

Ben and Lily looked at each other. They had saved some coins in their piggy bank. They had $5.00.

"Yes, Mom! We have enough money!" Ben said.

"Great! Then you can buy the squash with your own money. That's very grown-up of you. I'm proud of you, kids." Mom said.

She gave them the money and they paid the cashier. They put the squash in their basket and went back to the car.

"Now can we go to the mailbox, Mom?" Ben asked.

"Yes, of course. Let's go mail your card to Grandma. She will be very happy to receive it." Mom said.

They drove to the mailbox and Ben and Lily took turns to put the envelope in the slot. They waved goodbye to the card and hoped Grandma would like it.

They went home and Mom cooked the squash for dinner. It was delicious. Ben and Lily ate it all. They felt happy and full.

They called Grandma on the phone and told her about their day. They told her they mailed her a card and bought a squash. Grandma said she loved them very much and thanked them for the card and the squash. She said she would mail them a card back soon.

Ben and Lily smiled and said goodnight to Grandma. They hugged Mom and went to bed. They dreamed of flowers and hearts and squash.
